# Narada-purana

## Section 1. Purvabhaga

## Chapter 1. The Dialogue between Suta and the Sages

## \|\| 1.1.1 \|\|

*vṛnde vṛndāvanāsīnamindirānandamandiram \|*  
*upendraṃ sāṃdra kāruṇyaṃ parānandaṃ parātparam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Om, obeisance to the holy preceptors. Om, bow to Lord Ganesa. Om, salutations to glorious Lord Vasudeva. Om, after making obeisance to Narayana as well as to Nara, the most excellent among men, and also to goddess Sarasvati, one should begin the recitation of *Jaya* (*the Narada Purana*).  
Om, obeisance to Veda-Vyasa. I bow to Upendra (Lord Visnu), who abides (permanently) in Vrndavana and is the shrine of Bliss unto Indira (goddess Laksmi); who abounds in compassion and is greater than the greatest and whose form constitutes the highest Bliss.

## \|\| 1.1.2 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇumaheśākhyā yasyāṃśā lokasādhakāḥ \|*  
*tamādidevaṃ cidrū paṃ viśuddhaṃ paramaṃ bhaje \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I worship that Supreme primordial Lord whose form is the purest Consciousness (cid-rupa); who is the greatest (of all beings), and whose parts called Brahma, Visnu, and Mahesha (Siva) are (the deities) who accomplish (the cycle of creation, maintenance and destruction of) the world.

## \|\| 1.1.3 \|\|

*śaunakādyā mahātmāna ṛṣayo brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*naimiṣākhye mahāraṇye tapastepurmumukṣavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Saunaka and other noble-souled sages, the expounders of the Brahman, performed a penance in the great forest named Naimisa, with a desire to attain Final Liberation.

## \|\| 1.1.4 \|\|

*jitendri yā jitāhārāḥ santaḥ satyaparākramāḥ \|*  
*yajantaḥ parayā bhaktyā viṣṇumādyaṃ sanātanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They had conquered their sense-organs; had full control over their diet; they were saintly persons of truthful exploits. With greatest devotion, they worshipped the eternal, primordial Visnu.

## \|\| 1.1.5 \|\|

*anīrṣyāḥ sarvadharmajñā lokānugrahatatparāḥ \|*  
*nirmmamā nirahaṃkārāḥ parasminratamānasāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They were above jealousy and were conversant with all holy rites. They were devoutly engaged in blessing the world and had no feeling of my-ness (sense of personal possession). They were devoid of egotism and their minds revelled in the transcendental Atman.

## \|\| 1.1.6 \|\|

*nyastakāmā vivṛjināḥ śamādiguṇasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinottarīyāste jaṭilā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They had renounced all passions and longings and were sinless; they were endowed with self-control and other good qualities. With matted hair and the hide of black-antelope as their upper garments, they led a celibate life (Lit. they observed the vow of celibacy).

## \|\| 1.1.7 \|\|

*gṛṇantaḥ paramaṃ brahma jagaccakṣuḥsamaujasaḥ \|*  
*dharmaśāstrārthatattvajñāstepurnaimiṣakānane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They eulogised the Supreme Brahman, the eye of the universe. All of them were of equal prowess. They were the knowers of the meaning and reality of the sacred scriptures. They performed penance in the Naimisa forest.

## \|\| 1.1.8 \|\|

*yajñairyajñapatiṃ kecijjñānairjñānātmakaṃ pare \|*  
*kecicca parayā bhaktyā nārāyaṇamapūjayan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Some of them worshipped the Lord of sacrifices by performance of sacrifices; others worshipped the Deity, the Embodiment of spiritual knowledge, by means of the path of knowledge; some worshipped Narayana with devotion par excellence.

## \|\| 1.1.9 \|\|

*ekadā te mahātmānaḥ samājaṃ cakruruttamāḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāmupāyāñjñātumicchavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Desirous of understanding the means of righteousness, wealth, love and Final Beatitude (the four Purufdrthas), those excellent noble-minded (high-souled) sages met in a congregation.

## \|\| 1.1.10 \|\|

*ṣaḍviṃśatisahasrāṇi munīnāmūrddhvaretasām \|*  
*teṣāṃ śiṣyapraśiṣyāṇāṃ saṃkhyā vaktuṃ na śakyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The sages of sublimated sexuality numbered twenty-six thousand. It is impossible to enumerate the disciples and the pupils of their disciples.

## \|\| 1.1.11 \|\|

*munayo bhāvitātmāno militāste mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*lokānugrahakartāro vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Those sages of sanctified souls (through meditation), of great prowess, met together. Devoid of passion and jealousy, they desired to do (something) to bless the world.

## \|\| 1.1.12 \|\|

*kāni kṣetrāṇi puṇyāni kāni tīrthāni bhūtale \|*  
*kathaṃ vā prāpyate muktirnṛṇāṃ tāpārtacetasām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (The questions that made them ponder were): What are the sacred places of pilgrimage (kshetra), and the shrines or holy places (near the banks of sacred rivers, lakes, etc.) — the tirthas —? How is liberation (from Samsara) achieved by men distressed in their minds by worldly miseries (of three kinds).

## \|\| 1.1.13 \|\|

*kathaṃ harau manuṣyāṇāṃ bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*kena siddhyte ca phalaṃ karmaṇastrividhātmanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. How is the devotion of men unswervingly directed towards Hari? By what means can one achieve the fruit of the three types of activities (viz. mental, verbal and physical)?

## \|\| 1.1.14 \|\|

*ityevaṃ praṣṭumātmānamudyatān prekṣya śaunakaḥ \|*  
*prāñjalirvākyamāhedaṃ vinayāvanataḥ sudhīḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing the sages eagerly intent on asking him (these questions) in this manner, the intelligent Saunaka spoke these words with palms joined in reverence, and bowing down with humility. Shaunaka said:

## \|\| 1.1.15 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca-*  
*āste siddhāśrame puṇye sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ \|*  
*yajanmakhairbahuvidhairviśvarūpaṃ janārdanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the holy hermitage of Siddhasrama, there lives Suta, the most excellent of all the Pauranikas (exponents of the Puranas). With different types of sacrifices, he worships Janardana of universal form.

## \|\| 1.1.16 \|\|

*sa etadakhilaṃ vetti vyāsaśiṣyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*purāṇasaṃhitāvaktā śānto vai romaharṣaṇiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. That great sage, the son of Romaharsana, the quiescent disciple of Vyasa knows this completely. He is the propounder of the Purana texts. So the tradition goes.

## \|\| 1.1.17 \|\|

*yuge yuge'lpakān dharmān nirīkṣya madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*vedavyāsasvarūpeṇa vedabhāgaṃ karoti hi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing piety and religious rites being (progressively) reduced (in quantity and quality) from Yuga to Yuga (successively) the slayer of Madhu (Lord Visnu), assuming the form of Veda-Vyasa classifies the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.1.18 \|\|

*vedavyāsamuniḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇa iti dvijāḥ \|*  
*śuśrumaḥ sarvaśāstreṣu sūtastu vyāsaśāsitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О Brahmanas, we have heard that the sage Veda- Vyasa is Narayana himself. And Suta has been initiated into all sacred texts directly by Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.1.19 \|\|

*tena saṃśāsitaḥ sūto vedavyāsena dhīmatā \|*  
*purāṇāni sa vettyeva nānyo loke tataḥ paraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Suta has been instructed and initiated by that intelligent Veda-Vyasa. He does know all the Puranas. There is none competent than he (in this respect) in this world.

## \|\| 1.1.20 \|\|

*sa purāṇārthavilloke sa sarvajñaḥ sa buddhimān \|*  
*sa śānto mokṣadharmajñaḥ karmabhaktikalāpavit \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In this world, he is the only knower of the import of all Puranas. He is intelligent, omniscient and quiescent. He knows the path of righteousness leading to final liberation as well as the entire corpus of (the theory and practice of) the paths of action and devotion.

## \|\| 1.1.21 \|\|

*vedavedāṅgaśāstrāṇāṃ sārabhūtaṃ munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*jagaddhitārthaṃ tatsarvaṃ purāṇeṣūktavān muniḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О prominent sages, the sage Vyasa has, for the benefit of the universe, expounded, in the Puranas all those topics that constitute the essence of the Vedas, the Vedangas (the ancillary subjects pertaining to Vedas) and the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.1.22 \|\|

*jñānārṇavo vai sūtastatsarvatattvārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttameva pṛcchāma ityūce śaunako munīn \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Suta is indeed an ocean of knowledge. He proficiently knows the real nature of (and the exact truth about) everything. Hence, we shall ask him. So said Saunaka to the sages.

## \|\| 1.1.23 \|\|

*tataste munayaḥ sarve śaunakaṃ vāgvidāṃ varam \|*  
*samāśliṣya susamprītāḥ sādhu sādhviti cābruvan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then all those delighted sages embraced Saunaka, the most excellent of those conversant with the realm of speech. “Well-spoken. Well-advised”, said they (to express their approval).

## \|\| 1.1.24 \|\|

*atha te munayo jagmuḥ puṇyaṃ siddhāśramaṃ vane \|*  
*mṛgavrajasamākīrṇaṃ munibhiḥ pariśobhitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter, those sages went to the holy Siddhashrama in the forest. It abounded in groups of deer. It was graced with the residence of sages (living therein).

## \|\| 1.1.25 \|\|

*manojñabhūruhalatāphalapuṣpavibhūṣitam \|*  
*yuktaṃ sarobhiracchodairatithyātithyasaṃkulam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It was beautified with charming trees and creepers (full of abundant) flowers and fruits, apd was spotted with lakes of crystalline water and was inhabited by persons warmly hospitable to guests (and strangers arriving there).

## \|\| 1.1.26 \|\|

*te tu nārāyaṇaṃ devamanantamaparājitam \|*  
*yajantamagniṣṭomena dadṛśū romaharṣaṇim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. They (the sages of the Naimisa forest) saw the son of Romaharshana worshipping the infinite unvanquished Lord Narayana, by means of the Agnistoma sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.1.27 \|\|

*yathārhamarcitāstena sūtena prathitaujasaḥ \|*  
*tasyāvabhṛthamīkṣantastatra tasthurmakhālaye \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Suitably honoured by Suta, those sages of well-known powers, remained there in the hall of sacrifice, awaiting the concluding rites of ablution (Avabhrtha).

## \|\| 1.1.28 \|\|

*adharāvabhṛthasnātaṃ sūtaṃ paurāṇikottamam \|*  
*papracchuste sukhāsīnaṃ naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Afterwards, when Suta, the excellent-most of all Pauranikas completed the rites of Avabhrtha ablution, those residents of the Naimisa forest asked him, as he seated himself comfortably. The sages said:

## \|\| 1.1.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ-*  
*vayaṃ tvatithayaḥ prāptā ātitheyāstu suvrata \|*  
*jñānadānopacāreṇa pūjayāsmān yathāvidhi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О strict observer of religious vows we who ought to be hospitable to you as hosts, have come here as your guests. However, be pleased to honour us duly by means of homage in the form of charitable gift of perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.1.30 \|\|

*divaukaso hi jīvanti pītvā candra kalāmṛtam \|*  
*jñānāmṛtaṃ bhūsurāstu mune tvanmukhaniḥsṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Whereas the heaven-dwelling gods live by drinking the nectarine juice from the digits of the moon, the earth- dwelling gods (the Brahmanas) do so by drinking the nectarine juice of the perfect knowledge exuding from your mouth, О sage.

## \|\| 1.1.31 \|\|

*yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ yadādhāraṃ yadātmakam \|*  
*yasminpratiṣṭhitaṃ tāta yasmin vā layameṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\*. (Who is that lord) by whom all this (the universe) was created, who is the support of all this, who is the Soul of all this, in whom, О dear one, everything is well established and in whom everything will get dissolved?

## \|\| 1.1.32 \|\|

*kena viṣṇuḥ prasannaḥ syāt sa kathaṃ pūjyate naraiḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ varṇāśramācāraścātitheḥ pūjanaṃ katham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\*. By what does Visnu become propitiated? How is he worshipped by men? What is the code of conduct of life for the people in the various castes and walks of life? How is the guest to be worshipped?

(Better if 31 and 32 are taken together. This (31) verse then becomes a sort of an adjectival clause describing Vi?shu in the next verse).

## \|\| 1.1.33 \|\|

*saphalaṃ syādyathā karma mokṣopāyaḥ kathaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*bhaktyā kiṃ prāpyate puṃbhistathā bhaktiśca kīdṛśī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. What is that whereby the holy rites shall be fruitful? What is the means of salvation for men? What is achieved by men through devotion? And of what nature is devotion?

## \|\| 1.1.34 \|\|

*vada sūta muniśreṣṭha sarvametadasaṃśayam \|*  
*kasya no jāyate śraddhā śrotuṃ ttadvacanāmṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О Suta, the most excellent of all sages, explain these things, dispelling every doubtful factor. Who is not keenly desirous to hear the nectarine words of yours? Suta said:

## \|\| 1.1.35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca-*  
*śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ sarve yadiṣṭaṃ vo vadāmi tat \|*  
*gītaṃ sanakamukhyaistu nāradāya mahātmane \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Listen ye all, О sages. I shall recount what is desired by you. This has been narrated to the noble-souled Narada by those sages the chief of whom was Sanaka.

## \|\| 1.1.36 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ nāradopākhyametadvedārthasammitam \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ duṣṭagrahanivāraṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This Purana named after Narada is on a par with the Vedas in regard to its import (*artha*). It is destructive of all sins It wards off the influence of all evil planets.

## \|\| 1.1.37 \|\|

*duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ dharmyaṃ bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|*  
*nārāyaṇakathopetaṃ sarvakalyāṇakāraṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is conducive to piety and destructive of the effects of evil dreams. It yields as fruits worldly pleasures as well as salvation. Containing narratives of Narayana, it is the cause of everything blessed and auspicious.

## \|\| 1.1.38 \|\|

*dhamārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ hetubhūtaṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*apūrvapuṇyaphaladaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It brings about piety, wealth, love and liberation. It is highly efficacious as it yields unprecedented merit as its fruit. Listen to it with great concentration.

## \|\| 1.1.39 \|\|

*mahāpātakayukto vā yukto vāpyupapātakaiḥ \|*  
*śrutvaitadārṣaṃ divyaṃ ca purāṇaṃ śuddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One may be defiled by great sins or subsidiary ones. But on hearing this divine Purana pertaining to sages and ascetics, one shall regain purity.

## \|\| 1.1.40 \|\|

*yasyaikādhyāyapaṭhanād vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*adhyāyadvayapāṭhena rājasūyaphalaṃ tathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On reading a single chapter of this Purana one shall attain the benefit of (the performance of a) horse-sacrifice. Similarly, on reading two chapters, one attains the spiritual rewards of performance of Rajasuуa sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.1.41-42 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāse pūrṇimāyāṃ mūlarkṣe prayato naraḥ \|*  
*snātvā ca yamunātoye mathurāyāmupoṣitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*abhyarcya vidhivat kṛṣṇaṃ yatphalaṃ labhate dvijāḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti adhyāyatrayapāṭhataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. О Brahmins, by reading three chapters one attains the same merit as a man who takes bath in the waters of the Yamuna on the full-moon day in the month of Jyestha with the moon in the constellation Mula, who observes fast with great purity, at Mathura and who duly worships Krsna.

## \|\| 1.1.43-44 \|\|

*tatpravakṣyāmi vaḥ samyak śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama \|*  
*janmāyutārjitaiḥ pāpairmuktaḥ koṭikulānvitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*brahmaṇaḥ padamāsādya tatraiva pratitiṣṭhati \|*  
*śrutvāsya tu daśādhyāyān bhaktibhāvena mānavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. I shall explain (one thing more) very well. Even as I recount, listen well. A man who listens to ten chapters of this (Purana) with feelings of earnest devotion, shall attain to the region of Brahma and stay therein. He will be freed from sins accumulated in the course of ten thousand births. He shall be followed by a ten million members of his family.

## \|\| 1.1.45-50 \|\|

*nirvāṇamuktiṃ labhate nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*śreyasāṃ paramaṃ śreyaḥ pavitrāṇāmanuttamam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ puṇyaṃ śrotavyaṃ yatnato dvijāḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā sahito martyaḥ ślokaṃ ślokārdhameva vā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*paṭhitvā mucyate sadyo mahāpātakarāśibhiḥ \|*  
*satāmeva pravaktavyaṃ guhyād guhyataraṃ yataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vācayet purato viṣṇoḥ puṇyakṣetre dvijāntike \|*  
*brahmadro haparāṇāṃ ca dambhācārayutātmanām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*janānāṃ bakavṛttīnāṃ na brūyādidamuttamam \|*  
*tyaktakāmādidoṣāṇāṃ viṣṇubhaktiratātmanām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sadācāraparāṇāṃ ca vaktavyaṃ mokṣasādhanam \|*  
*sarvadevamayo viṣṇuḥ smaratāmārtināśanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

45-48a. No doubt or hesitation need be entertained in this matter that he will attain the final beatitude. This is more blessed than the most blessed. It is pre-eminently the best of all sanctifying things. It is meritorious and destructive of (the effects of) evil dreams. О Brahmins, this must be listened to, assiduously. A man of faith who reads at least a verse or even half of a verse is immediately absolved of heaps of great sins. Since this is the secret of all secrets, it must be narrated only to good men. This must be made to be read in front of Visnu, in the presence of Brahmins, in a holy place or shrine.

48b-49a . One shall not narrate this excellent Purana to persons engaged in injuring the cause of Brahmanas and to those persons who are religious-hypocrites like (proverbial) cranes (which are supposed to pretend meditation till a fish comes within their reach).

49b-50. This, being the means to liberation from samsara, should be recounted to those who are devoted to the pious course of life and whose mind (atman), with lust and other noxious qualities eschewed out, revels in the devotion to Visnu. For Visnu comprises within himself all gods and destroys the agonies and applications of those who remember him.

## \|\| 1.1.51-52 \|\|

*sadbhaktivatsalo vipro bhaktyā tuṣyati nānyathā \|*  
*aśraddhayāpi yannāmni kīrtite'tha smṛte'pi vā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vimuktaḥ pātakairmartyo labhate padamavyayam \|*  
*saṃsāraghorakāntāradāvāgnirmadhusūdanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. He is favourably disposed towards his pious devotees, О Brahmanas. He becomes pleased only with devotion and nothing else. A man is freed from sins if he glorifies or remembers Visnu’s name even without faith. He attains to the Eternal region (Vaikuntha) the unchanging region. Madhu-sudana (the destroyer of the demon Madhu) is like the big forest conflagration unto the terrible jungle of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.1.53 \|\|

*smaratāṃ sarvapāpāni nāśayatyāśu sattamāḥ \|*  
*tadarthadyotakamidaṃ purāṇaṃ śrāvyamuttamam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He quickly destroys all the sins of those who remember him, О excellent ones. This excellent Purana which indicates that meaning and purpose should be listened to.

## \|\| 1.1.53-55 \|\|

*smaratāṃ sarvapāpāni nāśayatyāśu sattamāḥ \|*  
*tadarthadyotakamidaṃ purāṇaṃ śrāvyamuttamam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*śravaṇāt paṭhanādvāpi sarvapāpavināśakṛt \|*  
*yasyāsya śravaṇe buddhirjāyate bhaktisaṃyutā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sa eva kṛtakṛtyastu sarvaśāstrārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*yadarjitaṃ tapaḥ puṇyaṃ tanmanye saphalaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

53a. By listening to it or reading it one is able to annihilate all sins.

53b-55. Only he who, with a devoted mind, is inclined to listen to this Purana, has really accomplished his objects in life (Krta-krtya) and can be regarded as adept in understanding and interpreting all the scriptural precepts. О Brahmins, I consider that whatever merits are earned or austerities performed by him, are really fruitful.

## \|\| 1.1.56 \|\|

*yadasya śravaṇe bhaktiranyathā na hi jāyate \|*  
*satkathāsu pravartante sajjanā ye jagaddhitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. (Unless one has a fund of merits) it is not possible for him to have devout inclination towards listening to God’s stories or Purana. Those good men who are the benefactors of the universe, are engaged in stories about the Supreme Spirit.

## \|\| 1.1.57-58 \|\|

*nindāyāṃ kalahe vāpi hyasantaḥ pāpatatparāḥ \|*  
*purāṇeṣvarthavādatvaṃ ye vadanti narādhamāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tairarjitāni puṇyāni kṣayaṃ yānti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*samastakarmanirmūlasādhanāni narādhamaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57a. The wicked or evil persons are exclusively devoted to sinful activities and are engaged in censure and quarrels.

57b-58. О excellent Brahmins, the merits (if any) earned by those vilest of men who (i) attribute laudatory nature to Purarias (or) (ii) who allege that the Puranas are merely laudatory passages (*Artha-vada*) become exhausted. (For the Puranas are really the means of eradication of all binding actions.

## \|\| 1.1.59 \|\|

*purāṇānyarthavādena bruvannarakamaśnute \|*  
*anyāni sādhayantyeva kāryāṇi vidhinā narāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A person who speaks of Puranas as being arthavada, falls into hell. О excellent Brahmins, men duly pursue and attain other objects of worldly pleasure.

## \|\| 1.1.60-62 \|\|

*purāṇāni dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sādhayanti na mohitāḥ \|*  
*anāyāsena yaḥ puṇyānīcchatīha dvijottamāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*śrotavyāni purāṇāni tena vai bhaktibhāvataḥ \|*  
*purāṇaśravaṇe buddhiryasya puṃsaḥ pravartate \|\| 61 \|\|*

*purārjitāni pāpāni tasya naśyantyasaṃśayam \|*  
*purāṇe vartamāne'pi pāpapāśena yantritaḥ \|*  
*ādareṇānyagāthāsu saktabuddhiḥ patatyadhaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-61a. But persons who are deluded do not do the same for accomplishing the Puranas. О excellent Brahmins, Puranas must be listened to with great devout feelings by the person who desires to accumulate merits without strain (trouble or exertion).

61b-62. Undoubtedly the sins incurred earlier by that person who feels inclined to listen to the Puranas are destroyed. Even while the Puranas exist, if a person, compelled by sins, feels drawn towards other gathas (folk songs and fables) and is attached to them, he faces downfall.

## \|\| 1.1.63 \|\|

*satsaṅgadevārcanasatkathāsu hitopadeśe nirato manuṣyaḥ \|*  
*prayātiviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ yaddehāvasāne'cyutatulyatejāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A man engaged in associating himself with the good, worshipping the deities, and narrating or listening to noble stories of God as well as in imparting beneficial instructions, goes to the highest region of Visnu. After death, he attains a brilliance comparable to that of Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.1.64 \|\|

*tasmādidaṃ nāradanāmadheyaṃ puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ śṛṇuta dvijendrā ḥ! \|*  
*yasmiñchrute janmajarādihīno naro bhavedacyutaniṣṭhacetāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Hence, О prominent Brahmanas, listen to this holy meritorious Purana named after Narada. On hearing this, a man becomes free from old age, rebirth, etc. His mind becomes stabilised in Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.1.65 \|\|

*varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ purāṇaṃ nijaprabhābhāvitasarvalokam \|*  
*saṃkalpitārthapradamādidevaṃ smṛtvā vrajenmuktipadaṃ manuṣyaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Purana is excellent and highly pre-eminent. It grants the desired boons. By its own lustre, it has sanctified all the worlds. By remembering the primordial Deity that bestows the cherished objects, a man attains the state of salvation.

## \|\| 1.1.66 \|\|

*brahmeśaviṣṇvādiśarīrabhedairviśvaṃ sṛjatyatti ca pāti viprāḥ \|*  
*tamādidevaṃ paramaṃ pareśamādhāya cetasyupayāti muktim \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О Brahmins, he creates, protects and annihilates the universe by assuming different bodies of Brahma, Visnu and Isa. By contemplating in one’s mind that primordial Lord the transcendental Ruler, one attains liberation.

## \|\| 1.1.67 \|\|

*yo nāma jātyādivikalpahīnaḥ paraḥ parāṇāṃ paramaḥ parasmāt \|*  
*vedāntavedyaḥ svajanaprakāśaḥ samīḍyate sarvapurāṇavedaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He who is devoid of all such (varieties based on ignorance) and alternatives such as name, caste (birth), etc., who is the greatest among the great beings, who transcends the greatest, who is comprehensible only through the Vedanta and who reveals himself unto his devotees, is highly praised by all Puranas and Vedas.

## \|\| 1.1.68 \|\|

*tasmāttamīśaṃ jagatāṃ vimuktimupāsanāyālamajaṃ murārim \|*  
*paraṃ rahasyaṃ puruṣārthahetuṃ smṛtvā naro yāti bhavābdhipāram \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\*. Hence, that Lord of the worlds, the cause of liberation, the Eternal, Slayer of Mura is competent to be worshipped. By remembering the great mystic secret, the cause of attainment of the Purusarthas (objectives) a man crosses the ocean of worldly existence.

\* - Can we net take it as one sentence thus “Hence by remembering that Lord... whose worship is sufficiently efficacious... a man crosses... existence'?

## \|\| 1.1.69 \|\|

*vaktavyaṃ dhārmikebhyastu śraddadhānebhya eva ca \|*  
*mumukṣubhyo yatibhyaśca vītarāgebhya eva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. This should be recited only to righteous persons, the faithful ones and to ascetics devoid of passion, and to persons seeking salvation.

## \|\| 1.1.70 \|\|

*vaktavyaṃ puṇyadeśe ca sabhāyāṃ devatāgṛhe \|*  
*puṇyakṣetre puṇyatīrthe devabrāhmaṇasannidhau \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. It should be recited in a holy place, in good assembly, in the temples in sacred places and sacred spots (near the bank of a holy river or lake) and in the presence of the gods (or images of gods) and the Brahmins.

## \|\| 1.1.71 \|\|

*ucchiṣṭadeśe vaktāra ākhyānamidamuttamam \|*  
*pacyante narake ghore yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Those who relate this excellent narrative in a place defiled with crumbs and other remnants of food are cooked in the terrible hell all the long while till the dissolution of the world.

## \|\| 1.1.72 \|\|

*mṛṣā śṛṇoti yo mūḍho dambhī bhaktivirjitaḥ \|*  
*so'pi tadvanmahāghore narake pacyate'kṣaye \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He who though infatuated, hypocrite and devoid of devotion, falsely pretends to listen to this Purana is also similarly cooked in the everlasting terrible hell.

## \|\| 1.1.73-74 \|\|

*naro yaḥ satkathāmadhye sambhāṣāṃ kurute'nyataḥ \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tadekāgramanā bhavet \|\| 73 \|\|*

*śrotā vaktā ca viprendrā eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*asamāhitacittastu na jānāti hi kiñcana \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. The man who carried on conversation with others in the middle of a holy discourse (about the Lord), goes to the terrible hell. Hence, О leading Brahmins the narrator and the listener should pay single-minded attention. This is the eternal path of righteousness. One without concentration of the mind does not understand anything.

## \|\| 1.1.75 \|\|

*tata ekamanā bhūtvā pibeddharikathāmṛtam \|*  
*kathaṃ saṃbhrāntacittasya kathāsvādaḥ prajāyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Hence, one shall imbibe the nectarine story of Hari with concentration of mind. How can a man of confused mind appreciate the holy story?

## \|\| 1.1.76-78 \|\|

*kiṃ sukhaṃ prāpyate loke puṃsā sambhrāntacetasā \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaṃ parityajya kāmaṃ duḥkhasya sādhanam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*samāhitamanā bhūtvā kuryādacyutacintanam \|*  
*yena kenāpyupāyena smṛto nārāyaṇo'vyayaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*api pātakayuktasya prasannaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yasya nārāyaṇe bhaktirvibhau viśveśvare'vyaye \|*  
*tasya syātsaphalaṃ janma muktiścaiva kare sthitā \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. What happiness is achieved in the world by a man of confused intellect and mind? Hence, one shall eschew all desires which are the cause of misery and meditate on Lord Visnu with the perfect concentration of the mind. If the eternal Lord Narayana is somehow remembered even by a sinful person, he shall undoubtedly be delighted. Fruitful indeed is the life of that man who entertains highest devotion to Lord Narayana, the eternal Lord of the universe. Salvation is as if just on the palm of his hand within his reach.

## \|\| 1.1.79 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyapuruṣārthā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*haribhaktiparāṇāṃ vai sampadyante na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. О excellent Brahmins, there is verily (absolutely) no doubt in this that the four objectives of human efforts, viz. Purusarthas of Virtue, Wealth, Love and Liberation are achieved by those who are devoutly attached to Hari.

## Chapter 2. Eulogy of Lord Visnu

## \|\| 1.2.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ sanatkumārastu nāradāya mahātmane \|*  
*proktavānsakalāndharmānkathaṃ tau militāvubhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages enquired:

1\. How did Sanatkumara relate everyone of the religious duties to Narada, the noble-souled sage? How did these two come together?

## \|\| 1.2.2 \|\|

*kasminsthāne sthitau sūta tāvubhau brahmavādinau \|*  
*harigītasamudgāne cakratustadvadasva naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Suta! In what place did those two expounders of the Brahman stay? Where did they sing the songs of (the glories of) Hari? Narrate that to us. Suta replied:

## \|\| 1.2.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*sanakādyā mahātmāno brahmaṇo mānasāḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*nirmamā nirahaṃkārāḥ sarve te hyūdhvaretasaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Sanaka and other great-souled (sages) were the mental sons of god Brahma; they were free from egotism or ‘I-ness.’ All of them observed perpetual celibacy.

## \|\| 1.2.4 \|\|

*teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi samakaśca sanandanaḥ \|*  
*sanasphumāraśca vibhuḥ sanātama iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I shall recount their names: — They were Sanaka, Sanandana, holy lord Sanatkumara and he who is remembered as Sanatana.

## \|\| 1.2.5 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktā mahātmāno brahmadhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*sahasrasūryasaṃkāśāḥ satyasandhā mumukṣavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They were devotees of Visnu. These noble-souled sages were engaged in the meditation of Brahman. They resembled a thousand suns (in brilliance). They were desirous of salvation and were highly truthful.

## \|\| 1.2.6 \|\|

*ekadā meruśṛṅgaṃ te prasthitā brahmaṇaḥ sabhām \|*  
*iṣṭaṃ mārge 'tha dadṛśuḥ gaṅgāṃ viṣṇipadīṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О Brahmanas! Once (while) they started towards their desired destination, the peak of Meru (to attend) god Brahma’s assembly, they saw on their way, the river Ganga, originating from Lord Visnu’s foot (Visnu-padi).

## \|\| 1.2.7-8 \|\|

*tāṃ nirīkṣya samudyuktāḥ strātuṃ sītājale 'bhavan \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra devarṣirnārado muniḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ājagāma dvijaśreṣṭhā dṛṣṭvā bhrāntṝnsvakāgrajān \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā strātumudyuktānnamaskṛtya kṛtāñjitiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. On seeing it, they were about to take their bath in the waters of the Sita (a branch of the Ganga). О excellent Brahmanas! In the meantime, the celestial sage Narada came there. On seeing his elder brothers about to take their bath, he bowed to them with his palms joined in reverence. With great devotion and love, he invoked the names of the Slayer of Madhu.

## \|\| 1.2.9-11 \|\|

*guṇannāmāni sapremabhaktiyukto madhudviṣaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇācyutānanta vāsudeva janārdana \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yajñeśa yajñapuruṣa kṛṣṇa viṣṇo namo 'stu te \|*  
*padmākṣa kamalākānta gaṅgājanaka keśava \|*  
*kṣirodaśāyindeveśa dāmodara namo 'stu te \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śrīrāma viṣṇo narasiṃha vāmana pradyumnasaṃkarpaṇa vātpadeva \|*  
*ajāniruddhāmalaruṅmurāraṃ tvaṃ pāhi naḥ sarvabhayādajastram \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. “Obeisance to you, О Narayana, О Acyuta, О Ananta (Infinite one), О Vasudeva, О Janardana, О Lord of sacrifices, О Yajna-purusa, О Кrsna, О Visnu, О Padmaksha (Lotus-eyed god), О Kamala-kanta (Consort of goddess Laksmi), О Ganga-janaka (the Proginator of the Ganga), О Kesava, О Ksiroda-shayin (O Lord who couches in the milky ocean), О god of gods, О Damodara, I bow to you. О Sri-Rama, О Visnu, О Narasimha, О Vamana, О Pradyumna, О Sankarshana, О Vasudeva, О Unborn god (Aja), О Aniruddha, О God of spotless splendour, О Murari (Enemy of Mura), you save us perpetually from apprehensions.

## \|\| 1.2.12 \|\|

*ityucca ranharernāma natvā tānsvāgrajānmunīn \|*  
*upāsīnaśca taiḥ sārddhaṃ sasnau prītisamanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Uttering the names of Hari in this way, and bowing down to the sages, his elder brothers, he (Narada) sat along with them, and took bath with great pleasure.

## \|\| 1.2.13-14 \|\|

*te ṣāṃ cāpi tu sītāyā jale lokamalāpa he \|*  
*strātvā saṃtartya devarṣipitanvigatakalmaṣāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*uttīryya saṃdhyopāstyādi kṛtvācāraṃ svakaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*kathāṃ pracakrurvividhāḥ nārāyaṇa guṇāśritāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. All the five of them performed ablutions in the waters of the Sita that dispel sins of the people, and performed the tarpana rites with reference to gods, sages and manes (pitrs). They were absolved of their sins. О Brahmanas! They came up (from the river) and performed the twilight prayers, and their other prescribed duties. They then held various discussions and discourses based on the attributes of Narayana.

## \|\| 1.2.15 \|\|

*kṛtatriyeṣu muniṣu gaṅgātīre manorame \|*  
*cakāranāradaḥ praśnaṃ nānākhyānakayāntare \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the sages had completed their sacred rites on the beautiful banks of the Ganga, Narada put these questions in the course of various discourses and narratives. Narada said:

## \|\| 1.2.16 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*sarvajñāḥ stha muniśreṣṭhāḥ bhagavadbhaktitatparāḥ \|*  
*yūyaṃ sarve jagannāthā bhagavantaḥ sanātanāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О excellent sages, all of you are omniscient. You are exclusively devoted to the Lord. All of you are the spiritual lords of the universe, highly blessed and eternal.

## \|\| 1.2.17 \|\|

*lokoddhāraparānyuṣmāndīneṣu kṛtasauhṛdān \|*  
*pṛcche tato vadata me bhagavallakṣaṇaṃ budhāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О learned sages! You are engaged in the (spiritual) uplift of the worlds, and entertain friendliness towards the indigent and the wretched. Hence, I (humbly) entreat you to relate the characteristics of the Lord.

## \|\| 1.2.18 \|\|

*yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*gaṅgāpādodakaṃ yasya sa kathaṃ jñāyate hariḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. How is Lord Hari realized — Hari, by whom the entire universe consisting of the mobiles and immobiles, is created, and the waters from whose feet constitute the holy Ganga?

## \|\| 1.2.19 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca trividhaṃ karma saphalaṃ jāyate nṛṇām \|*  
*jñānasya lakṣaṇa brūta tapasaścāpi mānadāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. How do the threefold religious acts of men become fruitful? О honour-bestowing ones! (Be pleased) to expound the characteristics of the perfect knowledge and penance.

## \|\| 1.2.20 \|\|

*atitheḥ pūjanaṃ vāpi yena viṣṇuḥ prasīdati \|*  
*evamādīni guhyāni harituṣṭikarāṇi ca \|*  
*anugṛhya ca māṃ nāthāstattvato vaktumarhatha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. How is the worship of a guest to be performed whereby Visnu becomes propitiated? О lords! Be gracious unto me. It behoves you to relate precisely and in details, these and other similar things considered to be mystic secrets, bringing satisfaction unto Hari. Shaunaka said: (Narada begins the eulogy of Visnu)

## \|\| 1.2.21 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*namaḥ parāya devāya parasmātparamātra ca \|*  
*parāvara nivāsāya saguṇāyāguṇāya ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Obeisance to the Supreme Lord, who is greater than the greatest. He is immanent in the greater and the lesser beings. He is both endowed with attributes and still devoid of attributes (saguna and nirguna). Salutations unto Him.

## \|\| 1.2.22 \|\|

*amāyāyātmasaṃjñāya mācine viśvarupiṇe \|*  
*yogīśvarāya yogāya yogagamyāya viṣṇave \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hail to the Lord devoid of Maya; Obeisance to the Deity termed Atman, the possessor of the deluding Potency called Maya and who constitutes the universe. I bow to the Lord of yogins, identical with Yoga and comprehensible through Yoga. Salutations to Visnu.

## \|\| 1.2.23 \|\|

*jñānāya jñānagamyāya sarvajñānaikahetave \|*  
*jñāceśvarāya jñeyāya jñātre vijñānasaṃpade \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Obeisance to the Perfect Knowledge, to one who can be realized through perfect knowledge, to the sole cause of all knowledge, to the Lord of perfect knowledge, to the Deity identical with Jneya (object of knowledge). Jnatr (the knower) and the Vijnana-sampad (riches of perfect knowledge).

## \|\| 1.2.24 \|\|

*dhyānāya dhyānagamyāya dhyātṛpātaharāya ca \|*  
*dhyāneśvarāya sudhiyedhyeyadhyātṛsvarupiṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to the meditation, to the one comprehensible through meditation, to him who dispels the sins of the meditator, to the Lord of meditation, to the intelligent one, and to one who represents the identity between the dhyeya (object of meditation), dhyatr (the subject, the person who meditates).

## \|\| 1.2.25 \|\|

*ādityavacandrāgnividhātṛdevāḥ siddhāśca yakṣāsuranāgasaṅghāḥ \|*  
*yacchaktiyuktāstamajaṃ purāṇaṃ satyaṃ stutīśaṃ satataṃ nato 'smi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I always bow down to that unborn primeval, real, truthful Lord of prayer, whose energy and power inspire the sun, moon, fire, the creator of the gods, the demigods known as Siddhas, Yaksas and the Asuras, and the groups of serpents.

## \|\| 1.2.26 \|\|

*yo brahmarupī jagatāṃ vidhātā sa eva pātā dvijaviṣṇurupī \|*  
*kalpāntarudrākhyatamuḥ sa devaḥ śeteṃ'ghripānastamajaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I take resort to that unborn Lord who assumes the form of Brahma, and creates the worlds, who alone is the protector (of the worlds) assuming the forms of Brahmanas and Visnu, and who assumes the body called Rudra for dissolving the world, at the end of the Kalpas, and then lies (in the form of a small child) licking (the big toe of) his foot.

## \|\| 1.2.27 \|\|

*yannāmasaṃkīrttanato gajendro grāhograbandhānmumuce sa devaḥ \|*  
*virājamānaḥ svapade parākhye taṃ viṣṇumādyaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I seek refuge in that primordial Deity Visnu — the Lord who shines in his region called Para (the transcendental), that Lord by reciting whose name, the mighty leader of elephants was released from the terrible grip of the crocodile (I seek refuge in that primordial Visnu).

## \|\| 1.2.28 \|\|

*śivasvarupī śivabhakti bhājāṃ yo viṣṇurupī haribhāvitānām \|*  
*saṃkalpapūrvātmakadehahetustaṃstameva nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He assumes the form of Siva in regard to those possessing devotion unto Siva; he assumes the form of Visnu for the sake of those who are sanctified by meditation upon Hari. Ever and anon, I seek refuge in him alone, who causes physical bodies in accordance with the previous conception.

## \|\| 1.2.29 \|\|

*yaḥ keśihantā narakāntakaśca bālo bhujāgreṇa dadhāra gotram \|*  
*devaṃ ca bhūmāravinodaśīlaṃ taṃ vāsudevaṃ satataṃ nato 'smi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I bow always unto that son of Vasudeva who slew Keshin and Naraka, who, even as a boy lifted up a mountain by means of the tip of his hand, and the God who habitually removes the burden of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.2.30 \|\|

*lebhe 'vatīryogranṛsiṃharupīyodaityavakṣaḥ kaṭhinaṃ śilāvat \|*  
*vidāryasaṃrākṣitavānsvabhaktaṃ prahlādamīśaṃ tamajaṃ manāmi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I salute to that unborn Lord who, incarnated in the terrific form of the Man-lion (from the pillar), tore up the chest of the demon (Hiranyakasipu), as hard as the rock, and who protected Prahlada, his own devotee.

## \|\| 1.2.31 \|\|

*vyomādibhirmūṣitamātmasaṃjñaṃ nirañjanaṃ nityamameyatattvam \|*  
*jagadvidhātāramakarmakaṃ ca paraṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣama nato 'smi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I pay obeisance to that Supreme Primeval Person designated as the Self (atman), who is embellished by means of the ether, etc., who is ever unsullied, Eternal and incomprehensible; who (though) the creator of the universe, is devoid of activities.

## \|\| 1.2.32 \|\|

*brahmendrarudrānilavāyumartyagandharvayakṣāsuradevasaṃghaiḥ \|*  
*svamūrtibhedaiḥ sthita eka īśastamādimātmā namahaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I worship that First Principle, the Soul (atman) who stays as undivided one, with all his different forms, viz., Brahma, Indra, Rudra, the fire-god, the wind-god and the categories or classes of beings e.g. the mortals, demigods, like Gandharvas and Yaksas, Asuras and gods (devas).

## \|\| 1.2.33 \|\|

*yato bhinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ samudbhūtaṃ sthitaṃ ca vai \|*  
*yasminneṣyati paścācca tamasti śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I have sought asylum in that from which all this (universe) became distinct, and was originated, sustained and in which it will get dissolved afterwards.

## \|\| 1.2.34 \|\|

*yaḥ sthito viśvarupeṇa saṅgīvātra pratīyate \|*  
*asaṅgī paripūrṇaśca tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I have resorted (for refuge) to him who stands in the form of the universe, and appears to be involved in and attached to the world but who, in reality, is not attached at all, and is perfect.

## \|\| 1.2.35 \|\|

*hṛdi sthito 'pi yo devo māyayā mohitātmanām \|*  
*na jñāyate paraḥ śuddhastamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I seek refuge in him who, though stationed in the heart (as antaratman), is not cognised by those whose selves or minds are deluded by Maya, and who is the supreme-most and the purest of all.

## \|\| 1.2.36 \|\|

*sarvasaṃganivṛttānāṃ dhyānayogaratātmanām \|*  
*sarvatra bhāti jñānātmā tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I seek shelter in him who is of the nature of the perfect knowledge. He shines forth everywhere to those who refrain from all attachments, and whose souls or minds revel in the path of meditation.

## \|\| 1.2.37 \|\|

*dadhāra mandāraṃ pṛṣṭe nirode 'mṛtamanthane \|*  
*devatānāṃ hitārthāya taṃ kūrmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When there was an impediment at the time of churning the ocean for the sake of nectar, he held the mount Mandara on his back, for the welfare of the gods. I seek refuge in that Tortoise.

## \|\| 1.2.38 \|\|

*draṣṭrāṅkureṇa yo 'nantaḥ samuddhṛtyārṇavāddharām \|*  
*tasthāvidaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ vārāhaṃ taṃ nato 'smyaham \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. With his pointed and curved fang, the Infinite Being lifted the earth from the ocean, and stabilised this entire universe. I bow down to that Boar.

## \|\| 1.2.39 \|\|

*prahlādaṃ gopayandaityaṃ śilātikaṭhinorasam \|*  
*vidārya hatavānyo hi taṃ nṛsiṃhaṃ nato 'smyaham \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Desirous of protecting Prahlada, he tore up the rock-like hard chest of the demon Hiranyakasipu and killed him. I pay obeisance to that Nrsimha (Man-lion).

## \|\| 1.2.40 \|\|

*labdhvā vairocanerbhūmiṃ dvābhyāṃ padbhyāmatītya yaḥ \|*  
*ābrahmabhuvanaṃ pādātsurebhyastaṃ nato 'jitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Having secured the gift of land from the son of Virocana (i.c. Bali), with two paces he covered the entire universe upto the region of god Brahma, and handed over the same to gods. I bow down to that Ajita (the unconquered Lord).

## \|\| 1.2.41 \|\|

*haihayasyāparādhena hyekaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*kṣatriyānvayabhettā yo jāmadagnyaṃ nato 'smi tam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Due to the crime committed by Kartavirya Arjuna of the Haihaya clan, he destroyed, for twenty-one times, the race of Ksatriyas. I bow down to that son of Jamadagni.

## \|\| 1.2.42 \|\|

*āvirbhūtaścaturddhā yaḥ kapibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*hatavānrākṣasānīkaṃ rāmacandraṃ nato 'smyaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He manifested himself in four forms (4 sons of Dasaratha). Surrounded by monkeys, he killed the army of the demons (Raksasas). I bow down to that Ramacandra.

## \|\| 1.2.43 \|\|

*mūrtidvayaṃ samāśritya bhūbhāramapahṛtya ca \|*  
*saṃjahāra kulaṃ svaṃ yastaṃ śrīkṛṣṇapyahaṃ bhaje \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Assuming (lit. by resorting to) the two forms (viz. Sri Krsna and Balarama), he removed the burden of the earth and (ultimately) destroyed his own family. I worship that Sri Krsna.

## \|\| 1.2.44 \|\|

*bhūmyādilokatritayaṃ saṃtṛtpātmānamātmani \|*  
*paśyanti nirmalaṃ śuddhaṃ tamīśānaṃ bhajāmyaham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. People of the three worlds beginning with the Earth see within their souls that pure Lord who is delighted within himself. I worship that Ruler of the universe who is resplendent and pure, devoid of impurities.

## \|\| 1.2.45 \|\|

*yugānte pāpino śuddhānbhittvā tīkṣṇasudhārayā \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa yo dharmaṃ kṛtādau tannamāmyaham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Having massacred all the impure sinners by means of his sharp-edged sword, at the end of the Kali Age, he re-established the Dharma at the beginning of the Krta Age. To him I salute.

## \|\| 1.2.46 \|\|

*evamādīnyanekāni yasya rupāṇi pāṇḍavāḥ \|*  
*na śakyaṃ tena saṃkhyātuṃ koṭyabdairapi taṃ bhaje \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I resort to him whose these and other innumerable forms are impossible to be enumerated by him (i.e. by any person) even in millions of years, О Pandavas. I worship him.

## \|\| 1.2.47 \|\|

*mahimānaṃ tu yannāmnaḥ paraṃ gantuṃ munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*devāsurāśca manavaḥ kathaṃ taṃ śrullako bhaje \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even great sages, gods, demons (Asuras) and Manus cannot fully comprehend the greatness of his name. How can I, an insignificant person, worship him (with full realisation)?

## \|\| 1.2.48 \|\|

*yannāmaśravaṇenāpi mahāpātakino narāḥ \|*  
*pavitratāṃ prapadyante ta kathaṃ staumi cālpadhīḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Even by hearing his name, men who have committed great sins attain sanctity. How can I, a weak-minded person of mean intellect, eulogise him (adequately)?

## \|\| 1.2.49 \|\|

*yathākathañcidyannamni kīrtite vā śrute 'pi vā \|*  
*pāpinastu viśuddhāḥ syuḥ śaddhā mokṣamavānpuyuḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If somehow or other (by a lucky chance) the sinners manage to glorify or hear his name, they become purified and the purified ones attain Liberation (from Samsara).

## \|\| 1.2.50 \|\|

*ātmanyātmānamādhāya yogino gatakalmaśāḥ \|*  
*paśyanti yaṃ jñānarupaṃ tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I seek refuge in that deity of the form of perfect knowledge whom Yogins, freed from sins, perceive after stabilising their individual soul (atman) in the (supreme) atman.

## \|\| 1.2.51 \|\|

*sāṅkhyāḥ sarveṣu paśyanti paripūraṇāntakaṃ harim \|*  
*tamādidevamajaraṃ jñānarupaṃ bhajāmyaham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Samkhyas (followers of the path of knowledge) perceive Hari of perfect atman, in everything. I worship that Ageless, Eternal (hence the First) Deity who is of the nature of perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.2.52 \|\|

*sarvasattvamayaṃ śāntaṃ sarvadraṣṭāramīśvaram \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣakaṃ devaṃ vande bhāvātmakaṃ harim \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I salute Lord Hari who is immanent in all living beings, is quiescent, omniscient (perceiver of everything), who has thousands of heads and who is very real (of positive existence).

## \|\| 1.2.53 \|\|

*yadbhūtaṃ yacca vai bhāvyaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ jagat \|*  
*daśāṅgulaṃ yo 'tsyatiṣṭattamīśamajaraṃ bhade \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I worship that unaging Supreme Ruler who stands the breadth of ten fingers above the universe of both past and the future, whether mobile or immobile.

## \|\| 1.2.54 \|\|

*aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ mahataśca mahattaram \|*  
*guhyādguhyatamaṃ devaṃ praṇamāmi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Again and again do I pay obeisance to that unborn mystic Deity, who is minuter than the minutest and greater than the greatest, and the secret-most among the secrets.

## \|\| 1.2.55 \|\|

*dhyātaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā śṛtaḥ praṇamito 'pi vā \|*  
*svapadaṃ yo dadātīśastaṃ vande puruṣottamam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I salute the Supreme Person, the Ruler of the universe who bestows his own region if he be meditated upon, remembered, worshipped, heard of or even bowed to.

## \|\| 1.2.56 \|\|

*iti stuvantaṃ paramaṃ pereśaṃ harṣāmbusaṃruddhavilocanāste \|*  
*munīśvarā nāradasaṃyutāstu sanandanādyāḥ prapudaṃ prajagmuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As Narada eulogised the great Lord thus, those great sages like Sanandana and others, with eyes bedimmed with tears of joy, became highly delighted, in the company of Narada.

## \|\| 1.2.57 \|\|

*ya idaṃ prātarutyāya pāṭhedvai paurupaṃ stavam \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He who gets up early in the morning and reads this hymn to the Supreme Person (Visnu) gets his soul purified of all sins, and attains to region of Visnu (Vaikuntha)

## Chapter 3. The Description Of The Sphere Of The Earth And Of Bharata

## \|\| 1.3.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kathaṃ sasarja brahmādīnādidevaḥ purā vibhuḥ \|*  
*tanmamākhyāhi sanaka sarvajño 'sti yato bhavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Narada enquired:

1\. How did the Omnipresent Primordial Deity create Brahma and others, formerly? О Sanaka, narrate this unto me, since your worship is omniscient. Sri Sanaka narrated:

## \|\| 1.3.2 \|\|

*śrīsanaka uvācā*  
*nārāyaṇo 'kṣaro 'nantaḥ sarvavyāpī nirañjanaḥ \|*  
*tenedamakhilaṃ vyātpaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Narayana is imperishable and Infinite. He is omnipresent and unsullied. This entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by him.

## \|\| 1.3.3 \|\|

*ādisarge mahāviṣṇuḥ svaprakāśo jaganmayaḥ \|*  
*guṇabhedamadhiṣṭhāya mūrttitrikamavāsṛjat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the time of the first creation, the self-luminous great Visnu constituting the universe, presided over a differentiation in the gunas, and created the three forms of the deities.

## \|\| 1.3.4-5 \|\|

*sṛṣṭyarthaṃ tu purā devo dakṣiṇāṅgātprajāpatim \|*  
*madhyerudrākhyamīthānaṃ jagadantakaraṃ mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pālanāyāsya jagato vāmāṅgādviṣṇumavyayam \|*  
*tamādidevamajaraṃ kecidāhuḥ śivābhidham \|*  
*kecidviṣṇuṃ sadā satyaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kecidūcire \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Formerly, the Lord created god Brahma from the right part of his Person, for the purpose of creation (of the worlds), О sage; from the middle, he created Isana (the Master) called Rudra, who causes the dissolution of the universe. For the sake of protecting this universe, he created the immutable Visnu from his left side. Some designate that imperishable Primordial Lord by the epithet Siva, some by the name Visnu (the Eternal Truth), while some call him Brahma.

## \|\| 1.3.6 \|\|

*tasya śaktiḥ parā viṣṇorjagatkāryapravartinī \|*  
*bhāvābhāvasvarupā sā vidyāvidyeti gīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Visnu’s Supreme Sakti (Energy) stimulating the process of the universe is both positive and negative (existent and non-existent) in nature, and is described ‘Vidya-avidya' (Spiritual Knowledge and Ignorance or Nescience).

## \|\| 1.3.7 \|\|

*yadā viśvaṃ mahāviṣṇorbhinnatvena pratīyate \|*  
*tadā hyavidyā saṃsiddhā bhavedduḥkhasya sādhanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the universe appears as distinct and separate from Great Visnu, that is the accomplishment (effect) of Nescience which is the cause of misery.

## \|\| 1.3.8 \|\|

*jñātṛjñeyādyupādhiste yadā naśyati nārada \|*  
*sarvaikabhāvanā buddhiḥ sā vidyetyabhidhīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Narada, when the conditioning factors such as the knower, the knowable etc. fuse together, and cease to exist, the knowledge or comprehension of the oneness of everything (in the universe) i.e. the existence of only one entity, viz., Brahman, is called Vidya (spiritual lore).

## \|\| 1.3.9 \|\|

*eṣaṃ māyā mahāviṣṇorbhinnā saṃsāradāyinī \|*  
*abhedabuddhyā dṛṣṭā cetsaṃsārakṣayakāriṇī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus the Maya of the great Visnu, if seen as distinct and separate from him, bestows (i.e. involves one in) the worldly existence, but if realized with the consciousness of nondifference from him, it brings about the destruction of the Samsara (or metempsychosis).

## \|\| 1.3.10 \|\|

*viṣṇuśaktisamudbhūtametatsarvaṃ varācaṃm \|*  
*yasmādbhinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ yacceṅgedyaccaneṅgati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The entire universe of the mobile and immobile beings, has been originated from Visnu’s (illusive) potency. All these things whether they move or not are different from it.

## \|\| 1.3.11 \|\|

*upādhibhiryathākāśo bhinnatvena pratīyate \|*  
*avidyopādhiyogenatathedamakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Just as, by means of the conditioning factors (such as a pot, a room) the ether differs (as the ether conditioned by the pot, etc.), so also the entire universe appears different through the conditioning factor of avidya (Nescience).

## \|\| 1.3.12 \|\|

*yathā harirjagadyāpī tasya śaktistathā mune \|*  
*dāhaśaktiryathāṅgāre svāśrayaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О Sage, even as Lord Hari pervades the entire universe so also does his (potency), just as the burning capacity of a (heated, fiery) coal manifests itself by pervading its substratum.

## \|\| 1.3.13 \|\|

*umeti kecidāhustāṃ śaktiṃ lakṣmīṃ tathā pare \|*  
*bhāratītyapare caināṃ girijetyambiketi ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Some call this potency (Sakti), Uma, others call it ksmi, still others call it Bharati, Girija and Ambika.

## \|\| 1.3.14-15 \|\|

*durgeti bhadrakālīti caṇḍī māheśvarītyapi \|*  
*kaumārī vaiṣṇavī ceti vārāhyendrī ca śāmbhavī \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brāhmīti vidyāvidyeti māyeti ca tathā pare \|*  
*prakṛtiśca parā ceti vadanti paramarṣasyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The great sages designate her as Durga, Bhadrakali, Candi, Mahesvari, Kaumari, Vaisnavi, Varahi, Aindri, Sambhavi, Brahmi, Vidya (spiritual knowledge), Avidya (Nescience), Maya (The illusive potency of the Lord) and Pard Prakrti (The Supreme Primordial Nature).

## \|\| 1.3.16 \|\|

*śeṣaśaktiḥ parā viṣṇorjagatsargādikāriṇī \|*  
*vyaktāvyaktasvarupeṇa jagahyāpya vyavasthitā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Sesasakti is Visnu’s transcendental power, the cause of creation, etc. of the universe. It pervades the universe in its ‘manifest-cum-unmanifest form’, and abides therein.

## \|\| 1.3.17 \|\|

*prakṛtiścapumāṃścaiva kālaśceti vidhisthitiḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāmekaḥ kāraṇatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One of these is the cause of creation, maintenance and dissolution, viz., Prakrti (The Primordial Nature), Purusa, Kala (Time), Vidhi (abidance of the opportune time or fate) and sthiti (steadiness or continuance in one state).

## \|\| 1.3.18 \|\|

*yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ brahmarupadhareṇa vai \|*  
*tasmātparataro devo nityaityabhidhīyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. All this (universe) has been created by the deity assuming the form of Brahma, but it is (authoritatively) stated that the Supreme Deity transcends him and is eternal.

## \|\| 1.3.19-22 \|\|

*rakṣāṃ karoti yo devo nitya ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*rakṣāṃ karoti yo devo jagatāṃ parataḥ pumān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmātparataraṃ yattadavyayaṃ paramaṃ padam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*akṣaro nirguṇaḥ śuddhaḥ paripūrṇaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paraḥ kālapupākhyo yogidhyeyaḥ parātparaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*paramātmā parānandaḥ sarvopādhivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*jñānaikavedyaḥ paramaḥ sañcidānandavigrahaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. The God who protects is called the Eternal Deity. The Lord who protects is the Purusa, greater than and beyond the worlds. What is greater than and beyond him is the highest imperishable region. (He is called) aksara (the imperishable), Nirguna (devoid of attributes), Suddha (pure), Paripurnа (perfect, complete) and Sanatana (eternal). The greatest being is called Kalarupa. He is greater than the greatest, worthy of being meditated upon by yogins. He is the greatest atman, the greatest bliss, devoid of all conditioning factors. He can be realised only through perfect knowledge. The greatest Being has Existence, Knowledge and Bliss for his physical bodies.

## \|\| 1.3.23 \|\|

*yo 'sau śuddho 'pi paramo hyahṝṅkāreṇa saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*dehīti procyate mūḍhairaho 'jñānaviḍambanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Although he is the greatest and the purest, He is accompanied by the Ego, and is then called dehin (the embodied soul) by persons of confused mind. Alas, the deception of Ignorance!

## \|\| 1.3.24 \|\|

*sa devaḥ paramaḥ śuddhaḥ sattvadiguṇabhedataḥ \|*  
*mūrtitrayaṃ samāpannaḥ sṛṣṭisthityantakāraṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. That greatest and purest Lord, on being differentiated through Sattva etc., assumes the forms of three Deities, and causes Creation, Sustenance and Dissolution.

## \|\| 1.3.25 \|\|

*yo 'sau brahmā jagatkartā yannābhikamalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*sa evānandarupātmā tasmānnāstyaparo mune \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The deity who is the creator of the universe is Brahma. The deity from whose umbilical lotus Brahma came out is the almariy in the form of Bliss. О sage, none except him is so.

## \|\| 1.3.26 \|\|

*antaryāmī jagadyāpī sarvasākṣī nirañjanaḥ \|*  
*bhinnābhinnasvarupeṇa sthito vai parameśvaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is the immanent Soul. He pervades the universe. He is the Cosmic witness. He is unsullied, The great Isvara abides both as different and non-different.

## \|\| 1.3.27 \|\|

*yasya śaktirmahāmāyā jagadvistrambhadhāriṇī \|*  
*viśvotpatternidānatvātprakṛtiḥ procyate budhaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. His Sakti is the great may a, the trustworthy upholder of the universe. In view of its being the material cause of the universe, it is called prakrti by scholars.

## \|\| 1.3.28 \|\|

*ādisarge mahāviṣṇorlokānkarttuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*prakṛtiḥ puruṣaśceti kālaśceti tridhā bhavet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Of Visnu who was exerting for creation of the the worlds, at the time of the primordial creation, there evolved three-fold forms, viz. Prakrti (primordial matter), Purusa and Kala (Time-spirit).

## \|\| 1.3.29 \|\|

*paśyanti bhāvitātmāno yaṃ brahmatyabhisaṃjñitam \|*  
*śuddhaṃ yatparamaṃ dhāma tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. What men of purified souls perceive as the pure highest, resplendent asylum called Brahman, is the supreme region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.3.30 \|\|

*evaṃ śuddho 'kṣaro 'nantaḥ kālarupī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*guṇarupīguṇādhārojagatāmādikṛdvibhuḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The pure, imperishable, iniinite Mahesvara in this way assumed the form of Kala (Time spirit), and with a form constituted of and affording support to gunas (modifications of Prakrti e.g. sattva etc.) the omnipresent Lord became the primary creator of the world.

## \|\| 1.3.31 \|\|

*pratṛtiḥ kṣobhamāpannā puruṣākhye jagadgurau \|*  
*mahānprādurabhūddhuddhistato 'haṃ samavarttata \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When prakrti became agitated through the Lord of the world called Purusa, the principle of Mahat became manifested. Therefrom evolved the Buddhi (Intellect) from which originated the Ahankara (Cosmic Ego).

## \|\| 1.3.32 \|\|

*ahṝṅkārāśca sūkṣmāṇi tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi ca \|*  
*tanmātrebhyo hi jātāni bhūtāni jagataḥ kṛte \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. From the Cosmic Ego were evolved the subtle primary elements called the tanmUtras and the subtle sense organs. All the gross elements were evolved out of the tanmatras for the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 1.3.33 \|\|

*ākāśavāyyagrijalabhūmayo 'bjabhāvātmaja \|*  
*yathākramaṃ kāraṇatāmekaikasyopayānti ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Of the elements, viz., the ether, air, fire, water and the earth the former becomes the cause of the latter one, in the due order, О Narada, the son of the lotus-born god Brahma.

## \|\| 1.3.34 \|\|

*tato brahmā jagaddhātā tāmasānasṛjatprabhuḥ \|*  
*tiryagyonigatāñjantūnpaśupakṣimṛgādikān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thereafter, Lord Brahma, the creator of the universe, (at first) created the tamasa beings, viz., the sub-human beings such as creatures, beasts, birds, deer, etc.

## \|\| 1.3.35 \|\|

*tamapyasādhakaṃ matvā devasargaṃ sanātanāt \|*  
*tato vaimānuṣaṃ sargaṃ kalpayāmāsa pahmajaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Considering that the Deva-sarga (the creation of celestials) was non-productive and fruitless, god Brahma the eternal lotus-bom deity, conceived of and created the Мanusа- sarga (the creation of human beings).

## \|\| 1.3.36 \|\|

*tato dakṣādikānputrānsṛṣṭisādhanatatparān \|*  
*ebhiḥ putrairidaṃ vyāptaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thereafter, he created Daksha and other Sons who were exclusively devoted to the task of creation. All this entire universe including gods, demons and human beings, is occupied through these sons.

## \|\| 1.3.37 \|\|

*bhurbhuvaśca tathā svaśca mahaśvaiva janastathā \|*  
*tapaśca satyamityevaṃ lokāḥ satyopari sthitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The following seven regions are stationed above: (above the earth) Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah, Mahah, Jana, Tapas and Satya (each one is above the other).

## \|\| 1.3.38-39 \|\|

*atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva sutalaṃ ca talātalam \|*  
*mahātalaṃ ca viprendra tato 'dhacca rasātalam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pātālaṃ ceti saptaiva pātālāni kramādadhaḥ \|*  
*eṣa sarveṣu lokeṣu lokanāthāṃśca sṛṣṭavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. There are seven nether worlds, each below the other, viz., Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talatala, Mahatala, Rasatala and Patala. He created the guardians of the worlds also, for all these regions.

## \|\| 1.3.40 \|\|

*kulācalānnadīścāsau tattallokanivāsinām \|*  
*varttanādīni sarvāṇi yathāyogyaṃmakalpayat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He duly created the principal (seven) mountains and rivers in each of these worlds, and assigned specific means of livelihood befitting the residence of the respective worlds.

## \|\| 1.3.41 \|\|

*bhūtale madhyago meruḥ sarvadevasamāśrayaḥ \|*  
*lokālokaśca bhūmyante tanmadhye satpa sāgarāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The mountain Meru, the resort of all gods, is located at the centre of the surface of the earth. The Lokaloka mountains form the farthest end (limit) of the earth. In between them are the seven seas.

## \|\| 1.3.42 \|\|

*dvīpāśca satpa viprendra dvīpe kulācalāḥ \|*  
*bāhyā nadyaśca vikhyātā janāścāmarasannibhāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O, prominent Brahmanas! There are seven continents and each continent has its own (chain of) principal mountains, and well-known rivers flowing therein, and the people thereof resemble the immortals i.e. gods.

## \|\| 1.3.43 \|\|

*jambūplakṣābhidhānau ca śālmalaśca kuśastathā \|*  
*krauñcaśākau puṣkaraśca te sarve devabhūmayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The names of the continents are: Jambu, Plaksha, Salmala, Kusa, Kraunca, Saка, and Puskara. All of them are regions (traversed by) gods.

## \|\| 1.3.44 \|\|

*ete dvīpāḥ samudraistu satpasatpabhirāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*lavaṇekṣusurāsarpirdadhikṣīrajalaiḥ samam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. These seven continents are surrounded by seven oceans, each having (for its liquid content) salt water, sugarcane juice, wine, ghee, curds, milk and sweet water.

## \|\| 1.3.45 \|\|

*ete dvīpāḥ samudrāśca pūrvasmāduttarerāḥ \|*  
*jñeyā dviguṇavistarā lokālokāñca parvatāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. These continents and oceans should be understood (to have dimensions) in this manner: the latter one is double the former one in extent, and the same with the Lokaloka mountains.

## \|\| 1.3.46 \|\|

*kṣārodadherupattaraṃ yaddhi mādreścaiva dakṣiṇām \|*  
*jñeyaṃ tadbhārataṃ varṣaṃ sarvakarmaphalapradam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The continent which is to the north of the salt sea, and to the south of the mountain Himalaya should be known as Bharata Varsa — the Indian continent. This continent confers the fruit of all actions.

## \|\| 1.3.47 \|\|

*atra karmāṇi kurvanti trividhāni tu nārada \|*  
*tatphalaṃ bhujyate caiva bhogabhūmidhanakramāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Narada! People perform three types of holy acts here, the fruit thereof is enjoyed in the following order: enjoyment of desired pleasures, land and affluence.

## \|\| 1.3.48 \|\|

*bhārate tu kṛtaṃ karma śubhaṃ vāśubhameva ca \|*  
*tatphalaṃ kṣayi viprendra bhujyate 'nyatrajantubhiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If any act whether auspicious or inauspicious is performed in Bharata, the fruit thereof, being of a perishable nature, is enjoyed by the creatures elsewhere (in the other worlds).

## \|\| 1.3.49-51 \|\|

*adyāpi devā icchanti janma bhāratabhūtale \|*  
*saṃcitaṃ sumahatpuṇyamakṣayyamamalaṃ śubham \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kadā labhāmahe janma varṣabhāratabhūmiṣu \|*  
*kadā puṇyena mahatā yāsyāma paramaṃ padam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dānairvāvividhairyajñaistapobhirvāthavā harim \|*  
*jagadīśaṃsameṣyāmo nityānandamanāmayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. Even today the celestials desire to secure birth in the Bharata-varsa. They think, “Great, auspicious, pure and everlasting merit has been accumulated by us. When shall we get the opportunity of being born in the Bharata varsa, where we shall attain to the supreme region (i.e. liberation) thanks to the great merits. Through charitable gifts or performance of different kinds of sacrifices or „various types of penances, we shall attain to Lord Hari, the Ruler of the Universe, of eternal bliss and free from ailments.”

## \|\| 1.3.52 \|\|

*yo bhāratabhuvaṃ prāpya viṣṇupūjāparo bhavet \|*  
*na tasya sadṛśo 'nyo 'sti triṣu lokeṣu nāradā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. О Narada! There is no one else in all the three worlds comparable in merits to that person who, after being born in Bharata, is devoted to the worship of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.3.53 \|\|

*harikīrtanaśīlo vā tadbhaktānāṃ piyo 'pi vā \|*  
*śukṣaṣurvāpi mahataḥ savedyo divijairapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A person habitually glorifying Lord Hari or a person beloved of his devotees or one who is eager to render service to the great persons, is worthy of being bowed down by the heaven- born gods.

## \|\| 1.3.54 \|\|

*haripūjārato nityaṃ bhaktaḥ pūjāsto 'ṣi vā \|*  
*bhaktocchiṣṭānnasevī ca yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A person delighting in the worship of Lord Hari or his devotees or a person regularly partaking of the leavings of the food of the devotees of Hari, attains to the highest region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.3.55 \|\|

*nārāyaṇeti kṛṣṇeti vāsudeveti yo vadet \|*  
*ahiṃsādiparaḥ śantiḥ so 'pi vandyaḥ surottamaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He who constantly utters the names of Visnu, such as Narayana, Krsna, and Vasudeva, and who is quiescent and devoted to non-violence, etc., is also worthy of being saluted by the foremost ones of gods.

## \|\| 1.3.56 \|\|

*śiveti nīlakaṇṭheti śaṅkaretica yaḥ smaret \|*  
*sarvabhūtahito nityaṃ so 'bhyarcyo divijaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It is traditionally remembered (i.e. laid dawn in Smrtis) that he who constantly remembers (and mutters the divine names) Siva, Nilakantha and Sankara and is always engaged in doing good to all living beings, deserves to be worshipped by the celestials.

## \|\| 1.3.57 \|\|

*gurubhaktaḥ śivadhyānī svāśramācāratatparaḥ \|*  
*anasūyuḥśucirdakṣo yaḥ so 'pyarcyaḥsureśvaraiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One devoted to his preceptors, a person meditating on Siva, a man engaged in performing the duties prescribed for his own stage of life, one devoid of jealousy and one who is pure, is worthy of being adored by leaders of gods.

## \|\| 1.3.58 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ hitakaraḥ śradhdāvānvarṇadharmayoḥ \|*  
*vedavādarato nityaṃ sa jñeyaḥ paṅkipāvanaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. One who is a benefactor of Brahmanas, one who cherishes faith (in the duties prescribed for) varnas (classes in society and their duties), one who is ever devotedly engaged in propounding the Vedas, should be regarded as one who sanctifies all persons who sit in the same row to dine with him.

## \|\| 1.3.59 \|\|

*abhedadarśī deveśe nārāyaṇaśivātmake \|*  
*sarvaṃ yo brahmaṇa nityamasmadādiṣu kā kathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A person who looks upon the pair of the Lords of gods consisting of Narayana and Siva equally without any discrimination, should always be saluted by god Brahma. What need be said of persons like us? (We must definitely worship him).

## \|\| 1.3.60 \|\|

*goṣu kṣānto brahmacārī paranindāvivarjitaḥ \|*  
*aparigrahaśī laśca devapūjyaḥ sa nārada \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A person who has established perfect control over his senses and organs, is celibate, refrains from slandering others and invariably abstains from having any possession (or acceptance of monetary gifts), is, О Narada, worthy of being worshipped even by gods.

## \|\| 1.3.61 \|\|

*steyādidoṣavimukhaḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ \|*  
*paropakāranirataḥ pūjanīyaḥ surāsuraiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. One who is averse to such censurable acts as stealing, is full of gratefulness, is a man of purity and truthful speech and takes delight in rendering help to others, deserves to be worshipped by gods and demons.

## \|\| 1.3.62 \|\|

*vedārthaśravaṇe buddhiḥ purāṇaśravaṇe tathā \|*  
*satsaṃge 'pi ca yasyāsti so 'pi vandyaḥ surottamaiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He whose mind and intellect are inclined to listen to the exposition of the Vedas and the Puranas, and is keen in associating with the righteous persons, deserves respect and salutations from excellent ones amongst the gods.

## \|\| 1.3.63 \|\|

*evamādīnyanekāni karmāṇi śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*karoti bhārate varṣe saṃbandho 'smābhireva ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Association with such persons be established by us — with persons who perform such and other sacred rites with perfect faith, in this continent of Bharata.

## \|\| 1.3.64 \|\|

*eteṣvanyatamo vipramātmānaṃ nārabhettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa eva duṣkṛtirmūḍho nāstyanyo 'smādacetanaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If anyone, despite being a Brahmana, does not begin any one of these sacred or holy activities, he is a man of wicked actions, dullard in mind, and none else is more insensible than he.

## \|\| 1.3.65 \|\|

*saṃprāpya bhārate janma satkarma suparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*pīyūṣakalaśaṃ suktvā viṣabhāṇḍamupāśritaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Even after being born in Bharata, a person who is totally averse to the performance of righteous acts, is like a person who prefers a pot of poison spurning aside the jar of nectar.

## \|\| 1.3.66 \|\|

*śrutismṛtyuditairddharmairnātmānaṃ pāvayettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa evātmavidhātī syātpāpināmagraṇīrmune \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О sage, a person who does not sanctify himself by performing religious rites prescribed in the Vedas and the Smrtis is the leader of sinners, confounder of his own self.

## \|\| 1.3.67 \|\|

*karmabhūmiṃ samāsādya yo na dharmaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sa ca sarvādhamaḥ prokto vedavidbhirmunīśvara \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. О prominent sage! After attaining birth in the land of holy rites (i.e. Bharata), if one does not abide by the path of righteousness (dharma), he is decried as the meanest of all, by knowers of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.3.68 \|\|

*śubhaṃ karma samutsṛjya duṣkarmāṇi karoti yaḥ \|*  
*kāmadhenuṃ parityajya arkakṣīraṃ saṃ mārgati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He who eschews auspicious rites and acts and performs evil deeds is (like a person who) abandons (the milk of) the wish-yielding cow (Kamadhenu) and seeks the milk-like exudation from the sun plant (*arka*).

## \|\| 1.3.69 \|\|

*evaṃ bhāratabhūbhāgaṃ praśaṃsanti divaukasaḥ \|*  
*brahmādyā api viprendra svabhogakṣayabhīravaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О leader of Brahmanas! In this way even the inhabitants of heaven like god Brahma and others who arc afraid of the termination of their period of enjoyment of pleasures, praise the land of Bharata.

## \|\| 1.3.70 \|\|

*tasmātpuṇyatamaṃ jñeyaṃ bhārataṃ varṣamuttamam \|*  
*devānāṃ durlabhaṃ vāpi sarvakarmaphalapradam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, the excellent subcontinent of Bharata should be regarded as exceedingly meritorious. It is accessible with great difficulty even to gods. It bestows the fruits of all holy rites and actions.

## \|\| 1.3.71 \|\|

*asminpuṇye ca bhūbhāge yastu satkarmasūdyataḥ \|*  
*na tasya sadṛśaṃ kaścitriṣu vidyate \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. In the three worlds, there is no one comparable to that person who diligently attempts to perform good and righteous acts in this holy land.

## \|\| 1.3.72 \|\|

*asmiñjāto naro yastu svaṅkarmakṣapaṇodyataḥ \|*  
*nararupaparicchannaḥ sa harirnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A man who is born in this land and who attempts to destroy and exhaust the balance of his actions in previous birth, is Lord Hari himself in the guise of a man. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.3.73 \|\|

*paraṃ lokaphalaṃ prepsuḥ kiryātkarmāṇyatandritaḥ \|*  
*nivedya haraye bhaktyā tatphalaṃ hyakṣayaṃ smṛtam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One who is desirous of attaining the highest worldly benefits or fruits, should vigilantly perform righteous and holy acts. If an act is performed, after dedicating with devotion the fruit thereof unto Lord Hari, that fruit is said to be ever lasting.

## \|\| 1.3.74 \|\|

*virāgī cetkarmaphaleṣvapi kiñcitra kārayet \|*  
*arpayetsukṛtaṃ karma prīyatāmitiṃ me hariḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. If one is devoid of any desire for the fruits of actions, one shall not cause any such acts to be done. He should dedicate a pious and religious act (to Lord Hari) by saying, “May Lord Hari be hereby pleased with me”.

## \|\| 1.3.75 \|\|

*ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarutpattidāyakāḥ \|*  
*phalāgṛdhnuḥ karmaṇāṃ tatprātproti paramaṃ padam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. All the worlds up to and including the region of god Brahma are the bestowers of rebirth. But a person who has no desire for the fruit even of meritorious acts, attains to the highest region namely Moksa— Liberation from samsara.

## \|\| 1.3.76 \|\|

*vedoditāni karmāṇi kuryādīśvaratuṣṭaye \|*  
*yathāśramaṃ tyaktukāmaḥ prānpoti padamavyayam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76 It is just for the propitiation of the Lord of the Universe, that one should perform sacred rites and actions prescribed in the Vedas as per his stage in life (ahama). One who is desirous of renouncing all karmas altogether including even those prescribed for his airama (stage of life), attains to the Eternal Region.

## \|\| 1.3.77 \|\|

*niṣkāmo vā sakāmo vā kuryātkarma yathāvidhi \|*  
*svāśramācāraśūnyaśca patitaḥ procyate budhaiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Irrespective of one’s desire for obtaining the fruit thereof, one should perform the holy rites in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the iastras (for performance of sacred acts). One who is fallen from the conduct of life (performance of duties) befitting the stage of his life, is called “a fallen fellow” by wise persons.

## \|\| 1.3.78 \|\|

*sadācāraparo vipro varddhate brahmatejasā \|*  
*tasya viṣṇuśca tuṣṭaḥ syādbhaktiyuktasya nārada \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A Brahmana devoted to righteous conduct shines forth with Brahmanical splendour. О Narada! Lord Visnu also is propitious to him who is endowed with devotion.

## \|\| 1.3.79 \|\|

*bhārate janma saṃprāpya nātmānaṃ tārayetu yaḥ \|*  
*pacyate niraye dhore sa tvācandrākratārakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. If, after being born in the continent of Bharata a person does not redeem himself, he is tortured in the terrible hell as long as the moon, the sun and the stars shine.

## \|\| 1.3.80 \|\|

*vāsadevaparo dharmo vāsudevaparaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevaparaṃ jñānaṃ vāsudevaparā gatiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Real Dharma has Vasudeva as the highest object. Penance is to be solely devoted to Vasudeva. Perfect knowledge refers to Lord Vasudeva and Lord Vasudeva is the ultimate goal.

## \|\| 1.3.81 \|\|

*vāsudevātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ tasmādanyatra vidyate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The entire Universe including the mobile and the immobile beings, from god Brahma down to a clump of grass, is identical with Lord Vasudeva. There is nothing else other than he.

## \|\| 1.3.82 \|\|

*sa eva dhātā tripurāntakaśca sa eva devāsurayajñarupaḥ \|*  
*sa evabrahmāṇḍamidaṃ tato 'nyanna kiñcidasti vyatiriktarupam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. He alone is god Brahma, the Creator of the Universe as well as god Rudra, the destroyer of Tripuras (Three Cities). He alone has assumed the forms of gods, demons, and sacrifice. He alone constitutes this Brahmanda (Cosmic Egg). There is nothing else that is separate and distinct from him.

## \|\| 1.3.83 \|\|

*asmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiñcidyasmādaṇīyānnatathā mahīyān \|*  
*vyātpaṃ hi tenedamidaṃ vicitraṃ taṃ devadevaṃ praṇametsamīṅyam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There is nothing else greater than he. There is nothing more minute or more immense than he. All this wonderful Universe is pervaded by him. One should bow down to that Lord of gods, worthy of being praised.

## Chapter 4. Anecdote of Markandeya

## \|\| 1.4.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śraddhāpūrvāḥ sarvadharmā manorathaphalapradāḥ \|*  
*śraddhayāsādhyate sarvaṃ śraddhayā tuṣyate hariḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanaka said:

1\. All pious rites performed with religious faith confer blessings in accordance with one’s cherished desires. Every thing is achieved through faith. It is through faith in him that Hari is propitiated.

## \|\| 1.4.2 \|\|

*bhaktirbhaktyaiva karttavyātathā karmāṇi bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*karmaścaddhāvihīnāni na sidhyantiṃ dvijo tamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Acts of devotion should be performed devoutly (and with reverential faith). All holy rites should be performed with devotion. О excellent Brahmana! Holy rites lacking in faith never become fruitful.

## \|\| 1.4.3 \|\|

*yathā'loko hi jantūnāṃ ceṣṭākāraṇatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tathaiva sarvasiddhīnāṃ bhaktiḥ paramakāraṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Just as the light (of the sun, etc.) is the cause of the activities of creatures, so also, devotion is the ultimate cause of all Siddhts (complete accomplishments of objects or acquisition of super-human powers).

## \|\| 1.4.4 \|\|

*yathā samasta lokānāṃ jīvanaṃ salilaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tathā samastasiddhīnāṃ jīvanaṃ bhaktiriṣyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Just as water is regarded to be the enlivening factor in all the world, similarly, devotion is laid down (i.e. regarded) as the life-inspiring force in all Siddhis (spiritual attainments).

## \|\| 1.4.5 \|\|

*yathā bhūmiṃ samāśritya sarve jīvanti jantavaḥ \|*  
*tathā bhaktiṃ samāśritya sarvakāryyāṇi sādhayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Just as all creatures live by resorting to the earth (as their support), so also, one should accomplish all objects by taking recourse to devotion.

## \|\| 1.4.6 \|\|

*śraddhāvāṃllabhate dharṃmaṃ śraddhāvātarthamāpnuyāt \|*  
*śraddhayā sādhyate kāmaḥ śraddhāvānmokṣamānpuyāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A person endowed with Sraddha (earnest faith) attains the Purusartha — the end of human life — called Dharma (righteousness); the possessor of Sraddha secures wealth; the desire for enjoyment (Kama) — the third objective of human life, is realized through faith, and a man of faith attains salvation (Moksa).

## \|\| 1.4.7 \|\|

*na dānairna tapobhirvā yajñairvā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*bhaktihīnermuniśceṣṭha tuṣyate bhagavānhariḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О Excellent Sage! Lord Hari is not pleased with charitable gifts, austere penances or sacrifices with sumptuous monetary gifts, should these acts be devoid of devotion.

## \|\| 1.4.8 \|\|

*merumātrasuvarṇānāṃ koṭikoṭisahasraśaḥ \|*  
*dattā cāpyarthanāśāya yatobhaktivivarjitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Charitable gifts of heaps of gold as huge as the mount Meru, and donated billions of times — if they be devoid of devotion — result only in wastage of wealth.

## \|\| 1.4.9 \|\|

*abhaktyā yattapastaptaiḥ kevalaṃ kāyaśoṣaṇam \|*  
*abhaktyā yaddhutaṃ havyaṃ bhasmani nyastahavyavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The penance performed without devotion is but the desiccation of the body. The offering of oblations to gods in sacrificial fire, if it be without devotion, is fruitless like the oblations consigned to ashes.

## \|\| 1.4.10 \|\|

*yatkiñcitkurute karṃmaśraddhayāpyaṇumātrumātrakam \|.*  
*tannāma jāyate puṃsāṃ śāśvataṃ pratīdāyakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Whatever sacred rite, howsoever insignificant it may be, if performed with faith, certainly becomes the bestower of perpetual happiness.

## \|\| 1.4.11 \|\|

*aśvameghasahasraṃ vā karṃma vedoditaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ niṣphalaṃ brahmanyadi bhaktivivarjitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Brahmana! A thousand horse-sacrifices or any other holy rite enjoined in the Vedas, (in fact) everything is fruitless, if it is performed without devotion.

## \|\| 1.4.12 \|\|

*haribhaktiḥ parā nṝṇāṃ kāmadhenūpamā smṛtā \|*  
*tasyāṃ satyāṃ pibantyajñāḥ saṃsāragaralaṃ hyaho \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Devotion to Hari is the highest blessing to men. It is remembered (in sacred texts) to be comparable to a Kama-Dhenu (Wish-yielding heavenly cow). Alas! The pity of it is that, when it (such a wish-yielding cow) is available, ignorant fools gulp and quaff the poison of sarfisdra (worldly existence).

## \|\| 1.4.13 \|\|

*asārabhūte saṃsāre sārametadajātmaja \|*  
*bhagavadbhaktasaṅgaśca haribhaktistitikṣutā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Son of Aja (God Brahma)! The following constitute the cream and quint-essence of this terrestrial existence which is otherwise worthless: — association with the devotees of Lord Hari, devotion to him and forbearance.

## \|\| 1.4.14 \|\|

*asūyopetamanasāṃ bhaktidānādikarṃma yat \|*  
*avehi niṣphalaṃ brahaṃsteṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О Brahmana! Know that devotion, charitable gifts and other holy acts are futile in the case of people whose minds are defiled with jealousy, and that Lord Hari is still further away from them.

## \|\| 1.4.15 \|\|

*pariśriyābhitatpānāṃ dambhācāraratātmanām \|*  
*mṛṣā tu kurvatāṃ karma teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hari is far off from them who are greatly distressed to see the affluence of others, those whose minds revel in hypocritical religious activities, and those engaged in wrong and futile actions.

## \|\| 1.4.16 \|\|

*pṛcchatāṃ ca mahādharṃmānvadatāṃ vai mṛṣā ca tān \|*  
*dharmeṣvabhaktimanasāṃ teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hari is still further away from those who falsely interpret the Dharma to those who inquire about the highest religious duties, and from those whose minds are not devoted to religious and virtuous acts.

## \|\| 1.4.17 \|\|

*vedapraṇihito dharṃmo dharṃmo vedo nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tatrāśraddhāparā ye tu teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*
