17\. Dharma (the path of righteousness) is laid down by the Vedas. The Vedas are identical with the Supreme Deity Narayana. Hence, Hari is far off from those who have no faith in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.4.18 \|\|

*yasya dharṃmavihīnāni dinānyāyānti yānti ca \|*  
*sa lohakārabhastreva śvasannapi na jīvati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If the days in the life of a person simply come and go without his performance of righteous acts, such a man is like the bellow» of a blacksmith which mechanically inhales and exhales the air, and is not a living being. (The man simply breathes but does not lead a real life).

## \|\| 1.4.19 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyāḥ puruṣārthāḥ sanātanāḥ \|*  
*śraddhāvatāṃ hi sidhyanti nānyathā brahmanandanā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О Son of god Brahma! The principal aims in human life or Purusarthas, viz. Dharma, (righteousness), Artha — (wealth), Kama — (love) and Moksa (liberation) are realized only by men of faith and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.4.20 \|\|

*svācāramanatikramya haribhaktiparo hi yaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ yadvai paśyanti sūrayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He who, without infringing his prescribed code of conduct, is engrossed in devotion to Hari, goes to the abode of Lord Visnu which is visualized only by the seers.

## \|\| 1.4.21 \|\|

*kurvanvedoditāndharṃmānmunīndra svāśramocitān \|*  
*haridhyānaparoyastu sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О leader of sages! He who performs religious rites befitting the stage of his life as enjoined by the Vedas, and who is wholly absorbed in contemplating Hari, attains the highest region.

## \|\| 1.4.22 \|\|

*ācāraprabhavo dharmaḥ dharṃmasya prabhuracyutaḥ \|*  
*āśramācārayuktena pūjitaḥ sarvadā hariḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Acara (good and righteous conduct of life) is the source of Dharma, of which Lord Visnu, the Imperishable, is the Master. God Hari is always worshipped by those who observe the righteous conduct befitting their asrama (stage of life).

## \|\| 1.4.23 \|\|

*yaḥ svācāraparibhraṣṭaḥ sāṅgavedāntago 'pi vā \|*  
*sa eva patito jñeyo yataḥ karmabahiṣkṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person fallen from the course of conduct prescribed for his stage of life, should be regarded as an apostate even though he might have mastered the Vedas, the Upanisads and the ancillary subjects of the Vedas, for he is excluded from holy rites (or duties laid down in the fastras).

## \|\| 1.4.24 \|\|

*haribhaktipari vāpi haridhyānaparo 'pi vā \|*  
*bhraṣṭo yaḥ svāśramācārātpatitaḥ so 'bhidhīyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Although a person is solely devoted to Lord Hari or is wholly engaged in contemplating him, he is called an apostate or fallen from the religious path, if he swerves from the prescribed code of conduct laid down for his stage of life (asrama).

## \|\| 1.4.25 \|\|

*vedo vā haribhaktirvā bhaktirvāpi maheśvare \|*  
*ācārātpatitaṃ mūḍhaṃ na punāti dvijottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О excellent Brahmana! Neither the Veda nor devotion unto Hari or to the great god Siva, sanctifies the confounded fellow who has fallen from his acara (the prescribed code of behaviour).

## \|\| 1.4.26 \|\|

*puṇyakṣetrābhigamanaṃ puṇyatīrthaniṣevaṇam \|*  
*yajño vā vividho brahmaṃstyaktācāraṃna rakṣati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О Brahmana! Pilgrimage to holy places, ablutions in sacred waters or performance of sacrifices of different types, cannot save one who has forsaken his acara(righteous conduct).

## \|\| 1.4.27 \|\|

*ācārātprāpyate svarga ācārātprāpyate sukham \|*  
*ācārātprāpyate mokṣa ācārātkiṃ na labhyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Heaven is attained through acara; happiness is derived through observing the code of righteous conduct; Liberation from samsara is secured through acara. What is there which is not obtainable through acara?

## \|\| 1.4.28 \|\|

*ācārāṇāntu sarveṣāṃ yogānāṃ caiva sattam \|*  
*haribhaktepari tathā nidānaṃ bhaktiriṣyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О excellent Sage! Reverential devotion is laid down as the primary cause of all acaras, yogas and even of devotedness to Hari.

## \|\| 1.4.29 \|\|

*bhaktyaiva pūjyate viṣṇurvāñchitārthaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsamastalokānāṃ bhaktirmāteti gīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Lord Visnu bestows the desired objects and fruitsonly When worshipped with devotion. Hence, adoration of God is glorified as the mother of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.4.30 \|\|

*jīvanti jantavaḥ sarve yathā mātarāśritāḥ \|*  
*tathā bhaktiṃ samāśritya sarve jīvanti dhārṃmikāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Just as all creatures come to life by resorting to their mother, so also all righteous persons live by taking recourse to pious devotion.

## \|\| 1.4.31 \|\|

*svāśramācārayuktasya haribhaktiryadā bhavet \|*  
*na tasya triṣu lokeṣu sadṛśo 'styajanandana \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If a person endowed with the course of conduct befitting his asrama, is also devoted to Lord Hari, О son of god Brahma, there is no one equal to such a person in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.4.32 \|\|

*bhaktyā sidhyanti karṃmāṇi karṃmāṇi karṃmābhistuṣyate hariḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstuṣṭe bhavejjñānaṃ jñānānmokṣamavāpyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Holy rites fructify through devotion. Hari is pleased with holy rites. Perfect knowledge dawns when he is pleased, and Liberation from samsara is attained through perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.4.33 \|\|

*bhaktistu bhagavadbhaktasaṅgena khalu jāyate \|*  
*tatsaṅgaṃ prāpyate pumbhiḥ sukṛtaiḥ pūrvasañcitaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Piety is generated by contacts with the votaries of the God and such contacts are secured by men, thanks to the merit accumulated in the previous births.

## \|\| 1.4.34 \|\|

*varṇāśramācāraratā bhagavadbhaktilālasāḥ \|*  
*kāmādidoṣanir muktāste santo lokaśikṣakāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Saintly people abiding by the rules of conduct to be observed by men according to their respective castes and stages in life, and ardently desirous of engaging in the devotion of God, and free from passions and other blemishes, are the preceptors of the world.

## \|\| 1.4.35 \|\|

*sastaṅgaḥ paramo brahmanna labhyetākṛtātmanām \|*  
*yadi labhyeta vijñeyaṃ puṇyaṃ janmāntarārjitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Association with saintly souls, the greatest achievement, cannot be secured by people who are not self-possessed, О Brahmana. If it be acquired at all, it should be known as being due to the merits earned in previous births.

## \|\| 1.4.36 \|\|

*pūrvārjitāni pāpāni nāśamāyānti yasya vai \|*  
*satsaṅgatirbhavettasya nānyathā ghaṭate hi sā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Associations with the good take place in case of a person, when the sins accumulated earlier, have been completely annihilated; otherwise it does not come about.

## \|\| 1.4.37 \|\|

*ravirhi raśimajālena divā hantibahistamaḥ \|*  
*santaḥ sūktimarīcyoścāntardhvāntaṃ hi sarvadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. During the day time, the Sun dispells the external darkness by means of the clusters of his rays, but saintly persons remove the internal darkness of ignorance at all times by means of the streams of light, in the form of wise sayings.

## \|\| 1.4.38 \|\|

*durlabhāḥ puruṣā loke bhagavadbhaktilālasāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṅgo bhavedyasya tasya śāntirhi śāśvatī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Few and rare are the persons who are eagerly desirous of being devoted to the Lord in this world. Perpetual peace accrues to him who comes in contact with such persons. Narada enquired:

## \|\| 1.4.39 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kiṃlakṣaṇā bhāgavatāste ca kiṃ karṃma kurvate \|*  
*teṣāṃ loko bhavetkīdṛktatsarvaṃ brūhi tattvataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. What are the characteristics of the Bhagavatas (devotees of the Lord)? What holy acts do they perform? What regions do they attain to? Narrate to me everything (about these) precisely.

## \|\| 1.4.40 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi bhakto rameśasya devadevasya citriṇaḥ \|*  
*etānnigadituṃ śaktastvato nāstyadhiko 'paraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You are indeed the real devotee of the discusbearing Lord of gods, the divine consort of goddess Laksmi. There is no one else better qualified and competent than you to recount this. Sanaka said:

## \|\| 1.4.41 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śṛṇu brahmanparaṃ guhyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyasya dhīmanaḥ ña \|*  
*yamuvāca jagannātho yoganidrāvimocitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Listen to that esoteric secret which the Lord of the Universe confided to the intelligent Markandeya, as he (the Lord) woke up from hisyogic slumber, О Brahamana.

## \|\| 1.4.42 \|\|

*yo 'sau viṣṇuḥ paraṃ jyotirdevadevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*jagatkarttā śivabrahma svarupavān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. That Supreme-most refulgent god Visnu is the Eternal Lord of the Devas. He is the Creater of the Universe as well as the pervader of the same, and has assumed the forms of Siva (destroyer of the Universe) as well as Brahma (the creator of the Universe).

## \|\| 1.4.43-44 \|\|

*yugānte raudrarupeṇa brahmāṇḍagrāhitaḥ \|*  
*jagatyekārṇavībhūte naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|\| 43 \|\|*

*bhagavāneva śeṣātmā śete vaṭadale hariḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyātābjajanmādyairābhūṣitatanūrūhaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. At the end of the yugas, he manifested himself in an immensely huge form as Rudra and swallowed up the whole Universe as one morsel. When the whole Universe became a vast sheet of cosmic water after the destruction of the mobile and immobile creation, the Lord, the only residual soul Hari, lies on the leaf of a banyan tree. The hairs over his body are embellished by innumerable lotus-born deities (Brahmas) and others.

## \|\| 1.4.45 \|\|

*pādāṅguṣṭāgraniryātagaṅgāśītāmbupāvanaḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmātsūkṣmataro devo brahmāṇḍagrāsaṃbṛṃhitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The god sanctifies every one by means of the cool water of the Ganga issuing out of his big toe. The Lord is subtler than the subtlest, yet he assumes an immense form and swallows the Universe.

## \|\| 1.4.46 \|\|

*vaṭacchade śayāno 'bhūtsarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tasminsthāne mahābhāgo nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyaḥ sthinastasya līlāḥ paśyanmahe śituḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Endowed with all Super-human potencies (Saktis), he lay resting on the leaf of a banyan tree. At that spot stood the highly blessed devotee of Narayana, the sage Markandeya who was observing all the sports of the great Lord.

## \|\| 1.4.47 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*tasminkāle mahāghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*harirekaḥ sthita iti mune pūrvaṃ hi śuśruma \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. *The sages said:* О Sage! Formerly, we heard that in that terrible period (of Universal deluge) when the mobile and immobile creation had already perished, it was Lord Hari alone who remained there.

## \|\| 1.4.48 \|\|

*jagatyekārṇavībhūte naṣṭe sthāvarañjagame \|*  
*sarvagrastena hariṇā kimarthaṃ so 'vaśeṣitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When the whole Universe had become one single cosmic ocean and when all the mobile and immobile beings were annihilated, how is it that he (Markandeya) alone was spared by god Hari who had swallowed everything.

## \|\| 1.4.49 \|\|

*paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hyatraṃ varttate 'tīva sūta naḥ \|*  
*harikīrtisudhāpāne kasyālasyaṃ prajā yate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О Suta! Exceedingly great is our curiosity in this regard. Who will forsooth get lethargic and idle at the opportunity of imbibing the nectar of the glory of Lord Hari?

## \|\| 1.4.50-51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*āsīnmunirmahābhāgo mṛkaṇḍuriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*śālagrāme mahātīrthe so 'tapyata mahātapāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yugānāma yutaṃ brahmangṛṇanbrahma sanātanam \|*  
*ṭa nirāhāraḥ kṣamāyuktaḥ satyasandho jitendriyaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51.  *Suta replied:* There was a highly blessed sage well-known by the name Mrkandu. He performed an austere penance at the important sacred place known as Salagrama, the great holy centre. For the duration of ten thousand Yugas, he repeated the sacred mystic syllable Оm, observing fast all the while. He exercised forbearance, control over his sense-organs, and practised truthfulness (in thought, word and deed).

## \|\| 1.4.52 \|\|

*ātmavatsarvabhūtāni paśyanviṣayaniḥspṛhaḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtahito dānta statāpa sumahattapaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Looking upon all living beings as his own atman (self), he performed that great penance entertaining no desire for worldly pleasures, and was solicitous for the welfare of all creatures, and held his sense-organs under control.

## \|\| 1.4.53 \|\|

*tattāpaḥśaṅkitāḥ sarve devā indrādayastadā \|*  
*pareśaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurnārāyaṇamanāmayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Afraid of his penance, lndra and all other gods sought refuge in the highest god Narayana who is free from all ailments.

## \|\| 1.4.54 \|\|

*kṣīrābdheruttaraṃ tīraṃ saṃprāpyatrivivaukasaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurdevadeveśaṃ pahmanābhaṃ jagadgurum \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After reaching the northern shore of the Milky Ocean, the residents of the celestial region eulogised Lord Visnu, the god with a lotus in his navel, the Supreme Lord of all gods, and the preceptor of the universe.

## \|\| 1.4.55 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*nārāyaṇākṣarānanta śaraṇāgatapālaka \|*  
*mṛkaṇḍutapasā trastānpāhi naḥ śaraṇāgatān \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. *The gods submitted:* О Narayana, the imperishable, infinite Lord, the protector of those who seek asylum in you, do protect us who, being afraid of Mrkandu’s penance, have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 1.4.56 \|\|

*jaya devādhideveśa jaya śaṅkhagadādhara \|*  
*jayo lokasvarupāya jayo brahmāṇḍahetave \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Victory to the Supreme Lord of the chiefs of gods! Victory to the wielder of the conch (Pancajanya), and the mace Kaumodaki! Hail to you whose form is the Universe and who is the cause of the Brahmanda. (the cosmic age or the Universe).

## \|\| 1.4.57 \|\|

*namaste devadeveśa namaste lokapāvana \|*  
*namaste lokanāthāya namaste lokasākṣiṇe \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Obeisance to you the Lord of gods. We bow to you the sanctifier of the worlds. Hail to you the Lord of the Universe and the witness of the Universe.

## \|\| 1.4.58 \|\|

*namaste dhyānagamyāya namaste dhyānahetave \|*  
*namaste dhyānarupāya namaste dhyānapākṣiṇe \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Obeisance to you who are comprehensible through meditation. Hail to you who are the object of contemplation. Obeisance to you whose form is contemplated and who is the witness of meditation.

## \|\| 1.4.59 \|\|

*keśihantre namastubhyaṃ madhuhantre parātmane \|*  
*namo bhūmyādirūpāya namaścaitanyarupiṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Obeisance to you the slayer of the Demon Kesin and the destroyer of Madhu. Hail to you the great atman (the Supreme soul) who assume the form of the earth, etc. and whose form is sentience itself.

## \|\| 1.4.60 \|\|

*namo jyeṣṭāya śuddhāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane \|*  
*arupāya svarupāya bahurupāya te namaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Hail to the eldest (eternal) God, the pure and attributeless one, yet whose nature is guna. Obeisance to you who are devoid of form yet who possess your own form and manifest yourself into many forms.

## \|\| 1.4.61 \|\|

*namo brahmaṇyadevāya gobrāhmaṇahitāya ca \|*  
*jagaddhitāya kṛṣṇāya govindāya namonamaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Obeisance to the Lord friendly to Brahmanas. Hail to you, О Krsna, the protector and benefactor of cows and Brahmanas. Hail to you Govinda, the benefactor of the Universe.

## \|\| 1.4.62 \|\|

*namo hikṣamagarbhāya namo brahmādirupiṇe \|*  
*namaḥ sūryyādirupāya havyakavyabhuje namaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Bow to Hiranya-garbha.8 Obeisance to the Lord who assumes the form of god Brahma and others. Hail to you who manifest yourself in the form of the sun and other gods. Obeisance to you, the enjoyer of the oblations of food offered to gods and deceased ancestors (havya and kavya).

## \|\| 1.4.63 \|\|

*namo nityāya vandyāya sadānandaikarupiṇe \|*  
*namaḥ smṛtārtināśāya bhūyo bhūyo namo namaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Obeisance to the Eternal Deity worthy of respect. Hail to you whose form constitutes perpetual bliss. Bow to you who destroy the distress of those who remember you. Obeisance to you again and again.”

## \|\| 1.4.64 \|\|

*evaṃ devastutiṃ śrutvā bhagavānkamalāpatiḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣatāmagātteṣāṃ śaṅkacatragadādharaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On hearing the eulogy sung by the devas, Lord Visnu, the Divine Consort of goddess Laksmi, the wielder of the conch (Panchajanya), discus (Sudarsana) and the mace (Kaumodaki) manifested himself to them.

## \|\| 1.4.65-67 \|\|

*vikacāmbujapatrākṣaṃ sūryyakoṭisamaprabham \|*  
*sarvālaṅkārasaṃyuktaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pītāmbaradharaṃ saumyaṃ svarṇayajñopavītinam \|*  
*stṛyamānaṃ munivaraiḥ pārṣadapravarāvṛttam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣyvā devasaṃghāste tattejohatatejasaḥ \|*  
*namaścakrurmudā yuktā aṣṭāṅgauravaniṃ gatāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. On seeing him, the multitude of gods made obeisance to him — the Lord whose eyes resembled the petals of a full blown lotus, whose lustre equalled the combined effulgence of a hundred million suns, whose person was bedecked all over with ornaments, whose chest was characterised by Srivatsa (a curl of golden hair on Visnu’s bosom), who was being eulogised by great sages and was surrounded by his prominent attendants (Parsadas). The brilliance of the devas was eclipsed by the majestic lustre of the Lord. With great joy, they bowed down to him laying themselves prostrate before him, touching the ground with eight parts of their bodies.

## \|\| 1.4.68 \|\|

*tataḥ prasanno bhagavānmeghagaṃbhīranisvanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca prīṇayandevānnatānindrapurogamān \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The Lord who was propitiated, addressed devas in a voice deep and majestic like the rumbling of clouds, thus giving delight to Indra and other devas who bowed down to him.

## \|\| 1.4.69 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*jāne vo mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ mṛkaṇḍutapasoṅgam \|*  
*yuṣmānna bādhate devāḥ sa ṛṣiḥ sajjanāgrāṇīḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. *The Lord said:* О gods! I do understand your mental agony caused to you by the penance of Мrkandu. But that sage is the foremost one among the saintly people and will not trouble you.

## \|\| 1.4.70 \|\|

*saṃpadbhiḥ saṃyutā vāpi vipadbhiścāpi sajjanāḥ \|*  
*sarvathānyaṃ na bādhante svapne 'pi surasattamāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О excellent gods! Whether endowed with affluence or bedevilled by adversities, the good shall by no means cause any harm unto others even in dreams.

## \|\| 1.4.71 \|\|

*satataṃ bādhyamāno 'pi viṣayākhyairarātibhiḥ \|*  
*avidhāyātmano rakṣāmanyāndveṣṭi kathaṃ sudhīḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Himself being harassed continuously by enemies called the ‘worldly pleasures’, how can the highly intelligent one be hostile towards others, instead of protecting himself.

## \|\| 1.4.72 \|\|

*tāpatrayābhidhānena bādhyamāno hi mānavaḥ \|*  
*anyaṃ krīḍayituṃ śaktaḥ kathaṃ bhavati sattamaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. How can the excellent one who is himself ever molested by three types of distresses (originating from the physical body, the external world and extra-mundane sources), be competent (or inclined) to trouble others?

## \|\| 1.4.73 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā bādhate yaḥ sadā parān \|*  
*nityaṃ kāmādibhiryukto mūḍhadhīḥ procyate tu saḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He who always troubles others mentally, verbally or physically, and who is always in the grip of passions, etc. is called a person of confounded mind.

## \|\| 1.4.74 \|\|

*yo lokahitakṛnmartyo gatāsuryo vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*niḥśaṅgaḥ procyate sadbhirihāmātra ca sattamāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The man who renders service to the world even at the risk of his life, and is devoid of rivalry or jealousy, is said to be an excellent man both here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.4.75 \|\|

*saśaṅkaḥ sarvadā duḥkhī niḥśaṅkaḥ sukhamānpuyāt \|*  
*gacchadhvaṃ svālayaṃ svasthāḥ krīḍayiṣyati vo na saḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A person troubled with fear or with suspicion is always miserable and a fearless or nonsuspicious person shall always be happy. Return to your abodes and rest' assured that he will not play false to you.

## \|\| 1.4.76-77 \|\|

*bhavatāṃ rakṣakaścāhaṃ viharadhvaṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*iti datvā varaṃ teṣāmatasīkusumaprabhaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*paśyatāmeva devānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*tuṣṭātmānaḥ suragaṇāṃ yayurnākaṃ yathāgatam \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. I am the Protector of you all. Be happy and sport about as you please.” After granting this boon to them, the Lord with the beauty and lustre of the atasi flowers (a blue flower) vanished there immediately even as the gods were simply gazing on. Delighted in their minds, all the multitudes of gods returned to the celestial world whence they had come.

## \|\| 1.4.78-79 \|\|

*mṛkaṇḍorapi tuṣṭātmā hariḥ pratyakṣatāmagāt \|*  
*arupaṃ paramaṃ brahmasvaprakāśaṃ nirañjanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ pītavāsasamacyacutam \|*  
*divyāyudhadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛkaṇḍurvismito 'bhavat \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Being pleased and propitiated in his mind, Hari revealed himself to Mrkandu. Mrkandu was surprised to see the formless Supreme Brahman, the self-luminous unsullied Acyuta resembling the atasi flowers in complexion and clad in yellow garments, holding in his hands thvine weapons.

## \|\| 1.4.80 \|\|

*dhyānādunmīlya nayanaṃ apaśyaddharimagrataḥ \|*  
*prasannavadanaṃ śāntaṃ dhātāraṃ viśvatejasam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Opening his eyes from meditation, he (Mrkandu) saw in front of him, Lord Hari of pleasing appearance, the quiescent creator of the world possessing and radiating lustre all around the world. With his hair standing on their ends on his body, with tears of joy welling up in the eyes, Mrkandu prostrated himself like a staff in front of the Eternal Lord of gods.

## \|\| 1.4.82 \|\|

*aśrubhiḥ kṣālayaṃstasya caraṇau harṣasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*śirasyañcalimādhāya stotuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Washing the feet of the Lord with tears of delight and joining together his palms over his head, he began to eulogise.

## \|\| 1.4.83 \|\|

*mṛkaṇḍuruvāca*  
*namaḥ pareśāya parātmarupiṇe parātparasprātparataḥ parāya \|*  
*apārapārāya parānukartre namaḥ parebhyaḥ parapāraṇāya \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Obeisance to the Supreme Lord who is the Param- atman, the great self. Hail to you who are greater than the greatest and transcendental (to everything else). Bow to you whose greatness is unfathomable and who redeem your devotees from enemies and are the most eminent one.

## \|\| 1.4.84 \|\|

*yo nāmajātyādivikalpahīnaḥ śabdādidoṣavyatirekarupaḥ \|*  
*bahusvarupo 'pi nirañjano yastamīśamīḍhyaṃ paramaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Mrkandu said: I worship the supreme Deity, the ruler of the Universe worthy of being praised — the Deity who is devoid of false notion such as name, caste,etc., and whose form is opposed to and unconnected with such defects as *sabda* (words) and who, though possessed of many forms, is unsullied by them.

## \|\| 1.4.85 \|\|

*devāntavedyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ hiraṇyagarbhādijagatsvarupam \|*  
*anūpamaṃ bhakti janānukampinaṃ bhajāmi sarveśvaramādimīḍyam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. I worship the Eternal Lord of all, the ancient Person knowable through the Upanisads (Vedanta), whose form is the universe itself (including god Brahma and others), who is beyond comparison and who is merciful to his devotees.

## \|\| 1.4.86 \|\|

*paśyanti yaṃ vītasamastadoṣā dhyānaikaniṣṭhā vigataspṛhāśca \|*  
*nivṛttamohāḥ paramaṃ pavitraṃ nato 'smi saṃsāranirvarttakaṃ tam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. I bow down to that great holy Deity who redeems his devotees from samsara, and who reveals himself to those who are free from all blemishes, those completely absorbed in meditation, those free from desires and those who have no delusion.

## \|\| 1.4.87 \|\|

*smṛtārtināśanaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaraṇāgatapālakam \|*  
*jagatsevyaṃ jagāddhāma pareśaṃ karuṇākaram \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. I bow down to the merciful great Lord Visnu, the destroyer of the distress and mental agony of those who remember him, the protector of those who seek refuge in him, worthy of being served by the universe and the asylum of the world.”

## \|\| 1.4.88 \|\|

*evaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavānviṣṇustena maharṣiṇā \|*  
*avāpa paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Being thus praised by that great sage, god Visnu, the wielder of conch (Pancajanya), discus (Sudarsana) and the mace (Kaumodaki) was highly pleased.

## \|\| 1.4.89 \|\|

*ayāliṅgya muniṃ devaścaturbhirdīrghabāhubhiḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaṃ prītyā varaṃ baraya suvrata \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Embracing the sage with all his four long arms, the Lord said with great pleasure, “O Sage, a strict observer of religious vows! Seek any boon.

## \|\| 1.4.90 \|\|

*prīto 'smi tapasā tena stotreṇa ca tavānagha \|*  
*manasā yadabhipretaṃ varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. О sinless sage! I am delighted by your penance as well as this hymn of praise. Choose whatever boon you have cherished in your mind, О highly virtuous sage”.

## \|\| 1.4.91 \|\|

*mṛkaṇḍurūvāca*  
*devadeva jagannātha kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tvaddarśanamapuṇyānāṃ durlabhaṃ ca yataḥ smṛtam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. *Mrkandu said:* “O God of gods! О Lord of the universe! I am certainly satisfied and have all my objects achieved by your manifestation to me, since it is remembered (in sastras) that your vision is impossible to those who are devoid of merit.

## \|\| 1.4.92-93 \|\|

*brahmādyā yaṃ na vaśyanti yoginaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*dharmiṣṭā dīkṣitāśvāpi vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*taṃ paśyāmi paraṃ dhāma kimato 'nyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe \|*  
*etenaiva kṛtārtho 'smi janārdana jagaddharo \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. I perceive you whom even god Brahma and others cannot see. Even the yogins who have fulfilled their vows, are extremely righteous, are initiated (in sacrifices or sacred lores), are devoid of passions and jealousy, cannot perceive you. I now visualise you who are the highest resort. What other boon should I choose? О Janardana, О Preceptor of the universe, I am perfectly satisfied with this vision only.

## \|\| 1.4.94 \|\|

*yatrāmasmṛtimātreṇa mahāpātakino 'pi ye \|*  
*tatpade paramaṃ yānni te dṛṣṭvā kiṣunācyuta \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. О Acyuta! Even by mere remembrance of your name persons with heinous sins, attain to your highest region, what then after getting your audience and a view”?

## \|\| 1.4.95 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*satyatpruktaṃ tvayā brahmānprīno 'smi tava paṇḍita \|*  
*madṛrśanaṃ hi viphalaṃ na kadācidbhaviṣyati \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. *The glorious Lord said:* The glorious Lord said:О Learned Brahmana! What you spoke is true. I am really pleased with you. Never can my vision be fruitless.

## \|\| 1.4.96 \|\|

*viṣṇirbhaktakuṭumbīti vadanti vivudhāḥ sadā \|*  
*tadeva pālayiṣyāmi majjano nānṛtaṃ vadet \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Learned men always say, “God Visnu treates his devotees as members of his family". I shall bear it out. My devotees would not utter what is untrue.

## \|\| 1.4.97 \|\|

*tasmāttvattapasātuṣṭo yāsyāmi tava putratām \|*  
*samastaguṇasaṃyukto dīrghajīvī svarupavān \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Hence, being propitiated by your penance, I shall become your son. He (my incarnation) will be endowed with all good qualities. He will be handsome and long-lived.

## \|\| 1.4.98 \|\|

*mama janma kule yasya katatkulaṃ mokṣagāmi vai \|*  
*mayi tuṣṭe muniśreṣṭha kimasādhyaṃ jagatraye \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The family in which I incarnate, attains salvation. О excellent sage! What is there that cannot be achieved in the three worlds, if I am pleased.

## \|\| 1.4.99 \|\|

*ityuktvā devadevaśo muneratasya samīkṣataḥ \|*  
*antardadhe mṛkaṇḍuśca tapasaḥ samavartata \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. After addressing thus, the Lord of devas vanished then and there, even as' the sage was watching. The sage Mrkandu completed his penance.

## Chapter 5. The Description of Markandeya's Life

## \|\| 1.5.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*brahmankathaṃ sa bhagavānmṛkaṇḍoḥ putratāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra ca tadbruhi harirbhārgavavaṃśajaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. О Brahmana sage! Be pleased to narrate to me how the glorious Lord became the son of Mrkandu and what Hari did after being born in the family of Bhargava.

## \|\| 1.5.2 \|\|

*śrūyate capurāṇeṣu mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*apaśyadvaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ cirañjīvyasya saṃplave \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It is heard mentioned in the puranas that Markandeya, the long-lived sage, perceived the maya of Visnu, at the time of Deluge (dissolution of the world).

## \|\| 1.5.3 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śruṇu nārada vakṣaayāmi kathāmetāṃ sanātanīm \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktisamāyuktāṃ mārkuṇḍeyamuniṃ prati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\.  *Sanaka replied:* Listen, О Narada. I shall narrate to you this ancient story about the sage Markandeya which is closely connected with devotion to Visnu.

## \|\| 1.5.4 \|\|

*tapaso 'nte mṛkaṇḍuste mṛkaṇḍustu bhāryāmudūhya sattamaḥ \|*  
*gārhasthyamakaroddhṛṣṭaḥ śānto dāntaḥ kṛtārthakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the conclusion of his penance, the excellent sage Mrkandu entered the householders stage, and gladly performed the duties prescribed for householders. He was self-controlled, quiescent and contented.

## \|\| 1.5.5 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā śucirdakṣā nityaṃ patiparāyaṇā \|*  
*manasā vacasā cāpi dehena ca pativratā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. His wife was pure, attentive and always devoted to her husband. She was chaste and true to her husband in thought, word and deed.

## \|\| 1.5.6 \|\|

*kāle dadhāra sā garbhaṃ haritejoṃśasaṃbhavam \|*  
*ruṣuve daśamāsānte putraṃ tejasvināṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At the proper time, she conceived in her womb the child born of a ray of the majestic lustre of Hari. At the end of the tenth month, she gave birth to an exceedingly brilliant son.

## \|\| 1.5.7 \|\|

*sa ṛṣiḥ paramaprīto dṛṣṭvā putraṃ sulakṣaṇam \|*  
*jātakaṃ kārayāmāsa maṅgalaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing the son endowed with all auspicious characteristics, that sage was extremely delighted. He caused all the prescribed post-natal auspicious rites to be performed in accordance with the iastric injunctions.

## \|\| 1.5.8-9 \|\|

*sa bālo vavṛdhe tatra śuklapakṣa ivīḍupaḥ \|*  
*tatastu pañcame varṣe upanīya mudānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śikṣāṃ cakāra viprendra vaidikīṃ dharmasaṃhitām \|*  
*namaskāryā dvijāḥ putra sadādṛṣṭā vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The boy grew up there like the moon in the bright half of the month, О prominent Brahmana. He invested the boy with the sacred thread, in his fifth year. With great joy, he imparted instructions to him in the Vedic lore and in scriptures on dharma. "O son! The Brahmanas should always be paid respects when seen. As per sacred precepts, the practice has been enjoined and observed.

## \|\| 1.5.10 \|\|

*trikālaṃ sūryamabhyarcya salilāñcalidānataḥ \|*  
*vaidikaṃ karma tartavyaṃ vedādhyayanapūrvakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After worshipping the sun with offerings of libation of water (with joining together of palms i.e. performing Sandhya- vandana) thrice a day, Vedic rites should be performed with due attention to the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.5.11 \|\|

*brahmacaryeṇa tapasā pūjanīyo hariḥ sadā \|*  
*niṣiddhaṃ varjanīyaṃ syādṛṣṭasaṃbhāṣaṇādikam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hari should always be worshipped through observance of celibacy and performance of penance. All forbidden acts such as conversation with the wicked (or on improper topics) should be avoided.

## \|\| 1.5.12 \|\|

*sādhubhiḥ saha vastavyaṃ viṣṇubhaktiparaiḥ sadā \|*  
*na dveṣaḥ kasyacitkāryaḥ sarveṣāṃ hitamācaret \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. One should always associate oneself with saintly persons engaged in devotion to Visnu. One should never entertain hatred or hostility to any one and one should perceive activities conducive to the welfare of all.

## \|\| 1.5.13-15 \|\|

*ijyādhyaṃyanadānāni sadā kāryāṇi te suta \|*  
*evaṃ pitrā samādiṣṭo mārkaṇḍeyo munīśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*cacāra dharmaṃ satataṃ sadā saṃcintayanharim \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyo mahābhāgo dayāvāndharmavatsalaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ātmavānsatyasandhaśca mārtaṇḍasadṛśaprabhaḥ \|*  
*vaśīṃ śānto mahājñānī sarvatattvārthakovidaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. О son! Performance of sacrifices, Vedic studies and granting of charitable gifts should always be carried on by you.” Ordered thus by his father, Markandeya, the prominent sage, abided by the path of righteousness, constantly contemplating on Hari. The highly fortunate (or the illustrious) sage was compassionate, a lover of *dharma* or piety. He was self- possessed and true of word. His splendour was like that of the Sun. He was self-controlled, quiescent, deeply learned and wise, and proficient in the knowledge of the true nature of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.5.16 \|\|

*tapaścacāraṃ mahāmacyutaprītikāraṇam \|*  
*ārādhito jagannātho mākraṇḍeyena dhīmatā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He performed a great penance that gave delight to Lord Acyuta. The Lord of the universe was propitiated by the intelligent Markandeya.

## \|\| 1.5.17 \|\|

*purāṇasaṃhitāṃ karttudattavānvaramacyutaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyo muni tapaścacāraṃ paramamacyutaprītikāraṇam \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyo munistasmānnārāyaṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Acyuta conferred on him the boon of being competent to compose a *purana samhita* (known as the Markandeya Purana) Hence, the sage Markandeya is remembered as Narayana.

## \|\| 1.5.18-20 \|\|

*cirajīvī mahābhakto devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*jagatyekārṇavībhūte svaprabhāvaṃ janārddanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tasya darśayituṃ vigrāstaṃ na saṃhṛtavānhariḥ \|*  
*mṛkaṇḍutanayo dhīmānviṣṇubhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmiñjale mahāghore sthitavāñchīrṇapatravat \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyaḥ sthitastāvadyāvacchete hariḥ svayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. He was long-lived. He was also a great devotee of the discus-bearing Lord of devas (Visnu). О Brahmana, when the universe was converted into one vast sheet of Cosmic water, Janardana did not absorb him in himself in order to show to him his prowess. The learned son of Mrkandu, endowed with devotion to Visnu, floated like a shattered dry leaf in that extremely terrible mass of water. As long as Hari lay there in his yogic slumber, Markandeya too remained there.

## \|\| 1.5.21-23 \|\|

*tasya pramāṇaṃ vakṣyāmi kālasya vadataḥ śruṇu \|*  
*daśabhiḥ pañcabhiścaiva nimeṣaiḥ parikīrtitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kāṣṭātatriṃśato jñeyā kalā pahmajanandana \|*  
*tatriṃśato kṣaṇo jñeyastaiḥ paṅbharghaṭikā smṛtā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tadvayena muhūrttaṃ syāddinaṃ tatriṃśatā bhavet \|*  
*triṃśaddinerbhavenyāsaḥ pakṣadvitayasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. I shall now describe to you the extent or the duration of that period. Listen to it, as I recount it: The time unit *kastha* is made up of fifteen times winking of eyes (nimeshas). О son of god Brahma, thirty *kasthas* should be known as making one kala (eight seconds). A Ksana (four minutes) should be known as made up of thirty kalas. Six kshanas constitute a ghafikd (twenty-four minutes). Two ghatikas constitute one muhurta (forty-eight minutes). Thirty muhurtas constitute a day (of twenty-four hours). Thirty days or two fortnights make one month.

## \|\| 1.5.24 \|\|

*ṛturmāsadvayena syāttatrayeṇāyanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*taddayena bhavedabdaḥ sa devānāṃ dinaṃ bhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Two months constitute one rtu (a season). Three such rtus make one *ayana* (time from one solstice to another). Two such ayanas make one year, which constitutes one complete day (day and night) of deuas.

## \|\| 1.5.25 \|\|

*uttaraṃ divasaṃ prāhū rātrirvai dakṣiṇāyanam \|*  
*mānuṣeṇaiva māsena pitṝṇāṃ dinamucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They say that the Uttarayana (northward transit of the sun) is the day of gods, and Daksinayana (southward transit of the sun) is their night. A human month is said to be one day of the pitrs (manes).

## \|\| 1.5.26 \|\|

*tasmātsuryendusaṃyoge jñātavyaṃ kalpamuttamam \|*  
*divyairvarṣasahasrairdvādaśabhirdaivataṃ yugam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The day of the pitrs is from one new moon day to another (lit. when the sun comes into contact with the moon). A thousand celestial years constitute the period of a kalpa and twelve yugas constitute one yuga of gods.

## \|\| 1.5.27 \|\|

*daive yugasahasre dve brāhmaḥ kalpau tu tau nṛṇām \|*  
*ekasatpatisaṃkhyātairdivyairmanvantaraṃ yugaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Two thousand divine yugas make two brdhma kalpas and according to human calculations, seventy-one divine yugas constitute a manvantara.

## \|\| 1.5.28 \|\|

*caturddaśabhiretaiśca brahmaṇo divasaṃmune \|*  
*yāvatpramāṇaṃ divasaṃ tāvadrātriḥ prakīrtitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О sage, fourteen such manvantaras make one day of god Brahma. The extent of the night is declared to be the same as that of the day.

## \|\| 1.5.29-30 \|\|

*nāśamāyāti viprendra tasminkāle jagannayam \|*  
*manuṣeṇa sahasreṇa yatpramāṇaṃ bhavecchṛṇu \|\| 29 \|\|*

*caturyugasahasrāṇi brahmaṇo divasaṃ mune \|*  
*tadvanmāso vatsaraśca jñeyastasyāpi vedhasaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. О leading Brahmana, at that time, all the three worlds perish. Listen.to the extent of time according to human calculations. О sage, a thousand cycles of four yugas make one day of Brahma. Similarly, the months and the years of god Brahma should be known (calculated).

## \|\| 1.5.31 \|\|

*parārddhadvayakālastu tanmatena bhavedvijāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇorahastu vijñeyaṃ tāvadrātriḥ prakīrtitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О Brahmanas, according to his calculations the period of two pardrdhas should be known as one day of Visnu. The period of night is also said to be of the same extent.

## \|\| 1.5.32 \|\|

*mṛkaṇḍutanayastāvatsthitaḥ saṃjīrṇaparṇavat \|*  
*tasminghore jalamaye viṣṇuśaktyupabṛṃhitaḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ paramaṃ dhyāyansthitavānharisānnidhau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the middle of that terrible deluge of water, the son of Mrkandu lay like a withered leaf for that period. He was sustained by the spiritual potency of god Visnu. He stood near Hari meditating on the Supreme Soul.

## \|\| 1.5.33 \|\|

*atha kāle samāyāte yoganidrāvimocitaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭavānbrahmarupeṇa jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When the proper time came, the Deity, waking up from yogic slumber, assumed the form of god Brahma and created this universe, consisting of the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 1.5.34 \|\|

*saṃhṛtaṃ tu jalaṃ vīkṣya sṛṣṭaṃ viśvaṃ mṛkaṇḍujaḥ \|*  
*vismitaḥ paramaprīto vavande caraṇau hareḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Noticing the recession of water and the creation of the universe, the son of Mrkandu was surprised as well as was extremely delighted. He saluted the feet of Hari.

## \|\| 1.5.35 \|\|

*śirasyañjalimādhāya mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiḥ sadānandaikavigraham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With palms joined in reverence over his head, the great sage Markandeya eulogised the Deity whose body is constituted solely of perpetual bliss. He praised him in desired and desirable, appropriate words.

## \|\| 1.5.36 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*sahasraśirasaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam \|*  
*vāsudevamanādhāraṃ praṇato 'smijanārdanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. *Markandeya said:* I bow unto Janardana, the God with thousands of heads, Narayana, free from ailments, Vasudeva, who needs no other support, himself being the support of all.

## \|\| 1.5.37 \|\|

*ameyamajaraṃ nityaṃ sadānandaikavigraham \|*  
*apratarkyamanirdeśyaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I pay obeisance to Janardana who is beyond all measures (immeasurable), who is un-aging and eternal, whose person consists of pure perpetual bliss, who cannot be specifically pointed out, and whose nature surpasses imagination.

## \|\| 1.5.38 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ paramaṃ nityaṃ viśākṣaṃ viśvasambhavam \|*  
*sarvatattvamayaṃ śāntaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I bow unto Janardana who is imperishable, who is the Eternal Supreme Being, universal-eyed (Omnipresent and Omniscient) who is the source of the universe, who is quiescent and who constitutes all principles (enumerated by Sankhyas).

## \|\| 1.5.39 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ siddhaṃ sarvajñānaikabhājanam \|*  
*parātparataraṃ rupaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I pay my deep respects to Janardana, the ancient Рurusа, the master of all super-human potencies, the sole receptacle for all perfect knowledge and whose form is greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 1.5.40 \|\|

*parañjyotiḥ paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*sarvaikarupaṃ paramaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanamam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I bow to Janardana who is the highest splendour, the greatest abode, whose region is the holiest and supreme- most and who is both multiformed and single.

## \|\| 1.5.41 \|\|

*taṃ sadānandacinmātraṃ parāṇāṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*sarvaṃ sanātanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I bow unto Janardana who is existence or entity, knowledge and bliss incarnate; whose region is higher than the highest; who is the most pre-eminent, eternal Deity.

## \|\| 1.5.42 \|\|

*saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ śāntaṃ māyātītaṃ sumāyinam \|*  
*arupaṃ bahurupaṃ taṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I pay respects to Janardana who is endowed with attributes as well as is transcendental to them; who is quiescent and beyond the deluding potency Мaуa, and yet is its (Maya's) master; who is formless yet has many forms.

## \|\| 1.5.43 \|\|

*yatratadbhagavānviśvaṃ sṛjatyavatti hanti ca \|*  
*tamādidevamīśānaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. My obeisance to that Janardana, the primordial Deity, the Ruler of the universe, who creates, preserves and annihilates it.

## \|\| 1.5.44 \|\|

*pareśa paramānanda śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*trāhi māṃ karuṇāsindho manotīti namo 'stute \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О great Lord! Embodiment of Supreme bliss, who are compassionate to those who seek refuge. О Ocean of mercy! Be pleased to save me, О Lord, who are beyond the comprehension of the mind. My obeisance to you.”

## \|\| 1.5.45 \|\|

*evaṃ stavantaṃ viprendraṃ mārkaṇḍeyajagadgurum \|*  
*uvāca parayā prītyā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Lord Visnu, the preceptor of the universe, the wielder of conch, discus and mace, addressed Markancjeya with great pleasure, as the prominent Brahmana Markandeya was thus eulogising him.

## \|\| 1.5.46 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*loke bhāgavatā ye ca bhagavadbhaktamānasāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tuṣṭo na sandeho rakṣāmyetāṃśca sarvadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. *The Lord said:* Those who are the devotees of the Lord in this world, those whose minds are devotedly directed towards the glorious Lord, are called the Bhagavatas (devotees of the Supreme Lord). Undoubtedly, I am always pleased with them and I protect them.

## \|\| 1.5.47 \|\|

*ahameva dvijaśreṣṭha nityaṃ pracchannavigrahaḥ \|*  
*bhagavadbhaktarupeṇa lokākrakṣāmi sarvadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О excellent Brahmana! It is I alone who, assuming the forms of devotees, protect the world in that guise, concealing my direct personality.

## \|\| 1.5.48 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kiṃlakṣaṇā bhāgavatā jāyante kena karṃmaṇā \|*  
*etadicchāmyadaṃ śrotuṃ kautuhalaparo yataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. *Markandeya said:* Markandeya said:What are the characteristics of real Bhagavatas? By performance of which holy rites are they born? I am extremely eager to hear this.

## \|\| 1.5.49 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvācā*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ bhāgavatānāṃ śruṇuṣva munisattam \|*  
*vaktuṃ teṣāṃ prabhāvaṃ hi śakyate nābdakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. *The Lord said:* О Excellent sage, listen to the characteristics of the Bhagavatas. It is impossible to recount in details their capacity and prowess; even in a hundred million years.

## \|\| 1.5.50 \|\|

*yo hitāḥ sarvajantūnāṃ gatāsūyā aamatsarā \|*  
*viśino nispṛhāḥ śāntāste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The excellent Bhagavatas are those who are the benefactors of all living beings, are devoid of jealousy and covetousness, who are quiescent and who exercise self-control.

## \|\| 1.5.51 \|\|

*karṃmaṇā manasā vācā parapīḍāṃ na kurvate \|*  
*aparigrahaśīlāśca te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Those who do not trouble others mentally, verbally and physically and those who are disposed to renounce their possessions and property (or those who refrain from accepting gifts), are regarded as Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.52 \|\|

*satkathāśravaṇe yeṣāṃ vartate sāttvikī matiḥ \|*  
*tadbhaktaviṣṇubhaktāśca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The devotees of Visnu as well as those who are devoutly attached to listening to the stories of the pious and who are of sattvic temperament — all these are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.53 \|\|

*mātāpitrośca śuśruṣāṃ kurvanti ye narottamāḥ \|*  
*gaṅgāviśveśvaradhiyā te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Those excellent men who serve their parents regarding them (respectable) like the sacred river Ganga and god Siva, the ruler of the universe,are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.54 \|\|

*ye tu devārccanaratā ye tu tatsādhakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ dṛṣṭvānumodante te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those who are engaged in the worship of gods and those who are helpmates or assistants in that worship, and those who appreciate the worship on seeing it, — all are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.55 \|\|

*vratināṃ ca yatīnāṃ ca paricaryāparāśaaca ye \|*  
*viyuktaparanindāśca te va bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Those who are intent on serving the observers of religious vows and ascetics, and those who abstain from reviling others and entertaining contempt for them, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.56 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ hitavākyāni ye vadanti narottamāḥ \|*  
*ye guṇagrāhiṇo loke te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Those excellent men who speak words beneficial to others.and those who appreciate the merits of others in the world are indeed (regarded) as Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.57 \|\|

*ātmavatsarvabhūtāni ye paśyanti narottamāḥ \|*  
*tulyāḥ śatruṣu mitreṣu te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Those excellent persons who perceive all living beings like their own atman and those who are equally disposed towards enemies as well as friends, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.58 \|\|

*dharṃmaśāstrapravaktāraḥ satyavākyaratāśca ye \|*  
*satāṃ śuśrūṣavo ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who propound the sacred scriptures (dharma- sastras) and those who are keen on making truthful statements and who render service to pious men, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.59 \|\|

*vyākurvate purāṇāni tāni śṛṇvanti ye tathā \|*  
*tadvaktari ca bhaktā ye te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who give exposition of the Puranas, those who listen to them and those who are devotees of the narrators of the Puranas are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.60 \|\|

*ye gobrāhmaṇaśuśrūṣaāṃ kurvate satataṃ narāḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those persons who constantly render service to cows and Brahmanas, and those who are interested in the pilgrimage to holy places, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.61 \|\|

*anyeṣāmudayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ye 'bhinavandanti mānavāḥ \|*  
*harināmaparā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those men who rejoice on seeing the prosperity of others, and those who are devoted to the repetitions of the name of Hari, are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.62 \|\|

*ārāmāropaṇaratāstaḍāparirakṣakāḥ \|*  
*kāsārakūpakarttāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who are interested in laying out parks and groves, those who maintain lakes in good repairs, and those who dig wells and tanks, are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.63 \|\|

*ye vai taḍāgakarttāro devasahmāni kurvate \|*  
*goyatrīniratā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who get big lakes and tanks constructed, those who build temples and those who are engaged (in repeating in undertone) the Gayatri mantrab are excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.64 \|\|

*ye 'bhinandanti nāmāni hareḥ śrutvātiharṣitāḥ \|*  
*romāñcitaśarīrāśca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Those who feel overjoyed on hearing the names of Hari and appreciate the same and those who get their hair standing on the ends through joy, all over their body (at the mention of Hari’s name), are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.65 \|\|

*tulasīkāvanaṃ dṛṣṭvā ye namaskurvate narāḥ \|*  
*tatkāṣṭāṅkitakarṇā ye te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Those men who bow down on seeing the grove of Tulasi (basil) plants, and those who embellish their ears with Tulasi twigs are indeed excellent Bhagavatas

## \|\| 1.5.66 \|\|

*tulasīgandhamāghrāya santoṣaṃ kurvate tu ye \|*  
*tanmūlamṛttikāṃ ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Those men who are delighted on inhaling the fragrance of the Tulasi plant, or the soil at its root, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.67 \|\|

*āśramācācaraniratāstathaivātithipūjakāḥ \|*  
*ye ca vedārthavaktāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Those who are engaged in conducting their lives according to their injunctions prescribed for their particular asrama (stages in life), those who reverently receive and worship guests, and those who explain the meaning of the vedas, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.68 \|\|

*śivāpriyāḥ śivāsaktāḥ śivapādārccane ratāḥ \|*  
*tripuṇḍradhāriṇo ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Those to whom god Siva is dear, those who are devoted to Siva, and those who revel in worshipping the feet of Siva, and those who wear the *tripundrа* mark (three horizontal parallel lines of ashes) on their foreheads, are indeed prominent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.69 \|\|

*vyāharanti ca nāmāni hareḥ śambhormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*rudrākṣālaṅkṛtā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Those who repeat the names of Hari as well as of god Siva, the Supreme atman, and those who are bedecked with Rudraksa-beads are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.70 \|\|

*ye yajanti mahādevaṃ ṛtubhirbahudakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*hariṃ vā parayā bhaktyā te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Those who worship the great god Siva by means of sacrifices, with liberal sacrificial fees to the priests, or adore Hari the same way with great devotion, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.71 \|\|

*viditāni ca śāstrāṇi parārthaṃ gravadanti ye \|*  
*sarvatra guṇabhājo ye te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Those who expound the scriptures as known (to them to the best of their knowledge) to others and those who appreciate and assimilate only the good qualities everywhere, are indeed known as Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.72 \|\|

*śive ca parameśe ca viṣṇau ca paramātmani \|*  
*samabuddhyā pravarttante te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Those who regard god Siva the great ruler of the world, and Visnu the Supreme Soul, with equal attitude, are indeed spoken as Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.73 \|\|

*śivāgrikāryaniratāḥ pañcākṣarajape ratāḥ \|*  
*śivadhyānaratā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who take delight in performing sacrificial rites in honour of Siva and those who revel in the repetition of the mantra with five syllables (viz. Om Namah Sivaya) and those who are engaged in contemplating god Siva are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.74 \|\|

*pānīyadānaniratā ye 'nnadānaratāstathā \|*  
*ekādarśīvrataratā vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Those who are engaged in serving waters to the thirsty, and those who are intent on catering the gifts of cooked food (to the hungry), and who observe the Ekadasi vow (consisting of complete fast and meditation on the eleventh day of each fortnight, as prescribed in the Sastras) are indeed eminently good Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.75 \|\|

*godānaniratā ye ca kanyādānaratāśca ye \|*  
*madarthaṃ karṃmakarttāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those who take delight in gifting away cows and those who are interested in getting virgins married (at their own cost) and those who perform holy rites dedicating the fruits thereof unto me, are indeed excellent Bhagavatas.

## \|\| 1.5.76 \|\|

*ete bhāgavatā vipra kecidatra prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*mayāpi gadituṃ śakyā nābdakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О Brahmana sage, some of the categories of Bhagavatas have been mentioned by me here. It is impossible to recount them wholly even in hundreds and millions of years even by me.

## \|\| 1.5.77 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi viprendra suśīlo bhava sarvadā \|*  
*sarvabhūtāśrayo dānto metro dharṃmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Hence, О prominent Brahmana! You also be well- behaved for all time to come, offering refuge to all beings, being a friend unto them, exercising self-control and ardently interested in dharma.

## \|\| 1.5.78 \|\|

*punaryugāntaparyyantaṃ dharṃmaṃ sarvaṃ samācaran \|*  
*manmūrttidhyānanirataḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamāpsyasi \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Until the end of this yuga, practice dharma in all respects, and be engaged in the meditation of my form (*murti*). You will thus attain to the highest nirvana (liberation).

## \|\| 1.5.79 \|\|

*evaṃ mṛkaṇḍuputrasya svabhaktasya kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*dattvā varaṃ sa deveśastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. After granting the boon thus to his devotee, the son of Mrkandu, the Lord of the devas, the ocean of mercy, vanished then and there.

## \|\| 1.5.80 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyo mahābhāgo haribhaktirataḥ sadā \|*  
*cacāra paramaṃ dharmamīje ca vidhivanmakhaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Markandeya, the extremely blessed sage, was always engrossed in devotion to Hari. He practised the great dharma and duly performed sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.5.81 \|\|

*śālaprāme mahākṣetre tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*dhyānakṣapitakarmā tu paraṃ nirvāṇamātpavān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. He performed a great penance in the highly sacred place Salagrama. After wiping of all the hoarded karmas (actions and their consequences) by means of meditation, he attained the great nirvana.

## \|\| 1.5.82 \|\|

*tasmājjantuṣu sarveṣu hitakṛddharipūjakaḥ \|*  
*īpsivaṃ manasā yadyanattadānprotyasaṃśayam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Hence, a person who adores Hari, the benefactor of all creatures, undoubtedly attains whatever is mentally desired by him.

## \|\| 1.5.83 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*etatsarvaṃ nigaditaṃ tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*bhagavadbhakti māhātmyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. *Sanaka said:* О excellent Brahmana! In this way the greatness of devotion unto the Lord, about which a query was made by you, has been completely recounted by me in details. What else do you wish to hear.

## Chapter 6. The Glory of the Ganga

## \|\| 1.6.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*bhagavadbhaktimāhātmyaṃ śrutvā prītastu nāradaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha sanakaṃ jñānavijñānapāragam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Suta said:*

1\. On hearing the glorification of devotion unto the Lord, Narada was pleased, and he again asked Sanaka, the master of spiritual knowledge and philosophy.

## \|\| 1.6.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ tīrthānāṃ ca tathottamam \|*  
*parayā dayayā tathavaṃ brūhiṃ śāstrārthapāraga \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

2\. О Master of interpreting scriptural precepts! Kindly tell me the truth as to what is the excellent-most of all the places of pilgrimage and the sacred-most of all sacred spots.

## \|\| 1.6.3 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śuṇu brahmantaraṃ guhyaṃ sarvasaṃpatkaraṃ param \|*  
*duḥsvanpanāśanaṃ puṇyaṃ dharmyaṃ pāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Sanaka replied:*

3\. О Brahmana! Listen to this utmost secret which bestows all riches and which is the holy thing that destroys the effects of evil dreams, and the auspicious thing that is conducive to virtue and destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.6.4 \|\|

*śrotavyaṃ munibhirnityaṃ duṣṭagrahanivāraṇam \|*  
*sarvarogapraśamanamāyurvardhdanakāraṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This should be listened to even by sages. It for-ever wards off the influence of evil planets, subdues all ailments and causes longevity.

## \|\| 1.6.5 \|\|

*kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ tīrthānāṃ ca tathottamam \|*  
*gaṅgāyamunayoryogaṃ vadanti paramarṣayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Great sages say that the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna is the most excellent of all sacred spots, and the most sacred of all holy places.

## \|\| 1.6.6 \|\|

*sitāsitodakaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmādyāḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*munayo manavaścaiva sevante puṇyakāṅkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All divinities headed by god Brahma, all sages and all Manus, desirous of acquiring merits, resort to this sacred confluence of waters, with dark and white hues.

## \|\| 1.6.7 \|\|

*gaṅgā puṇyanadī jñeyā yato viṣṇupadodbhavā \|*  
*ravijā yamunā brahmaṃstayoryogaḥ śubhāvahaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Ganga should be known as a merit-giving holy river since it has its source from the feet of Visnu, О Brahmana, and the Yamuna is born of the Sun. Hence their confluence is bound to be very auspicious.

## \|\| 1.6.8 \|\|

*smṛtārtināśinī gaṅgā nadīnāṃ pravarā mune \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakarī sarvopadra vanāśinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Sage, the Ganga is the most distinguished of all rivers. When remembered, it destroys the distress and absolves the rememberers of all sins and removes all harms and injuries.

## \|\| 1.6.9 \|\|

*yāni kṣetrāṇi puṇyāni samudrānte mahītale \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṇyatamaṃ jñeyaṃ prayāgākhyaṃ mahāmune \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О great sage! The holy place called Prayaga should be known as the sacred-most, and the most meritorious of all the holy spots on the earth, delimited by the oceans.

## \|\| 1.6.10 \|\|

*iyāja vedhā yajñena yatra devaṃ ramāpatim \|*  
*tathaiva munayaḥ sarve cakraśca vividhānmakhān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It was here that god Brahma performed a sacrifice to propitiate the Lord of the goddess Laksmi. All sages also similarly perform different sacrifices for him.

## \|\| 1.6.11 \|\|

*sarvatīrthābhiṣekāṇi yāni puṇyāni tāni vai \|*  
*gaṅgābindvabhiṣekasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The meritorious ablutions in all other sacred waters (taken together) do not deserve to be even a fraction, one- sixteenth of the merits accrued from the ablution with a drop of water of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.6.12 \|\|

*gaṅgā gaṅgeti yo brūyādyojanānāṃ śate sthitaḥ \|*  
*so 'pi mucyeta pāpebhyaḥ kimu gaṅgābhiṣekavān \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Even a man staying a hundred yojanas away from the Ganga and uttering repeatedly the name of Ganga, is also released from all sins. What then of a person who actually performs ablution in the water of the Ganga?

## \|\| 1.6.13 \|\|

*viṣṇupādodbhavā devī viśveśvaraśiraḥ sthitā \|*  
*saṃsevyā munibhirdevaḥ kiṃ punaḥ pāmarairjanai \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The goddess (viz. the holy river Ganga) originating from Visnu’s feet and held over the head respectfully by the Lord of the Universe (viz. Siva), deserves to be resorted to by sages and gods. What need be said that it should be resorted to by hapless human beings?

## \|\| 1.6.14 \|\|

*yatsaikataṃ lalāṭe tu dhriyate manujottamaiḥ \|*  
*tatraiva netraṃ vijñeyaṃ vidhyarddhādhaḥ samujjvalat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If the sand of the Ganga is applied on the forehead by excellent persons, it should be known that a brilliant (third) eye will be developed there beneath a crescent moon (the devotee will have a similarity of form like god Siva).

## \|\| 1.6.15 \|\|

*yanmajjana mahāpuṇyaṃ durlabhaṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*sārupyadāyakaṃ viṣṇoḥ kimasmātkathyate parama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bath taken into the Ganga is highly meritorious. It is difficult to have it even to the resident of celestial regions. It bestows the Sarupya (similarity in form) with Visnu. What more can be said to be greater than this?

## \|\| 1.6.16 \|\|

*yatra strātāḥ pāpino 'pi sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*mahadvimānamāruḍhāḥ prayānti paramaṃ padam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even sinners taking their bath there in the Ganga become absolved of all their sins. Seated in a great aerial car, they proceed ahead to the highest region (Vaikuntha).

## \|\| 1.6.17 \|\|

*yatra snātā mahātmānaḥ pitṛmātṛkulāni vai \|*  
*sahasrāṇi samuddhṛtya viṣṇuloke vrajanti vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By taking their bath therein (in the Ganga), noble- souled persons redeem thousands of members on the sides of their father’s family and mother’s family, and go to the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.6.18 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu yo gaṅgāṃ smarati dvica \|*  
*puṇyakṣetreṣu sarveṣau sthitavānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О Brahmana! There is no doubt in this that he who remembers the Ganga attains the merit of performing ablutions in all the sacred waters and staying in all the holy places.

## \|\| 1.6.19 \|\|

*yatra snātaṃ naraṃ dṛṣṭvā pāpo 'pi svargabhūmibhāk \|*  
*madaṅgasparśemātreṇa devānāmādhapo bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By the sight of a person who has taken a bath in the Ganga, even a sinner attains to the celestial world. One should become over-Lord of gods merely by touching my body (i.e. the waters of the Ganga).

## \|\| 1.6.20 \|\|

*tulasīmūlasaṃbhūtā dvijapādodbhāvā tathā \|*  
*gaṅgodbhavā tu mṛllokānnayatyacyutarupatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The mud and dust from the root of the Tulasi plant, the foot of a Brahmana or from the bed of the river Ganga confers upon people assimilation type of mukti-sarupyata — (similarity of form) with Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.6.21 \|\|

*gaṅgā ca tulasī caiva haribhaktiracañcalā \|*  
*atyantadurllabhā nṝṇāṃ bhaktirddharmapravaktari \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Extremely rare indeed are the following: viz. the Ganga, the Tulasi plant, unflinching devotion to Hari and devoted attachment to the expounder of the Dharmas, (among the people).

## \|\| 1.6.22 \|\|

*saddharmavaktuḥ padasaṃbhavāṃ mṛdaṃ gaṅgodbhavāṃ caiva tathā tulasyāḥ \|*  
*mūlodbhavāṃ bhaktiyuto manuṣyo dhṛtvā śirasyeti padaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A man endowed with devotion, who applies over his head the dust from the feet of the expounder of the sacred dharmas, or the dust and mud taken from the bed of the Ganga, or from the root of the Tulasi plant, attains Visnu’s region.

## \|\| 1.6.23 \|\|

*kadā yāsyāmyahaṃ gaṅgāṃ kadā paśyāmi tāmaham \|*  
*vāñcchatyapi ca yo hyevaṃ so 'pi viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He who ardently desires and yearns, “When shall I go to the Ganga? When shall I see that river?”, goes to the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.6.24 \|\|

*gaṅgāyā mahimā brahmanvaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi \|*  
*na śakyate viṣṇunāpi kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It is not possible even for Visnu to describe adequately the greatness of the Ganga even in hundreds of years. Of what use is a garrulous talk by others, О Brahmana?

## \|\| 1.6.25 \|\|

*aho māyā jagatsarvaṃ mohayatyetadadbhutam \|*  
*yato vai narakaṃ yānti gaṅgānātri sthite 'pi hi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is exceedingly surprising that the Maya deludes the entire universe, and that people do fall into the hell, despite the existence of the name of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.6.26 \|\|

*saṃsāraduḥkha vicchedi gaṅgānāma prakīrtitam \|*  
*tathā tulasyā bhaktiśca harikīrtipravaktari \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The name of the Ganga is glorified as one that dispels the misery of the worldly existence. Similarly renowned is the plant Tulasi and devotion to the expounder of Hari’s glory.

## \|\| 1.6.27 \|\|

*sakṛdapyuccaredyastu gaṅgetyevākṣaradvayam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He who mentions, even for once, the two syllables Ganga, becomes completely liberated from all sins, and goes to the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.6.28 \|\|

*yojanatritayaṃ yastu gaṅgāyāmadhigacchati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryalokaṃ sameti hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He who goes within three yojanas (one yojana = 12.8 km) of the Ganga, becomes absolved from all sins, and attains to the region of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.6.29 \|\|

*seyaṃ gaṅgā mahāpuṇyā nadī bhaktyā niṣevitā \|*  
*meṣataulimṛgākarṣu pāvayatyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The river Ganga is highly meritorious. If resorted to, with great devotion, when the Sun is in Mesa (the sign Aries of the Zodiac) and Tula (Libra, the 7th sign of the zodiac as well as in the month of Mrgasirsha, it sanctifies the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.6.30-31 \|\|

*godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇā revā sarasvatī \|*  
*tuṅgabhadrā ca kāverī kāliṃndī bāhudā tathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vetravatī tāmraparṇī sarayūśca dvijottama \|*  
*evamādiṣu tīrtheṣu gaṅgā mukhyatamā smṛtā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. There are many holy rivers, viz. the Godavari, the Bhimarathi, the Krsna, the Reva, the Sarasvati, Tungabhadra the Kaveri, the Kalindi, the Bahuda, the Vetravati, the Tamraparni, the Sarayu, etc. Among all these rivers, the Ganga is remembered (in Smrti works) as the holiest of all, О excellent Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.6.32 \|\|

*yathā sarvagato viṣṇurjagavdyāpya pratiṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*tatheyaṃ vyāpinī gaṅgā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Just as the Omnipresent Visnu stays, by pervading the whole of the universe, similarly, the Ganga is all-pervading and destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.6.33 \|\|

*aho gaṅgā jagaddhātrī snānapānādibhirjagat \|*  
*punāti pāvanītyeṣā na kathaṃ sevyate nṛbhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Ganga is as if a nurse unto the universe. It sanctifies the world when bathed in it, or when its waters are drunk. Thus it is Pavani (purifier). What a pity, that it is not resorted to by men!

## \|\| 1.6.34 \|\|

*tīrthānāmuttamaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*vārāṇasīti vikhyātaṃ sarvadevaniṣevitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Varanasi is well-known as the holiest of all holy centres, and the sacred-most of all sacred spots. It is resorted to by all Devas.

## \|\| 1.6.35 \|\|

*te eva śravaṇe dhanye saṃvidāte bahuśrutam \|*  
*iha śrutimatāṃ puṃsāṃ kāśī yābhyāṃ śrutāsakṛt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Only those two persons are intelligent: learned and well informed, and the men of Vedic learning by whom the word Kasi is frequently heard.

## \|\| 1.6.36 \|\|

*ye yaṃ smaranti saṃsthānamavimuktaṃ dvijottamam \|*  
*nirdhūtasarvapāpāste śivalokaṃ vrajanti vai \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О excellent Brahmana! Those who remember the sacred place Avimukta (i.e. Kail) shake off all their sins, and proceed to the region of god Siva.

## \|\| 1.6.37 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ śatastho 'pi avimuktaṃ smaredyadi \|*  
*bahupātakapūrṇo 'pi padaṃ gacchatyanāmayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A man, even if standing at a distance of hundred yojanas from it, remembers the holy place avimukta, attains to the region of no ailment i.e. Moksa, although he may be full of many sins.

## \|\| 1.6.38 \|\|

*prāṇaprayāṇasamaye yo 'vimuktaṃ smaredvūja \|*  
*so 'pi pāpavinirmuktaḥ śaivaṃ padamavānpuyāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О Brahmana! If at the time of breathing his last, a person remembers avimukta (at the last moment), he is released from sins and goes to the region of god Siva.

## \|\| 1.6.39 \|\|

*kāśīsmaraṇajaṃ puṇyaṃ bhuktvā svarge tadantataḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāmekarāḍū bhūtvā kāśīṃ prāpya ca muktibhāk \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The person enjoys the merits resulting from remembering Kasi, in the heaven. At the end of that period, he is born as the sole emperor of the earth, and then after going to Kasi, he attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.6.40 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena vārāṇasyā guṇānprati \|*  
*nāmāpi gṛhṇātāṃ kāśyāścaturvargo na dūrataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. What need there is of a long exposition regarding the merits of Varanasi? The fulfilment of the four-fold aims of human life (Purusarthas) is not far from (hose who at least take the name of Kasi.

## \|\| 1.6.41 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayoryogo 'dhikaḥ kāśyā api dvijā \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa narā yānti parāṃ gatim \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The confluence of the Ganga and the Yamuna is superior even to Kasi, О Brahmana. For, merely by having a look at it, men reach the highest goal (Liberation).

## \|\| 1.6.42 \|\|

*makarasthe ravau gaṅgā yatra kutrāvagāhitā \|*  
*punāti strānapānādyairnayantīndrapuraṃ jagat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If ablution is performed anywhere in the Ganga when the Sun is in the Makara (capricorn) sign of the zodiac, it sanctifies the universe by a bath in it or by drinking its water. it takes the whole universe to the capital of heaven (Indra’s city).

## \|\| 1.6.43 \|\|

*yo gaṅgāṃ bhajate nityaṃ śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*liṅgarupīṃ kathaṃ tasyā mahimā parikīrtyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Even god Sankara, the benefactor of the world who assumes the form of a linga,u is always devoted to the Ganga. How can its greatness be adequately described?

## \|\| 1.6.44 \|\|

*harirupadharaṃ liṅgaṃ liṅgarupadharo hariḥ \|*  
*īṣadapyantaraṃ nāsti bhedakṛccānayoḥ kudhīḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Linga assumes the form of Hari. Lord Hari assumes the form of the Linga. There is not even the slightest difference between these two. One who differentiates between these, is a person of evil intellect.

## \|\| 1.6.45 \|\|

*anādinidhane deve hariśaṅkarasaṃjñite \|*  
*ajñānasāgare magnā bhedaṃ kurvanti pāpinaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Only sinners, immersed in the ocean of ignorance, seek to make any difference between Hari and Sankara, the glorious Lords without beginning or end.

## \|\| 1.6.46 \|\|

*yo devo jagatāmaśaḥ kāraṇānāṃ ca kāraṇam \|*  
*yugānte nigadantyetadrudrarupadharo hariḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. They (i.e. learned men) say that Lord Hari who is the ruler of all the worlds and the ultimate cause (of all the causes), assumes the form of Rudra at the end of the Yugas.

## \|\| 1.6.47 \|\|

*rudro vai viṣṇurupeṇa pālayatyakhilañjagat \|*  
*brahmarupeṇa sṛjati prānteḥ hayetatrayaṃ haraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. It is Lord Rudra who protects the entire universe in the form of Visnu, and creates it assuming the form of Brahma. In the final analysis, god Siva alone is all these three.

## \|\| 1.6.48 \|\|

*hariśaṅkarayormadhye brahmaṇaścāpi yo naraḥ \|*  
*bhedaṃ karoti so 'bhyeti narakaṃ bhṛśadāruṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The man who differentiates between Lord Hari, god Siva and god Brahma, goes to the exceedingly terrible hell.

## \|\| 1.6.49 \|\|

*haraṃ hariṃ vidhātāraṃ yaḥ paśyatyekarupiṇam \|*  
*sa yāti paraṃmānandaṃ śāstrāṇāmeṣa viṣvayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This is the conclusion of all scriptures that he who sees Нага, Hari and Brahma all constituting the same deity attains the supreme bliss.

## \|\| 1.6.50 \|\|

*yo 'sāvanādiḥ sarvajño jagatāmādikṛdvibhuḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ saṃnihitastatra liṅgarupī janārdanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. God Visnu (Janardana) who is omniscient and beginningless, and who is the omnipresent Lord and Creator of the worlds, is ever present there (at Kasi) in the form of a Linga.

## \|\| 1.6.51 \|\|

*kāśīviśveśvaraṃ liṅgajyotirliṅgaṃ taducyate \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ jyotirāproti manujottamaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Linga of Lord Kasi-Visvesvara is called Jyotir- linga. On seeing it, the excellent one of men merges in the supreme light of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.6.52 \|\|

*kāśīpradakṣiṇā yena kṛtā trailokyapāvanī \|*  
*satpadvīpāsābdhiśailā bhūḥ parikramitāmunā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If Kasi, the sanctifier of the three worlds, is circumambulated, it is as good as the circle-ambulation of the whole earth consisting of seven continents, oceans and mountains.

## \|\| 1.6.53 \|\|

*dhātumṛddārapāṣāṇalekhyādyā mūrtayo 'malāḥ \|*  
*śivasya vācyutasyāpi tāsu saṃnihito hariḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There are spotless (brilliant) murtis (images) of Siva or Acyuta made of metals, clay, wood or stone or their representations in paintings, etc. But Lord Hari is present in them all.

## \|\| 1.6.54 \|\|

*tulasīkānanaṃ yatra yatra pahmavanaṃ dvijā \|*  
*purāṇapaṭhanaṃ yatra yatra saṃnihito hariḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. God Hari is present wherever there is a grove of Tulasi plants oi where there is a cluster of lotuses, or where the puranas are being read, О Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.6.55 \|\|

*purāṇasaṃhitāvaktā harirityabhidhīyate \|*  
*tadbhaktiṃ kurvatāṃ nṝṇāṃ gaṅgāstrānāṃ dine dine \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The propounder of the text of the puranas is also called Hari. Men who are devoted to them have (to their credit the merit of performing) bath in the Ganga every day.

## \|\| 1.6.56 \|\|

*purāṇaśravaṇe bhaktirgaṅgāstrānasamā dvija \|*  
*tadvaktari ca yā bhaktiḥ sā prayāgopamā smṛtā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It is stated in Smrtis that pious inclination to listen to the pwrdnas is on a par with the ablutions in the Ganga, and devotion unto the propounder is comparable to bath into Prayaga.

## \|\| 1.6.57 \|\|

*purāṇadharmakathanairyaḥ samuddharate jagat \|*  
*saṃsārasāgare magnaṃ sa hariḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He who, by recounting the purana dharmas, redeems and uplifts the entire world that is sunk and immersed in the ocean of worldly existence, is glorified as Hari himself.

## \|\| 1.6.58 \|\|

*nāsti gaṅgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ \|*  
*nāsti viṣṇusamaṃ daivaṃ nāsti tattvaṃ guroḥ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. There is no other sacred water like that of the Ganga. There is no greater teacher than (honour, self- confidence. There is no other deity like Visnu, and there is no other primary principle (or Brahman) other than the spiritual preceptor.

## \|\| 1.6.59 \|\|

*varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhastārakāṇāṃ yathā śaśī \|*  
*yathā payodhiḥ sindhūnāṃ tathā gaṅgā parā smṛtā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Just as the Brahmana is the most excellent of all castes, or the moon is the best of all constellations, and just as the ocean is the best of all rivers, so the Ganga is remembered as the greatest river.

## \|\| 1.6.60 \|\|

*nāsti śāntisamo bandhurnāsti satyātparaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*nāsti mokṣātparo lābho nāsti gaṅgāsamā nadī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. There is no kinsman on a par with calmness; there is no greater penance than truthfulness: no other acquisition is greater than liberation from samsaraf and there is no other river on a par with the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.6.61 \|\|

*gaṅgāyāḥ paramaṃ nāma pāpāraṇyadavānalaḥ \|*  
*bhavavyādhiharā gaṅgā tasmātsevyā prayantataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The great name of the Ganga is like a forest conflagration unto the jungle of sins. The Ganga is the healer of the sickness called Samsara (worldly existence); hence, it should be resorted to with assiduity.

## \|\| 1.6.62 \|\|

*gāyatrī jāhnavī cobhe sarvapāpahare smṛte \|*  
*etayorbhaktihīno yastaṃ vidyātpatitaṃ dvija \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The Gayatri mantra and the river Ganga both of these are remembered to be the destroyers of all sins, О Brahmana. A person who is lacking in devotion to these two, should be known as a fallen fellow, О Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.6.63 \|\|

*gāyatrī chandasāṃ mātā mātā lokasya jāhnavī \|*  
*ubhe te sarvapāpānāṃ nāśakāraṇatāṃ gate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The Gayatri is the mother of all Vedic metres, the Ganga is the mother of the world. Both of them are the cause of destruction of all sins.

## \|\| 1.6.64 \|\|

*yasya prasannā gāyatrī tasya gaṅgā prasīdati \|*  
*viṣṇuśaktiyute te dve samakāmaprasiddhede \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If any one is favoured by Gayatri, the Ganga too is pleased with him. Both of these possess the potency of Visnu and both equally bestow desired objects as well as renown.

## \|\| 1.6.65 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmarupāṇāṃ phalarupe nirañjane \|*  
*sarvalokānugrahārthaṃ pravartete mahottame \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Both of them are quite pure. They are, as it were, the fructification of the Purusarthas (desired objectives of human life, viz. righteousness, wealth, love and liberation from samsara). These great and excellent ones function for conferring blessings on the world.

## \|\| 1.6.66 \|\|

*atīva durllabhā nṝṇāṃ gāyatrī jāhnavī tathā \|*  
*tathaiva tulasībhaktirharibhaktiśca sāttvikī \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Rare indeed and very difficult to attain are the Gayatri, the Ganga, devotion to the Tulasi plant and devotion of Sattvic nature to Hari.

## \|\| 1.6.67 \|\|

*aho gaṅgā mahābhāgā smṛtā pāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*harilokapradā dṛṣṭā pītā sārupyadāyinī \|*  
*yatra strātā narā yānti viṣṇoḥ padamanuttamam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. О! How blessed is the Ganga! On being remembered, it destroys sins, on being seen it bestows the region of Hari. When its water is drunk, it grants sarupya (similarity of form like Visnu). And men who perform ablutions therein, attain the excellent region of Vishu.

## \|\| 1.6.68 \|\|

*nārāyaṇo jagaddhātā vāsudevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgāstrānaparāṇāṃ tu vāñchitārthaphalapradaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. God Narayana, the Creater of the Universe, Vasu- deva, the eternal deity, is the bestower of the fruits of all desired objects, to persons who are devoted to regular ablutions in the waters of Ganga.

## \|\| 1.6.69 \|\|

*gaṅgājalakaraṇenāpi yaḥ sikto manujottamaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The excellent person who is sprinkled with at least a drop of water of Ganga, is liberated from all sins and he attains the highest region, Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 1.6.70 \|\|

*yadvindusevanādeva sagarānvayasambhavaḥ \|*  
*visṛjyarākṣasaṃ bhāvaṃ saṃprātpaḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. It is only by taking in just a drop of its water that a descendant in the family of King Sagara, eschewed the state of Raksasa and attained to the supreme region.

## Chapter 7. The Glory of the Ganga (contd.)

## \|\| 1.7.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*ko 'sau rākṣasabhāvāddhi mocitaḥ sagarāvanvaye \|*  
*sagaraḥ ko muniśreṣṭha tanmramākhyātumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada enquired:*

1\. О excellent sage! It behoves you to relate to me who this Sagara was, and which descendant of the family of Sagara, was freed from the state of being a Raksasa (demon).

## \|\| 1.7.2 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śruṇuṣva muniśārdūla gaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*yajjalasparśamātreṇa pāvitaṃ sāgaraṃ kulam \|*  
*gataṃ viṣṇupadaṃ vipra sarvalokottamottamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. *Sanaka narrated:* О prominent sage! Listen to the pre-eminent greatness of the Ganga, by mere contact with whose sacred waters, the whole dynasty of Sagara was sanctified, and attained the region of Visnu, which is the excellent-most of all excellences in the world, О Brahmana!

## \|\| 1.7.3 \|\|

*āsīdravikule bāhurnāma vṛkātmajaḥ \|*  
*bubhuje pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ dharmato dharmatatparaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the Solar race, there was born a king named Bahu, the son of king Vrka. Exclusively devoted to righteousness in duty, he enjoyed and ruled the whole earth righteously.

## \|\| 1.7.4 \|\|

*brahmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścānye ca jantavaḥ \|*  
*sthāpitāḥ svasvadharmeṣu tena bāhurviśāṃpatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Brahmanas, the Ksatriyas, the Vaisyas, the Sudras and other living beings were established by him in their respective dharmas (duties). King Bahu was (in the real sense of the term) the Lord of the subjects. (visampati).

## \|\| 1.7.5 \|\|

*aśvamedhairiyājāsau satpadvīpeṣu satpabhiḥ \|*  
*atarppayadbhūmidevān gobhūsvarṇāśukādibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In each of the seven continents (of the earth), he performed seven horse-sacrifices. He propitiated (to their heart’s content) the Brahmanas by means of cows, lands, gold, garments and such other gifts.

## \|\| 1.7.6 \|\|

*aśāsannītiśāstreṇa yatheṣṭaṃ paripanthinaḥ \|*  
*mene kṛtārthamātmānamanyātapanivāraṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. As per advice given in the treatises on politics, he subdued and controlled the enemies, as he pleased. He considered himself as having achieved his ambition in life by removing the troubles and miseries of others.

## \|\| 1.7.7 \|\|

*candanāni manojñāni baliṃ yatsarvadā janāḥ \|*  
*bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇaurdivyaistadrāṣṭre sukhino mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The people in his land always offered exquisite sandle- wood as gifts. All the people in his kingdom were bedecked in very costly (divine) ornaments, and they were happy, О Sage.

## \|\| 1.7.8-9 \|\|

*akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī phalapuṣpasamanvitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vavarṣa bhūmau devendraḥ kāle kāle muniśvaraḥ \|*  
*ādharmaniratāpāye prajā dharmeṇa rakṣitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The earth yielded rich food-grains without being ploughed. It was full of fruits and flowers. The king of the devas showered rain on the earth at the proper time, О excellent sage. In time of calamities, due to indulgence in unrighteousness, the subjects were protected as per dharma (duties of kingship).

## \|\| 1.7.10 \|\|

*ekadā tasya bhūpasya sarvasaṃpadvināśakṛt \|*  
*ahṝṅkāro mahāñjajñe sāsūyo lopahetukaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Once, great arrogance which is destructive of all riches and the cause of transgressions and failures, and which was accompanied by jealousy, took possession of that king.

## \|\| 1.7.11 \|\|

*ahaṃ rājā samastānāṃ lokānāṃ pālako balī \|*  
*karttā mahākratūnāṃ ca mattaḥ pūjyo 'sti ko 'paraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*
