11\. “I am the monarch, the powerful protector of all the worlds. I am the performer of great sacrifices. Who else is more worthy of being worshipped than I?

## \|\| 1.7.12 \|\|

*ahaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ śrīmāñjitāḥ sarve mayarayaḥ \|*  
*vedavedāṅgatattvajño nītiśāstra viśāradaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I am affluent and clever. All enemies have been subdued by me. I am the knower of the principles (the real knowledge) of the Vedas, and of the ancillaries of Vedas (Vedangas), and am expert in the science and art of politics.

## \|\| 1.7.13 \|\|

*ajeyo 'vyāhataiśvaryo mattaḥ ko 'nyo 'dhiko bhuvi \|*  
*ahṝṅkāraparasyaivaṃ jātāsūyā pareṣvapi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I am invincible. Unchallengeable and unthwarted is my Lordship (Supremacy). Who else is superior to me in this world?” As arrogance increased in him, he became also jealous of others.

## \|\| 1.7.14 \|\|

*asūyāto 'bhavatkāmastasya rājño munīśvara \|*  
*eṣu sthiteṣu tu naro vināṣaṃ yatyasaṃśayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О excellent sage! As sequel to jealousy, passion too crept into that king. When all these possess a man, he undoubtedly goes to ruin.

## \|\| 1.7.15 \|\|

*yauvanaṃ dhanasaṃpattiḥ prabhutvamavivekitā \|*  
*ekaikamapyanarthāya kimu yatra catuṣṭayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Youth, affluence, power and authority as well as indiscretion — even one of these is sure to bring about mishaps and ruin. What then, when all these four operate collectively?

## \|\| 1.7.16 \|\|

*tasyāsūyā nu mahatī jātā lokavirodhinī \|*  
*svadehanāśinī vigra sarvasaṃpadvināśinī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmana! The jealousy that held sway over him was very great. It was antagonistic to all his worldly interests, was destructive of all his riches and even of his physical body.

## \|\| 1.7.17 \|\|

*asūyāviṣṭamanasi yadi saṃpatpravarttate \|*  
*tuṣāgniṃ vāyusaṃyogamiva jānīhi suvrata \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If wealth begins to over-influence a person whose mind is affected by envy, know that it is like the fire in combination with gusts of wind which consume husk.

## \|\| 1.7.18 \|\|

*asūyopetamanasāṃ dambhācāravatāṃ tathā \|*  
*paruṣoktiratānāṃ ca sukhaṃ neha paratra ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Neither here nor hereafter can there be any happiness to persons whose minds are affected by jealousy, whose conduct of life is full of hypocrisy, and who always use harsh words.

## \|\| 1.7.19 \|\|

*asūyāviṣṭacittā nāṃ sadā niṣṭhurabhāṣiṇām \|*  
*priyāvā tanayā vāpi bāndhavā apyarātayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. To men of harsh speech whose minds are possessed of jealousy, even the beloved wife, the sons or other kith and kin are enemies.

## \|\| 1.7.20 \|\|

*manobhilāṣaṃ kurute yaḥ samīkṣya parastriyam \|*  
*sa svasaṃpadvināśāya kuṭhāro nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If anyone harbours in his mind any lustful desire on seeing another man’s wife that is nothing but an axe that brings about the destruction of all his riches. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.7.21 \|\|

*yaḥ svaśreyovināśāya kuryādyatnaṃ naro mune \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ śreyasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa kuryānmatsūraṃ kudhīḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О sage! If a man wishes to attempt to bring about the destruction of his own well-being that man of crooked intellect harbours malicious thoughts on seeing the good of others.

## \|\| 1.7.22 \|\|

*mitrāpatyagṛhakṣetra dhanadhānyapaṣuṣvapi \|*  
*hānimicchannaraḥ kuryādasūyāṃ satataṃ dvija \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Brahmana! If a man feels inclined to incur the loss of friendship, progeny, house, landed property, riches, food grains, etc., and cattle and other animals, he may very well indulge in jealousy all along.

## \|\| 1.7.23 \|\|

*atha tasyāvinītasya hyasūyāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*haihayāstālalajaṅghāśca balino 'rātayo 'bhavan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. As his mind was possessed of jealousy and he became more impudent, the powerful kings of Haihaya and Tala-jangha families became his enemies.

## \|\| 1.7.24 \|\|

*yasyānukūlo lakṣmīśaḥ saubhāgyaṃ tasya varddhate \|*  
*sa eva vimukho yasya saubhāgyaṃ tasya hīyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If the Lord of Laksmi is favourable to any one, his fortune flourishes, but if he is adverse to him, his fortune dwindles down.

## \|\| 1.7.25 \|\|

*tāvatputrāśca pautrāśca dhanadhānyagṛhādayaḥ \|*  
*yāvadīkṣeta lakṣmīśaḥ kṛpāpāṅgena nārada \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Narada! Sons, grand-sons, riches, food-grains, homestead, etc. favour one, only as long as the Lord of Laksmi casts favourable side-glances mercifully.

## \|\| 1.7.26 \|\|

*api mūrkhāndhabadhirajaḍāḥ śūrā vivekinaḥ \|*  
*ślādhyā bhavanti viprendra prekṣitā mādhavena ye \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О prominent Brahmana! Even the foolish, blind, deaf and stupid persons become heroic, praise-worthy and discriminating, if they are glanced at favourably by Madhava, the Consort of Laksmi.

## \|\| 1.7.27 \|\|

*saubhāgyaṃ tasya hīyeta yasyāsūyādilāñchanam \|*  
*jāyate nātra saṃdeho jantudveṣo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There is no doubt that the good fortune of a person who is contaminated with jealousy, etc., dwindles down and that particularly hatred towards all living beings is generated in his mind.

## \|\| 1.7.28 \|\|

*satataṃ yasya kasyāpi yo dveṣaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*tasya sarvāṇi naśyanti śreyāṃsi munisatam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If a man hates continuously some one or the other, all his blessings and religious merits perish, О excellent sage.

## \|\| 1.7.29 \|\|

*asūyā varddhate yasya tasya viṣṇuḥ parāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ mahī saṃpanadviśyati tato dhruvam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Visnu becomes averse to him in whom jealousy goes on increasing. After this, that person’s wealth, stock of grains, lands and affluence are definitely destroyed.

## \|\| 1.7.30 \|\|

*vivekaṃ hantyahṝṅkārastvavivekāttu jīvinām \|*  
*āpadaḥ saṃbhavantyevetyahṝṅkāraṃ tyajettataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Egotism and arrogance destroy the power of discrimination, as a consequence of which, adversities befall living beings. One should, therefore, eschew egotism.

## \|\| 1.7.31-32 \|\|

*ahaṃ kāro bhavedyasya tasya nāśo 'tivegataḥ \|*  
*asūyāvisṛṣṭamanasastasya rājñaḥ paraiḥ saha \|\| 31 \|\|*

*āyodhanamabhīddhoraṃ māsamekaṃ nirantaram \|*  
*haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca ripubhiḥ sa parājitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. He who becomes puffed with pride precipitates his ruin erelong. The king “whose mind was possessed with jealousy put up a continuous terrible fight for the period of a month with his enemies, the Haihayas and the Talajanghas in which he was ultimately defeated. He then repaired to the forest.

## \|\| 1.7.33 \|\|

*sa tu bāhustato duḥkhī antarvatnyā svabhāryayā \|*  
*avāpa paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā mahatsaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Although Bahu was dejected, he felt great pleasure on seeing a great lake. He was then accompanied by his pregnant wife.

## \|\| 1.7.34 \|\|

*asūyopetamanasastasya bhāvaṃ nirīkṣya ca \|*  
*sarogatavihaṅgāste līnāścitramidaṃ mahat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It was a great miracle that perceiving the nature or temperament of the king whose mind was possessed of jealousy, all the birds residing in the lake hid themselves.

## \|\| 1.7.35 \|\|

*aho kaṣṭamaho rupaṃ ghoramatra samāgatam \|*  
*viśantastvarayā vāsamityūcuste vihaṅgamāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. While the birds were hastily entering their respective abodes, they exclaimed: “Alas! How painful it is! What a terrible form has come down here!”

## \|\| 1.7.36 \|\|

*so 'vagāhyasarobhūpaḥ patnībhyāṃ sahito mutā \|*  
*pītvā jalaṃ ca sukhadaṃ vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Accompanied by both of his wives, the king joyously entered the lake, drank its water that gave him abundant pleasure. He, thereafter, went and rested under a tree.

## \|\| 1.7.37 \|\|

*tasminbāhau vanaṃ yāte tenaiva parirakṣitāḥ \|*  
*durguṇānvigaṇayyāsyadhigdhigityabruvanprajāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. While the king Bahu was proceeding to the forest, the subjects, though erstwhile protected by him, exclaimed “Fie! Fie”, after considering Bahu’s evil propensities.

## \|\| 1.7.38 \|\|

*yo vā ko vā guṇī martyaḥ sarvaśvādhyatarodvijaḥ \|*  
*sarvasaṃpatsamāyukto 'pyaguṇīnindito janaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О Brahmana! A man endowed with good qualities, whoever he may be, is worthy of being praised by every one. A person devoid of good qualities, is censured by men, though he may be possessed of all kind of riches.

## \|\| 1.7.39 \|\|

*apakīrtisamo mṛtyurlokeṣvanyo na vidyate \|*  
*yadā bāhurvanaṃ yātastadā tadrāgagā janāḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭiṃ paramāṃ yātā davathau vigate yathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There is nothing comparable to ignominy in this world which is as painful as death. When Bahu went to the forest, the people of his kingdom felt much relief and pleasure, as though an inflammation of the eye had subsided.

## \|\| 1.7.40 \|\|

*nindāto bahuśo bāhurmṛtavatkānanesthitaḥ \|*  
*nihatya karma ca yaśo loke dvajavarottama \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О excellent Brahmana! Censured on many occasions, Bahu remained in the forest like a dead man, with his fame in the world destroyed, and activities cut off.

## \|\| 1.7.41 \|\|

*nāstyakīrtisamo mṛtyurmāsti krodhasamo ripuḥ \|*  
*nāsti nindāsamaṃ pāpaṃ nāsti mohasamāsavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “There is no death like ignominy (ill-reputation); there is no enemy like anger; there is no sin like slandering and there is no intoxicating liquor like delusion.

## \|\| 1.7.42 \|\|

*nāstyasūyāsamā kīrtirnāsti kāmasamo 'nalaḥ \|*  
*nāsti rāgasamaḥ pāśo nāsti saṅgasamaṃ viṣam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There is no ill fame like jealousy; there is no fire like passions; there is no snare like attachment; there is no poison like intimate contact (sexual intercourse)."

## \|\| 1.7.43 \|\|

*evaṃ vilapyabahudhā bāhuratyantaduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*jīrṇāṅgomanasastāpād vṛddhabhāvādabhūdasau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Being extremely dejected, Bahu lamented in this and many other ways. Due to mental agony as well as to old age, the limbs of his body became wasted and feeble.

## \|\| 1.7.44 \|\|

*gate bahutithe kāle aurvāśramasamīpataḥ \|*  
*sa bāhurvyādhinā graste mamāra munisattama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After the passage of a great deal of time, the king Bahu was overwhelmed with sickness, and he died in the vicinity of the hermitage of sage Aurva, О excellent sage!

## \|\| 1.7.45 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā ca duḥkhārtā kaniṣṭhā garbhiṇī tadā \|*  
*ciraṃ vilapya bahudhā sahagantuṃ mano dadhe \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. His younger wife became very miserable. After lamenting for a long time, she thought of going with him (to the other world, by immolating herself in the fire), even though she was pregnant.

## \|\| 1.7.46 \|\|

*samānīya casaidhāṃsi citāṃ kṛtvātiduḥkhitā \|*  
*samāropya tanpūruḍhaṃ svayaṃ samupacakrame \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Deeply grieving she brought the fuel herself and prepared the funeral pyre. After placing (Bahu’s body) on the pyre, she began to ascend the pyre herself.

## \|\| 1.7.47 \|\|

*etasminnantare dhīmanaurvastejonidhirmuniḥ \|*  
*etadvijñātavānsarvaṃ parameṇa samādhinā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In the meantime, the intelligent sage Aurva, the receptacle of spiritual lustre, understood all this by means of his deep trance.

## \|\| 1.7.48 \|\|

*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ varttamānaṃ trikālajñāmunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*gatāsūyā mahātnānaḥ paśyantijñāna cakṣuṣā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. With the vision of their perfect knowledge, the noble- souled prominent sages who are cognizant of whatever exists in the three units of time — the past, the future and the present — and who are devoid of jealousy, see everything.

## \|\| 1.7.49 \|\|

*tapobhistejasāṃ rāśiraurvapuṇyasamo muniḥ \|*  
*saṃprātpastatra sādhvī ca yatra bāhupriyā sthitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The most meritorious sage, Aurva, the store-house or treasure of brilliance accrued through penance, reached the place where the beloved wife of Bahu was standing.

## \|\| 1.7.50 \|\|

*citāmāroḍhumudyuktāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munisattamaḥ \|*  
*provāca dharmamūlāni vākyāni munisattamaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On seeing that she was about to ascend the funeral pyre, that leading sage spoke to her these words, based on dharma, О excellent sage!

## \|\| 1.7.51 \|\|

*aurva uvāca*  
*rājavaryapriye sādhvi mā kuruṣvātisāhasam \|*  
*tavodare cakravartī śanuhantā hi tiṣṭati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. *Aurva said:* “O chaste lady! О beloved wife of the excellent king! Please do not proceed ahead with this risky venture. An emperor, verily the slayer of enemies, stays within your womb.

## \|\| 1.7.52 \|\|

*rajasvalā rājasutenārohati cintāśubho \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. О blessed princess! The following (ladies) do not ascend a funeral pyre, viz. those with infant children (depending on them), pregnant women, those whose monthly course has not yet started, and women in the menses.

## \|\| 1.7.53 \|\|

*brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ proktā niṣkṛtiruttamaiḥ \|*  
*dāmbhinonindakasyāpi bhrūṇaghrasya na niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Means for expiation for Brahmana-slaughter and other sins have been mentioned by excellent men, but there is no expiation for an imposter, a person who slanders, and killing a child in embryonic stage.

## \|\| 1.7.54 \|\|

*nāstikasya kṛtanghasya dharmopekṣākarasya ca \|*  
*viśvāsaghātakasyāpi niṣkṛtirnāsti suvrate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О observer of good vows! There is no atonement for an atheist, an ungrateful fellow, a person indifferent to dharma and a treacherous fellow.

## \|\| 1.7.55 \|\|

*tasmādetanmahatpāpaṃ karttuṃ nārhasi śobhane \|*  
*yadetadduḥkhamutpannaṃ tatsarvaṃ śāntimeṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Hence, О splendid lady! It does not behove you to commit this great sin. The misery that has befallen you shall subside completely.”

## \|\| 1.7.56 \|\|

*ityuktā muninā sādhvī viśvasya tadanugraham \|*  
*vilalāpātiduḥkhārtā samuhyadhavapatkujau \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thus advised by the sage, the chaste lady believed in his blessings. Taking up the lotus-like feet of her husband (in her hands), she lamented very much and was extremely distressed.

## \|\| 1.7.57 \|\|

*aurvo 'pi tāṃ punaḥ prāha sarvaśāstrārthakoviduḥ \|*  
*mārodīrāja nanaye śriyamagrye gamiṣyasi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The sage Aurva who was an adept in the interpretation of scriptural texts, consoled her again, “O Princess do not cry. Later on, you will attain prosperity in due course.

## \|\| 1.7.58 \|\|

*mā bhuṃ cāstramāhābhāgepreto dāhyo 'dya sajjanaiḥ \|*  
*tasmācchokaṃ parityajya kuru kālocitā kri pām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. О extremely blessed lady! Please do not shed tears. The dead body should now be cremated by good men. Hence, controlling your grief, perform the rites befitting the occasion.

## \|\| 1.7.59 \|\|

*paṇḍite vāpimūrkhe vā daridre vāśriyānvite \|*  
*durvṛtte vā suvṛtte vā mṛtyoḥsarvatratulyatā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The god of Death is impartially alike to all, be he a learned man or a fool, an indigent fellow or a person in affluent circumstances, a wicked person or a man of good behaviour.

## \|\| 1.7.60-61 \|\|

*nagare vā tathāmanye dainyamatrātiricyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

*yadyatpurātanaṃ karmatattaderviha yujyate \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ daivamevātra manye sopādhikā janāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. I consider it so in a city(?). Indigence is surpassed in this respect here. Whatever is the past, ancient act (*karma*), it is directed in this world. I consider that the fate alone is the cause of this, and men are simply conditioned thereby.

## \|\| 1.7.62 \|\|

*garbhe vā bālyabhāve vā yauvane vāpi vārddhake \|*  
*mṛtyorvaśaṃ prayātavyaṃ jantubhiḥ kamalānane \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. О lady of lotus face! All creatures have to succumb to the influence of the god of Death, whether one is even in the womb or in infancy or in youth or in old age.

## \|\| 1.7.63 \|\|

*hanti pāti ca govindro jantūnkarmavaśe sthitān \|*  
*pravādaṃ ropayantyajñā hetumātreṣu jantuṣu \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. It is Lord Govinda who destroys or protects creatures that are conditioned by and are at the mercy of their own actions. Ignorant persons super-impose a false belief on the creatures that are but casual causes.

## \|\| 1.7.64 \|\|

*tasmāduḥkhaṃ parityajya sukhitī bhava suvrate \|*  
*kuru patyuśca karmāṇi vivekena sthirā bhava \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Hence, О lady of pious observances, shed off your sorrow, and be happy. Perform the funeral rites of your husband. Try to be steady (in mind) through sensible discrimination and thought.

## \|\| 1.7.65 \|\|

*etaccharīraṃ duḥkhānāṃ vyādhīnāmathutairgṛtam \|*  
*sukhābhāsaṃ bahukleśaṃ karmapāśena yantritam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. This physical body (of ours) is surrounded by ten thousands of miseries and ailments. It is subject to much pain and torture. It has only a semblance of happiness, but is full of sufferings. It is fettered by the bonds of actions.”

## \|\| 1.7.66 \|\|

*ityāścāsya mahābuddhistayā kāryāṇyakārayat \|*  
*tyaktaśokā ca sā tanvī natā prāha munīśvaram \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Consoling her thus, the highly intelligent sage made her perform all the funeral rites. That gentle lady controlled her grief, bowed down to that prominent sage and said to him.

## \|\| 1.7.67 \|\|

*kimatra citraṃ yatsantaḥ parārthaphalakāṅkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*nahi drumāśca bhogārthaṃ phalanti jagatītale \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “What is surprising there that good men always wish for the benefits and well-being of others, as it is not for their own enjoyment that trees bear fruits on the earth.

## \|\| 1.7.68 \|\|

*yo 'nyaduḥkhāni vijñāya sādhuvākyaiḥ prabodhayet \|*  
*sa eva viṣṇuḥsattvastho yataḥ parihite sthitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He who, realising the miseries of others, enlightens them through good advice, is the veritable Lord Visnu, the main-stay of sattva guna, for he is ready to render service to others.

## \|\| 1.7.69 \|\|

*anya duḥkhena yo duḥkhī yo 'nyaharṣeṇa harṣitaḥ \|*  
*sa eva jagatāmīśo nararupadharo hariḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He who feels miserable at the miseries and sorrows of others, and who feels delighted at the happinessof other people, is himself Hari, the Lord of the worlds, who has assumed a human form.

## \|\| 1.7.70 \|\|

*sadbhiḥ śrutāni śāstrāṇi paraduḥkhavimuktaye \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ duḥkhanāśāya iti santo vadanti hi \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Scriptures have been heard and learnt by good men only to relieve others of their misery. It is for the destruction of the misery of every individual: So say the pious men.

## \|\| 1.7.71 \|\|

*yatra santaḥ pravarttate tatra duḥkhaṃ na bādhate \|*  
*vartate yatra mārtāṇḍaḥ kathaṃ tatratamo bhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Misery cannot affect anyone at a place where good men function. How can there be darkness when the sun shines?”

## \|\| 1.7.72 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vādinī sā tu svapatyuścāparāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*cakāra tatsarastīre muniproktavidhānataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Speaking these and similar words, that lady performed all the other (funeral) rites of her husband, on the bank of that lake, in accordance with the instructions of that sage.

## \|\| 1.7.73 \|\|

*sthite tatra munau rājā devarāḍiva saṃjvalan \|*  
*citāmadhyādviniṣkramya vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*prapede paramaṃ dhāma natvā caurvaṃ munīśvaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. As the sage was standing by, the king appearing brilliant like the king of gods, rose out of the funeral pyre and ascended an excellent aerial car. After bowing down to Aurva, the leader of sages, he attained to the Supreme Abode.

## \|\| 1.7.74 \|\|

*mahāpātakayuktā vā yuktā vā copapātakaiḥ \|*  
*paraṃ padaṃ prayāntyeva mahadbhiravalokitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Persons whether defiled by great sins11 or by subsidiary typeslla of sins, do attain to the Supreme Region when graciously glanced at by great men.

## \|\| 1.7.75 \|\|

*kalevaraṃ vā tadbhasma taddhūmaṃ vāpi sattama \|*  
*yadi paśyati puṇyātmā sa prayāti parāṃ gatim \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. If a highly meritorious person looks (favourably) at the dead body or its ashes or the column of smoke (going up from the funeral pyre), the dead man attains the highest goal, О excellent one.

## \|\| 1.7.76 \|\|

*patyuḥ kṛtakriyā sā tu gatvāśramapadaṃmuneḥ \|*  
*cakāra tasya śuśrūṣāṃ sapatnyā saha nārad \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О Narada! After performing the funeral rites of her husband, she went to the hermitage of the sage and accompanied by her co-wife, she rendered service to him.

## Chapter 8. The Glory of the Ganga (Contd).

## \|\| 1.8.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*evamaurvāśrame te dve bāhubhārye munīśvara \|*  
*cakrāte bhaktibhāvena śuśrūṣaāṃ prativāsararam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. О leading sage! Thus, in the hermitage of Aurva, the two wives of Bahu continued to render services with the feeling of devotion, every day.

## \|\| 1.8.2 \|\|

*gate varṣārdhdake kāle jyeṣṭhā rājñī tu yā dvija \|*  
*tasyāḥ pāpamatirjātā sapatnyāḥ saṃpadaṃ prati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Brahmana! After the lapse of half the year, the elder queen became evil-minded towards the good fortune of her со-wife (since she was pregnant)

## \|\| 1.8.3 \|\|

*tatastayā garo dattaḥ kaniṣṭhāyai tu pāpayā \|*  
*na svaprabhāvaṃ cakre vai garo muniniṣevayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then poison was administered to the junior queen by the elder sinful lady. But the poison was not effective, thanks to her service to the sage.

## \|\| 1.8.4 \|\|

*bhūlepanādibhiḥ samyagyataḥ sāmudinaṃ muneḥ \|*  
*cakāra sevāṃ tenāsau jīrṇapuṇyena karmaṇā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. As she served the sage very well by scrubbing and smearing the ground (with cowdung, etc.) and other activities, the poison became digested as the effect of her holy (meritorious) acts.

## \|\| 1.8.5 \|\|

*tato māsa traye 'tīte gareṇa sahitaṃsutam \|*  
*suṣāva suśubhe kāle śuśrūṣānaṣṭakilbiṣā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After three more months, she, all of whose sins were wiped out due to her services (to the sage), gave birth to her son along with the poison, at a highly auspicious time.

## \|\| 1.8.6 \|\|

*aho satsaṃgatirloke kiṃ pāpaṃ na vināśayet \|*  
*na tadātisukhaṃ kiṃ vā narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О! What sin in the world is there which association with righteous men does not destroy? What happiness does it not give unto the men of meritorious acts?

## \|\| 1.8.7 \|\|

*jñānājñānakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yaccānyatkārītaṃ paraiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśayatyāśu paricaryā mahātmanām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Services rendered unto the noble-souled, immediately destroyed the sins committed knowingly or otherwise or those one is compelled to do by others.

## \|\| 1.8.8 \|\|

*jaḍo 'pi yāti pūjyatvaṃ satsaṃgājjagatītalaṃ \|*  
*kalāmātro 'pi śītāśuḥ śaṃbhunā svīkṛto yathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Even the dull attains to the state of being worshipped in this world, thanks to the association with the good, even as a digit of the moon when accepted (on his forehead) by god Siva (became so to the world).

## \|\| 1.8.9 \|\|

*satsaṃgatiḥ parāmṛddhiṃ dadāti hi nṛṇāṃ sadā \|*  
*ihāmutra ca vignendra santaḥ pūjyatamāstataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О leading Brahmana! Indeed, association with the good always bestows on men the greatest prosperity, both here and hereafter. Hence good men are the worthiest to be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.8.10 \|\|

*aho mahagduṇānvaktuṃ kaḥ samartho munīśvarā \|*  
*garbhaṃ prātpo garo jīrṇo māsatrayamaho 'dbhutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О leading sage! Who is competent to describe adequately the good qualities of the great? It was miraculous that the poison that was administered to the child in the womb became digested (and came out after) three months.

## \|\| 1.8.11 \|\|

*gareṇa sahitaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā tejonidhirmuniḥ \|*  
*jātakarma cacakārāsau tannāma sagareti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing the son born along with the poison, the sage, a receptacle of brilliance, performed the post-natal rites and named the son Sagara (a child with the poison).

## \|\| 1.8.12 \|\|

*pupoṣa sagaraṃ bālaṃ tanmātā prītipūrvakam \|*  
*caulopavītakarmāṇi tathā cakre munīśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The child’s mother brought up the boy Sagara with great affection. The prominent sage performed the rites of tonsure and the investiture with the sacred thread in the appropriate manner.

## \|\| 1.8.13-14 \|\|

*śāstrāṇyadhyāpayāmāsa rājayogyāni mantravit \|*  
*samarthaṃ sagaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kiñcidudbhinnaśaiśavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mantravatsarva śāstrāstraṃ dattavānsa munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sagaraḥ śikṣitastena samyagaurvarṣiṇā mune \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Observing that Sagara had outgrown the stage of early childhood, and that he was very capable, the leader of sages who was a past master in the knowledge of mantras, taught him scriptures (science and arts) that were befitting and essential for kingship. He granted him mastery over (the use of weapons) and miraculous missiles alongwith the requisite mantras (incantation of mystic formulae), О sage. Sagara was trained well by that sage Aurva.

## \|\| 1.8.15 \|\|

*babhūva balavāndharmi kṛtajño guṇavānsudhīḥ \|*  
*dharmajñaḥ so 'pi sagaro muneramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*sabhitkuśāṃvupuṣpādi pratyahaṃ samupānayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The virtuous Sagara became powerful, righteous, grateful and intelligent. He possessed all good qualities. Every day he brought sacrificial twigs, kula grass, water, flowers, etc., for immense splendour.

## \|\| 1.8.16 \|\|

*sa kadācidguṇinidhiḥ praṇipatya svamātaram \|*  
*uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā sagaro vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On one occasion Sagara, full of modesty, and storehouse of good qualities, bowed down to his mother with palm joined in reverence and inquired.

## \|\| 1.8.17 \|\|

*sagara uvāca*  
*mātargataḥ pitā kutra kiṃnāmā kasya vaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ mesamācakṣva śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. *Sagara inquired:* “O mother! Where is my father? What is his name? In which family was he born? Kindly narrate to me all these details as I am interested in hearing about them.

## \|\| 1.8.18-20 \|\|

*pitrā vihīnā ye loke jīvanto 'pi mṛtopamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*darīdro 'pi pitā yasya hyāste sa dhanadopamaḥ \|*  
*yasya mātā pitā nāsti sukhaṃ tasya na vidyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dharmahīno yathā mūrkhaḥ paratreha ca ninditaḥ \|*  
*mātāpitṛvihīnasya ajñasyāpyavivekinaḥ \|*  
*aputrasya vṛthāṃ janma ṛṇagrastasya caiva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Those who are devoid of father in this world, are as good as dead ones, even though they may be alive. A person whose father is alive is comparable to Kubera, the lord of wealth, even though he may be indigent. He who is bereft of both father and mother has no happiness. Just as a foolish person devoid of virtues is censured both here and hereafter, so also futile is the life (lit. birth) of a parentless orphan, of an ignorant fellow, of a thoughtless person, of a childless man, and of one immersed in debt.

## \|\| 1.8.21 \|\|

*candrahīnā yathā rātriḥ pahmahīnaṃ yathā saraḥ \|*  
*patihīnā yathā nārī pitṛhīnastathā śiśuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Like a night devoid of the moon, like a lake devoid of lotuses and like a woman devoid of her husband is a boy without his father.

## \|\| 1.8.22 \|\|

*dharmahīno yathā jantuḥ karmahīno yathā gṛhī \|*  
*paśuhīno yathā vaiśyastayā pitrā vinārbhaktaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A child without his father is like a creature without a virtue, or like a householder not practising holy religious rites or like a person from Vaisya community (whose main job is agriculture and tending of cows) without having any cattle or animals.

## \|\| 1.8.23 \|\|

*satyahīnaṃ yathā vākyaṃ sādhuhīnā yathā sabhā \|*  
*tapo yathā dayāhīnaṃ sathā pitrā vivārbhakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A child without his father is like a statement devoid of truth, or like an assembly without good men or like a penance without (the sense of) mercifulness.

## \|\| 1.8.24 \|\|

*vṛkṣahīnaṃ yathāraṇyaṃ jalahīnā yathā nadī \|*  
*bedahīno yathā vājī tathā pitrā vinārbhaktaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A child without his father is like a forest without trees, or like a river devoid of water or a horse without quickness or speed.

## \|\| 1.8.25 \|\|

*yathā lagutaro loke mātaryāvñāparo naraḥ \|*  
*tathā pitrā vihīnastu bahuduḥkhānvitaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О mother! just as a man engaged in begging is considered despicable and wretched, so also a son without his father is overwhelmed by many miseries.”

## \|\| 1.8.26 \|\|

*itītitaṃ sutenaiṣā śrutvā niḥśvāsya duḥkhitā \|*  
*saṃpṛṣṭaṃ tadyathāvṛttaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hearing what was so far spoken by her son, the poor miserable mother sighed deeply, and in reply to his questions, she narrated to him everything as it had taken place.

## \|\| 1.8.27 \|\|

*tacchutvā sagaraḥ kruddhaḥ kopasaṃrakta locanaḥ \|*  
*haniṣyāmītyarātīnsa pratijñāmakarottadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing it, Sagara flung into rage and with his eyes turned red due to fury, he immediately took the pledge: ‘I shall kill the enemies one and all’.

## \|\| 1.8.28 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇīkṛtya muniṃ jananīṃ ca praṇamya saḥ \|*  
*prasthāpitaḥ pratasthe ca tenaiva muninā vadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After circumambulating the sage Aurva and bowing down to his mother, he set out and was given a due send-off by the sage himself.

## \|\| 1.8.29 \|\|

*aurvāśramādriniṣkrāntaḥ sagaraḥ satyavāk śuciḥ \|*  
*vaśiṣṭaṃ svakulācāryaṃ prātpaḥ prītisamanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Starting from the hermitage of Aurva, the pure and truthful Sagara approached with great pleasure Vasistha, his family preceptor.

## \|\| 1.8.30 \|\|

*praṇamya gurave tasmai viśiṣṭāya mahātmane \|*  
*sarvaṃ vijñāpatrāmāsa jñānadṛṣṭyā vijānate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He bowed down to Vasistha, his noble-souled preceptor. He reported to him everything, although the sage had known it all through his vision of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.8.31 \|\|

*aindrāstraṃ vāruṇaṃ brāhmamāgreyaṃ sagaro nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tenaiva munināvāpa khaḍgaṃ vajropamaṃ dhanuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Prince Sagara acquired the miraculous missiles specially empowered by gods Indra, Varuna, Brahma and Agni, through that sage (Vasistha). So also he obtained from him a sword and a bow comparable to Indra’s thunderbolt.

## \|\| 1.8.32 \|\|

*tatastenābhyanujñātaḥ sagaraḥ saumanasyavān \|*  
*āśīrbhirarcitaḥ sadyaḥ pratasthe praṇipatya tam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Honoured by the blessings of the sage and permitted by him, Sagara paid respects to Vasistha and started immediately.

## \|\| 1.8.33 \|\|

*ekenaiva tu cāpena sa śūraḥ paripanthinaḥ \|*  
*saputrapautrānsagaṇānakarotsvargāsinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Only with his single bow, that heroic prince converted his enemies alongwith their sons, grandsons and followers into residents of the other world (i.e. slew them).

## \|\| 1.8.34 \|\|

*taccāpamuktabāṇāgnisaṃtatāstadarātavaḥ \|*  
*kecidvinaṣṭā saṃtrastāstathā cānye pradudruvuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. His enemies were distressed by the fire generated from the arrows discharged from his bow. Some of them perished, while others became frightened and fled.

## \|\| 1.8.35 \|\|

*kecidviśīrṇa keśāścavalmīkopari saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*tṛṇānyabhakṣayankecinnagrāśca viviśurjanalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Some of them lay dead on anthills with their hair dishevelled and scattered. Some of them ate grass. Even as they were naked some entered water (to hide themselves).

## \|\| 1.8.36 \|\|

*śakāśca yavanāśvevatathā cānye mahībhṛtaḥ \|*  
*satvaraṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurvaśiṣṭaṃ prāṇalolupāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In their ardent desire to save their lives the Sakas, the Yavanas as well as other kings immediately sought refuge in Vasistha.

## \|\| 1.8.37 \|\|

*jitakṣitirbāhuputro ripūngurusamīpagān \|*  
*cārairvijñātavānsadyaḥ prātpa ścācāryasannidhim \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Getting the intelligence through his spies, of the approach of his enemies to his preceptor, Bahu’s son, now the conqueror of the world, promptly came to the presence of his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.8.38 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ bāhusutaṃ niśamya munirvaśiṣṭaḥ śaraṇāgatāṃstān \|*  
*trātuṃ ca śiṣyābhihitaṃ ca kartuṃ vivārayāmāsa tadā kṣaṇena \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing that Bahu’s son has arrived, Vasistha reflected for a while as he wanted to save Bahu’s enemies who had sought refuge in him and also to carry out what his disciple had conveyed to him.

## \|\| 1.8.39 \|\|

*cakāra muṇḍāñśabarānyavanāṃllambamūrddhajān \|*  
*andhāṃśca śmaśrulānsarvānmuṇḍānvedavahiṣkṛtān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He made Sabaras shave off their heads and made Yavanas wear long tresses of hair. He made Andhras retain the moustaches but shave off their heads. All these were ex-communicated from the Vedic fold.

## \|\| 1.8.40 \|\|

*vasiṣṭamuninā tena hataprāyānnirīkṣya saḥ \|*  
*prahasanprāha sagaraḥ svaguruṃ tapaso nidhim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing that they had been made no better than dead by sage Vasistha, Sagara laughingly said to his preceptor the store-house of penance.

## \|\| 1.8.41 \|\|

*// sāgara uvāca*  
*bho bho guro durācārānetānrakṣasi tānvṛthā \|*  
*sarvathāhaṃ haniṣyāmi matpiturdeśahārakān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. *Sagara said:* "O Sir, in vain do you try to protect these wicked persons. By all means I shall see to it, that all these fellows who deprived my father of his ancestral land are killed.

## \|\| 1.8.42-43 \|\|

*upekṣeta samarthaḥ sandharmasya paripanthinaḥ \|*  
*sa eva sarvanāśāya hetubhūto na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bāndhavaṃ prathamaṃ matvā durjatāḥ sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*ta eva balahīnāścedbhajante 'tyantasādhutām \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. If in spite of being capable of annihilating the enemies of righteousness, one were to neglect them and look upon the entire world at first, as being one’s relatives, he himself becomes the cause of total destruction. For those very wicked persons, if powerless, pretend (lit. outwardly resort to) extreme piety to be extremely righteous.

## \|\| 1.8.44 \|\|

*aho māyākṛtaṃ karma khalāḥ kaśmalacetasaḥ \|*  
*tāvatkurvanti kāryāṇi yāvatsyātprabalaṃ balam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Alas! All the (pseudo-) righteous acts (mentioned above) are done fraudulently to deceive others. The wicked ones are sinfully disposed by nature. So long as one's army is powerful, they behave and perform good acts or obey.

## \|\| 1.8.45 \|\|

*dāsabhāvaṃ ca śatrūṇāṃ vārastrīṇāṃ ca sauhṛdam \|*  
*sādhubhāvaṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ śreyaskāmo na viśvaset \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A person who desires to gain his own ultimate good, should not believe in the assumption of the role of servants or slaves by the enemies, in the professions of loving friendliness of prostitutes and in the innocent appearance of serpents.

## \|\| 1.8.46 \|\|

*prahāsaṃ kurvate nityaṃ yāndantāndarśayankhalāḥ \|*  
*tāneva darśayantyāśu svasāmarthya viparyaye \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Showing off their teeth, the wicked always indulge in jokes and pleasantries (while we are powerful). But when there is a reversal of one’s power, they quickly show those very teeth (in a different way).

## \|\| 1.8.47 \|\|

*piśunā jihvayā pūrvaṃ paruṣaṃ pravadanti ca \|*  
*atīva karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ vadantyeva tathābalāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vile persons at first (while in power) speak stern and abusive language with their tongue. But when they become powerless, they use it to speak in extremely pitiable words.

## \|\| 1.8.48 \|\|

*śreyaskāmo bhavedyastu nītiśāstrārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*sādhutvaṃ samabhāvaṃ ca khalānāṃ naiva viśvaset \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He who desires his welfare and he who is adept in treatises on polity, shall not believe in the outward goodness or (pseudo-) equability or equanimity of wicked persons.

## \|\| 1.8.49 \|\|

*durjanaṃ praṇatiṃ yānte mitraṃ kaitavaśīlitam \|*  
*duṣṭāṃ bhāryāṃ ca viśvasto mṛta eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Undoubtedly, a person who believes in the following is no better than dead: — a wicked man who (outwardly) shows submission, a friend who indulges in roguery and a wife of evil unfaithful nature.

## \|\| 1.8.50 \|\|

*mā rakṣa tasmādetānvai gorupavyāghrakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*hatvaitānakhilān duṣṭāṃstvatprasādānmahīṃ bhaje \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Hence, verily, please do not afford protection to these persons who are like cows in (outward) appearance but are (cruel) like tigers in their deeds. After killing all these wicked persons, I shall rule over the earth with your grace”.

## \|\| 1.8.51 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭastadvacaḥ śrutvā suprīto munisattamaḥ \|*  
*karābhyāṃ sagasyayāṅgaṃ spṛśannidamuvāca ha \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing his words, Vasistha, the excellent sage, was highly pleased with him. Stroking (patting) Sagara’s body gently with his hands (to express his approbation), he spoke to him as follows:

## \|\| 1.8.52 \|\|

*vasiṣṭa uvāca*  
*sādhu sādhu mahābhāga satyaṃ vadasi suvrata \|*  
*tathāpi madvacaṛ śrutvā parāṃ śāntiṃ labhiṣyasi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. *Vasistha said:* “Well done! Well done! О blessed one. What you speak is the truth, О prince of noble rites. Still you will attain great peace of mind by paying heed to my words.

## \|\| 1.8.53 \|\|

*mayaite nihitāḥ pūrvaṃ tvatpratijñāvirodhinaḥ \|*  
*hātānāṃ hanave kīrtiḥ kā samutpadyate vada \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. These persons who stood against your pledge have already been killed by me. Tell me, what fame can accrue to you by killing those who have already been killed?

## \|\| 1.8.54 \|\|

*bhūmīśa jantavaḥ sarve karmapāśena yantritāḥ \|*  
*tathāpi pāpairnihatāḥ kimarthaṃ haṃsi tānpunaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О Lord of the Earth, all creatures are fettered by shackles of their own actions. They are, however, already killed by their own sinful acts. Why do you kill them again?

## \|\| 1.8.55 \|\|

*dehastu pāpajanitaḥ pūrvapamevainasā hataḥ \|*  
*ātmā hyabhedyaḥ pūrṇatvācchāstrāṇāmeṣa niścayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. This is the decisive conclusion of all scriptures that the physical body produced by sins is already killed at the outset by those very sins, but the soul is impregnable because it is full and perfect.

## \|\| 1.8.56 \|\|

*svakarmaphalabhogānāṃ hetumātrā hi jantavaḥ \|*  
*karmāṇi daivamūlāni devādhīnamidaṃ jagat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Creatures are but instruments in the enjoyment of fruits of their own actions. The karmas are the outcome or the result of Fate (lit. have the Fate as their root). The entire universe is subject to the control of Fate.

## \|\| 1.8.57 \|\|

*ātmā hyabhedyaḥ rakṣitā duṣṭaśikṣitā \|*  
*tato narairasvatantraiḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ sādhyate vada \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Since Fate alone is the protector of the good and the chastiser of the wicked what is it that can be achieved by men who are not free (have no free will). Tell me.

## \|\| 1.8.58 \|\|

*śarīraṃ pāpasaṃbhūtaṃ pāpenaiva pravartate \|*  
*pāpamūlamidaṃ jñātvā kathaṃ hantuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The physical body is born through sin and it functions through sin. Why did you attempt to kill even after knowing that all this is rooted in evil?

## \|\| 1.8.59 \|\|

*ātmā śuddho 'pi dehastho dehīti procyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*tasmādidaṃ vapurbhūpa pāpamūlaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Though the soul (*atman*) is pure, it is called the embodied one, by learned men, since it abides in the body. Hence, О king, there is no doubt in this that the physical body is rooted in evil.

## \|\| 1.8.60 \|\|

*pāpamūlavapurhantuḥ kā kīrtistava bāhuja \|*  
*bhaviṣyatīti niścitya naitānhiṃsīstataḥ suta \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О son of Bahu, what renown can come to you by killing the body rooted in evil? Thinking decisively (on these lines) О son, do not do them to death”

## \|\| 1.8.61 \|\|

*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ virarāma sa kopataḥ \|*  
*spṛśankareṇa sagaraṃ nandanaṃ munayastadā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On hearing these words of the preceptor, the prince refrained from his angry venture. The sage patted his son-like disciple with his hands and consoled him.

## \|\| 1.8.62 \|\|

*athātharvanidhistasya sagarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*rājyābhiṣekaṃ kṛtavānmunibhiḥ saha suvrataiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then (sage Vasistha) expert in the Atharva Veda performed the coronation ceremony8 of the noble-souled Sagara with the co-operation of sages who were strict observers of religious vows.

## \|\| 1.8.63 \|\|

*bhāryādvayaṃ ca tasyāsītkeśinī sumati stathā \|*  
*kāśyapasya vidarbhasya tanaye munasattama \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He (Sagara) had two wives, Kesini and Sumati. They were the daughters of Vidarbha of Kasyapa’s family.

## \|\| 1.8.64 \|\|

*rājye pratiṣṭite dṛṣṭvā muniraurvastaponidhiḥ \|*  
*vanādāgatya rājānaṃ saṃbhāṣya svāśramaṃ yayau \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Seeing that Sagara was well established in his kingdom the sage Aurva, the store-house of penance, came from the forest and after holding conversation with the king, returned to his hermitage.

## \|\| 1.8.65 \|\|

*kadācittasya bhūpasya bhāryābhyāṃ prārthitomuniḥ \|*  
*varaṃ dadāvapatyārthamaurvo bhārgavamantravit \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On one occasion the sage Aurva who knew the Bhargava mantra was requested by the two queens of that king. He granted them the boon of having children.

## \|\| 1.8.66 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ dhyānasthito bhūtvā trikālajño munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*keśitīṃ sumatiṃ caiva idamāha praharṣayam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The prominent sage, the knower of the past, the present and the future, remained in meditation for a moment. Giving delight to the queens Kesini and Sumati, he addressed them thus.

## \|\| 1.8.67 \|\|

*aurva uvāca*  
*ekā vaṃśadharaṃ caikamanyā ṣaḍyutāni ca \|*  
*apatyārthaṃ mahābhāge vṛṇutāṃ ca yathepsitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*Aurva said:*

67\. “One of you will give birth to a single son who will keep the continuity of your race. The other will give birth to sixty thousand sons О blessed ladies; choose either of the boons for the sake of having children.

## \|\| 1.8.68 \|\|

*atha śrutvā vacastasya muneraurvasya nārada \|*  
*keśinyekaṃ sutaṃ vavre vaṃśasantānakāraṇam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On hearing the words of the sage Aurva, О Narada, queen Kesini chose a single son who will be the cause of perpetuation of their family lift.

## \|\| 1.8.69 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi sumatyā hyabhavansutāḥ \|*  
*nāmnāsamañjāḥ keśinyāstanayo munisattama \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. According to the boon sixty thousand sons were born of Sumati, О excellent sage, and the son of Kesini was Asamanjas by name.

## \|\| 1.8.70 \|\|

*asamañjāstu karmāṇi cakāronmattaceṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgarāḥ sarve hyāsandurvṛttacetasaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Asamanjas committed mischievous pranks like a mad man. On seeing him (act that way) the other sons of Sagara too became evil-minded and ill-behaved

## \|\| 1.8.71 \|\|

*tadvālabhāvaṃ saṃduṣṭaṃ jñātvā bāhusuto nṛpaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa vidhivatputrakarma vigarhinam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On seeing their childhood thus vitiated (by these mischievous deeds), king Sagara, the son of Bahu, pondered over anxiously about the despicable activities of his son as brought about Fate.

## \|\| 1.8.72 \|\|

*aho kaṣṭatarā loke durjanānāṃ hi saṃgatiḥ \|*  
*kārukaistāḍyate vahṇirayaḥsaṃyogamātrataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He reflected: “Alas! Extremely painful indeed is the association with the wicked persons. Fire is always beaten by blacksmiths for its only fault of being in contact with iron.

## \|\| 1.8.73 \|\|

*aṃśumānnāma tanayo babhūva hyasamañjasaḥ \|*  
*śāstrajño guṇavāndharmī pitāmahahite rataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Asamanjas had a son named Amsuman. He was a knower of scriptures, righteous and engaged in what was beneficial to his grandfather. He was endowed with all good qualities.

## \|\| 1.8.74 \|\|

*durvṛttāḥ sāgarāḥ sarve lokopadrava kāriṇaḥ \|*  
*anuṣṭānavatāṃ nityamantarāyā bhavanti te \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. But all the sons of Sagara committed evil deeds and harassed the people. They always created obstacles in the undertaking of holy rites of those who practised them regularly.

## \|\| 1.8.75 \|\|

*hutāni yāni yajñeṣu havīṃṣi vidhitraddijaiḥ \|*  
*bubhuje tāni sarvāṇi nirākṛtya divaukasaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They drove off the gods (to whom oblations were offered) and partook of all sacrificial offerings duly submitted by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.8.76 \|\|

*svargādāhṛtya savataṃ rambhādyā devayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhajanti sāgarāstā vai kacagrahabalātkṛtāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They always brought by force celestial ladies like Rambha and others dragging them by the tresses of their hair, and the sons of Sagara enjoyed them against their will.

## \|\| 1.8.77 \|\|

*pārijātādivṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpāṇyāhṛtya te khalāḥ \|*  
*bhūṣayanti svadehāni madyapānaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Those wicked fellows were addicted to the drinking of wine. They plucked and brought the flowers of Parijata and other celestial trees and adorned their bodies with them.

## \|\| 1.8.78 \|\|

*sādhuvṛttīḥ samājahnuḥ sadācārānanāśayan \|*  
*mitraiśca yodrumārabdhā balino 'tyantapāpinaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Those great sinners but very powerful ones, abducted women who were well-behaved and chaste and destroyed men of good conduct. They even began fighting with their friends.

## \|\| 1.8.79 \|\|

*etaddṛṣṭvātiduḥkhārtā devā indrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*vicāraṃ paramaṃ cakrureteṣuṃ nāśahetave \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. On seeing this, the gods, the leader of whom was Indra, became extremely distressed. They began to think deeply of the means of bringing about their destruction.

## \|\| 1.8.80 \|\|

*niścitya vivudhāḥ sarve pātālāntaragocaram \|*  
*kapilaṃ devadeveśaṃ yayuḥ pracchannarupiṇaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Taking a decision in the matter, all the Devos assuming disguised forms approached Kapila, the Lord of the chiefs of gods, who was at that time present in the Nether world.

## \|\| 1.8.81 \|\|

*dhyāyantamātmanātmānaṃ parānaidaikavigraham \|*  
*prāṇamya daṇḍavadrūmau tuṣṭuvuvridaśāstataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The gods prostrated themeelves on the ground before him like a staff and extolled him who was meditating in his mind on the Atman, who is the very embodiment of pure and absolute bliss. They eulogised him as follows:

## \|\| 1.8.82 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*namaste yogine tubhyāṃ sāṅkhyayogaratāya ca \|*  
*nararupapraticchinnaviṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*The gods prayed:*

82\. “Obeisance to you, the yogin who are absorbed and delightfully engaged in Sankhya-Yoga; salutations to you who are Lord Visnu Himself, disguised in the form of a human being, but who is all the while victorious (Jisnu).

## \|\| 1.8.83 \|\|

*namaḥ pareśabhaktāya lokānugrahahetave \|*  
*saṃsārāraṇyadāvāgre dharmapālanasetave \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Bow to the devotee of the Supreme Lord; obeisance to you who are the Cause and bestower of benediction to all the world. Salutations to you who like the forest conflagration are the destroyer of the forest of samsara; we bow to you who are like a bridge affording protection to (the observers of) Dharma.

## \|\| 1.8.84 \|\|

*mahate vītarāgāya tubhyaṃ bhūyo namo namaḥ \|*  
*sāgaraiḥ pīḍitānasmāṃstrāyasva śaraṇāgatān \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. We bow again and again to you who are the great one totally devoid of passions and attachment. Be pleased to save us who have been afflicted by the sons of Sagara and have approached to you as a refuge for protection.”

## \|\| 1.8.85 \|\|

*kapila uvāca*  
*ye tu nāśamihecchanti yaśobaladhanāyuṣām \|*  
*ta eva lokānbādhante nātrāśvāryaṃ sugetamāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*Kapila said:*

85\. “O excellent gods, only those who seek destruction of their own fame, power, wealth and longevity, harass the world. There is nothing surprising in this.

## \|\| 1.8.86 \|\|

*yastu bādhitumiccheta janānniraparādhinaḥ \|*  
*taṃ vidyātsarvalokeṣu pāpabhogarataṃ surāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. О gods, know that a person who intends to harass innocent persons in this world, is one who is engaging himself in the enjoyment of sins.

## \|\| 1.8.87 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā yastvanyānbādhate sadā \|*  
*taṃ hanti daivamevāśu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. No doubt need be entertained in that that the Fate quickly destroys a person who continuously harrasses others physically, mentally or Verbally.

## \|\| 1.8.88 \|\|

*alpairahobhire vaite nāśameṣyanti sāgarāḥ \|*  
*ityuktaṃ muninā tena kapilena mahātmanā \|*  
*praṇamya taṃ yathānyāyaṃ gatā nākaṃ divaukasaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. These sons of Sagara will meet their death in a very few days.” When this assurance was given by that noble- souled sage Kapila, the heaven-dwellers bowed to him duly and returned to the celestial world. »

## \|\| 1.8.89 \|\|

*atrāntare tu sagarovasiṣṭādyairmaharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ārebhe hayamedhākhyaṃ yajñaṃ karttumanuttamam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. In the mean-time, Sagara began to perform the Yajna (sacrifice) called Hayamedha (horse-sacrifice) with the help and guidance of Vasisstha and other great sages.

## \|\| 1.8.90 \|\|

*tadyajñe yojitaṃ satpimapahṛtya sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*pātāle sthāpayāmāsa kapilo yatra tiṣṭati \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Indra, the Lord of gods, took off the horse that was fixed for that sacrifice and placed it in the Nether world where Kapila was staying.

## \|\| 1.8.91 \|\|

*gūḍhavigrahaśakreṇa hṛtamaśvaṃ tu sāgarāḥ \|*  
*anveṣṭuṃ babhrabhurlokān bhūrādīṃśca suvismitāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In order to find out the horse taken away by Indra with his physical body invisible, the sons of Sagara were extremely surprised and they wandered over the earth and other worlds in search of it.

## \|\| 1.8.92 \|\|

*ahaṣṭasatpayaste ca pātālaṃ gantu mudyatāḥ \|*  
*cakhnurmahītalaṃ sarvamekaiko yojanaṃ pṛthak \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. When they could not trace the horse, they attempted to make their way to the Patala, the nether-world. And each one of them severally dug up the earth’s surface to a depth of a Yojana (eight miles).

## \|\| 1.8.93 \|\|

*mṛttikāṃ khanitāṃ te caudadhitīre samākiran \|*  
*tadvāreṇa gatāḥ sarve pātālaṃ sagarātmajāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The earth dug out by them, they scattered on the shores of the ocean. All the sons of Sagara reached Patala through that passage.

## \|\| 1.8.94-96 \|\|

*vicinvanti hayaṃ tatra madonmattā vicetasaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tatrāpaśyanmahātmānaṃ koṭisūryasamaprabham \|*  
*kapilaṃ dhyānanirataṃ vājinaṃ ca tadantike \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tataḥ sarve tu saṃrabdhā muniṃ dṛṣṭvātivegataḥ \|*  
*hantumudyuktamanaso vidravantaḥ samāsadan \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. The sons of Sagara who were perplexed and mad with arrogance searched for the horse. There they beheld the noble-souled Kapila dazzling with the lustre of ten million suns together, absorbed in meditation. And they espied the sacrificial horse near him. On seeing the sage they became very furious. With great speed they rushed at him and attacked him with the intention of killing him.

## \|\| 1.8.97-98 \|\|

*hanyatāṃ hanyatāmeṣa vadhyatāṃ vadhyatāmayam \|*  
*guhyatāṃ gṛhyatāmāśu ityūcuste parasparam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*hṛtāśvaṃ sādhubhāvena bakavaddhyānatatparam \|*  
*santi cāro khalā loke kurvantyāḍambaraṃ mahat \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. They shouted to one another: “Let him be struck down. Let him be struck. Let him be slain. Let him be killed. Let him be taken captive. Let him be quickly taken prisoner. It is he only by whom the horse is taken away and like a stork he pretends to be absorbed in meditation, showing off to be a saint. Alas! There are wicked persons in this world who put up a great show (of saintliness)”.

## \|\| 1.8.99-100 \|\|

*ityuccaranto jahasuḥ kapilaṃ te munīśvaram \|*  
*samastendriyasaṃdohaṃ niyamyātmānamātmani \|\| 99 \|\|*

*āsthitaḥ kapilasteṣāṃ tatkarma jñātavānnahi \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Shouting thus, they laughed and jeered at Kapila, the leader of sages who had exercised perfect control over his sense organs and stabilized his mind in the Atman. As he was absorbed in meditation, Kapila did not notice their activities.

## \|\| 1.8.101 \|\|

*āsannamṛtyavaste tu vinaṣṭamatayo munim \|*  
*padbhiḥ saṃtāḍayāmāsurbuhūṃ ca jagṛhuḥ pare \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Those sons of Sagara whose death was imminent, lost their sense and kicked the sage, while others caught bold of his arms.

## \|\| 1.8.102 \|\|

*tatastyaktasamādhistu sa munirvismitastadā \|*  
*uvāca bhāvagambhīraṃ lokopadravakāriṇaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. When the sage left off his trance, he was surprised (to see all this). In a deep majestic voice, he spoke to them who caused harassment to the world.

## \|\| 1.8.103 \|\|

*aiśvaryamadamattānāṃ kṣudhitānāṃ ca kāminām \|*  
*ahṝṅkāravimūḍhānāṃ viveko naiva jāyate \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. “The following persons lose their power of discrimination viz. those who are intoxicated with the arrogance of affluence; those who are oppressed with hunger; the passionate ones and those who are puffed with self-conceit.

## \|\| 1.8.104 \|\|

*nidherādhāramātreṇa mahī jvalati sarvadā \|*  
*tadeva mānavā bhuktvā jvalantīti kimadbhutam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The earth blazes internally continuously by merely being the receptacle of a treasure. What wonder is there when men blazed forth after enjoying the same?

## \|\| 1.8.105 \|\|

*kimatra citraṃ sujanaṃ bādhante yadi durjanāḥ \|*  
*mahīruhāṃ ścānutaṭe pātayanti nadīrayāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. What is surprising in it, if wicked men annoy and harass the good people? The force of the current in a river makes the trees on the bank fall down.

## \|\| 1.8.106 \|\|

*yatra śrīryauṃvanaṃ vāpi śāradā vāpi tiṣṭati \|*  
*tatrāśrīrvṛddhatā nityaṃ murkhatvaṃ cāpi jāyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Misfortune, old age and foolishness always occur where there is wealth, youth and learning.

## \|\| 1.8.107 \|\|

*aho kanakamāhātmyamākhyātuṃ kena śakyate \|*  
*nāmasāmyādaho citraṃ dhattūro 'pimadapradaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. By whom can the greatness of Kanaka (gold) be described adequately? Alas! It is wonderful that similarity in name (viz. kanaka) makes the Dhattura plant (the thorn-apple tree) cause intoxication. (The word kanaka means Dhattura as well).

## \|\| 1.8.108 \|\|

*bhavedyadi khalasya śrīḥ saiva lokavināśinī \|*  
*yathā sakhāgneḥ pavanaḥ pannagasya yathā viṣam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. If a wicked person became endowed with affluence, that very same fortune of being affluent is destructive of the world, just as the violent gust of a wind is a friend of fire and poison that of a serpent.

## \|\| 1.8.109 \|\|

*aho dhanamadāndastu paśyannapi na paśyati \|*  
*yadi paśyatyāmahitaṃ sa paśyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Alas! One blinded with the arrogance of his wealth does not see, though he may look on. If he sees wherein lies his welfare and interest, he sees properly.”

## \|\| 1.8.110 \|\|

*ityuktvā kapilaḥ kruddho netrābhyāṃ sasṛje 'nalam \|*  
*sa vahniḥ sāgarānsarvānbhasmasādakarotkṣaṇāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Uttering these words, the infuriated Kapila created and discharged fire out of his eyes. The fire reduced the sons of Sagara to ashes instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.8.111 \|\|

*yannetrajānalaṃ dṛṣṭvā pātālatalavāsinaḥ \|*  
*akālapralayaṃ matvā cukruśuḥ śokalālasāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. On seeing the fire issuing forth from the eyes of Kapila, the residents of the nether-world thought that the time of the dissolution of the universe had arrived prematurely. And they screamed out in their excess of sorrow.

## \|\| 1.8.112 \|\|

*tadagnitāpitāḥ sarve dandaśūkāśca rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*sāgaraṃ viviśuḥ śīghraṃ satāṃ kopo hi duḥsahaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. All the reptiles and Raksasas were scorched by that fire. They entered into the ocean immediately. Indeed the fury of saintly persons is simply unbearable.

## \|\| 1.8.113 \|\|

*atha tasya mahīpasya samāgamyādhvaraṃ tadā \|*  
*devadūta uvācedaṃ sarvaṃ vṛttaṃ hi yakṣate \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Thereafter a messenger of gods came to the place of the sacrifice of the king. He reported everything that had taken place to the king who was desirous of performing that sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.8.114 \|\|

*etatsamākarṇya vacaḥ sagaraḥ sarvavitprabhuḥ \|*  
*daivena śikṣitā duṣṭā ityuvācāti harṣitaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. On hearing those words of the messenger the emperor Sagara, the knower of everything, became extremely glad and remarked, “The wicked ones have been tamed and subdued by the Fate.

## \|\| 1.8.115 \|\|

*mātā vā janako vāpi bhrātā vā tanayo 'pi vā \|*  
*adharmaṃ kurute yastu sa eva ripuriṣyate \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Whether it be the mother or the father or the brother or the son, whoever commits a sin should be considered to be an enemy.

## \|\| 1.8.116 \|\|

*yastvadharmeṣu nirataḥ sarvalokavirodhakṛt \|*  
*taṃ ripuṃ paramaṃ vidyācchāstrāṇāmeṣa nirṇayaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. This is the decision arrived at in the scriptures — one should consider that person as the greatest enemy who is engaged in evil actions and who entertains hostility to all the people.”

## \|\| 1.8.117 \|\|

*sagaraḥ putranāśe 'pi na śuśoca munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*durvṛttanidhanaṃ yasmātsatāmutsāha kāraṇam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. О eminent sage, Sagara did not feel sorry for the loss of his sons; for, the death of a person of evil conduct, enthuses good people.

## \|\| 1.8.118 \|\|

*yajñeṣvanadhikāratvādaputrāṇāmiti smṛteḥ \|*  
*pautraṃ tamaṃśumantaṃ hi putratve katavānprabhuḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Since the Smrti text ordains that a person who has no son is not eligible to perform a sacrifice, the king installed his grandson Amsuman as his son.

## \|\| 1.8.119 \|\|

*asamañjaḥsutaṃ tu sudhīyaṃ vāgvidāṃvaram \|*  
*yuyoja sāravidbhūyo hyaścānayanakarmaṇi \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Moreover, the king, the knower of the essentials about sacrifice, deputed the son of Asamanjas with the assignment of bringing back the horse. — the son who was highly intelligent and the most excellent one among those who were skilled in speech.

## \|\| 1.8.120 \|\|

*sa gatastadviladvāre dṛṣṭvā taṃ munipuṅgavam \|*  
*kapilaṃ tejasāṃrāśiṃ sāṣṭāṅgaṃpraṇanāmahā \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. It is reported that when he went to the entrance to that hollow chasm, he saw there pre-eminent sage Kapila, a mass of brilliance. And he prostrated himself before the sage, touching the ground with eight limbs of his body.

## \|\| 1.8.121 \|\|

*kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vinaye nāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca śāntamanasaṃ devadevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. With his palms joined in reverence, he stood humbly before the sage. He addressed that eternal Lord of gods who was of quiescent and serene mind, as follows:

## \|\| 1.8.122 \|\|

*aṃśumānuvāca*  
*dauḥśīlyaṃ yatkṛtaṃ brahmanmatpitṛvyaiḥ kṣamasvatat \|*  
*paropakāraniratāḥ kṣamāsārā hi sādhavaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*Amsuman said:*

122\. О Brahmana sage, kindly forgive the wicked offence committed by my uncles. Indeed, saintly persons who are engaged in rendering help to others are essentially of a forbearing nature.

## \|\| 1.8.123 \|\|

*durjaneṣvapi sattveṣu dayāṃ kurvanti sādhavaḥ \|*  
*nahi saṃharatejyotsnāṃ candraścāṇḍālaveśmanaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Saintly persons show mercy even to the wicked. Indeed, the moon does not withdraw its beams of moon-light from the abode of a *candala*.

## \|\| 1.8.124 \|\|

*bādhyamāno 'pi sujanaḥ sarveṣāṃ sukhakṛdbhavet \|*  
*dadāti paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ bhakṣyamāṇo 'maraiḥ śaśī \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. A good man, even when he is harassed and troubled, gives happiness to all. Just as the moon that ish being eaten by the immortals gives the greatest pleasure and satisfaction to everyone.

## \|\| 1.8.125 \|\|

*dāritaśchinna evāpi hyāmodenaiva candanaḥ \|*  
*saurabhaṃ kurute sarvaṃ tathaiva sujanojanaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Even when split and cut to pieces, the sandle wood renders everything fragrant. So is also a good person.

## \|\| 1.8.126 \|\|

*kṣāntyā ca tapasā cāraistadguṇajñā munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*saṃjātaṃ śāsituṃ lokāṃstvāṃ viduḥ puruṣottama \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. О Supreme Being, prominent sages, by their penance, forbearance and *acara* (behaviour and activities) know the excellent attributes of *purusottama* (Supreme Man), and they know that you are that Supreme Person yourself born to chastise and discipline the world.

## \|\| 1.8.127 \|\|

*namo brahmanmune tubhyaṃ namaste brahmamūrttaye \|*  
*namo brahmaṇyaśīlāya brahmadhyānaparāya ca \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Salutations to you, О Brahmana sage. Obeisance to you who are the embodiment of Brahman. Bow to you who are by nature favourable and friendly to Brahmanas and engaged in meditation on the Brahman.”

## \|\| 1.8.128 \|\|

*iti stuto munistena prasannavadanastadā \|*  
*varaṃ varaya cetyāha prasanno 'smi tavānagha \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The sage who was thus eulogised by him evinced his delight on his countenance. He said, “O sinless one, I am highly pleased with you. Seek any boon of me.”

## \|\| 1.8.129 \|\|

*evamukte tu muninā hyaṃśumānpraṇipatyatam \|*  
*prāpayāsmatpitṝnbrāhmaṃ lokamityabhyabhāṣata \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. When the sage spoke to him thus, Amsuman bowed down to him and requested, “Be pleased to take our ancestors to the world of Brahman”.

## \|\| 1.8.130 \|\|

*tatastasyādisaṃtuṣṭo muniḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*gaṅgāmānīya pautraste nayiṣyati pitṝndivam \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Thereafter the highly delighted sage assured him, “Your grandson will bring down the Ganga respectfully and lead your ancestors to the heaven.

## \|\| 1.8.131 \|\|

*tvatpautreṇa samānītā gaṅgā puṇyajalā nadī \|*  
*kṛtvaitāndhūtapāpānvai nayiṣyati paraṃ padam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The Ganga, the river of holy waters, brought down by your grandson shall absolve these your ancestors of all their sins and lead them to the highest region.

## \|\| 1.8.132 \|\|

*prāpayainaṃ hayaṃ vatsa yataḥ syātpūrṇamadhvaram \|*  
*pitāmahāntikaṃ prāpya sāśvaṃ vṛttaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. О dear child, take this horse back so that the sacrifice can be completed”. Accordingly reaching the vicinity of his grand-father, Amsuman related everything that happened and submitted the horse too.

## \|\| 1.8.133 \|\|

*sagarastena paśunā taṃ yajñaṃ brahmaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*vidhāya tapasā viṣṇumārādhyāpapadaṃhareḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Sagara performed his sacrifice by means of the sacrificial animal in the company of the Brahmanas (sacrificial priests). He propitiated Lord Visnu by performing penance and attained the region of Hari.

## \|\| 1.8.134 \|\|

*jajñe hyaṃśumataḥ putro dilīpa iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhagīratho jāto yo gaṅgāmānayaddivaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. A son was born to Amsuman. He became famous as Dilipa. From him was borne Bhagiratha who brought the Ganga from the heaven.

## \|\| 1.8.135 \|\|

*bhagīrathasya tapasā tuṣṭo brahmā dadau mune \|*  
*gaṅgāṃ bhagīrathāyāḥ cintayāmā sa dhāraṇe \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. О sage, God Brahma who was pleased with the penance of Bhagiratha, bestowed the Ganga on him. He (Bhagiratha) then began to think how to hold the water-fall of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.8.136 \|\|

*tataśca śivamārādhya taddvārā svarṇadīṃ bhuvam \|*  
*ānīya tajjalaiḥ spṛṣṭvā pūtānninye divaṃ pitṝn \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Thereafter, he propitiated god Siva and brought the heavenly river to the earth. He helped his ancestors to go to the heaven as they became sanctified by touching the waters of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.8.137 \|\|

*bhagīrathānvaye jātaḥ sudaso nāma bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*yasya putro mitrasahaḥ sarvalokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. A king named Sudas was born in the family of Bhagiratha. His son Mitrasaha was well-known in all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.8.138 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭaśāpātprātpaḥ sa saudāso rākṣasīṃ tanum \|*  
*gaṅgābinduniṣeveṇaṃpunarmukto nṛpo 'bhavat \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. That son of Sudas got the form of a Raksasa due to the curse of Vasistha. When the drops of the water of the Ganga were sprinkled over him that king became liberated again.

## Chapter 9. The Glory of the Ganga

## \|\| 1.9.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*śatpaḥ kathaṃ vasiṣṭena saundāso nṛpasattamaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgābindūbhiṣekeṇa punaḥ śuddho 'bayatkatham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. How was the excellent king, the son of Sudas, cursed by Vasistha? How was he purified again by means of ablution in the drops of the waters of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.9.2 \|\|

*sarvametadaśeṣeṇa bhrātarme vaktumahrasi \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ vadatāṃ caiva gaṅgākhyānaṃ śubhāvaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О brother, it behoves you to relate to me completely all these things. The episode of the Ganga is conducive to the blessedness both of those who listen as well as those who relate it.

## \|\| 1.9.3 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*saudāsaḥ sarvadharmajñaḥ sarvajño guṇavāñchuciḥ \|*  
*bubhuje pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ pitṛvadrañjayanprajāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

3\. The son of Sudas was the knower of all Dharmas. He knew everything and was possessed of all good qualities and was pious and pure. He enjoyed the whole of the earth, giving delight to his subjects like their own father.

## \|\| 1.9.4 \|\|

*sageraṇa yathā pūrvaṃ mahīyaṃ satpasāgarā \|*  
*rakṣitā tadvadamunā sarvadharmāvirodhinā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Just as this earth consisting of seven oceans was protected and ruled over by Sagara in former time, he ruled over the earth and did not oppose any Dharma.

## \|\| 1.9.5 \|\|

*putrapautrasamāyuktaḥ sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*triṃśadaṣṭasahasrāṇi bubhuje pṛthivīṃ yuvā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Blessed with sons and grand-sons, endowed with all prosperity and glory, he enjoyed the earth for thirty eight thousand years and still retained his youth.

## \|\| 1.9.6 \|\|

*saudāsastvekadā rājā mṛgayābhiratirvanam \|*  
*viveśva sabalaḥ samyak śodhitaṃ hyāsamantribhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Enthusiastic over hunting expeditions, the royal son of Sudas entered the forest which was carefully cleared by his trustworthy ministers, along with his army.

## \|\| 1.9.7 \|\|

*niṣādaiḥ saditastatra vinighranmūgalañcayam \|*  
*āsasāda nadīṃ revāṃ dharmajñaḥ sa pipāsitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Accompanied by Nisada hunters, he killed various groups of animals. That knower of Dharma became thirsty and came to the river Reva (Narmada).

## \|\| 1.9.8 \|\|

*sudāsatanayastatra snātvā kṛtvāhnikaṃ mune \|*  
*bhuktvā ca mantribhiḥ sārdhdaṃ tāṃ niśāṃ tatra cāvasat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О sage, the son of Sudas took his bath there and performed the daily rites. After taking food along with his ministers, he stayed there for the night.

## \|\| 1.9.9 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samuthāya kṛtvā paurvāhnikīṃ kriyām \|*  
*babhrāma mantrisahito narmadātīraje vane \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter he got up early in the morning and performed all the forenoon rites. Accompanied by his ministers, he wandered in the forest on the banks of the Narmada.

## \|\| 1.9.10 \|\|

*vanādvanāntaraṃ gacchanneka eva mahīpattiḥ \|*  
*ākarṇakṛṣṭabāṇaḥ sat kṛṣṇasāraṃ samanvagāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Alone, the lord of the Earth wandered from one forest to the other. Keeping the bow drawn till the tip of the arrow reached his ear, he chased a deer.

## \|\| 1.9.11 \|\|

*dūrasainyo 'śvamārūḍhaḥ sa rājānuvrajanmṛgam \|*  
*vyāghradvayaṃ guhāsaṃsthamapaśthamapaśyatsurate ratam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Mounted on a horse, the king who intensely chased the deer, left his army far behind. There he saw in a cave a tiger couple engaged in sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 1.9.12 \|\|

*mṛgapṛṣṭaṃ parityajya vyāghrayoḥ saṃmukhaṃ yayau \|*  
*dhanuḥsaṃhitabāṇena tenāsau śaraśāstravit \|\| 12 \|\|*

12.14. He abandoned his pursuit of the deer and came in front of the tiger couple. He was conversent with the science called Dhanurveda. He fitted an arrow to his bow and discharged the arrow at the tigress and made her fall down with the shaft of sharp point and depressed joints (nata-parva). As the tigress fell down, she changed herself into hideous ogress thirty six Yojanas in length. She roared like the rumbling clouds and thunder.

## \|\| 1.9.14-15 \|\|

*taḍitvaddhoranirghoṣā rākṣasī vikṛtābhavat \|*  
*patitāṃ svapriyāṃ vīkṣya dviṣansa vyāghrarākṣasaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pratikriyāṃ kariṣyāmītyuktavā cāntardadhe tadā \|*  
*rājā tu bhayasaṃvigno vanesainyaṃ sametya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

14- 15. On seeing his beloved wife fallen down, the tiger giant hatefully threatened the king, “I shall take revenge for this”. After saying so, he vanished there. The king who was frightened in his mind, returned and rejoined his army in the forest. He reported everything that had happened and came back to his capital city.

## \|\| 1.9.15-18 \|\|

*pratikriyāṃ kariṣyāmītyuktavā cāntardadhe tadā \|*  
*rājā tu bhayasaṃvigno vanesainyaṃ sametya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadrṛttaṃ kathayansarvānsvāṃ purīṃ sa nyavarttata \|*  
*śaṅkamānastu tadrakṣaḥkṛtyā drājā sudāsajaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*paritatyāja mṛgayāṃ tataḥ prabhṛti nārada \|*  
*gate bahutithe kāle hayamedhamakhaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*samārebhe prasannātmā vaśiṣṭādyamunīśvaraiḥ \|*  
*tatra brahmādidevebhyo havirdattvā yathāvidhi \|\| 18 \|\|*

15- 18. The king, the son of Sudas, began to suspect that the demon would perpetrate something terrible. So from that time, he gave up hunting altogether, О Narada. After a lapse of a great deal of time, the king with a happy mind began to perform a horse-sacrifice in the company of (under the direction of) Vasistha and other sages. After offering oblations to Brahma and other gods according to the injunctions of the Sastras and concluding the sacrifice, Vasistha and the performer of the sacrifice who had taken the final holy oblations went out.

## \|\| 1.9.19 \|\|

*samāpya yajñaniṣkrānto vaśiṣṭaḥ strātako 'pi ca \|*  
*atrāntare rākṣaso 'sau nṛpahisitabhāryakaḥ \|*  
*kartuṃ pratikriyāṃ rājñe samāyātoruṣānvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the meanwhile, the demon whose wife had been killed by the king, came there angrily in order to wreak revenge on the king

## \|\| 1.9.20 \|\|

*sa rākṣasastasya gurau prayāte vaśiṣṭaveṣaṃ tu tadaiva dhṛtvā \|*  
*rājānamabhyetya jagāda bhokṣye māṃsaṃ samicchāmyahamityuvāca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When the preceptor Vasistha had gone out, the demon disguised himself as Vasistha. Approaching the king at that time, he told, “I want to take food here”. I desire to eat meat.”

## \|\| 1.9.21 \|\|

*bhūyaḥ samāsthāya sa sūdavaṣaṃ paktvāmiṣaṃ mānupamasya vādāt \|*  
*sthitaśca rājāpi hari yapātre dhṛtvā gurorāgamanaṃ pratīkṣan \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Instantly the Raksasa assuified the guise of the royal cook, cooked human flesh and presented it to the king. The king held it in a vessel of gold and stood awaiting the arrival of the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.9.22 \|\|

*tanmāṃsaṃ hemapātrasthaṃ saudāso vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*samāgatāya guruve dadau tasmau sasādaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The humble son of Sudas respectfully served the flesh kept in that gold vessel, to the preceptor when he came there.

## \|\| 1.9.23 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa guruḥ kimiti vismitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On seeing the preparation, the preceptor wondered what it was and began to reflect

## \|\| 1.9.24 \|\|

*apaśyanmānuṣaṃ māsaṃ parameṇa samādhinā \|*  
*aho 'sya rājño dauḥśīlyamabhakṣyaṃ dattavānmama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By means of his concentration of mind (Samadhi), he came to know that it was human flesh “O! How depraved in character is this king that he has served this forbidden food to me!”

## \|\| 1.9.25 \|\|

*iti viramayamāpannaḥ pramanyurabhavanmuniḥ \|*  
*abho 'jyaṃ madvighātāya datta hi pṛthivīpate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Along with this surprise, the sage felt great indignation and annoyance. “O lord of the earth, this prohibited food has been given to me with a view to bringing about my ruin.

## \|\| 1.9.26 \|\|

*tasmāttavāpi bhavatu hyetadeva hi bhojanam \|*  
*nṛmāṃsaṃ rakṣasāmeva bhojyaṃ dattaṃ mama tvayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hence, let this be your regular diet. Human flesh, the food fit only for the Raksasas has been given to me by you.

## \|\| 1.9.27 \|\|

*tadyāhi rākṣasatvaṃ tvaṃ tadāhārocitaṃ nṛpā \|*  
*iti śāpaṃ dadatyasminsaudāso bhayavihvūlaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, О king, assume the status of a Raksasa which is accustomed to this (human flesh) as the usual diet.” When the preceptor uttered this imprecation to him, the son of Sudas was agitated and overwhelmed with fear.

## \|\| 1.9.28 \|\|

*ājñatpo bhavataiveti sakaṃpo 'sma vyajijñapat \|*  
*bhūrāśṛ cintayāmāsa vaśiṣṭastena noditaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Trembling with fear, he immediately submitted, “I have been so commanded by your holiness yourself!” Urged by this statement, Vasistha reconsidered the situation.

## \|\| 1.9.29 \|\|

*rakṣasā vañcitaṃ bhūpaṃ jñātavān divyacakṣuṣā \|*  
*rājāpi jalamādāya vaśiṣṭaṃ śaptumudyataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With his divine vision, he came to know that the king was deceived by the Raksasa. The king on his part took up water in his hand and was about to curse Vasistha.

## \|\| 1.9.30 \|\|

*samudyataṃ guruṃ śaptaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo ruṣānvitam \|*  
*madayantī priyātasya pratyuvācātha suvratā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Seeing the king enraged and attempting to curse his preceptor, his beloved queen Madayanti, a strict observer of religious vows, intervened thus.

## \|\| 1.9.31 \|\|

*madayantyuvāca*  
*bho bho kṣatriyadāyāda kopa saṃhartumarhasi \|*  
*tvayā yatkarma bhoktavyaṃ tatprātpaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*Madaynti said:*

31\. “O scion of a noble Ksatriya family, it behoves you to curb your anger. There is no doubt in this that the Karman which you alone have to experience, has visited upon you.

## \|\| 1.9.32 \|\|

*guru tukṛtya huṅkṛtya yo vadenmṛḍhadhīrnaraḥ \|*  
*araṇye nirjale deśa sa bhaveddhahyarākṣasaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The stupid fellow who roars and grunts saying HUM and TUM to one’s preceptor, becomes a Brahma-Raksasa in a forest, in a waterless tract.

## \|\| 1.9.33 \|\|

*jitendriyā jitakrodhā guru śuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ \|*  
*prayānti brahmasadanamiti śāstreṣu niścayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. This is the decisive conclusion of the scriptures that those who have conquered the sense-organs, those who have controlled their irate nature and those who are engaged in serving the preceptor, go to the abode of Brahma.”

## \|\| 1.9.34 \|\|

*tayokto bhūpatiḥ kopaṃ tyaktvā bhāryāṃ nananda ca \|*  
*jalaṃ kutra kṣipāmīti cintayāmāsa cātmanā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Dissuaded by her, the king eschewed his wrath. He appreciated the intercession of his wife. He thought to himself, “Where shall I throw this water (taken for uttering the Curse.”

## \|\| 1.9.35 \|\|

*tajjalaṃ yatra saṃsiktaṃ tadbhavedbhasma niścitam \|*  
*iti matvā jalaṃ tattu pādayornyakṣipatsvayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It is certain that the spot where this water is sprinkled will be reduced to ashes.” Thinking thus, he poured the water on his own feet, of his own accord.

## \|\| 1.9.36 \|\|

*tajjalaspaśimātreṇa pādau kalmāṣatāṃ gatau \|*  
*kalmāṣapāda ityevaṃ tataḥ prabhṛti vistṛtaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By the mere contact of that water his feet took the variegated complexion of black and white. So, thenceforth, he became known as Kalmasapada (one whose feet are black and white in complexion.)

## \|\| 1.9.37 \|\|

*kalmāṣapādo matimān priyayāścāsitastadā \|*  
*manasā so 'tibhītastu vavande caraṇaṃ guroḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The intelligent king Kalmasapada was then consoled by his beloved wife. Excessively frightened in his mind, he saluted his preceptor and bowed down to his feet.

## \|\| 1.9.38 \|\|

*uvāca ca prapannastaṃ prāñjalirnayakovidaḥ \|*  
*kṣamasva bhagavansarvaṃ nāparādhaḥ kṛto mayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Resorting with palms joined with reverence, the king, an adept in political stratagems humbly submitted thus! “O holy sir, be pleased to forgive me about everything (that has happened), but the fact of the matter is that no offence or sin has been committed by me.”

## \|\| 1.9.39 \|\|

*tacchutvovāca bhūpālaṃ munirniḥśvasya duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ garhayāmāsa hyavivekaparāyaṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hearing this, the sad sage heaved a deep sigh and he censured himself for his own thoughtlessness. He said to the king.”

## \|\| 1.9.40 \|\|

*avivero hi sarveṣāmāpadāṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*vivekarahito loke paśureva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “Absence of discrimination is the greatest cause of all adversities. There is no doubt about this that one who is devoid of discrimination is no better than a beast.

## \|\| 1.9.41 \|\|

*rājñā tvajānatā nūnametatkarmocitaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*vivekarahito 'jño 'haṃ yataḥ pāpaṃ samācaret \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Indeed, this king had not known the mischief of the Raksasa. What he did was proper. It was I who was thoughtless and ignorant. Hence I committed the sin of cursing him.

## \|\| 1.9.42 \|\|

*vivekaniyato yāti yo vā ko vāpi nirvṛttim \|*  
*vivekahīnamānpoti ko vā yo vāpyanirvṛtim \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He who is controlled by discretion and thoughtfulness — whoever he may be — invariably attains bliss. He who lacks discretion, whoever he may be, meets with the opposite of bliss.”

## \|\| 1.9.43 \|\|

*ityuktavā cātmanātmānaṃ pratyuvāca munirnṛpam \|*  
*nātyantiṅkaṃ bhavedetaddādaśābdaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After saying this to himself, the sage replied to the king, “This curse will not be permanent. It will last for twelve years.

## \|\| 1.9.44 \|\|

*gaṅgābindūbhiṣiktastu tyakttvā vai rākṣasīṃ tanum \|*  
*pūrvarupaṃ tvamāpanno bhokṣyase medinīmimām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Being sprinkled over with the drops of the waters of the Ganga, you will give up the physical form of a Raksasa. Reassuming your original form, you will enjoy this earth.

## \|\| 1.9.45 \|\|

*tadvindusekasaṃbhūtajñānena gatakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*harisevāparo bhūtvā parāṃ śāntiṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Your sins will be dispelled through the perfect knowledge as a result of the sprinkling of the drops of the waters of the Ganga. You will be solely devoted to the service of Lord Hari and will attain the highest spiritual peace.”

## \|\| 1.9.46 \|\|

*ityuktvātharvavidbhūpaṃ vaśiṣṭaḥ svāśramaṃ yayau \|*  
*rājāpi duḥkhasaṃpanno rākṣasīṃ tānumāśritaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying this to the king, Vasistha, the knower of the Atharva Veda, returned to his hermitage. The king also filled with grief, took up the physical form of a Raksasa.

## \|\| 1.9.47 \|\|

*kṣutpapāsāviśeṣārto nityaṃ krodhaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇakṣapādyutirbhīmo babhrāma vijane vane \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He was particularly oppressed with hunger and thirst and was always furious. With a complexion as dark as the night in the dark fortnight, and terrific in appearance, he wandered over the tenantless forest.

## \|\| 1.9.48 \|\|

*mṛgāṃśca vividhāṃstatra mānuṣāṃśca sarīsṛpān \|*  
*vihaṅgamānplavaṅgāṃśca praśastāṃstānabhakṣayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. There he killed and devoured different kinds of beasts, men, reptiles, birds and monkeys.

## \|\| 1.9.49 \|\|

*asthibhirbahubhirbhūyaḥ pītaraktakalevaraiḥ \|*  
*raktāntapretakeśaiśaaca citrāsīdbhūrbhayaṅkarī \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even the ground allround became terrible and it became spotted with various colours, as it was littered with innumerable bones, bodies out of which all blood was sucked and the hairs of the dead bodies mixed with blood.

## \|\| 1.9.50 \|\|

*ṛtutraye sa pṛthivīṃ śatayo janavistṛtām \|*  
*kṛtvātiduḥkhitāṃ paścādvanāntaramupāgamat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In the course of three seasons (i.e. six months) he rendered the land of a hundred yojanas in extent, very miserable, and then went over to another forest.

## \|\| 1.9.51 \|\|

*tatrāpi kṛtavānnityaṃ naramāṃsāśanaṃ sadā \|*  
*jagāma narmadātīraṃ munisiddhaniṣevitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even there also, he continued to eat human flesh every day. He then went to the banks of the Narmada resorted to by the sages and Siddhas.

## \|\| 1.9.52 \|\|

*vicarannarmadātīre sarvalokabhayaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*apaśyatkañcana muniṃ ramantaṃ priyayā saha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Moving about on the banks of the Narmada, that Raksasa (king) who frightened all the world, happened to see a certain sage engaged in amorous sports with his beloved.®

## \|\| 1.9.53 \|\|

*kṣudhānalena saṃtatpastaṃ muniṃ samupādravat \|*  
*jāgrāha cātivegena vyādho mṛgaśiśaṃ yathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Scorched by the fire of hunger, he rushed at the sage and caught hold of him with great force, like a hunter catching the fawn of a deer.

## \|\| 1.9.54 \|\|

*brāhmaṇī svapatiṃ vīkṣya niśācarakarasthitam \|*  
*śirasyañjalimādhāya provāca bhayavihvālā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On seeing her husband struggling within the grip of the demon, the highly frightened Brahmana lady entreated to him with palms joined in reverence over her head.

## \|\| 1.9.55 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca*  
*bho bho nṛpatiśārdūla trāhi māṃ bhayavihvalām \|*  
*prāṇapriya pradānena kuru pūrṇaṃ manoratham \|\| 55 \|\|*

*The Brahmana lady prayed:*
