55\. “O tiger among kings, save me who am now extremely frightened. Be pleased to make my desire fulfilled by restoring my beloved husband who is dearer to me than my very life breath.

## \|\| 1.9.56 \|\|

*nānmā mitrasahastvaṃ hi sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*na rākṣasastato 'nāthāṃ pāhi māṃ vijane vane \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. You are not a real Raksasa. You are a king born of the solar race, by the name Mitrasaha. Hence protect me, «a helpless woman, in this forest, devoid of human population.

## \|\| 1.9.57 \|\|

*yā nārī bharttṛrahitā jīvatyapi mṛtopamā \|*  
*tathāpi bālavaidhavyaṃ kiṃ vakṣyāmyarimardana \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A woman bereft of her husband, is comparable to a dead person, though she may be alive. Still, О suppressor of enemies, what more can I say about widowhood in the early age?

## \|\| 1.9.58 \|\|

*na mātāpitarau jāne nāpi bandhuṃ ca kañcana \|*  
*patireva paro bandhuḥ paramaṃ jīvanaṃ mama \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I do not know either my mother or my father. I do not know any other kinsman. My husband alone is the greatest, relative unto me. He is my very life.

## \|\| 1.9.59 \|\|

*bhavānyettyakhilāndharmānyoṣitāṃ varttanaṃ yathā \|*  
*trāyasva bandhurahitāṃ bālāpatyāṃ janeśvara \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О Lord of the people, you know all the Dharmas. You know how ladies ought to make their livelihood. Hence, save me who am a woman having no kinsman and a lady (mother) having an infant child (in the arms).

## \|\| 1.9.60 \|\|

*kathaṃ jīvāmi patyāsminhīnā hi vijane vane \|*  
*duhitāhaṃ bhagavatastrāhi māṃ patidānataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. How can I live in this tenantless forest without my husband? О sir, I am your daughter. Be pleased to save me, by bestowing upon me my husband, as a charitable gift.

## \|\| 1.9.61 \|\|

*praṇadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vadantīti mahāprājñāḥ prāṇadānaṃ kuruṣva me \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Highly intelligent men say: — “There never has been or there can never be in future a nobler charitable gift than that of saving one’s life.” Please give unto me the charitable gift of my vital breath (viz. my husband).”

## \|\| 1.9.62 \|\|

*abhakṣayakṛṣṇasāraśiśuṃ vyāghro yathā balāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After praying him thus, she fell at the feet of the Raksasa. Though implored thus by the Brahmana woman, the Raksasa devoured the Brahmana like a tiger devouring the fawn of a spotted antelope.

## \|\| 1.9.63 \|\|

*tato vilapya bahudhā tasya patnī pativratā \|*  
*pūrvaśāpahataṃ bhūpamaśapatkrodhitā punaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. That chaste wife of the Brahmana lamented very much. Becoming infuriated again, she cursed the king, though he had already been cursed.

## \|\| 1.9.64 \|\|

*patiṃ me suratāsaktaṃ yasmāddhiṃsitavānbalāt \|*  
*tasmātstrīsaṅgamaṃ prātpastvamapi prāpsyase mṛtim \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. “Inasmuch as you have forcibly killed my husband who was engaged in sexual inter-course, hence the moment you are united with a woman, you will die.”

## \|\| 1.9.65 \|\|

*śatvaivaṃ brāhmaṇī kruddhā punaḥ śāpāntaraṃ dadau \|*  
*rākṣasatvaṃ dhruvaṃ te 'stu matpatirbhakṣito yataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. After cursing him thus the indignant Brahmana lady uttered another imprecation once again on him: “Since you had devoured my husband, your Raksasahood will be permanent.”

## \|\| 1.9.66 \|\|

*so 'pi śāpadvayaṃ śrutvā tayā dattaṃ niśācaraḥ \|*  
*pramanyuḥ prāhi visṛjankopādaṅgārasaṃcayam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On hearing these two curses uttered by her, the Raksasa flew in rage and was as if emitting sparks of fire due to anger. The Raksasa said:

## \|\| 1.9.67 \|\|

*duṣṭe kasmātpradattaṃ mevṛthā śāpadvayaṃ tvayā \|*  
*ekasyaivāparādhasya śāpastveko mamocitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “O wicked woman, why have you heaped two curses on me in vain (without any reason)? As my offence was only one, it would have been but proper to pronounce one imprecation on me.

## \|\| 1.9.68 \|\|

*yasmātkṣipasi duṣṭāgyemayi śāpantaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*piśācayonimadyaiva yāhi putrasamanvitā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О vilest of wicked woman, since you have uttered a second curse on me, you will go to the state of a female ghost (Pisaci) just now to-day, along with your son.”

## \|\| 1.9.69 \|\|

*tenaivaṃ brahmaṇī śatpā piśācatvaṃ tadā gatā \|*  
*kṣudhārtā susvaraṃ bhīmārurodāpatyasaṃyutā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The Brahmana woman, who was cursed by him thus, immediately assumed a ghostly form. She was distressed with hunger. The terrible woman along with her son went on screaming aloud.

## \|\| 1.9.70 \|\|

*rākṣasaśca piśācī ca krośantau nirjane vane \|*  
*jagmaturnarmadātīre vanaṃ rākṣasasevitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Screaming loudly in that tenantless forest, the Raksasa and the Pisaca woman went to the forest, on the bank of Narmada inhabited by Raksasas.

## \|\| 1.9.71 \|\|

*audāsīnyaṃ gurau kṛtvā rākṣasīṃ tanumā śritaḥ \|*  
*tatrāste duḥkhasaṃtatpaḥ kaścillokavirodhakṛt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. At that place, there lived a demon who was tormented with miseries and was antagonistic to the world. He had assumed the physical form of a Raksasa, because he was indifferent towards his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.9.72 \|\|

*rākṣasaṃ ca piśācīṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ravavaṭamāgatau \|*  
*uvāca krodhabahulo vaṭastho brahmarākṣasaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. On seeing the Raksasa and the Pisaci coming to his banyan tree (occupied by him), the Brahmana demon (Brahma- Raksasa) already on that banyan tree said furiously: —

## \|\| 1.9.73 \|\|

*kimarthamāgatau bhīmau yuvāṃ matsthānamīpsitam \|*  
*īdṛśau kena pāpena jātau me bruvatāṃ dhruvam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. “O terrible ones, why have you both come to this abode fondly occupied by me. Certainly you must tell me for what sins of yours, you have become like this.”

## \|\| 1.9.74 \|\|

*saudāsastadvacaḥ śrutvātayā yaccātmanā kṛtam \|*  
*sarvaṃ nivedayitvāsmai paścādetaduvāca ha \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On hearing his words, the son of Sudas related to him everything that was committed by himself as well as by that lady. Thereafter he said to him thus.

## \|\| 1.9.75 \|\|

*saudāsa uvāca*  
*kastvaṃ vada mahābhāga tvayā vai kiṃ kṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*sakhyurmamāti snehena tatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 75 \|\|*

*Sudas's Son Said:*

75\. О highly blessed one, who are you? Please tell me what was done by you before. It behoves you to relate everything to me, your friend, out of your great friendliness.

## \|\| 1.9.76 \|\|

*karoti vañcanaṃ mitre yo vā ko vāpi duṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*sa hi pāpapālaṃ bhuṅkte yātanāstu yugāyutam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Indeed, that wicked-minded fellow, whoever he might be, but who deceived his friend, experiences the fruit of his sins and undergoes tortures in hell, for ten thousand Yugas.

## \|\| 1.9.77 \|\|

*jantūnāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni kṣīyante mitradarśanāt \|*  
*tasmānmitreṣu matimānna kuryādvaṃyanaṃ kadā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. All miseries of creatures are diminished (and disappear) at the sight of a friend. Hence, no sensible person shall practice deception on his friends.”

## \|\| 1.9.78 \|\|

*kalmāṣapādenetyukto vaṭastho brahmarākṣasaḥ \|*  
*uvāca prītimāpanno dharmavākyāni nārada \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. О Narada, the Brahma-Raksasa, already on the banyan tree, who was thus urged by Kalmasapada, spoke these virtuous words delightfully:

## \|\| 1.9.79 \|\|

*brahmarākṣasa uvāca*  
*ahamāsaṃ purā vipro māgadho vedapāragaḥ \|*  
*somadatta iti khyāto nānmā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*The Brahma-Raksasa said:*

79\. “Formerly, I was a Brahmana in the country called Magadha. I had mastered the Vedas and was wellknown by the name Somadatta. I was devoted to the practice of Dharma.

## \|\| 1.9.80 \|\|

*pramatto 'haṃ mahābhāga vidyayā vayasā dhanaiḥ \|*  
*audāsīnyaṃ guroḥ kṛtvā prātpavānīdṛśīṃ gatim \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. О blessed one, I became too much elated and arrogant due to my learning, wealth and youthful age. I showed indifference towards my preceptor and consequently I was reduced to this stage (of being a Brahma-Raksasa).

## \|\| 1.9.81 \|\|

*nalabhe 'haṃ sukhaṃ kiṃ cijjitāhāro 'tiduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*mayā tu bhakṣitā viprāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. I am unable to derive any happiness. I am fed up with the food I take (?) since I am distressed. Formerly, hundreds and thousands of Brahmanas were devoured by me.

## \|\| 1.9.82 \|\|

*kṣutpipāsāparo nityamantastāpena pīḍitaḥ \|*  
*jagatrāsakaro nityaṃ māṃsāśanaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Still I was tormented by hunger and thirst. 1 was afflicted by internal agony. I created a terror in the whole universe and I was always engaged in eating flesh.

## \|\| 1.9.83 \|\|

*gurvavajñā manuṣyāṇāṃ rākṣasatvapradāyinī \|*  
*mayānubhūtametaddhi tataḥ śrīmānna cācaret \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Disrespect and indifference to the preceptor lead to Raksasa-hood in human beings. This has indeed been experienced by me. Hence, no one in prosperity shall do like-wise.”

## \|\| 1.9.84 \|\|

*kalmāṣapāda uvāca*  
*gurustu kīdṛśaḥ proktaḥ kastvayāślāghitaḥ purā \|*  
*tadvadasva sarave sarvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 84 \|\|*

*Kalmasapada said:*

84\. “Of what nature is a preceptor as laid down in Sastras? Who was panegyrized by you formerly? О friend, tell me everything. I am extremely curious and anxious to know it.”

## \|\| 1.9.85 \|\|

*brahmarākṣasa uvāca*  
*guravaḥ santi bahavaḥ pūjyā vandyāśca sādaram \|*  
*yātānahaṃ kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sarave \|\| 85 \|\|*

*The Brahma-Raksasa said:*

85\. “There are many categories of preceptors. All of them are worthy of being worshipped and honoured respectfully. О friend, listen with single-minded attention as I narrated them (viz. categories of preceptors).

## \|\| 1.9.86-88 \|\|

*adhyāpakaśca vedānāṃ vedārthayutibaidhakaḥ \|*  
*śāstravaktā dharmavaktā nītiśāstropadeśakaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*mantropadeśavyākhyākhyākṛdvedasadaṃhṛttathā \|*  
*vratopadeśakaścaiva bhayatrātānnado hi ca \|\| 87 \|\|*

*śvaśuro mātulaścaiva jyeṣṭhabhrātā pitā tathā \|*  
*upanetā niṣektā ca saṃskarttā mitrasattama \|\| 88 \|\|*

86-88. They are as follows: — One who teaches the Vedas, one who explains the connection between the Vedic passage and its interpretation (i.e. the interpreter of the Vedas), the expounder of the scriptures, the exponent of the Dharmas, the instructor in moral philosophy (or politics), one who initiates in the Mantras, one who explains the Mantras, one who dispels doubts in Vedic passages, one who instructs in religious observances and vows, one who saves from dangerous situation, one who provides with food, the father-in-law, the maternal uncle, the eldest brother, the father, one who invests the sacred thread, the impregnator and the consecrator, О excellent friend.

## \|\| 1.9.89 \|\|

*ete hi guravaḥ proktāḥ pūjyā vandyaśca sādaram \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. These are said to be the" preceptors. They deserve to be worshipped and bowed with great respect.”

## \|\| 1.9.90 \|\|

*kalmāṣapāda uvāca*  
*guravo bahavaḥ proktā eteṣāṃ katamo varaḥ \|*  
*tulyāḥ sarve 'pyuta sarave tadyathāvaddhi brūhi me \|\| 90 \|\|*

*Kalmasapada enquired:*

90\. “O friend, many preceptors have been mentioned by you. Who is the most excellent of all these? Or, are all of them of equal status? Tell me precisely.”

## \|\| 1.9.91-92 \|\|

*brahmarākṣasa uvāca*  
*sādhu sādhu mahāprājña yatpṛṣṭaṃ tadvadāmi te \|*  
*gurumāhātmyakathanaṃ śravaṇaṃ cānumodanam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ śreya ādhatte tasmādvakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*ete samānapūjārhāḥ sarvadā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*The Brakma-Raksasa replied:*

91-92. “Very nice! A very good question! О highly intelligent one. I shall explain to you what has been enquired by you of me. The narration of the glory of preceptors, listening to that glory and approbation of the same — all these accord welfare unto all. Hence, I shall explain now: — There is no doubt in this that all these are equally worthy of being worshipped at all times.

## \|\| 1.9.93-94 \|\|

*tathāpi śruṇu vakṣyāmi śāstrāṇāṃ sāraniścayam \|*  
*adhyāpakāśca vedānāṃ mantravyākhyākṛtastathā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*pitā ca dharmavaktā ca viśeṣaguravaḥ smṛtāḥ eteṣāmapi bhūpāla śṛṇuṣva pravaraṃ gurum \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. Still, however, listen to me. I shall relate to you the essential and crucial decision of the scriptures (in the matter). The teacher of the Vedas, the person who explains the Mantras, the father and expounder of the Dharma — these are regarded to be special types of preceptors in the Smrti texts. О lord of the earth, listen as to who should be regarded as the most excellent of all these.

## \|\| 1.9.95-96 \|\|

*sarvaśāstrārthatatvajñairbhāṣitaṃ pravadāmi te \|*  
*yaḥ purāṇāni vadati dharmayuktāni paṇaḍitaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*saṃsārapāśavicchedakaraṇāni sa uttamaḥ \|*  
*devapūjārhakarmāṇi devatāpūjane phalam \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. I shall explain unto you what has been proclaimed by the knowers of the principles and interpretations of all scriptures. That learned man who explains the Puranas along with the Dharmas which contribute to the snapping asunder of the noose of the worldly existence, is the most excellent preceptor. It is from the Puranas that one knows the various rites proper for the worship of Devas and the fruit (one achieves) of the worship of the deities.

## \|\| 1.9.97-100 \|\|

*jāyate ca purāṇebhyastasmāttānīha devatāḥ \|*  
*sarvavedārthasārāṇi purāṇānīti bhūpate \|\| 97 \|\|*

*vadanti munayaścaiva tadūktā paramo guruḥ \|*  
*yaḥ saṃsārārṇatvaṃ tarttumudyogaṃ kurute naraḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*śruṇuyātsa purāṇāni iti śāstravibhāgakṛt \|*  
*proktavānsarvadharmāśca purāṇeṣu mahīpate \|\| 99 \|\|*

*tarkastu vādahetuḥ syānnītistvaihikasādhanam \|*  
*purāṇāni mahābuddhe ihāmutra sukhāya hi \|\| 100 \|\|*

97-98a. Hence, О king, gods and sages say that the Puranas constitute the essence of the meaning of all Vedic passages. The expounder of the Puranas is, therefore, the greatest of all the preceptors.

98b-100. The man who strives to cross the ocean of worldly existence should listen to the Puranas — so says the classifier of the scriptures (i.e. the sage Vyasa). О king, it was he who laid down in details all the Dharmas in the Puranas. Logic or reasoning is only for the sake of arguments in dispute. Ethics or politics is the means for worldly affairs and Puranas indeed are conducive to the happiness both here and hereafter, О highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 1.9.101 \|\|

*yaḥ śṛṇoti purāṇāni satataṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tasya syānnirmalā buddhirbhūyo dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The intellect (or mind) of a person who always listens to the Puranas with great devotion becomes free from impurities. He shall be devoted again to Dharma.

## \|\| 1.9.102 \|\|

*purāṇaśravaṇādbhaktirjāyate śrīpatau śubhā \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktanṛṇāṃ bhūpa dharme buddhiḥ pravarttate \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. О king, thanks to listening to the Puranas, auspicious devotion towards the Lord of Laksmi, is thereby engendered. The intellect of men who are the devotees of Visnu is engaged in Dharma.

## \|\| 1.9.103-107 \|\|

*dharmātpāpāni naśyanti jñānaṃ śuddhaṃ ca jāyate \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ ye phalānyabhilipsavaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*śruṇuyuste purāṇāni prāhuritthaṃ purāvidaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tu gautamamuneḥ sarvajñādrūhyavādinaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*śrutavānsarvadharmārtha gaṅgātīre manorame \|*  
*kadācitparameśasya pūjāṃ karttumahaṃ gataḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*upasthitāyāpi tasmai praṇāmaṃ na hyakāriṣam \|*  
*sa tu śānto mahābuddhirgauntamastejasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*mantroditāni karmaṇi karotītimudaṃ ya yau \|*  
*yastvarcito mayā devaḥ śivaḥ sarvajagadguruḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

103-105a. Sins are destroyed due to Dharma and the knowledge becomes pure. Those who are well versed in the ancient lore say thus: — “Those who are desirous of attaining the fruits of Purusarthas, viz. Dharma, wealth, love and liberation from Samsara, should listen to the Puranas” On the beautiful banks of the Ganga, I heard all the topics on religion or Dharma from sage Gautama, who was omniscient and expounder of the Brahman or the Vedas.

105b-107. Once, I went to perform the worship of god Siva. Although he (Gautama) was present, i did not make obeisance to him. But Gautama, the highly intelligent sage, the very receptacle of great lustre was calm. He rejoiced at the proper performance of the rites as mentioned in the Mantras and since Lord Siva, the preceptor of all the universe, was worshipped by me.

## \|\| 1.9.108-113 \|\|

*gurvavajñā kṛtāyena rākṣasaṃtve niyuktavān \|*  
*jñānato 'jñānato vāpi yo 'vajñāṃ kurute guroḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tasyaivāśu praṇaśyanti dhīvidyārthātmajakriyāḥ \|*  
*śuśrūṣāṃ kurute yastu guruṇāṃ sādaraṃ naraḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tasya saṃpadbhavedbhūpa iti prāhurvipaścitaḥ \|*  
*tena śāpena dagdho 'hamantaścaiva kṣadhāgninā \|\| 110 \|\|*

*mokṣaṃ kadā prayāsyāmi na jāne nṛpasattama \|*  
*evaṃ vadati viprendra vaṭasthe 'sminniśācare \|\| 111 \|\|*

*dharmaśāstraprasaṃgena tayoḥ pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam \|*  
*etasminnantare prātpaḥ kaścidvipro 'tidhārmikaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*kaliṅgadeśasaṃbhūto nānmrā garga iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vahangaṅgājalaṃ skandhe stuvan viśveśvaraṃ prabhum \|\| 113 \|\|*

108-110a. Since disrespect was shown towards the preceptor, he (Siva) turned me into a Raksasa. If a person, knowingly or unknowingly, shows contempt and disrespect towards the preceptor, his intelligence, learning, wealth and all holy observances perish. О king, the learned men say that if a man renders service unto the preceptors with great respect, he is endowed with affluence.

110b-112a. I am burnt by that curse. Internally I am being consumed by the fire of hunger. О excellent king, I do not know when I shall be liberated.” О prominent Brahmana (Narada), when the Brahma-Raksasa residing on the banyan tree was discussing thus, the sins of both of them were dispelled, as they were engaged in discussion on the topics of Dharma.

112b-113. In the meantime, a highly righteous Brahmana came there. He was born in the land of Kalinga (Orissa) He was known by the name Garga. He was carrying the holy water of the Ganga on his shoulders. He was eulogising Lord Visvesvara.

## \|\| 1.9.114-115 \|\|

*gāyannāmāni tasyaiva mudā hṛṣṭatan ruhaḥ \|*  
*tamāgataṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā piśācīrākṣasau ca tau \|\| 114 \|\|*

*prātpā naḥ pāraṇetyuktvā prādvavannūrdhvabāhavaḥ \|*  
*tena kīrtitanāmāni śrutvā dūre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*aśaktāstaṃ dharṣayitumidamūcuśca rākṣasāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. He was singing the names of Lord Siva. With a thrill of joy, his hair over his body stood on their ends. On seeing the sage arrive, the Pisaci and the Raksasa rushed at him, raising their arms aloft and saying: — “Our break-fast has arrived!” But they stood away on hearing the names recited by him, as they were unable to attack him. The Raksasa said as follows: —

## \|\| 1.9.116 \|\|

*aho vipra mahābhāga namastubhya mahātmane \|*  
*nāmakīrtanamāhātmyādrākṣasā dūragāvayam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. "O highly blessed Brahmana, salutations to you who are a noble-souled one. Thanks to the greatness of the recitation of the names of God, we, the Raksasas, have to stay away at a distance.

## \|\| 1.9.117 \|\|

*asmābhirbhakṣitāḥ pūrvaṃ viprāḥ koṭisahasraḥ \|*  
*nāmaprāvaraṇaṃ vipra rakṣati tvāṃ mahābhayayāt \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. О Brahmana, thousands and millions of Brahmanas have been formerly devoured by us. It is the covering shield of the holy names of Visnu that protects you from the great fear of death.

## \|\| 1.9.118 \|\|

*nāmaśravaṇamātreṇa rākṣasā api bho vayam \|*  
*parāṃ śāntiṃ samāpannā mahimnā hyacyutasya vai \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. О respected sir, that even we, the Raksasas have attained great tranquility and solace by merely listening to (his hallowing) names, is due to the greatness of Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.9.119 \|\|

*sarvathā tvaṃ mahābhāga rāgādiruhitohyasi \|*  
*gaṅgājalābhiṣekeṇa pāhyasmātpātakoccayāt \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. О highly blessed one, you are in every respect free from attachment and passion. Be pleased to absolve us of the heaps of sins, by making us perform the ablution with the waters of the Ganga, by sprinkling it over us.

## \|\| 1.9.120 \|\|

*harise vāparo bhūtvā yaścātmānaṃ tu tārayet \|*  
*sa tārayenagatsarvamiti śaṃsanti sūrayaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Wise and learned persons proclaim that he who redeems his own Atman by engaging himself in service to Hari, shall redeem the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.9.121 \|\|

*avahāya harernāma ghorasaṃsārabheṣajam \|*  
*kenopāyena labhyeta muktiḥ sarvatra durlabhā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Except by Hari’s name which is the panacea for all terrible ills of the worldly existence, by what other means can liberation, which is so very difficult to attain everywhere, be secured?

## \|\| 1.9.122 \|\|

*lohoḍupena pratarannimajatyudake yathā \|*  
*tayaivākṛtapuṇyāstu tārayanti kathaṃ parān \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Just as a person trying to cross a river or a sea by means of a raft of iron, sinks under water, similarly, how can they who have not performed meritorious acts, redeem others?

## \|\| 1.9.123 \|\|

*aho caritraṃ mahatāṃ sarvalokasukhā vaham \|*  
*yathā hi sarvalokānāmānandāya kalānidhiḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. О! The conduct of life of great men is conducive to the happiness of every one, just as the moon contributes to the delight of all.

## \|\| 1.9.124 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni pavitrāṇi dvijottam \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi gaṅgāyāḥ kaṇasyāpi samānina \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. О excellent Brahmana, whatever sacred and holy waters are there on the earth, they are not equal in holiness even to a particle of the waters of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.9.125 \|\|

*tulasīdalapradalasaṃmiśramapi sarṣapamātrakam \|*  
*gaṅgājalaṃ punātyeva kulānāmekaviṃśatim \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. A drop of the water of the Ganga, of the size of a mustard seed mixed with the Tulasi leaf, definiteli sanctifies twentyone generations.

## \|\| 1.9.126 \|\|

*tasmādvipra mahābhāga sarvaśāstrārthakovida \|*  
*gaṅgājalapradānena pāhmasmānpāpakarmiṇaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Hence, О highly blessed Brahmana, О expert one in the meanings of all scriptures, protect us, the perpetrators of sinful acts, by giving us the water of the Ganga.”

## \|\| 1.9.127 \|\|

*ityākhyātaṃ rākṣasaistairgaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*niśamya vismayā viṣṭo babhūva dvijasatamaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. On hearing this excellent discourse on the greatness of the Ganga related by those Raksasas, the excellent Brahmana was very much surprised.

## \|\| 1.9.128 \|\|

*eṣāmapīddaśī bhaktirgaṅgāyāṃ lokamātari \|*  
*kimu jñānaprabhāvāṇāṃ mahatāṃ puṇyaśālinām \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. (He thought) “Even in these (Raksasas,) there is such a devotion towards the Ganga, the mother of the worlds. How much more there should be devotion of the great men of meritorious deeds who are endowed with sound perfect knowledge?”

## \|\| 1.9.129 \|\|

*athāsau manasā dharmaṃ viniścitya drijottamaḥ \|*  
*sarvapūtahito bhaktaḥ prāprotīti paraṃ padam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Then the excellent Brahmana mentally came to a conclusion on the Dharma that a devotee who is a benefactor of all living beings attains the highest region.

## \|\| 1.9.130 \|\|

*tato vipraḥ kṛpāviṣṭo gaṅgājalapranuttamamam \|*  
*tulasīdalasaṃmiśraṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsvasecayat \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Then the Brahmana, full of mercy, sprinkled the excellent waters of the Ganga mixed with a Tulasi leaf over the Raksasas.

## \|\| 1.9.131 \|\|

*rākṣasāstena siktāstu sarṣapopamabindunā \|*  
*vimṛjya rākṣasaṃ bhāvamabhavandevatopamāḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. On being sprinkled by the drops of water of the size of a mustard, those Raksasas gave up their Raksasa state and became refulgent like Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.132 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ samyakte jagmurhastathaiva ca \|*  
*koṭisūryapratīkāśā babhūvurvivudharṣabhāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The Brahmana lady accompanied by her son and her husband — Brahmana Somadatta — became prominent among gods resembling a hundred million suns in brilliance.

## \|\| 1.9.133 \|\|

*śaṅkhacakragadācihnā harisārupyamāgatāḥ \|*  
*stuvanto brāhmaṇaṃ samyakte jagmurha rimāndiram \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. They were distinctly characterised by conches, discuses and the iron maces. They attained to Sarupya (similarity in form) with Hari. Eulogising the Brahmana very much, they went to the abode of Hari, i.e. Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 1.9.134 \|\|

*rājā kalmāṣapādastu nijarupaṃ samāsthitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma mahatīṃ cintāṃ dṛṣṭvā tānmuktigānadhān \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. The king Kalmasapada regained his own (Royal) form. On seeing those sinless Brahmanas being liberated, he began to think deeply.

## \|\| 1.9.135 \|\|

*tasmin rājñi suduḥkhārte gūḍharupā sarasvatī \|*  
*dharmamūlaṃ mahāvākyaṃ babhāṣe 'gādhayā girā \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. When the king was extremely distressed and miserable, a mysterious secret voice uttered in deep sonorous tone this great statement based on Dharma:

## \|\| 1.9.136 \|\|

*bho bho rājanmahābhāga na duḥkhaṃ gantumarhasi \|*  
*rājastavāpi bhāgānte mahacchreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. “O highly blessed king, it does not behove you to be miserable. О king, at the end of your enjoyment of pleasures, you also will attain to the highest beatitude (Moksa).

## \|\| 1.9.137 \|\|

*satkarmadhūtapāpā ye haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*prayānti nātra saṃdehastadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. There is no doubt that those who have washed off their sins by means of good acts and who are engaged in devotion to Hari, attain to the highest region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.9.138 \|\|

*sarvabhūtadayāyuktā dharmamārgapravartinaḥ \|*  
*prayānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ gurupūjāparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Those who are merciful towards all living beings, those who function along the path of Dharma and those who are eagerly devoted to the worship of the preceptor, attain to the highest region.”

## \|\| 1.9.139 \|\|

*itīritaṃ samākarṇya bhāratyā nṛpasatamaḥ \|*  
*manasā nirvṛttiṃ prāpyasasmāra ca gurorvacaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. On hearing this utterance of Bharati (Goddess of speech), the excellent king attained deep mental satisfaction and tranquillity and remembered the words of his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.9.140 \|\|

*stuvanguruṃ ca taṃ vignaṃ hariṃ caivātiharṣitaḥ \|*  
*pīrvavṛttaṃ ca viprāya sarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayat \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. With great delight, he praised his preceptor, that Brahmana (from Kalinga) and Lord Visnu. He narrated all his former story to that Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.9.141 \|\|

*tato nṛpastu kāliṅgaṃ praṇamya vidhirvamune \|*  
*nāmāni vyāharanviṣṇoḥ sadyo vārāṇasīṃ yayau \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. О sage, thereafter, the king made obeisance to the Brahmana from Kalinga duly. Repeating the names of Visnu, he immediately proceeded to Varanasi.

## \|\| 1.9.142 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsaṃ tatra gaṅgāyāṃ snātvā dṛṣṭvā sadānivam \|*  
*brāhmaṇīdattaśa pāttu mukto mitrasaho 'bhavat \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. He took bath in the Ganga there for six months and paid visits to god Sadasiva. King Mitrasaha thereby became free from the curse of the Brahmana lady.

## \|\| 1.9.143 \|\|

*tatastu svapurīṃ prātpo vasiṣṭena mahātmanā \|*  
*abhiṣikto munuśreṣṭha svakaṃ rājyamapālayat \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. Thereafter, he went to his capital city. О excellent sage, he was then crowned by the noble-souled Vasistha. He protected his own kingdom thereafter.

## \|\| 1.9.144 \|\|

*pālayitvā mahīṃ kṛtstrāṃ bhuktvā bhogānstriyaṃ vinā \|*  
*vaśiṣṭātprāpya santānaṃ gato mokṣaṃ nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. He ruled over the entire earth. He enjoyed all worldly pleasures except that from his queen. He got a son begot by Vasistha. Ultimately the excellent king attained salvation.

## \|\| 1.9.145 \|\|

*naitaccitraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha viṣṇorvārāṇasīguṇān \|*  
*gṛṇañchṛṇvansmarangaṅgāṃ pītvā mukto bhavennaraḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. О excellent Brahmana, it is not surprising that the man who praises the excellences of Visnu and Varanasi listens to them and muses over them and drinks the water of the Ganga, becomes liberated from Samsara.

## \|\| 1.9.146 \|\|

*tasmānmāhimne viprendra gaṅgāyāḥ śakyate nahi \|*  
*pāraṃ gantuṃ surādhīśairbrahmaviṣṇuśivarapi \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Hence, О leading Brahmana, it is not possible to reach the other shore of the great glory of the Ganga (i.e. to describe it exhaustively), even to the lords of gods, viz. Brahma, Visnu and Siva.

## \|\| 1.9.147 \|\|

*yannāmasmaraṇādeva mahāpātakakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*vimukto brahmasadanaṃ naro yāti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Undoubtedly, by merely remembering the names of the Ganga, a man becomes absolved of millions of heinous sins and attains to Brahma’s abode.

## \|\| 1.9.148 \|\|

*gaṅgā gaṅgeti yannāma sakṛdapyucyate yadā \|*  
*tadaiva pāpanimukto brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. If the name ‘Ganga’ is repeated even once, one is immediately liberated from all sins, and he is honoured in the region of god Brahma.

## Chapter 10. The Defeat of the Devas by Bali

## \|\| 1.10.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*viṣṇupādāgrasaṃbhūtā yā gaṅgetyabhidhīyate \|*  
*tadutpattiṃ vada bhrātaranugrāhyo 'smi te yadi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. О brother, if I am considered worthy of being blessed by you, kindly narrate to me the origin and other details of the river that is called the Ganga and that has its source from the feet of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.10.2 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi gaṅgotpattiṃ tavānagha \|*  
*vadṛtāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiṃva puṇyadāṃ pāpanāśinīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Sanaka narrated:*

2\. О Narada, listen. I shall relate to you, О sinless one, the source or the origin of the Ganga that bestows merits on the speakers as well as on the listeners, and destroys their sins.

## \|\| 1.10.3 \|\|

*āsīdindrādidevānāṃ janakaḥ kaśyapo muniḥ \|*  
*dakṣātmaje tasya bhārye ditiścāditireva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There was a certain sage, Kasyapa, who was the father of Indra and other gods. Diti and Aditi, the daughters of Daksa, were his wives.

## \|\| 1.10.4 \|\|

*agaditirdevamātāsti daityānāṃ jananī ditiḥ \|*  
*te tayorātmajā vipra parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Aditi was the mother of all Devas or gods and Diti was the mother of Daityas. О Brahmana, those two wives of Kasyapa and their sons vied with each other, seeking to vanquish the other.

## \|\| 1.10.5 \|\|

*sadā sapūrvadevāstu yato daityāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ādir daityo diteḥ putro hiraṇyakaśipurbalī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Daityas were called Purvadevas, as they had been always senior to Devas. The first Daitya, the son of Diti, was the powerful Hiranyakasipu.

## \|\| 1.10.6 \|\|

*prahlādastasya putro 'bhūtsumahāndaityasattamaḥ \|*  
*virocana stasya suto babhūva dvijabhaktimān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Prahlada, the extremely noble and the righteous- most Daitya, was his son. Prahlada’s son Virocana was a great devotee of Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.10.7 \|\|

*tasya putro 'titejasvī balirāsītpratāpavān \|*  
*sa eva vāhinīpālo daityānāmabhavanmuneḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. His son was the extremely brilliant and valorous Bali. О sage, he alone was the real leader of the armies of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.10.8 \|\|

*balena mahatā yukto bubhuje medinīmimām \|*  
*vijitya vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ svargaṃ jetuṃ mano dadhe \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was endowed with great strength. He enjoyed this earth. After conquering the entire earth, he became desirous of conquering the heaven.

## \|\| 1.10.9 \|\|

*gajāśca yasyāyutakoṭilakṣāstāvanta evāścarathā munīndra \|*  
*gajegaje pañcaśatī padāteḥ kiṃ varṇyate tasya camūrvariṣṭā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О excellent sage, his elephants were in billions. The number of his horses and the chariots came to as many. For every elephant, the number of foot-soldiers was five hundred. How can his excellent army be described adequately?

## \|\| 1.10.10 \|\|

*amātyakoṭyagrasarāvamātyau kumbhāṇḍanāmāpyatha kūpakarṇaḥ \|*  
*pitrā samaṃ śauryaparākramābhyāṃ bāṇo baleḥ putraśatagrajo 'bhūt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. His ministers were Kumbhanda and Kupakarna who surpassed the leaders of millions of ministers. Bali had a hundred sons, the eldest of whom was Bana. He was equal to his father in heroism and prowess.

## \|\| 1.10.11 \|\|

*baliḥ surāñjetumanāḥ pravṛttaḥ sainyena yukto mahatā pratasthe \|*  
*dhvajātapartrairgaganāburāśestaraṅgavidyutsmaraṇaṃ prakurvan \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Bali was actuated by a desire of vanquishing the gods. He started the campaign accompanied by a great army. Through banners and umbrellas, he reminded the people of the flashes of lightning which were the billows on the ocean in the form of the sky.

## \|\| 1.10.12 \|\|

*avāpya vṛtrāripuraṃ surārī rurogha daityairmṛgarājagāḍhaiḥ \|*  
*suraśca yuddhāya purāttathaiva viniryayurvajrakarādayaśca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Arriving at the city of the slayer of Vrtra (viz. Amaravati), the demon laid siege to it through Daityas, strong and vehement like lions. The thunder-bolt-bearing Indra and other gods came out of the city for fighting with them.

## \|\| 1.10.13 \|\|

*tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghoraṃ gīrvāṇadaityayo \|*  
*kalpāntameghānirdhoṣaṃ ḍiṇḍiṃmadhvanisaṃbhramam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A terrible battle ensued thereafter between the gods and Daityas, with shouts like thunders of clouds at the end of the universe, mixed with the sounds of big drums.

## \|\| 1.10.14 \|\|

*mumucuḥ śarajālāni daḥtyāḥ sumanasāṃ bale \|*  
*devāśca daityasenāsu saṃgrāme 'tyantadāruṇe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In that extremely terrible battle, Daityas discharged volleys of arrows on the army of Devas. The gods too retaliated like-wise on the army of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.10.15 \|\|

*jahi dāraya bhindhīte chindhi māraya tāḍaya \|*  
*ityevaṃ sumahānghoṣo vadatāṃ senayorabhūt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Yelling sounds and shouts came up from both the armies (such. as ‘Kill’, ‘Tear’, ‘Hit’, ‘Split’, ‘Annihilate’, ‘Strike down’, etc.

## \|\| 1.10.16-17 \|\|

*śaradundubhinidhvānaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ suradviṣām \|*  
*bhāṅkāraiḥ syandanānāṃ ca bāṇakreṅgāraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aśvānāṃ heṣitaiścaiva gajānāṃ bṛṃhitaistathā \|*  
*ṭaṅgārairdhanuṣāṃ caiva lokaḥ śabdatmayo 'bhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The whole world was filled with various sounds such as the sounds of conches, whistling arrows, kettle-drums, the roaring sound of the shouting demons, the creaking of the chariots, the hissing of the arrows, the neighing of horses, the trumpeting of the elephants and the twanging sound of the bow-strings.

## \|\| 1.10.18 \|\|

*surāsuravinirmuktabāṇaniṣpeṣajānale \|*  
*akālapralayaṃ mene nirīkṣya sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Beholding the fire that originated from the mutual friction of the shafts discharged by gods and Asuras, the whole universe regarded it as an untimely Pralaya (the dissolution of the world).

## \|\| 1.10.19 \|\|

*babhau devadviṣāṃ senā sphuracchastraughadhāriṇī \|*  
*caladvidyunnibhā rātriśchāditā jaladairiva \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The army of the enemies of gods, wielding a stream of refulgent weapons shone like the night over-cast with clouds with streaks of lightning flashing across.

## \|\| 1.10.20 \|\|

*tasminyuddhe mahādhorairgirīn kṣitpān surāribhiḥ \|*  
*nārācaiścūrṇayāmāsurvevāste laghuvikramāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In that war, the agile, active and valorous gods, by means of their arrows, smashed to smithereens the huge boulders of mountainous rocks, hurled by the Asuras.

## \|\| 1.10.21 \|\|

*kecitsatāḍayāmāsurnāgairnāgānrathānrathaiḥ \|*  
*aśvairaśvāṃśca kecittu gadādaṇḍairathārddayan \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Some of them confronted the elephants with their elephants, the chariots by means of their chariots, the horses with other horses. Some hit them with the handles of maces and iron bars.

## \|\| 1.10.22 \|\|

*paridhaistāḍitāḥ kecitpetuḥ śoṇitakarddame \|*  
*samuktrāntāsavaḥ kecidvimānāni samāśritāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Some of them, on being hit with Parighas (Iron clubs), fell into the marsh of blood. Some of them whose vital breath had come out i.e. (died), occupied the aerial cars.

## \|\| 1.10.23 \|\|

*ye daityā nihatā devaiḥ prasahya saṅgare tadā \|*  
*te devabhāvamāpannā daiteyānsamupādravan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those Daityas who were forcibly killed by the gods in the battle, assumed the forms of devas and rushed at demons.

## \|\| 1.10.24 \|\|

*atha daityagaṇāḥ krudvāstaḍyamānāḥ survairbhṛśam \|*  
*śastrairbahuvidhairddevānnijadhnuratidāruṇāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the extremely terrible hosts of demons who became infuriated on being beaten soundly by the gods, hit back gods by means of various kinds of weapons (such as)

## \|\| 1.10.25-27 \|\|

*dṛṣadbhirbhidipālaiśca khaḍgaiḥ paraśutomaraiḥ \|*  
*paridhaiśchurikābhiśca kuntaiścakraiśca śaṅkubhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*musalairaṅkuśeśvaiva lāṅgalaiḥ paṭṭiśaistathā \|*  
*śaktyopalaiḥ śataghrībhiḥ pāśaiśca talamuṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śūlairnālīkanārācaiḥ kṣepaṇīyaiḥsamudraraiḥ \|*  
*rathāśvanāgapadagaiḥ saṅkulo vavṛdhe raṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Rocks, Bhindipalas (a cubit-long wooden club), swords, axes, tomaras, (Javelins), Parighas (Iron clubs), daggers, spears, discus, pointed poniards, pestles, goads, plough-shares, Pattisas (a spear with sharp points) Jaktis, stones, Sataghnis (a cylinderical piece of wood studded with iron pikes and capable of killing hundreds of people), nooses, mailed fists, tridents, pointed iron spikes and pounding rods. The battle grew more and more tumultuous and fierce through the confrontation between the chariots, horses, elephants and foot-soldiers.

## \|\| 1.10.28 \|\|

*devāśca vividhāstrāṇi daiteyebhyaḥ samākṣipan \|*  
*evamaṣṭasahasrāṇi yuddhamāsītsudāruṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The gods hurled various kinds of weapons at Daityas. In this way, the extremely terrible battle continued for eight thousand years.

## \|\| 1.10.29 \|\|

*atha daityabale vṛddhe parābhūtā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*suralokaṃ parityatajya sarve bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the army of Daityas became powerful, the defeated heaven-dwellers abandoned their celestial region in great fright and fied precipitately.

## \|\| 1.10.30-33 \|\|

*nararupaparicchannā viceru ravanītale \|*  
*vairocanistribhuvanaṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bubhuje 'vyāhataiścaryapravṛddhaśrīrmahābalaḥ \|*  
*ityāja cāśvameghaiḥ sa viṣṇuprīṇanatatparaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*indratvaṃ cākarotsvarge dikpālatvaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*devānāṃ prīṇanārthāya yaiḥ kriyante dvijairmakhāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*teṣu yajñeṣu sarveṣu havirbhuṅkte sa daityarāṭ \|*  
*aditiḥ svātmajānvīkṣya devamātātiduḥkhitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. The defeated gods disguised themselves as human beings and wandered over the earth. The son of Virocana, Bali, was devotedly attached to Narayana. He enjoyed the three worlds without any obstruction to his overlordship. His prosperity flourished. The mighty Daitya desirous of propitiating Visnu, performed many horse-sacrifices. He discharged the duties of Indra in the heaven as well as those of the guardians of cardinal points. The king of Daityas began to part- take of oblations offered in all various sacrifices performed by Brahmanas for propitiating Devas. On seeing her sons in such a plight Aditi, the mother of Devas, became distressed.

## \|\| 1.10.34-41 \|\|

*vṛthātra nivasāmīti matvāgāddhimavadgiram \|*  
*śakrasyaiśvaryamicchantī daityānāṃ ca parājayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*haridhyānaparā bhūtvā tapastepe 'tiduṣkaram \|*  
*kiñcitkālaṃ samāsīnā tiṣṭantī ca tataḥ param \|\| 35 \|\|*

*pādenaikena suciraṃ tataḥ pādāgramātrataḥ \|*  
*kañcitkālaṃ phalāhārā tataḥ śīrṇadalāśanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tato jalāśamā vāyubhojanāhāravarjitā \|*  
*sañcidānandasandohaṃ dhyāyatyātmānamatmanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*divyābdānāṃ sahasraṃ sā tapo 'tapyata nārada \|*  
*durantaṃ tattapaḥ śrutvā daiteyā māyino 'ditim \|\| 38 \|\|*

*devatārupamāsthāya saṃprocurbalinoditāḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tapyate mātaḥ śarīrapariśoṣaṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yadi jananti daiteyā mahahukhaṃ tato bhavet \|*  
*tyajedaṃ duḥkhabahulaṃ kāyaśoṣaṇakāraṇam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*prayāsasādhyaṃ sukṛtaṃ na praśaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ \|*  
*śarīraṃ yantato rakṣyaṃ dharmasādhanatatparaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

34-35a. She thought to herself, “I am staying in vain”, and then she went to the mountain Himalaya. Wishing for the prosperity of Indra and the defeat of Daityas, she who was devotedly attached to meditation on Hari, performed a severe penance.

35b-38a. While performing the penance she did it in the sitting posture for some time and then performed it while in a standing posture. For a long time, she stood on only one leg. Thereafter, she stood on the tip of her feet. For some time her diet was fruits. Thereafter, she subsisted on the withered leaves fallen down from trees. Then she lived only on water. Afterwards she gave up food altogether and subsisted on air only. She began to meditate on the Supreme Atman through her individual Atman. She contemplated on the Deity, the embodiment of existence, knowledge and bliss. О Narada she performed the penance for one thousand divine years.

38b-41. On hearing of that unending penance of Aditi, Daityas, expert in their science of creating illusions, assumed the form of Devas as per command of Bali. They approached Aditi and said, “O mother, why do you perform this penance desiccating your body. If Daityas come to know of this, great misery may befall us. Leave off this (penance) causing so much misery and drying up your body. Learned men do not approve of a meritorious act which requires to be achieved only with very great difficulty and troubles. Those who are eager to achieve Dharma should assiduously preserve and take care of their body.

## \|\| 1.10.42 \|\|

*ye śarīramupekṣante te syurātmavighātinaḥ \|*  
*sukhaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭa subhage putrānasmānna khedaya \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Those who neglect their body are the slayers of Atman. О fortunate and blessed lady, stay here happily. Please do not cause grief to us, your sons.

## \|\| 1.10.43-46 \|\|

*mātrā hīnā janā mātarmṛtaprāyā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*gāvo vā paśavo vāpiyatra gāvo mahīruhāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*na labhante sukhaṃ kiñcinmātrā hīnā mṛtopamāḥ \|*  
*daridro vāpi rogī vā deśāntaragato 'pi vā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*māturdarśanamātreṇa labhate paramāṃ mudam \|*  
*anne vā salile vāpi dhanādau vā priyāsu ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kadācidvimukho yāti jano mātari ko 'pi na \|*  
*yasya mātā gṛhe nāsti yatra dharmaparāyaṇā \|*  
*sādhvī ca strī patiprāṇā gantavyaṃ tena vai vanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-45a. О mother, undoubtedly those who are devoid of their mothers are no better than dead, whether they be cows or other animals or even trees. None of these derives any happiness without their mother. Whether one is an indigent fellow or an ailing one, or one in exile in a foreign land, one derives the greatest joy at the mere sight of one’s mother.

45b-46. One may perhaps develop aversion to food, water, richs, etc. and even to lovely women. But there iis none who turns his face away from his mother. If one has neither a mother nor a chaste wife devoted to religion (righteousness) and loyally attached to her husband at home, he should rather betake himself to the forest.

## \|\| 1.10.47 \|\|

*dharmaśca nārāyaṇabhaktihīnāṃ dhanaṃ ca sadbhogavivarjitaṃ hi \|*  
*gṛhaṃ ca māryātanayervihīnaṃ yathā tathā mātṛvihīnamartyaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A person devoid of his mother is like the righteous path of life devoid of devotion to Narayana, or like wealth which is not enjoyed in any decent manner or like house-hold without a wife or a son.

## \|\| 1.10.48 \|\|

*tasmāddevi paritrāhi duḥkhārtānātmajāṃstavā \|*  
*ityuktāpyaditirdaipyairna cacāla samādhitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, О gentle lady, save us who are your sons and who are extremely distressed. Even though she was thus importuned by Daityas, Aditi did not get disturbed from her trance.

## \|\| 1.10.49 \|\|

*evamuktvāsurāḥ sarve haridhyānaparāyaṇām \|*  
*nirīkṣya krodhasaṃyuktā hantuṃ cakrurmanoratham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When Daityas found that in spite of their speech to her, Aditi was still absorbed in meditation on Hari, they were extremely infuriated and wanted to kill her.

## \|\| 1.10.50 \|\|

*kalpāntameghanirghoṣāḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanāḥ \|*  
*daṃṣṭragrairasṛjanvahniṃ so 'dahatkānanaṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Due to fury, their eyes turned red. They roared like clouds at the end of the Kalpa (when the universe is dissolved). By the gnashing of the tips of their curved fangs (in anger), they created fire which burnt down the forest instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.10.51-52 \|\|

*śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ nānājīvasamākulam \|*  
*tenaiva dagdhā daiteyā ye pradharṣayituṃ gatāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*saivāvaśiṣṭā jananī surāṇāmabdācchatādacyutasaktacitā \|*  
*saṃrakṣitā viṣṇusudarśanena daityāntakena svajanānukampinā \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The forest extended to a hundred Yojanas. It was teeming with various kinds of living beings. The very same fire burnt Daityas who had gone there to destroy Aditi. Only Aditi, the mother of gods, remained alive. She had been meditating on Acyuta (Visnu) for hundreds of years. She was protected by the Sudarsana discus of Visnu who killed Daityas and took pity on his own devotees.

## Chapter 11. The Glory of the Ganga: The Origin of the River

## \|\| 1.11.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*aho hyatyadbhutaṃ proktaṃ tvayā bhrātaridaṃ mama \|*  
*sa vahniraditiṃ muktvā kathaṃ tānadahatkṣaṇāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. You have mentioned, my brother, an extremely miraculous incident. How did that forest fire spare Aditi and burnt all Daityas in a moment?

## \|\| 1.11.2 \|\|

*vadāditermahāsattvaṃ viśeṣāścaryakāraṇam \|*  
*paropadeśaniratāḥ sajjanā hi munīśvarāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Be pleased to tell me in details about the immense inherent strength of Aditi that caused this special surprise. Indeed, prominent sages and good men are always engaged in tendering advice to others.

## \|\| 1.11.3 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada māhātmyaṃ haribhaktiratātmanām \|*  
*haridhyānaparānsādhūnkaḥ samarthaḥ prabādhitum \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Sanaka replied:*

3\. О Narada, listen to the greatness of those who revel in devotion to Hari. Is there any person who is capable of harassing saintly persons engaged in the meditation of Hari?

## \|\| 1.11.4 \|\|

*haribhaktiparo yatra tatra brahmā hariḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*devāḥ siddhā munīśvāśca nityaṃ tiṣṭanti sattamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Gods Brahma, Hari, Siva and others, Siddhas and prominent leaders of sages — all stay permanently at the residence of a person who is engaged in devotion to Hari.

## \|\| 1.11.5 \|\|

*harirāste mahābhāga hṛdaye śāntacetasām \|*  
*harināmaparāṇāṃ ca kimu dhyānaratātmanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О highly blessed Narada, Lord Hari is enshrined in the hearts of his devotees who are serene-minded and are always engaged in repeating his name. Need it be said that he abides in the hearts of those who are engaged in contemplating on him?

## \|\| 1.11.6 \|\|

*śivapūjārato vāpi viṣṇupūjāparo 'pi vā \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭati tatraiva lakṣmīḥ sarvāśca devatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Laksmi, the goddess of wealth, and all the deities stay only there, where a person is engaged in Siva’s worship or where one devoted to the worship of Visnu, resides.

## \|\| 1.11.7 \|\|

*yatra pūjāparo viṣṇorvahnistatra na bādhate \|*  
*rājā vā taskaro vāpi vyādhayaśca na santi hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Neither a fire nor a tyrant nor a thief can molest any person devoted to Visnu’s worship. Nor is he affected by diseases.

## \|\| 1.11.8 \|\|

*pretāḥ piśācāḥ kūṣmāṇḍagrahā bālagrahāstathā \|*  
*ḍākinyo rākṣasāścaiva na bādhante 'cyutārcakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Neither ghosts nor evil spirits nor the Kushrpanda (evil spirits), evil planets, nor the goblins that attack children nor Dakinis (witches) nor Raksasas can dare to trouble a worshipper of Acyuta.

## \|\| 1.11.9 \|\|

*parapīḍāratā ye tu bhūtavetālakādayaḥ \|*  
*naśyanti yatra sadbhakto harilakṣmyarcane rataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Those Bhutas, Vetalas (goblins and genii) and others, who take delight in afflicting others, take to flight from the residence of an excellent devotee engaged in the worship of Hari and Laksmi.

## \|\| 1.11.10 \|\|

*jitendriyaḥ sarvahito dharmakarmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭati tatraiva sarvatīrthāni devatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All the sacred places and Deities stay there only, where a person who has subdued his sense-organs, or one who is a benefactor unto all, or one who is devoted to Dharma and holy rites, stays.

## \|\| 1.11.11 \|\|

*nimiṣaṃ nimiṣārddhaṃ vā yatra tiṣṭanti yoginaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva sarvaśreyāṃsi tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All fortunes and blessings are found at that place only where yogins stay even for a moment or a half. That spot is a holy place and that is a real penance-grove.

## \|\| 1.11.12 \|\|

*yannāmoccāraṇādeva sarve naśyantyupadravāḥ \|*  
*stotrairvāpyarhaṇābhirvā kimu dhyānena kathyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All troubles disappear at the mere utterance of Hari’s names. What need be said of those who propitiate him through eulogies, worship or through meditation?

## \|\| 1.11.13 \|\|

*evaṃ tenāgninā vipra dagdhaṃ sāsurakānanam \|*  
*sāditirnaiva dagdhābhūdviṣṇucakrābhira kṣitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Brahmana, in this way, the whole forest along with Asuras was consumed by the fire. But Aditi was not even scorched, since she was protected by the discus of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.11.14 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannavadanaḥ pahmapatrāyatekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*prādurāsītsamīpe 'syāḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereupon, the gracious-looking Lord with a pleasant countenance, and eyes large like the petals of a lotus, revealed himself just in front of her, wielding in his hands a conch, the discus Sudarsana, and the mace Kaumodaki.

## \|\| 1.11.15 \|\|

*īṣadvāsyasphuraddantaprabhābhāṣitadiṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*spṛśankareṇa puṇyena prāha kaśyapavallabhām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Illuminating various quarters with the lustre of his refulgent teeth which appeared slightly as he smiled gently, and touching the beloved wife of Kafyapa with his holy hand, the Lord said:

## \|\| 1.11.16 \|\|

*śrībhagavānanuvāca*  
*devamātaḥ prasanno 'smi tapasārādhitastvayā \|*  
*ciraṃ śrāntāsi bhadraṃ te bhaviśaṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*The glorious Lord said:*

16\. “O mother of Devas, I am pleased with you, by virtue of your propitiation through performance of penance for a long time. You are exhausted. You will certainly be blessed with good fortune.

## \|\| 1.11.17 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya dāsyāmi yatte manasi rocate \|*  
*mā bhairbhadre mahābhāge dhruvaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Seek any boon that you cherish in your heart and I shall grant it to you. О gentle Lady, you need not be afraid. Good fortune will certainly come to your lot.”

## \|\| 1.11.18 \|\|

*ityuktādevamātā sā devadevena cakriṇā \|*  
*tuṣṭāva praṇipatyainaṃ sarvalokasukhāvaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The mother of Devas who was thus addressed by the discus-bearing Lord of the gods bowed to him, and eulogised the Lord, the bestower of happiness unto all people.

## \|\| 1.11.19 \|\|

*aditiruvāca*  
*namaste devadeveśa sarvavyāpiñjanārdanā \|*  
*sattvādiguṇabhedena lokavyāpārakāraṇa \|\| 19 \|\|*

*Aditi prayed:*

19\. (‘Salutation to you О Janardana, the Lord of the chiefs of Devas, О omnipresent one, you are the cause of the functioning of the world through Sattva and other Gunas.

## \|\| 1.11.20 \|\|

*namaste bahuparupāyārupāya ca mahātmane \|*  
*sarvaikaruparupāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I bow to you who have innumerable forms and arc still a formless one, to you who are the Supreme Soul. Salutations to you who comprise all forms within yourself. Obeisance to you who possess all excellences and are still without an attribute.

## \|\| 1.11.21 \|\|

*namaste lokanāthāya paramajñānarupiṇe \|*  
*sadbhaktajanavātsalyaśāline maṅgalātmane \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I bow to you, the Lord of the worlds, the embodiment of Supreme spiritual knowledge. Salutations to the Deity ever favourably disposed to good devotees. Obeisance to you who are of auspicious nature.

## \|\| 1.11.22 \|\|

*yasyāvatārarupāṇi hyarcayanti munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*tamādipuruṣaṃ devaṃ namāmi hyarthasiddhaye \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For the achievement of desired object, I bow unto that Lord, the Primordial Person whose incarnated forms are worshipped by prominent sages.

## \|\| 1.11.23 \|\|

*śrutayo yaṃ na jānanti na jānanti ca sūrayaḥ \|*  
*taṃ namāmi jagaddhetuṃ samāyaṃ cāpyamāyinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I bow down to that Cause of the universe, the Controller of Maya, yet devoid of Maya (i.e. not influenced by her) whom the Srutis do not know and who is beyond the comprehension of sages.

## \|\| 1.11.24 \|\|

*yasyāvalokanaṃ citraṃ māyopadravakāraṇam \|*  
*jagadrūpaṃ jagaddhetuṃ taṃ vandeṃ sarvavanditam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I salute to him whom all pay obeisance, who is of a mysteriously surprising vision; who is the cause of the removal of Maya, whose form constitutes the whole of the universe, and who is the cause of the universe.

## \|\| 1.11.25 \|\|

*yatpādāmbujakiñjalkasevārakṣitamastakāḥ \|*  
*avāpuḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ taṃ vande kamalādhavam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I offer obeisance unto the consort of Kamala (the Goddess Laksmi). People who bow to his feet (lit. whose forehead is saved by the service rendered to the filaments of his lotus-like feet) attain the highest Siddhi (Moksa).

## \|\| 1.11.26 \|\|

*yasya brahmādayo devā mahimānaṃ na vai viduḥ \|*  
*atyāsannaṃ ca bhaktānāṃ taṃ vande bhaktasaṃginam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. God Brahma and other Devas do not comprehend his glory, but he is very close to his devotees. I salute that close associate of devotees.

## \|\| 1.11.27 \|\|

*yo devastyaktasaṅgānāṃ śāntānaṃ karuṇārṇavaḥ \|*  
*karoti hyātmanaḥ saṅgaṃ taṃ devaṃ saṅgavarjitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Though he himself is absolutely unattached and companionless, the Lord who is the ocean of mercy, blesses with his contact, people who have renounced all association and attachment, and who are calm and quiet. I bow to him.

## \|\| 1.11.28 \|\|

*yajñeśvaraṃ yajñakarmasu niṣṭitam \|*  
*namāmi yajñaphaladaṃ yajñakarmaprabodhakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I salute to the Lord of sacrifices; one who is the very rite of performance of sacrifices; one who is established in the rites of sacriflces; ohe who bestows the fruit of sacrifices; one who enlightens people about the sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 1.11.29 \|\|

*ajāmilo 'pi pāpātmā yannāmoccāraṇādanu \|*  
*prātpavānparamaṃ dhāma taṃ vande lokasākṣiṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I bow down to that Lord, who is the witness unto all the universe. By uttering his name, even Ajamila, the sinning soul, instantaneously attained to the Supreme region (Vaikuntha).

## \|\| 1.11.30 \|\|

*harirupī mahādevaḥ śivarupī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*iti lokasya netā yastaṃ namāmi jagadgurum \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Mahadeva is a form of Hari and Janardana is in the form of Siva. Thus, that Lord is the leader of the world. I bow down to that preceptor of the universe.

## \|\| 1.11.31 \|\|

*brahmādyā api deveśā yanmāyāpāśayantritāḥ \|*  
*na jānanti paraṃ bhāvaṃ taṃ vande sarvanāyakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I bow to the Leader of all, the noose of whose Maya binds and restrains Brahma and other lords of gods who, therefore, do not know his essential, Supreme nature.

## \|\| 1.11.32 \|\|

*hyatpahmastho 'piñyogyānāṃ dūrastha iva bhāsate \|*  
*pramāṇātītasadbhāvastaṃ vande jñānasākṣiṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I salute to that witness of perfect wisdom who appears to be stationed far away, though (actually) he is enthroned in the lotus of the heart of Yogins. his very presence is beyond the scope of cognition by means of valid knowledge.

## \|\| 1.11.33 \|\|

*yanmukhaḥ drvāhyaṇo jāto bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyo 'jani \|*  
*ūrvorvaiśyaḥ samutpannaḥ padyāṃ śūdro 'bhyajāyata \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Obeisance unto that Lord from whose mouth was born the Brahmana, from whose arms, came forth the Ksattriya; from whose thighs was born the VaiSya and from whose feet the Sudra was born.

## \|\| 1.11.34 \|\|

*manasaścandramā jāto jātaḥ sūryaśca cakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*mukhādagnistarthendraśca prāṇādvāyurajāyata \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. From whose mind was evolved the moon, from whose eyes the sun was born, from whose mouth Agni the fire God and Indra came forth, from whose Prana (vital breath) the wind-god was born.

## \|\| 1.11.35 \|\|

*ṛgyajuḥsāmarupāya satyasvaragatātmane \|*  
*ṣaḍaṅgarupiṇe tubhyaṃ bhūyobhūyo namo namaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I bow to the Lord who is the embodiment of the Rk, Yajus and Saman (Vedas), whose Atman has permeated the seven notes of the musical scale. I bow to you again and again — you whose form is comprised of six Angas.

## \|\| 1.11.36 \|\|

*tvamindraḥ pavanaḥ somastvamīśānastvamantakaḥ \|*  
*tvamagnirnirṛtiścaiva varuṇastvaṃ divākaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О Lord, you are Indra, Pavana (the wind God), Soma (the moon God), you are Isana, you are the annihilator (of the world); you are Agni (the fire God) Nirrti, (the Deity of death); you are Varuna, the Lord of the seas and also Divakara, the sun-god.

## \|\| 1.11.37 \|\|

*devāśca sthāvarāścaiva piśācāścaiva rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*girayaḥ siddhagandharvānadyo bhūmiśca sāgarāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The celestial residents, the immobile beings, Pisacas, Raksasas, mountains, Siddhas, Gandharvas (Heavenly musicians), the rivers, earth and oceans — all these are your manifestations.

## \|\| 1.11.38 \|\|

*tvameva jagatāmīśo yatrāsi tvaṃ parātparaḥ \|*  
*tvadrūpamakhilaṃ deva tasmānnityaṃ namo 'stu te \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You alone are the Lord of the worlds; wherever you are, you are greater than the greatest; everything exists within your person; О Lord, my obeisance be to you for ever.

## \|\| 1.11.39 \|\|

*anāthānātha sarvajña bhūtadevendravigraha \|*  
*daiteyairbādhitānputrānmama pāhi janārdana \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О protector of the helpless! О omniscient Lord! О Lord, who comprise within your body all living beings right upto the Lord of gods. О Janardana, protect my sons who are harrassed by Daityas”.

## \|\| 1.11.40 \|\|

*iti stutvā devamātā devaṃ natvā punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā harṣāśrukṣālitastanī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Eulogising him thus and bowing again and again unto the Lord, the mother of the Devas spoke with palms joined in reverence, and tears of joy drenching her bosom.

## \|\| 1.11.41 \|\|

*anugrāhyāsmi deveṃśa tvayā sarvādikāraṇa \|*  
*akaṇṭakāṃ śriyāṃ dehi matsutānāṃ divaukasām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “O Lord of Devas; О the first cause of everything, it behoves you to bless me. Be pleased to grant unto my sons, the heaven-dwellers, prosperity, freedom from nuisance and troubles.

## \|\| 1.11.42 \|\|

*antaryyāmiñjagadrūpa sarvajñā parameśvara \|*  
*ajñātaṃ kiṃ tava śrīśa kiṃ māmīhayasi prabho \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О indwelling soul of the world! One immanent in the universe! О omniscient! Supreme Lord! What is unknown to you, О Lord of Laksmi? What is it that you make me long for (is already known to you)?

## \|\| 1.11.43 \|\|

*tathāpi tava vakṣyāmi yanme manasi rocate \|*  
*vṛthāputrāsmi deveśa daiteyaiḥ paripīḍitā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. I shall, however, tell you what appeals to my mind. О Lord of Devas, I have become as if bereaved of my sons. The existence of my sons is in vain and futile, as they are harassed by Daityas.

## \|\| 1.11.44 \|\|

*tānna hiṃsitumicchāmi yataste 'pi sutā mama \|*  
*tānahatvā śriyaṃ dehi matsutebhyaḥ sureśvara \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I do not wish to cause any harm unto Daityas, since they too are my sons. О Lord of gods, without killing them, bless my sons with fortune and prosperity.”

## \|\| 1.11.45 \|\|

*ityukto devedeveśaḥ punaḥ prītimupāgataḥ \|*  
*uvāca harṣayanvipra devamātaramādarāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The Lord of the chiefs of Devas who was thus addressed again, became delighted. О Brahmana, he respectfully addressed the mother of Devas in words giving her delight.

## \|\| 1.11.46 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*prīto 'smi devi bhadraṃ te bhaviṣyāmi suto hyaham \|*  
*yataḥ sapantiputreṣu vātsalyaṃ devi durlabham \|\| 46 \|\|*

*The Lord said:*

46\. О gentle lady! I am pleased with you. May good betide you. I shall, therefore, be your son, since О goddess, affection towards sons of one’s со-wife is rare.

## \|\| 1.11.47 \|\|

*tvayā tu yatkṛtaṃ stotraṃ tatpaṭhānti narāstu ye \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃpadvarā putrā na hīyante kadācana \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Men who read and recite this prayer composed by you will never be deficient in excellent riches and sons.

## \|\| 1.11.48 \|\|

*tvātmaje vānyaputre vā yaḥ samatvena vartate \|*  
*na tasya putraśokaḥ syādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He who treats his own son as well as that of another person with equality, will never experience sorrow, due to separation or bereavement of his son. This is the eternal Dharma.”

## \|\| 1.11.49 \|\|

*aditiruvāca*  
*tāha voḍhuṃ kṣamā deva tvāmādyapuruṣaṃ param \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāṇḍaromāṇaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvakāraṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*Aditi said:*

49\. “O Lord, I am unable to bear you (in my womb) — you who are the Supreme First Person, the greatest Being with innumerable cosmic eggs constituting the hair on your body; you, the Lord of all, the cause or creator of the world.

## \|\| 1.11.50 \|\|

*yatprabhāvaṃ na jānanti śrutayaḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*tamahaṃ devadeveśaṃ dhārayāma kithaṃ prabho \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О Lord, how can I bear that Supreme chief of the leaders of gods, whose prowess even the arutis and all the deities cannot comprehend.

## \|\| 1.11.51 \|\|

*aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ parātparataraṃ prabhum \|*  
*dhārayāmi kathaṃ deva tvāmahaṃ puruṣottamam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О Lord, you are the Purusottama (the Supreme Person), the eternal Lord (hence unborn), minuter than the minutest and greater than the greatest. How can I bear you?

## \|\| 1.11.52 \|\|

*mahāyātakayukto 'pi yannāmasmṛtimātrataḥ \|*  
*mucyate sa kathaṃ devogrāmyeṣu janimarhati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. How docs that Lord, the very remembrance of whose name liberates a man, vitiated by great sins, deserve the birth among the rustic and the unrefined?

## \|\| 1.11.53 \|\|

*yathā śūkaramatsyādyā avatārāstava prabho \|*  
*tathāyamapi ko veda tava viśveśa ceṣṭitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. May this incarnation of yours, О Lord, be like that of your other incarnations, like the boar, the fish. Who can comprehend your activities, О Lord of the universe?

## \|\| 1.11.54 \|\|

*tvatpādapahmapraṇatātvannāmasmṛtitatparā \|*  
*tvāmeva cintaye deva yathecchāsi tathā kuru \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I bow down to your lotus feet. I am devotedly attached to the remembrance of your names. О Lord, I contemplate exclusively on you. Do as you please.”

## \|\| 1.11.55 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*tayoktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*dattvābhayaṃ devamāturidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 55 \|\|*

*Sanaka Said:*

55\. On hearing the words uttered by her, Janardana, the Lord of Devas, granted to the mother of gods the boon of fearlessness (and security from dangers). He addressed her the following words:

## \|\| 1.11.56 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*satyamuktaṃ mahābhāge tvayā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi śṛṇu vakṣyāmi guhyādguhyataraṃ śubhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

*The glorious Lord said:*

56\. “O highly blessed Lady, there is no doubt about the truth that has been uttered by you; however, О auspicious lady, I shall tell you the secret of secrets.

## \|\| 1.11.57 \|\|

*rāgadveṣavihīnā ye madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*vaṃhati satataṃ teṃ māṃ gatāsūyā adāmbhikāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. My votaries who are devoid of passionate attachment and hatred and are devoutly attached to me, who are devoid of jealousy and are free from hypocrisy, do perpetually bear me.

## \|\| 1.11.58 \|\|

*paropatāpavimukhāḥ śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*matkathāśravaṇāsaktā vahanti satataṃ hi mām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who are disinclined to cause injury to others, who are interested and engaged in devotion to Siva, and who are intensely devoted to the listening of my stories, perpetually bear me.

## \|\| 1.11.59 \|\|

*pativratāḥ pariprāṇāḥ patibhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*vahanti satataṃ devi striyo 'pi tyaktapratsarāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О gentle Lady, even those chaste women who love their husbands like their very vital breath, and are exclusively devoted to their husbands and have eschewed malice and rivalry, perpetually bear me.

## \|\| 1.11.60 \|\|

*mātāpitrośca śuśrūṣurgurubhakto 'tithipriyaḥ \|*  
*hitakṛdvāhyaṇānāṃ yaḥ sa māṃ vahati sarvadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He who renders service to his parents, is a devotee to the preceptor, who likes to receive and serve guests, and who is benefactor unto the Brahmanas, perpetually bears me.

## \|\| 1.11.61 \|\|

*puṇyatīrtharatā nityaṃ satsaṅganiratāstathā \|*  
*lokānugrahaśīlāśca satataṃ te vahanti mām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those who always take delight in visiting holy places, who are engaged in associating themselves with saintly people, and who are habitually obliging and favouring other people — all these perpetually bear me.

## \|\| 1.11.62 \|\|

*paropakāraviratāḥ paradravyaparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*naṣuṃsakāḥ parastrīṣu te vahanti ca māṃ sadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who are interested in helping others, those who are not desirous of the wealth of another person and who cherish no illicit desire when other men’s wives are concerned — these bear me perpetually.

## \|\| 1.11.63 \|\|

*tulasyupāsanaratāḥ sadā nāmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*gorakṣaṇaparā ye ca satataṃ māṃ vahanti te \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who always worship with Tulasi plant, those who are attached to the names of the Lord and those who carefully protect cows — all these bear me perpetually.

## \|\| 1.11.64 \|\|

*pratigrahanivṛttā ye parānnavimukhāstathā \|*  
*annodakapradātāro vahṝnti satataṃ hi mām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Those who desist from accepting monetary gifts, those who do not take food at another man’s house and those who make gifts of food and water to the needy, do perpetually bear me.

## \|\| 1.11.65 \|\|

*tvaṃ tu devi patiprāṇā sādhvī bhūtahite ratā \|*  
*saṃprāpya putrabhāvaṃ te sādhayiṣye manoratham \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О gentle Lady, you value your husband like your own vital breath; you are virtuous and you take delight in the welfare of all living beings. Hence, shall assume the state of being your son and fulfil your desire.”

## \|\| 1.11.66 \|\|

*ityuktvā devedevaśo hyaditiṃ devamātaram \|*  
*dattvā kaṇṭhagatāṃ mālāmabhayaṃ ca tirodadhe \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After addressing thus to Aditi the mother of Devas, the Lord of the chiefs of Devas gave her the necklace from his neck and blessed her with fearlessness and protection from danger, and vanished.

## \|\| 1.11.67 \|\|

*sā tu saṃhṛṣṭamanasā devasīrdakṣanandinī \|*  
*praṇamya kamalākāntaṃ punaḥ svasthaānamāvrajat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The mother of the gods, the daughter of Daksa, bowed to the consort of Laksmi with extremely delighted mind and went back to her own abode.

## \|\| 1.11.68 \|\|

*tato 'ditirmahābhāgā suprītā lokavanditā \|*  
*asūta samaye putraṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Thereafter, the highly blessed Aditi, who was extremely glad and was respected all over the world, in due course of time gave birth to a son whom the whole world paid obeisance.

## \|\| 1.11.69 \|\|

*śaṅgacakradharaṃ śāntaṃ candramaṇḍalamadhyagam \|*  
*sudhākalaśadadhyannakaraṃ vāmanasaṃjñitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He was named Vamana. He was holding a conch and a discus, in his hands. He was quiescent. He shone in the middle of the lunar sphere. The pot of nectar and curds mixed with cooked rice were in his hands.

## \|\| 1.11.70 \|\|

*sahasrādityasaṃkāśaṃ vyākośakamalekṣaṇam \|*  
*sarvābharaṇaṃsaṃyuktaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ harim \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He was Lord Visnu himself resembling thousand suns in brilliance. His eyes were like a full blown lotus. He was adorned with all ornaments and was clad in yellow garment.

## \|\| 1.11.71 \|\|

*stutyaṃ munigaṇairyuktaṃ sarvalokaikanāyakam \|*  
*āvirbhūtaṃ hariṃ jñātvā kaśyapo harṣavihvalaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya prañjalirbhūtva stotuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Realising that Hari who was worthy of being eulogised and was the sole leader of all the worlds, had manifested himself accompanied by hosts of sages, Kasyapa was overwhelmed with joy. With palms joined in reverence, he bowed to him and began to praise him.

## \|\| 1.11.72 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca*  
*namonamaste 'khilakāraṇāya namonamaste 'khailapālakāya \|*  
*namonamaste 'maranāyakāya namonamo daiteyavināśanāya \|\| 72 \|\|*

*Kashyapa prayed:*

72\. “I pay obeisance again and again to the cause (the creator) of all the worlds. I bow again and again to the protector of the entire universe. I salute again and again to the leader of immortal beings. Obeisance to the destroyer of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.11.73 \|\|

*namonamo bhaktajanapriyāya namonamaḥ sajjanarañjitāya \|*  
*namonamo durjananāśanāya namo 'stu tasmai jagadīśvarāya \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Obeisance, obeisance to one who is the beloved of his devotees. Salutations to him who is beloved of the good people. I bow again and again to the annihilator of the wicked. My bow to the lord of the universe.

## \|\| 1.11.74 \|\|

*namonamaḥ kāraṇavāmanāya nārāyaṇāyāmitavikramāya \|*  
*saśārṅgacakrāsigadādhārāya namo 'stu tasmai puruṣottamāya \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Salutations to Vamana, the cause of the universe. Obeisance to Narayana of infinite prowess. I bow to the wielder of the discus (Sudarsana), the sword (Nandaka), the mace (Kaumodaki) along with the Sarnga bow. Obeisance be to that Supreme Person.

## \|\| 1.11.75 \|\|

*namaḥ payorāśinivāsanāya namo 'stu saddhṛtkamalasthitāya \|*  
*namo 'stu sūryādyamitaprabhāya namonamaḥ puṇyakathāgatāya \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Salutations to the resident of the ocean of milk. Obeisance to one enthroned in the lotus-like heart of the pious. Obeisance to the Lord of immeasurable splendour of luminaries like the sun, etc. I bow again and again to the God glorified in holy stories.

## \|\| 1.11.76 \|\|

*namonamor'kenduvilocanāya namo 'stu te yajñaphalapradāya \|*  
*namo 'stu yajñāṅgavirājitāya namo 'stu te sajjanavallabhāya \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. I pay obeisance to him whose eyes are the sun and the moon. Salutations be to you, the bestower of the fruits of sacrifices. Salutations to the god who is the resplendent embodiment of sacrifice. Obeisance to you the lover of saintly persons (or beloved of saints).

## \|\| 1.11.77 \|\|

*namo jagatkāraṇakāraṇāya namo 'stu śabdādivivarjitāya \|*  
*namo 'stu te divyasukhapradāya namo namo bhaktamanogatāya \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Obeisance to the Primary Cause of the creative factors of the universe. Salutations to him who is beyond the range of sound, etc. Bow to you the bestower of divine bliss. I bow again and again to one who abides in the minds of his devotees.

## \|\| 1.11.78 \|\|

*namo 'stu te dhvāntavināśakāya namo 'stu śabdādivivarjitāya \|*  
*namo 'stu te dhvāntavināśakāya mandaradhārakāya \|*  
*namo 'stu te yajñavarāhanāmne namo hiraṇyākṣavidārakāya \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Obeisance to you the dispeller of darkness (of ignorance). Salutations to you the supporter of the mount Mandara (at the time of churning the ocean for nectar). Bow to you who are designated as Yajnavaraha (Boar incarnation representing Yajna) Salutations to the slayer of Hiranyaksa.

## \|\| 1.11.79 \|\|

*namo 'stu te vāmanarupabhāje namo 'stu te kṣatrakulāntakāya \|*  
*namo 'stu te rāvaṇamardanāya namo 'stu te nandasutāgrajāya \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Obeisance to you who have assumed the form of a divine dwarf (Vamana). Salutations to the annihilator of the Ksattriya race (i.e. Parasurama). I bow to you the suppressor of Ravana (i.e. Sri Rama). Obeisance to the elder brother of cow-herd Nanda’s daughter (i.e. Sri Krsna).

## \|\| 1.11.80 \|\|

*namaste kamalākānta namaste sukhadāyine \|*  
*smṛtārtināśine tubhyaṃ bhūyo bhūyo namonamaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. О consort of goddess Laksmi, Obeisance to you. Salutations to you, the bestower of happiness. I bow again and again to you, the destroyer of the distress of those who remember you.

## \|\| 1.11.81 \|\|

*yajñeśa yajñavinyāsa yajñavinghavināśana \|*  
*yajñarupa yajadrūpa yajñāṅgaṃ tvāṃ yajāmyaham \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. О Lord of sacrifices, О receptacle of sacrifices, О destroyer of obstacles to sacrifices, О embodiment of Yajna, О sacrificer incarnate, I worship you whose person is constituted of the various parts of Yajna.”

## \|\| 1.11.82 \|\|

*uvāca prahasanharṣaṃ vardhdayankaśyapasya saḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thus eulogised, Vamana, the Lord of the earth, the sanctifier of the worlds, laughingly spoke thus, enhancing the delight of Kasyapa.

## \|\| 1.11.83 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*tāta tuṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te bhaviṣyati surārcitā \|*  
*acirātsādhayiṣyāmi nikhilaṃ tvanmanoratham \|\| 83 \|\|*

*The glorious Lord said:*

83\. “O dear father who are worshipped by gods, I am pleased with you. You will be blessed with good fortune. Ere long, I shall accomplish for you all your desires.

## \|\| 1.11.84 \|\|

*ahaṃ janmadvaye tvevaṃ yuvayoḥ putraghatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*asmiñjanmanyapi tathā sādayāmyuttamaṃ sukham \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. In the two previous births of mine, I had been a son unto both of you. Similarly, in this birth also I shall achieve what is excellent happiness for you.”

## \|\| 1.11.85 \|\|

*atrāntare balirdaityo dīrghasatraṃ mahāmakham \|*  
*ārebhe guruṇā yuktaḥ kāvyena ca munīśvaraiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. In the meantime, the Daitya Bali began a great sacrifice of long duration with the help of his preceptor Kavya (i.e. Sukra) and other great and prominent sages.

## \|\| 1.11.86 \|\|

*tasminmakhe samāhūto viṣṇurlakṣmīsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*haviḥ svīkaraṇārthāya ṛṣibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. In that sacrifice, Visnu accompanied by Laksmi had been invoked by the sages, the expounders of the Brahman or the Vedas, in order to accept the sacrificial offerings.

## \|\| 1.11.87 \|\|

*pravṛddhaiśvaryardaityasya varttamāne mahākratau \|*  
*āmantrya mātāpitarau sa baṭurvāmano yayau \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Taking leave of his mother and father, that Brah- mana bachelor Vamana, went over to the great sacrifice of the supremely affluent Daitya, that was being performed.

## \|\| 1.11.88 \|\|

*smitena mohayaṃllokaṃ vāmano bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*havirbhoktumivāyāto baleḥ pratyakṣato hariḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Vamana, favourably disposed towards his devotees, fascinated the world with his smile. He was Hari himself who had come as if to take part of the sacrificial oblations offered by Bali, directly.

## \|\| 1.11.89 \|\|

*durvṛtto vā suvṛtto vā jaḍo vāyaṃ hito 'pi vā \|*  
*yo bhaktiyuktastasyāntaḥ sadā saṃnihito hariḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Hari is always present in the heart of persons endowed with devotion, irrespective of whether his votary is evil-minded or good-natured, whether he is insentient or benevolent.

## \|\| 1.11.90 \|\|

*āyāntaṃ vāmanaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛṣayo jñānacakṣauṣaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā nārāyaṇaṃ devamudyayuḥ sabhyasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. On seeing Vamana coming, the sages, blessed with the vision of spiritual knowledge, knew him to be Lord Narayana. They stood up (to show him respect), along with the other members of assembly.

## \|\| 1.11.91 \|\|

*etajjñātvā daityagururekānte balimabravīt \|*  
*svasāramavicāryaiva khalāḥ kāryāṇi kurvate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Having come to know of this, the preceptor of Daityas said to Bali in privacy. Indeed wicked men commit many acts without judging (estimating correctly) their own strength and weakness.

## \|\| 1.11.92 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*bho bho daityapate saumya hyapahartā tava śriyam \|*  
*viṣṇurvāmanarupeṇa hyaditeḥ putrātāṃ gataḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*Sukra said:*

92\. “O gentle-natured Lord of Daityas, Visnu who in the form of Vamana (Dwarf) is born as the son of Aditi, will deprive you of your riches and glory.

## \|\| 1.11.93 \|\|

*tavādhvaraṃ sa āyāti tvayā tasyāsureśvara \|*  
*na kiñcidapi dātavyaṃ manmataṃ śṛṇu paṇḍita \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. О Lord of Asuras, he will pay a visit to your sacrifice. Nothing should be given to him by you. О learned one, please listen to my advice.

## \|\| 1.11.94 \|\|

*ātmabuddhiḥ sukhakarī gurubuddhirviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*parabuddhirvināśāya strībudhdiḥ pralayaṅkarī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. One’s own intellect is conducive to happiness. Particularly so is the intellect (i.e. intellectual guidance) of the preceptor. The intellect of an enemy is destructive and a woman’s intellect causes complete destruction (lit. dissolution).

## \|\| 1.11.95 \|\|

*śatrūṇāṃ hitakṛtadyastu sa hantavyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. He who is the benefactor of one’s enemy should be especially killed straightway”.

## \|\| 1.11.96 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*evaṃ guro na vaktavyaṃ dharmamārgavirodhataḥ \|*  
*yadādatte svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ kimasmādadhikaṃ varam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*Bali replied:*

96\. “O preceptor, you should not tender such an advice which is contrary to the path of virtue. If Visnu himself partakes of oblations or gifts, what can be better than that?

## \|\| 1.11.97 \|\|

*kurvanti viduṣo yajñānviṣṇuprīṇanakāraṇāt \|*  
*sa cetsākṣāddhavirbhogī mattaḥ ko 'bhyadhiko bhuvī \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Learned men perform sacrifices for the purpose of propitiating Visnu. If he personally comes and partakes of oblations offered, who can be superior to me on this earth?

## \|\| 1.11.98 \|\|

*daridreṇāpi yatkiñciddīyate viṣṇave guro \|*  
*tadeva paramaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. If anything is given to Visnu, even by an indigent person, О preceptor, that is the greatest of charitable gifts. That gift which is so given, becomes ever-lasting in its benefits.

## \|\| 1.11.99 \|\|

*smṛto 'pi parayā bhaktyā punāti puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*yena kenāpyarcitaśveddadāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Even when simply remembered with great devotion, the Supreme Person sanctifies the rememberer. By whomsoever he is worshipped, he awards to him the highest state of existence i.e. Moksa.

## \|\| 1.11.100 \|\|

*harirharati pāpāniduṣṭacittairapi smṛtaḥ \|*  
*anicchayāpi saṃspṛṣṭo dahatyeva hi pāvakaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Even when remembered by evil-minded persons, Hari dispels their sins, just as the fire even if touched unwillingly, (invariably) does burn.

## \|\| 1.11.101 \|\|

*jihvāgre vasate yasya hari rityakṣaradvayam \|*  
*sa viṣṇulokamānpoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. If the two syllables HA-RI stay at the tip of the tongue, that man attains the region of Visnu from which the return to Samsara is very difficult (impossible).

## \|\| 1.11.102 \|\|

*govindeti sadā dhyāyedyastu rāgādivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti viṣṇubhavanamiti prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Wise men say that he who constantly meditates on Govinda, without passionate attachment, etc. (to the worldly objects), goes to Visnu’s abode.

## \|\| 1.11.103 \|\|

*agnau vā brahmaṇe vāpihūyate yadvavirguro \|*  
*haribhaktyā mahābhāga tena viṣṇuḥ prasīdati \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. О highly blessed preceptor, if oblations are offered to the fire or to Brahmana with devotion to Hari, Visnu becomes delighted with it (viz. oblations offered to fire or the gift given to a Brahmana.)

## \|\| 1.11.104 \|\|

*ahaṃ tu harituṣyyarthaṃ karomyadhvaramuttamam \|*  
*svayamāyāti cedviṣṇuḥ kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. I am performing this excellent sacrifice for the propitiation of Hari. If Hari himself comes to it, I am undoubtedly satisfied and have accomplished my objects.”

## \|\| 1.11.105 \|\|

*evaṃ vadati daityandre viṣṇurvāmanarupadhṛk \|*  
*praviveśādhvarasthānaṃ hutavahnimanoramam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Even as the Lord of Daityas was speaking thus, Visnu who had assumed the form of a Dwarf, entered the sacrificial hall that was charming (and resplendent) due to the consecrated fire.

## \|\| 1.11.106 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā koṭisūryābhaṃ yogyāvayavasundaram \|*  
*vāmanaṃ sahasotthāya pratyagṛhṇātkṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. On seeing Vamana who had the refulgence of ten million suns and who was extremely handsome, Bali stood up suddenly and greeted him with palms folded in reverence.

## \|\| 1.11.107 \|\|

*dattvāsanaṃ ca prakṣālya pādau vāmanarupiṇam \|*
