*sakuṭuṃbo vahanmūrdhnā paramāṃ mudamātpavān \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. He offered him a seat. After washing the feet of the Lord in the form of Vamana, he (sprinkled the water of washing) over his own head and on the heads of other members of his family. He derived great joy thereby.

## \|\| 1.11.108 \|\|

*viṣṇave 'smai jagaddhānme dattvārghyaṃ vidhivadūliḥ \|*  
*romāñcitatanurbhūtvā harṣāśrunayano 'bravīt \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. After duly offering Argkya (respectful offerings given to a distinguished guest) to Visnu, the abode of the universe, Bali was greatly delighted. All the hairs over his body stood on their ends and tears of joy welled up in his eyes.

## \|\| 1.11.109 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalo maravaḥ \|*  
*jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ me 'dya kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*Bali said:*

109\. I have accomplished the purpose of my birth to-day. It is to-day that my sacrifice has become fruitful. My life has also become fruitful to-day. Undoubtedly, I have achieved the goal of human life and I am contented.

## \|\| 1.11.110 \|\|

*amoghāmṛtavṛṣṭirme samāyātātidurlabhā \|*  
*tvadāgamanamātreṇa hyanāyāso mahotsavaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Extremely rare (opportunity of the) shower of nectar which never goes waste, has come to my lot. By your very arrival a great festival has been accomplished without entailing any strain.

## \|\| 1.11.111 \|\|

*ete ca ṛṣayaḥ sarve kṛtārthāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yaiḥ pūrvaṃ hi tapastaptaṃ tadadya saphalaṃ prabho \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. There is no doubt in this that all these sages have also «achieved their goal in life. Whatever penance they have formerly performed, has become fruitful to-day.

## \|\| 1.11.112 \|\|

*kṛtārtho 'smi kṛtārtho 'smi kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. I am blessed and contented. I repeat that I am really blessed and contented. Undoubtedly, I have achieved the purpose of my life. Hence, obeisance unto you. Salutations unto you. Repeated bows to you.

## \|\| 1.11.113 \|\|

*tvadājñayā tvanniyogaṃ sādhayāmīti manmanaḥ \|*  
*atyutsāhasamāyuktaṃ samājñāpaya māṃ prabho \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. I think that I should carry out your behest with your own permission. О Lord, command me who have been fired with great enthusiasm.”

## \|\| 1.11.114 \|\|

*evamurke dīkṣitena prahasanvāmano 'bravīt \|*  
*dehi me tapasi sthātuṃ bhūmiṃ tripadasaṃmitām \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thus urged by that Daitya who was consecrated (for the sacrifice), Vamana said laughingly: — “Give unto me as much space as can be measured by my three steps, in order to stand in and perform the penance.”

## \|\| 1.11.115 \|\|

*etacchṛātvā baliḥ prāha rājyaṃ yācitavānnahi \|*  
*grāmaṃ vā nagaraṃ cāpi dhanaṃ vā kiṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. On hearing it, Bali said: “You have not requested for a kingdom. Not even a village or a city or even wealth has been requested for by you. What have you done? (what a gift you have requested!).”

## \|\| 1.11.116 \|\|

*tanniśamya baliṃ prāha viṣṇuḥ sarvaśarīrabhṛt \|*  
*āsannabhraṣṭarājyasya vairāgyaṃ janamannivā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. On hearing it, Visnu who bears all bodies (by pervading them) said to Bali as if with a view to create detachment in him who was about to be deposed from his kingdom.

## \|\| 1.11.117 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*śṛṇu daityandra vakṣyāmi guhyādguhyatamaṃ param \|*  
*sarvasaṃgavihīnānāṃ kimarthaiḥ sādhyatevada \|\| 117 \|\|*

*The glorious Lord said:*

117\. “O Lord of Daityas, listen to me. I shall tell you the great secret of secrets. Please tell me what can be realised through riches in the case of those who have eschewed all worldly contacts and attachment.

## \|\| 1.11.118 \|\|

*ahaṃ tu sarvabhūtānāmantaryāmīti bhāvaya \|*  
*mayi sarvamidaṃ daitya kimanyaiḥ sādhyate vada \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Think over this that 1 am the Inner Controller in all living beings. О Daitya, all these things existing in the universe are within me. Tell me what can be achieved by others (i.e. objects or gifts).

## \|\| 1.11.119 \|\|

*rāgadveṣavihīnānāṃ śāntānāṃ tyaktamāyinām \|*  
*nityānandasvarupāṇāṃ kimanyaiḥ sādhyate dhanaiḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. What can be realised by means of other external riches in the case of those who are devoid of attachment and hatred, who are quiescent and have eschewed Maya and who are embodiment of eternal bliss?

## \|\| 1.11.120 \|\|

*ātmavatsarvabhūtāni paśyatāṃ śāntacetasām \|*  
*abhinnamātmanaḥ sarvaṃ ko dātā dīyate ca kim \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. To those who perceive all living beings like their own Atman (Self), to those whose minds are quite serene and to those to whom everything is non-different from the Atmany who is the giver and what can be given?

## \|\| 1.11.121 \|\|

*pṛthvīyaṃ kṣatriyavaśā iti śāstreṣu niścitam \|*  
*tadājñāyāṃ sthitāḥ sarve labhante paramaṃ sukham \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. It is the decisive conclusion in all Scriptures that this Earth is subject to the control of the Ksatriyas. All the people who abide by their behests, achieve the greatest happiness.

## \|\| 1.11.122 \|\|

*dātavyo munibhiścāpi ṣaṣṭāṃśo bhūbhuje bale \|*  
*mahīyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu dātavyā sarva yatnataḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. О Bali, the revenue of one-sixth part of the entire produce should be given to the king even by sages. This Earth should be granted to the Brahmanas with special efforts.

## \|\| 1.11.123 \|\|

*bhūmidānasya māhātmyaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*paraṃ nirvāṇamānpoti bhūmido nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. The greatness of the charitable gift of land cannot be adequately described, as such a kind of gift has never been offered before (in the past) nor will it ever be so (in future). Undoubtedly a donor of lands attains the Supreme Nirvana (Emancipation from Samsara).

## \|\| 1.11.124 \|\|

*svalpāmapi mahīṃ dattvā śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. By giving a small piece of land to a Brahmana who is well versed in the Vedas and maintains the sacrificial fires, the donor attains Brahmaloka (region of Brahman), return from which is difficult.

## \|\| 1.11.125 \|\|

*bhūmidaḥ sarvadaḥ prokto bhūmido mokṣabhāgbhavet \|*  
*atidānaṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ sarvapāpaprāṇāśanam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. A donor of lands is said to be a giver of all. A giver of lands will attain emancipation from samsara. It is to be known as the highest type of religious gift. It absolves the donor of all sins.

## \|\| 1.11.126 \|\|

*mahāpātakayukto vā yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*daśahastāṃ mahīṃ dattvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Even if one is vitiated by five great sins or even by all kinds of sins, one is absolved from them by gifting away ten cubits of land (hasta — 24 Angulos or 18 inches).

## \|\| 1.11.127 \|\|

*satpātre bhūmidātā yaḥ sarvadānaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*bhūmidānasamaṃ nānyatriṣu lokeṣu vidyate \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. He who bestows a charitable gift of land on a deserving person, shall attain the fruit of all kinds of charitable gifts. There is nothing in the three worlds which is equivalent to a charitable land grant.

## \|\| 1.11.128 \|\|

*dvijāya vṛttihīnāya yaḥ pradadyānmahīṃ bale \|*  
*tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ na kṣamo 'bdaśatairaham \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. О Bali, even in hundreds of years, I shall not be able to describe adequately the meritorious benefits of a person who donates lands to a Brahmana who has no means of livelihood.

## \|\| 1.11.129 \|\|

*saktāya devapūjāsu vṛttihīnāya daityapa \|*  
*svalpāmapi mahīṃ dadyādyaḥ sa viṣṇurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. О Lord of Daityas, he who gives in charity even a small piece of land to a person who has no means of subsistence, but who is interested in the worship of the Lord, is undoubtedly Visnu himself.

## \|\| 1.11.130 \|\|

*ikṣugodhūma tuvarīpūgavṛkṣādisaṃyutā \|*  
*pṛthvī pradīyate yena sa viṣṇurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. There is no doubt in this that he, by whom a piece of land with a flourishing crop of sugarcane, wheat, pulses, areca palm and other trees is donated, is Lord Visnu incarnate.

## \|\| 1.11.131 \|\|

*vṛttihīnāya viprāya daridrāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*svalpāmapi mahīndattvā viṣṇusāyujyamānpuyāt \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. By donating even a small piece of land to an indigent Brahmana who has no means of livelihood and who is burdened with a big family, one shall attain Sayujya (identity) with god Visnu (by being absorbed into his divine essence).

## \|\| 1.11.132 \|\|

*saktāya devapūjāsu viprāyāḍhakikāṃ mahīm \|*  
*dattvā labheta gaṅgāyāṃ trirātrasnānajaṃ phalam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. By giving a piece of land sufficient for sowing one adhака — full of grain to a Brahmana who is interested in divine worship, one attains the benefit of performing ablution in the holy Ganga for three days.

## \|\| 1.11.133-134 \|\|

*viprāya vṛttihīnāya sadācāraratāya ca \|*  
*droṇikāṃ pṛthivīṃ dattvā yatphalaṃ labhate śṛṇu \|\| 133 \|\|*

*gaṅgātīrthāśvamedhānāṃ śatāni vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā yatphalamānpoti tadāpnoti sa puṣkalam \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. Listen to the benefit one derives by giving a dronika of land (i.e. a piece of land sufficient to sow a drona or four adhakas of grain) to a Brahmana who is devoid of any means of subsistence and who is engaged in saintly conduct of life. Such a person attains that enormous merit which a man obtains by performing hundreds of ablutions in the Ganga, pilgrimage to a hundred sacred places and performance of a hundred horse sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.11.135 \|\|

*dadāti khārikāṃ bhūmiṃ daridrāya dvijāya yaḥ \|*  
*tasya puṇyaṃ pravakṣyāmi vadato me niśāmaya \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. I shall explain to you the merit that accrues to a person who gives a Kharika of land (i.e. land sufficient for sowing 16 dronas of grain) to an indigent Brahmana. Please be attentive to it, even as I relate it to you.

## \|\| 1.11.136 \|\|

*aśvamedhasahasrāṇi vājapeyaśatāni ca \|*  
*vidhāya jāhnavītīre patphalaṃ tallabheddhuvam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. He, the donor, shall obtain that fruit which one obtains after performing thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of Vajapeya sacrifices on the bank of the holy Ganga.

## \|\| 1.11.137 \|\|

*bhūmidānaṃ mahādānamatidānaṃ prakīrttitam \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanamapavargaphalapradam \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The gift of a land is glorified as a great gift — a gift which surpasses all other kinds of donations. It subsides (i.e. absolves the donor of) all the sins and confers on him the benefit of liberation from samsara.

## \|\| 1.11.138 \|\|

*atrotihāsaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu daityakuleśvara \|*  
*yacchutvā śraddhayā yukto bhūmidānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. О Lord of Daitya clans, listen to me as I shall relate to you an ancient anecdote in this connection. A person who listens to this with faith, shall obtain the merit of donating lands.

## \|\| 1.11.139 \|\|

*āsītpurā dvijavaro brāhmakalpe mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*daridro vṛttihīnaśca nāmnā bhadramatirbale \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. О Bali, formerly in the Brahma Kalpa, there was a highly intelligent and excellent Brahmana by name Bhadramati. He was indigent and had no means of livelihood.

## \|\| 1.11.140 \|\|

*śrutāni sarvaśāstrāṇi tena vedadivāniśam \|*  
*śrutāni ca purāṇāni dharmaśāstrāṇi sarvaśaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. All scriptures have been ever heard (i.e. learnt) by that Brahmana who was expert in the knowledge of the Vedas. All the Puranas and treatises on the Dharmasastra been mastered by him.

## \|\| 1.11.141 \|\|

*abhavaṃstasya ṣaṭpatnyaḥ śrutiḥ sindhuryaśovatī \|*  
*kāminī mālinī caiva śobhā ceti prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. He had six wives, viz. Sruti, Sindhu, Yasovati, Kamini, Malini and Sobha.

## \|\| 1.11.142-143 \|\|

*āsu pantīṣu tasyāsañcatvariṃśacchatadvayam \|*  
*putrāṇāmasuraśreṣṭha sarve nityaṃ bubhukṣitāḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*akiñcano bhadramatiḥ kṣudhārttānātmajānpriyāḥ \|*  
*paśyansvayaṃ kṣudhārttaśca vilalāpākulendriyaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. О excellent Asura, from these wives he begot two hundred and forty sons. All of them suffered from perpetual starvation. On seeing his sons and wives starving with hunger and himself feeling the poignancy of hunger, the indigent Bhadramati lamented loudly with all his sense-organs afflicted and famished with hunger.

## \|\| 1.11.144 \|\|

*dhigjanma bhāgyarahitaṃ dhigjanma dhanavarjitam \|*  
*dhigjanma dharmarahitaṃ dhigjanma khyātivarjitam \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. “Fie upon this life devoid of good fortune! Shame upon that life wanting in wealth! Fie upon that life which is wanting in virtue! Fie upon that life which is devoid of good name!

## \|\| 1.11.145-147 \|\|

*narasya bahvapatyasya dhigjanmaiśvaryavārjitam \|*  
*aho guṇāḥ saumyatā ca vidvattā janma satkule \|\| 145 \|\|*

*dāridyāmbudhimagnasya sarvametanna śobhate \|*  
*priyāḥ putrāścapautrāśca bāndhavā bhrātarastathā \|\| 146 \|\|*

*śiṣyāśca sarvamanujāstyajantyaiśvaryavārjitam \|*  
*cāṇḍālo vā dvijo vāpi bhāgyavāneva pūjyate \|\| 147 \|\|*

145-147. Pity the life of a man bereft of prosperity and burdened with a number of children! Alas! Virtues, gentleness, scholarship, nobility of birth — all these do not shine in a man immersed in the ocean of destitution. Beloved wives, sons, grandsons, brothers, kinsmen and disciples — nay, all men forsake the man devoid of wealth. Only the fortunate one irrespective of his being a Brahmana or a Candala, is respectfully honoured.

## \|\| 1.11.148-149 \|\|

*daridraḥ puruṣo loke śavavallokaninditaḥ \|*  
*aho saṃpatsaṃmāyukto niṣṭuro vāpyaniṣṭhuraḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*guṇahīno 'pi guṇavānmūrkho vāpyatha paṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryaguṇayuktaścetpūjya eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

148-149. A poor man is condemned in the world like a dead body. Alas! If a person is endowed with wealth, he is hailed as a kind man though he may be ruthless; though he be deficient in all good qualities, he is still considered to be endowed with all virtues; though he be foolish, he is still regarded as a scholar. One is undoubtedly praiseworthy only if one is endowed with the virtue of being rich.

## \|\| 1.11.150 \|\|

*aho daridratā duḥkhaṃ tatrāpyāśātiduḥkhadā \|*  
*āśābhibhūtāḥ puruṣā duḥkhamaśnuvate 'kṣayam \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Alas! Indigence is certainly miserable. Still more grievously painful is the wishful expectation (of getting something from others). Men overwhelmed with false wishful expectations (from others) experience everlasting misery.

## \|\| 1.11.151 \|\|

*āśayādāsā ye dāsāste sarvalokasya \|*  
*āśā dāsī yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ dāsāyate lokaḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Those who are the slaves of wishful expectations are the bondsmen or helots of the entire world. But the whole world submits to those who have subdued their wishful (but false) hopes.

## \|\| 1.11.152 \|\|

*māno hi mahatāṃ loke dhanamakṣayamucyate \|*  
*tasminnāśākhyaripuṇā māne naṣṭe daridratā \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Honour is said to be the everlasting wealth of great men in the world. If honour is ruined by the enemy called “hopeful expectation”, one is faced with poverty.

## \|\| 1.11.153 \|\|

*sarvaśāstrārthavettāpi daridro bhāti mūrkhavat \|*  
*naiṣkiñcanyamahāgrāhagrastānāṃ ko vimocacakaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Even an expert in the interpretation of all scriptural texts appears to be a fool if he is poverty-stricken. Who can rescue those persons in the grip of the great crocodile called “pennylessness”?

## \|\| 1.11.154 \|\|

*aho duḥkhamaho duḥkhamaho duḥkhaṃ daridratā \|*  
*tatrāpi putrabhāryāṇāṃ bāhulyamatiduḥkhadam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. О misery! О misery! Poverty itself is a great misery. There too, if one has numerous wives and sons, it is all the more painful.”

## \|\| 1.11.155 \|\|

*evamuktvā bhadramatiḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|*  
*anyamaiśvaryadaṃ dharmaṃ manasācintayattadā \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. After lamenting thus (lit. saying this) Bhadramati, the master of all scriptural topics, mentally thought about other religious rites (efficacious in) bestowing prosperity.

## \|\| 1.11.156 \|\|

*bhūmidānaṃ viniścitya sarvadānottamottamam \|*  
*dānena yo 'numantāti sa eva kṛtavānpurā \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. He came to the decision that charitable gift of lands is the most excellent of all charitable gifts. He who consents to a charitable gift, is as good as one who has formerly given it.

## \|\| 1.11.157 \|\|

*prāpakaṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*dānānāmuttamaṃ dānaṃ bhūdānaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Dana or a charitable gift is the greatest merit or virtue that enables one to reach (his destination). It bestows the fruit of all cherished desires. The gift of lands is glorified as the best of all danas.

## \|\| 1.11.158-159 \|\|

*yaddattvā samavānpoti yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*iti niścatya matimāndhīro bhadramatirbale \|\| 158 \|\|*

*kauśāmbīṃnāma nagarīṃ kalatrāpatyayugyayau \|*  
*sughoṣanāmaviprendraṃ sarvaiśvaryasamanvalitam \|\| 159 \|\|*

158-159. After making a gift of land, a man obtains whatever is most desirable to him”. О Bali, after deciding thus, the intelligent and self-possessed Bhadramati went to the city named Kausambi, along with his wives and children. He approached the leading Brahmana thereof named Sughosa who was endowed with affluence. О Bali, he then requested Sughosa for a plot of land extending to five cubits (hastas).

## \|\| 1.11.160-162 \|\|

*gatvā yācitavānbhūmiṃ pañcahastāyatāṃ bale \|*  
*sughoṣo dharmaniratastaṃ nirīkṣya kuṭumbikram \|\| 160 \|\|*

*manasā prīyamāṇena samabhyarcyedamabravīt \|*  
*kṛtārtho 'haṃ bhadramate saphalaṃ mama janma ca \|\| 161 \|\|*

*matkula pāvanaṃ jātaṃ tvadanugrahato dvija \|*  
*ityuktvā taṃ samabhyarcya sughoṣo dharmatatparaḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

160-162. Observing that he was a man burdened with a large family, Sughosa, who was virtuously inclined, honoured him with a delighted mind and addressed him thus: “O Bhadramati, I feel I have achieved my objectives in life. My life is fruitful. О Brahmana, thanks to your blessings, my family has become sanctified”. After saying these words and honouring him suitably, the highly intelligent and virtuous Sughosa donated to him a plot of land extending to five cubits (hastas).

## \|\| 1.11.163-167 \|\|

*pañcahastamitāṃ bhūmiṃ dadau tasmai mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*pṛthivī vaiṣṇavī puṇyā pṛthivīṃ viṣṇupālitā \|\| 163 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāstu pradānena prīyatāṃ me janārdanaḥ \|*  
*mantreṇānena daityendra sughoṣastaṃ dvijottamam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*viṣṇubuddhyā samabhyarcya tāvatīṃ pṛthivīṃ dadau \|*  
*so 'pi bhadramatirvipro dhīmatā yācitāṃ bhuvam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*dattavānharibhaktāya śrotriyāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*sughoṣo bhūmidānena koṭivaṃśasamanvitaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

*prapede viṣṇubhavanaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati \|*  
*bale bhadramatiścāpi yataḥ prārthitavāñchriyam \|\| 167 \|\|*

163-165a. (The mantra to be uttered at the time of donation) “The holy earth belongs to Visnu. The Earth is protected by Visnu. Thanks to the gift of this earth, may lord Janardana be pleased with me”. Sughosa conceived that excellent Brahmana to be Visnu and worshipped him with the (above) Mantra and granted him that much land, О lord of Daityas!

165b-167. The Brahmana Bhadramati gave the piece of land as requested by that intelligent one who was a Brahmana devotee of Hari, well-versed in the Vedas and had a large family to support. Due to the merit accrued from the gift of the land, Sughosa along with ten million members of his family, attained Visnu’s abode on reaching which one ceases to worry and grieve. О Bali, since he sought glory and prosperity, Bhadramati also stayed in Visnu’s abode for ten thousand yugas along with the members of his family.

## \|\| 1.11.168-170 \|\|

*sthitavānviṣṇubhavane sakuṭumbo yugāyutam \|*  
*tathaiva brahmasadane sthitvā koṭiyugāyutam \|\| 168 \|\|*

*aindraṃ padaṃ samāsādya sthitavānkalpapañcakam \|*  
*tato bhuvaṃ samāsādya sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

*jātismaro mahābhāgo bubhuje bhogamuttamam \|*  
*tato bhadramatirdaitya niṣkāmo viṣṇutatparaḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

168-170. Similarly, he stayed in the region of Brahma for ten thousand crores of yugas, and he attained the abode of Indra where he stayed for five kalpas. Thereafter, he came back to the Earth. He was endowed with every affluence, he was highly blessed. He could even remember his previous births. He enjoyed all excellent pleasures. Thereafter, О Daitya, Bhadramati became free from all desires. Devotedly attached to Visnu, he gave his lands unto the Brahmanas who had no means of livelihood.

## \|\| 1.11.171-172 \|\|

*pṛthivīṃ vṛttihīnebhyo brahmaṇebhyaḥ pradattavān \|*  
*tasya viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā tattvaiśaavaryamanuttamam \|\| 171 \|\|*

*koṭivaṃśasametasya dadau mokṣamanuttamam \|*  
*tasmāddaityapate mahyaṃ sarvadharmaparāyaṇa \|\| 172 \|\|*

171-172. Lord Visnu became pleased with him. He conferred upon him all excellent rites and blessed him along with ten million members of his family, by bestowing upon them the highest emancipations from samsara. Hence, О Lord of Daityas, interested in all holy rites, give unto me a plot of land measuring three steps. I shall perform penance there for the sake of salvation.”

## \|\| 1.11.173-177 \|\|

*tapaścariṣyemokṣāya dehi me tripadāṃ mahīm \|*  
*vairocanistato dṛṣṭaḥ kalaśaṃ jalapūritam \|\| 173 \|\|*

*ādade pṛthivīṃ dātuṃ varṇine vāmanāya \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ sarvagatojñātvā jaladhārāvarodhinam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*kāvyaṃ hastasthadarbhāgraṃ tacchare saṃnyaveśayat \|*  
*darbhāgre 'bhūnmahāśāstraṃ koṭisūryasamaprabham \|\| 175 \|\|*

*amodhaṃ brahmamatyugraṃ kāvyākṣigrāsalolupam \|*  
*āyāya bhārgavasurānasurānekacakṣuṣā \|\| 176 \|\|*

*paśyeti vāndideśe ca darbhāgraṃ śastrasannibham \|*  
*balirdadau mahāviṣṇormahīṃ tripadasaṃmitām \|\| 177 \|\|*

173b-176a. The delighted son of Virocana, thereafter, took up a pitcher filled with water to grant the land to Vamana in the guise of a religious student. Visnu, the omnipresent, realised that Kavya (Sukra) was obstructing the flow of water (from the spout of the pitcher). He, therefore, introduced the tip of the Kusa grass that was in his hand into the spout of the pitcher. At the tip of the blade of the darbha grass, there was the never-failing great weapon pertaining to Brahma (Brahmastra). It had the lustre of ten million suns. It was very fierce and was desirous of plucking the eye of Kavya.

176b-177. “O preceptor, Bhargava, see the gods or the demons with a single eye (probably implying “Look at them impartially”)”, so commanded the tip of the darbha grass which resembled a weapon. Bali granted Visnu as much land as could be measured in three spaces.

## \|\| 1.11.178 \|\|

*vavṛdhe so 'pi viśvātmā ābrahmabhuvanaṃ tadā \|*  
*amimīta mahīṃ dvābhyāṃ padbhyāṃ viśvatanurhariḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. Visnu that Soul of the Universe began to grow in size till he reached the abode of Brahma. Hari who contains the Universe in his own person measured the world in two paces.

## \|\| 1.11.179-180 \|\|

*sa ābrahmakaṭāhāntapadānyetāni saprabhaḥ \|*  
*pādāṅkuṣṭāgranirbhinnaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ vibhide dvidhā \|\| 179 \|\|*

*taddārā bāhyasalilaṃ bahudhāraṃ samāgatam \|*  
*dhautaviṣṇupadaṃ toyaṃ nirmalaṃ lokapāvanam \|\| 180 \|\|*

179-180. The refulgent Lord covered all the Regions delimited by the semi-spheroidal crust of the region of Brahma. The outer crust of the egg of the Universe pierced by the tip of his tow was split into two. Through it, the cosmic water enveloping the outer crust of the egg of the universe, orushed in many torrential currents and washed the feet of Visnu — water that thereby became pure and sanctified the world.

## \|\| 1.11.181 \|\|

*ajāṇḍabāhyanilayaṃ dhārārupamavarttata \|*  
*tajjalaṃ pāvanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ brahmādīnpāvayatsurān \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. The water was enveloping the egg of Brahma (that is the Universe) from outside. It rushed in jets of currents. That water was extremely sacred and it sanctified god Brahma and other gods.

## \|\| 1.11.182 \|\|

*satparṣisevitaṃ caiva nyapatanmerumūrddhani \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. It was served and resorted to by the seven sages (The Ursa Major). Then it fellon the top of mount Meru.

## \|\| 1.11.183 \|\|

*etaddaṣṭvādbhutaṃ karma brahmādyā devatāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo manavaścaiva hyastuvanharṣavihvalāḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. On seeing this miraculous phenomenon, gods of whom Brahma was prominent, the sages and the Manus were overwhelmed with ecstatic delight and they eulogised him.

## \|\| 1.11.184 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*namaḥ pareśāya parātmarupiṇe parātparāyāpararupadhāriṇe \|*  
*brahmātmane brahmaratātmabuddhaye namo 'stu te 'vyāhatakarmaśīline \|\| 184 \|\|*

*The gods said:*

184\. “Obeisance to the great lsa (The Ruler of the Universe) whose form is the Supreme Self; Salutations to him who transcends the transcendents; bow to him that assumes the highest form; salutations to the Atman of Brahma. Obeisance to him whose Soul and Intellect take delight in the Brahman; bow to him whose activities are invariably unobstructed.

## \|\| 1.11.185 \|\|

*pareśa paramānanda paramātmanparātpara \|*  
*sarvātmane jaganmūrtte pramāṇātīta te namaḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. О great Isa, the highest bliss, О Supreme Atman, greater than the greatest. Obeisance to you the indwelling soul of all; О embodiment of the Universe, who are beyond the pale of valid means of knowledge, we bow to you.

## \|\| 1.11.186 \|\|

*viśvataśvakṣuṣe tubhyaṃ viśvato bāhave namaḥ \|*  
*viśvataḥ śirase caiva viśvato gataye namaḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. Obeisance to you who (being immanent in the Universe) have eyes all round; salutation to you who have arms and heads all round; bow to you who course everywhere.

## \|\| 1.11.187 \|\|

*evaṃra stuto mahāviṣṇurbrahmādyaiḥ svarddavaukasām \|*  
*dattvābhayaṃ ca mumude devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. Thus eulogised by Brahma and others, the great Visnu granted the boon of fearlessness to the heavendwellers and the Eternal Lord of devas was over-joyed.

## \|\| 1.11.188 \|\|

*virocanātmajaṃ daityaṃ padaikārthaṃ babandha ha \|*  
*tataḥ prapannaṃ tu baliṃ jñātvā cāsmai rasātalam \|*  
*dadau tadvārapālaśca bhaktavaśyo babhūva ha \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. Due to Bali’s inability to grant land for one more step, he imprisoned Bali, the son of Virocana. Thereafter, knowing that he was dedicated unto him, he (Visnu) gave him (Bali) the dominion in the nether world called Rasatala for his residence. The Lord who is ever under the control of his devotees, became his (Bali’s) doorkeeper.

## \|\| 1.11.189 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*rasātale mahāviṣṇurvirocanasutasya vai \|*  
*kiṃ bhojyaṃ kalpayāmāsa ghore sarpabhayākule \|\| 189 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

189\. “What diet was assigned by MahaVisnu to the son of Virocana, in the terrible region of Rasatala which is dangerous due to the fear of serpents?”

## \|\| 1.11.190-191 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*amantritaṃ haviryattu hūyate jātavedasi \|*  
*apātre dīyate yacca taddhoraṃ bhogasādhanam \|\| 190 \|\|*

*hutaṃ haviraśucinā dṛttaṃ satkarma yatkṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ tatra bhogārhamadhaḥ pātaphalapradam \|\| 191 \|\|*

*Sanaka replied:*

190-191. The oblations consigned to the fire without proper chanting of the Mantras, whatever is given to a non-deserving person, black magic for obtaining the means of enjoyment, what is consigned to the sacred fire, whatever is given in charity or holy rites performed by persons in an impure state — in fact all acts, etc. which bring about one’s downfall — all these deserve to be Bali’s means of enjoyment.

## \|\| 1.11.192 \|\|

*evaṃ rasātalaṃ viṣṇurbalaye sāsurāya tu \|*  
*dattvābhayaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ surāṇāṃ tridivaṃ dadau \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. In this way god Visnu gave the nether world called Rasatala to Bali along with all his Asuras. Offering fearlessness (a secure place) to all gods, Visnu granted them heaven.

## \|\| 1.11.193 \|\|

*pūjyamāno 'maragaṇaiḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*gandharvairgīyamānaśca punarvāmanatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. While he was being worshipped by the groups of immortals (gods), eulogised by great sages and sung about by Gandharvas, he once again resumed the form of the divine Dwarf (Vamana).

## \|\| 1.11.194 \|\|

*etaddṛṣṭvā mahatkarmamuno brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*paraspare smitamukhāḥ praṇebhuḥ puruṣottamam \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. Witnessing this great deed, the sages, the expounders of the Brahman, smiled at one another and bowed to the Supreme Person (Purushottama).

## \|\| 1.11.195 \|\|

*sarvabhūtatmako viṣṇurvāmanatvamupāgataḥ \|*  
*mohayannikhilaṃ lokaṃ prapede tapase vanam \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Lord Visnu, the Soul abiding in all living beings, who had assumed the state of a Dwarf (Vamana) fascinated the entire world and repaired to forest for performing penance.

## \|\| 1.11.196 \|\|

*evaṃ prabhāvā sā devī gaṅgā viṣṇupadodbhavā \|*  
*yasyāḥ smaraṇamātreṇa mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. Of such sanctifying power is the goddess Ganga who originated from Visnu’s feet. By merely remembering her, one is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.11.197 \|\|

*idaṃ tu gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ yaḥ paṭhe cchṛṇuyādapi \|*  
*devālaye nadītīre so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. Whoever reads or listens to this narrative of the glory of the Ganga, in a temple or on the banks of the river, shall obtain the fruit of the performance of a horse-sacrifice (Asvamedha).

## Chapter 12. A dialogue between god Dharma and King Bhagiratha

## \|\| 1.12.1 \|\|

*nātada uvāca*  
*śrutaṃ tu gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ vāñchitaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*adhunā lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi bhrātarme dānapātraghayoḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada inquired:*

1\. The great glory of the Ganga has been heard. It is desirable, as it destroys all sins. Now, dear brother, tell me the characteristic of charitable gifts as well as of the persons deserving the same.

## \|\| 1.12.2 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramo guruḥ \|*  
*tasmai tānāni deyāni dattasyānantyamicchatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Sanaka replied:*

2\. A Brahmana is the greatest preceptor of all classes in the society. Charitable gifts should be given to him by one who is desirous of securing perpetuation of the fruit of his charitable gifts.

## \|\| 1.12.3 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhṇīyātsarvato bhayavarjitaḥ \|*  
*na kadāpi kṣatraviśo gṛhṇīyātāṃ pratigraham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Without any fear or reservation, a Brahmana should accept charitable gifts from all, but neither a Ksatriya nor a Vaisya should ever accept a charitable gift or a donation.

## \|\| 1.12.4 \|\|

*caṇḍasya putrahīnasya dambhācāraratasya ca \|*  
*svakarmatyāginaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Whatever is given to one who is of a fiery temper or is sonless or is addicted to hypocritical conduct of life and one who avoids his righteous duties and acts prescribed for his caste and state in life, becomes futile.

## \|\| 1.12.5 \|\|

*paradāraratasyāpi paradravyābhiliṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*nakṣatrasūcakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Whatever is donated to a person indulging in adultery with another man’s wife or to one who covets the wealth of another person, or to one who is an astrologer in name only (an imposter), is useless.

## \|\| 1.12.6 \|\|

*asūyāviṣṭamanasaḥ kṛtanghasya ca māyinaḥ \|*  
*ayājyayājakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Whatever is given in charity to a man whose mind is prejudiced with jealousy or to an ungrateful person, or to a cheat or to a person who officiates as a priest at the sacrifice of an unauthorized and ineligible person, is fruitless.

## \|\| 1.12.7 \|\|

*nityaṃ yācñāparasyāpi hiṃsakasya khalasya ca \|*  
*rasavikrayiṇaśvaiva dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Whatever is given to one who is a perpetual beggar, or to one who is violent and wicked or to a vendor of liquors, is profitless.

## \|\| 1.12.8 \|\|

*nāmaikā da vedavikrayiṇaścāpi smṛtivikrayiṇastathā \|*  
*dharmavikrayiṇo vipra dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whatever is given to a person who sells the Vedas (teaches after receiving fees for teaching) or one who sells the Smrtis (i.e. charges fees for giving the rulings from Smrtis) or to one who makes money by performing holy rites, is valueless, О Brahmana!

## \|\| 1.12.9 \|\|

*gānena jīvikā yasya yasya bhāryā ca puścalī \|*  
*paropatāpinaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Whatever is donated as a charitable gift to a person who makes a living by singing songs or one whose wife is an unchaste slut or a person who harasses others, becomes useless.

## \|\| 1.12.10 \|\|

*asijīvī maṣījīvī devalo grāmayājakaḥ \|*  
*dhāvako vā bhavetteṣāṃ dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Whatever is given to the following persons is unproductive of merits: viz. one who makes a living by sword (a person belonging to the military profession); one who earns his livelihood by preparation of ink (or clerical profession) an idol worshipper by profession, the village priest and a washerman.

## \|\| 1.12.11 \|\|

*pākakartuḥ parasyārthe kavaye gadahāriṇe \|*  
*abhakṣya bhakṣakasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Whatever is given to one who works as a cook for another, to a poet or to the remover of an ailment or to one who eats prohibited food, is futile.

## \|\| 1.12.12 \|\|

*śūdrānnabhojinaścaiva śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhinaḥ \|*  
*paiṃśvalānnabhujaścāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Whatever is given in charity to one who habitually partakes of Sudra’s food or to one who cremates the corpses of Sudras or to one who takes food prepared by an unchaste woman, becomes futile.

## \|\| 1.12.13 \|\|

*nāmavikrayiṇo viṣṇoḥ saṃdhyākarṃmorjjhitasya ca \|*  
*duṣpratigrahadagdhasya dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Whatever is donated in charity to one who sells the name of Visnu (i.e. accepts money for the japa, etc. of Visnu) or to one who has given up the performance of Sandhya prayers and to one who is (as it were) burnt by acceptance of monetary gifts from evil men, is unproductive.

## \|\| 1.12.14 \|\|

*divāśayanaśīlasya tathā maithunakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sadhyābhojina evāpidattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Whatever is given to one who sleeps during the day or to one who indulges in sexual intercourse during day time or to one who takes food at the time of twilight (both the dawn and the dusk) is ineffectual.

## \|\| 1.12.15 \|\|

*mahāpātakayuktasya tyaktasya jñātibāndhavaiḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍasya cāpi golasya dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Whatever is donated in charity to a person vitiated by great sins or by one who is excommunicated by his kinsmen and relatives or to a person who is a Kunda (an adulterine son of a woman by another person while her husband is alive) or by a person who is a gola (the bastard son of a widow) is fruitless.

## \|\| 1.12.16 \|\|

*parivatteḥ śaṭhasyāpi parivattuḥ pramādinaḥ \|*  
*strījitasyātiduṣṭasya dattaṃ bhavita niṣphalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Whatever is given to a rogue or to a person who has married before his elder brother’s marriage or one who has taken his share of ancestral property before his elder brother or an erring fellow or a henpecked husband or an extremely wicked person, is unproductive of merit.

## \|\| 1.12.17 \|\|

*madyamāṃsāśinaścāpi strīviṭasyātilobhinaḥ \|*  
*caurasya piśunasyāpi dattaṃ bhavati niṣphalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Whatever is given to one who partakes of meat and wine or to a lecherous libertine, or by a greedy person or to a thief or to a treacherous back-biter, is valueless.

## \|\| 1.12.18 \|\|

*ye kecitpāpaniratā ninditāḥ sujanaiḥ sadā \|*  
*na tebhyaḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna ca vadyāddijottama \|*  
*satkarmaniratāyāpi deyaṃ yatnena nārada \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О excellent Brahmana, one should neither give any gift nor accept any donation from those who are engaged in sinfill activities or those who are always censured by good people. О Narada, a charitable gift must be given with special efforts to one who is engaged in good and noble activities.

## \|\| 1.12.19 \|\|

*yaddānaṃ śraddhayā dattaṃ tathā viṣṇusamarpaṇam \|*  
*yācitaṃ vāpi pātreṇa bhavettaddānamuttamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. That dana (charitable gift) is excellent which is offered with faith, after dedication unto Visnu and requested for by a deserving person.

## \|\| 1.12.20 \|\|

*paralokaṃ samuddaśya hyaihikaṃ vāpi nārada \|*  
*yaddānaṃ dīyate pātre tatkāmyaṃ madhyamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Narada, the gift that is offered to a deserving person with a desire to get its benefit either in this world or in the next, is remembered (in Smrti works) to be mediocre.

## \|\| 1.12.21 \|\|

*dagbhena cāpi hiṃsārthaṃ parasyāvidhināpi ca \|*  
*kruddhenāśraddhayāpātre taddānaṃ madhyamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That dana is considered to be the meanest — the dana or charitable gift that is offered with hypocrisy or for causing injury to others or is given in violation of the scriptural injunctions in the matter or to an undeserving person, and by an infuriated person or by a person lacking in faith.

## \|\| 1.12.22 \|\|

*adhamaṃ balitoṣāyamadhyamaṃ svārthasiddhaye \|*  
*uttamaṃ hariprītyarthaṃ prāhurvedavidāṃ varāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The lowest type of charitable gift is only for the satisfaction of merely an act of giving (oblation?). The mediocre dana is for achieving selfish ends and the excellent type of dana is for the propitiation of Lord Hari — so say excellent experts in the knowledge of Vedas.

## \|\| 1.12.23 \|\|

*dānabhogavināśāśca rāyaḥ syurgatayastridhā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Charitable gifts, enjoyment and destruction — these are the three ways of going away or spending of wealth.

## \|\| 1.12.24 \|\|

*yo dadāti ca nobhukte taddhanaṃ nāśakāraṇam \|*  
*dhanaṃ dharmaphalaṃ vipra dharmo mādhavatuṣṭikṛt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The riches belonging to a person who neither gifts it away nor enjoys it himself, are the causes of his ruin. О Brahmana, wealth is that the fruit of which is Dharma and Dharma is that which propitiates god Visnu.

## \|\| 1.12.25 \|\|

*taravaḥ kiṃ na jīvanti te 'pi loke parārthakāḥ \|*  
*yatra mūlaphalairvṛkṣāḥ parakāryaṃ prakurvate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Do not trees lead a life? They live in this world for the sake of others, for they oblige others by providing them with their roots and fruits.

## \|\| 1.12.26-27 \|\|

*manuṣyā yadi viprāgthra na parārthāstadā mṛtāḥ \|*  
*parakāryaṃ na ye martyāḥ kāyenāpi dhanena vā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*manasā vacasā vāpi te jñeyāḥ pāpakṛttamāḥ \|*  
*atretihāsaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tattvataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. If men do not help others they are (no better than) dead, О prominent Brahmana. Those men who do not render service to others physically, mentally, by word of mouth or through money, should be considered as the most sinful persons. О Narada, listen attentively to an ancient anecdote which I shall narrate to you in this connection.

## \|\| 1.12.28 \|\|

*yatra dānādikānāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*gaṅgāmāhātmyasahitaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In that story the characteristics of dana (and other righteous deeds) have been described along with the greatness of the Ganga. which destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.12.29-30 \|\|

*bhagīrathasya dharmasya saṃvādaṃ puṇyakāraṇam \|*  
*āsīdbhagīratho rājā sagarānvayasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śaśāsa pṛthivīṃ metāṃ satpadvīpāṃ sasāgarām \|*  
*sarvadharmarato nityaṃ satyasaṃdhaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. It is in the form of a dialogue between king Bhagi- ratha and god Dharmaraja, as it is conducive to merit, Formerly, there was a king named Bhagiratha» born in the lineage of Sagara. He ruled over the entire world consisting of seven continents, along with seven oceans. He was always engaged in righteous acts. He was truthful and very brave.

## \|\| 1.12.31 \|\|

*kandarpasaddaśo rupe yāyajṛko vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*prāleyādrisamo dhairye dharme dharmasamo nṛpaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He was good-looking like the god of Love. He constantly performed sacrifices. In courage he was equal to the Himalaya and in piety (Dharma) he was equal to god Dharmaraja (god of Death). He was very intelligent.

## \|\| 1.12.32 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|*  
*sarvasaṃpatsamāyuktaḥ sarvānandakaro mune \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He was richly endowed with all auspicious characteristics, О sage. He was an expert in all scriptural matters. He had all riches and prosperity. He gave delight to every one.

## \|\| 1.12.33 \|\|

*ātithyaprayato nityaṃ vāsudevārcanerataḥ \|*  
*parākramī guṇanidhirmaitraḥ kāruṇikaḥ sadhīḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He was specially solicitous in offering hospitality to guests, and was engaged forever in the worship of Lord Vasudeva. He was very valorous and a receptacle of good qualities. He was friendly, merciful and intelligent.

## \|\| 1.12.34 \|\|

*etādṛśaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ jñātvā dṛṣṭo bhagīratham \|*  
*dharmarājo dvijaśreṣṭha kadāciddraṣṭumāgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Having come to know that Bhagiratha was a king of this nature, god Dharmaraja became delighted. О excellent Brahmana, on one occasion he came down to see him.

## \|\| 1.12.35 \|\|

*samāgataṃ dharmarājamarhayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā dharmaḥ prī uvāca tam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The king greeted and honoured god Dharmaraja who had come to him, in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the scriptures (for receiving a distinguished guest). Dharmaraja who was pleased with him addressed him as follows:

## \|\| 1.12.36 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca*  
*rājandharmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaprasiddho 'si jagattraye \|*  
*dharmarājo 'tha kīrtiṃ te śrutvā tvāṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*God Dharmaraja said:*

36\. О king, you are the most excellent among the knowers of righteousness. You are famous in the three worlds. On hearing about your fame, Dharmaraja himself has come to see you personally.

## \|\| 1.12.37 \|\|

*sanmārganirataṃ satyaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam \|*  
*draṣṭumicchanti vibudhāratavo tkuṣṭaguṇapriyāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Gods, fond of your excellent qualities, wish to see you, a truthful monarch engaged in the path -of good and the welfare of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.12.38 \|\|

*kīrtirnītiśca saṃpattirvartate yatra bhūpate \|*  
*vasanti tatra niyataṃ guṇāḥsantaśca devatāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О king, good qualities, saintly people and deities abide there where fame, morality or righteousness and affluence reside.

## \|\| 1.12.39 \|\|

*aho rājanmahābhāga śobhanīcaritaṃ tava \|*  
*sarvabhūtahitatvādi mādṛśāmapi durlabham \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О highly blessed king, your conduct of life is splendid and exemplary. Your qualities such as striving for the welfare of all living beings, etc. are difficult to be found even in people like me”.

## \|\| 1.12.40 \|\|

*ityuktavantaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ praṇipatya bhagīrathaḥ \|*  
*provāca vinayāviṣṭaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ ślakṣṇayā gitaṃ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When god Dharmaraja said this, Bhagiratha bowed down to him. Delighted yet overcome with a sense of modesty, he submitted to him in soft refined words.

## \|\| 1.12.41 \|\|

*bhagīratha uvāca*  
*bhagavansarvadharmajña samadarśit sureśvara \|*  
*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo yatpṛcchāmi vadasva tat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*Bhagiratha submitted:*

41\. “O Lord, the knower of all Dharmas (righteous duties), you are an impartial witness to everything. Filled with divine grace for me, be pleased to explain what I ask of you.

## \|\| 1.12.42 \|\|

*dharmā kīdṛgvidhāḥ proktāḥ ke lokā dharmaśālinām \|*  
*kiyatyo yātanāḥ proktāḥ keṣāṃ tāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. How many types of dharmas (sacred duties) are there? What regions are reserved for persons who are righteous habitually? How many kinds of tortures are there and to whom are they meted out?

## \|\| 1.12.43 \|\|

*tvayā saṃmānanīyā ye śāsanīyāśca ye yathā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ me mahābhāga vistarādvaktumarhasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Who are the persons to be honoured by you and who are to be chastised? О highly blessed one, it behoves you to mention all this in details.”

## \|\| 1.12.44 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca*  
*sādhu sādhu mahāvuddhe matiste vimalorjitā \|*  
*dharmādharmānpravakṣyāmitattvataḥ śṛṇu bhaktitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*Dharmaraja explained:*

44\. “Well done, О highly intelligent one, very well done. Your intellect is unblemished and powerful. I shall explain to you factually in details what are the righteous acts and what are the evil ones. Listen to it with faith and devotion.

## \|\| 1.12.45 \|\|

*dharmā bahuvidhāḥ proktāḥ puṇyalokapradāyakāḥ \|*  
*tathaiva yātanāḥ proktā asaṃkhyā ghoradarśatāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Dharmas (righteous duties) have been proclaimed as being of various kinds. They are the bestowers of meritorious worlds. The tortures too are declared to be numerous and are very terrible to be viewed.

## \|\| 1.12.46 \|\|

*vistarādgadituṃ nālamapi varṣaśatāyutaiḥ \|*  
*tasmātaṃsamāsato vakṣye dharmādharmamidarśanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It is not possible to describe in details the examples of virtues and evils in hundreds and ten thousands of years. Hence, I shall mention them succincdy.

## \|\| 1.12.47 \|\|

*tathaiva yātanāṃ vai mahāpuṇyaṃ prakīrtatam \|*  
*tathaivādhyātmaviduṣo dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The gift of the means of livelihood to Brahmanas is glorified as highly meritorious. Similarly, what is given unto a knower of spiritual lore is of ever-lasting benefit.

## \|\| 1.12.48 \|\|

*kuṭumbinaṃ yā śāstrajñaṃ śrotriyaṃ vā guṇānvitam \|*  
*yo dattvā syāpayedṛtiṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Listen to the meritorious benefits attained by one who bestows means of livelihood upon a scholar of scriptural texts who is burdened with a large family or upon a Vedic scholar blessed with all good qualities and stabilises him.

## \|\| 1.12.49 \|\|

*mātṛtāḥ pitṛtaścaiva dvijaḥ koṭikulanvitaḥ \|*  
*nirviśya viṣṇubhavanaṃ kalpaṃ tatraiva mādate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The twice-born donor accompanied by ten million members of his family on his mother’s side and on his father’s side, will enter Visnu’s abode and rejoice there for a period of a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.12.50 \|\|

*gaṇyante pāṃsavo bhūmergaṇyante vṛṣṭivindavaḥ \|*  
*na gaṇyante vidhātrāpi brahahmavṛttiphalāni vai \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Particles of dust on the earth can be counted. Drops of rain can be enumerated. But the benefits of providing Brahmanas with means of livelihood cannot be estimated even by the Creator (god Brahma).

## \|\| 1.12.51 \|\|

*samastadevatārupo brāhmaṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*jīvanaṃ dadatastasya kaḥ puṇyaṃ gadituṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A Brahmana is glorified as the embodiment of all deities. Who is competent to recount the merits of a person who provides him with the means of livelihood?

## \|\| 1.12.52 \|\|

*yo viprahitakṛnnityaṃ sa sarvānkṛtavānmakhān \|*  
*sa strātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu tatpaṃ tenākhilaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He who is always a benefactor to Brahmanas, has performed all sacrifices (i.e. he attains the same benefits as one who performs all sacrifices). He gets the credit of performing ablutions in all sacred waters and all types of penance have been performed by him.

## \|\| 1.12.53 \|\|

*yo dadasveti viprāṇāṃ jīvanaṃ prerayetparam \|*  
*so 'pi tatphalamāpnoti kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He too who induces another to provide Brahmanas with means of livelihood saying ‘Give’, attains the same merit as that of the donor. What need is there to expatiate on it?

## \|\| 1.12.54 \|\|

*taḍāgaṃ kārayedyastu svayamevāpareṇa vā \|*  
*vaktuṃ tatpuṇyasaṃkhyānaṃ nālaṃ varṣaśatāyuṣā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If a person constructs a lake or causes it to be dug through others, it is not possible to enumerate the merits of that person even with a span of life extending to a period of hundred years.

## \|\| 1.12.55 \|\|

*ekaścedadhvago rājaṃstaḍāgasya jalaṃ pibet \|*  
*katkartuḥ sarvapāpāni naśyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Even if a single wayfarer drinks the water of that lake, there is no doubt that all the sins of the digger of that lake are wiped out.

## \|\| 1.12.56 \|\|

*ekāhamaṣi yatkuryādbhūmisthamudakaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sa muktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ śatavarṣaṃ vaseddivi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If a man is able to retain water on the surface of the earth, even for a single day, he will be absolved of all sins and shall reside in heaven, for a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.12.57 \|\|

*kartuṃ taḍāgaṃ yo martyaḥ sāhyakaḥ śaktito bhavet \|*  
*so 'pi tatphalanāpnoti tuṣṭaḥ preraka eva ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A person who associates himself with the work of digging a lake, according to his capacity, attains the fruit of the same (i.e. digging it himself), so also does the person who is glad at it or who persuades persons to do it.

## \|\| 1.12.58 \|\|

*mṛdaṃ siddhārthamātrāṃ vā taḍāgādyo vahiḥ kṣipet \|*  
*tiṣṭatyabdaśataṃ svarge vimuktaḥ pāpakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If a man throws out of the tank mud of the size of a white mustard, he stays in the heaven for a hundred years, liberated from millions of sins.,

## \|\| 1.12.59 \|\|

*devatā yasya tuṣyanti guravo vā nṛpottama \|*  
*taḍāgapuṇyabhāksa syādityeṣā śāśvatī śrutiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О excellent king, the eternal Sruti states that if the deities or preceptors are pleased with any one, he shall derive the merit of digging lakes.

## \|\| 1.12.60 \|\|

*iti hāsaṃ pravakṣyāmi tavātra nṛpasattama \|*  
*yaṃ śṛtvā sarvapāyebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In this connection, О excellent king, I shall narrate to you a mythological anecdote on listening to which, one is undoubtedly liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.12.61 \|\|

*gauḍadeśe 'tivikhyāto rājāsīdvīrabhadrakaḥ \|*  
*mahāpratīpī vidyāvānsadā vipraprapūjakaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In the Gauda land, there was a very famous king named Virabhadraka. He was very valiant and learned. He was ever worshipful to Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.12.62 \|\|

*vedaśāstrakulācārayukto mitrakvirdhanaḥ \|*  
*tasya rājñī mahābhāgā nānmā campakamañjarī \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He was a follower of the code of conduct as prescribed in the Vedas and Smrtis or scriptural texts and those handed down by family traditions. He increased his circle of friends. His queen named Campakamanjari was a highly fortunate lady.

## \|\| 1.12.63 \|\|

*tasya rājño mahāmātyāḥ kṛtmākṛsyavicāraṇāḥ \|*  
*dharmāṇāṃ dharmaśāstrestu sadā kurvanti niścayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The great ministers of that king thought and pondered over what should be or should not be done. They always came to a decision in matters of Dharmas through Dharmasastras.

## \|\| 1.12.64 \|\|

*prāyaścittaṃ cikittsāṃ ca jyotiṣe dharmanirṇayam \|*  
*vināśāstreṇa yo brūyāttamāhurbrahmaghātakam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If a person, without consulting the Sastric texts, gives a decision in matters of expiation (of sins), medical diagnosis, or astrological topics, he is called a Brahmana-slayer in Smrtis.

## \|\| 1.12.65 \|\|

*iti niścitya manasā manvādīritadharmkān \|*  
*ācāryebhyaḥ sadā bhūpaḥ śṛṇoti vidhipūrvakam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Coming to this conclusion in his mind, the king always used to listen to the holy Dharmas as proclaimed by Manu and other Smrti-writers, in accordance with injunctions.

## \|\| 1.12.66-69 \|\|

*na ko 'pyanyāyavartī tasya rājye 'varo 'pi ca \|*  
*dharmeṇa pālyamānasya tasya deśasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*jātaṃ samatvaṃ svargasya saurājyasya śubhāvaham \|*  
*sa caikadā tu nṛpatirmṛgayāyāṃ mahāvane \|\| 67 \|\|*

*mantryādibhiḥ parivṛto babhrāma madhyabhāskaram \|*  
*daivādākheṭaśūnyasya hyatiśrāntasya tatra vai \|\| 68 \|\|*

*nṛparītasya saṃjātaṃ saraso darśanaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tataḥ śuṣkāṃ tu sarasīṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra vyacintayat \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-67a. While the king was ruling that country according to Dharma (Sastric rules of government), there was no person prone to injustice or mean in his kingdom. That realm of the king became equal to the celestial world, as it was being administered through Dharma. It was auspiciously blessed with good king.

67b-69. One day, the king went into a great forest for hunting. Surrounded by ministers and others he wandered till midday. Due to ill-luck, he did not get any game. He became tired. О king, surrounded by men, he chanced to see a lake. On seeing that dried up lake he thought.

## \|\| 1.12.70 \|\|

*kimayaṃ sarasīśṛṅgebhuvaḥ kena vinirmitā \|*  
*kathaṃ jalaṃ bhavedatra yena jīvedayaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “By whom and wherefor has this lake been built on an elevated piece of land? How can there be water here so that he, the king and his associates may survive?”

## \|\| 1.12.71 \|\|

*tato buddhiḥ samabhavatkhāte tasyā nṛpottama \|*  
*hastamātraṃ tato garttaṃ khātvā toyamavātpavān \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. О excellent king, then it occurred to him to dig it further. By digging a pit to the depth of a cubit (about 18 inches), he found water.

## \|\| 1.12.72 \|\|

*tena toyena pītena rājñastṛtpirajāyata \|*  
*mantriṇaścāpi bhūmiśa buddhisāgarasaṃjñinaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. By drinking that water the thirst of the king and that of the minister Buddhisagara was quenched.

## \|\| 1.12.73-74 \|\|

*sa buddhisāgaro bhūpaṃ prāha dharmārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*rājanniyaṃ puṣkariṇī varṣājalavatī purā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*adyaināṃ baddhavaprāṃ ca karttuṃ jātā matirmama \|*  
*tadbhavānmodatāṃ deva dattādājñāṃ ca me 'nagha \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. The minister Buddhisagara, an expert in matters regarding Dharma, submitted to the king: “O king, formerly this lake had plenty of rain water. Today, I am inclined to build a strong embankment round it. May it please your majesty and grant me the permission for the same, О sinless Lord.”

## \|\| 1.12.75 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacastasya mantriṇo nṛpasattamaḥ \|*  
*mumude 'titarāṃ bhūpaḥ svayaṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On hearing these words of the minister, the excellent king was highly delighted and the king himself undertook to construct it.

## \|\| 1.12.76-77 \|\|

*tameva mantriṇāṃ tatra yuyoja śubhakarmaṇi \|*  
*tato rājājñayā so 'pi buddhisāgarako mudā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sarasīṃ sāgaraṃ karttumudyataḥ puṇyakṛttamaḥ \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ caiva pañcāśatsarvato vistṛtāyatām \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. He entrusted that very minister with the work of that auspicious task. Then, at the behest of the king, the highly meritorious and gifted Buddhisagara joyously attempted to convert that lake into a sea (i.e. a big lake) extending it to fifty Dhanus. (1 dhanu = 4 hastas or about 6 feet) all round.

## \|\| 1.12.78 \|\|

*sarasīṃ baddhasu śilāṃ cakārāgādhaśambarām \|*  
*tāṃ vinirmāya sarasīṃ rājñe sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Having constructed the lake deep with water and with a strong embankment of stones all round he reported the matter to the king in details.

## \|\| 1.12.79 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tataḥ prabhṛti vai sarve 'pi vanacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*pānthāḥ pipāsitā bhūpa labhante sma jalaṃ śubham \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. О king, thereafter, all the thirsty way-farers roaming in forest (and beasts of the jungle as well) got splendid, translucent water for drinking from that lake.

## \|\| 1.12.80 \|\|

*kadācitsvāyuṣaścānte sa mantrī buddhisāgaraḥ \|*  
*pramṛto gatavāṃllokaṃ lokaśāsturmama prabho \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. One day, when his span of life in the world ended, that minister Buddhisagara died. О lord, he came to my region, since I am the ruler and chastiser of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.12.81 \|\|

*tadarthaṃ tu mayā pṛṣṭo dharmo dharmalipiṅkaraḥ \|*  
*citragutpastu tatkarma mahyaṃ sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Citragupta, the accountant of the deeds committed by men, was asked by me about him (the minister). He reported to me everything that he did during his life time.

## \|\| 1.12.82 \|\|

*upadeṣṭā svayaṃ cāsau dharmakāryasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*tasmāddharmavimānaṃ tu samāroḍhumihārhati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. He himself was the advisor in meritorious activities to the king. Hence, he deserved to ride in the Dharma — aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.12.83 \|\|

*ityukte citragutpena samājñatpo mayā nṛpa \|*  
*vimānaṃ dharmasaṃjñaṃ tu āroḍhuṃ buddhisāgaraḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. О king, when this was reported by Citragupta, Buddhisagara was commanded by me to get into the aerial car called Dharma.

## \|\| 1.12.84 \|\|

*atha kālāntare rājansarājā vīrabhadrakaḥ \|*  
*mṛto gato mama sthānaṃ namaścakre mudānvitaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Then, after some time, О king, the ruler Virabhadraka died and came to my abode. With joy, he bowed to me.

## \|\| 1.12.85 \|\|

*mayā tu tatra tasyāpi pṛṣṭaṃ karmākhilaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*kathitaṃ citragutpena dharmaṃ sarasisaṃbhavam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. О king, all the deeds done by him were completely inquired of by me. The merit accruing from the construction of the lake was reported by Citragupta.

## \|\| 1.12.86-87 \|\|

*tadā samyaṅmayā rājā bodhito 'bhūdyathāśṛṇu \|*  
*adhityakāyāṃ bhūpāla saikatasya gireḥ parā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*lāvakenāmunācañcvā khātaṃ dvyaṃṅguprambuni \|*  
*tataḥ kālāntare tena vārāheṇa nṛpottama \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. Now please listen how the king was properly enlightened by me: “O king, formerly on the ridge of the sand dume, a quail had dug up with its beak and water to the depth of two angulas (finger-breadths) had come up. Then after some time, О excellent king, a boar dug it up with its snout to the depth of a cubit (18 inches).

## \|\| 1.12.88-89 \|\|

*khanitaṃ hastamātraṃ tu jalaṃ tuṇḍena cātmanaḥ \|*  
*tato 'nyadāmuyā kālyāhasta yugmamitaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*khāto jale mahārāja toyaṃ māsadvayaṃ sthitam \|*  
*pītaṃ kṣudrairvanacaraiḥ sattvaistṛṣṇāsamākulaiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Then, on another occasion, it was made to extend to two hastas by this Kali (a black heron.) О great king, in that dug up lake, water remained for two months. It was drunk by small wild animab which were afflicted with thirst.

## \|\| 1.12.90-93 \|\|

*tato varṣatrāyānte tu gajatānena suvrata \|*  
*hastatrayamitaḥ khātaḥ kṛtastatrādhikaṃ jalam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*māsatraye sthitaṃ tacca payo jīvairvanecaraiḥ \|*  
*bhavāṃstatra samāyāto jalaśoṣāda nantaram \|\| 91 \|\|*

*māse tatra tu saṃprātpaṃ hastaṃ khātvā jalaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tatastasyopadeśena mantriṇo nṛpate tvayā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pañcāśaddhanurutkhātaṃ jātaṃ tatatra mahājalam \|*  
*punaḥ śilābhiḥ sudṛḍhaṃ baddhaṃ jātaṃ mahatsaraḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣāśca ropitāstatra sarvalokopakāriṇaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

90-93. О king, observer of holy vows, thereafter, at the end of three years, it was dug up to a depth of three *hastas* (cubits) by this elephant and more water sprang up. The water that stood there for three months (was drunk up) by the residents and animals roaming in the forest. Your honour visited that spot after the water had been completely dried up. О king, after digging to a depth of hasta, water rose up and it stood for a month. Then О king, on the advice of the minister you caused it to be dug up to an extent of 50 *dhanus* (about 300 feet). It abounded in water. The great lake was made more durable with bank built up of stones. Trees were planted all round rendering great help to all people.

## \|\| 1.12.94 \|\|

*tena svasvena puṇyena pañcaite jagatīpate \|*  
*vimānaṃ dharmyamāruḍhāstvamāṇyenaṃ samāruha \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. О lord of the Universe, these five have got into the aerial car called Dharma, thanks to their respective merit. You too, get into it.”

## \|\| 1.12.95 \|\|

*iti vākyaṃ samākarṇya mama rājā sa bhūmipa \|*  
*āruroha vimānaṃ tatṣaṣṭho rājā samāṃśabhāk \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. О king, on hearing this statement of mine, that king got into the aerial car as the sixth one, sharing equal amount of merit with them.

## \|\| 1.12.96 \|\|

*iti te sarvamākhyātaṃ taḍāgajanitaṃ phalam \|*  
*śrutvaitanmucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇāntikāt \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Thus, everything connected with the meritorious benefit accruing from constructing the lake has been narrated to you. After this, one is liberated from sins committed from birth till death.

## \|\| 1.12.97 \|\|

*yo naraḥ śraddhayo yukto vyākhyātaṃ śruṇuyātpaṭhet \|*  
*so 'pyāpnotyakhilaṃ puṇyaṃ saronirmāṇasaṃbhavam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The man who devoutly listens to and reads this discourse, derives all the merit that is credited to one for constructing a lake.

## Chapter 13. A Discourse on Dharma

## \|\| 1.13.1 \|\|

*dharmarāja uvāca*  
*devatāyatanaṃ yastu kurute kārayatyapi \|*  
*śivasyāpi harervāpi tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Dharmaraja said:*

1\. Listen to the meritorious benefit to a person who himself builds or pursuades others to build a temple of either Siva or Hari.

## \|\| 1.13.2 \|\|

*mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaścaiva lakṣakoṭikulānvitaḥ \|*  
*kalpatrayaṃ viṣṇupade tiṣṭatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is no doubt that he (such a builder) will stay in lord Visnu’s region for three kalpas in the company of a hundred thousand and ten million members of his family on his mother’s side as well as on his father’s side.

## \|\| 1.13.3 \|\|

*mṛdaiva kurute yastu devatāyatanaṃ niraḥ \|*  
*mṛdaiva kurute yastu devatāyatanaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yāvatpuṇyaṃ bhavettasya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Listen to the extent of merit, if a man builds the shrine with mud and clay. I shall now recount it.

## \|\| 1.13.4 \|\|

*divyadehadharo bhūtvā vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*kalpatrayaṃ viṣṇupade tiṣṭatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Taking up a brilliant divine body and travelling by an excellent aerial car, he will stay in Visnu’s region for three kalpas. Entertain no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.13.5 \|\|

*mṛdaiva kurute yastu devatāyatanaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yāvatpuṇyaṃ bhavettasya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Listen to me even as I recount, the extent of merit if a person constructs the shrine (of Siva or Visnu) with earthen materials.

## \|\| 1.13.6 \|\|

*divyadehadharo bhūtvā vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*kalpatrayaṃ viṣṇupade sthitvā brahmapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He will assume a lustrous, divine body and ride in an excellent heavenly car. After staying in Visnu’s region for three Kalpas, he will then proceed to the capital of god Brahma.

## \|\| 1.13.7-8 \|\|

*kalpavadvayaṃ sthitastatra punaḥ kalpaṃ vaseddivi \|*  
*tatastu yogināmeva kule jāto dayonvitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vaiṣṇavaṃ yogamāsthāya muktiṃ vrajati śāśvatīm \|*  
*dārubhiḥ kurute yastu tasya syāddiguṇaṃ phalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. After staying there for two kalpas, he will reside in the celestial world for the period of one kalpa. He will afterwards be born in the family of Yogins and be merciful (to all). Adopting the Yoga pertaining to Visnu, he will attain eternal emancipation from samsara. If a man builds the temple with wood, meritorious benefit twice this, will accrue to him.

## \|\| 1.13.9 \|\|

*triguṇaṃ ceṣṭakābhistu śilābhistaccaturgaṇam \|*  
*sphuṭikābhiḥ śilābhistu jñeyaṃ daśaguṇottaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If he builds the temple in brick, the meritorious benefit is three times that of building the temple with earthen material. If it is built with stones, the benefit is four times and if the shrine is constructed with crystal slabs, the benefit should be known to be ten time.

## \|\| 1.13.10-13 \|\|

*tānmībhistacchataguṇaṃ hemnā koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*devālayaṃ taḍāgaṃ vā grāmaṃ vā pālayettu yaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kartuḥ śataguṇaṃ tasya puṇyaṃ bhavati bhūpate \|*  
*devālayasya śuśrūṣāṃ lepasecanamaṇḍanaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kuryādyatsatataṃ bhaktyā tasya puṇyamanantakam \|*  
*vetanādviṣṭito vāpi puṇyakarmapravarttitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*te gacchanti dharādhārāḥ śāścataṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|*  
*tāḍāgārddhaphalaṃ rājankāsāre parikīrtitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. If the temple is built of copper (sheets and ingots), the meritorious benefit is hundred-fold and if it is built of gold, the merit that accrues to him is ten million times (that of constructing the shrine of clay).  
(10b.) If aperson looks after the temple, a lake or a village, О king, his meritorious benefit is hundred times that of the builder. If a person looks after the temple by scrubbing or sweeping with a broom, smearing it and sprinkling water or embellishing it with devotion, he derives infinite merit. Those who perform meritorious deeds in return for salary or without any remuneration go to Visnu’s eternal region perpetually. О king, the merit in digging a small artificial lake is stated to be half the merit of digging a big lake containing lotuses.

## \|\| 1.13.14 \|\|

*kūpe pādaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ vāpyāṃ padmākaronmitam \|*  
*vāpīśataguṇaṃ proktaṃ kulyāyāṃ bhūpateḥ phalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The merit accruing from digging a well is one-fourth and that of a tank should be known as equal to that of a lotus pond. О king, the meritorious benefit in digging a canal is said to be hundred times greater than that of constructing a tank.

## \|\| 1.13.15 \|\|

*dṛṣadbhistudhanīḥkuryānmṛdā niṣkiñcano janaḥ \|*  
*tayoḥ phalaṃ samānaṃ syādityāha kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A rich person should build up a tank with stones (stone embankment) and a poor man should build it with an earthen bank. But the lotus-bom god Brahma says that the merit derived by them both is equal.

## \|\| 1.13.16 \|\|

*dadyādāḍhyāstu nagaraṃ hastamātramakiñcanaḥ \|*  
*bhuvaṃ tayoḥ samaphalaṃ prāhurvedavido janāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. People who know the Vedas say that if a prosperous, affluent person gifts away a whole city and an indigent fellow donates a plot of land extending to a hand (18 inches), both of them have equal meritorious benefit.

## \|\| 1.13.17 \|\|

*dhanāḍhyaḥ kurute yastu taḍāgaṃ phalasādhanam \|*  
*daridraḥ kurute kūpaṃ samaṃ puṇyaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If a rich man constructs a big tank which may cause much benefit and an impoverished person digs a well, the merit in both the cases is declared to be equal.

## \|\| 1.13.18 \|\|

*āśramaṃ kārayedyastu bahujantūpakārakam \|*  
*sa yāti brahmabhuvanaṃ kulatrayasamanvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A person causes a hermitage to be built — a hermitage that is of great use to many creatures, he goes to god Brahma’s world along with three generations of family.

## \|\| 1.13.19 \|\|

*dhenurvā brahmaṇo vāpi yo vā ko vāpi bhūpate \|*  
*kṣaṇārddhaṃ tasya chāyāyāṃ tiṣṭansvargaṃ nayatyamum \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О king, if a cow or a Brahmana or any one stands in the shed even for half a moment, the builder thereof is taken to heaven.

## \|\| 1.13.20 \|\|

*ārāmakārakā rājandevatāgṛhakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*taḍāgagrāmakarttāraḥ pūjyante hariṇā saha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О king, those who lay out parks and gardens, those who construct temples and those who dig lakes and build up villages (human settlements) are worshipped along with Hari.

## \|\| 1.13.21 \|\|

*sarvalokopakārārthaṃ puṣpārāmaṃ janeśvarā \|*  
*kurvate devatārthaṃ vā teṣāṃ puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Listen, О king, to the rewards of merit accruing to those who lay out flower gardens for the benefit of all people or for the worship of deities.

## \|\| 1.13.22 \|\|

*tatra yāvanti parṇāni kusumāni bhavanti ca \|*  
*tāvadvarṣāṇi nākastho modate kulakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With ten million members of his family, he stays in the celestial region and enjoys himself as many years as there are flowers and fruits there (in the flower garden).

## \|\| 1.13.23 \|\|

*prākārakāriṇastasya kaṇṭakāvaraṇapradāḥ \|*  
*prayānti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yugānāmekasatpatim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23 Those who construct a compound-wall round them and those who make thorny hedges around them, proceed to god Brahma’s abode and stay there for seventy one yugas or one kalpa.

## \|\| 1.13.24 \|\|

*tulasīropaṇaṃ ye tu kurtate manuje śvara \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṇyaphalaṃ rājanvadato me niśāmaya \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Lord of men, listen to me as I relate to you the blessings that await those who plant Tulasi (the basil plant), О king.

## \|\| 1.13.25 \|\|

*satpakoṭikulairyukto mātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā \|*  
*vasetkalpaśataṃ sāgraṃ nārāyaṇapadaṃ nṛpa \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О king, for a period of a hundred kalpas and more, he will stay at the feet i.e. in the region of Narayana, accompanied by seventy million members of his family from his mother’s side as well as from his father’s side.

## \|\| 1.13.26 \|\|

*ūrddhapuṇḍradharo yastu tulasīmūlamṛtstrayā \|*  
*gopikācandanenāpi citrakūṭamṛdāpi vā \|*  
*gaṅgāmṛtikayā caiva tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Listen to the reward of merit got by one who wears the Urdhva-pundra (a vertical mark on the forehead) with the mud taken from the root from the Tulasi plant or the paste of Gopicandana (a species of white clay said to be brought from Dvaraka and used by Visnu’s worshippers for marking the forehead), or the sandal-paste or mud taken from Citrakuta or that from the bed of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.13.27 \|\|

*vimānavaramāruḍho gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*saṃgīyamānacarito modate viṣṇuṃmadire \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Such a person rides in an excellent aerial car and goes to Visnu’s abode. He enjoys himself there while his praise is being sung about, by hosts of Gandharvas and Apsaras,

## \|\| 1.13.28 \|\|

*patrāṇi tulasīmūlādyāvanti patitāni vai \|*  
*tāvanti brahmahatyādipātakāni hatāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As many of the sins grevious like that of Brahmana- slaughter are dispelled, as the leaves that fall at the root of the Tulasi plant.

## \|\| 1.13.29 \|\|

*tulasyāṃ secayedyastu jalaṃ culukamātrakam \|*  
*kṣīrodavāsinā sārddhaṃ vasedācandratārakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A man who sprinkles at least a handful of water on the Tulasi plant, shall stay along with god Visnu, the dweller in the milky ocean, as long as the moon and the stars shine.

## \|\| 1.13.30 \|\|

*dadāti brāhmaṇānāṃ yaḥ komalaṃ tulasīdalam \|*  
*sa yāti brahmasadane kulatritayatasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He who gives a tender leaf of the Tulasi plant to Brahmanas, goes to god Brahma’s abode (Satyaloka) accompanied by three generations of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.31 \|\|

*śālaprāmer'payedyastu tulasyāstu dalāni ca \|*  
*sa vasedviṣṇubhavane yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He who offers in worship the leaves of the Tulasi plant on the Salagrama (stone) will stay in Visnu’s abode (Vaikuntha), till the time of the dissolution of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.13.32 \|\|

*kaṇṭakāvaraṇaṃ yastu prākāraṃ vāpi kārayet \|*  
*so 'pyekaviṃśatikulairmodate viṣṇumandire \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He who makes a thorny hedge all around or builds a wall encompassing (a garden of flowers), rejoices in Visnu’s abode in the company of twentyone generations of his family (usually ten predecessors plus himself plus ten successors).

## \|\| 1.13.33 \|\|

*yo 'rccayeddharipādābjaṃ tulasyāḥ komalairdalaiḥ \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛttirviṣṇulokānnareśvara \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О lord of men, he who worships the lotus feet of lord Hari by means of the tender leaves of the Tulasi plant, does not ever return from the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.13.34 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ yaḥ kṣīreṇa snāpayeddharim \|*  
*kulāyutayutaḥ so 'pi modate vaiṣṇave pade \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who performs the ablution of Hari with milk on the full moon day or on the Dvadasi (twelfth) day (both of the dark and bright half of the month) enjoys himself in the region of Visnu, accompanied by ten thousand members of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.35 \|\|

*prasthamātreṇa payasā yaḥ snāpayati keśavam \|*  
*kulāyutāyutayutaḥ so 'pi viṣṇupure vaset \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He who bathes lord Kesava (Visnu) with a prastha measure of milk, lives in god Visnu’s city (Vaikuntha), accompanied by ten crores of the members of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.36 \|\|

*ghṛtaprasthena yo viṣṇuṃ dvādaśyāṃ snāpayennaraḥ \|*  
*kulakoṭiyuto rājansāyujyaṃ labhate hareḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The man who bathes Visnu with a prastha of ghee on the Dvadasi (twelfth) day, О king, attains the type of liberation called Sayujyata (identity with the deity) along with ten million members of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.37 \|\|

*pañcāmṛtena yaḥ snānamekādaśyāṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*viṣṇoḥ sāyujyakaṃ tasya bhavetyulaśatāyutaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He who performs the ablution of Visnu on the Ekadasi (eleventh day in each half of the month) with Pancamrta (sweet mixture of milk, sugar, curds, ghee and honey) attains Sayujyata (identity) with Visnu, accompanied by millions of the members of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.38 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ vā nṛpottama \|*  
*nālikerodakairviṣṇuṃ snāpayettatphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Listen to the fruit attained by the excellent person which performs the ablution of god Visnu with the water taken from the tender coconut fruit on the Ekadasi (eleventh), Dvadasi (twelfth) day or the full moon day, О excellent king.

## \|\| 1.13.39 \|\|

*daśajanmārjitaiḥ pāpairvimukto nṛpasattama \|*  
*śatadvayakulairyukto modate viṣṇunā saha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Such a person shall be liberated from the sins accumulated during the course of ten (previous) births. He rejoices along with Visnu and two hundred members of his family, О excellent king.

## \|\| 1.13.40 \|\|

*ikṣutoyena deveśaṃ yaḥ snāpayati bhūpate \|*  
*keśavaṃ lakṣapitṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О king, he who bathes the lord of gods (i.e. Visnu) with sugar-cane juice shall attain to Vaikuntha (Visnu’s region) along with a hundred thousand ancestors.

## \|\| 1.13.41 \|\|

*puṣpodakena govindaṃ tathā gandhodakena ca \|*  
*snāpayitvā hariṃ bhaktyā vaiṣṇavaṃ padamānpuyāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By bathing lord Govinda with water mixed with flowers as well as with scented water and worshipping lord Hari with devotion, a person will attain the region of Visiiu.

## \|\| 1.13.42 \|\|

*jalena vastrapūtena yaḥ snāpayati mādhavam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇunā saha modate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He who bathes Madhava (the consort of Laksmi) with water filtered and purified with a piece of cloth, becomes liberated from all sins and rejoices with Visnu.

## \|\| 1.13.43 \|\|

*kṣīrādyaiḥ snāpayedyastu ravisaṃkramaṇe harim \|*  
*sa vasedviṣṇusadane trisatpapuruṣaiḥ saha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He who bathes Hari with milk, etc., when the sun is in transit (from one sign of zodiac to another), stays in Visnu’s region along with twenty one generations.

## \|\| 1.13.44-49 \|\|

*śuklapakṣe caturddaśyāmaṣṭamyāṃ pūrṇimādine \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ekādaśyāṃ bhānuvāre dvādaśyāṃ pañcamītithau \|*  
*somasūryoparāge ca manvādiṣuyugādiṣu \|\| 45 \|\|*

*arddhodaye ca sūryasya puṣyārke rohiṇībudhe \|*  
*tathaiva śaniro hiṇyāṃ bhaumāśvinyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śanyāṃ bhṛvabhṛge caivabhṛgurevurevatisaṅgame \|*  
*tathā budhānurādhāyāṃ śravaṇārke tathaiva ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tathā ca somaśravaṇe hastayukte bṛhaspatau \|*  
*budhāṣṭamyāṃ budhāṣāḍhe puṇye vine tathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*strāpaye tpayasā viṣṇuṃ śāntimān vāgyataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*ghṛtena madhunā vāpi dadhnā vā tatphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 49 \|\|*

44-49. Listen to the reward for the merit accruing from bathing lord Visnu with milk, ghee, curd, or honey on the ol lowing occasions: On the Astami (eighth day) or the fourteenth day in the bright half of a month, on the full moon day, on the Ekadasi day, on a Sunday, on the Dvadasi (twelfth) day, and on the Pancami (fifth day of the two halves of the month), during the period of the lunar or the solar eclipse, on the anniversary of Manvantaras and the beginnings of Yugas, etc., when the Moon has partially risen (Ardhodaya), when the Sun accompanies the constellation Рusуa when the planet Budha (Mercury) is with the constellation Rohini, when the planet Saturn is in the constellation Rohini, when the planet Mars is in the company of the constellation Asvini, on Saturdays, when the planet Venus is in conjunction with Mrgasiras (the Orion) or the Revati constellation, when the planet Mercury is with Anuradha, when the Sun accompanies Sravana, when the Moon is in Sravana, when Brhaspati (the planet Jupiter) is in conjunction with constellation Hasta, when there is Budhastami day or the Mercury is in conjunction with the constellation Asadha or on other auspicious days. Such a person must be quiescent, pure and restrained in speech.

## \|\| 1.13.50 \|\|

*sarvayajñaphalaṃ prāpye sarvapāpavivaparjitaḥ \|*  
*vaseṣṭiṣṇupure sārdaṃ trisatpapuruṣairmṛpa \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He accomplishes the merit of performing all sacrifices О King. Being absolved of all sins, he will stay in Lord Visnu’s city (Vaikuntha) with twenty-one generations of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.51 \|\|

*tatraiva jñānamāsādya yogināmapi durlabham \|*  
*mokṣamāproti nṛpate punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. While staying there, he attains perfect spiritual wisdom which is rarely accessible even to Togins. О king, he attains liberation from Samsara from which it is difficult to return (to the cycle of births and deaths).

## \|\| 1.13.52 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśaayāṃ somavāre ca bhūpate \|*  
*śivaṃ saṃstrāpya dugdhena śivasāyujyamānpuyāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. By bathing god Siva with milk on the fourteenth day of the dark half of the month or on a Monday, a person shall attain liberation called Sayujyata (identification) with Siva, О King.

## \|\| 1.13.53 \|\|

*nālikerodakenāpi śivaṃ saṃstrāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamyāminduvāre vā śivasāyujyamaśnute \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. By bathing Siva devotedly with the juice of a tender coconut fruit on the Astami (eighth day) of the half of the month or on a Monday, one attains absorption in Lord Siva.

## \|\| 1.13.54 \|\|

*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāmaṣyamyāṃ vāpi bhūpate \|*  
*ghṛtena madhunā strāpya śivāṃ tatsāmyatāṃ vrajet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. By bathing god Siva with ghee or honey on the eighth or the fourteenth day in the bright half of the month a person attains equality with him, О Lord of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.13.55 \|\|

*tilatailena saṃstrāpya viṣṇuṃ vā śivamevaṃ ca \|*  
*sa yāti tattatsārupyaṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha satpabhiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. By bathing god Visnu or god Siva with Sesamum oil one attains the Sarupya (similarity of form) with the respective deity, along with seven of his ancestors.

## \|\| 1.13.56 \|\|

*śivamiśrurasenāpi yaḥ snāpayati bhaghaktitaḥ \|*  
*śivaloke vasetkalpaṃ sasatpapuruṣaiḥ saha \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He who bathes Siva devotedly with sugarcane juice will stay in the region of god Siva for the period of a Kalpa, along with seven generations.

## \|\| 1.13.57 \|\|

*ghṛtena snāpayelliṅgamutthāne dvādaśīdine \|*  
*kṣīreṇa vā mahābhāga tatphalaṃ śṛṇu madgirā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О blessed one, listen vo the meritorious benefit attained by one who bathes the Lihga idol of god Siva with ghee on the Dvadasi day in the bright half of month of Karttika when god Visnu arises from his slumber of four months, as I describe it to you.

## \|\| 1.13.58 \|\|

*janmāyutakṛtakaiḥ pāpairdarmukto manujo nṛpa \|*  
*koṭi saṃkhyaṃ samuddhṛkatya svakulaṃ śivatāṃ vrajet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. He will be liberated, О king, from the sins committed in ten thousand previous births. The man shall uplift the members of his family numbering to ten million and he will attain Sivahood.

## \|\| 1.13.59 \|\|

*sampūjya gandhakusumairviṣṇuṃ viṣṇutithau nṛpa \|*  
*janmāyutārjitaiḥ pāpairmukto vrajati tatpadam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О king, after worshipping Visnu with fragrant flowers on the day sacred to Visnu (i.e. eleventh or the twelfth day in the dark and bright half of the month), he will be liberated from the sins accumulated in the course of ten thousand births and proceed to his region (Vaikuntha).

## \|\| 1.13.60 \|\|

*padmapuṣpeṇa yo viṣṇuṃ śivāṃ vā pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*sa yāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ kulakoṭisamanvitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The person who worships god Visnu or god Siva with lotus flowers, goes to Visnu’s abode accompanied by ten million members of his family.

## \|\| 1.13.61 \|\|

*hariṃ ca ketakīpuṣpaiḥ śivaṃ dhattūrajairniśi \|*  
*saṃpūjya pāpanirmukto vasedbhiṣṇupure yugam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By worshipping god Hari with the Ketaki flowers and god Siva with the Dhattura flowers at night, one will be absolved from sins and will abide in god Visnu’s city (Vaikuntha) for a Yuga.

## \|\| 1.13.62 \|\|

*hariṃ tu cāmpakaiḥ purṣperarkaṣpaiśca śaṅkaram \|*
