*tatrāpi devatābuddhirdānabuddhiśca sattama \|*  
*bhogabuddhistathā nṝṇāṃ janmāntaratapaḥ phalam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Even there, О excellent one, the inclination of the intellect towards the (worship, etc. of) deities, charitable gifts and enjoyment of pleasures is the fruit of austerities performed by men in the course of previous births.

## \|\| 1.34.38 \|\|

*mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya yo hariṃ nārcayetsakṛt \|*  
*mūrkhaḥ ko 'sti parastasmājjaḍabuddhiracetanaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Who can be more stupid than he who after attaining the rare human life (i.e. birth as a human being) does not worship Hari even once? He is insentient and of sluggish intellect.

## \|\| 1.34.39 \|\|

*durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ nārcayanti ca ye harim \|*  
*teṣāmatīva mūrkhāṇāṃ vivekaḥ kutra tiṣṭhati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Where is the sense of discrimination in those bloody fools who do not worship Hari even after attaining the human birth?

## \|\| 1.34.40 \|\|

*ārādhito jagannātho dadātyabhimataṃ phalam \|*  
*kastaṃ na pūjayedviprasaṃsārāpripradīpitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The lord of the universe, if propitiated, grants the desired benefits. О Brahmana which person who is being scorched by the fire of worldly existence, shall not worship him?

## \|\| 1.34.41 \|\|

*caṇḍālo 'pi muniśreṣṭa viṣṇubhakto dvijādhikaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktivihīnaśca dvijo 'pi śvapacādhamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О excellent sage, even a *Candala* who is a devotee of Visnu, is superior to a Brahmana. Even a Brahmana devoid of devotion to Visnu is the worst king of *Candala* (who cooks dog’s flesh for food).

## \|\| 1.34.42 \|\|

*tasmātkāmādikaṃ tyaktvā bhajeta harimavyayam \|*  
*yasmiṃstuṣṭe 'khilaṃ tuṣyedyataḥ sarvagato hariḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, one should eschew lust and other (base emotions) and worship the unchanging Hari. If he is pleased everything is pleased, since Hari is omnipresent.

## \|\| 1.34.43 \|\|

*yathā hastipade sarvaṃ padamātraṃ pralīyate \|*  
*tathaḥā carācaraṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇāviva pralīyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Just as all other foot-prints get merged in the big foot-print of an elephant so also the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings gets merged in Visnu alone.

## \|\| 1.34.44 \|\|

*ākāśena yathā vyātpaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*tathaiva hariṇā vyātpaṃ viśvametaccarācaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Just as the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by the firmament, so also it is pervaded by Hari.

## \|\| 1.34.45 \|\|

*janmano maraṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ janma vai mṛtyusādhanam \|*  
*ubhe te nikaṭe viddhi tannāśo harisevayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Death of men is due to birth, and death is the cause of the subsequent birth. Know, that both of them are near at hand and their destruction is brought only by service to Hari.

## \|\| 1.34.46 \|\|

*dhyātaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā praṇato vā janārdanaḥ \|*  
*saṃsārapāśavicchedīkastaṃ na pratipūjayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If meditated upon, remembered, worshipped or bowed-to, Janardana severs the bondage of worldly existence who then would not worship him?

## \|\| 1.34.47 \|\|

*yannāmoccāṃraṇādeva mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*yaṃ samabhyarcya viprarṣe mokṣabhāgī bhavennaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Brahmanical sage, by the mere utterance of his names, great sins are destroyed; on worshipping him a man attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.34.48 \|\|

*aho citramaho citramaho citramidaṃ dvija \|*  
*harināmni sthite lokaḥ saṃsāre parivarttate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Still, О Brahmana, it is surprising; it is astonishing l It is simply astounding that all people undergo the sufferings of recurring worldly existence even when the name of Hari is present.

## \|\| 1.34.49 \|\|

*bhūyobhūyo 'pi vakṣyāmi satyametattapodhana \|*  
*nīyamāno yamabhaṭairaśakto dharmasādhanaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О ascetic, I shall aver you the truth again and again. As one is being led by the soldiers of Yama, one is incapable of achieving Dharma.

## \|\| 1.34.50 \|\|

*yāvannendriyavaikalyaṃ yāvadvyādhirna bādhate \|*  
*tāvadevārcayedviṣṇuṃ yadi muktimabhīpsati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If one wishes for salvation, one should worship Visnu as long as there is no defect in the sense organs and as long as no sickness harasses one.

## \|\| 1.34.51 \|\|

*māturgarbhādviniṣkrānto yadā jantustadaiva hi \|*  
*mṛtyuḥ saṃnihito bhūyāttasmāddharmaparo bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Mrtyu (the God of Death) is present near the creature from the very moment of its coming out of its mother’s womb. Hence, one should be engaged in Dharma.

## \|\| 1.34.52 \|\|

*aho kaṣṭamaho kaṣṭamahokaṣṭamidaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*vinaśvaraṃ samājñāya dharmaṃ naivācaratyayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Alas! It is a pity. Ah! How pitiful it is! It is a pity that even after realising that the body is perishable, he (the worldly-minded man) does not perform holy rites.

## \|\| 1.34.53 \|\|

*satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyamuddhṛtya bhujamucyate \|*  
*dambhācāraṃ parityajyaṃ vāsudevaṃ samarcayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Raising up the arm it is proclaimed: ...“It is truth. It is the truth, that after eschewing religious hypocrisy and arrogance, one should worship Vasudeva”.

## \|\| 1.34.54 \|\|

*bhūyo bhūyo hitaṃ vacmi bhujamuddhṛtya nārada \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ sarvātmanā pūjyastyājyāsūyā tathānṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О Narada, I raise my arm and repeatedly proclaim what is beneficial. Eschewing completely envy and false-hood, Visnu should be worshipped with heart and Soul.

## \|\| 1.34.55 \|\|

*krodhamūlo manastāpaḥ krodhaḥ saṃsārabandhanam \|*  
*dharmakṣayakaraḥ krodhastasmāttaṃ parivarjayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The root of mental distress is anger. It is wrath which binds one to the worldly existence. Fury causes destruction of Dharma. Hence, one should avoid it.

## \|\| 1.34.56 \|\|

*kāmamūlamidaṃ janma kāmaḥ pāpasya kāraṇam \|*  
*yaśaḥ kṣayakaraḥ kāmastasmāttaṃ parivarjayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The birth has its root in lust; lust is the cause of sin; lust causes the destruction of fame. Hence, one shall shun it.

## \|\| 1.34.57 \|\|

*samastaduḥkhajālānāṃ mātsaryaṃ kāraṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*narakāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ ca tasmāttadapi saṃtyajet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. It is remembered that malicious spite is the cause of all sorts of miseries; it is the way (lit. cause) of attainment of hell. Hence, one should eschew that also.

## \|\| 1.34.58 \|\|

*mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ \|*  
*tasmāttadabhisaṃyojya parātmani sukhī bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The cause of bondage and liberation of men is their mind itself. Hence, one should be happy after dedicating it to the Supreme Atman.

## \|\| 1.34.59 \|\|

*aho dhairyamaho dhairyamaho dhairyamaho nṛṇām \|*  
*viṣṇau sthite jagannāthe na bhajanti madoddhatāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О the dare-devilry of men! О the fool-hardiness of men! О the mindless arrogance of the people. Even when Visnu, the lord of the universe, is present, those haughty fellows do not worship him.

## \|\| 1.34.60 \|\|

*anārādhya jagannāthaṃ sarvadhātāramacyutam \|*  
*saṃsārasāgare magnāḥ kathaṃ pāraṃ prayānti hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Without propitiating Acyuta, the lord of all worlds, the creator of everything, how do they who are submerged in the ocean of worldly existence, cross the same?

## \|\| 1.34.61 \|\|

*acyutānantagovindanāmoccāraṇabheṣajāt \|*  
*naśyanti sakalā rogāḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I solemnly assert the truth repeatedly that all ailments perish, thanks to the medicine in the form of uttering the Names of the Lord like Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda.

## \|\| 1.34.62 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa jagannātha vāsudeva janārddana \|*  
*itīrayanti ye nityaṃ te vai sarvatra vanditāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. “O Narayana, О Jagannatha, О Vasudeva, О Janardana.” Those who continuously utter these names of God are honoured everywhere.

## \|\| 1.34.63 \|\|

*adyāpi ca muniśreṣṭa brahmādyā api devatāḥ \|*  
*yatprābhāvaṃ na jānanti taṃ yāhi śaraṇaṃ mune \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О leading sage, seek refuge in that deity whose prowess, Brahma and other deities have not understood even till to-day.

## \|\| 1.34.64 \|\|

*aho maurkhyamaho maurkhyamaho maurkhyaṃ durātmanām \|*  
*hṛtpadmasaṃsthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ na vijānanti nārada \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Alas, the foolishness of the wicked-minded ones! Alas, the stupidity! О the idioticness (of people), О Narada, they do not know that Visnu is stationed in the lotus of the heart (and nowhere else).

## \|\| 1.34.65 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla bhūyobhūyo vadāmyaham \|*  
*hariḥ śraddhāvatāṃ tuṣyenna dhanairna ca bāndhavaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О leading sage, listen to what I repeatedly say. Hari is delighted with those who possess faith. He is not pleased with or enamoured of riches or kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.34.66 \|\|

*bandhumattvaṃ dhanāḍhyatvaṃ putravattvaṃ ca sattama \|*  
*viṣṇubhaghaktimatāṃ nṝṇāṃ bhavejjanmani janmani \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О excellent one, in every birth, men endowed with devotion to Visnu, shall possess the good fortune of having plenty of kinsmen, riches and sons.

## \|\| 1.34.67 \|\|

*pāpamūlamayaṃ dehaḥ pāpakarmaratastathā \|*  
*etadviditvā satataṃ pūjanīyo janārddanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. This body is the root of sins. It is engaged in sinful activities. On realising this, Janardana should always be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.34.68 \|\|

*putramitrakalatrādyā bahavaḥ syuśca saṃpadaḥ \|*  
*haripūjāratānāṃ tu bhavatyena na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. There is no doubt at all in this, that those who are engaged in the worship of Hari, shall be blessed with many sons, friends, womenfolk, etc. as well as all riches.

## \|\| 1.34.69 \|\|

*ihāmutra sukhaprepsuḥ pūjayetsatataṃ harim \|*  
*ihāmutrāsukhaprepsuḥ paranindāparo bhavet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He who is desirous of attaining happiness here and hereafter, shall worship Hari continuously. He who is desirous of unhappiness here and hereafter may engage himself in censuring others.

## \|\| 1.34.70 \|\|

*dhigjanma bhaktihīnānāṃ devadeve janārddane \|*  
*satpātradānaśūnyaṃ yattaddhanaṃ dhikpunaḥ punaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Fie upon the life of those who are devoid of devotion to Janardana, the lord of Devas. Again and again fie upon that wealth (which is not donated in the charitable gift to the deserving persons).

## \|\| 1.34.71 \|\|

*na namedviṣṇave yasya śarīraṃ karmabhedine \|*  
*pāpānāmākaraṃ tadvai vijñeyaṃ munisattama \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. О excellent sage, that body should be known as the mine of sins, the body that does not bow down to Visnu, the destroyer of Karmans.

## \|\| 1.34.72 \|\|

*satpātradānarahitaṃ yaddravyaṃ yena rakṣitam \|*  
*cauryeṇa rakṣitamiva viddhi lokeṣu niścitam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. If anyone hoards and preserves wealth that has not been distributed among deserving persons, know that it is certainly like that wealth which is preserved by a thief in the world.

## \|\| 1.34.73 \|\|

*taḍillolaśriyā mattāḥ kṣaṇaṃbhayuraśālinaḥ \|*  
*nārādhayanti viśveśaṃ paśupāśavimocakam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who are proud and arrogant due to the wealth that is as unsteady as lightning, and that is momentary do not propitiate the lord of the universe, the deity who separates the Jiva from its bonds of Samsara.

## \|\| 1.34.74 \|\|

*sṛṣṭistu dvividhā proktā daivāsuravibhedataḥ \|*  
*hari bhakti yutā daivī taddhīnā hyāsurī mahā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The creation is said to be of two kinds as differentiated by the Divine and Demoniac. That creation which is endowed with devotion to Hari is the Divine one. That which is devoid of it is considered to be demoniac.

## \|\| 1.34.75 \|\|

*tasmācchṛṇaṣva viprendra haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*śreṣṭhāḥ sarvatra vikhyātā yato bhaktiḥ sudurlabhā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Hence, О leading Brahmana, listen. Those who are absorbed in devotion to Hari are the excellent ones and are well known everywhere since Bhakti is extremely rare.

## \|\| 1.34.76 \|\|

*asūyārahitā ye ca vipratrāṇaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*kāmādirahitā ye ca teṣāṃ tuṣyati keśavaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Kesava is delighted with those persons who are devoid of envy, are engaged in the protection of the Brahmanas and are devoid of lust and other base emotions.

## \|\| 1.34.77 \|\|

*saṃmārjanādinā ye tu viṣṇuśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ \|*  
*satpātradānaniratāḥ prayānti paramaṃ padam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Those who are engaged in serving Visnu by sweeping (the premises of the temple) and other activities and those who are eager to bestow charitable gifts on the deserving persons attain the greatest region.

## Chapter 35. A Disquisition on Spiritual Knowledge (The Anecdote of Vedamali.)

## \|\| 1.35.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*punarvakṣyāmi māhātmyaṃ devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śuṇvatāṃ sadyaḥ pāparāśiḥ praṇaśyati \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. Again I shall recount the greatness of the discusbearing Lord of Devas. Heaps of sins of those who read and listen shall perish thereby.

## \|\| 1.35.2 \|\|

*śāntā jitāriṣaḍvargā yogenāpyanahṝṅkṛtāḥ \|*  
*yajanti jñānayogena jñānarūpiṇamavyayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Those who are quiescent, have conquered the group of six enemies, viz. lust, fury, covetousness, delusion, arrogance and malice and have not become arrogant even due to their Yogic power, and worship the unchanging deity of the form of Jnana (spiritual knowledge) through Jnana Yoga (the path of knowledge).

## \|\| 1.35.3 \|\|

*tīrthasnānairviśuddhā ye vratadānatapomakhaiḥ \|*  
*yajanti karmayogena sarvadhātāramacyutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Those who are purified by means of ablution in holy waters, observances of holy vows, charitable gifts, austerities and sacrifices, worship Acyuta, the creator of all, by means of Karma Yoga, the path of holy rites.

## \|\| 1.35.4 \|\|

*lubdhā vyasanito 'jñāśca na yajanti jagatpatim \|*  
*ajarāmaravanmūḍhāstiṣṭanti narakīṭakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Greedy persons, ignorant ones, those who indulge in vices — do not worship the lord of the universe. Those men of confused intellect think they are devoid of old age and death. They are worms of men who continue to remain so.

## \|\| 1.35.5 \|\|

*taḍillekhāśriyā mattā vṛthāhṝṅkāradviṣitāḥ \|*  
*na yajanti jagannāthaṃ sarvaśraiyovidhāyakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Those who are proud due to their prosperity and glory that is as evanescent as the streak of lightning, those who are vainglorious and defiled by arrogance, do not worship the lord of universe who creates and lays down all sorts of welfare.

## \|\| 1.35.6 \|\|

*haridharmaratāḥ śāntā haripādābjasevakāḥ \|*  
*daivātke 'pīha jāyante lokānugrahatatparāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In this world, fortunately, a few are born who are engaged in Hari’s Dharma, are quiescent, serve the lotuslike feet of Hari and who take interest in blessing all worlds.

## \|\| 1.35.7 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā yo yajedbhaktito harim \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ sarvalokottamottamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He who worships Hari with devotion mentally, physically, and verbally, attains the greatest abode which is the most excellent of all excellent things in the universe.

## \|\| 1.35.8 \|\|

*atraivodāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In this context, they cite this ancient mythological anecdote which destroys the sins of those who read and listen.

## \|\| 1.35.9 \|\|

*tatpravakṣyāmi caritaṃ yajñamālisumālinoḥ \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa vācimedha phalaṃ labhet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I shall (now) recount that narrative of Yajnamali and Sumali, by merely listening to which one may attain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.35.10 \|\|

*kaścidāsītpurā vipra brahmaṇo raivateṃ'tare \|*  
*vedamāliriti khyāto vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О Brahmana, formerly in the Raivata Manvantara there was a Brahmaina well-known as Vedamali. He was a master of the Vedas and the Vedangas (the six ancilaries like Siksas, Chandas, etc.).

## \|\| 1.35.11 \|\|

*sarvabhūtadayāyukto haripūjāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*putramitrakalatrārthaṃ dhanārjanaparo 'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was kind-hearted and merciful towards all living beings. He was absorbed in the worship of Hari. He became interested in amassing wealth for his sons, friends and wife.

## \|\| 1.35.12 \|\|

*apaṇyaṃvikrayaṃ cakre tathā ca rasivikrayam \|*  
*caṇḍālādyairapi tathā saṃbhaṣī tatpratigrahī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He regularly sold those things which are forbidden; he regularly conversed with Candalas and others. He accepted monetary gifts from them.

## \|\| 1.35.13 \|\|

*tapasāṃ vikrayaṃ cakre vratānāṃ vikrayaṃ tathā \|*  
*parārthaṃ tīrthagamanaṃ kalatrārthamakārayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He sold his austerities; he sold his Vratas (holy rites) (i.e. performed them in return for monetary consideration), he went on pilgrimage on behalf of others. He did (all those) for the sake of his wife.

## \|\| 1.35.14 \|\|

*kālena gacchatā vipra jātau tasya sutāvubho \|*  
*yajñamālī sumālī ca yamalāvatiśobhanau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О Brahmana, as time passed on, two sons were born to him. They were Yajnamali and Sumili. They were twins of great splendour.

## \|\| 1.35.15 \|\|

*tataḥ pitā kumārau tāvatisnehasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*poṣayāmāsa vātsalyādbahubhiḥ sādhanaistadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, out of affection, the father who was full of too much of affection, nourished them by means of many articles.

## \|\| 1.35.16 \|\|

*vedamālirbahūpāyairdhanaṃ saṃpādya yatnataḥ \|*  
*svadhanaṃ gaṇayāmāsa kiyatsyāditi veditum \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After strenuously amassing wealth by many means, Vedamali began to count it in order to understand how much it amounted to.

## \|\| 1.35.17 \|\|

*nidhikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ koṭikoṭiguṇānvitam \|*  
*vigaṇayya svayaṃ dṛṣṭo vismitaścārthacintayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After counting his treasure which amounted to many billions, he was much delighted. He wondered at the thought of so much of wealth.

## \|\| 1.35.18 \|\|

*asatpratigrahaiścaiva apaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayaiḥ \|*  
*meyā tapo vikrayādyairetaddhanamupārjitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. (He thought: —) “This wealth has been earned and accumulated by me through the acceptance of monetary gifts from bad people, through selling prohibited goods and through such other means such as selling of austerities.

## \|\| 1.35.19 \|\|

*nādyāpi śāntimāpannā mama tṛṣṇātiduḥsahā \|*  
*merutulyasuvarṇāni hyasaṃkhyātāni vāñchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. My unbearable thirst (for gold) has not been pacified till now. It covets to possess innumerable gold pieces as huge as the mount Meru.

## \|\| 1.35.20 \|\|

*aho manye mahākaṣṭaṃ samastakleśasādhanam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāṃpnoti punaranyañca kāṅkṣati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Alas, I consider it as one (involving) great pain and the source of all strenuous means. One attains all desires, but again one covets still other things.

## \|\| 1.35.21 \|\|

*jīryanti jīryataḥ keśāḥ dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ \|*  
*cakṣuḥśrotre ca jīryete tṛṣṇekā taruṇāyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As one grows old his hairs (turn grey); the teeth become old (and feeble); the eyes (sight) and ears (power of listening) become feeble but his longing and yearning for more grow young.

## \|\| 1.35.22 \|\|

*mamedriyāṇi sarvāṇi mandabhāvaṃ vrajanti ca \|*  
*balaṃ hataṃ ca jarasā tṛṣṇā taruṇatāṃ gatā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All my sense-organs have become feeble and weak; my strength has been subdued (and dwindled) by old age but my longing has attained its prime of youth.

## \|\| 1.35.23 \|\|

*kaṣṭāśā varttate yasya sa vidrānatha paṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*suśānto 'pi pramanyuḥ syāddhīmānapyatimūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Only he is a real scholar and a learned man, the man whose Asa (yearning, hope) has been quelled. (If it is not quelled) the quietest man will be the most furious and the most intelligent one will have extremely confused mind.

## \|\| 1.35.24 \|\|

*āśā bhaṅgakarī puṃsāmajeyārātisannibhā \|*  
*tasmādāśāṃ tyajetprājño yadīcchecchāśvataṃ sukham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Asa (longing) causes frustration and disappointment among men. It is like an invincible enemy. If an intelligent man desires permanent happiness he must eschew Asa.

## \|\| 1.35.25 \|\|

*balaṃ tejoḥ yaśaśvaiva vidyāṃ mānaṃ ca vṛddhatām \|*  
*tathaiva satkule janma āśā hatyativegataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With great force, Asa destroys strength, brilliance, fame, learning, honour, prosperous state and nobility of birth.

## \|\| 1.35.26 \|\|

*nṛṇāmāśābhibhūtānāmāścaryamidasucyate \|*  
*kiñciddātāpi cāṇḍālastasmādadhikatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This is being mentioned to the dismay of men overwhelmed with Asa (yearning, hope) that even a Candala who gives away something is superior to them.

## \|\| 1.35.27 \|\|

*āśābhibhūtā ye martyā mahāmohā mahoddhatāḥ \|*  
*avamānādikaṃ duḥkhaṃ na jānanti kadāpyaho \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Those who are in the vicious grip of Asa (yearning) are men of great delusion and of too much arrogance. Alas! they are never conscious of the pangs of being miserably) disrespected, etc.

## \|\| 1.35.28 \|\|

*mayāpyevaṃ bahukliśairetaddhanamupārjitam \|*  
*śarīramapi jīrṇaṃ ca jarasāpahataṃ balam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This enormous wealth has been hoarded by me after undergoing many hardships. The body has been rendered old and emaciated. Old age has taken away the energy.

## \|\| 1.35.29 \|\|

*itaḥ paraṃ yatiṣyāmi paralokārthamādarāt \|*  
*evaṃ niścitya viprendra dharmamārga rato 'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Henceforth, I shall endeavour eagerly (and earnestly) for the sake of the other world”. After deciding thus, О leading Brahmana, he became absorbed in the path of righteousness.

## \|\| 1.35.30 \|\|

*tadaiva taddhanaṃ sarvaṃ caturddhā vyabhajattathā \|*  
*svayaṃ tu bhāga dvitaya svārjitārthādapāharat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the very same time, he divided his assets into four parts. He kept two parts of his accumulated wealth for himself.

## \|\| 1.35.31-32 \|\|

*śeṣaṃ ca bhāgadvitayaṃ putrayorubhayordadau \|*  
*svenārjitānāṃ pāpānāṃ nāśaṃ kartumanāstadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prapātaḍāgārāmāṃśca tathā devagṛhānbahūn \|*  
*annādīnāṃ ca dānāni gaṅgātīre cakāra saḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The two remaining parts he gave his two sons. Thereafter, with the intention of destroying the sins accumulated by him, he built water sheds and parks, got lakes dug up, and built many temples. He distributed cooked food and other charitable gifts on the banks of the Ganga.

## \|\| 1.35.33 \|\|

*evaṃ dhanamaśeṣaṃ ca viśrāṇya haribhaktimān \|*  
*nāranārāyaṇa sthānaṃ jagāma tapase vanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After having distributed his entire possessions thus, he became imbued with devotion to Hari. He went to the forest-abode of Nara and Narayana for performing penance.

## \|\| 1.35.34 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyanmahāramyamāśramaṃ munisevitam \|*  
*phalitaiḥ puṣaapitaiścaiva śobhitaṃ vṛkṣasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There he saw a very beautiful hermitage frequented by sages and embellished with groups of trees bearing fruits and flowers.

## \|\| 1.35.35 \|\|

*gṛṇadbhiḥ paramaṃ brahma śāstracintāparaistathā \|*  
*paricaryāparairvṛddhairmunibhiḥ pariśobhitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Its splendidness had been heightened by old sages who eulogised the great Brahman, who were engaged in pondering over the topics in the scriptural texts and who were absorbed in service to the lord.

## \|\| 1.35.36 \|\|

*śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ tatra muniṃ jānanti saṃjñakam \|*  
*gṛṇantaṃ paramaṃ brahma tejorāśiṃ dadarśa ha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. There he saw a sage named Jananti who was surrounded by his disciples, who was eulogising the great Brahman, and who appeared like a mass of splendour.

## \|\| 1.35.37 \|\|

*śamādiguṇasaṃyuktaṃ rāgādirahitaṃ munim \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vedamālirnanāma tam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing the sage who was devoid of passionate attachment and other similar base feelings, who was endowed with the good qualities of Sama (self-control), etc. and who subsisted only on dry decaying leaves, Vedamali bowed to him.

## \|\| 1.35.38 \|\|

*tasya jānantirāgantoḥ kalpayāmāsa cārhaṇam \|*  
*kandamūlaphalādyaistu nārāyaṇadhiyā mune \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О sage, with bulbous roots, roots, fruits and other things, sage Jananti greeted the guest taking him to be Narayana himself.

## \|\| 1.35.39 \|\|

*kṛtātithyakriyastena vedamālī kṛtāñjaliḥ \|*  
*vinayāvanato bhūtvā provāca vadatāṃ varam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On being hospitably received and honoured by him, Vedamali bowed down with humility, kept his palms joined in reverence and spoke to the sage who was the most excellent among fluent speakers.

## \|\| 1.35.40 \|\|

*bhagavankṛtakṛtyo 'smi vigataṃ kalmaṣaṃ mama \|*  
*māmuddhara mahābhāga jñānadānena paṇḍita \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “O holy Sir, О learned one, I am contented. My sin is removed. О blessed one, uplift me by imparting me (the gift of) perfect knowledge.”

## \|\| 1.35.41 \|\|

*evamuktastatastena jānantirmunisattamaḥ \|*  
*provāca prahasanvāgmī vedamāliṃ guṇānvitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus requested by him, the excellent sage Jananti the eloquent speaker laughingly spoke to Vedamali endowed with good qualities.

## \|\| 1.35.42 \|\|

*jānantiruvāca*  
*śṛṇaṣva vipraśārdūla saṃsāracchedakāraṇam \|*  
*pravakṣyāmi samāsena durlabhaṃ tvakṛtātmanām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*Jananti said:*

42\. О leading Brahmana, listen: I shall succinctly enunciate the way of severance from worldly existence. It is very difficult to get (bring into practice) indeed for those who are not self-possessed.

## \|\| 1.35.43 \|\|

*bhaja viṣṇuṃ paraṃ nityaṃ smara nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|*  
*parāpavādaṃ paiśunyaṃ kadācidapi mā kṛthāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Perpetually worship Visnu, the greatest deity; continuously remember lord Narayana. Never indulge in slandering others or backbiting.

## \|\| 1.35.44 \|\|

*paropakāranirataḥ sa dā bhava mahāmate \|*  
*haripūjāparaścaiva tyaja mūrkhasamāgamam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О highly intelligent one, be always engaged in helping others and in worshipping Hari. Avoid close contact with the fools.

## \|\| 1.35.45 \|\|

*kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca mohaṃ ca madamatsarau \|*  
*parityajyātmavallokaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāntiṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By avoiding lust and fury, covetousness and delusion, haughtiness and malicious spite and by viewing (considering) the whole world like your own Atman, you will attain peace and quietude.

## \|\| 1.35.46 \|\|

*asūyāṃ paranindāṃ ca kadācidapi mā kuru \|*  
*draṃbhācāramahṝṅkāraṃ naiṣṭhuryaṃ ca parityaja \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Never be envious. Never blame others. Avoid hypocritical conduct of life, egotism and ruthlessness.

## \|\| 1.35.47 \|\|

*dayāṃ kuruṣva bhuteṣu śuśrūṣāṃ ca tathā satām \|*  
*tvayā kṛtāṃśca dharmānvai mā prakāśaya pucchatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Show kindness to all living beings. Render service to the good. Even to those who enquire, do not reveal the righteous actions performed by you.

## \|\| 1.35.48 \|\|

*anācāraparāndṛṣṭvā nopekṣāṃ kuru śaktitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayasvātiyiṃ nityaṃ svakuṭuṃbāvirodhataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Do not overlook if you see people engaged in evil ways of life. Worship guests every day in accordance with your capacity and without detriment to your family.

## \|\| 1.35.49 \|\|

*patraiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairvāpi dūrvābhiḥ pallavairatha \|*  
*pūjayasva jagannāthaṃ nārāyaṇamakāṃ mataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Without any (specific) desire, worship Narayana, the lord of the universe, by means of flowers and leaves, Durva grass, sprouts or fruits.

## \|\| 1.35.50 \|\|

*devānṛpīnpitṝścāpi tarpayasva yathāvidhi \|*  
*agreśca vidhivadvapra paricaryāparo bhava \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In accordance with the injunctions, propitiate Devas, pit re and sages. О Brahmana, be interested in the due maintenance of holy fire.

## \|\| 1.35.51 \|\|

*devatāyatane nityaṃ saṃmārjanaparo bhava \|*  
*tathopalepanaṃ caiva kuruṣva susamāhitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Every day, with great concentration be engaged in the sweeping and scrubbing of the temple (of Visnu) with due care. Smear it also duly.

## \|\| 1.35.52 \|\|

*śīrṇasphaṭitasaṃdhānaṃ kuru devagṛhe sadā \|*  
*mārgaśobhāṃ ca dīpaṃ ca viṣṇorāyatane kuru \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Join the broken parts and always repair the decaying sections in a temple. Beautify the path of and illuminate the temple of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.35.53 \|\|

*kandamūlaphalairvāpi sadā pūjaya mādhavam \|*  
*pradakṣiṇanamaskāraiḥ stotrāṇāṃ paṭhanaistathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Always worship Madhava at least with bulbous roots, fruits and roots. Worship him by means of circumambulations, obeisances and recitals of prayers.

## \|\| 1.35.54 \|\|

*yurāṇaśravaṇaṃ caiva purāṇapaṭhanaṃ tathā \|*  
*vedāntapaṭhanaṃ caiva pratyahaṃ kuru śaktitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Every day, according to your capacity listen to or read the Purdrtas as well as the Vedantic texts.

## \|\| 1.35.55 \|\|

*evaṃ sthiti tava jñānaṃ bhaghaviṣyatyuttamottamam \|*  
*jñānātsamastapāpānāṃ mokṣo bhavati niścitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If this is strictly followed, you will have the most excellent knowledge. Certainly one is absolved of all sins, through perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.35.56 \|\|

*evaṃ prabodhitastena vedamālirmahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tathā jñānarato nityaṃ jñānaleśamavāptavān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thus enlightened by him, Vedamali, of great intellect, became absorbed in the (path of) knowledge continuously and attained a small quantum of perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.35.57 \|\|

*vedamāliḥ kadācittu jñānaleśapracoditaḥ \|*  
*ko 'haṃ mama kriyā keti svayameva vyaktintayat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On one occasion, urged by the quantum of perfect knowledge, Vedamali began to think to himself like this. “Who am I? What is my duty?

## \|\| 1.35.58 \|\|

*mama janma kathaṃ jātaṃ rūpaṃ kīdṛgvidhaṃ mama \|*  
*evaṃ vicāraṇaparoḥ divāniśamatandritaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. How was I bom? Of what nature is my form?” Thus, he began to think and muse by day and night alertly.

## \|\| 1.35.59 \|\|

*aniścitamatirbhūtvā vedamālirddhijottamaḥ \|*  
*punarjānantimāgamya praṇamyedamuvāca ha \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Unable to come to any decision, Vedamali, the excellent Brahmana, came again to Jananti, bowed to him and said thus: —

## \|\| 1.35.60 \|\|

*vedamāliruvāca*  
*mama cittamatibhrātaṃ guro brahmavidāṃ vara \|*  
*ko 'haṃ mama kriyā kā ca mama janma kathaṃ vada \|\| 60 \|\|*

*Vedamali said:*

60\. О preceptor, О foremost one among the knowers of Brahman, my mind is much confused. Who am I? What is my rite? How am I bom? Tell me.

## \|\| 1.35.61 \|\|

*jānantiruvāca*  
*satyaṃ satyaṃ mahābhāgaṃ cittaṃ bhrātaṃ suniścitam \|*  
*avidyānilarya cittaṃ kathaṃ sadbhāvagagameṣyati \|\| 61 \|\|*

*Jananti said: —*

61\. О highly blessed one, true. It is certainly true that your mind is confused. The mind is the abode of *Avidya* (ignorance). How will it attain good nature?

## \|\| 1.35.62 \|\|

*mameti gaditaṃ yattu tadapi bhrāntiriṣyate \|*  
*ahṝṅkāro manodharma ātmano nahi paṇḍita \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When you say the word 'My it is certainly a misconception. О learned one, the egotism is a quality of the mind and not of the Atman.

## \|\| 1.35.63 \|\|

*punaśca ko 'hamityuktaṃ vedamāle tvayā tu yat \|*  
*mama jātyādi śūnyasya kathaṃ nāma karomyaham \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Moreover, О Vedamali, it has been mentioned by you thus: “who am I?” How can I ascribe a name to one who is devoid of name and nativity?

## \|\| 1.35.64 \|\|

*anaupamyasvabhāvasya nirguṇasya parātmanaḥ \|*  
*nīrūpasyāprameyasya kathaṃ nāma karomyaham \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. How can I mention the name of the deity devoid of form, of the deity who is incomprehensible? His nature is incomparable. He is the supreme Atman, devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 1.35.65 \|\|

*parajyotiḥ svarūpasya paripūrṇāvyayātmanaḥ \|*  
*avicchinnasvabhāvasya kathyate ca kathaṃ kriyā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. How can the activity of the Atman who is the embodiment of Supreme Splendour, perfect, immutable and of indiscernible nature be described.

## \|\| 1.35.66 \|\|

*svaprakāśātmano vipra nityasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*anantasya kriyā caiva kathaṃ janma ca kathyate \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О Brahmana, the Atman is the self-luminous, eternal, infinite, Supreme Soul. How can the action and the birth of that Atman be spoken of?

## \|\| 1.35.67 \|\|

*jñānaikavedyamajaraṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|*  
*paripūrṇaṃ parānandaṃ tasmānnānyadiha dvija \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The great eternal Brahman is devoid of age, is comprehensible only through perfect knowledge. О Brahmana, there is nothing else that is fuller and more blissful than that.

## \|\| 1.35.68 \|\|

*tattvamasyādivākyebhyo jñānaṃ mokṣasya sādhanam \|*  
*jñāne tvanāhate siddhe sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ bhavet \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The knowledge through the statements such as ‘That thou art’ etc. is the means of achievement of salvation. When the unobstructed knowledge is achieved, everything becomes identical with Brahman.

## \|\| 1.35.69 \|\|

*evaṃ prabodhitastena vedamālirmunīśvara \|*  
*mumoda paśyannātmānamātmanyevācyutaṃ prabhum \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О excellent sage, thus enlightened by him, Vedamali realised the Atman, Lord Acyuta, in his own soul and rejoiced.

## \|\| 1.35.70 \|\|

*upādhirahitaṃ brahma svaprakāśaṃ nirañjanam \|*  
*ahameveti niścitya parāṃ śāntimavāptavān \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He came to the conclusion....“I alone am the self- luminous Brahman, unsullied and unlimited by the conditioning factors”, and he attained the deepest calmness and peace.

## \|\| 1.35.71 \|\|

*tataśca vyavahārārthaṃ vedamālirmunīśvaram \|*  
*guruṃ praṇamya jānanti sadā dhyānaparo 'bhavat \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Thereafter, Vedamali bowed down to his preceptor Jananti, the leading sage, for the sake of formality and became absorbed in the meditation for ever.

## \|\| 1.35.72 \|\|

*gate bahutithe kāle vedamālirmunīśva \|*  
*vārāṇasīpuraṃ prāpya paraṃ mokṣamavāptavān \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. After a lapse of time, О leading sage, Vedamali reached the city of Varanasi and attained salvation.

## \|\| 1.35.73 \|\|

*ya imaṃ paṭhate 'dhyāyaṃ śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa karmapāśavicchedaṃ prāpya saukhyamavānpuyāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He who reads or listens to this chapter with great attention shall be severed from all bonds of Каrman and attain happiness.

## Chapter 36. The Efficacy of Service Unto Visnu, The Story of Yajnamali and Sumali

## \|\| 1.36.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*vedamāleḥ sutau proktau yāvubhau munisattama \|*  
*yajñamālī sumālī ca tayoḥ karmādhunocyata \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. О excellent sage, the story of the two sons of Vedamali who had been mentioned before, viz. Yajnamali and Sumali, is being narrated now.

## \|\| 1.36.2 \|\|

*tayorādyo yajñamālī vibheda pitṛsaṃcitam \|*  
*dhanaṃ dvidhā kaniṣṭasya bhāgamekaṃ dadau tadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The elder of the two, viz. Yajnamali divided the assets accumulated by his father, into two parts and gave one of the parts to his younger brother.

## \|\| 1.36.3-4 \|\|

*sumālī ca dhanaṃ sarvaṃ vyasanābhirakataḥ sadā \|*  
*apādānā dibhiścaiva nāśayāmāsa bho dvija \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gītavādyarato nityaṃ madyapānarato 'bhavat \|*  
*veśyāvibhramalubdho 'sau paradārato 'bhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. О Brahmana, Sumali always indulged in all vices. He was absorbed in singing and playing on musical instruments. He was addicted to liquor. He was enamoured of the coquetry of prostitutes. He was interested in other men’s wives. Removing (i.e. spending away) the wealth thus, Sumali squandered all the wealth.

## \|\| 1.36.5 \|\|

*sarvasminnāśamāyāte hiraṇye pitṛsaṃcite \|*  
*apahṛtya paraṃ dravyaṃ vārastrīnirato 'bhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When all the gold hoarded by his father had been squandered, he continued to be interested in harlots by stealing other men’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.36.6 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā sumālinaḥ śūlaṃ yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*babhūva duḥkhito 'tyarthaṃ bhrātaraṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing the (evil) conduct of Sumali, Yajnamali of great intellect became distressed much and spoke to his brother thus: —

## \|\| 1.36.7 \|\|

*alamamatyantakaṣṭena vṛttenāsmatkule 'nuja \|*  
*tvameka eva duṣṭātmā mahāpāparato 'bhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “O younger brother, enough of this wrong and evil conduct. In our family, you alone are interested in this great sin. You are the only wicked-minded fellow born in our family.

## \|\| 1.36.8 \|\|

*evaṃ nivārayantaṃ taṃ bahuśo jyeṣṭasodaram \|*  
*haniṣyāmīti niścitya khaḍgahastaḥ kace 'grahīt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the elder brother thus tried to wean him (from evil ways) by diverse methods on many occasions, Sumali took a sword in his hand and caught hold of his elder brother by his tuft of hair on his head deciding to himself, “I will kill him”.

## \|\| 1.36.9 \|\|

*tato mahāravo jajñe nagare bhṛśadāruṇaḥ \|*  
*babandhurnāgarāścainaṃ kupitāste sumālinam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter, a terrific uproar took place in the city. The infuriated citizens bound Sumali.

## \|\| 1.36.10 \|\|

*yajñamālī hyameyātmā paurānsaṃprārthya duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*bandhanānmocayāmāsa bhrātṛsnehavimohitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. But Yajnamali, (the depth of feelings in) whose heart could not be measured, became distressed. He was deluded by fraternal affection. He implored the citizens and got his brother liberated from the bondage.

## \|\| 1.36.11 \|\|

*yajñamālī punaścāpi bibhide svadhanaṃ dvidhā \|*  
*ādade svayamarddhaṃ ca dadāvarddhaṃ yavīyase \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Again Yajnamali split his (remaining) wealth into two parts. He took half of his assets and gave the other half to his younger brother.

## \|\| 1.36.12 \|\|

*sumālī tvatimūḍhātmā taddhanaṃ cāpi nārada \|*  
*mūrkhaiḥ pāraṃvaḍacaṇḍālairbubhuje ca sahoddhataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. But Sumali who was haughty and whose soul was excessively confounded, О Narada, squandered that wealth too by enjoying it along with fools, heretics and Candalas.

## \|\| 1.36.13 \|\|

*asatāmupabho gāya durjanānāṃ vibhūtayaḥ \|*  
*picumandaḥ phalāḍhyo 'pi kākairevopabhujyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The riches of wicked men are for the enjoyment of men of evil ways. The Neem (Margosa) tree laden with plenty of fruits is enjoyed only by crows.

## \|\| 1.36.14 \|\|

*bhrātrā dattaṃ dhanaṃ tañca sumālī nāśayanmune \|*  
*madyapānapramattaśca gomāṃsā dīnyabhakṣayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О sage, Sumali wasted that wealth also given by his brother. He became inebriated by drinking liquor. He (unhesitatingly) ate beef and other forbidden foodstuffs.

## \|\| 1.36.15 \|\|

*tyakto bandhujanaiḥ sarvaiścāṇḍālastrīsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*rājñāpi bādhito vipraprapede nirjanaṃ vanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He was excommunicated by his kinsmen along with his Candala women. О Brahmana, he was arrested (and punished) by the king.

## \|\| 1.36.16 \|\|

*yajñamālī sudhīrvipra sadā dharmarato 'bhavet \|*  
*avāritaṃ dadāvannaṃ satsaṅgagatakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmana, Yajnamali of good intellect was always absorbed in righteous activities. All his sins were wiped off, thanks to his association with the good. He distributed cooked food without restriction.

## \|\| 1.36.17 \|\|

*pitrā kṛtāni sarvāṇi taḍāgādīni sattama \|*  
*apālayatprayatnena sadā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О excellent one, he strenuously maintained all the lakes and other things erected by his father. He was always engrossed in pious rites.

## \|\| 1.36.18 \|\|

*viśrāṇitaṃ dhanaṃ sarvaṃ yajñamālermahātmanaḥ \|*  
*satpātradānaniṣṭasya dharmamārgapravartinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. All the wealth of Yajnamali of great Atman was distributed among good men. He was a follower of the righteous path and he abided by his principle of giving charitable gifts to the deserving.

## \|\| 1.36.19 \|\|

*aho sadupabhogāya sajjanānāṃ vibhūtayaḥ \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣaphalaṃ sarvamamaraireva bhujyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О! The riches of good men are for the enjoyment of the good. All the fruits of the wish-yielding tree are enjoyed only by the immortal Devas.

## \|\| 1.36.20 \|\|

*dhanaṃ viśrāṇya dharmārthaṃ yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ viṣṇugṛhe samyakparicaryyāparo 'bhavat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After distributing his wealth in pious and charitable acts (for the sake of piety), Yajnamali of great intellect engaged himself in the continuous service in the abode of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.36.21 \|\|

*kālena gacchatā tau tu vṛddhabhāvamupāgatau \|*  
*yajñamālī sumālī ca hyekakāle mṛtāvubhau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As time passed on, Yajnamali and Sumali who attained old age died simultaneously.

## \|\| 1.36.22 \|\|

*haripūjāratasyāsya yajñamālimahātmanaḥ \|*  
*hariḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa vimānaṃ pārṣadā vṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hari despatched his aerial chariot filled by his attendants to the noble-souled Yajnamali who was engaged in the regular worship of Hari.

## \|\| 1.36.23-25 \|\|

*divyaṃ vimānamāruhya yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*pūjyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ stūyamāno munīśvaraiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*gandharvairgīyamānaśca sevitaścāpsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kāmadhenvā puṣyamāṇaścitrābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*komalaistulasīmālyairbhūṣitastejasāṃ nidhiḥ \|*  
*gacchanviṣṇupadaṃ divyaṃmanujaṃ pathi dṛṣṭavān \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Yajnamali of great intellect got into the divine chariot. He was being worshipped by the groups of Devas; he was being eulogised by leading sages. Gandharvas sang about him. Groups of Apsaras served him. He was being nourished by the divine wish-yielding cow Kamadhenu. He was bedecked in various kinds of ornaments. He adorned himself with tender garlands of Tulasi leaves. He shone as the storehouse of brilliance. As he was going to the divine region of Visnu, he saw his younger brother on the way.

## \|\| 1.36.26-27 \|\|

*tāhyamānaṃ yamabhaṭaiḥ kṣuttṛḍbhyāṃ paripīḍitam \|*  
*pretabhūtaṃ vivastraṃ ca duḥkhitaṃ pāśaveṣṭitam \|*  
*itastataḥ prādhāvantaṃ vilapantamanāthavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

*krośantaṃ ca sudantaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā manasi vivyathe \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. He was being beaten by the soldiers of Yama. He was afflicted with hunger and thirst. He had become a ghost. He was naked, miserable and bound by nooses. He ran about here and there. He was crying helplessly. He was weeping and lamenting. On seeing him, he (Yajnamali) was excessively distressed in his mind.

## \|\| 1.36.28 \|\|

*yajñamālīdayāyukto viṣṇudūtānsamīpagān \|*  
*ko 'yaṃ bhaṭairbādhyamānaṃ ityapṛcchatkṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Overwhelmed by sympathy, Yajnamali asked the emissaries of Visnu who were near him, with his palms joined in reverence. He asked: — “Who is this man harassed by the soldiers of Yama?”

## \|\| 1.36.29 \|\|

*atha te haridūtāstaṃ yajñamālimahaujasam \|*  
*asau sumālī bhrātā te pāpātmeti samabruvan \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then those emissaries of Hari spoke thus to Yajnamali of great power. “This is Sumali, the sinful soul, your brother”.

## \|\| 1.36.30 \|\|

*yajñamālī samākarṇya vyākhyātaṃ viṣṇukiṅkaraiḥ \|*  
*manasā duḥkhamāpannaḥ punaḥ papraccha nārada \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О Narada, on hearing what was explained by the servants of Visnu, Yajnamali was mentally depressed. He asked them again:

## \|\| 1.36.31 \|\|

*kathamasya bhavenmokṣaḥ sāṃcitaiḥ pāpasaṃcayaiḥ \|*  
*tadupāyaṃbadadhvaṃ me yūyaṃ hi mamabāndhavāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “Please tell the remedy by means of which his liberation from the hoarded heaps of sins may become possible. Indeed you are my kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.36.32-33 \|\|

*sakhyaṃ sāptapadīnaṃ syādityāhurdharmakovidāḥ \|*  
*satāṃ sāptapadī maitrī satsatāṃ tripadī tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*satsatāmapi ye saṃtasteṣāṃ maitraghī pade pade \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Those who are adepts in Dharma say that friendship originates in seven words spoken or seven steps walked together. The friendship of good men is based on (exchanging) seven words (or accompanying seven steps). But that of very good men (the friendship) is contracted in three words (or steps). Those who are very very good men have friendship at every step (word).

## \|\| 1.36.34 \|\|

*tasmānme bāndhavā yūyaṃ māṃ netuṃ samupāgatāḥ \|*  
*yato 'yaṃ mama bhrātāpi mucyate tadihocyatām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence, you are my kinsmen. You have come to take me (to heaven). How is my brother to be liberated? May this be kindly explained”.

## \|\| 1.36.35 \|\|

*yajñamālivacaḥ śrutvā viṣṇudūtā dayālavaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ smitāmukhāḥ procuryajñamāliharipriyam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing the words of Yajnamali, the sympathetic emissaries of Visnu spoke to Yajnamali who was a favourite of Hari. They spoke with their faces beaming with smiles. Visnu’s emissaries said:

## \|\| 1.36.36 \|\|

*viṣṇudūtā ūcuḥ*  
*yajñamālinmahābhāga nārāyaṇaparāyaṇa \|*  
*upāyaṃ tava vakṣyāmaḥ sumālipremamuktidam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “O highly blessed Yajnamali, absorbed (in the devotion) to Narayana, we shall mention to you the means that will accord living liberation to Sumali.

## \|\| 1.36.37 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ yatsumahatkarma tvayā prāktanajanmani \|*  
*pravakṣyāmaḥ samāsena tacchraṇuṣva samāhitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. We shall succinctly recount to you the great work that had been performed by you in your previous birth. Listen to it with great attention.

## \|\| 1.36.38 \|\|

*purā tvaṃ vaiśyajātīyo nāmnā viśvaṅghabharaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tvayā kṛtāni pāpāni ahantyagaṇitāni vai \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Formerly, you were born of a Vaisya family. You were remembered by the name Visvambhara. Countless and great sins were committed by you.

## \|\| 1.36.39-40 \|\|

*sukarmavāsanāhīno mātāpitrorvirodhakṛt \|*  
*ekadā bandhubhistyaktaḥ śokasaṃtāpapīḍitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kṣudhāgnināpi saṃtaptaḥ prāptavānharimandiram \|*  
*tadā vṛṣṭirabhūttatra tatsthānaṃ paṅkilaṃ hyabhūta \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. You were devoid of even traces of good deeds. You opposed even your parents. Once, when you were forsaken by your kinsmen, you were afflicted by grief and distress. You were oppressed by the fire of hunger. Thus you reached a temple of Hari. There had been a downpour and the whole place became marshy.

## \|\| 1.36.41 \|\|

*dīrīkṛtastvayā paṅkastatsthāne sthātumicchayā \|*  
*upalepanatāṃ prāptaṃ tatsthānaṃ viṣṇumandire \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The mud was removed by you, since you desired to stay there. This became the service of smearing in the temple of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.36.42 \|\|

*tena puṇyaprabhāvena upalepakṛtena ca \|*  
*viprajanma tvayā prāptaṃ hari bhaktistathācalā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Brahmana, you stayed in that temple during that night. You were bitten by a serpent and you died. Thanks to the power of your meritorious deed of smearing and scrubbing, the birth as a Brahmana was attained by you. Your devotion to Hari was steady.

## \|\| 1.36.43 \|\|

*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ saṃprāpya harisannidhim \|*  
*vasādya jñānamāsādya paraṃ mokṣaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. You will reach the presence of Hari and stay there for a hundred crores of Kalpas. Afterwards you will acquire spiritual knowledge and attain the great salvation.

## \|\| 1.36.44 \|\|

*anujaṃ pātakiśreṣṭhaṃ tvaṃ samuddharttamicchasi \|*  
*upāyaṃ tava vakṣyāmastaṃ nibodha mahāmate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You desire to uplift your younger brother who is the greatest sinner. We shall tell you the means thereof. О highly intelligent one, understand it.

## \|\| 1.36.45 \|\|

*gocarmamātrabhūmestu upalepanajaṃ phalam \|*  
*dattvoddhara mahābhāga bhrātaraṃ kṛpayānvitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You donate to your brother the benefit of smearing an area extending to a Gocarma. О highly blessed one, thus kindly uplift your brother."

## \|\| 1.36.46 \|\|

*evamukto viṣṇudūtairyajñamālī mahāpatiḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ pradadau tasmai bhrātre pāpavimuktaye \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus urged by the emissaries of Visnu, the highly intelligent Yajnamali gave that much merit to his brother for the sake of liberation from sins.

## \|\| 1.36.47 \|\|

*sumālī bhrātṛdattena puṇyena gatakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*babhūva yamadūtāstu taṃ tyaktvā prapalāyitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Through the merit bestowed by his brother, Sumali became free from sins. The emissaries of Yama left him off and fled.

## \|\| 1.36.48 \|\|

*vimānaṃ cāgataṃ sadyaḥ sarvabhogasamanvitam \|*  
*tadā sumālī svaryānamāruhya mumude mune \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. An aerial chariot that contained all means of enjoyment of pleasures came there immediately. О sage, Sumali then stepped into the heavenly vehicle and rejoiced.

## \|\| 1.36.49 \|\|

*tāvubhau bhrātarau vipra suravṛndanamaskṛtau \|*  
*avāpaturbhṛśaṃ prītiṃ samāliṅgya parasparam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О Brahmana, both the brothers were bowed to by groups of Devas. By embracing each other they attained great pleasure.

## \|\| 1.36.50 \|\|

*yajñamālī sumālī ca stūyamānau maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*gīyamānau ca gandharvairviṣṇulokaṃ prajagmatuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Being eulogised by great sages and sung about by Gandharvas, Yajnamali and Sumali went to Visnu’s world.

## \|\| 1.36.51 \|\|

*avāpya harisālokyaṃ sumālī munisattama \|*  
*yajñamālī coṣatustau kalpamekaṃ mudānvitau \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Attaining Salokya (stay in the same region) with Hari, О excellent sage, Sumali and Yajnamali lived there joyously for the period of a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.36.52 \|\|

*bhuktvā bhogānbahūṃstatra yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tatraiva jñānasaṃpannaḥ paraṃ mokṣamupāgataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After enjoying many pleasures there, Yajnamali of great intellect, became richly endowed with perfect knowledge and attained the great salvation (Moksa).

## \|\| 1.36.53 \|\|

*sumālī tu mahābhāgo viṣṇuloke mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*sthitvā bhūmiṃ punaḥ prāpya vipratvaṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The highly blessed Sumali rejoiced in the Visnuloka (region of Lord Visnu). (Afterwards) he came to the Earth again and was born as a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.36.54 \|\|

*atiśuddhe kule jāto guṇavānvedapāragaḥ \|*  
*sarvasaṃpatsamopeto haribhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He was born in a very pure family. He had all good qualities. He was a master of the Vedas. He was endowed with all riches. He was devoted to Hari.

## \|\| 1.36.55-56 \|\|

*vyāharanharināmāni prapede jāhnavītaṭam \|*  
*tatra snātaśca gaṅgāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā viśveśvaraṃ prabhum \|\| 55 \|\|*

*avāpa paramaṃ sthānaṃ yogināmapi durlabham \|*  
*upalepanamāhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te munīśvara \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Repeating the names of Hari, he reached the banks of the Ganga. He took his bath in the Ganga. After seeing lord Visvesvara he attained the greatest abode, difficult of access even to the Yogins. О leading sage, the great merit accruing from smearing Visnu’s temple, has been recounted to you.

## \|\| 1.36.57-61 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena saṃpūjyo jagatāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*akāmādapi ye viṣṇoḥ sakṛtpūjāṃ prakurvate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ bhavabandhastu kadācidapi jāyate \|*  
*haribhaktiratānyastu haribuddhyā samarcayet \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tasya tuṣyanti viprendra brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|*  
*haribhaktiparāṇāṃ tu saṃgināṃ saṃgamātrataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo mahāpātakavānapi \|*  
*haripūjāparāṇāṃ ca harināmaratātmanām \|\| 60 \|\|*

*śuśrūṣāniratā yānti pāpino 'pi parāṃ gatim \|\| 61 \|\|*

57-59a. Hence, the lord of the worlds should be, with best possible efforts, worshipped. Those who worship Visnu even for once, without any specific desire, never get entangled in the worldly existence. Those who worship people engaged in the devotion of Hari thinking them to be Hari himself, are delightedly blessed by Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara.

59b-61. Even a great sinner is liberated from all sins by the mere contact with those who came into contact with those devoted to Hari. Those who are engaged in the service of those who are devoted to Hari and of those who are engaged in the repetitions of the names of Hari, attain the greatest goal, even if they happen to be sinners.

## Chapter 37. The Greatness of Visnu: The Story of Gulika, The Hunter

## \|\| 1.37.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*bhūyaḥ śṛṇuṣva viprendra māhātmyaṃ kamalāpateḥ \|*  
*kasya no jāyate prītiḥ śrotuṃ harikathāmṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. О leading Brahmana, listen once again to the greatness of the lord of Laksmi. What person is not delighted to hear the nectarine stories of Hari?

## \|\| 1.37.2 \|\|

*narāṇāṃ viṣayāndhānāṃ mamatākulacetasām \|*  
*ekameva harernāma sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. To men blinded by sensual objects, to those whose minds are agitated by the feelings of ‘mine-ness’, the only thing that destroys all sins is the name of Hari.

## \|\| 1.37.3 \|\|

*sakṛdvā na namedyastu viṣṇuṃ pāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*śvapacaṃ taṃ vijānīyātkadācinnālapeñca tam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. If anyone, even for once, does not bow to Visnu the destroyer of the sins of men, know him to be a Candala (one who cooks dog’s flesh for food). Never shall anyone converse with him.

## \|\| 1.37.4 \|\|

*haripūjāvihīnaṃ tu yasya veśma dvijottama \|*  
*śmaśānasadṛśaṃ taddhi kadācidapi no viśet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О excellent Brahmana, if no worship of Hari is performed in any house, know that to be on a par with the cremation ground. Never shall one enter it.

## \|\| 1.37.5 \|\|

*haripūjāvihīnāśca vedavidveṣiṇastathā \|*  
*godvijadveṣaniratā rākṣasāḥ parikīrttitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Those who are devoid of the worship of Hari, those who hate the Vedas, and those who are engaged in the hatred of cows and Brahmanas are said to be Raksasas.

## \|\| 1.37.6 \|\|

*yo vā ko vāpi viprendra vipradveṣaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*samarcayati govindaṃ tatpūjā viphalā bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О leading Brahmana, if anyone is engaged in the hatred of the Brahmanas — no matter who he is — and he worships Govinda, that worship is futile.

## \|\| 1.37.7 \|\|

*anyaśreyovināśārthaṃ yer'cayanti janārdanam \|*  
*sā pūjaiva mahābhāga pūjakānāśu hṝnti vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О highly blessed one, if any one were to worship Janardana for the destruction of another man’s welfare, the very same act of worship immediately kills the worshippers.

## \|\| 1.37.8 \|\|

*haripūjākaro yastu yadi pāpaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tameva viṣmudveṣṭāraṃ prāhustattvārtthakovidāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If a worshipper of Hari commits a sin, he alone is the hater of Visnu, so say the persons who are experts in the interpretations of principles.

## \|\| 1.37.9 \|\|

*ye viṣṇuniratāḥ saṃti lokānugrahatatparāḥ \|*  
*dharmakāryaratāḥ śaśvadviṣṇurupāstu te matāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Those who are engaged in the worship of Visnu and 'are interested in blessing (and obliging) the world, and those who are always engaged in the righteous activities are considered to be persons in the eternal form of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.37.10 \|\|

*koṭijanmārdajitaiḥ puṇyairviṣṇubhaktiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*dṛḍhabhaktimatāṃ viṣṇau pāpabuddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Devotion to Visnu is the result of the merits accumulated in the course of ten million births. How can they who have steady devotion to Visnu be sinfully inclined?

## \|\| 1.37.11 \|\|

*janmakoṭyarjitaṃ pāpaṃ viṣṇupūjāratātmanām \|*  
*kṣayaṃ yāti kṣaṇādeva teṣāṃ syātpāpadhīḥ katham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Within a moment the sins accumulated in the course of crores of births, perish, if people are engaged in the worship of Visnu. How can they have sinful intentions?

## \|\| 1.37.12 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktivihīnā ye caṇḍālāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*caṇḍālā api vai śreṣṭhā haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Those who are devoid of devotion to Visnu are said to be Candalas. If the Cabalas are devotionally engaged in the worship of Hari, they are verily excellent persons.

## \|\| 1.37.13 \|\|

*narāṇāṃ viṣayāndhānāṃ sarvaduḥkhavināśinī \|*  
*hariseveti vikhyātā bhuktimuktipradāyinī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Service to Hari is reputed to be the destroyer of all miseries of men blinded by sensuous objects. It yields both worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 1.37.14 \|\|

*saṃgātsnehādbhayāllobhādajñānādvāpi yo naraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇorupāsanaṃ kuryātso 'kṣayaṃ sukhamaśnute \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If a man worships Visnu as a result of his association, or due to real love, or due to fear, or out of covetousness or due to ignorance, he enjoys inexhaustible happiness.

## \|\| 1.37.15 \|\|

*haripādodakaṃ yastu kaṇamātraṃ pibedapi \|*  
*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu viṣṇoḥ priyataro bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He who drinks even a drop of the water that has washed the feet of Hari, becomes a great favourite of Visnu. He is equal to one who has taken his ablutions in all the sacred waters.

## \|\| 1.37.16 \|\|

*akālamṛtyuśamanaṃ sarvavyādhivināśanam \|*  
*sarvaduḥkhopaśamanaṃ haripododaka smṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The water that has washed the feet of Hari is remembered as something that subdues premature death, that destroys all ailments and that removes all miseries.

## \|\| 1.37.17 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ dhāma jyotiṣāṃ jyotiruttamam \|*  
*ye prapannā mahātmānasteṣāṃ muktirhi śāśvatī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Narayana is the greatest splendour (or the Supreme abode), the most excellent of all luminaries. Salvation is perpetual to those noble-souled ones who seek refuge in Narayana.

## \|\| 1.37.18 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In this context, they cite the following ancient mythological anecdote. It is destructive of all sins of those who read and listen to this.

## \|\| 1.37.19 \|\|

*āsītpurā kṛtayuge guliko nāma lubdhakaḥ \|*  
*paradāraparadravyaharaṇe satatodyataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Formerly, in the Krta Yuga, there was a hunter named Gulika. He always attempted to abduct other men’s wives or to take away other men’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.37.20 \|\|

*paranindāparo nityaṃ jantūpadravakṛttathā \|*  
*hatavānbrāhmaṇān gāśca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He was always engaged in censuring others. He regularly tortured all creatures. He killed Brahmanas and cows in hundreds and thousands.

## \|\| 1.37.21 \|\|

*devasvaharaṇe nityaṃ parasvaharaṇe tathā \|*  
*udyuktaḥ sarvadā vipra kīnāśānāmadhīśvaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О Brahmana, this lord of demonic fellows was always eager to rob godly assets and other men’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.37.22 \|\|

*tena pāpānyanekāni kṛtāni sumahānti ca \|*  
*na teṣāṃ śakyate vaktuṃ saṃkhyā vatsarakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. So many great sins were committed by him, that it is impossible to enumerate them even in the course of crores of years.

## \|\| 1.37.23-24 \|\|

*sa kadā cinmahāpāpo jatṛnāmantakopamaḥ \|*  
*sauvīrarājño nagaraṃ sarvaiśvaryasamanvitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yoṣiddhirbhūṣitārbhiśca sarobhinirmalodakaiḥ \|*  
*alaṅkṛtaṃ vipaṇibhiryayo devapuropamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Once this great sinner who could be compared to the god of death in regard to his dealings with creatures, went to the capital city of the King of Sauvira. It was filled with all kinds of riches. It was richly decorated with well- adorned women and lakes of translucent water as well as trading centres. It was comparable to the city of gods.

## \|\| 1.37.25 \|\|

*tasyopavanamadhyasthaṃ ramyaṃ keśavamandiram \|*  
*chaditaṃ hemakalaśairdṛṣṭvā vyādho mudaṃ yayau \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There was a beautiful temple of Kesava situated in the middle of a park therein. On seeing that it was covered with golden domes resembling pots, the hunter was very much pleased.

## \|\| 1.37.26 \|\|

*harāmyatra suvarṇāni bahūnīti viniścitam \|*  
*jagāmābhyantaraṃ tasya kīnāśaścauryalolupaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The hunter who resembled god of Death and who was ardently longing for stealing, made up his mind thus “I shall take away much of the gold from here” and he went into the temple.

## \|\| 1.37.27 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyaddvijavaraṃ śāntaṃ tattvārthakovidam \|*  
*paricaryāparaṃ viṣṇoruttaṅkaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There he saw Uttanka, the storehouse of austerities, the quiescent excellent Brahmana, an adept in the interpretation of the principles, and engaged in rendering service to Visnu.

## \|\| 1.37.28-29 \|\|

*ekākinaṃ dayāsuṃ ca nispṛhaṃ dhyānalolupam \|*  
*cauryāntarāyakartāraṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā lubdhako mune \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dravyajātaṃ tu devasya hartukāmo 'tisāhasī \|*  
*uttaṅkaṃ hṝntumārebhe vidhṛtāsirmadoddhataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The Brahmana who was devoid of desire, was alone. He was eager to meditate. О sage, yet, the hunter regarded him as one who would put obstacles in his act of stealing. Desirous of taking away the collected treasures of the lord, the dare-devil who was very haughty, took out his sword and began to kill Uttanka.

## \|\| 1.37.30 \|\|

*pādenākramya tadvakṣo jaṭāḥ saṃgṛhya pāṇinā \|*  
*hṝntuṃ kṛtamatiṃ vyādhamuttaṅkaḥ prekṣya cābravīt \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The hunter pressed down his chest under his foot and caught hold of his matted hair with his hand. On seeing that the hunter had decided to kill him, Uttanka spoke thus: —

## \|\| 1.37.31 \|\|

*uttaṅka uvāca*  
*bho bho sādho vṛthā māṃ tvaṃ haniṣyasi nirāgasam \|*  
*mayā kimaparāddhaṃ te tadvadasva mahāmatte \|\| 31 \|\|*

*Uttanka said: —*

31\. О my good man, in vain do you try to kill me, utterly sinless. О intelligent man, tell me in what way I have offended you.

## \|\| 1.37.32 \|\|

*kṛtāparādhināṃ loke śaktāḥ śikṣāṃ prakurvate \|*  
*nahi saumya vṛthā ghnanti sajjanā api pāpinaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. My gentle friend, powerful persons in the world chastise the offenders and teach them a lesson. But good men do not kill even the sinners in vain.

## \|\| 1.37.33 \|\|

*virodhiṣvapi mūrkheṣu nirīkṣyāvasthitān guṇān \|*  
*virodhaṃ nahi kurvanti sajjanāḥ śāntacetasaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Good men of calm minds perceive the good qualities present even in the offending fools. And they do not offend them in return.

## \|\| 1.37.34 \|\|

*bahudhā bodhyamāno 'pi yo naraḥ kṣamayānvitaḥ \|*  
*tamuttamaṃ naraṃ prāhurviṣṇoḥ priyataraṃ sadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They call him the excellent man, the person who continues to be forbearing even when he is being harassed. He is the favourite of Visnu for ever.

## \|\| 1.37.35 \|\|

*sujano na yāti vairaṃ parahitabuddhirvanāśakāle 'pi \|*  
*chede 'pi candanataruḥ surabhayati mukhaṃ kuṭhārasya \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even at the time of death, a good man thinks of the welfare of others, but he does not become inimical (to his offender). Even when cut, the sandal tree renders the face (i.e. edge) of the hatchet fragrant.

## \|\| 1.37.36 \|\|

*aho vidhiḥ subalavānbā dhate bahudhā janān \|*  
*sarvasaṃgavihīno 'pi bādhyate hi durātmanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Alas! fate is very powerful. It afflicts people in many ways, for even a man who has eschewed all intimate contacts (with worldly affairs) is being harassed by the wicked-minded.

## \|\| 1.37.37 \|\|

*aho niṣkāraṇaṃ loke bādhante bahudhā janān \|*  
*sarvasaṃgavihīno 'pi bādhyate piśunairjanaiḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi sādhūnbādhante na samānānkadācana \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Alas! (many) in the world oppress the people in many ways without reason. Even a man who has eschewed all intimate contact (with worldly affairs) is harassed by back-biters and calumniators. There too they harass the good men and never their equals.

## \|\| 1.37.38 \|\|

*mṛgamīnasajjanānāṃ tṛṇajalasaṃtoṣavihitavṛttānām \|*  
*lubdhakadhīvarapiśunā niṣkāraṇavairiṇo jagati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In this universe, the hunter, the fisherman and the calumniator are the causeless (unreasonable) enemies of the deer, the fish and the good people who maintain themselves with grass, water and contentment.

## \|\| 1.37.39 \|\|

*aho balavatī māyā mohayatyakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*putramitrakalatrārthaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhena yojayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Alas! the Maya is very powerful. It deludes the entire universe and makes all people miserable for the sake of sons, friends and women.

## \|\| 1.37.40 \|\|

*paradravyāpahāreṇa kalatraṃ poṣitaṃ tvayā \|*  
*ante tatsarvamutsṛjya eka eva prayati vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By looting other people’s wealth you have maintained your wife and women dependents. In the end, you have to leave everyone and go alone.

## \|\| 1.37.41 \|\|

*mama mātā mama pitā mama bhāryā mamātmajāḥ \|*  
*mamedamiti jantūnāṃ mamatā bādhate vṛthā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “My mother”, “My father”, “My wife,” “My sons” “This is mine”. Thus the feelings of ‘Му-ness’ of all creatures harass them in vain.

## \|\| 1.37.42 \|\|

*yāvadarjayati dravyaṃ bāndhavāstāvadeva hi \|*  
*dharmādharmauṃ sahaivāstāmihāmutra na cāparaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. One has (the benefits of having) the kinsmen only as long as one earns wealth. It is the Dharma and Adharma (merits and sins) that remain with one both here and hereafter and not anything else.

## \|\| 1.37.43 \|\|

*dharmādharmārjitairdravyaiḥ poṣitā yena ye narāḥ \|*  
*mṛtamagnimukhe hutvā ghṛtānnaṃ bhuñjate hi te \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. (Defective) Men who are nourished by means of wealth earned through Dharma as well as Adharma by a person, consign him (that very person) to flames and enjoy rich food soaked in ghee.

## \|\| 1.37.44 \|\|

*gacchantaṃ paralokaṃ ca naraṃ tu hyanutiṣṭataḥ \|*  
*dharmādharmauṃ na ca dhanaṃ na putrā na ca bāndhavāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Only the Dharma and the Adharma follow the man who goes to the other world, not his wealth, nor his sons, nor any of his kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.37.45 \|\|

*kāmaḥ samṛddhimāyāti narāṇāṃ pāpakarmiṇām \|*  
*kāmaḥ saṃkṣayamāyāti narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Lust of men indulging in sinful activities increases (day by day). Lust of men of meritorious deeds becomes reduced and quelled.

## \|\| 1.37.46 \|\|

*vṛthaiva vyākulā lokā dhanādānāṃ sadārjane \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. All people are always unnecessarily worried and agitated over the problem of earning wealth, etc.

## \|\| 1.37.47 \|\|

*yadbhāvi tadbhavatyeva yadabhāvyaṃ na tadbhavet \|*  
*iti niścitabuddhīnāṃ na cintā bādhate kvacit \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “What is destined to happen does definitely happen. What is not to occur shall never occur”. If people come to this decision, no anxiety worries them at all.

## \|\| 1.37.48 \|\|

*rdavādhīnamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*tasmājjanma ca mṛtyuṃ ca daivaṃ jānāti nāparaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The whole of this universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is under the control of fate. Оnlу fate and none else can know the happening of birth and death.

## \|\| 1.37.49 \|\|

*yatra kutra sthitasyāpi yadbhāvyaṃ tadbhaved dhruvam \|*  
*lokastu tatra vijñāya vṛthāyāsaṃ karoti hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Wherever one may stay, whatever is destined to happen certainly happens. Being ignorant and unaware of it, the whole world exerts itself in vain.

## \|\| 1.37.50 \|\|

*aho duḥkhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ mamatākulacetasām \|*  
*mahāpāpāni kṛtvāpi parānpuṣyānti yatnataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Alas! the misery of men who are worried due to the feelings of ‘My-ness! Even by committing great sins (those people) assiduously go on feeding others.

## \|\| 1.37.51 \|\|

*arjitaṃ ca dhanaṃ sarvaṃ bhuñjate bāndhavāḥ sadā \|*  
*svayamekatamo mūḍhastatpāpaphalamaśnute \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. It is the kinsmen who enjoy all wealth earned by one. Alone and perplexed, one experiences the adverse effects of all one’s sins.”

## \|\| 1.37.52 \|\|

*iti bravāṇaṃ tamṛṣiṃ vimucya bhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*gulikaḥ prāñjaliḥ prāha kṣamasveti punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. As the sage said this, Gulika, the hunter became frightened. He let off the sage and with palms joined in reverence repeatedly begged of the sage to forgive him.

## \|\| 1.37.53 \|\|

*satsaṃgasya prabhāveṇa harisannidhimātrataḥ \|*  
*gatapāpo lubagdakaśca hyanutāpīdamabravīt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. By the mere presence of Hari and thanks to the power of the association of the good, the hunter became free from sins. Repenting for his misdeeds he said thus: —

## \|\| 1.37.54 \|\|

*mayā kṛtā ni pāpāni mahānti subahūni ca \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi naṣṭāni viprendra tava darśanāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “O leading Brahmana, many great sins have been committed by me. All of them have perished at your very sight.

## \|\| 1.37.55 \|\|

*aho 'haṃ pāpadhīrnityaṃ mahāpāpamupācaram \|*  
*kathaṃ me niṣkṛtir bhūyo yāmi kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Alas! I have been sinfully inclined. I have continuously committed great sins. О holy lord, how is my redemption possible? To whom shall I approach for refuge?

## \|\| 1.37.56 \|\|

*pūrvajanmārjitaiḥ pāpairlubdhakatvamavāptavān \|*  
*atrāpi pāpajālāni kṛtvā kāṃ gatimāpnuyām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I have been born as a hunter due to the sins accumulated in the previous births. By committing sins here too (I do not know) what state I shall attain?

## \|\| 1.37.57 \|\|

*aho mamāyuḥ kṣayameti śīghraṃ pāpānyanekāni samarjjitāni \|*  
*prātikriyā naiva kṛtā mayaiṣāṃ gatiśca kā syānmamajanma kiṃ vā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Alas! My span of life gets reduced quickly. Many sins have been accumulated. I have not atoned for them. What will be my state after death? What will be my next birth?

## \|\| 1.37.58 \|\|

*aho vidhiḥ pāpaśatā kulaṃ māṃ kiṃ sṛṣṭavānpāpataraṃ ca śaśvat \|*  
*kathaṃ ca yatpāpaphalaṃ hi bhokṣye kiyatsu janmasvahamugrakarmā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Alas! Why did the creator make me one defiled by hundreds of sins? I am perpetually becoming more and more sinful. How shall I reap the adverse effects of those sins? For how many births am I to be one committing terribly fierce deeds?”

## \|\| 1.37.59 \|\|

*evaṃ vinindannātmānamātmanā lubdhakastadā \|*  
*antastāpāgnisaṃtaptaḥ sadyaḥ pañcatvamāgataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thus cens\\iring his own self, the hunter became scorched by means of the fire of his own mental agony. He died instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.37.60 \|\|

*uttaṅkaḥ patitaṃ prekṣya lubagdhakaṃ taṃ dayāparaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇupādodakenaivamabhyaṣiñcanmahāmatiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On seeing the fallen hunter, the kind-hearted highly intelligent (sage) Uttanka sprinkled him with the water that had washed the feet of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.37.61 \|\|

*haripādodakasparśāllubdhako gatakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamāruhya munimetadathābravīt \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thanks to the contact with the water from the feet of Visnu the hunter became free from his sins. Seated in a divine aerial car, he spoke to the sage thus: —

## \|\| 1.37.62 \|\|

*gulika uvāca*  
*uttaṅka muniśārdūla gurustvaṃ mama suvrata \|*  
*vimuktastvatprasādena mahāpātakakañcukāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

*Gulika said:*

62\. О leading sage Uttanka of holy rites, you are my preceptor. I have been freed from the slough of great sins. Thanks to your favour.

## \|\| 1.37.63 \|\|

*gatastvadupadeśānme saṃtāpo munipuṅgava \|*  
*tathaiva sarvapāpāni vinaṣṭānyativegataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О leading sage, thanks to your instructions, my distress has gone. Similarly, all sins have been quelled quickly.

## \|\| 1.37.64 \|\|

*haripādodakaṃ yasmānmayi tvaṃ siktavānmune \|*  
*prāpito 'smi tvayā tasmāttadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. О sage, since the water from the feet of Visnu has been sprinkled on me by you, I have been enabled to attain the greatest region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.37.65 \|\|

*tvayāhaṃ tārito vipra pāpādasmāccharīrataḥ \|*  
*tasmānnato 'smi te vidvanmatkṛtaṃ tatkṣamasva ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О Brahmana, I have been redeemed from this sinful body by you. Hence, О learned one, I bow down unto you. Forgive the misdeed committed by me (or the maltreatment given by me to you)”.

## \|\| 1.37.66 \|\|

*ityuktvā devakusumairmuniśreṣṭhaṃ samākiram \|*  
*pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After saying this he showered the leading sage with divine flowers. After circumambulating him thrice, he prostrated himself before him.

## \|\| 1.37.67 \|\|

*tato vimānamāruhya sarvakāmasamanvitam \|*  
*apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaḥ prapede harimandiram \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thereafter, he got into the aerial chariot equipped with all desirable things and occupied by the groups of celestial damsels. He then went to the abode of Hari.

## \|\| 1.37.68 \|\|

*etaddṛṣṭvā vismito 'sau hyuttaṅkastapasāṃnidhiḥ \|*  
*śirasyañjalimādhāya tuṣṭāva kamalāpatim \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On seeing this, Uttanka, the storehouse of austerities, became surprised. Keeping the palms joined over his head in reverence, he eulogised the lord of Kamala (Goddess Laksmi).

## \|\| 1.37.69 \|\|

*tena stuto mahāviṣṇurdattavānvaramattamam \|*  
*vareṇa tenoktaṅko 'pi prapede paramaṃ padam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Eulogised by him, Mahavishnu granted him an excellent boon. Thanks to that boon Uttanka attained the highest region (Moksa).

## Chapter 38. Uttanka's Eulogy of Visnu: Uttanka Liberated

## \|\| 1.38.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kintatstotraṃ mahābhāga kathaṃ tuṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*uktaṅkaḥ puṇyapuruṣaḥ kīdṛśaṃ labdhavānvaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. О blessfed one, what is that hymn? How was Janardana propitiated? What sort of a boon did Uttanka, the meritorious person, attain?

## \|\| 1.38.2 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*uttaṅkastu tadā vipro haridhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pādodakasya māhātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭāva bhaktitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

2\. Uttanka, the Brahmana engrossed in the meditation on Hari,' saw the great efficacy (greatness) of the water from the feet of Lord Visnu and eulogised him devoutly.

## \|\| 1.38.3 \|\|

*uttaṅka uvāca*  
*nato 'smi nārāyaṇamādidevaṃ jagannivāsaṃ jagadekabandhum \|*  
*cakrābjaśārṅgīsidharaṃ mahāntaṃ smṛtārtinighnaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Uttanka prayed:*

3\. I bow down unto Narayana, the primordial deity, the supporting abode of the universe, the sole kinsman unto the whole universe. I seek refuge in the great deity holding the discus, the lotus, the Sarnga bow and the sword and who destroys the distress of anyone immediately after being remembered.

## \|\| 1.38.4 \|\|

*yannibhijābja prabhavo vidhātā sṛjatyamuṃ lokasamuñcayaṃ ca \|*  
*yatkrodhajo hṝnti jagañca rudrastamādidevaṃ praṇato 'smi viṣṇum \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I bow down to Visnu, that primordial deity, from whose umbilical lotus was born god Brahma who creates the aggregation of worlds and from whose fury was born Rudra who annihilates the universe.

## \|\| 1.38.5 \|\|

*padmāpatiṃ padmadalāyatākṣaṃ vicitravīryaṃ nikhilaikahetum \|*  
*vedāntavedyaṃ pukuṣaṃ purāṇaṃ taijonidhiṃ viṣṇumahaṃ prapannaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Suppliantly, I betake myself to Visnu who is the lord of Padma (goddess Laksmi), whose eyes are as large as the petals of a lotus, whose prowess is of mysterious and miraculous nature, who is the sole cause of all, who is the ancient Purusa comprehensible through the Vedanta texts and who is the store-house of brilliance.

## \|\| 1.38.6 \|\|

*ātmākṣaraḥ sarvagato 'cyutākhyo jñānātmako jñānavidāṃ śaraṇyaḥ \|*  
*jñānaikavedyo bhagavānanādiḥ prasīdatāṃ vyaṣṭisa praṣṭirupaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He is the imperishable Atman, the omnipresent deity named Acyuta who is of the nature of perfect knowledge and is worthy of being the refuge of those who possess perfect knowledge. May the primordial lord, comprehensible only through perfect knowledge, be propitious unto me — The Lord who is of the form of *Vyasti* (Distributive pervasion) and *Samasti* (aggregate collective) — as well be pleased.

## \|\| 1.38.7 \|\|

*anantavīyo guṇajātihīnāṃ guṇātmako jñānavidāṃ varaṣṭaḥ \|*  
*nityaḥ prapannārti haraḥ parātmā dayāṃbudhirme varadastu bhaghūyāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He is of infinite prowess, devoid of attributes and births, of the nature of Gunas, the most excellent among the possessors of perfect knowledge. He is eternal and he removes the distress of those who seek shelter in him. May that great Atman, the ocean of mercy, be the bestower of boons unto me.

## \|\| 1.38.8 \|\|

*yaḥ sthūlasūkṣmādiviśeṣabhedaurjagadyathāvatsvakṛtaṃ praviṣṭaḥ \|*  
*tvameva tatsarvamanantasāraṃ tvattaḥ paraṃ nāsti yataḥ parātman \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. You have precisely pervaded the universe created by you, entering it through the special qualities of subtlety and grossness. О great Atman, you alone are identical with all those, as there is no other infinite essence excepting you.

## \|\| 1.38.9 \|\|

*agocaraṃ yattava śuddharūraṃ māyāvihīnaṃ guṇajātihīnam \|*  
*nirañjanaṃ nirmalamaprameyaṃ paśyanti santaḥ paramārthasaṃjñam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Your pure form is invisible; it is devoid of Мaуa, and of attributes and births; it is unsullied; free from impurities and unmeasurable. Good men observe that pure form which is termed the true and the great entity.

## \|\| 1.38.10 \|\|

*ekena hemraiva vibhūṣaṇāni yātāni bhedatvamupādhibhedāt \|*  
*tathaiva sarveṣvara eka eva pradṛśyate bhinna ivārivalātmā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All ornaments are identical inasmuch as the same gold is present in all of them. They assume different forms due to the conditioning factors. Similarly, the same lord of all, the Atman of everyone, though single appears as different due to conditioning factors.

## \|\| 1.38.11 \|\|

*yanmāyayā mohitacetasastaṃ paśyanti nātmānamapi prasiddham \|*  
*ta eva māyārahitāstadeva pasaayanti sarvātmakamātmarupam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Those whose minds are deluded by his Maya do not perceive even the well-known Atman. Those very persons when freed from Maya, perceive the same as their ownself being the self of all.

## \|\| 1.38.12 \|\|

*vibhuṃ jyotiranaupamyaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñaṃ namāmyaham \|*  
*samastametadudbhūtaṃ yato yatra pratiṣṭitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I bow down to the lord named Visnu, the incomparable brilliance, from whom all this visible world has originated and in whom that has been established.

## \|\| 1.38.13 \|\|

*yataścaitanyamāyātaṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya vai namaḥ \|*  
*aprameyamanādāramādhārādheyarūpakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to that lord whose form is consciousness; and from whom sentience has originated. Obeisance to that lord who is incomprehensible, who has nothing to support and who is of the form of both the supporter and the supported.

## \|\| 1.38.14 \|\|

*paramānandacinmātraṃ vāsudevaṃ nato 'smyaham \|*  
*hṛdguhānilayaṃ devaṃ yogibhiḥ parisevitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I bow down to Vasudeva who is the embodiment of pure bliss and knowledge. I bow down to that Lord whose abode is the cavity of the heart and who is served by Yogins.

## \|\| 1.38.15 \|\|

*yogānāmādibhūtaṃ taṃ namāmi praṇavasthitam \|*  
*nādātmakaṃ nādabījaṃ praṇavātmakamavyayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I bow down to that deity who has become the first among the Yogins and who abides in the Pranava (*Оm*). I bow down to that unchanging deity of the nature of Nada (mystic sound) who is the Bija (seed) of the Nada and who is of the nature of Pranava.

## \|\| 1.38.16 \|\|

*sadbhaghāvaṃ sañcidānandaṃ taṃ vande tigmacakriṇam \|*  
*ajaraṃ sākṣiṇaṃ tvasya hyavāṅmanasagocaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I bow down to that deity who has the nature of Being (or Existence) and who is Existence, knowledge and Bliss, the possessor of that fiery sharpedged discus; who is the unageing cosmic witness and who is beyond the ken of speech and mind.

## \|\| 1.38.17-19 \|\|

*nirañjanamanantākhyaṃ viṣṇurupaṃ nato 'smyaham \|*  
*indriyāṇi mano buddhiḥ sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vāsudevātmakānyāhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetra jñameva ca \|*  
*vidyāvidyātmakaṃ prāhuḥ parātparataraṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*anādinidhanaṃ śāntaṃ sarvadhātāramacyutam \|*  
*ye prapannā mahātmānasteṣāṃ muktirhi śāśvatī \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. I bow down to the form of Visnu that is called Ananta (Infinite) and is unsullied. They say that the sense organs, the mind, the intellect, the inherent power, the brilliance, the strength, fortitude, the Ksetra (the body) and the Ksetrajna - (the Soul) — all these are of the nature of Vasudeva. They call him one who is of the form of both Vidya and Avidya (knowledge аnd Nescience). They call him greater than the greatest. Perpetual is the salvation of those great noble souls who seek refuge in the quiescent Acyuta who has neither beginning nor destruction and who is the creator of every thing.

## \|\| 1.38.20 \|\|

*varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ purāṇaṃ sanātanaṃ sarvagataṃ samastam \|*  
*nato 'smi bhūyo 'pi nato 'smi bhūyo 'pi nato 'smi bhūyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Repeatedly, I bow unto him who is the most excellent, a bestower of boons who is the ancient and eternal deity identifying with everything and pervading all.

## \|\| 1.38.21 \|\|

*yatpāda toyaṃ bhaghavarogavaidyo yatpādapāṃśurvimalatvasiddhyai \|*  
*yannāma duṣkarmanivāraṇāyacaya tamaprameyaṃ puruṣaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 21 \|\|*
