21\. I worship that incomprehensible Рurusa, the water from whose feet is an antidote for the ailment of worldly existence (Samsara)y the dust of whose feet is conducive to the achievement of purity and whose name is efficacious to ward off evil rites.

## \|\| 1.38.22 \|\|

*sadrūpaṃ tamasadrūpaṃ sadasadrūpamavyayam \|*  
*tattadvilakṣaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhācchraṣṭhataraṃ bhaje \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I worship him who is of the form of Sat (Existent) and who is of the form of Asat (non-Existent) and who is of the form of both Sat and Asat; who is unchanging, and different from all these. He is the excellent one, more excellent than the most excellent.

## \|\| 1.38.23 \|\|

*nirañjanaṃ nirākāraṃ pūrṇamākāśamadhyagam \|*  
*paraṃ ca vidyāvidyābhyāṃ hṛdaṃbujanivāsinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He is unsullied, formless, perfect and stationed in the midst of firmament. He is beyond both Vidya and Avidya; and is abiding in the lotus of the heart.

## \|\| 1.38.24 \|\|

*svaprakāśamanirdeṣyaṃ mahatāṃ ca mahattaram \|*  
*aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ sarvopādhivivarjitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He is self-luminous, unspecifiable, greater than the greatest, and minuter than the minutest. He is devoid of all conditioning factors.

## \|\| 1.38.25 \|\|

*yannityaṃ paramānandaṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|*  
*viṣṇusaṃjñaṃ jagaddhāma tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. 1 sought refuge in that supporting abode of the universe termed Visnu, which is eternal, the greatest bliss and which is the greatest eternal Brahman.

## \|\| 1.38.26 \|\|

*yaṃ bhajanti kriyāniṣṭāyaṃ paśyanti ca yoginaḥ \|*  
*pūjyātpūjyataraṃ śāntaṃ gato 'smi śaraṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I sought asylum in that quiescent Lord whom, those who strictly adhere to holy rites, worship, whom the Yogins perceive and who is more worthy of being worshipped than anyone ebe.

## \|\| 1.38.27 \|\|

*yaṃ na paśyanti vidvāṃso ya etadvyāvya tiṣṭati \|*  
*sarvasmādadhikaṃ nityaṃ nato 'smi vibhumavyayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I bow down to the unchanging Lord who is eternal and superior to all, whom even learned men do not perceive and who stands pervading this entire universe.

## \|\| 1.38.28 \|\|

*antaḥ karaṇasaṃyogājjīva ityucyate ca yaḥ \|*  
*avidyākārya rahitaḥ paramātmeti gīyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It is he who is called Jiva (the individual Soul) due to the contact with internal sense-organ (i.e. the Mind). It is he who is sung about as the greatest Atman when he is devoid of Avidya and the physical body.

## \|\| 1.38.29 \|\|

*sarvātmakaṃ sarvahetuṃ sravakarmaphalappadam \|*  
*varaṃ vareṇyamajanaṃ praṇato 'smi parātparam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I bow down to that deity who is identical with every thing, is the cause of all; who is the bestower of the benefits of all holy rites and is the most excellent of all; who is unborn and greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 1.38.30 \|\|

*sarvajñaṃ sarvagaṃ śāntaṃ sarvāntayā miṇaṃ harim \|*  
*jñānātmakaṃ jñānanidhiṃ jñānasaṃsthaṃ vibhuṃ bhaje \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I worship Hari who is omniscient, omnipresent and quiescent; who is die immanent soul of all and is identical with perfect knowledge; who is the storehouse of perfect knowledge and the Lord stationed in perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.38.31 \|\|

*namāmyahaṃ vedanidhiṃ murāriṃ vedānta vijñānasuniścitārtham \|*  
*sūryeduvatprojjvalane tramindraṃ ravagasvarupaṃ vapatisvarūpam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I bow down to the receptacle of the Vedas, the slayer of demon Mura (Visnu) whose import is well decided by the sound knowledge of the Vedanta (contained in upanisads) who is the Lord with the shining eyes in the form of the Sun and the Moon, and who has the form of the bird, viz., that of Vipati (lord of the birds).

## \|\| 1.38.32 \|\|

*sarveśvaraṃ sarvagataṃ mahāntaṃ vedātmakaṃ vedavidāṃvariṣṭam \|*  
*taṃvāṅmano 'cintyamanantaśaktiṃ jñānaikavedyaṃ puruṣaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I worship that Purusa who is the great lord of all, omni-present; who is identical with the Vedas and is the most excellent of all knowers of the Vedas; who is beyond the ken of speech and the mind; is incomprehensible, of infinite power and knowable only through perfect spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 1.38.33 \|\|

*indrāgnikālāsurapāśivāyusomeṣamārttaṇḍapurandarādyaiḥ \|*  
*yaḥ pāti lokānparipūrṇabhāvastamaprameyaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I seek refuge in that incomprehensible and unmeasurable Lord, who possesses the perfect nature and who protects the worlds through Indra, Agni, Kala (i.e. Yama), Asura (i.e. Nirrti), Pasin (Varuna), Vayu, Soma (the Moon) lsa, Martanda (the Sun), Purandara and others.

## \|\| 1.38.34 \|\|

*sahasraśīrṣaṃ ca sahasrapādaṃ sahasrabāhuḥ ca sahasranetram \|*  
*samastayajñaiḥ parijuṣṭamādyaṃ nato 'smi tuṣṭipradamugravīryam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I bow down to that deity who has thousand hands, thousand feet, thousand arms and thousand eyes, who is served by means of Yajnas, and who is the primordial deity of fierce valour, the bestower of contentment and pleasure.

## \|\| 1.38.35-36 \|\|

*kālātmakaṃ kālavibhāgahetuṃ guṇatrayātītamahaṃ guṇajñam \|*  
*guṇapriyaṃ kāmadamastasaṃgamatīndriyaṃ viśvabhaghujaṃ vitṛṣṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nirīhamagryaṃ manasāpyagamyaṃ manomayaṃ cānnamayaṃ nirūḍham \|*  
*vijñānabhedaṃ pratipannakalpaṃ na vāṅmayaṃ prāṇamayaṃ bhajāmi \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. I worship the deity who is identical with Kala (Time, Death); who is the cause of the division of Time, who is beyond the three Gunas, but is the knower of attributes; who is the appreciator of good qualities, the bestower of desired objects, contactless and unknowable through the sense-organs; who is the enjoyer of the universe yet is devoid of thirst (i.e. desire for worldly things); who is devoid of desire, the foremost (one), who cannot be approached even mentally; who is inherent in the vestures (Kosas) constituted of the mind and food (mental) and physical vestures, who is discerned through spiritual wisdom and attained through Kalpas (sacred precepts?) and who is not identical with either speech or Pranas (vital breaths).

## \|\| 1.38.37 \|\|

*na yasya rūpaṃ na balaprabhāvo na yasya karmāṇi na yatpramāṇam \|*  
*jānanti devā kamalodbhavādyastoṣyāmyahaṃ taṃ kathamātmarūpam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. How can I eulogise that deity of the form of Atman about whom the lotus-born deity and other Devas (deities) do not know anything? They do not know his form, or strength or prowess, or activities or valid means of knowing him (or his magnitude).

## \|\| 1.38.38 \|\|

*saṃsārasidhau patitaṃ kadaryaṃ mohākulaṃ kāmaśatena baddham \|*  
*akīrtibhājaṃ piśunaṃ kṛtaghnaṃ sadāśuciṃ pāparataṃ pramanyum \|*  
*dayāṃbudhe pāhi bhayākulaṃ māṃ punaḥ punastvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О ocean of mercy, protect me! I am fallen into the ocean of worldly existence; I am miserly and deluded; I am bound by hundreds of lustful entanglements, I am infamous slanderous, ungrateful. I am always impure, engaged in sinful activities and extremely furious. I am frightened as well. I seek refuge in you again and again. Save me”.

## \|\| 1.38.39 \|\|

*iti prasāditastena dayālasuḥ kamalāpatiḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣatāmagāttasya bhagavāṃstejasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thus propitiated by him, the sympathetic lord of Kamala (Laksmi), the lordly receptacle of all brilliance became visible to him directly.

## \|\| 1.38.40-43 \|\|

*atasī puṣpasaṃkāśaṃ phullapaṅkajalocanan \|*  
*kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śrīvatsakaustubhadharaṃ hemayajñopavītinanam \|*  
*nāsāvinyastamuktā bhavardhamānatanucchavim \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pītāṃbaradharaṃ devaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣimat \|*  
*tulasīkomaladalairarcitāṅghniṃ mahādyutim \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kiṅkiṇīnūpurā dyaiśca śobhitaṃ garuḍadhvajam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nānāma viprendro daṇḍavatkṣitimaṇḍale \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. He resembled the Atasi (blue) flower (in complexion). His eyes were like full-blown lotuses. He was bedecked in coronet, ear-rings, necklaces and bracelets. He was wearing the Kaustubha jewel and the golden line of hair on the chest called Srivatsa. He had golden sacred thread. The beauty of his body was hightened by the lustre of the pearl placed at the tip of his nose. He was clad in yellow robes. The lord was adorned with garlands of sylvan flowers. His feet were worshipped with the tender leaves of Tulasi plant. He had a great lustre. He was adorned with tinkling ornaments and anklets, etc. On seeing the Garuda-emblemed deity, the leading Brahmana bowed down and prostrated himself like a staff, on the ground.

## \|\| 1.38.44 \|\|

*abhyaṣiñcaddhareḥ pādāvuttaṅko harṣavāribhiḥ \|*  
*murāre rakṣa rakṣeti vyāharannānyadhīstadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With tears of delight, Uttanka sprinkled the feet of Hari. Without his mind turning to anyone else he said, “O Murari, save me, save me”.

## \|\| 1.38.45-46 \|\|

*tamutthāpya mahāviṣṇurāliliṅga dayāparaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇuṣva vatseti provāca munipuṅgavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*asādhyaṃ nāsti kiñcitte prasanne mayi sattama \|*  
*itīritaṃ samākarṇya hyuttaṅkaścakrapāṇinā \|*  
*punaḥ praṇamya taṃ prāha devadevaṃ janārddanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Raising him up, Maha-Visnu, the merciful deity, embraced the leading sage and said, “O dear child, choose your boon. О excellent one, when I am delighted, there is nothing which cannot be achieved by you”. On hearing this uttered by the discus-bearing deity, Uttanka again bowed to Janardana, the lord of Devas and said:

## \|\| 1.38.47 \|\|

*kiṃ māṃ mohayasīśa tvaṃ kimanyairdeva me varaiḥ \|*  
*tvayi bhaktirdṛḍhā me 'stu janmajanmāntareṣvapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “O Lord, why do you delude me? О Lord, of what use are other boons unto me? May my devotion to you be firm and stable in everyone of my births.

## \|\| 1.38.48 \|\|

*kīṭeṣu pakṣiṣu mṛgeṣu sarīsṛpeṣu rakṣaḥ piśācamanujeṣvapi yatra tatrajajātasya me bhavatu keśava te prasāddāttvayyeva bhaktiracalāvyabhicāraṇī ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Among the worms, birds, animals, reptiles, Raksasas, Pisacas or human beings — wherever I may be bom, О Kesava! may my devotion to you alone be steady and unswerving through your grace”.

## \|\| 1.38.49 \|\|

*evamastviti lokeśaḥ śaṅkhaprāntena saṃspṛśan divyajñānaṃ dadau tasmai yogināmapidurlamabhagham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Saying “May it be so”, the Lord of the worlds touched him with the tip of his conch. He granted him the divine knowledge difficult to be attained even by Yogins.

## \|\| 1.38.50 \|\|

*puḥ stuvantaṃ viprendraṃ devadevo janārddanaḥ idamāha smitamukho hastaṃ tacchirasi nyasan \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. As the leading Brahmana began to eulogise again, Janardana, the lord of Devas, said thus with a beam of smile flickering on his face and placed his hand on his head.

## \|\| 1.38.51 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca ārādhaya kriyāyogairmāṃ sadā dvijasattam \|*  
*naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ vraja mokṣaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 51 \|\|*

*Sri Bhagavan said:*

51\. О excellent Brahmana, propitiate me always by means of holy and Yogic rites. Go to the abode of Nara and Narayana. You will attain salvation.

## \|\| 1.38.52 \|\|

*tvayā kṛtamidaṃ stotraṃ yaḥ paṭhetsatataṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpyānte mokṣabhāgī bhavettataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The man who always reads the song of prayer composed by you, attains ail desires and in the end he shall attain salvation”.

## \|\| 1.38.53 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhādhavo vipraṃ tatraivāntardadhe mune \|*  
*naranarāyaṇasthānamuttaṅko 'pi tato yayau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О sage, after saying this to the Brahmana, Madhava (Visnu) vanished there itself. Thereafter, Uttanka went to the abode of Nara and Narayana.

## \|\| 1.38.54 \|\|

*kasmādbhaktiḥ sadā kāryā devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*haribhaktiḥ parā proktā sarvakāmapalapradā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Hence, devotion to the discus-bearing lord of Devas should always be practised. Bhakti (devotion) towards Hari is said to be the greatest means that yields all desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.38.55-56 \|\|

*utaṅko bhāktibhāvena kriyāyogaparo mune \|*  
*pūjayanmādhayavaṃ nityaṃ naranārāyaṇāśrame \|\| 55 \|\|*

*jñānavijñānasaṃpannaḥ saṃcchinnadvaitasaṃśayaḥ \|*  
*āvāpa duravāpaṃ vai tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. О sage, engaged in the Yogic and holy rites with great devotional feelings, Uttanka worshipped Madhava continuously in the hermitage of Nara and Narayana. He was richly endowed with wisdom and perfect knowledge. All his dualistic doubts were quelled. He attained the greatest region of Visnu difficult to be attained by all.

## \|\| 1.38.57 \|\|

*pūjito namito vāpi saṃsmṛto vāpi mokṣadaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇo jagannātho bhaktānāṃ mānavarddhanaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Worshipped, bowed to or well-remembered, Narayana, the lord of the universe, bestows salvation. He increases the honour of devotees.

## \|\| 1.38.58 \|\|

*tasmānnārāyaṇaṃ devamanantamaparājitam \|*  
*ihāmutra sukhaprepsuḥ pūjayedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence, one who desires to attain happiness here and hereafter should worship with great devotion, Lord Narayana who is infinite and unvanquished.

## \|\| 1.38.59 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhedidamākhyānaṃ śṛṇuyādvāsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*so 'pi sarvāghanirmuktaḥ prayāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He who listens to or reads this narrative with great attention becomes liberated from all sins. He goes to the abode of Hari.

## Chapter 39. The Greatness of Visnu: The Story of Raivata

## \|\| 1.39.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*bhūyaḥ śṛṇuṣva viprendra māhātmyaṃ parameṣṭinaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. О leading Brahmana, listen, once again, to the greatness of Paramesthin. It is meritorious and destructive of all sins. It yields worldly pleasures and salvation to men.

## \|\| 1.39.2 \|\|

*aho harikathā loke pāpaghnī puṇyadāyinī \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ vadatāṃ caiva tadbhaktānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Lo! The story of Hari is destructive of sins in the world. It bestows merits upon those who listen to the same or narrate it particularly so to his devotees.

## \|\| 1.39.3 \|\|

*haribhaktirasāsvādamuditā ye narottamāḥ \|*  
*namaskaromyahaṃ tebhyo yatsaṃgānmukti bhāgnaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I bow down to those excellent men who rejoice after tasting the exquisite juice of devotion to Hari. Thanks to association with them, a man attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.39.4 \|\|

*haribhaktiparā ye tu harināmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*durvṛttā vā suvṛttā vā tebhyo nityaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Obeisance, obeisance for ever to those men who are absorbed in repeating the names of Hari, irrespective of whether they are of good conduct or evil-minded.

## \|\| 1.39.5 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgaraṃ tartuṃ ya icchenmu nipuṅgava \|*  
*sa bhajeddharibhaktānāṃ bhaktānvai pāpahāriṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О leading sage, he who wishes to cross the ocean of worldly existence should worship the devotees of the devotees of Hari.

## \|\| 1.39.6 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā dhyātaḥ praṇamito 'pi vā \|*  
*samuddharati govindo dustarādbhava sāgarāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Seen, remembered, worshipped, meditated upon or bowed to, Govinda uplifts people from the ocean of worldly existence which is very difficult to cross.

## \|\| 1.39.7 \|\|

*svapanbhuñjan vrajaṃstiṣṭannatiṣṭaśca vadaṃstathā \|*  
*cintayedyo harernāma tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Salutations for ever to that man who thinks of Hari’s name even while he is sleeping or eating or walking, or standing or sitting or talking.

## \|\| 1.39.8 \|\|

*aho bhāgyamaho bhāgyaṃ viṣṇu bhaktiratātmanām \|*  
*yeṣāṃ muktiḥ karasthaiva yogināmapi durlabhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О how wonderful! Wonderful is the good fortune of those who are engrossed in devotion to Visnu since salvation which is inaccessible even to the Yogins is as if in their hand (within their reach).

## \|\| 1.39.9 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*vadatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpa praṇāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In this context they cite the following mythological anecdote which is destructive of all sins of those who speak about and listen to this.

## \|\| 1.39.10 \|\|

*āsītpurā mahīpālaḥ somavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*jayadhvaja iti khyāto nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Formerly, there was a king born of the lunar race. He was known as Jayadhvaja. He was devoted to Narayana.

## \|\| 1.39.11 \|\|

*viṣṇordevālaye nityaṃ saṃmār janaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*dīpadānarataścaiva sarvabhūtadayāparaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was regularly absorbed in the activities of scrubbing and cleaning in the temple of Visnu. He used to be engaged in offering lights as well. He sympathised with all living beings.

## \|\| 1.39.12 \|\|

*sa kadācinmahīpālo revātīre manorame \|*  
*vicitrakusumopetaṃ kṛtavānviṣṇumandiram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Once, that king built a temple of Visnu on the beautiful banks of the river Reva. It consisted of wonderful flowers of various colours.

## \|\| 1.39.13 \|\|

*sa tatra nṛpaśārdūlaḥ sadā saṃmārjane rataḥ \|*  
*dīpadānaparaścaiva viśeṣeṇa haripriyaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The leading king was always engaged in sweeping and cleaning in the -temple. He was particularly fond of Hari and regularly lighted lamps there.

## \|\| 1.39.14 \|\|

*harināmaparo nityaṃ harisaṃsaktamānasaḥ \|*  
*paripraṇāmanirato haribhaktajanapriyaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He was deeply interested in repeating the names of Hari. His mind was always drawn towards Hari. He was engaged in worshipping and bowing to Hari. He was fond of persons devoted to Hari.

## \|\| 1.39.15 \|\|

*vītihotra iti khyāto hyāsīttasya purohitaḥ \|*  
*jayadhvajasya caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His priest was famous by the name of Vitihotra. On observing the conduct of Jayadhvaja, he was surprised.

## \|\| 1.39.16 \|\|

*kadācidupaviṣṭaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ viṣṇutatparam \|*  
*apṛcchadvītihotrastu vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Once Vitihotra who was a master of the Vedas and the ancillaries to Vedas, asked the king who was devoted to Visnu while he was leisurely seated (somewhere).

## \|\| 1.39.17 \|\|

*vītihotra uvāca*  
*rājanparamadharmajña haribhaktiparāyaṇa \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktimatāṃ puṃsāṃ śreṣṭho 'si bharatarṣabha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*Vitihotra said:*

17\. О king, the knower of the great Dharma, engaged in devotion to Hari, О leading member of the family of Bharata, you are the most excellent among men endowed with devotion to Visnu.

## \|\| 1.39.18 \|\|

*saṃmārjanaparo nityaṃ dīpadānaratastathā \|*  
*tanme vada mahābhāga kiṃ tvayā viditaṃ phalam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. You are constantly engaged in sweeping and cleaning as well as in lighting the lamps (in the shrine of Visnu). Hence, О blessed one, tell me what benefit by this has been known by you.

## \|\| 1.39.19 \|\|

*saṃpādanena varttīnāṃ tailasaṃpalādanena ca \|*  
*saṃyukto 'si sadā bhadrayadviṣṇorgṛhamārjane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О gentle Sir, you are always engaged in collecting wicks and oil as well as in cleaning the abode of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.39.20 \|\|

*karmāṇyanyāni saṃtyeva viṣṇoḥ prītikarāṇi ca \|*  
*tathāpi kiṃ mahābhāga etayoḥ satatodyataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There are other activities pleasing to Visnu. Still, О blessed one, why are you engaged only in these two activities continuously?

## \|\| 1.39.21 \|\|

*sarvātmanā mahāpuṇyaṃ nareśa vidita ca yat \|*  
*tad brūhi me guhyatamaṃ prītirmayi tavāsti cet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О lord of men, if you have any love towards me, tell me the secret of the same which is highly meritorious in every respect and known to you.

## \|\| 1.39.22 \|\|

*purodhasaivamuktastu prahasansa jayadhvajaḥ \|*  
*vinayāvanato bhūtvā provācejaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On being requested thus by his priest, Jayadhvaja laughingly spoke these words. He bowed down with humility and kept his palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.39.23 \|\|

*jayadhvaja uvāca*  
*śṛṇuṣva vipraśārdūla mayaivācaritaṃ purā \|*  
*jātismaratvājjānāmi śrotṝṇāṃ vismayapradam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*Jayadhvaja said:*

23\. О leading Brahmana, listen. Thanks to my faculty of remembering previous births, I know what had been performed by me formerly. It is conducive to the surprise of those who listen.

## \|\| 1.39.24 \|\|

*āsītpurā kṛtayuge brahmansvārociṣeṃ'tare \|*  
*raivato nāma viprendro vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Formerly, in the Svarocisa Manvantara of the Krtayuga, О Brahmana, there was a prominent Brahmana named Raivata. He was a master of the Vedas and the Vedangas.

## \|\| 1.39.25 \|\|

*ayājyayājakaścaiva sadaiva grāmayojakaḥ \|*  
*piśuno niṣṭhuraścaiva hyapaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He used to perform Yajnas on behalf of those who were not eligible for the same. He was a common priest for the whole village. He was a ruthless backbiter. He even sold forbidden goods.

## \|\| 1.39.26 \|\|

*niṣiddhakarmācaraṇātparityaktaḥ sa bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*daridro duḥkhitaścaiva śīrṇāṅgo vyādhito 'bhavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was abandoned by his kinsmen because he used to perform forbidden rites. Hence, he became indigent and miserable. He became sickly with shattered limbs.

## \|\| 1.39.27 \|\|

*sa kadāciddharthaṃ tu pṛthivyāṃ paryaṭan dvijaḥ \|*  
*mamāra narmadātīre śvāsakāsaprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. For the purpose of wealth, he was wandering over the Earth. Once the Brahmana was afflicted by Asthma and hiccough. He died on the banks of the Narmada.

## \|\| 1.39.28 \|\|

*tasminmṛte tasya bhāryā nāmnā bandhumatī mune \|*  
*kāmacāraparā sā tu parityaktā ca bandhubhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О sage, when he died, his wife named Bandhumati became a wayward wanton woman. Hence, she was forsaken by her kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.39.29 \|\|

*tasyāṃ jāto 'smi caṇḍālo daṇḍaketuriti śrutaḥ \|*  
*mahāpāparato nityaṃ brahmadveṣaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I was born of her as a Candala, popularly known as Dandaketu. I was always engaged in great sins and was a habitual hater of Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.39.30 \|\|

*paradāraparadravyalolupo jantuhiṃsakaḥ \|*  
*gāvaśca viprā bahavo nihatā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I was covetous of other men’s wealth and enamoured of other men’s wives. I killed many creatures. Many cows, Brahmanas, birds and animals were killed by me.

## \|\| 1.39.31 \|\|

*merutulyasuvarṇāni bahūnyapahṛtāni ca \|*  
*madyapānarato nityaṃ bahuśo mārgarodhakṛt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Many huge pieces of gold like the Meru mountain were stolen by me. I was always engaged in drinking liquor. Many times I had been a highway robber too.

## \|\| 1.39.32-33 \|\|

*paśupakṣimṛgādīnāṃ jantūnāmantakopamaḥ \|*  
*kadācitkāmasaṃtapto gantu kāmo ratiṃ striyaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śūnyaṃ viṣṇugṛhaṃ dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭaśca striyā saha \|*  
*niśi rāmopabhogārthaṃ śayitaṃ tatra kāminā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. I was comparable to the god of death for animals, birds, deer and other creatures. Once I was overwhelmed by lust and was desirous of having sexual intercourse with my wife. On seeing a lonely abode of Visnu I entered it in the company of my wife. In order to enjoy my wife during that night, I lay there lustfully.

## \|\| 1.39.34-36 \|\|

*brahmansvavastraprāntena kiyaddeśaḥ pramārjitaḥ \|*  
*yāvantyaḥ pāṃśukaṇikāstatra saṃmārjitā dvija \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tāvajjanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tadaiva kṣayamāgatam \|*  
*pradīpaḥ sthāpitastatra suratārthaṃ dvijottama \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tenāpi mama duṣkarma niḥśeṣaṃ kṣayamāgatam \|*  
*evaṃ sthite viṣṇugṛhe hyāgatāḥ purapālakāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. О Brahmana, by my clothes some space in the temple was swept by me. The sins committed by me in the course of so many births as the number of dust particles swept, were quelled immediately. О excellent Brahmana, a lamp had been kept there by me for the sexual intercourse. On account of this also my evil actions were entirely wiped off. When such was the situation, the city guards came there to the temple of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.39.37 \|\|

*jāro 'yamiti māṃ tāṃ ca hatavantaḥ prasahya vai \|*  
*āvāṃ nihatya te sarve nivṛttāḥ purakṣakāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. They caught hold of her and me saying “Here is an adulterer” and killed us. After killing us both, the city guards returned.

## \|\| 1.39.38 \|\|

*yadā tadaiva saṃprāptā viṣṇudūtāścaturbhujāḥ \|*  
*kirīṭakuṇḍaladharā vanamālāvibhūṣitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Immediately the emissaries of Visnu came there. All of them had four arms. They were wearing crowns and earrings. They were bedecked in garlands of sylvan flowers.

## \|\| 1.39.39 \|\|

*taistu saṃpreritāvāvāṃ viṣṇudūtairakalmaṣaiḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamāruhya sarvabhogasamanvitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Directed by those sinless emissaries of Visnu, we both entered a divine aerial car, equipped with all means of enjoyment.

## \|\| 1.39.40 \|\|

*divyadehadharau bhūtvā viṣṇulokamupāgatau \|*  
*tatra sthitvā brahmakalpaśataṃ sāgraṃ dvijottama \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. We ourselves assumed divine forms and went to Visnuloka. О excellent Brahmana, we stayed there for a period of a hundred Kalpas of Brahma and more.

## \|\| 1.39.41 \|\|

*divyabhogasamāyuktau tāvatkālaṃ divi sthitau \|*  
*tataśca bhūmibhāgeṣu devayogeṣu vai kramāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. For a similar period, we stayed in the heaven too, equipped with all divine pleasures. Then by turns we lived on the Earth as well as in the Deva regions.

## \|\| 1.39.42 \|\|

*tena puṇyaprabhāveṇa yadūnāṃ vaṃśasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tenaiva me 'cyutā saṃpattathā rājyamakaṇṭakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. As a result of that meritorious activity I was born as a scion of the family of Yadus. For the same reason my riches never dwindle and my kingdom is devoid of thorns (i.e. enemies and other turbulence).

## \|\| 1.39.43 \|\|

*brahmankṛtvopabhogārthamevaṃ śreyo hyavāptavān \|*  
*bhaktyā kurvanti ye saṃtasteṣāṃ puṇyaṃ na vedyaham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Brahmana, after doing something for my own enjoyment, such welfare has been attained by me. I do not know the extent of the benefit and merit of those good men who perform these things with devotion.

## \|\| 1.39.44 \|\|

*tasmātsaṃmārjane nityaṃ dīpadāne ca sattama \|*  
*yatiṣye parayā bhaktyā hyahaṃ jātismaro yataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence, О excellent one, with great devotion I endeavour to fulfil my duties of sweeping the floor and lighting the lamps, since I have the faculty of remembering the previous birth.

## \|\| 1.39.45 \|\|

*yaḥ pūjayejjagannāthamekākī vigataspṛhaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He who worships the lord of the universe with single- minded attention and absence of desire (for any fruit therefrom) becomes free from all sins and goes to the greatest region.

## \|\| 1.39.46 \|\|

*avaśenāpi yatkarma kṛtvemāṃ śriyamāgataḥ \|*  
*bhaktibhadbhiḥ praśāntaiśca kiṃ punaḥ samyagarcanāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I have attained this much of prosperity after performing the holy rites helplessly. What then will not be attained by quiescent and devout persons by worshipping perfectly?”.

## \|\| 1.39.47 \|\|

*iti bhūpavacaḥ śrutvā vītihotro dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*anantatuṣṭimāpanno haripūjāparo 'bhavat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing the words of the king, the excellent Brahmana Vitihotra was infinitely contented. He became absorbed in the worship of Hari.

## \|\| 1.39.48 \|\|

*tasmācchṛṇuṣva viprendra devo nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*jñānato 'jñānato vāpi pūjakānāṃ vimuktidaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, listen, О Chief of Brahmanas! The unchanging lord Narayana is the bestower of salvation to those who worship him with or without perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.39.49 \|\|

*anityā bāndhavāḥ sarve vibhavo naiva śāśvataḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ sannihito mṛtyuḥ kartavyo dharmasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. All the kinsmen are casual and unsteady, wealth is never permanent. God of death is continuously near at hand. Hence, Dharma (religious and pious acts) must be accumulated.

## \|\| 1.39.50 \|\|

*ajño loko vṛthā garvaṃ kariṣyati mahoddhataḥ \|*  
*kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyo dhānādīnāṃ kimucyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is the ignorant people who in their extreme arrogance, are vainglorious. Even the body is near (in the very shadow of) dangers. What needs be spoken about riches, etc.

## \|\| 1.39.51 \|\|

*janmakoṭisahasreṣu puṇyaṃ yaiḥ samupārjitam \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhaktirbhavecchuddhā devadeve janārdane \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Pure devotion unto Janardana, the God of gods, will be generated only in those people who have accumulated merit during the course of thousands of crores of previous births.

## \|\| 1.39.52 \|\|

*sulabhaṃ jāhnavī snānaṃ tathevātithipūjanam \|*  
*sulabhāḥ sarvayajñāśca viṣṇubhaktiḥ sudurlabhā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The ablution in the Ganga is easily accessible; so also is the worship of guests; all the Yajnas too can be easily performed but devotion towards Visnu is very difficult to obtain.

## \|\| 1.39.53-54 \|\|

*durlabhā tulasīsevā durlabhaḥ saṃgamaḥ satām \|*  
*sarvabhūtadayā vāpi sulabhā yasya kasya cit \|\| 53 \|\|*

*satsaṃgastulasīsebā haribhaktiśca durlabhā \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. The service to the Tulasi plant is difficult to get; intimate contact with the saintly people is also inaccessible; but the merciful nature towards all living beings may be easy to some. But contact with the good, service to the Tulasi plant and devotion towards Hari — every thing is difficult to get.

## \|\| 1.39.55 \|\|

*durlabhaṃ prāpyaṃ mānuṣyaṃ na tathā gamayed budhaḥ \|*  
*arcayeddhi jagannāthaṃ sārametaddvijottama \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A sensible man should not waste it in vain, after attaining the rare birth as a human being. He should worship the Lord of the universe. This is essential, О excellent Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.39.56 \|\|

*tarttuṃ yadīcchati jano dustaraṃ bhavasāgaram \|*  
*haribhaktiparo bhūyādetadeva rasāyanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If any man wishes to cross the impassable ocean of worldly existence, let him be devoted to Hari. This is the only panacea.

## \|\| 1.39.57 \|\|

*bhrātarāśraya govindaṃ mā vilaṃbaṃ kuru priya \|*  
*āsannameva nagaraṃ kṛtāntasya hi dṛśyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О brother, seek the support of Govinda. О beloved one, do not delay. The city of Krtanta (God of death) is seen nearby.

## \|\| 1.39.58 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ jagadyoniṃ sarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|*  
*samarcayasva viprendra yadi bhuktimabhīpsasi \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. О leading Brahmana, if you wish to attain liberation, worship Narayana, the source of the origin of the universe, the cause of the cause of all.

## \|\| 1.39.59 \|\|

*sarvādhāra sarvayoniṃ sarvāntaryāmiṇaṃ vibhum \|*  
*ye prapannā mahātmānaste kṛtārthā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Undoubtedly only those noble-souled ones who have resorted to the Lord, the support of all, the source of origin of all, the immanent soul of all, have attained their goal in life.

## \|\| 1.39.60 \|\|

*te vandyāste prapūjyāśca namaskāryā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yer'cayanti mahāviṣṇuṃ praṇatārtipraṇāśanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those who worship Maha-Visnu, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow down to him, are worthy of being saluted, worshipped and especially bowed to.

## \|\| 1.39.61 \|\|

*ye viṣṇubhaktā niṣkāmā yañjati parameśvaram \|*  
*triḥsaptakulasaṃyuktā ste yānti harimandiram \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those devotees of Visnu who worship the Supreme Lord without any specific desire, go to the abode of Hari along with twenty-one generations of his family.

## \|\| 1.39.62 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktāya yo dadyānniṣkāmāya mahātmane \|*  
*pānīyaṃ vā phalaṃ vāpi sa eva bhagavatpriyaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Only he becomes the beloved favourite of the Lord — he who gives water or fruit to a noble-souled devotee of Visnu, who is devoid of any desire.

## \|\| 1.39.63 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktiparāṇāṃ tu śuśrūṣāṃ kurvate tu ye \|*  
*te yānti viṣṇubhuvanaṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who render service to the devotees of Visnu go to Visnu’s world and stay there till the final dissolution of all living beings takes places.

## \|\| 1.39.64 \|\|

*ye yañjati spṛhāśūnyā haribhaktān hariṃ tathā \|*  
*ta eva bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ puṃnati svāṅghripāṃśunā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Only those can purify the universe with the dust of their feet who worship Hari and Hari’s devotees, without any specific desire (in return).

## \|\| 1.39.65 \|\|

*devapūjāparo yasya gṛhe vasati sarvadā \|*  
*tatraiva sarvadevāśca tiṣṭanti śrīharistathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If anyone devoted to the worship of the Lord stays in a house, Devas as well as Sri Hari also stay there.

## \|\| 1.39.66 \|\|

*pūjyamānā ca tulasī yasya tiṣṭati veśmani \|*  
*tatra sarvāṇi śreyāṃsi varddhatyaharahardvija \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О Brahmana, welfare and happiness increase day by day in that house where Tulasi is planted and worshipped.

## \|\| 1.39.67 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilārūpī yatra tiṣṭati keśavaḥ \|*  
*na bādhante grahāstatra bhūtavetāla kādayaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Evil planets, goblins, Vetalas, etc., do not harass anyone in that place where Kesava stays in the form of Salagrama stone.

## \|\| 1.39.68 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilā yatra tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam \|*  
*yataḥ saṃnihitastatra bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. That spot is a holy centre, that place is a penance grove, where the Salagrama stone stands, since lord *Madhusudana* is present there.

## \|\| 1.39.69 \|\|

*purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsā dharmaśāstrāṇi ca dvija \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О celestial sage, know that house to be devoid of auspiciousness and on a par with the cremation ground, if there is no worship of the Salagrama stone.

## \|\| 1.39.70 \|\|

*sāṃgā vedāstathā sarve viṣṇorūpaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The Puranas, Nyaya (texts), Mimamsa (texts), Dharma- sastras, Vedas along with their Angas — all these are glorified as the form of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.39.71 \|\|

*bhaktyā kurvanti ye viṣṇoḥ pradakṣiṇacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*te 'pi yānti paraṃ sthānaṃ sarvakarmanibarhaṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The persons who circumambulates Visnu four times with devotion, goes to the highest abode that quells all Karmans.

## Chapter 40. The Greatness of Visnu (The Story of Sudharma)

## \|\| 1.40.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vibhūtiṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ mune \|*  
*yāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ kīrtayatāṃ sadyaḥ pāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

1\. О sage, henceforth I shall tell you the Vibhuti (greatness and Super-human powers) pertaining to Visnu. If people listen to it or narrate it, their sins are reduced immediately.

## \|\| 1.40.2 \|\|

*vaivasvateṃ'tare pūrvaṃ śakrasya ca bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*saṃvādaḥ sumahānāsīttaṃ vakṣyāmi niśāmaya \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly, in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, a lengthy dialogue between Indra and Brhaspati took place. I shall narrate it; listen to it attentively.

## \|\| 1.40.3 \|\|

*ekadā sarvabhogāḍhyo vibudhaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇo bṛhaspatimabhāṣata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Once Indra who was richly endowed with the enjoyment of all pleasures and was surrounded by all Devas and the celestial damsels, spoke to Brhaspati.

## \|\| 1.40.4 \|\|

*indra uvāca*  
*bṛhaspate mahābhāga sarvatattvārthakovida \|*  
*atītabrahmaṇaḥ kalpe sṛṣṭiḥ kīdṛgvidhā prabho \|\| 4 \|\|*

*Indra said:*

4\. О lord, О highly blessed Brhaspati, О expert in the interpretation of all principles, of what nature was the creation in the Kalpa of Brahma which had gone by.

## \|\| 1.40.5 \|\|

*indrastu kīdṛśaḥ prokto vivudhāḥ kīdṛśāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca kīdṛśaṃ karma yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. How was Indra as narrated by them? How were Devas as remembered by them? Of what nature was their holy rite? It behoves you to recount this precisely.

## \|\| 1.40.6 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca*  
*na jñāyate mayā śakra pūrvedyuścaritaṃ vidheḥ \|*  
*vartamānadinasyāpi durjñeyaṃ pratibhāti me \|\| 6 \|\|*

*Brhaspati said:*

6\. О Indra, the conduct of Brahma on his previous day is not known to me. Even that of his present day appears to be very difficult to comprehend.

## \|\| 1.40.7 \|\|

*manavaḥ samatītāśca tānvaktumapi na kṣamaḥ \|*  
*yo vijānāti taṃ te 'dya kathayāmi niśāmaya \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Many Manus have gone by. Even to recount them I am not competent. I shall tell you who knows it to day, listen.

## \|\| 1.40.8 \|\|

*sudharma iti vikhyātaḥ kaścidāste pure tava \|*  
*bhuñjāno divyabhogāṃśca brahmalokādihāgataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There is some one in your city well-known as Sudharma. He has come here from Brahma’s world and is now enjoying the divine pleasures.

## \|\| 1.40.9-10 \|\|

*sa vā eta dvijānāti kathayāmi niśāmaya \|*  
*evamuktastu guruṇā śakrastena samanvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*devatāgaṇasaṃkīrṇaḥ sudharmanilayaṃ yayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. I shall tell you. Listen. Indeed he knows this. When he was informed thus by his preceptor, Indra went to the abode of Sudharma accompanied by the preceptor (Brhaspati) and surrounded by groups of Devas.

## \|\| 1.40.11 \|\|

*samāgataṃ devapatiṃ bṛhaspatisamanvitam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā yathārhaṃ devarṣe pūjayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О celestial sage, on seeing the lord of Devas arrived in the company of Brhaspati, he (Sudharma) received him and worshipped him respectfully.

## \|\| 1.40.12 \|\|

*sudharmeṇārcitaḥ śaṅkro dṛṣṭvā tacchriyamuttamām \|*  
*manasā vismayāviṣṭaḥ provāca vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When he was greeted and honoured by Sudharma, Indra observed his excellent glory. He was surprised in his mind. Then he respectfully addressed him thus:

## \|\| 1.40.13 \|\|

*indra uvāca*  
*atītabrahmakalpasya vṛttāntaṃ vetsi cedbudha \|*  
*tadākhyāhi samāyāta etatpraṣṭuṃ sayājakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*Indra said:*

13\. “O learned one, if you know the conduct of life and other details in the Kalpa of Brahma which had gone by, narrate it. I have come here accompanied by my preceptor in order to enquire about this.

## \|\| 1.40.14 \|\|

*gatanidrāṃśca devāṃśca yena jānāsi suvrata \|*  
*tadvadasvādhikaḥ kasmādasmadbhyo 'pi divi sthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О sage of holy observances, since you know Devas too who have no sleep, tell us who is the greater? How are they greater than we, the residents of heaven?

## \|\| 1.40.15 \|\|

*tejasāyaśasā kīrtyā jñānena ca parantapa \|*  
*dānena vā tapobhirvā kathametādṛśaḥ prabho \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О lord, О tormentor of enemies, how were they in brilliance, fame, renown, perfect knowledge, charitable gifts or penances?”

## \|\| 1.40.16 \|\|

*ityukto devarājena sudharmā prahasaṃstadā \|*  
*provāca vinayāviṣṭaḥ pūrvavṛttaṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On being requested thus by the king of Devas, Sudharma who was endowed with humility, laughingly recounted what happened before, duly.

## \|\| 1.40.17 \|\|

*sudharma uvāca*  
*caturyugasahasrāṇi brahmaṇo dinamucyate \|*  
*ekasmin divase śakra manavaśca caturdaśa \|\| 17 \|\|*

*Sudharma said:*

17\. “O Indra, a thousand cycles of four Yugas are said to constitute a day of Brahma. In one day, О Indra, there are fourteen Manus.

## \|\| 1.40.18-19 \|\|

*indrāścaturdaśa proktā devāśca vividhāḥ pṛthak \|*  
*indrāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ manvādīnāṃ ca vāsava \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tulyatā tejasā lakṣmyā prabhāveṇa balena ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. (During that period) Indras are also said to be fourteen; Devas are separate and of different kinds. О Vasava (Indra), all the Indras, Manus and others, are equal in brilliance, glory, prowess and strength. I shall mention their names. Listen with great attention.

## \|\| 1.40.20-21 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ pūrvaṃ tataḥ svārociṣastathā \|*  
*uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vaivasvato manuścaiva sūryasāvarṇiraṣṭamaḥ \|*  
*navamo dakṣasāvarṇiḥ sarvadevahite rataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The Svayambhuva Manu was the first (one), then Svarocisa. Thereafter, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata, Caksusa and Vaivasvata (the son of the Sun) and Surya Savarni was the eighth. The ninth Manu was Daksha Savarni who was engaged in the welfare of all Devas.

## \|\| 1.40.22-23 \|\|

*daśamo brahmasāvarṇirddharmasāvarṇikastataḥ \|*  
*tatastu rudrasāvarṇī rocamānastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhautyaścaturdaśaḥ prokta ete hi manavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*devānindrāṃśca vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva vibudharṣabha \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23a. The tenth was Brahmasavarni and Dharmasavarni was the next. Thereafter, Rudrasavarni, and Rocamana is remembered as the next. Bhautya is said to be the fourteenth (Manu). These are the Manus.

23b. О leading Deva, listen, I shall recount Devas and Indras.

## \|\| 1.40.24 \|\|

*yāmā iti samākhyātā devāḥ svāyaṃbhuveṃ'tare \|*  
*śacīpatiḥ samākhyātasteṣāmindro mahāpatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the Svayambhuva Manvantara those who were well known as Yamas were Devas. Their Indra was the highly intelligent Sacipati.

## \|\| 1.40.25 \|\|

*pārāvatāśca tuṣitā devāḥ svārociṣeṃ'tare \|*  
*vipaścinnāma devendraṃ sarvasaṃpatsamanvitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the Svarocisa Manvantara, Devas were Paravatas and Tusitas. The lord of Devas was one named Vipascit who was endowed with all riches.

## \|\| 1.40.26 \|\|

*sudhāmānastathā satyāḥ śivāścāya prartadanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmindraḥ suśāntiśca tṛtīye parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the third Manvantara, the set of Devas were the Sudhamans, Satyas, Sivas and Pratardanas. Their Indra was glorified as Susanti.

## \|\| 1.40.27-28 \|\|

*sutāḥ pārāharāścaiva sutyāścāsudhiyastathā \|*  
*teṣāmindraḥ śivaḥ proktaḥ śakrastāmasakeṃ'tare \|*  
*vibhānāmā devapatiḥ pañcamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*amitābhādayo devāḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'pi ca tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*āryādyā vibudhāḥ proktāsteṣā mindro manojavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In the Tamasa Manvantara Devas were Sutas, Paraharas, Sutyas and Asudhis. О Indra, their Indra is said to be Siva. One named Vibhu is glorified as the fifth Devapati (Indra) and Devas are Amitabha and others. Listen to them in the sixth (Manvantara). Aryas and others are said to be Devas and their Indra is Manojava.

## \|\| 1.40.29 \|\|

*ādityavasurudrādyā devā vaivasvataṃ'tare \|*  
*indraḥ purandaraḥ proktaḥ sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Devas are the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras and others. Purandara is said to be Indra. He is equipped with all desirable things.

## \|\| 1.40.30 \|\|

*aprameyāśca vibudhāḥ sutapādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇupūjāprabhāveṇa teṣāmindro baliḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Aprameyas, beginning with Sutapa are glorified as Devas in the eighth Manvantara. Thanks to the power of the Puja of Visnu, Bali is remembered as their Indra.

## \|\| 1.40.31 \|\|

*pārādyā navame devā indraścādbhuta ucyate \|*  
*suvāsanādyā vibudhā daśame parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the ninth (Manvantara) Para and others are Devas. Adbhuta is said to be Indra.  
In the tenth (Manvantara), Suvasana and others are glorified as Devas.

## \|\| 1.40.32-33 \|\|

*śāntirnāma ca tatrendraḥ sarvabhogasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vihṝṅgṝmādyā devāśca teṣāmindro vṛṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ekādaśe dvādaśe tu nibodhakathāyāmi te \|*  
*krabhuvanāmā ca devendro harinābhāstathā surāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Their Indra was named Santi. He was equipped with all means of enjoyment. In the eleventh (Manvantara), Devas were Vihangama and others. Vrsa is remembered as their Indra. Understand the details in the twelfth Manvantara. I shall narrate the Indra is one named Rbhu and Devas are Hari-Nabhas.

## \|\| 1.40.34 \|\|

*sutrāmādyāstathā devāstrayodaśatame 'ntare \|*  
*divaspatirmahāvīryasteṣāmindraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the thirteenth Manvantara, Sutramas and others are Devas, Divaspati of great prowess is glorified as their Indra.

## \|\| 1.40.35 \|\|

*caturdaśe cākṣupādyā devā indraḥ śuciḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ te manavaḥ proktā indrā devāśca tattvataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the fourteenth Manvantara, the Cakcusas and others are Devas. Suci is remembered as Indra. Thus the Manus, Indras and Devas have been recounted to you precisely.

## \|\| 1.40.36 \|\|

*ekasminbrahmadivase svādhikāraṃ prabhuñjate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In the course of one day of Brahma, all these enjoy their rights.

## \|\| 1.40.37 \|\|

*lekeṣu sarvasargeṣu sṛṣṭirekavidhā smṛtā \|*  
*karttāro bahavaḥ saṃti tatsaṃkhyāṃ vetti kovidaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In all worlds, in the course of all creations, the manner of creation is remembered to be of one type. The makers are many. Only an expert knows their number.

## \|\| 1.40.38 \|\|

*mayi sthite brahmaloke brahmāṇāṃ bahavo gatāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na saṃkhyātu śakto 'smyadya dvijottama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О excellent Brahmana, while I was staying in the Brahmaloka many Brahmas came and went away. I am unable to enumerate them.

## \|\| 1.40.39 \|\|

*svargalokamapi prāpya yāvatkālaṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|*  
*catvāro manavo 'tītā mama śrīścātivistarā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Listen, how much time I had spent after reaching the heaven. Four Manus have come and gone and my glory is still very extensive.

## \|\| 1.40.40 \|\|

*sthātavyaṃ ca mayātraiva yugakoṭiśataṃ prabho \|*  
*tataḥ paraṃ gamiṣyāmi karmabhūmiṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О lord, for the period of a hundred crores of Yugas, I have to stay here; thereafter, I will go to the Karmabhumi. Listen to me.

## \|\| 1.40.41 \|\|

*mayā kṛtaṃ purā karma vakṣyāmi tava suvrata \|*  
*vadatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О observer of holy rites, I shall describe the holy rites performed by me formerly. It is destructive of all sins of those who talk and listen.

## \|\| 1.40.42 \|\|

*ahamāṃsa purā śakra gṛdhraḥ pāpo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sthitaśca bhūmibhāge vai amedhyāmiṣabhojanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Indra, formerly, I was a vulture who was particularly sinful. I was stationed on the surface of the Earth with fecal matter and raw flesh as my diet.

## \|\| 1.40.43 \|\|

*ekadāhaṃ viṣṇugṛhe prākāre saṃsthitaḥ prabho \|*  
*patito vyādhaśastreṇa sāyaṃ viṣṇorgṛhāṅgaṇe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On one occasion, I was perching on the rampart of a Visnu temple. О lord, I was hit by the weapon of a hunter in the evening. I died and fell in the courtyard of a temple of Visnu (from its rampart).

## \|\| 1.40.44 \|\|

*mayi kaṇṭhagataprāṇe bhaṣaṇo māṃsalolupaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha māṃ svavakreṇa śvabhiranyaiścarandrutaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Even as I was having the vital breath reaching my throat (i.e. when my death was imminent), a dog covetous of my flesh caught hold of me by means of its jaw. It was hotly chased by the other dogs.

## \|\| 1.40.45 \|\|

*vahanmāṃ svamukhenaiva bhīto 'nyairbhaṣaṇaistathā \|*  
*gataḥ pradakṣiṇā kāraṃ viṣṇostanmandiraṃ prabho \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О lord, carrying me in hie jaw, the dog, frightened of the other dogs, went round that temple of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.40.46 \|\|

*tenaiva tuṣṭimāpanno hyantarātmā jaganmayaḥ \|*  
*mama cāpi śunaścāpi dattāvanparamaṃ padam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Lord who is identical with the universe and who is the immanent soul, became delighted with that act. He gave me and the dog the greatest of his region.

## \|\| 1.40.47 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇā kāratayā gatasyāpīdṛṃ phalam \|*  
*saṃprāptaṃ vibudhaśreṣṭha kiṃ punaḥ samyagarcanāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О leading Deva, such was the benefit for one who went in the form of a circumambulation. What then would not be attained by worshipping him properly?”

## \|\| 1.40.48 \|\|

*ityukto devarājastu sudharmeṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*manasā prītimāpanno haripūjā rato 'bhavat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus addressed by Sudharma, the noble-souled one» the king of Devas was mentally delighted. He became engaged in the worship of Hari.

## \|\| 1.40.49 \|\|

*tathāpi nirjarāḥ sarve bhārate janmalipsavaḥ \|*  
*samarcayanti deveśaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam \|*  
*tānarcayanti satataṃ brahmādyā devatāgaṇāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Still all Devas are desirous of taking birth in the Bharata land. They worship Narayana, the lord of Devas, devoid of ailments. Brahma and other groups of Devas worship them (Probably: him) for ever.

## \|\| 1.40.50 \|\|

*nārāyaṇānusmaraṇodyatānāṃ mahātmanāṃ tyaktaparigrahaṇām \|*  
*kathaṃ bhavatyugrabhavasya bandhastatsaṅgalubdhā yadi muktibhājaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. How can there be the bondage of the terrible worldly existence for those noble souls, who endeavour to remember Narayana and who have eschewed acceptance of monetary gifts even when those coveting their association attain salvation?

## \|\| 1.40.51 \|\|

*ye mānavāḥ pratidinaṃ parimuktasaṅgā nārāyaṇaṃ garuḍavāhanamarcayanti \|*  
*te sarvapāpanikaraiḥ parito vimuktā viṣṇoḥ padaṃ śubhataraṃ pratiyānti hṛṣṭāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Those men who have eschewed contact with worldly affairs and worship the Garuda-vehicled Narayana every day, are liberated from all sins and delightfully attain the auspicious region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.40.52 \|\|

*ye mānavā vigatarāgaparāvarajñā nārāyaṇaṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ smaranti \|*  
*dhyānena tena hatakilbiṣacetanāste mātuḥ payodhararasaṃ na punaḥ pibanti \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Those men who are devoid of passionate attachment, those who know the greater and the smaller entities, and those who always remember Narayana, the preceptor of the gods, get their sins quelled through meditation. Having died once, they do not imbibe again the tasty juice from the breasts of their mothers, i.e. they are not born again.

## \|\| 1.40.53 \|\|

*ye mānavā harikathāśravaṇāstadoṣāḥ kṛṣṇāṅghrapadmabhajane ratacetanāśca \|*  
*te vā puṃnati ca jaganti śarīrasaṃgāt saṃbhāṣaṇādapi tato harireva pūjyaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Those men whose blemishes have been dispelled through listening to the stories of Hari, those whose minds are engaged in worshipping the lotus-like feet of Krsna, sanctify the worlds through the contact of their bodies or through their talks. Hence, it is Hari alone who is to be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.40.54 \|\|

*haripūjāparā yatra mahāntaḥ śuddhabuddhayaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva sakalaṃ bhadraṃ yathā nimne jalaṃ dvija \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О Brahmana, even as it is true that water flows, down and remains at a lower level, so ako all welfare and happiness stay gathered together only where there are great men who are devoted to the worship of Hari and who possess pure intellects.

## \|\| 1.40.55 \|\|

*harireva paro bandhurharireva parā gatiḥ \|*  
*harireva tataḥ pūjyo yataścetanyakāraṇam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Hari alone is the greatest and the closest kinsman. Hari alone is the highest goal. Therefore, Hari alone should be worshipped since he is the cause of sentience.

## \|\| 1.40.56 \|\|

*svargāpavargaphaladaṃ sadānandaṃ nirāmayam \|*  
*pṛjyasya muniśreṣṭha paraṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. О leading sage, worship the deity of perpetual bliss, the bestower of heavenly benefits and salvation, the deity free from ailments. Great happiness and welfare will befall you.

## \|\| 1.40.57 \|\|

*pūjayanti hariṃ ye tu niṣkāmāḥ śuddhamānasāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā sarvānkāmān prayacchati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Lord Visnu becomes delighted with those people ton arcayanU is probably a misprint for tam arcayanti as god Visnu alone is meant, who becoming devoid of lust and desires worship him with purity of mind and he grants them all their desires (desired objects).

## \|\| 1.40.58 \|\|

*yastvetacchṛṇuyādvāpi paṭhedvā susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnotyaśvamedhasya phalaṃ munivarottama \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. О the best one among prominent sages, he who listens to this or reads this with great attention, attains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.40.59 \|\|

*ityetatte samākhyātaṃ haripūjāphalaṃ dvija \|*  
*saṃkocavistarābhyāṃ tu kimanyatkathayāmi te \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О Brahmana, thus the benefit of the worship of Hari has been recounted to you partly in detail and partly in brief. What else shall I recount to you?”

## Chapter 41. The Glory of the Lord's Name

## \|\| 1.41.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*ākhyātaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ mune tattvārtha kovida \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi yugānāṃ sthitilakṣaṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. О sage, expert in the interpretation of principles, everything has been narrated by you. Now, I wish to hear the situation and the characteristics of different Yugas.

## \|\| 1.41.2 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*sādhu sādhu mahāprājña mune lokopakāraka \|*  
*yugadharmānprabakṣyāmi sarvalokopakārakān \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

2\. Well done, О sage, well done, О highly intelligent one who render service to the worlds, I shall explain the Yuga- Dharmas (the specific righteous activities in different Yugas) helping all worlds.

## \|\| 1.41.3 \|\|

*dharmo vivṛddhimāyāti kāle kasmiṃściduttama \|*  
*tathā vināsamāyāti dharṃma eva mahītale \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О excellent one, on certain occasions, Dharma flourishingly) increases and on other occasions Dharma undergoes destruction on the surface of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.41.4 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti caturyugam \|*  
*divyairdvādaśabhirjñeyaṃ vatsaraistatra sattama \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There are four Yugas, viz. Krta,Treta, Dvapara and Kali. О excellent one, it should be known that all together they consist of twelve thousand divine years.

## \|\| 1.41.5 \|\|

*saṃdhyāsandhyāṃśayuktāni yugāni sadṛśāni vai \|*  
*kālato veditavyāni ityuktaṃ tattvā darśibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All these Yugas, fully consisting of Sandhyas (intermediary period) and Sandhyamsas (such subsidiary periods) are equal in every cycle. They must be known as extending to the same period. So it has been mentioned by the seers of the true principles.

## \|\| 1.41.6 \|\|

*ādye kṛtayugaṃ prāhustatastretāvidhānakam \|*  
*tataśca dvāparaṃ prāhuḥ kalimantyaṃ viduḥ kramāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They call the first, the Krtayuga, then comes the Treta Yuga. Then they say is the Dvapara and the last one they know to be the Kali Age.

## \|\| 1.41.7 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*nāsankṛtayuge vipra sarve devasamāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О Brahmana, there were no separate Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Raksasas and the serpents in Krtayuga All were remembered as equal to Devas.

## \|\| 1.41.8 \|\|

*sarve hṛṣṭāśca dharmiṣṭā na tatra krayavikrayau \|*  
*vedānāṃ ca vibhāgaśca na yuge kṛtasaṃjñake \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All were always full of’delight and righteousness. There was neither buying nor selling. There was no classification of the Vedas in the Krtayuga.

## \|\| 1.41.9 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāḥ svācāratatparāḥ \|*  
*sadā nārāyaṇaparāstapodhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Brahmanas, the Ksatriyas, the Vaisyas and the Sudras were interested in their respective duties and conduct of life. They were always engrossed in penance and meditation and werfc devoted to Narayana.

## \|\| 1.41.10 \|\|

*kāmādidoṣanirmuktāḥ śamādiguṇatatparāḥ \|*  
*dharmasādhanacittāśca gatāsūyā adāṃbhikāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They were free from lust and other defects. They were endowed with good qualities, such as aama, (selfcontrol), etc. Their minds were engaged in seeking the means of Dharma; they were devoid of envy and jealousy; they were not arrogant or hypocrites.

## \|\| 1.41.11 \|\|

*satyavākyaratāḥ sarve caturāśramadharmiṇaḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ sarvaśāstravicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All were engaged in speaking truthful words; all practised the respective holy rites of their stage in life; they were richly endowed with Vedic study and were clever in all scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.41.12 \|\|

*caturāśramayuktena karmaṇā kālayoninā \|*  
*akāmaphalasaṃyogāḥ prayānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Those who are not in communion with lustful benefits, attain the greatest goal by means of holy rites pertaining to the four Asramas (stages in life) and originating at the proper time.

## \|\| 1.41.13 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaḥ kṛtayuge śuklavarṇaḥ sunirmalaḥ \|*  
*tretādharmānpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the Krta Yuga, Narayana is of white complexion and is perfectly free from impurities. I shall declare the peculiar features of Treta. Listen with great attention.

## \|\| 1.41.14 \|\|

*dharmaḥ pāṇḍuratāṃ yāti tretāyāṃ munisattama \|*  
*haristu raktātāṃ yāti kiñcitkleśānvitā janāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О excellent sage in the Treta Yuga, Dharma assumes pale white colour. Hari attains red colour. People undergo slight sufferings.

## \|\| 1.41.15 \|\|

*kriyāyogaratāḥ sarve yajñakarmasu niṣṭitāḥ \|*  
*satyavratā dhyānaparāḥ sadādhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All are absorbed in the path of holy rites; they abide by the holy performance of Yajna; they hold steadfastly to truthfulness; they are devoted to meditation, they are always engaged in meditation.

## \|\| 1.41.16 \|\|

*dvipādo vartate dharmo dvāpare ca munīśvara \|*  
*hariḥ pītatvamāyāti vedaścāpi vibhajyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О leading sage, in the Dvapara, Dharma stands on two legs, Hari assumes yellow colour; the Vedas are classified.

## \|\| 1.41.17 \|\|

*asatyaniratāścāpi kecittatra dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇādyāśca varṇāḥ syuḥ kecidrāgādidurguṇāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At that time even some excellent Brahmanas are absorbed in untruths. Among the Brahmanas and the people of other castes, some possess the evils of passionate attachment to worldly objects.

## \|\| 1.41.18 \|\|

*kecitsvargāpavargārthaṃ viprayajñānprakurvate \|*  
*keciddhanādikāmāśca kecitkalmaṣacetasaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О Brahmana, some of them perform Yajnas for the attainment of heaven and salvation; some are desirous of wealth etc., and some have their minds affected by sin.

## \|\| 1.41.19 \|\|

*dharmādharmauṃ samau syātāṃ dvāpare viprasattama \|*  
*adharmasya prabhāveṇa kṣīyante ca prajāstathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О excellent Brahmana, in Dvapara, Dharma and Adharma are equal mutually and balanced. Due to the power of Adharma the subjects dwindle in power and glory.

## \|\| 1.41.20 \|\|

*alpāyuṣo bhaviṣyanti keciñcāpi munīśvara \|*  
*kecitpuṇyaratān dṛṣṭvā asūyāṃ vipra kurvate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О leading sage, some are short-lived. О Brahmana, on seeing some engaged in meritorious rites, some men begin to envy them.

## \|\| 1.41.21 \|\|

*kalisthitiṃ pravakṣyāmi tacchṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ \|*  
*dharmaḥ kaliyuge prāpte pādenaikena vartate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I shall describe the situation in the Kali Yuga. Listen to it with attention. At the advent of Kali Yuga, Dharma stands on one leg.

## \|\| 1.41.22-23 \|\|

*tāmasaṃ yugamāsādya hariḥ kṛṣṇatvameti ca \|*  
*yaḥ kaścidapi dharmātmā yajñācārānkaroti ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yaḥ kaścidapi puṇyātmā kriyāyogarato bhavet \|*  
*naraṃ dharmarataṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'sūyāṃ prakurvate \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Entering the Tamasic Yuga (i.e. Kali Yuga) Hari assumes blackness of complexion. Some righteous soul performs Yajnas and conventional religious routines. Some meritorious soul may be engaged in the path of holy rites. On seeing a man absorbed in Dharma, all people are afflicted with jealousy.

## \|\| 1.41.24 \|\|

*vratācārāḥ praṇaśyanti jñānayajñādayastathā \|*  
*upadravā bhaviṣyanti hyadharmasya pravatanāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Holy rites and good conduct perish. Similarly do perfect knowledge, Yajna, etc., owing to the prevalence of Adharma calamities shall befall.

## \|\| 1.41.25 \|\|

*asūyāniratāḥ sarve daṃbhācāraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*prajāścālpāyuṣaḥ sarvā bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the Kali Yuga, all people are engrossed in envy and jealousy; they are devoted to arrogant conduct of life; the subjects will be short-lived.

## \|\| 1.41.26 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*yugadharmāḥ samākhyātāstvayā saṃkṣepato mune \|*  
*kaliṃ vistarato brūhi tvaṃ hi dharmavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

26\. О sage, the characteristic features of the different Yugas have been succinctly mentioned by you. Kindly recount Kali in detail as you are the most excellent among the knowers of Dharma.

## \|\| 1.41.27 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścamunisattama \|*  
*kimāhārāḥ kimācārāḥ bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О excellent sage, what will be the diet and conduct of life of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras in the Kali Yuga?

## \|\| 1.41.28 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla sarvalokopakāraka \|*  
*kalidharmānpravakṣyāmi vistareṇa yathātatham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

28\. О leading sage rendering service to all worlds, I shall recount the characteristics of the Kali Yuga precisely and in detail.

## \|\| 1.41.29 \|\|

*sarve dharmā vinaśyanti kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvamāgate \|*  
*tasmātkalirmahāghoraḥ sarvapātakasaṃkaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When Krsna assumes black complexion all Dharmas perish. Hence, Kali is extremely terrible; it is the mixture of all sins.

## \|\| 1.41.30 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā dharmaparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge prāpte dvijā vedaparāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras are averse to righteousness. At the advent of the terrible Kali Yuga, the Brahmanas turn their faces away from the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.41.31 \|\|

*vyājadharmaratāḥ sarve asūyāniratāstathā \|*  
*vṛthāhṝṅkāraduṣṭāśca satyahīnāśca paṇḍitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. All people are engaged in the pretence of righteousness; they are engrossed in jealousy and envy. Learned men are vainglorious and wicked as well as devoid of truthfulness.

## \|\| 1.41.32 \|\|

*ahamevādhika iti sarve 'pi vivadanti ca \|*  
*adharmalolupāḥ sarvale tathā vaitaṃhikā narāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Everyone begins to argue. “I am superior to all”; all people ardently love to perform sins; all men are captious and disputatious.

## \|\| 1.41.33 \|\|

*ataḥ svalpāyuṣaḥ sarve bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge \|*  
*alpāyuṣṭvānmanuṣyāṇāṃ na vidyāgrahaṇaṃ dvija \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence, in the Kali Yuga all will be short-lived. О Brahmana, as the span of life is short, men do not grasp enough learning.

## \|\| 1.41.34 \|\|

*vidyāgrahaṇaśūnyatvādadharmo vartate punaḥ \|*  
*vyātkrameṇa prajāḥ sarvā mniyante pāpatatparāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. As the understanding of different lores diminishes, sin increases. All subjects die to the reverse order (young men die and are survived by the elders). People are engaged in sins.

## \|\| 1.41.35-36 \|\|

*brāhmaṇādyāstathā varṇāḥ saṃkīryante parasparam \|*  
*kāmakrodhaparā mūḍhā vṛthāsaṃtāpapīḍitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śūdratulyā bhaviṣyanti sarve varṇā kalau yuge \|*  
*uttamā nīcatāṃ yānti nīcāścottamatāṃ tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The Brahmanas and other castes get mixed with other castes mutually; all castes will be more or less like the Sudras, overwhelmed by lust and fury, confounded and afflicted by unnecessary distress. In the Kali Yuga the excellent men become mean and the base men rise to excellence.

## \|\| 1.41.37 \|\|

*rājano dravyaniratāstathā hyanyāyavarttinaḥ \|*  
*pīḍayanti prajāścaiva karairatyarthayojitaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The kings are greedily absorbed in wealth; they are tyrannous; imposing heavy taxes they inflict pain on their subjects.

## \|\| 1.41.38 \|\|

*śavavāhābhaviṣyanti śūdrāṇāṃ ca dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*dharmastrīṣvapi gacchanti patayo jāradharmiṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Brahmanas become the pall-bearers of the Sudras; husbands approach their legally wedded wives in the manner of paramours.

## \|\| 1.41.39 \|\|

*dviṣanti pitaraṃ putrā bhartāraṃ ca striyo 'khilāḥ \|*  
*paristrīnirataḥ sarve paradravyaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Sons hate fathers; women begin to hate their husbands; men are enamoured of other men’s wives; people misappropriate other men’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.41.40 \|\|

*matsyāmiṣeṇa jīvanti duhṝntaścāpyajīvikām \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge vipra sarve pāparatā janāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О Brahmana, in the terrible Kali Yuga, the people are engaged in sins; they maintain themselves by means of fish and flesh; they milk even goats and sheep (Reading Ajavikam not Ajivikam).

## \|\| 1.41.41 \|\|

*satāmasūyāniratāṃ upahāsaṃ prakurvate \|*  
*sarittīreṣu kuddālairvāpayiṣyanti cauṣadhīḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those wht are jealous begin to ridicule good men; on the banks of rivers they dig with hoes and spades and grow medicinal herbs. (?)

## \|\| 1.41.42 \|\|

*pṛthvī niṣphalatāṃ yāti bījaṃ puṣpaṃ vinaśyati \|*  
*veśyālāvaṃyaśīleṣu spṛhā kurvanti yoṣitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The Earth loses its fertileness (lit. fruitfulness). The seed and the flower perish; women desire to imitate the make-up and the coquetry of prostitutes.

## \|\| 1.41.43 \|\|

*dharmavikrayiṇo viprāḥ striyaśca bhagavikrayāḥ \|*  
*vedavikrayakāścānye śūdrācāraratā dvijāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Brahmanas sell their Dharmas, women resort to orosti- tution; others sell the Vedas; Brahmanas are absorbed in the conduct of life of the Sudras.

## \|\| 1.41.44 \|\|

*sādhūnāṃ vidhavānāṃ ca vittānya paharanti ca \|*  
*na vratāni cariṣyanti brāhmaṇā dravyalolupāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Brahmanas (priests), greedy for money, take away the wealth of good men and pious widows, but do not perform.the holy observances.

## \|\| 1.41.45 \|\|

*dharmācāraṃ parityajya vṛthāvādairviṣajjitāḥ \|*  
*dvijāḥ kurvanti daṃbhārthaṃ pitṛśrāddhādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Brahmanas abandon righteous conduct; they are well-equipped with modes of unnecessary arguments; it is mostly out of religious hypocrisy that they perform such rites; as the Sraddha, etc., for the Pitrs.

## \|\| 1.41.46 \|\|

*apātreṣveva dānāni prayacchanti narādhamāḥ \|*  
*dugdhalobhanimittena goṣu prītiṃ ca kurvate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Base men give charitable gifts to the undeserving persons; covetous of the milk, they (pretend) to love cows.

## \|\| 1.41.47-48 \|\|

*na kurvanti tathā viprāḥ snānaśaucādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*apātreṣveva dānāni prayacchanti narādhamāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sādhunindāparāścaiva vipranindāparāstathā \|*  
*na kasyāpi mano vipra viṣṇubhaktiparaṃ bhavet \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Brahmanas do not perform ablutions and other purificatory rites properly. The vilest Brahmanas become absorbed in holy rites at the improper time. They are engaged in blaming good men and the Brahmanas. О Brahmana, the mind of none becomes devoted to Visnu.

## \|\| 1.41.49 \|\|

*yajvinaśca dvijānaiva dhanārtharājakiṅkarāḥ \|*  
*tāḍayanti dvijānduṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvamāgate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When Krsna assumes the dark colour the wicked servants of the king begin to beat Brahmanas who perform Yajnas. They do so for extorting money out of them.

## \|\| 1.41.50 \|\|

*dānahīnā narāḥ sarve ghore kaliyuge mune \|*  
*pratigrahaṃ prakurvanti patitānāmapi dvijāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О sage, in the terrible Kali Yuga, men are devoid of (i.e. abstain from giving) charitable gifts. Brahmanas accept monetary gifts even from fallen men.

## \|\| 1.41.51 \|\|

*kaleḥ prathamapāde 'pi viṃnindanti hariṃ narāḥ \|*  
*yugānte ca harernāma naivakaścidvadiṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even in the first quarter of Kali Yuga, men begin to- censure Hari; towards the end of the Yuga none will repeat the name of Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.52 \|\|

*śūdrastrīsaṃganiratā vidhavāsaṃgalolupāḥ \|*  
*śūdrānnabhoganiratā bhaviṣyanti kalau dvijāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the Kali Yuga, Brahmanas will be indulging in sexual intercourse with Sudra women. They will be craving for union with widows; they will be engaged in the enjoyment of the cooked food of the Sudras.

## \|\| 1.41.53 \|\|

*vihāya vedasanmārgaṃ kupathācārasaṃgatāḥ \|*  
*pāṣaṇḍāścabhaviśaṣyanticaturāśramanindakāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Giving up the good Vedic path, they will be pursuing evil ways and manners. They will become heretics and censure the system of the four Asramas (stages in life).

## \|\| 1.41.54 \|\|

*na cadvijā tiśuśrūṣāṃ kurvanti caraṇodbhavāḥ \|*  
*dvijātidharmāngṛhṇanti pākhaṇḍaliṅgino 'dhamāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Sudras will not serve the twice-born. Assuming the airs of heretics, the base-born assume and practice holy rites of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.41.55 \|\|

*kāṣāyaparivītāśca jaṭilā bhasmadhūlitāḥ \|*  
*śūdrādharmānpravakṣyantī kūṭayuktaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Sudras will clothe themselves in ochre-robes; they will have matted hair; they will smear ashes all over their bodies. Thus equipped and employing deceptive arguments, they will begin to expatiate on Dharma.

## \|\| 1.41.56 \|\|

*dvijāḥsvācāramutḥsṛjyacaparapākānnabhojinaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyantidurātmānaḥ śūdrāḥ pravrajitāstathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The Brahmanas will give up their conventional activities and duties and will partake of other’s cooked food; wicked- minded Sudras will renounce and become wandering recluses.

## \|\| 1.41.57 \|\|

*utkocajīvinastatra bhaviṣyanti kalau mune \|*  
*dharmaṭīnāstu pāṣaṇḍā kāpālā bhikṣavo 'dhamāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О sage, people will take up bribes as their means of livelihood in the Kali Yuga; heretics without piety, the mendicant Kapalikas and base men will be in plenty in the Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 1.41.58 \|\|

*dharmavidhvaṃsaśīlānāṃ dvijānāṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*śūdrā dharmānpravakṣyantihyadhiruhyottamāsanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Occupying excellent seats, Sudras will expatiate on Dharma — religious duties — to Brahmanas who habitually destroy Dharma.

## \|\| 1.41.59 \|\|

*ete cānyeca bahavo nagnaraktapaṭādikāḥ \|*  
*pāṣaṇḍāḥ pracāriṣyanti prāyo vedavidūṣakāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. These and many other heretics such as nude asceties (Digambaras), red-roled mendicants, will roam about; most of whom will be decrying the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.41.60 \|\|

*gītavāditrakuśalāḥ kṣudradharmasamāśrayāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyantikalau prāyo dharmavidhvaṃsakā narāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the Kali Yuga, the men who generally destroy Dharma will be adept in singing and playing on musical instrument; they will resort to petty and insignificant holy rites.

## \|\| 1.41.61 \|\|

*alpadravyā vṛthāliṅgā vṛthāhṝṅkāradūṣitāḥ \|*  
*hartāraṃ paravittānāṃ bhavitāro narādhamāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. People will be extremely vile. They themselves not possessing much wealth but defiled by vain-gloriousness will be exhibiting for nothing a false show of symbols of piety.

## \|\| 1.41.62 \|\|

*pratigrahaparā nityaṃ jagadunmārgaśīlinaḥ \|*  
*ātmastutiparāḥ sarve paranindāparāstathā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They are always dependent on monetary gifts; they practise treading the wrong path in the world; all of them are fond of boasting about themselves and decrying others.

## \|\| 1.41.63 \|\|

*viśvastaghātinaḥ krūrā dayādharmavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyanti narā vipra kalau cādharmabāndhavāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О Brahmana, in the Kali Yuga, men will be cruel, treacherous, merciless and devoid of piety; they will be the kinsmen of the sinning ones.

## \|\| 1.41.64 \|\|

*paramāyuśca bhavitā tadā varṣāṇi ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge vipra pañcavarṣā prasūyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then the maximum expectation of life will be sixteen years. О Brahmana, in the terrible Kali Yuga, a girl of five years will give birth to children.

## \|\| 1.41.65 \|\|

*saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāśca yuvāno 'taḥ pare jarā \|*  
*svakarmatyāginaḥ sarve kṛtaghnābhinnavṛttayaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Men of seven or eight years will be the so-called youths and beyond that age is old age. All will abandon their holy duties. They will be ungrateful and breakers of codes of discipline in the society.

## \|\| 1.41.66 \|\|

*yācakāścadvijā nityaṃ bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge \|*  
*parāvamānaniratāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paraveśmani \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In the Kali Yuga, the Brahmanas will always be beggars. They will not mind being disrespected by others. They will be delighted to stay in other men’s houses.

## \|\| 1.41.67 \|\|

*tatraiva nindāniratā vṛthāviśraṃbhiṇo janāḥ \|*  
*nidāṃ kurvanti satataṃ pitṛmātṛsuteṣu ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. There itself, they will entertain vain faith and will be engaged in censuring. They will be censuring in the presence of their fathers, mothers and sons.

## \|\| 1.41.68 \|\|

*vadanti vācā dharmāṃśca cetasā pāpalolupāḥ \|*  
*dhanavidyāvayomattāḥ sarvaduḥkhaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. They will be expatiating verbally on Dharmas but in their heart of heart, they will be indulging in sins. They will be proud due to their wealth, learning or age; they will be experiencing all miseries.

## \|\| 1.41.69 \|\|

*vyādhitaskaradurbhikṣaiḥ pīḍitā atimāṃyinaḥ \|*  
*prapuṣyanti vṛthaivāmī na vicārya ca duṣkṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They will be afflicted by sickness, famine and robbers. Without minding the sinful nature of the act, they will be employing deceptive means and nourishing (their dependents) for nothing.

## \|\| 1.41.70 \|\|

*dharmamārgapraṇetāraṃ tiraskurvanti pāpinaḥ \|*  
*dharmakārye rataṃ caiva vṛthāviśraṃbhiṇo janāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Sinners slight and dishonour the person who points out the righteous path. Those who are vainly self-complacent disrespect one who is engaged in holy rites.

## \|\| 1.41.71 \|\|

*bhaviṣyanti kalau prāpte rājāno mlecchajātayaḥ \|*  
*śūdrā bhaikṣyaratāścaiva teṣāṃ śuśrūṣaṇe dvijāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After the advent of the Kali age, Sudras and outcastes will become kings and the Brahmanas will be engaged in rendering service to them. They will be begging for alms.

## \|\| 1.41.72 \|\|

*na śiṣyo na guruḥ kaścinna putro lana pitā tathā \|*  
*na bhāryā na patiścaiva bhavitāro 'tra saṃkare \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. No one will be the true disciple, preceptor, son, father, wife or husband in this confused mixture of castes.

## \|\| 1.41.73 \|\|

*kalau gate bhaviṣyanti dhanāḍhyā api yācakāḥ \|*  
*rasa vikrayiṇaścāpi bhaviṣyanti dvijātayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. When Kali Yuga advances, even rich persons will become beggars. The twice-born will be selling liquid beverages.

## \|\| 1.41.74 \|\|

*dharmakañcukasaṃvītā muniveṣadharā dvijāḥ \|*  
*apaṇyavikrayaratā agamyāgāminastathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The Brahmanas will be covered with their cloak of piety. They will be assuming the guise of sages. They will be engaged in selling forbidden goods and indulging in sexual contacts with forbidden women.

## \|\| 1.41.75 \|\|

*vedanindāparāścaiva dharmaśāstravinindukāḥ \|*  
*śūdravṛttyaiva jīvanti narakārhā dvijā mune \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. О sage, the Brahmanas who desire to be thrown into hell will maintain themselves through the activities befitting Sudras; they will invariably hate the Vedas and the Dharma Sastras.

## \|\| 1.41.76 \|\|

*anāvṛṣṭabhayaṃ prāptā gaganāsaktadṛṣṭayaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyanti kalau martyāsarve kṣudbhayakātarāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In the Kali Yuga, men will be terribly afraid of hunger. Frightened of drought, they will be continuously gazing at the sky.

## \|\| 1.41.77 \|\|

*kandaparṇaphalāhārāstāpaṃsā iva mānavāḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ tārayiṣyanti anāvṛṣṭyātidukhitāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Extremely distressed by absence of rain, men will somehow sustain themselves by eating bulbous roots, leaves and fruits like the ascetics.

## \|\| 1.41.78 \|\|

*kāmārtā hrasvadehāśca lubdhā ścādharmatatparāḥ \|*  
*kalau sarve bhaviṣyanti svalpabhāgyā bahuprajāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. In the Kali age, all the people will be distressed through lust, greed and be engaged in sinful activities. They will be short in stature, deficient in good luck and prolific in their progeny.

## \|\| 1.41.79 \|\|

*striyaḥ svapoṣaṇaparā veśyā lāvaṇyaśīlikāḥ \|*  
*pativākyamanādṛtya sadānyagṛhatatparāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Women will be self-supporting. They will be using the beauty aids like prostitutes; they will disobey their husbands’ behests and will be interested in staying in other people’s houses.

## \|\| 1.41.80 \|\|

*duḥśīlā duṣṭaśīleṣu kariṣyinti sadā spṛhām \|*  
*asadvṛttā bhaviṣyanti puruṣeṣu kulāṅganāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Women of wicked nature entertain a lustful design for men of wicked nature. Even women of noble families will be unfaithful to their husbands through evil activities.

## \|\| 1.41.81 \|\|

*caurādibhayabhītāśca kāṣṭayantrāṇi kurvate \|*  
*durbhikṣakarapīḍābhiratīvopadrutā janāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Being panick-stricken with the fear of robbers, etc., people will adopt wooden-contrivances as a security measure. People will be extremely harassed by droughts and overtaxation.

## \|\| 1.41.82 \|\|

*godhūmānnayavānnāḍhye deśe yāsyanti duḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*nidhāya hṛdyakarmaṇi prerayanti vacaḥ śubham \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Being distressed, they will be going to such lands as are full of wheat and barley. Offering the people pleasing tasks, they urge them with auspicious pleasing words (?)

## \|\| 1.41.83 \|\|

*svakāryasiddhiparyantaṃ bandhutāṃ kurvate janāḥ \|*  
*bhikṣavaścāva mitrādisnehasaṃbandhayantritāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. People will maintain fraternal relationships till their purpose is achieved. Even mendicants are restrained by friendly relationships.

## \|\| 1.41.84 \|\|

*annopādhinimittena śiṣyāngṛhṇanti bhikṣavaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. With food as a conditioning factor, disciples will be taken by mendicants.

## \|\| 1.41.85 \|\|

*ubhābhyāmatha pāṇibhyāṃ śiraḥkaṇḍūyanaṃ striyaḥ \|*  
*kurvantyo gurubhartṛāṇāmājñāmullaṅghayanti ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

85 Women scratch their heads with their hands and disobey the behests of their husbands and other elders.

## \|\| 1.41.86 \|\|

*pāṣaṇḍālāpaniratāḥ pāṣaṇḍajanasaṃginaḥ \|*  
*yadā dvijā bhaviṣyanti tadā vṛddhiṃ kalirvrajet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. When Brahmanas become absorbed in talks on heresy, when they cultivate the company of heretics, the age of Kali will be advancing.

## \|\| 1.41.87 \|\|

*yadā prajā na yakṣyanti na hoṣyanti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*tadaiva tu kalervṛddhiranumeyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. That the Kali Yuga has advanced should be inferred by clever people at the very same time when people cease to perform Yajnas and the twice-born do not perform Ноmа rites.

## \|\| 1.41.88 \|\|

*adharmavṛddhirbhavitā bāsamṛtyurapi dvijā \|*  
*sarvadharmeṣu naṣṭeṣu yāti niḥśrīkatāṃ jagat \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. When the Dharmas perish, the whole universe becomes inglorious; infant-mortality is bound to occur and there will be growth of Adharma (absence of virtue), О Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.89 \|\|

*evaṃ kaleḥ svarūpaṃ te kathitaṃ viprasattama \|*  
*haribhaktiparāneṣa na kalirbādhate kvacit \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Thus, О excellent Brahmana, the general features of Kali have been narrated to you. But nowhere does the dark age of Kali affect those people who are devoted to Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.90 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyuge tretāyāṃ dhyānameva ca \|*  
*dvāpare yajñamevāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Tapas (penance) is the greatest thing in the Krta Yuga. Dhyana (meditation) in the Treta Yuga, and Yajna in the Dvapara. They say that Dana (charitable gift) alone is the greatest in the Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 1.41.91 \|\|

*yatkṛte daśabhirvarṣaistretāyāṃ śaradā ca yat \|*  
*dvāpare yañca māsena hyahorātreṇa tatkalau \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. What is acquired in Krta in ten years, in the Treta in a year, and in the Dvapara in a month, is acquired in the course of a day and a night in the Kali age.

## \|\| 1.41.92 \|\|

*dhyāyankṛte jayanyajñaistretāyāṃ dvāparer'cayan \|*  
*yadāpnoti tadāpnoti kalau saṃkīrtya keśavam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. What one achieves by meditating in the Krta Yuga, by performing Yajnas in the Tretd and by worshipping in the Dvapara, one obtains in the Kali Yuga by repeating the name and glorifying Kesava.

## \|\| 1.41.93 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ harernāma kīrtayanti ca ye narāḥ \|*  
*kurvanti haripūjāṃ vā na kalirbādhate ca tān \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Kali does not oppress those persons who perform the worship of Hari or who repeat his names and glorify Hari day and night.

## \|\| 1.41.94 \|\|

*namo nārāyaṇāyeti kīrtayanti ca ye narāḥ \|*  
*niṣkāmā vā sakāmā vā na kalirbādhate ca tān \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Kali does not affect those men who with or without desire for the fruits there-of glorify the deity saying “Obeisance to Narayana.”

## \|\| 1.41.95 \|\|

*harināmaparā ye tu ghore kaliyuge dvija \|*  
*ta eva kṛtakṛtyāśca na kalirbādhate hi tān \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. О Brahmana, in the terrible Kali Yuga, only those are contented and blessed, those who are absorbed in the names of Hari. Kali does not harass them.

## \|\| 1.41.96 \|\|

*haripūjāparā ye ca harināmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*ta eva śivatulyāśca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Those who are engaged in the worship of Hari, and are devoted to the repetition of the names of Hari, are equal to Siva. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.41.97 \|\|

*samastajagadādhāraṃ paramārthasvarupiṇam \|*
