*ghore kaliyuge prāpte viṣṇuṃ dhyāyanna sīdati \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. After the advent of the terrible Kali Yuga, if one meditates on Visnu whose form is real and who is the support of the entire universe, one does not go to ruin or distress.

## \|\| 1.41.98 \|\|

*aho ati subhāgyāste sakṛdvai keśavārcakāḥ \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge prāpte sarvadharmavivarjite \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. After the advent of the terrible Kali age that is devoid of all virtue, those who worship Kesava even once, are extremely fortunate.

## \|\| 1.41.99 \|\|

*nyūnātiriktadoṣāṇāṃ kalau vedoktakarmaṇām \|*  
*harismaraṇamevātra saṃpūrṇatvavidhāyakam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. In the Kali age, the holy rites enjoined in the Vedas are likely to be defiled by deficiency or superfluity. Only the remembrance of Hari is conducive to the perfection or completion of the same.

## \|\| 1.41.100 \|\|

*hare keśava govinda vāsudeva jaganmaya \|*  
*itīrayanti ye nityaṃ nahi tānbādhate kaliḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Kali does not harass those who always utter the names of Visnu, thus — “O Hari О Kesava, О Govinda, О Vasudeva, the embodiment of the universe.”®

## \|\| 1.41.101 \|\|

*śiva śaṅkara rudreśa nīlakaṇṭha trilocana \|*  
*iti jalpanti ye vāpi kalistānnāpi bādhate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Kali does not harass even those who utter the names of Siva, thus — “O Siva, О Sankara, О Rudra, О Isa, О bluenecked one, О Three-eyed God!”

## \|\| 1.41.102 \|\|

*mahādeva virūpākṣa gaṅgādhara mṛḍāvyaya \|*  
*itthaṃ vadanti ye vipra te kṛtārthā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. О Brahmana, those who speak or utter the names of God thus “O Mahadeva (O great God), О Virupaksa (three-eyed one), О Gangadhara (the bearer of the Ganga on the head), О immutable Mrda”, have undoubtedly their objects achieved and are happy.

## \|\| 1.41.103 \|\|

*janārdana jagannāta pītāṃbaradharācyuta \|*  
*iti vāpyuñcarantīha na ca teṣāṃ kalerbhayam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Or, those who utter the name of the Lord, thus: “O Janardana, О Jagannatha, О yellow-robed Acyuta,” need not be afraid of Kali.

## \|\| 1.41.104 \|\|

*saṃsāre sulabhāḥ puṃsāṃ putradāradhanādayaḥ \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge vipra haribhaktastu durlabhā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. О Brahmana, in this world, sons, wives, riches and other things are easily accessible to men. But devotion to Hari is difficult to get.

## \|\| 1.41.105 \|\|

*karmaśraddhāvihīnā ye pāṣaṇḍā vedanindakāḥ \|*  
*adharmaniratā naiva narakārhā harismṛteḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Those who are devoid of faith in holy rites, those who are heretics and censure the Vedas and those who are engaged in Adharma (sinful activities) do not desire hell, should they remember Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.106 \|\|

*vedamārgabahiṣṭānāṃ janānāṃ pāpakarmaṇām \|*  
*manaḥ śuddhivihīnānāṃ harināmnaiva niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. It is only through the repetition of the names of Hari that redemp i is attained by the people who commit sins, who are beyond the pale of Vedic path and who are wanting in mental purity.

## \|\| 1.41.107 \|\|

*daivādhīnaṃ jagatsarvamidaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*yathāpreritametena tathaiva kuruteṃ dvija \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. О Brahmana, this entire universe is submissive to Daiva (fate, destiny). The mobile and immobile beings do only as they are directed by this destiny.

## \|\| 1.41.108 \|\|

*śaktitaḥ sarvakarmāṇi vedoktāni vidhāya ca \|*  
*samarpayenmahāviṣṇau nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. After performing according to one’s capacity all the holy rites prescribed in the Vedas, a person devoted to God Narayana should dedicate them to Lord Mahavisnu.

## \|\| 1.41.109 \|\|

*samarpitāni karmāṇi mahaviṣṇau parātmani \|*  
*saṃpūrṇatāṃ prayāntyeva harismaraṇamātrataḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Holy rites dedicated to Mahavisnu, the Supreme Atman, become complete merely by the remembrance of Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.110 \|\|

*haribhaktiratānāṃ ca pāpabandho na jāyate \|*  
*ato 'tidurlabhā loke haribhaktirdurātmanām \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Sins do not bind those who are engaged in devotion to Hari. Hence, devotion to Hari is difficult to be attained by the wicked-minded in the world.

## \|\| 1.41.111 \|\|

*aho hariparā ye tu kalau ghore bhayaṅkare \|*  
*te subhāgyā mahātmānaḥ satsaṃgara hitā api \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. О! In the frightful and terrific Kali Yuga, those who are devoted to Hari are very fortunate and noble-souled even if they are not in close contact with saintly persons.

## \|\| 1.41.112 \|\|

*harismaraṇaniṣṭānāṃ śivanāmaratātmanām \|*  
*satyaṃ samastakarmāṇi yānti saṃpūrṇatāṃ dvija \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. О Brahmana, it is true that all the holy rites of those who are engrossed in the remembrance of Hari and those who are absorbed in the repetition of Siva's names attain perfect completion.

## \|\| 1.41.113 \|\|

*aho bhāgyamaho bhāgyaṃ harināma ratātmanām \|*  
*tridarśerapi te pūjyāḥ kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. О how fortunate are those who are engaged in the names of Hari! What a good luck! They are worthy of being worshipped even by Devas. Of what use is much talk?

## \|\| 1.41.114 \|\|

*tasmātsamastalokānāṃ hitameva mayocyate \|*  
*harināmaparānmartyānna kalirbādhartakvacit \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Hence, only what is beneficial to the worlds, is being proclaimed by me. Nowhere does Kali harass those men who are fond of the names of Hari.

## \|\| 1.41.115 \|\|

*harernāmaiva nāmaiva nāmaiva mama jīvanam \|*  
*kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. My very life is only the name of Hari, only that name and nothing but that name. I emphatically declare that in the Kali Yuga salvation is never possible otherwise, not at all."

## \|\| 1.41.116 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evaṃ sa nārado viprāḥ sanakena prabodhitaḥ \|*  
*parāṃ nirvṛttimāpannaḥ punaretaduvāca ha \|\| 116 \|\|*

*Suta said:*

116\. О Brahmana, thus enlightened by Sanaka, Narada attained great delight. He again submitted thus: —

## \|\| 1.41.117 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavansarvaśāstrajña svayātikaruṇātmanā \|*  
*prakāśitaṃ jagajjyotiḥ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|\| 117 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

117\. О holy lord, О knower of all scriptural texts, the splendour of the universe, the great eternal Brahman has been revealed by you who are extremely merciful at heart.

## \|\| 1.41.118 \|\|

*etadeva paraṃ puṇyametadeva paraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ smaretpuṇḍarīkākṣaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. This is the greatest merit. This is the greatest penance that one remembers the lotus-eyed lord who destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.41.119 \|\|

*brahmannānājagañcaitadekacitsaṃprakāśitam \|*  
*tvayoktaṃ tatpratīye 'haṃ kathaṃ dṛṣṭāntamantarā \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. О Brahmana, this universe is manifold. It has been mentioned by you to have been evolved out of this knowledge alone. How can I understand it without an illustrative example?

## \|\| 1.41.120 \|\|

*tasmādyena yathā brahma pratītaṃ bodhitena tu \|*  
*tadākhyāhi yathā cittaṃ sīdatsthitimavāpnuyāt \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Hence elucidate that thing by the enlightenment of which the Brahman can be known. Tell it to me so that the depressed mind can steady itself.

## \|\| 1.41.121 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vaco viprā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sanakaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ smarannārāyaṇaṃ param \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. О Brahmana, on hearing these words of the noble- souled Narada, Sanaka remembered the great Narayana and replied thus:

## \|\| 1.41.122 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca*  
*brahmannahaṃ dhyānaparo bhaveyaṃ sanandanaṃ pṛccha yathābhilāṣam \|*  
*vedāntaśāstre kuśalastavāyaṃ nivartayedvā paramāryavandyaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*Sanaka said:*

122\. О Brahmana, I am going to perform meditation. Ask Sanandana as you please. He is an adept in the Vedanta Sustra. He is worthy of being revered and saluted by the noble. He will clear your doubts.

## \|\| 1.41.123 \|\|

*itīritaṃ samākarṇya sanakasya sa nāradaḥ \|*  
*sanandanaṃ mokṣadharmānpraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. On hearing these words uttered by Sanaka, Narada began to ask Sanandana about the Moksa Dharmas i.e. holy rites leading to salvation.

## Chapter 42. Cosmogony: The Origin of the Universe (Dialogue between Bhrigu and Bharadvaja)

## \|\| 1.42.1 \|\|

*śrīnārada uvāca*  
*kutaḥ sṛṣṭamidaṃ brahmañjagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*pralaye ca kamabhyeti tanme brūhi sanandana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada submitted:*

1\. О Brahmana, kindly narrate to me whence this universe comprised of the mobiles and immobiles was created and to whom it goes at the time of dissolution. О Sanandana!

## \|\| 1.42.2 \|\|

*sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ sabalāhakaḥ \|*  
*sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavano loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By whom was this world created along with the oceans, the sky, the mountains, the clouds, the earth, the fire and the wind?

## \|\| 1.42.3 \|\|

*kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ \|*  
*śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmavidhiḥ katham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How were the Bhutas (Elements or living beings) created? How were the different castes divided? What is the arrangement for their purity? How do they get impurities? What are their rules regarding Dharma and Adharma?

## \|\| 1.42.4 \|\|

*kīdṛśo jīvatāṃ jīvaḥ kva vā gacchanti ye mṛtāḥ \|*  
*asmāllokādamuṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ śaṃsatu me bhavān \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Of what nature is the soul of the living individuals? Where do those who die go? May your honour recount every- thing from this world to the other.

## \|\| 1.42.5 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi cetihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*bhṛguṇābhihitaṃ śāstraṃ bharadvājāya pṛcchate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*Sanandana replied:*

5\. О Narada, listen. I shall tell you this ancient mythological anecdote, the scripture narrated by the sage Bhrigu to Bharadvaja who enquired of him about this.

## \|\| 1.42.6 \|\|

*kailāsaśikhare dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānaṃ mahaujasam \|*  
*bhṛgumaharṣimāsīnaṃ bharadvājo 'nvapṛcchata \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing the brilliant great sage Bhrigu, of enormous prowess, seated on the top of mount Kailasa, Sage Bharadvaja enqi ired of him.

## \|\| 1.42.7 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*kathaṃ jīvo vicarati nānāyoniṣu saṃtatam \|*  
*kathaṃ muktiśca saṃsārājjāyate tasya mānada \|\| 7 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*

7\. О bestower of honour, how does the individual soul continuously transmigrate into the different forms of life (existence)? How is its liberation from the cycle of worldly existence effected?

## \|\| 1.42.8 \|\|

*yaśca nārāyaṇaḥ sraṣṭā svayaṃbhūrbhagavansvayam \|*  
*sevyasevakabhāvena vartete iti tau sadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. (How is it) О revered sir, that he who is Lord Narayana himself and god Brahma, the self-born creator, always conduct themselves (as if) in the master-servant relationship?

## \|\| 1.42.9 \|\|

*praviśanti laye sarve yamīśaṃ sacarācarāḥ \|*  
*lokānāṃ ramaṇaḥ so 'yaṃ nirguṇaśca nirañjanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. How is it that the controller of universe in whom all the mobile and immobile beings enter at the time of dissolution (of the universe), is (as a matter of fact) devoid of all attributes and untinged (by anything)?

## \|\| 1.42.10-15 \|\|

*anīrdaśyo 'pratarkyaśca kathaṃ jñāyeta kairmune \|*  
*kathamenaṃ parātmānaṃ kālaśaktiduranvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*atarkyacaritaṃ vedāḥ stuvanti kathamādarāt \|*  
*jīvo jīvatvamullaṅghya kathaṃ brahma samanvayāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tanme brūhi kṛpānirgha \|*  
*evaṃ sa bhagavānpṛṣṭo bharadvājena saṃśayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*maharṣirbrahmasaṃkāśaḥ sarvaṃ tasmai tato 'bravīt \|*  
*bhṛguruvāca*  
*mānaso nāma yaḥ pūrvo viśruto ve maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*anādinidhano devastathā tebhyo 'jarāmaraḥ \|*  
*avyakta iti vikhyātaḥ śāśvato 'thākṣayo 'vyayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yataḥ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni jāyante ca mriyanti ca \|*  
*so 'mṛjatprathamaṃ devo mahāntaṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-12a. How and by whom can he who cannot be specifically particularised and reasoned about, be realized? How do the Vedas respectfully eulogise this great Atman, who cannot be pursued by Kala (time) and Sakti and whose conduct is beyond comprehension? How does the individual soul transcend his Jivatva — (the state of being the individual soul) and merge unto the Brahman? О store-house of mercy, I wish to hear this. Kindly narrate it to me (in details).”

12b-13a. When the venerable one was thus asked about his problem by Bharadvaja, the great sage resembling Brahman (or god Brahman) thereupon explained everything to him.

*Bhrigu replied:*

13b-l5. The primeval Lord Visnu who was well known to the great sages by the designation Manasa is the god without the beginning and end, unageing and immortal. He is well known as the unmanifest, permanent, everlasting and unchanging. It is from him that the living beings are created. They are born of him and they die in him. That lord at first created the principle called Mahat (the great principle).

## \|\| 1.42.16-17 \|\|

*ākāśamiti vikhyātaṃ sarvabhūtadharaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ākāśādabhavadvāri salilādagnimārutau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*agnimārutasaṃyogāttataḥ samabhavanmahī \|*  
*tatastejo mayaṃ divyaṃ padmaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. He is the lord that supports the elements. (He created what is well known as Аkasа (ether). From Akasa originated the water and from the water, fire and wind were evolved. As a result of the contact of fire and wind, the earth was evolved. Thereafter, a brilliant lotus was created by the selfborn deity.

## \|\| 1.42.18 \|\|

*tasmātpadmātsamabhavadvrahmā vedamayo vidhiḥ \|*  
*ahṝṅkāra iti khyātaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtakṛt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. From that lotus originated Brahma, the creator who is the embodiment of the Vedas. He is well known as Ahamkara (the Cosmic Ego), the creator of other elements and the soul of them all.

## \|\| 1.42.19-22 \|\|

*brahmā vai sa mahātejā ya ete pañca dhātavaḥ \|*  
*śailāstasyāsthisaṃdhāstu medo masiṃ ca medinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*samudrāstasya rudhiramākāśamudaraṃ tathā \|*  
*pavanaścaiva niśvāsastejo 'gnirnimnagāḥ śirāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*agnīṣomau ca candrākārai nayane tasya viśrute \|*  
*nabhaścordhvaśirastasya kṣitiḥ padau bhujau diśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*durvijñeyo hyacintyātmā siddhairapi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sa eṣa bhagavānviṣṇurananta iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. That highly brilliant one was Brahma. The five elements were the five Dhatus (constituents or ingredients of the body). The mountains were his groups of bones (skeletal structure). the earth was the suet and the flesh. The oceans constituted his blood and the firmament his belly. The air (god) was his respiration. The Agni (fire) was his brilliance and the rivers were his blood vessels. Agni and Soma, the sun and the moon were well known as his eyes. The sky is the crown of his head; the earth constitutes his feet and the quarters his arms. There is no doubt about this that he is incomprehensible, and his nature is inconceivable even by the Siddhas. He is the Lord Visnu well known as Ananta (Infinite).

## \|\| 1.42.23 \|\|

*sarvabhūtātmabhūtastho durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ \|*  
*ahṝṅkārasya yaḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtabhaghavāyavai \|*  
*tataḥ samabhavadviśvaṃ pṛṣṭo 'haṃ yadiha tvayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He is stationed in all living beings as their soul. He cannot be realized by those who are not self-possessed. He is the creator of Ahamkara which is the cause of origin of all elements. Thence out of the elements was evolved the universe. And it is this that I have been asked by you.

## \|\| 1.42.24 \|\|

*bhagdvāja uvāca*  
*gaganasya diśāṃ caiva bhūtalasvānilasya ca \|*  
*kānyatra parimāṇāni saṃśayaṃ chindhi tattvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*

24\. What are the magnitudes of the sky, the quarters, the surface of the earth, and the wind? Clear this doubt precisely.

## \|\| 1.42.25 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*anantametadākāśaṃ siddhadaivatasovitam \|*  
*ramyaṃ nānāśrayākīrṇaṃ yasyāṃ to nādhigamyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*

25 Infinite is this beautiful sky inhabited by Siddhas and gods It supports (in its expanse) all the things scattered about, but its limits could not be ascertained.

## \|\| 1.42.26-27 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ gateradhastāttu candrādityau na paśyataḥ \|*  
*tatra devāḥ svayaṃ dīptā bhāskarābhāgnivarcasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*te cāpyantaṃ na paśyanti nabhasaḥ prathitaujasaḥ \|*  
*durgamatvādanantatvāditi me vada mānada \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Neither the moon nor the sun sees its end although they go up and down. Even the gods who are self-refulgent like the brilliance of the sun or the fire and whose prowess is well known, cannot perceive the end of the firmament, as it is both inaccessible and infinite, say so, О bestower of respects.

## \|\| 1.42.28 \|\|

*upariṣṭopariṣṭāttu pjvaladbhiḥ svayaṃprabhaghaiḥ \|*  
*niruddhametadākāśaṃ hyaprameyaṃ surairapi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This firmament which is over-crowded higher and higher up with highly blazing self-luminous bodies is incomprehensible even to gods.

## \|\| 1.42.29 \|\|

*prathivyante samudrāstu samudrānte tamaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*tamasoṃ'te jalaṃ prāhurjalasyānte 'gnireva ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At the extremity of the earth are the oceans. Darkness is remembered as existing at the (other) extremity of the oceans. They say that there is water at the end of that darkness and at the end of the water there is only fire.

## \|\| 1.42.30 \|\|

*rasātalānte salilaṃ jalānte pannagādhipāḥ \|*  
*tadante punarākāśamākāśānte punarjalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the extremity (bottom) of Rasatala (the netherworld) there is water, and at the (lowest) extremity of water, there are lordly serpents. At its end, there is ether again and at the end of the ether, there is water again.

## \|\| 1.42.31 \|\|

*evamantaṃ bhagavataḥ pramāṇaṃ salilasya ca \|*  
*agnimārutatoyebhyo durjñeyaṃ daivatairapi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Ending with this limit of water is the magnitude of the lord which is more incomprehensible than that of fire, wind and water even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.42.32 \|\|

*agnimārutatoyānāṃ varṇā kṣititalasya ca \|*  
*ākāśasadṛśā hyete bhidyante tattvadaśanāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The colours or nature of the fire, wind, and the surface of the earth are like those of the firmament. But they are distinguished, when the reality is viewed or realized.

## \|\| 1.42.33 \|\|

*paṭhanti caiva munayaḥ śāstreṣu vividheṣu ca \|*  
*trailokye sāgare caiva pramāṇaṃ vihitaṃ yathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sages read about it in the various scriptures as the magnitude of the three worlds and of the ocean, as has been laid down therein.

## \|\| 1.42.34 \|\|

*adṛśyo yastvagamyo yaḥ kaḥ pramāṇa mudīrayet \|*  
*siddhānāṃ devatānāṃ ca parimītā yadā gatiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. But who can tell the magnitude of what is invisible and what cannot be approached, and when the movement of Siddhas and Devas is restricted.

## \|\| 1.42.35-36 \|\|

*tadāgaṇyamanantasya nāmānanteti viśrutam \|*  
*nāmadheyānurupasya mānasasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yadā tu divyaṃ yadrūpaṃ hrasate varddhate punaḥ \|*  
*ko 'nyastadvedituṃ śakyo yo 'pi syāttadvidho 'paraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Therefore, the designation Ananta (connoting the un-accountability) of the immeasurable infinity (viz. Visnu) has become famous. When the divine form of the noble-souled Manasa (god Visnu) who is so according to his designation (Ananta), decreases or increases again, who else is able to know it? If there be any other, he must be of His nature.

## \|\| 1.42.37 \|\|

*tataḥ puṣkarataḥ saṣṭaḥ sarvajño mūrtimānprabhuḥ \|*  
*brahmā dharmamayaḥ pūrvaḥ prajāpatiranuttamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thereafter from the Puskara (the lotus) was created the embodied omniscient lord Brahma Who is Dharma incarnate, the first and the lorcmost Prajapati (Lord of Creation).

## \|\| 1.42.38 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*puṣkaro yadi saṃbhūto jyeṣṭaṃ bhavati puṣkaram \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ pūrvajaṃ cāha bhavānsaṃdeha eva me \|\| 38 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*

38\. My doubt is that if god Brahma is born of a lotus, the lotus becomes the elder (of the two). But your holiness stated that god Brahma was the first-born (in the whole of creation).

## \|\| 1.42.39-40 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*mānasasyeha yā mūrtirbrahmatvaṃ samupāgatā \|*  
*tasyāsanavidhānārthaṃ pṛthivī padmamucyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

*karṇikā tasya padmasya merurgaganamucchritaḥ \|*  
*tasya madhye sthito lokānsṛjatyeṣa jagadvidhiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*

39-40a. In order to offer a seat unto the physical form of Manasa (Visnu) that attained the state of Brahma the earth is called Padma (Lotus). The pericarp of that lotus is the Meru which is as lofty as the sky.

40b. This god Brahma, occupying a seat in its middle, creates peoples and the universe.

## \|\| 1.42.41 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ kathaṃ sa sṛjati prabhuḥ \|*  
*merumadhye sthito brahmā tadvahirdvijasattama \|\| 41 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
41\. О excellent Brahmana, kindly explain how lord Brahma seated in the middle of the Meru, creates different kinds of subjects outside the mount Meru.

## \|\| 1.42.42 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ mānaso manasāsṛjat \|*  
*saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
42\. Manasa mentally created the different subjects. In order to maintain and protect the living beings, water was created at the outset.

## \|\| 1.42.43 \|\|

*yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam \|*  
*yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ varddhante yena ca prajāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Water which is vital to all living beings was created at first. It is the very life of all beings and subjects grow and multiply thereby.

## \|\| 1.42.44 \|\|

*parityaktāśca na śyanti tenadaṃ sarvamāvṛttam \|*  
*pṛthivī parvatā meghā mūrtimantaśca ye pare \|*  
*sarvaṃ tadvāruṇaṃ jñeyamāpastastaṃbhire punaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If they are abandoned by it, they perish. The whole universe is surrounded by it. The earth, the mountains, the clouds and all other embodied beings — everything should be known as Varuna (presided over by Varuna, the deity of waters) The waters uphold and support everything.

## \|\| 1.42.45 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*kathaṃ salilamutpannaṃ kathaṃ caivāgnimārutau \|*  
*kathaṃ vā medinī sṛṣṭetyatra me saṃśayo mahān \|\| 45 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
45\. How was water produced? How were Agni (fire) and Marut (wind) created? How was the earth created? My great doubt is in this respect.

## \|\| 1.42.46 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*brahmakalpe purā brahman brahmarṣīṇāṃ samāgame \|*  
*lokasaṃbhavasaṃdehaḥ samutpanno mahātmanām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
46\. О Brahmana, in a former Kalpa of Brahma, in the assembly of Brahmanical sages, some noblc-souled (sages) had a doubt about the origin of the world.

## \|\| 1.42.47 \|\|

*te 'tiṣṭandhyānamālaṃbya maunamāsthāya niścalāḥ \|*  
*tyaktāhārāḥ sparddhamānā divyaṃ virṣaśataṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vying with one another, those Brahmanas adopted silence and set meditating. They were motionless and they forsook all food. Thus they remained for a hundred divine years.

## \|\| 1.42.48 \|\|

*teṣāṃ brahmamayī vāṇī sarveṣāṃ śrotramāgamat \|*  
*divyā sarasvatī tatra saṃbabhūva nabhastalāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A speech originating from the Brahman (or words sacred as those of the Vedas) reached the cars of all. A divine speech came out of the atmosphere.

## \|\| 1.42.49 \|\|

*purāstimitamākāśamanantamacalopamam \|*  
*naṣṭacandrārkapavanaṃ prasuptamiva saṃbabhau \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Formerly, the infinite firmament became still and unruffled like a huge mountain. As the sun, the moon and the wind were lost, it appeared as if it was sleeping.

## \|\| 1.42.50 \|\|

*tataḥ salilamutpannaṃ tamasīva tamaḥ param \|*  
*tasmāñca salilotpīḍādudatiṣṭata mārutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. From that originated water, like a thicker darkness from darkness. From the overflowing froth and foam of the water, the wind rose up.

## \|\| 1.42.51-52 \|\|

*yathābhavanamacchidraṃ niḥśabdamiva lakṣyate \|*  
*tañcābhasā pūryamāṇaṃ saśabdaṃ kurute 'nilaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tathā salilasaṃruddhe nabhasoṃ'taṃ nirantare \|*  
*bhittvārṇavatalaṃ vāyuḥ samutpatati ghoṣavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Just as an abode (or rather an empty vessel) without any outlet appears silent but when filled with water the wind makes it full of sound, so also, when the extremity of the firmament is continuously restrained by water, the roaring wind pierces through the surface of the sea and rises up.

## \|\| 1.42.53 \|\|

*eṣu vā carate vāyurarṇavotpīḍasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*ākāśasthānamāsādya praśāntiṃ nādhigacchati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The wind originating from the over-flowing froth of the ocean moves amongst those. After reaching the place of the sky it does not calm down.

## \|\| 1.42.54 \|\|

*tasminvāyvambusaṃgharṣe dīptatejā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*prādurāsīdūrdhvaśikhaḥ kṛtvā nistimiraṃ tamaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the struggle between wind and water, fire of a mighty fire of great brilliance blazed up dispelling all darkness from the sky.

## \|\| 1.42.55 \|\|

*agniḥ pavanasaṃyuktaḥ khaṃ samākṣipate jalam \|*  
*tadagnivāyusaṃparkāddhanatvamupapadyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The fire in collaboration with the wind raises water to the sky, where it assumes the form of clouds due to the contact with fire and wind.

## \|\| 1.42.56 \|\|

*tasyākāśaṃ nipatitaḥ snehāttiṣṭati yo 'paraḥ \|*  
*sa saṃghātatvamāpanno bhūmitvamanugacchati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As it goes up the sky, another part of this (i.e. water) that stays behind due to sliminess solidifies into the earth.

## \|\| 1.42.57 \|\|

*rasānāṃ sarvagandhānāṃ snehānāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā \|*  
*bhūmiryo niriyaṃ jñeyā yasyāḥ sarvaṃ prasūyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. This earth should be known as the source of origin of tastes, smells, sliminess as well as of living beings. It is from the earth that everything is delivered out.

## \|\| 1.42.58 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*ya ete dhātavaḥ pañca rakṣyā yānasṛjatprabhuḥ \|*  
*āvṛtā yairime lokā mahābhūtābhisaṃjñitaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
58\. (Defective) The five subtle, Dhatus (properties of the five elements) which the lord created (are the Gunas). These worlds are surrounded by what are termed as Mahabhutas (great elements).

## \|\| 1.42.59 \|\|

*yadāsṛjatsahasrāṇi bhūtānāṃ sa mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*paścātteṣveva bhūtatvaṃ kathaṃ samupapadyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When the highly intelligent deity created thousands of bhUtas (living beings), how does bhUtatva (the state of being an element) is begotten in them specifically afterwards (in their post-creation stage).17

## \|\| 1.42.60 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*amitāni mahāṣṭāni yānti bhūtāni saṃbhavam \|*  
*atasteṣāṃ mahābhūtaśabdo 'yamupapadyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. (Defective) Innumerable/immeasurable are the great elements (?). (From them) living beings arc created. Hence the term “great element” (mahabhuta) is suitably applicable to them.

## \|\| 1.42.61 \|\|

*ceṣṭā vāyuḥ khamākāśamūṣmāgniḥ salilaṃ dravaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivī cātra saṃghātaḥ śarīraṃ pāñcabhautikam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Our body is the aggregate of five elements since our Cesta (activity) is Akasa (ether), the heat is Agni (fire) the liquid portion is Salila (water) and the mass is Prthivi.

## \|\| 1.42.62 \|\|

*ityataḥ pañcabhiryuktairyuktaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*śrotre ghrāṇo rasaḥ sparśo dṛṣṭiścendriyasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Hence, the mobile and immobile living beings do consist of these five elements. The ears, nose, taste, touch and vision are termed Indriyas (sense-organs).

## \|\| 1.42.63 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*pañcabhiryadi bhūtaistu yuktāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ \|*  
*sthāvarāṇāṃ na dṛśyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
63\. If (you say) that the mobile and immobile beings consist of five elements (I object to it) since in the body of the immobile beings, the five Dhatus (Primary elements) are not seen.

## \|\| 1.42.64 \|\|

*anūṣmaṇāmaceṣṭānāṃ ghanānāṃ caiva tattvataḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣāṇāṃ nopalabhyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The five Dhatus arc not perceived in the body of the trees, which are devoid of heat and activity and which are actually solid in form.

## \|\| 1.42.65 \|\|

*va śṛṇvanti na paśyanti na gandharasavedinaḥ \|*  
*na ca sparśaṃ hi jānanti te kathaṃ pañca dhātavaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. They do not hear, do not see, they are not cognisant of smell and taste nor do they perceive touch. How can they consist of the five Dhatus (elementary ingredients?).

## \|\| 1.42.66 \|\|

*adravatvādanignitvādabhūmitvādavāyutaḥ \|*  
*ākāśasyāprameyatvādṛkṣāṇāṃ nāsti bhautikam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. There is no Bhautika feature (the state of being evolved out of the elements) in the trees due to their not being a liquid, not being a fire, not being the earth and not being the wind, not being akasa (the sky) as the sky is comprehensible and immeasurable.

## \|\| 1.42.67 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*ghanānāmapi vṛkṣaṇāmākāśo 'sti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṣpapalavyaktirnityaṃ samupapadyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

*Bhrigu replied:*  
67\. There is no doubt at all that though the trees are of solid nature there is ether in them. (Hence, the perpetual outcome of fruits and flowers from them comes to pass).

## \|\| 1.42.68 \|\|

*ūṣmato mlāyate parṇaṃ tvakphalaṃ puṣpameva ca \|*  
*mlāyate śīryate cāpi sparśastenātra vidyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Due to heat the leaf withers; the bark, the fruits and flowers too wi ther and decompose. Hence, there is the (sensation of) touch in them.

## \|\| 1.42.69 \|\|

*vāyyagnyaśaninirdhoṣaiḥ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ viśīryate \|*  
*śrotreṇa gṛhyate śabdastasmācchṛṇvanti pādapāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The fruits and flowers become shattered due to the loud report of thunder and the (roaring) sounds of wind and fire. The sound is heard through the ears. Hence, trees do hear.

## \|\| 1.42.70 \|\|

*vallī veṣṭayate vṛkṣānsarvataścaiva gacchati \|*  
*nahyadṛṣṭaśca mārgo 'sti tasmātpaśyanti pādapāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The creeper twines round the tree or spreads all round. The path cannot remain invisible. Hence trees can see.

## \|\| 1.42.71 \|\|

*puṇyāpuṇyaistathā gadhairdhūpaiśca vividhairapi \|*  
*arogāḥ puṣpitāḥ saṃti tasmājjighranti pādapāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Through merits and demerits and through scents and different kinds of incense, trees that are not affected by sickness, blossom. Hence, trees do smell.

## \|\| 1.42.72 \|\|

*sukhaduḥkhayorgrahaṇācchinnasya ca virohaṇāt \|*  
*jīvaṃ paśyāmi vṛkṣāṇāmacaitanyaṃ na vidyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Since there is perception of happiness and misery, since the tree if lopped off grows again, I see a soul in the trees. They are not insentient.

## \|\| 1.42.73 \|\|

*tena tajjalamādatte jarayatyagnimārutau \|*  
*āhārapariṇāmāñca snaho vṛddhiśca jāyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. (Defective) Hence, it takes up water; through fire and wind it consumes the food; as the food undergoes metabolism the growth of the tree takes place.

## \|\| 1.42.74 \|\|

*jaṅgamānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śarīre paṃñca dhātavaḥ \|*  
*pratyekaśaḥ prabhidyante yaiḥ śarīraṃ viceṣṭate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The five Dhatus (dements) are present in the body of all mobile beings. They act in diverse ways on the body whereby the body functions.

## \|\| 1.42.75 \|\|

*tvak ca māṃsaṃ tathāsthīni majjā snāyuśca pañcamaḥ \|*  
*ityetadiha saṃghātaṃ śarīre pṛthivīmaye \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The skin, the flesh, the bones, the marrow and the fifth (Dhatu) — the sinews — these constitute the earth element in the body.

## \|\| 1.42.76 \|\|

*tejo hyagnistathā krodhaścakṣuruṣmā tathaiva ca \|*  
*agnirjanayate yañca pañcāgneyāḥ śarīriṇaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The Tejas clement (energy) is the body, (the gastric) lire anger and the eyes as well as the body temperature. These five constitute the fire element in the body (the embodied being) which are created by the (element called) fire.

## \|\| 1.42.77 \|\|

*śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ tathāsyaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ koṣṭameva ca \|*  
*ākāśātprāṇināmete śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The five ether elements (i.e. the spaces) in the body of living beings are — the ears, the nostrils, the mouth, the heart and the belly.

## \|\| 1.42.78 \|\|

*śleṣmā pittamatha svedo vasā śoṇitameva ca \|*  
*ityāpaḥ pañcadhā dehe bhavanti prāṇināṃ sadā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Water elements always present in the bodies of the living beings are five, viz. — the phlegm, the bile, the sweat, the fat and the blood.

## \|\| 1.42.79-80 \|\|

*prāṇātprīṇayate prāṇī vyānāvdyāyacchate tathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*gacchatyapāno 'dhaścaiva samāno hyadyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*udānāducchvasitīti pañca (prati)bhadāñca bhāṣate \|*  
*ityete vāyavaḥ pañca veṣṭayantīhadehinam \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Five types of (organic elemental winds envelop the embodied being. It is through the Prana that the living being delights (others) (?). The Vyana is diffused throughout the body. The Apana blows downwards. Samana is stationed in the cardiac region. Through the Udana the living being breathes and through all the five types it speaks.

## \|\| 1.42.81 \|\|

*bhūmergandhaguṇānvetti rasaṃ cādūbhyaḥ śarīravān \|*  
*tasya gandhasya vakṣyāmi vistarābhihitānguṇān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The embodied being perceives the quality of smell from the earthly element and the taste from the water element in him. I shall recount in detail the quality of smell.

## \|\| 1.42.82-83 \|\|

*iṣṭaścānuṣṭagandhaśca madhuraḥ kaṭureva ca \|*  
*nirhārī saṃhataḥ snigdho rukṣo viśada eva ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

*evaṃ navavidho jñeyaḥ pārthivo gandhavistaraḥ \|*  
*jyotiḥ paśyati cakṣurbhyaḥ sparśaṃ vetti ca vāyunā \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. The smell is of nine varieties — the agreeable, the disagreeable, the sweet one, the pungent one, that which spreads wide, that which is harmonious and compact. That which is bland and mild, that which is dreamy and sullied, that which is manifestly calm. Such is the smell that pertains to the earth element. The embodied being secs the splendour through the eyes and perceives touch through the wind element.

## \|\| 1.42.84 \|\|

*śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca rasaścāpi guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*rasajñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The sound, the touch, the colour and the taste also are remembered as qualities (of water). I shall recount to you the knowledge of taste (i.e. the details of quality of taste). Listen even as I recount it.

## \|\| 1.42.85 \|\|

*raso bahuvidhaḥ prokta ṛṣibhiḥ prathitātmabhiḥ \|*  
*madhuro lavaṇastiktaḥ kaṣāyo 'mlaḥ kaṭustathā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. 86a The taste has been mentioned to be manifold by the sages of renowned souls. Sweet, saline, bitter, astringent, sour and pungent. Thus, the six types of taste are rcmembeied to be pertaining to the water clement.

## \|\| 1.42.86-91 \|\|

*eṣa ṣaḍidhavistāro raso vārimayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaśca triguṇaṃ jyotirucyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

*jyotiḥ paśyati rūpāṇi rūpaṃ ca bahudhā smṛtam \|*  
*hrasvo dīrdhastathā sthūlaścaturasro 'ṇuvṛttavān \|\| 87 \|\|*

*śuklaḥ kṛṣṇastathā rakto nīlaḥ pīto 'ruṇastathā \|*  
*kaṭhinaścikkaṇaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ picchilo mṛdu dāruṇaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*evaṃ ṣoḍaśavistāro jyotīrupaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatraikaguṇamākāśaṃ śabda ityeva tatsmṛtam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tasya śabdasya vakṣyāmi vistaraṃ vividhātmakam \|*  
*ṣaḍjo ṛṣabhagāndhārau madhyamodhaivatastathā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*pañcamaścāpi vijñeyastathā cāpi niṣādavān \|*  
*eṣa saptavidhaḥ prokto guṇa ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

86b-89a. The fiery element is said to be possessing three qualities, viz., the sound, the touch and the colour. The fiery dement perceives the colours and colours are said to be manifold (All types of features are included in the word colour — Rupa). The Rupas of the fiery clement are sixteen (?), viz. short, long, stout, symmetrical, atomic, circular, white, black, red, blue, yellow, pink, hard, smooth, delicate, slimy, soft and rough.

89b-91. The ether has only one quality, viz. the sound. I shall tell you the diverse extension (varieties) of the sound — viz- Sadja, Rsabha, Gandhara, Madhyama, Dhaivata, Pahcama and Nisada. The quality of the ether (viz. sound) is thus said to be of seven types.

## \|\| 1.42.92-95 \|\|

*aiśvaryyeṇa tu sarvatra sthito 'pi payahādiṣu \|*  
*mṛdaṅgabherīśaṅkhānāṃ stanayitno rathasya ca \|\| 92 \|\|*

*evaṃ bahuvidhākāraḥ śabda ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*vāyavyastu guṇaḥ sparśaḥ sparśaśca bahudhā smṛtaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*uṣṇaḥ śītaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ snigdho viśada eva ca \|*  
*tathā kharo mṛduḥ ślakṣṇo lavurgurutaro 'pi ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

*śabdasparśau tu vijñeyau dviguṇau vāyurityuta \|*  
*evamekādaśavidho vāyavyo guṇa ucyate \|\| 95 \|\|*

92-93a. Thanks to its power, sound is present everywhere. Yet it manifests itself in various kinds of drums such as drums, kettle-drums and Mrdanga and the conch, clouds and the chariot. Thus the sound originating from the ether is of various kinds.

93b-95. The special quality pertaining to Vayu is the quality of touch. But the quality of touch is remembered (slated traditionally) to be of various kinds. The special quality pertaining to the wind is of eleven varieties, viz. hot, cool, pleasing and painful; soft, clearly manifest touch, the rough touch, the smooth touch, the slimy touch, the light touch and the heavy touch. Vayu has two Gunas, viz. the sound and the touch.

## \|\| 1.42.96 \|\|

*ākāśajaṃ śabdamāhurebhirvāyuguṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*avyāhataiścetayate naveti viṣamā gatiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. (Defective) They say that the sound has been originated from the ether along with qualities of Vayu unobstructcd. Whether perceived or not, its (Vayu's) movement is uneven (zigzag or irregular).

## \|\| 1.42.97 \|\|

*āpyāyante ca te nityaṃ dhātavastaistu dhātubhiḥ \|*  
*āpo 'gnirmāruścaiva nityaṃ jāgrati dehiṣu \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The Dhatus are always developed further by these Dhatus. The fire, the water and the wind — all these are always alert in the embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.42.98-99 \|\|

*mūlamete śarīrasya vyāpya prāṇāniha sthitāḥ \|*  
*pārthivaṃ dhātumāsādya yathā ceṣṭayate balī \|\| 98 \|\|*

*śrito mūrddhānamagnistu śarīraṃ paripālayet \|*  
*prāṇo mūrddhani vāgnau ca vartamāno viceṣṭate \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. They are the root cause of the body. They stay enveloping the Pranas. When the powerful (Prana) functions depending on the element called the earth, the Agni (fire element) rests on the top of the head and protects the body. Staying either in the cerebrum or in the fire, the Prana functions.

## \|\| 1.42.100-102 \|\|

*sa jantuḥ sarvabhūtātmā puruṣaḥ sa sanātanaḥ \|*  
*mano buddhirahṝṅkāro bhūtāni viṣayaśca saḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*evaṃ tviha sa sarvatra prāṇaistu paripālyate \|*  
*pṛṣṭatastu samānena svāṃ svāṃ gatimupāśritaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*vastimūlaṃ gudaṃ caiva pāvakaṃ samupāśritaḥ \|*  
*vahanmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vāpyapānaḥ parivartate \|\| 102 \|\|*

100-101 a. That creature is the Atman of all living beings. It is the eternal Purusa. It is the mind, the intellect, the ego, the living beings and the object of the senses. Thus everywhere it is being protected by the Pranas.

101b-102. From behind it is enabled to attain its respective movement, by the vital air called Samana. The Apana functions after resorting to the fire-element at the root of the bladder and the rectum where it makes the urine and the faecal matter flow out.

## \|\| 1.42.103 \|\|

*prayatne karmaniyame yaca ekastriṣu vartate \|*  
*udāna iti taṃ prāhuradhyātmajñānakovidāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Experts in anatomical (spiritual) knowledge call that (particular organic wind) the Udana which though single functions in three (spheres) viz. in exertions, in activities and in restraint.

## \|\| 1.42.104 \|\|

*saṃdhiṣvapi ca sarveṣu saṃniviṣṭastathānilaḥ \|*  
*śarīreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāna ityupadiśyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The (vital) wind that abides in all the joints in the human bodies is called Vyana.

## \|\| 1.42.105 \|\|

*bāhuṣvagnistu vitataḥ samānena samīritaḥ \|*  
*rasānvāru doṣāṃśca vartayannati ceṣṭate \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The fire that is diffused in the arms is urged by Samana. It functions by creating the Rasas (lymphatic juices or secretions) and the many Dosas (disorders in the three bodily humours) and functions.

## \|\| 1.42.106 \|\|

*apānaprāṇayormadhye prāṇāpānasamīhitaḥ \|*  
*samanvitastvadhiṣṭānaṃ samyak pacati pāvakaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. In the middle of Prana and Apana the (gastric) fire attains its stable position and urged by Prana and Apana, it digests well.

## \|\| 1.42.107 \|\|

*āspaṃhi pāyuparyantamante syādgudasaṃjñite \|*  
*retastasmātprajāyante sarvasrotāṃsi dehinām \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. (Defective) The digestive-system (?) extends from the mouth to the Payu (Anus) which is otherwise called Guda (rectum). Hence, all the lymphatic vessels of the embodied beings produce Retas (semen virile).

## \|\| 1.42.108 \|\|

*prāṇānāṃ sannipātāśca sannipātaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*ūṣmā cāgirīti jñeyo yo 'nnaṃ pacati dehinām \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. When the organic wind called a combined derangement of the humours (causing fever) takes place, the heat should be known as (gastric) fire. It digests the food of the embodied beings.

## \|\| 1.42.109 \|\|

*agnivegavahaḥ prāṇo gudānte pratihanyate \|*  
*sa ūrdhvamāgamya punaḥ samutkṣipati pāvakam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The Prana that carries the force and heat of the fire goes down to the end of the anus and is obstructed at the extremity of the rectum. It comes up once again and casts the fire upwards.

## \|\| 1.42.110 \|\|

*pakvāśayastvadho nābhyā ūrdhvamāmāśayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nābhimūle śarīrasya sarve prāṇāśca saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The abdomen is beneath the umbilical region and the Amdiaya (the receptacle of the raw or uncooked matter the upper part of the belly) is remembered to be above it. All the Pranas are stationed at the root of (pakvasaya) the umbilicus of the body.

## \|\| 1.42.111 \|\|

*prasthitā hṛdayātsarve tiryagūrdhdamadhastathā \|*  
*vahṝntyannarasānnāḍyo daśaprāṇapracoditāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The Nadis (tubular vessels) proceed from the heart and go everywhere—to the sides, above and below. Urged by the ten Pranas they carry the nutritive juicy elements (to all parts of the body).

## \|\| 1.42.112 \|\|

*eṣa mārgo 'pi yogānāṃ yena gacchanti tatpadam \|*  
*jitaklamāḥ samā dhīrā mūrddhanyātmānamādadhan \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The path of the Yogas is also this. Thereby the people attain that highest region. The self-possessed men of equanimity overcoming strain, keep the Atman at the head (in the Sahasrara Lotus)

## \|\| 1.42.113 \|\|

*evaṃ sarveṣu vihitaprāṇāpāneṣu dehinām \|*  
*tasminsamidhyate nityamagniḥ sthālyāmivāhitaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. When the Prana and Apana of the embodied beings function thus, Agni (fiery element) is generated and kindled as through in (or under) a cooking pot (?).

## Chapter 43. The Traditional Duties of Brahmanas

## \|\| 1.43.1 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*yadi prāṇapatirvāyurvāyureva viceṣcate \|*  
*śvasityābhāṣate caiva tato jīvo nirarthakaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*

1\. If the wind is the lord of the Pranas and it is the wind alone that functions, breathes and speaks, there is no purpose served by the Jiva, (the individual soul is superfluous).

## \|\| 1.43.2 \|\|

*ya ūṣmabhāva āgneyo vahninaivopalabhyate \|*  
*agnirjarayate caitattadā jīvo nirarthakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. If the heat belongs to the fire, (the clement called the Fire), if it is perceived through fire and if the fiery element digests (food, etc.) it, ihe Jiva, is futile.

## \|\| 1.43.3 \|\|

*jantoḥ pramniyamāṇasya jīvo naivopalabhyate \|*  
*vāyureva jahātyenamūṣmabhāvaśca naśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When a creature dies, the so-called individual soul is not perceived leaving. Only the wind leaves him off and the heat is extinguished.

## \|\| 1.43.4 \|\|

*yadi vāthumayo jīvaḥ saṃśleṣo yadi vāyunā \|*  
*vāyumañjalavatpaśyedgacchetsaha marudguṇaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. If however, the individual soul is identical with Asu (i. c. Prana, the vital wind) and if it has contact with the wind, it may be seen on a part with the zone of the wind along with the groups of Maruts.

## \|\| 1.43.5 \|\|

*saṃśleṣo yadi vā tena yadi tasmātpraṇaśyati \|*  
*mahārṇavavimuktatvādanyatsalilabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Or if the contact be with it (the wind) and if it perishes thereby like a pot of water due to its being released (separated) from a great ocean.

## \|\| 1.43.6 \|\|

*kṛpe vā salilaṃ dadyātpradīpaṃ vā hutāśane \|*  
*kṣipraṃ praviśya naśyeta yathā naśyatyasau tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If anyone pours water into the well or places the lamp into the fire, it perishes immediately. Similarly, the individual soul too perishes instantaneously.

## \|\| 1.43.7-8 \|\|

*pañcadhāraṇake hyasmiñcharīre jīvitaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*yeṣāmanyatarābhāvāñcaturṇāṃ nāsti saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*naśyantyāpo hyanāhārādvāyurucchvāsanigrahāt \|*  
*naśyate koṣṭabhedārthamagrirnaśyatyabhojanāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The body consists of the five elements and (they say that) it is in this that the soul lives. Therefore, if one of the elements perishes all the others also must undoubtedly perish. If food (and beverages) are not taken in, the watery element perishes. The wind element perishes by means of the restraint of the breath. The (gastric) fire perishes by abstaining from taking food and if anything is taken to purge the belly.

## \|\| 1.43.9 \|\|

*vyādhitraṇaparikleśairmedinī caiva śīryate \|*  
*pīḍite 'nyatare hyeṣāṃ saṃghāto yāti pañcatām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Through sickness, wounds and similar distress the earth element also gets shattered. If anyone of these elements is afflicted, the whole mass of the elements perishes.

## \|\| 1.43.10 \|\|

*tasminpañcatvamāpanne jīvaḥ kimanudhāvati \|*  
*kiṃ khedayati vā jīvaḥ kiṃ śṛṇoti bravīti ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If that (body constituted of five elements) perishes, what is it that the individual soul pursues? What is it that the individual soul feels afflicted? What does it hear or speak?

## \|\| 1.43.11 \|\|

*eṣā gauḥ paralokasthaṃ tārayiṣyatimāmiti \|*  
*yo dattvā mriyate jantuḥ sā gauḥ kaṃ tārayiṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “When I am in the other world this cow will redeem me". A person thinks like this, offers the gift of a cow and then dies. But whom is it that the cow will redeem?

## \|\| 1.43.12 \|\|

*gauścapratigrahītā ca dātā caiva samaṃ yadā \|*  
*ihaiva vilayaṃ yānti kutasteṣāṃ samāgamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the cow, the giver (of that cow) and the acceptor — all these are dissolved here in this world, simultaneously, whence can there be the reunion of all of them?

## \|\| 1.43.13 \|\|

*vihagairupabhuktasya śailāgrātpatitasya ca \|*  
*agninā copayuktasya kutaḥ saṃjīvanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Whence can these be enlivened again — he who is swallowed up by birds, he who falls down from the top of a mountain and he who is consumed by fire?

## \|\| 1.43.14 \|\|

*chinnasya yadi vṛkṣasya na mūlaṃ pratirohati \|*  
*jīvanyasya pravartante mṛtaḥ kva punareṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14 If the root of a tree is cut, it does not grow again. When a man is alive all his parts function. But how will the dead come back again?

## \|\| 1.43.15 \|\|

*jīvamātraṃ purā sṛṣṭaṃ yadetatparivartate \|*  
*mṛtāḥ praṇaśyanti bījādbījaṃ praṇaśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All the individual souls had been created formerly and they revolve again and again. The dead ones perish even as the seeds perish one after the other.

## \|\| 1.43.16 \|\|

*iti me saṃśayo brahmanhṛdaye paridhāvati \|*  
*ta nivartaya sarvajña yatastvāmāśrito hyaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmana, this is the doubt that surges in my heart. О omniscient one, clarify it since I depend upon you (and have approached you for this).

## \|\| 1.43.17 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*evaṃ pṛṣṭastadānena sa bhṛgarbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*punarāhu muniśreṣṭha tatsaṃdehanivṛttaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*

17\. О excellent sage, Bhrigu the son of Brahma who was asked thus by him spoke again to clear his doubts.

## \|\| 1.43.18 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*na prāṇāḥ santi jīvasya dattasya ca kṛtasya ca \|*  
*yāti dehāntaraṃ prāṇī śarīraṃ tu viśīryate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
18\. When the individual is killed or dies himself the Pranas cease to exist. The living being (i.e. his soul) transmigrates to another body and this body decays and becomes shattered.

## \|\| 1.43.19 \|\|

*na śarīrāśrito jīvastasminnaṣṭe praṇaśyati \|*  
*samidhāmagnidagdhānāṃ yathāgrirddaśyate tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Jiva is not dependent on the body. It does not perish when the body perishes. Just as the fire is seen (to be present) even after the sacrificial twigs are completely burned.

## \|\| 1.43.20 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*agneryathā tasya nāśāttadvināśo na vidyate \|*  
*indhanasyopayogānte sa vāgnirnopalabhyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
20\. (You say) that when they (the sacrificial twigs) perish the fire does not perish. But after the fuel has been used up the fire is not verily seen.

## \|\| 1.43.21 \|\|

*naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam \|*  
*gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence, I understand that if fire is extinguished without further addition of fuel, it definitely perishes since, where it goes is not known. There is no proof of its existence.

## \|\| 1.43.22-25 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*samidhāmupayogānte sa cāgnirnopalabhyate \|*  
*naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate \|*  
*samidhāmupayogānte yathāgnirnopalabhyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ākāśānugatatvāddhi durgrāhyo hi nirāśrayaḥ \|*  
*tathā śarīrasaṃtyāge jīvo hyākāśavatsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*na naśyate susūkṣmatvādyathā jyotirna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāndhārayate hyagniḥ sa jīva upadhāryatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
22-25. (You say as follows: —) After the twigs have been used up the fire is not seen. I understand that the tranquil fire without fuel does perish since where it goes is not known. There is no proof of its existence. (Yet understand this.) Just as the fire is not perceived after the consumption of fuel as it has vanished into the ether, and so is without any base and as it is difficult to be perceived, so also, when the body is forsaken ihc Jiva remains like the ether (invisible). Since it is very subtle it does not perish, undoubtedly in the same way as the fire. The fiery element sustains the Prana. May that be understood as the Jiva.

## \|\| 1.43.26-27 \|\|

*vāyusaṃdhāraṇo hyagnirnaśyatyucchvāsanigrahāt \|*  
*tasminnaṣṭe śarīrāgnau tato dehamacetanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*patitaṃ yāti bhūmitvamayanaṃ tasya hi kṣitiḥ \|*  
*jagamānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The (gastric) fire that is sustained by the wind (i.c. the body temperature is sustained by respiration) perishes when the breath is curbed. When the fire of the physical body perishes the insentient body falls down and merges into the earth. Indeed, the ultimate goal of the mobile and immobile beings is the earth.

## \|\| 1.43.28-29 \|\|

*ākāśaṃ pavano 'nveti jyotistamanugacchati \|*  
*teṣāṃ trayāṇāmekatvādvayaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yatra khaṃ tatra pavanastatrāgniryatra mārutaḥ \|*  
*amūrtayaste vijñeyā mūrtimantaḥ śarīriṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The wind follows (or merges into) the ether; the fiery element too follows it. Since all the three constitute one unit the set of two (viz. the earth and water) is established on the earth. Where there is the ether, the wind is present too. The fire is present where there is the wind. These must be known to be without forms but the embodied beings have forms.

## \|\| 1.43.30 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*yadyagnimārutau bhūmiḥ khamāpaśca śarīriṣu \|*  
*jīvaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇastatretyetadācakṣva me 'nagha \|\| 30 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
30\. О sinless one, if the fire, the wind, the earth, the ether and the water are present in the embodied beings, what are the characteristics of the Jiva. Kindly explain this to me.

## \|\| 1.43.31 \|\|

*pañcātmake pañcaratau pañcavijñānasaṃjñake \|*  
*śarīre prāṇināṃ jīvaṃ vettubhicchāmi yādṛśam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. 1 wish to understand of what nature is the Jiva in the bodies of living beings which are constituted by a set of five things viz. the elements) and take delight in five things (e.g. taste, smell, etc.) and have five cognitive senses.

## \|\| 1.43.32 \|\|

*māṃsaśoṇitasaṃghāte medaḥsnāyvasthisaṃcaye \|*  
*bhidyamāne śarīre tu jīvo naivopalabhyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The body is a mass of flesh and blood, fat, bones and sinews. When it is shattered and split the Jiva is not perceived.

## \|\| 1.43.33 \|\|

*yadyajīvaśarīraṃ tu pañcabhūtasamanvitam \|*  
*śarīre mānase duḥkha kastāṃ vedayate rujam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. If the body is without a Jiva but it contains only the five elements, who experiences the pain in the course of mental and physical distress?

## \|\| 1.43.34 \|\|

*śṛṇoti kathitaṃ jīvaḥ karṇābhyāṃna śṛṇoti tat \|*  
*maharṣe manasi vyagre tasmājjīvo nirarthakaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О sage, by means of his pair of ears, the Jiva hears what is uttered, but when the mind is preoccupied he does not hear it. Hence, the Jiva is futile.

## \|\| 1.43.35 \|\|

*sarve paśyanti yadṛśyaṃ manoyuktena cakṣuṣā \|*  
*manasi vyākule cakṣuḥ paśyannapi na paśyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. What should be seen, everyone sees with the eyes in collaboration with the mind. When the mind is agitated, the eye does not perceive though it may look at things.

## \|\| 1.43.36 \|\|

*na paśyati na cāghrāti na śṛṇoti na bhāṣate \|*  
*na ca smarśamasau vetti nidrāvaśagataḥ punaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He does not see, or smell or hear, or speak or know the touch when he (the agent called Jiva) is under the influence of slumber.

## \|\| 1.43.37 \|\|

*hṛṣyati kruddhyate ko 'tra śocatyudvijate ca kaḥ \|*  
*icchati dhyāyati dveṣṭi vākyaṃ vācayate ca kaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Who is it that is delighted? Who is infuriated? Who bewails? Who is alarmed? Who shuns? Who wishes? Who meditates? Who is malicious? Who reads or utters words?

## \|\| 1.43.38 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*taṃ pañcasādhāraṇamatra kiñciccharīrameko vahateṃ'tarātmā \|*  
*sa vetti gandhāṃśca rasāñchutīśca sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca guṇāṃśca ye 'lye \|\| 38 \|\|*

*Bhrigu replied:*  
38\. The body holds one that is common to the five. It is the Antaratman (the inner immanent soul). It is he who perceives the odour, taste, sound, touch, form and the Gunas (attributes).

## \|\| 1.43.39 \|\|

*pañcātmake pañcaguṇapradarśī sa sarvagātrānugatoṃ'tarātmā \|*  
*saveti duḥkhāni sukhāni cātra tadviprayogāttu na vetti deham \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Antaratman is present throughout the body, in the body consisting of five elements; it perceives the five Gunas it is this that experiences pleasure and pain always. Separated from it the body does not understand anything.

## \|\| 1.43.40 \|\|

*yadā na rūpaṃ na sparśo noṣyabhavaśca pāvake \|*  
*tadā śānte śarīrāgnau dehatyāgena naśyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When there is no perception of colour, no touch and no heat in the fire within the body, the fire is tranquil. When the bodily fire (temperature) is cooled down, (the body) dies by being forsaken by Jiva (who does not die).

## \|\| 1.43.41 \|\|

*āpomayamidaṃ sarvamāpomūrtiḥ śarīriṇām \|*  
*tatrātmā mānaso brahmā sarvabhūteṣu lokakṛt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The whole of this (universe; (?) is full of water; it is the water that is the physical body of the embodied being. There the Atman is Brahma in all the living beings. He is the creator of the worlds. He is called Manasa.

## \|\| 1.43.42 \|\|

*ātmānaṃ taṃ vijānīhi sarvalokahitātmakam \|*  
*tasminyaḥ saṃśrito dehe hyabbinduriva puṣkare \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. That which rests in the physical body like the water-drop on the lotus-leaf is the Atman. Know that the Atman is conducive to the welfare of all worlds.

## \|\| 1.43.43 \|\|

*kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ lokahitātmakam \|*  
*tamorajaśca sattvaṃ ca viddhi jīvaguṇānimām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Know him аз the indwelling soul (Kshetrajna), the eternal well-wisher of the worlds. Know that the Gunas (attributes) of the Jiva are Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

## \|\| 1.43.44 \|\|

*acetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ kṣetravido vadanti prāvartayadyo bhuvanāni sapta \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Some say that insentience is the attribute of the Jiva. But it is active and it activates everything. Those who know the *ksetra* (the physical body) say that the Supreme Atman has set the seven worlds in motion

## \|\| 1.43.45 \|\|

*na jīvanāśo 'sti hi dehabhede mithyaitadāhurmuna ityabuddhāḥ \|*  
*jīvastu dehāntaritaḥ prayāti daśārddhatastasya śarīrabhedaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. When the physical body is changed, there is no destruction of the Jiva. О sage, those who have not understood this, call this as untrue. The Jiva moves about in the world (only) after being covered by the body. And its change of body takes place due to its fifth stage (death). (The other four being infancy, childhood, youth and old age).

## \|\| 1.43.46 \|\|

*evaṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣu gūḍhaścarati sarvadā \|*  
*dṛśyate tvagryā budhyāsūkṣmayā tattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus hidden in all the living beings, the Atman always moves about. It is perceived through the subtle and excellent intellect by the seers of the truth.

## \|\| 1.43.47 \|\|

*taṃ pūrvāpararātreṣu yuñjānaḥ satataṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*labdhāhāro viśuddhātmā paśyatyātmānamātmani \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. (Defective) The wise person continuously practising Yoga in the initial and final watches of the night and with his soul sanctified by assimilating pure food realizes the Supreme soul within his own soul.

## \|\| 1.43.48 \|\|

*cittasya hi prasādena hitvā karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukhamānantyamaśnute \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. By dint of the serenity and composure of the mind, and by giving up both auspicious and inauspicious Karmans, one should stabilise oneself in the Atman and be delighted in the mind. He shall thereafter attain infinite bliss.

## \|\| 1.43.49 \|\|

*mānaso 'gniḥ śarīreṣu jīva ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*sṛṣṭiḥ prajāpatereṣā bhūtādhyātmaviniścaye \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The mental fire in the bodies is called the Jiva (in the bodies). In the matter of decision regarding Bhutatman, the creation of the lord of subjects is as follows:

## \|\| 1.43.50 \|\|

*asṛjadbrāhmaṇāneva pūrvaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*ātmatejo 'bhinir vṛttānbhāskarāgnisamaprabhān \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. At the beginning (of creation) it was the Brahmanas alone that Brahma the Prajapati created. They were evolved out of his own brilliance. Their lustre was like that of the Sun and fire.

## \|\| 1.43.51 \|\|

*tataḥ satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca tathā brahma ca śāśvatam \|*  
*ācāraṃ caiva śaucaṃ ca svargāya vidadhe prabhuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereafter the Lord created the following things as conducive to the attainment of heaven, viz. truthfulness Dharma (virtue), the eternal Brahman (i. e. the Vedas), the conventional duties and purity both physical and mental.

## \|\| 1.43.52-54 \|\|

*devadāna vagandharvā daityāsuramahoragāḥ \|*  
*yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca piśācā manujāstathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāṇāmasitastathā \|*  
*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*cāturvarṇyasya varṇena yadi varṇo vibhidyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

*svedamūtrapurīṣāṇi śleṣmā pitta saśoṇitam \|*  
*tvantaḥ kṣarati sarveṣāṃ kasmādvarṇo vibhajyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-53a. (Defective) Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Daityas, Asuras and the great serpents, Yaksas, Raksasas, Nagas, Pisacas and human beings (were created). The human beings (were classified) into Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras.

*Bharadvaja said:*  
53b-54. (You say) that one Varna (caste) in the fourfold division of men is different from the other. What is the criterion thereof? Sweat, urine, faecal matter, phlegm, bile and blood circulate within everyone. Then on what basis is the caste divided?

## \|\| 1.43.55 \|\|

*jaṅgamānāmasaṃkhyeyāḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jātayaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vividhavarṇānāṃ kuto varṇaviniścayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Among both the mobile and immobile beings there are innumerable groups and classes. Among these different Varnas how is a particular Varna arrived at?

## \|\| 1.43.56 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*na viśeṣo 'sti varṇānāṃ sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ jagat \|*  
*brahmaṇā pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ hi karmaṇā varṇatāṃ gatam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*Bhrgu said:*

56\. Originally, there was no distinction among the people. The whole universe formerly created by Brahma was Brahmanical by nature. Though originally created as equals by Brahma, it was as a result of their Karmans; (acts) that people got divided into different castes.

## \|\| 1.43.57 \|\|

*kāmabhogāḥ priyāstīkṣṇāḥ krodhatāpriyasāhasāḥ \|*  
*tyaktasvakarmaraktāṅgāste dvijāḥ kṣatratāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Some of those Brahmanas became fond of erotic enjoyments. They were furious by temperament. They were violent and zealous. They liked risky adventures. They forsook their original duties (of Brahmanas), became red in complexion (i. e. full of Rajo-guna) and attained Ksatriya-hood.

## \|\| 1.43.58 \|\|

*gobhyo vṛttiṃ samāsthāya pītāḥ kṛṣyupajīvinaḥ \|*  
*svadharṃmannānutiṣṭanti te dvijā vaiśyatāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those Brahmanas, who maintained themselves by means of agriculture and lived by tending and rearing up cattle and did not practise original duties as Brahmanas (grew) yellow (a mixture of rajas and tamas) and became Vaisyas.

## \|\| 1.43.59 \|\|

*rhisānṛtaparā lubdhāḥ sarvakarmopajīvinaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāḥ śaucapāribhrāṣṭāste dvijāḥ śūdratāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those Brahmanas who were engrossed in violence and untruthfulness, greedy and maintained themselves by means of all types of jobs (even forbidden to Brahmanas) and were thus fallen from purity of conduct became dark (full of Tamoguna) and degenerated to the status of Sudras.

## \|\| 1.43.60 \|\|

*ityetaiḥ karmabhirvyāptā dvijā varṇāntaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇā dharmatantrasthāstapasteṣāṃ na naśyati \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thus the (original) Brahmanas affected adversely by these activities were changed into other castes. The power of austerities of those Brahmanas who maintained their prescribed religious rituals and duties, does not perish.

## \|\| 1.43.61-62 \|\|

*brahma dhārayatāṃ nityaṃ vratāni niyabhāṃstathā \|*  
*brahma caiva purā sṛṣṭaṃ yena jānanti tadvidaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ bahuvidhāstvanyāstatra tatra dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*piśācajā rākṣasāḥ pretā vividhā mlecchajātayaḥ \|*  
*sā sṛṣṭirmānasī nāma dharmatantraparāyaṇā \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62a. There are many sub-divisions of Brahmanas in the different places, but all of them observe holy virtues, rites and restraints. They perpetually retain the Brahman (i. e. they study the Vedas regularly). Brahman (i.e. Vedas) had already been created formerly. Those who know them understand (everything else).

62b-c. There are many types of Pisacas, Raksasas, Pretas and Mleccha (outcastc) tribes. The creation by (Brahma’s) mind is verily intent on the religious rituals and duties.

## \|\| 1.43.63 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ kena bhavati kṣatriyo vā dvijottama \|*  
*vaiśyaḥ śūdraśca viprarṣe tadbrūhi vadatāṃ vara \|\| 63 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
63\. О excellent Brahmana, how does one become a Brahmana or a Ksatriya? О Brahmanical sage, how does one become a Vaisya or a Sudra? О excellent one among the fluent speakers, please explain it unto me.

## \|\| 1.43.64 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*jātakarmādibhiryastu saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpanno brahmakarmasvavasthitaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
64\. One who is as follows is called a Brahmana. He should have been consecrated duly by means of post-natal purificatory rites and other holy rites as well and should himself be pure. He must possess the learning (recitation, etc.) of the Vedas. He must strictly adhere to the religious duties and rites prescribed for Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.43.65 \|\|

*śaucācārasthitaḥ samyagvidyābhyāsī gurupriyaḥ \|*  
*nityavratī satyaparaḥ sa vai brāhmaṇa ucyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He must closely follow the rules of cleanliness both mental and physical and pure conduct. He must have soundly studied the different lores. He must be fond of his preceptors and elders. He must perpetually observe the holy vows and rites. He must be devoted to truthfulness. Such a person is verily called a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.43.66 \|\|

*satyaṃ dānamatho 'droha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṛpā ghṛṇā \|*  
*tapasyāṃ dṛśyate yatra sa brāhmaṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. He in whom these qualities are seen is remembered as a Brahmana, viz. Truthfulness, charitable gifts, non maliciousness (absence of wickedness), kindness, mercy, sympathy and austerity.

## \|\| 1.43.67 \|\|

*kṣatrajaṃ sevate karma vedādhyayanasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*dānādānaratiryastu sa vai kṣatriya ucyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. One who is as follows, is called a Ksatriya. He practises the duties assigned to a Ksatriya, i.e. the military profession). He practises studying the Vedas He must be interested in giving religious gifts and collecting taxes.

## \|\| 1.43.68 \|\|

*viśatyāśu paśubhyaśca kṛṣyādānaratiḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sa vaiśya iti saṃjñitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Derivation of the word Vaisya is as follows: — *visati asu iti Vaisyah*. One who enters (worldly transactions) immediately is called a Vaisya. Through the animals he is interested in taking to agricultural activities. He loves to donate charitable gifts and is pure. He is endowed with the study and the learning of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.43.69 \|\|

*sarvaghabhakṣaratirnityaṃ sarvakarmakaro 'śuciḥ \|*  
*tyaktavedastvanācāraḥ sa vai śūdra iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One who is always habituated to all kinds of diet, one who regularly performs all odd jobs, is impure, one who has forsaken the study of the Vedas and one who has no conventional duty is remembered as a Sudra.

## \|\| 1.43.70 \|\|

*śūdre caitadbhavellakṣma dvije tacca na vidyate \|*  
*na vai śūdro bhavecchūdro brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇo na ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. If a (born) Sudra possesses all good characteristics and a (born) Brahmana does not possess the same that Sudra is no longer a Sudra and that Brahmana is no longer a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.43.71 \|\|

*sarvopāyaistu lobhasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ \|*  
*etatpavitraṃ jñānānāṃ tathā caivātmasaṃyamaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. By every possible means restraint be put on covetousness and anger. This as well as self-control is the holiest of all wisdom.

## \|\| 1.43.72 \|\|

*varjyau sarvātmanā tau hi śreyoghātārthamudyatau \|*  
*nityakrodhācchriyaṃ rakṣettapo rakṣettu matsarāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Those two (covetousness and anger) attempt to destroy welfare. They must be avoided by all means. One shall save one’s prosperity and glory from perpetual anger; one shall save one’s austerity (power of penance) from malice.

## \|\| 1.43.73 \|\|

*vidyāṃ mānāpamānābhaghyāmātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One should save one’s learning from (the feeling of both) honour and dishonour and one should save oneself from errors and mistakes.

## \|\| 1.43.74 \|\|

*yasya sarve samāraṃbhaghā nirāśīrbandhanā dvija \|*  
*tyāge yasya hutaṃ sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. О Brahmana, he is a real renouncer and intelligent man, he whose every religious enterprise (e.g. sacrifice) is unfettered by longing expectations and he who has dedicated every thing (in his possession) to *Tyaga* (renunciation for the sake of others).

## \|\| 1.43.75 \|\|

*ahiṃstraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ maitrāyaṇa gataścaret \|*  
*parigrahātparityajya bhavedbaddhyā jitendriyaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. One should refrain from injuring or doing violence to all living beings; he should be friendly unto all. Renouncing all possessions and monetary gifts he should subdue his sense- organs intelligently.

## \|\| 1.43.76-78 \|\|

*aśokasthānamāti vediha cāmutra cābhayam \|*  
*taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmamanā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*ajitaṃ jetukāmena vyāsaṃgeṣu hyasaṃginā \|*  
*indriyairgṛhyate yadyattattavdyaktamiti sthitiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*avyaktamiti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyamatīndriyam \|*  
*aviśraṃbheṇa mantavyaṃ viśraṃbhe dhārayenmanaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. One shall abide by that which causes no sorrow, one that will afford him freedom from fear here and hereafter. The (Brahmana) should be perpetually engaged in austerities, self-control, restraint over the mind. He should be desirous of conquering what is not conquered. One should remain unattached to worldly affairs. What can be perceived by means of the sense organs is *Vyakta* (the manifest). That which is beyond the scope of the sense organs, and which can be grasped by inference from its symptoms and characteristic features should be known as *Avyakta* (unmanifest). If there is a nuclear conviction of reality one should continue to ponder more and more. When one is (thoroughly) convinced (about the truth) he should steady the mind therein.

## \|\| 1.43.79 \|\|

*manaḥ prāṇena gṛhṇīyātprāṇaṃ brahmaṇi dhārayet \|*  
*nivedādeva nirvāṇaṃ na ca kiñcidviccitayet \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The mind shall be controlled through the Prana (Breath-control) and the Prana should be concentrated in the Brahman. One attains Nirvana (extinction as a prelude to salvation) through Nirveda (complete detachment). One should not be worried or think of anything else.

## \|\| 1.43.80-83 \|\|

*sukhaṃ vai brahmaṇo brahmannirvedenādhigacchati \|*  
*śauce tu satataṃ yuktaḥ sadācārasamanvitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*svanukrośaśca bhūteṣu taddvijātiṣu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*satyaṃvrataṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ satyaṃ visṛjate prajā \|\| 81 \|\|*

*satyena dhāryate lokaḥ svaḥ satyenaiva gacchati \|*  
*anṛtaṃ tamaso rūpaṃ tamasā nīyate hyadhaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*tamograstāna paśyanti prakāśantamasāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*suduṣprakāśa ityāhurnarakaṃ tama eva ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

80-81a. О Brahmana, it is verily by dispassion (and renunciation) that one gets (real) happiness. One should always be (striving) for purity and should be endowed with the norm of the conduct of the good.

81b-82a. Highest compassion for all beings — all these constitute the characteristic of twice-borns. He (a twice-born) should observe Truthfulness as a sacred vow and should practise Penance, (mental and physical) purity. It is the truth that creates the subjects. The whole world is sustained by Truth. One goes to heaven only by truthfulness.

82b-83. Falsehood is the feature of darkness; one is led downwards through darkness. Those who have been caught hold of by darkness, those who have been enveloped by darkness do not see the brilliant light (of heaven). They say that Naraka (hell) is darkness itself; it cannot be brilliant with light.

## \|\| 1.43.84 \|\|

*satyānṛtaṃ tadubhaghayaṃ prāpyate jagatīcaraiḥ \|*  
*tatrāpyevaṃvidhā loke vṛttiḥ satyānṛte bhavet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Both Satya (truth) and Anrta (falsehood) is attained by the people roaming over the Earth. Even in that case, the predilection in the world should be thus towards Truth and falsehood.

## \|\| 1.43.85-86 \|\|

*dharmādharmauṃ prakāśaśca tamo duḥkhasukhaṃ tathā \|*  
*śārīrairmānasairduḥkhaiḥ sukhaiścāpyasukhodayaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*lokasṛṣṭaṃ prapaśyanto na muhyanti vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*tatra duḥkhavimokṣārthaṃ prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. Light and darkness indicate Dharma and Adharma as also happiness and misery. Wise, foresighted persons who observe what is created in the world affected by miseries and pleasures both physical and mental but both originating from or leading up to Asukha (i. e. unhappiness), do not become deluded. A clever man should (therefore) endeavour to get liberated from misery.

## \|\| 1.43.87-88 \|\|

*sukhaṃ hyanityaṃ bhūtānāmiha loke paratra ca \|*  
*rāhugrastasya somasya yathā jyotsnā na bhāsate \|\| 87 \|\|*

*tathā tamobhibhūtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ naśyate sukham \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. Both here and hereafter pleasure is non-permanent. Just as the light of the moon eclipsed by Rahu becomes faded and dim, so also the happiness of living beings, oppressed by darkness, perishes.

## \|\| 1.43.89 \|\|

*tatkhalu dvividhaṃ sukhamucyacate śarīraṃ mānasaṃ ca \|*  
*iha khalvamuṣmiṃśca loke vastupravṛttayaḥ sukhārthamabhidhīyante nahītaḥ paratrāparvagaphalādviśiṣṭataramasti \|*  
*sa eva kāmyo guṇaviśeṣo dharmārthaguṇāraṃbhagastaddheturasyotpattiḥ sukhaprayojanārthamāraṃbhāḥ \|*  
*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*vadaitadbhavatābhihitaṃ sukhānāṃ paramā sthitiriti \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Happiness is said to be of two kinds, viz. the physical and the mental. Here, in this world verily all actions in regard to any object are said to be pursued for the sake of happiness. As to the other world there is nothing better than *Apavarga* (salvation). That alone is to be desired. It is a desirable quality. Its origin is caused by the endeavour for the same through virtuous activities. All the activities are aimed at the acquisition of happiness which is its purpose.

## \|\| 1.43.90 \|\|

*na tadupagṛhṇīmo na hyeṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ mahati sthitānām \|\| 90 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja said:*  
90\. It has been said by you that pleasures have the greatest status. We do not accept this. Nor is it so in the case of sages who establish themselves in the Supreme.

## \|\| 1.43.91 \|\|

*aprāpya eṣa kāmya guṇaviśeṣo na cainamabhiśīlayanti \|*  
*tapasi śrūyate trilokakṛdbrahmā prabhurekākī tiṣṭati brahmacārī na kāmasukhoṣvātmānamavadadhāti \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. This desirable special quality cannot be attained. They do not practise this. It is reported that Lord Brahma, the creator of the three worlds, stands alone in austerity. He is a celibate. He does not entangle himself in erotic pleasure.

## \|\| 1.43.92 \|\|

*api ca bhagavānviśveśvara umāpatiḥ kāmamabhivartamānamanaṅgatvena samamanayat \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Moreover, Lord Visvesvara, husband of Uma, controlled Kama who attacked him by reducing him to bodilessness.

## \|\| 1.43.93-94 \|\|

*tasmādbhūmau na tu mahātmabhirañjayati gṛhīto na tveṣa tāvadviśiṣṭo guṇaviśeṣa iti \|\| 93 \|\|*

*naitadbhagavataḥ pratyemi bhavatā tūktaṃ sukhānāṃ paramāḥ striya iti lokapravādo hi dvividhaḥ phalodayaḥ sukṛtātsukhamavāpyate 'nyathā duḥkhamiti \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94 Hence, this is not accepted by noble-souled ones. Nor am I convinced of this by you. It has been stated by you that women constitute the highest, ultimate happiness. It is only a popular saying in the world. There are two types of benefit (or result). Happiness results from good deeds and misery otherwise.

## \|\| 1.43.95 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*atrocyate anṛtātkhalu tamaḥ prādurbhūtaṃ tatastamograstā adharmamevānuvartante na dharmaṃ krodhalobhamohahiṃsānṛtādibhikhacchannāḥ khalvasmiṃlloke nāmutra sukhamāpnuvanti vividhavyādhirujopatāpairavakīryante vadhabandhanaparikleśādibhiśca kṣutpipāsāśramakṛtairupatāpairupatapyante varṣavātātyuṣṇātiśītakṛtaiśca pratibhayaiḥ śārīrairduḥkhairupatapyante bandhudhanavināśaviprayogakṛtaiśca mānasaiḥ śaukairabhibhūyante jarāmṛtyukṛtaiścānyairiti yastvetaiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

Bhrigu said:  
95\. Here it is being (thus) explained. Darkness (Tamoguna) has manifested itself from *Anrta* (falsehood). Those who are prevailed upon by darkness pursue only Adharma and not Dharma. Those who have been affected by anger, covetousness, delusion, violence, falsehood and similar vicious things do not attain happiness either in this world or in the other one. They are shattered and scattered through various kinds of sickness, pain and oppressions. They are afflicted by various distressing features such as capital punishment, imprisonment and tortures; they are overwhelmed by the distress and strain of hunger, thirst and tedium; they are subjected to various miseries of physical strain due to rain, gusts of wind, oppressing heat and biting cold; they are afflicted by various mental miseries caused by the death of or separation from kinsmen or the destruction of wealth; they are also dejected due to other causes such as old age, death, etc.

## \|\| 1.43.96 \|\|

*śārīraṃ mānasaṃ nāsti na jarā na ca pātakam \|*  
*nityameva sukhaṃ svarge sukhaṃ duḥkhamihobhayam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. In the heaven there is neither physical nor mental pain; there is no old age or sin; it is always pleasure alone there; but here (in this world) both pleasure and pain are experienced.

## \|\| 1.43.97 \|\|

*narake duḥkhamevāhuḥ sukhaṃ tatparamaṃ padam \|*  
*pṛthivī sarvabhūtānāṃ janitrī tadvidhāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. They say that there is only misery in the hell, that the highest region (of the Lord) has pure happiness. The earth is the mother of all living beings; women are also of the same nature.

## \|\| 1.43.98-99 \|\|

*pumānprajāpatistatraśukraṃ tejomayaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*ityetallokanirmātā dharmasya caritasya ca \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tapasaśca sutaptasya svādhyāyasya hutasya ca \|*  
*hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ svādhyāye śāntiruttamā \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. The male is lord of the progeny (begetter). They know that the semen virile is of the fiery element. Hence, he is the creator of the worlds of Dharma, of good conduct, of well-performed penance, of self-study (of the Vedas) and of the performance of Ноmа. The sin is subdued through the sacrificial rites. There is excellent tranquility in the self-study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.43.100 \|\|

*dānena bhogānityāhusta pasā svargamāpnuyāt \|*  
*dānaṃ tu dvividhaṃ prāhuḥ paratrārthamihaiva ca \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. They say that enjoyment of pleasures is due to charitable gifts; and that one shall attain heavenly pleasures through penance. They say that Dana (charitable gift) is of two types; that for the purpose of benefit here and that for the purpose of benefit in the other world.

## \|\| 1.43.101 \|\|

*sadbhyo yaddīyate kiñcittatparatropatiṣṭate \|*  
*asadbhyo dīyate yattu taddānamiha bhujyate \|*  
*yādṛśaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tādṛśaṃ phalamaśnute \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Whatever is given to the good men is conducive to the pleasures in the other world; whatever is given as charitable gift to bad men is conducive to the pleasures in this world only. The benefit enjoyed (from charitable gifts) is in accordance with charitable gift offered. Bharadvaja enquired:

## \|\| 1.43.102 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*kiṃ kasya dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃ vā dharmasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*dharmaḥ katividho vāpi tadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 102 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja enquired:*  
102\. What is performance of holy rites? Who performs them? What are the characteristics of Dharma? Of how many types is Dharma? It behoves you to explain it.

## \|\| 1.43.103 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*svadharmācaraṇe yuktā ye bhavanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svargapalāvāptiryo 'nyathā sa vimuhyate \|\| 103 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
103\. The acquisition of the benefit of heavenly pleasures is only unto those learned men who are engrossed in carrying out their prescribed religious duties. He who is otherwise becomes deluded. Bharadvaja submitted:

## \|\| 1.43.104 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*yadetañcāturāśramyaṃ brahmarṣivihitaṃ purā \|*  
*teṣāṃ sve sve samācārāstanme vaktumihārhasi \|\| 104 \|\|*

*Bharadvaja submitted:*  
104\. It behoves you to explain to me here the respective conventional duties of the four stages of life ordained formerly by Brahmanical sages.

## \|\| 1.43.105 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*pūrvameva bhagavatā brahmaṇā lokahitamanutiṣṭatā dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthamāśramāścatvāro 'bhinirddiṣṭāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*Bhrigu said:*  
105\. Four Aframas (stages of life) have been specified for the preservation of Dharma, even at the very outset, by Lord Brahma who used to carry out what is beneficial to the worlds

## \|\| 1.43.106 \|\|

*tatra gurukulavāsameva prathamamāśramamāharanti samyagatra śaucasaskāraniyamavrataviniyatātmā ubhe saṃdhye bhāskarāgnidaivatānyupasthāya vihāya taddhyālasyaṃ gurorabhivādanavedābyāsaśravaṇapavitraghīkṛtāntarātmā triṣavaṇamupaspṛśya brahmacaryāgniparicaraṇaguruśuśrūṣā nityabhikṣābhaikṣyādisarvaniveditāntarātmā guruvacananideśānuṣṭānāpratikūlo guruprasādalabdhasvādhyāyatatparaḥ syāt \|\| 106 \|\|*
