When both merits and sins are shed off and fruits accruing therefrom to the body (tanoh) are destroyed, such persons being unattached at first resort to the Saguna Brahman that is in the space of one’s heart and then visualize the Nirguna Brahman.

81b-82a. Just as a spider residing in his web made of threads woven by itself, becomes free by cessation of weaving out the thread, the same way a person who is released from Samsara sheds off all miseries and they (the miseries) are shattered down and destroyed like a clump or sod of earth dashing against a rocky mountain (*adri*).

82b-83a. Just as the Ruru (a species of deer) casting off its old horns or a serpent casting off its slough, slips away without being noticed, similarly, a liberated person casts оff his sorrow.

83b-84. Just as a bird, leaving off a tree (drumam) falling into the water flies up to a safer place, in the same manner this person gives up joys and sorrows and becoming liberated and dissociated from his subtle bodies, attains to the highest region (viz. Moksa).

## \|\| 1.45.85 \|\|

*idamamṛtapadaṃ niśamya rājā svayamihapañcaśikhena bhāṣyamāṇam \|*  
*nikhilamabhisamīkṣya niścitārthaḥ paramasukhī vijahāra vītaśokaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Having listened to the discourse full of nectarine words delivered by Pancasikha himself the king Janadeva carefully pondered upon every point contained therein and ascertained the truth in it. Casting off his sorrow he lived joyfully merged in the supreme bliss.

## \|\| 1.45.86 \|\|

*api ca bhavati maithilena gītaṃ nagaramupāhitamagninābhivīkṣya \|*  
*na khalu mama hi dahyate 'tra kiñcitsvayamidamāha kila sma bhūmipālaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. It is reported that beholding his capital city enveloped in fire, it was exclaimed by the king of Mithila himself: “In this burning city, nothing of mine is burning."

## \|\| 1.45.87 \|\|

*imaṃ hi yaḥ paṭhati vimokṣaniścayaṃ mahāmune satatamavekṣate tathā \|*  
*upadravānanubhaghavate hyaduḥ khitaḥ pramucyate kapilamivaitya maithilaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. О great sage! He who reads this exposition on the ascertainment of (the means to) Moksa and continuously ponders over it, is not affected by calamities and sorrows and becomes emancipated as did the king of Mithila, after this meeting with Pancasikha.

## Chapter 46. The Narration of Spiritual matters

## \|\| 1.46.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tacchṛtvā nārado viprā maithilādhyātmamuttamam \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha taṃ prītyā sanandanamudāradhīḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Suta said:*

1\. О Brahmanas, on hearing that excellent spiritual discourse, the liberal-minded Narada delightedly asked Sanandana again.

## \|\| 1.46.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*ādhyātmikādatrividhaṃ tāpaṃ nānubhavedyathā \|*  
*prabrūhi tanmune mahyaṃ prapannāya dayānidhe \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Narada said:*  
2\. О sage, О storehouse of mercy! I seek refuge in you. To me kindly relate those things whereby one may not experience the three types of distress such as the Adhyatmika Adhidaivika, etc.

## \|\| 1.46.3 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*tadasya trividhaṃ duḥkhamiha jātasya paṇḍita \|*  
*garbe janmajarādyeṣusthāneṣu prabhaviṣyataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
3\. О learned one, three types of miseries occur to our born here. They occur in the womb or in the course of the process of being born or in the old age.

## \|\| 1.46.4 \|\|

*nirastātiśayāhlādasukhabhāvaikalakṣaṇā \|*  
*bheṣajaṃ bhagavatprāptiraikā cātyantikī matā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The panacea (for all worldly ills) is the ultimate attainment of the lord, characterised by the state ofhappiness unexcelled in bliss.

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*tasmāttatprāptaye yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ paṇḍitairnaraiḥ \|*  
*tatprāptihetujñānaṃ ca karma coktaṃ mahāmune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hence, effort to attain it (viz. God-realization) must be made by learned men. О great sage, the cause of attaining it is said to be both knowledge and activity.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*āgamotthaṃ vivekāñca dvidhā jñānaṃ tathocyate \|*  
*śabdabrahmāgamamayaṃ paraṃ brahmavivekajam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Knowledge is said to be of two kinds: that which arises out of the Vedic texts and that which arises from discrimination. The Sabdabrahman is that which arises out of the Agamas. The great Supreme Brahman is that which arises out of discrimination between Reality and illusion.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*manurapyāha vedārthaṃ smṛtvāyaṃ munisattamamaḥ \|*  
*tadetacchrūyatāmatra subodhaṃ gadato mama \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The excellent sage Manu too, after remembering the meaning of the Vedas says thus: May that be heard even as I recount it in an easily understandable manner.

## \|\| 1.46.8 \|\|

*dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat \|*  
*śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Two Brahmans are to be understood, viz., the Sabdabrahman and the Supreme Brahman. One who is an adept in the Sabdabrahman understands the great Brahman."

## \|\| 1.46.9 \|\|

*dve vidye veditavye cetyāha cātharvaṇī śrutiḥ \|*  
*paramā tvakṣaraprāptirṛgvedādimayā parā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Atharvana Veda also says — “Two Vidyas are to be known”. The greatest Vidya is the attainment of the Imperishable (Brahman). The other one is the lore of the ftgveday etc.

## \|\| 1.46.10-11 \|\|

*yattadavyaktamajaramanīhamajamavyayam \|*  
*anirdeśyamarūpaṃ ca pāṇipādādisaṃyutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ nityaṃ bhūtayo nimakāraṇam \|*  
*vyāpyaṃ vyāptaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ taṃ vai paśyanti sūrayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Verily, wise sages see him who is unmanifest, unageing, devoid of longing, birthless and unchanging; who cannot be specifically pointed out, who is formless, devoid of hands and feet, powerful and omnipresent, eternal, causeless but the source of origin of living beings, who is pervaded and who pervades everything else.

## \|\| 1.46.12 \|\|

*tadbūhya tatparaṃ dhāma taddhyeyaṃ mo7kāṅkṣibhiḥ \|*  
*śrutivākyoditaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That is thc Brahmany the greatest abode. It must be meditated upon by those who seek salvation. It is the subtle one mentioned by the Vedic texts — the greatest region of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.46.13 \|\|

*tadeva bhagavadvācyaṃ svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*vācako bhagavacchabdastasyoddiṣṭo 'kṣayātmanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That same form of the greatest Atman is expressed by the word Bhagavat. The word Bhagavat connotes it. It is so indicated in regard to the imperishable Atman.

## \|\| 1.46.14 \|\|

*evaṃ nigaditārthasya yattatvaṃ tasya tattvataḥ \|*  
*jñāyate yena tajjñānaṃ paramanyatrayīmayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. That whereby the reality of what has been thus described is factually realized, is the real perfect knowledge. The other consists of the Trinity of Vedas.

## \|\| 1.46.15 \|\|

*aśabdagocarasyāpi tasya vai brahmaṇo dvijā \|*  
*pūjāyāṃ bhagavacchabdaḥ kriyate hyaupacārikaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmana, though the Brahman is beyond the ken of Sabdas (sounds and words) the word Bhagavat is used formally in order to honour or to adore the same.

## \|\| 1.46.16 \|\|

*jñeyaṃ jñāteti tathā bhakāror'thadvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*tenāgamapitā sraṣṭā gakāro 'yaṃ tathā mune \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О holy lord, the word Bhagavat connotes the pure and Supreme Brahman called also Mahavibhuti (One endowed with the highest Potency) and is the cause of all causes.

## \|\| 1.46.16-17 \|\|

*jñeyaṃ jñāteti tathā bhakāror'thadvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*tenāgamapitā sraṣṭā gakāro 'yaṃ tathā mune \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ \|*  
*jñānavairāgyayoścaiva ṣaṇṇāṃ bhaga itīraṇā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16a. The syllable *bha* has two meanings (1) that which is to be known and (2) the knower. О sage, similarly the syllable ga means the creator, the father of the Agamas.

17\. Six things are indicated by the term Bhag viz: perfect prosperity and glory, prowess renown, splendour, perfect knowledge and detachment.

## \|\| 1.46.18 \|\|

*vasaṃti tatra bhūtāni bhūtātmanyakhilātmani \|*  
*sarvabhūteṣvaśeṣeṣu vakārārthastato 'vyayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the Bhatatman which is the soul of all, all the living beings reside. Hence, the meaning of the word ‘va’ is the unchanging lord who abides in all living beings.

## \|\| 1.46.19 \|\|

*evameva mahāśabdo bhagavāniti sattama \|*  
*paramabrahmabhūtasya vāsudevasya nānyagaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus О excellent one, the great word Bhagavan belongs to Vasudeva who is the greatest Brahman. It docs not refer to anyone else.

## \|\| 1.46.20 \|\|

*tatra pūjyapadārthoktiḥ paribhāṣāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*śabdo 'yaṃ nopacāreṇa cānyatra hyupacārataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. As a technical phrase the word indicates an object of worship. This word indicates Vasudeva without being used in a secondary sense. When referring to other objects the word is used in a secondary sense.

## \|\| 1.46.21 \|\|

*utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānāmāgatiṃ gatim \|*  
*vetti vidyāmavidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavāniti \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He who knows the origin, dissolution, the advent as well as the departure of the living beings and also he who knows Vidya and Avidya, should be expressed by the term Bhagavan.

## \|\| 1.46.22 \|\|

*jñānaśaktibalaiśvaryavīryatejāṃsyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*bhagavacchabdavācyāni vinā heyairguṇādibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Knowledge, power, strength, prosperity, virility and splendour, the entirety of all these arc expressed by the word Bhagavat. Only the despicable qualities are excluded.

## \|\| 1.46.23 \|\|

*sarvāṇi tatra bhūtāni vasaṃti paramātmani \|*  
*bhūteṣu vasanādeva vāsudevastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. All the living beings reside in the great Atman. The lord is remembered as Vasudeva, because he abides in the Bhutas.

## \|\| 1.46.24 \|\|

*khāṇḍikyaṃ janakaṃ prāha pṛṣṭaḥ keśidhvajaḥ purā \|*  
*nāmavyākhyāmanantasya vāsudevasya tattvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Formerly when requested, Kesidhvaja mid Khandikya of the Janaka dynasty. He factually explained the meaning of the epithet Vasudeva, the Infinite.

## \|\| 1.46.25 \|\|

*bhūteṣu vasate soṃ'tarvasaṃtyatra ca tāni yat \|*  
*dhātā vidhātā jagatāṃ vāsudevastataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He lives in the Bhutas and the Bhutas live in him. He is the creator and the protector of all worlds. Hence, Vasudeva is a lord — the Governor.

## \|\| 1.46.26 \|\|

*sa sarvabhūtaprakṛtiṃ vikāraṃ guṇādidoṣāṃśca mune vyatītaḥ \|*  
*atītasarvāvaraṇo 'khilātmā tenāstṛtaṃ yadbhuvanāntarālam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О sage, he transcends the Prakrti of all living beings, the aberrations and the faults such as the Gunas, etc. He goes beyond all coverings. He is the Atman of all, the space between the worlds is occupied by him.

## \|\| 1.46.27 \|\|

*samastakalyāṇaguṇaṃ guṇātmako hitvātiduḥkhāvṛtabhūtasargaḥ \|*  
*icchāgṛhītābhimatorudehaḥ saṃsādhitāśeṣajagaddhito 'sau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He is endowed with ail auspicious qualities and is of the nature of good qualities. (Defective). He eschews the creation of the Bhutas over-whelmed by too much of misery; he assumes a splendid form voluntarily in accordance with his Will. He achieves the welfare of the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.46.28 \|\|

*tejobalaiśvaryamahāvabodhaṃ svavīryaśaktyāduguṇaikarāśiḥ \|*  
*paraḥ parāṇāṃ sakalā na yatra kleśādayaḥ saṃti parāvareśe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He is one sole repository of splendour, strength, prosperity, great enlightenment, virility and other qualities. He is greater than the greatest. In the lord of the finite and the infinite beings, there are no (such imperfections of Avidya such as distress and others.

## \|\| 1.46.29 \|\|

*sa īśvaro vyaṣṭisamaṣṭirūpo 'vyaktasvarūpaḥ prakaṭasvarūpaḥ \|*  
*sarveśvaraḥ sarvanisargavettā samaskaśaktiḥ parameśvarākhyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He is the lord called Paramesvara. He is of the form of Vyasti and Samasti (the Microcosm and Macrocosm); he is both of the unmanifest and manifest forms; he is the overlord of all, the knower of the entire creation, and he is omnipotent

## \|\| 1.46.30 \|\|

*sa jñāyate yena tadastadoṣaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ nirmalameva rūpam \|*  
*saṃdṛśyate cāpyavagamyate ca tajjñānamato 'nyaduktam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. That whereby he is known is free of defects; it is an extremely pure form devoid of impurities. It is seen and understood. That is the perfect knowledge, anything other than this is said to be Ajnana (Ignorance).

## \|\| 1.46.31 \|\|

*svādhyāyasaṃyamābagyāṃ sa dṛśyate puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*tatprāptikāraṇaṃ brahma tavetatpratipadyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. That Purusottama is seen by means of Svadhyaya (study of the Vedas) and Samyama (self-control i.e. Yoga), either of them being the cause of attaining him, is called Brahma.

## \|\| 1.46.32 \|\|

*svādhyāyādyogamāsīta yogātsvādhyāyamāmanet \|*  
*svādhyāyayogasaṃpattyā paramātmā prakāśate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. One should practise Yoga after Svadhyaya; and one should commit to memory the prescribed Vedic texts after through Yoga. The great Atman is revealed through the accomplishment of Svadhyaya and Yoga.

## \|\| 1.46.33 \|\|

*tadīkṣaṇāya svādhyāyaścakṣuryogastathāparam \|*  
*na māṃsacakṣuṣā draṣṭuṃ brahmabhūtaḥ sa śakyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Svadhyaya is the eye for visualising him. The other eye is Yoga. (The Lord) who is Brahman cannot be seen through the physical eye.

## \|\| 1.46.34 \|\|

*// nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavaṃstamahaṃ yogaṃ jñātumicchāmi taṃ vada \|*  
*jñāte yannākhilādhāraṃ paśyeyaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

34\. О Holy lord, I wish to know that Yoga. Kindly elucidate that after knowing which I would be able to see the Supreme Ruler, the support of all.

## \|\| 1.46.35 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*keśidhvajo yathā prāha khāṇḍikyāya mahātmane \|*  
*janakāya purā yogaṃ tathāhaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 35 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
35\. I shall expound that Yoga, in the same manner as Kesidhvaja formerly explained it to the noble-souled Khandikya of Janaka race.

## \|\| 1.46.36 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*khāṇḍikyaḥ ko 'bhavadbrahman ko vā keśidhvajo 'bhavat \|*  
*kathaṃ tayośca saṃvādo yogasaṃbandhavānabhūt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*Narada said:*  
36\. О holy lord, who was Khandikya? Who was Kesidhvaja? How did it happen that they had a dialogue in relation to Yoga.

## \|\| 1.46.37 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*dharmadhvajo vai janaka tasya puśe 'mitadhvajaḥ \|*  
*kṛtadhvajo 'sya bhrātābhūtsadādhyātmaratirnṛpaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
37\. Dharmadhvaja of Janaka family was the father. His son was Amitadhvaja. Krtadhvaja was his brother who was a king who always took delight in spiritual topics. The blessed twice-born Kesidhvaja was the son of Krtadhvaja. The son of Amitadhvaja was named Khandikya of the Janaka dynasty.

## \|\| 1.46.38 \|\|

*karmamārge hi khāṇḍikyaḥ svarājyādavaropitaḥ \|*  
*purodhasā mantribhiśca samaveto 'lpasādhanaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Khandikya who followed the path of action, was banished from his kingdom, accompanied by his preceptor and the ministers. He had limited resources only.

## \|\| 1.46.39 \|\|

*rājyānnirākṛtaḥ so 'tha durgāraṇyacaro 'bhavat \|*  
*iyāḍaja so 'pi subahūna yajñāñjñānavyapāśrayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After being exiled from the kingdom, he wandered, through the impassable forests. He (Kesidhvaja) performed many Yajnas and resorted to Jnana also.

## \|\| 1.46.40-42 \|\|

*brahmavidyāmadhiṣṭāya tartuṃ mṛtyumapi svayam \|*  
*ekadā vartamānasya yāge yogavidāṃ vara \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tasya dhenuṃ jaghānograḥ śārdūlo vijane vane \|*  
*tato rājā hatāṃ jñātvā dhenuṃ vyāghreṇa cartvijaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*prāyaścittaṃ sa papraccha kimatreti vidhīyatām \|*  
*te cocurnavayaṃvidmaḥ kaśeruḥ pṛcchyatāmiti \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. By resorting to the lore about Brahman, he wished to cross the ocean of death. О foremost one among the knowers of Yoga, once as he was performing a sacrifice, a fierce tiger killed his cow in the lonely forest. On knowing that the cow11 was killed by a tiger, he asked the sacrificial priests about the atonement: “What shall be done in this context?” They replied — “We do not know. May Kaseru be consulted.”

## \|\| 1.46.43 \|\|

*kaśerurapi tenoktastatheti prāha nārada \|*  
*śunakaṃ pṛccha rājendra veda sa vetsyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Narada, on being asked by him, Kaseru said — “O leading king! I do not know it. Please refer to Sunaka. He will know it, i.e. must be knowing it.

## \|\| 1.46.44-45 \|\|

*sa gatvā tamapṛcchañca so 'pyāha nṛpatiṃ mune \|*  
*na kaśerurnacaivāhaṃ na cānyaḥ sāṃprataṃ bhuvi \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vettyeka eva tvacchatruḥ khāṇḍikyo yo jitastvayā \|*  
*sa cāha taṃ vrajāmyeṣa praṣṭumātmaripuṃ mune \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. He went and asked him. О sage, he told the king, — “Neither Kaseru, nor I, nor anyone in the world now knows it. Only your enemy Khandikya who was defeated by you, knows it. О sage, he said, “I shall go to my enemy in order to consult him.”

## \|\| 1.46.46-48 \|\|

*prāpta eva mayā yajñe yadi māṃ sa haniṣyati \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ sa cetpṛṣṭo vadiṣyati ripurmama \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tataścāvikalo yogo muniśreṣṭha bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ityuktvā rathamāruhya kṛṣṇājinadharo nṛpaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vanaṃ jagāma yatrāste khāṇḍikyaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tamāyāntaṃ samālokya khāñjaḍikyo ripumātmanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. If he kills me, the benefit of the Yajna becomes already acquired by. re.1 If on being asked, my enemy explains the atonement, О excellent sage, the Yoga will be unaffected.” Saying thus, the king, clad in deer skin, rode in the chariot and went to the forest where Khandikya the king was present. On seeing his enemy coming, Khandikya said with his eyes reddened with anger. He kept his bow fully drawn. Wrongly numbered in the printed text.

## \|\| 1.46.49-55 \|\|

*provāca krodhatāmrākṣaḥ samāropitakārmukaḥ \|*  
*khāṇḍikya uvāca*  
*kṛṣṇājinatvakkavacabhāvenāsmānhaniṣyasi \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇājinadhare vetsi na mayi prahariṣyati \|*  
*mṛgānāṃ vada pṛṣṭeṣu mūḍha kṛṣṇājinaṃ na kim \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ matvā vṛthā cogrāḥ prahitāḥ śitasāyakāḥ \|*  
*sa tvāmahaṃ haniṣyāmi na me jīvanvimokṣyase \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ātatāyyasi durbuddhe mama rājyaharo ripuḥ \|*  
*keśidhvaja uvāca*  
*khāṇḍikya saṃśayaṃ praṣṭuṃ bhavantamahamāgataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*na tvāṃ hṝntuṃ vicāryataitkopaṃ bāṇaṃ ca muñca vā \|*  
*tataḥ sa mantribhiḥ sārddhamekānte sapurohitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*mantrayāmāsa khāṇḍikyaḥ sarvaireva mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tamūrmantriṇo vadhyo ripureṣa vaśaṅgataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*hate 'tra pṛthivī sarvā tava vaśyā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*khāṇḍikyaścāha tānsarvāneva meva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*Khandikya said:*  
49-52a. O, will you kill us with the deerskin for youi coat of mail? You seem to know (i.e. think) “Noone will strike me since I wear deer skin”. О fool, tell me. Is there no deerskin on the back of the deer? I thought that sharp and fierce arrows discharged on them would be futile, I will now kill you. You will not be allowed to go alive. О evil-minded one, you arc a desperado; my enemy who has taken away my kingdom.  
*Kesidhvaja said:*  
“O Khandikya, it is with a view to clear a doubt that I have come to you, and not to kill you. Considering this, leave off either your anger or the arrow. ”

52b-55. Thereafter, he (Khandikya) discussed the matter in private with his ministers and his preceptors and priests. Khandikya, the highly intelligent one, consulted everyone. The ministers advised him — “This enemy who has come under our control must be killed. If he is killed the entire earth will be under your control.” Khandikya replied to all of them — “Undoubtedly it is so.

## \|\| 1.46.56 \|\|

*hate tu pṛthivī sarvā mama vaśyā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*paralokajayastasya pṛthivī sakalā mama \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If he is killed the entire earth will be under my control. But the conquest of the other world will be his, while the whole of the earth may be mine.

## \|\| 1.46.57 \|\|

*na hanmi cellokajayo mama vayatvaḥsuṃdharā \|*  
*paralokajayo 'nantaḥ svalpakālo mahījayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If I don’t kill him, the conquest of the other world is mine without the earth. The conquest of the other world lasts till infinity, while the conquest of the earth is of a short duration.

## \|\| 1.46.58 \|\|

*tasmānnainaṃ haniṣye 'haṃ yatpṛcchati vadāmi tat \|*  
*tatastamabhyupetyāha khāṇḍikyo janako ripum \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence, I will not kill him. I will tell him what he asks.” Then Khandikya Janaka approached his enemy and said: —

## \|\| 1.46.59 \|\|

*praṣṭavyaṃ yattvayā sarvaṃ tatpṛccha tvaṃ vadāmyaham \|*  
*tataḥ prāha yathāvṛttaṃ homadhenuvadhaṃ mune \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “Whatever you have to ask me (freely) ask me. I shall tell you.” Then, О sage, he told him about the slaughter of his sacrificial cow.

## \|\| 1.46.60 \|\|

*tataśca taṃ sa papraccha prāyaścittaṃ hi tadrūtam \|*  
*sa cācaṣṭa yathānyāyaṃ mune keśidhvajāya tat \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then he asked him about the expiatory observance of this Vrata. О sage, he duly explained everything to Kesidhvaja.

## \|\| 1.46.61-62 \|\|

*prāyaścittamaśeṣaṃ hi yadvai tatra vidhīyate \|*  
*viditārthaḥ sa tenaivamanujñāto mahātmanā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yāgabhūmimupāgatya cakre sarvāṃ kriyāṃ kramat \|*  
*krameṇa vidhivadyāgaṃ nītvā so 'vabhṛthāplutaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. All the expiatory rites ordained in the context were explained by him. After understanding the matter, and being permitted by the noblc-souled one he went back to the sacrificial ground and performed the rites duly. After completing the sacrifice duly he took his ceremonial ablution (Avabhrtha).

## \|\| 1.46.63-70 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyastato bhūtvā cintayāmāsa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*pūjitā ṛtvijaḥ sarve sadasyā mānitā mayā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tathaivārthijano 'pyarthojito 'bhimatairmayā \|*  
*yathāhaṃ martyalokasya mayā sarvaṃ vicaṣṭitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*aniṣpannakriyaṃ cetastathā na mama kiṃ yathā \|*  
*itthaṃ tu cintayanneva saṃmāra sa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*khāṇḍikyāya na datteti mayā vaigurudakṣiṇā \|*  
*sa jagāma tato bhūyo rathamāruhya pārthivaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*svāyaṃbhuvaḥ sthito yatra khāṇḍikyo 'raṇyadurgamam \|*  
*khāṇḍikyo 'pi punarddaṣṭvā tamāyāntaṃ dhṛtāyudhaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tasthau hṝntuṃ kṛtamatismamāha sa punarnṛpaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tu nāpakārāya prāptaḥ khāṇḍikya mā krudhaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*gurorniṣkṛtidānāya māmavehi semāgatam \|*  
*niṣpādito mayā yāgaḥ samyak tvadupadeśataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*so 'haṃ te dātumicchāmi vṛṇīṣva gurudakṣiṇām \|*  
*ityukto mantrayāmāsa sa bhūyo mantribhiḥ saha \|\| 70 \|\|*

63-65a. Becoming contented» the king began to think — “All the sacrificial priests have been worshipped. All the members of the sacrificial assembly have been honoured. All the suppliants have been duly provided with the desired objects by me. Whatever was worth doing in this world has been performed by me. How is it that I feel in my mind as though some religious duty has not been finished?

65b-66a. While pondering over thus, the king remembered — ” O, the requisite fees due to the preceptor have not been given to Khandikya by me.”

66b-67a. The king thereupon got into his chariot again and went to the impassable forest region where Khandikya the devotee of Svayambhu, was staying.

67b-68a. On seeing him coming again, Khandikya took up his weapon. He stood ready with the intention to kill him. The king Kesidhvaja then told him.

68b-70. “O Khandikya, do not be angry. I have not come here to do any harm to you; know that I have come to requite my preceptor. In accordance with your instruction the sacrifice has been duly performed by me. I wish to give you the Gurudaksina (Preceptor’s fees). Please choose it and tell me. On being thus requested, the king again consulted his ministers.

## \|\| 1.46.71 \|\|

*gurorniṣkṛtikāmo 'ya kimayaṃ prārthyatāṃ mayā \|*  
*tamūcurmantriṇo gajyamaśeṣaṃ yācyatāmayam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. “He is desirous of paying the fees of the preceptor. What shall be requested by me?” The ministers said to him — “He may be requested for the gift of the entire kingdom”.

## \|\| 1.46.72 \|\|

*kṛtābhiḥ prārthyate rājyamanāyāsitasainikaiḥ \|*  
*prāhasya tānāha nṛpaḥ sa khāṇḍikyo mahāpatiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. King Khandikya laughed and said — “The kingdom is being begged by contented people whose soldiers have not undergone any stress or strain!

## \|\| 1.46.73-74 \|\|

*svalpakālaṃ mahīrājyaṃ mādṛśaiḥ prārthyate katham \|*  
*etametadbhaṃvato 'tra svārtha sādhanamantriṇaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*paramārthaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra yūyaṃ nātra vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā samupetyaiṃnaṃ sa tu keśidhvajaṃ nṛpam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74a. The kingdom of the earth is of a short duration. How can it be requested for by people like me? This is it. You people are such advisors as advocate selfish interest. What is the truth underlying this? You arc not clever enough to know it.’’

74b. After saying this he went up near the king Kesidhvaja and said — “will you certainly give the preceptor’s fees?’’ When he said ‘Of course’, Khandikya spoke to him.

## \|\| 1.46.76-78 \|\|

*bhavānadhyātmavijñānaparamārthavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*yadi ceddīyate mahyaṃ bhavatā guruniṣkrayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tatkleśapraśamāyālaṃ yatkarma tadudīraya \|*  
*keśidhvaja uvāca*  
*na prārthitaṃ tvayā kasmānmama rājyamakaṇṭakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*rājyalābhāḥ ddhi nāstyanyatkṣatriyāṇāmatipriyam \|*  
*khāṇḍikya uvāca*  
*keśidhvaja nibodha tvaṃ mayā na prārthitaṃ yataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-77a. “You are truly an expert in the perfect knowledge of spiritual matters. If the preceptor’s fee is proposed to be given to me by you, kindly explain to me that holy rite which is capable of subduing the distress.

*Kesidhvaja said:*

77b-78a. Why was my thornless kingdom not requested for by you? There is nothing more pleasing to Ksatriyas than the acquisition of a kingdom.

*Khandikya said:*

78b. О Kesidhvaja, you understand, why it (kingdom) has not been requested for by me?

## \|\| 1.46.79-81 \|\|

*rājyametadaśeṣeṇa yanna gṛghranti paṇḍitāḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyāṇāmayaṃ dharmo yatprajāparipālanam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*vadhaśca dharmayuddhena svarājyaparipanthinām \|*  
*yatrāśaktasya me doṣo naivāstyapakṛte tvayā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*bandhāyaiva bhavatyeṣā hyavidyā cākramojjhitā \|*  
*janmoparbhāgalipsārthamiyaṃ gajyaspṛhā mama \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. Learned men do not yearn much for the entire kingdom. It is the duty of the Ksatriyas to protect the subjects. Those who are inimical to their own kingdom are to be killed in an honest straightforward war. It was my fault, since I had been weak. There was no harm done by you. This Avidya will only be conducive to bondage though devoid of a direct onslaught. If I were to crave for the kingdom it is a desire for further births and their enjoyment.

## \|\| 1.46.82 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ dopajāneva dharmamevānurudhyate \|*  
*na yācñā kṣatrabandhūnāṃ dharmāyaitatsatāṃ matam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Begging and importunity may not be defective in the case of others. They follow only Dharma. It is the considered opinion of good (wise) persons that begging is not conducive to the religious duties (binding on) Ksattriyas.

## \|\| 1.46.83-85 \|\|

*ato na yācita rājyamavidyāntargataṃ tava \|*  
*rājyaṃ gṛdhnanti vidvāṃso mamatvākṛṣṭacetasaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*ahaṃmānamahya pānamadamattā na mādṛśāḥ \|*  
*keśidhvaja uvāca*  
*ahaṃ ca vidyayā mṛtyuṃ tartukāmaḥ karomi vai \|\| 84 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ yajñāṃśca vividhānbhoge puṇyakṣayaṃ tathā \|*  
*tadidaṃ te mano diṣṭyā vivekaiścaryatāṃ gatam \|\| 85 \|\|*

83-84a. Hence, the kingdom that belongs to you and is embedded in Avidya, is not requested for. Even the learned men whose minds are drawn towards Mamatva (sense of possession) yearn for a kingdom. Those who are inebriated due to the great intoxicating beverage of Ahammana (egotistic self-esteem) (crave for kingdom) but not people like me.

*Kesidhvaja said:*

84b-85. By means of Vidya, I am desirous of crossing (surmounting) death. I rule the kingdom and perform various sacrifices. By enjoyment of pleasures, the merit dwindles downr but fortunately your mind is richly endowed with the discriminating faculty.

## \|\| 1.46.86 \|\|

*śrūyatāṃ cāpyavidyāyāḥ svarūpaṃ kulanandana \|*  
*anātmanyātmabuddhiryā hyasve svaviṣayā matiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Listen, О delighter of thejanaka family, to the form or nature of Avidya. It is the misapprehension of the soul in objects which are not the soul. It is the mistaking of one’s own what is not one's own.

## \|\| 1.46.87 \|\|

*avidyātarusaṃnbhūtaṃ bījametaddvidhā sthitam \|*  
*pañcabhūtātmake dehe dehī mohatamovṛttaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. This is the seed, the outcome of the tree of Nescience stationed in two types. In the physical body consisting of the fine elements the embodied being is enveloped in delusory darkness.

## \|\| 1.46.88-89 \|\|

*ahametaditītyuñcaiḥ kurute kumatirmatim \|*  
*ākāśavāyvagrijalapṛthivībhiḥ pṛthak sthite \|\| 88 \|\|*

*ātmanyātmamayaṃ bhāvaṃ kaḥ karoti kalevare \|*  
*kalevaropabhogyaṃ hi gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. The man of crooked intellect has the deep conviction of ‘I am this’, with regard to the body severally composed of the five elements, viz. Ether, wind, fire, water and earth. Who will entertain the false conception that the body which is not the soul, is the soul? The objects of enjoyment such as the house, the field, etc. have indeed to be enjoyed through the body.

## \|\| 1.46.90 \|\|

*adehe hyātmani prājño mamedamiti manyate \|*  
*itthaṃ ca putrapautreṣu taddehotpāditeṣu ca \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Though the Atman is not the body, even the intelligent man thinks ‘This is mine'. It is thus that he feels in regard to sons and grandsons procreated by that body.

## \|\| 1.46.91 \|\|

*karoti paṇḍitaḥ svāmyamanātmani kalevare \|*  
*sarvadehopabhogāya kurute karma mānavaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Even the learned man feels the sense of ownership in regard to the body which is non-Atman. Every man performs every action for the enjoyment of the body.

## \|\| 1.46.92-98 \|\|

*dehaṃ cānyadyadā puṃsaḥsadā bandhāya tatparam \|*  
*mṛṇmayaṃ hi yathā gehaṃ lipyate vai mṛdaṃ bhasā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā deho mṛdaṃbholepanasthitiḥ \|*  
*pañcabhogātmakairbhogaiḥ pañcabhogātmakaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*āpyāyate yadi tataḥ puṃso garvo 'tra kiṅkṛtaḥ \|*  
*anekajanmasāhastraṃ sasārapadavīṃ vrajan \|\| 94 \|\|*

*mohaśramaṃ prayāto 'sau vāsanāreṇuguṇṭhitaḥ \|*  
*prakṣālyate yadā saumya reṇurjñānoṣṇavāriṇā \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tadā saṃsārapānthasya yāti mohaśramaḥ śamam \|*  
*mohaśrame śamaṃ yāte svacchāntaḥkaraṇaḥ pumān \|\| 96 \|\|*

*ananyātiśayādhāraḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamṛcchati \|*  
*nirvāṇamaya evāyamātmā jñānamayo 'malaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*duḥkhājñānamayā dharmāḥ prakṛteste tunātmanaḥ \|*  
*jalasya nāgninā saṃgaḥ sthālīsaṃgāttathāpi hi \|\| 98 \|\|*

92-93a. When the body itself is something other than the man, it is always interested in binding him. Just as the house made of the earth (a mud-house) is scrubbed, cleaned, and plastered with water and mud, similarly the physical body consisting of earth and other elements is maintained with smearing, etc. with mud and water.

93b-94a. If the body that consists of fivefold means of enjoyment is developed by the same fivefold means of enjoyment, what is it that the man can be proud of?

94b-96a. The individual soul goes through the path of worldly existence in the course of many thousands of births. He is enveloped by the dust of Vasanas, impressions of actions and experiences. He attains delusion and exhaustion. О gentle one, when the dust particles are washed off by means of hot water of perfect knowledge, the delusory exhaustion of the wayfarer in the path of worldly existence is subdued.

96b-97a. When delusion and exhaustion are subdued, the man's inner sense organ, the heart becomes clear. Getting a support that cannot be excelled by anything else, he attains the highest bliss of Salvation.

97b-98a. The Atman is of the nature of bliss. It is of the nature of perfect knowledge. It is free from impurities. Misery, ignorance and attributes that are their off-shoots belong to Prakrti and not to the Atman.

98b. Although water has no direct contact with fire, it has the indirect contact through the pot.

## \|\| 1.46.99-100 \|\|

*śabdodrekādikāndharmānkaroti hi yathā budhaḥ \|*  
*tathātmā prakṛteḥ saṃgādahaṃmānādidūṣitaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*bhajate prākṛtāndharmānnyastastaṃbho hi so 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*tadetatkathitaṃ bījamavidyāyā mayā tava \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Just as a wise person carries on his functions of uttering sound, etc., similarly the Atmany polluted with ego, etc. due to his contact with Prakrti resorts to dharmas (attributes) connected with Prakrti. When he sheds olf the ego, he is immutable and changeless. The seed (root-cause) of Avidya has thus been narrated to you by me.

## \|\| 1.46.101 \|\|

*kleśānāṃ ca kṣayakaraṃ yogādanyanna vidyate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. There is nothing other than Yoga that is destructive of miseries.

## Chapter 47. Exposition of the wav to realize the soul

## \|\| 1.47.1 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*etadadhyātmamānāḍhyaṃ vacaḥ keśidhvajasya saḥ \|*  
*khāṇḍikyo 'mṛtavacchratvā punarāha tamīrayan \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*

1\. On hearing these words of Kesidhvaja that consisted of an estimate of spiritual topics and that was like nector, Khandikya spoke again, urging him.

## \|\| 1.47.2 \|\|

*khāṇḍikya uvāca*  
*tad brūhi tvaṃ mahābhāga yogaṃ yogaviduttama \|*  
*vijñātayo gaśāstrārthastvamasyāṃ nimisaṃtatau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*Khandikya said:*  
2\. О highly blessed one, О the most excellent one among the knowers of Yoga, recount details of Yoga. In this dynasty of Nimi, you alone are the person who have understood the topics in the Yogasastra.

## \|\| 1.47.3 \|\|

*keśidhvaja uvāca*  
*yogasvarūpaṃ khāṇḍikya śrūyatāṃ gadato mama \|*  
*yatra sthito na cyavate prāpya brahmalayaṃ muniḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Kesidhvaja said :*  
3\. О Khandikya, even as I recount, may the nature of the Yoga be heard. A sage who is established in Yoga, docs not fall off after attaining merger into the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.47.4 \|\|

*mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ \|*  
*bandhasya viṣayāsaṃgi mukternirviṣayaṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation of men. When addicted to the sensual objects, it is the cause of bondage. When it is devoid of objects, it is the cause of liberation.

## \|\| 1.47.5 \|\|

*viṣayebhyaḥ samāhṛtya vijñānātmā budho manaḥ \|*  
*cintayenmuktaye tena brahmabhūtaṃ pareśvaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A wise man possessing discriminative knowledge, should withdraw the mind from the sense-objects and through it for the sake of salvation meditate on the Brahman, the greatest Isvara.

## \|\| 1.47.6 \|\|

*ātmabhāvaṃ nayettena tadbrīhyadhyāpanaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*vikāryamātmanaḥ śaktyā lohamākarṣako yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By means of the power of the Atman he should make the mind that is prone to aberration, meditate on the Brahman by infusing it with the nature of Atman, even as a magnet does it to a piece of iron.

## \|\| 1.47.7 \|\|

*ātmaprayatnasāpekṣā viśiṣṭā yā manogatiḥ \|*  
*tasyā brahmaṇi saṃyogo yoga ityabhidhīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The special movement of the mind that depends on the efforts of self is to conjoin to the Brahman and such union with the Brahman is called Yoga.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*evamatyantavaiśiṣṭyayuktadharmopalakṣaṇam \|*  
*yasya yogaḥ sa vai yogī mumukṣuramidhīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This includes the holy rites with special and peculiar characteristics. He who possesses Yoga is Yogin. He is called a Mumuksu (one desirous of liberation).

## \|\| 1.47.9 \|\|

*yogayuk prathamaṃ yogī yuñjamāno 'bhidhīyate \|*  
*viniṣyannasamādhistu parabrahmopalabdhimān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At the outset, the Yogin who practises Yoga is called Yunjamana. He who is called Vinispannasamadhi (of accomplished meditation) is one, who has attained the greatest Brahman.

## \|\| 1.47.10 \|\|

*yadyantarāyadoṣeṇa dūṣyate nāsya mānasam \|*  
*janmāntarairabhyasanānmuktiḥ pūrvasya jāyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If due to defects and obstacles his mind is not defiled, the former one attains salvation, thanks to the repeated practice in the course of many other births.

## \|\| 1.47.11 \|\|

*viniṣpannasamādhistu muktistatraiva janmani \|*  
*prāpnoti yogī yogāgnidagdhakarmacayo 'cirāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The latter one who is called Vinispannasamdahi (i.e. the knower of Brahman.) attains salvation in the very same birth. The Yogin attains everything ere long after burning the Karmans through the fire of Yoga.

## \|\| 1.47.12-14 \|\|

*brahmacaryamahiṃsāṃ ca satyāsteyāparigrahān \|*  
*seveta yogī niṣkāmo yigitāṃ svamano nayan \|\| 12 \|\|*

*svādhyāyaśaucasaṃtoṣatapāṃsi niyamānyamān \|*  
*kurvvīta brahmaṇi tathā parisminpravaṇaṃ manaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ete yamāśca niyamāḥ pañca pañcaprakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*viśiṣṭaphaladāḥ kāmyā niṣkāmānāṃ vimuktidāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Л Yogin shall practise five Yamas (restraints) and five Niyamas (observances): Celibacy, non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing and non-acceptance of monetary gifts (these are the Yamas). Svadhyaya (self-study of the Vedas), Sauca (purificatory rites), Santosa (contentment) Tapas (penance) and concentration of the mind on the great Atman. He must keep his mind devoid of lusts. Thus the five Yamas and the five Niyamas have been recounted. If people practise these with specific desires, they yield special benefits; if people practise these without desires they yield salvation.

## \|\| 1.47.15 \|\|

*evaṃ bhadrāsanādīnāṃ samāsthāya guṇairyutaḥ \|*  
*yamākhyairniyamākhyaiśca yuñjīta niyato yatiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus the ascetic should practise the good postures, (like Bhadrasana). He must be endowed with good qualities. He must perform the Yoga with what are called Yamas and Niyamas.

## \|\| 1.47.16 \|\|

*prāṇākhyamavalaṃbasthamabhyāsātkurute tu yat \|*  
*prāṇāyāmaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sabījo 'bīja eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If what arc called Pranas (vital airs) are restrained by practice, it should be known as Pranayama. It has two subdivisions: the Sabija (with seed) and the Abija (without seed).

## \|\| 1.47.17 \|\|

*paraspareṇābhibhavaṃ prāṇāpānau yadā nilau \|*  
*kurutaḥ sadvidhānena tṛtīyaḥ saṃyamāttayoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When the two vital Airs — Prana and Араnа, over- power each other (are merged together), by regulating them both by proper means, that is the third (variety of breath- control, viz., Kumbhaka).

## \|\| 1.47.18 \|\|

*tasya cāṃlabanavatsthūlaṃ rūpaṃ dviṣatpate \|*  
*ālaṃbanamanantasya yogino 'bhyasataḥ smṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О lord of the enemies, its form is as gross as its Alambana (support) the support of the Ananta (endless one) is obtained by the Yogin as he practises.

## \|\| 1.47.19 \|\|

*śabdādiṣvanuraktāni nigṛhyākṣāṇi yogavit \|*  
*kuryyāñcittānukārīṇi pratyāhāraparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The knower of the Yogas shall curb the sense organs drawn towards their objects such as sound, etc. Being devoted to and insistent on Pratyahara (withdrawal of the mind from sense-objects), he should make the senses (withdrawn from sense objects but) merging in the mind.

## \|\| 1.47.20 \|\|

*vaśyatā paramā tena jāyate niścalā tmanām \|*  
*indriyāṇāmavaśyaistairna yogī yogasādhakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If the sense-organs become steady, they become extremely submissive. If they are non-submissive, the Yogin cannot achieve Yoga.

## \|\| 1.47.21 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmena pavanaiḥ pratyāhareṇa cendriyaiḥ \|*  
*vaśīkṛtaistataḥ kuryātsthiraṃ cetaḥ śubhāśraye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After keeping the vital airs under control by means of Pranayama and the sense-organs by means of Pratyahara, the practitioner of Yoga shall make the mind stabilised in an auspicious support.

## \|\| 1.47.22 \|\|

*khāṇḍikya uvāca*  
*kathyatāṃ me mahābhāga cetaso yaḥ śubhāśrayaḥ \|*  
*yadādhāramaśeṣaṃ tu hṝnti doṣasamudbhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*Khandikya said:*  
22\. О highly blessed one, may it be mentioned to me, the auspicious support of the mind, by having which the mind dispels the outcome of defects entirely.

## \|\| 1.47.23 \|\|

*keśidhvaja uvāca*  
*āśrayaścetaso jñānin dvidhā tañca svarūpataḥ \|*  
*rūpaṃ mūrtamamūrtaṃ ca paraṃ cāparameva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*Kesidhvaja said:*  
23\. О wise one, the support of the mind is twofold, that too based on the form. The form may be embodied or unembodied; it may be Para (greater) or Apara (smaller).

## \|\| 1.47.24 \|\|

*trividhā bhāvanā rūpaṃ viśvametattridhocyate \|*  
*brahmākhyā karmasaṃjñā ca tathā caivobhayātmikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There are three types of Bhavanas (conceptions). The form and the universe is said to be threefold; The first is called Brahma bhavana, the other is known as Каrmа-bhavana and the third is of the nature of both Karma and Brahma.

## \|\| 1.47.25 \|\|

*karmabhāvātmikā hyekā brahmabhāvātmikāparā \|*  
*ubhayātmikā tathaivānyā trividhā bhāvabhāvanā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. One Bhavana is of the nature of Karman, the other one is of the nature of the Brahman, and the third one is of the nature of both. Thus there arc three types of Bhavabhavana (conception).

## \|\| 1.47.26 \|\|

*sanakādyā sadā jñānin brahmabhāvanayā yutāḥ \|*  
*karmabhāvanayā cānye devādyāḥ sthāvarāścarāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О wise one, Sanaka and others are always endowed with the Brahmabhavana. while the others, Devas etc. the mobile and immobile beings — all these arc endowed with Karmabhavana.

## \|\| 1.47.27 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhādiṣu ca brahmakarmātmikā dvidhā \|*  
*adhikārabodhayukteṣu vidyate bhāvabhāvanā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In Hiranyagarbha and others, the Bhavana is of the combined nature of the Brahman and Karman. In those invested with authority and with enlightenment, there is the Bhavabhavana.

## \|\| 1.47.28 \|\|

*akṣīṇeṣu samasteṣu viśeṣajñānakarmasu \|*  
*viśvametatparaṃ cānyadbhedabhinnadṛśāṃ nṛpa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О king, in the eyes of those who differentiate regarding that this is the Universe, that other is some thing diffe- ent, when all the particularised Karmans and knowledge are not diminished completely.

## \|\| 1.47.29 \|\|

*pratyastamitabhedaṃ yatsattāmātramagocaram \|*  
*vacasāmātmasaṃtodyaṃ tajjñānaṃ brahmasaṃjñitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. That knowledge is termed Brahman, the knowledge where the differences have completely vanished which is Existence alone, which is beyond the scope of words and which is self-produced.

## \|\| 1.47.30 \|\|

*tacca viṣṇoḥ paraṃ rūpamarūpasyājanasya ca \|*  
*viśvasvarūpaṃ vairūpyalakṣaṇaṃ paramātmanaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30 That is the great form of Visnu who is formless and unborn. The characteristics of the great Atman are contrary to the diversity of the form of the entire Universe.

## \|\| 1.47.31 \|\|

*na tadyogayujā śakyaṃ nṛpa cintayituṃ yataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthūlaṃ hare rūpaṃ cintyaṃ yañcakṣugocaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О king, since that (i.e. the greatest form of Visnu) cannot be meditated upon by one who practises Yoga, the gross form of Hari that could be seen by means of the eyes should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 1.47.32-35 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānvāsavo 'tha prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*maruto vasavo rudrā bhāskārāstārakā grahāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gandharvā yakṣadaityāśca sakalā devayotayaḥ \|*  
*manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ śailāsamudrāḥ sarito drumāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*bhūpa bhūtānyaśeṣāṇi bhūtānāṃ ye ca hetavaḥ \|*  
*pradhānādiviśeṣāntāścetanāñcetanātmakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ekapādaṃ dvipādaṃ ca bahupādamapādakam \|*  
*mūrttametaddhare rūpaṃ bhāvanātritayātmakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. All these constitute the universe, viz. — Lord Hiranyagarbha, Vasava (i.e. Indra), Prajapati, Maruts, Vasus, Rudras, Bhaskaras (i.e. Adityas), constellations, planets, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Daityas, Deva-Yonis (all kinds of divine and semi-divine beings), human beings, animals, mountains, oceans, rivers, trees, in fact. О king, all living beings, all those causes of the Bhutas namely those beginning with the Pradhana and ending with the Visesas, those who are sentient and non- sentient, the single-footed, the bipeds, the multi-footed, and the footless — all these are the embodied forms of Hari. They arc of the nature of Bhavanas of the three types.

## \|\| 1.47.36 \|\|

*etatsarvamidaṃ viṃśvaṃ jagadetañcarācaram \|*  
*parabrahmasvarūpasya viṣṇoḥ śaktisamanvitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All this universe, consisting of the mobile and immobile beings, is endowed with the potency of Visnu of the form of the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 1.47.37 \|\|

*viṣṇuśaktiḥ parā proktā kṣetrajñākhyā tathāparā \|*  
*avidyākarmasaṃjñānyā tṛtīyā śaktiriṣyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The greatest Sakti is said to be Visnu Sakti; the other Sakti is called Ksetrajna and the third Sakti is called Avidyakarman.

## \|\| 1.47.38-39 \|\|

*yeyaṃ kṣetrajñaśaktiḥ sā ceṣṭitā nṛpa karmajā \|*  
*asārabhūte saṃsāre proktā tatra mahāmate \|\| 38 \|\|*

*saṃsāratāpānakhilānavāpnotyanusaṃjñitān \|*  
*tayā tirohitatvāttu śaktiḥ kṣetrajña saṃjñitā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. О king, the Sakti that is called Ksetrajna is produced through Karmam. О highly intelligent one, in this worthless worldly existence, it is of the active nature. It attains the distresses of worldly existence. The individual soul is enveloped and concealed by this Sakti. Hence it is called Ksetrajna Sakti.

## \|\| 1.47.40 \|\|

*sarvabhūteṣu bhūpāla tāratamyena lakṣyate \|*  
*aprāṇavatsu khalvalpā sthāvareṣu tato 'dhikā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О king, this is seen in all living beings in varying degrees. In lifeless ones, it is very little and in the immobile beings it exists a little more than that.

## \|\| 1.47.41 \|\|

*sarīsṛpeṣu tebhyo 'nyāpyatiśaktyā patatriśu \|*  
*patatrribhyo mṛgāstebhyaḥ svaśaktyā paśavo 'dhikāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the reptiles, it is more than in the immobile beings. It is very powerful in birds. The deer are more powerful than the birds and the beasts are superior to the deer in their strength.

## \|\| 1.47.42 \|\|

*paśubhyo manujāścātiśaktyā puṃsaḥprabhāvitāḥ \|*  
*tebhyo 'pi nāgagandharvayakṣādyā devatā nṛpa \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Human beings are more powerful than beasts and men wield more power (among human beings). О king, superior to them are the Nagas, Gandharvas, Yaksas and other gods.

## \|\| 1.47.43-44 \|\|

*śakraḥ samastadevebhyastataścātiprajāpatiḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho 'pi tataḥ puṃsaḥ śaktyupalakṣitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*etānyaśeṣarūpāṇi tasya rūpāṇi pārthiva \|*  
*yatastacchaktiyogena yuktāni nabhasā yathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Indra is the most powerful among Devas and superior to him is Prajapati. Hiranyagarbha is more powerful than he. О king, all these are his forms, since they are invested with his potency as though with the Ether.

## \|\| 1.47.45 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñasya yogidhyeyaṃ mahāmate \|*  
*amṛrtaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ yatsadityucyate budhaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О highly intelligent one, the second unembodied form of the Brahman called Visnu is termed sat by the learned men. It is worthy of being meditated upon by the Yogins.

## \|\| 1.47.46 \|\|

*samastāḥ śaktayaścaitā nṛpa yatra pratiṣṭitāḥ \|*  
*nahi svarūparūpaṃ vai rūpamanyaddharermahat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О king, it is there that all these potencies are founded. These are not the real forms of Hari. It is another and very great.

## \|\| 1.47.47 \|\|

*samastaśaktirūpāṇi tatkaroti janeśvara \|*  
*devatiryaṅmanuṣyādiceṣṭāvanti svalīlayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О lord of men, he assumes the forms of all potencies (Saktis) having the activities of Devas, animals and human beings in his own sports.

## \|\| 1.47.48 \|\|

*jagatāmupakārāya tasya karmanimittajā \|*  
*ceṣṭā tasyāprameyasya vyāpinyavihitātmikā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. His activities based on the Karmans (of other beings) are for helping the worlds. The activities of the incomprehensible Being are pervasive and very benevolent.

## \|\| 1.47.49 \|\|

*tadrūpaṃ viśvarūpāya cintyaṃ yoga yujā nṛpa \|*  
*tasya hyātmaviśuddhyarthaṃ sarvakilbiṣanāśanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О king, that form of the deity, the embodiment of the Universe must be meditated upon for the purification of the soul. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.47.50 \|\|

*yathāgnirūddhataśikhaḥ kakṣaṃ dahati sānilaḥ \|*  
*tathā cittasthito viṣṇuryogināṃ sarvakilbiṣam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Just as the fire with shooting flames in collaboration with the wind burns down heaps of dry grass and wood, so also Visnu, abiding in the minds of Yogins destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.47.51 \|\|

*tasmātsamastaśaktīnāmāndyānte tatra cetasaḥ \|*  
*kurvīta saṃsthitaṃ sādhu vijñeyā śuddhalakṣaṇā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. (Defective) Hence, this potency is the first and foremost of all potencies. The devotee shall keep it in the mind. If it is duly stabilised it should be known as one with pure characteristics (?)

## \|\| 1.47.52 \|\|

*śubhāṃśrayaḥ sacittasya sarvagasya tathātmanaḥ \|*  
*tribhāvabhāvanātīto muktaye yogināṃ nṛpa \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It is the auspicious support of the Atman that is present everywhere and is accompanied by the mind. It is beyond the three Bhavabhavanas (emotional conceptions). О king, it is conducive to the salvation of the Yogins.

## \|\| 1.47.53 \|\|

*anye tu puruṣavyāghra cetaso ye vyāpā8yāḥ \|*  
*aśuddhāste samastāstu devādyāḥ karmayonayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О tiger among men, all other supports of the mind, Devas and others with Karmans as their source of origin, are impure.

## \|\| 1.47.54 \|\|

*mūrttaṃ bhagavato rūpaṃ sarvāpāśrayanispṛhaḥ \|*  
*eṣā vai dhāraṇā jñeyā yañcitaṃ tatra dhāryate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. (Defective) One who has no desire for any of these supports shall meditate on the embodied form of the Lord. This is to be known as Dharana since the mind is concentrated there.

## \|\| 1.47.55 \|\|

*tatra mūrttaṃ hare rūpaṃ yādṛk cintyaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*tacchrūyatā manādhāre dhāraṇā nopapadyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О ruler of men, may it be heard of what nature should Hari’s form be, for being meditated upon. There cannot be a Dharana (retention) without a support.

## \|\| 1.47.56-60 \|\|

*prasannacāruvadanaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam \|*  
*sukapolaṃ suvistīrṇaṃ lalāṭaphalakojjvam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*samakarṇāṃsavinya stacārukarṇopabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*kambugrīvaṃ suvistīrṇaśrīvatsāṃkitavakṣasam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*balitriṃbhāginā bhugnanābhinā codareṇa vai \|*  
*pralaṃbāṣṭabhujaṃ viṣṇumatha vāpi caturbhujam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*samasthitorujaghanaṃ susthirāṅghrikarāṃbujaṃm \|*  
*cintayedbūhyabhūtaṃ taṃ pītanirmalavāsasam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kirīṭacārukeyūrakaṭakādivibhūṣitam \|*  
*śārṅgaśaṅkhagadākhaḍgaprakāśavalayāñcitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

56-60. The form shall be — one with beautiful and delighted face; with the eyes large like the petals of a lotus; fine cheeks with a wide and brilliant forehead; its earrings placed equally between ears and shoulders; the neck resembling a conch shell, with the chest marked with Srivatsa; the three folds in the skin in the curved umbilical region and the belly appearing beautiful; Visnu may be conceived as having eight long arms or four arms, his thighs large and symmetrical, firm lotus-like hands and feet clad in pure yellow robes; bedecked in coronet, beautiful bracelets, armlets, etc. He is surrounded by a halo and is wielding the Sarnga bow, a Sankha, a mace and a sword. He is to be meditated thus as the Brahman also.

## \|\| 1.47.61 \|\|

*cintayettanmayo yogī samādhāyātmamānasam \|*  
*tāvadyāvad dṛḍhībhūtā tatraiva nṛpa dhāraṇā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The Yogin shall identify himself with the deity, after concentrating his mind and meditate upon Visnu, О king, until the Dharana becomes firmly fixed therein.

## \|\| 1.47.62 \|\|

*vadatastiṣṭato yadvā svecchayā karma kurvataḥ \|*  
*nāpayāti yadā cittātsiddhāṃ manyeta tāṃ tadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Whether the devotee is talking something or standing by or is engaged in some voluntary activity, the retention (Dharana) does not vanish from the mind. In that case he should consider that (i.e. Dharana) as achieved.

## \|\| 1.47.63 \|\|

*tataḥ śaṅkhagadācakraśārṅgādi rahitaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*cintaye dbhagavadrūpaṃ praśāntaṃ sākṣasūtrakam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thereafter, the sensible man shall meditate upon the Lord’s form without Sankha, Gada, Cakra, Sarnga (bow), etc., but it is tranquil with the rosary in the hands.

## \|\| 1.47.64 \|\|

*sā yadā dhāraṇā tadvadavasthānavatī tataḥ \|*  
*kirīṭakeyūramukhairbhūṣaṇai rahitaṃ smaret \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. When this Dharana is more or less stabilised, one shall meditate upon the Lord’s form without such ornaments as coronet, bracelets, etc.

## \|\| 1.47.65 \|\|

*tadekāvayavaṃ caivaṃ cetasā hi punarbudhaḥ \|*  
*kuryāttato 'vayavini prāṇidhānaparo bhavet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then the sensible man should mentally dwell on that single limb; and subsequently he shall become engrossed in the one (Lord) that has the limbs.

## \|\| 1.47.66 \|\|

*tadrūpapratyaye caikasaṃnatiścānyaniḥspṛhā \|*  
*taddhyānaṃ prathamairaṅgaiḥ ṣaṅbhirniṣpādyate nṛpa \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. At the perception of that form (there shall be) one obeisance and absence of desire for other objects. О king, his meditation is fulfilled by the first six Angas (of meditation).

## \|\| 1.47.67 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ kalpanāhīnaṃ svarūpagrahaṇaṃ hi yat \|*  
*manasā dhyānaniṣpādyaṃ samādhiḥ so 'bhidhīyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. When his perception of the form of the deity without any fanciful conception becomes the outcome of mental meditation, it is called Samadhi.

## \|\| 1.47.68 \|\|

*vijñānaṃ prāpakaṃ prāpye paraṃ brahmaṇi pārthiva \|*  
*prāpaṇīyastathaivātmā prakṣīṇāśeṣabhāvanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О king, in regard to the thing to be achieved i.e. the great Brahman, that which makes the achievement possible is Vijnana (perfect knowledge). That which is to be attained to is the Atman whose Bhavanas have been dispelled.

## \|\| 1.47.69 \|\|

*kṣetrajñakaraṇījñānaṃ karaṇaṃ tena tasya tat \|*  
*niṣpādya muktikāryaṃ vai kṛtakṛtyo nivartate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. It is the perfect knowledge of the Ksetrajna and the sense-organs therefore. After facilitating the achievement of the task of liberation, it has its purpose achieved and it recedes.

## \|\| 1.47.70 \|\|

*tadbhāvabhāvanāpannastato 'sau paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*bhavatyabhedī bhedaśca tasyājñānakṛto bhavet \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then the devotee shall achieve the emotional identity with the great Atman, he shall become non-diflerent from him. The difference is caused by the ignorance about him.

## \|\| 1.47.71 \|\|

*vibhedajanake jñāne nāśa mātyantikaṃ gate \|*  
*ātmano brahmaṇābhedaṃ saṃmataṃ kaḥ kariṣyati \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When Ajnana, the cause of differentiation, is utterly dispelled who will agree to this that the Atman is different from the Brahman?

## \|\| 1.47.72 \|\|

*ityuktaste mayā yogaḥ khāṇḍikya paripṛcchataḥ \|*  
*saṃkṣepavistarābhyāṃ tu kimanyatkriyatāṃ tava \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. О Khandikya, thus partly in detail and partly in brief, the Yoga has been recounted to you, since you have been asking me about it. What more can I do for you?

## \|\| 1.47.73 \|\|

*khāṇḍikya uvāca*  
*kathito yogasadbhāvaḥ sarvameva kṛtaṃ mama \|*  
*tavopadeśātsakalo naṣṭaścittamalo mama \|\| 73 \|\|*

*Khandikya said:*  
73\. The excellent nature of the Yoga has been expounded by you. Everything has been done for me. Thanks to your instructions, the impurity in my mind has been entirely annihilated.

## \|\| 1.47.74 \|\|

*mameti yanmayā proktamasadetanna cānyathā \|*  
*naredraṃ gadituṃ śakyamapi vijñeyavedabhiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. What has been called by me as ‘Mine’ is incorrect and not otherwise. Even by those who know what should be known, О king, it cannot be mentioned otherwise.

## \|\| 1.47.75 \|\|

*ahaṃ mametyavidyeyaṃ vyavahārastathānayoḥ \|*  
*paramārthastva saṃlāpyo vacasāṃ gocaro na yaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The feelings ‘I’ and ‘My’ are the outcome of Avidya so also their utterance. The truth which is inexpressible is beyond the scope of words.

## \|\| 1.47.76 \|\|

*tadguccha śreyase sarvaṃ mamaitadbhavatā kṛtam \|*  
*yadvimuktiparo yogaḥ proktaḥ keśidvajāvyayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О Kesidhvaja, go, for the attainment of further welfare. Everything has been done for me by you since the unchanging Yoga devoted to salvation lias been explained to me.

## \|\| 1.47.77 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*yathārhapūjayā tena khāṇḍikyena sa pūjitaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma puraṃ brahmaṃstataḥ keśidhvajo nṛpaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
77\. Thereafter, having been worshipped duly by Khandikya, king Kesidhvaja returned to his capital duly worshipped by Khandikya, О Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.47.78 \|\|

*khāṇḍikyo 'pi sutaṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ yogasiddhaye \|*  
*viśālāmagamatkṛṣṇe samāveśitamānasaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Khandikya made his son the king. With his mind, dedicated to Krsna, he went to Visala for the achievement of mastery over Yoga.

## \|\| 1.47.79 \|\|

*sa tatraikāntiko bhūtvā yamādiguṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇvākhye nirmale brahmaṇyavāpa nṛpatirlayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. He was endowed with the qualities of Yama, etc. He was solely engrossed in deep meditation. The king attained dissolution by merging himself into the pure Brahman called Visnu.

## \|\| 1.47.80 \|\|

*keśidhvajo 'pi muktayarthaṃ svakarmakṣapaṇonmukhaḥ \|*  
*bubhuje viṣayānkarma cakre cānabhisaṃdhitam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. For the sake of liberation and eager to dispel his Karmans, he enjoyed the sensual pleasures and performed holy rites without any desire in view.

## \|\| 1.47.81 \|\|

*sa kalyāṇopabhogaiśca kṣīṇapāpo 'malastataḥ \|*  
*avāpa siddhimatyantatritāpakṣapaṇīṃ mune \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O sage, by means of auspicious enjoyment of pleasures, he wiped off all sins and became free from impurities. He attained Siddhi that utterly quelled the three kinds of Тaра (misery).

## \|\| 1.47.82 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛṣṭavān \|*  
*tāpatrayacikitsārthaṃ kimanyatkathayāmi te \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thus everything that you had asked me has been recounted to you. What else shall I narrate to you for dispell ing the three types of distress?

## Chapter 48. The story of Bharata

## \|\| 1.48.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*śrutaṃ mayā mahāmāga tāpatrayacikitsitam \|*  
*tathāpi me mano bhrāntaṃ na sthitiṃ labhateṃ'jasā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Narada said:*

1\. О blessed one, the antidote for the three types of distress has been heard by me. Still my mind is confused. It does not attain proper stability, easily.

## \|\| 1.48.2 \|\|

*ātmavyatikramaṃ brahmandurjanācaritaṃ katham \|*  
*soḍhuṃ śakyeta manujaistanmamākhyāhi mānada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Brahmana, how can the sinful transgression against one’s own self committed by wicked men, be tolerated by men? О bestower of honour, recount it to me.

## \|\| 1.48.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tacchrṛtvā nāradenoktaṃ brahmaputraḥ sanandanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca harṣasaṃyuktaḥ smaranbhagharataceṣṭitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*Suta said:*

3\. On hearing what has been spoken by Narada, Sunandana, the son of Brahma, remembered the activities of Bharata. With great delight he said:

## \|\| 1.48.4 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*atra te kathayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*yaṃ śrutvā tvanmano bhrāntamāsthānaṃ labhate bhūśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
4\. In this context, I shall tell you the ancient traditional story on hearing which your confused mind shall attain great stability.

## \|\| 1.48.5 \|\|

*āsītpurā muniśreṣṭha bharato nāma bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*ārṣabho yasya nāmnedaṃ bhārataṃ khaṇḍamucyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О excellent sage, formerly, there was a king named Bharata. He was the son of Rsabha. This sub-continent is named Bharatakhanda after him.

## \|\| 1.48.6 \|\|

*sa rājā prāptarājyastu pitṛpaitāmahaṃ kramāt \|*  
*pālayāmāsa dharmeṇa pitṛbadrañjayan prajāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After attaining the kingdom belonging to his father and grandfather in due succession, he protected it righteously. He delighted the subjects like their father.

## \|\| 1.48.7 \|\|

*rddaje ca vividhairyajñairbhagavantamadhokṣajam \|*  
*sarvadevātmakaṃ dhyāyannānākarmasu tanmatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He performed various kinds of sacrifices and worshipped Lord Visnu, the embodiment of all Devas. He meditated upon him with the mind centering round him in the course of carrying out different activities.

## \|\| 1.48.8 \|\|

*tataḥ samutpādya sutānvirakto viṣayeṣu saḥ \|*  
*muktvā rājyaṃ yayau vidvānpulastyapuhāśramam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He procreated sons. He was unattached to sensuous objects. The learned king left the kingdom and went to thr hermitage of Pulastya and Pulaha.

## \|\| 1.48.9-22 \|\|

*śālagrāmaṃ mahākṣetraṃ mumukṣujanasevitam \|*  
*tatrāsau tāpaso tāpaso bhūtvā viṣṇorārādhanaṃ mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

*cakāra bhaktibhāvena yathālabdhasaparyayā \|*  
*nityaṃ prātaḥ samāplutya nirmale 'bhali nārada \|\| 10 \|\|*

*upatiṣṭedraviṃ bhaktyā gṛṇanbrahmākṣaraṃ param \|*  
*athāśrame samāgatya vāsudevaṃ jagatpatim \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pūjayanprayato bhūtvā bhaktiprasarasaṃplutaḥ \|*  
*sacaikadā mahābhāgaḥ snātvā prātaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*cakranadyāṃ japaṃstasthau muhurtatrayamaṃbuni \|*  
*athājagāma tattīraṃ jalaṃ pātuṃ pipāsitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āsannapsavā brahmannaikaiva hiṇī vanāt \|*  
*tataḥ samabhavattatra pītaprāye jale tayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*siṃhasya nādaḥ sumahān sarvaprāṇibhayaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sā siṃhasannādādutplutā nimnagātaṭam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*atyuñcārohaṇenāsyā nadyāṃ garbhaḥ papāta ha \|*  
*tamuhyamānaṃ vegena vīcimālāpariplutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jagrāha bharato garbhātpatitaṃ mṛgapotakam \|*  
*garbhapracyutiduḥkhena prottuṅgākraṇena ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*munīndra sā tu hariṇī nipapāta mamāra ca \|*  
*hariṇīṃ tāṃ vilokyātha vipannāṃ nṛpatāpasaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mṛgapotaṃ samāgṛhya svamāśramamupāgataḥ \|*  
*cakārānudinaṃ cāsau mṛgapotasya vai nṛpaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*poṣaṇaṃ puṣyamāṇaśca sa tena vavṛdhe mune \|*  
*cacārāśramaparyantaṃ tṛṇāni gahaneṣu saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dūraṃ gatvā ca śārdūlatrāsādabhyāyayau punaḥ \|*  
*prātargatvādidūraṃ ca sāyamāyātyathāśramam \|\| 22 \|\|*

9-10a. He went to the great holy centre Salagrama frequented by people desirous of liberation. О sage, he became an ascetic and performed the propitiation of Visnu with great devotion, rendering service(unto the Lord) with things obtained by him.

10b- 11a. О Narada, every day in the morning he plunged into the pure clear water and prayed to the Sun with devotion muttering the Supreme syllable expressive of the Brahman (i.e. Оm or Gayatri).

11b-13a. He then returned to the hermitage. With great purity and devotional piety, he worshipped Vasudeva the Lord of the universe with the materials of worship such as sacrificial twigs, Kusa grass, clay, etc. brought by himself. He worshipped with fruits, flowers, leaves of Tulasi and clear water.

13b-14a. On one occasion, that highly blessed king took his ablution in the River Cakra. With great purity and attention he stayed in the water performing Japa for three Muhurtas.

14b-15a. О Brahmana, a thirsty hind who was about to be delivered of a young one, came to the bank from the forest, in order to drink water.

15b-16a. As she had almost completed drinking the water, there arose the great roaring sound of a lion which was frightful to all living beings.

16b-17a. On hearing the roaring sound of the lion, the hind leapt to the bank of the river. While she was climbing the steep side of the bank, the foetus fell down into the river.

17b-18a. Bharata caught hold of the fawn that fell off from its mother’s womb and was carried away by the forceful current and the waves of the river.

18b-19a. О leading sage, due to the misery on account of the fall of the foetus and the steep ascent, that hind fell down dead.

19b-22. On seeing the hind dead in the tragic circumstances, the royal saint took up the fawn and brought it to his hermitage. The king nurtured the young one of the hind day by day. О sage, nourished by him, it duly grew up. At first the fawn used to graze at the outskirts of the hermitage. Then it went to the forest, it went far into the forest but, afraid of tigers, it returned soon. After some time it used to go very far into the forest in the morning and return to the hermitage in the evening.

## \|\| 1.48.23-26 \|\|

*punaśca bharatasyābhūdāśramasyoṭajāntare \|*  
*tasyatasminmṛge dūrasamīpaparivartini \|\| 23 \|\|*

*āsīñcetaḥ samāsaktaṃ na tathā hyacyute mune \|*  
*vimuktarājyatanayaḥ projjhitāśeṣabāndhavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mamatva sa cakāroñcaistasminhariṇapotake \|*  
*kiṃ vṛkaibhakṣito vyāghnaiḥ kiṃ siṃhena nipātitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*cirāyamāṇe niṣkānte tasyāsīditi mānasam \|*  
*prītiprasannavadanaḥ pārśvasthe cābhavanmṛge \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-24a. Bharata kept it inside the hut in the hermitage during nights. His mind became highly involved with the deer-fawn that used to be near him or away from him by turns. О sage, his mind was not so much drawn towards Visnu.

24b-25a. Remember that he had abandoned his kingdom and even sons; that he had eschewed all connections with his kinsmen. Still he had great affection (feeling of kinship) with the fawn.

25b-26. When the fawn was away from the hermitage for a long time, his mind was agitated by various doubts such as, “Has it been devoured by the wolves?” “Have tigers seized upon it?” “Has it been struck down by the lion?” When the fawn was by his side his face was bright with delight and love.

## \|\| 1.48.27 \|\|

*samādhibhaṅgastasyāsīnmamatvākṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*kālena gacchatā so 'tha kālaṃ cakre mahīpatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. As his mind was attracted by the feelings of ‘myness’, his *Samadhis* (trances and concentration) became disturbed often. After some time the king died.

## \|\| 1.48.28 \|\|

*piteva sāstraṃ putreṇa mṛgapotena vīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*mṛgameva tadādrākṣīttyajanprāṇānasāvapi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the time of passing away, he was looking at the fawn. Like a father by the son, he was looked at by the fawn with tears in its eyes.

## \|\| 1.48.29 \|\|

*mṛgo babhūva sa mune tādṛśīṃ bhāvanāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*jāti smaratvādudvignaḥ saṃsārasya dvijottama \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О sage, since his mental fancy was of that nature, he was born as a deer — О excellent Brahmana. Since he had the faculty of remembering previous births, he became unenamoured of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.48.30 \|\|

*vihāya mātaraṃ bhūyaḥ śālagrāmamupāyayau \|*  
*śuṣkaistṛṇaistathā parṇaiḥ sa kurvannātmapoṣaṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He left off his mother (i.e. the mind) and went to Salagrama. He nourished himself by means of dry leaves and grass.

## \|\| 1.48.31 \|\|

*mṛgatvahetubhūtasya karmaṇo niṣkṛtiṃ yayau \|*  
*tatra cotsṛṣṭadeho 'sau jajñe jātismaro dvijaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus he expiated for the evil action that had been the cause of his birth as a fawn. Having left off his body, he was born again as a Brahmana who had the faculty of remembering his previous births.

## \|\| 1.48.32 \|\|

*sadācāravatāṃ śuddhe yāgināṃ pravare kule \|*  
*sarvavijñāna saṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstrārthatattvavit \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He was born in a leading, pure family of Yogins of good conduct. He was richly endowed with all knowledge. He was conversant with all principles and topics in the scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.48.33-34 \|\|

*apaśyatsa muniśreṣṭhaḥ svātmānaṃ prakṛteḥ param \|*  
*ātmanodhigatajñānāddvevādīni mahāmune \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarvabhūtānyabhe dena dadarśa sa mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*na papāṭha guruproktaṃ kṛtopanayanaḥ śrutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. That excellent sage perceived his own Atman beyond Prakriti. О great sage, thanks to the knowledge of Atman that he had acquired, that highly intelligent one saw Devas and others, nay, all living beings, without any difference. He was invested with the sacred thread, but he did not repeat the Vedic text as uttered by his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.48.35 \|\|

*na dadarśa ca karmāṇi śāstrāṇi jagṛhe na ca \|*  
*ukto 'pi bahuśaḥ kiñcijjaṇḍa vākyamabhāṣata \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He did not observe holy rites. He did not learn scriptural texts. When he was addressed many times, he made some stupid irrational statement.

## \|\| 1.48.36 \|\|

*tadapyasaṃskāraguṇaṃ grāmabhāṣoktisaṃyutam \|*  
*apaddhastavapuḥ so 'pi malināṃbaradhṛṅ mune \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Even that speech lacked in qualities of cultural refinement. It was often uttered in vulgar rustic language. О sage, accursed in body, he was always clad in dirty clothes.

## \|\| 1.48.37-40 \|\|

*klinnadantāntaraḥ sarvaiḥ paribhūtaḥ sa nāgaraiḥ \|*  
*saṃmānena parāṃ hāniṃ yogarddheḥ kurute yataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*janenāvamato yogī yogasiddhiṃ ca vindati \|*  
*tasmāñcareta vai yogī satāṃ dharmamadūṣayan \|\| 38 \|\|*

*janā yathāvamanyeyurgaccheyurnaiva saṃgatim \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhavacanaṃ vicintyetthaṃ mahāmatiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa jaḍonmattākṛtiṃ jane \|*  
*bhuṅkte kulmāṣavaṭakān śākaṃ tranyaphalaṃ kaṇān \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. Saliva oozed from the interstices of his teeth. He was always harassed by citizens. He used to remember the words of Hiranyagarbha (or Brahma) as follows: “Excess of respect affects the prosperity of Yoga. A Yogin dishonoured by the people achieves Yogic power. Hence, a Yogin should perform holy rites of good men without defiling them. He should so perform them that the people should begin to disrespect him and avoid associating with him.” The highly intelligent one thus thought of the words of Hiranyagarbha, and showed himself to the public as one with sluggish features and of unsound mind. He regularly ate cakes made of Kulmasa grain, vegetables and fruits from the forests.

## \|\| 1.48.41-46 \|\|

*yadyadāpnoti sa bahūnatti vai kālasaṃbhavam \|*  
*pitaryuparate so 'tha bhrātṛbhrātṛvyabāndhavaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kāritaḥ kṣetrakarmādi kadannāhārapoṣitaḥ \|*  
*sarūkṣapīnāvayavo jaḍakārī ca karmaṇi \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sarvalokopakaraṇaṃ babhūvāhāravetanaḥ \|*  
*taṃ tādṛśamasaṃskāraṃ viprākṛtiviceṣṭitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kṣattā sauvīrarājyasya viṣṭiyogyamamanyata \|*  
*sa rājā śibikārūḍho gantuṃ kṛtamatirdvija \|\| 44 \|\|*

*babhūvekṣumatītīre kapilarṣervarāśramam \|*  
*śreyaḥ kimatra saṃsāre duḥkhaprāye nṛṇāmiti \|\| 45 \|\|*

*praṣṭuṃ taṃ mokṣadharmajñaṃ kapilākhyaṃ mahāmunim \|*  
*uvāha śibikāmasya kṣatturvacanacoditaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

41-42a. He ate whatever he got and whenever it happened. When his father passed away, he was compelled to work in the fields by his brothers, nephews and other kinsmen.

42b-43a. All his limbs became stout, though he was fed on rotten food. He became a sluggish worker. With food for his wages, he helped the whole world.

43b-44a. (On seeing) him so unrefined but having the features and activities of a Brahmana, a charioteer of the Sauvira king considered him worthy of being taken as an unpaid labourer.

44b-45a. О Brahmana, that king was seated in a palanquin. He was thinking of going to the excellent hermitage of sage Kapila on the banks of Iksumati river.

45b-46. He wanted to ask the great sage Kapila who was well learned in the topic of virtues leading to salvation, as follows — “What is it that is conducive to the welfare of men in this world which is mostly full of miseries.” On being urged by the words of the charioteer, he carried his palanquin.

## \|\| 1.48.47 \|\|

*nṛṇāṃ viṣṭigṛhītānāmanyeṣāṃ so 'pi madhyagaḥ \|*  
*gṛhīto viṣṭinā vipra sarvajñānaikabhājanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Brahmana, he, the sole receptacle of all knowledge, was taken as an unpaid labourer. He was one among other men who too were unpaid labourers.

## \|\| 1.48.48 \|\|

*jātismaro 'sau pāpasya kṣayakāma uvāha tām \|*  
*yayau jaḍagatistatra yugamātrāvalokanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Endowed with the faculty of remembering events of past lives, he bore the palanquin as he was desirous of wiping off his sins. He, the most excellent one among the intelligent men, slowly walked ahead gazing at the yoke of the palanquin.

## \|\| 1.48.49-52 \|\|

*kurvanmatimatāṃ śreṣṭhaste tvanye tvaritaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*vilokya nṛpatiḥ so 'tha viṣamaṃ śibikāgatam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kimetadityāha samaṃ gamyatāṃ śibikāvahāḥ \|*  
*punastathaiva śibikāṃ vilokya viṣamāṃ hasan \|\| 50 \|\|*

*rājovāca*  
*kiṃ śrānto 'syalpamadhvānaṃ tvayoḍhā śibikā mama \|*  
*kimāyāsasaho na tvaṃ pīvā nāsi nirīkṣyase \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-50a. The other bearers walked quickly. On observing the irregular movement of the palanquin, the king said — “О palanquin-bearers! What is this? Go ahead at even step.”

50b-51. Again the movement of the palanquin was irregular. The king laughed and asked them, “what is this? You are moving otherwise!” When the king (mildly rebuked) them many times, the palanquin-bearers said — “This fellow does not thus move quickly.”

*The king said:*

52\. “Are you tired? You have borne the palanquin only for a short distance. Arc you not used to strenuous work? Aren’t you seen a bulky fellow?”

## \|\| 1.48.53 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*nāhaṃ pīvā na caivoḍhā śibikā bhavato mayā \|*  
*na śrānto 'smi na cāyāso voḍhānyo 'sti mahīpate \|\| 53 \|\|*

*The Brahmana said:*

53\. “I am not stout. Your palanquin has not been borne by me. I am not tired. I have no fatigue or trouble. О lord of the earth, the bearer is another one.”

## \|\| 1.48.54 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate pīvātvadyāpi śibikā tvayi \|*  
*śramaśca bhāro dvahane bhavatyeva hi dehinām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*The king said:*  
54\. “You are actually seen to be stout. The palanquin is still above you. Fatigue in carrying a load occurs to embodied beings (as they have to exert and carry the load).

## \|\| 1.48.55 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*pratyakṣaṃ bhavatā bhūpa yaddṛṣṭaṃ mama tadvada \|*  
*balavānabalaśceti vācyaṃ paścādviśeṣaṇam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*The Brahmana said:*  
55\. “O king, tell me what you have directly perceived. The qualifications of strong or weak may be added afterwards.

## \|\| 1.48.56 \|\|

*tvayoḍhā śibikā ceti tvayyadyāpi ca saṃsthitā \|*  
*mithyā tadapyatra bhavān śṛṇotu vacanaṃ mama \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. This is a false statement — “The palanquin is borne by you. The palanquin is still above you.” All this is false, О Sir, listen to my words now.

## \|\| 1.48.57 \|\|

*bhūmau pādayugaṃ cātha jaṅghe pādadvaye sthite \|*  
*ūru jaṅghādvayāvasthau tadādhāraṃ tathodaram \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The two feet are on the ground. The shanks rest on the pair of feet. The thighs are on the pair of shanks. The belly has the support of the pair of thighs and hips.

## \|\| 1.48.58 \|\|

*vakṣasthalaṃ tathā bāhū skandhau codarasaṃsthitau \|*  
*skandhāśritayeṃ śibikā mamādhāro 'tra kiṅkṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The chest, the arms and the shoulders rest on the belly. This palanquin is supported by the shoulders. How can it be said that I am the support?

## \|\| 1.48.59 \|\|

*śibikāyāṃ sthitaṃ cedaṃ dehaṃ tvadupalakṣitam \|*  
*tatra tvamahamapyatretyucyate cedamanyathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The body designated as ‘you’ is stationed within the palanquin. ‘‘You are there. I am here”. This is also a wrongly put statement.

## \|\| 1.48.60 \|\|

*ahaṃ tvaṃ ca tathānye ca bhūtairuhyāśca pārthiva \|*  
*guṇapravāhapatito bhūtavargo 'pi yātyayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О king, you, I, and the others are to be borne by the elements; the whole class of living beings (and the elements) are fallen in the current of the Gunas.

## \|\| 1.48.61 \|\|

*karmavaśyā guṇaścaite sattvādyāḥ pṛthivīpate \|*  
*avidyāsaṃcitaṃ karmataścāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. О Lord of the earth, these — sattva and other Gunas are subject to the control of Karmans. The Karman accumulated due to ignorance is present in all creatures

## \|\| 1.48.62 \|\|

*ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraḥ śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛte paraḥ \|*  
*pravṛddhyapacayau na sta ekasyākhilajantuṣu \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The Atman is pure, imperishable and quiescent. It is devoid of Gunas. It is beyond Prakrti. The Atman alone abides in all creatures but he has no increase (fatness) or decrease (slimness).

## \|\| 1.48.63 \|\|

*yadā nopacayastasya nacaivāpacayo nṛpa \|*  
*tadāpi bāliśo 'si tvaṃ kayā yuktyā tvayeritam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О king, when there is neither increase nor decrease, it was childish ignorance (that prompted you to say I am stout). On what basis was it uttered by you?

## \|\| 1.48.64-66 \|\|

*bhūpādajaṅghākaṭyūrujaṭharādiṣu saṃsthitā \|*  
*śibikeyaṃ yadā skandhe tadā bhāraḥ samastvayā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tathānyajantubhirbhūpa śibikoḍhāna kevalam \|*  
*śailadrumagṛhottho 'pi pṛthivīsaṃbhavo 'pi ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*yathā puṃsaḥ pṛthagbhāvaḥ prākṛtaiḥ karaṇairnṛpa \|*  
*soḍhavyaḥ sumahānbhāraḥ katamo nṛpa te mayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. (Defective) This palanquin rests equally on the ground pair of feet, shanks, thighs, hips, belly and other things as well as on the shoulders. When the burden is equal, О king, the palanquin is not borne by you or the other creatures alone. A great burden originating from mountains, trees or houses nay, from the whole earth has to be borne by you and by me. As the Purusa has distinctness (separate existence) from the sense organs which are the products of Prakrti what heavy load is to be borne by me, О King. О King the Purusa is separated from the sense organs produced from Prakrti \[?\]

## \|\| 1.48.67 \|\|

*yaddravyo śibikā ceyaṃ taddravyo bhūtasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*bhavato me 'khilasyāsya samatvenopabṛṃhitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The material that constitutes this palanpuin is a conglomeration of all elements, grown large equally in regard to you, me or the entire world.

## \|\| 1.48.68 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*evamuktvābhavaṃnmaunī sa vahañśibikāṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*so 'pi rājāvatīryorvyāṃ tatpādau jagṛhe tvaran \|\| 68 \|\|*

*Sanandana said:*  
68\. After saying this the Brahmanawho was bearing the palanquin became silent. Thereupon the king hurriedly got down to the ground and touched his feet.

## \|\| 1.48.69 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*bho bho visṛjya śibikāṃ prasādaṃ kuru me dvija \|*  
*kathyatāṃ ko bhavānatra jālmarupadharaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*The King said: —*  
69\. О Brahmin, be pleased with ine. Leave off the palanquin. May it be revealed to me who you are, in the guise of a low and degraded man.

## \|\| 1.48.70 \|\|

*yo bhavānyadapatyaṃ vā yadāgamanakāraṇam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vidvanmahyaṃ śuśrūṣave tvayā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. I am eager to serve you. О learned one, may everything be mentioned by you, viz — who you are, whose son you are and what the reason for coming here is?

## \|\| 1.48.71-73 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*śrūyatāṃ ko 'hamityetadvaktuṃ bhūpa na śakyate \|*  
*upayoganimittaṃ ca sarvatrāgamanakriyā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sukhaduḥkhopabhogau tu tau dehādyupapādakau \|*  
*dharmādharmodbhavau bhoktuṃ janturdehādimṛcchati \|\| 72 \|\|*

*sarvasyaiva hi bhūpāla jantoḥ sarvatra kāraṇam \|*  
*dharmādharmauṃ yatastasmātkāraṇaṃ pṛcchyate kutaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*The Brahmin said: —*  
71-73. May it be heard, О king. It cannot he explained who I am. Everywhere the action of arrival is prompted by some utility \[enjoyment of pleasures\]. The enjoyment of pleasures and the experience of miseries is accomplished through the body, etc. A creature attains the body, etc. in order to experience the outcome of Dharma and Adharma, О king, everywhere, in the case of every creature the reason is Dharma or Adharma. Hence, how is it that the reason is being asked?

## \|\| 1.48.74 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*dharmādharmauṃ na saṃdehaḥ sarvakāryeṣu kāraṇam \|*  
*upabhoganimittaṃ ca dehāddehāntarāgamaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*The king said: —*  
74\. There is no doubt in this that Dharma or Adharma is the cause of all effects. The transmigration from one body to another is for experiencing pleasure or pain.

## \|\| 1.48.75 \|\|

*yattvetadbhavatā proktaṃ ko 'hamityetadātmanaḥ \|*  
*vaktuṃ na śakyate śrotuṃ tanmameccā pravartate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. As to your statement that it cannot be said who am I in regard to the Atman I wish to slate as follows.

## \|\| 1.48.76 \|\|

*yo 'sti yo 'hamiti brahmankathaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate \|*  
*ātmanyeva na doṣāya śabdo 'hamiti yo dvijā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О brahmin, How is it that it is not possible to say “I am he who exists. О twice-born, the word Aham (I) refers to the Atman and not to the body.

## \|\| 1.48.77 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*śabdo 'hamiti doṣāya nātmanyevaṃ tathaiva tat \|*
