685-686a. Procedure for the march. The king should first offer oblations of sesame in the (sacred) fire and then worship the lord of direction (in which he is to proceed). He should then pay obeisance to the deities and brahmanas and start after receiving their blessings. (The worship of the respective deities) should be according to the prescribed specifications of complexion, dress, unguents etc. and with the chanting of their mantras.

686b-687a. Indra should be worshipped as mounted on (his white elephant) Airavata, resplendent with (his consort) Saci, as holding the thunderbolt in his hand, as of golden complexion and as adorned with divine ornaments.

687b-688a. Agni should be worshipped (in an idol having seven hands, seven tongues, six faces, seated on a goat, with his consort Svaha, red-complexioned, and holding the раШа twig and sacrificial ladle as weapons.

688b-689a. Yama should be worshipped as holding the rod as a weapon, with red eyes, mounted on a buffalo, seated with his consort Syamala, red-complexioned, looking up and beneficent.

689b-690a. Nirrti should be worshipped as holding the sword and shield, blue-complexioned, mounted on a man as his vehicle, with raised hair, odd-eyed, with a high neck and lordly.

690b-691a. Varuna should be worshipped as holding the serpent-rope, yellow-complexioned, seated on a whale, with his consort Kalika and adorned with gem-set ornaments.

691b-692a. Vayu should be worshipped as the life of living beings, two-armed, holding a rod and riding a black antelope with his consort Anjanl.

692b-693a. Kubera should be worshipped as riding a horse, holding a pitcher in his hand, two-armed, golden-head, accompanied by his consort Citralekha and lording over the (semidivine) Yaksas and Gandharvas.

693b-694a. (Isana) should be worshipped as holding the bow Pinaka in his hand, seated on the bull, with his consort Gauri, as the best of all, fair-complexioned with the crescent moon on his crest and with his sacred thread formed by a serpent.

694b-695a. Procedure when march is delayed’ In case a king cannot move off immediately for some reason or other, he should (still) make a start along with his flag, weapons, missiles and vehicles (exactly at the auspicious time determined as above).

695b-696a, The place up to which he should march (before stopping) shall be two hundred

696b-697a. The king should not stay for more than seven days at one place and the others five days. In case of a longer delay (the ceremony of) starting should be made at another (auspicious) lagna (to be determined as before).

697b-698a. If there is untimely rain accompanied by lightning and thunder, or the three types of (major) natural calamities, the king should not move forward for three days.

698b-699. Omens at the time of march. The sounds of ratnakuiya, she-jackal, crow and pigeon and of ruru, parrot etc. (if heard from) the left and of potaki and the bird bharadvaja from the right (are auspicious).

## \|\| 1.56.700 \|\|

*cāṣaṃ tyaktvā catuṣpāttu śubhadāvāmato matāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ tyaktvā prayāṇe tu kṛkalāsena vīkṣitaḥ \|\| 700 \|\|*

700\. The forest-crow is inauspicious, while four-legged animals on the right arc auspicious. And, so is being stared at by a chameleon, but not by one of black colour.

## \|\| 1.56.701 \|\|

*vārāhaśaśagodhāstu sarpāṇāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubham \|*  
*hṛtekṣaṇaṃ neṣṭamevāvyapatyayaṃ kapiṛkṣayoḥ \|\| 701 \|\|*

701\. Hearing the boar, hare, godha, cat and serpent being spoken about is auspicious but the sound made by them or seeing them is not auspicious. It is the contrary in the case of the monkey and the bear (which can be seen and heard but not spoken about).

## \|\| 1.56.702 \|\|

*mayūracchāganakulacāṣapārāvatāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭamātreṇa yātrāyāṃ vyastaṃ sarvaṃ praveśane \|\| 702 \|\|*

702\. The peacock, deer, mongoose, wild, crow and pigeon are auspicious at being seen at the commencement of a journey; the reverse is the case when one returns (home).

## \|\| 1.56.703 \|\|

*yātrāsiddhirbhaveddṛṣṭe śaverādanavajite \|*  
*praveśe rodanayutaḥ śavaḥ śavapradastathā \|\| 703 \|\|*

703\. A corpse, without any mourning, if seen (at the commencement of a journey), will fulfil the objective of the journey. On the other hand, a corpse, accompanied by mourning, seen on the return, will turn one into a corpse.

## \|\| 1.56.704-709 \|\|

*patitaklībajaṭilamattavāntauṣadhādibhiḥ \|*  
*abhyaktavasāsthicarmāṅgāradāruṇarogibhiḥ \|\| 704 \|\|*

*guḍakārpāsalavaṇaripupraśnatṛṇoragaiḥ \|*  
*vandhyākuñjakakāṣāyamuktakeśabubhukṣitaiḥ \|\| 705 \|\|*

*prayāṇasamaye nagnairddṛṣṭaiḥ siddhirna jāyate \|*  
*prajvalāgnīnsuturaganṛpāsanapurāṅganāḥ \|\| 706 \|\|*

*gandhapuṣaapākṣatacchatracāmarāndolikaṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyekṣuphalamṛtsnānnamadhvājyadadhigodayāḥ \|\| 707 \|\|*

*madyamāṃsasudhādhautavastraśaṅkhavṛṣadhvajāḥ \|*  
*puṇyastrīpuṇyakalaśaratnabhṛṅgāragodvijāḥ \|\| 708 \|\|*

*bherīmṛdaṅgapaṭahaghaṇṭāvīṇādiniḥsvanāḥ \|*  
*vedamaṅgalaghoṣāḥ syuḥ yā yināṃ kāryasiddhidāḥ \|\| 709 \|\|*

704-706a. The following, if seen at the time of setting out, will destroy the aim (of the journey): An outcaste, eunuch, bearded, drunk, vomit, medicine, one bathed in oil, fat, bone, skin, charcoal, diseased, molasses, cotton, salt, threat from an enemy, thirst, serpent, sterile woman, dwarf, saffron-clothed, clean shaven, hungry and the naked.

706b-709. On the other hand, the following seen/heard (at the start of a journey) will fulfil its aim: Blazing fire, horse, throne, brahmanas, unguents, flowers, sanctified rice grain, umbrella, chowrie, swing, king, foodstuff, sugcrcane, fruits, bengal gram, cooked rice, honey, ghee, curd, cow, bull, fish, flesh, wine, white cloth, sound of conch, flags, courtesans, filled pitchers of water, gem, gold vessel, mirror, the sound of cattle drums, mrdangas, pa\[ahasy bells and lutes, and the auspicious chant of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.56.710 \|\|

*ādau viruddhaśakunaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāyīṣṭadevatām \|*  
*smṛtvā dvitīye viprāṇāṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ nivartayet \|\| 710 \|\|*

710\. If one secs an adverse omen for once, he might remember his personal deity (and proceed); if he secs it for a second time he might worship the brahmins (and proceed); if he sees it for the third) he must return home.

## \|\| 1.56.711 \|\|

*sarvadikṣukṣutaṃ neṣṭaṃ gokṣutaṃ nidhanapradam \|*  
*aphalaṃ yadbālavṛddharogipainasikaiḥ kṛtam \|\| 711 \|\|*

711\. Sneezing heard from any side is inauspicious and the sneezing of cows is deadly. However, it is harmless if done by children, old men, diseased persons and persons suffering from cold.

## \|\| 1.56.712 \|\|

*parastrī dvijadevasvaṃ tatrapṛśeddiggajāśvakān \|*  
*hanyātparapuraprāpto na strīrnityaṃ nirāyudhān \|\| 712 \|\|*

712\. Binding on the conqueror. The conqueror who has taken the enemy’s capital should not touch another’s woman, nor the wealth of brahmins and gods, nor the elephants, and horses, nor the distressed and the disarmed.120 RETURN TO THE CAPITAL

## \|\| 1.56.713 \|\|

*ādau saumyāyane kāryaṃnavavāstupraveśanam \|*  
*vidhāya pūrvadivase vāstupūjābalikriyām \|\| 713 \|\|*

713\. Occupation of a new residence. The first occupation of a newly built house should be done during ihe northward course of the Sun and after worshipping and offering oblations to the Building, the previous day.

## \|\| 1.56.714 \|\|

*māghaphaālgunavaiśākhajyeṣṭamāseṣu śobhanam \|*  
*praveśo madhyamo jñeyaḥ saumyakārtikamāsayoḥ \|\| 714 \|\|*

714\. (Occupying the house) during the months of Magha, Phalguna, Vaisakha and Jyestha is auspicious, while it is middling in the months of Margaslrsa (Saumya) and Karitika:

## \|\| 1.56.715 \|\|

*śaśījyānteṣu varuṇatvāṣṭramitrasthiroḍuṣu \|*  
*śubhaḥ prevaśo devejyaśukrayorddṛśyamānayoḥ \|\| 715 \|\|*

715\. Occupation (of the house) is auspicious in the asterisms of Mrgasiras (Sasi), Pusya (Ijya), Revatl, Satabhisak (Vanina), Cilra (Tvasfra), Anuradha (Milra) and the fixed asterisms, (wsh.,Uttaraphalguni, Uttarasatfha, Uuarabhadrapada and Rohini), (care being taken to see that) Jupiter and Venus are visible (.sh., not set).

## \|\| 1.56.716 \|\|

*vyarkāravāre tithiṣu riktāmāvarjiteṣu ca \|*  
*divā vā yadi vā rātrau praveśo maṅgalapradaḥ \|\| 716 \|\|*

716\. Occupation is auspicious both during day and night, on week-days other than Sundays and Tuesdays, and tithis othei than the empty lunar days (rikta, viz., the 4th, 9th and 14th) and new moon.

## \|\| 1.56.717 \|\|

*candratārābalopete pūrvāhne śobhane dine \|*  
*sthiralagne sthirāṃśe ca naidhane śuddhisaṃyute \|\| 717 \|\|*

717\. Thus, at an auspicious time, on an auspicious day, in the forenoon, when both the Moon and the asterisms are strong,180 in a fixed lagna (i.ewhen the‘fixed’ signs, Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius, are rising), and in a ‘fixed’ division of that lagna, not affected by deadly indications, characterised by blemishlessness.

## \|\| 1.56.718 \|\|

*trikoṇakendrasaṃsthaiś saumyaistryāyārigaiḥ paraiḥ \|*  
*lagrāntyāṣṭamaṣaṣṭasthavarjitena dviyāṃśunā \|\| 718 \|\|*

718\. When the benefic planets occupy the trikonas and the kendras, while the others occupy the 3rd, 11th and 6th houses, when the Moon occupies a house other than the 6th and the 8th from lagna.

## \|\| 1.56.719 \|\|

*karturṣā janmabhe lagne tābhyāmupacaye 'pi vā \|*  
*praveśalgne syāmṛddhiranyabheśokaniḥsvatā \|\| 719 \|\|*

719\. In the birth asterism or birth-sign of the master or when they are in exaltation, the occupation will result in prosperity, otherwise misery and penury will result.

## \|\| 1.56.720 \|\|

*darśanīya gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ vidhidhairmaṅgalasvanaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvārkaṃ vāmato vidvānbhṛṅgāraṃ cāgrato viśet \|\| 720 \|\|*

720\. The wise man shall enter the charming and attractive house, accompanied by variegated and auspicious sounds (of music and instrumentation), with the Sun on the left and with a pot of water carried in front. PROGNOSTICATION OF RAIN

## \|\| 1.56.721-722 \|\|

*varṣāpraveśe śaśini jalarāśigatepi vā \|*  
*kendrage vā śuklapakṣe cātivṛṣṭiḥ śubhekṣite \|\| 721 \|\|*

*alpavṛṣṭiḥ pāpadṛṣṭe prāvṛṭkāle 'cirādbhavet \|*  
*candraśceddhārgave sarvamevaṃvidha guṇānvite \|\| 722 \|\|*

721-722a. If (when the possibility of rains is considered) it is the advent of the rainy season, the Moon being in a ‘watery sign’ (Jala-rdfi)11, in the kendra if it is the bright fortnight and is aspected by benefic planets, there would be heavy rains. On the other hand, if the aspection (of the Moon) is by malefic planets and if it is summer, there would only be a little rain.

722b. The same will occur also when Venus is characterised by the different things mentioned for the Moon.

## \|\| 1.56.723 \|\|

*prāvṛṣīnduḥ sitātsaptarāśigaḥ śubhavīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*mandātrrikoṇasaptastho yadi vā vṛddhikṛdbhavet \|\| 723 \|\|*

723\. If in the rainy season, the Moon occupies the seventh house from Venus and is aspected by benefic planets, or in the trikona or 7th house from Saturn, there would be (immediate) rain.

## \|\| 1.56.724 \|\|

*sadyo vṛṣṭikaraḥ śukro yadā budhasamīpagaḥ \|*  
*tayorṃmadhyagate bhānau bhavedṣṭivināśanam \|\| 724 \|\|*

724\. Venus will produce immediate rain if it is near Mercury. If, however, the Sun occurs between the two, there would be no rain.

## \|\| 1.56.725 \|\|

*maghādipañcadhiṣṇyasthaḥ pūrve svātitraye pare \|*  
*pravarṣaṇaṃ bhṛguḥ kuryādviparīte na varṣaṇam \|\| 725 \|\|*

725\. Venus in the five asterisms beginning with Magha (.., Magha, Purvaphalguni, Uttaraphalguni, Hasta and Citra) will cause rain, if the three asterisms Svati, Visakha and Anuradha follow (i.e., in the regular motion of the planet). If otherwise (».., in the retrograde motion of the planet), there would be no rains.

## \|\| 1.56.726 \|\|

*purataḥ pṛṣṭato bhānorgrahā yadi samīpagāḥ \|*  
*tadā vṛṣṭiṃ prakurvanti na te cetpratilomagāḥ \|\| 726 \|\|*

726\. Planets near the Sun cause rains when they are just before or behind the Sun (in their regular motion), but not in their retrograde motion.

## \|\| 1.56.727 \|\|

*vāmabhāgasthitaḥ śukro vṛṣṭikṛccettu yāmyagaḥ \|*  
*udayāsteṣu vṛṣṭiḥ syādbhānorārdrāpraveśane \|\| 727 \|\|*

727\. Venus coursing on the left will bring about rains if it is moving south. There would be rains in the morning and in the evening as the Sun enters the asterism Ardra.

## \|\| 1.56.728 \|\|

*saṃdhyayoḥ sasyavṛddhiḥ syātsarvasaṃpannṛṇānniśi \|*  
*stokavṛṣṭiranarghaḥ syādavṛṣṭiḥ sasyasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 728 \|\|*

728\. There would be increase in vegetation during the twilights (due to rains falling at these times) and there would be prosperity on all counts for people during nights. Light rains will then reduce prices and no rains will increase crops.

## \|\| 1.56.729 \|\|

*ādrodayegrabhinnā cadbhavediti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*candrejye jñetha vā śukre kendrenbītirvinaśyati \|\| 729 \|\|*

729\. If there is a division in the rising of Ardra, there will, no doubt, be a calamity. If, however, the Moon, Jupiter or Venus is in a kendra, the calamity will not occur.

## \|\| 1.56.730 \|\|

*pūrvāṣāḍhā gato bhānurjīmūtaiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*varṣatyārdrādimṛlāntaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pratyahaṃ tathā \|\| 730 \|\|*

730\. The Sun occupying the asterism Purvasadha and surrounded by clouds, will cause noticeable rains on all days from Ardra to Mula.

## \|\| 1.56.731-741 \|\|

*vṛṣṭiścetpauṣṇabheṃ tasmāddaśarkṣeṣu na varṣati \|*  
*siṃhe bhinne kujo vṛṣṭirabhinne karkaṭe tathā \|\| 731 \|\|*

*kanyodaye prabhinne cetsarvadā vṛṣṭiruttama \|*  
*ahirbudhnyaṃ pūrvaśasyaṃ paraśasyā ca revatī \|\| 732 \|\|*

*bharaṇī sarvasasyā ca sarvanāśāya cāśvinī \|*  
*guroḥ saptamarā tisthaḥ pratyaggo bhṛgujo yadā \|\| 733 \|\|*

*tadātivarṣaṇaṃ bhūri prāvṛṭkāle balojjhite \|*  
*āsaptamarkṣaṃśaśinaḥ pariveśagatottarā \|\| 734 \|\|*

*vidyutprapūrṇamaṇḍūkāsvanāvṛṣṭirbhavettadā \|*  
*yadāpratyaṅnatā maghāḥ khasaptopari saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 735 \|\|*

*patanti dakṣiṇasthā yebhavedvṛṣṭistadācirāt \|*  
*nakhairlikhantomārjārāścāvaniṃ lohasaṃyute \|\| 736 \|\|*

*rathyāyāṃ setubandhāḥ syurbālānāṃ vṛṣṭihetavaḥ \|*  
*pipīlikāśreṇayaśchinnāḥ khadyotā bahavastadā \|\| 737 \|\|*

*drumādirohaḥ sarpāṇāṃ prītirdurvṛṣṭisūcakāḥ \|*  
*udayāstamaye kāle vivarṇor'ketha vā śaśī \|\| 738 \|\|*

*madhuvarṇo 'tivāyuścedativṛṣṭirbhavettadā \|*  
*prāṅmukhasya tu kūrmasya navāṅgeṣu dharāmimām \|\| 739 \|\|*

*vibhajya navadhā khaṇḍe maṇḍalāni pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*antarvedāśca ṣāñcālastasyedaṃ nābhimaṇḍalam \|\| 740 \|\|*

*prācyā māgadhalāṭotthā deśāstanmukhamaṇḍalam \|*  
*strīkaliṅgakirātākhyā deśāstadbāhumaṇḍalam \|\| 741 \|\|*

731-732a. If there had been rains on Revatl (Paufnabka), there would be no rains for ten days. If Simha is divided, how can there be rains and if Karkafa is divided, how can there be no rains. If the rise of Kanya is divided there would always be plenty of rains.

732b-733a. (Rains in) Uttarabhadrapada are indicative of vegetation in the beginning and Revatl of vegetation in the end. Rains in BharanI are indicative of vegetation throughout, while ASvini is indicative of destruction of all vegetation.

733b-734a. When Venus is in the 7th sign ahead of Jupiter, there would be heavy rains, especially if the rainy season is at its height.

734b-735a. If a halo (Jmivcsha) occurs around the Moon, extending to seven asterisms (from it), there would be rains, heavily interspersed with lightning and accompanied by the croaking of frogs.

735b-736a. If the clouds in the centre of the sky are inclined towards the west or towards the south, there would be rains shortly.

736b-737a. Cats pawing the ground, encrustations occur- ring on metal and children building bunds on the pathways are indicative of rains.

737b-738a. Moving rows of ants, profusion of glow-worms, serpents climbing up trees arc indicative of (immediate rains).

738b-739a. The Sun and the Moon, at rising or setting, appearing dull or coloured like honey and if there be severe wind at that time, heavy showers would follow, immediately. (KURMAVIBHAGA: DIVISION OF THE GLOBE)

739b-740a. This land (of India) has been laid out as if divided into nine sections \[mantfala) and set in a clockwise direction on nine parts (of the body)of a tortoise facing east.

740b-741. The (central) navel region consists of Antar- veda and Pancala. The face-region, in the east, is formed by the region forming Magadha and Lata. The (right) fore-leg is formed by Stri-(rajya), Kalihga and Kirata.

## \|\| 1.56.742 \|\|

*avantī draviḍā bhillā deśāstatpārśvamaṇḍalam \|*  
*gauḍakaiṅkaṇaśālvāndhrapauḍrastatpādamaṇḍalam \|\| 742 \|\|*

742\. The (right) flank region consists of Avanii, Dravida and Bhilla. The (right) hind leg region is constituted of by the countries of Gautfa, Korikana, Salva, Andhra, and Paumlra.

## \|\| 1.56.743 \|\|

*siṃdhukāśimahārāṣṭrasaurāṣṭrāḥ pucchamaṇḍalam \|*  
*pulindacīnayavanagurjarāḥ pādamaṇḍalam \|\| 743 \|\|*

743\. The tail-region is formed by Sindhu, Kasi, Maha- rastra and Saurastra. The (left) foot-region consists of Pulinda, Cina, Yavana and Gurjara.

## \|\| 1.56.744 \|\|

*kurukāśmīramādreyamatsyāstatpārśvamaṇḍalam \|*  
*khasāṃgavaṅgabāhlīkaṃ kāṃbojāḥ pāṇimaṇḍalam \|\| 744 \|\|*

744\. The (left) Hank region is made up of Kuru, Kasmlra, Madreya and Matsya. The (left) foreleg region is constituted of by Khasa, Anga, Vanga, Valhlka and Kamboja.132

## \|\| 1.56.745 \|\|

*kṛttikādīni dhiṣṇyāni trīṇi triṇi kramānnyaset \|*  
*nābhyādiṣu navāṅgeṣu pāpairduṣṭaṃ śubhaiḥ śubham \|\| 745 \|\|*

745\. In the nine parts commencing with the navel place three asterisms each, beginning with Krttika. When any of these stars is aspected by malefic planets, there would be misery (for the region represented by it), and when aspected by bcnefic planets, (there would be happiness for the region). (UTPATA: POR10TUOUS PHENOMENA)

## \|\| 1.56.746 \|\|

*devatā yatra nṛtyanti patanti prajvalanti ca \|*  
*muhū rudanti gāyanti prasvidyanti hasaṃti ca \|\| 746 \|\|*

746\. (Portentuous phenomena are said to present themselves) when (idols of) deities (in temples) frequently dance, fall and burn; weep, sing, sweat and laugh;

## \|\| 1.56.747 \|\|

*vamantyagniṃ tathā dhūmaṃ snehaṃ raktaṃ payo jalam \|*  
*adhomukhādhitiṣṭanti sthānātsthānaṃ vrajanti ca \|\| 747 \|\|*

747\. Vomit fire, fumes, oil, blood and water; stand upside down and move from place to place.

## \|\| 1.56.748 \|\|

*evamādyā hi dṛśyante vikārāḥ pratimāsu ca \|*  
*gandharvanagaraṃ caiva divā nakṣatradarśanam \|\| 748 \|\|*

748\. Such freak occurrences seen in the idols of deities (constitute portentuous phenomena). So also are mansions in the air (gandharva-nagara), asterisms becoming visible during day;

## \|\| 1.56.749 \|\|

*mahotkāpatanaṃ kāṣṭatṛṇaraktapravarṣaṇam \|*  
*gāndharvaṃ dehadigdhūmaṃ bhūmikaṃpaṃ divā niśi \|\| 749 \|\|*

749 The fall of a mighty meteor and the raining of twigs, grass and blood, atmospheric smoke in mansions in the air, and earthquake during day or night;

## \|\| 1.56.750 \|\|

*anagnau ca sphuliṅgāśca jvalanaṃ ca vinendhanam \|*  
*niśīndracāpamaṇḍūkaṃ śikhare śvetavāyasaḥ \|\| 750 \|\|*

750\. Sparks without fire and flames without fuel, rainbow during night, mantfukafikhara, and white crow;

## \|\| 1.56.751 \|\|

*dṛśyante visphuliṅgāśca gogajāśvoṣṭragātrataḥ \|*  
*jantavo dvitriśiraso jāyante vāpi yoniṣu \|\| 751 \|\|*

751\. Sparks of fire emanating from cows, elephants, horses and camels, two-headed and three-headed animals being born from unnatural wombs.

## \|\| 1.56.752-758 \|\|

*prātaḥ sūryāścatasṛṣu hyarditāyugapadraveḥ \|*  
*jambūkagrāmasaṃvāsaḥ ketūnāṃ ca pradarśanam \|\| 752 \|\|*

*kākānāmākulaṃ rātrau kapotānāṃ divā yadi \|*  
*akāle puṣpitā vṛkṣā dṛśyante phalitā yadi \|\| 753 \|\|*

*kāryaṃ tacchedanaṃ tatra tataḥ śāntirmanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*evamādyā mahotpātā bahavaḥ sthānanāśadā \|\| 754 \|\|*

*kecinmṛtyupradāḥ kecicchatrubhyaśca bhayapradāḥ \|*  
*madhyādbhayaṃ yaśo mṛtyuḥ kṣayaḥ kīrtiḥ sukhāsukham \|\| 755 \|\|*

*aisvaryaṃ dhanahāniṃ ca madhucchannaṃ ca vālmikam \|*  
*ityādiṣu ca sarveṣūtpāteṣu dvijasattama \|\| 756 \|\|*

*śāntiṃ kuryātprayatnena kalpoktavidhinā śubham \|*  
*ityetatkathitaṃ vipra jyautiṣaṃ te samāsataḥ \|\| 757 \|\|*

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi cchandaḥ śāstramanuttamam \|\| 758 \|\|*

752-753a. Mock-suns in the four directions along with the (real) Sun; jackals inhabiting villages; and the appearance of comets; and agitated flock of crows, in the night and pigeons during the day.

753b-754a. So also trees flowering out of time and seen bearing fruits likewise; they should first be cut down by the wise and then rites for averting the evil foretold should be performed.

754b-755a. Many are such portentuous phenomena which are destructive in the different regions. Some bring about death and some others fear from enemies.

755b-756a. An anthill covered with honey (at the nine places, viz.,) the top (and the eight directions from the east) is indicative, respectively, of fear, fame, death, depletion, reputation, happiness, misery, prosperity and loss of wealth.

756b-757a. О great brahmin! at the occurrence of all such portentuous phenomena, (if of an inauspicious nature), rites for averting evil should be performed with care as specified by the ritual texts.

757b-758. О brahmin! Thus has been narrated to you the discipline of Jyotisham all its aspects. I shall now set out the exquisite science of metrics.

## Chapter 57. The Description of Prosody

## \|\| 1.57.1 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ cāpi chando dvividhamucyate \|*  
*mātrāvarṇavibhedena taccāpi dvividhaṃ punaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanandana said:

1\. Metres are of two varieties: (1) those of the Vedas (2) those of secular or classical literature. Again metres can be divided into two classes: Mdtra-Vrtta — a metre regulated by the number of prosodial instants in it and (2) a metre regulated by number of syllables it contains.

## \|\| 1.57.2 \|\|

*mayau rasau tajau bhanau gururlaghurapidvija \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ chandasi proktāśchandaḥśāstraviśāradaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. MA and ТА (standing for Magana and Tagana. These and others are explained in later verses,) RA and SA, ТА and JA, BHA and NA, the GURU (i.e. long) and the LAGHU (short), О Brahmana, these are said to be the basis in prosody as explained by experts in the science of Prosody.

## \|\| 1.57.3 \|\|

*sarvago magaṇaḥ prokto mukhalo yagaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*madhyalo ragaṇaśvaiva prāntyagaḥ sagaṇo mataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Magana is that set of three syllables where all are long ones (— — — Mollosus). Tagana is that set of three syllables where the first syllable is short (v — — Bacchius). The Ragana is that set of three syllables), in which the middle one is short (— v — Amphimacer), and the Sagana is that set of three syllables in which the last one is long (vv — Anapestus).

## \|\| 1.57.4 \|\|

*tagaṇoṃ'talaghuḥ khyāto madhyago jo bhaādigaḥ \|*  
*trilaghurnagaṇaḥ proktastrikā varṇagaṇā mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Tagana is that set in which the last one is short (— — v Antibacchius). The Jagana is that set of three syllables in which the middle one is long (v — v Amphibrachys) and the Bhagana is that set of three syllables in which the first one is long (— v v Dactylus.) The Nagana is said to consist of three short syllables (v v v Tribrachys). Osage, the Ganas or sets of syllables contain three in each.

## \|\| 1.57.5-6 \|\|

*caturlāstu gaṇāḥ pañca proktā āryādisaṃmatāḥ \|*  
*saṃyogaśca visargaścānusvāro laghutaḥ paraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*laghordīrghatvamākhyāti dīrgho go lo laghurmataḥ \|*  
*pādaścaturthabhāgaḥ syādvicchedoyatirucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Five Gaijas are mentioned with four short syllables. They are admitted in the Лгуй and other metres. If a conjunct consonant, the aspirate Visarga or the Anusvara comes after a short syllable that short syllable is considered to be prosodially long. The abbreviated term for a long syllable is GU and that for a short syllable is LA. A fourth of a verse is called a Pdda (foot). A break in the middle is called a Tati (Caesura).

## \|\| 1.57.7 \|\|

*samamarddhasamaṃ vṛttaṃ viṣamaṃ cāpi nārada \|*  
*tulyalakṣaṇataḥ pādacatuṣke samamucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О Narada, a Vrtta (metre) is classified into three: Sama, Ardhasama and Vifama. If all the four feet have the same characteristics, the metre is called Sama.

## \|\| 1.57.8 \|\|

*āditrike dvicaturthe samamarddhasamaṃ tatam \|*

8\. If the first and the third feet have one set of characteristics (i.e. combination and arrangement of the Ganas) and the second and the fourth feet have another set of characteristics, the metre is called Ardhasama. If all the four feet have different characteristics it is called Vifama.

14-15. These are the names of the different metres. By means of Prastdra1 they may have many combinations. In the Prastdra for each metre, first take one foot with all long syllables. Beneath the first long syllable put a short syllable. All the remaining syllables must be as they are above. In the next line do like-wise until all of them become short.

*naṣṭāṅkārddhe same laḥ syādvipam saiva sorddhagaḥ \|*

*kṛtvā sekānvadaitsaṃkhyāmiti prāhuḥ purāvidaḥ \|*

*uddiṣṭāṅkasamāhāraḥ saiko vā janayedimām \|*  
*saṃkhyaiva dviguṇaikonā sadbhiradhvā prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. (These verses form a group requiring arithmetical calculations. An explanatory translation with illustrations is necessary in stead of a literal one. Here Prastdra, Naffa\> Uddifta, Ekadyyadi-la-ga-kriya, Sahkhydna and Adhva-yoga are the technical terms in Sk. Prosody.2 These are retained as the explanation of these terms will be more useful than their word- to-word rendering.) Prastdra means UA representation or enumeration of all the possible combinations of certain given numbers or of short or long syllables in a metre”. If a Prastdra is Naffa (lost) and needs ascertainment of the ‘lost Vrtta, the procedure is called Nafpa-prtayaya. The variety (Bheda) of Prastara is determined in the following way: If the JVflj/a number be even, one should record a Laghu (v) for it. The number is to be halved and if it be still even, one is to record another Laghu (v) for it. If the Naffa number is odd (not divisible by 2), record a Guru (—) for it. Add one to that odd number and divide it half. If that number be uneven, record a Guru (—) for it. This should be continued till the number of syllables in that foot is completed.3 If the type or Bheda of a Prastara is known but not the number of its variety Uddiftdiika)y it is ascertained as follows: In the Uddifta, there are signs of Laghu and Guru (in a certain arrangement). One should write the number 1 over the head of the first syllable and go on doubling the numbers over the heads of the subsequent syllables. One should add number 1 to the number above the Laghu (v) syllable and that is the number of the Uddifta or variety of that Prastdra. (For example: We want to know the number of a variety of a four-syllabled metre with the following distribution of Laghu- Guru syllables in its metrical foot: 12 4 8 Guru Guru Guru Laghu / As the number 8 is above the head of Laghu, we should add 1 to it. And 8 + 1 9 is the Uddisfahka of the variety of the metre.) The next two processes are a bit complicated. But briefly they are as.follows:) Eka-dvyadi-la-ga-kriyd is the method of ascertaining the complete number of Prastaras of a particular Chanda. It is called calculation or Safikhydna. We hereby know the number of Laghus and Gurus in a Prastdra. Thus in a Prastara of a metre with four-syllabled foot, there will be the following varieties: No. (1) All the four syllables Laghu... 1 (2) One Guru + three Laghu syllables... 4 (3) Two Gurus + Two Laghus... 6 (4) Three Gurus + One Laghu... 4 (5) All four Guru Syllables... 1 Total: 16 Vrttas Thus 16 is the total number of Prastaras according to the Sadkhyana. This total can be arrived at by adding one to the Udd is tanka. As noted above the numbers of Uddistas are: 1+2+4+8 — 15 1 =16 By deducting one from doubling the number of Prastara is also called Adhva by the wise people.4

21\. О sage! I have lightly indicated to you the characteristics of Chandas Sastra (the Science of Prosody). The details of subtle varieties of Prastdras are infinite.

## Chapter 58. Buka's Temptation

## \|\| 1.58.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*anūcānaprasaṃgena vedāṅgānyakhilāni ca \|*

Narada submitted:

1\. When there was a reference to the term Anucana (wellversedness in Vedas) all the Veddngas (ancillaries to the Vedas) were heard (by me) from your lotus-like mouth (as they were being explained) partially in brief and partially in details.

## \|\| 1.58.2-3 \|\|

*śukotpattiṃ samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmate \|*  
*sanandana uvāca*

*vijahāra mahodevo bhaumaibhūtagaṇaivṛtaḥ \|*

2a. Narrate to me in details the (story of) the birth of Shuka, О highly intelligent sage. Sanandana narrated:

2b-3. It is reported that formerly, on one occasion, on the peak of mount Meru, in an extensive forest of Karnikara trees, Lord Mahadcva accompanied by multitudes of terrible goblins sported himself. The daughter of the Lord of mountains, goddess Parvatl, was also there with them.

## \|\| 1.58.4-15 \|\|

*tatra divyaṃ tapastepe kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ \|*

*dhārayansa tapastepe putrārthaṃ sunisaṃttamaḥ \|*

4-5a. The holy sage Vyasa (Kfsna Dvaipayana) performed a divine penance there. He was devoted to the practice of Yoga. By dint of his yogic power, he entered (withdrew) in the soul and performed Dharana. That excellent-most sage performed those austerities for the sake of a son.

5b-7a. “May my son have the virility of Fire, Earth, Wind and Ether all roundt”. With this solemn vow of performance of penance, he practised severe austerities and sought after the Lord of gods who is impossible to be attained by persons who are not self-possessed. This chapter incorporates chapters 323 (from v. 11 onwards), 324, 325 of the SdnH Paroa of the Mbh. In the notes on these, Mbh=AfM. Sdnti Parva, the next reference is to chapter No. and Verse Nos. f For abhitah of the NP. ambhasah would be a better reading as the puissance of five Mahdbhutas is desired. The Mbh. also includes ‘water’ in the list of MahdbhUtas whose strength is requested.

7b-8a. It is reported that the powerful sage stood for one hundred years, subsisting on the air only, and propitiated the multi-formed great god (Mahadeva), the consort of Uma.

8b-12a. There were (in attendance) all Brahmanical sages, heavenly sages, guardians of the worlds, demigods like Sadhyas, along with eight (twelve) Adityas, Rudras, the Sun god and the Moon god, Gandharva (king) Visvavasu, Siddhas, bcvis of divine damsels. There the great god Rudra, wearing an auspicious garland of Karnikara flowers, shone like the Moon in the autumn.

12b-13a. It was surprisingly mysterious to all the three worlds that his (Vyasa s) complexion did not fade nor exhaustion overcame him.

13b-14a. As he, of immeasurable splendour, was absorbed in Yoga, the locks of his matted hair due to his splendour appeared to glisten like the blazing flames of fire.

14b-15. О Narada! Pleased at heart with this type of penance and such devotion of the sage, the great god Mahadeva made up his mind (to bestow favour on him) and the three-eyed Lord spoke to him smilingly.

## \|\| 1.58.16 \|\|

*yathā hyagniyathā vāyuryathā bhūmiryathā jalam \|*  
*yathā khe ca tathā śuddho bhaviṣyati sutastaṃva \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “Your son shall be as pure as the Fire, as the Wind, as the Earth, as the Water and as the Sky.

## \|\| 1.58.17 \|\|

*tadbhāvabhāgī tadbuddhistadātmā tadupāśrayaḥ \|*

17\. He will be the partaker of consciousness of himself being the Brahman; his intelligence and mind shall be concentrated on the Brahman; he shall be permanently established in the Brahman. By dint of his (Brahmanic) splendour, he will be renowned all over the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.58.18 \|\|

*evaṃ labdhvā varaṃ devo vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ \|*

18\. After having obtained that excellent boon from the Lord, Vyasa, the son of Satyavati, was one day engaged in churning the sacrificial sticks, with the desire of making a fire (for sacrificial purpose).

19\. At that time, the illustrious sage happened to see a heavenly damsel called Ghrtaci who, in consequence of her brilliant splendour, possessed excellent beauty.

## \|\| 1.58.20 \|\|

21\. After making Vyasa deeply agitated with passion, the most beautiful Ghftaci, transforming herself into a she- parrot, approached him.

## \|\| 1.58.22 \|\|

*sa tāmapsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpeṇānyenasaṃvṛtām \|*

22\. Even after seeing the celestial lady disguised in another form, he was overcome with cupid (passionate love) who spread in every part of his body.

## \|\| 1.58.23 \|\|

*sa tu mahatā nigṛhṇan hṛcchayaṃ muniḥ \|*

23\. With great (moral) courage, the sage tried to restrain his passion. But his mind being extremely agitated, Vyasa was unable to control it.

## \|\| 1.58.24-25 \|\|

*bhāvitvāñcaiva bhāvyasya ghṛtācyā vapuṣā \|*

24-25. Due to the inevitability of Destiny (lit. what was to happen) the heart of the sage was fascinated by the (beautiful) form (of GhrtacI). With the desire to do this (vie. the kindling of fire) while he was suppressing his passion with special efforts, all of a sudden his semen fell on the churning sticks. It was thus that the great ascetic auka was born, while Vyasa continued the churning of sacrificial sticks.

## \|\| 1.58.26-27 \|\|

*paramarṣirmahāyogī araṇīgarbhasaṃbhavaḥ \|*

26-27. The foremost of sages, the great Yogi, was (thus) born of (lit. from the womb of) two (sacrificial) churning sticks. Just as a blazing sacrificial fire after being fed with oblations of ghee, sheds his effulgence all around, in the same way Shuka was born as if blazing with his brilliance, assuming a wonderfully beautiful form and excellent, unsurpassable complexion, O, foremost of Brahmanas.

30-31a. High sounding heavenly kettle-drums began to beat lustily. Gandharva Visvavasu, Narada and Tumburu, and the pair of Gandharvas Haha and Huhii eulogised the nativity of Shuka.

31b-33a. There arrived the regents of different worlds of whom Indra was the leader, and gods, heavenly sages and Brahmanical sages as well. And the wind-god showered all varieties of heavenly flowers. (In this manner) all the world, the mobile and immobile, became highly delighted.

33b-34a. The highly resplendent, noble-souled god Mahadeva along with the goddess Uma performed with due formalities the ceremony of investiture of thread of the sage’s son (i.e. Shuka) as soon as he was born. Grammatically the verse is loose and defective.

34b-36a. To him gifted Indra, the Lord of gods, a wonderful-looking heavenly water-pot (Kamandalu) out of love and gods gave him clothes. Thousands of swans, peacocks, cranes, parrots and blue jays hovered around him clockwise, О Narada.

36b-37a. The highly intelligent great sage, having obtained his divine nativity from the two sacrificial sticks, stayed there, observing his holy vows with great attention.

37b-38a. As soon as he was born, the Vedas with all their esoteric secrets and all their abstracts, approached him for dwelling in him even as they approached his father.

38b-39a. Although he was conversant with Vedas, Vedangas (accessories of the Vedas) together with their commentaries he remembering that it was his duty (to have a guru, as per ancient religious practice), selected Bfhaspati as his preceptor, О prominent Brahmana.

39b-40. Having studied all the Vedas along with their mysteries and abstracts as well as Itihasa (History, like the MahdBharata) and all the sciences and scriptural texts based on the Vedas, the great sage paid his tuition-fees to his preceptor and performed the rite of Samdvartana (the formal conclusion of the life as a religious student).

42b-43. The mind (intelligence) of Shuka who was the observer of the path leading to Emancipation (from the cycle of Samsara did not take interest in the three Airamas (stages of life) depending on the house-holder’s stage of life.

*ārjavenaiva gantavyaṃ na sukhāya kṣaṇāttvayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*na draṣṭavyā viśeṣā hi viśeṣā hi prasaṃginaḥ \|*  
*ahṝṅkāro na kartavyo yājye tasminnarādhipe \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sthātavyaṃ vasathe tasya sa te chetsyati saṃśayam \|*  
*sa dharmakuśalo rājā mokṣaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yathā yathā ca te brūyāttatkāryamaviśaṅkayā \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa dharmātmā jagāma mithilāṃ muniḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

44-45a. Desirous as he was of the highest beatitude and endowed with humility as he was, he bowed down to him and requested him: ‘You are an expert in the religious path that leads to Emancipation from Sam

sara. May you be pleased to elucidate that to me, so that I may be blessed with Supreme tranquility of mind.” Here ends chapter 324 of the Mbh. Sdnti.

45b-46a. Hearing the words of his son, the great sage advised him, “Do you learn the scripture pertaining to Moksa as well as all other different religious duties/

46b-47a. At the behest of his father, shuka, the excellent- most among the knowers of the Brahman (or Vedas) learnt the entire Yoga-Sastra and the (Sdnkhya) philosophy of Kapila completely.

47b-49a. Seeing his son resplendent with the splendour of the Vedas and endowed with the glory of Brahman and thoroughly conversant with Moksa-shdstra\> he directed him then “Go to Janaka, the king of Mithila. That king will explain to you everything about the meaning of the Moksa-Sastra.

49b-50a. At the behest of his father, Shuka went (was about to go) to Janaka, the king of Mithila, in order to enquire about the definite knowledge (nistha) about duties leading to Moksa and the nature of that ultimate goal.

50b-54. (As he was about to depart) he was instructed (by his father). “You go by the way traversed by ordinary mortals.” Shuka was not surprised (at this instruction). He was further advised: “You should not go through the sky by your Yogic power. You should proceed there with simplicity and straightforwardness and not for seeking pleasure. Specialities (friendship etc.) should not be seen (formed) by you, as those specialities (or contacts) become binding. Even though the king is adopted by us as one on whose behalf sacrifices are to be performed by us, you should not entertain any pride about it. You should stay in his premises. He will dispel all your doubts as the king is proficient in Dharma (religious duties) as well as scriptures regarding (the path to) Moksa. You should abide unhesitatingly by whatever he asks you to do. Being thus instructed, the righteous-souled sage Shuka proceeded to Mithila.

## \|\| 1.58.55 \|\|

*pabhdyāṃ śaktontarikṣeṇa krāntuṃ bhūmiṃ sasāgarām \|*  
*sagirīṃ ścāpyatikramya bhārataṃ varṣamāsadat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Though he had the capability of traversing through the sky the whole of the earth alongwith the oceans, he crossed on foot the mountains and reached the sub-continent called Bharata. NP. reads: Sataih brdhyd Shriyd yuktam. But Satath brdhyd is meaningless and an obvious miscopying of Sa lam brdhmyd of the Mbh. Sanli. 325.5a.

## \|\| 1.58.56 \|\|

*sa deśānvividhānsphītānatikramya mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*videhānvai samāsādya janakena samāgamat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The great sage passed through different prosperous and rich countries. At last reaching the country (known as) Videha, he approached Janaka.

## \|\| 1.58.57 \|\|

*rājadvāraṃ samāsādya dvārapālairnivāritaḥ \|*  
*tasthau tatra mahāyogī kṣutpipāsādivarjitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. When he arrived at the gate of (Janaka’s) palace, he was stopped by the door-keepers. The great Yogin stood there unaffected by hunger or thirst.

## \|\| 1.58.58-61 \|\|

*ātape glānirahito dhyānayuktaśca nārada \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu dvārapālānāmekastatra vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*madhyaṅgatamivādityaṃ dṛṣṭvā śukamavasthitam \|*  
*jūjayitvā yathānyāyamabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*prāveśayattataḥ kakṣaāṃ dvitīyāṃ rājaveśmanaḥ \|*  
*tatrāntaḥpurasaṃbaddhaṃ mahaccaitragthopamam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*suvibhaktajalākrīḍaṃ ramyaṃ puṣpitapādapam \|*  
*darśayitvāsane sthāpya rājānaṃ ca vyajijñapat \|\| 61 \|\|*

58-60a. О Narada, even in the heat of the sun, he was not distressed by exhaustion or dejection and was absorbed in meditation. One of the porters who was posted there saw Shuka standing, blazing like the mid-day sun. He worshipped Shuka with due formalities and paying obeisance to him with his palms joined, led him to the second apartment of the king’s palace.

60b-61. Near the harem, there was a beautiful garden like Chaitraratha park (of Kubera). It abounded in trees in full blossom and had separate swimming pools and playgrounds. Showing him that garden, the porter made him sit and humbly reported (his arrival) to the king.

## \|\| 1.58.62 \|\|

*śrutvā rājā śukaṃ prāptaṃ vārastrīḥ sa nyayuṅkta ca \|*  
*sevāyai tasya bhāvasya jñānāya munisatama \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Having heard that Shuka had arrived, the king appointed courtesans for his service as well as to gauge the disposition and the inclinations of his mind.

## \|\| 1.58.63 \|\|

*taṃ cārukeśyaḥ śuśreṇyastaruṇyaḥ priyadarśanāḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmaraktāṃbaradharāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. All those damsels were young, beautful-looking with fine tresses of hair, possessing excellent hips, clad in red clothes of fine texture and decked with ornaments of burnished gold.

## \|\| 1.58.64-68 \|\|

*saṃlāpālāpakuśālā bhāvajñāḥ sarvakovidāḥ \|*  
*paraṃ pañcāśatastasya pādyādīni vyakalpayan \|\| 64 \|\|*

*deśa kālopapannena sādhvannenāpyatarpayan \|*  
*tasya bhuktavatastāta tāstataḥ purakānanam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*suramyaṃ darśayāmāsurekaikatvena nārada \|*  
*krīḍantyaśca hasaṃtyaśca gāyantyaścaiva tāḥ śukam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*udārasatvaṃ satvajñāḥsarvāḥ paryyacaraṃstadā \|*  
*āraṇeyastu śuddhātmā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*dhyānastha eva satataṃ na hṛṣyati na kupyati \|*  
*pādaśaucaṃ tu kṛtvā vai śukaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsya ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

64-65a. All of them were experts in agreeable conversation, competent to read the minds of man and skilled in all (amorous) acts. They were more than fifty. They arranged for his reception with water for washing feet etc. They gratified him with such articles of food as were agreeable in the season.

65b-66a. When he had eaten his food, they showed him beautiful parks in the town one by one, О Narada.

66b-67a. Sporting, giggling and singing, those ladies, conversant with male psychology, entertained that noble-souled sage.

67b-68. The pure-souled ascetic, born of sacrificial fire- sticks, had conquered his anger and had subdued his sense- organs. He was always absorbed in meditation. He was neither delighted nor angry at these.

## \|\| 1.58.68-72 \|\|

*dhyānastha eva satataṃ na hṛṣyati na kupyati \|*  
*pādaśaucaṃ tu kṛtvā vai śukaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsya ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*niṣasādāsane puṇye tamevārthaṃ vyacintayat \|*  
*pūrvarātre tu tatrāsau bhūtvā dhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*madhyarātre yathānyāyyaṃ nidrāmāhārayatprabhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya kṛtvā śaucamanantaram \|\| 70 \|\|*

*strībhiḥ parivṛtto dhīmāndhyānamevānvapadyata \|*  
*anena vidhinā tatra tadahaḥśeṣamapyuta \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tāṃ ca rātriṃ nṛpakule vartayāmāsa nārada \|\| 72 \|\|*

68b-69a. Shuka washed his feet and after completing his Sandhya prayer, seated himself on a holy seat meditating on that object for which he had come there.

69b-70a. In the earlier part of the night, he became absorbed in meditating upon Narayana. In the middle part of the night he duly went to sleep.

70b-71a. Getting up early in the morning and after performing the necessary rites of bodily purification and ablution, the highly intelligent sage, though he was surrounded by women, was once again absorbed in meditation.

71b-72. It is in this manner that he spent the remaining part of the day and that night in the palace of the king, О Narada. Here ends ch, 325 in the Mbh. shanti.

## Chapter 59. The diabgue between Shuka andjanaka

## \|\| 1.59.1-8 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*tataḥ sa rājā sahito mantribhirdvijasattama \|*  
*puraḥ purohitaṃ kṛtvā sarvāṇyantaḥ purāṇi ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śirasā cārdhyamādāya guruputraṃ samabhyagāt \|*  
*mahadāsanamādāya sarvaratnavibhūṣitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pradadau guruputrāya śukāya paramocitam \|*  
*tatropaviṣṭaṃ taṃ kārṣṇiśāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pādyaṃ nivedya prathamaṃ sārghyaṃ gāṃ ca nyavedayat \|*  
*sa ca tāṃmantrataḥ pūjāṃ pratigṛhya dvijottamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*paryapṛcchanmahātejārājñaḥ kuśalamavyayam \|*  
*udārasattvābhijano rājāpi gurusūnave \|\| 5 \|\|*

*āvedya kuśalaṃ bhūmau niṣasāda tadājñayā \|*  
*so 'pi vaiyāsakiṃ bhūyaḥ pṛṣṭvā kuśalamavyayam \|*  
*kimāgamanimityeva paryapṛcchadvidhānavit \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śuka uvāca*  
*pitrāhamukto bhadraṃ te mokṣadharmārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*videharājohyādyome janako nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatra tvaṃ gaccha tūrṇaṃ vai sa te hṛdayasaṃśayam \|*  
*pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca sarvaṃ chetsyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sanandana continued:

1-3a. The next morning, О excellent Brahmana, with the family priest at the head (of the procession), the king accompanied by his ministers and all the members of his harem, approached the preceptor’s son (Shuka). He carried the articles of worship (axghya) on his head and took with him a highly valuable seat bedecked with all (kinds) of precious stones. He offered that extremely suitable seat to Shuka, the son of his preceptor.

3b-4a. When Shuka, the son of Krsh^a-(Dvaipayana Vyasa) occupied the seat, the king worshipped him according to the prescribed rites. At first he offered him water to wash his feet. He then presented him a cow alongwith articles of worship.

4b-5a. The excellent Brahmana accepted the worship offered in accompaniment of the prescribed Mantras. The highly resplendent ascetic enquired after king’s unfailing welfare and prosperity.

5b-6a. The noble-minded monarch with his entourage of noble men and officers duly reported about his welfare to the son of his preceptor. With his permission, he sat on the ground.

6b-7a. Conversant with etiquettes and proper procedure as he was, the king enquired of Shuka, the son of Vyasa after his welfare and asked him the object of his visit. This chapter consists of ch. 326 and of a few more verses from ch. 327 of the Mbh. Sdnti. Shuka replied:

7b-8. Prosperity be unto you! My father has informed me that “the King ofVidehas known all over the world as Janaka, is my first1 (disciple?), is well-versed in the virtuous path leading to Moksa, you therefore go to him quickly. If you have any doubt in your heart regarding the religion of Pravrtti (sacrifices and such other ritualistic matter) or about the religious path of renunciation (Nivritti), he will definitely dispel them all.”

## \|\| 1.59.9 \|\|

*so 'haṃ piturniyogāttvā mupapraṣṭumihāgataḥ \|*  
*tanme dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9 At the command of my father, I have therefore, come hereto you to discuss with you (these matters). Hence, it behoves you, О foremost among the upholders of dharma to instruct me precisely.

## \|\| 1.59.10 \|\|

*kiṃ kāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha mokṣārthaśca kimātmakaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ ca mokṣaḥ kartavyo jñānena tapasāpi vā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. What should be done by a Brahmana here? What is the essence of those religious duties which are conducive to Liberation? How is the Liberation (from Samsara) to be achieved? Is it obtainable by (spiritual) knowledge or by penance. Janaka replied:

## \|\| 1.59.11 \|\|

*janaka uvāca*  
*yatkāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha janmaprabhṛti tacchuṇu \|*  
*kṛtopanayanastāta bhavedvedaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Listen tome, dear child, what are the duties of a Brahmana since his birth. After the investiture of the sacred thread, he should devote himself to the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.59.12 \|\|

*tapasā guruvṛttyā ca brahmacaryeṇa cānvitaḥ \|*  
*devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca hyatṛṣṇaścānasūyakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By performing penance, services to his preceptor and observance of celibacy and by remaining devoid of greed and jealousy, he should do his duties to Devas and Pitrs.

## \|\| 1.59.13 \|\|

*vedānadhītya niyato dakṣiṇāmapavartya ca \|*  
*abhyanujñāmanuprāpya samāvarteta vai dvijaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Having studied the Vedas regularly and controlled his senses, and after paying off the tuition-fee of his preceptor, and after taking the permission of his teacher he should formally conclude his stage of religious studentship (by performance of Samdvartana ceremony).

## \|\| 1.59.14 \|\|

*samāvṛttastu gārhasthye sadāro niyato vaset \|*  
*anasūyuryathānyāyamāhitāgniranādṛte \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After completion of the Samavartana, he should betake himself to the householder’s stage of life. (After marriage) he should live in the company of his spouse, devoid of malice and jealousy, and he should duly and continuously maintain domestic (sacrificial) fire.2

## \|\| 1.59.15 \|\|

*utpādya putrapautrāṃśca vanyāśramapade vaset \|*  
*tānevāgnīnyathānyāyaṃ pūjayannatithipriyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After procreating sons and grandsons, he should retire as a hermit to a forest and continue to worship the same (domestic) sacrificial fires and receive lovingly guests with due hospitality.

## \|\| 1.59.16 \|\|

*sarvānagnīnyathānyāyamātmanyāropya dharmavit \|*  
*nirdvandvo vītarāgātmā brahmāśramapade vaset \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, the knower of Dharma should establish all (sacrificial) fires within his soul and rising above the pair of opposites, and banishing all passionate attachment from his soul, he should pass his life in the stage of life called Brahma- frama (or Sannyasa). Shuka enquired:

## \|\| 1.59.17 \|\|

*śuka uvāca*  
*utpanne jñānavijñāne pratyakṣe hṛdi śaśvate \|*  
*na vinā gurusaṃvāsājjñānasyādhigamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (It may be true that) when perfect spiritual knowledge dawns and the eternal entity (the Brahman) is realised directly, (Mokfd) is automatically attained). But they say that attainment of (true spiritual) knowledge is not possible without direct association with and personal stay with the spiritual preceptor.

## \|\| 1.59.18 \|\|

*kimavaśyaṃ tu vastavyamāśrameṣu na vā nṛpa \|*  
*etadbhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi tadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Is it necessary for a person to go through the three stages of life (studenthood, the life of a householder and that of a forest-hermit)? This is what I ask you. It behoves you to explain this. Janaka explained:

## \|\| 1.59.19 \|\|

*janaka uvāca*  
*na vinā jñānavijñāne mokṣasyādhigamo bhavet \|.*  
*na vinā gurusaṃbadhājjñānasyādhigamastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Attainment of Liberation from Samsara is not possible till one accomplishes knowledge (understanding the nature of Brahman etc. theoretically from the scriptural studies) and the true conception of Reality. But the knowledge (or the nature of Brahman) is not possible without association with the (spiritual) preceptor.3

## \|\| 1.59.20 \|\|

*ācāryaḥ plāvitā tasya jñānaṃ plava ihocyate \|*  
*vijñāya kṛtakṛtyastu tīrṇastatrobhayaṃ tyajet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The preceptor is the pilot or helmsman, while spiritual knowledge is the boat. After attaining knowledge and crossing the ocean of Samsara, one may abandon both.

## \|\| 1.59.21 \|\|

*anucchedāya lokānāmanucchedāya karmaṇām \|*  
*kṛtvā śubhāśubhaṃ karma mokṣo nāmeha labhyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In order to prevent the annihilation of worlds and for forestalling the destruction of acts (on which the existence of the world depends), a person performs both auspicious and inauspicious deeds. It is only after that, that the Liberation is achieved.

## \|\| 1.59.22 \|\|

*bhāvitaiḥ kāraṇaiścāryaṃ bahusaṃsārayoniṣu \|*  
*āsādayati śuddhātmā mokṣaṃ hi prathamāśrame \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When (through performance of penanee) one becomes perfectly purified in one’s soul, by means of purificatory causes4 in the course of many births in the world, he attains Liberation from Samsara even in the first (Brahmacarya) stage of life.

## \|\| 1.59.23 \|\|

*tamāsādya tu muktasya dṛṣṭārthasya vipaścitaḥ \|*  
*tridhāśrameṣu konvartho bhavetparamabhīpsataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. What paramount desirable object is to be achieved by going through the three stages of life by a person who has attained Liberation from Samsara, or by a learned person who has seen the Reality.

## \|\| 1.59.24 \|\|

*rājasāṃstāmasāṃścaiva nityaṃ doṣānvisarjayeta \|*  
*sāttvikaṃ mārgamāsthāya paśyedātmānamātmanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One should always cast off defects or faults caused by the attributes Rajas and Tamos. Adhering to the path characterised by Sattva, he should behold the Supreme soul, by means of (or within) his own individual soul.

## \|\| 1.59.25 \|\|

*sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani \|*  
*saṃpaśyannaiva lipyeta jale vāricarago yathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Realizing his own soul in all created beings and beholding all creatures within his soul, he should behave (without being attached to anything in the Samsara) like an aquatic animal which does not become wet though moving through waters.

## \|\| 1.59.26 \|\|

*pakṣīvatpavanādvardhvamamutrānuntyaśnute \|*  
*vihāya dehaṃ nirmukto nirdvandvaḥ śubhasaṃgataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Transcending the pairs of opposite attributes and associated with auspiciousness, he becomes completely liberated (from Sarfisdra) after casting off the physical body and attains Infinity in the next world like a bird, soaring up high in the sky above (the currents of) the wind.

## \|\| 1.59.27 \|\|

*atra gāthāḥ purā gītāḥ śṛṇu rājñā yayātinā \|*  
*dhāryate yā dvijaistāta mokṣaśāstraviśāradaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In this context, listen to the Gatkds sung in ancient times by King Yayati. They are remembered in their hearts by all twice-borns who are experts in the philosophy of Liberation.

## \|\| 1.59.28 \|\|

*jyotiścātmani nānyatra ratnaṃ tatraiva caiva tat \|*  
*svayaṃ ca śakyaṃ taddraṣṭuṃ susamāhitarcatasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The resplendent lustre (i.e. the Supreme soul) is in one’s soul. It is a jewel5 there itself. It is possible to be observed by oneself, but only with concentrated mind.

## \|\| 1.59.29 \|\|

*na bibheti paro yasmānna bibheti parācca yaḥ \|*  
*yaśca necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate sa tu \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He who behaves in such a way that others are not afraid of him and when a person is not inspired with fear at the sight of another person, he who neither covets nor hates anything, attains to the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.59.30-31 \|\|

*yadā bhāvaṃ na kurute sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam \|*  
*pūrvairācarito dharmaścaturāśramasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*anena kramayogena bahujātisukarmaṇām \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. When a person does not entertain evil thoughts about any of the living beings, when one abides by the path of virtue (or religious duty) called Caturdirama Dharma (A Dharma constituted of four stages of life) which has been practised by one’s ancestors, when according to the serial order of these ASramas (stages of life) he performs (for many births) good actions physically, mentally and verbally, he attains (realizes) the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.59.32 \|\|

*rsuyojya tapasātmānamīrṣyāmutsṛjya mohinīm \|*  
*tyaktva kāmaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca tato brahmatvamaśnute \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If a person, eschewing malice that deludes people and having cast off passion and greed (from the mind), unites his soul with penance, he attains the state of (being one with) Brahman.

## \|\| 1.59.33 \|\|

*yadā śrāvye ca dṛśye ca sarvabhūteṣu cāvyayam \|*  
*samo bhavati nirdvudvo brahma saṃpadyate tadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When one is equally disposed to all beings whether visible or audible, and supersedes the (reactions at) naturally opposite pairs (like pleasure and pain), one gels to the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.59.34-35 \|\|

*yadā stuti ca rnidāṃ ca samatvena ca paśyati \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ cāyasaṃ caiva sukhaduḥkhe tathaiva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śītamuṣṇaṃ tathaivārthamanarnthaṃ priyamapriyam \|*  
*jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva brahma saṃpadyate tadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. When one looks upon with an equal eye (without feeling attraction of repulsion), to naturally opposite pairs (Dvandvas) like praise and blame, a piece of gold and iron, pleasure and pain, cold and heat, attainment of worldly prosperity and adversity, pleasing and displeasing, life and death — then one attains to the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.59.36 \|\|

*prasāryeha yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ \|*  
*tarthedriyāṇi manasā saṃyantavyāni bhikṣuṇā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Just as a tortoise spreads out its limbs and withdraws again (within itself), in the same way, the sense-organs are to be restrained by the recluse through his inind.

## \|\| 1.59.37 \|\|

*tamaḥ parigataṃ veśya yathā dīpena dṛśyate \|*  
*tathā buddhipradīpena śakya ātmā nirīkṣitum \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Just as one’s place of residence plunged in darkness is seen with (the light emanating from) a lamp, in the same manner it is possible to visualize the Atman with the brilliant light of intelligence.

## \|\| 1.59.38 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ prapaśyāmi tvayi buddhimatāṃvara \|*  
*yañcānyadapi vettavyaṃ tattvato vetti tadbhavān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I, however, can clearly see that you are endowed with all these (within you), О prominent one among the intelligents. If there be anything else to be known, your worship will know it fundamentally (and correctly).

## \|\| 1.59.39 \|\|

*brahmarṣe viditaśvāsi viṣayāntamupāgataḥ \|*  
*guroścaiva prasādena tava caivopaśikṣayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О Brahmanical sage, you are already famous as one who have transcended (lit. gone to the other end of) worldly objects of sense through the grace of your spiritual preceptor as well as through your personal discipline (i.e. disciplined way of life).

## \|\| 1.59.40 \|\|

*tasya caiva prasādena prādurbhūtaṃ mahāmuneḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ divyaṃ samādīptaṃ tenāsi vidito vidito mama \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It is through the grace of that great sage that the refulgent divine knowledge has revealed itself to you. You are known to me on account of that (spiritual knowledge).

## \|\| 1.59.41 \|\|

*ardhikaṃ tava vijñānamadhi kāvagatistava \|*  
*adhikaṃ ca tavaiśvaryaṃ tañca tvaṃ nāvabudhyase \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Your knowledge about Moksa is more profound; your understanding is deeper, your spiritual glory is so immense that you don’t realize it yourself.

## \|\| 1.59.42 \|\|

*bālyādvā saṃśayādvāpi bhayādvāpi vimeṣajāt \|*  
*utpanne cāpi vijñā ne nādhigacchanti tāṅgatim \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Maybe due to immaturity or due to doubts or fears caused by delusion, some people do not attain that spiritual goal (Moksa) even though knowledge leading to Moksa is dawned in them.

## \|\| 1.59.43 \|\|

*vyavasāyena śuddhena madvidhaiśchinnasaṃśayāḥ \|*  
*vimucya hṛdayagranthīnārtimāsādayanti tām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When all the doubts have been dispelled by persons like me, they, by dint of their pure determined efforts, cut the knots (of doubt) in their heart and do not fall a victim to distress (i.e. are not distressed).

## \|\| 1.59.44 \|\|

*mavāṃścotpannavijñānaḥ sthirabaguddhiralolupaḥ \|*  
*vyavasāyādṛte brahmannāsādayati tatpadam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Your honour is a person in whom perfect knowledge has been generated and is steady in intellect and are free from covetousness. One, however, cannot attain that goal (of Moksa) without determined efforts.

## \|\| 1.59.45 \|\|

*nāsti te sukhaduḥkheṣu viśeṣo nāsti vastuṣu \|*

45\. You entertain no differentiation between pleasure and pain and attach no importance to objects of senses. You have no curiosity and attraction for dancing and music. Nor does any passion overpower you.

## \|\| 1.59.46 \|\|

*na bandhuṣu nibandhaste na bhayeṣvasti te bhayam \|*  
*paśyāmitvāṃ mahābhāga tulyanindātmasaṃstutim \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. You feel no bonds to your kinsmen. You are not inspired with fear at fearful objects. I find that to you censure and praise are all equal.

## \|\| 1.59.47 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca tvānupaśyāmi ye cānye 'pi manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*āsthitaṃ paramaṃ mārge akṣayaṃ cāpyanāmayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I see that you are a person among other wise persons who have taken to the highest imperishable path devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.59.48 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ brāhmaṇasyeha mokṣārthaścāpadātmakaḥ \|*  
*tasminvai vartase viprakimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О Brahmana you are already existing in that state (called Moksa) which is the fruit attained by a Brahmana and it is not a particular region. What else do you (want to) ask me about?” Sanandana said:

## \|\| 1.59.49 \|\|

*sanandana uvāca*  
*etacchutvā tu vacanaṃ katātmā kṛtaniścayaḥ \|*  
*ātmanātmānamāsthāya dṛṣṭvā cātmānamātmanā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Having heard this exhortation (of Janaka), Shuka who was self-controlled and had determined (to see the Atman), began to abide in his soul mentally (by withdrawing himself from worldly objects) and he realized the (Universal) soul within his individual Atman.

## \|\| 1.59.50-52 \|\|

*kṛtakāryaḥ sukhī śāntastūṣṇīṃ prāyādudaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*śaiśiraṃ girimāsādya pārāśaryaṃ dadarśa ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śiṣyānadhyāpayantaṃ ca pailādīnvedasaṃhitāḥ \|*  
*ārarṇeyo viśuddhātmā divākarasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*piturjagrāha pādau caja sādaraṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*tato nivedayāmāsa pituḥ sarvamudāradhīḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-51a. Having accomplished his object, he was filled with bliss and (mental) tranquillity. He silently proceeded to the north. On reaching the Satiira (the Himalaya) mountain, he espied Vyasa, the son of Parasara who was teaching his disciples like Paila and others, the compilations of the Vedas.

5 lb-52. Shuka (the sage born of Arani) of extremely pure mind (soul) and brilliant like the sun-god, respectfully clasped his father’s feet and felt delighted at heart. The noble-minded Shuka reported everything to his father.

## \|\| 1.59.53-54 \|\|

*śuko janakarājena saṃvādaṃ mokṣasādhanam \|*  
*tacchatvā vedakartāsau prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*samāliṅgya sutaṃ vyāsaḥ svapārśvasthaṃ cakāra ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Having heard the dialogue between Shuka and king Janaka on the means of getting Moksa (liberation fiom Sariisara), Vyasa, the author (arranger) of the Vedas, embraced his son with a heart full of ecstatic delight and seated him by his side.

## \|\| 1.59.55 \|\|

*tataḥ pailādayo viprā vedān vyāsādadhītya ca \|*  
*śailaśṛṅgādbhuvaṃ prāptā yājanādhyāpane ratāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereafter, the Brahmanas like Paila and others completed their course of Vedic study under Vyasa. They came down to the earth from the mountain-summit and engaged themselves in teaching the Vedas and performing sacrifices.

## Chapter 60. The Dialogue between Shuka and SanatKumara

## \|\| 1.60.1 \|\|

*sanadana uvāca*  
*avatīrṇeṣu vipreṣu yāsaḥ putrasahāyavān \|*  
*tūrṣṇīṃ dhyānaparo dhīmānekānte samupāviśat \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanandana continued: —

1\. When the Brahmanas (disciples of Vyasa) descended (from the height of Vyasa’s hermitage) or departed, the intelligent Vyasa with only his son (Shuka) as the companion, remained silently absorbed in meditation in the hermitage.

## \|\| 1.60.2 \|\|

*tamuvācāśarī rī vāk vyāsaṃ putrasamanvitam \|*  
*bho bho maharṣe bāsiṣṭha brahmaghoṣo na vartate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. An incorporeal voice2 addressed Vyasa along with his son: “O great sage: О descendant of Vasishtha: (How is it that) there is no chanting sound of the Vedas (in your hermitage)?

## \|\| 1.60.3 \|\|

*eko dhyānaparastūṣṇī kimāḥse cintayanniva \|*  
*brahmaghoṣairvirahitaḥ parvato 'yaṃ na śobhate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Why are you sitting thus silent and absorbed in meditation, as if you are (anxiously) brooding over something? This mountain devoid of the vibrant echoes (of Vedas) docs not appear splendid.

## \|\| 1.60.4 \|\|

*tasmādadhīṣva bhagavansārddha putreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*vedānvedavidā caiva suprasannamanāḥ sadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О venerable Sir, with a delighted heart, recite the Vedas along with your intelligent son who is well-versed in the Vedas.”

## \|\| 1.60.5 \|\|

*tacchutvā vacanaṃ vyāso nabhovāṇīsamīritam \|*  
*śukena saha putreṇa vedābhyāsamathākarot \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing that speech addressed to him by the ethereal voice, Vyasa began to chant the Vedas along with his son Shuka.

## \|\| 1.60.6 \|\|

*tayorabhyasatorevaṃ bahukālaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*vāto 'timātraṃ pravavau samudrānilavījitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. While both of them were chanting the Vedas for a pretty long time, there arose, О excellent Brahmana, a violent wind which was as if driven by the gales that break out on the seas.

## \|\| 1.60.7-8 \|\|

*tato 'nadhyāya iti taṃ vyāsaḥ putramavārayat \|*  
*śuko vāritamātrastu kautūhalasamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*apṛcchatpitaraṃ tatra kuto vāyurabhūdayam \|*  
*ākhyātumarhati bhavānsarvaṃ vāyorvicaiṣṭitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Then Vyasa prohibited his son from continuing the Vedic study, as it was not the time suitable for studies (and hence a holiday). As soon as he was so bidden (to suspend Vedic recitation), Shuka, out of curiosity asked his father: “whence is the wind blowing? It behoves you to explain to me all the activities of the wind/

## \|\| 1.60.9 \|\|

*śukasyaitadvacaḥ śrutvā vyāsaḥ paramavismitaḥ \|*  
*anadhyāyanimitta'sminnidaṃ vacanaṃ mabravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vyasa was extremely surprised to hear these words of Shuka. He replied to Shuka that it was an ill omen which indicated the suspension of the recitation of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.60.10 \|\|

*divyaṃ te cakṣurutpannaṃ svasthaṃ te niścalaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*tamasā rajasā cāpi tyaktaḥ satye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “You are blest with the spiritual vision. Your steady mind has been at ease; you are free from the attributes of Rajas and Tamas. You are well established in the Truth.

## \|\| 1.60.11 \|\|

*tasyātmani svayaṃ vedānbuddhvā samanucintaya \|*  
*devayānacaro viṣṇoḥ pitṛyānaśca tāmasaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hence realising the Vedas in your own self do you reflect and meditate: the path pertaining to the Supreme soul is known as the path of gods (Deva-yana). The path that is made of Tamas is called the path of Pitrs (Pitr-ydna).

## \|\| 1.60.12-18 \|\|

*dvāvetau pratyayaṃ yātau divaṃ cādhaśca gacchataḥ \|*  
*pithivyāmantarikṣe ca yataḥ saṃyānti vāyavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sapta te vāyumārgā vai tānnibodhānupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*tatra devagaṇāḥ sādhyāḥ samabhūvanmahābalāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*teṣāmapyabhavatputraḥ samāno nāma durjayaḥ \|*  
*udānastasya putro 'bhūvdyānastasyābhavatsutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*apānaśca tato jajñe prāṇaścāpi tataḥ param \|*  
*anapatyo 'bhavatprāṇo durddharṣaḥ śatrumardanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pṛtharkkṃmāṇi teṣāṃ tu pravakṣyāmi yathā tathā \|*  
*prāṇināṃ sarvato vāyuśceṣṭā vartayate pṛthak \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prīṇanāñcaiva sarveṣāṃ prāṇa ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*preṣayatyabhrasaṃghātāndhūmajāṃścoṣmajāṃstathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*prathamaḥ prathame mārge pravaho nāma so 'nilaḥ \|*  
*aṃbare snehamātrebhyastaḍidbhyaścottamadyutiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

12a. Both of these have come to be realized — one as leading to the heaven and the other to the world below since the winds blow over the world and high up in the atmosphere. I2b-I3a. The winds go on blowing both on the surface of earth as well as in the sky. They blow in seven courses. Listen and understand as I recount them one after another.

13b-14a. The (physical) body is endowed with senses which are domineered over by the (semi-divine beings called) Sadhyas and many (other) great powerful beings. They brought forth an unconquerable son called SamdnaA

14b-15a. From Samdna was born a son called Uddna; from Uddna sprang Vydna\\ from whom was created Apana, From Apana arose lastly the vital air called Prana.

15b-16a. The invincible tormentor of enemies, the Prana was issueless (as had no further function of such production) I shall now recount to you the different functions of these vital winds (as they are factually observed).

16b-17a. The vital wind causes all the various functions of all living beings and because living creatures are made to be pleased6 (NP) (are enabled to live — Mbh — ibid v. 35),

17b-18. The wind mentioned first (in the above list) and which is known by the epithet Pravaha (or Samana) impels the masses of clouds born of smoke and heat, to go by the first track. Moving through the sky and coming in contact with the water contained in the clouds, the wind manifests itself in its brilliance among the flashes of lightning.

## \|\| 1.60.19-35 \|\|

*āvaho nāma so 'bhyeti dvitīyaḥ śvasano nadan \|*  
*udayaṃ jyotiṣāṃ śaśvatsomādīnāṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*antardeheṣu codānaṃ yaṃ vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*yaścaturbhyaḥ samudrebhyo vāyurddhārayate jalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*uddhṛtya dadate cāpo jīmūtebhyo vane 'nilaḥ \|*  
*yo 'ddhiḥ saṃyojya jīmūtānparjanyāya prayacchatī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*udvaho nāma baṃhiṣṭhastṛtīyaḥ sa sadāgatiḥ \|*  
*saṃnīyamānā bahudhā yena nīlā mahāghanāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*varṣamokṣakṛtāraṃbhāste bhavanti ghanāghanāḥ \|*  
*yo 'sau vahati devānāṃ vimānāni vihāyasā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*caturthaḥ saṃvaho nāma vāyuḥ sa girimardanaḥ \|*  
*yena vegavatā rugṇāḥ kriyante tarujā rasāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pañcamaḥ sa mahāvego vivaho nāma mārutaḥ \|*  
*yasminpariplave divyā vahṝntyāpo vihāyasā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*puṇyaṃ cākāśagaṅgāyāstoyaṃ tiṣṭati tiṣṭati \|*  
*dūrātpratihato yasminnekaraśmirdivākaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yoniraṃśusahasrasya yena yāti vasuṃdharām \|*  
*yasmādāpyāyate somo nidhirdivyo 'mṛtasya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhaḥ parivaho nāma sa vāyurjīvatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ prāṇārnyo 'takāle nirasyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yasya dharme 'nuvartete mṛtyuvevasvatāvubhau \|*  
*samyaganvīkṣatā buddhyā śāntayādhyātmanityayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dhyānābhyāsābhirāmāṇāṃ yo 'mṛtatvāya kalpate \|*  
*yaṃ samāsādya vegena diśāmantaṃ prapedire \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dakṣasya daśa putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi prajāpateḥ \|*  
*yena vṛṣṭyā parābhūtastoyānyena nivartate \|\| 31 \|\|*

*parīvaho nāma varo vāyuḥ sa duratikramaḥ \|*  
*evamete diteḥ putrā marutaḥ paramādbhutāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*anāramantaḥ sarvāṅgāḥ sarvacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*etattu mahadāścaryaṃ yadayaṃ parvatottamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kaṃpitaḥ sahasā tena pavamānena vāyunā \|*  
*viṣṇorniḥśvāsavāto 'yaṃ yadā vegasamīritaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sahasodīryate tāta jagatpravyathate tadā \|*  
*tasmādbrahmavido brahma na paṭhantyativāyutaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

19-20a. The second wind known as Avaha goes on blowing with a loud noise. It is due to (the power of) this wind that Soma and other luminaries rise and appear (our body is a replica in miniature of the cosmos). Within the body this wind is known as Uddna by the learned and the wise.

20b-21a. The wind holds (within itself) the waters from the four oceans and having taken up the water gives it to the clouds for the sake of Protection.6

21b-22a. The winds having equipped (filled) the clouds with waters, presents it to the presiding deity of rains. It is the mighty wind, third in the above enumeration and is famous as Udvaha.

22b-23a. The wind carries the blue big clouds and divides them into various portions, which it makes them shower rain and the clouds become solidified.

23b-24a. It is that wind which carries the celestial cars of gods. It is that fourth wind (in the list) called Samvaha which is capable of subduing mountains. The fifth wind called Vivaka is full of great might and speed. By that hard blowing wind, the internal juices of trees are made sick or dry.

24b-25a. It holds up (supports from below) all the heavenly waters in the sky and prevents them from falling down. Supporting up the sacred waters of the celestial Ganga, the wind blows to prevent them from flowing downwards. And the holy river water stays on (high up in the sky).

25b-26a. The Sun is the source of thousands of rays and it throws (a flood of) light on the earth. But it is through the obstruction of this.

26b-28a. Through the action of that wind, the Moon, after waning, waxes again till he shows his full disc. That wind is known as Parivaha and it is the excellent among the living beings7 and from it Soma, the divine store of nectar, is obtained.

28b-29a. That wind takes away the life of all living creatures at the time of death. His Law is abided by Death and god Yama, the son of the sun-god.

29b-30a. That Law becomes the source of immortality which is attained by Yogins of quiescent mind (intellect) who are ever engaged in Yogic meditation.

30b-31a. By resorting to this wind, thousands of Daksa’s grandsons through his (Daksa’s) ten sons quickly and with speed attained the limits of the universe (broke through them to reach Moksa). NP read? yati vasundharam — ‘goes to the earth. Mbh. (ibid) v. 47 reads bhati vasundharam ‘enlightens or sheds light on the earth. I prefer the Mbh. reading.

31b-32a. It is the wind called Parivaha which is irresistible by anybody8 overwhelmed with whose showers he does not revert (?)

32b-33a. In this way all these wind-gods, the sons of Aditi, are extremely miraculous. They blow about (without being attached to anybody) everywhere. They have access everywhere and are the end of everything.9

33b-34a. It was indeed a great miracle that this excellent mountain was suddenly shaken by the blowing of that wind.

34b-35. This wind is the exhalation from (the nose of) Visnu. When it blows forcibly, О child, the whole world gets agitated. Hence when a stormy wind blows violently persons well-versed in the Veda do not recite it.

## \|\| 1.60.36-39 \|\|

*vāyorvāyubhayaṃ hyuktaṃ brahma tatpīḍitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ parāśarasutaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*uktvā putramadhīṣveti vyomagaṅgāmagāttadā \|*  
*tato vyāse gate snātuṃ śuko brahmavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*svādhyāyamakarodbrahmanvedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|*  
*tatra svādhyāyasaṃsaktaṃ śukaṃ vyāsasutaṃ mune \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sanatkumāro bhagavānekānte samupāgataḥ \|*  
*utthāya satkṛtastena brahmaputro hi kārṣṇinā \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-37a. The Vedas are a form of the wind. If uttered with force and loudly (at this time) the external wind gets pained.” (Hence one should not recite the Vedas when stormy winds blow).10 After addressing these words to his son, the spiritually powerful son of Parasara asked his son to resume the recitation of the Vedas (when the storm subsides). He then left to take his ablutions in the heavenly Ganga.

37b-38a. Thereafter when Vyasa departed to take his bath, shuka, the foremost among the knowers of the Vedas and the master of the Vedas and accessories to Vedas (like shгкshй, Kalpa etc.) resumed his self-study (and recitation) of the Vedas.

38b-39. Then Venerable Sanatkumara11 approached auka, the son of Vyasa who was engaged in the recitation of the Vedas in solitude, О sage. Shuka, the son of Krsna Dvaipayana got up and the son of god Brahma (Sanatkumara) was received by him.

## \|\| 1.60.40 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca viprendra śukaṃ vidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ karoṣi mahābhāga vyāsaputra mahādyute \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О excellent Brahmana! Then Sanatkumara who was prominent among the knowers of the Veda enquired, “O highly fortunate son of Vyasa, О highly brilliant sage! What are you doing (now)?” Shuka said:

## \|\| 1.60.41 \|\|

*śuka uvāca*  
*svādhyāye saṃpravṛtto 'haṃ brahmaputrādhunā sthitaḥ \|*  
*tvaddarśanamanuprāptaḥ kenāpi sukṛtena ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О son of Brahma, I am now engaged in the self study of the Vedas. It is a (great) holy merit of mine whereby I have been able to see you.

## \|\| 1.60.42 \|\|

*kiñcittvāṃ praṣṭumicchāmi tattvaṃ mokṣārthasādhanam \|*  
*tadvadasva mahābhāga yathā ta jjñānamāpnuyām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I wish to ask you something about the principle that is conducive to the attainment of salvation. Please recount it, О highly blessed one, so that I may attain that perfect knowledge. Sanatkumara said:

## \|\| 1.60.43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca*  
*nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣurnāsti vidyāsamaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*nāsti rāgasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgasamaṃ sukham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There is no (other) vision on a par with learning, there is no (other penance on a par with learning. There is no (other misery on a par with sensuous attachment. There is no other happiness on a par with renunciation.

## \|\| 1.60.44 \|\|

*nivṛttiḥ karmaṇaḥ pāpātsatataṃ puṇyaśīlatā \|*

44\. Refraining from sinful activities, being continuously engaged in meritorious activities, good behaviour and adherence to conventional duties — these are the most excellent things contributing to welfare.

## \|\| 1.60.45 \|\|

*mānuṣyamasukhaṃ prāpya yaḥ sajjati sa muhyati \|*

45\. Having obtained the birth as a human being (the life in) which is fraught with sorrow he who becomes attached to it becomes stupefied; such a man is incapable of being emancipated from sorrow. Attachment (to worldly objects) is an indication of misery.

## \|\| 1.60.46 \|\|

*saktasya buddharbhavati mohajālavivarddhinī \|*  
*mohajālāvṛto duḥkhamihāmutra tathāśnute \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The intellect of one attached to the worldly affairs heightens one’s vicious snare of delusion. One ensnared by delusion attains misery here and hereafter.

## \|\| 1.60.47 \|\|

*sarvopāyena kāmasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ \|*  
*kāryaḥ śreyorthinā tau hi śreyoghātārthamudyatau \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Restraint of lust and fury by all means must be pursued by one who seeks welfare. These two are conducive to the destruction of (spiritual) welfare (the moment) they crop up.

## \|\| 1.60.48 \|\|

*nityaṃ krodhāttapo rakṣecchriyaṃ rakṣeñca matsarāt \|*

48\. One must continuously guard one’s penance against fury; one must save one’s splendour and glory from (jndecent) rivalry; one must save one’s learning from being over-honoured and disrespected; one must save oneself from blunders.

## \|\| 1.60.49 \|\|

*ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ kṣamā ca paramaṃ balam \|*

49\. Absence of cruelty is the greatest Dhamai forbearance is the greatest strength; knowledge of the Atman is the greatest knowledge and truthfulness is the greatest of benefits.

## \|\| 1.60.50 \|\|

*yena sarvaṃ parityaktaṃ sa vidvānsa ca paṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*indriyairindriyārthebhyaścaratyātmavaśairiha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He is an erudite scholar who renounces everything. He moves about the objects of the sense-organs by means of those sense-organs that are fully submissive to himself.

## \|\| 1.60.51-53 \|\|

*asajjamānaḥ śāntātmā nirvikāraḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ātmabhūtairatadbhūtaḥ saha caiva vinaiva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sa vimuktaḥ paraṃ śreyo na cireṇādhigacchati \|*  
*adarśanamasaṃsparśastathaivābhāṣāṇaṃ sadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yasya bhūtaiḥ saha mune sa śreyo vindate mahat \|*  
*na hiṃsyātsarvabhūtāni bhūtairmaitrāyaṇaścaret \|\| 53 \|\|*

51 -52a. He who is not getting entangled; he whose soul is quiescent; he who is without aberration; he who has concentration;he who does not identify himself with those beings that do not become one with the Atman, that is, he who is with them and without them, becomes liberated and ere long attains the greatest welfare.

52b-53a. One who never sees others, never touches others, never talks with others, soon accomplishes his summum bonum. О sage.

53Б-55. No one shall injure any living being; one shall move on friendly terms with all the living beings. After attaining this birth no one shall be inimical to anyone. Voluntary indigence, perfect contentment, indifference and absence of ficklemindedness — these, they say are conducive to the welfare of one who is the knower of the Atman, of one who has conquered the Atman.

## \|\| 1.60.56-60 \|\|

*aśokaṃ sthānamātiṣṭa iha cāmutra cābhayam \|*  
*nirāśiṣo na śocanti tyajedāśiṣamātmanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*parityajyāśiṣaṃ saumya duḥkhagrāmādvimokṣyase \|*  
*taparonityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmanā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ajitaṃ jetukāmena bhāvyaṃ saṃgeṣvasaṃginā \|*  
*guṇasaṃgeṣveṣvanāsakta ekacaryā rataḥ sadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇo na cirādeva sukhamāyātyanuttamam \|*  
*dvandvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu varāko ramate muniḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kiñcinprajñānatṛpto 'sau jñānatṛpto na śocati \|*
