*prāgbhāge prathame pāde sanakena mahātmanā \|*  
*dvitīye mokṣadharmākhye mokṣopāyanirūpaṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vedāṅgānāṃ ca kathanaṃ śukotpattiśca vistarāt \|*  
*sanandanena gaditā nāradāya mahātmane \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-3a. In the first quarter of the earlier (first) division, there is a dialogue between Suta and Saunaka, then there is a succinct description of Creation. Many holy religious stories connected with Pravztti (activity) have been narrated in the first quarter of the first division by Sanaka, the great soul.

3b-4. In the second quarter called ‘Moksa Dharma, there is the review of the means to salvation, the detailed narration of the aucillaries of the Vedas and the birth of Shuka. All these have been recounted to the noble-souled Narada by Sanandana.

## \|\| 1.97.5-9 \|\|

*mahātantre samuddiṣṭaṃ paśupāśavimokṣaṇam \|*  
*mantrāṇāṃ śodhanaṃ dīkṣāmantroddhāraśca pūjanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prayogāḥ kavacaṃ nāmasahasraṃ stotrameva ca \|*  
*gaṇeśasūryaviṣṇūnāṃ śivaśaktyoranukramāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sanatkumāramuninā nāradāya tṛtīyake \|*  
*purāṇalakṣaṇaṃ caiva pramāṇaṃ dānameva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pṛthakpṛthak samuddiṣṭaṃ dānakālapuraḥsaram \|*  
*caitrādisarvamāseṣu tithīnāñcapṛthakpṛthak \|\| 8 \|\|*

*proktaṃ pratipadādīnāṃ vrataṃ sarvāghanāśanam \|*  
*sanātanena muninā nāradāya caturthake \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-7a. In the third quarter, the following have been narrated to Narada by sage Sanatkumara: Pasu’s (individual soul’s) liberation from Pasa (bondage of Samsara) as explained in Maha Tantra; the consecration of the Mantras, the initiation, ihe uplift of the Mantras, the mode of worship, practical application, Kavaca (recitation of mantras as protection or coat of mail), the thousand names, the hymns to Ganesa, Surya, Visnu, Siva and Sakti in due order.

7b-9. The following topics have been recounted toNarada by Sage Sanatana in the fourth quarter: The characteristics of the Purana, the authorities and means of valid knowledge, charitable gifts, etc. have been mentioned separately alongwith the proper time for the gifts. The holy vows that destroy all sins and that have to be observed on the Pratipad (first day) and other (subsequent) Tithis in all the months such as of Gaitra etc.

## \|\| 1.97.10 \|\|

*pūrvabhāgo 'yamudito bṛhadākhyānasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*asyottare vibhāge tu praśna ekādaśīvrate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus the first division is summarised. It is called Brhadakhyana. In the second division there is the enquiry about the vowed observance of Ekadasl.

## \|\| 1.97.11-18 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhenātha saṃvādo māndhātuḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*rukmāṅgadakathā puṇyāmohinyutpattikarma ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vasuśāpaśca mohinyai paścāduddharaṇakriyā \|*  
*gaṅgākathā puṇyatamā gayāyātrānukīrtanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kāśyā māhātmyamatulaṃ puruṣottamavarṇanam \|*  
*yātrāvidhānaṃ kṣetrasya bahvākhyānasamanvitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*prayāgasyātha māhātmyaṃ kurukṣetrasya tatparam \|*  
*haridvārasya cākhyānaṃ kāmodākhyānakaṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*badarītīrthamāhātmyaṃ kāmākṣāyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*prabhāsasya ca māhātmyaṃ puṣkarākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gautamākhyānakaṃ paścādvedapādastavastataḥ \|*  
*gokarṇakṣetramāhātmyaṃ lakṣmaṇākhyānakaṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*setumāhātmyakathanaṃ narmadātīrthavarṇanam \|*  
*avantyāścaiva māhātmyaṃ madhurāyāstataḥ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bṛndāvanasya mahimā paśorbrahmāntike gatiḥ \|*  
*mohinīcaritaṃ paścādevaṃ paścādevaṃ vai nāradīyakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

11-18. It is a dialogue between Vasistha and Mandhata: It contains the meritorious story of Rukmangada, the origin and activities of MohinI, the curse on Mohini by Vasu and then the way of extrication therefrom; the holiest story of the Ganga, the narration of the pilgrimage to Gaya; the incomparable greatness of Kasi; the description of Purusottama, the injunctions regarding the pilgrimage to the holy centres alongwith many incidental anecdotes; the greatness of Prayaga; thereafter, that of Kuruk.setra; the description of Haridvara; the narration of Kamoda; the greatness of tlie holy centre Badarl as well as that of Kamiksa; the greatness of Prabhasa; then the description of Puskara; the story of Gautama afterwards and then the hymn called Vedapiida; the greatness of the holy centre of Gokarna; the narrative of Laksmnna; the narration of the greatness of Setu (the Bridge built by Rama from Bharata to Lanka); the description of the sacred river Narmada; the greatness of Avanti; and that of Mathura; the greatness of Vrnd.ivana; the approach of the Pasu (individual soul) near Brahman, the story of Mohini thereafter. These are the contents of the Naradiya Purana.1

## \|\| 1.97.19-21 \|\|

*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyāśrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti brahmaṇo dhāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yastvetadiṣupūrṇāyāṃ dhenūnāṃ saptakānvitam \|*  
*pradadyāddijarṃyāya saṃlabhenmokṣameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yaścānukramaṇīmetāṃ nāradīyasya varṇayet \|*  
*śṛṇuyadvaikacittena so 'pi svargagatiṃ labhet \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The man who hears this with devotion or narrates it with great concentration goes to the abode of Brahma; no hesitation or doubt need be entertained in this respect. He who gives (the manuscript of) this book to an excellentJBrahmana on the Isupiirna (on the full moon day of the 5th month viz. Sravana) alongwith seven cows, attains salvation. He who describes this index of Naradiya Purana or listens to it with concentration attains Heaven.

## Chapter 98. The Markandeya Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.98.1 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca*  
*atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi mārkaṇḍeyābhidhaṃ mune \|*  
*purāṇaṃ sumahatpuṇyaṃ paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ sadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sri Brahma said:

1\. О sage, henceforth, I shall narrate the Purana named Markandeya.1 It is highly meritorious to those who read and listen to it.

## \|\| 1.98.2 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya śakunīnsarvadharmanirūpaṇam \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇaṃ tannavasāhasramīritam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. All the Dharmas have been reviewed therein with reference to the wise birds (in the Vindhya mountains)2. Markandeya Purana is said to contain nine thousand verses.3 The correct reading should beIfd Рйгтта; it will mean “Full-moon day of Awina (Scpteinber-October).

## \|\| 1.98.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyamuneḥ praśno jaimineḥ prāksamīritaḥ \|*  
*pakṣiṇāṃ dharmasaṃjñānaṃ tato janmanirūpaṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. According to the NP.. Vayu, Matsya, Agni and Bh.P the Markandeya P. consists of 9000 verses but the Venkatesvar edition gives only 6447 verses (PJ. VIII.2. (349). It is possible that when NP. was finally redacted, the stories of Rama, PurQravas, Nahusa, Krsna etc. must have been in the then MSS of Mk. P., but they came to be deleted later and the printed editions of the Mk.P. do not include them. Hence the deficiency in the number of verses.

## \|\| 1.98.4 \|\|

*pūrvajanmakathā caiṣāṃ vikriyā cā divaspateḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrā balasyātha draupadeyakathānakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The story of their previous birth; the aberration of Divaspati (Lord of Heaven); the pilgrimage of Bala, the narrative of the sons of Draupadl.

## \|\| 1.98.5 \|\|

*hariścandrakathā puṇyā yuddhamāḍībakābhidham \|*  
*pitāputrasamākhyānaṃ dattātreyakatha tataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The holy story of HariScandra; the battle named Adlbaka;1 the narrative of the father and son (viz. Mahamati and Sumati), then the story of Dattatreya.2

## \|\| 1.98.6 \|\|

*haihasasyātha caritaṃ mahākhyānasamanvitam \|*  
*madālakasākathā proktā hyalarkacaritānvitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then the story of Haihaya alongwith the great narrative, (the story of Kuvalayasva?) then the story of Madalasa is mentioned alongwith the story of Alarka.

## \|\| 1.98.7 \|\|

*sṛṣṭisaṃkīrtanaṃ puṇyaṃ navadhāpārikīrtitam \|*  
*kalpāntakālanirdeśo yakṣasṛṣṭinirūpaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The holy glorification of the creation is made in nine ways; the end of the period of Kalpa is pointed out, the review of the creation of the Yaksas.

## \|\| 1.98.8 \|\|

*rudrādisṛṣṭirapyuktā dvīpacaryānukīrtanam \|*  
*manūnāṃ ca kathā nānākīrtitāḥ pāpahārikāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The creation by Rudra and others is mentioned; the activities in the continents have been mentioned; the stories of the Manus, diverse and destructive of sins, have been mentioned.

## \|\| 1.98.9 \|\|

*tāsu durgākathātyantaṃ puṇyadā cāṣṭameṃ'tare \|*  
*tatpaścātpraṇavotpattistrayītejaḥ samudbhavā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Among those stories, the story of Durga is exceedingly meritorious, in the eighth Manvantara. Thereafter, the origin of Pranava hailing from the brilliance of the three Vedas.

## \|\| 1.98.10 \|\|

*mārtaṇḍasya ca janmākhyātanmāhātmyasamanvitā \|*  
*vaivasvatānvayaścāpi vatsaprīścaritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The narration of the nativity of Martantja alongwith its greatness; the race of Vaivasvata; then the story of Vatsaprl.

## \|\| 1.98.11 \|\|

*khanitrasya tataḥ proktā kathā puṇyā mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*avikṣiccaritaṃ caiva kimicchavratakīrttanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the holy story of the noble-sou Jed Khanitra is mentioned; the story of Aviksit and the glorification of “Kimiccha” Vrata1 (the vowed observance called “What do you wish?”)

## \|\| 1.98.12 \|\|

*nariṣyantasya caritaṃ ikṣvākucaritaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*nalasya caritaṃ paścādrāmacandrasya satkathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The story of Narisyanta, then the story of Iksvaku, thereafter, the story of Nala, and then the excelleAt story of Ramacandra.

## \|\| 1.98.13 \|\|

*kuśavaṃśasamākhyānaṃ somavaṃśānukīrttanam \|*  
*pururavaḥ kathā puṇyā nahuṣasya kathādbhutā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The narration of the line of Kusa; the description of the lunar race; the holy story of Puriiravas and the wonderful story of Nahusa.

## \|\| 1.98.14 \|\|

*yayāticaritaṃ puṇyaṃ yaduvaṃśānukīrttanam \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇabālacaritaṃ māthuraṃ caritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The holy story of Yayati, the enumeration of the scions of the family of Yadu; the story of infant Krsna and then the story of his life at Mathura.

## \|\| 1.98.15 \|\|

*dvārakācaritaṃ cātha kathā sarvāvatārajā \|*  
*tataḥ sāṃkhyasamuddeśaḥ prapañcāsattvakīrtanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The story of his life at Dvaraka, the stories of all incarnations. Then the description of the Sankhya philosophy, the glorification of Sattva quality in the world.

## \|\| 1.98.16-18 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyasya caritaṃ purāṇaśravaṇe phalam \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā purāṇamidamādarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyābhidhaṃ vatsa sa labhetparamāṃ gatim \|*  
*yastu vyākurute caitacchaivaṃ sa labhate padam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tatprayacchellikhitvā yaḥ sauvarṇakarisaṃyutam \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ dvijavaryāya sa labhendbrahmaṇaḥ padam \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Then the story of Markandeya; the benefit of listening to the Parana. The man who listens to this Purana called Markandeya with great devotion and respect, О dear one, attains the greatest goal. He who writes a gloss on this, attains the region of Siva; lie who writes the whole Purana and gives it to an excellent Brahmana on the full moon day in the month of Karttika alongwith the replica of an elephant in gold, attains the region of Brahma. He who narrates or listens to this index (of topics in this Purana) shall attain the benefit desired as in the case of the whole Markandeya Purana.

## Chapter 99. The Agni Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.99.1 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tavāgneyapurāṇakam \|*  
*īśānakalpavṛttāntaṃ vasiṣṭhāyānalo 'bravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sri Brahma said:

1\. Henceforth, I shall describe to you the Agni Purana. The Fire-god recounted the events of Isana Kalpa1 to Vasistha.

## \|\| 1.99.2 \|\|

*tatpañcadaśasāhasraṃ nānā caritamadbhutam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It comprises fifteen thousand2 verses of various wonderful stories. It dispels all the sins of men who listen to this.

## \|\| 1.99.3 \|\|

*praśnaḥ pūrvaṃ purāṇasya kathā sarvāvatārajā \|*  
*sṛṣṭiprakaraṇaṃ cātha viṣṇupūjādikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the outset is the enquiry about the Purana, then the story of all incarnations, then the chapter on the Creation and then the (mode of) worship of Visnu and other things.3

## \|\| 1.99.4 \|\|

*agnikāryaṃ tataḥ paścānmantramudrādilakṣaṇam \|*  
*sarvadīkṣāvidhānaṃ ca abhiṣekanirūpaṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the rites of fire worship, thereafter, the characteristics of the Mantras and Mudras (gestures), etc., the injunctions regarding all initiations; the review of the procedure of ablutions.

## \|\| 1.99.5 \|\|

*lakṣaṇaṃ maṇḍalādīnāṃ kuśāpāmārjanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pavitrāropaṇavidhirdevālayavidhistataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The characteristics of МагцЫа (mystic diagram) etc., then the rite of Marjana (wiping off) with the water from Kusa grass; the injunction regarding the wearing of the Pavitra (Kusa grass with a loop and a tail worn like a ring), and then the instructions regarding the temples.

## \|\| 1.99.6-7 \|\|

*śālagrāmādipūjā ca mūrtilakṣma pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*nyāsādīnāṃ vidhānaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpūrtakaṃ tataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vināyakādipūjā ca nānādīkṣāvidhiḥ param \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā sarvadevānāṃ brahmaṇḍasya nirūpaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Then the worship of Salagrama etc., the separate signs and symbols of the Murtis, the injunctions regarding the Nyasa rites, the worship of Vinayaka etc. alongwith their Pratistha (installation), thereafter the rules regarding initiation of diverse kinds; the installation of all deities and the review of the Cosmic egg.

## \|\| 1.99.8 \|\|

*gaṅgāditīrthamāhātmyaṃ dvīpavarṣānuvarṇanam \|*  
*ūrddhvādholokaracanā jyotiścakranirūpaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The greatness of the Ganga and other holy rivers, the description of the continents and the sub-continents, the arrangement of the upper and the lower worlds, the review of Jyotiscakra (the circle of the luminaries.)

## \|\| 1.99.9 \|\|

*jyotiṣaṃ ca tataḥ proktaṃ śāstraṃ yuddhajayārṇavam \|*  
*ṣaṭkarma ca tataḥ proktaṃ mantramantrauṣadhīgaṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Jyotisa (Astrology and Astronomy) is then described and then the scripture “Yuddhajayarnava” (Ocean of the conquests in battles), then the six holy rites are narrated and also the collections of Mantras and medicinal herbs to be used with Mantras.

## \|\| 1.99.10 \|\|

*kubjikādisamarcatvaṃ ṣoḍhā nyāsavidhistathā \|*  
*koṭihomavidhānaṃ ca manvantaranirūpaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The rites of worshipping Kubjika (an unmarried girl of eight years) etc., then the six types of Nyasa rites, then the injunction regarding “kotihoma” (a crore of Homas), the review of the Manvantaras.

## \|\| 1.99.11 \|\|

*brahmacaryādidharmāṃśca śrāddhakalpavidhistataḥ \|*  
*grahayajñastataḥ proktovaidikasmārtakarma ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The pious rites of Brahmacarya (vow of celibacy) etc., then the rules regarding the rituals of Sraddha, then Graha- Yajna (the sacrifice for the planets) is mentioned, then the various holy rites laid down in the Vedas and the Smrtis.

## \|\| 1.99.12 \|\|

*prāyaścittānukathanaṃ tithīnāṃ ca vratādikam \|*  
*vāravratānukathanaṃ nakṣatravratakīrtanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The narration of expiatory rites, the Vratas etc. to be performed on the various Tithis, days of the week and the constellations.

## \|\| 1.99.13 \|\|

*māsikavratanirddeśo dīpadānavidhistathā \|*  
*navavyūhārcanaṃ proktaṃ narakāṇāṃ nirūpaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The guidance regarding monthly Vratas, the rules regarding the charitable gifts of lamps, the worship of the Navavyuhas (the nine manifestations) and the review of hells.

## \|\| 1.99.14 \|\|

*vratānāṃ cāpi dānānāṃ nirūpaṇamihoditam \|*  
*nāḍīcakrasamuddeśaḥ saṃdhyāvidhiranuttamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The review of Vratas (sacred vowed observances) and charitable gifts, the direction regarding Nadi Gakra (circle of nerves) and the excellent rules regarding the Sandhya prayers.

## \|\| 1.99.15 \|\|

*gāyatryarthasya nirddeśo liṅgastotraṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*rājyābhiṣekamantroktirddharmakṛtyaṃ ca bhūbhujām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The stipulation regarding the meaning of the Gayatrl, then the hymn unto the Linga, the specification of the Mantras for the coronation of kings; the righteous duties (and activities) of kings.

## \|\| 1.99.16 \|\|

*svapnādhyāyastataḥ proktaḥ śakunādinirūpaṇam \|*  
*maṇḍalādikanirddeṃśo ratnadīkṣāvidhistataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the chapter on dreams is mentioned, the review of omens, etc., the specification regarding Mandala (mystic diagram) etc., then the rules regarding ‘Ratna Diksa

## \|\| 1.99.17 \|\|

*rāmoktanītinirddeśo ratnānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*dhanurvidyā tataḥ proktā vyavahārapradarśanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The guidance in polity mentioned by Rama, then the characteristics of Ratnas (jewels), then the science of archery is described, then the method of dealing is revealed.

## \|\| 1.99.18 \|\|

*devāsuravimardākhyā hyāyurvedanirūpaṇam \|*  
*gajādīnāṃ cikitsā ca teṣāṃ śāntistataḥ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The narrative of the conflict between the Devas and the Asuras, the review of Ayurveda (Medical Science), the Veterinary science (e. g. the treatment of elephants etc., and their pacification).

## \|\| 1.99.19 \|\|

*gonarādicikitsā ca nānāpūjāstataḥ param \|*  
*śāntayaścāpi vividhāśchandaḥ śāstramataḥ param \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The treatment of cows, diagnosis and treatment of men, etc., then the different kinds of Pujas; different kinds of Santis (pacificatory rites); then the science of prosody.

## \|\| 1.99.20 \|\|

*sāhityaṃ ca tataḥ paścādekārṇādisamāhvayāḥ \|*  
*siddhaśabdānuśiṣṭiścakośaḥ sargādivargakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then literature (literary criticism) and the (lexicon of) single-syllabled norms, thereafter, the enumeration of the formation of words, then lexicon according to the different groups and formations.

## \|\| 1.99.21 \|\|

*pralayānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca śārīrakanirūpaṇam \|*  
*varṇanaṃ narakāṇāṃ ca yogāśtramataḥ param \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The characteristics of dissolutions; the review of the Sariraka (limbs of the body in AP. ch. 370), description of hells, then the Yoga system of Philosophy.

## \|\| 1.99.22 \|\|

*brahmajñānaṃ tataḥ paścātpurāṇaśravaṇe phalam \|*  
*etadāgneyakaṃ vipra purāṇaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter, the knowledge of the Brahman, the benefit of listening to the Purana, О Brahmana, this is mentioned as the Agni Purana.

## \|\| 1.99.23-25 \|\|

*tallikhitvā tu yo dadyātsuvarṇakalamānvitam \|*  
*tiladhenu yutaṃ cāpi mārgaśīrṣyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*purāṇārthavide so 'tha svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*eṣānukramaṇī proktā tavāgneyasya muktidā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śṛṇvatāṃ paṭhatāṃ caiva nṛṇāṃ ceha paratra ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. He who writes this and gives it to a person who knows the meanings of the Purana, on the full moon day in the month of Margashir?a in accordance with the injunctions, alongwith a gold lotus and a replica of a cow in gingelly seeds, is honoured in the heavenly world. This index of topics in the Agni Purana narrated to you is the bestower of salvation unto the men who read and listen to this. It benefits them both here and hereafter.

## Chapter 100. The Bhavisya Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.100.1 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca*  
*atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ sarvasiddhidam \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃ bhavataḥ sarvalokābhīṣṭapradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sri Brahma, said:

1\. Henceforth, I shall recount to you the Bhavisya Purana1 which yields all Siddhis and which bestows the desired objects of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.100.2 \|\|

*yatrāhaṃ sarvadevānāmādikartā samudgataḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭyarthaṃ tatra saṃjāto manuḥ svāryabhuvaḥ purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In it, I have come up as the primordial maker of all the Devas. For the purpose of creation, there was born the Svayambhuva (son of the self-born) Manu formerly.

## \|\| 1.100.3 \|\|

*sa māṃ praṇamya papraccha dharmaṃ sarvāthasādhakam \|*  
*ahaṃ tasmai tadā prītaḥ prāvocaṃ dharmasaṃhitām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He bowed to me and asked me about Dharma (pious and religious duties) that is the means of achieving all objects.

## \|\| 1.100.4 \|\|

*purāṇānāṃ yadā vyāso vyāsaṃ caktre mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tadā tāṃ saṃhitāṃ sarvāṃ pañcadhā vyabhajanmuniḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the highly intelligent Vyasa classified the Puranas, thesage divided that Samhita(of the Bhavisya Purana) into five divisions.

## \|\| 1.100.5 \|\|

*adhorakalpavṛttāntaṃ nānāścaryakathanvitam \|*  
*tatrādimaṃ smṛtaṃ parvaṃ brāhmaṃ yatrāstyupakramaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The incidents of Aghora Kalpa are mentioned alongwith many wonderful stories. There the first Parvan is Brahma where the Upakrama (beginning) is mentioned.

## \|\| 1.100.6 \|\|

*sūtaśaunakasaṃvāde purāṇapraśnasaṃkramaḥ \|*  
*ādityacaritaprāyaḥ sarvākhyānasamanvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Tn the course of the dialogue between Suta and Saunaka there is the transmission of the enquiry regarding the Purana. It is full of the stories of the sun and accompanied by all narratives.

## \|\| 1.100.7 \|\|

*sṛṣṭyādilakṣaṇopetaḥ śāstrasarvasvarūpakaḥ \|*  
*pustalekhakalekhānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The entire form of the scripture is endued with the characteristics of creation etc. Thereafter, the characteristics of the calligraphy of the writers of books are mentioned.

## \|\| 1.100.8 \|\|

*saṃskārāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cātra kīrtitam \|*  
*pakṣasyāditithīnāṃ ca kalpāḥ sapta ca kīrtitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The characteristic features of all Samskaras (purificatory rites) are mentioned here. Seven rituals regarding the Tithis of the lunar fortnight are mentioned.

## \|\| 1.100.9-10 \|\|

*aṣṭamyādyāḥ śeṣakalpā vaiṣṇave parvaṇi smṛtāḥ \|*  
*śaive ca kāyato bhinnāḥ saure cāntyakathānvayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pratisargāhvayaṃ paścānnānākhyānasamanvitam \|*  
*purāṇasyopasaṃhārasahitaṃ parva pañcamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The Kalpas for the remaining Tithis beginning with Astaml (eighth day) are mentioned in the section called Vaishnava Parvan. In the next Parvan called Saiva Parvan those who are different in bodies are mentioned. (?) In the Saura Parvan the final stories are mentioned. The next Parvan is called Pratisarga. It contains different stories alongwith the conclusion of the Purana. It is the fifth Parvan.

## \|\| 1.100.11-12 \|\|

*eṣu pañcasu pūrvasmin brahmaṇo mahimādhikāḥ \|*  
*dharme kāme ca mokṣe tu viṣṇoścāpi śivasya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīye ca saure vargacatuṣṭaye \|*  
*pratisargāhvayaṃ tvantyaṃ proktaṃ sarvakathānvitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Among these five, in the first Parvan, the glory of Brahma is very much greater than that of Visnu or Siva in regard to Dharma, Kama (love) and Moksa (salvation). Thus the story mentioned in the second, third and the fourth section (Varga) called Saura and in the last one named Pratisarga has been recounted.

## \|\| 1.100.13 \|\|

*sabhaviṣyaṃ vinirddiṣṭaṃ parva vyāsena dhīmatā \|*  
*caturddaśasahasraṃ tu purāṇaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Parvan alongwith the Bhavisya has been proclaimed by the intelligent Vyasa. The Purana consists of fourteen thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.100.14 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃ sarvadevānāṃ sāmyaṃ yatra prakīrtitam \|*  
*guṇānāṃ tāratamyena samaṃ brahmeti hi śrutiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Bhavisya is that Parvan (Purana) where the equality among all the deities is glorified. In the point of view Not found in the published version of this Purana of the comparison of the Gunas, the Sruti says that “Brahman is equal.”

## \|\| 1.100.15-16 \|\|

*taṃ likhitvā tu yo dadyātpauṣyāṃ vidvānvimatsaraḥ \|*  
*guḍadhenuyutaṃ hemavastramālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vācakaṃ pustakaṃ cāpi pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*gandhādyairbhojyabhakṣyaiśca kṛtvā nīrājanādikam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. That a learned person who being free from jealousy writes or gets written this Purana and on the full moon day of the month called ‘Pausa (December-January) worships duly both the reader (of this Purana) and the book (the manuscript of this Purana) alongwith the replica of a cow made of jaggery as well as gold, clothes, garlands and ornaments.

## \|\| 1.100.17 \|\|

*yo vai jitendriyo bhūtvā sopavāsaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*atha vaikahaviṣyāśī kīrtayecchṛṇuyādapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Or a person who has subdued his sense-organs, observes fasts or takes only one meal per day of sacred Havisya food (food worthy of being oblated in sacrificial fire), hears or glorifies (recounts) this with concentrated mind becomes absolved of terrible sins and attains to the supreme region of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.100.18-19 \|\|

*sa muktaḥ pātakairghoraiḥ prayāti brahmaṇaḥ padam \|*  
*yo 'pyanukramaṇīmetāṃ bhaviṣyasya nirūpitām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*paṭhedvā śṛṇuyāccaitāṃ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. He who reads or listens to this index to Bhavisya Purana as mentioned here shall attain worldly pleasures and liberation.

## Chapter 101. The Brahma-Vaivarla Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.101.1 \|\|

*śrībrahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ daśamaṃ tava \|*  
*brahmavaivartakaṃ nāma vedamārgānudarśakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sri Brahma said:

1\. О dear child, I shall recount to you the tenth Purana named Brahmavaivarta.1 It points out the path of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.101.2 \|\|

*sāvarṇiryatra bhagavānsākṣāddevarṣaye sthitaḥ \|*  
*nāradāya purāṇārthaṃ prāha sarvamalaukikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In it the Lord himself assumed the form of Savarna and narrated the subject matter of the Purana to Narada,1 the divine sage. He mentioned the entire miraculous non-mundane subject matter to him.

## \|\| 1.101.3 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ sāraḥ prītirharau hare \|*  
*tayorabhedasiddhyarthaṃ brahmavaivartamuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The essence of virtue (dharma), wealth, love and liberation from bondage of samsara is the pleasure in and love for Hari and Нага. In order to establish their non-difference is meant the excellent Brahrnavaivarta (transformation of Brahman).

## \|\| 1.101.4 \|\|

*rathantarasya kalpasya vṛttāntaṃ yanmayoditam \|*  
*śatakoṭipurāṇe tatsaṃkṣipya prāha vedavit \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The events of Rathantara Kalpa narrated in details by me in the Purana of hundred crores of verses were condensed and narrated by the knower of the Vedas (i.e. Vyasa).

## \|\| 1.101.5 \|\|

*vyāsaścaturddhā saṃvyasya brahmavaivartasaṃjñite \|*  
*aṣṭādaśasahasraṃ tatpurāṇaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the Purana called Brahrnavaivarta he condensed it into four parts. This Purana is reputed to contain eighteen thousand verses.2

## \|\| 1.101.6 \|\|

*brahmaprakṛtivighneśakṛṣṇakhaṇḍasamanvitam \|*  
*tatra sūtarṣisaṃvāde purāṇopakramastataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It consists of parts (sections) called Brahma, Prakrti, Ganesa and Krsna. There the Purana starts with the dialogue between Suta and Sages.

## \|\| 1.101.7 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiprakaraṇaṃ tvādyaṃ tato nāradavedhasoḥ \|*  
*vivādaḥ sumahānyatra dvayorāsītparābhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The first chapter (prakarana) pertains to the creation; then there is a great verbal disputation between Narada and Vedhas (god Brahma) in which both of them met with a great defeat.

## \|\| 1.101.8-11 \|\|

*śivalokagatiḥ paścājjñānalābhaḥ śivātmane \|*  
*śivavākyena tatpaścānmarīcernāradasya tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gamanaṃ caiva sāvarṇerjñānārthaṃ siddhasevite \|*  
*āśrame sumahāpuṇye trailokyāścaryakāriṇī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*etaddhi brahmakhaṇḍaṃ hi śrutaṃ pāpavināśanam \|*  
*tataḥ sāvarṇisaṃvādo nāradasya samīritaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇamāhātmyasaṃyukto nānākhyānakathottaram \|*  
*prakṛteraṃśabhūtānāṃ kalānāṃ cāpi varṇitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-10a. Then the attainment of Siva’s world. The acquisition of perfect knowledge through the realisation of S;va’s Atman through Siva’s exposition. Thereafter, О Marlci, Narada goes to the hermitage of Savarni1 which was resorted to by Siddhas for the purpose of perfect knowledge. That is an exceedingly meritorious hermitage causing wonderment in the three worlds. This is well known as Brahma Khanka.# It is destructive of sins.

10b-11. Then the dialogue between Savarni and Narada is recounted. It contains the greatness of Krsna and a number of various different anecdotes, the greatness of the Kalas (digits) that are parts of Prakrti is described.

## \|\| 1.101.12 \|\|

*māhātmyaṃ pūjanādyaṃ ca vistareṇa yathāsthitam \|*  
*etatprakṛtikhaṇḍaṃ hi śrutaṃ bhūtividhāyakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The mode of worship in the precise manner has been described in detail. This is the well known Prakrti Khantfa that brings about prosperity.

## \|\| 1.101.13 \|\|

*gaṇeśajanmasaṃpraśnaḥ sapuṇyakamahāvratam \|*  
*pārvatyāḥ kārtikeyena saha vighneśasaṃbhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The word of enquiry about the nativity of Ganesa: Parvati’s great and meritorious Vrata (holy vow); the birth of Vighnesa along with Karttikeya.

## \|\| 1.101.14-16 \|\|

*caritaṃ kārtavīryasya jāmadagryasya cādbhutam \|*  
*vivādaḥ sumahānāsījjāmadagryagaṇeśayoḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etadvighneśakhaṇḍaṃ hi sarvavighnavināśanam \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇajanmasaṃpraśno janmākhyānaṃ tato 'dbhutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gokule gamanaṃ gaścātpūtanādivadādbhūtāḥ \|*  
*bālyakaumārajā līlā vividhāstatra varṇitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-15a. The wonderful story of Karttavirya andjamada- gnya (Parasurama). A great dispute arises between Ganesa and Jamadagnya (Parasurama). This is the Vighnesa Khanka that dispels all obstacles.

15b-16. The enquiry regarding the birth of Sri Krsna: The narration of his birth in wonderful manner, his departure to Gokula (the cowherds' colony), the miracles of killing Putana, etc.; his sports during infancy and boyhood of diverse kinds, are described.

## \|\| 1.101.17 \|\|

*rāsakrīḍā ca gopībhiḥ śāradī samudāhṛtā \|*  
*rahasye rādhayā krīḍā varṇitā bahuvistarā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Rasa sport in the autumn alongwith the cowherd- esses is mentioned; his secret dalliance with Radha is described in detail.

## \|\| 1.101.18 \|\|

*sahākrūreṇa tatpaścānmathurāgamanaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*kaṃsādīnāṃ vadhe vṛtte kṛṣṇasya dvijasaṃskṛtiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereafter, Hari goes to Mathura accompained by Akrura. After the killing of Kaihsa and others Krsna is consecrated as a twice-born (i.e. investiture with the sacred thread.)

## \|\| 1.101.19 \|\|

*kāśyasāṃdīpaneḥ paścādvidyopādānamadbhutam \|*  
*yavanasya vadhaḥ paścāddvārakāgamanaṃ hareḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The wonderful learning of all lores from Sandlpani ofKasi, the killing of Yavana, thereafter the departure of Hari to Dvaraka.

## \|\| 1.101.20 \|\|

*narakādivadhastatra kṛṣṇena vihito 'dbhutaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇakhaṇḍamidaṃ vipra nṛṇāṃ saṃsārakhaṇḍanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The killing of Naraka etc, was wonderfully carried out by Krsna. О Brahmana, this is the Krsna Kharuja that cuts at the root of worldly existence of men.

## \|\| 1.101.21 \|\|

*paṭhitaṃ ca śrutaṃ dhyātaṃ pūjitaṃ cābhivanditam \|*  
*ityetadbrahmavaivartapurāṇaṃ cātyalaukikam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. This is read, heard, meditated upon, worshipped and saluted. Thus is the Supramundane Brahmavaivarta Purana.

## \|\| 1.101.22 \|\|

*vyāsoktaṃ cādi saṃbhūtaṃ paṭhañchṛṇvanvimucyate \|*  
*vijñānājñānaśamanāddhorātsaṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This is narrated at the outset by Vyasa. One who reads it and listens to it is liberated from the terrible ocean of worldly existence through the acquisition of perfect knowledge and the suppression of ignorance.

## \|\| 1.101.23 \|\|

*likhitvedaṃ ca yo dadyānmādhyāṃ dhenusamanvitam \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpnoti sa mukto 'jñānabandhanāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He who writes this out and makes a gift of it on the full moon day in the month of Magha alongwith a cow attains Brahmaloka. He is liberated from the bondage of ignorance.

## \|\| 1.101.24 \|\|

*yaścānukramaṇīṃ cāpi paṭhedvā śṛṇuyādapi \|*  
*so 'pi kṛṣṇaprasādena labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He too, who reads or listens to this index (contents of this Purana) attains the desired benefit, thanks to Krsna’s grace.

## Chapter 102. The Linga Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.102.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu putra pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ liṅgasaṃjñitam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

God Brahma said:

1\. О son, listen, I shall recount to you the Purana called Linga.1 It bestows worldly pleasures and salvation on those who read and listen to it.

## \|\| 1.102.2 \|\|

*yacca liṅgābhidhaṃ tiṣṭhanvahniliṅge haro 'bhyadhāt \|*  
*mahyaṃ dharmādisiddhyarthaṃ magnikalpakathāśrayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It was while stationed in the huge fiery column that Нага narrated (the subject matter in the Purana) named Linga to me in order that virtue etc, may be realised. The story refers to the incidents of the Agni Kalpa.1

## \|\| 1.102.3 \|\|

*tadeva vyāsadevena bhāgadvayasamanvitam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ liṅgamuditaṃ bahvākhyānavicitritam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The same thing was described by the holy Lord Vyasa in two parts. The Linga Purana is mentioned to be miraculous with many narratives.

## \|\| 1.102.4 \|\|

*tadekādaśasāhasraṃ haramāhātmyasūcakam \|*  
*paraṃ sarvapurāṇānāṃ sārabhūtaṃ jagattraye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It comprises of eleven thousand verses.2 It indicates the greatness of Нага. It is greater than all the other Puranas. It is the essence of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.102.5 \|\|

*purāṇopakrame praśnaḥ sṛṣṭiḥ saṃkṣepataḥ purā \|*  
*yogākhyānaṃ tataḥ proktaṃ kalpākhyānaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is the enquiry at the start of the Purana. The former creation is succinctly described. Then the Yoga system is narrated; thereafter, the Kalpa is recounted.

## \|\| 1.102.6 \|\|

*liṅgodbhavastadaṃbā ca kīrtitā hi tataḥ param \|*  
*sanatkumāraśailādisaṃvādaścātha pāvanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The origin of the Linga; then Amba is glorified; then the holy dialogue between Sanatkumara and Silada’s son i.e. Nandin.

## \|\| 1.102.7 \|\|

*tato dādhīcacaritaṃ yugadharmanirūpaṇam \|*  
*tato bhuvana kośākhyā sūryasomānvayastataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, the story of Dadhlca, the review of the Yugadharma (virtue peculiar to the different Yugas), then the narrative of the Bhuvana Kosa (The globe of the world), then the Solar and the Lunar races are described.

## \|\| 1.102.8 \|\|

*tataśca vistarātsargastripurākhyānakaṃ tathā \|*  
*liṅgapratiṣṭhā ca tataḥ paśupāśavimokṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the creation is described in detail; then the story of the Tripuras; the installation of the Linga and then the liberation of the Pasu (individual soul) from Pasa (bondage i.e. from samsara)

## \|\| 1.102.9 \|\|

*śivavratāni ca tathā sadācāranirūpaṇam \|*  
*prāyaścitānyariṣṭāni kāśīśrīśailavarṇanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The holy rites of Siva, the survey of good conduct Expiatory rites; Aristas (evil portents, harassments etc.); then the description of Kasi and Sri Saila.

## \|\| 1.102.10 \|\|

*andhakākhyānakaṃ paścādvārāhacaritaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*nṛsiṃhacaritaṃ paścājjalandharavadhastataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The narration of Andhaka; then the story of Varaha (The Divine Boar), the story of Nrsimha and then the slaying of Jalandhara.

## \|\| 1.102.11 \|\|

*śaivaṃ sahasranāmātha dakṣayajñavināśanam \|*  
*kāmasya dahanaṃ paścādgirijāyāḥ karagrahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The thousand epithets of Siva, the destruction of Daksa’s sacrifice. Каша is burnt down, then the story of the marriage of Girija.

## \|\| 1.102.12 \|\|

*tato vināyakākhyānaṃ nṛpākhyānaṃ śivasya ca \|*  
*upamanyukathā cāpi pūrvabhāga itīritaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then the story of Vinayaka, that of the kings and that of Siva; then the story of Upamanyu. This is the summary of the first section.1

## \|\| 1.102.13 \|\|

*viṣṇumāhātmyakathanamaṃbarīṣakathā tataḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāranandīśasaṃvādaśca punarmune \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The narration of the greatness of Visnu, then the story of Ambarlsa, О sage, again there is the dialogue between Sanatkumara and Nandlsa.

## \|\| 1.102.14 \|\|

*śivamāhā tmyaseyuktaḥ strānayāgādikaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*sūryapūjāvidhiścaiva śivapūjā ca muktidā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The greatness of Siva, the mode of ablution and sacrificial system (yaga) etc. the injunction regarding the worship of the sun-god. Then the worship of Siva that confers liberation from samsara.

## \|\| 1.102.15 \|\|

*dānāni bahudhāktāni śrāddhaprakaraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhātaṃ tramuditaṃ tato 'ghorasya kīrtanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Many types of charitable gifts are mentioned; then the chapter onSraddha, the Pratistha Tantra (the ritualistic text of installation), then the glorification of Aghora.

## \|\| 1.102.16 \|\|

*vajreśvarī mahāvidyā gāyatrīmahimā tataḥ \|*  
*tryaṃbakasya ca māhātmyaṃ purāṇaśravaṇasya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The great Vidya of Vajresvari, then the glory of Gayatri, the greatness of Tryambaka, (the three-eyed Lord) as well as that of listening to the Purana.

## \|\| 1.102.17 \|\|

*evaṃ coparibhāgaste laiṅgasya kathito mayā \|*  
*vyāsena hi nibaddhasya rudrāmāhātmyasūcitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus the latter half of thcLinga Purana as composed by Vyasa has been recounted by me and the greatness of Rudra is indicated.2

## \|\| 1.102.18-21 \|\|

*likhitvaitatpurāṇaṃ tu tiladhenusamanvitam \|*  
*phaālgunyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ yo dadyādbhaktyā dvijātaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sa labhecchivasāyujyaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭecchṛṇuyādvāpi laiṅgaṃ pāpāpahaṃ naraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sa bhuktabhogo loke 'sminnante śivapuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*liṅgānukramaṇīmetāṃ paṭhedyaḥ śṛṇuyāttathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tāvubhau śivabhaktau tu lokadvitayabhoginau \|*  
*jāyatāṃ girijābhartuḥ prasādānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-19a. This Purana must be written and gifted to a Brahmana with devotion on the full moonday in the month of Phalguna alongwith gingelly seeds and a cow. He who does so, attains Sayujya with Siva. He does not have to suffer from old age or death.

19b-20a. The man who reads or listens to the Linga Purana that dispels sins, enjoys pleasures in this world and at the end attains to Siva’s city.

20b-21. The man who reads the index and the man who listens to this — both of them are the devotees of Siva. They enjoy both the worlds through the Grace of the Lord o#f Girija. There is no doubt about this.

## Chapter 103. The Varaha Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.103.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi vārāhaṃ vai purāṇakam \|*  
*bhāgadvayayutaṃ śaśvadviṣṇumāhātmyasūcakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

God Brahma said:

1\. О dear one, listen. I shall recount the Varaha Purana1. It is comprised of two parts and it continuously indicates the greatness of Visnu.

## \|\| 1.103.2-3 \|\|

*mānavasya tu kalpasya prasaṃgaṃ matkṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*nibabandha purāṇe 'smiṃścaturviṃśasahasrake \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vyāso hi viduṣāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇo bhuvi \|*  
*tatrādau śubhasaṃvādaḥ smṛtobhūmivarāhayoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The context of the Manasa Kalpa composed by me before, or description of the acts I did in the Manava Kalpa before was compiled by Vyasa, the most excellent one among scholars in this Purana that comprises twenty-four thousand verses. Vyasa is the incarnation of Visnu himself on the earth. There at the outset is the auspicious dialogue between the Earth and Varaha. (Divine Boar-Visnu).

## \|\| 1.103.4 \|\|

*athādikṛtavṛttānte raṃbhasya caritaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*durjayasya ca tatpaścācchrāddhakalpa udīritaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the course of the incidents of the earlier period, there is the story of Rambha and then that of Durjaya, thereafter Sraddha Kalpa (the rituals of theSraddha) is described.

## \|\| 1.103.5 \|\|

*mahātapasa ākhyānaṃ gauryutpattistataḥ parā \|*  
*vināyakasya nāgānāṃ senānyādityayorapi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The narration of the great penance (Mahatapas)-then the origin of Gaurl, Vinayaka, the Nagas, the commandcr-in- chicf (i.e. Karttikeya) and Aditya (the sun).

## \|\| 1.103.6 \|\|

*gaṇānāṃ ca tathā devyā dhanadasya vṛṣasya ca \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ satyatapaso vratākhyānasamanvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then there is the narrative of the Ganas of the.goddess, of Kubera and that of Vi sa; then the narrative of Satya- tapasa alongwith the narration of vratas.

## \|\| 1.103.7 \|\|

*agastyagītā tatpaścādrudragītā prakīrtitā \|*  
*mahiṣāsuravidhvaṃsamāhātmyaṃ ca triśaktijam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, Agastyaglta and Rudraglta are narrated; then the glory of the destruction of demon Mahisa (Buffalo) brought about by the three Saktis.

## \|\| 1.103.8 \|\|

*parvādhyāyastataḥ śvetopākhyānaṃ gopradānikam \|*  
*ityādi kṛtavṛttāntaṃ prathame darśitaṃ mayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then is the chapter on Parvans (religious festivals), the incidental narrative of Sveta and the charitable gift of cows. All these incidents had already been pointed out by me in the section on Bhagavad Dharma (virtuous pathway to the Lord).

## \|\| 1.103.9-12 \|\|

*bhagavaddharmake paścādvatatīrthakathānakam \|*  
*dvātriṃśadaparādhānāṃ prāyaścittaṃ śarīragam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tīrthānāṃ cāpi sarveṣāṃ māhātmyaṃ pṛthagīritam \|*  
*mathurāyā viśeṣeṇa śrāddhādīnāṃ vidhistataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*varṇanaṃ yamalokasya ṛṣiputraprasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*vipākaḥ karmaṇāṃ caiva viṣṇuvratanirūpaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*gokarṇasya ca māhātmyaṃ kīrtitaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*ityevaṃ pūrvabhāgo 'yaṃ purāṇasya nirūpitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. Thereafter, the narration ofVratas andTlrthas, the expiatory bodily rites for thirty two offences. The greatness of holy centres is mentioned separately and particularly of Mathura, thereafter, the rules of procedure regarding Sraddha etc., the description of the world of Yama, in thecontext of the son of the sage, the ultimate result of Karmans and the review of Visnu's Vratas, the greatness of Gokarna that is destructive of sins, is mentioned. Thus the early part (i.e. the first part) of the Purana is reviewed.

## \|\| 1.103.13-14 \|\|

*uttare pravibhāge tu pulastyakururājayoḥ \|*  
*saṃvāde sarvatīrthānāṃ māhātmyaṃ vistarātpṛthak \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aśeṣadharmāścākhyātāḥ pauṣkaraṃ puṇyaparva ca \|*  
*ityevaṃ tava vārāhaṃ proktaṃ pāpavināśanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. In the latter part, in the course of the dialogue between Pulastya and the king of Kurus, the greatness of all the holy centres is mentioned in detail, severally. AH the virtues too have been mentioned. The holy Parvan pertaining to Puskara is mentioned. Thus the Variiha Purana. that is destructive of sins is recounted to you.

## \|\| 1.103.15-17 \|\|

*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva bhagavadbhaktivardhanam \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ garuḍa kṛtvā tiladhenusamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*likhitvaitacca yo dadyāccaitryāṃ viprāya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa labhedvaiṣṇavaṃ dhāma devarṣigaṇavanditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yo vānukramaṇīmentāṃ śṛṇotyapi paṭhatyapi \|*  
*so 'pi bhaktiṃ labhedviṣṇau saṃsārocchedakāriṇīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. This increases devotion to the Lord, of those who read and listen to this. He who writes out this Purama an\] gives it to a Brahmana with devotion, along with a gold replica of Garuda and gingelly seeds and a cow, on the full moon day in the month of Chaitra, attains the abode of Visnu. He is paid obeisance by the groups of Devas and sages. He who reads or listens to this index obtains devotion to Visnu that is the cause of dissolution of worldly existence.

## Chapter 104. The Skanda Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.104.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ skandasaṃjñakam \|*  
*yasminpratipadaṃ sākṣānmahādevo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

God Brahma said:

1\. О dear one,‘listen. I shall recount Skanda Purana1 wherein Lord Mahadeva is present in every word.

## \|\| 1.104.2 \|\|

*purāṇe śatakoṭo tu yacchaivaṃ varṇitaṃ mayā \|*  
*lakṣaṃ tasyārthaṃ jātasya sāro vyāsena kīrtitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the Purana of a hundred crores of verses, I had described the story of Siva. In a hundred thousand verses, the essence of those topics has been described by Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.104.3 \|\|

*skandāhvayastatra khaṇḍāḥ saptaiva parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*ekāśītisahasraṃ tu skāndaṃ sarvoghakṛtaṃnam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He has named it Skanda. There are seven khan^as (parts) in it. It cbmprises eighty one thousand verses. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.104.4 \|\|

*yaḥ śṛṇoti paṭhedvāpi sa tu sākṣācchivaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*yatra māheśvarā dharmāḥ ṣaṇmukhena prakāśitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He who listens to this or reads this becomes Siva himself. Therein all the rites and rituals regarding Mahesvara have been revealed by Sanmukha (Skanda).

## \|\| 1.104.5-6 \|\|

*kalpe tatpuruṣe vṛttāḥ sarvasiddhividhāyakāḥ \|*  
*tasya māheśvaraścātha khaṇḍaḥ pāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kiñcinnyūnārkasāhasro bahupuṇyo bṛhatkathaḥ \|*  
*sucaritraśatairyuktaḥ skandamāhātmyasūcakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. These incidents which bring about all Siddhis had happened in the Tatpurusa Kalpa. The Mahesvara Khanka-, the first Skandha of this (Purana) destroys all sins. It consists of a little less than twelve thousand verses. It is highly merito- tious and contains big stories. It contains hundreds of good stories. It indicates the greatness of Skanda.

## \|\| 1.104.7 \|\|

*yatra kedāramāhātmye purāṇopakramaḥ purā \|*  
*dakṣayajñakathā paścācchivaliṅgārcane phalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The following are the topics dealt with1 in the context of the greatness of Kedara, the Purana has its starting point; thereafter the story of Daksa’s Yajna and then the benefit of worshipping Siva Linga. Although the Ycnkatesvara Edt. contains more than 12,000 verses more than the extent recorded in the NP and other Puranas, the Venkatesvare edition does not include the Mathura, and Mdgha Mahatmyas in the Vaishnavas khanda, though the NP mentions them as a part of that khapda. Needless to say that the author of the NP had a different edition than those before the modern editors of (he Bombay, Lucknow and Calcutta edidons. As the SK. P. is a stupendously voluminous Purana a detailed analysis of all its contents is not possible here for want of space.

## \|\| 1.104.8 \|\|

*samudramathanākhyānaṃ devendracaritaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pārvatyāḥ samupākhyānaṃ vivāhastadanantaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The narration of churning the ocean, then the story of Indra, the ruler of the Devas; the narrative of Parvati and her subsequent marriage.

## \|\| 1.104.9 \|\|

*kumārotpattikathanaṃ tatastārakasaṃgaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pāśupatākhyānaṃ caṇḍākhyānasamanvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The birth of Kurrulra (Skanda) is narrated thereafter, then the battle wilh Taraka, then the narration of Pasupati, alongwith that of Ganda.

## \|\| 1.104.10 \|\|

*dyūtapravartanākhyānaṃ nāradena samāgamaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kumāramāhātmye pañcatīrthakathānakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The narration of being engaged in the game of dice the meeting with Narada. Then in the context of the greatness of Kumara, the story of five TTrthas (holy centres).

## \|\| 1.104.11 \|\|

*dharmavarmanṛpākhyānaṃ nadīsāgarakīrtanam \|*  
*indradyumnakathā paścānnāḍījaṅghakathānvitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The anecdote of king Dharmavarman; the enumeration of rivers and oceans; thereafter, the story of Indra- dyumna alongwith the story of Nadi-jangha.

## \|\| 1.104.12 \|\|

*prādurbhāvastato mahyāḥ kathā damanakasya ca \|*  
*mahīsāgarasaṃyogaḥ kumāreśakathā tataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The appearance of the Earth, the story ofDamanaka, the contact between the Earth and the ocean, then the story of Lord Kumara.

## \|\| 1.104.13 \|\|

*tatastārakayuddhaṃ ca nānākhyānasamanvitam \|*  
*vadhaśca tārakasyātha pañcaliṅganiveśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then the fight with Taraka alongwith various anecdotes, the killing of Taraka, the installation of five Lirigas.

## \|\| 1.104.14 \|\|

*dvīpākhyānaṃ tataḥ puṇyamūrddhalokavyavasthitiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇḍasthitimānaṃ ca varkareśakathānakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The holy narration of the continents, the orderly arrangement of the upper worlds, the situation and magnitude of the Cosmic Egg, the story of Varkaresa.

## \|\| 1.104.15 \|\|

*mahākālasamudbhūtiḥ kathā cāsya mahādbhutā \|*  
*vāsudevasya māhātmyaṃ koṭitīrthaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The origin of Mahakalaand his extremely miraculous story, the greatness of Vasudeva, thereafter the Koti Tirtha.

## \|\| 1.104.16 \|\|

*nānātīrthasamākhyānaṃ guptakṣetre prakīrtitam \|*  
*pāṇḍavānāṃ kathā puṇyā mahāvidyāprasādhanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The narration of different holy centres, Gupta Ksetra (near the confluence of the Main with the sea) the holy story of the Pamjavas and the achievement of great Vidya.

## \|\| 1.104.17 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāsamāptiśca kaumāramidamadbhutam \|*  
*aruṇācalamāhātmyaṃ sanakabrahmasaṃkathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The wonderful conclusion of pilgrimage to holy centres by Kumara; the greatness of Arunacala, the conversation between Sanaka and Brahma.

## \|\| 1.104.18 \|\|

*gaurītapaḥ samākhyānaṃ tattattīrthanirūpaṇam \|*  
*māhiṣāsuramākhyānaṃ vadhaścāsya mahādbhutaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The description of Gauri’s penance, the review of different holy centres, the narrative of demon Mahisa and his wonderful death. Actually we find that the NP touches a fringe of this part of the SkP and a great number of topics are not even mentioned. The same is the case with other Kharjtdas. One wonders whether a shorter version of the Sk. P, was used by the NP or a casual mention of a few chapters was looked upon as a table of contents in those days. Many of the topics not mentioned by the NP are found in other Pura(ias also and as such one should think thrice before branding them spurious.

## \|\| 1.104.19 \|\|

*droṇācale śivāsthānaṃ nityadāparikīrtitam \|*  
*ityeṣa kathitaḥ skānde khaṇḍo māheśvaro 'dbhutaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The permanent residence of Siva in Dronacala has ever been glorified. Thus the part of MaheSvara Khanda has been recounted.

## \|\| 1.104.20 \|\|

*dvitīyo vaiṣṇavaḥ khaṇḍastasyākhyānāni me śuṇu \|*  
*prathamaṃ bhūmivārāhasamākhyānaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The second part is called the Vaishnava Khanda. Listen to the stories contained in it. At the outset, the narrative of the Earth and Varaha.

## \|\| 1.104.21 \|\|

*yatra veṅkaṭakudhrasya māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kamalāyāḥ kathā puṇyā śrīnivāsasthitistataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The greatness of the mountain Venkata, destructive of sins is mentioned therein; the holy story of Kamala, the residence of Srinivasa therein.

## \|\| 1.104.22 \|\|

*kulā lākhyānakaṃ cātra suvarṇamukharī kathā \|*  
*nānākhyānasamāyuktā bhāradvājakathādbhutā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The story of Kulala (potter), the story of Suvarna- mukhari,1 the wonderful tale of Bharadvaja alongwith different narratives.

## \|\| 1.104.23 \|\|

*mataṅgāñjanasaṃvādaḥ kīrtitaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ \|*  
*puruṣottamamāhātmyaṃ kīrtitaṃ cotkale tataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The dialogue between Matanga and Anjana that is destructive of sins, the greatness of Purusottama2 (Jagannatha) in Orissa thereafter.

## \|\| 1.104.24 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyasamākhyānamaṃbarīṣasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*indradyumnasya cākhyānaṃ vidyāpatikathā śubhā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The story of Markendeya, the tale of king Ambarlsa and the auspicious stories of Indradyumna and Vidyapati.

## \|\| 1.104.25 \|\|

*jaimineḥ samupākhyānaṃ nāradasyāpi vāḍava \|*  
*nīlakaṇṭhasamākhyānaṃ narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Brahmana, thereafter, there are the stories of Jaimini, Narada and Nllakantha, then the description of Narasimha.

## \|\| 1.104.26 \|\|

*aśvamedhakathā rājño brahmalokagatistathā \|*  
*rathayāvrāvidhiḥ paścājjanmasthānavidhistathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The story of horse-sacrifice of the king and his attainment of Brahmaloka, the procedure regarding the Ratha Yatra (chariot procession), the rules regarding the abode of birth. The NP. refers to the following chapters from Sk. P. II in VV 9 1-11 chs: 3-8; 9-15, 16-32, 33, 36-40, 53, 66 (from the GM edition) The GM text of the Sk. P. devotes the whole of III — Uttarardha to Arunacala.

## \|\| 1.104.27 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāmūrtyupākhyānaṃ guṇḍivākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*ratharakṣāvidhānaṃ ca śayanotsavakīrtanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The anecdote of Daksinamurti, the tale of Guntfiva, the arrangement for the maintenance of the chariot, the glorification of the Sayana-Utsava (the festival of Deity’s going to sleep).

## \|\| 1.104.28 \|\|

*śvetopākhyānamatroktaṃ pṛthutsavanirūpaṇam \|*  
*dolotsavo bhagavato vrataṃ sāṃvatsarābhidham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The story of Sveta is mentioned here; then the review ofPrthutsava (the great Festival), the Dolotsava (Festival of the Swing) of the lord and the observance called annual Vrata, the Akamika Puja (worship without entertaining any desire in return) of Visnu. Different kinds of Yoga and means thereto according to the teaching of Uddalaka.

## \|\| 1.104.29 \|\|

*pūjā cākāmikā viṣṇoruddālakaniyogataḥ \|*  
*yogasādhanamatroktaṃ nānāyoganirūpaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The ten incarnations are enumerated; the rite of ablution etc. is glorified; then the greatness of Badarika1 that is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.104.30-32 \|\|

*daśāvatārakathanaṃ srānādiparikīrtanam \|*  
*tato badarikāyāśca māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*agnyāditīrthamāhātmyaṃ vainateyaśilābhavam \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ bhagavadvāse tīrthaṃ kāpālamocanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*pañcadhārābhidhaṃ tīrthaṃ merusaṃsthāpanaṃ tathā \|*  
*tataḥ kārtikamāhātmye māhātmyaṃ madanālasam \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. The greatness of Agni and other holy centres situated in the rock of Vainateya; the cause for the residence of the Lord; the holy centre named Panchadhara, the situation of Meru. In the context of Karttika, the glory of Madalasa.

## \|\| 1.104.33 \|\|

*dhūmrakeśasamākhyānaṃ dinakṛtyāni kartike \|*  
*pañcabhīṣmavratākhyānaṃ kīrtitaṃ bhuktimuktidam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The narrative of Dhiimrake^a, the daily rites and duties in the month of Karttika,2 the description of “Pancha- Bhlsma” Vrata that bestows worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 1.104.34 \|\|

*tato mārgasya māhātmye vidhānaṃ snānajaṃ tathā \|*  
*puṇḍrādikīrtanaṃ cātra mālādhāraṇapuṇyakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then in the context of the greatness of Marga- slrsa,3 the rules of procedure regarding the bath, the glorification of Pundra (the mark on the forehead) etc., the meritorious nature of wearing garlands, etc.

## \|\| 1.104.35 \|\|

*pañcāmṛtasnānapuṇyaṃ ghaṇṭānādādijaṃ phalam \|*  
*nānāpuṣpārcanaphalaṃ tulasīdalajaṃ phalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The merit in the ablution with Pancamrta, the benefit originating from ringing the bell etc.; the benefit of worshipping with different kinds of flowers, the benefit accruing from the Tulasi leaves.

## \|\| 1.104.36 \|\|

*naivedyasya ca māhātmyaṃ harivāsarakīrtanam \|*  
*akhaṇḍaikādaśīpuṇyaṃ tathā jāgaraṇasya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The greatness of Naivedya (food offering) to God, the glorification of Harivasara (Hari’s day i.e. Ekadasi) The AkhandaikadasI (the unbroken Ekadasi) as well as the merit of keeping awake during Ekadasi.

## \|\| 1.104.37 \|\|

*yasyotsavavidhānaṃ ca nāmamāhātmyakīrtanam \|*  
*dhyānādipuṇyakathanaṃ māhātmyaṃ mathurābhavam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The rules regarding the festival thereof, the narrative of illustrious names of God, recounting of the merit of meditation, the greatness of Mathura, etc.

## \|\| 1.104.38 \|\|

*mathurātīrthamāhātmyaṃ pṛthaguktaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*vanānāṃ dvādaśānāṃ ca māhātmyaṃ kīrtitaṃ tataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereafter, the greatness of the holy centre Mathura is separately mentioned, then the greatness of twelve forests is mentioned.

## \|\| 1.104.39 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavatasyātra māhātmyaṃ kīrtitaṃ param \|*  
*vajraśāṇḍilyasaṃvāda antarlīlāprakāśakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In this context, the greatness of Srimad Bhagavata1 is mentioned in the course of dialogue between Vajra and Sarujilya, the inner sports are revealed.

## \|\| 1.104.40 \|\|

*tato māghasya māhātmyaṃ snānadānajapodbhavam \|*  
*nānākhyānasamāyuktaṃ daśādhyāyairnirūpitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then the greatness of the months ofMagha is reviewed in ten chapters in regard to bath, charitable gifts and Japas alongwith suitable anecdotes connected therewith.

## \|\| 1.104.41 \|\|

*tato vaiṣṇavamāhātmye śayyādānādijaṃ phalam \|*  
*jaladā nādividhayaḥ kāmākhyānamataḥ param \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then in the context of the greatness of the devotees of Visnu the benefit of Sayyadana (charitable gift of beds) is mentioned; the rules regarding the gift of water are mentioned; then the story of Kama.

## \|\| 1.104.42 \|\|

*śrutadevasya caritaṃ vyādhopākhyānamadbhutam \|*  
*tathākṣayatṛtīyāderviśeṣātpuṇyakīrtanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The story of Srutadeva, the wonderful anecdote of the Vyadha (hunter), the special glorification of Ak?aya Trtiya8 (the everlasting Trtiya i.e. the third day of the bright half of VaiSakha)

## \|\| 1.104.43 \|\|

*tatastvayodhyāmāhātmye cakrabrahmāhvatīrthake \|*  
*surāpāpavimokṣākhye tathādhārasahasrakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the context of the greatness of Ayodhya1 the two holy Tlrthas viz. Cakratlrtha and Brahmatxrtha are mentioned. These two bring about the liberation from the sin of drinking spirituous liquor; the heavenly door with a thousand shUpports.

## \|\| 1.104.44 \|\|

*svargadvāraṃ candraharidharmaharyupavarṇanam \|*  
*svarṇavṛṣṭerupākhyānaṃ tilodāsarayūyutiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The description of Candrahari and Dharmahari, the anecdote of Svarnavrsti (shower of gold); the confluence of Tiloda and Sarayu.

## \|\| 1.104.45 \|\|

*sītākuṇḍaṃ guptaharisaraṃyughargharānvayaḥ \|*  
*gopratāraṃ ca dugdhodaṃ gurukuṇḍādipañcakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The holy pool of Slta, the lineage of Guptahari, the confluence of Sarayu and Gharghara; the holy centres of Gopratara, Dugdhoda and the set of five (Tlrthas) beginning with Gurukunda.

## \|\| 1.104.46 \|\|

*somārkā dīni tīrthāni trayodaśa tataḥ param \|*  
*gayākūpasya māhātmyaṃ sarvāghavinivartakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereafter, the description of thirteen Tirthas such as Soma, Arka etc., the greatness of Gaya-kiipa (the well of Gaya) that causes all sins to recede.

## \|\| 1.104.47 \|\|

*māṇḍavyāśramapūrvāṇi tīrthāni tadanantaram \|*  
*ajitādi mānasāditīrthāni gaditāni ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thereafter, the holy spots beginning with the hermi- age of Mandavya, that of Ajita etc., and Manasa etc. are mentioned.

## \|\| 1.104.48 \|\|

*ityeṣa vaiṣṇavaḥ khaṇḍo dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ brahmakhaṇḍaṃ marīce śṛṇu puṇyadam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus the second Khanda called Vaishnava is explained. Hereafter, О Marici, listen to the Brahmakhanda that bestows merit. (The summary of Brahma Khanda)

## \|\| 1.104.49 \|\|

*yatra vai setumāhātmye phalaṃ snāne kṣaṇodbhavam \|*  
*gālavasya tapaścaryā rākṣasākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In the context of the greatness of Setu (Bridge built by Rama over the sea), the benefit resulting from bath and mere sight; the penance of Galava, the story of Raksasas.

## \|\| 1.104.50 \|\|

*cakratīrthādimāhātmyaṃ devīpattanasaṃyute \|*  
*vetālatīrthamahimā pāpanāśādikīrtanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The greatness of Cakratlrtha etc, the greatness of Vetalatlrtha which is in Devlpattana2 (city of the Goddess), the glorification of the holy place called Papanaga (the destruction of sins).

## \|\| 1.104.51 \|\|

*maṅgalādikamāhātmyaṃ brahmakuṇḍādivarṇanam \|*  
*hanumatkuṇḍamahimāgastyatīrthabhavaṃ phalam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The greatness of Mangala etc., the description of Brahmakunda etc, the greatness of Hanumatkunda, the benefit resulting from Agastyatirtha.

## \|\| 1.104.52 \|\|

*rāmatīrthādikathanaṃ lakṣmītīrthanirūpaṇam \|*  
*śaṅkhāditīrthamahimā tathā sādhyāmṛtādijaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The narrative of Ramatlrtha etc, the review of Laksmitlrtha, the greatness of Sankha and other Tirthas. So also the benefit accruing from Sadhyamrta etc.

## \|\| 1.104.53-54 \|\|

*dhanuṣkoṭyādimāhātmyaṃ kṣīrakuṇḍādijaṃ tathā \|*  
*gāyatryādikatīrthānāṃ māhātmyaṃ cātra kīrtitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rāmanāthasya mahimā tattvajñānopadeśanam \|*  
*yātrāvidhānakathanaṃ setai muktipradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. The greatness of Dhanuskoti etc. and that of Kslra- Kunda etc., the greatness of Gayatri and o'.her Tirthas is described here; the greatness of Ramanatha; the instruction in the perfect knowledge of Reality, the recounting of rules regarding the pilgrimage to Setu which yields salvation to men.

## \|\| 1.104.55 \|\|

*dharmāraṇyasya māhātmyaṃ tataḥ paramudīritam \|*  
*sthāṇuḥ skandāya bhagavānyatra tattvamupādiśat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereafter, the greatness of Dharmaranya1 (forest of Dharma) is mentioned. It was here that Lord Sthanu instructed Skanda in Tattva (Philosophic principles).

## \|\| 1.104.56 \|\|

*dharmāraṇyasusaṃbhūtistatpuṇyaparikīrttanam \|*  
*karṃmasiddheḥ samākhyānaṃ ṛṣivaṃśanirūpaṇam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The origin of Dharmaranya; the glorification of its merit, the narration of Karmasiddhi (achievements of the fruit of actions, the review of the family-lines of the sages.

## \|\| 1.104.57 \|\|

*apsarastīrthamukhyānāṃ māhātmyaṃ yatra kīrtitam \|*  
*varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca dharmatattvanirūpaṇam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The greatness of main Apsarastirthas (Holy centres of the divine damsels) is mentioned; the review of the principles of Dharma (duties) of the castes and stages of life.

## \|\| 1.104.58-59 \|\|

*divaḥ sthānavibhāgaśca bakulārkakathā śubhā \|*  
*chatrānandā tathā śāntā śrīmātā ca mataṅginī \|\| 58 \|\|*

*puṇyadā ca samākhyātā yatra devyaḥ samāsthitāḥ \|*  
*indreśvarādimāhātmyaṃ dvārakādinirūpaṇam \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. The division of heavenly spots, the auspicious story of Bakularka, the goddesses Chatrananda, Santa, Srimata, MatanginI and Punyadaare stationed herein, the greatness of Indresvara etc., the review of Dvaraka etc.

## \|\| 1.104.60 \|\|

*lohāsurasamākhyānaṃ gaṅgākūpanirūpaṇam \|*  
*śrīrāmacaritaṃ caiva satyamandiravarṇanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The narrative of the demon Lohasura, the review of Gangakupa, the story of Sri Rama, the description of Satya Mandira.

## \|\| 1.104.61 \|\|

*jīrṇoddhā rasya kathanamāsanapratipādanam \|*  
*jātibhedaprakathanaṃ smṛtidharmanirūpaṇam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The narrative of the repair to the ruins; the acceptance of seats, the mentioning of different castes, the review of the holy rites in accordance with the Smrtis.

## \|\| 1.104.62 \|\|

*tatastu vaiṣṇavā dharmā nānākhyānairudīritāḥ \|*  
*cāturmāsye tataḥ puṇye sarvadhamanirūpaṇam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then the holy rites prescribed for Vaishnavas are mentioned through different narratives, thereafter, the exposition of holy rites, observances etc., in regard to the holy Caturmasya (the four months of the rainy season when special Vratas are observed).

## \|\| 1.104.63 \|\|

*dānapraśaṃsā tatpaścādvratasya mahimā tataḥ \|*  
*tapaścaiva pūjāyāḥ sacchidrakathanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The eulogy of charitable gifts, thereafter the greatness of Vratas, the narration of loop-holes (causes of failures) in penance and worship.

## \|\| 1.104.64 \|\|

*tadvṛttīnāṃ bhidākhyānaṃ śālagrāmanirūpaṇam \|*  
*bhārakasya vadhopāyo vṛkṣācāmahimā tathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The narration of making amends for them (loopholes); the review of Salagrama; the means for the destruction of Bharaka, the glory of the worship of trees.

## \|\| 1.104.65 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ śāpaśca vṛkṣatvaṃ pārvatyanutapastataḥ \|*  
*harasya tāṇḍavaṃ nṛtyaṃ rāmanāmanirūpaṇam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The cause of Visnu in regard to the state of being a tree, then Parvatl’s subsequent penance, the Tandava dance of Нага, the review of the name Rama.

## \|\| 1.104.66 \|\|

*harasya liṅgapatanaṃ kathā baijavanasya ca \|*  
*pārvatījanmacaritaṃ tārakasya vadho 'dbhutaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The fall of the Lihga of Нага, the story of Baijavana, the story of the nativity of Parvatl, the wonderful killing of Taraka.

## \|\| 1.104.67 \|\|

*praṇavaiśvaryakathanaṃ tārakācaritaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dakṣayajñasamāptiśca dvādaśākṣarabhūṣaṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The narration of prosperity through the Pranava, the activities of Taraka, the conclusion of Daksa’s Yajna, the mantra of Twelve syllables (viz. orii namo bhagavate Vasu- devaya) which is its embellishment.

## \|\| 1.104.68 \|\|

*jñānayogasamākhyānaṃ mahimā dvādaśākṣareḥ \|*  
*śravaṇādikapuṇyaṃ ca kīrtitaṃ śarmadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The narration of the path of knowledge and the greatness of twelve-syllabled Mantra. The merit of Sravana (the means of hearing), etc. that causes happiness to men.

## \|\| 1.104.69 \|\|

*tato brāhmottare bhāge śivasya mahimādbhutaḥ \|*  
*pañcākṣarasya mahimā gokarṇamahimā tataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Then in the latter half of the Brahmakhanda the wonderful greatness of Siva is narrated, then the greatness of the five-syllabled Mantra: Namah Sivaya and that of Gokarna.

## \|\| 1.104.70 \|\|

*śivarātraiśca mahimā pradoṣavra takīrtanam \|*  
*somavāravrataṃ cāpi sīmantinyāḥ kathānakam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The greatness of Sivaratri, the glorification of Pradosa Vrata,1 the Vrata on Mondays, the anecdote of Simantini.

## \|\| 1.104.71 \|\|

*bhadrāyutpattikathanaṃ sadācāranirūpaṇam \|*  
*śivavarmasamuddeśo bhadrāyūdvāhavarṇanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The narration of the origin of Bhadrayu, the review of good conduct, the guidance of Sivavarman (?) and the description of Bhadrayu’s marriage.

## \|\| 1.104.72 \|\|

*bhadrāyumahimā cāpi bhasmamāhātmyakīrtanam \|*  
*śabarākhyānakaṃ caiva umāmāheśvaraṃ vratam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The greatness of Bhadrayu, the glorification of the greatness of Bhasma (Sacred ashes), the story of Sahara (Hunter), the Vratacalled Uma-Maheshvara.

## \|\| 1.104.73 \|\|

*rudrākṣasya ca māhātmyaṃ rudrādhyāyasya puṇyakam \|*  
*śravaṇādikapuṇyaṃ ca brahmakhaṇḍo 'yamīritaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The greatness of the Rudraksa bead, the merit of the ‘Rudrildhyaya Mantra, the merit of Sravana (hearing), etc. Thus the Brahmakhanda has been recounted.

## \|\| 1.104.74 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ caturthaṃ tu kāśīkhaṇḍamanuttamam \|*  
*vindhyanāradayoryatra saṃvādaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Henceforth, the fourth part, the excellent Kasi Khanda1 (is summarised). The dialogue between Vindhya and Naradais described.

## \|\| 1.104.75 \|\|

*satyalokaprabhāvaścāgastyāvāse surāgamaḥ \|*  
*pativratācaritraṃ ca tīrthayātrā praśaṃsanam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The greatness of Satyaloka, the arrival of the Devas in the residence of Agastya, the story of a chaste lady, the praising of the pilgrimage to holy centres.

## \|\| 1.104.76 \|\|

*tataśca saptapuryākhyā saṃyaminyā nirūpaṇam \|*  
*budhasya ca tathendrāgnyorlokāptiḥ śivaśarmaṇaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Then the narration of the seven cities, the review of Samyarnini, the attainment of the worlds of Budha (Mercury), Indra and Agni by Sivasarman.

## \|\| 1.104.77 \|\|

*agneḥ samudbhavaścaiva kravyādvaruṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*gandhavatyalakāpuryorīśvaryāśca samudbhavaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The origin of fire, the origin of Varuna from fire (?) the origin of the two cities Gandhavati and Alaka and the nativity of Hvari.

## \|\| 1.104.78 \|\|

*candrārkabudhalokānāṃ kujejyārkabhuvāṃ kramāt \|*  
*mama viṣṇordhruvasyāpi tapolokasya varṇanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The description of these worlds, viz., the moon, the sun, the mercury, the Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, my world, Visnu’s world of Dhruva’s world (?) and the Tapoloka.

## \|\| 1.104.79 \|\|

*dhruvalokakathā puṇyā satyalokanirīkṣaṇam \|*  
*skandāgastyasamālāpo maṇikarṇīsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The meritorious story of the world of Dhruva, the survey of Satyaloka, the conversation between Skanda and Agastya, the origin of Manikarnl.

## \|\| 1.104.80 \|\|

*prabhāvaścāpi gaṅgāyā gaṅgānāmasahasrakam \|*  
*vārāṇasīpraśaṃsā ca bhairavāvirbhavastataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The prowess of the Ganga, the thousand names of the Gahga, the praise of Varanasi, the appearance of Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.104.81 \|\|

*daṇḍapāṇijñānavāpyorudbhavaḥ samanantaram \|*  
*tataḥ kalāvatyākhyānaṃ sadācāranirūpaṇam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thereafter, the origin of Dandapani and Jftanavapi (the well of Knowledge), then the narration of Kalavati and the exposition of good conduct.

## \|\| 1.104.82 \|\|

*brahmacārisamākhyānaṃ tataḥ strīlakṣaṇāni ca \|*  
*kṛtyākṛtyavinirdeśo hyavimukteśavarṇanam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The narration of a celibate, then the characteristics of women, the stipulation of what should be done and what should not be done, the description of Avimukteia.

## \|\| 1.104.83 \|\|

*gṛhasthayogino dharmāḥ kālajñānaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*divodāsakathā puṇyā kāśikāvarṇanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The duties of householders and the Yogins, then the knowledge of Kala (Time), the holy story of Divodasa, the description of KaSika.

## \|\| 1.104.84 \|\|

*māyāgaṇapateścātha bhuvi prādurbhavastataḥ \|*  
*viṣṇumāyāprapañco 'tha divodāsavimokṣaṇam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The appearance on the Earth of Maya Ganapati, the Universe due to Visnu’s Maya, then the liberation of Divodasa.

## \|\| 1.104.85 \|\|

*tataḥ pañcanadotparttirbindumādhavasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tato vaiṣṇavatīrthākhyā śūlinaḥ kāśikāgamaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then the origin of Pancanada and that of Bindu Madhava; then the enumeration of holy centres belonging to Visnu, the arrival at Kasi of the trident-bearing Lord.

## \|\| 1.104.86 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyena saṃvādo jyeṣṭheśākhyā maheśituḥ \|*  
*kṣetrākhyānaṃ kandukeśaḥ vyāghreśvarasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The dialogue between Jaigisavya and MaheSa, the name Jyesthesa of Mahesa, the enumeration of holy temples, the origin of Kandukesa and VyaghreSvara.

## \|\| 1.104.87 \|\|

*śaileśaratneśvarayoḥ kṛttivāsasya codbhavaḥ \|*  
*devatānāmadhiṣṭānaṃ durgāsuraparākramaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The origin of Sailesa and Ratnesvara as well as that of Krttivasas; the abode of the deities; Durga’s exploit over the Asuras.

## \|\| 1.104.88 \|\|

*durgāyā vijayaścātha oṅkāreśasya varṇanam \|*  
*punarāeṅkāra māhātmya triloconasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Durga’s victory, the description of Omkaresa, then the greatness of Orhkara, the origin of the three-eyed Lord Siva.

## \|\| 1.104.89 \|\|

*kedārākhyā ca dharmeśa kathā viṣṇubhujodbhavā \|*  
*vīreśvarasamākhyānaṃ gaṅgāmāhātmyakīrtanam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The narration of Kedara, the story of Dharmesa born of Visnu’s arms (?), the narrative of Vlresvara, the glorification of the greatness of Gariga.

## \|\| 1.104.90 \|\|

*viśvakarmeśamahimā dakṣayajñodbhavastathā \|*  
*satīśasyāmṛteśāderbhujastaṃbhaḥ parāśare \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The greatness of ViSvakarmeSa, the origin of Daksa’s Yajna as well as that of Satlsa, Amrtesa and others, the benumbing of the arms of Parashara.

## \|\| 1.104.91 \|\|

*kṣetratīrthakadaṃbaśca muktimaḍapasaṃkathā \|*  
*viśveśavibhavaścātha tato yātrāparikramaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The group of holy centres and shrines, the dialogue in the Mukti-Mancjapa (The pandal of salvation) the prosperity of Yiiveaa. and then the circumambulatory pilgrimage. (Thus the fourth part is summarised)

## \|\| 1.104.92 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ tvavantyākhyaṃ śṛṇu khaṇḍa ca pañcamam \|*  
*mahākālavanākhyānaṃ brahmaśīrṣacchidā tataḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Hereafter, listen to the description of the fifth part called Avanti Khanka.1 The narration of the forest Mahakala Vana; then the chopping off of the head of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.104.93 \|\|

*prāyaścittavidhiścāgnerutpattiśca surāgamaḥ \|*  
*devadīkṣā śivastotraṃ nānāpātakanāśanam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. THe rules regarding expiatory rites.; the origin of Agni; the arrival of the Devas, the initiation of theDevas; Siva’s hymn that is destructive of different kinds of sins.

## \|\| 1.104.94 \|\|

*kapolamocanākhyānaṃ mahākālavanasthitiḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ kanakhaleśasya sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The narration of Kapalamocana, the situation of the forest Mahakalavana, the holy centre of the Lord Kanakhala that is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.104.95 \|\|

*kuṇḍamapsarasaṃjñaṃ ca saro rudrasya puṇyadam \|*  
*kuḍaveśaṃ ca vidyādhraṃ markaṭeśvaratīrthakam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The pool called after the Apsaras (celestial damsels) and the lake of Rudra that is meritorious, the holy centres of the Lord of Kudava, Vidyadhara, and Markateshvara.

## \|\| 1.104.96 \|\|

*svargadvāracatuḥsiṃdhutīrthaṃ śaṅkaravāpikā \|*  
*śaṅkarāka gandhavatītīrthaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The holy waters of Svargadvaracatussindhu (the four rivers that constitute the doorways to heaven), Sank- aravapika (The tank of Sankara), Sahkararka, Gandhavati Tirtha, that is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.104.97 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikānaṃśatīrthe ca harisiddhidam \|*  
*piśācakādiyātrā ca hanumatkavaceśvarau \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Dasashvamedhika and Anamsha Tirtha that bestow all Siddhis, the procession of Pisacaka, etc, Hanumadlsvara, Kava- cesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.98 \|\|

*mahākāleśayātrā ca valmīkeśvaratīrthakam \|*  
*śukre ca pañcame cākhye kuśasthalyāḥ pradakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The procession of or pilgrimage to MahakaleSa, the holy centre of Valmikesvara, the circumabulationsof KuSas- thall in the fifth Tirtha called Sukra (?).

## \|\| 1.104.99 \|\|

*akrūrasaṃjñakantvekapādaṃ candrārkavaibhavam \|*  
*karabheśākhyatīrthaṃ ca laṭukeśāditīrthakam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The centres of Akriira, Ekapada and Candrarkavai- bhava; the holy shrine called Karabhesa and those of Lakufesa and others.

## \|\| 1.104.100-101 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeśaṃ yajñavāpī someśaṃ narakāntakam \|*  
*kedāreśvararāmeśasaubhāgyeśanarārkakam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*keśavārkaṃ śaktibhedaṃ svarṇasāramukhāni ca \|*  
*oṅkāreśāditīrthāni andhakaśrutikīrtanam \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. Магкавд1еshа, Yajna-vapi-somesa, Narakantaka, Kedarelvara, Ramesha, Saubhagyefe, Nararkara shrines. Then Ke^avarka, Saktibheda, Svarnasara, and other shrines, the holy spots of Omkaresa etc, the glorification of AndhakMruti.

## \|\| 1.104.102 \|\|

*kālāraṇye liṅgasaṃkhyā svarṇaśṛṅgābhidhānakam \|*  
*kuśasthalyā avantyāścojjayinyā abhidhānakam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The number of Lingas in the Kalaranya, the shrine named SvargaSrnga (gold horn), the names of Kusasthali, Avanti and Ujjayini.

## \|\| 1.104.103 \|\|

*padmāvatīvai kumudvatyamarāvatināmakam \|*  
*viśālāpratikalpābhidhānaṃ ca jvaraśāntikam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The shrines named Padmavati, Kumudvati, and Amaravati the names of Vi^ala, and Pratikalpa and Amaravati, the subduing of fever.

## \|\| 1.104.104 \|\|

*śivānāmādikaphalaṃ nāgodgītā śivastutiḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣavadhākhyānaṃ tīrthaṃ suṃdarakuṇḍakam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The benefit of the names of Siva etc., the eulogy of Siva sung by the Nagas (Serpents), the narrative of killing Hiranyaksha, the holy centre of Sundarakunda.

## \|\| 1.104.105 \|\|

*nīlagaṅgāpuṣkarākhyaṃ vindhyavāsanatīrthakam \|*  
*puruṣottamābhidhānaṃ tu tattīrthaṃ cāghanāśanam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The holy centres of Vindhyavasin (residing in Vindhya) called Nilagangapu?kara, the holy centre destructive of sins, called Puru^ottama.

## \|\| 1.104.106 \|\|

*gomatī vāmanaṃ kuṇḍo viṣṇornāmasahasrakam \|*  
*vīreśvarasaraḥ kālabhairavasya ca tīrthakam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The Gomat! river, the holy pool of Vamana, the thousand names of Visnu, the lake of VireSvara, the shrine of Kalabhairava.

## \|\| 1.104.107 \|\|

*mahimā nāgapañcamyā nṛsiṃhasya jayantikā \|*  
*kuṭumbeśvarayātrā ca devasādhakakīrtanam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The greatness of Nagapaftcami, the Jayantika (birth anniversary) of Nrsimha, the procession of KutumbeSvara, the glorification of divine Sadhakas.

## \|\| 1.104.108 \|\|

*rundrakuṇḍaprabhṛtiṣu bahutīrthanirūpaṇam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The holy shrine called Karkaraja, the bearing of Vighnesa and other Devas, the review of many holy centres in the Rudrakunda (the holy pit of Rudra) and others.

## \|\| 1.104.109 \|\|

*yātrāṣṭatīrthajā puṇyā revāmāhātmyamucyate \|*  
*dharmaputrasya vairāgyo mārkaṇḍeyena saṃgamaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The holy pilgrimage of the eight holy centres, the greatness of Reva, the detachment of Dharmaputra, his meeting with Markandeya.

## \|\| 1.104.110 \|\|

*prāgrīyānubhavākhyānamamṛtāparikīrttanam \|*  
*kalpe kalpe pṛthaṅ nāma narmadāyāḥ prakīrtitam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Narration of the most excellent experience, the glorification of Amfta; Different names of Narmada in the different Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.104.111 \|\|

*stavamārṣaṃ nāmedaṃ ca kālarātrikathā tataḥ \|*  
*mahādevastutiḥ paścātpṛthakkalpakathādbhutā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The hymn of Narmada composed by the sages, the story of Kalaratri; thereafter the prayer of Mahadeva, the wonderful stories of several Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.104.112 \|\|

*viśalyākhyānakaṃ paścājjāleśvarakathā tathā \|*  
*gorīvrata samākhyānaṃ tripurajvālanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The story of Vifatlya, the story of JaleSvara, the description of Gaurl Vrata, the burning of Tripuras.

## \|\| 1.104.113 \|\|

*dehapātavidhānaṃ ca kāverīsaṃgamastataḥ \|*  
*dārutīrthaṃ brahmāvartaṃ yatreśvarakathānakam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The injunctions regarding the casting off of the body, then the confluence of Kaverl, the holy shrines of Daru tirtha and Brahmavarta, alongwith the story of Iivara.

## \|\| 1.104.114-115 \|\|

The following series of shrines are then described: Agni Tirtha, Ravi Tirtha, Meghanada Tirtha, Adidaruka Tirtha, Deva Tirtha, Narmadeia, Kapila Tirtha, Karafija Tirtha, Kundalesa, Pippalada, Vimalesha and Sulabhrt, then the story of abduction of Saci and killing of Abhraka. (v. 1. Andhaka)

Then the holy narrative of Vyadha (the hunter); then the holy centre of Pu?karinyarka; then the following holy pools and shrines — ApretyeSvara Tirtha, Sakra Tirtha, Karojika, KumareSa, Agastyeia, Anande5a, Matfja, Loke5a, Dhanadega, MangaleSa, Kamaja, Nageia, Gopara. Gautama, Saiikhacudaka, NaradeSa, Nandikega, Varushe5vara Tirtha, Dadhiskanda and other holy centres; then Hanuma- tegvara, Ramegvara and other holy centres, Some5a, Pinga- legvara.

*indreśaṃ kaṃbukeśaṃ ca someśaṃ kohanaṃ śakam \|*

Nandika) Narayana, Ko(i5a, Vyasa Tirtha, Prabhasaka, Nagega, Sankar-?anaka, Pra5raye5vara Tirtha, the holy confluence of Airandi, Suvarnagila Tirtha, Karafija, Kamaha, Bhandira, Rohini- bhava, Cakra Tirtha, Dhautapapa, Skanda, the holy place named after Angiras, Kofi Tirtha, Tirtha called AyonI, Angara Tirtha, Trilocana Tirtha, Indre5a, Kambukega, Somega, Kohanesa, Narmada, Arka, Agneya, the excellent Bhargavegvara Brahma, Daiva, Margesa, Adivarahakesvara, Ramesa, Siddheia Ahalya, Kahkategvara, Sakra, Saumya, Nade5a, Toyega, Ruk- minibhava, Yojanega, Varahega, DvadasI Siva Tirtha, Siddhega, Mangalega, Lingatirtha, Varaha Tirtha, Kunde5a, Sveta- varaha, Garbhavega, Ravigvara.

## \|\| 1.104.130-135 \|\|

*śuklādīni ca tīrthāni huṅkārasvāmitīrthakam \|*

*kāmodaśūlāropākhye māṇḍavyaṃ gopakeśvaram \|*

*āmaleśaṃ kapāleśaṃ śṛṅgairaṇḍībhavaṃ tataḥ \|*

130-135. The holy centres of Sukla etc., Hunkarasvami Tirtha, Sangamega, Nahushe5a, Moksana, Pancagopa, Nagasava, Siddhega, Markandatirtha, Akruratirtha, Kamo- datirtha, Sularopatirtha, Mamjavya, Gopake5vara, Kapilega, Pingalega, Bhutega, Ganga Tirtha, Gautama Tirtha, Agvamedha, Bhrgukaccha Kedarela, the dispeller of sins, Kalakalega, Jalega, Salagrama, Varahaka, Candraprabhasa, Aditya, Sripati Tirtha, Hamsaka, Mulyasthana (the original abode), Sulega, the Tirtha called Ugra, Citradaivaka, Sikhiga, Koshi Tirtha, Daga- kanya, Suvarnaka, Rnamok^a, (that which liberates from indebtedness), BharaBhuti, Puiikha Mun

## \|\| 1.104.136-140 \|\|

*dṛmijaṅgalamāhātmye rohitāśvakathā tataḥ \|*

*vadhau dhundhostataḥ paścāttataścitravahodbhavaḥ \|*  
*mahimāsya tataścaḍīśaprabhāvo ratīśvaraḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

*kedāreśo lakṣatīrthaṃ tato viṣṇupadībhavam \|*

*cakrākhyaṃ lalitākhyānaṃ tīrthaṃ ca bahugomayam \|*

*śravaṇeśaṃ śuddhapaṭaṃ devāndhupretatīrthakam \|*
