136-140. In the context of the greatness ofDrmijangala, there is the story of Rohitagva, the narration of Dhundhumara the strategem of destroying Dhundhu; the killing of Dhundhu and the birth of Citravaha, his greatness, the prowess of Candida, RatHvara, KedareSa the Laksatlrtha, the holy water originating from VisnupadI (Firmament), Mukhara, Cyavana, Andhasya and the lake of Brahma, the Tirthas of Cakra, Lalita, the holy centres full of cows, Rudravarta and Markanda, the holy centres that dispel sins, aravanesa, Suddhapata, Devandhupretatirtha, the origin of holy centre Jihvoda, Sivodbheda and their eulogy in regard to their efficacy.

## \|\| 1.104.141 \|\|

*eṣa khaṇḍo hyavantyākhyaḥ śṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ nāgarākhyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ ṣaṣṭho 'bhidhīyate \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. This is the summary of the part called Avanti Khanda;1 it is destructive of sins of those who listen. Henceforth, the sixth part named Nagarakhanda is being narrated. The Ndgarakhan4ax

## \|\| 1.104.142 \|\|

*liṅgotpattisamākhyānaṃ hariścandrakathā śubhā \|*  
*viśvāmitrasya māhātmyaṃ triśaṅkusvargatistathā \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. The narration of the origin of Linga, the auspicious story of HariScandra, the greatness of Viivamitra, the attainment of heaven by TriSanku.

## \|\| 1.104.143 \|\|

*hāṭake śvaramāhātmye vṛtrāsuravadhastathā \|*

143\. In the context of the greatness of HatakeSvara, the killing of demon Vftra, the description of the holy centres Nagabila, Sarikha Tirtha and Acalesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.144 \|\|

*camatkārapurākhyānaṃ camatkārakaraṃ param \|*

144-I45a. The narration of the city of Camatkara, that is very interesting, then the description of these holy centres — Gayasirsa, Balasakhya, Balamanda, Mrgahvaya, Visnupada, Gokarna, Yugarupa and Samasraya (that is the support of the people).

## \|\| 1.104.145-146 \|\|

*viṣṇupādaṃ ca gokarṇaṃ yugarūpaṃ samāśrayaḥ \|*

*bhrūṇagartaṃ naleśaṃ ca bhaiṣmaṃ vaiḍuramarkakam \|*  
*śāramiṣṭhaṃ somanāthaṃ ca daurgamātarjakeśvaram \|\| 146 \|\|*

145b-146. Siddhesvara, the holy pool ofNagas, the holy centre of seven sages, of Agastya as well as that of Bhruna- garta, Nalesa, of Bhisma, Vaiduram, Arkaka (pertaining to the Sun-God), Sarmistha (related to Sarmistba), Somanatha, Daurga, Atarjakesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.147-150 \|\|

*jāmadagnyavadhākhyānaṃ naiḥkṣatriyakathānakam \|*

*muṇḍīrāditrikārkaṃ ca satīpariṇayāhvayam \|*  
*rudraśīrṣaṃ ca yāgeśaṃ vālakhilyaṃ ca gāruḍam \|\| 148 \|\|*

*lakṣmīśāpaḥ saptaviṃśasomaprāsādameva ca \|*  
*aṃbābaddhaṃ pāṇḍukākhyamāgneyaṃ brahmakuṇḍakam \|\| 149 \|\|*

*gomukhaṃ lohayaṣṭyākhyamajāpāleśvarī tathā \|*  
*śānaiścaraṃ rājavāpī rāmeśo lakṣmaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

147-150. The story of killing of Jamadagni; the story of (Parasurama’s vow of) making (the country) devoid of Ksatriyas, the holy centres of Ramahrada, Nagapura, Sadlinga, Yajnabhii, the three shrines of Trikarka beginning with Mundira, the marriage of Sati, the shrines of Rudraslrsha, Yagesa, Valakhilya and Garuda. The curse of Laksmi, the twentyseven palaces of Soma; the shrine called Panduka erected by Amba, Agneya (belonging to the fire God), Brahma- kunda, Gomukha, the shrine called Lohayasti, the goddess Ajapalesvarl, the shrine of Saniscara, (Saturn), the RajavapI (Royal tank) Ramesa, Laksmanesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.151-158 \|\|

*kuśeśākhyaṃ laveśākhyaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvottamottamam \|*

*tato vai revatī cātra bhaktikātīrthasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*kṣemaṅkarī ca kedāraṃ śuklatīrthamukhārakam \|\| 152 \|\|*

*satyasaṃdheśvarākhyānaṃ tathā karṇotpalākathā \|*

*tato vāstupadākhyānamajāgṛhakathānakam \|*  
*saubhāgyāndhuśca śuleśaṃ dharmarājakathānakam \|\| 154 \|\|*

*miṣṭānnedaśvarākhyānaṃ gāṇāpatyatrayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*jābālicaritaṃ caiva makareśakathā tataḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

*kāleśvaryandhakākhyānaṃ kuṇḍamāpyarasaṃ tathā \|*  
*puṣyādityaṃ rauhitāśvaṃ nāgarotpattikīrttanam \|\| 156 \|\|*

*bhārgavaṃ caritaṃ caiva vaiśvāmaitraṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*sārasvataṃ paippalādaṃ kaṃsārīśaṃ ca paiṇḍakam \|\| 157 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo yajñacaritaṃ sāvitryākhyānasaṃyutam \|*  
*raivataṃ bhārtayajñākhyaṃ mukhyatīrthanirīkṣaṇam \|\| 158 \|\|*

151-158. The excellentmost among the excellent Lingas — Kushesa and Lavesa. The story of Astasasti and that ofDamayanti, the origin of the holy centre Bhaktika Tirtha, Ksemamkari, Kedara, Sukla Tirtha, Mukharka, the narration of the shrine Satyasandhesvara, the story of Karnotpala, Atesvara, the shrines of Yajnavalkya, Gauri, andGanesa. Then the description of Vastupada, the narration of Ajagrha, Sau- bhagyandhu (the well of good fortune), the shrine Siilesa, the story of Dharmaraja, the story of Lord the bestower of sweets, three shrines of Ganapati, the story of Jabali and the story of Makareai, the description of Kalesvari and Andhaka, the holy pool of Apsaras (celestial damsels), the shrines of Pu?yaditya and Rauhitasva, the narrative of the origin of Nshgara, the stories of Bhrigu Visvamitra, Sarasvati, Pippalada, Kamsarisa and Pendaka, the story of the Yajna of Brahma alongwith the narration of Savitri, Raivata, Bharata Yajna and the survey of the important holy centres.

## \|\| 1.104.159 \|\|

*kauravaṃ hāṭakeśākhyaṃ prabhāsaṃ kṣetrakatrayam \|*

159\. The three Ksetras (holy shrines) of Кацгауа, (i. e. the descendants of Kuru) Hatakesa and Prabhasa, the three forests of Paushkara, Naimisa, and Dharma.

## \|\| 1.104.160 \|\|

*vārāṇasī dvārakākhyāvantyākhyeti purītrayam \|*

160\. The three cities viz. Varanasi, Dvaraka and Avanti, the three Vanas (Parks) viz. Vrndavana, Khandavavana and Advaika (?) \[ta?\] vana.

## \|\| 1.104.161 \|\|

*kalpaḥ śālastathā nandigrāmatrayamanuttamam \|*  
*asiśuklapitṛsaṃjñaṃ tīrthatrayamudāhṛtam \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. The three excellent villages, viz. Kalpagrama, Salagrama and Nandigrama, the three Tirthas (holy centres) viz. Asi Tirtha, Sukla Tirtha and Pitr Tlrtha.

## \|\| 1.104.162-165 \|\|

*rśyarbudau raivataścaiva parvatatrayamuttamam \|*

*sārddhakoṭitrayaphalamekaikaṃ caiṣu kīrttitam \|*

*hāṭakeśakṣetraphalapradaṃ proktaṃ catuṣṭayam \|*  
*sāṃbādityaṃ śrāddhakalpaṃ yaudhiṣṭhiramathāndhakam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*jalaśāyi caturmāsamaśūnyaśayanavratam \|*  
*maṅkaṇeśaṃ śivarātristulāpuruṣadānakam \|\| 165 \|\|*

162-163a. The three excellent Parvatas (mountains) viz. Sri Parvata, Arbuda Parvata (mount Abu) and Raivata Parvata; the three rivers Ganga, Narmada, and Sarasvati, each of these is glorified as yielding one and a half crore of benefits.

163b-164a. The four holy centres of Kupika, Sankha- tlrtha, Amaraka and Balamandana are said to yield the same benefit as Hatakesaksetra.

164b-165. The Sraddhakalpa (rituals regarding Sraddha) according to Samba (alongwith Amba and Aditya?), that of Yudhisthira and Andhaka; the holy rite of ASunya Say an a in the four months (of the rainy season), lying down on water., the shrine of Mankanesha, the festival of Sivaratri, Tulapu- rusadana rite.

## \|\| 1.104.166 \|\|

*pṛthvīdānaṃ vānakeśaṃ kapālamocaneśvaram \|*

166\. The gift of lands, the shrines of Vanakesa and KapalamocaneSvara, Papapintfa (the lump of sins), Masalainga (the worship of Linga for a month), the glorification of the extent and magnitude of Yugas.

## \|\| 1.104.167 \|\|

*niṃveśaśākaṃbharyākhyā rudraikādaśakīrtanam \|*  
*dānamāhātmyakathanaṃ dvādaśādityakīrtanam \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. The narration ofNimbeSa and Sakambharl deities, the description of RudraikadaSa (the eleven Rudras), the narration of the greatness of charitable gifts and the glorification of twelve Adityas. The Prabkdsa khanda1

## \|\| 1.104.168-169 \|\|

*ityeṣanāgaraḥ khaṇḍaḥ prabhāsākhyo 'dhunocyate \|*  
*someśo yatra viśveśor'kasthalaṃ puṇyadaṃ mahat \|\| 168 \|\|*

*siddheśvarādikākhyānaṃ pṛthagatra prakīrtitam \|*

168a. Thus Nagara khanda (has been summarised). Now the part called Prabhasa khanda is being mentioned.

168b-169. The shrines Somesa and ViSveSa, the great and meritorious holy centre called Arkasthala, the narration of Siddheivara etc., is made here separately; the shrines of Agni- Tirtha, KapardHa and Kedaresha and the bestowers of goals (heavenly abodes).

## \|\| 1.104.170 \|\|

*bhīmabhairavacaṇḍīśabhāskarendukujeśvarāḥ \|*  
*budhejyabhṛgusaurāguśiravīśā haravigrahāḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. The different forms of Нага — viz. Bhlma, Bhairava, Candida, etc., the planets viz. the Sim, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu and Sikhin (Ketu).

## \|\| 1.104.171 \|\|

*siddheśvarādyāḥ pañcānye rudrāstatra vyavastatra vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*varārohā hyajā pālā maṅgalā laliteśvarī \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Then five others SiddheSvara and the forms ofRudra, are stationed there. The goddesses of excellent beauty — Aja, Pala, Mangala and Lalitesvari.

## \|\| 1.104.172-174 \|\|

*lakṣmīśo vāḍaveśaścorvīśaḥ kāmesvarastathā \|*  
*gaurīśavaruṇeśākhyaṃ durvāseśaṃ gaṇeśvaram \|\| 172 \|\|*

*kumāreśaṃ caṇḍakalpaṃ śakulīśvarasaṃjñakam \|*  
*tataḥ prokto 'tha koṭīśabālabrahmādisatkathā \|\| 173 \|\|*

*narakeśasaṃvartteśanidhīśvarakathā tataḥ \|*  
*balabhadreśvarasyātha gaṅgāyā gaṇapasya ca \|\| 174 \|\|*

172-174. Then the shrines of Laksmisha, YadaveSa, Urvisa, Kamesvara, Gaurisa, VaruneSa, DurvaseSa, GaneSvara, KumareSa, Candakalpa and Sakulisvara. Then the holy story of Kotisa, Balabrahma, etc., then the stories ofNarakeSa, SamvarteSa and Nidhisvara, then that of BalabhadreSvara, Ganga and Ganapa.

## \|\| 1.104.175 \|\|

*jāṃbavatyākhyasaritaḥ pāṇḍukūpasya satkathā \|*  
*śatamedhalakṣamedhakoṭimedhakathā tathā \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. Then the good story of the river named Jambavati and the well called Pandukupa, the story of Satamedha (hundred sacrifices), Lakshamedha (hundred-thousand sacrifices) and Kotimedha (a crore of sacrifices.)

## \|\| 1.104.176-178 \|\|

*durvāsārkaghaṭasthānahiraṇyāsaṃgamotkathā \|*

*kumāryāḥ kṣetrapāsya brahmeśasya kathā pṛthak \|*  
*piṅgalāsaṃgameśasya śaṅkarārkaghaṭeśayoḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

*ṛṣitīrthasya nandārkatritakūpasya kīrtanam \|*  
*sasopānasya parṇārkanyaṅkumatyoḥ kathādbhutā \|\| 178 \|\|*

176-177a. The prominent story of Durvasas, Arka, Ghatasthana (place of Water pot) and Hiranyasangama (confluence of the Hiranya), the separate stories of Nagararka, Krsna, Sankarsana and Samudra (sea), Kumari (Virgin), Rshetrapala (the guardian of the fields) and Brahmeia.

177b-178. The glorification of Pingala and Sangameia, Sankara, Arkesa, Ghatesa, the holy centre Rsitlrtha, Nandarka- tritakupa, the wonderful story of Parnarka and Nyankumatl with Sopana.

## \|\| 1.104.179 \|\|

*vārāhasvāmivṛttāntaṃ chāyāliṅgākhyagulphayoḥ \|*  
*kathā kanakanandāyāḥ kutīgaṅgeśayostathā \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. The news (or the details) of Varahasvamin and that of Chayaliiiga and Gulpha, the story of Kanakananda as well as that of Kunti and Gangega.

## \|\| 1.104.180 \|\|

*camasodbedaviduratrilokeśakathā tataḥ \|*  
*maṅkaṇeśatraipureśaṣaṇḍatīrthakathāstathā \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Then the story of Camasa, Udbheda, Vidura and TrilokeSa (Lord of the three worlds), then the stories of МапкапеЗа, Traipurega and sharida-Tirtha. Khawfa which agrees with the extant published Sk. P., showing the degree of authenticity of the Khanka.

## \|\| 1.104.181 \|\|

*sūryaprācī trīkṣaṇayorumānātakathā tathā \|*  
*bhūddhāraśūlasthalayoścyavanārkeśayostathā \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Then the stories of SiiryapracI and Triksana (threeeyed) as well as that of Umanatha, the stories of Bhuddara (the uplifter of the Earth), Siilasthala (spot of Trident), that ofCyavana and Arkesa.

## \|\| 1.104.182 \|\|

*ajāpāleśabālārkakuberasthalajā kathā \|*  
*ṛṣitoyā kathā puṇyā saṃgāleśvarakīrtanam \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. The story of the'holy spots of AjapaleSa, Balarka and Kuberasthala, the meritorious story of Rsitoya, the glorification of Sarigalesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.183 \|\|

*nāradādityakathanaṃ nārāyaṇanirūpaṇam \|*  
*taptakuṇḍasya māhātmyaṃ mūlacaṇḍīśavarṇanam \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. The narration of Narada and Aditya, review of Narayana, the greatness of Taptakuntfa, description of Mulacanqllsa.

## \|\| 1.104.184 \|\|

*caturvaktragaṇādhyakṣakalaṃbeśvarayoḥ kathā \|*  
*gopālasvāmiva kulasvāminormarutāṃ kathā \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. The story of the four-faced presiding deity of the attendants and Kalambesvara, the story of Gopalasvamin and Vakulasvamin, as well as the Maruts (Winds).

## \|\| 1.104.185 \|\|

*kṣemārkennatavighneśajalasvāmikathā tataḥ \|*  
*kālameghasya rukmiṇyā durvāseśvarabhadrayoḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Then the stories of Ksemarka, Unnata Vighnesa and Jalasvami, the stories of Kalamegha, Rukmini, Durvasa, IgvaraBhadra.

## \|\| 1.104.186 \|\|

*śaṅkhāvartamokṣatīrthagoṣpadācyutasadmanām \|*  
*jāleśvarasya huṅkāreśvaracaṇḍīśayoḥ kathā \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. The stories of the shrines Sankhavarta, Moksa- tirtha, Gospada and Acyutasadman ((Abode of Acyuta) and of the deities Jalesvara, Humkaresvara and Candlsa.

## \|\| 1.104.187 \|\|

*āśāpurasthavighneśakalākuṇḍakathādbhutā \|*  
*kapileśasya ca kathā jaradgavaśivasya ca \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. The wonderful story of Vighnesa stationed in Asapura and that of Kalakunda, the story of Kapilesa and of JaradgavaSiva (Siva with an old cow).

## \|\| 1.104.188 \|\|

*nalakarkeṭeśvarayorhāṭakeśvarajā kathā \|*  
*nāradeśayantrabhūṣādurgakūṭagaṇeśajā \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. The story of Nala and Karotesvara and that ofHata- kesvara, the Yantra and the Bhiisa (ornament) of Naradesa, Durgakuta and Ganesa’s story.

## \|\| 1.104.189 \|\|

*suparṇailākhyabhairavyorbhallatīrthabhavā kathā \|*  
*kīrtanaṃ kardamālasya guptasomeśvasya ca \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. The story ofBhairavIs called Suparna, Ela and that of Bhallatirtha, the glorification of Kardamala and Gupta Some ivara.

## \|\| 1.104.190 \|\|

*bahusvarṇeśaśṛṅgeśakoṭīśvarakathā tataḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeśvarakoṭīśadāmodaragṛhotkathā \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. The stories of Bahusvarne^a (Lord of much gold), SrngeSa and Kotlsvara, the stories of Markan^esvara, Damodaragrha and Kotxsa.

## \|\| 1.104.191 \|\|

*svarṇarekhā brahmakuṇḍaṃ kuntībhīmeśvarau tathā \|*  
*mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ ca sarvasvaṃ kṣetre vastrāpathe smṛtam \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. Svarnarekha, Brahmakun^a, the shrines of Kuntl- ^vara and Bhimesvara, the pit of MrgI (hind) is remembered in the temple of Sarvasva and Vastrapatha.

## \|\| 1.104.192 \|\|

*durgābhilleśagaṅgeśaraivatānāṃ kathādbhutā \|*  
*tator'budeśvara kathā acaleśvarakīrtanam \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. The wonderful stories of Durga, BhileSa, Gange^a and Raivata, then the story of Arbudesvara, the glorification of Acaleshvara.

## \|\| 1.104.193 \|\|

*nāgatīrthasya ca kathā vasiṣṭāśramavarṇanam \|*  
*bhadrakarṇasya māhātmyaṃ trinetrasya tataḥ param \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. The story of Nagatirtha, the description of Vasistha’s hermitage, the great eminence of Bhadrakarna and that of Trinetra (the three-eyed) thereafter.

## \|\| 1.104.194 \|\|

*kedārasya ca māhātmyaṃ tīrthāṅgamanakīrtanam \|*  
*koṭīśvararūpatīrthahṛṣīkeśakathārastataḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. The greatness of Kedara, the glorification of the arrival at the holy centre, the stories of the holy centre in the form of Kotisvara and that of Arsikesa.

## \|\| 1.104.195 \|\|

*siddheśaśukreśvarayormaṇikarṇīśakīrtanam \|*  
*paṅgutīrthayamatīrthavārāhatīrthavarṇanam \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. The glorification of Siddhega, Sukresvara and Manikarnlga, the description of Pangutlrtha, Yamatirtha and Varaha tlrtha.

## \|\| 1.104.196 \|\|

*candraprabhāsarpiḍodaśrīmātāśuklatīrthajam \|*  
*kātyāyanyāśca māhātmyaṃ tataḥ piṇḍārakasya ca \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. The greatness of Gandra Prabhasa, Pintfoda, Srimata, Suklatirtha and Katyayani, then the greatness of Pindaraka.

## \|\| 1.104.197 \|\|

*tataḥ kanakhalasyātha cakramānuṣatīrthayoḥ \|*  
*kapilāgnitīrthakathā tathā raktānubandhajā \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. Then the glory of Kanakhala, Cakratlrtha and Manusatirtha, the story of Kapilagnilirtha and that of Raktanu- bhandha.

## \|\| 1.104.198 \|\|

*gaṇeśapārtheśvarayoryāntrāyāmujjvalasya ca \|*  
*caṇḍīsthānanāgodbhavaśivakuṇḍamaheśajā \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. The pilgrimage to Ganesa and Parthesvara shrines, the story of Ujjvala, Candlsthana (abode of the Goddess), the greatness of Sivakunda originating from Naga, the story of Mahega.

## \|\| 1.104.199 \|\|

*kāmeśvarasya mārkaṇḍeyotpatteśca kathā tataḥ \|*  
*uddālakeśasiddheśagatatīthakathā pṛthak \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. The story of Ramegvara and the origin of Mark- andeya, the stories severally of Uddalakesa, Siddhega and Gatatirtha.

## \|\| 1.104.200 \|\|

*śrīdevaravātotpattiśca vyāsagautamatīrthayoḥ \|*  
*kulasaṃtāramāhātmyaṃ rāmakoṭyāhvatīrthayoḥ \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. The origin of Sridevakhata and the shrines of Vyasatirtha and Gautama-tirtha, the greatness of Kutasantara and that of the Tirthas of Rama and Koti.

## \|\| 1.104.201 \|\|

*candrodbhedeśānaśṛṅgabrahmasthānodbhavo 'dbhutam \|*  
*tripuṣkararudrahradaguheśvara kathā śubhā \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. The wonderful origin of Candrodbheda, lshanashmga, and Brahmasthana, the auspicious stories of Tripuskara, Rudrahrada and Guhesvara.

## \|\| 1.104.202 \|\|

*avimuktasya māhātmyamumāmāheśvarasya ca \|*  
*mahaujasaḥ prabhāvaśca jaṃbūtīrthasya varṇanam \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. The greatness of Avimukta and Uma-Maheshvara, the glory of Mahaujas, the description of Jambutlrtha.

## \|\| 1.104.203 \|\|

*gaṅgādharamiśrakayoḥ kathā vāthaphalastutiḥ \|*  
*dvārakāyāśca māhātmye candraśarmakathānakam \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. The story of Gangadhara and Misraka and the eulogy of the benefit (of reading this). In the context of the greatness ofDvaraka, the story of Gandrasharman.

## \|\| 1.104.204 \|\|

*jāgarādyarcanādyākhyā vratamekādaśībhavam \|*  
*mahādvādaśikākhyānaṃ prahlādarṣisamāgamaḥ \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. The holy rite of Ekadasi and the narration of (the mode) of worship,and keeping awake (on Ekadasi night), the description of Mahadvadagika and the meeting of Prahlada and the sage.

## \|\| 1.104.205 \|\|

*durvāsasa upākhyānaṃ yātropakramakīrtanam \|*  
*gomatyutpattikathanaṃ tasyāṃ snānādijaṃ phalam \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. The anecdote of Durvasas, the glorification of the beginning of Yatra (pilgrimage), the narration of the origin of Gomati and the benefit of ablution etc., therein.

## \|\| 1.104.206 \|\|

*cakratīrthasya māhātmyaṃ gomatyudadhisaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*sanakādihradākhyānaṃ nṛgatīrthakathā tataḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. The greatness of Cakratirtha, the confluence of the river Gomati (near Dvaraka) and the ocean (the Arabian sea), the narration of the Hrada (deep pool) of Sanaka and others, then the story of Nrgatirtha.

## \|\| 1.104.207 \|\|

*gopracārakathā puṇyā gopīnāṃ dvārakāgamaḥ \|*  
*gopīsaraḥ samākhyānaṃ brahmatīrthādikīrtanam \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. The holy story of Gopracara, the arrival of cowherdesses at Dvaraka, the narration of Gopisaras (the lake of the cowherdesses); the glorification of Brahmatirtha.

## \|\| 1.104.208 \|\|

*pañcanadyāgamākhyānaṃ nānākhyānasamanvitam \|*  
*śivaliṅgagadātīrthakṛṣṇapūjādikīrtanam \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. The narration of the advent of five rivers, alongwith different stories and the glorification of Sivalinga, Gadatlrtha and the worship etc. of Kfsna.

## \|\| 1.104.209 \|\|

*trivikramasya mūrtākhyā durvāsaḥkṛṣṇasaṃkathā \|*  
*kuśadaityavadhoñcāraviśeṣārcanajaṃ phalam \|\| 209 \|\|*

209\. The story of the Murti (the idol) ofTrivikrama, the conversation between Durvasas and Krsna, the benefit of the recital of death of Kusha daitya and the special worship thereof.

## \|\| 1.104.210 \|\|

*gomatyāṃ dvārakāyāṃ ca tīrthāgamanakīrtanam \|*  
*kṛṣṇamandirasaṃprekṣā drāravatyabhiṣecanam \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. The glorification of the advent of all the Tlrthas in Gomati and Dvaraka, the survey of Krsna’s temple and the coronation at Dvaravatl.

## \|\| 1.104.211 \|\|

*tatratīrthāvāsakathā dvārakāpuṇyakīrtanam \|*  
*ityeṣa saptamaḥ proktaḥ khaṇḍaḥ prābhāsiko dvijāḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. There the story of the residence (of all Tirthas) that holy centre; the glorification of the merit of Dvaraka. О Brahmana, this is the summary of the seventh part called Prabhasika Khanka.

## \|\| 1.104.212-213 \|\|

*skāndesarvottarakathe śibamāhātmyavarṇane \|*  
*likhitvaitattu yo dadyāddhemaśūlasamanvitam \|\| 212 \|\|*

*mādhyāṃ satkṛtya viprāya sa śaive modate pade \|\| 213 \|\|*

212-213. In the course of description of the greatness of Siva in the Skanda Purana with all the gloriousmost stories, he who writes this out and gives it to a Brahmana on the full moon day in the month of Magha, receiving him duly and with the charitable gift of a gold trident, rejoices in the region of Siva.

## Chapter 105. The Vamana Ригйпа1: Contents

## \|\| 1.105.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ vāmanābhidham \|*  
*trivikramacaritrāḍhyaṃ daśasāhasrasaṃkhyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Brahma said:*

1\. О dear one, listen, I shall recount to you the Purana named Vamana. It contains stories of Trivikrama and comprises ten thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.105.2 \|\|

*kūrmakalpasamākhyānaṃ vargatrayakathānam \|*  
*bhāgadvayasamāyuktaṃ vaktṛśrotṛśubhāvaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It contains the narratives of events of the Kurma Kalpa; it has stories descriptive of Vargatraya (the three aims of life viz. virtue, love and wealth). It is in two parts. It is auspicious to the narrator as well as to the listener.

## \|\| 1.105.3 \|\|

*purāṇapraśnaḥ prathamaṃ brahmaśīrṣacchidā tataḥ \|*  
*kapālamocanākhyānaṃ dakṣayajñavihiṃsanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the outset, there is the enquiry about the Purana; the cutting off of the head of Brahma, the story of Kapala- mocana, the destruction of Daksa’s Yajna.

## \|\| 1.105.4 \|\|

*harasya kālarūpākhyā kāmasya dahanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*prahlādanārāyaṇayoryuddhaṃ devāsurāhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The description of (and narration about) Нага in the form of Kala, then the burning of Kama, the fight between Prahlada and Narayana, the war between the Devas and the Asuras.

## \|\| 1.105.5 \|\|

*sukeśyarkasamākhyānaṃ tato bhuvanakośakam \|*  
*tataḥ kāmyavratākhyānaṃ śrīdurgācaritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The narration of the story of SukeshI and Arka, then the Bhuvanakoia (description of the worlds), then the description of Kamyavratas (Vratas performed with some desired object), then the-story of Sri Durga.

## \|\| 1.105.6 \|\|

*tapatīcaritaṃ paścātkurukṣetrasya varṇanam \|*  
*satyāmāhātmyamatulaṃ pārvatījanmakīrtanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then the story of Tapati, description of Kurukshetra, the incomparable greatness of Satya, the glorification of the nativity of Parvatl.

## \|\| 1.105.7 \|\|

*tapastasyā vivāhaśca gauryupākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kauśikyupākhyānaṃ kumāracaritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Her penance, and then the marriage, thereafter, the story of Gauri, thereafter, the subsidiary story of Kaushiki and then the story of Kumara.

## \|\| 1.105.8 \|\|

*tato 'ndhakavadhākhyānaṃsādhyopākhyānakantataḥ \|*  
*jābālicaritaṃ paścādarajāyāḥ kathādbhutā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the story of killing Andhaka, then the narrative of Sadhyas, afterwards, the story of Jabali, the wonderful story of Araja.

## \|\| 1.105.9 \|\|

*andhakeśarayoryuddhaṃ gaṇatvaṃ cāndhakasya ca \|*  
*marutāṃ janmakathanaṃ baleśca caritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The fight between Andhaka and lshvara, Andhaka given the status of a Gana (attendant of Siva), the narration of the Maruts, then the story of Bali.

## \|\| 1.105.10 \|\|

*tatastu lakṣmyāścaritaṃ traivikramamataḥ param \|*  
*prahlādatīrthayātrāyāṃ procyante 'tha kathāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then Laksmi’s story, thereafter the story ofTri- vikrama, then auspicious stories are being narrated in the course of pilgrimage of Prahlada.

## \|\| 1.105.11 \|\|

*tataśca dhundhu caritaṃ pretopākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*nakṣatrapuruṣākhyānaṃ śrīdāmacaritaṃ tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereafter, the story of Dhundhu; then the story of the Preta (Ghosts), the story of Naksatrapurusa (The name of a Vrata), then the story of Sridama.

## \|\| 1.105.12 \|\|

*trivikramacaritrānte brahmaproktaḥ stavottamaḥ \|*  
*prahlādabalisaṃvāde sutale hariśaṃsanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At the end of the story of Trivikrama, there is an excellent hymn composed by Brahma. In the course of conversation between Prahlada and Bali in Sutala (Nether- worlds), Hari is praised.

## \|\| 1.105.13 \|\|

*ityeṣa pūrvabhāgo 'sya purāṇasya tavoditaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇṇato 'syottaraṃ bhāgaṃ bahadvāmanasaṃjñakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thus the story of the first half of this Purana is mentioned to you. Hereafter, listen to its latter half called Brhad Vamana.

## \|\| 1.105.14 \|\|

*māheśvarī bhāgavatī saurī gāṇeśvarī tathā \|*  
*catasraḥ saṃhitāścātra pṛthak sāhasrasaṃkhyayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There are four Samhitas (compendiums) therein each consisting of a thousand verses. They are Mahesvarl, Bhagavati, Sauri and Ganegvari.1

## \|\| 1.105.15 \|\|

*māheśvaryāṃ tu kṛṣṇasya tadbhaktānāṃ ca kīrtanam \|*  
*bhāgavatyāṃ jaganmātukhatārakathādbhutā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the compilation called Maheshvari, there is the glorification of Krsna and his devotees. In the compendium Bhagavati, there is the wonderful story of the incarnation of the Mother of the Universe.

## \|\| 1.105.16 \|\|

*sauryāṃ sūryasya mahimā gaditaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ \|*  
*gāṇeśvaryāṃ gaṇeśasya caritaṃ ca maheśituḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the compendium Sauri, the glory of the Sun is spoken (praised) which is destructive of sins. In the compendium Ganesvarl there is the story of Ganesha and Mahesha.

## \|\| 1.105.17 \|\|

*ityetadvāmanaṃ nāma purāṇaṃ suvicitrakam \|*  
*pulastyena samākhyātaṃ nāradāya mahātmane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This is a wonderful Purana named Vamana. It is narrated by Pulastya to the noble-souled Narada.

## \|\| 1.105.18 \|\|

*tato nāradataḥ prāptaṃ vyāsena sumahātmanā \|*  
*vyāsāttu labdhavāṃścaitat tacchiṣyo romaharṣaṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then it was acquired from Narada by Vyasa, a very great Atman. From Yyasa his disciple Romaharsana acquired this.

## \|\| 1.105.19 \|\|

*sa cākhyāsyati viprebhyo naimiṣīyebhya eva ca \|*  
*evaṃ paraṃparāprāptaṃ purāṇaṃ vāmanaṃ śubham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He will narrate it to the Brahmanas of Naimisa forest. Thus the auspicious Vamana Purana has been traditionally handed down and acquired.

## \|\| 1.105.20-22 \|\|

*ye paṭhanti ca śṛṇvanti te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*likhitvaitatpurāṇaṃ tu yaḥ śaradviṣuver'payet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*viprāya vedaviduṣe ghṛtadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*sa samuddhṛtya narakānnayetsvargaṃ pitṝnsvakān \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dehānte bhuktabhogo 'sau yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Those who read this or listen to this, attain the greatest goal. He who writes this out and gives it to aBrahmana Vedic scholar at the time of autumnal equinox alongwith ghee and a cow, uplifts his Pitrs (ancestors) from hells and leads them to heaven. After enjoying all worldly pleasures and dying thereafter, he attains the great region ofVisnu. All this evidence shows that the author of the NP had positively a different and a larger version than the extant KP. The extant (both Venkatesvara and Kasiraja) editions of KP tally to a great extent with the Brdhmi Samhitd and the other Samhitas seem to have been lost. Hazra notes that originally the Кйгта was a Pdhcardtra Purana which was subsequently Paiupatised. (vide PR. pp. 57. ff.)

## Chapter 106. The Kurma Ритйпа: Contents

## \|\| 1.106.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa marīce tvaṃ purāṇaṃ kūrmasaṃjñakam \|*  
*lakṣmīkalpānucaritaṃ yatra kūrmavapurhariḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ māhātmyaṃ ca pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*indradyumnaprasaṃgena prāharṣibhyo dayānvitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

God Brahma said:

1-2. О dear child, О Marici, listen to the Purana called Kurma. It covers the events of the Laksmi Kalpa. In the context of Indradyumna, the merciful Hari, assuming the form of a tortoise, proclaimed it to the sages the respective greatness of virtue, love, wealth and salvation.

## \|\| 1.106.3 \|\|

*tatsaptadaśasāhasraṃ sucatuḥ saṃhitaṃ śubham \|*  
*yatra brāhmāḥ purā proktā dharmā nānāvidhā mune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It consists of seventeen thousand verses.1 It is very- auspicious with four Samhitas. О sage, many of the Brahma dharmas (religious duties) mentioned formerly, have been explained in it.

## \|\| 1.106.4 \|\|

*nānanākathāprasaṃgena nṛṇāṃ sadgatidāyakāḥ \|*  
*tatra pūrvavibhāge tu purāṇopakramaḥ purā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They are dealt with in the context of different stories. They are the bestowers of good position (hereafter) unto men. In the first subdivision there is the usual beginning at the outset.

## \|\| 1.106.5 \|\|

*lakṣmīndradyumnasaṃvādaḥ kūrṃmarṣigaṇasaṃkathā \|*  
*varṇāśramācārakathā jagadutpattikīrtanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is the dialogue between Laksmi and Indradyumna and the conversation between the Divine Tortoise and the groups of sages. Then is the account of the four castes (Varnas) and stages in life (ASramas, and their (prescribed) duties, the narration of the creation of the Universe.

## \|\| 1.106.6 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ sargaḥ śāṅkaraṃ caritaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There is a brief description about the calculation of Time (such as Yugas, Manvantaras), at the end of the dissolution, there is the eulogy of the Lord (by Siddhas), then a brief description of the creation (of the universe) and the story of Sankara.

## \|\| 1.106.7 \|\|

*sahasranāma pārvatyā yogasya ca nirūpaṇam \|*  
*bhṛguvaṃśasamākhyānaṃ tataḥ svāyambhuvasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The thousand names of Parvatl, the exposition of the Yoga philosophy, the description of the family of Bhrigu, and then that of Svayambhuva (Manu).

## \|\| 1.106.8 \|\|

*devādīnāṃ samutpattirdakṣayajñāhatistataḥ \|*  
*dakṣasṛṣṭikathā paścātkaśyapānvayakīrtanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The origin of the Devas and others, then the destruction of Daksa’s Yajna, the story of the creation by Daksa, then the narration of the lineage of Kafyapa (containing the account of the Solar and Lunar dynasties).

## \|\| 1.106.9 \|\|

*ātreyavaṃśakathanaṃ kṛṣṇasyaṃ caritaṃ śubham \|*  
*mārtaṇḍakṛṣṇasaṃvādo vyāsapāṇḍavasaṃkathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The description of the family of Atri, the auspicious story of Kxsna, the dialogue between Krsna and Martanda (The Sun-god) and the conversation between Vyasa and the Panda vas.

## \|\| 1.106.10 \|\|

*yugadharmānukathanaṃ vyāsajaiminikīrtanam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāśca māhātmyaṃ prayāgasya tataḥ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The narration of the characteristic nature of different Yugas (Yugadharma), the glorification of Vyasa and Jaimini, the greatness of Varanasi and Prayaga.

## \|\| 1.106.11-12 \|\|

*trailokyavarṇanaṃ caiva vedaśākhānirūpaṇam \|*  
*uttare 'syā vibhāge tu purā gītaiśvarī tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vyāsagītā tataḥ proktā nānādharmaprabodhinī \|*  
*nānāvidhānāṃ tīrthānāṃ māhātmyaṃ ca pṛthak tataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The description of the three worlds, the review of the branches of Vedas. In the latter half of the Purana there are the Isvaraglta and the Vyasaglta. These two illuminate the different kinds ofDharmas; the greatness of the different holy centres is mentioned separately.

## \|\| 1.106.13 \|\|

*pratisargaprakathanaṃ brāhmīyaṃ saṃhitā smṛtā \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ bhāgavatīsaṃhitārtha nirūpaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then there is the narration ofPralisarga (Dissolution of the Universe). This much is the summary of the first division named Brahmi Sariihita. Henceforth, the compendium Bhagavatl Samhita is reviewed.

## \|\| 1.106.14 \|\|

*kathitā yatra varṇānāṃ pṛthakvṛttirudāhṛtā \|*  
*pāda'syāḥ prathame proktā brāhmaṇānāṃ vyavasthitiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In this division, the separate activities of the different castes are narrated. In the first quarter of this Samhita, the determination of duties etc. of the Brahmanas has been narrated.

## \|\| 1.106.15 \|\|

*sadā cāgatmikā vatsa bhogasaukhyavivarddhanī \|*  
*dvitīye kṣattriyāṇāṃ tu vṛttiḥ samyakprakīrtitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О dear one, it consists of good and disciplined life and it enhances their enjoyment and the happiness of worldly pleasures. In the second quarter, the functions of the profession of the Ksatriyas are clearly enunciated.

## \|\| 1.106.16-19 \|\|

*yayā tvāśritayā pāpaṃ vidhūyeha vrajeddivam \|*  
*tṛtīye vaiśyajātīnāṃ vṛttiruktā caturvidhā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yayā caritayā samyaglabhe gatimuttamām \|*  
*caturthe 'syāstathā pāde śūdravṛttirudāhṛtā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yayā saṃtuṣyati śrīśo nṛṇāṃ śreyovivarddhanaḥ \|*  
*pañcame 'syāstataḥ pāde vṛttiḥ saṃkarajoditā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yayā caritayāpnoti bhāvinīṃ gatimuttamām \|*  
*ityeṣā pañcapadyuktā dvitīyā saṃhitā mune \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19a. Ifa (Ksatriya) abides by these, he shall eschew sins and go to heaven. In the third quarter, the fourfold activities of the Vaisyas have been explained. If these are followed, one shall attain excellent salvation. In its fourth quarter, the activities of the Sudras are explained. If these are followed, Lord Visnu becomes pleased and increases the welfare of men. In the fifth quarter the duties and functions of the mixed castes are explained. If they are followed, one attains excellent state of future life.

19b. О sage, thus is narrated the second compendium (Samhita) consisting of five sections (Paftcapadi).

## \|\| 1.106.20 \|\|

*tṛtīyātroditā saurī nṝṇāṃ kāryavidhāyinī \|*  
*ṣoḍhā ṣaṭkarmasirddhi bodhayantī ca kāminām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The third compendium is called Sauri. It lays down the various duties of men. To men who desire (to obtain some objects), it instructs the six karmans and their Siddhis in six different ways.

## \|\| 1.106.21 \|\|

*caturthīvaiṣṇavo nāma mokṣadā parikīrtitā \|*  
*catuṣpadī dvijātīnāṃ sākṣādbrahmasvarūriṇī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The fourth compendium is called Vaisnavl. It is glorified as the bestower of Liberation from Samsara. It consists of four sections (Catus-padi). It is veritable Brahma i.e. the Veda incarnate to the twice-borns.

## \|\| 1.106.22 \|\|

*tāḥ kramātṣaṭcaturdvīṣusāhasrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The four Samhitas contain respectively six thousand, four thousand, two thousand and five thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.106.23 \|\|

*etatkūrmapurāṇaṃ tu caturvargaphalapradam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvotkṛṣṭagatipradam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. This Kurma Purana yields the benefit of four Vargas (the aims oflife) viz. Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksa. It yields the best of all goals to the men who read and listen to it.

## \|\| 1.106.24 \|\|

*likhitvaitattu yo bhaktyā hemakūrmasamanvitam \|*  
*brāhmaṇāyā yane dadyātsa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He who writes this (Purana) with devotion and gives it to a Brahmana during the transit of the sun from the tropics, alongwith the replica of a tortoise in gold, attains the greatest goal.

## Chapter 107. The Matsya Purdria: Contents

## \|\| 1.107.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*atha mātsyaṃ purāṇaṃ te pravakṣye dvijasattama \|*  
*yatroktaṃ saptakalpānāṃ vṛttaṃ saṃkṣipya bhūtale \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lord Brahma said:

1\. О excellent Brahmana, I shall, henceforth, recount the Matsya Purana to you. In it, all the events of the seven Kalpas in the world, have been condensed.

## \|\| 1.107.2 \|\|

*vyāsena vedaviduṣā nārasiṃhopavarṇane \|*  
*upakramya taduddiṣṭaṃ caturddaśasahasrakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It has been composed by Vyasa, a scholar in the Vedas, in about fourteen thousand verses. He has begun by describing Narasimha. The Vayu, the Matsya and the Bk. P. state this figure, but AP. gives 13000 and the Br. V. 18000 verses as the figure. Actually the Anand- asrama edition contains 14,062 verses. The contents of that edition tally with those given by the NP. here.

## \|\| 1.107.3 \|\|

*manumatsyasusaṃvādo brahmāṇḍakathanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*brahmadevāsurotpattirmārutotpattireva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The discussion between Manu and Matsya, then the narration (description) of the Cosmic Egg; the creation of the Devas, Asuras and the Marut (wind) from the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.107.4 \|\|

*madanadvādaśī tadvallokapālābhipūjanam \|*  
*manvantarasamuddeśo vaiśyarājyābhivarṇanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Madana-DvadaSI (the twelfth lunar day in honour of Madana) and the worship of the' guardians of the worlds; the survey of the Manvantaras, the description of the government of the kingdom by the Vaisyas.

## \|\| 1.107.5 \|\|

*sūryavaivasvatotpattirbudhasaṃgamanaṃ tathā \|*  
*pitṛvaṃśānukathanaṃ śraddhākālastathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The birth of Vaivasvata (Manu) from the sun, the contact with Budha (Mercury), the narration of the lineage of the Pitrs; the opportune time for (performance of) Sraddha).

## \|\| 1.107.6 \|\|

*pitṛtīrthapracāraśca somotpattistathaiva ca \|*  
*kīrtanaṃ somavaṃśasya yayāticaritaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The peregrination among the Pitr-Tirthas, the origin of Soma (the moon), the glorification of the lunar race and the story of Yayati.

## \|\| 1.107.7 \|\|

*pitṛvaṃśānukathanaṃ sṛṣṭavaṃśānukīrtanam \|*  
*bhṛguśāpastathā viṣṇordaśadhā janmane kṣitau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The story of Karttavirya, the narration of the created race, Bhrigu’s curse to Visnu to take ten births on the Earth.

## \|\| 1.107.8 \|\|

*kīrttanaṃ pūruvaṃśasya vaṃśo hautāśanaḥ param \|*  
*kriyāyogastataḥ paścātpurāṇaparikīrtanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the glorification of Puru’s race, the race of Huta- sana (the fire), the path of activity. Thereafter, the narration of the Purana.

## \|\| 1.107.9 \|\|

*vrataṃ nakṣatrapuruṣaṃ mārtaṇḍaśayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvrataṃ tadvadrohiṇīcandrasaṃjñitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Vrata (holy rite) called Naksatra Purusa, Mar- tanda-Sayana, the Vrata of Krsnastami (the eighth day of the dark half of Sravana observance in honour of Krsna’s birth) and that of Rohinlcandra.

## \|\| 1.107.10 \|\|

*taḍāgavidhi māhātmyaṃ pādapotsarga eva ca \|*  
*saubhāgyaśayanaṃ tadvadagastyavratameva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The greatness of constructing tanks; the gift of the trees, the Vrata called Saubhagya and Sayana Agastya Vrata.

## \|\| 1.107.11 \|\|

*tathānantatṛtīyāyā rasakalyāṇinīvratam \|*  
*tathaivānaṃ dakaryāśca vrataṃ sārasvataṃ punaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Vrata of Anantatrtiya, that of RasakalyaninI, that of Anandakari and then the Sarasvata (belonging to Sarasvati) Vrata.

## \|\| 1.107.12 \|\|

*uparāgābhiṣekaśca saptamīśanaṃ tathā \|*  
*bhīmākhyā dvādaśī tadvadanaṅgaśayanaṃ tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Uparagabhiseka (Ablution at the time of eclipse SaptamX Say an a, Bhima DvadaSI, Anangasayana rite.

## \|\| 1.107.13 \|\|

*aśūnyaśayanaṃ tadvattathaivāṅgārakavratam \|*  
*saptamīsaptakaṃ tadvadviśokadvādaśīvratam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Aanyasayanavrata, Angarakavrata (holy rite of Mars) Saptami saptaka (seven Saptamls i.e. seventh lunar day) Visokadvadashrvrata (holy rite on the twelfth lunar day for wiping off grief).

## \|\| 1.107.14 \|\|

*merupradānaṃ daśadhā grahaśāntistathaiva ca \|*  
*grahasvarūpakathanaṃ tathā śivacaturdaśī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The gift of Meru, ten-fold specification of evil planets; the narration of the forms of planets, Sivacaturdasi (the fourteenth day of Siva).

## \|\| 1.107.15 \|\|

*tathā sarvaphalatyāgaḥ sūryavāravrataṃ tathā \|*  
*saṃkrāntisnapanaṃ tadvadvibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The abandonment of all fruits, the holy observance of Suryavara (Sunday), the taking of bath at the time of Sankranti (Solar Transit from one sign of Zodiac to another), the holy rite of ViBhuti DvadaSi.

## \|\| 1.107.16 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭīvratānāṃ māhātmyaṃ tathā snānavidhikamaḥ \|*  
*prayāgasya tu māhātmyaṃ dvīpalokānuvarṇanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The greatness of shasthlvratas (holy rites on#the sixth Lunar day) (leading shastivratas — sixty holy rites), then the rules of procedure regarding holy baths, the greatness of Prayaga, the description of continents and the worlds.

## \|\| 1.107.17 \|\|

*tathāntarikṣacāraśca dhruvamāhātmyameva ca \|*  
*bhavanāni suredrāṇāṃ tripurodyotanaṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The movement in the firmament, the greatness of Dhruva (Pole Star), the abodes of the leading Devas, the illumination of the three cities.

## \|\| 1.107.18 \|\|

*pitṛpravaramāhātmyaṃ manvantaravinirṇayaḥ \|*  
*caturyugasya saṃbhūtiryugadharmanirūpaṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The greatness of leading Pitrs, the description of Manvantaras, the creation of the set of four Yugas and the review of Yugadharma (the characteristics peculiar to the different Yugas).

## \|\| 1.107.19 \|\|

*vajrāṅgasya tu saṃbhūti stārakotpattireva ca \|*  
*tārakāsuramāhātmyaṃ brahmadevānukīrtanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The birth of Vajranga and the nativity of Taraka, the greatness of the demon Taraka, the glorification of God Brahma.

## \|\| 1.107.20 \|\|

*pārvatīsaṃbhavastadvattathā śivatapovanam \|*  
*anaṅgadehadāhaśca ratiśokastathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The nativity of Parvati, the penance-grove of Siva, the burning of the body of Ananga (Cupid) and the grief of Rati.

## \|\| 1.107.21 \|\|

*gaurītapovanaṃ tadvacchivenātha prasādanam \|*  
*pārvatīṛṣisaṃvādastathairodvāhamaṅgalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The penance-grove of Gaurl, soothing by Siva, the conversation between Parvati and the sages, the auspicious celebration of Siva’s marriage.

## \|\| 1.107.22 \|\|

*kumārasaṃbhavastadvatkumāravijayastathā \|*  
*tārakasya vadho ghoro narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The birth of Kumara and the victory of Kumara, the terrible killing of Taraka, the description of Narasimha.

## \|\| 1.107.23 \|\|

*padmodbhavavisargastu tathaivāndhakaghātanam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāstu māhātmyaṃ narmadāyāstathaiva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The creation of the lotus-born deity; the killing of Andhaka, the greatness of Varanasi as well as that of Narmada.

## \|\| 1.107.24 \|\|

*pravarānukramastadvatpitṛgāthānukīrtanam \|*  
*tathobhayamukhīdānaṃ dānaṃ kṛṣṇājinasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The description of Pitrs according to the Gotras and Pravaras, the glorification of the Pitrgatha (song of Pitrs) Ubhayamukhidanam (gift of a cow while giving birth to a calf and hence two-faced) and the gift of Krsnajina (deerskin of a black antelope).

## \|\| 1.107.25 \|\|

*tataḥ sāvitryupākhyānaṃ rājadharmāstathaiva ca \|*  
*vividhotpātakathanaṃ grahaṇāntastathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then the story of Savitrl, the duties of a king, the narration of different kinds of evil portents ending with eclipses.

## \|\| 1.107.26 \|\|

*yātrānimittakathanaṃ svapnamaṅgalakīrtane \|*  
*vāmanasya tu māhātmyaṃ vārāhasya tataḥ param \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The narration of omens at the time of journey, the glorification of auspicious signs in dreams, the greatness of Vamanaand that of Varaha (Boar) thereafter.

## \|\| 1.107.27 \|\|

*samudramathanaṃ tadvatkālakūṭābhiśāntanam \|*  
*devāsuravimardaśca vāstuvidyā tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The churning of the ocean, the suppression (nullification) of the poison Kalaku(a, the clash between the Devas and the Demons; then the science of Engineering (planning the foundation and construction of a house).

## \|\| 1.107.28 \|\|

*pratimālakṣaṇaṃ tadvaddevatāyatanaṃ tathā \|*  
*prāsādalakṣaṇaṃ tadvanmaṇḍapāna ca lakṣaṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The characteristic features of an image (idol); then (the construction) of the temple, the characteristic features of a mansion, the characteristics of a pavilion.

## \|\| 1.107.29 \|\|

*bhaviṣyarājñāmuddeśo mahādānānukīrtanam \|*  
*kalpānukīrtanaṃ tadvatpurāṇe 'sminprakīrtitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The indication of future kings, the glorification of great gifts, the narration of Kalpas — All these are narrated in this Purana.

## \|\| 1.107.30 \|\|

*pavitrametatkalyāṇamāyuḥ kīrtivivarddhanam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sa yāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. This Purana is pure and conducive to welfare; it causes increase in longevity and fame. He who reads this or listens to it, goes to Hari’s abode.

## \|\| 1.107.31 \|\|

*likhitvaitattu yo dadyāddhemamatsyagavānvitam \|*  
*viprāyābhyarcya viṣuve sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He who writes this and gifts it over to a Brahmana after worshipping him on the equinoctial transit, alongwith a gold fish and a cow attains the greatest region.

## Chapter 108. The Garuda Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.108.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*marīce śṛṇu vakṣyābhi purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ śubham \|*  
*garuḍāyābravītpṛṣṭo bhagavāngaruḍāsanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

God Brahma, said:

1\. О Marlci, listen, I shall recount to you the auspicious Garuda Purana.1 On being asked, the Lord Visnu, seated on Garuda, recounted this to Garuda.

## \|\| 1.108.2 \|\|

*ekonaviṃśasāhasraṃ tārkṣyakalpakathānvitam \|*  
*purāṇopakramapraśnaḥ sargaḥ saṃkṣepatastataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It consists of nineteen thousand verses. The story deals with the events of the Tark?ya Kalpa. There is the usual enquiry about the beginning of the Purana, creation of the Universe is described svccinctly.

## \|\| 1.108.3 \|\|

*sūryādipūjanavidhirdīkṣāvidhirataḥ param \|*  
*śrāddhapūjā tataḥ paścānnavavyūhārcanaṃ dvija \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Brahmana, there are rules of the procedure of the worship of the sun; thereafter, the rules regarding initiation ceremony; then there is the worship in connection with Sraddhas, after this (injunctions regarding) the worship of nine Vytihas (manifestations of the Lord).

## \|\| 1.108.4 \|\|

*pūjāvidhānaṃ ca tathā vaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*yogādhyāyastato viṣṇornāmasāhasrakīrtanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the injunctions regarding the worship, the Paft- jara (ritualisticcage) pertaining to Visnu, the chapter on Yoga system and the glorification of Visnu’s thousand names.

## \|\| 1.108.5 \|\|

*dhyānaṃ viṣṇostataḥ sūryapūjā mṛtyuñjayārcanam \|*  
*mālāmantraḥ śivārcātha gaṇapūjā tataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The meditation on Visnu, then the worship of the Sun, thereafter, the Arcana (worship) of Mrtyuftjaya, the Mala- mantra (Garland mantra), the worship of Siva and then the worship of his attendants.

## \|\| 1.108.6 \|\|

*gopālapūjā trailokyamohanaśrīdharārcanam \|*  
*viṣṇvarcā pañcatattvārcā cakrārcā devapūjanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The adoration of Gopala, the worship of Sridhara, the fascinator of the three worlds, the worship of Visnu of the five Tattvas, the discus and the worship of the Lord.

## \|\| 1.108.7 \|\|

*nyāsādisaṃdhyopāstiśca durgārcātha surārcanam \|*  
*pūjā māheśvarī cātaḥ pavitrāropaṇārcanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The rites ofNyasa, etc., the Upasti, performance of Sandhya prayers, the worship of Durga and then the worship of the Devas, the worship of Maheshvara, and then the rite of wearing the Pavitra (Darbha grass with a loop worn in the finger like a ring) and worshipping.

## \|\| 1.108.8 \|\|

*mūrtidhyāṃnavāstumānaṃ prāsādānāṃ ca lakṣaṇam \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā sarvadevānāṃ pṛthakpūjā vidhānataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The meditation on the idol of the Lord, the measurements of the sites of the buildings; the characteristics of palaces, the mode of installation of all the Devas with the several modes of worship. The confusion is due to difference in Mss. or versions of the GP. available to the writer of the Ригёца, e. g.GP. I.ch. 107 (ref. to the РагЗДага Smf ti) is not known to the NP. noted by Dr. Ramshankar Bhattacharya (GP. Intro, p. 14-15)the table of contents given in the NP agrees more closely with the Jibanand edt. of the GP. (though Venkafelvara edt. of GP also tallies with that of the NP). The Pretakalpa in the NP. differs in some respects from all the printed editions of the GP as accretions went on increasing in the Pretakalpa (R. S. Bhattacharya — ibid, p. 16). A few slips in the readings of the NP (Venkateivara) edt. NP. Sraddha(verse 3) for GP. I. 10 Sreyddi Pqjd. NP. VidhiKriya (verse 9 for GP. I. 53) Nidhi Kriya.

## \|\| 1.108.9 \|\|

*yogo 'ṣaṭāṅgo dānadharmāḥ prayaścittavidhikriyā \|*  
*dvīpeśanarakākhyānaṃ sūryavyūhaśca jyotiṣam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Yoga with its eight ancillaries, the Dharmas regarding the charitable gifts, the activity and the rules of procedure regarding the expiatory rites, the narration of different continents and their Lords, the description of hells, the solar system (planetary system around the sun) and Jyotisa (Science of Astrology and Astronomy.)

## \|\| 1.108.10 \|\|

*sāmudrikaṃ svarajñānaṃ navaratnaparīkṣaṇam \|*  
*māhātmyamatha tīrthānāṃ gayāmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The science ofSamudrika (Palmistry of prediction based on the characteristic marks on the body), the knowledge of the notes, scrutiny tests of the Navaratnas (the nine precious stones) the glory of the holy centres, the excellent greatness of Gaya.

## \|\| 1.108.11 \|\|

*tato manvantarākhyānaṃ pṛthakpṛthagvibhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*pitrākhyānaṃ varṇadharmā dravyaśuddhiḥ samarpaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the description of the Manvantaras severally alongwith their divisions, the enumeration of the Pitrs, the duties of the different Varnas (castes), the purification of the materials of worship, the dedication of benefit unto God.

## \|\| 1.108.12 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ vināyakasyārcā grahayajñastathaā śramāḥ \|*  
*jananākhyaṃ pretaśaucaṃ nītiśāstraṃ vratoktayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sraddha, worship of vinayaka, Grahayajna (sacrifice for propitiating the planets), the Asramas \\(stages of life), the impurity due to birth and death (in the family), Nitisastra (science of Polity and Ethics), statements about the holy rites.

## \|\| 1.108.13 \|\|

*sūryavaṃśaḥ somavaṃśo 'vatārakathanaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*rāmāyaṇaṃ harervaṃśo bhāratākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Solar race, the lunar race, the narration of the incarnations of Hari, the story of Rama, (the Ramayana), the genealogical line of Hari (the Harivarhsa) and then the story of Bharata.

## \|\| 1.108.14 \|\|

*āyurvedanidānaṃ prāk cikikatsā dravyajā guṇāḥ \|*  
*rogaghnaṃ kavacaṃ viṣṇorgāruḍaṃ traipuro manuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The science of life, pathology at the outset and (then) the treatment, then materia-medica (Dravyaja Gunah), the Kavaca (Mantras as coat ofmail) that dispels ailments and which pertains to Visnu and Garuda, the mantra pertaining to Tripura.

## \|\| 1.108.15 \|\|

*praśnacūḍāmaṇiścānto hayāyurvedakīrtanam \|*  
*oṣaghīnāma kathanaṃ tato vyākaraṇohanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. PraSna-cuda-mani (a treatise on answering astrologi- cally problems asked) at the end, the exposition of the veterinary science branch about Horses, the enumeration of the names of drugs and then discussion about grammar.

## \|\| 1.108.16 \|\|

*chandaḥ śāstraṃ sadācārastataḥ snānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tarpaṇaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca saṃdhyā pārvaṇakarma ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The science of prosody, good conduct and discipline, and then the rules regarding ablution, the rites of Tarpana Vaisvadeva, the twilight prayers and the holy rites (offering ablutions to Pitrs during Parvans such as the full moon and the new moon days and such other special days.

## \|\| 1.108.17 \|\|

*nityaśrāddhaṃ sarpiḍākhyaṃ dharmasāro 'ghaniṣkṛtiḥ \|*  
*pratisaṃkrama uktāḥ sma yugadharmāḥ kṛteḥ phalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Nityasraddha (the daily Sraddha), the description of Sapinda rite, the essence of Dharma, the atonement of sins, the secondary creation, the dissolution and the particular characteristics of the Yugas are narrated, the benefit of religious rites.

## \|\| 1.108.18 \|\|

*yogaśāstraṃ viṣṇubhaktirnamaskṛtiphalaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ cātha nārasiṃhastavottamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The system of Yoga philosophy, the devotion to Visnu, the benefit of obeisance to Hari, the greatness of Visnu, the excellent hymn to Narasimha.

## \|\| 1.108.19 \|\|

*jñānāmṛtaṃ guhuṣṭakaṃ stotraṃ viṣṇvarcanāhvayam \|*  
*vedāntasāṃkhyasiddhānto brahmajñānaṃ tathālmakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The nectar of perfect knowledge, the set of eight verses in praise of Guha (Karttikeya), the eulogy of Visnu, the principal tenets of Vedanta and Samkhya, the knowledge of the Brahman and the Atman.

## \|\| 1.108.20 \|\|

*gītāsāraḥ phalotkīrtiḥ pūrvakhaṇḍo 'yamīritaḥ \|*  
*athāsyaivottare khaṇḍe pretakalpaḥ puroditaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The gist of the Bhagavadgita, glorification of the fruit thereof — these are the topics mentioned in the first section. Then in the second section Pretakalpa (the rituals after the death) is narrated.

## \|\| 1.108.21 \|\|

*yatra tārkṣyeṇa saṃpṛṣṭo bhagavānāha vāḍavāḥ \|*  
*dharmaprakaṭanaṃ pūrvaṃ yogināṃ gatikāraṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О Brahmana, on being asked by Tarksya (Garuda) the lord communicated all these things, the revelation of Dharmas, the cause of salvation of the Yogins.

## \|\| 1.108.22 \|\|

*dānādikaṃ phalaṃ cāpi proktamantrorddhadaihikam \|*  
*yamalokasthamārgasya varṇana ca taḥ param \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The benefit of charitable gifts etc. is mentioned and then the Mantras for the rites of obsequies, then the description of the path leading to the world of Yama.

## \|\| 1.108.23 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśaśrāddhaphalako vṛttāntaścātra varṇitaḥ \|*  
*niṣkṛtiryamamārgasya dharmarājasya vaibhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The details (regarding the performance) are stated alongwith the fruit of sixteen Sraddhas. Expiatory rites in regard to the path of Yama, then the greatness of Dharmaraja.

## \|\| 1.108.24 \|\|

*pretapīḍāṃvinirddeśaḥ pretacihnanirūpaṇam \|*  
*pretānāṃ caritākhyānaṃ kāraṇaṃ pretatāṃ prati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Specific mention of the harassment of the Pretas (ghosts), review of the characteristic signs of the Pretas, the narration of the stories of the Pretas; the cause of ghosthood.

## \|\| 1.108.25 \|\|

*pretakṛtyavicāraśca sarpiḍīkaraṇoktayaḥ \|*  
*pretatvamokṣaṇākhyānaṃ dānāni ca vimuktaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Consideration of religious rites for the ghosts; statements regarding Sapintfikarana (the rite regarding the offerings of the balls of rice to the departed), the description of the release from ghost-hood, the charitable gifts for the purpose of salvation (of the ghosts).

## \|\| 1.108.26 \|\|

*āvaśyakottamaṃ dānaṃ pretasaukhyakarohanam \|*  
*śārīrakavinirdeśo yamalokasya varṇanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The indispensable excellent charitable gift; the inference of things causing happiness to the ghosts; the description of the embodied soul, the description of Yama’s world.

## \|\| 1.108.27 \|\|

*pretatvoddhārakathanaṃ karmakṛrttṛvinirṇayaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyoḥ pūrvakriyākhyānaṃ paścātkarmanirūpaṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The narration of the uplift from ghosthood; the specification regarding the holy rites and the doer, the narration of the rites to be performed before death, the exposition of subsequent rites.

## \|\| 1.108.28 \|\|

*madhyaṣoḍaśakaśrāddhaṃ svargaprāptikriyohanam \|*  
*sūtakasyātha saṃkhyāṃnaṃ nārāyaṇabalikriyā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The ‘middle sixteen Sraddhas, the stipulation of activities for the attainment of heaven, the reckoning of Sutaka (period of impurity due to birth), the rite of Narayana Bali (oblation unto Narayana.)

## \|\| 1.108.29 \|\|

*vṛṣotsargasya māhātmyaṃ niṣiddhaparivarjanam \|*  
*apamṛtyukriyoktiśca vipākaḥ karmaṇāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The greatness of Vpsotsarga (the rite of setting a bull calf free), the avoidance of forbidden activities, statement of the rites when accidental and premature death takes place, the fruits of human action.

## \|\| 1.108.30 \|\|

*kṛtyākṛtyavicāraśca viṣṇudhyānavimuktaye \|*  
*svargatau vihitākhyānaṃ svargasaukhyanirūpaṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The consideration ofKrtya and Akrtya (what should be done and what should not be done), meditation on Visnu for the purpose of Salvation, narration of the rites laid down for the attainment of heaven, the description of happiness in heaven.

## \|\| 1.108.31 \|\|

*bhūrlokavarṇanaṃ caiva saptādholokavarṇanam \|*  
*pañcorddhvalokakathanaṃ brahmāṇḍasthitikīrtanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The description of Bhurloka, (the Earth,) the description of seven nether-worlds, the narration of five upper worlds, the description of the position of the Cosmic Egg.

## \|\| 1.108.32 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍānekacaritaṃ brahmajīvanirūpaṇam \|*  
*ātyantikaṃ layākhyānaṃ phalastuti nirūpaṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Many stories concerning the cosmic egg, the exposition of the Brahman and the JIva (the individual soul); the narration of the ultimate dissolution (of the Universe) and the narration of the eulogy of benefits.

## \|\| 1.108.33 \|\|

*ityetadgāruḍaṃ nāma purāṇaṃ bhuktimuktidam \|*  
*kīrtitaṃ pāpaśamanaṃ paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus is the Purana named after Garuda; it yields worldly pleasures and salvation; it is glorified as destructive of sins of those men who read and listen to it.

## \|\| 1.108.34 \|\|

*likhitvaitatpurāṇaṃ tu viṣuve yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*sauvarṇahaṃsayugmāḍhyaṃ viprāya sa divaṃ vrajet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who writes out this Purana and gifts it to a Brahmana at the time of equinoctial transit, alongwith a pair of swans made of gold, goes to heaven.

## Chapter 109. The Brahmania Purana: Contents

## \|\| 1.109.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi brahmāṇḍākhyaṃ purātanam \|*  
*yacca dvādaśasāhasramādikalpakathāyutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*God Brahma said:*

1\. О dear one, listen, I shall recount to you the ancient (Purana) named Brahmantfa.1 It comprises twelve thousand verses. It deals with the events of the Adikalpa.

## \|\| 1.109.2 \|\|

*prakriyākhyo 'nuṣaṅgākhya upodghātastṛtīyakaḥ \|*  
*caturtha upasaṃhāraḥ pādāścatvāra eva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It has four Padas (quarters), the first one is called Prakriyapada, then is the Anusangapada, the third one is Upodghata Pada (quarter of Introductory matter) and the fourth one is Upasamhara (conclusion).

## \|\| 1.109.3 \|\|

*pūrvapādadvayaṃ pūrvo bhāgo 'tra samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyo madhyamo bhāgaścaturthastūttaro mataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The first two quarters constitute the first or earlier section, the third quarter forms the middle section and the fourth quarter, the final section.

## \|\| 1.109.4 \|\|

*ādau kṛtyasamuddeśo naimiṣākhyānakaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhotpattiśca lokakalpanameva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the beginning, there is the stipulation of duties, then the story of the Naimisha forest, the origin of Hiranyagar- bha, the conception of the different worlds.

## \|\| 1.109.5 \|\|

*eṣa vai prathamaḥ pādo dvitīyaṃ śṛṇu mānada \|*  
*kalpamanvantarākhyānaṃ lokajñānaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This is the (summary of the) first quarter. О bestower of honour, listen to the second. The narration of the Kalpas and the Manvantaras, the knowledge of the worlds, thereafter.

## \|\| 1.109.6 \|\|

*mānasīsṛṣṭikathanaṃ rudraprasavavarṇanam \|*  
*mahādevavibhūtiśca ṛṣisargastataḥ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The narration of the mental creation, the description of Rudra’s offsprings, the elegance and prowess of Mahadeva and thereafter, the creation by the sages.

## \|\| 1.109.7 \|\|

*agnīnāṃ vijayaścātha kālasadbhāvavarṇanam \|*  
*priyavratānvayoddeśaḥ pṛthivyāyāmavistaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The conquest of fires, the description of the existence of Kala (Time), the specification of the family of Priya- vrata, the length and extent of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.109.8 \|\|

*varṇanaṃ bhāratasyāsya tato 'nyeṣāṃ nirūpaṇam \|*  
*jambvādisaptadvīpākhyā tato 'dholokavarṇanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The description of the (sub-continent) Bharata and then the review of other sub-continents, the description of Jam- budvipa and other continents, then the description of the nether-worlds.

## \|\| 1.109.9 \|\|

*urddhvalokānukathanaṃ grahacārastataḥ param \|*  
*ādityavyūhakathanaṃ devagrahānukīrtanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The enumeration of the upper worlds, and thereafter, the movements of the planets, the narration of the Solar Array (Planetary system), the enumeration of the Divine planets.

## \|\| 1.109.10 \|\|

*nīlakaṇṭhāhvayākhyānaṃ mahādevasya vaibhavam \|*  
*amāvāsyānukathanaṃ yugatattvanirūpaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The explanation of the name Nilakantha, prowess of Mahadeva, description of the New moon day, the review of the principles of the different Yugas.

## \|\| 1.109.11 \|\|

*yajñapravartanaṃ cātha yugayorantyayoḥ kṛtiḥ \|*  
*yugaprajālakṣaṇaṃ ca ṛṣipravaravarṇanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The institution of the Yajnas, the last two Yugas and their activity, the characteristic features of the human beings etc. in different Yugas, the description of the spiritual lineage of the sages.

## \|\| 1.109.12 \|\|

*vedānāṃ vyasanākhyānaṃ svāyambhuvanirūpaṇam \|*  
*śeṣamanvantarākhyānaṃ pṛthivīdohanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The narration of the classification of the Vedas, the description of Svayambhuva Manu and the enumeration of the remaining Manvantaras and then the milking of the Earth.

## \|\| 1.109.13 \|\|

*cākṣuṣe 'dyatane sarge dvitīyo 'ṅghriḥ purodale \|*  
*athopodghātapāde tu saptarṣiparikīrtanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The first part, the second quarter ends with the current creation in the Caksusa Manvantara. Then in the Upod- ghata quarter, the glorification of the seven sages.

## \|\| 1.109.14 \|\|

*prajāpatyanvayastasmāddevādīnāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tato jayābhilāṣaśca marudutpattikīrtanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The family of Prajapati; the birth of the Devas and others therefrom; the desire for victory, the narration of the origin of the Maruts,

## \|\| 1.109.15 \|\|

*kāśyapeyānukathanaṃ ṛṣivaṃśanirūpaṇam \|*  
*pitṛkalpānukathanaṃ śrāddhakalpastataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The narration of the descendants of Kasyapa, the review of the families of the sages, the narration of the Pitr Kalpa, and thereafter, the Sraddha Kalpa (the rituals regarding the Sraddha).

## \|\| 1.109.16 \|\|

*vaivasvatasamutpattiḥ sṛṣṭistasya tataḥ param \|*  
*manuputrānvayaścānto gāndharvasya nirūpaṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The origin of Vaivasvata Manu and thereafter, the creation by him, and the family of Manu’s sons, ultimately the review of the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.109.17 \|\|

*ikṣvākuvaṃśakathanaṃ vaṃśo 'treḥ sumahātmanaḥ \|*  
*amāvasoranvayaśca rajeścaritamadbhutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The narration of the family of Iksvaku, the family of the noble-souled Atri, the family of Amavasu and the wonderful story of Raji.

## \|\| 1.109.18 \|\|

*yayāticaritaṃ cātha yaduvaṃśanirūpaṇam \|*  
*kārtavīryasya caritaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The story of Yayati, the review of the family of Yadu; the story of Karttavirya, thereafter, the story of Jamada- agni and his son.

## \|\| 1.109.19 \|\|

*vṛṣṇivaṃśānukathanaṃ sagarasyātha saṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavasyānucaritaṃ pitṛkāryavadhāśrayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The description of the family ofVrsni, the birth of Sagara, the story ofBhargava (ParaSu-Rama) subsequent to the killing of his father.

## \|\| 1.109.20 \|\|

*sagarasyātha caritaṃ bhārgavasya kathā punaḥ \|*  
*devāsurāhavakathā kṛṣṇāvirbhāvavarṇanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The story of Sagara, the story of Bhargava once again, the story of the battle between the Devas and Asuras, the description of the manifestation ofKrsna.

## \|\| 1.109.21 \|\|

*indrasya tu stavaḥ puṇyaḥ śukreṇa parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇumāhātmyakathanaṃ balivaṃśanirūpaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The meritorious hymn in praise of Indra glorified by Sukra, the narration of the greatness of Visnu and the review of the family of Bali.

## \|\| 1.109.22 \|\|

*bhaviṣyarājacaritaṃ saṃprāpte 'tha kalau yuge \|*  
*samupoddhātapādo 'yaṃ tṛtīyo madhyame dale \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The story of the future kings after the advent of the Kali age. This is the quarter of Upodghata in the middle section, the third quarter (in the Purana).

## \|\| 1.109.23 \|\|

*caturthamupasaṃhāraṃ vakṣye khaṇḍe tathottare \|*  
*vaivasvatāntarākhyānaṃ vistareṇa yathātathām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I shall recount the fourth quarter viz. Upasamhara (Conclusion) in the final section, the narration of Vaivasvata Manvantara precisely and in detail.

## \|\| 1.109.24 \|\|

*pūrvameva samuddiṣṭaṃ saṃkṣepādiha kathyate \|*  
*bhaviṣyāṇāṃ manūnāṃ ca caritaṃ hi tataḥ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. What has been mentioned before is mentioned here succinctly; thereafter; the story of the future Manus.

## \|\| 1.109.25 \|\|

*kalpapralayanirdeśaḥ kālamānaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*lokāścaturddaśa tataḥ kathitāḥ prāptalakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The specification of the Kalpas and the dissolution (then), thereafter the measurement of Time, then the fourteen worlds are mentioned along with their respective characteristics.

## \|\| 1.109.26 \|\|

*varṇanaṃ narakāṇāṃ ca vikarmācaraṇaistataḥ \|*  
*manomayapurākhyānaṃ layaḥ prākṛtikastataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The description of hells (attained) by impious activities, the narration of Manomayapura (City of Mind) and thereafter, the Prakrtika Laya (Dissolution within Prakrti).

## \|\| 1.109.27 \|\|

*śaivasyātha purasyāpi varṇanaṃ ca tataḥ param \|*  
*trividhā guṇasaṃbandhājjantūnāṃ kīrtitā gatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter, the description of Siva’s city. The threefold goal of creatures, thanks to the contact with the Gunas, is described.

## \|\| 1.109.28 \|\|

*anirdeśyāpratarkyasya brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ varṇanaṃ hi tataḥ param \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereafter, the description by means of positive and negative assertions (i. e. invariable concomitance and logical discontinuance) of the Brahman, the great Atman, that is beyond specifications and argumentation.

## \|\| 1.109.29 \|\|

*ityeṣa upasaṃhārapādo vṛttaḥ sahottaraḥ \|*  
*catuṣpādaṃ purāṇaṃ te brahmāṇḍaṃ samudāhṛtakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus the quarter section on Upasamhara has been summarised. Thus the Brahmanda Purana comprising four quarters has been described to you.

## \|\| 1.109.30-37 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśamanaupamyaṃ sārātsārataraṃ dvija \|*  
*brahmāṇḍaṃ yaccaturlakṣaṃ purāṇaṃ yena vaṭhyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tadetadasya gaditamatrāṣṭādaśadhā pṛthak \|*  
*pāsaśaryeṇa muninā sarveṣāmapi mānada \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vastutastūpadeṣṭrātha munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*mattaḥ śrutvā purāṇāni lokebhyaḥ pracakāśire \|\| 32 \|\|*

*munayo dharmaśīlāste dīnānugrahakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*mayācedaṃ purāṇaṃ tu vasiṣṭāya puroditam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tena śaktisutāyoktaṃ jātūkarṇyāya tena ca \|*  
*vyāso labdhvā tataścaitatprabhañjanamukhodgatam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*pramāṇīkṛtya loke 'sminprāvartayadanuttamam \|*  
*ya idaṃ kīrtayedvatsa śṛṇoti ca samāhitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sa vidhūyeha pāpāni yāti lokamanāmayam \|*  
*likhitvaitatpurāṇaṃ tu svarṇasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vastreṇācchāditaṃ yastu brāhmaṇāya prayacchati \|*  
*sa yādi brahmaṇo lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 37 \|\|*

30-33a. О Brahmana, this Purana called Brahmanda is the eighteenth Purana, the most essential of all chief (Puranas). What is originally composed of four hundred thousand verses has been narrated separately in eighteen books, О bestower of honour, by the sage Vyasa the son of Parasara who is the real instructor of all the sages of purified souls. Those sages who by nature practise religious virtues and bless the wretched ones, heard these Puranas from me and revealed them to the world.

33b-36a. Formerly, this Purana has been narrated by me to Vasistha; it was passed on by him to his son Sakti, by him it was recounted to Jatukarnya. Then Vyasa obtained it from the mouth of the Wind-God, making it authoritative in the world; he propagated this excellent Purana in the Public (the world). О dear one, whoever glorifies this and listens to it with great concentration, dispels all sins and attains the world devoid of ailments.

36b-37. He who writes out this Purana and gives it to a Brahmana after covering it with a cloth and placing it on a gold throne, attains the world of Brahman. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.109.38 \|\|

*marīce 'ṣṭādaśaitāni mayā proktāni yāni te \|*  
*purāṇāni tu saṃkṣepācchrotavyāni ca vistarāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О Marici, these eighteen Puranas narrated briefly by me to you should be heard in full.

## \|\| 1.109.39 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni yaḥ śṛṇoti narottamaḥ \|*  
*kathayedvā vidhānena neha bhūyaḥ sa jāyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The excellent man who listens to the eighteen Puranas or narrates them in accordance with the injunctions, is not born here again.

## \|\| 1.109.40 \|\|

*sūtrametatpurāṇānāṃ yanmayoktaṃ tavādhunā \|*  
*tannityaṃ śīlanīyaṃ hi purāṇaphalamicchatā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Sutra (summarised form) of the Puranas which has been mentioned by me to you now, should be practised everyday by one who desires the benefit out of the Puranas.

## \|\| 1.109.41 \|\|

*na dāṃbhikāya pāpāya devagurvanusūyave \|*  
*deyaṃ kadāpi sādhūnāṃ dveṣiṇe na śaṭhāya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This should not be narrated to any one who is arrogant, hypocrite, sinful, malicious to the Devas and preceptors, knavish or one who hates good men.

## \|\| 1.109.42 \|\|

*śāntāya śamacittāya śuśrūṣābhiratāya ca \|*  
*nirmatsarāya śucaye deyaṃ sadvaiṣṇavāya ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It must be imparted to one who is quiescent, of tranquil mind, interested in service, devoid of indecent rivalry, is pure and is a good devotee of Visnu,

## Chapter 110. The Exposition of Vratas to be performed on Pratipadsy the first day of the Lunar fortnight

## \|\| 1.110.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*purāṇasūtramakhilaṃ śrutaṃ tava mukhādvibho \|*  
*marūcaye yathā proktaṃ brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Narada said:

1\. О holy sir, I have heard the full gist of all the Puranas, conveyed by you directly and orally in the same manner as it was narrated to Marici by Brahma, the highest deity.

## \|\| 1.110.2 \|\|

*adhunā tu mahābhāga tithīnāṃ vai kathānakam \|*  
*kramato mahyamākhyāhi yathā syādvataniścayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О highly blessed one, now recount to me, in due order, the story of the Tithis (i. e. the details of the different lunar days) whereby the holy rites and observances can be decided upon.

## \|\| 1.110.3 \|\|

*yasminmāse tu yā puṇyā tithiryena uvāsitā \|*  
*yadvidhānaṃ ca pūjādestatsarvaṃ vada sāṃpratam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Now please narrate to me the particular holy Vrata (vow or rite) alongwith its detailed procedure of worship etc. and enlighten me on what (particular) holy lunar day (tithi) and in what (particular) month that Vrata is to be performed.1 Sanatana said:

## \|\| 1.110.4 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi tithīnāṃ te vrataṃ pṛthak \|*  
*tithīśānukramādeva sarvasiddhividhāyakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О Narada, listen I shall recount to you the holy rites (Vratas) of the Tithis separately. They bring about all the Siddhis (accomplishments of objects) in the order of the Tithis and their lords.

## \|\| 1.110.5-6 \|\|

*caitre māsi jagadbrahmā sasaja prathame 'hani \|*  
*śuklapakṣe samagraṃ vai tadā sūryodaye sati \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vatsarādau vasaṃtādau balirājye tathaiva ca \|*  
*pūrvaviddhaiva kartavyā pratipatsarvadā budhaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. God Brahma created the entire Universe on the first day in the bright half of Chaitra, at the time of sunrise.2 It was in the beginning of the year and that of the spring in the kingdom of Bali (?). The Pratipad is to be taken always when it is in conjunction with the previous Tithi, by wise persons.1

## \|\| 1.110.7 \|\|

*tatra kāryā mahāśāntiḥ sarvakalmaṣanāśinī \|*  
*sarvotpātapraśamanī kaliduṣkṛtahāriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At that time, the great rite of Santi (the pacificatory rite) should be performed. It is destructive of all sins. It jubdues all evil portents. It dispels the sins of Kali.

## \|\| 1.110.8 \|\|

*āyuḥ pradāpuṣṭikarī dhanasaubhāgyavarddhinī \|*  
*maṅgalyā ca pavitrā ca lokadvayamukhāvahā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It bestows longevity, causes nourishment and enhances wealth and good fortune. It is auspicious and holy and is conducive to happiness in both the worlds.

## \|\| 1.110.9-10 \|\|

*tasyāmādau tu saṃpūjyo brahmā vahnivapurdharaḥ \|*  
*pādyārdhyapuṣpadhūpaiśca vastrālaṅkārabhojanaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*homairbalyupahāraiśca tathā brāhmaṇatarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ krameṇa devebhyaḥ pūjā kāryā pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. On that day, at the outset, god Brahma who had assumed the physical body of the fire-god, should be worshipped with respectful formalities such as washing the feet with water and other respectful offerings (Padyas Arghyas), flowers, incense, clothes, ornaments, meals, sacrificial oblations, presents and the propitiation of the Brahmanas. Thereafter, the worship of deities should be performed separately of each god.

## \|\| 1.110.11-12 \|\|

*kṛtvoṅkāra namaskāraṃ kuśodakatilākṣataiḥ \|*  
*savastraṃ sahiraṇyaṃ ca tato dadyāddijātaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāṃ vedaviduṣe vratasaṃpūrtihetave \|*  
*evaṃ pūjāviśeṣeṇa vrataṃ syātsaurisaṃjñakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. After paying obeisance to the Omkara with (the offerings of) water from the Kusa grass, gingelly-seeds and raw rice-grains, (the devotee) shall give religious fee or gift (Daksina) to a Brahmana who is a Vedic Scholar, alongwith clothes and gold for the purpose of complete and perfect performance of the Vrata. This Vrata that has such a special Puja in it, is called Sauri Vrata2 (Vrata pertaining to the Sun).

## \|\| 1.110.13-16 \|\|

*ārogyadaṃ nṛṇāṃ vipra tasminneva dine mune \|*  
*vidyāvratamapi proktamasyāmeva tithau mune \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tilakaṃ nāma ca proktaṃ kṛṣṇenājātaśatrave \|*  
*atha jyeṣṭhe site pakṣe pakṣatyāṃ divasodaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

*devodyānabhavaṃ hṛdyaṃ karavīraṃ samarcayet \|*  
*raktatanturīdhānaṃ gandhadhūpavilepanaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prarūḍhasaptadhānyaiśca nāragairbījapūrakaiḥ \|*  
*abhyukṣyākṣatatoyena mantreṇetthaṃ kṣamāpayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-14a. О Brahmana, this holy rite yields good health to men. О sage, Vidyavrata3 is also to be performed on that day. О sage, on the same Tithi, the holy rite called Tilaka4 was told by Krsna to Ajatasatru (Yudhisthira).

14b-16. In the month of Jyestha, in the bright half, on the first day at sunrise, one should worship the pleasing Karavira tree that grows in the temple garden.1 It must be tied with a red thread, scents, incense and unguents must be offered along- with the germinating seven grains, oranges and pomegranates. It must be sprinkled with water mixed with unbtoken rice grain. The following Mantra should be uttered for praying for forgiveness.

## \|\| 1.110.17-20 \|\|

*karavīra vṛṣāvāsa namaste bhānuvallabha \|*  
*daṃbholimṛḍadurgādidevānāṃ satataṃ priya \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ākṛṣṇeneti vedoktamantreṇetthaṃ kṣamāpayet \|*  
*evaṃ bhaktyā samabhyacya dattvā viprāya dakṣiṇām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kuryātpaścātsvabhavanaṃ vrajet \|*  
*nabhaḥ śukle pratipadi lakṣmībuddhipradāyakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ nidānaṃ paramaṃ vratam \|*  
*somavāraṃ samārabhya sārdhamāsatrayaṃ dvija \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-19a. “Obeisance to you О Karavira, the residence of meritorious acts, beloved of the sun, always liked by (one who wields thunderbolt Dambholi) i.e. Indra, Mrcja, (Siva), Durga and other deities.” He should then crave forgiveness through the Vedic Mantra2 “AKrsnena” etc. (RV. I. 35.2). After worshipping thus with great devotion and after giving due Daksina to a Brahmana, he should circumambulate and go to his house.

19b-20. On the first day in the bright half of the month of Sravana, there is a great Vrata3 that yields good fortune and intellect. It is the cause of all the Purusarthas) viz. virtue, wealth, love and liberation. О Brahmana, beginning on a Monday, this Vrata should be continued for three and a half months.

## \|\| 1.110.21-22 \|\|

*kārtikāsitabhūtāyāmupoṣyaṃ vratatatparaḥ \|*  
*pūrṇāyāṃ śivamabhyarcya suvaṇa vaṃśasaṃyutam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vāyanaṃ sumahatpuṇyaṃ devatāprītivardhakam \|*  
*dadyādviprāya saṃkalpya dhanavṛddhyai munīśvara \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. After observing fast on the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Karttika, the devotee, earnest and interested in the Vrata, should worship Siva on (the following) full moon day. On the Pratipad following it He should offer Vayana (sweet-meats and other presents) alongwith a gold flute (?) to a Brahmana for the purpose of increase in the wealth. О leading sage, it is highly meritorious and it increases the pleasure of the deities.

## \|\| 1.110.23 \|\|

*bhādraśuklapratipadi vrataṃ nāmnā mahattamam \|*  
*vrataṃ maunāhvayaṃ kecitprāhuratra śivor'cyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the first day in the bright half of Bhadrapada, the Vrata named ‘Mahatma’ (the greatest one) should be performed. Some call this Vrata by the name of Mauna1 (silence). Siva is worshipped in this rite.

## \|\| 1.110.24-29 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ tu pacenmaunī ṣoḍaśatriguṇāni ca \|*  
*phalāni piṣṭapakvāni dadyādviprāya ṣoḍaśa \|\| 24 \|\|*

*devāya ṣoḍaśānyāni bhujyante ṣoḍaśātmanā \|*  
*sauvarṇaṃ śivamabhyarcya kumbhopari vidhānavit \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ dhenusahitamācāryyāya pradāpayet \|*  
*idaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra deva devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*caturdaśābdaṃ dehāntaṃ bhuktabhogaḥ śivaṃ vrajet \|*  
*āśvine sitapakṣatyāṃ katvāśokavrataṃ naraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*aśoko jāyate vipradhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*aśokapūjanaṃ tatra kāryaṃ niyamatatparaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vratānte dvādaśe varṣe mūrtiṃ cāśokaśākhinaḥ \|*  
*samarpya gurave bhaktyā śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-27a. The devotee shall, in silence, cook three times sixteen fruits alongwith ground flour. He shall give one set of sixteen to a Brahmana. He shall give another set of sixteen to the Deity. One set of sixteen, he himself eats. Over the water pot, the knower of the injunctions worships a gold image of Siva and gives everything of it to the preceptor alongwith a cow. О Brahmana, after observing this Vrata of the trident-bearing Lord of the Devas forfourteen years, the devotee enjoys worldly pleasures, till his death (thereafter) 9 he attains to Siva.

27b-29. О Brahmana, a man who performs Afokavrata on the first day in the bright half of the month of Asvina, (himself) becomes Asoka (free from grief). He is endowed with riches and grains. The Asoka tree must be worshipped by those who are exclusively devoted to these observances and rites. At the end of the Vrata in the twelfth year, he should offer the replica of an Ashoka tree with great devotion to the preceptor. He is thereby honoured in Sivaloka.

## \|\| 1.110.30 \|\|

*asyāmeva pratipadi navarātraṃ samārabhet \|*  
*pūrvāhne pūjayeddevīṃ ghaṭasthāpanapūrvakam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One shall begin Navaratra 3 (the festival of nine nights) on this very Pratipad. He should worship the goddess in the forenoon alongwith the rite of installing the water-pot.

## \|\| 1.110.31 \|\|

*aṅkurāropaṇaṃ kṛtvā yavairgodhūmamiśritaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pratidinaṃ kuryādekabhuktamayācitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He should sow to germinate barley grains mixed with wheat. He should take only one meal once a day. The food consumed should not be one that is requested for.

## \|\| 1.110.32-33 \|\|

*upavāsaṃ yathāśakti pūjāpāṭhajapādikam \|*  
*mārkaṃṇḍeya purāṇoktaṃ caritatritayaṃ dvija \|\| 32 \|\|*

*paṭhanīyaṃ navadinaṃ bhuktimuktī abhīpsatā \|*  
*kumārīpūjanaṃ tatra praśastaṃ bhojanādibhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In accordance with his ability, he should observe fast. The worship of the goddess, repetition of the Mantras and recitation of the holy texts (the Saptashati) should also be done in accordance with one's capacity. О Brahmana, the three Caritas (stories) mentioned in the Магкавдкуа Purana should be read for all the nine days, by one who desires to get worldly pleasures and salvation. The worship of virgins alongwith the rite of feeding, is praised.

## \|\| 1.110.34 \|\|

*itthaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra sarvasiddhyālayo naraḥ \|*  
*jāyate bhuvi durgāyāḥ prasādānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О Brahmana, after performing the Vrata thus, the man becomes a receptacle of all Siddhis on the Earth, by the grace ofDurga.

## \|\| 1.110.35 \|\|

*athorjasitapakṣatyāṃ navarātroditaṃ caret \|*  
*viśeṣādannakūṭākhyaṃ viṣṇuprītivivardhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On the first day in the bright half in the month of Urja (Karttika), one should perform all the rites mentioned for Navaratra. Particularly, the rite called Annakuta1 (a heap of cooked articles of food) causes the increase in the delight of Visnu.
