## \|\| 1.110.36 \|\|

*sarvapākaiḥ sardadohaiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvārthasiddhaye \|*  
*kartavyamannakūṭaṃ tu govarddhanasamarcane \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In the course of worship of Govardhana, Annakuta must be made with all cooked articles and with all milk products by everyone, for achieving all objects by the worshipper.

## \|\| 1.110.37 \|\|

*sāyaṃ gobhiḥ saha śrīmadgovarddhanadharādharam \|*  
*samarcya dakṣiṇīkṛtya bhuktimuktī samāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the evening the devotee should worship Govardhana mountain alongwith the cows, and offer suitable Daksina. He shall attain worldly pleasures and liberation.

## \|\| 1.110.38-46 \|\|

*atha mārgasitādyāyāṃ dhanavratamanuttamam \|*  
*naktaṃ viṣṇvarcanaṃ homaiḥ sauvarṇīṃ hutabhuktanum \|\| 38 \|\|*

*raktavastrayugācchannāṃ dvijāya pratipādayet \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā dhanairdhānyaiḥ samṛddho jāyate bhuvi \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vahninā dagdhapāpastu viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|*  
*pauṣaśuklapratipadi bhānumabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ekabhaktavrato martyo bhānulokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*māghaśuklādyadivase vahniṃ sākṣānmaheśvaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

*samabhyacya vidhānena samṛddho jāyate bhuvi \|*  
*atha phaālgunaśuklādau devadevaṃ digaṃbaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dhūlidhūsarasarvāṅgaṃ jalairukṣetsamantataḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā laukikenāpi saṃtuṣṭo hi maheśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*svasāyujyaṃ pradiśati bhaktyā samyaksamarcitaḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhe tu sitādyāyāṃ viṣṇuṃ viśvavihāriṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya vidhānena viprānsaṃbhojayedvatī \|*  
*evaṃ śucisitādyāyāṃ brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ gurum \|\| 45 \|\|*

*viṣṇunā sahito brahmā sarvalokeśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*svasāyujyaṃ pradiśati sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

38-40a. The excellent Dhanavrata is to be performed on the first day in the bright half of the month of Margasirsha. Visnu is to be worshipped at night alongwith Homas. The observer of the Vrata should give a replica in gold of the fire- god to a Brahmana after covering it with two red clothes. By performing this vrata thus, one becomes flourishing in wealth and food-grains on the Earth. With his sins burned in fire, he is honoured in the Visnuloka.

40b-41a. On the first day in the bright half of the month of Pausa, one should worship the Sun-god with devotion. The man must restrict his diet to one meal a day. Performing the Vrata thus, that mortal being shall attain the world of the Sun.

41b-42a. On the first day in the bright half of the month of Magha, one shall worship the Fire god as Mahegvara himself, in accordance with the injunctions. He becomes rich and flourishing on the Earth.

42b-44a. On the first day in the bright half of the month of Phalguna, one should, with water, sprinkle Digambara (the naked Lord Siva), the Lord of the Devas, all of whose limbs have turned grey due to dust. He should sprinkle the water all over his body. Indeed, god Mahesvara is delighted even with such secular rites and activities. On being worshipped with devotion, he grants his own Sayujya (Salvation wherein the devotee becomes one with the Deity).

44b-46. On the first day in the bright half of the month of Vaigakha, one shall worship Visnu who sports in the Universe. He should worship in accordance with the injunctions. The man who observes the Vrata should feed the Brahmanas. Similarly, on the first day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha and Asa

## \|\| 1.110.47-48 \|\|

*āsu dvādaśamāsānāṃ pratipatsu dvijottama \|*  
*vratāni tubhyaṃ proktāni bhuktimuktipradāni ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vrateṣveteṣu sarveṣu brahmacaryaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*bhojane tu haviṣyānnaṃ sāmānyata udāhṛtam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. О excellent Brahmana, Vratas to be observed on the first day of the twelve months — Vratas bestowing worldly pleasures here and Liberation from Samsara hereafter have been recounted to you. Brahmacarya (observance of celibacy) is laid down in all these Vratas. The diet during these Vratas is prescribed as Havisyanna (cooked rice soaked in ghee) as common to all.

## Chapter 111. Exposition of Vratas to be observed on Dvitiyas (second Tithi in lunar fortnight)

## \|\| 1.111.1 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi dvitīyāyā vratāni te \|*  
*yāni kṛtvā naro bhaktyā brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatana said:

1\. О Brahmana, listen. I shall recount to you the Vratas of Dvitlyas (to be observed on the second day of the lunar fortnight). On observing them with devotion, a man is honoured in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.111.2-6 \|\|

*caitraśukladvitīyāyāṃ brahmaṇaṃ ca saśaktikam \|*  
*haviṣyānnena gandhādyaiḥ stoṣya sarvakratūdbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*phalaṃ labdhvākhilānkāmānante brahmapadaṃ labhet \|*  
*asminneva dine vipra bālendumuditaṃ pare \|\| 3 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya niśāraṃbhe bhuktimuktiphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*atha vāsmindine bhaktyā dasrāvabhyarcya yatnataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*suvarṇarajate netre pradadyācca dvijātaye \|*  
*pūrṇayātrāvrate hyasmindadhnā vāpi ghṛtena ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*netravrataṃ dvādaśa vatsarānvai kṛtyā bhavedbhūmipatirdvijendra \|*  
*surūparūpo 'rigaṇapratāpī dharmābhirāmo nṛpavargamukhyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-3a. On the second day in the bright half of the month of Chaitra, the devotee should propitiate Brahma alongwith his Sakti. He should eulogise the deity and propitiate him with Havisyanna (cooked rice soaked in ghee), scents and other things. He shall thus attain the benefit of all sacrifices. After realising all desires, he shall attain the region of the supreme spirit in the end.

3b-4a. О Brahmana, on this very day, others worship the rising crescent moon at the beginning of the night. They attain worldly pleasures and liberation.

4b-6. Or on this day, one shall devotedly worship the twin gods, ASvins and offer gold and silver eyes to a Brahmana covering them with a pot filled with curd or ghee? О leading Brahmana, by performing this Netravrata1 for twelve years one becomes verily a king. He attains a comely form. He becomes valorous against the hosts of his enemies. He becomes interested in Dharma, and the chief of all kings.

## \|\| 1.111.7-9 \|\|

*rādhaśukladvitīyāyāṃ brahmaṇaṃ viṣṇurūpiṇam \|*  
*samarcya saptadhānyānyāḍhyakuṃbhopari vidhānataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*viṣṇulokamavāpnoti bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaśukladvitīyāyāṃ bhāskaraṃ bhuvanādhipam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*catuvaktrasvarūpaṃ ca samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*bhojayitvā dvijān bhaktyā bhāskaraṃ lokamāpnuyāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-8a. On the second day in the bright half of the month of Radha (Vaiakha), one shall worship Brahma in the form of Visnu in accordance with the injunction, over a pitcher containing seven kinds of grains. After enjoying all desirable worldly pleasures here one attains Visnuloka thereby.

8b-9. On the second day in the bright half of the month ofJye?tha, one should worship the Sun-god, Lord of the worlds who has assumed the form of the ibur-faced Lord, in accordance with the injunctions. After feeding the Brahmanas with devotion, he shall attain the world of Sun-God.

## \|\| 1.111.10-12 \|\|

*āṣāḍhasya site pakṣe dvitīyā puṇyasaṃyutā \|*  
*tasyāṃ rathaṃ samāropya rāmaṃ saha subhadrayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dvijādibhirvratī sārdhaṃ parikramya purādikam \|*  
*jalāśayāntikaṃ gatvā kārayecca mahotsavam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tadante devabhavane niveśya ca yathāvidhi \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayeccaiva vratasyāsya prapūrtaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The second day in the bright half of the month of Asadha is very meritorious. On that day, the observer of the Vrata takes Balarama in procession alongwith Subhadra. He goes round the various parts of the city, alongwith Brahmanas and others. After going near a tank or a river, he should celebrate the great festival. At the end of it, he should re-instate them duly in the Lord’s abode. He should feed Brahmanas for completing the holy rite.

## \|\| 1.111.13 \|\|

*nabhaḥ śukladvitīyāyāṃ viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*svapitīti tithiḥ puṇyā hyaśokaśayanāhvayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Prajapati or the creator of the universe sleeps on the second day in the bright half of the month of Nabhas (Sravana) That tithi is therefore very sacred. It is called Ashokashayana.x

## \|\| 1.111.14-21 \|\|

*saśaktika tu śayyāsthaṃ pūjayitvā caturmukham \|*  
*imamuccārayenmantraṃ praṇamya jagatāṃ patim \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkānta śrīvāsa śrīpate prabho \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmada \|\| 15 \|\|*

*candrārddhadānamatroktaṃ sarvasiddhividhāyakam \|*  
*bhādraśukladvitīyāyāṃ śakrarūpaṃ jagadvidhim \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā vidhānenana sarvakratuphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*āśvine māsi vai puṇyā dvitīyā śuklapakṣagā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dānaṃ pradattametasyāmanantaphalamucyate \|*  
*ūrjjaśukladvitīyāyāṃ yamo yamunayā purā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhojitaḥ svagṛhe tena dvitīyaiṣā yamāhvayā \|*  
*puṣṭipravarddhanaṃ cātra bhaginyā bhojanaṃ gṛhe \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vastrālaṅkārapūrvaṃ tu tasmai deyamataḥ param \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yasyāṃ tithau yamunayā yamarājadevaḥ saṃbhojito nijakarātsvasṛsauhṛdena \|*  
*tasyāṃ svasuḥ karatalādiha yo bhunakti prāpnoti ratnadhanadhānyamanuttamaṃ saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

14- 16a. One should worship the four-faced deity lying in the bd alongwith his Sakti. After bowing down to the Lord of the worlds, one shall utter this Mantra: “O Srikanta (lover of Sri) О Srivatsadharin (one who bears the Srivatsa mark), Srivasa (abode of good fortune), О Sripati (Lord of Sri), О Dharmartha-Kamada (the bestowerof virtue, wealth, and love) may not my wedded life perish.” Here the charitable gift of a crescent made of gold is recommended. It brings about all Siddhis.

16b-17a. On the second day in the bright half of the month of Bhadrapada, one should worship the creator of the universe in the form of Indra in accordance with the prescribed injunctions. He shall obtain the fruit of the performance of all sacrifices.

17b-21. The second day in the bright half of the month Alvina is very holy. The charitable gift made on this day is said to yield endless benefits. Formerly, Yama was fed by Yamuna in her house on the second day in the bright half of Karttika. Hence, this is called Yamadvitlya.1 If one takes food in the house of one’s sister on this day, it is conducive to nourishment. He must give her clothes and ornaments. It is the tithi on which Lord Yamaraja was fed by Yamuna with her own hand, out of sisterly affection. Hence, he who takes his food from the hand of his sister on that day, attains excellent jewels, wealth and food-grains.

## \|\| 1.111.22 \|\|

*mārgaśukladvitīyāyāṃ śrāddhena pitṛpūjanam \|*  
*ārogyaṃ labhate cāpi putrapautrasamanvayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pitrs should be worshipped through Sraddha on the second day in the bright half of the month of Margashlrsa. Then the devotee obtains good health alongwith his sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 1.111.23-24 \|\|

*pauṣaśukladvitīyāyāṃ gośṛṅgodakamārjanam \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ nṝṇāmāste bālendudarśanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yor'ghyadānena bālenduṃ haviṣyāśī jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*pūjayetsājyasumanedharmakāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On the second day in the bright half of the month of Pausa, the rite of sprinkling with the water a cow’s horns, is the bestower of all desires unto men. The sight of the rising moon is also conducive to the attainment of all desires. For the purpose of achieving virtue, love and wealth, the devotee should restrict his diet to cooked rice soaked in ghee and subdue his sense-organs and worship the rising moon by offering Arghya and flowers alongwith ghee.

## \|\| 1.111.25-31 \|\|

*māghaśukladvitīyāyāṃ bhānurūpaṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*samabhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ pūjayedraktapuṣpakaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*raktairgaṃvaistathā svarṇamūrtiṃ nirmāya śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pūrṇaṃ tāmrapātraṃ gāghṛmairvāpitaṇḍulaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*samarpya deve bhaktyaiva sa mūrtiṃ pradadeddvije \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte vrate vipra sākṣātsūrya ivoditaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*durāsado durādharṣo jāyate bhuvimānavaḥ \|*  
*iha kāmānvarāmbhuktvā yātyante brahmaṇaḥ padam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvadevastuto 'bhīkṣṇaṃ vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*atha phaālgunaśuklāyā dvitīyāyāṃ dvijottamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*puṣpaiḥ śivaṃ samabhyarcya suśvetaiśca sugandhibhaḥ \|*  
*puṣpairvitānakaṃ kṛtvā puṣpālaṅkaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*naivedyairvividhairdhūpairdīparnīrājanādibhiḥ \|*  
*prasādya praṇameccaiva sāṣṭāṅgaṃ patito bhuvi \|\| 31 \|\|*

25-29a. On the second day in the bright half of the month of Magha, one shall duly worship Prajapati in the form of Sun, with red flowers and red unguents. He shall make an image of the deity in gold, according to his capacity. He should take a copper vessel full of wheat or rice grains. He should dedicate all these things to the Lord and offer the same to aBrahmana. If this Vratais thus performed, the devotee shall be like the rising sun. The man will be unapproachable and unthwartable in the world. After enjoying all excellent worldly pleasures here, he attains Brahma’s region in the end. He will be seated in an excellent aerial chariot, eulogised frequently by the Devas.

29b-31. An excellent Brahmana should worship Siva with white and fragrant flowers on the second day in the bright half of the month of Phalguna. He should make a canopy and decorate it with flowers and ornamental fittings. He should propitiate the Lord with Naivedyas of various kinds. He should offer incense and lights. He should perform Nlrajana rite (waving of lights). Prostrating on the ground with eight limbs touching it, he shall make obeisance to the Lord.

## \|\| 1.111.32 \|\|

*evamabhyarcya deveśaṃ martyo vyādhivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*dhanadhānyasamāyukto jīvedvirṣaśataṃ dhruvam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Worshipping the Lord of the Devas thus, the man becomes free from all sickness. With plenty of wealth and food-grains, he shall certainly live for a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.111.33 \|\|

*yadvidhānaṃ dvitīyāsu śuklapakṣagatāsu vā \|*  
*proktaṃ tadeva kṛṣṇāsu karttavyaṃ vidhikovidaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The injunctions regarding the Dvitlyas of the bright half of the month should be followed in the case of those of the dark half of the month also, by the people clever in the matter of procedures.

## \|\| 1.111.34 \|\|

*vahnireva pṛthaṅmāḥsu nānārūpavapurddharaḥ \|*  
*pūjyate hi dvitīyāsu brahmacaryyādi pūrvavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It is the fire-god alone that is worshipped separately in the different months. He assumes different forms and so is worshipped on the Dvitlyas. The vow of celibacy etc. are to be observed as before.

## Chapter 112. Enumeration of Vratas to be observed on Trtiyds (third day of a lunar fortnight

## \|\| 1.112.1 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi tṛtīyāyā vratāni te \|*  
*yāni samyagvidhāyāśu nārī saubhāgyamāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatana said:

1\. О Narada, listen. I shall recount to you the Vratas pertaining to Tftiya (third day in the lunar fort-night). On observing these Vratas perfectly, a woman shall attain married bliss and good fortune.

## \|\| 1.112.2-5 \|\|

*caitraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ gaurīṃ kṛtvā sabhartṛkām \|*  
*sauvarṇā rājatīṃ vāpi tāmnīṃ vā mṛṇyayīṃ dvija \|\| 2 \|\|*

*abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyairvastrairābharaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*dūrvākāṇḍaiśca vidhivatsopavāsā tu kanyakā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*varārthinī ca saubhāgyaputrabhartrarthinī tathā \|*  
*dvijabhāryā bhartṛmatīḥ kanyakāṃ vā sulakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*siṃdūrāñjanavastrādyaiḥ pratoṣya prītamānasā \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādvratasaṃpūrtikāmyayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. An unmarried virgin desirous of a bridegroom, and one desirous of matrimonial bliss and good fortune for her sons and husband, should perform Gauri Vrata.1 The image of Gauri is made of gold, silver, copper or clay along with that of her Lord (Siva) on the third day in the bright half of the month of Chaitra. О Brahmana, she then worships it with scents, fragrant flowers, clothes, auspicious ornaments, and bundles of Diirva grass. She observes fast. She propitiates Brahmaira women whose husbands and sons are alive and girls with auspicious characteristics, by offering them saffron, collyrium, clothes and other things. Delighted ip her mind, she should keep awake that night with the desire to fulfil the Vrata.

## \|\| 1.112.6 \|\|

*tatastāṃ pratimāṃ vipra gurave pratipādayet \|*  
*dhātujāṃ mṛnmayīṃ vā tu nikṣipecca jalāśaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О Brahmana, she should give that image to the preceptor if it is metallic. If it is made of clay, she should immerse it in a tank or a river.

## \|\| 1.112.7 \|\|

*evaṃ dvādaśavarṣāṇi kṛtvā gaurīvrataṃ śubham \|*  
*dhenudvādaśasaṃkalpaṃ dadyādutsargasiddhaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She should perform this auspicious Gauri Vrata for twelve years. With the due formal resolve to donate, she should offer twelve cows also for the achievement of her desires.

## \|\| 1.112.8 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena gaurī saubhāgyadāyinī \|*  
*strīṇāṃ yathā tathā nānyā vidyate bhuvanatraye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. What more needs be spoken? There is no other bes- tower of good fortune and matrimonial bliss to women in all the three worlds like Gauri.

## \|\| 1.112.9 \|\|

*dhanaṃ putrānpatiṃ vidyāmājñāsiddhiṃ yaśaḥ sukham \|*  
*labhate sarvameveṣṭaṃ gaurīmabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A woman attains wealth, good husband, sons, learning, ability to command, fame and happiness — in fact all desired happiness, by worshipping Gauri with devotion.

## \|\| 1.112.10 \|\|

*rādhaśuklatṛtīyā yā sākṣayā parikīrtitā \|*  
*tithistrotāyugādyā sā kṛtasyākṣayakāriṇī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The third day in the bright half of the month of Vaisakha is glorified as Akshaya Trtlya.1 That is the Tithi on which Tretayuga began. Whatever holy rite is performed on this day is made everlasting (Aksaya) by this Trtlya.

## \|\| 1.112.11-13 \|\|

*dve śukle dve tathā kṛṣṇe yugādī kavayo viduḥ \|*  
*śukle pūrvāhnike grāhye kṛṣṇe caiva tapastatha \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvāparaṃ hi kalirbhādre pravṛttāni yugāni vai \|*  
*tatra rādhatṛtīyāyāṃ śrīsametaṃ jagadgurum \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇaṃ samabhyarcetpuṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*yadvā gaṅgāṃbhasi snāto mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-12a. Wise men know that two inaugural days of Yugas (viz. that of Krta and Treta) were in the bright half of the month, while those of the other two Yugas (viz. Dvapara and Kali) were in the dark fortnight (of the lunar month). The two (inaugural) days in the bright fortnight are to be accepted (observed) in the earlier half of the day. Out of the Yugadi days in the dark fortnight, Dvapara began in Magha while the Kali Age commenced in Bhadrapada. Thus commenced the Yugas on these days.

12b-13. The devotee should worship Narayana, the preceptor of the universe accompanied by Sri, with flowers, incense and unguents on the third day in the bright half of the month of Vaisakha. Or if he takes his holy dip in the waters of the Ganga, he is absolved of all sins.

## \|\| 1.112.14 \|\|

*akṣatnaiḥ pūjayedviṣṇuṃ snāyādapyakṣatairnaraḥ \|*  
*saktūnsaṃbhojayedviprānsvayamabhyavaharecca tān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He should worship Visnu with unbroken rice-grains. He shall have his ablution with water mixed with unbroken rice grains. He should feed Brahmanas with the flour of barley first fried and then ground. He himself shall partake of it.

## \|\| 1.112.15 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtavidhirvipra naro viṣṇuparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇulokamavāpnoti sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmana, the man who performs the rites thus and who is devoted to Visnu attains Visnu’s world. He is bowed to by all the Devas.

## \|\| 1.112.16 \|\|

*atha jyeṣṭhatṛtīyā tu śuklā raṃbheti nāmataḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ sabhāryaṃ vidhivatpūjayedvāhmaṇottamam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The third day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha is well known by the name Rambha.1 On that day, one should duly worship and honour an excellent Brahmana accompanied by his wife.

## \|\| 1.112.17-21 \|\|

*gandhapuṣpāṃśukādyaistu nārī saubhāgyakāmyayā \|*  
*raṃbhāvratamidaṃ vipra vidhivatsamupāśritam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dadāti vittaṃ putrāṃśca matiṃ dharme śubhāvahām \|*  
*athāṣāḍhatṛtīyāyāṃ śuklāyāṃ śuklavāsasā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*keśavaṃ tu salakṣmīkaṃ sastrīke tu dvijer'cayet \|*  
*bhojanaiḥ surabhīdānairvastraiścāpi vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*priyervākyairbhṛśaṃ prītā nārī saubhāgyavāñchayā \|*  
*samupāsya vrataṃ caitaddhanadhānyasamanvitā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*devadevaprasādena viṣṇulokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*nabhaḥ śuklatṛtīyāyāṃ svarṇagaurīvrataṃ caret \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-18a. With the desire for conjugal blessedness a woman should perform this holy rite and worship the Brahmana couple with scents, fragrant flowers, silken garments, etc. О Brahmana, if this holy Rambha rite is duly observed, it yields wealth, sons, and auspicious inclination towards Dharma (virtuous and religious rites).

18b-21a. The lady who desires conjugal bliss should wear white clothes in the third day in the bright half of the month of Ashatfha and worship Kesava accompanied by Laksmi symbolised or represented in a Brahmana accompanied by his wife. She should propitiate them with meals, charitable gifts of cows, clothes and ornaments and pleasing words. By observing this Vrata, the lady shall be blessed with wealth and food-grains. By the grace of the Lord of the Devas, she shall attain Visnu’s world.

21b. Svarna-Gauri Vrata is to be performed on the third day in the bright half of the month of Sravana.

## \|\| 1.112.22 \|\|

*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirbhavānīmabhipūjayet \|*  
*putrāndehi dhanaṃ dehi saubhāgyaṃ dehi suvrate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22а-23а. The lady devotee should worship goddess Bhavani by means of the sixteen Upacaras (articles and modes of worship and service) with the Prayer — “O goddess of holy rites, obeisance be to you. Be pleased to grant me sons and wealth, grant me conjugal blessedness. Do bestow on me all other desired things.”

## \|\| 1.112.23-28 \|\|

*anyāṃśca sarvakāmānme dehi dehi namo 'stu te \|*  
*evaṃ saṃprārthya deveśīṃ bhavānīṃ bhavasaṃyutām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vratasaṃpūrtikāmā tu vāyanaṃ dāpayettathā \|*  
*evaṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāṇi kṛtvā nārī vrataṃ śubham \|\| 24 \|\|*

*udyāpanaṃ caredbhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitā \|*  
*maṇḍape maṇḍale śuddhe gaṇeśādisurārcanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tāmramayaṃ pātraṃ kalaśoparivinyaset \|*  
*sauvarṇīṃ pratimāṃ tatra bhavānyāḥ pratipūjayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ samyak tato homaṃ samācaret \|*  
*veṇupātraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pakvānnaparipūritaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*samarpya devyai naivedyaṃ dvijeṣvetannivedayet \|*  
*vāyanaṃ ca tataḥ paścāddadyātsaṃbandhibandhuṣu \|\| 28 \|\|*

23b-24a. After praying thus to Bhavani the goddess of the Devas, accompanied by God Siva, the lady devotee, desirous of completion of the holy rite should make the gift of sweet meats etc. to Brahmanas.

24b-25a. After performing this auspicious Vrata for sixteen years, she should perform the concluding ceremony of the Vrata (Udyapana) with great devotion. She should not exhibit stinginess in the matter of expenses.

25b-28. In a pandal in a pure Mandala (mystic diagram) she should perform the worship of GaneSa and other gods. She should then place a flat saucer-like copper-dish over the water pot and worship a gold-image of Bhavani therein with scents and fragrant flowers. Thereafter, the Ноmа should be performed. Sixteen bamboo vessels (baskets) shall be filled with sweet dishes and cooked rice, offered to the Devi as Naivedya and distributed among Brahmanas, kinsmen and relatives.

## \|\| 1.112.29 \|\|

*pratimāṃ gurave dattvā dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ tathā \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ labhetphalaṃ nārī vratācaraṇatatparā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The woman interested in the observance of this Vrata shall attain the full benefit by giving the gold image to the preceptor and monetary gifts to the other Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.112.30 \|\|

*bhādraśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ vrataṃ vai hāritālakam \|*  
*kuryādbhaktyā vidhānena pādyārdhyārcana pūrvakam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On the third day in the bright half of the month of Bhadrapada, the lady devotee should perform the Vrata of Haritalika1 with great devotion, in accordance with the injunctions, alongwith the rites of Padya (viz. offering water for washing the feet, hands, worship) Arghya and Arcana.

## \|\| 1.112.31-32 \|\|

*tatastu kāñcane pātre rājate cāpi tāmrake \|*  
*vaiṇave mṛnmaye vāpi vinyasyānnaṃ sadakṣiṇam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*saphalaṃ ca savastraṃ ca dvijāya pratipādayet \|*  
*tadante pāraṇaṃ kuryādiṣṭabandhujanaiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Then the cooked rice and the Daksina should be placed in a gold, silver, copper, bamboo or a clay vessal alongwith fruits and clothes. The same shall then be given to a Brahmana. At the end of it, she should have the Parana (break the fast) alongwith the kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.112.33 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtavratā nārī bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa gaurīsahacarībhavet \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The woman who observes this holy rite shall enjoy all desirable pleasures. She shall become a friend and attendant of Gauri, thanks to the efficacy of this Vrata.

## \|\| 1.112.34 \|\|

*saubhāgyadravyavastrāṇi vaṃśapātrāṇi ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*dātavyāni prayatnena brāhmaṇebhyo yathāvidhi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Sixteen bamboo-baskets filled with bliss-yielding articles and clothes should be enthusiastically given to a Brahmana in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.112.35-36 \|\|

*anyebhyo vipravaryebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ ca prayatnataḥ \|*  
*bhūyasīṃ ca tato dadyādviprebhyo devituṣṭaye \|\| 35 \|\|*

*evaṃ yā kurute nārī vrataṃ saubhāgyavarddhanam \|*  
*sā tu devīprasādena saubhāgyaṃ labhate dhruvam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. She should then give generous monetary gifts to the other excellent Brahmanas also for the satisfaction of the goddess. The woman who performs this holy rite of Saubhagya Vardhana (that which increases conjugal blessedness) certainly attains it, thanks to the grace of the Goddess.

## \|\| 1.112.37-38 \|\|

*yadā tṛtīyā bhādre tu hastarkṣasahitā bhavet \|*  
*hastagaurīvrataṃ nāma taduddiṣṭaṃ hi śauriṇā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tathā koṭīśvarī nāma vrataṃ proktaṃ pinākinā \|*  
*lakṣeśvarī caiva tathā tadvidhānamudīryate \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. When the Trtiya in the month of Bhadrapada coincides with the constellation Hasta, the Vrata taught by Sauri (Kfsna?) is called Hastagaurivrata1. The Vrata called Kofisvari and LakseSvari2 has been proclaimed by Siva the Pinakabearing Lord. Its rules of procedure are being mentioned:

## \|\| 1.112.39 \|\|

*asyāṃ vrataṃ tu saṃgrāhyaṃ yāvadvarṣacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*upavāsena kartavyaṃ varṣe varṣe tu nārada \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On this day, the Vrata has to be taken up for four years. О Narada, every year it has to be performed alongwith the observance of fast.

## \|\| 1.112.40 \|\|

*akhaṇḍānāṃ taṇḍulānāṃ tilānāṃ vā munīsvara \|*  
*lakṣamekaṃ viśodhyātha kṣipetpayasi saṃsṛte \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Unbroken rice grains or gingelly seeds should be selected, О leading sage, to the extent of one hundred thousand. They should be cleaned and put in boiling water.

## \|\| 1.112.41 \|\|

*tatpakkena tu nirmāya devyā mūrtiṃ suśomanām \|*  
*prakare gandhapuṣpāṇāṃ puṣpamālāvibhūṣitām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. When the grains are cooked well, a splended image of the goddess should be made. It should be embellished with scented flowers and flower garlands.

## \|\| 1.112.42-44 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya pārvatīṃ tatra pūjayedbhaktibhāvitaḥ \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpairdīpairnaivedyavistaraiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vividhaiśca phalairvipra namaskṛtya kṣamāpayet \|*  
*tato visarjayaddevīṃ jalamadhye 'tha dakṣiṇām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dattvā vidhijñaviprebhyo bhuñjīyācca pare dine \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ vipra koṭilakṣeśvarīvratam \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Goddess Parvatl should be installed therein and worshipped with great devotion, with scents, fragrant flowers, incense, lights and detailed Naivedya offerings and fruits. О Brahmana, she should bow to the goddess and crave forgiveness. Then she should immerse the image of the goddess in the middle of a water-tank. Daksina is then offered to the Brahmanas who are knowers of religious rites and procedures. She should then partake of her food the next day. Thus, О Brahmana, the Koti Laksheshvari Vrata has been narrated to you.

## \|\| 1.112.45 \|\|

*gaurīlokaṃ prayātyante vratasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*iṣaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ bṛbadgaurīvrataṃ caret \|\| 45 \|\|*

45a. In the end she goes to the world of Gaurl, thanks to the power of this Vrata.

45b. On the third day in the bright half of the month of Isa (i«e. Asvina), the lady devotee should perform BrhadGauri1 Vrata.

## \|\| 1.112.46 \|\|

*pañcavarṣaṃ vidhānena pūrvoktenaiva nārada \|*  
*ācāryaṃ pūjayedante viprānanyāndhanādibhiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О Narada, this Vrata is to be performed for five years in accordance with the rules of procedure mentioned above. At the end, she should worship the main preceptor and other Brahmanas with cash presents etc.

## \|\| 1.112.47-50 \|\|

*suvāsinīḥ pañca pūjyā vastrālaṅkāracandanaiḥ \|*  
*kañcukaiścaiva tāṭaṅkaiḥ kaṇṭhasūtrairharipriyāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vaṃśapātrāṇi pañcaiva sūtraiḥ saṃveṣṭitāni ca \|*  
*siṃdūraṃ jīrakaṃ caiva saubhāgyadravyasaṃyutam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*godhīmapiṣṭajātaṃ ca navāpūpaṃ phalā dikam \|*  
*vāyanāni ca pañcaiva tābhyo dadyācca bhojayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

*arghaṃ dattvā vāyanāni paścādbhuñjīta vāgyatā \|*  
*tatphalaṃ dhārayetkaṇṭhe sarvakāmasamṛddhaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. Five Suvasinis (married women whose husband are alive) should be worshipped asHaripriyas (beloveds of Hari) with clothes, ornaments, sandal paste, bodices, earrings and necklaces; five bamboo baskets are used and they are tied round with threads. The baskets are filled with saffron, cumin-seeds, and bliss-yielding articles. Vayanas (presepts of sweet-meats) comprising of ground wheat flour, fresh ApGpa (baked pies), fruits etc. These must be given to the Suvasinis who also be fed. After giving as worshipful gift half the materials gathered as Vayanas, she shall silently take her food. For the increase of the desired objects, a fruit (out of the gift) should be worn round the neck.

## \|\| 1.112.51 \|\|

*tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya sālaṅkārā sakhījanaiḥ \|*  
*gītavādyayutā nadyāṃ gaurīṃ tāṃ tu visarjayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Getting up early in the morning, bedecked in ornaments and accompanied by her friends, she should go to a river to the accompaniment of songs and instrumental music. There Gauri image is ritualistically bidden farewell to (into the river) with the prayer:

## \|\| 1.112.52 \|\|

*āhūtāsi mayābhadre pūjitā ca yathā vidhi \|*  
*mama saubhāgyadānāya yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ tvayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “O gentle lady, you had been invoked by me and worshipped duly (as per procedure), you may be pleased to go away at will, for granting me conjugal bliss”.

## \|\| 1.112.53 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ bhaktyā dvija devīprasādataḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā bhogāṃstu dehānte gaurīlokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After observing the holy rite, thus, О Brahmana, and after enjoying all worldly pleasures, thanks to the grace of the goddess, she shall attain Gauri’s world after death.

## \|\| 1.112.54-55 \|\|

*ūrjaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ viṣṇugaurīvrataṃ caret \|*  
*pūjayitvā jagadvandyāmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*suvāsinīṃ bhojayitvā maṅgaladravyapūjitām \|*  
*visarjayetpraṇamyaināṃ viṣṇugaurīpratuṣṭaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. On the third day in the bright half of the month of Orja (Karttika), she (the lady) should perform Visnugauri- vrata.1 After worshipping the goddess worthy of being saluted by the whole world, with different modes of worship and services and after feeding the suvasini (a married woman with husband alive) who has been honoured duly with auspicious articles, she should bid farewell to the goddess after bowing to her, for obtaining the grace of satisfaction of Visnugauri.

## \|\| 1.112.56 \|\|

*mārgaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ haragaurīvrataṃ śubham \|*  
*kṛtvā pūrvavidhānena pūjayejjagadaṃbikām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On the third day in the bright half of the month of Margashirsha, a woman should perform the auspicious HaraGauri Vrata in accordance with the injunctions laid down before, in the above-mentioned Vrata and should worship Jagadambika (Mother of the Universe).

## \|\| 1.112.57 \|\|

*etadvrataprabhāveṇa bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*devīlokaṃ samāsādya modate ca tayā saha \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. As a result of the prowess of this Vrata, she shall enjoy all charming worldly pleasures. Attaining the world of the goddess, she rejoices with her.

## \|\| 1.112.58-60 \|\|

*pauṣaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ brahmagaurīvrataṃ caret \|*  
*pūrvoktena vidhānena pūjitāpi dvijottama \|\| 58 \|\|*

*brahmagaurīprasādena modate tatra saṃgatā \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ pūjyā saubhāgyasuṃdarī \|\| 59 \|\|*

*pūrvoktena vidhānena nālikerārghyadānataḥ \|*  
*prasannā diśati svīyaṃ lokaṃ tu vratatoṣitā \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-59a. On the third day in the bright half of the month of Pausa, a woman should perform the Brahmagaurivrata1 in accordance with the injunctions laid down above. О excellent Brahmana, on being worshipped, BrahmaGauri shall be delighted. Thanks to her grace, the lady devotee becomes associated with the goddess and rejoices herself.

59b-60. On the third day in the bright half of the month ofMagha, (goddess) Saubhagya-Sundaii2 should be worshipped in accordance with the rules of procedure mentioned before, by means ofoffering Arghya with coconuts. Delighted and rendered pleased by means of the Vrata, the goddess grants her own world.

## \|\| 1.112.61 \|\|

*phaālgunasya site pakṣe tṛtīyā kulasaukhyadā \|*  
*pūjitā gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ sarvamaṅgaladā bhavet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The third day in the bright half of the month of Phalguna, is the bestower of family happiness. If the goddess is worshipped with scents, fragrant flowers etc., she shall be the bestower of all auspiciousness.

## \|\| 1.112.62 \|\|

*sarvāsu ca tṛtīyāsu vidhiḥ sādhāraṇo mune \|*  
*devīpūjā viprapūjā dānaṃ homo visarjanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. О sage, in all these Trtiyas (vratas on the third days of the lunar fortnight) the rules regarding the PCija of the goddess, the honour to the Brahmana, the charitable gifts, Ноmа and the ritualistic dismissal of the goddess are the same.

## \|\| 1.112.63 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitānīha tṛtīyāyā vratāni te \|*  
*bhaktyā kṛtāni ceṣṭāṃstu kāmāndardyumanogatān \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus the Vratas to be performed on Trtiyas have been narrated to you here. If observed with great devotion, they shall bestow all desirable objects cherished in mind.

## Chapter 113. The Exposition of the holy rites to be performed on Caturthis (the fourth day in # the Lunar fortnight)

## \|\| 1.113.1 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu vipraṃ pravakṣyāmi caturthyāste vratānyaham \|*  
*yāni kṛtvā narā nāryo 'bhīṣṭānkāmānavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatana said:

1\. О Brahmana listen, I shall recount to you the holy vows and rites to be observed on Caturthi days.1 On observing them, men and women shall attain their cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.113.2-4 \|\|

*caitramāsacaturthyāṃ tu vāsudevasvarūpiṇam \|*  
*gaṇapaṃ samyagabhyarcya dattvā kāñcanadakṣiṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viprāya viṣṇulokaṃ tu gaccheddevanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhasya caturthyāṃ tu prārthyaṃ saṃkarṣaṇāhvayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gṛhasthadvijamukhyebhyaḥ śaṅkhaṃ dattvā vidhānavit \|*  
*prāpya saṃkarṣaṇaṃ lokaṃ modate bahukalpakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-3a. On the fourth day in the Lunar fortnight in the month of Chaitra, , one should duly worship Ganapa (i.e. GaneSa) in the form of Vasudeva and offer gold as Daksina to a Brahmana. He will be bowed to by the Devas (thereby), and then go to Visnuloka.

3b-4. On the Caturthi day in the month of Vaisakha, the devotee should pray to the deity called Samkarsana. By giving a conch-shell to imporant Brahmana householders, the knower of religious injunctions shall attain the world of Samkarsana and rejoice there for many Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.113.5 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāsacaturthyāṃ tu prārcya pradyumnarūpiṇam \|*  
*phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca yuthebhyo dattvā svargaṃ labhennaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On the Caturthi day in the month of Jyestha the person should worship the deity in the form of Pradyumna. By giving fruits and roots to the herds (of cattle or beasts), he shall attain heaven.

## \|\| 1.113.6 \|\|

*āṣāḍhasya caturthyāṃ tu saṃprapūjyāniruddhakam \|*  
*yatibhyo 'lābupātrāṇi dattvābhīṣṭaṃ labhennaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the Caturthi day in the month of Asatfha, a man should worship Aniruddha. By giving pot-gourd-vessels to ascetics, he attains the cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.113.7 \|\|

*caturmūrtivratānyevaṃ kṛtvā dvādaśavatsaram \|*  
*udyāpanaṃ vidhānena kartavyaṃ phalamicchatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After performing these holy rites of the four Murtis for twelve years, the Udyapana rite should be performed in accordance with the injunctions, by the devotee who wishes for the benefit thereof.

## \|\| 1.113.8 \|\|

*anyajjyeṣṭhacaturthyāṃ tu satīvratamanuttamam \|*  
*kṛtvā gaṇapatermāturloke modeta tatsamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On the Caturthi day in the month of Jyesfha, there is another Vrata viz. the excellent Sativrata. By performing it, the devotee rejoices in the world of the mother of Ganapati on a par with him.

## \|\| 1.113.9-10 \|\|

*tathā'ṣāḍhacaturthyāṃ tu vratamanyacchubhāvaham \|*  
*rathantarāhvakalpasya hyādibhūtaṃ dinaṃ yataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śraddhāpūtena manasā gaṇeśaṃ vidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā labheccāpi phalaṃ devādidurgamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. There is another auspicious Vrata on the Caturthi day in the month of Asadha, since it is the day on which Kalpa called Rathantara began. The man should worship Ganesa duly with his mind sanctified by faith. He shall attain the benefit inaccessible even to the Devas and others.

## \|\| 1.113.11-30 \|\|

*śrāvaṇasya caturthyāṃ tu jāti candrodaye mune \|\| 11 \|\|*

*gaṇeśāya pradadyācca hyarghyaṃ vidhividāṃvaraḥ \|*  
*lambodaraṃ caturbāhuṃ trinetraṃ raktavarṇakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nānāratnavibhūṣāḍhyaṃ prasannāsyaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*āvāhanādibhiḥ sarvairupacāraiḥ samarcayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*naivedyaṃ modakaṃ dadyādgaṇeśaprītidāyakam \|*  
*evaṃ vrataṃ vidhāyātha bhuktvā modakameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sukhaṃ svapyānniśāyāṃ tu bhūmāveva kṛtārcanaḥ \|*  
*vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa kāmānmanasi cintitān \|\| 15 \|\|*

*labdhvā leke paraṃ cāpi gaṇeśapadamāpnuyāt \|*  
*nānena sadṛśaṃ cānyadvratamasti jagattraye \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmātkāryaṃ prayatnena sarvānkāmānabhīpsatā \|*  
*athāsminneva divase dūrvāgaṇapati vratam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kecidicchanti devarṣe tadvidhānaṃ vadāmi te \|*  
*haimaṃ nirmāya gaṇapaṃ tāmrapātropari sthitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*veṣṭitaṃ raktavastreṇa sarvatobhadramaṇḍale \|*  
*pūjayedraktakusumaiḥ patrikābhiśca pañcabhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bilvapatramapāmārgaṃ śamī dūrvā haripriyā \|*  
*ābhiranyaśca kusumairabhyarcya phalamodakaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ācāryāya vidhijñāya satkṛtya vinivedayet \|*  
*upahāraṃ prakalpyātha dadyādarghaṃ samudyate \|*  
*tataḥ saṃprārathya vighneśamūrtiṃ sopaskarāṃ mune \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ācāryāya vidhijñāya satkṛtya vinivedayet \|*  
*kṛtvaivaṃ pañca varṣāṇi samupāsya yathāvidhi \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhuktveha bhogānakhilān lokaṃ gaṇapatervrajet \|*  
*atha bhādracaturthyāṃ tu bahulādhenusaṃjñakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pūjanī yo 'tra yatnena sraggandhayavasādibhiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śaktaśceddānamācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aśaktaḥ puretāṃ tu namaskṛtya visarjayet \|*  
*pañcābdaṃ vādaśābdaṃ vā ṣoḍaśābdamathāpi vā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vrataṃ kṛtvā samudyāpya dhenuṃ dadyātpayasvinīm \|*  
*prabhāveṇa vratasyāsya bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*satkṛto devatāvṛndairgolokaṃ samavāpnuyāt \|*  
*atha śukla caturthyāṃ tu siddhavaināyakavratam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*āvāhanādibhiḥ sarvairupacāraiḥ samarcanam \|*  
*ekāgramānaso bhūtvā dhyāyetsiddhivināyakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ekadantaṃ śūrpakarṇaṃ gajavaktraṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*pāśāṅkuśadharaṃ devaṃ taptakāñcanasannibham \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ekaviṃśati patrāṇi caikaviṃśatināmabhiḥ \|*  
*samarpayedbhaktiyuktastāni nāmāni vai śṛṇu \|\| 30 \|\|*

11-17a. On the Caturthi day in the month of Sravaija, О sage, when the moon has risen, the devotee, the most excellent among the knowers of the procedure, should offer Arghya unto Ganesha. He shall meditate on Lambodara (God Ganesha), the three-eyed, four-armed deity who is red-complexioned, whose face beams with pleasure, and who is bedecked in different kinds of jewels and ornaments. He should worship him with all modes of services such as invocation, etc. He should offer Modaka (sweet meat) as Naivedya which gives pleasure to Ganesha. After performing the Vrata thus, he shall partake of the Modakas. During the night, after the worship, he should gladly sleep on the bare ground. Thanks to the power of this Vrata, he shall obtain all desires cherished in his mind in. this world, and (after death) shall attain the region of Ganeia. In all the three worlds, there is no other Vrata like this. Hence, it must be observed with all (possible) efforts by one who wishes to attain all cherished desires.

17b-18a. О celestial sage, some wish that the holy rite called Durvaganapativrata1 should be performed on this very same day. I shall tell you the injunctions regarding its performance.

18b-23a. The devotee should make the image of Gana- pati in gold and place it over a copper vessel aftercovering it with a red cloth. He should worship the (entire set) on the mystic diagram called Sarvatobhadra, with red flowers five kinds of leaves viz. Bilva, Apamarga, Sami, Durva, and Hari- priya (i.e. TulasI).With these leaves and other flowers he should perform worship. He shall offer fruits and sweetmeats as Naivedya. After that, О ascetic, with pleasure, he should offer the Arghya. Then, О sage, after praying to it, he should give the image of VighneSa (ganesa) alongwith the adjuncts to the preceptor who knows the rules of procedure. He should honour him befittingly and then give it to him. He should continue the Vrata for five years, after duly performing worship. After enjoying all pleasures here he will go to the world of Ganapati.

23b-27a. On the Gaturthi day (in the dark half) of the month of Bhadrapada, is the holy rite called Bahuladhenuka. On this day, the deity cow is to be assiduously worshipped with scents, garlands, barley, and other things. After circumambulating the cow deity, he should offer charitable gifts, if he can afford. If he cannot afford it, he shall bow to it and set it free. He should continue the Vrata for five, ten or sixteen years. He shall then perform the Udyapana rite and give a milch cow (as charitable gift). Thanks to the power of this Vrata, he shall enjoy all charming worldly pleasures, and duly honoured and greeted by groups of Devas, he shall attain Goloka (the world of cows).

27b-30. On the fourth day in the bright half (of the monthofBhadrapada)is the holy rite called Siddha-Vainayaka- vrata (or ‘Siddhi-Vinayaka vrata). Through invocation and all other modes of service, the worship should be performed. Concentrating the mind, he should meditate on Siddhivinayaka. He should meditate on Lord Ganesaas Ekadanta (single-tusked) Surpakarna (one with winnow-like ears), Gajavaktra (elephantfaced), CatuRibhuja (four-armed), Pasankusa-Dhara (one holding in his hand, a noose and a goad), the Lord resembling molten gold (in complexion). He should offer twentyone leaves uttering the twentyone names (one by one) with devotion. Listen to those names.

## \|\| 1.113.31-37 \|\|

*sumukhāya śamīpatraṃ gaṇādhīśāya bhṛṅgajam \|*  
*umāputrāya bailvaṃ tu dūrvāṃ gajamukhāya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*laṃbodarāya badarīṃ dhattūraṃ harasūnave \|*  
*śūrpakarṇāya tulasīṃ vakratuṇḍāya śiṃbijam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*guhāgrajāyāpāmārgamekadantāya bārhatam \|*  
*herambāya tu siṃdūraṃ catirhetre ca patrajam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarveśvarāyāgastyasya patraṃ prītivivarddhanam \|*  
*dūrvāyugmaṃ tato gṛhya gandhapuṣpākṣatairyutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*pūjāṃ nivedayedbhaktiyukto modakapañcakam \|*  
*ācamayya namaskṛtya saṃprārthya ca visarjjayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vināyakasya pratimāṃ haimīṃ sopaskarāṃ mune \|*  
*nivedayecca gurave dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtārcano bhaktyā pañca varṣāṇi nārada \|*  
*upāsya labhate kāmānaihikāmuṣmikān śubhān \|\| 37 \|\|*

31-37. Sami-leaf should be offered to Sumukha (the good-faced Deity), the Bhrnga-leaf to GanadhlSa, the Bilva- leaf to the son of Uma, Durva-grass to the elephant-faced God, Badari to Lambodara (the big-bellied deity), Dhattura to the son of Нага (Siva), Tulasi-leaf to Surpakarna (God with ears like winnowing baskets) Sami-leaf to Vakra-tungla (God with a curved trunk), Apamarga leaf to Guhagraja (Elder brother of Karttikeya), Barhata leaves (those of brinjals) to Ekadanta (Single-tusked god), Sindura (saffron) to Heramba, leaf of the fragrant plant called Patra to Gaturhotra, the leaf of the Agas- tya tree which is pleasing to Sarvesvara (Lord of all). He should them take up a pair of the leaves of Durva grass along with scents, fragrant flowers and unbroken rice- grains. With great devotion, he should offer worship and five Modakas as Naivedya. After the rite of Acamana, obeisance and prayer, he should ritualistically bid farewell to the Deity. О sage, he should give the image of Vinayaka, made of gold, to the preceptor along with adjuncts. He should then give Daksina (religious gifts) to Brahmanas. О Narada, one who performs worship with devotion like this for five years, shall attain all cherished desires as a result of his Upasana (devotion and worship) here, as well as all splend^l things hereafter.

## \|\| 1.113.38-39 \|\|

*asyāṃ caturthyāṃ śaśinaṃ na paśyecca kadācana \|*  
*paśyan mithyābhiśāpa tu labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*atha taddoṣanāśāya mantraṃ paurāṇikaṃ paṭhet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*siṃhaḥ prasenamamadhītsiṃho jāṃbavatā hataḥ \|*  
*sakumāraka mā rodīstava hyeṣa syamantakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Never shall one look at the moon on this Caturthi day (i.e. night). There is no doubt about this that, if one looks at the moon, he will be falsely accused. In order to mitigate the defect thereof (i.e. of looking at the moon this night), this (following) Mantra from the Purana should be recited: “The lion killed Prasena, the lion was killed by Jamba- van. О gentle boy, Do not cry. This Syamantaka jewel is offered to you.”

## \|\| 1.113.40-45 \|\|

*iṣaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu kaparddīśaṃ vināyakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pauruṣiṇa tu sūktena pūjayedupacārakaiḥ \|*  
*akāraṇānmuṣṭigatāṃstaṇḍulānsakaparddikān \|\| 41 \|\|*

*viprāya baṭave dadyādgandhapuṣpārcitāya ca \|*  
*taṇḍulā vaiśvadaivatyā haradaivatyamiśritāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kapardigaṇanātho 'sau prīyatāṃ taiḥ samarpitaiḥ \|*  
*caturthyāṃ kārtike kṛṣṇe karakākhyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*strīṇāmevādhikāro 'tra tadvidhānamudīryate \|*  
*pūjayecca gaṇādhīśaṃ snātā strīsamalaṅkṛtā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tadagre pūrṇapakvānnaṃ vinyasetkarakāndaśa \|*  
*samarpya devadevāya bhaktyā prayatamānasā \|\| 45 \|\|*

40-43a. On the Caturthi day in the bright half of the month ofAsvina, one should worship Vinayaka (Kapardlsa — the god with cowrie-like knotted hair) by means of the Purusa Sukta. He should render services without any reason (i.e. without any ulterior motive). He should offer the rice grains along- with the shell-coins to a Brahmana religious student who is worshipped with scents and fragrant flowers with prayer: “The rice grains have Visve Devas as their deity. They are mixed with the shell coins whose presiding deity is Нага. May the leader of the Ganas of Siva (Kapardin) be pleased, when (the couries) are so dedicated.”

43b-44a. The holy rite called Karakavrata1 is to be performed on the Caturthi day in the dark half of the month of Karttika. Only women are authorised to perform this Vrata. The rules of the procedure on it are being mentioned. Like other material, the NP. seems to have borrowed this verse from the VP. IV. 13.42. The verse appears in a similar context in the Vayu P. 96. 42 and Вг. P. 16.36

44b-45. The woman should take her bath and bedeck herself. She should then worship god Ganesa. In front of the deity ten bowls filled with cooked rice shall be kept and be dedicated to the Lord of the Devas with devotion and purity of the mind.

## \|\| 1.113.46-47 \|\|

*devo me prīyatāmevamuccāryyātha samarpayet \|*  
*suvāsinībhyo viprebhyo yathākāmaṃ ca sādaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tataścandrodaye rātrau dattvārghaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*bhuñjīta miṣṭamannaṃ ca vratasya paripūrtaye \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. She should utter (pray): — “May the deity be gracious unto me.” Saying this she should dedicate them to God Ganesa. Presents shall be given respectfully to Suvasinis (married women) and the Brahmanas according to desire. Then at night, when the moon rises, she should duly offer Arghya and partake of sweet-meats and cooked rice for the fulfilment of the Vrata.

## \|\| 1.113.48 \|\|

*yadvā kṣīreṇa karakaṃ pūrṇaṃ toyena vā mune \|*  
*sapūgākṣataratnāḍhyaṃ dvijāya pratipādayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Or О sage, the bowls may be filled with milk or water alongwith a rice, a betel nut, rice-grains and jewels and gifted over to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.113.49 \|\|

*etatkṛtvā vrataṃ nārī ṣoḍaśadvādaśābdakam \|*  
*upāyanaṃ vidhāyātha vratametadvisarjjayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The woman devotee should perform this holy rite for sixteen or twelve years. After making the due presents, she should ritualistically conclude this Vrata.

## \|\| 1.113.50-53 \|\|

*yāvajjīvaṃ tu vā nāryā kāryyaṃ saubhāgyavāñchayā \|*  
*vratenānena sadṛśaṃ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyadāyakam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vidyate bhuvaneṣvanyattasmānnityamiti sthitiḥ \|*  
*ūrjjaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu nāgavratamudāhṛtam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*prātarvrataṃ tu saṃkalpya dhenuśṛñjagalaṃ śuci \|*  
*pītvā snātvātha madhyāhne śaṅkhapālādipannagān \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śeṣaṃ cāhvāmapūrvaistu pūjayedupacārakaiḥ \|*  
*kṣīreṇāpyāyanaṃ kuryādetannāgavrataṃ smṛtam \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-51a. Or the holy rite shall be observed by the woman throughout her life with a desire for conjugal blessedness. There is no other Vrata like this that yields conjugal blessedness to women. Hence it should be continuously performed.

51b-53. On the fourth day in the bright half of the month of Karttika, the holy rite Nagavrata1 is to be celebrated. The devotee shall perform the Samkalpa rite in the morning, and drink pure water from a cow's horn. After the bath, he shall worship the serpents Sankhapala and others as well as Sesa by means of diverse services (in worship) beginning with invocation. He should make Apyayana (developing and nourishing) by means of milk. This is known as Nagavrata.

## \|\| 1.113.54 \|\|

*evaṅkṛte tu viprendra nṛbhirnāgavrate śubhe \|*  
*viṣāṇi naśyantyacirānna daśanti ca pannagāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О leading Brahmana, if this auspicious observance of Nagavrata is performed thus by men, poisons perish ere long, and serpents do not bite them.

## \|\| 1.113.55-59 \|\|

*mārgaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu varṣaṃ yāvanmunīśvarā \|*  
*kṣapayedekabhaktena naktenātha dvitīyakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ayācitopavāsābhyāṃ tṛtīyakacaturthake \|*  
*evaṃ krameṇa vidhivaccatvāryabdāni mānavaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*samāpya ca tato 'syānte vratasnāto mahāvratī \|*  
*kārayeddhemaghaṭitaṃ bhūgaṇermūṣakaṃ ratham \|\| 57 \|\|*

*aśakto varṇakaireva śubhraṃ cābjaṃ supatrakam \|*  
*tasyopari ghaṭaṃ sthāpya tāmrapātreṇa saṃyutam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pūrayettaṇḍalaiḥ śubhraistasyopari gaṇeśvaram \|*  
*nyasedvastrayugācchannaṃ gandhādyaiḥ pūjayecca tam \|\| 59 \|\|*

55-59. О leading sage, this Vrata is to be celebrated on th e fourth day in the bright half of the month of MargashIrsha.

## \|\| 1.113.60-61 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ modakaṃ kalpyaṃ gaṇeśaḥ prīyatāmiti \|*  
*jāgarairśītavādyādyaiḥ purāṇākhyānakaiścaret \|\| 60 \|\|*

*prabhāte vimale snātvā homaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|'*  
*tilavrīhiyavaśvetasurṣapājyaiḥ sakhaṇḍakaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Modaka is to be offered as Naivedya saying: “May Ganesa be pleased.” The night shall be spent by keeping awake through songs and instrumental music as well as in the narration of the Puranas. After the day has dawned, he should take bath and perform Ноmа in accordance with injunctions, with gingelly seeds, rice grains, barley grains and white mustard along with ghee and sugar-candy.

## \|\| 1.113.62-64 \|\|

*gaṇo gaṇādhipaścaiva kūṣmāṇḍastripurāntakaḥ \|*  
*laṃbodaraikadantau ca rukmadaṃṣṭraśca vighnapaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*brahmā yamo 'tha varuṇaḥ somasūryahutāśanāḥ \|*  
*gandhamādī parameṣṭhītyevaṃ ṣoḍaśanāmabhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*praṇavādyairṅeṃnamoṃ'taiḥ pratyekaṃ dahane hunet \|*  
*vakratuṇḍeti ṅeṃtena barmāntenāṣṭayukchatam \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. The following sixteen names of the deity should be uttered in the dative case. Оm is prefixed to them and Namah is added at the end. (For example, here the 1st name is Gana. It should be uttered and addressed as: Оm Ganaya namah). The names of the god are: Gana, Ganadhipa, Kiism- anda, Tripurantaka, Lambodara, Ekadanta, Rukma-daihs(ra, Vighnaha, Brahma, Yama, Varuna, Soma, Surya, Hutasana, Gandhamadin and Paramesfhin. With the utterance of each name, one oblation is offered into the fire. A hundred and eight Homas are performed with the utterance of ‘Vakra-tunda and ‘Varman in the dative case (i.e. Vakra-tundaya and Varmane.

## \|\| 1.113.65-66 \|\|

*tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ śaktyā hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret \|*  
*dikpālānpūjayitvā ca brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*catutviṃśatisaṃkhyākān modakaiḥ pāyasaistathā \|*  
*savatsāṃ gāṃ tato dadyādācāryāya sadakṣiṇām \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Thereafter, he performs Homas with Vyahrtis to the extent of his capacity and then the Piirnahuti is performed. After worshipping the guardians of the quarters, he should feed Brahmanas (twenty-four in number) with sweet-meats and milk-pudding. He should then give a cow along with its calf to the preceptor, along with monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.113.67-71 \|\|

*anyobhyo 'pi yathāśakti bhūyasīṃ ca tato dadet \|*  
*praṇamya dakṣiṇīkṛtya pravisṛjya dvijottamām \|\| 67 \|\|*

*bandhubhiḥ saha bhuñjīta svayaṃ ca prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*etadvrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā bhuktvā bhogānihottamān \|\| 68 \|\|*

*sāyujyaṃ labhate viṣṇorgaṇeśasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*kecidvaravrataṃ nāma prāhuretasya nārada \|\| 69 \|\|*

*vidhānametadevāpi phalaṃ cāpīha tatsamam \|*  
*pauṣamāsacaturthyāṃ tu vighneśaṃ prārthya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*vipraikaṃ bhojayeccaivaṃ modakairdakṣiṇāṃ dadet \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte mune bhūyādvratī saṃpattibhājanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

67-69a. He shall give cash presents to others also, according to his capacity (the more the better). After obeisance and circumambulation (around the Brahmanas), the excellent Brahmanas should be bidden farewell to. He should, then, with great delight in his mind, take his food along with his kinsmen. By performing this vrata, a man enjoys excellent worldly pleasures here, and attains the Liberation called Sayujya (absorption in the Deity) with Visnu, thanks to the Grace of Ganesa.

69b-70a. О Narada, some call this by the name Vara- vrata.1 Its rules of procedure and benefit are the same as in the case of the former.

70b-71. On the Caturthi day in the month of Pausaf the devotee should pray to Vighnesa with great devotion. He should feed a single Brahmana with sweet-meats and offer monetary gifts also. О sage, if this is performed, the Vratin (the performer of the holy vow) shall become the recepicnt of riches.

## \|\| 1.113.72-75 \|\|

*māghakṛṣṇacaturthyāṃ tu saṃkaṣṭavratamucyate \|*  
*tatropavāsaṃ saṃkalpya vratī niyamapūrvakam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*candrodayamabhivyāpya tiṣṭhetprayatamānasaḥ \|*  
*tataścandrodaye prāpte mṛnmayaṃ gaṇanāyakam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vidhāya vinyasetpīṭhe sāyudhaṃ ca savāhanam \|*  
*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*modakaṃ cāpi naivedyaṃ saguḍaṃ tilakuṭṭakam \|*  
*tator'ghyaṃ tāmraje pātre raktacandanamiśritam \|\| 75 \|\|*

72-73a. The holy vow Saiiikastavrata is to be observed on the fourth day in the dark half of the month of Magha. The Vratin should decide on observance of fast upto the rise of the moon, with his mind controlled.

73b-74a. After the rise of the moon, the image of Ganesa, made of clay, should be placed on the pedestal alongwith his weapons and the vehicle.

74b-75. It should be worshipped with the sixteen Upa- caras (modes of service) in accordance with injunctions. Modaka and ground gingelly seeds alongwith jaggery shall be offered as Naivedya. Arghya is offered in a copper vessel mixed with red- sandal paste.

## \|\| 1.113.76-78 \|\|

*sakuśaṃ ca sadūrvaṃ ca puṣpākṣatasamanvitam \|*  
*saśamīpatradadhi ca kṛtvā candrāya dāpayet \|\| 76 \|\|*

*gaganārṇavamāṇikya candra dākṣāyaṇīpate \|*  
*gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ gaṇeśapratirūpaka \|\| 77 \|\|*

*evaṃ dattvā gaṇeśāya divyārghyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*śaktyā saṃbhojya viprāgryānsvayaṃ bhuñjīta cājñayā \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. Kusa grass, Durva grass, flowers, raw rice grains, Samipatra (leaves of the Sami tree) and curds should be mixed together and offered to the Moon (with the prayer), ‘Ю moon, the ruby in the ocean of the Armament, О Lord of Daksa’s daughters, О representative of Ganesa, kindly accept the Arghya offered by me.” Uttering this he should offer the divine Arghya, that is destructive of sins to Ganesa. After feeding excellent Brahmanas in accordance with his capacity, he should take food himself with their formal permission.

## \|\| 1.113.79 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra saṃkaṣṭākhyaṃ śūbhāvaham \|*  
*samṛddho dhanadhānyaiḥ syānna ca saṃkaṣṭamāpnuyāt \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. О Brahmana, by performing this auspicious Vrata called Samkasta, he shall become flourishing with wealth and foodgrains. He shall never attain difficulty or pain.

## \|\| 1.113.80-82 \|\|

*māghaśuklacaturthyāṃ tu gaurīvratamanuttamam \|*  
*tasyāṃ tu gaurī saṃpūjyā saṃyuktā yoginīgaṇaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*naraiḥ strībhirviśeṣeṇa kundapuṣpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ \|*  
*raktasūtre raktapuṣpaistathaivālaktakena ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

*dhūpairdīpaṃśca balibhiḥ saguḍainārdrakeṇa ca \|*  
*payasā pāyasenāpi lavaṇena ca pālakaiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-82. The excellent holy vow Gaurlvrata1 is to be ooserv- ed on the fourth day in the bright half of the month of Magha. On that day, Gauri is to be worshipped alongwith the groups of Yoginls by men as well as by women in particular. The articles of worship are the following: Kunda flowers, Kumkuma, red threads, red flowers, Alaktaka (the juice of red lac), incense, lights, oblations, ginger with jaggery, milk and milk puddings, salt and the greens called Palakas.

## \|\| 1.113.83 \|\|

*pūjyāścāvidhavā nāryastathā viprāḥ suśobhanāḥ \|*  
*saubhāgyavṛddhaye deyo bhoktavyaṃ bandhubhiḥ saha \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Married women who are not widows and splendid Brahmanas are to be worshipped for the increase in conjugal bliss. Gifts must be made. One shall take food alongwith kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.113.84 \|\|

*idaṃ gaurīvrataṃ vipra saubhāgyārogyavarddhanam \|*  
*prativarṣaṃ prakarttavyaṃ nārībhiśca naraistathā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. О Brahmana, this Gaurivrata is conducive to the increase of conjugal blesssedness. This must be performed every year both by men and women.

## \|\| 1.113.85 \|\|

*ḍhuṇḍhivrataṃ paraiḥ proktaṃ kaiścitkuṇḍavrataṃ smṛtam \|*  
*lalitāvratamityanyaiḥ śāntivratamathāparaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The same holy rite is called Dhuntjhivrala by others. By some it is galled as Kuntfavrata. Others call it Lalitavrata and still others call it Santivrata.

## \|\| 1.113.86 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ sarvamasyāṃ kṛtaṃ mune \|*  
*bhavetsaha sraguṇitaṃ prasādāddantinaḥ sadā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Ablution, charitable gift, japa and hojna, О sage, all these rites performed on this day shall become thousandfold, thanks to the Grace of Dantin (god Ganesa).

## \|\| 1.113.87 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ phaālgune māsi ḍhuṇḍhirājavrataṃ śubham \|*  
*tilaṣiṣṭairdvijān bhojya svayaṃ cāśnīta mānavaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. On the fourth day in the month of Phalguna falls the auspicious Vrata of Dhundhiraja. Brahmanas are fed with cakes of ground gingelly-seed flour. The vower should also partake of it himself.

## \|\| 1.113.88 \|\|

*gaṇeśārādhanaparo dānahomaprapūjanaiḥ \|*  
*tilaireva kṛtaiḥ siddhiṃ prāpnuyāttatprasādataḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. One who is interested ift the propitiation of Ganesa shall attain Siddhi by offering religious gifts, Ноmа and Piija with gingelly seeds alone, thanks to His grace.

## \|\| 1.113.89 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ gajavaktraṃ ca kṛtvā saṃpūjya yatnataḥ \|*  
*dvijāgryāya pradātavyaṃ sarvasaṃpatsamṛddhaye \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The image of the elephant-faced deity should be made of gold. After worshipping assiduously, it must be given to an excellent Brahmana, for the flourishing increase in all riches.

## \|\| 1.113.90 \|\|

*yasminkasminbhavenmāsi caturthī ravivārayuk \|*  
*sāṃgārakā vā viprendra sā viśeṣaphalapradā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. If a GaturthI day coincides with Sunday or Tuesday in any of the twelve months, О leading Brahmana, it yields special benefits.

## \|\| 1.113.91 \|\|

*sarvāsu ca caturthīṣu śuklāsvapyasitāsu ca \|*  
*vighneśa eva deveśaḥ saṃpūjyo bhaktitatparaiḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In all the Caturthls, whether of the dark half or of the bright half of the month, Vighnes'a (God Ganesha), the Lord of the Devas should be worshipped by those who are eagerly engaged in devotion.’

## Chapter 114. The Exposition of Holy Vratas to be performed on Pahcami days (fifth days of Lunar fortnight)

## \|\| 1.114.1 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi pañcamyāste vratānyaham \|*  
*yāni bhaktyā samāsthāya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatana said:

1\. О Brahmana, I shall recount to you the Vratas to be performed on Paftcamis1 (fifth days in the halves of Lunar months). On observing these rites with devotion, one shall attain all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.114.2 \|\|

*proktā matsyajayantī tu pañcamī madhuśuklagā \|*  
*asyāṃ matsyāvatārārcā bhaktaiḥ kāryā mahotsavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The PancamI (fifth day) in the bright half of the month of Chaitra is called Matsya jayanii. On this day, the worship of the incarnation of the Lord as (Divine) Fish is to be performed with great festivities, by devotees.

## \|\| 1.114.3-11 \|\|

*śrīpañcamīti caiṣoktā tatra kāryaṃ śriyor'canam \|*  
*gandhādyairupacāraistu naivedyaiḥ pāyasādibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yo lakṣmīṃ pūjayeccātra taṃ vai lakṣmīrna muñcati \|*  
*pṛthvīvrataṃ tathā cāndraṃ hayagarīvavrataṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kāryaṃ tattadvidhānena tattatsiddhimabhīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*atha vaiśākhapañcamyāṃ śeṣaṃ cābhyarcya mānavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarvairnāgagaṇairyuktamabhīṣṭaṃ labhate phalam \|*  
*tathā jyeṣṭhasya pañcamyāṃ pitṝnabhyarcayetsudhīḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sarvakāmaphalāvāptirbhavedvai viprabhojanaiḥ \|*  
*athāṣāḍhasya pañcamyāṃ vāyuṃ sarvagataṃ mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

*grāmādbahirvinirgatya dharopasthe samāstitaḥ \|*  
*dhvajaṃ ca pañcavarṇaṃ tu vaṃśadaṇḍāgrasaṃsthitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samucchritaṃ nidadhyāttu kalpitābje tu madhyataḥ \|*  
*tatastanmūladeśe tu dikṣu sarvāsu nārada \|\| 9 \|\|*

*lokapālānsamabhyarcya kuryādvāyuparīkṣaṇam \|*  
*prathamādiṣu yāmeṣu yo yo vāyuḥ pravartate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasmai tasmai digīśāya pūjāṃ samyak prakalpayet \|*  
*evaṃ sthitvā nirāhārastatra yāmacatuṣṭayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-4a. This is called Sripanchami1 also. On this day, the worship of Sri is to be performed by the articles of worship such as scents etc., and the Naivedyas of milk pudding etc., Laksmi never forsakes a person who worships Laksmi here (on this day).

4b-5a. Prthvlvrata, Candravrata and Hayagrivavrata are also to be performed by those who wish to attain different Siddhis, in accordance with the respective injunctions.

5b-6a. On the PancamI day in the month of Vaisakha, the man shall worship Sesa, endowed with the attributes of serpents. He shall attain the desired benefit.

6b-7a. The intelligent devottee shall worship the Pitrs (Manes) on the PancamI day in the month of Jyestha. He shall have the acquisition of all desired benefits through feeding the Brahmanas.

7b-11a. О sage, Vayu who is present everywhere is to be worshipped on the PancamI day in the month of Asadha. He should go out of the village and climb up to the ridge of a mountain. To a bamboo pole he should tie a banner of five colours. It should be succintly high. He should fix the pole in the middle of the mystic diagram of a lotus. О Narada, at its root in all the quarters, he should worship the guardians of the quarters and test the direction of the blow of the wind. Beginning with the first Yama, (period of three hours), he shall duly worship the Lord of that quarter in which the wind blows.

11b. He shall thus stay there for four YaJmas without taking food.

## \|\| 1.114.12 \|\|

*sāyamāgatya gehaṃ svaṃ bhuktvā svalpaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*lokapālānnamaskṛtya svapyādbhūmitale śucau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He should then return home in the evening. He should partake light food. With concentration of mind and after bowing down to the guardians of the world, he should lie down on bare yet clean ground and go to sleep.

## \|\| 1.114.13 \|\|

*yaḥ svapno jāyate tasyāṃ rātrau yāme caturthake \|*  
*sa eva bhavitā nūnaṃ svapna ityāha vai śivaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The dream that comes to him in the fourth Yama (quarter) on that night shall come true. So says Siva.

## \|\| 1.114.14 \|\|

*aśubhe tu samutpanne śivapūjāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*sopavāso nayedaṣṭayāmaṃ taddinameva vā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If anything inauspicious happens in the dream, the devotee should be engaged in the worship of Siva and observe fast for all the eight subsequent Yamas (i.e. 24 hours) or for the day alone (i.e. 12 hours).

## \|\| 1.114.15-16 \|\|

*bhojayitvā dvijānaṣṭau tataḥ śubhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*vratametatsamuditaṃ śubhāśubhanidarśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nṛṇāṃ saubhāgyajanakamiha loke paratra ca \|*  
*śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapañcamyāṃ vrataṃ hyannasamṛddhidam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16a. He should then feed eight Brahmanas. Thereby he shall attain auspicious benefits. This holy rite is called “Subha- subha-Nidar^ana”1 (The test for auspicious and inauspicious results). It causes blessedness to men in this world as well as in other world.

16b. The auspicious rite called Anna-samrddhi-da (the bestower of plentitude of food) is to be observed on the Paft- cami day in the dark half of the month of Sravana.

## \|\| 1.114.17-19 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ dinaśeṣe tu sarvāṇyannāni nārada \|*  
*pṛthak pātreṣu saṃsthāpya jalairāplāvayetsudhīḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tato pātrāntare tattu niṣkāsyāṃbu nidhāpayet \|*  
*prātarbhānau samudite pitṝṃścaiva tathā ṛṣīn \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devāṃścābhyarcya susnātaṃ kṛtvā naivedyamagrataḥ \|*  
*tadannaṃ yācakebhyastu prayacchetprītamānasaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. О Narada, on the previous Caturthi day when there is yet some part of the day, the intelligent devotee shall put all cooked food in different vessels and pour water therein. Then he should put it in another vessel after draining off all water. The next day, after sunrise, he should worship the Pitrs, the sages and the Devas after due ablution. He should then offer Nai- vedya to the Devas. With delighted mind, he shall give cooked food to beggars.

## \|\| 1.114.20 \|\|

*sarvaṃ dinaṃ kṣipedevaṃ pradoṣe tu śivālaye \|*  
*gatvā saṃpūjayeddevaṃ liṅgarūpiṇamīśvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He shall spend the whole of the day in this activity. At sunset he shall go to Siva’s temple and worship the Lord Isvara in the form of Linga.

## \|\| 1.114.21 \|\|

*gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ samyakpūjayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*japetpañcākṣarī vidyāṃ śataṃ cāpi sahasrakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After duly worshipping Mahesvara with scents, fragrant flowers, etc he shall repeat the five-syllabled Mantra (Om Sivaya Namah) a hundred or thousand times.

## \|\| 1.114.22-26 \|\|

*japaṃ nivedya devāya bhavāya bhavarūpiṇe \|*  
*stutvā sarvairvaundikaiśca paurāṇaiścāpyanākulaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*prārthayeddevamīśānaṃ śaśvatsarvānnasiddhaye \|*  
*śāradīyāni cānnāni tathā vāsaṃtikānyapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yāni syustaiḥ samṛddho 'haṃ bhūyāṃ janmani janmani \|*  
*evaṃ saṃprārthya deveśaṃ gṛhamāgatya vai svakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*datvānnaṃ brāhmaṇādibhyaḥ pakvaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*etadannavrataṃ vipra vidhinā'caritaṃ nṛbhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarvānnasaṃpajjanakaṃ paraloke gatipradam \|*  
*śrāvaṇe śuklapañcajamyāṃ nṛbhirāstikyatatparaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-23a. After dedicating the benefit of Japa to Lord Siva, the embodiment of the universe, he should eulogise the Lord with all Vedic and Pauranic hymns. Without agitation or perturbation, he should pray to Lord Isana for the sake of perpetual acquisition of cooked food.

23b-24a. “In all my births may I be richly blessed with all those foodgrains whether harvested during the autumn or during the spring.”

24b-26. After praying thus to the Lord of the Devas, he should come back to his own house. He should give cooked food to the Brahmanas and eat it himself silently. О Brahmana, this Annavrata (Holy rite of cooked food), if observed duly by men, is conducive to the production of all fobd and wealth in this world, and yields salvation in the other world.

## \|\| 1.114.27-29 \|\|

*dvārasyobhayato lekhyā gomayena viṣolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*gandhādyaiḥ pūjayettāṃśca tathendrāṇīmanantaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saṃpūjya svarṇarūpyādidadhyakṣatakuśāṃbubhiḥ \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpairdīpairnaivedyasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taddravyaṃ saṃpraṇamya ca \|*  
*saṃprārthya bhaktibhāvena viprāgryeṣu samarpayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. This rite (in propitiation of serpents) is performed on the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Sravana, by men firm in their belief in the Vedas. On either side of the door-way, figures of poisonous serpents should be drawn in cowdung. He should worship them with scents, etc. Thereafter he should worship Indranl with gold, silver, etc, curds, raw rice-grains, water from Kusha grass, scents, fragrant flowers, incense, lights and hoards of Naivedyas. After circumambulating and bowing down, he should pray with great devotion. He should give the articles of worship to leading Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.114.30 \|\|

*yadidaṃ svarṇaraupyādi dravyaṃ vai viprasātkṛtam \|*  
*tadanantaphalaṃ bhūyānmama janmani janmani \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “In all my births, may these gold, silver, etc. that have been given to Brahmanas be productive of endless benefit.”

## \|\| 1.114.31 \|\|

*ityevaṃ dadato dravyaṃ bhaktibhāvena nārada \|*  
*prasannaḥ syāddhanādhyakṣaḥ svarṇādikasamṛddhidaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О Narada, he who gifts away along with this utterance, the articles with great devotion, will delight Kubera, the presiding deity of wealth, who bestows affluence like gold, upon his devotees.

## \|\| 1.114.32 \|\|

*etadvrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā viprānsaṃbhojya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*paścātsvayaṃ ca bhuñjīta dārāpatyasuhṛddṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After observing the holy rite, the man should feed Brahmanas with devotion. Thereafter, he should partake of his food surrounded by his wife, children and friends.

## \|\| 1.114.33-34 \|\|

*bhādre tu kṛṣṇapañcamyāṃ nāgān kṣīreṇa tarpayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yastasyā'saptamaṃ yāvatkulaṃ sarpātsunirbhayam \|*  
*bhādrasya śuklapañcamyāṃ pūjayedṛṣisattamān \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34a. The devotee should propitiate serpents with milk on the fifth day in the dark half of the month of Bhadra- pada, (thereby) the entire family upto the seventh generation shall be free from the fear of serpents.

34b. One should worship the excellent sages1 on the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Bhadrapada.

## \|\| 1.114.35 \|\|

*prātarnadyādike snātvā kṛtvā nityamatandritaḥ \|*  
*gṛhamāgatya yatnena vedikāṃ kārayenmṛdā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35.37a. In the morning, he should take his bath in the river etc. and perform Nitya rites, Sandhya prayers etc. He should then return home and make a platform with clay. He should smear and clean it with cowdung and decorate it with flowers. О Brahmana, he should then strew Kusa grass thereon and worship the seven sages, by means of scents, different flowers, incense and splendid lights.

## \|\| 1.114.37-39 \|\|

*gandhaiśca vividhaiḥ puṣpairdhūpairdīpaiḥ suśobhaneḥ \|*  
*kaśyapo 'trirbharadvājau viśvāmitro 'tha gautamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*jamadagnirvasiṣṭhaśca saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*etaibhyo 'ghya ca vidhivatkalpayitvā pradāya ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*naivedyaṃ vipacedvīmānśyāmākādyairakṛṣṭakaiḥ \|*  
*tannivedya visṛjyemānsvayaṃ cādyāttadeva hi \|\| 39 \|\|*

37b-39. The sages are Kasyaj a, Atri, Bharadvaja, Vish- vamitra, Gautama, Jamadagni and Vasistha. Arghya should be duly offered to these. The intelligent devotee should cook

## \|\| 1.114.40-41 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sapta varṣāṇi prativatsaram \|*  
*kṛtvā vratānte varayedācāryān sapta vaidikān \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pratimāḥ saptakurvīnta suvarṇena svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*jaṭilāḥ sākṣasūtrāśca kamaṇḍalusamanvitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. In this manner, he should perform this ^holy rite every year, for seven years. At the conclusion of the Vrata, he should choose seven Vedic scholars as his Acaryas (preceptors). He should make seven images in gold, according to his capacity. They must have matted hair, rosary and water pot.

## \|\| 1.114.42 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya kalaśeṣvetāṃstāmreṣu mṛnmayeṣu vā \|*  
*snāpayedvidhi vadbhaktyā pṛthakpañcāmṛtairapi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. These images should be placed in copper vessels or clay pots and the rite of ablution is performed severally with Pancamrta.

## \|\| 1.114.43-44 \|\|

*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*arghyaṃ datvā tato homaṃ tilavrīhiyavādibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ṭhasahastomā'iti ṛkhā nāmanantraistu vā pṛthak \|*  
*puṇyairmantraistathaivānyairhutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. With sixteen types of services and articles of worship, they are worshipped with devotion. Arghya is offered then, and the homa is performed with gingelly seeds, grains, or barley grains etc. The Rk. ‘Sahastoma (RV X.130.7) should be used while performing homa or the names of the sages shall themselves be the Mantras. Or with other holy mantras also the homa can be performed. Then the Purnahuti is offered.

## \|\| 1.114.45-46 \|\|

*tatastu sapta gā dadyādvastrālaṅkārasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*ācāryaṃ pūjayejjaiva vastrālaṅkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*anujñayā guroḥ paścānmūrtīrvipreṣu cārpayet \|*  
*bhojayitvā tu tānbhaktyā praṇipatya visarjayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. He should then give seven cows as gifts, fully bedecked in ornaments and clothes. He should worship his preceptor also with clothes, ornaments, etc. With the permission of the preceptor, he should thereafter dedicate the images unto the Brahmanas. After feeding them with devotion, he should bow down to them and bid them farewell.

## \|\| 1.114.47 \|\|

*tataśceṣṭaiḥ sahāsīnaḥ svayaṃ brāhmaṇaśeṣitam \|*  
*bhuṅktvā vai ṣaḍrasopetaṃ pramudyātsaha bandhubhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thereafter, the food left over by the Brahmanas consisting of articles of six different tastes should be taken by him along with kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.114.48 \|\|

*etatkṛtvā vrataṃ gāṅgaṃ bhogānbhuktvātha vāñchitān \|*  
*saptarṣīṇāṃ prasādena vimānavarago bhavet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After performing this holy rite with its ancillaries he shall enjoy all desired worldly pleasures, thanks to the grace of seven sages. He shall go hence in an excellent aerial car.

## \|\| 1.114.49-52 \|\|

*āśvine śuklapañcamyāmupāṅgalalitāvratam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ svarṇamayīṃ mūrtiṃ śaktyā nirmāya nārada \|*  
*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pūjayettāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*pakvānnaṃ phalasaṃyuktaṃ saghṛtaṃ dakṣiṇānvitam \|*  
*dvijavaryāya dātavyaṃ vratasaṃpūrtihetave \|\| 51 \|\|*

*"savāhanā śaktiyutā varadā pūjitā mayā \|*  
*mātarmāmanugṛhyātha gamyatāṃ nijamandiram \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. On the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Alvina, the holy rite ofUpanga-Lalita-Vrata1 is to be observed. О Narada, the image of the goddess should be made in gold in accordance with one’s ability. The devotee should worship her in accordance with the injunctions, with all the sixteen types of services. In order to make the Vrata perfect and complete, cooked rice alongwith fruits, ghee and monetary gifts should be given to an excellent Brahmana — “The boon-granting deity accompanied by Sakti has been worshipped by me alongwith her vehicle. О Mother, you may be pleased to go to your own abode after blessing me” (The foregoing is the final prayer).

## \|\| 1.114.53 \|\|

*kārtike śuklapañcamyāṃ jayāvratamanuttamam \|*  
*kartavyaṃ pāpanāśāya śraddhayā dvijasattama \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О excellent Brahmana, the holy rite of the excellent Jaya vrata is to be observed on the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Karttika with good faith, for the destruction of sins.

## \|\| 1.114.54-55 \|\|

*pūjayitvā jayāṃ vipra yathāvidhi samāhitaḥ \|*  
*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ śuciralaṅkṛtaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vipraikaṃ bhojayeccāpi tasmai dattvā ca dakṣiṇām \|*  
*visarjayettataḥ paścātsvayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. О Brahmana, the devotee should, with great concentration, worship Jaya according to injunction. Clean (in body and mind) and bedecked in ornaments, he should worship her with sixteen types of services. He should feed a single Brahmana and give him monetary gifts. Then he should bid farewell to him and himself partake of his food silently.

## \|\| 1.114.56 \|\|

*yastu vai bhaktisaṃyuktaḥ snānaṃ kuryāj jayādine \|*  
*naśyanti tasya pāpāni siṃhākrāntā mṛgā yathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If any one takes his holy dip on the day of Jaya, with great devotion, all his sins perish like dear attacked by a lion.

## \|\| 1.114.57 \|\|

*yadaśvamedhāvabhṛthe phalaṃ snānena kīrtitam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ prāpyate viprasnānenāpi jayādine \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О Brahmana, the fruit that has been glorified as the result of the Avabhrtha (concluding) bath in a horse sacrifice, is attained by bath on the day of Jaya.

## \|\| 1.114.58 \|\|

*aputro labhate putraṃ vandhyā gabha ca vindati \|*  
*rogī rogātpramucyeta baddho mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. One devoid of sons gets a son, a barren woman becomes pregnant, a sick man is freed from ailments and a prisoner is released from bondage.

## \|\| 1.114.59 \|\|

*mārgaśukle ca pañcamyāṃ nāgāniṣṭvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*nāgebhyo hyabhayaṃ labdhvā modate saha bāndhavaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. By worshipping serpents duly on the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Margaftrsa one attains fearlessness from serpents and rejoices alongwith the kinsmen.

## \|\| 1.114.60 \|\|

*pauṣe 'pi śuklapañcamyāṃ sampūjya madhusūdanam \|*  
*labhate bāñchitānkāmānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the month of Pau?a too, on the fifth day in the bright half, one attains all cherished desires by worshipping Madhusudana. No doubt need be entertained in this matter.

## \|\| 1.114.61 \|\|

*pañcamyāṃ pratimāse tu śukle kṛṣṇe ca nārada \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ pūjanaṃ śastaṃ nāgānāṃ cāpi sarvathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. О Narada, the worship of the Pitrs and the serpents on the fifth day in the bright or dark half of any month is recommended in every respect.

## Chapter 115. The Exposition of the holy vdws to be observed on Sap (hi (sixth) days (in lunar fortnights)

## \|\| 1.115.1 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca*  
*śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi ṣaṣṭhyāścaiva vratāni te \|*  
*yāni samyagvidhāyātra labhaghetsarvānmanorathān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatana said:

1\. О Brahmana, listen. I shall recount to you the holy rites to be observed on shasthl days1 (sixth day in the lunar fortnight). On observing them perfectly, one shall obtain all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.115.2-6 \|\|

*caitramāse śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ kumāravratamuttamam \|*  
*tatreṣṭvā ṣaṇmukhaṃ devaṃ nānāpūjā vidhānataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ prāpnuyāccirajīvinam \|*  
*vaiśākhaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca pūjayitvā ca kārtikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*labhate mātṛjaṃ saukhyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamāse śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ vidhineṣṭvā divākaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

*labhate vāñchitānkāmāṃstatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*āṣāḍhaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ vai skandavratamanuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*upoṣya pūjayitvainaṃ śivomāpriyamātmajam \|*  
*labhate 'bhīpsitānkāmānputrapautrādisaṃtatīḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
