21\. Hence no man shall glance at other’s women, or one’s own daughter or daughter-in-law with lustful eyes and thoughts. Immediately the man falls or incurs sins.

## \|\| 2.7.22-23 \|\|

*evaṃ sañcintayitvā ca sūkṣmāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*yadidaṃ vurtalaṃ vaktraṃ sonnataṃ dṛśyate śubham \|\| 22 \|\|*

*asthipañjarametaddhi carmamāṃsāvṛtaṃ tviti \|*  
*vasā medo'tha nayane sojvale strīṣu saṃsthite \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. It was because he thought over like this that he looked at her, with a subtle, penetrating view-point. It is nothing but a mere skeleton (lit. cage) of bones covered with flesh and skin that appears a face, lofty, circular and splendid. The shining eyes seen present in women comprise suet and flesh.

## \|\| 2.7.24 \|\|

*atyucchritamidaṃ māṃsaṃ stanayoḥ samavasthitam \|*  
*nimnāṃśatāṃ darśayati trivalī jaṭharasthitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The extremely protruding mass of flesh has been piled up over the breasts. The three folds of skin on the upper part of the belly (which are regarded as a mask of beauty) show lesser (distribution of) flesh.

## \|\| 2.7.25 \|\|

*punarevādhikaṃ kṣiptaṃ māṃsaṃ jaghanavartmani \|*  
*mūtradvāramidaṃ guhyaṃ yatra mugdhaṃ jagattrayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the buttocks again, more flesh has been stacked. This is the passage for urine. It is a private part, of which the three worlds are enamoured.

## \|\| 2.7.26 \|\|

*apānavāyunā juṣṭaṃ sadaiva pratikutsitam \|*  
*bhastrāvargādhikaṃ kṣiptaṃ māṃsaṃ jaghanavartmani \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is joined with the Apana wind (i.e. this wind functions there). It is always vile (with bad odour) and contemptible always. More flesh is heaped up than the swollen bellows in the part of the buttocks.

## \|\| 2.7.27 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ yadvaddvidhā kāṣṭhaṃ tadvajjaṅghā dvidhā dhruvam \|*

27\. Just as a log of wood is sawn into two (half way through), so also is the region of shanks (thighs?). It (the body) is filled with semen, flesh, bone, fat and marrow. How can it be beautiful?

## \|\| 2.7.28 \|\|

*māṃsamedovasāsāre kiṃ sāraṃ dehināṃ vada \|*

28\. What is there by way of essence, in the body of men wherein the main constituents are flesh, fat and marrow? Tell me which man will be enamoured of the body, nourished and grown plump by means of faeces, urine and other dirts.

## \|\| 2.7.29 \|\|

*evaṃ vicārya bahudhā viriñcarjñānacakṣuṣā \|*

29\. *Virinci* (God Brahma) pondered thus, after seeing everything with his vision of knowledge. He took courage and spoke to that lady whose gait was like that of a female elephant.

## \|\| 2.7.30 \|\|

*yathāhi manasā sṛṣṭā mayā tvaṃ varavarṇinī \|*

30\. “O fair-complexioned lady, since you have been created by me mentally you have become a lady of beautiful limbs, competent to madden the minds of men.”

## \|\| 2.7.31-34 \|\|

*tamuvāca tadā sā tu praṇamya caturānanam \|*  
*paśya mūrcchānvitaṃ nātha jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mohitaṃ mama rūpeṇa sayogi yadakalmaṣam \|*  
*sa nāsti triṣu lokeṣu yaḥ pumānmama darśanāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bhavantamāditaḥ kṛtvā na kṣobhaṃ yāti padmaja \|*  
*ātmastutirna kartavyā kenacicchubhamicchatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*stavanānnarakaṃ yāti viśuddho'pi ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi stavanaṃ brahman kartavyaṃ kāryahetunā \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-33a. Then she bowed to the fourfaced God and said: “O Lord, see the entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings deluded and falling unto senselessness. It includes even the Yogins who are totally sinless. О lotus-born deity, keeping you in the beginning (inclusive of you), there is no man in the three worlds who does not get agitated and perturbed on seeing me.

33b-34. Boasting about oneself should not be indulged in by one who wishes for one's own auspicious welfare. Even an extremely pure man falls into hell due to selfpraise. Still, О Brahma, the glorification or self-praise must be stated to achieve some special end.

## \|\| 2.7.35 \|\|

*sāhaṃ sṛṣṭā tvayā brahman kasyacitkṣobhaṇāya vai \|*  
*tamādiśa jagannātha kṣobhayiṣye na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О Brahma, indeed, it must be to make some one excited and perturbed that I have been created by you. О Lord of the Universe, command me. Mention who he is. I shall definitely make him excited.

## \|\| 2.7.36-37 \|\|

*māṃ dṛṣṭvāpi kṣitau deva bhūdharaścāpi muhyati \|*  
*kiṃ punaścetanopetaḥ śvāsocchvāsī narastviti \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tathā coktaṃ purāṇeṣu nārīvīkṣaṇavarṇanam \|*  
*unmādakaraṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ duścaravratanāśanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. О Lord, on seeing me even a mountain becomes infatuated. What then of an ordinary man endowed with consciousness who inhales and exhales? The description of the powerful impact of a woman’s glance is described in the Puranas. It causes madness in men and is destructive of all holy vows and rites difficult to be observed.

## \|\| 2.7.38 \|\|

*sanmārge tāvadāste prabhavati puruṣastāvadeveṃdri yāṇāṃ \|*  
*lajjāṃ tāvadvidhatte vinayamapi samālambate tāvadeva \|*  
*bhrūcāpākṣepayuktāḥ śravaṇapathagatā nīlapakṣmāṇa ete \|*  
*yāvallīlāvatīnāṃ na hṛdi dhṛtimuṣo dṛṣṭibāṇāḥ patanti \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Till then the man treads the path of the good, till then the man has perfect control over his sense organs, till then he retains his humility and sense of shame, till the shaft-like glances of dalliance-minded damsels pierce his heart and destroy his fortitude. The shafts that are discharged fiom the well-drawn bow of the eye-brow, the eyes having blue lashes, reach up to the cars.1

## \|\| 2.7.39 \|\|

*dhiktasya mūḍhamanasaḥ kukaveḥ kavitvaṃ \|*  
*yaḥ strīmukhaṃ ca śaśinaṃ ca samīkaroti \|*  
*bhrūkṣepavismitakaṭākṣanirīkṣitāni \|*  
*kopaprasādahasitāni kutaḥ śaśāṃke \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Fie upon the poetry of that stupid ill-informed poet who equates the face of a lady to the moon. Is there any of these in the moon — viz. the knittingof the eyebrow, the side- glances expressing the wounding look, fury, pleasure and laughter?

## \|\| 2.7.40 \|\|

*pītaṃ hi madyaṃ manujena nātha karoti mohaṃ suvicakṣaṇasya \|*  
*smṛtā ca dṛṣṭā yuvatī nareṇa vimohayedeva surādhikā hi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О Lord, only when it is drunk does the spirituous liquor cause delusion in the mind of a clever man. But a youthful maiden excites delusion even when she is seen or remembered by a man. So she is more powerful than the spirituous liquor.

## \|\| 2.7.41 \|\|

*mohanārthaṃ tvayā sṛṣṭā narāṇāṃ prapitāmaha \|*  
*tamādiśa jagannātha trailokyaṃ mohayāmyaham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О great grand sire of the world I have been created by you for fascinating men. Command me. Who is it? I shall enchant even the three worlds. Brahma said:

## \|\| 2.7.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca- satyamuktaṃ tvayā devi nāsādhyaṃ bhuvanatraye \|*  
*nāganāsoru subhage mattamātaṅgagāmini \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Lady with thighs like the trunk of an elephant, О fortunate one with the gait like that of an elephant in rut, the truth has been expressed by you. There is nothing that cannot be achieved by you in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.7.43 \|\|

*yā tvaṃ dūṣayase ceto mamāpi varavarṇini \|*  
*tanmayā sugṛhītaṃ tu kṛtaṃ jñānāṅkuśena hi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О fair-complexioned lady, you are defiling even my mind also although I control and steady it by means of the goad of perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 2.7.44 \|\|

*sā tvaṃ kathaṃ na lokānāṃ cetāṃsyapahariṣyasi \|*  
*satyametadviśālākṣi tava rūpaṃ vimohanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Such being your charm how then will you not captivate the minds of people? О large-eyed lady, truly your beauty of form is seductive.

## \|\| 2.7.45 \|\|

*sāmaraṃ hi jagatsarvaṃ niśceṣṭamapi lakṣaye \|*  
*yannimittaṃ mayā sṛṣṭā tatsādhaya varānane \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I find that the entire Universe including the immortal being, is motionless. О excellent-faced lady, achieve that for which you have been created.

## \|\| 2.7.46 \|\|

*vaidiśe nagare rājā nāmnā rukmāṅgadaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*yasya sandhyāvalī bhāryā tava rūpopamā śubhe \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О auspicious lady, on the earth, in the city of Vidisa1 there is a king named Rukmaiigada whose wife Sandhyavall is comparable to you in beauty.2

## \|\| 2.7.47 \|\|

*yasyāṃ dharmāṅgado jāto pituratyadhikaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*daśanāgāyutabalaḥ pratāpena raviryathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. His son Dharmahgada was born of her. The son surpasses the father. He is endowed with the strength of a hundred elephants. He is like the sun in exploits.

## \|\| 2.7.48-52 \|\|

*yaḥ kṣāntyā dharayā tulyo gāmbhīrye sāgaropamaḥ \|*  
*tejasā vahnivaddīptaḥ krodhe vaivasvatopamaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tyāge vairaucaniryadvadgatau hi pavanopamaḥ \|*  
*saumyatve śaśitulyastu rūpavān manmatho yathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*jīvabhārgavayostulyo yo nītau rājanandanaḥ \|*  
*pitrā bhuktaṃ samastaikaṃ jaṃbūdvīpaṃ varānane \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dharmāṅgadena dvīpāni sañjitānyaparāṇyapi \|*  
*pitrostu vrīḍayā yena na jñātaṃ pramadāsukham \|\| 51 \|\|*

*svayaṃ prāptāḥ parityaktā yena bhāryāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*yo na vākyādvicalate sahaiva hi piturgṛhe \|\| 52 \|\|*

48-52. In forbearance he is equal to the Earth; in profundity he is comparable to the ocean; like the fire, he shines with his brilliance, he is comparable to Vaivasvata Yama, God of Death in fury; he is like Bali in munificence; he is comparable to the wind god in mobility; in gentleness he is equal to the moon; he is as handsome as Manmatha the god of love; the prince is equal to Jiva (Brhaspati) and Bhargava (Sukra) (preceptors of Devas and Daityas) in statesmanship. О fair-faced lady, the entire Jambiidvlpa alone is enjoyed by his father (Rukmangada). But the other Dvipas (continents) are conquered by Dharmangada. He has not yet known the thrill of a contact with a youthful maiden due to his bashfulness. Thousands of women come to him of their own accord but they are avoided by him. He does not move astray from his pledged word.

## \|\| 2.7.53 \|\|

*yasya vai trīṇi subhage mātṝṇāṃ cāruhāsini \|*  
*śatāni kanakābhāse tvaviśeṣeṇa paśyati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О fortunate lady with sweet smiles, in his father’s house three hundred mothers look upon him equally without any difference in their affection, О lady with gold-like complexion!

## \|\| 2.7.54 \|\|

*tasya dharmapradhānasya putraratnāṃcitasya ca \|*  
*samīpaṃ gaccha cārvaṅiga mandare parvatottame \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О woman of beautiful limbs! On the excellent mount Mandara, approach the King to whom Dharma is of prominent importance and who is adorned with the jewel of a son.

## \|\| 2.7.55 \|\|

*tatra vatsyati rājā vai turageṇātivāhitaḥ \|*  
*tava gītena cārvaṅiga mohito'śva vihāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The king carried away to that place by his horse will stay there enamoured of your song, О woman of beautiful limbs, even leaving off his horse.

## \|\| 2.7.56-57 \|\|

*adhiruhya gireḥ pṛṣṭaṃ sa saṅgaṃ yāsyati tvayā \|*  
*tatra devi tvayā vācyaṃ militvā bhūbhujā tviha \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ahaṃ bhāryā bhaviṣyāmi tava rājanna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yadbravīmi hyahaṃ nātha tatkāryaṃ hi tvayā dhruvam \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Climbing on to the top of the mountain he will come into contact with you. On meeting the king there, О gentle lady, you must say thus: — О king, undoubtedly, I will become your wife. But О lord, whatever Isay must be definitely carried out by you.

## \|\| 2.7.58-62 \|\|

*mohitastava rūpeṇa tathaiva pratipadyate \|*  
*yatastaṃ śapathairdhṛtvā dakṣiṇena kareṇa vai \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vācyaḥ katipayaiḥ subhru dinairapagataistviti \|*  
*surate tava cārvaṅiga yadā mugdho hi lakṣyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tadā prahasya rājño vai smāraṇīyaṃ purā vacaḥ \|*  
*yastvayā śapatho rājankṛto madvākyapālane \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tatpālaya mahīpāla manye'ha samayastviti \|*  
*evamukte tvayā mugdho rājā vai satyagauravāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

*pālayāmi na sandeho brūhi kiṃ te dadāmyaham \|*  
*evamukte tu vacane tvayā vācyo varānane \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-62. Enamoured of your beauty the king will promise it to you. Thereupon, after a few days have elapsed you shall hold him by the right hand with imprecations. О woman of lovely eyebrows and charming limbs, when the king appears to be rapturously eager for cohabitation with you, you shall laughingly remind the king of his earlier words: “O King, you have sworn that you will abide by my word. Hence, О king, keep your promise. I think the time has now come for the same.” When this is said by you, the king will certainly say thus on account of the high value and importance of the promise. “There is no doubt about it, I shall keep it. Tell me what shall I give you?” When he replies thus, О auspicious fair-faced lady, Ruk- mangada, the king and father of Dharmangada must be addressed thus by you.

## \|\| 2.7.63-69 \|\|

*rukmāṅgado mahīpālo dharmāṅgadapitā śubhe \|*  
*nopavāsastvayā kāryo jātu vai harivāsare \|\| 63 \|\|*

*suratasraṃsakārī me hyupavāso bhavetpriya \|*  
*sumugdhāṃ yauvanopetāṃ svabhāryāṃ yo na sevate \|\| 64 \|\|*

*parvāpekṣī durācāraḥ sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*trirātramapaviddhāhaṃ tvayā bhūpa upoṣaṇāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

*nāhaṃ nimeṣamapyekaṃ sthātuṃ śaktā tvayā vinā \|*  
*śrāddhakāle tu samprāpte upāviṣṭairdvijaiḥ kila \|\| 66 \|\|*

*yācate saṅgamaṃ bhāryā yadi bhogyā tadaiva sā \|*  
*evaṃ sambodhyamāno'pi yadā rājā vacastava \|\| 67 \|\|*

*na kariṣyati cārvaṅiga tadā vācyaṃ paraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yadi na tyajase rājannupavāsaṃ harerdine \|\| 68 \|\|*

*svahastena śiraśchitvā svaputrasya varāsinā \|*  
*dharmāṅgadasya rājendra mamotsaṅge kṣipa svayam \|\| 69 \|\|*

63-68a. “Never should the fast be observed on the Ekadasi day of Hari. О my darling, your fast is St hindrance to my sexual intercourse with you. He who does not attend to his own wife who is charming and who is endowed with youthful virility, he who expects another opportunity (i.e. he who postpones) is a man of wicked actions. Certainly, he goes to hell. Due to your fasting, I am abandoned by you for three nights. But actually I am incapable of staying even a moment without you. When the time of Sraddha has come and the Brahmanas sit and wait (for the performance), if the wife solicits the husband for cohabitation, she must be enjoyed at the very same time.” О woman of sweet limbs, even after being urged thus, if the king does not carry out your request, you shall say thus thereafter:

68b-69. “O King if you do not abandon your fast on the day of Hari, cut off the head of your own son Dharmangada with an excellent sword, and place it on my lap.

## \|\| 2.7.70 \|\|

*yadyetanmatpriyaṃ tvaṃ hi na karoṣi mahīpate \|*  
*dharmakṣīṇo bhavān gantā narake nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О king if you do not carry out this loving wish of mine, you shall become deficient in virtue, merits and you will undoubtedly fall into hell.”

## \|\| 2.7.71-72 \|\|

*śrutvā tvadīyaṃ vacanaṃ varāṅgane \|*  
*na hiṃsyate prāṇasamaṃ ca putram \|*  
*saṅgṛhya vākyaṃ vasudhāmarāṇāṃ \|*  
*sambhokṣyate mādhavavāsare'sau \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tato jano yāsyati pūrvavacca \|*  
*yamāntikaṃ kiṅkarapāśabaddhaḥ \|*  
*lipipramāṇaṃ narakādhivāsī \|*  
*bhaviṣyate sādhu kṛtaṃ tvayā hi \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. О excellent lady, if, on hearing your words, he does not injure his son who is like his own vital breath unto him, he shall pay heed to the advice of the Brahmanas and shall take food on the day of Ekadasl. Thereupon, the people will go near Yama as before after being tied with ropes by the attendants. Taking the writing (of Chitragupta) as authority, there will be persons occupying hell. Thus what you do will be splendid.

## \|\| 2.7.73 \|\|

*atha yadi nihanti tanayaṃ rājā satyena saṃyutaḥ śrīmān \|*  
*niḥśeṣāmarapūjyaṃ vrajati padaṃ padmanābhasya \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Or if the glorious king, abiding by the promise, really kills his son he will go to the region of Padmanabha, that is worthy of being worshipped by the immortal beings wholly.

## Chapter 8. The description of Mount Mandara

## \|\| 2.8.1 \|\|

*sautiruvāca- sā śrutvā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ nārī kamalalocanā \|*  
*uvāca nāma me dehi yena gacchāmi mandiram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sauti said:

1\. On hearing the words of Brahma, that lotus-eyed woman said — “Give a name unto me with which I should go to Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 2.8.2 \|\|

*pitrā nāma prakartavyamapatyānāṃ jagatpate \|*  
*nāma pāpaharaṃ proktaṃ tatkuruṣva kuśadhvaja \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Lord of the Universe, children must be named by the father. The name is said to be destructive of sins. О Kusha- emblemedGod, kindly do so.” Brahma said:

## \|\| 2.8.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca- yasmādidaṃ jagatsarvaṃ tvayā sundari mohitam \|*  
*mohinī nāma te devi saguṇaṃ hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Since, О beautiful woman, the entire universe is enchanted by you. О gentle lady, Mohinl (enchantress) as your name shall be true to your attributes.

## \|\| 2.8.4 \|\|

*daśāvasthāgataḥ samyag darśanātte bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yadi prāpnoti vai subhru tvatsamparkaṃ sukhāvaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О woman of lovely eyebrows, if he comes into a pleasure-giving contact with you, thanks to a clear vision of yours, he will have to experience all the ten states of a love-lorn lover).

## \|\| 2.8.5 \|\|

*evamuktā varārohā praṇamya kamalāsanam \|*  
*vīkṣyamāṇāmarairmārge pratasthe mandarācalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On being thus commanded, the fair lady bowed down to the lotus-seated deity and set off to the mountain Mandara wistfully gazed at on the way by the immortal ones (gods).

## \|\| 2.8.6 \|\|

*tṛtīyena mūhūrtena samprāptā girimastakam \|*  
*yasya saṃveṣṭane nāgo vāsukirnahi pūryate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By the third Muhiirta (one Muhurta — =» 48 minutes) she reached the summit of the mountain. It had been impossible for Vasuki to go round it once (i.e. to encircle it bodily).1

## \|\| 2.8.7 \|\|

*yo dhṛto hariṇā pūrvaṃ mathito devadānavaiḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍlakṣayojanaḥ sindhuryasyāsau gahvaro bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It was this mountain that was formerly lifted up by Hari (in the form of Divine Tortoise) and used for churning (the milk ocean) by the Devas and Danavas. Sindhu (the ocean) which extends to six hundred thousand Yojanas is the deep pit made by this mountain.

## \|\| 2.8.8 \|\|

*kūrmadehena sampṛkto yo na bhinno girirmahān \|*  
*patatā yena rājendrā sindhorguhyaṃ pradarśitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This great mountain was not broken even when it rubbed against the physical body of the Divine Tortoise. О leading king, when it fell into the ocean all the hidden parts of the ocean were exposed by this mountain.

## \|\| 2.8.9 \|\|

*gataṃ brahmāṇḍamārgeṇa payo yasmādgirerdvijāḥ \|*  
*kūrmāsthi gharṣatā yena pāvako janito mahān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О Brahmanas, water gushed out from this mountain went up through the path of the Brahmanda (Cosmic Egg). Great fire was generated by this mountain due to attrition when it came into contact with the bony shell of the (Divine) Tortoise.

## \|\| 2.8.10 \|\|

*yasminsa vasate devaḥ saha bhūtairdigambaraḥ \|*  
*na devairdānavairvāpi dṛṣṭo yo hi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It is on this mountain that Lord Digambara (naked deity i.e. Siva) resides along with his goblins, but, О exellent Brahmanas, he is not visible either to the Devas or to the Danavas.

## \|\| 2.8.11 \|\|

*daśavarṣasahasrākhye kāle mahati gacchati \|*  
*keyūragharṣaṇe yena kṛtaṃ devasya cakriṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It was for a great period of time viz. ten thousand years that this mountain ground and rubbed the armlets of the discus-bearing Lord.1

## \|\| 2.8.12 \|\|

*ratnānāṃ mandiraṃ hyeṣa bahudhātusamanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This is a veritable mansion of jewels equipped with many kinds of minerals.

## \|\| 2.8.13 \|\|

*krīḍāvihāro'pi divaukasāṃ yastapasvināṃ yastapaso'pi hetuḥ \|*  
*surāṅganānāṃ rativarddhano yo ratnauṣadhīnāṃ prabhavo girirmahān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is the sporting ground of the heaven-dwellers; it is the place for penance of the sages, it enhances the zest of the divine maidens for sexual dalliance; this great mountain is the source of jewels and medicinal herbs.

## \|\| 2.8.14 \|\|

*daśaikasāhasramitaśca mūle tatsaṅkhyayā vistaratāṃ gato'sau \|*  
*dairghyeṇa tāvanti hi yojanāni trailokyayaṣṭīva samucchrito'sau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Its girth at the root is ten thousand Yojanas, its width at the top is also that much. With the length too being as many Yojanas, it rises up as the measuring rod of the three world.

## \|\| 2.8.15 \|\|

*sakāñcanai ratnamayaiśca śṛṅgaiḥ prakāśayanbhūmitalaṃ viyacca \|*  
*yasmingataḥ kaśyapanandano vai viraśmitāmeti vinaṣṭatejāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It illuminates the surface of the Earth and the sky by means of its golden peaks full ofjewels and gems. On reaching it the son of Kasyapa (i.e. Sun) loses his splendour. He becomes devoid of rays.

## \|\| 2.8.16-17 \|\|

*kāñcanākārabhūtāṅgaṃ sammprāptā kāñcanaprabhā \|*  
*sūryatejonihantāraṃ mandaraṃ tejasā svayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kurvatī nṛpakāmārthamupaviṣṭā śilātale \|*  
*nīlakāntimaye divye saptayojanavistṛte \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The lady of golden splendour reached the Man- dara mountain whose parts are the abodes of gold (ingots). Endowed with her own splendour she made the mountain Man- dara the destroyer of the brilliance of the sun, (i.e. surpass it) with her own lustre. For the purpose of exciting the lustful passion of the king, she sat on the rocky surface of the mountain that extended to seven Yojanas and that had a divine bluish splendour.

## \|\| 2.8.18 \|\|

*tasyāṃ śilāyāṃ rājendra liṅgaṃ tiṣṭhati kauliśam \|*  
*daśahasta pramāṇaṃ hi vistarādūrddhvasaṅkhyayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О leading king,1 there stands on that rocky surface an adamantine Linga, ten Hastas in height as well as in girth.

## \|\| 2.8.19 \|\|

*vṛṣaliṅgeti vikhyātaṃ prāsādābhrasamaṃ param \|*  
*tasminbālā dvijaśreṣṭhāścakre saṅgītamuttamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It is famous by the name of Vrsalinga. It appeared like a great palace among the clouds. О excellent Brahmanas that girl gave a sweet and excellent performance of music.

## \|\| 2.8.20 \|\|

*tantrītālasamāyuktaṃ klamahānikaraṃ param \|*  
*samīpavartinī tasya bhūtvā liṅgasya bhāminī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. That charming lady sat near that Linga and played on the strings of the lute beating time harmoniously. Her songs were exquisitely destructive of tedium.

## \|\| 2.8.21-22 \|\|

*mūrcchanātālasahitaṃ gāndhāradhvanisaṃyutam \|*  
*tasminpravṛtte rājendra gīte manmathavarddhane \|\| 21 \|\|*

*babhūva sthāvarāṇāṃ hi spṛhā tasminmunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*na ca daivaṃ na cādevaṃ gītaṃ tādṛgbabhūva ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. It had the Miircchana (the regulated rise and fall of sounds) and the Tala (beating time). It had the Gandhara note in its composition. О leading king (?), when the song that heightened passionate love flowed forth from her like this, О leading sages, even the immobile beings began to desire it. Neither divine nor non-divine music had ever been like that before.

## \|\| 2.8.23-24 \|\|

*mohinīmukhanirgītaṃ gītaṃ satvavimohanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śrutvaiva gītaṃ hi digambarastu tenaiva rūpeṇa varāṅganāyāḥ \|*  
*kāmāturo bhoktumanāścacāla tāṃ mohinīṃ pārvatidṛṣṭilajjaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On hearing that sweet note flowing out of the mouth of Mohini, the note that enchanted all living beings, Lord Siva became lustful and wanted to enjoy her in that very form of Digambara (nakedness). But, on being seen by Parvati he felt ashamed.

## Chapter 9. A dialogue between Rukmangada and Dharmatigada

## \|\| 2.9.1-3 \|\|

*sautiruvāca- rukmāṅgadastu rājendro bhuktvā bhogāṃstu mānuṣān \|*  
*sampūjya bahuśo devaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ harim \|\| 1 \|\|*

*datvā mūrdhni padaṃ viprāḥ śatrūṇāṃ raṇaśālinām \|*  
*kṛtvā śūnyaṃ yamapathaṃ jitvā vaivasvataṃ yamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vaikuṇṭhasya tu panthānaṃ sampūrṇaṃ mānavaiḥ kṛtam \|*  
*āhūya tanayaṃ kāle dharmāṅgadamabhāṣata \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sauti said:

1-3. О Brahmanas, the leading king Rukmangada enjoyed all human pleasure. In diverse ways he worshipped the yellow-robed Lord Hari. He had already plared his feet on the heads of his enemies who dared to fight him. By making the pathway leading to Yama’s land empty he conquered Yama, the son of Vivasvat (Sun). He made the path of Visnu’s world thronged with human beings. At the proper time, he called his son Dhannangada and spoke thus:

## \|\| 2.9.4 \|\|

*etāṃ vasumatīṃ putra vasupūrṇāṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*paripālaya vīryeṇa svadharme kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “O son, protect this earth full of wealth all round, with your own might. B~ firmly resolved in your own duties.

## \|\| 2.9.5 \|\|

*putre samarthe jāte yo rājyaṃ na pratipādayet \|*  
*tasya dharmastathā kīrtirvinaśyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If the father does not hand over the kingdom when the son has become competent, there is no doubt in this that his merits and fame perish.

## \|\| 2.9.6 \|\|

*samarthena ca putreṇa yo na yāti pitā sukham \|*  
*avaśyaṃ pātakī so'pi vijñeyo bhuvanatraye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The father who does not feel happiness, thanks to his efficient son, must be certainly known as the greatest sinner in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.9.7 \|\|

*piturbhārakṣamaḥ putro bhāraṃ nodvahate tu yaḥ \|*  
*māturuccāravajjāto dvijihvo viṣavarjitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The son who, after becoming strong enough to do so, does not take up the burden of his father, is no better than the excrement of his mother. He is a two-tongued serpent devoid of poison.

## \|\| 2.9.8 \|\|

*sa putro yo'dhikakhyātaḥ piturbhavati bhūtale \|*  
*prakāśayati sarvatra svakarairiva bhāskaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He is the real son who becomes more famous than the father on this Earth and illuminates the places like the sun with his rays.

## \|\| 2.9.9 \|\|

*putrāpanayajairduḥkhai rātrau jāgarti yatpitā \|*  
*sa putro narakaṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasamplavam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If the father keeps awake during the night due to the sorrow resulting from the misdemeanour of the son, the son stays in hell till the final dissolution of all living beings.

## \|\| 2.9.10 \|\|

*piturvacanamādṛtya sarvaṃ yaḥ kurute gṛhe \|*  
*sa yāti deva sāyujyaṃ stūyamāno divi sthitaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He who honours the words of his father and carries out his behests in the house, attains Sayujya with the deity, while he will be eulogised by the gods stationed in the heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.11 \|\|

*so'ha prajākṛte putra āsaktaḥ karmabhiḥ kṣitau \|*  
*na bhuktaṃ naiva suptaṃ tu svecchayā pālane sthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О son, as for me, I have been attracted by holy actions in the world for the sake of subjects. Stationed in the activity of protection (i.e. abiding by my duty as their protector) I have never enjoyed or slept of my own accord.

## \|\| 2.9.12 \|\|

*asamarthe tvayi suta na prāptaṃ hi mayā sukham \|*  
*viṣṇuvāsarabhoktṝṇāṃ nigrahe kṛtabuddhinā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О son, As long as you were unable to shoulder the responsibilities of the kingdom, ease and happiness was not attained by me, as I was determined to restrain those who partook of food on the day of Lord Visnu (i.e. on Ekadasi days).

## \|\| 2.9.13 \|\|

*kecicchaive sthitā mārge saure kecidvyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*viriñcimārgagāścānye pārvatyāśca sthitāḥ pare \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Among the people some (i.e. Saivites) followed the path of the devotees of Siva. Some abided by the path of the Sun, others were the followers of Brahma, while others (i.e. Shaktas) stood in the path of Parvatl.1

## \|\| 2.9.14-16 \|\|

*sāyaṃ ca prātarāsīnā agnihotre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*bālo yuvā vā vṛddho yā gurviṇī vā kumārikā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarogo vikalo vāpi na śaknoti hyupoṣitum \|*  
*ityevaṃ jalpitaṃ yaistu tānnirasya samantataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vacobhistu purāṇoktairvāsarairbahubhistvaham \|*  
*sambodhayitvā bahuśaḥ prajānāṃ sukhahetave \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. (Many excuses were offered by people for eating food on Ekadasi day). “In the morning and in the evening, we are sitting up and performing the Agnihotra (Fire-worship) rites. Moreover a small boy, a young man, an old man, a pregnant woman, a small girl, a sick man or a physically handicapped person cannot undertake a fast.” When people protested like this, I refuted them everywhere by means of words mentioned in the Puranas. I spent many days over this. For the purpose of abiding happiness of the subjects, I enlightened them in various ways.

## \|\| 2.9.17-18 \|\|

*nigṛhya tānharidine nirāhārānkaromi ca \|*  
*śāstradṛṣṭyā tu viduṣo mūrkhāndaṇḍanapūrvakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śāsayitvā kṛtāḥ sarve nirāhārā harerdine \|*  
*tena me na sukhaṃ kiñcidavalīḍhaṃ dharātale \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. I chastised them and made them desist from taking food. The scholars were made to refrain from food (on the authority of sacred scriptures (i.e. they were convinced that sacred texts prescribed the Ekadasi rite). The ignorant people were made to refrain from taking food by chastising them by means of deterrent punishment. Thus all were forced to observe fast on the day of Hari. Thereby being thus engaged I did not enjoy any personal happiness on the Earth.

## \|\| 2.9.19 \|\|

*kaccinna duḥkhena janānyojayetkila putraka \|*  
*svebhyo vāpi parebhyo vā yo rakṣecca prajā nṛpaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О dear son, the king who wishes to protect his subjects shall not inflict on them miseries from himself or from others (from his own people or officers or through enemies).

## \|\| 2.9.20 \|\|

*tasyāmī hyakṣayā lokāḥ purāṇeṣu prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*so'ha prajākṛte saumya saṃsthito nātmanaḥ kvacit \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. To such a king ever-lasting worlds have been declared (as a reward) in the Puranas. I exist for the sake of the subject О gentle boy, and never for myself.

## \|\| 2.9.21 \|\|

*saukhyamicchāmyahaṃ bhoktuṃ mṛgayādisamudbhavam \|*  
*na pānadyūtajaṃ putra kāmaye'ha kadācana \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I wish to enjoy the pleasures derived from hunting and other strenuous exercises. О son, I never desire the pleasures of drinking bouts and gambling.

## \|\| 2.9.22-23 \|\|

*eṣu sakto'cirātputra vināśaṃ yāti pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tvatprasādādahaṃ putra mṛgayā vyājato'dhunā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*girīnvanāni saritaḥ sarāṃsi vividhāni ca \|*  
*bhoktukāmaḥ priyānkāmāṃstvayi bhāraṃ niveśya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Dear son, a king indulging in these vices will perish ere long. Through your favour, my dear son, I wish now to roam about the mountains, forests, rivers and lakes of diverse kinds under the pretext of hunting. After entrusting you with the burden of kingdom, I am desirous of enjoying covetable pleasures.

## \|\| 2.9.24 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ yatsthitaṃ hṛdaye mama \|*  
*kṛte tava mahākīrtirakṛte narakasthitiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All these things which I had in my mind have been disclosed to you. If they are carried out, you will earn a great fame; if they are not done, you will fall into hell. Dharmangada said:

## \|\| 2.9.25 \|\|

*dharmāṃgada uvāca- sarvametatkariṣyāmi bhuṅkṣva bhogānmano'nugān \|*  
*gurvīṃ rājyadhuraṃ tāta tvadīyāmuddharāmyaham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “I shall do all these things. Enjoy the pleasures that appeal to your mind. О dear father, I shall bear the heavy burden of kingdom with pleasure.

## \|\| 2.9.26 \|\|

*nahi me'nya smṛto dharmastvadvākyakaraṇaṃ vinā \|*  
*piturvākyamakurvāṇaḥ kurvandharmānadho vrajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. No other holy virtue except the execution of your behest is acceptable to me. A son who does not act according to the directives of his father incurs fall, though he may be performing holy rites.

## \|\| 2.9.27 \|\|

*tasmātkariṣye vacanaṃ tvadīyaṃ prāñjali sthitaḥ \|*  
*evamukte tu vacane rājā hṛṣṭo babhūva ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, I shall carry out your order: Here have I joined my palms (in reverential promise).” When these words were spoken, the king became delighted.

## \|\| 2.9.28 \|\|

*gantukāmo mṛgānbhūyo labdhvā jñātvā vanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*dharmāṅgado'pi hṛṣṭātmā prajā āhūya cābravīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Learning again the availability of the game, Ruk- mangada became desirous of going to the forest. Dharmari- gada was delighted in his mind. He summoned his subjects and said:

## \|\| 2.9.29 \|\|

*pitrā niyukto bhavatāṃ pālanāya hitāya ca \|*  
*piturvākyaṃ mayā kāryaṃ sarvathā dharmamicchatā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “I have been commanded by my father to strive for your protection and welfare. My father’s behests must be carried out in every respect by me who wish for the attainment of Dharma.

## \|\| 2.9.30 \|\|

*nānyo hi dharmaḥ putrasya piturvākyaṃ vinā prajāḥ \|*  
*mayi daṇḍadhare śāstā na yamo bhavati kvacit \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О subjects, a son has no other Dharma (holy duty) except the execution of the directives of his father. When I hold the rod of justice, even Yama cannot be the chastiser.

## \|\| 2.9.31 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā tu yuṣmābhiḥ smartavyo garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*brahmārpaṇaprayogeṇa yajanīyo janārdanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After realising this, the Gannja-emblemed Lord (i.e. Visnu) should be remembered by you аЦ. Janardana is to be worshipped by you after dedicating the fruit thereof to the Brahman.

## \|\| 2.9.32 \|\|

*mamatvaṃ hi parityajya svajātivihitena ca \|*  
*ye na vo hyakṣayā lokā bhaveyurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You must eschew the sense of my-ness, and the feeling of possessiveness). You must worship in the manner laid down for your caste. Thereby, you will gain everlasting worlds. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.9.33 \|\|

*pitṛmārgādhiko hyeṣa bhavatāṃ darśitaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*brahmārpaṇakriyāyuktā bhavantu jñānakovidāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О subjects, something in addition to the path of mv father has been pointed out to you, since you will be endowed with the rite of dedicating the fruit to the Brahman. May all of you be adapts in perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 2.9.34 \|\|

*na bhoktavyaṃ haridine paitro mārgastu śāśvataḥ \|*  
*viśeṣo hi mayākhyāto bhavatāṃ brahmasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. You must not take food on the day of Hari. This is the permanent path in accordance with the injunction of my father. A special additional thing has been mentioned to you by me viz. abidance in the Brahman.

## \|\| 2.9.35 \|\|

*prayoktavyā ca tattvajñaiḥ punarāvṛttidurlabhā \|*  
*yadupoṣyaṃ haridinaṃ tadavaśyamiti sthitiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This adherence to the Brahman is to be practised by persons who know the truth. It is rare to be achieved. There is no return therefrom. As for the observance of the fast, the stipulation is that it must be observed necessarily.’

## \|\| 2.9.36 \|\|

*anunīya prajāḥ sarvāḥ samāśvāsya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*na divā na ca śarvaryāṃ śete dharmāṅgadaḥ sadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Dharmangada had no rest or sleep by day or at night. He spent his day in consoling and cajolling his subjects again and again.

## \|\| 2.9.37 \|\|

*sarvatra bhramate śauryātkurvanniṣkaṇṭakāṃ kṣitim \|*  
*paṭaho raṭate nityaṃ mṛgāriripumastake \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He used to tour everywhere, through his heroic valour. He weeded the earth of all the thorns (undesirable elements). The following loud proclamation used to be announced daily with the beating of drums placed on the heads of elephants:

## \|\| 2.9.38-41 \|\|

*abhuktvā dvādaśīṃ lokā mamatvena vivarjitāḥ \|*  
*trividheṣu ca kāryeṣu deveśaścintyatāṃ hariḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*havyakavyavaho devaḥ sa eva puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*sūrye yo hi kṛśākāśe visarge jagatāṃ patiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*smarttavyo manujaiḥ sarvairdharmakāmārthakāmukaiḥ \|*  
*svajātivihito'pyevaṃ sanmārge caiva mādhavaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sa eva bhoktā bhoktavyaḥ sa eva puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*viniyogastu tasyaiva sarvakarmasu yujyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. “O people of the world, may Hari the Lord of the Devas, be contemplated while engaged in the threefold activities (?) Refrain from taking food on the Dvadasi day; be free from the feeling of possessiveness. The Lord partakes of oblation offered to gods and manes. He alone is the Supreme person. The Lord of the worlds is to be remembered in the Sun, in the Krsakasa (in the minutest of Ethereal space) and in the Visarga (subsidiary creation) by all men who are desirous of accomplishing virtue, love and wealth. Worship of Visnu has been enjoined among the duties of one’s own caste. It is in the path of the good. Madhava himself is the Enjoyer and (the object of enjoyment. He alone is the supreme Man (Purusottama). Employment of him alone in all holy rites is the proper thing.

## \|\| 2.9.42-43 \|\|

*evaṃ raṭanti vipredrā ḥ! paṭahe meghaniḥsvane \|*  
*evaṃ dharmamavāpyātha pitā dharmāṅgadasya hi \|\| 42 \|\|*

*jñātvā putraṃ kriyopetamātmano hyadhikaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*uvāca bhāryāṃ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sthitāṃ lakṣmīmivāparām \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Thus it proclaimed to the people by means of beating of drums with the rumbling sound of the cloud, О leading Brahmanas. Thus the father of Dharmangada realised the virtue of his son. О Brahmanas, on realising that his son was equipped with the practical holy rites even more than himself, the delighted king said to his wife who stood there like another Laksmi.

## \|\| 2.9.44 \|\|

*sandhyāvali hyahaṃ dhanyastvaṃ cāpi varavarṇinī \|*  
*ubhayorjanitaḥ putraḥ śaśāṅkadhavalaḥ kṣitau \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “O fair-complexioned Sandhyavail, I am blessed. You too are blessed. To both of us is born as son white as the moon on the Earth.

## \|\| 2.9.45 \|\|

*karṇābhyāṃ śrūyate mokṣo na dṛṣṭaḥ kenacitkvacit \|*  
*so'smābhiradhikaṃ prāpto mokṣaḥ satputrasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Salvation has never been seen by anyone anywhere. Much about it has been heard by the ears. But the birth of our good son is the super-salvation that has been attained by us.

## \|\| 2.9.46 \|\|

*putre vinayasampanne vṛttaśauryasamanvite \|*  
*pratāpini varārohe piturmokṣo gṛhe dhruvam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О fair lady, if the son is richly endowed with humility, good conduct and heroism, if he is valorous, certainly it is salvation obtained by the father in his very house.

## \|\| 2.9.47 \|\|

*ānandaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śatānandaṃ sutena yaḥ \|*  
*pitā bhavati cārvaṅiga satkarmakaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Bliss is the form of the Brahman. Hundred such blisses are acquired by the father through his son, О woman of beautiful limbs, by his auspicious and holy rites.

## \|\| 2.9.48 \|\|

*naitatsāmyaṃ bhaveddevi loke sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*satputraḥ piturādāya bhāramudvahate tu yaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О gentle lady, there is nothing on a par with this in the whole world consisting of mobile and immobile beings, if the good son takes over the burden of his father and lifts it himself.

## \|\| 2.9.49 \|\|

*sau'ha gamiṣyāmi vanāya hṛṣṭo vihāraśīlo mṛgahiṃsanāya \|*  
*svecchācaraścātha viśālanetre vimuktapāpo janarakṣaṇāya \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. So, I am delighted now. I shall go to the forest for hunting the deer and have some good sports. О woman of wide eyes, I am freed of my sins by affording protection to the people. I shall now freely move about.

## Chapter 10. The dialogue between Rukmangada and Vamadeva

## \|\| 2.10.1-2 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca - tataḥ prāha viśālākṣī bharturvākyaṃ niśamya sā \|*  
*satyamuktaṃ tvayā rājanputrasaukhyātparaṃ sukham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*na bhavediha rājendra munīnāṃ bhāṣitaṃ yathā \|*  
*tulyaṃ bhavati loke'smin viṣṇvākhyasya parasya hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vasiffha continued:

1-2. On hearing the words of her husband, the wide-eyed lady said: “O king, the truth has been spoken by you. О leading king, just as the sages say, there cannot be a greater happiness than that of a son. In this world it is equal to that of the greatest being named Visnu.

## \|\| 2.10.3-4 \|\|

*putrebhārastvayā nyastaḥ saptadvīpasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*mārgī hiṃsāṃ parityajya yajñairiṣṭvā janārdanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhogaspṛhāṃ parityajya sevasya suranimnagām \|*  
*etannyāyyaṃ bhavati bho na nyāyyo mṛganigrahaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The burden of responsibility arising out of the administration of the seven continents has been placed on the son by you. Abstaining from the violence to the deer, worship Janardana by means of sacrifices; abandon desire for worldly pleasures; serve the celestial river; this is the proper and justifiable course of life to you but not the killing of the deer.

## \|\| 2.10.5 \|\|

*hṛdaye nakhapāto hi vṛddhāyā bhūpate yathā \|*  
*tathā viṣayasevā hi pitṝṇāṃ putriṇāṃ viduḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О king, resorting to worldly pleasures by fathers hav- ing grown up sons is like leaving the amorous marks with the nail on the breasts of an old woman.

## \|\| 2.10.6 \|\|

*gṛhe vāpi hṛṣīkeśaṃ pūjayasva mahīpate \|*  
*nirdoṣamṛgayūthānāṃ na yuktaṃ sūdanaṃ tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О ruler of the Earth, worship Lord Hisikesa (Visnu) in the house. It is not proper on your part to kill innocent herds of deer.

## \|\| 2.10.7-8 \|\|

*ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ purāṇe parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*hiṃsayā vartamānasya vyartho dharmmo bhavediti \|*  
*kurvannapi vṛthā dharmānyo hiṃsāmanuvartate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*parairupahatāṃ bhūpa nopabhuñjanti sādhavaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍvidhaṃ nṛpate proktaṃ vidvadbhirjīvaghātanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8a. Non-violence has been glorified as the greatest virtue in the Puranas. One who maintains himself through violence pursues holy rites in vain. He who follows the path of violence does not gain anything, even if he follows the righteous path. О king, good men do not enjoy those things polluted and hurt by others.

8b. Violence to living beings is said to be of six types, О king.

## \|\| 2.10.9 \|\|

*anumodayitā pūrvaṃ dvitīyo ghātakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*viśvāsakastṛtīyo'pi caturtho bhakṣakastathā \|*  
*pañcamaḥ pācakaḥ proktaḥ ṣaṣṭho bhūpātra vikrayī \|*  
*hiṃsayā saṃyutaṃ dharmamadharmaṃ ca vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The first man responsible for violence is the person who approves of it; the second one is the actual killer; the third one is the person who believes in it (who has faith in it); the fourth man (guilty) of violence is he who eats (the meat); the fifth man is the person who cooks and О king the sixth one is the person who is a participant in it. Learned men know the Dharma connected with violence is Adharma.

## \|\| 2.10.10 \|\|

*na pāpaṃ kurute bhūpa putre bhāraṃ niveśya vai \|*  
*dharmaṃ samāśrayansamyaksañjātapalitaḥ pitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О king, a father who resorts to Dharma and who has become old in age, does not commit sins after entrusting the burden to the son.

## \|\| 2.10.11 \|\|

*parityajya imaṃ bhāvaṃ mṛgahiṃsāsamudbhavam \|*  
*mṛgaśīlā hi rājāno vinaṣṭāḥ śataśo nṛpa \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Eschew the emotional feeling connected with the violence done to the deer. О king, hundreds of kings addicted to the vice of hunting deer have perished.

## \|\| 2.10.12-13 \|\|

*tasmādduṣṭaṃ hi tanmanye yadatra mṛgapātanam \|*  
*dayā varā mṛge rājñāṃ dharmiṇāmapi dṛśyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nivārito mayā hi tvaṃ hitabuddhyā punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ bhāryāṃ nṛpo vacanamabravīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Hence I consider the act of striking down deer as wickedness. Excellent deep sympathy and mercy towards deer is seen in the righteous kings. It is with the earnest desire for your welfare that you are being prevented by me.” To his wife who repeatedly urged thus, the king spoke these words:

## \|\| 2.10.14 \|\|

*nahi hiṃse mṛgāndevi mṛgavyājena kānane \|*  
*paryyaṭiṣye dhanuṣpāṇiḥ kurvankaṇṭakaśodhanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О gentle lady, I do not wish to hurt or kill the deer. Under the pretext of hunting deer, I will wander in the lorest weeding out thorns (undesirable element) with the bow kept ready in the hand.

## \|\| 2.10.15 \|\|

*janamadhye suto me'stu kānane'ha varānane \|*  
*śvāpadebhyaśca dasyubhyaḥ prajā rakṣyā mahībhṛtā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. May my son be among the people, О fairfaced lady, and may I be in the forest. The subjects must be protected from both the beasts of prey and the robbers, by the king.

## \|\| 2.10.16 \|\|

*ātmanāvātha putreṇa gopanīyāḥ prajā śubhe \|*  
*prajā arakṣannṛpatiḥ sadharmmo'pi vrajatyadhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О auspicious lady, the subjects must be protected by oneself or through one’s son. The king who does not protect his subjects faces downfall, though he may be virtuous or religious.

## \|\| 2.10.17-20 \|\|

*so'ha rakṣaṇamuddiśya gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ priye \|*  
*vimuktabhāvo'hamiti meruśṛṅge raviryathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*evamuddiśya tāṃ rājā āruroha hayottamam \|*  
*doṣāpatisamaprakhyaṃ nirdoṣaṃ kṣitibhūṣaṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devavāhasamaṃ rūpe prabhañjanasamaṃ jave \|*  
*dharāmādṛtya bhūpālo datvā taṃ dakṣiṇaṃ karam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sahasrakoṭidātāraṃ kāminīkucapīḍanam \|*  
*aśokapallavākāraṃ vajrāṅkuśavirohaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. О beloved lady, it is with the protection of people in view that I will be going to the forest. I am devoid of false emotions and feelings. After saying this to her, the king climbed on to an excellent horse like the sun on the peak of the Meru mountain. The horse was defectless, lustrous like the moon, and was as it were the ornament unto the Earth. It was like the celestial horse Uccaihsravas in respect ofits beauty; it was like the Wind God in its speed. Paying respect to the Earth the king offered his right hand (?) which had given gifts of thousands and crores, which used to press and rub the breasts of beautiful ladies, which had the shape and appearance of the tender sprouts of the Asoka tree and which bore the marks of a thunderbolt and goad.

## \|\| 2.10.21 \|\|

*sampratasthe mahīpālaścālayāno mahītalam \|*  
*sādhayāno yayau deśānkānanaṃ sa nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The ruler of the Earth set off on his journey making the ground quake (beneath him). The excellent king passing many lands reached the forest.

## \|\| 2.10.22 \|\|

*vājivegena nirddhūtā vāraṇāḥ syandanā hayāḥ \|*  
*padātayo nipetuste mūrcchitāḥ kṣitimaṇḍale \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Elephants, horses and chariots were shaken off due to the velocity of the horse. The foot soldiers fell unconscious on the surface of the Earth.

## \|\| 2.10.23 \|\|

*sa rājā sahasā prāpto munīnāmāśramaṃ param \|*  
*yojanānāṃ samuttīrya śatamaṣṭotaraṃ nṛpa \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О king, after traversing hundred and eight Yoja- nas (one Yojana = 12 kins.) that king all at once reached the great Asrama (hermitage) of the sages.

## \|\| 2.10.24-27 \|\|

*praviveśāśramaṃ ramyaṃ kadalīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitam \|*  
*aśokabakulopetaṃ punnāgasaralāvṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mātuliṅgaiḥ kapitthaiśca kharjūraiḥ panasādibhiḥ \|*  
*nārikelaistathā tālaiḥ ketakaiḥ siṃnduvārakaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*candanaiḥ satamālaiśca sālaiḥ pippalacampakaiḥ \|*  
*kramukairdāḍimaiścaiva dhātrīvṛkṣaiḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nimbavṛkṣaiśca bahuśastathāmrairlodhrapādapaiḥ \|*  
*paripakvaphalairnamraiḥ khagārūḍhaiḥ samāvṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. He entered the beautiful hermitage abounding in trees such as clusters of plantain trees, Asoka, Bakula Mimusops Elengi), Punnaga (nut-meg), Sarala (pine trees), Matulinga (citron trees), Kapittha (feronia elephantum), date palms, jack trees, \[coconut palms, palmyra, Ketakas, Sinduvaras, Sandalwoods, Tamalas (Xanlhochymus epictorius), Pippalas, Campakas, Areca palms, Dadimas (pomegranates), thousands of embylic myrobalans, margoas trees, mango trees, Lodhras (a tree with red-white flowers) and many other trees full of ripe fruits. They bent down due to the weight of fruits and many birds perched on them.

## \|\| 2.10.28-29 \|\|

*hṛdyena vāyunā yuktaṃ puṣpagandhāvṛtena hi \|*  
*paśyamāno muniṃ rājā dadarśa hutabhukprabham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vāmadevaṃ dvijavaraṃ bahuśiṣyasamāvṛtam \|*  
*avaruhya hayāddṛṣṭvā praṇanāma ca sādaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Sweet smelling wind gently blew, wafting the fragrance of the flowers. Searching for the sages therein the king saw Vamadeva1, the most excellent Brahmana who had the lustre of fire and who was surrounded by many disciples. On seeing him the king got down from his horse and bowed to him with great respect.

## \|\| 2.10.30 \|\|

*tenāpi muninā rājā hyarghādyairabhipūjitaḥ \|*  
*upaviśyāsane kauśe prāha saṃhṛṣṭayā girā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The king was honoured and greeted with Arghya and other things by that sage. Sitting on the Kusa grass scat he said in a delighted tone

## \|\| 2.10.31 \|\|

*adya me pātakaṃ kṣīṇaṃ samprāptaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tava padāmbhojaṃ samyagdhyānaparasya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “On seeing today the lotus-like feet of yours who are ever engrossed in deep meditation, my sins have been eliminated and fruition of my meritorious deeds has been achieved.’

## \|\| 2.10.32 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya rukmāṅgadamahīpateḥ \|*  
*saṃpṛṣṭvā kuśalaṃ prāha vāmadevo mudānvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing the words of king Rukmangada, sage Vamadeva rejoiced much. After enquiring about his health and welfare he said thus:

## \|\| 2.10.33 \|\|

*rājaṃstvayātipuṇyena viṣṇubhaktena vīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*mamāśramo mahābhāga puṇyo jāto dharātale \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О highly blessed king, my hermitage visited by you, a highly meritorious devotee ofVisnu, has become the most sanctified on the surface of the Earth.

## \|\| 2.10.34 \|\|

*kaste'nyastulyatāmeti pārthivo dharaṇītale \|*  
*yena vaivasvato mārgo bhagno nirjitya vai yamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Which other king on the Earth can attain equality with you by whom Yama has been vanquished and the path leading to his abode has been broken.

## \|\| 2.10.35 \|\|

*prāpitaḥ sakalo loko vaikuṇṭhaṃ padamavyayam \|*  
*upoṣayitvā nṛpate dvādaśīṃ pāpanāśinīm \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О king, by compelling them to observe fast on the Dvadasi day that is destructive of sins, the entire world has been Jed to the imperishable region of Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 2.10.36 \|\|

*caturbhiḥ śobhanopāyaiḥ prajāḥ saṃyamya bhūtale \|*  
*svakarmasthā vikarmasthā nītā madhubhidaḥ padam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After controlling and restraining the subjects on the surface of the Earth soundly through the four splendid Upayas (means of success, viz. Saman, dana, dantfa, bheda) they have been led to the region of the slayer of Madhu (i.e. of Visnu) whether they abide by their duties or carry on the duties of others.

## \|\| 2.10.37-38 \|\|

*so'smākaṃ dra ṣṭukāmānāṃ saṃprāpto darśanaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*śvapaco'pi mahīpāla viṣṇubhakto dvijādhikaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*viṣṇubhaktivihīnastu dvijo'pi śvapacādhikaḥ \|*  
*durlabhā bhūpa rājāno viṣṇubhaktā mahītale \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. О king, you have come within our view and we had been desirous of seeing you. О king, even a Candala who is a devotee of Visnu is superior to a Brahmana. Even a Brahmana devoid of devotion to Visnu is inferior to a Candala. О king, rare indeed are those kings who are devoted to Visnu on the surface of this Earth.

## \|\| 2.10.39-40 \|\|

*nāvaiṣṇavo bhavedrā jā kṣitilakṣmīprasādhakaḥ \|*  
*yo na rājā harerbhakto deveṣvanyeṣu bhaktimān \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yathā jāre patiṃ tyaktvā ratā strī sa tathā nṛpaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vyatikramastasya nṛpaterbhavati dhruvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. No king who is not a devotee of Visnu can be the person who embellishes the glory and splendour of the Earth. If the king is not devoted to Hari but is devoted to other Deities, that king is like a woman who has abandoned her husband and is attached to her paramour. Certainly this kind of adverse behaviour affects that king.

## \|\| 2.10.41-45 \|\|

*dharmasyārthasya kāmasya prajñāyāśca gaterapi \|*  
*tattvayā nyāyavihitaṃ kṛtaṃ viṣṇoḥ prapūjanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tena dhanyo'si nṛpate vayaṃ dhanyāstavekṣaṇāt \|*  
*ityevaṃ bhāṣamāṇaṃ tu vāmadevaṃ nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*uvācāvanato bhūtvā prakṛtyā vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*kṣāmaye tvā dvijaśreṣṭha nāhametādṛśo vibho \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tvatpādapāṃsunā tulyo nāhaṃ vipra bhavāmi hi \|*  
*na viprebhyo'dhikā devā bhavantīha kadācana \|\| 44 \|\|*

*parituṣṭairdvijairbhaktirjantorbhavati mādhave \|*  
*dveṣyo bhavati tai ruṣṭaiḥ satyametanmayeritam \|\| 45 \|\|*

41-43a. His behaviour will be contrary to virtue, wealth, love, intelligence and salvation. Hence, the worship of Visnu that is reasonably laid down has been performed by you. Hence, О king, you are blessed. We too are blessed since we have seen you. Even as Vamadeva spoke thus to him, the excellent king, naturally endowed with humility bowed down humbly and said:

43b-45. О excellent Brahmana, I crave your forgiveness, О holy Lord, I am not like this. О Brahmana, I am not equal to even the dust of your feet. Never can even the Devas be superior to Brahmanas. A creature (i.e. the individual soul) becomes devoted to Madhava through the Brahmanas who are satisfied. If they are furious he becomes worthy of being hated (by Madhava). This is the truth that has been stated by me.

## \|\| 2.10.46 \|\|

*tamāha vāmadevastu brūhi kiṃ te dadāmyaham \|*  
*nādeyaṃ vidyate rājangṛhāyātasya te'dhunā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Vamadcva then asked him — Tell me. What shall I give you? О king, there is nothing that cannot be given to you who have come to my house as my guest now.

## \|\| 2.10.47 \|\|

*abhīṣṭaṃ hi mahīpāla yo dadāti mahītale \|*  
*paṭahaṃ vāsare viṣṇoḥ prajābhojanavāraṇam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О king, if he gives anything on the earth, it must be that which is the most pleasing to him like the announcement through drums on the day of Visnu which prevents people from taking food.

## \|\| 2.10.48 \|\|

*tamāha nṛpatirvipraṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭastadā \|*  
*prāptameva mayā sarvaṃ tvadaṅighrayugalekṣaṇāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The king thereupon joined his palms in reverence and said to him — I have achieved everything by the sight of the pair of your feet.

## \|\| 2.10.49 \|\|

*mamaikaḥ saṃśayo brahman vartate bahukālataḥ \|*  
*taṃ pṛcchāmi dvijāgryaṃ tvāṃ sarvasandehabhañjanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О Brahmana, I have a doubt that has persisted for a long time. I am asking you the same since you are a leading Brahmana, who dispel all doubts.

## \|\| 2.10.50 \|\|

*trailokyasundarī bhāryā mama kena sukarmaṇā \|*  
*yā vilokayate dṛṣṭyā māṃ sadā manmathādhikam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. By what meritorious deed has my wife become the most beautiful lady in the three worlds. She looks upon me as though I am superior to Manmatha.

## \|\| 2.10.51 \|\|

*yatra yatra padaṃ devī dadāti varavarṇinī \|*  
*tatra tatra nidhānāni prakāśayati medinī \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Wherever the fair-complexioned gentle lady sets her foot, the earth reveals its great treasures.

## \|\| 2.10.52 \|\|

*yasyāścāṅgaṃ jarāhīnaṃ valīpalitavarjitam \|*  
*sadā bhāti muniśreṣṭha śāradenduprabhā yathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Her limbs are devoid of the symptoms of old age. There arc neither wrinkles nor greying hairs. О excellent sage she shines always like the lustre of the autumnal moon.

## \|\| 2.10.53 \|\|

*vināgnināpi sā vipra sādhayatyeva ṣaḍrasam \|*  
*annaṃ pacati yatsvalpaṃ tasminbhuñjanti koṭayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О Brahmana, even without fire she prepares dishes of six tastes. Grores of men take their meal out of the little quantity of food that she cooks.

## \|\| 2.10.54 \|\|

*pativratā dānaśīlā sarvabhūtasukhāvahā \|*  
*nāvajñā kriyate brahman vākyenāpi prasuptayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. She is a chaste woman. She is by nature munificent; she causes happiness to all living beings. О Brahmana, disrespect is not expressed by her through words even when she is asleep.

## \|\| 2.10.55 \|\|

*yasyāṃ jātastu tanayo mamājñāyāṃ sthitaḥ sadā \|*  
*ahameva dharāpṛṣṭhe putrī dvijavarottama \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. My son who is born of her abides by my behest always. О excellent one among the leading Brahmana, on the surface of this earth, I am the only one who have a son in the sense of the term.

## \|\| 2.10.56 \|\|

*yasya putraḥ piturbhakto hyadhiko guṇasañcayaiḥ \|*  
*ekadvīpapatiścāhaṃ vidito dharaṇītale \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. My son is a great devotee of his father. He surpasses me by means of his attributes. It is well known on the surface of the Earth that I am only the ruler of a single continent.

## \|\| 2.10.57-60 \|\|

*putro mamādhiko jātaḥ saptadvīpaprapālakaḥ \|*  
*madarthe yena viprendra samānītā nṛpātmajā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*vidyullekheti vikhyātā raṇe jitvā mahībhujaḥ \|*  
*atha tenādhipatinā rūpadra viṇaśālinā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmāsena raṇe jitvā kṛtvā sarvānnirāyudhān \|*  
*yo gatvā pramadārājyaṃ jitvā tāḥ pramadā raṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ājahāra śubhāstāsāṃ madhyādaṣṭau varāṅganāḥ \|*  
*pradadau mayi tāṃ sarvāṃ praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-58a. My son has surpassed me in this respect as he is the protector of all the seven continents. О leading Brahmana, for my sake, the princess well-known by the name of Vidyul- lekha, had been brought by him after conquering many kings in the battlefield.

58b-59a. In the course of six months that Lord equipped with the wealth of beauty conquered those kings and made them stripped of their weapons.

59b-60. He went to the realm of damsels and conquered them in the battle. He brought eight excellent ladies from among them with force and presented them to me with repeated obeisances.

## \|\| 2.10.61 \|\|

*yāni vāsāṃsi divyāni yāni ratnāni bhūtale \|*  
*tāni me pradadau putrau jananyā tūpavarṇitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Urged by his mother, my son brought and handed over to me the divine and exquisite garments and jewels on the surface of the Earth.

## \|\| 2.10.62 \|\|

*ekāhnā pṛthivīṃ sarvāmatītya bahuyojanām \|*  
*punarāyāti śarvaryāṃ matpādābhyaṅgakāraṇāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Within a day he takes a round of many Yojanas over the Earth and returns to me by nightfall for the purpose of massaging my feet.

## \|\| 2.10.63 \|\|

*niśīthe'ṅagāni saṃvāhya dvāri tiṣṭhati daṃśitaḥ \|*  
*prabodhayanpreṣyajanānnidra yā saṅkulendri yān \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After massaging my feet, he stands at the threshold at midnight with his coat of mail on. He wakens and pulls up the attendants and servants who are overwhelmed by drowsiness.

## \|\| 2.10.64 \|\|

*tathāyaṃ me muniśreṣṭha deho rogavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*aprameyaṃ mama sukhaṃ vaśagā hi priyā gṛhe \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. That is why, О excellent sage, this physical body of mine is free from sickness and ailments. My happiness is immeasurable. My beloved in the house is fully subservient to me.

## \|\| 2.10.65 \|\|

*vājino vāraṇāścaiva dhanadhānyamanantakam \|*  
*vartaṃte hi janaḥ sarvo mamājñāpālakaḥ kṣitau \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I have numerous horses and elephants. The food- grains and riches I possess are infinite. All the people on the Earth obey my behests.

## \|\| 2.10.66 \|\|

*kena karmaprabhāveṇa mamedaṃ sāmprataṃ sukham \|*  
*iha janmakṛtaṃ vāpi parajanmakṛtaṃ tathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. My present happiness is infinite. What is that meritorious action thanks to the power of which I possess it? Is it what has been performed in the course of this birth or the previous one?

## \|\| 2.10.67-68 \|\|

*mama puṇyaṃ vada brahman vicārya svamanīṣayā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*dehe na rogo vaśagā priyā ca gṛhe vibhūtirnṛharau ca bhaktiḥ \|*  
*vidvatsu pūjā dvijadānaśaktirmanye'hametatsukṛtaprasūtam \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. О Brahmana, recount to me about my merit after pondering over it in your mind. There is no ailment in the body; the beloved wife is submissive; there is affluence in the house, devotion to Hari and reverence to scholars as well as capacity to give liberally to the Brahmanas. I consider this as originating from my merits.

## Chapter 11. Rukmdngada meets Mohini

## \|\| 2.11.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- tacchrutvā nṛpatervākyaṃ mahājñānī munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*cintayitvā kṣaṇaṃ jñātvā kāraṇaṃ tamuvāca ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*Vasistha said:*

1\. On hearing the words of the king, the excellent sage of sound and perfect knowledge thought for a moment. He understood its real cause and said thus: — Vdmadevasaid:

## \|\| 2.11.2 \|\|

*vāmadeva uvāca- purā tvamavanīpāla śūdra jātisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*dāridra yṇe parābhūto duṣṭayā bhāryayā tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О king, formerly you were born of the Sudra caste.1 You were oppressed by poverty and harassed by a wicked wife.

## \|\| 2.11.3 \|\|

*parasevanayā caiva vetanena bhujikriyā \|*  
*nivasanduḥkhasantapto bahuvarṣāṇi pārthiva \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You sustained yourself by serving others and receiving wages. О king, thus you continued to live for many years, distressed due to misery.

## \|\| 2.11.4-5 \|\|

*kadāciddvijasaṃsargāttīrthayātrāṃ gato bhavān \|*  
*tataḥ sarvāṇi tīrthāni parikramya mahīpate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dvijasevāparo jāto mathurāṃ puṇyarūpiṇīm \|*  
*tatra snātaṃ tvayā viprasaṅgena yamunājale \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Thanks to your coming into contact with some Brahmanas, once, your honour went on a pilgrimage to holy centres. О king, after going over all holy centres you reached the holy centre Mathura and became interested in serving Brahmanas. There, in the company of Brahmanas, you took bath in the waters of the Yamuna.

## \|\| 2.11.6-8 \|\|

*viśrāntisaṃjñake tīrthe sarvatīrthottamottame \|*  
*mandire ca varāhasya kathyamānāṃ kathāṃ nṛpa \|\| 6 \|\|*

*purāṇoktāṃ ca śuśrāva aśūnyaśayanavratam \|*  
*caturbhiṃ pāraṇairyasya niṣpattistu vidhīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yena cīrṇena deveśo jīmūtābhaḥ prasīdati \|*  
*lakṣmībhartā jagannātho niḥśeṣāghaughanāśanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. At the holy centre named Vlfranti which is the most excellent of all holy centres, in the temple of the Divine Boar (Varaha), О king you heard the Puranic story being recounted. The holy riteof Aarnya Say ana, was being explained. As the Vrata is to be observed for four months on the 2nd tithi of the dark half of each month from Sravana onwards, there are, for the completion of the Vrata four paranas — one breaking of fast per month. Hence for its conclusion there are four Paranas (breaking of the fasts). By its observance the Lord of the Devas, Hari, with the lustrous complexion like the cloud who is the Lord of the worlds and the consort of goddess Laksmi and the destroyer of all sins, is pleased.

## \|\| 2.11.9 \|\|

*tatkṛtaṃ bhavatā rājanpunarabhyetya mandiram \|*  
*aśūnyaśayanaṃ puṇyaṃ gṛhe vṛddhikaraṃ param \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Coming again to the temple that holy rite was performed by your honour. This observance called ASunya- sayana (non-vacant bed) is highly conducive to prosperity at home.

## \|\| 2.11.10-11 \|\|

*akṛtvedaṃ mahārāja vrataṃ pātakanāśanam \|*  
*gārhasthyamanutiṣṭheta vandhyāvanniṣphalo bhavet \|*  
*sukhamīdṛgvidhaṃ loke durlabhaṃ pratibhāti me \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇasya tu māsasya dvitīyāyāṃ mahīpate \|*  
*grāhyametadvrataṃ puṇyaṃ janmamṛtyujarāpaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11a. If any one continues the life of a house-holder without observing this rite that destroys sins, О great king, his life is rendered fruitless like that of a barren woman. It appears to me that a happiness of this sort is very rare.

11b. О king, this holy rite must be undertaken on the Dvitiyaday in the month of Sravana.lt is destructive of rebirths, death and old age.

## \|\| 2.11.12 \|\|

*lakṣmīyukto jagannāthaḥ pūjanīyo'tra pārthiva \|*  
*phalaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpaiścāruraktānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*śayyādānairvastradānaistathā brāhmaṇabhojanaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О king, on this day the Lord of the Universe should be worshipped in the company ofLaksmi with fruits, flowers, incense, sweet-smelling red unguents, charitable gifts of beds and clothes as well as by feeding Brahmagas.

## \|\| 2.11.13 \|\|

*tattvayā sarvametaddhi kṛtaṃ rājansudustaram \|*  
*tasyaiva karmaṇaḥ puṣṭiraśūnyasya mahīpate \|*  
*imānevāgrataḥ puṇyāstvayoktānvistarācchṛṇu \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О king, everything of this Vrata has been performed by you though they were difficult. О king, this is the full fruition of the same holy rite called Agunya. Listen to the other sacred rites mentioned (or observed) by you in detail.

## \|\| 2.11.14 \|\|

*nāprasanne jagannāthe bhaveyuriti niścitam \|*  
*pūrvajanmani deveśastvayāśūnyena pūjitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It is certain that these results will not have taken place, if the Lord of the Universe had been displeased. The Lord of the Devas had been worshipped by you in the previous birth through the observance of Agunya rite. (Formerly this was mentioned as Ajoka Sayana, vide supra 1.111.13. In the region of the author of the NP a month is РйгртЛп1а Hence the word "dark half is not probably used.

## \|\| 2.11.15 \|\|

*iha janmani rājendra dvādaśyārcayase harim \|*  
*avaśyaṃ prāpyase rājan viṣṇoḥ sāyujyatāṃ dhruvam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О leading king, in this birth, you are worshipping Hari by means of the holy rite of Dvadasi. Surely you will attain the identity with Visnu.

## \|\| 2.11.16 \|\|

*eṣa praśno mayā rājanvyākhyātaste sumaṅgalaḥ \|*  
*sampadāṃ prabhavopeto jñāterutkarṣaṇārthakaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О king, thus your enquiry of auspicious nature has been explained by me regarding the origin of your affluence and leading to prosperity of your kinsmen.

## \|\| 2.11.17 \|\|

*kimanyatte mahīpāla dadāmīha karomi ca \|*  
*avaśyaṃ sarvayogyo'si bhakto'si tvaṃ janārdane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О king, what else shall I give you or do for you? By all means you are worthy of everything, as you are a devotee of Janardana. The king submitted: —

## \|\| 2.11.18 \|\|

*rājovāca- utsuko'ha dvijaśreṣṭha mandaraṃ parvataṃ prati \|*  
*tatrāścaryāṇyanekāni dra ṣṭukāmastavājñayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О excellent Brahmana, I am eagerly desirous of visiting the Mandara mountain. With your permission, I wish to see the various miraculous things there.

## \|\| 2.11.19-20 \|\|

*laghurbhūtvā guruṃ tyaktvā putropari dvijottama \|*  
*rājyaśāsanajaṃ bhāraṃ durvahaṃ yacca bhūmipaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*so'ha svecchācaro yāto matkṛtyaṃ tanayaścaret \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ rājño vāmadevo'bravīdidam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. О excellent Brahmana, after transferring the weighty burden of administering the kingdom that other kings find unbearable, to my son, I have become light(less burdened). I am free to roam about as I please. My duty will be looked after by my son. On hearing the words of the king, Vamadeva spoke thus:

## \|\| 2.11.21 \|\|

*etaddhi paramaṃ kṛtyaṃ putrasya nṛpapuṃgava \|*  
*yatkleśātpitaraṃ premṇā vimocayati sarvadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О prominent king, this is the highest duty of the son that he should always extricate his father from distress, out of affection.

## \|\| 2.11.22 \|\|

*piturvacanakārī ca manovākkāyaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāgīrathīsnānamahanyahani jāyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He who carries out the order of his father to the best of his mental, verbal and physical capacity, shall derive the benefit of having a holy dip in Gariga every day.

## \|\| 2.11.23 \|\|

*nirasya pitṛvākyaṃ tu vrajetsnātuṃ surāpagām \|*  
*no śuddhistasya putrasya itītthaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It is heard mentioned in the Vedic text that if the son goes to Ganga for a holy dip against the expressed desire of his father, he will not attain the usual purity and sanctity.

## \|\| 2.11.24 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ gaccha yathākāmaṃ kṛtakṛtyo'si bhūpate \|*  
*hariprasādātte jāto vaṃśe putraḥ sa puṇyakṛt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О king, you are contented and blessed. Go as you please. Thanks to the favour of Hari, a meritorious son has been born in your family.

## \|\| 2.11.25 \|\|

*evamukte tu muninā samāruhya turaṅgamam \|*  
*yayau śīghragatiḥ śrīmānsadāgatiriva svayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After this had been spoken by the sage, the glorious king mounted his horse and rode swiftly like the Wind God himself.

## \|\| 2.11.26-30 \|\|

*vīkṣyamāṇo girīnsarvānvanāni saritastathā \|*  
*sarvāścaryāṇi rājendra ḥ! sarāṃsyupavanāni ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*so'cireṇaiva kālena samprāpto mandarācalam \|*  
*bhrāmayitvā giriṃ śvetaṃ gandhamādanameva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*atītya ca mahāmeruṃ dṛṣṭvā caivottarānkurun \|*  
*śatasūryapratīkāśaṃ sarvataḥ kāṃcanā vṛtam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*saṅghṛṣṭaṃ haribāhubhyāṃ sravantaṃ kāñcanaṃ rasam \|*  
*tadbhūbhāgaṃ nagākīrṇaṃ bahudhātuvibhūṣitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bahunirjharasaṃyuktaṃ bahukandarabhūṣitam \|*  
*nimnagāyutasampūrṇaṃ dhautaṃ gaṅgājalaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-2 7a. Looking at and observing all the mountains, forests, rivers and the wonderful lakes and parks, the king ere long reached the mountain Mandara.

27b-28a. On his way he went round the white mountain 4GandhamadanaV crossed the Mahameru and saw the northern Kurus.

28b-30. He reached the Mandara mountain refulgent with the splendour of a hundred suns and covered in gold all round. On being rubbed with the hands of Hari it had generated liquid gold. The whole region there was full of trees and decorated with many metals and minerals. With many fountains over it, it was embellished with many caves. It was full of ten thousand rivers and was washed by the auspicious waters of the river Ganga.

## \|\| 2.11.31-33 \|\|

*viśvastairyuvatīvṛndaiḥ kāntāśarmopasevibhiḥ \|*  
*ghaṭapramāṇairnṛpate paripakvaiḥ sugandhiṃbhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*phalairyuvatisambhūtaiḥ kucairiva vibhūṣitam \|*  
*dvirephadhvanisaṃyuktaṃ kokilasvaranāditam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*anekasattvavirutaiḥ samantānnāditaṃ girim \|*  
*saṃpaśyamāno nṛpatirviveśa sa mahāgirim \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-32a. It was frequented by bevies of youthful maidens with rendezvous for serving their lovers. The mountain was adorned with ripe, sweet smelling, potlike big fruits of trees which resembled the breasts of youthful damsels.

32b-33. The place was resonant with the buzzing sound of the bees and was reverberating with the cooing of cuckoos. On seeing the mountain resound with the cries of many living beings all round, the king entered the great mountain.

## \|\| 2.11.34-35 \|\|

*āroḍhukāmastu kutūhalāttamanveṣayankena pathā praroham \|*  
*sa vīkṣate yāvadasau samantāttāvatsamastaṃ drumapakṣisaṃgham \|\| 34 \|\|*

*visarpamāṇaṃ dhvaninā gṛhītaṃ vimohinīvaktrasamudbhavena \|*  
*upaplavantaṃ tarasā mahīpastenaiva sārddhaṃ sa jagāma tūrṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. He desired to climb on to the top of the mountain. He was curious to find out the path whereby he could climb up. As he spied allround, he saw flocks of birds from the trees moving out attracted by the charming voice of an enchanting lady. He saw the birds flying quickly over the trees and he too went swiftly alongwith them.

## \|\| 2.11.36-37 \|\|

*tasyā'pi karṇe dhvanirāviveśa vimohinīvaktrasamadbhavo yaḥ \|*  
*vimohito yena vimucya vāhaṃ trivikrameṇeva vilaṅghyamānam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*mārgaṃ girermohinigītamugdhaṃ kṣaṇena rājā sahasā dadarśa \|*  
*girau sthitāṃ taptasuvarṇabhāsaṃ kāmasya yaṣṭīmiva nirmitāṃ ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The enchantingly sweet sound coming out of the mouth of that bewitching beauty entered his ears also. Fascinated by it, he left off his horse that had crossed the path as if in three steps. The whole path of the mountain was spell-bound by the sweet song of the enchantress. Instantaneously, the king saw a lady stationed on the mountain. She had the lustre of molten gold. She was created like the staff of Kama.

## \|\| 2.11.38-40 \|\|

*śakrasya liṅgaṃ gagane prasaktaṃ sampūjayantīmiva lokasūtyai \|*  
*kṣamāsvarūpāmiva vai rasāyā gireḥ sutāyā iva rūparāśim \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sindhostu velāmiva rūpayuktāṃ tasyāstanuṃ vai ratimandirākhyām \|*  
*vikarṣamāṇāṃ sahasā trinetraṃ liṅgāśrayaṃ devavinodanārtham \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tatpuṇyakartturmanasābhilāṣāṃ vyavasthito mohinirūpadarśī \|*  
*vimohito'sau nipapāta rājā vimohinīkāmaśareṇa viddhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. She was worshipping the Linga that rose high into the sky, for the welfare of the world. She was like the embodied form of the Earth and she was as it were the culmination of beauty like a Parvati, the daughter of the mountain Himalaya. She had the beauteous form of the seashore. Her body could be called the very mansion of sexual pleasure. She appeared to drag even the three-eyed lord stationed in the Linga, suddenly for the pleasure of the Lord. She was the personified form of the mental wish of a meritorious person. On seeing the beautiful form ofMohinl, the king was enamoured by the enchanting arrows of the god of love and the king fell down senselessly.

## \|\| 2.11.41 \|\|

*jvareṇa tīvreṇa gṛhītadehaḥ samīpamasyāḥ sa sasarpa śīghram \|*  
*visarpiṇaṃ bhūmipatiṃ sunetrā vilokayāmāsa kaṭākṣadṛṣṭyā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Regaining consciousness again as if his body was seized with a very high fever, he moved swiftly to her presence. The lady of beautiful eyes noted the approaching king with her side-glances.

## \|\| 2.11.42-44 \|\|

*vimucya vīṇāṃ virarāma gītātprāptaṃ ca kāryaṃ sahasaiva mene \|*  
*vidhūnayantī mṛgapakṣisaṅghānsuvāsasā gaṇḍabhujau nivārya \|\| 42 \|\|*

*śilīmukhān śvāsasugandhamugdhān jagāma devī nṛpateḥ samīpam \|*  
*tyaktvā haraṃ pūjyatamaṃ suliṅgaṃ gatvā tu pārśve tamudāraceṣṭā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vimohinī nīrajapatranetrā uvāca vākyaṃ madhuraṃ manojñam \|*  
*rukmāṅgadaṃ kāmaśarābhitaptamuttiṣṭha rājanvaśagā tavāham \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. She stopped singing and kept lute aside. She thought of her duties for the occasion. She drove off the flocks and herds of birds and animals. She covered her cheeks and arms with a fine cloth. She shook off the bees that were attracted by the fragrance of her breath. The gentle lady then went near the king after leaving off the worship-worthy Linga. After going near him, the enchanting lady of elegant movements and eyes like the petals of the lotus spoke these sweet words to Rukman- gada who had already been scorched by the arrows of Kama — О king, get up, I am under your control.

## \|\| 2.11.45-47 \|\|

*kiṃ mūrcchayā dehamimaṃ kṣiṇoṣi yastvaṃ dharābhāramimaṃ mahāntam \|*  
*tṛṇīkṛtaṃ bhūpa samudvahethā yanmāmakaṃ rūpamavekṣya hāri \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kiṃ muhyase durbalagauriveha paṅke nimagnā sudṛḍho bhava tvam \|*  
*dhīro'si vīro'si viḍambayethāḥ kimarthamātmānamudāraceṣṭam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yadyasti vāñchā tava bhūpatīśa mamānukūle surate'tihṛdye \|*  
*pradāya dānaṃ ca sudharmayuktaṃ bhuṅkṣva svadāsīmiva māṃ ratijñām \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Why do you waste this body of yours by falling in a swoon. You are a person who bear the burden of the Earth as though it was only a blade of grass. Why do you, on seeing my enchanting form, lose sense, like a weak cow sinking beneath the mire? Be steady and firm. You are bold. You are a brave warrior. Why do you make yourself ridiculous? You of elegant activities. О Lord of kings, if you have any desire to have extremely pleasant and favourable sexual intercourse with me as a willing partner, after giving charitable gifts with due rites, you' can do so. You can freely enjoy me like your own slave. I am an adept in the sexual act.

## Chapter 12. Stipulation of the conditions

## \|\| 2.12.1-3 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- vyāhṛte śobhane vākye mohinyā nṛpatistadā \|*  
*unmīlya netre rājendra śatapatranibhe tathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sagadgadamuvācedaṃ mugdho mohinidarśanāt \|*  
*mayā bāle subahuśaḥ pūrṇacandra nibhānanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭāstathānubhūtāśca nedṛgdṛṣṭaṃ vapuḥ kvacit \|*  
*yādṛśaṃ tvaṃ dhārayase rūpaṃ lokavimohanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vasistha said:

1-3. When these splendid words were uttered by MohinI, the leading king opened his eyes resembling a lotus. Deluded by the sight of Mohini, he uttered the following words in a faltering tone “O young woman, many ladies with faces like the full moon have been seen and enjoyed by me. But I have never seen such a beautiful person like yours; such personal beauty as you have, fascinates the whole world.

## \|\| 2.12.4 \|\|

*so'ha darśanamātreṇa tvadīyena varānane \|*  
*manobhavaśarairviddhaḥ patitaḥ sahasā kṣitau \|*  
*ajalpitavaco devi mohitastava tejasā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О fair-faced lady, by your sheer sight I have been struck and hit by the arrows of Cupid. I have suddenly fallen on the Earth. О gentle lady, I prattled much on being fascinated by your brilliance.

## \|\| 2.12.5 \|\|

*kuru prasādaṃ karabhoru mahyaṃ dāsyāmi sarvaṃ tava cittasaṃstham \|*  
*nādeyamastīha jagattraye'pi tavānurāgeṇa nibaddhacetasaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О lady of beautiful thighs resembling the trunk of an elephant, be favourable to me. I shall grant you whatever you have in mind. My mind has been bound by your love and as such there is nothing in the three worlds that is not worth giving to you.

## \|\| 2.12.6-7 \|\|

*imāṃ dharāṃ bhūdharabhūṣitāṅgīṃ samudra vastrāṃ śaśisūryanetrām \|*  
*ghanastanīṃ vyomasubaddhadehāṃ niṣkānanāṃ sundari vāmaśīlām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pātālaguhyāṃ bahuvṛkṣaromṇadyaṃ saptādharāṃ subhru tavāsmi dātā \|*  
*sakośabaddhāṃ gajavājipūrṇāṃ samantrihṛdyāṃ nagaraiḥ sametām \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. О lady of beautiful eyebrows, lam ready to give you this entire Earth whose limbs are bedecked in the mountains, whose garments are the oceans, whose eyes are the moon and the sun, whose bosom are the clouds (or is supple and firm), whose body is well set with the firmament (?), whose face is a gold coin, whose nature is beautiful, whose private parts are the nether worlds, whose hair is constituted by many trees and who has seven mountain lips (?). О beautiful lady I will give you the Earth alongwith my treasury, elephants, horses and cities accompanied by the ministers and therefore hearty.

## \|\| 2.12.8 \|\|

*ātmānamapi dāsyāmi tava cārvaṅiga saṅgame \|*  
*kiṃ punarddhanaratnādi prasīda mama mohini \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Mohin! of charming limbs, for a contact with you I will give even my soul; what then about wealth, gems etc? Be favourable to me.

## \|\| 2.12.9 \|\|

*nṛpasya vacanaṃ śrutvā mohinī madhurākṣaram \|*  
*samuvāca smitaṃ kṛtvā tamutthāpya nṛpaṃ tadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing the words of the king Mohini smiled, raised the king up and said in sweet voice.

## \|\| 2.12.10 \|\|

*na dharāṃ bhūdharopetāṃ varaye vasudhādhipa \|*  
*yadvadiṣyāmyahaṃ kāle tatkāryamaviśaṅkayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О king, I do not wish to choose the Earth along- with the mountains and oceans.. Whatever I say on a certain occasion must be carried out without hesitation.

## \|\| 2.12.11-12 \|\|

*bhajiṣyāmi na sandehaḥ kuruṣva samayaṃ mama \|*  
*rājovāca- yena santuṣyase devi samayaṃ taṃ karomyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*daśāvasthāṃ gato deho mama tvatsaṅgamaṃ vinā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. I will resort to you. There is no doubt about it. Enter into this agreement with me. The king said: О gentle lady, I will enter into that agreement whereby you shall be satisfied. For want of the sexual contact with you my body has attained well nigh the tenth state (of a loveborn person). Mohini said:

## \|\| 2.12.13 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- dīyatāṃ dakṣiṇo hasto bahudharmakarastava \|*  
*yena me pratyayo rājan vacane tāvake bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Give unto me your right hand that has practised many holy rites, whereby I will be able to believe in your words, О king.

## \|\| 2.12.14 \|\|

*rājā tvaṃ dharmaśīlo'si satyakīrtirjagattraye \|*  
*na vaktāsyanṛtaṃ kāle mārgo'ya laukikaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. You are a king. You practise religious and holy rites regularly. You have won fame for truthfulness in the three worlds. You will never utter a lie on any occasion. Still this is a worldly convention of making you promise which has been followed by you.

## \|\| 2.12.15 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ rājendro mohinīṃ hṛcchayāturaḥ \|*  
*abravīnnṛpatistāṃ tu suprasannamanā nṛpa \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When Mohini said these words, the king who was overwhelmed with mental agony said with a delighted heart.

## \|\| 2.12.16 \|\|

*janmaprabhṛti vāmoru nānṛtaṃ bhāṣitaṃ mayā \|*  
*svaireṣvapi vihāreṣu kadāpi varavarṇini \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О beautiful lady, I have never uttered a lie since my birth. О fair-complexioned lady, even in the course of fun and sports I have never spoken a lie.

## \|\| 2.12.17 \|\|

*athavā vyāhṛtairvākyaiḥ kimebhiḥ pratyayākṣaraiḥ \|*  
*datto hyeṣa mayā hasto dakṣiṇaḥ puṇyalāñchanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Or of what avail are these words uttered by me by way of convincing you in so many words? Look that my right hand, marked by merits, is offered to you.

## \|\| 2.12.18 \|\|

*yanmayā sukṛtaṃ kiñcitkṛtamājanma sundari \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ tava vāmoru yadikuryānna te vacaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О beautiful woman, of lovely thighs, if I do not carry out your words, whatever merit has been accumulated by me ever since my birth shall become yours.

## \|\| 2.12.19 \|\|

*antare hyeṣa datto me dharmo bhāryā bhavāṅgane \|*
