*tava rūpeṇa me kṣobhaḥ sahasā pratyupasthitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. (In case I fail to carry out your words) my virtue and piety have been given in exchange to you. О lady become my wife. I have been forcibly and extremely perturbed and excited by your beauty.

## \|\| 2.12.20 \|\|

*ṛtadhvajasutaścāhaṃ nāmnā rukmāṅgado nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākuvaśasambhūtaḥ suto dharmāṅgado mama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I am a king by name Rukmangada, the son of Rtadhvaja, born in the race of Iksvaku. Dharmarigada is my son.

## \|\| 2.12.21 \|\|

*mṛgavyājena gahanaṃ praviṣṭaścārulocane \|*  
*tato dṛṣṭo vane hṛdyo vāmadevāśramo mayā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О lady of charming eyes, under the pretext of hunting the deer, I have entered the forest. Then the pleasant hermitage of Vamadeva was seen by me.

## \|\| 2.12.22 \|\|

*muninā jalpitaṃ tatra kiñcit tena visarjitaḥ \|*  
*āruhya vāhanaśreṣṭhaṃ mandaraṃ dra ṣṭumāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Something was mentioned by that sage. Thereafter I was bid adieu by him. Riding on my excellent horse I came here to see mount Mandara.

## \|\| 2.12.23 \|\|

*bhramamāṇo girivaraṃ kutūhalamanāstadā \|*  
*prāptaṃ macchravaṇe gītaṃ tava vaktravinirgatam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With my mind curious and enthusiastic I was roaming over the excellent mountain, when the sweet song emanating from your mouth reached my ears.

## \|\| 2.12.24 \|\|

*tena gītena cākṛṣṭastvatsamīpamupāgataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭeḥ pathamanuprāptā mama tvaṃ cārulocane \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Attracted by that song, I have approached you, О lady of charming eyes, you have come within the range of my vision.

## \|\| 2.12.25 \|\|

*tato'ha mūrcchito devi visaṃjñaḥ patitaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*samprataṃ cetanāyuktastava vākyāmṛtena hi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thereafter, О gentle lady, I fell unconscious on the ground. Now I have regained consciousness, thanks to your nectarine words.

## \|\| 2.12.26 \|\|

*punarjātamivātmānaṃ manye'ha lokamohini \|*  
*pratyuttarapradānena prasādaṃ karttumarhasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О enchantress of the worlds, I consider myself as a person born again. It behoves you to favour me by replying to me suitably.

## \|\| 2.12.27 \|\|

*nṛpeṇaivaṃ samuddiṣṭā mohinyāhottaraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ brahmabhavā rājaṃstvadarthaṃ samupāgatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On being requested by the king thus, Mohinl spoke in reply: — О king, I am born of God Brahma and have come here for your sake.

## \|\| 2.12.28 \|\|

*śrutvā kīrtiṃ smaropetā mandaraṃ kanakācalam \|*  
*parityajya surānsarvānviśvambharapurogamān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing about your fame, I was overwhelmed by Cupid. I have forsaken all gods, the chief of whom was Indra, and come to the golden mountain of Mandara.

## \|\| 2.12.29 \|\|

*samāhitamanāstvatra tapasyāniratā sthitā \|*  
*sampūjayantī deveśaṃ gītadānena śaṅkaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With my mind in concentration, I stayed here engaged in penance. I am worshipping God Sankara, the Lord of the Devas, by offering (singing) songs unto him.

## \|\| 2.12.30 \|\|

*gītadānamahaṃ manye surāṇāmativallabham \|*  
*sarvadānādhikaṃ bhūpa hyanantagatidāyakam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I consider presentation of music is the great favourite of the deities. О king, it is superior to all other Danas (charitable gifts) and it is the bestower of endless salvation.

## \|\| 2.12.31-32 \|\|

*yena tuṣṭaḥ paśupatiḥ sadyaḥ pratyupakārakaḥ \|*  
*īpsito'ya mayā prāpto bhavānavanipālakaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*abhiprīto'si me rājannabhiprītā hyahaṃ tava \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Pasupati (god Siva) is satisfied with it and has immediately granted me the boon. You, (he king of the Earth have been attained by me and this was what I had liked. О king you are loved by me and I am loved by you.

## \|\| 2.12.33 \|\|

*tamevamuktvā dvijarājavaktrā karaṃ gṛhītvā nṛpatestu vegāt \|*  
*utthāpayāmāsa dharāśayānamindra sya yaṣṭīmiva mohinī sā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After saying thus to him, Mohini caught hold of the hand of the king and quickly lifted him up even as he was lying on the ground like the thunderbolt of Indra.

## Chapter 13. The Fascination of Mohini

## \|\| 2.13.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- utthāpayitvā rājānaṃ mohinī vākyamabratīt \|*  
*mā śaṅkāṃ kuru rājendra kumārīṃ viddhykalmaṣām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasitfha said:

1\. Lifting up the king, Mohini spoke these words: О leading king, do not entertain any doubt. Know me to be a virgin without sins.

## \|\| 2.13.2-3 \|\|

*udvahasva mahīpāla gṛhyoktavidhinā hi mām \|*  
*anūḍhā kanyakā rājan yadi garbhaṃ bibharti hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prasūyati divākīrtiṃ sarvavarṇavigarhitam \|*  
*cāṇḍālayonayastisraḥ purāṇe kavayo viduḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3а. О king, marry me in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Grhyastitras. If an unmarried virgin becomes pregnant, she delivers of a son of ill fame who will be despised by the people of ail castes.

## \|\| 2.13.3-4 \|\|

*prasūyati divākīrtiṃ sarvavarṇavigarhitam \|*  
*cāṇḍālayonayastisraḥ purāṇe kavayo viduḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kumārīsaṃbhavā tvekā sagotrāpi dvitīyakā \|*  
*brāhmaṇyāṃ śūdra janitā tṛtīyā nṛpapuṃgava \|\| 4 \|\|*

3b-4. In the Purana, the wise know (i. e. say) that there are three types of Candalas. One is the child born of an unmarried virgin; the second type is the progeny of Sagotra marriage (i.e. marriage between a man and a woman of the same Gotra or lineage). О leading king, the third type of Candala is the progeny of a Brahmapa lady begot by a Sudra.1

## \|\| 2.13.5-8 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādrā jan kumārīṃ māṃ samudvaha \|*  
*tatastāṃ capalāpāṅgī nṛpo rukmāṅgado girau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*udvāhya vidhinā yuktastasthau rājā hasanniva \|*  
*rājovāca- na tathā tridivaprāptiḥ prīṇayenmāṃ varānane \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tava prāptiryathā devi mandare'sminsukhāya vai \|*  
*manye purandarāddevi hyātmānamadhikaṃ kṣitau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*trailokyasundarīṃ prāpya bhāryāṃ tvāṃ cārulocane \|*  
*tasmādyadanukūlaṃ te tatkaromi praśādhi mām \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-6a. For this reason, О king marry me a virgin.” Thereafter, King Rukmangada married that lady of tremulous side-glances, on that mountain itself, in accordance with the (Grhya-siitra) injunctions. United with her the king said smilingly: The king said:

6b-7a. О fair-faced lady, attainment of heaven is not as much conducive to happiness as winning you, О gentle lady, on this Mandara mountain. It does not please me so much as this meeting with you.

7b-8. О gentle lady, even though I am on this Earth I consider myself superior to Purandara (god Indra) since I have obtained О fair-eyed lady, you, the most beautiful lady in the three worlds as my wife. Hence I shall do whatever is favourable to you. Command me.

## \|\| 2.13.9 \|\|

*ihaiva ramase bāle athavā mandire mama \|*  
*malaye meruśikhare vane vā nandane vada \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Tell me whether you wish to sport about here itself, О young lady, or in my palace or on the Malaya mountain or on the top of the Meru or in the Nandana park.

## \|\| 2.13.10 \|\|

*tacchrutvā nṛpatervākyaṃ mohinī madhuraṃ nṛpa \|*  
*uvācānuśayaṃ rājanvacanaṃ prītivarddhanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On hearing the words of the king that were indicative of his close attachment to her, MohinI spoke these sweet words that increased the pleasure of the king: —

## \|\| 2.13.11 \|\|

*sapatnīnāṃ kaṭākṣāṇāṃ kṣatāni nagare mama \|*  
*bhaviṣyanti mahīpāla kathaṃ gacchāmi te puram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О king, in your capital city I shall be the victim of wounding side-glances of my co-wives. How can I, therefore, go over to your city?

## \|\| 2.13.12 \|\|

*māsma sīmantinī kācidbhaveddhi kṣitimaṇḍale \|*  
*yasyāḥ sapatnīprabhavaṃ duḥkhamāmaraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Let there not be, in the whole of the Earth, any woman who will be facing the misery originating from co-wives, throughout her life (till death).

## \|\| 2.13.13 \|\|

*sāhaṃ labdhā mahīpāla manasā vaśagā tava \|*  
*jñātvā sapatnīprabhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhartā kṛto mayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О king, I have been obtained by you. From the bottom of my heart, I am subservient to you. It was after understanding that there would be the misery from co-wives that you have been wooed as my husband by me.

## \|\| 2.13.14 \|\|

*vatsyāmi parvataśreṣṭhe bahvāścaryasamanvite \|*  
*na tvaṃ vasasi rājedra sandhyāvalyā vinā kvacit \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I will be able to reside on the excellent mountain that contains many miraculous features. But, О leading king the only thing is you cannot stay anywhere without Sandhy avail.

## \|\| 2.13.15 \|\|

*tasyāstvaṃ virahe duḥkhī saputrāyā bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*duḥkhena bhavato rājanbhūri duḥkhaṃ bhavenmama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On being separated from her and her son, you will be definitely unhappy. Your sadness, О king, will increase my sorrow.

## \|\| 2.13.16 \|\|

*yatraiva bhavataḥ saukhyaṃ tatrāhamapi saṃsthitā \|*  
*yatra tvaṃ raṃsyase rājaṃstatra me mandaro giriḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I shall establish myself soundly wherever you will derive sufficient happiness. О king, where you are happily diverted, I shall also be happy, feeling that your place of residence is mount Mandara to me.

## \|\| 2.13.17 \|\|

*bhartṛsthāne hi vastavyamṛddhihīne'pi bhāryayā \|*  
*sa meruḥ kāñcanamayaḥ sannidhāne pracakṣate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The wife must live in the place where her husband stays, even if it is notan affluent one. They say (i.e. wise people say) that, in the proximity of her husband (hat place is the veritable mountain Meru of gold.

## \|\| 2.13.18 \|\|

*manoratho nāma meruryatra tvaṃ ramase vibho \|*  
*bhartṛsthānaṃ parityajya svapiturvāpi varjitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О Lord, where you feel happy is surely my Meru, the place of my desire. Staying in the place of one’s father after eschewing that of one’s husband, is to be avoided.

## \|\| 2.13.19 \|\|

*pitṛsthānāśrayaratā nārī tamasi majjati \|*  
*sarvadharmavihīnāpi nārī bhavati sūkarī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A woman interested in staying permanently in the abode of her father sinks in darkness of hell. All her holy rites shall be fruitless and she shall be born as a sow.

## \|\| 2.13.20 \|\|

*evaṃ jānāmyahaṃ doṣaṃ kathaṃ vatsyāmi mandare \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi tvayā sārddhamīśastvaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I know such evil consequences. How, then can I stay on in the Mandara mountain? I will go along with you. You are the Lord of my happiness and misery.”

## \|\| 2.13.21 \|\|

*mohinyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā rājā saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*pariṣvajya varārohāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing the words of Mohinl, the king was delighted in his mind. After embracing the beautiful, lady, he spoke these words: —

## \|\| 2.13.22 \|\|

*bhāryāṇāṃ mama sarvāsāmupariṣṭādbhaviṣyasi \|*  
*mā śaṅkāṃ kuru vāmoru yato duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You will be above all my wives. О lady of beautiful thighs, do not have any doubt that you will have to face misery!

## \|\| 2.13.23 \|\|

*jīvitādadhikā srubhu bhaviṣyasi gṛhe mama \|*  
*ehi gacchāva tanvaṅiga sukhāya nagaraṃ prati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О lady of beautiful eyebrows, in my house you will be far superior to my own life. О lady of slender frame, come on. We shall proceed to the city for our mutual happiness.

## \|\| 2.13.24 \|\|

*bhuṅkṣva bhogānmayā sārddhaṃ tatrasthā svecchayā priye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О my beloved wife, staying there, enjoy freely all the worldly pleasures along with me.

## \|\| 2.13.25 \|\|

*sā tvevamuktā śaśigauravaktrā rukmāṅgadenātmavināśanāya \|*  
*samprasthitā nūpuraghoṣayuktā vikarṣayantī girijātaśobhām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It was eventually for his own destruction that Rukmarigada told her thus. Mohini whose face was as white and fair as the moon, started from there producing the tinkling sound of her anklets. It seemed that she even dragged the beauty of the mountain too after her.

## Chapter 14. The salvation of Godhd, (the lizard)

## \|\| 2.14.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- samprasthitāvubhau rājangiriśīrṣāddharātalam \|*  
*paśyamānau bahūnbhāvāngirijātānmanoharān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasiffha continued:

1\. О king, both of them set off from the top of the mountain towards the surface of the Earth, surveying the various features of the mountain that captivated their mind.

## \|\| 2.14.2 \|\|

*kecidvidrumasaṅkāśāḥ kecidra jatasannibhāḥ \|*  
*kecinnīlasamaprakhyāḥ kecitkāñcanasatviṣaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Some of the regions resembled corals, some were white like silver, some had the blue lustre of sapphire and some regions had golden hue.

## \|\| 2.14.3 \|\|

*kecitsphāṭikavarṇābhā haritālanibhāḥ pare \|*  
*anyonyaśleṣatāṃ prāptau sakalaiḥ sthāvarairiva \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Some of them were crystal-coloured and others resembled the yellow orpiment. All the immobile beings were as if closely knit together.

## \|\| 2.14.4 \|\|

*samprāpya vasudhāṃ bhūpo hyapaśyadvājināṃ varam \|*  
*khanyamānaṃ khureṇorvīṃ kuliśābhena veginā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After reaching the foot of the mountain (ground level), the king saw his excellent horse scrapping the ground with his powerful hoofs that resembled the thunderbolt.

## \|\| 2.14.5 \|\|

*tasya dārayataḥ pṛthvadyaṃ sutīkṣṇena khureṇa hi \|*  
*gṛhagodhābhavattasmin bhūbhāgāntargatā kila \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. As it scrapped and dug up the Earth with its sharp hoofs, a domestic lizard that had been beneath the ground came out.

## \|\| 2.14.6 \|\|

*nirgacchamānā nṛpate khureṇa vidalī kṛtā \|*  
*vidīryamāṇāṃ nṛpatirapaśyatsadayāparaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. While coming out, О king (?) it was crushed beneath the hoof of the horse. The kind-hearted king saw it being crushed.

## \|\| 2.14.7-8 \|\|

*abhyadhāvata vegena hā hateti priyāṃ vadan \|*  
*tataḥ sa vṛkṣapatreṇa komalena mahīpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*utsārya tāṃ khurādāśu prākṣipatṛṇaśādvale \|*  
*tatastu mohinīṃ prāha prekṣya mūrcchāgatāṃ hi tām \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Crying out to his beloved wife “Alas it is crushed V he rushed to it. Then, with the tender leaf of a tree the king scrapped it from the hoof and threw it on a plot of grassy land. Seeing that it had become senseless he spoke to Mohinl: —

## \|\| 2.14.9 \|\|

*śīghramāhara cārvaṅiga jalaṃ jalajalocane \|*  
*yena mūrcchāgatāṃ siñce gṛhagodhāṃ vimardditām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O lady of beautiful limbs and lotus-like eyes! Bring some water immediately so that I can sprinkle it on the lizard that has become unconscious due to its being crushed.

## \|\| 2.14.10 \|\|

*sā bharturvacanācchīghramānayacchītalaṃ jalam \|*  
*tenābhyaṣiñcannṛpatirgṛhagodhāṃ vimūrcchitām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the instance of her husband, she brought some cool water immediately. With that the king sprinkled the unconscious domestic lizard.

## \|\| 2.14.11-13 \|\|

*avāpa cetanāṃ rājan śītalājjalasecanāt \|*  
*abhighāteṣu sarveṣu śastaṃ vāriprasecanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*athavā klinnavastreṇa sahasā bandhanaṃ hitam \|*  
*samprāptacetanā bhūpa godhā vacanamabravīt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rājānamagrato vīkṣya vedanārtā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*rukmāṅgada mahābāho nibodha mama ceṣṭitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. О king, Being sprinkled with cold water the lizard regained consciousness. In all cases of smiting blows, sprinkling with water is recommended. Or it is beneficial if it is immediately bandaged with a damp cloth. О king (?), after regaining consciousness the lizard spoke these words. Seeing the king in front of her, though it was distressed with (acute) pain it (the lizard) spoke out slowly: “O mighty-armed Rukmari- gada, listen to my story of life.

## \|\| 2.14.14 \|\|

*śākale nagare ramye bhāryāhaṃ hyagrajanmanaḥ \|*  
*rūpayauvanasampannā tasya nātipriyā vibho \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О Lord, I was the wife of a Brahmana, in the beautiful city of Sakala.1 I was endowed with beauty and youth. But I was not liked much by him.

## \|\| 2.14.15 \|\|

*sadā vidveṣasaṃyukto mayi niṣṭhurajalpakaḥ \|*  
*nānyasya kasyaciddveṣṭā sa tu me nṛpate patiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О king, that husband of mine did not hate anyone else, but he was always full of hatred towards me. He invariably spoke harsh words to me.

## \|\| 2.14.16 \|\|

*tato'ha krodhasaṃyuktā vaśīkaraṇalambhanāt \|*  
*apṛcchaṃ pramadā rājanyāstyaktāḥ patibhiḥ kila \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I was furious on account of this. In order to attain the power of Vashi-karana (attraction), О king I consulted those young women who had been abandoned by their husbands, (but who later on controlled them).

## \|\| 2.14.17 \|\|

*tābhiruktā hyahaṃ bhūpa vaśyo bhartā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*asmākaṃ pratyayo jāto bhartṛtyāgāvamānanāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О king, I was informed by them — “Your husband will be subservient. We have been convinced (because once) we too had been abandoned and slighted by our husbands.

## \|\| 2.14.18 \|\|

*pravrajyābheṣajairvaśyā jātā hi patayastu naḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ pṛccha tāṃ varārohe dāsyate bheṣajaṃ śubham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Indeed our husbands became meek and submissive through the medicines and potions given by an ascetic woman. О beautiful lady, you too ask her. She will give you the auspicious medicines.

## \|\| 2.14.19-20 \|\|

*na vikalpastvayā kāryo bhavitā dāsavatpatiḥ \|*  
*tato'ha tvaritaṃ gatvā tāsāṃ vākyena bhūpate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*prāsādaḥ kathitastasyāḥ pṛcchantyā mama mānavaiḥ \|*  
*śatastambhasamāyuktaḥ kāntimatsudhayāyutaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. You need not entertain any doubt. Your husband will be obedient like a slave. О king, at their instance I started from the place immediately. As I asked the people on the way, they pointed out her palace consisting of hundred columns and white-washed in a shining form.

## \|\| 2.14.21 \|\|

*praviśya taṃ sutejaskāmapaśyaṃ brahmacāriṇīm \|*  
*prāvṛtāṃ dīrghavastreṇa sandhyārāgasavarṇinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After entering it, I saw the brilliant woman under the vow of celibacy. She had covered herself with a long cloth. She had the tawny coloured complexion like that of the dusk.

## \|\| 2.14.22 \|\|

*dīrghābhiḥ sā jaṭābhistu saṃvṛtā dīptisaṃyutā \|*  
*paricārakaistu saṃyuktā vījyamānā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The refulgent lady wore long matted hairs; a number of attendants were waiting upon her; she was being fanned gently by them.

## \|\| 2.14.23 \|\|

*akṣasūtrakarā sā tu japantī bhagamālinī \|*  
*sarvavaśyakaraṃ mantraṃ kṣobhakaṃ pratyayāvaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With a rosary of beads in her hand, she was repeating the Mantra that was Vasyakara (conducive to attract and subdue people), that could cause excitement which could be verified (and hence was convincing.) She had the garland of happiness giving beads (?) round her neck).

## \|\| 2.14.24-25 \|\|

*tato'ha praṇatā bhūtvā padbhyāṃ nyasyāṅgulīyakam \|*  
*mṛdukāñcanasambhūtaṃ atiriktaprabhānvitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tato hṛṣṭā'bhavaddṛṣṭvā padasthaṃ cāṅgulīyakam \|*  
*apṛṣṭayā tayā jñātaṃ mama bhartturvimānanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Thereafter, I placed a soft lustrous ring of fine gold with superb brilliance at her feet and bowed to her. On seeing the ring placed at her feet she become delighted. Even before being asked, she had understood the disrespect to me by my husband.

## \|\| 2.14.26-27 \|\|

*tayoktāhaṃ tato bhūpa tāpasyā praṇatā sthitā \|*  
*cūrṇo rakṣānvito hyeṣa sarvabhūtavaśānugaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tvayā bhartari saṃyojyo rakṣyaṃ grīvāśayāṅkuram \|*  
*bhaviṣyati patirvaśyo nānyāṃ yāsyati sundarīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Then, О king, I was advised by the ascetic lady when I bowed to her and stood by. “This medicinal powder alongwith this amulet brings all living beings under control. The powder must be given to your husband (for being taken in) and the amulet must be worn round the neck. Certainly the husband will become submissive. He will not go to any other beautiful woman.

## \|\| 2.14.28 \|\|

*cūrṇarakṣāṃ gṛhītvāhaṃ prāptā bhartṛgṛhaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*pradoṣe payasā yuktaścūrṇo bhartari yojitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Taking the medicinal powder and the amulet, I soon reached the house of my husband. At nightfall, the powder was mixed with milk and given to my husband.

## \|\| 2.14.29-30 \|\|

*grīvāyāṃ hi kṛtā rakṣā na vicāro mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*yadā sa pītacūrṇastu bhartā nṛpavarottama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tadahaḥ kṣayarogo'bhūtpatiḥ kṣīṇo dine dine \|*  
*guhye tu krimayo jātāḥ kṣataduṣṭavraṇodbhavāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The amulet was tied round the neck and I ceased to be anxious over anything. О excellent king, when my husband drank the potion with the medicinal powder, the consumptive disease took possession of him the same day. My husband became weaker and weaker day by day. Worms originating from cuts and putrefying wounds abounded in his private parts.

## \|\| 2.14.31-32 \|\|

*dinaiḥ katipayairjātairdīpavadra vidarśanāt \|*  
*hatatejāstathā bharttā māmuvācākulendri yaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*krandamāno divā rātrau dāso'smi tava śobhane \|*  
*trāhi māṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaṃ na gaccheyaṃ parastriyam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Within a few days, he became pale and dim like a lamp when the sun has risen. My husband became agitated and perturbed in his sense organs. Lamenting over his lot day and night he told me: О splendid lady, I am your slave. I seek refuge in you. Save me. I will never approach another woman.

## \|\| 2.14.33 \|\|

*tattasya ruditaṃ śrutvā bhayabhītā mahīpate \|*  
*tasyāṃ niveditaṃ sarvaṃ kathaṃ bhartā bhavetsukhī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О king, on hearing his lamentation I became much terrified. I informed the ascetic lady about everything and asked her. How shall my husband be happy?

## \|\| 2.14.34 \|\|

*tayāpi bheṣajaṃ dattaṃ dvitīyaṃ dāhaśāntaye \|*  
*datte tu bheṣaje tasminsustho'bhūttatkṣaṇātpatiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A second course of medicine was given by her for subduing the burning sensation. When the medicine was administered, my husband attained normal health instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.14.35 \|\|

*pūrvacūrṇodbhavo dāhaḥ śāntastenauṣadhena ha \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti me bhartā vaśyo'bhūdvacane sthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The burning sensation originating from the previous powder was nullified by that medicine. Thereafter, my husband became subservient to me. He abided by my words and advice.

## \|\| 2.14.36 \|\|

*kālena pañcatāṃ prāptā gatā narakayātanām \|*  
*tāmrabhrāṣṭre hyahaṃ dagdhā yugāni daśa pañca ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In due course of time, I passed away and fell into the hell called Tamrabhrastra (Copper frying pan) where I underwent torture for the period of fifteen Yugas.

## \|\| 2.14.37 \|\|

*sūkṣmāṇi tilamātrāṇi kṛtvā khaṇḍānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kiñcitpātakaśeṣeṇa dharāyāmavatāritā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Pieces as subtle and minute as gingelly seeds were cut off from my body and I was tortured: When a little of my sin remained still, I was born on the Earth.

## \|\| 2.14.38 \|\|

*gṛhagodhāmayaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtaṃ bhāskarajena me \|*  
*sāhamatra sthitā bhūpa varṣāṇāmayutaṃ purā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The form of a lizard was given to me by Yama (the son of the Sun). Thus, О king, I have been here for the last ten thousand years.

## \|\| 2.14.39 \|\|

*yānyāpi yuvatirbhūpa bharturvaśyaṃ samācaret \|*  
*vṛthādharmā durācārā dahyate tāmrabhrāṣṭrake \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О king, if any young maiden were to perform Vaslkarana rite to attract and control her husband, all her holy rites will be futile; she will be considered wicked and sinful in action and she will be burned and tortured in Tamrabhrastraka (hell).

## \|\| 2.14.40 \|\|

*bhartā nātho gatirbhartā daivataṃ gurureva ca \|*  
*tasya vaśyaṃ caredyā tu sā kathaṃ sukhamāpnuyāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. To a lady the husband is the Lord, he is the goal; lie is the deity and he is the preceptor. If she were to perform the Vaslkarana rite in respect of him, how can she attain happiness?

## \|\| 2.14.41 \|\|

*tiryagyoniśataṃ yāti krimikuṣṭhasamanvitā \|*  
*tasmādbhūpāla kartavyaṃ strībhirbhartṛvacaḥ sadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She is born among hundreds of species of animals and creatures including the germs of leprosy. Hence, О king, the behest of the husband must always be carried out by a woman.

## \|\| 2.14.42 \|\|

*sāhaṃ yāsye punaryoniṃ kutsitāṃ pātakānvitām \|*  
*yadi noddharase rājannadya māṃ śaraṇāgatām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О king, unless you redeem me who have sought refuge in you, I shall have to be born again as a despicable creature with all my sins.

## \|\| 2.14.43-44 \|\|

*sukṛtasya pradānena vijayājanitena hi \|*  
*yā tvayā saṅgame puṇye kṛtā śravaṇadvādaśī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sarayvāścaiva gaṅgāyāḥ pāpanāśavidhāyake \|*  
*pretaniryātanī puṇyā mānasepsitadāyinī \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. You can redeem me by giving me the merit acquired by you by observing the holy rite of Vijaya DvadaSl1 associated with the constellation (Naksatra) Sravana at the confluence of Ganga and Sarayu. This confluence is destructive of sins. The holy rite is conducive to the redemption of ghosts. It is the bestower of all mentally cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.14.45 \|\|

*yasyāṃ gṛhe'pi bhūpāla saṃsmṛto manujairhariḥ \|*  
*sarvatīrthaphalāvāptiṃ kurute nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On that day, О king, even if Hari is remembered in their own house by men, there is no doubt about it that he enables them to attain the merit accrued by visiting holy centres.

## \|\| 2.14.46 \|\|

*dattaṃ japtaṃ hutaṃ yacca kṛtaṃ devārcanādikam \|*  
*sarvaṃ tadakṣayaṃ bhūpa yatkṛtaṃ vijayādine \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О king, whatever meritorious act like charitable gifts, oblations to fire, worship of gods, is performed on the day of Vijaya it has ever-lasting beneficial effect.

## \|\| 2.14.47-49 \|\|

*evaṃvidhaṃ phalaṃ yasyāstaddehi sukṛtaṃ mama \|*  
*dvādaśyāmupavāsena trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇe \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdopavāsasya phalaṃ prāpnotyupoṣaṇe \|*  
*dayāṃ kṛtvā mahīpāla dharmamūrtirbhavān kṣitau \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vaivasvatapathadhvaṃsī paritrāhi suduḥkhitām \|*  
*gṛhagodhāvacaḥ śrutvā mohinī vākyamabravīt \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49a Please do grant unto me that merit. If one observes fast on the DvadasI day and performs Parana on the Trayo- dail day, one acquires the benefit of observing fast for twelve years. О king, take pity on me and pass on that merit tome. On the Earth, you are the very physical manifestation of Dharma (virtue). You are the destroyer of the path of Yama. О save me. I am utterly miserable.

49b. On hearing the words of the lizard, MohinI spoke these words:

## \|\| 2.14.50 \|\|

*svakṛtaṃ tu jano'śnāti sukhaduḥkhātmakaṃ vibho \|*  
*tasmātkimanayā kāryaṃ pāpayā bhartṛduṣṭayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О Lord, whether happiness or misery one experiences, it has the result of his own actions. Hence, what have you to do with this sinful creature who had been wicked to her own husband?

## \|\| 2.14.51 \|\|

*yayā bhartā vaśaṃ nīto rakṣācūrṇādibhirnṛpa \|*  
*sādhubhyo yatkṛtaṃ rājanyaśaḥsvargakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О king, by means of amulets, medicinal powder and other things she gained control over her husband. О king, whatever is given to good men may be conducive to fame and heavenly pleasure.

## \|\| 2.14.52-53 \|\|

*ubhayorbhraṃśatāmeti pāpebhyo yatkṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śarkarāmiśritaṃ kṣīraṃ kādra veye niyojitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*viṣavṛddhiṃ karotyeva tadvatpāpakṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*parityajemāṃ tvaṃ pāpāṃ gacchāvo nagarāya vai \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. What is rendered as a gift etc to the sinners causes downfall of both (the giver and the receiver). It falls off both the worlds. If milk mixed with sugar is given to a serpent, it will certainly increase its poison. Similar indeed is the help rendered to the sinners. Leave off this sinful creature. Let us go to the city.

## \|\| 2.14.54 \|\|

*janmavyāpārasaktānāmātmasaukhyaṃ vinaśyati \|*  
*rukmāṅgada uvāca- brahmātmaje kathaṃ vākyamīdṛśaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ tvayā \|*  
*na sādhūnāmidaṃ vṛttaṃ bhavatīti varānane \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If one delves into the births and dealings of others one’s happiness perishes. RukmUngada said: О daughter of Brahma, how is it that these things were uttered by you? О fair-faced lady, how can you say that this is not the conduct or way of life of good men?

## \|\| 2.14.55 \|\|

*ātmasaukhyakarāḥ pāpā bhavanti paratāpinaḥ \|*  
*viprapannā varārohe paropakaraṇāya vai \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О fair lady, those who are opposed to helping others are sinners. They do everything for their own happiness and harass others. They are opposed to rendering obligation to others.

## \|\| 2.14.56 \|\|

*śaśī sūryo'tha parjanyo medinī hutabhugjalam \|*  
*candanaṃ pādapāḥ santaḥ paropakaraṇāya vai \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The moon, sun, cloud, earth, fire, water, sandal, trees and good men are always for helping others.

## \|\| 2.14.57-58 \|\|

*śrūyate kila rājāsīddhariścandro varānane \|*  
*cāṇḍālamandirāvāsī bhāryātanayavikrayī \|\| 57 \|\|*

*asatyavacanādbhīto duḥkhādduḥkhataraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tasya satyena santuṣṭā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. О fair-faced lady, it is heard that there was a king named Harifcandra. Afraid of uttering a lie he experienced various miseries one after the other. He had to stay #in the house of a Candala. He had to sell his wife and son. Thanks to his steadfast adherence to truth, Sakra and other Devas became satisfied.

## \|\| 2.14.59 \|\|

*vareṇa chandayāñcakrurhariścandraṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*tena satyavatā coktā devā brahmapurogamāḥ \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭā hi vibudhā varaṃ me dātumarhatha \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. They asked Hariscandra1 the king to choose any boon. Brahma and other Devas were given this reply by that truthful king — If the Devas are satisfied it behoves them to grant this boon:

## \|\| 2.14.60-62 \|\|

*eṣā hi nagarī sarvā sadrumā sasarīsṛpā \|*  
*sabālabṛddhataruṇā sanārī sacatuṣpadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*prayātu kṛtapāpāpi svargatiṃ nagarī mama \|*  
*ayodhyāpātakaṃ gṛhya gantāhaṃ narakaṃ dhruvam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ekākī nahi gacchāmi parityajya janaṃ kṣitau \|*  
*svargaṃ vibudhaśārdūlāḥ satyametanmayeritam \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. May this entire city alongwith its trees, reptiles, children, young men, old men, women, and quadrupeds go to heaven. Even if it had committed sins, I shall take over the entire sins of Ayodhya and would like to go to hell. I do not wish to go to heaven alone after leaving people on the Earth. О great Devas, this is the truth, I utter.

## \|\| 2.14.63 \|\|

*tasya tāṃ sthiratāṃ jñātvā saha tenaiva sā purī \|*  
*jagāma svargalokaṃ ca indrā dīnāmanujñayā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On seeing his steadfastness, Indra and others permitted it. The entire city went to the heavenly world alongwith him.

## \|\| 2.14.64 \|\|

*so'pi svarge sthito rājā svapureṇa samanvitaḥ \|*  
*kāmagena vimānena pūjyamāno'marairapi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The king is stationed in heaven in the company of his city. He moves about in the aerial chariot that goes wherever he pleases. He is being worshipped even by the immortal beings.

## \|\| 2.14.65 \|\|

*asthidānaṃ kṛtaṃ devi kṛpayā hi dadhīcinā \|*  
*devānāmupakārārthaṃ śrutvā daityaiḥ parājitān \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О gentle lady, on hearing that the Devas had been defeated by the Daityas, the gift of his own bones was made by Dadhici for helping the Devas.

## \|\| 2.14.66 \|\|

*kapotārthaṃ svamāṃsāni śibinā bhūbhujā purā \|*  
*pradattāni varārohe śyenāya kṣudhitāya vai \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О fair lady, his own flesh was given to the hungry vulture by king Sibi formerly, for protecting a dove.

## \|\| 2.14.67 \|\|

*jīmūtavāhano rājā purāsītkṣitimaṇḍale \|*  
*tenāpi jīvitaṃ dattaṃ pannagāya varānane \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Formerly, there was a king over this earth named Jirmitavahana2. О fairfaced lady, his own life was given up by him for the sake of serpents.

## \|\| 2.14.68 \|\|

*tasmāddayālunā devi bhavitavyaṃ mahībhujā \|*  
*śucāvamedhye'pi śubhe samaṃ varṣati vāridaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Hence, О gentle lady, a king should be kind-hearted and sympathetic. О splendid lady, the cloud showers its waters equally on an unholy and pure spot.

## \|\| 2.14.69-70 \|\|

*cāṇḍālapatitau candro hlādayecca nijaiḥ karaiḥ \|*  
*tasmādimāṃ varārohe gṛhagodhāṃ suduḥkhitām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*uddhariṣye nijaiḥ puṇyairdauhitrairnāhuṣo yathā \|*  
*vimohinīṃ tiraskṛtya gṛhagodhāmuvāca ha \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. The moon should delight even the Can^alas and the fallen persons through his rays. Hence, О fair lady, I shall uplift this distressed lizard by means of my own merits in the same way as Nahu^a through his daughter’s descendant (P).1 Disregarding the enchantress thus, he spoke to the lizard.

## \|\| 2.14.71 \|\|

*dattaṃ dattaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ vijayāsambhavaṃ tava \|*  
*gaccha viṣṇugatām̐ llokānvidhūtāśeṣakalmaṣā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. My merit originating from the holy rite of Vijaya is given, (I repeat) is given unto you, by me. Be free from all sins and go to the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.14.72-74 \|\|

*tadvākyātsahasā bhūpa divyābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*vimucya dehaṃ tajjīrṇaṃ gṛhagodhāsamudbhavam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*jagāmāmantr! ya taṃ bhūpaṃ dyotayantī diśo daśa \|*  
*sīmantamiva kurvāṇā vaiṣṇavaṃ padamadbhutam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yadyogigamyaṃ hutabhukprakāśaṃ varaṃ vareṇyaṃ paramātmabhūtam \|*  
*tasmādiyaṃ caiva śikhipradīpā jagatprakāśāya nṛpaprasūtā \|\| 74 \|\|*

72-74. О king, on his uttering this, she eschewed the old and emaciated form of the lizard and became a beautiful lady bedecked in celestial ornaments. She took leave of the king and went away brightening the ten quarters and making (as if) a wonderful boundary line to the region of Visnu. It is the place approachable only by Yogins. It is an excellent region brilliant like fire. It is the greatest Atman. Hence she is also like the lamp of fire for the illumination of the universe and was transformed by the king.

## Chapter 15. The dialogue between thefather (Rukmdfigada) and the son (.DharmdAgada)

## \|\| 2.15.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- vimocya pātakādrā jā gṛhagodhāṃ hasanniva \|*  
*uvāca mohinīṃ hṛṣṭaḥ śīghramāruhyatāṃ hayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasiffha said:

1\. After setting the lizard free from the sin, the delighted king laughingly said to Mohinl — May the horse be mounted instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.15.2-3 \|\|

*yojanāyutagāmī ca kṣaṇātkṛṣṇahayo yathā \|*  
*tadākarṇya vaco rājño mohinī madalālasā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*āruroha samaṃ bhartrā taṃ hayaṃ vātaveginam \|*  
*uvāca ca vaco bhūpaṃ bhartāraṃ cāruhāsinī \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Like Krsna’s horse (?) this can go ten thousand Yojanas in a moment. On hearing the words of the king, MohinI, the ardently passionate lady, climbed on to the horse which was as swift as the wind, alongwith her husband. The lady of sweet smiles spoke these words to the king her husband.

## \|\| 2.15.4 \|\|

*pracodayemamarvāṇaṃ svapurāya mahīpate \|*  
*putravaktraṃ spṛhā dra ṣṭuṃ lampaṭā tava vartate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О king, drive this horse towards your city. My desire to see the face of your son is intense.

## \|\| 2.15.5 \|\|

*tavādhīnā nṛpaśreṣṭha gamyatāṃ yatra te manaḥ \|*  
*mohinyā vacanaṃ śrutvā pratasthe nagaraṃ prati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О excellent king, I am at your disposal. You may go wherever you are inclined to go. On hearing the words of Mohini, he started towards his city.

## \|\| 2.15.6-9 \|\|

*paśyamānaḥ susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pādapānparvatānnadīḥ \|*  
*vanāni suvicitrāṇi mṛgānbahuvidhānapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*grāmāndurgāṃstathā devānnagarāṇi śubhāni ca \|*  
*sarāṃsi ca vicitrāṇi bhūbhāgānsumanoharān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*acireṇāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā vāmadevasya bhūpate \|*  
*ākāśastho mahīpālo namaskṛtya tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*punareva yayau rājā vāyuvegena vājinā \|*  
*paśyamāno bahūndeśāndhanadhānyasamanvitān \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. With great delight he observed the trees, the mountains, the rivers, the different kinds of forests, the animals of various sorts, villages, forts, lands, splendid cities, lakes of variegated nature and the charming plots of lands on the way. On seeing the hermitage of Vamadeva soon, the king who was in a hurry, bowed down from the firmament itself. Again the king proceeded on his way on his horse that was as swift as the wind-god. Observing many lands fully endowed with riches and food grains.

## \|\| 2.15.10-12 \|\|

*āsasāda puraṃ rājā vaidiśaṃ svavaśaṃ ca tat \|*  
*tamāyāntaṃ nṛpaṃ śrutvā cārairddharmāṅgadaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pitaraṃ harṣasaṃyukto bhūpālānvākyamabravīt \|*  
*eṣā prakāśamāyāti udīcīdiṅ nṛpottamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*matpiturvājinākrāntā tattejaḥ parirañjitā \|*  
*tasmādgacchāmahe sarve sammukhaṃ hyavanīpateḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The king reached Vidisa (a city in Madhya Pradesh) that was under his control. His son Dharmangada had already heard through his spies that the king, his father, was coming. With great delight he spoke these words to the vassal kings: — О excellent kings, this northern quarter is becoming brighter on being illuminated by his splendour and on being occupied by my father’s horse. Hence, let us all go to greet the king face to face.

## \|\| 2.15.13 \|\|

*piturāgatamātrasya sammukhaṃ na suto vrajet \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ yāvadindrā ścaturddaśa \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If the son does not come face to face with (i.e. does not personally go to receive) his father immediately on his arrival, he falls into the terrible hell and stays there as long as fourteen Indras reign.

## \|\| 2.15.14 \|\|

*sammukhaṃ vrajamānasya putrasya pitaraṃ prati \|*  
*pade pade yajñaphalaṃ procuḥ paurāṇikā dvijāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Brahmanas well-versed in the Puranas say that if the son goes ahead to receive his father face to face, (personally Jhe derives the fruit of a Yajna for every step he takes).

## \|\| 2.15.15 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhadhvaṃ vrajāmyeṣa bhavadbhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*abhivādayituṃ premṇā eṣa me devadevatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Get up. I shall go to greet him lovingly surrounded by you all. He is my deity of deities.

## \|\| 2.15.16 \|\|

*tathetyuktaistu taiḥ sarvairbhūmipālairnṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*jagāma sammukhaṃ padbhyāṃ krośamātraṃ pitustadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When the king approved of his words saying “So be it,” the prince accompanied by all of them went on foot for a distance of a Krosa (3 km.) to greet his father personally face to face.

## \|\| 2.15.17 \|\|

*tato rājasahasreṇa mūrtimāniva manmathaḥ \|*  
*sa gatvā dūramadhvānamāsasāda nṛpaṃ pathi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Appearing like the embodied form of Manmatha and accompanied by a thousand kings, he went a long distance and met the king on the way.

## \|\| 2.15.18 \|\|

*saṃprāpya pitaraṃ snehājjagāma dharaṇīṃ tadā \|*  
*śirasā rājabhiḥ sārddhaṃ praṇāmamakarottadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Meeting his father, he prostrated to him by falling at his feet on the ground affectionately. Alongwith the vassal kings, he bent his head down and made obeisance.

## \|\| 2.15.19-20 \|\|

*premṇā samāgataṃ prekṣya taṃ patantaṃ nṛpaiḥ saha \|*  
*avaruhya hayādrā jā samutthāpya sutaṃ vibho \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhujābhyāṃ sādhu pīnābhyāṃ paryaṣvañjata bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*mūrdhni caivamupāghrāya uvāca tanayaṃ tadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. With great love the king observed his son falling at his feet immediately after arrival along with the vassal kings. The king got down from the horse. With his brawny arms he lifted up his son and warmly embraced him closely. Sniffing at his head the king then spoke to his son.

## \|\| 2.15.21 \|\|

*kaccitpāsi prajāḥ sarvāḥ kacciddaṇḍayase ripūn \|*  
*nyāyāgatena vittena kośaṃ putra bibharṣi ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О son, I hope you are protecting your subjects. I also hope you are punishing the enemies. I presume you fill the treasury only with such amounts as are earned by justifiable means.

## \|\| 2.15.22 \|\|

*kaccidvipreṣvatyadhikā vṛttirdattānapāyinī \|*  
*kaccitte kāntaśīlatvaṃ kaccidvaktā na niṣṭhuram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I hope, never failing maintenance amounts that are more than sufficient have been handed over to the Brahmanas. I hope you practise attractive and pleasant manners, and that you do not speak harsh words.

## \|\| 2.15.23 \|\|

*kaccidgāvo na duhyante putra cāṇḍālaveśmani \|*  
*kaccidvacanakartārastanayāśca pituḥ sadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I hope cows are now milked in the houses of Can- dalas and sons carry out the behests of their fathers always.

## \|\| 2.15.24 \|\|

*kaccidvadhūḥ śvaśrūvākye vartate bhartari kvacit \|*  
*kaccidvivādānvipraistu samaṃ nekṣasa ātmaja \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I hope the daughter-in-law obeys the mother-in-law and her own husband. О son, I hope you never enter into verbal disputes with the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.15.25 \|\|

*kaccidgāvo na rudhyante viṣaye vividhaistṛṇaiḥ \|*  
*tulāmānāni sarvāṇi hyannādīnāṃ sadekṣase \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I hope the cows are not restrained in the land and are fed on different kinds of grass. I hope you scrutinise the weights and balances of foodgrains and other things.

## \|\| 2.15.26 \|\|

*kuṭumbinaṃ karaiḥ putra nātyarthamabhidūyase \|*  
*kaccinna dyūtapānādi vartate viṣaye tava \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О son, I hope you do not impose too much of a burden on the householder by means of taxes. I believe game of dice and over-addiction to liquor are not present in your land.

## \|\| 2.15.27 \|\|

*kaccidbhinnarasairlokā bhinnavākyaiḥ pure tava \|*  
*na dānairjīrṇavastraiśca nopajīvanti mānavāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I hope there are people of different tastes and different opinions expressed in words in your city. I (further) hope the men do not maintain themselves on liberal gifts of others and do not wear old ragged clothes.

## \|\| 2.15.28 \|\|

*kacciddṛṣṭvā svayaṃ putra hastyaśvaṃ parirakṣasi \|*  
*kaccicca mātaraḥ sarvā hyaviśeṣeṇa paśyasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О son, I hope you personally survey the elephants and horses in your army and protect them. I hope you look after all your mothers without partiality.

## \|\| 2.15.29 \|\|

*kaccinna vāsare viṣṇornarā bhuñjati putraka \|*  
*śaśini kṣīṇatāṃ prāpte kaccicchrāddhaparo naraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О son, I hope men do not take food on the day of Visnu(on the Ekadasi day). I hope men are interested in performing Sraddha when the moon is waning (on the New Moon day).

## \|\| 2.15.30 \|\|

*kacciccāpararātreṣu sadā nidrā ṃ! vimuñjasi \|*  
*nidrā mūlamadharmasya nidrā pāpavivarddhinī \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I hope you always eschew slumber in the latter halves of the nights. Slumber is the root of sins.

## \|\| 2.15.31 \|\|

*nidrā dāridra yjananī nidrā śreyovināśinī \|*  
*nahi nidrā nvito rājā ciraṃ śāsti vasundharām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Slumber is the mother of poverty. It is destructive of prosperity and welfare. No king who is a slave unto slumber rules over the Earth for a long time.

## \|\| 2.15.32 \|\|

*puṃścalīva sadā bharturlokadvayavināśinī \|*  
*evamuccaramāṇaṃ taṃ tanayo vākyamabravīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Just as an unchaste woman destroys both the worlds of her husband so also slumber destroys both the worlds of the king. When the father said all these things, the son spoke these words.

## \|\| 2.15.33 \|\|

*dharmāṅgado mahīpālaṃ praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*sarvametatkṛtaṃ tāta punaḥ kartāsmi te vacaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The son Dharmangada bowed to the king again and again and said. О dear father, all these things have been done by me. I shall again carry out your behests.

## \|\| 2.15.34 \|\|

*piturvacanakartāraḥ putrā dhanyā jagattraye \|*  
*kiṃ tataḥ pātakaṃ rājan yo na kuryātpiturvacaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In all the three worlds those sons who carry out the instructions of their fathers, are blessed. О king, what is more sinful than not carrying out the directives of one’s own father?

## \|\| 2.15.35 \|\|

*pitṛvākyamanādṛtya vrajetsnātuṃ trimārgagām \|*  
*na tattīrthaphalaṃ bhuṅkte yo na kuryātpiturvacaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If the son disobeys his father and goes to Gahga for his holy dip, he does not attain the benefit of the holy river. He who does not carry out his father’s directives does not enjoy the fruits of pilgrimage to holy centres.

## \|\| 2.15.36 \|\|

*tvadadhīnaṃ śarīraṃ me tvadadhīnaṃ hi jīvitam \|*  
*tvadadhīno hi me dharmastvaṃ ca me daivataṃ param \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. My body is subservient to you; my life is at your disposal.1 My duty is subservient to you. You are my great deity.

## \|\| 2.15.37 \|\|

*trailokyasyāpi dānena na śuddhyte ṛṇātsutaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punardehavittābhyāṃ kleśadānādibhirvibho \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A son cannot free himself from indebtedness to his father even by making a gift of the three worlds. О Lord, what then by means of physical strain, monetary gift and other things.

## \|\| 2.15.38-39 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tanayaṃ bahubhūpālasaṃvṛtam \|*  
*rukmāṅgadaḥ pariṣvajya punarāha sutaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*satyametattvayā putra vyāhṛtaṃ dharmavedinā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*piturabhyadhikaṃ kiñciddaivataṃ na sutasya hi \|*  
*devāḥ parāṅmukhāstasya pitaraṃ yo'vamanyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Even as his son surrounded by many kings said thus, Rukmangada embraced the son and spoke these words: О son, you have spoken the truth. You are the knower of virtue. There is no othdr greater deity for a son than his father. If the son disrespects the father, even the gods turn their faces from him.

## \|\| 2.15.40 \|\|

*so'ha mūrdhnā tvayā putra dhṛtastatkṣitirakṣaṇāt \|*  
*jitvā dvīpavatīṃ pṛthvadyaṃ bahubhūpālasaṃvṛtām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Since you have conquered the Earth consisting of many continents and possessing many kings and since you protect that Earth, I have been held by you on your head.

## \|\| 2.15.41 \|\|

*etatsaukhyaṃ paraṃ loke etatsvargapadaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*piturabhyadhikaḥ putro yadbhavetkṣitimaṇḍale \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This is the greatest happiness in the world, certainly this is the heavenly region on the surface of the Earth, that the son is superior to the father.

## \|\| 2.15.42 \|\|

*so'ha putra kṛtārthastu kṛtaḥ sadguṇavartmanā \|*  
*tvayā sādhayatā bhūpānyathā haridinaṃ śubham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О son, I have been made contented by you who traverse the path of good qualities and who make all the kings observe holy rite on the auspicious day of Hari.

## \|\| 2.15.43 \|\|

*tatpiturvacanaṃ śrutvā putro dharmāṅgado'bravīt \|*  
*kva gatastu bhavāṃstāta niveśya mayi sampadaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing these words of his father, Dharmarigada, the son said ‘‘O father, where did you go after depositing all the riches in me?

## \|\| 2.15.44 \|\|

*kasminsthāne tviyaṃ prāptā sūryāyutasamaprabhā \|*  
*manye nirvedamāpanna imāṃ sṛṣṭvā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. At what place was this lady with the lustre of ten thousand suns attained by you? I think, after creating her Praja- pati (Brahma) had become disgusted with the world and detached from it.

## \|\| 2.15.45 \|\|

*naitadrū pā mahīpāla nārī trailokyamadhyataḥ \|*  
*manye bhūdharajāteyamathavā sāgarodbhavā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О king, in the whole of the three worlds there is no other woman with this form and beauty. I think she is born of the mountain or originated from the ocean.

## \|\| 2.15.46-47 \|\|

*māyā vā mayadaityasya pramadārūpasaṃsthitā \|*  
*aho sunipuṇo dhātā yeneyaṃ nirmitā vibho \|*  
*bālāgraśatabhāgo hi vyalīko nopapadyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*iyaṃ hi yogyā kanakāvadātā gṛhāya tubhyaṃ jagatīpatīśa \|*  
*evaṃvidhā me jananī yadi syāt ko'nyo'sti mattaḥ sukṛtī manuṣyaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Or she may be the Maya (illusion) of the Daitya Maya, with the form of a young woman assumed by her. О Lord, indeed, Brahma by whom she has been created is very clever. There is no slightest defect even to the extent of a hundred part of the tip of a hair. О Lord of the kings of the Earth, she is worthy of being the heroine of your house since she is as pure as gold. If I were to have a mother of such a type, which man is more meritorious than I?”

## Chapter 16. The Anecdote of a chasle Lady

## \|\| 2.16.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- dharmāṅgadavacaḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭo rukmāṅgado'bravīt \|*  
*satyaṃ te jananī putra samprāptā mandare mayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasitfha said:

1\. On hearing the words of Dharmangada, Rukmangada became delighted and said: It is true, О son, your new mother has been obtained by me on the Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 2.16.2 \|\|

*vedāśrayasutā bālā madarthaṃ kṛtaniścayā \|*  
*kurvantī dāruṇaṃ putra tapo devagirau purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She is the daughter of Vedasraya (support of the Vedas i.e. Brahma). Formerly, О dear son, she had been performing a terrible penance on the divine mountain Mandara, with the determination of attaining me.

## \|\| 2.16.3 \|\|

*itaḥ pañcadaśādahno hayagāmī gato hyaham \|*  
*mandare parvataśreṣṭhe bahudhātusamanvite \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Some fifteen days before I started from here, riding on the horse I reached the Mandara, the most excellent of the mountains, containing many metals and minerals.

## \|\| 2.16.4 \|\|

*tasya mūrddhani bāleyaṃ toṣayantī maheśvaram \|*  
*sthitā gānaparā dṛṣṭā mayā tatra sudarśanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This damsel of comely appearance was seen by me seated on the top of the mountain, propitiating Mahesvara and engaged in singing.

## \|\| 2.16.5 \|\|

*tato'ha mūrcchayā yuktaḥ patito dharaṇītale \|*  
*anaṅgabāṇasaṃviddho vyādhaviddho yathā mṛgaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hit by the arrows of Ananga (the God of Love), I became unconscious and fell on the ground like the deer hit by a hunter.

## \|\| 2.16.6 \|\|

*tato'hamanayā devyā cālitaścārunetrayā \|*  
*vṛtaścaivāpi bhartṛtve kiñcitprārthanayā saha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereafter, I had been shaken (and revived into) consciousness)by this gentlelady of charming eyes; with some importunity I have been chosen as her husband.

## \|\| 2.16.7 \|\|

*mayā cāpi pratijñātaṃ svadakṣiṇakarānvitam \|*  
*seyaṃ bhāryā viśālākṣī kṛtā bhūdharamastake \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I too have taken the pledge with offering of my right hand. This lady of large eyes has been made my wife by me on the top of the mountain.

## \|\| 2.16.8 \|\|

*avaruhya dharāpṛṣṭhe samāruhya turaṅgamam \|*  
*dinatrayeṇa tvaritaḥ samprāptastava sannidhau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Descending to the ground level (at that foot of the mountain), we got up on to the horse. Hurried (travelling therefrom) we have come to you within three days.

## \|\| 2.16.9 \|\|

*paśyamāno girīndeśānsarāṃsi saritastathā \|*  
*iyaṃ hi jananī putra tava prītivivarddhinī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. -11. On my way I had the pleasure of seeing mountains, different lands, lakes and rivers. О son, she is your mother. She would heighten your pleasure. Make obeisance to this lady of charming limbs as though to your own natural mother. On hearing the words of his father, the son, the suppressor of his enemies, bent down his head as far as the ground level and spoke these words: — О gentle lady, О dear mother, favour me. I am your son, servant and slave.

## \|\| 2.16.12-13 \|\|

*namaskaromi jananīṃ bahubhūpālasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*taṃ putramavanīṃ prāptaṃ mohinī prekṣya bhūpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bharturdākṣiṇyayogācca avatīrya turaṅgamāt \|*  
*avāgūhata bāhubhyāmutthāpya patitaṃ sutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Accompanied by many kings I make obeisance to my mother. On seeing the son prostrating on the ground and thanks to the chivalry of her husband, the king, Mohini got down from the horse, raised up the son and embraced him with her hands.

## \|\| 2.16.14-22 \|\|

*pariṣvaktastadā mātrā punarevābhyanandayat \|*  
*tatastāṃ sumanojñaistu cāruvastraiśca bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhūṣayitvā samāropya punareva hayottamam \|*  
*svapṛṣṭhe caraṇaṃ kṛtvā tasyā rājīvalocanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tenaiva vidhinā bhūpa pitaraṃ cānvarohayat \|*  
*bhūpālaiḥ saṃvṛto gacchanpadbhyāṃ dharmāṅgadaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*praharṣapulako hyāsījjananīṃ prekṣya mohinīm \|*  
*stūyamānaḥ svayaṃ cāpi meghagambhīrayā girā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhanyaḥ sa tanayo loke mātaro yasya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*navā navatarā bhāryāḥ pituriṣṭā manoharāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yasyaikā jananī loke pitā tasyaiva duḥkhabhāk \|*  
*piturduḥkhena kiṃ saukhyaṃ putrasya hṛdi vartate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ekasyā vandane mātuḥ pṛthivī phalamaśnute \|*  
*mātṝṇāṃ vandane mahyaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tasmādabhyadhikaṃ puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyati dine dine \|*  
*evamuccaramāṇo'sau rājabhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*praviṣṭo nagaraṃ ramyaṃ vaidiśaṃ ṛddhisaṃyutam \|*  
*hayasthaḥ prayayau rājā mohinyā saha tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

14-16a. Embraced by his mother, he saluted her once again. He adorned her with nice clothes and charming ornaments. Dharmangada, the son with eyes like lotus, requested her to place her legs on his back and mount the horse. In the same manner, he made his father too mount the horse.

16b-17a. He himself walked on foot surrounded by the vassal kings. On looking at his step-mother he was delighted and had his hair standing on their ends. Praising himself in a resonant voice like the rumbling sound of the cloud he said.

17b-21a. Blessed is the son who has many mothers in the world, new, fresh and charming beloved wives of his father. If one has only one mother, one’s father is miserable. If the father is miserable what happiness can the son have in the heart? By saluting one mother the son has only the merit of bowing to one earth. By saluting many mothers I will have greater benefit day by day.

2lb-22. Saying thus he entered the city surrounded by the vassal kings. He entered the beautiful city ofVaidiia endowed with (i.e. abounding in) all prosperity. Seated on the horse alongwith Mohini the king too followed instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.16.23 \|\|

*tato gṛhavaraṃ prāpya pūjyamāno janairnṛpaḥ \|*  
*avaruhya hayāttasmānmohinīṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then he entered the excellent mansion. On being greeted and honoured by the people, the king got down from the horse and spoke these words to Mohini.

## \|\| 2.16.24 \|\|

*dharmāṅgadasya putrasya gṛhe gaccha manohare \|*  
*eṣa te guruśuśrūṣāṃ kariṣyati yathā guṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О charming one, go to the house of Dharmangada our son. In accordance with his attributes, he will render service to you as befitting an elderly person.

## \|\| 2.16.25 \|\|

*na sakhī naiva dāsī te śuśrūṣāmācarediti \|*  
*sā caivamuktā patyā tu prasthitā sutamandiram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Neither a chaperon nor a servant can render such a willing service! On being thus advised by her husband, she started for the mansion of their son.

## \|\| 2.16.26-27 \|\|

*dharmāṅgadena sā dṛṣṭā gacchantī mandirāya vai \|*  
*ātmano bhartṛvākyena parityajya mahīpatīn \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhadhvaṃ piturādeśādimāṃ śuśrūṣaye hyaham \|*  
*sa evamuktvā gatvā tu bāhubhyāṃ parigṛhya vai \|*  
*krame pañcadaśe prāpte paryaṅke tvavaropayat \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. She was seen entering the mansion by Dharmangada, at the instance of her husband’s words. He thereupon left the vassal kings saying — “All of you stay here. At the behest of my father, I shall render personal service unto her. On saying this he entered the mansion an^ grasped the hands of his step-mother. After walking fifteen steps, they reached the cot. He made Mohini sit there.

## \|\| 2.16.28-29 \|\|

*kāñcane paṭṭasūtreṇa racite komale dṛḍhe \|*  
*mṛdvāstaraṇasaṃyukte maṇiratnavibhūṣite \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ratnadīpaiśca bahuśaḥ khacite sūryasaprabhe \|*  
*tataḥ pādodakaṃ cakre mohinyā dharmabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. It was made of gold with silk cloth spread over. It was soft and firm. A soft bed-sheet was spread over it. It was bedecked in gems and jewels. Many jewelled lamps having the refulgence of the sun, were fitted on to it. Thereafter, the prince who had virtue as his ornament (i.e. Dharmangada) offered water for washing the feet of Mohini.

## \|\| 2.16.30-31 \|\|

*sandhyāvalyā gurutvena hyapaśyattāṃ nṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*naivamasyābhavadduṣṭaṃ manastāṃ mohinīṃ prati \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sukumāro'pi tanvaṅgī pīnorujaghanastanīm \|*  
*mene varṣāyutasamāmātmānaṃ ca trivatsaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The prince considered her even elderly to Sandhyavali. His mind did not have any ignoble feelings towards Mohini. Though he was beautiful and graceful and she a charming lady with plump and stout thighs, buttocks and breasts, he considered her a lady ten thousand years old and himself a boy of three years.

## \|\| 2.16.32 \|\|

*prakṣālya caraṇau tasyāstajjalaṃ śirasi nyadhāt \|*  
*uvācāvanato bhūtvā sukṛtī mātarasmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After washing her feet, he applied (sprinkled) that watet on his head. With the head bent down in humility he said: Mother, I am meritorious (with you as my mother).

## \|\| 2.16.33 \|\|

*ityuktvā naranārībhiḥ svayaṃ ca śramanāśanam \|*  
*cakāra sarvabhogaistāṃ yuyoja ca mudānvitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After saying this, he dispelled her fatigue by his own efforts and by those of men and women (servants). With great joy he placed all means of pleasures at her disposal.

## \|\| 2.16.34-37 \|\|

*kṣīrodamathane jāte kuṇḍale cāmṛtasrave \|*  
*ye labdhe dānavāñjitvā pātāle dharmamūrtinā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mohinyā karṇayoścakre svayameva vṛṣāṅgadaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottarasahasraiśca dhātrīphalanibhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mauktikai racitaiḥ śubhrairhāro devyāḥ kṛto hṛdi \|*  
*niṣkaṃ palaśataṃ svarṇaṃ kuliśāyutabhūṣitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*hāraṃ laghūttaraṃ cakre māturnṛpasutastadā \|*  
*valayā vajrakhacitā dviraṣṭau karayordvayoḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-35a. At the time of the churning of the milk ocean two earrings were produced. They used to emit nectarine juice. These were acquired by Dharmamurti.1 After conquering Danavas in the Pa tala (nether worlds). Vrsarigada (i.e. Dharmangada) himself put these in the ears of Mohini.

35b-36a. A necklace of a thousand and eight auspicious white pearls each like the fruit of the embylic myrobalan was put on the bosom of the gentle lady.

36b-37. Then the prince offered her a subsidiary light necklace of gold coins of a hundred Palas inset with ten thousand diamonds to his mothers. He gave her twice eight bangles (i.e. sixteen) studded with diamonds for both the hands.

## \|\| 2.16.38-46 \|\|

*ekaike niṣkakoṭībhirmūlyavidbhirnaraiḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*keyūranūpurau tasyā anarghau sa nṛpātmajaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pradadau pituriṣṭāyā bhūṣaṇārthaṃ raviprabhau \|*  
*kaṭisūtraṃ tu śarvāṇyā yadāsītpāvakaprabham \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tadbhraṣṭaṃ bhayabhītāyāḥ saṅgrāme tārakāmaye \|*  
*kālanemau sthite rājye patitaṃ mūlapācane \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tadgṛhītaṃ tu daityena mayena lokamāyinā \|*  
*taṃ hatvā malaye daityaṃ daityakoṭisamāvṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saṃvatsararaṇe ghore piturvacanakāraṇāt \|*  
*avāpa kaṭisūtraṃ tu daityarājapriyāsthitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*taddadau pituriṣṭāyāḥ sānandapulako nṛpaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ pūrvaṃ yā bhāryā lokasundarī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ sīmantakaścāsītsaudāminisamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*sā praviṣṭā samaṃ patyā yadā pāvakamaṅgalā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*samudre kṣipya sīmantaṃ duḥkhena mahatānvitā \|*  
*sāgarastattu saṅgṛhya ratnaśreṣṭhayugaṃ kila \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dadau dhamāṅgadāyātha tasya vīryeṇa toṣitaḥ \|*  
*jananyāḥ pradadau hṛṣṭaḥ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 46 \|\|*

38-43a. They were made by men who knew their value. For each of the hands, a crore of gold coins was spent. The prince gave invaluable armlets and anklets to the beloved wife of his father as ornament. They had the refulgence of the sun. The girdle of fiery refulgence that SarvanI (Parvatl) had, fell off as she was extremely terrified in the course of the fight called Tarakamaya (pertaining to the demon Taraka) while Kalanemi was ruling over the kingdom. It then fell into Mulapacana (original fire). Thereafter, it was picked up by the demon Maya who wielded his power of illusion over the whole world. Dharmangada had killed that Daitya on Mount Malaya although he had been surrounded by a crore of Daityas. At the instance of his father, he had killed him in the course of a terrible war that lasted for a year (on the mountain Malaya). He got the girdle that the beloved of the king of the Daityas had on her person. The king gave that to his father’s beloved great queen with his hair standing on their ends out of delight.

43b-46. Formerly, HiranyakaSipu’s queen who was an outstanding beauty in the world, had a crest jewel that had the refulgence of lightning. She immolated herself in her husband’s funeral pyre. Before dying, the extremely distressed lady had cast her crest-jewel into the sea. The sea collected the excellent jewel and presented it to Dharmangada on being delighted at his prowess. The delighted prince now gave that jewel which had the brilliance of a crore of suns to his stepmother.

## \|\| 2.16.47 \|\|

*agniśauce śubhe vastre kañcuke sumanohare \|*  
*sahasrakoṭimūlye te mohinyāḥ saṃnyavedayat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He gave MohinI two auspicious clothes sanctified in fire and two charming bodices, a thousand crores in value.

## \|\| 2.16.48-49 \|\|

*devamālyaṃ sugandhāḍhyaṃ tathā devavilepanam \|*  
*sarvadevaguroḥ pūrvaṃ siddhahastātsudurlabham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*dharmāṅgadena vīreṇa dvīpānāṃ vijaye tathā \|*  
*labdhaṃ tat pradadau devyā mohinyāḥ kāmavarddhanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Dharmangada then gave the gentle lady Mohini, the divine garland and the sweet-smelling divine unguent that was very rare and had been acquired from the accomplished hands of the preceptor of all the Devas by the heroic Dharman- gada in the course of his conquest of all the continents. He gave her the unguent that enhanced her love.

## \|\| 2.16.50 \|\|

*saṃbhūṣya parayā bhaktyā paścātṣaḍrasabhojanam \|*  
*ānītaṃ mātṛhastena bhojayāmāsa bhūmipa \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After embellishing her with great devotion, he fed her with meals consisting of dishes of six tastes and brought by his natural mother herself

## \|\| 2.16.51 \|\|

*purastādeva jananīṃ vākyaiḥ sambodhya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*mayā tvayā ca kartavyaṃ rājño vākyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even before this, he had addressed his natural mother and enlightened her by means of many words. There is no doubt about this that the behest of the king must be carried out by me as well as by you.

## \|\| 2.16.52-54 \|\|

*yā iṣṭā nṛpaterdevi sāsmākaṃ hi garīyasī \|*  
*iṣṭā yā bhūpaterbhartustasyā yā duṣṭamācaret \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sā patnī narakaṃ yāti yāvadindrā ścaturdaśa \|*  
*sāpatnabhāvaṃ yā kuryādbhartṛsneheṣṭayā saha \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ snehaviyogārthaṃ tapyate tāmrabhrāṣṭrake \|*  
*yathā sukhaṃ bhavedbhartustathā kāryaṃ hi bhāryayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-53a. О gentle lady, she who is the king’s beloved is a highly respectable woman for us. The wife who acts wickedly against the lady-love of the king, her husband, falls into hell and stays there till fourteen Indras reign.

53b-54. She who nurses feelings of enmity against the lady-love of her husband and tries to separate them in their love, is fried in Tamrabhrasfa hell (the frying pan made of copper.) Everything that is conducive to the happiness of her husband, should be done by the wife.

## \|\| 2.16.55 \|\|

*anukūlaṃ hitaṃ tasyā iṣṭāyā bharturācaret \|*  
*yathā bhartā tathā tāṃ hi paśyeta varavarṇini \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О fair-complexioned lady, she must view her as she views her husband. She must do what is favourable and beneficent to the lady-love of her husband.

## \|\| 2.16.56 \|\|

*hīnāyāścāpi śuśrūṣāṃ kṛtvā yāti triviṣṭapam \|*  
*paścātsthāne bhavetsāpi manasā yābhavatpriye \|\| 56 \|\|*

56a. Even if she (the husband’s lady-love) happens to be of a lower caste, the wife who renders service to her, goes to heaven.

56b. Afterwards she will occupy the same loving place in the mind of her husband.

## \|\| 2.16.57 \|\|

*sarvānbhogānavāpnoti bharturiṣṭaṃ pragṛhya hi \|*  
*īrṣyābhāvaparityāgātsarveśvarapadaṃ labhet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After acceding to the wish of her husband she derives all worldly pleasures. By eschewing the feelings of malice and jealousy, she attains the region of the Lord of every one.

## \|\| 2.16.58 \|\|

*sapatnī yā sapatnyāstu śūśrūṣāṃ kurute sadā \|*  
*bharturiṣṭāṃ saṃnirīkṣya tasyā loko'kṣayo bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On seeing a cowife to be the most beloved of her husband, if a woman renders service to her, she will attain an eternal place in heaven.

## \|\| 2.16.59-60 \|\|

*bharturiṣṭā purā veśyā hyabhavatsā kuleṣu vai \|*  
*śūdra jāteḥ suduṣṭasya parityaktakriyasya tu \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ācaradveśyayā sārddhaṃ sā bhāryā patirañjinī \|*  
*prakṣālanaṃ dvayoḥ pādau dvayorucchiṣṭabhojinī \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. There was a very wicked man of the Sudra caste. He had abandoned all holy rites.1 He had a wife and also a beloved lady, a prostitute whom he kept in his house. The wife who wanted to please her husband served him as well as the prostitute. She washed the feet of both of them. She partook only of the leavings of the food of both of them.

## \|\| 2.16.61 \|\|

*ubhayorapyadhaḥ śete ubhayorvai hitaṃ ratā \|*  
*veśyayā vāryamāṇāpi sadācārapathe sthitā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Though she was prevented from doing this by the prostitute, she continued her activities of service. She ever remained in the path of the good. She was engaged in what was beneficent for both of them; while both of them lay on the cot, she used to lie down beneath on the bare ground.

## \|\| 2.16.62 \|\|

*evaṃ śuśrūṣayantyā hi bhartāraṃ veśyayā saha \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālo vartantyā duḥkhasāgare \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thus she served her husband alongwith the prostitute for a long time, wading through the ocean of misery.

## \|\| 2.16.63-64 \|\|

*aparasmindine bhartā māhiṣaṃ mūlakānvitam \|*  
*abhakṣayata niṣpāvaṃ durmedhāstailamiśritam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tadapathyabhujastasya avamanya pativratām \|*  
*abhavaddāruṇo rogo gude tasya bhagandaraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Without caring for the advice of the chaste wife the man committed many blunders in the matter of his diet etc. He drank the milk of the buffalo alongwith radish. The foolish fellow ate the winnowings (of corn) mixed with oil. As a result of this he had a terrible fistula in the anus.

## \|\| 2.16.65-67 \|\|

*sandahyamāno'titarāṃ divārātrau sa bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*tasya gehe sthitaṃ vittaṃ samādāya jagāma sā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*veśyānyasmai dadau prītyā yūne kāmaparāyaṇā \|*  
*tataḥ sa dīnavadano vrīḍayā ca samanvitaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*uvāca prarudanbhāryāṃ śūdro vyākulacetanaḥ \|*  
*paripālaya māṃ devi veśyāsaktaṃ suniṣṭhuram \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-66a. He was extremely distressed by day and night. The prostitute took everything valuable that the house contained and went over to another young man. The lustful woman gave him all the wealth.

66b-67. Now the Sudra man became much ashamed. With distress evident in his face, he lamented and spoke thus to his wife: О gentle lady, save me though I had been very cruel to you and much attached to a prostitute.

## \|\| 2.16.68 \|\|

*na mayopakṛtaṃ kiñcittava sundari pāpinā \|*  
*ramate veśyayā sārddhaṃ bahūnabdānsumadhyame \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О beautiful lady, the sinner that I am, I have never done a good thing to you. О lady of slender waist, for many years I sported about alongwith the prostitute.

## \|\| 2.16.69 \|\|

*yo bhāryāṃ praṇatāṃ pāpo nānumanyeta garvitaḥ \|*  
*so'śubhāni samāpnoti janmāni daśa pañca ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The sinful haughty man who does not console his wife who bows down to him, attains all inauspicious things in the course of fifteen rebirths.

## \|\| 2.16.70 \|\|

*divākīrtigṛhe tasmādyoniṃ prāpsyāmi garhitām \|*  
*tavāpamānato devi mano na kaluṣīkṛtam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О gentle lady, since I had disrespected you, I shall attain the despicable birth in the house of a Canglala. But your mind has not been turbid despite insults.

## \|\| 2.16.71 \|\|

*iti bhartṛvacaḥ śrutvā bhāryā bhartāramabravīt \|*  
*purā kṛtāni pāpāni duḥkhāni prabhavanti hi \|*  
*tāni sakṣamate vidvān savijñeyo nṛṇāṃ varaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On hearing these words of her husband, the wife spoke to the husband. It is the sins committed in the previous births that yield miseries. A learned man who bears them with fortitude, should be known as the most excellent ^among men.

## \|\| 2.16.72 \|\|

*tanmayā pāpayā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ vai pūrvajanmani \|*  
*tadbhajantyā na me duḥkhaṃ na viṣādaḥ kathañcana \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. I had been sinful in the previous births. Now I experienced the fruits thereofin this birth. Hence, I have neither sorrow nor misery.

## \|\| 2.16.73 \|\|

*evamuktvā samāśvāsya bhartāramanuśāsya ca \|*  
*ānītaṃ janakādvittaṃ bandhubhyo varavarṇinī \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. By saying this she consoled and cautioned her husband. The fair-complexioned lady brought some money from her father and other kinsmen.

## \|\| 2.16.74-75 \|\|

*kṣīrodanilayāvāsaṃ manyate sma satī patim \|*  
*divā divā triryatnena rātrau guhyaviśodhanam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*rajanīkaravṛkṣotthaṃ gṛhya niryāsamañjasā \|*  
*nakhena pātayedbhartuḥ krimīnkuṣṭhācchanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. The chaste lady considered her husband a Visnu, the resident of the milk ocean. She cleaned his anus and other private parts assiduously by day as well as by night, by means of turmeric juice and water. She scraped the germs and worms in the body of her husband, by means of her nail.

## \|\| 2.16.76 \|\|

*mayūrapucchasaṃyuktaṃ pavanaṃ cākarottadā \|*  
*na devi rātrau svapiti na divā ca varānanā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. She fanned him with peacock feathers. О gentle lady, ihe fair-faced lady slept neither during the day nor at night.

## \|\| 2.16.77-78 \|\|

*bhartṛduḥkhena santaptā apaśyajjavalitaṃ jagat \|*  
*yadyasti vasudhā devī pitaro devatāstathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*kurvantu rogahīnaṃ me bhartāraṃ gatakalmaṣam \|*  
*caṇḍikāyai pradāsyāmi raktaṃ māṃsasamudbhavam \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Distressed by the misery of her husband, she felt that the whole universe was blazing (?). She said — If there is goddess of earth, if there are manes, if there are deities, may they make my husband free from ailments. May he be free from sins. I shall give unto Goddess Gandika blood mixed with flesh.

## \|\| 2.16.79 \|\|

*nṛcchāgamahiṣopetaṃ bharturārogyahetave \|*  
*sādaraṃ kārayiṣyāmi upavāsāndaśaiva tu \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. I shall offer the flesh of goats, buffaloes and even human beings for the well being of my husband. With great respect I shall observe ten fasts.

## \|\| 2.16.80 \|\|

*śarīraṃ sthāpayiṣye'ha sūkṣmakaṇṭakasaṃstare \|*  
*nopabhokṣyāmi madhuraṃ nopabhokṣyāmi vai ghṛtam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. I shall place my body on a bed of sharp-pointed thorns. I shall not take sweet things. I shall not take ghee.

## \|\| 2.16.81 \|\|

*bāhyābhyaṅgavihīnāhaṃ saṃsthāsye dinasañcayam \|*  
*jīvatāṃ rogahīno hi bhartā me śaradāṃ śatam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. I shall remain for days together without anointing the body externally with oil. May my husband live for a hundred years without any ailment.

## \|\| 2.16.82-84 \|\|

*evaṃ pravyāharantī sā vāsare vāsare gate \|*  
*atha kālena cālpena tridoṣo'sya vyajāyata \|\| 82 \|\|*

*trikaṭuṃ pradadau bharturyatnena mahatā tadā \|*  
*śītārtaḥ kampamāno'sau patnyaṅgulimakhaṇḍayat \|\| 83 \|\|*

*ubhayordantayoḥ śleṣaḥ sahasā samapadyata \|*  
*tatkhaṇḍamaṅgulervaktre sthitaṃ nṛpativallabhe \|\| 84 \|\|*

82-83a. As day followed day, she blurted out like this in her agony. Within a short while, all the three humours in his system were upset. With great effort she gave her husband the three astringent medicines (black and long pepper and dry ginger).

83b-84. Once due to chilliness the man was quaking and shivering. His jaws suddenly came together and the finger of the wife was bitten off by the teeth coming^ together. О queen of the Lord of men, the piece of finger remained within the rigid mouth.

## \|\| 2.16.85 \|\|

*atha vikrīya valayaṃ krītvā kāṣṭhāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*citāṃ sarpiryutāṃ cakre madhye dhṛtvā patiṃ tadā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. She sold off her bangle and brought a great deal of fuel. She prepared the funeral pyre. After placing her dead husband on it, she poured ghee over the pyre (fuel).

## \|\| 2.16.86-89 \|\|

*avaruhya ca bāhubhyāṃ pādenākṛṣya pāvakam \|*  
*mukhe mukhaṃ samādhāya hṛdaye hṛdayaṃ tathā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*jaghane jaghanaṃ devi ātmanaḥ sanniveśya vai \|*  
*dāhayāmāsa kalyāṇī bharturdehaṃ rujānvitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*ātmanā saha cārvaṅgī jvalite jātavedasi \|\| 88 \|\|*

*vimucya dehaṃ sahasā jagāma patiṃ samādāya ca devalokam \|*  
*viśodhayitvā bahupāpasaṅghānsvakarmaṇā duṣkarasādhanena \|\| 89 \|\|*

86-89. She too climbed on the funeral pyre joining her face to his face, her heart near his heart and О gentle lady, her buttocks near his buttocks. With her foot she dragged the fire. The auspicious lady of charming limbs set fire to the ailing body of the husband alongwith her body. As the fire blazed brightly, she cast off her body and went to the world of the Devas taking her husband with her after annihilating many of his sins by means of her holy rites very difficult to be performed.

## Chapter 17. The statement of Mohini

## \|\| 2.17.1 \|\|

*putra uvāca- tasmādīrṣyāṃ parityajya mohinīmanubhojaya \|*  
*na mātarīdṛśo dharmo lokeṣu triṣu labhyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

The son (Dharmangadd) said:

1\. Hence, О Mother, eschew jealousy and feed Mohini. A holy rite (dharma) like this cannot be attained in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.17.2-3 \|\|

*svahastena priyāṃ bharturbhāryāṃ yā tu prabhojayet \|*  
*sapatnīṃ tu sapatnī hi kiñcidannaṃ dadāti ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tadanantaṃ bhaveddevi mātarityāha nābhijaḥ \|*  
*kuru vākyaṃ mayoktaṃ hi svāmini tvaṃ prasīda me \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The wife who, with her own hands, feeds the beloved lady love of her husband, the co-wife who gives a little quantity of cooked rice to the co-wife shall, О gentle lady, О dear mother, become immortal — So says god Brahma. О Mistress (of the Mansion) be favourable to me carry out what has been related by me.

## \|\| 2.17.4 \|\|

*tātasya saukhyaṃ kartavyamāvābhyāṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*bhavetpāpakṣayaḥ samyak svargaprāptistathākṣayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О fair-complexioned lady, what is conducive to the happiness of my dear father must be performed by both of us. The sins shall be exterminated perfectly. Similarly, the attainment of heaven shall be everlasting.

## \|\| 2.17.5-6 \|\|

*putrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā devī sandhyāvalī tadā \|*  
*abhimantr! ya pariṣvajya tanayaṃ sā punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mūrdhni cainamupāghrāya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|*  
*kariṣye vacanaṃ putra tvadīyaṃ dharmasaṃyutam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. On hearing the words of her son then, the queen Sandhyavali invited her son and embraced him again and again. She sniffed at his head and spoke these words: “O son I shall carry out your words pregnant with dharma (virtues).

## \|\| 2.17.7 \|\|

*irṣyāṃ mānaṃ parityajya bhojayiṣyāmi mohinīm \|*  
*śataputrā hyahaṃ putra tvayaikena sutena hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Eschewing jealousy and false prestige I shall feed Mohini. I have the pleasure of being the mother of a hundred sons, О son, with you as my only son.

## \|\| 2.17.8 \|\|

*niyamairbahubhirjāto dehakleśakarairbhavān \|*  
*vratarājena cīrṇena prāptastvamacirātsutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It was after observing many holy rites and restraints causing bodily exertion, that you were born. Since I observed the holiest of holy rites, the ‘king of holy rites, you were attained by me as my son.

## \|\| 2.17.9 \|\|

*nahīdṛśaṃ vrataṃ loke phaladāyi pradṛśyate \|*  
*sadyaḥ pratyayakārīdaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In this world there is no other holy rite that is seen to be yielding benefits like this. This gives convincing proofs immediately. This is destructive of great sins.

## \|\| 2.17.10 \|\|

*kiṃ jātairbahubhiḥ putraiḥ śokasantāpakārakaiḥ \|*  
*varamekaḥ kulālambī yatra viśramate kulam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Of what avail is it if many sons who cause sorrow and distress are born? It is better to have one son, as the main prop of the family, where the entire family takes comfortable rest.

## \|\| 2.17.11 \|\|

*trailokyādupariṣṭhāhaṃ tvāṃ prāpya jaṭhare sthitam \|*  
*dhanyāni tāni śūlāni yairjātastvaṃ suto'nagha \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On attaining you as one stationed in my womb, I have reached the top of the three worlds (I am above the three worlds). О sinless one, blessed are those pains of labour whereby you are born as my son.

## \|\| 2.17.12 \|\|

*saptadvīpapatiḥ śūraḥ piturvacanakārakaḥ \|*  
*āhlādayati yastātaṃ jananīṃ vāpi putrakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You are the son who delight both father and mother you are the heroic son who have become the Lord of seven continents; you have carried out the words of your father.

## \|\| 2.17.13-15 \|\|

*taṃ putraṃ kavayaḥ prāhurvācākhyamaparaṃ sutam \|*  
*evamuktvā tu vacanaṃ devī sandhyāvalī tadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vīkṣāṃ cakre'tha bhāṇḍāni ṣaḍrasasya tu hetave \|*  
*tasyā vīkṣaṇamātreṇa paripūrṇāni bhūpate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ṣaḍrasasya sukhoṣṇasya mohinībhojanecchayā \|*  
*amṛtasvādukalpasya janasya tu mahīpate \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Poets (Learned Philosophers) call only that person real son — the person who delights both the father and the mother. Others are only ‘so-called’ sons. After saying these words, queen Sandhyavali just glanced at the pots and utensils for the purpose of a meal consisting of dishes of all the six tastes. By her very glance the utensils were full of dishes that would be pleasantly warm and that would be as tasty as Nectar, which she wished that Mohini should partake of. A better emendation: abhinandya ‘‘praised”, ‘approved of in stead of abhi-mantrya in the text.

## \|\| 2.17.16 \|\|

*tato darvīṃ samādāya kāñcanīṃ ratnasaṃyutām \|*  
*pariveṣayadavyagrā mohinyāścāruhāsinī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She took a golden ladle studded with jewels. Smiling sweetly, she served food to Mohini without any perturbation.

## \|\| 2.17.17 \|\|

*kāñcane bhājane ślakṣṇe mānabhojanaveṣṭite \|*  
*śanaiḥ śanaiśca bubhuje iṣṭamannaṃ susaṃskṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. She slowly ate the desired and well cooked food in a polished excellent vessel, all round which beverages and edible dishes had been placed.

## \|\| 2.17.18-19 \|\|

*upaviśyāsane devī śātakaumbhamaye śubhe \|*  
*vījyamānā varārohā vyajanena sugītinā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dharmāṅgadagṛhītena śikhipucchabhavena tu \|*  
*sā bhuktvā brahmatanayā tadannamamṛtopamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The gentle lady, the daughter of Brahma, sat on an auspicious golden seat and took food that was comparable to nectar. While taking food, the fair lady was fanned with a fan of peacock feathers held by Dharmangada, in accompaniment of music.

## \|\| 2.17.20-21 \|\|

*caturguṇena śītena kṛtvā śaucamathātmanaḥ \|*  
*jagṛhe putradattaṃ tu tāmbūlaṃ tatsugandhimat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*varacandanayuktena hastena varavarṇinī \|*  
*tataḥ prahasya śanakaiḥ prāha sandhyāvaladyaṃ nṛpa \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. After washing with cool water (her hands and mouth gurgling four times), she accepted the fragrant Tambula (chewing betel leaves) given by her (step)-son. The fair-com- plexioned lady took it with her hand over which excellent sandal paste had been applied. Then О king, she laughed and said slowly to Sandhyavali.

## \|\| 2.17.22 \|\|

*jananī kiṃ tu devi tvaṃ vṛṣāṅgadanṛpasya tu \|*  
*na mayā hi parijñātā śramasveditayā śubhe \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O gentle lady, are you the mother of king Vrshan- gada (i.e. Dharmangada)? О auspicious lady, due to perspiring tiredness you cauld not be recognised by me.”

## \|\| 2.17.23 \|\|

*vadatyevaṃ brahmasutā yāvatsandhyāvaladyaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tāvatpraṇamya nṛpateḥ putro vacanamavrabīt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О king, while the daughter of Brahma was speaking thus to Sandhyavali, the son of the king bowed to her and spoke these words.

## \|\| 2.17.24 \|\|

*udare hyanayā devyā dhṛtaṃ saṃvatsaratrayam \|*  
*tava bhartuḥ prasādena vṛddhiṃ saṃprāptavānaham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “I had been held in her belly (womb) by this gentle lady for three years. I flourished thanks to the favour of your husband.

## \|\| 2.17.25 \|\|

*santyanekāni mātṝṇāṃ śatāni mama saṃndari \|*  
*asyāḥ pītaṃ payo bhūri kucayoḥ snehasamplutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Beautiful lady, I have hundreds of mothers. But much milk flowing out from the breasts of this lady out of (motherly) affection has been drunk by me.

## \|\| 2.17.26 \|\|

*anayā sā rujā tīvrā vidhṛtā prāyaśo jarā \|*  
*iyaṃ māṃ janayitvaiva jātā śithilabandhanā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. That severe pain which more or less amounts to old age has been endured by her. It was after giving birth to me that she had become disjointed in her limbs.

## \|\| 2.17.27 \|\|

*tannāsti triṣu lokeṣu yaddatvā cānṛṇo bhavet \|*
