77\. Like the ten-headed Ravana who had abducted Sita, he had carried the slender-limbed auspicious daughter of the ruler of Kasi, named Ratnavali on his lap.

## \|\| 2.27.78 \|\|

*adhautapādāṃ suśroṇīṃ saumyadikchīrṣaśāyinīm \|*  
*patikāmā kumārī sā nāvindatsadṛśaṃ patim \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Without washing her feet, she had gone to sleep with her head directed towards the north. The virgin of beautiful buttocks was desirous of obtaining a husband, but did not obtain one befitting her.

## \|\| 2.27.79 \|\|

*sarvayoṣidvarā bālā rudatī nidra yākulā \|*  
*pitā tasyāḥ pradāne tu cintāviṣṭo hyaharnniśam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. That girl was the foremost among all women. Overwhelmed by slumber she was crying. In the matter of giving her in marriage, her father had been extremely anxious day and night.

## \|\| 2.27.80 \|\|

*dīpacchāyāśrite tanvi śayane sā vyavasthitā \|*  
*aṭamānena pāpena dṛṣṭā sā rūpaśālinī \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. О lady of slender limbs, this beautiful girl, occupying a bed spread in the shadow of the lamp was seen by the sinful demon who was roaming about.

## \|\| 2.27.81-83 \|\|

*dīparatnaiḥ sukhacite dhārayaṃtī ca kaṃkaṇe \|*  
*ubhayordaśa ratnāni niṣke ca daśapañca ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

*sīmante sapta ratnāni keyūre'ṣṭau ca pañca ca \|*  
*evaṃ ratnācitāṃ bālāṃ śātakumbhasamaprabhām \|\| 82 \|\|*

*jahāra rājabhavanāttāṃ tadā cāruhāsinīm \|*  
*vāyumārgaṃ samāśritya kṣaṇātprāptaḥ svamālayam \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. He saw her in the light of gems and jewels that were shining like lamps. She was wearing two bangles well studded with bright gems and jewels. In each bangle there were ten jewels, and in the necklace of gold coin (?) there were fifteen jewels. On the crest, there were seven jewels. On the armlets there were eight and five (thirteen) jewels. The demon abducted such a virgin bedecked in jewels and with gold-like lustrous complexion. He carried away the girl of sweet smiles from the palace of the king. Through the aerial path he reached his own abode in a moment.

## \|\| 2.27.84-87 \|\|

*taṃ parvataṃ sa yatrāste patirme śālamāśritaḥ \|*  
*tatra tasya guhāṃ dṛṣṭvā suvarṇasadṛśaprabhām \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tadbhayasyāsahā tatra praviveśāsya paśyataḥ \|*  
*anekairmaṇivinyāsaiḥ saṃyuktāṃ citramandirām \|\| 85 \|\|*

*nānādra vyasamākīrṇā śayanāsanasaṃyutām \|*  
*bhojanaiḥ pānapātraiśca bhakṣyabhojyairanekadhā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*praviśya tatra śayyāyāṃ mumocotpalalocanām \|*  
*rudatīmatisantrastāṃ pīnaśroṇipayodharām \|\| 87 \|\|*

84-87. He came to that mountain where my husband (was sleeping) beneath the Sala tree. There she saw his cave that had the lustre of gold. Unable to bear the terror struck by him, she entered the cave even as he was looking on. The cave had been beautified by many jewels and it4iad mansions of variegated colours. Many articles lay scattered here and there. It contained beds and seats. Pols of beverages and edibles with various kinds of dishes had been kept there. After entering the cave, the demon placed that weeping girl of lilylike eyes, the excessively frightened girl of plump bosom and buttocks, on to a bed.

## \|\| 2.27.88 \|\|

*tasyāstu ruditaṃ śrutvā tasya bhāryā hi rākṣasī \|*  
*ājagāma tvarāyuktā yatrāsau rākṣasaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. On hearing the weeping of the girl, his wife the ogress hurriedly came to the place where the demon was standing.

## \|\| 2.27.89 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṅgīṃ taptakāñcanasaprabhām \|*  
*papraccha nijabhartāraṃ kruddhā nirbhartsatī satī \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. On seeing that girl whose lustre was like that of molten gold and everyone of whose limbs was beautiful, she became infuriated. Rebuking her husband she asked thus:

## \|\| 2.27.90 \|\|

*kimarthamāhṛtā ceyaṃ jīvantyāṃ mayi nirghṛṇa \|*  
*anyāṃ samīhase bhāryāṃ nāhaṃ bhāryā bhavāmi te \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. “O ruthless one, why is this girl brought here when I am alive? Do you wish for another wife? I will no longer be your wife then.

## \|\| 2.27.91 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ bhartā rākṣasīmasitekṣaṇām \|*  
*uvāca rākṣaso harṣātsvāṃ priyāṃ cārulocanām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. That demon joyously spoke to his beloved wife of beautiful eyes, the ogress of black eyes who had spoken to him thus.

## \|\| 2.27.92 \|\|

*tvadarthamāhṛtaṃ bhakṣyaṃ mayā kāśyāḥ śubhānane \|*  
*daivopapāditaṃ dvāri dvitīyaṃ mama tiṣṭhati \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. “O splendid-faced lady, this pabulum (eatable) prey has been brought by me from Kasi for your sake. A second one is standing at the gate. It has been brought to me by providence.

## \|\| 2.27.93 \|\|

*śālavṛkṣāśritaḥ śete vipraścaiko varānane \|*  
*tamānaya tvarāyuktā yenāhaṃ bhakṣyamācare \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. О fair-faced lady, a Brahmana is lying beneath the Sala tree. Bring him here quickly so that I can make a meal of him.

## \|\| 2.27.94 \|\|

*rākṣasasya vacaḥ śrutvā kumārī sābravīdidam \|*  
*mithyā rākṣasi bhartā te bhāṣate tvadbhayādayam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. On hearing the words of the Raksasa that virgin spoke thus: — “O RaksasI, out of his fear for you, your husband utters a lie.

## \|\| 2.27.95-96 \|\|

*jñātvā tvāṃ jarayopetāṃ virūpāmatijihmagām \|*  
*suptāṃ pitṛgṛhe rātrau māṃ samāsādya kāmataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*anūḍhāṃ rudatīṃ bhadre bhāryārthaṃ samupānayat \|*  
*itīritamupākarṇya vacanaṃ rājakanyayā \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. He knows that you are old in age, hideous in form and torturous in your gait. At night when I was soundly sleeping in my father’s house, he came to me passionately. О gentle lady, since I am not married he has brought me here to make me his wife in spite of my cries.”

## \|\| 2.27.97 \|\|

*krodhayuktātimātraṃ vai babhūva kṣipatī vacaḥ \|*  
*tasyāśca rūpamālokya satyamevāvadhārayat \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. On hearing these words uttered by the princess, the ogress became extremely infuriated. On seeing the beautiful form (of the princess), she decided that it was the truth. In her anger she hurled words (at her husband).

## \|\| 2.27.98 \|\|

*cintayāmāsa cāpyevaṃ bhāryārthe hyāhṛteti ca \|*  
*avaśyaṃ mūrdhni kīlaṃ me ropayiṣyati rākṣasaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. She thought thus — ‘‘She has been brought here to be made his wife. Of necessity, this demon will strike a wedge in my head.

## \|\| 2.27.99 \|\|

*māsma sīmantinī kācidbhavetsā bhuvane traye \|*  
*yā sāpatnyena duḥkhena pīḍyamānā hi jīvati \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Let there not be any woman in the фгее worlds who undergoes the misery of having a co-wife. There will hardly be any woman in the three worlds who will survive the harassment due to the misery of being a co-wife.

## \|\| 2.27.100 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva duḥkhānāṃ mahaccedaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sāmānyadra vyabhogādiniṣṭhā caivāparā bhavet \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. There is no doubt about this that it is the greatest of all miseries when there is another woman to have a share in the wealth and enjoyment of pleasures.”

## \|\| 2.27.101 \|\|

*evaṃ sā bahu sañcintya bhartāraṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*madīyā mama bhakṣyārthaṃ tvayānītā sulocanā \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. After thinking much like this, she spoke these words to her husband, “This girl is mine, as this lady of charming eyes has been brought by you as food for me.

## \|\| 2.27.102-104 \|\|

*taṃ vipramānayiṣyāmi bhakṣyārthaṃ tava suvrata \|*  
*tataḥ sa rākṣasaḥ prāha gaccha gaccheti satvaram \|\| 102 \|\|*

*sṛkkiṇī sravate'tyarthaṃ tasya bhakṣaṇakāmyayā \|*  
*tataḥ sā rākṣasī ghorā śrutvā patisamīritam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*nirjagāma durantāśā dadarśa dvijasattamam \|*  
*rūpayauvanasaṃyuktaṃ vidyāratnavibhūṣitam \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-103a. I shall bring that Brahmana to be your prey, О Suvrata (one of holy rites)”. Then the Raksasa urged “Go, go quickly. The corner of my mouth drips too much of saliva due to my desire to eat him.”

103b-104. Thereafter, on hearing the words uttered by her husband, the terrible Raksasi set out with infinite hope. She saw the excellent Brahmana endowed with comely features and blooming youth as well as adorned with the jewels of learning.

## \|\| 2.27.105 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā māyayā bhūtvā saṃndarī ṣoḍaśābdikā \|*  
*hṛcchayena samāviṣṭā tadantikamupāgamat \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. On seeing him she was overwhelmed with love pangs in the heart. Through her Maya (power of illusion), she became a beautiful maiden of sixteen years and approached him.

## \|\| 2.27.106 \|\|

*abravītsā pṛthuśroṇī taṃ vipraṃ prītisaṃyutā \|*  
*kastvaṃ kasmādihāyātaḥ kimarthamiha tiṣṭhasi \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The maiden of large buttocks spoke to the Brahmana with great pleasure — “Who are you? Whence have you come here? Why do you stay here?

## \|\| 2.27.107 \|\|

*pṛcchāmi patikāmāhaṃ rākṣasī hṛcchayāturā \|*  
*svabhartrāhaṃ parityaktā tvāṃ patiṃ kartumāgatā \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. I ask you this as I am desirous of making you my husband. I am an ogress overcome with pangs of love. I have been abandoned by my husband. I have come here to make you my husband.”

## \|\| 2.27.108 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasyā bhartā me bhayasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ prājño dhairyamālambya tāṃ śubhe \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. On hearing her words my husband was frightened. О splendid lady, yet he emboldened himself. The intelligent (Brahmana) spoke these words: —

## \|\| 2.27.109 \|\|

*rakṣomānuṣasaṃyogaḥ kathaṃ rākṣasi sambhavet \|*  
*mānuṣāstu smṛtā bhakṣyā rākṣasānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. “O Ogress, how can there be the copulation of a Raksasi and a human being? There is no doubt about this that men are remembered as the prey of Rakshashas.”

## \|\| 2.27.110 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ sā tu punastaṃ prāha sādaram \|*  
*asambhāvyaṃ ca jagati saṃbhaveddaivayogataḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. On hearing those words she spoke to him again respectfully — “The impossible is made possible, thanks to the intercession of the Providence.

## \|\| 2.27.111 \|\|

*purāṇe śrūyate hyetadbhaviṣyaṃ bhārate sthitam \|*  
*hiḍambā rākṣasī vipra bhīmabhāryā bhaviṣyati \|\| 111 \|\|*

111: This is heard in the Purana. This is a future incident mentioned in the Bharata, О Brahmana, Hidamba an ogress will become the wife of Bhima.1

## \|\| 2.27.112 \|\|

*mānuṣotpāditaḥ putro bhaviṣyati ghaṭotkacaḥ \|*  
*avadhyaḥ sarvaśastrāṇāṃ śaktyāmṛtyumavāpsyati \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The son procreated by a human being will be Ghatotkaca. He will be one who cannot be killed by any other weapon. He will attain death through the weapon called Sakti (of Indra, hurled by Karna against Ghatotkaca).

## \|\| 2.27.113 \|\|

*tasmādviṣādaṃ mā vipra kuru tvaṃ daivayogataḥ \|*  
*bhāryā tavāhaṃ sañjātā daivaṃ hi balavattaram \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Hence, О Brahmana, do not grieve. It is through Providential intercession that I have become your wife. Fate is indeed very powerful.

## \|\| 2.27.114-115 \|\|

*martyalokaṃ gate śakre vairocani nirīkṣaṇe \|*  
*tadantaraṃ samāsādya bhartā me ghorarākṣasaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*tadgṛhācchaktimaharaddīptāmagniśikhāmiva \|*  
*seyaṃ samāśritā cātra śālavṛkṣe tu vāsavī \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. When Indra went to the mortal world to meet Bali, my husband, the terrible Raksasa had a convenient opportunity. He stole Sakti from his abode as though it were the blazing flame. And that Sakti belonging to Indra has been kept here in the Sala Tree.

## \|\| 2.27.116 \|\|

*ahatvaikaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha na gacchati purandaram \|*  
*yadvadhāya prakṣipettāṃ so'maro'pi vinaśyati \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. О excellent Brahmana, without killing at least one it does not go back to Indra. The person for whose slaying it was hurled will perish even if he be immortal.

## \|\| 2.27.117 \|\|

*sāhamāruhya śālāgraṃ śaktimānīya bhāsvarām \|*  
*tvatkare saṃmpradāsyāmi bharturnidhanakāmyayā \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Hence, I shall climb up to the top of this Sala tree, bring the shining Sakti to you and hand it over to you with a desire for the death of my husband.

## \|\| 2.27.118 \|\|

*yadi tvamanayā śaktyā na hiṃsasi niśācaram \|*  
*khādayiṣyati durmedhāstvāṃ ca māṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. If you do not hit and injure the night-prowler with this Sakti, there is no doubt that the evil-minded one will swallow you as well as me.

## \|\| 2.27.119 \|\|

*tava śatrurmahāneṣa mamāpi ca parantapa \|*  
*yenāhṛtā kumārīha bhāryārthaṃ mandabuddhinā \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. He is a great enemy of yours as well as that of me, О scorcher of enemies, since, by that foolish fellow, a virgin has been brought here for being made his wife.

## \|\| 2.27.120 \|\|

*sapatnabhāvo janito mama bhartrā durātmanā \|*  
*vyāpādite'sminnubhayoḥ krīḍanaṃ sambhaviṣyati \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Hence, an enmity (inimical feelings) has been generated in me against my husband of the wicked soul. If he is killed, it will be possible for both of us to have sexual dalliance.

## \|\| 2.27.121 \|\|

*yadyanyathā vadervākyaṃ tvāmahaṃ rativarddhana \|*  
*tadātmakṛtapuṇyasya na bhaveyaṃ hi bhāginī \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. О Rativardhana (one who intensifies, lustfulness) if I am making a false statement to you, may I not be the partaker of benefits of the merit performed by myself.

## \|\| 2.27.122 \|\|

*yā gatirbrahmahatyāyāṃ kutsitā prāpyate naraiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ gatiṃ hi prapadye'ha yadyetadanṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. If this were to be a lie, may I attain that condition of a despicable nature which is attained by men on committing: Brahmana slaughter.

## \|\| 2.27.123 \|\|

*madyaṃ hi pibato brahman brāhmaṇasya durātmanaḥ \|*  
*yā gatirvihitā ghorā tāṃ gatiṃ prāpnuyāmyaham \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. О Brahmana, may I get that state, the terrible state that is laid down in the case of an evil-minded Brahmana who drinks liquor.

## \|\| 2.27.124 \|\|

*gurudāraprasaktasya jantoḥ pāpaniṣeviṇaḥ \|*  
*yā gatistāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha mithyā procya samāpnuyām \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. By uttering a lie, may I attain that fate, O excellent Brahmana, of that creature that is engaged in seducing the preceptor’s wife and that resorts to sinful actions.

## \|\| 2.27.125-126 \|\|

*svarṇanyāsāpaharaṇe medinīharaṇe ca yā \|*  
*ātmano hanane yā hi vihitā munibhirdvija \|\| 125 \|\|*

*gatistāmanugacchāmi yadyetadanṛtaṃ vade \|*  
*pañcamyāṃ ca tathāṣṭamyāṃ yatpāpaṃ māṃsabhakṣaṇe \|\| 126 \|\|*

125-126. If I tell a lie, may I incur that sin which the following undergo viz he who steals gold and misappropriates the sum given on trust; he who forcibly occupies another man's land; he who commits suicide; he who eats meat on the Paftcami (fifth) and AstamI (eighth) day, of a lunar fortnight.

## \|\| 2.27.127 \|\|

*strīsaṅgame tarucchede yatpāpaṃ śaśinaḥ kṣaye \|*  
*yaducchiṣṭe ghṛtaṃ bhokturmaithunena divā ca yat \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. The man who commits the sin of cutting off a tree or cohabiting with a woman on the new moon day, the sin acquired by taking in ghee while one is defiled by Ucchista\> the sin of sexual intercourse during the day time.

## \|\| 2.27.128 \|\|

*vaiśvadevamakartuśca gṛhiṇo hi dvijasya yat \|*  
*bhikṣāmadāturbhikṣubhyo vidhavāyā dvibhojanāt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The householder Brahmana who does not perform the holy rite of Vaisvadeva, the person who does not give alms to the mendicant, the widow who takes meal twice a day.1

## \|\| 2.27.129 \|\|

*tailaṃ bhoktuśca saṅkrāntau gobhistīrthaṃ ca gacchataḥ \|*  
*tathā mṛdamanuddhṛtya snātuḥ parajalāśaye \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. The person who uses gingelly oil on the day of Samkranti (the transit of the sun from one sign of Zodiac to another), the person who goes to the holy centre along with the cows (?), the person who takes bath in another man’s tank without taking out mud therefrom.

## \|\| 2.27.130 \|\|

*niṣiddhavṛkṣajanitaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ ca khādataḥ \|*  
*gāmasevayato baddhvā pākhaṇḍapathagāminaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. The person who chews the tooth stick twig from a. forbidden tree; the person who does not serve cows, but binds, them; the person who treads the heretic’s path.

## \|\| 2.27.131 \|\|

*pitṛdevārcanaṃ kartuḥ kāṣṭhagrāvasthitasya yat \|*  
*gohīnāṃ mahiṣīṃ dharturbhinnakāṃsye ca bhuñjataḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The person who performs the worship of the Pitrs and the Devas standing on a piece of wood or rock (?), the person who keeps only a buffalo without a cow also, the person who takes food off a bell metal vessel that is broken.

## \|\| 2.27.132 \|\|

*adhautabhinnapārakyavastrasaṃvītakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*nagnastrīprekṣaṇaṃ karturabhakṣyasya ca bhojinaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The person who perforins holy rites clad in unwashed or tom clothes or those belonging to others. The person who stares at a naked woman and the person who partakes of forbidden food.

## \|\| 2.27.133 \|\|

*kathāyāṃ śrīharervighnaṃ karturyatpātakaṃ dvija \|*  
*tena pāpena lipye'ha yadi vacmi tavānṛtam \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. О Brahmana, if I tell you a lie, may I be tarnished with the same sin as that of a person who creates obstacles in the discourse about Srihari.

## \|\| 2.27.134 \|\|

*uktānyetāni pāpāni yānyanuktānyapi dvija \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ bhāginī cāhaṃ yadyetadanṛtaṃ vade \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. О Brahmana, if I tell a lie, may I be the person who incurs all these sins1 that I have mentioned and also those I have not mentioned.”

## \|\| 2.27.135 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbodhito devi bhartā me pāpayā tayā \|*  
*tatheti niścayaṃ cakre bhavitavyena mohitaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. О gentle lady, my husband who was thus addressed by that sinful woman was deluded by the inevitable future and he decided accordingly, saying “So be it.”

## \|\| 2.27.136 \|\|

*nirdra vyo vyasanāsakto madvākyakaluṣīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*uvāca rākṣasīṃ vākyaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. That indigent Brahmana who had been indulging in vices and so perturbed extremely due to my harsh word» spoke thus to the ogress. His words (proved to be) the best- ower of all achievements.

## \|\| 2.27.137 \|\|

*śīghramānaya tāṃ śaktiṃ karomi vacanaṃ tava \|*  
*sarvametatpradeyaṃ hi tvayā me rākṣase hate \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. “Bring that aakti quickly. I shall carry out your directions. When the Raksasa is killed, all these things should be given by you to me.

## \|\| 2.27.138-140 \|\|

*dra vyāśayā praviṣṭo'ha sāgaraṃ timisaṃkulam \|*  
*tacchrutvā rākṣasī śaktiṃ samānīya nagasthitām \|\| 138 \|\|*

*dadau madbhartṛsirddhythaṃ vimuñcantīṃ mahārciṣam \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu rākṣasaḥ kāmamohitaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*gamanāyodyataḥ kanyāṃ sā bhītā vākyamabravīt \|*  
*kumārīsevane rakṣo mahāpāpaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 140 \|\|*

138-139a It is with a keen desire for wealth that I undertook (the voyage) through the sea full of whales and sharks”. On hearing these words, the ogress brought the Sakti that was on the top of the tree and that emitted brilliant lustre. She gave it to my husband for the realisation of their desire.

139b-140. In the meantime, the Raksasa who was overwhelmed by passion attempted to rape the virgin. She became terrified and spoke these words — “O Raksasa, there is a great sin in cohabiting with a virgin.

## \|\| 2.27.141 \|\|

*chalenāhaṃ hṛtā kāśyāḥ suptā pitṛgṛhāttvayā \|*  
*tava doṣo na cehāsti bhavitavyaṃ mamedṛśam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. While I was sleeping I had been fraudulently brought here from my father’s house at Kasi. It is not your fault in this regard. My fate is evidently of this nature.

## \|\| 2.27.142 \|\|

*guhāmadhyagatāyāstu ko me trātā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vidhiyogādbhavedbhartā vidhiyogādbhavetpriyā \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. I am in the middle of a cave. Who ^ill be the protector here? It is through fate that one gets a husband. It is through fate that one gets a wife.

## \|\| 2.27.143 \|\|

*bhavedvidhivaśādvidyā gṛhaṃ saukhyaṃ dhanaṃ kulam \|*  
*vidhinā preryamāṇastu janaḥ sarvatra gacchati \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. Fate alone plays the chief part in the matter of acquiring learning, house, happiness, wealth and nobility of birth. It is urged by the fate that man goes anywhere.

## \|\| 2.27.144 \|\|

*avaśyaṃ bhavitā bhartā tvameva rajanīcara \|*  
*vidhinā vihite mārge kiṃ kariṣyati paṇḍitaḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. О night-prowler, of necessity you alone will be my husband. When the path is traced out by fate, what will (even) a scholar do?

## \|\| 2.27.145 \|\|

*tasmādānayata vipraṃ śālavṛkṣāśritaṃ tviha \|*  
*ghṛtaṃ jalaṃ kuśānagniṃ vivāhaṃ vidhinā kuru \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Hence bring that Brahmana who has resorted to that Sala tree. Fetch ghee, water, Kusha grass and fire. Celebrate marriage in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 2.27.146 \|\|

*vināpi darbhatoyāgnīnnyathoktavidhimantarā \|*  
*brāhmaṇasyaiva vākyena vivāhaḥ saphalo bhavet \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Even without the Darbha grass, water and fire, even without the traditional rites laid down, a marriage may be fruitful if it is blessed with the permissive statement of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.27.147 \|\|

*na hato yadi viprastu bhāryayā tava rākṣasa \|*  
*vṛtte homasya kārye tu taṃ bhavān bhakṣayiṣyati \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. О Raksasa, if that Brahmana has not already been killed (bring him here quickly). When the holy rites of Ноmа have been performed, you will be able to eat him up.

## \|\| 2.27.148 \|\|

*evamukte tu vacane tayā vai rājakanyayā \|*  
*viśvastamānaso darpānnirjagāma sa rākṣasaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. When these words were addressed by that princess the Raksasa had full belief in his mind. He set out proudly.

## \|\| 2.27.149 \|\|

*satvaraṃ hṛcchayāviṣṭastamānetuṃ bahiḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. Afflicted by pangs of love he hastened out to bring that Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.27.150 \|\|

*tasya nirgacchato devi kṣutamāsītsvayaṃ kila \|*  
*savyaṃ cāpyasphurannetraṃ svavastraṃ skhalitaṃ tathā \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. О gentle lady, as he was setting out he himself sneezed, his left eye throbbed and his own clothes dropped down.

## \|\| 2.27.151-153 \|\|

*anādṛtya tu tatsarvaṃ nirgato'sau darīmukhāt \|*  
*bibhrāṇāṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ svāmapaśyannitambinīm \|\| 151 \|\|*

*ghaṭayantīṃ tu sambandhaṃ bhāryābhartṛsamudbhavam \|*  
*parityajāmi tvāṃ pāpaṃ rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmiṇam \|\| 152 \|\|*

*mānuṣīpramadāsaktaṃ maccharīrasya dūṣakam \|*  
*tacchrutvā dāruṇaṃ vākyaṃ bhāryayā samudīritam \|*  
*īrṣyākopasamāyuktastvabhyadhāvanniśācaraḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

151-153. Unmindful of everything, he set out from the cave. There he saw his wife in human form engaged in that form of union as is usual between a husband and a wife. She said — T am abandoning you, a sinful Raksasa of ruthless action. You are enamoured of a young woman of human species. You are the defiler of my body.” On hearing these terrible words uttered by his wife, the night-prowler (demon) became infuriated and malicious. He rushed at her.

## \|\| 2.27.154 \|\|

*utkṣipya bāhū pravidārya vaktraṃ saṃprasthito bhakṣayituṃ ca cobhau \|*  
*kālena vegātpavano yathaiva samuccaranvākyamanarthayuktam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. He lifted up his arms. He kept his mouth wide open. He rushed at them to devour both of them. Uttering curses of harmful nature, he rushed at them like a violent storm, that blows in the proper season.

## Chapter 28. Kdfthild's story (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.28.1 \|\|

*kāṣṭhīlovāca- rākṣasaṃ dhāvamānaṃ tu kālāntakayamopamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sā rākṣasī prāha bhartāraṃ mama śaṅikatā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Kaffhild said:

1\. On seeing the Raksasa, comparable to the black anni- hilator Yama, rushing at them, the Ogress became afraid and spoke thus to my husband.

## \|\| 2.28.2 \|\|

*prakṣipasvānalaprakhyāṃ śaktiṃ hemavibhūṣitām \|*  
*mamāyaṃ pañcatāṃ yātu digambararipupriya \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “Hurl this Sakti that is as refulgent as fire and bedecked in gold. May this husband of mine die and become the beloved of Digambara’s enemy (i.e. Yama).

## \|\| 2.28.3 \|\|

*tasyā vākyānmama patiḥ pauruṣe tu vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*mumoca vipulāṃ śaktiṃ rakṣovakṣasthalaṃ prati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At her instance, my husband assumed great manliness and hurled the massive Sakti at the chest of the Raksasa.

## \|\| 2.28.4-5 \|\|

*jvalantī jvalanaprakhyā dyotayantī diśo daśa \|*  
*divyāṃśutīkṣṇavaktrāntā kiṅikaṇīśatanāditā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*raktacandanaliptāṅgī raktavastropaśobhitā \|*  
*hṛdi tasya nipatyāsau śaktirviprakaracyutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The Sakti that blazed brilliantly like fire and illuminated the ten quarters, the point of which was sharp and emitted divine rays and was jingling with hundreds of tinkling bells fitted into it, the body of which was smeared with red sandal paste, and was beautified with (the covering) of red cloth. It went oflf from the hands of the Brahmana, pierced into the heart of the Raksasa.

## \|\| 2.28.6-7 \|\|

*kṛtvā bhasmāvaśeṣaṃ tu rākṣasaṃ gaganaṃ yayau \|*  
*pātayitvā svabhartāraṃ viprahastena rākṣasī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ mene hṛṣṭatanūruhā \|*  
*athovāca dvijaṃ hṛṣṭā rākṣasī śubhalocanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. After reducing the Raksasa to ashes, it went up into the sky. After felling (killing) her husband through the hands of the Brahmana, the ogress considered herself as having achieved her goal. Hairs stood on end due to her delight. The delighted ogress then spoke to the splendid-eyed Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.28.8 \|\|

*ehi kānta guhāṃ ramyāṃ praviśa tvaṃ yadṛcchayā \|*  
*bhuṅkṣva bhogānmayā sārddhaṃ ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “O my lover, come on, Enter freely my beautiful cave. Enjoy all the great pleasures, divine as well as human, in my company.”

## \|\| 2.28.9 \|\|

*tatheti prāṇanātho me prāha hṛṣṭavapustadā \|*  
*tataḥ sādāya me kāntaṃ svāṃ praviṣṭā guhāṃ mudā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “So be it” said my husband who was extremely delighted. Then she took my husband and entered her cave joyfully.

## \|\| 2.28.10 \|\|

*asaṃvīkṣyaiva tadbhasma bhartṛdehasamudbhavam \|*  
*kucābhyāmunnatābhyāṃ sā madbhartāramapīḍayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Without caring to look at the ashes to which her husbands body had been reduced, she clasped my husband with her protruding breasts.

## \|\| 2.28.11-12 \|\|

*darśayāmāsa tāṃ tanvīṃ kumārīṃ śayane sthitām \|*  
*iyaṃ tenāsitāpāṅgī bimboṣṭhī kāñcanaprabhā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhāryārthe samupānītā vārāṇasyā dvijottama \|*  
*yasyāḥ sīmāṃ na laṅghanti pātakāni hyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. She pointed out to him that maiden ofslender body who was lying down on the bed. — “O excellent Brahmana, this lady of black side-glances, with lips red like the Bimba fruit and of gold-like lustrous complexion had been brought (by my husband) to make her his wife, from Varanasi, the city whose limits are not transgressed by all sins.

## \|\| 2.28.13 \|\|

*śaktikṣetraṃ ca tāṃ prāhuḥ puṇyaṃ pāpakṣayaṅkaram \|*  
*yā gṛhaṃ tripurāreśca pañcagavyūtisaṃsthitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That city is called Sakti Ksetra (the sacred place of Divine Power) and is holy and destructive of sins. It is the abode of Tripurari (God Siva) and it extends to five Gavyutis (i.e. fifteen Kilometers).

## \|\| 2.28.14 \|\|

*yasyāṃ mṛtāḥ punarmartyā garbhavāsaṃ viśanti na \|*  
*sa tvamasyā gṛhaṃ pitr! yaṃ punarnaya sulocanām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Men who die therein are never reborn into any womb. Kindly take this lady of bright eyes to her father’s house.

## \|\| 2.28.15 \|\|

*imāni tava ratnāni śayanānyāsanāni ca \|*  
*mayā saha samastāni vikrīṇīhi nijecchayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. These jewels, beds and seats are at your disposal. If you wish you can sell all these things including myself.

## \|\| 2.28.16 \|\|

*tvadarthe rākṣaso ghoro mayā brahmanniṣūditaḥ \|*  
*mugdhayā tava rūpeṇa preṣito yamasādanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmana, for your sake the terrible Raksasa was slain by me who am enamoured of your comely features. He has been sent to the abode of Yama.

## \|\| 2.28.17 \|\|

*tasmānmamopari vibho kṛtvā viśvāsamātmanā \|*  
*bhajasva māṃ viśālākṣa bhaktāṃ vai kāmarūpiṇīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence, О Lord, have confidence in me. О largeeyed one, I am your devotee. I can assume any form I like. ‘Enjoy me.

## \|\| 2.28.18 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ bhartā me cārulocane \|*  
*rākṣasyāṃ kāmataptāyāṃ kumāryāḥ sannidhau śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О lady of beautiful eyes, on hearing these words of the love-lorn ogress, my husband spoke these words to the Raksasi in the presence of that virgin.

## \|\| 2.28.19 \|\|

*uvāca rākṣasīṃ tāṃ tu saśaṅko madhuraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*subhage nītiśāstreṣu viśvastavyā na yoṣitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. As he was guarded and suspicious he spoke sweet words — “O blessed lady, (it is mentioned) in the treatises on polity and ethics that women should not be trusted.

## \|\| 2.28.20-21 \|\|

*kaumāraṃ yā patiṃ hanti sā kathaṃ māṃ na hiṃsati \|*  
*matto rūpādhikaṃ matvā paraṃ puruṣalampaṭā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*so'ha viśvāsabhāvena viśvastaste varānane \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. How will she not injure me, she who kills her husband ever since her girlhood days? Considering another man more handsome, this lascivious woman (may cause my death). О fair-faced lady, still I continue to believe in you.

## \|\| 2.28.22 \|\|

*adya vātha paredyurvā pakṣe māse'tha vatsare \|*  
*vyāpādaya yathecchaṃ vā tvāṃ prapanno'smi bhāmini \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О beautiful woman, I have sought refuge in you, kill me, if you please, to-day or tomorrow or after a fortnight or a month or a year.

## \|\| 2.28.23-24 \|\|

*evameva tvayā kāryaṃ nādya copakṛtaṃ tava \|*  
*ātmā te sarvathā deyaḥ pratīkārasya hetave \|\| 23 \|\|*

*madarthe nihato bhartā tvayā niḥśaṅkayā yataḥ \|*  
*tato'ha nottaraṃ vacmi paraṃ kiṃñcitsulocane \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. This must be done by you only thus (as though) I have not helped you today (?) For the sake of vengeance (help in return?) the soul must be offered by you. (You must give yourself up). Since you unhesitatingly killed your husband for my sake, О lady of good eyes, I do not say anything тоге.”

## \|\| 2.28.25 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya madbhartuḥ sābravīdidam \|*  
*viśvastahiṃsanaṃ brahman brahmahatyā samaṃ bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing the words of my husband, she spoke thus: “O Brahmana, killing some one who has trusted in one is on a par with the slaughter of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.28.26 \|\|

*yadyevaṃ rākṣasīṃ krūrāṃ manyase patighātinīm \|*  
*patiṃ tathāpi garheyaṃ viśvastaṃ ghātaye katham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If, on account of this, you consider me a cruel Rak- sasl, the destroyer of her husband (my reply is) I hate my husband. How will I kill one who confides in me and believes in me?

## \|\| 2.28.27 \|\|

*sūkṣmā hi dharmasya gatirna jñāyeta kathañcana \|*  
*kenāpi kutraciddevadaityarākṣasakādinā \|*  
*kecinmanuṣyāḥ paṭavo dharmasūkṣmatvacintane \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The way of Dharma (virtue and piety) is very subtle. It cannot be understood by any means, by any one anywhere, whether Daitya or Raksasa or others. But some men are clever in thinking about the subtleties of Dharma.

## \|\| 2.28.28 \|\|

*ye'nityena śarīreṇa naiṣkarmyaṃ sādhayantyuta \|*  
*śrūyate ca purāṇeṣu kiñcidatra nigadyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. (Those who know Dharma) attain Naiskarmya (freedom from the Karmans i.e. Moksa) through their perishable physical body. This is heard in the Puranas. Same thing is being mentioned here.

## \|\| 2.28.29 \|\|

*dharmasyaivānukūlyena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*daśāvatāragrahaṇe duḥkhaṃ prāptamanekadhā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It is through the favourable nature of Dharma that Visnu the powerful God could assume ten incarnations. But in them much misery was experienced by him.1

## \|\| 2.28.30 \|\|

*kva sītārthaṃ śrīnivāso rāmo lakṣmaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*vilāpaṃ kurute nāgapāśabandhādikarmasu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Where is Rama, the abode of Sri, who for the sake ofSlta, accompanied by Laksmana lamented in the course of the events and they were bound by the serpentine nooses?

## \|\| 2.28.31 \|\|

*kva devadevo vasudevasūnurvijñānarūpo nikhilaprapañcī \|*  
*hā kaṣṭamityasradṛgādiceṣṭaḥ pārthograsenādikabhṛtyakṛtyaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Where is Vasudeva’s son, the lord of Devas, of the form of perfect knowledge? And where is the fully worldly man who sheds tears saying “O what a pity?” who makes signs and gestures with his eyes and who acts as servant unto Partha (i.e. Arjuna), Ugrasena and others? (What a lot of difference there is!)

## \|\| 2.28.32 \|\|

*īśasya kṛtyaṃ dvija durvibhāvyaṃ dharmānukūlyena samāsthitasya \|*  
*vyāsaḥ svayaṃ vedavibhāgakarttā pārāśaristattvadṛgijyamūrtiḥ \|*  
*kanyātvavidhvaṃsakavīryajanmā kānīnasaṃjño'nujadāragāmī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. О Brahmana, the activities of the Lord are beyond human scrutiny1 though he abides by the favourable Dharma. Vyasa1 2 the son of Parasara, is himself the classifier of the Vedas. He was a man of truthful vision. His very form is worthy of being worshipped. (But) he was born of the semen virile of one who destroyed the virginity (of a woman). Hence he is called a Kanina (son of an unmarried girl). Moreover, he had sexual intercourse with the wives of his younger brothers.2

## \|\| 2.28.33 \|\|

*parivettā ca didhiṣūḥ śantunuḥ svaḥsaritpatiḥ \|*  
*didhiṣūtanayaḥ sākṣādvasuḥstrīvādamṛtyubhāk \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Santanu was a Parivettr (one who had married before his elder brother Devapi). He was the second husband of a lady (Satyavati who married twice). At first he was the husband of the heavenly river. His son was the veritable Vasu (Bhlsma), the unmarried elder brother (whose younger brother vicitra-Virya was married before him); he attained death due to the arguments of a woman (Amba) who became Sikhandu1 in the next birth.

## \|\| 2.28.34 \|\|

*ye golakasutāḥ kuṇḍāḥ pāṅḍavāḥ samayonigāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṅkīrtanaṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Pandavas were born of adultery (as each was born from a different person other than their legal father Pandu. Thus they were actually bastards. All of them cohabited with the same woman, viz. Draupadi. Still their glorification is considered holy and sacred. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.28.35-37 \|\|

*yaṃ dhyāyanti smarantyaddhā yogamūrtiḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*viṣṇurveśyāsamāsaktaḥ prahlādādyupadeśakṛt \|*  
*śrīnṛsiṃho'suradhvaṃsī devadevādhidaivatam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*saṃsāravāsanādhvaṃsī devadevādhidaivatam \|*  
*saṃsāravāsanādhvaṃsī svarṇākṣabhavanasthitiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Visnu whom people meditate upon and truly remember, who is called Yogamurti (Embodiment of Yoga) and who is eternal, was enamoured of courtesans. Srinrsimha who advised Prahlada and others and who destroyed Asuras is considered as the deity and Lord of the Devas (Defective). He is the destroyer of even the impression of worldly existence, he is the deity and Lord of the Devas. He was the destroyer of Hiranyaksa (Hiranyakasipu?) but he stayed in his abode (?)

## \|\| 2.28.38 \|\|

*jāmadagnyaḥ svayaṃ siddhastapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ \|*  
*īśvaraḥ kṣatrasaṃhārabhrūṇahatyādikarmakṛt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The son of Jamadagni (ParaSurama) had realised his soul himself. He had destroyed his sins by means of his austerities. He was Lord himself. But he was the perpetrator of such deeds as massacres of Ksattriyas and killing of children in the womb.

## \|\| 2.28.39 \|\|

*svayamevarṣabho yogī lokaśikṣāparo dvijaḥ \|*  
*lokaglānikaro jātaḥ kurvandharmānurodhataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He himself was a leading Yogin. He was a Brah- mana engaged in educating people, but acting within the perview of Dharma, he became one who brought agony into the world.

## \|\| 2.28.40 \|\|

*nārado nārado bhūyo bhūyo bhūyo'pi nāradaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparo nāro naro narahito'maraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Narada was a Narada (destroyer of groups of men)1 again and again. Narada was devoted to Narayana. Nara means one who is a benefactor of men and also one who is immortal.

## \|\| 2.28.41 \|\|

*gautamo gautamo vipra gopaceṣṭāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*vedabāhyārthasaṃyuktaśāstrī vedopakārakṛt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Gautama was Gotama (most timid like a cow). О Brahmana, he was devoted to the activities of a cowherd. He had written a treatise (i.e. Nyaya sutra) the topics of which are beyond the pale of the Vedas; (but he is called) one who helps the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.28.42-48 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhaścorvaśījāto'gastyo'pi svayamīśvarau \|*  
*yena lokopakarārthaṃ vāsiṣṭhaṃ śāstramuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ yasminpurāṇāni vedāḥ sāmyatvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*yaḥ svayaṃ rāmacandra sya guruḥ sarveśvarasya ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ gādhijāśaptastiryagyonimupāgamat \|*  
*yo damitvā vibhurvindhyaṃ vātāpiṃ sāgaraṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ mṛtakādātā duṣkaraṃ samupāsate \|*  
*yo vidhiḥ karmasākṣyādivandyo mānyaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mohinīmohito dehamutsasarja kathaṃ sa ca \|*  
*yaḥ śivaḥ śivadaḥ sākṣātprakṛtīśaḥ parātparaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ devapatnīgaḥ śmaśānāśubhaceṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddvija sadācāro niṣevyo vidhinā vidhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tamahaṃbhāvanāyukto no heyādyo vidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sa śāntimāpnuyādagryāṃ dharmyāmubhayasaṃsthitām \|\| 48 \|\|*

42-44a Vasistha and even Agastya, who were born of Urvasi, are considered to be masters. By Vasistha a sacred treatise of excellent nature named Vasisthasmrti had been composed for helping the whole world. In that work the Puranas and the Vedas are considered to be equal. He was himself the preceptor of Sri Rama who was none other than the Almighty (Visnu). Why was he cursed by Gadhija (Visva- mitra)? Why was he born in the womb of a lower animal?1 2

44b-45a The powerful Agastya had overpowered the Vindhya mountain, the demon Vatapi and also the ocean. How is he the receiver of hire money (?)2 He served in the way that is difficult for others to do.

45b-46a. The creator is worthy of being worshipped by the sun etc. and is the honourable grandsire of the world. How did he become enamoured of a lady of fascinating beauty and give up his body?

46b-47a. God Siva, the bestower of auspicious things, is the lord of Prakrti. He is greater than the greatest. How did he carnally approach the wives of the Devas? How does he pursue inauspicious activities in the cremation ground?

47b-48. Hence, О Brahmana, it is the prescribed rule that good conduct must be pursued duly. He who is the foremost among the knowers of things shall not abandon good conduct by having the egotist feeling, (then) he will obtain the highest peace conducive to virtue here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.28.49 \|\|

*āpavargyaḥ smṛto dharmo dhanaṃ dharmaikasādhanam \|*  
*tanmayā sādhito dharmaḥ sarvottamadhanātmanā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Dharma is remembered as conducive to Apavarga (salvation). Wealth is the only thing through which Dharma can be achieved. That Dharma I have achieved in the form of wealth that is the greatest of all.

## \|\| 2.28.50-51 \|\|

*śṛṇu viprātra dharmasya gatiṃ sūkṣmāṃ vadāmyaham \|*  
*yadā samāgato bhartā mama kanyāṃ samāharan \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tvāṃ paśyan nijakarmasthaṃ ko'pi doṣo na tasya vai \|*  
*mayā pṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ nāma kanyeyaṃ samupāhṛtā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. О Brahmana, listen. In this connection, I shall recount to you the subtle way of Dharma. Abducting a girl, my husband was coming this way. He saw you were involved because you were brought there by your Karman. That was not his fault. He was asked by me- — “Why was this girl brought?”

## \|\| 2.28.52-53 \|\|

*tadā tena mṛṣā vākyamuktaṃ madbhakṣaṇārthakam \|*  
*tanniśamyāha māṃ baddhā svayaṃ cāsthānidarśanāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ye vadanti ca dāmpatye bhāryā mokṣavirodhinī \|*  
*na te tattvadṛśo jñeyā na sā bhāryā virodhinī \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Then a lie was uttered by him that it was for his food. On hearing that, the girl in bondage told me everything pointing out his desire. Those who say that in wedded life the wife is a hindrance to salvation, cannot be understood as knowers of reality. Since the wife is not an obstacle.

## \|\| 2.28.54 \|\|

*bhāryā samuddharetpāpātpatantaṃ niraye patim \|*  
*sā bhāryānyā karmavallīrūpā saṃsāradāyinī \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Only she is the real wife who is able to uplift a husband falling into the hell. Any other woman is like a twining creeper of Karman, the bestower of worldly bondage.

## \|\| 2.28.55 \|\|

*pāpaṃ kimatra tanmattaḥ samyakchṛṇu svayaṃ vara \|*  
*alīkaṃ naiva vaktavyaṃ prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭhagatairapi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. What is sinful in this you hear from me, О my bridegroom who have come to me by yourself. Even if the vital breaths come to the throat, falsehood should not be uttered.

## \|\| 2.28.56 \|\|

*satyamevācaret satye sākṣāddharmo vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*satye samāsthito brahmā satye santaḥ samāsthitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One must always be truthful. Dharma is directly based on Truth. God Brahma is based on Truth. All good men abide by Truth.

## \|\| 2.28.57 \|\|

*satye samāsthitaṃ viśvaṃ sarvadā sacarācaram \|*  
*satyaṃ brūyāditi vaco vedānteṣu pragīyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The entire universe is established in the Truth, the universe consisting of the mobile and the immobile beings is always based on Truth. The words “One shall always speak the Truth”1 are proclaimed in the Vedantas.

## \|\| 2.28.58 \|\|

*satyaṃ brahmasvarūpaṃ hi tatsatyamabhidhīmahi \|*  
*satyaṃ tu sarvadā vipra maṅgalaṃ maṅgalapradam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The Truth is of the form of Brahman. We call Brahman by the word Truth. О Brahmana, the Truth is always auspicious. It is the bestower of everything that is auspicious.

## \|\| 2.28.59 \|\|

*asatyamātmakṣayadaṃ sadyaḥ pratyayakārakam \|*  
*strīṣu satyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ tatrāpi śṛṇu kāraṇam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Untruth is the bestower of self destruction though immediately it may breed the confidence of belief. But Truth should not be spoken to women. Listen to the reason thereof.

## \|\| 2.28.60 \|\|

*nidhiṃ striyai na kathayedityādau doṣavāraṇam \|*  
*uktaṃ taddharmajanakaṃ dharmasūkṣmatvadarśakam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In such directives as “Do not reveal to the woman (the extent of) the treasury”, it prevents future faults. That is said to be the cause of Dharma which reveals the subtlety of Dharma.

## \|\| 2.28.61 \|\|

*kuśā dvijā jalaṃ vahnirvedā bhūkāladiksurāḥ \|*  
*sākṣye yatra vivāheṣu dāmpatyaṃ tadudīritam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. That is called wedded life where the witnesses of marriage had been Kusa grass, Brahmanas, water, fire, Vedas, Earth, time, space and Devas.

## \|\| 2.28.62 \|\|

*samaṅgīkaraṇaṃ karma vivāhe tu vidhīyate \|*  
*strīpuṃsordvijasaṃskāre nirdiṣṭaṃ guruśiṣyayoḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The rite of acceptance is laid down -in the celebra- tion of marriage. If the woman and the man are consecrated by Brahmanas, they are regarded as the teacher and the disciple.

## \|\| 2.28.63 \|\|

*tasmātparasparaṃ jñeyau guruśiṣyau vadhūvarau \|*  
*nānayoraṇumātro'pi bhedo bodhyo vijānatā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Hence, the bride and the bridegroom are mutually related as teachers and disciples. No difference at all, even to the minutest extent, should be understood by a discriminating man as existing between these two.

## \|\| 2.28.64 \|\|

*tattatkarmānurūpatvātprādhānyastrīniyojyayoḥ \|*  
*kvacidvyatyayadoṣaśceddaivamevātra kāraṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The importance of women and employees is in accordance with the difference in rites. If there is the defect of contrariety (in relations etc.) anywhere, the cause of it is fate alone.

## \|\| 2.28.65-66 \|\|

*daivādhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*daivaṃ tatpūrvajanmāni sañcitāḥkarmavāsanāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*prāptaṃ niṣevannanyonyaṃ vartate kāmakārakam \|*  
*śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ vipra taṃ tu śāntaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. The entire universe consisting of gods, Asuras, and human beings is subservient to Fate. Fate is the accumulation of impressions of Karmas in the previous births. He who enjoys and experiences whatever comes to his lot, whether auspicious or inauspicious and behaves spontaneously with both, is called a quiescent person by the learned knowledgeable men.

## \|\| 2.28.67 \|\|

*śāntaḥ satyasamācāro janturlokapratārakaḥ \|*  
*evamādi viditvā tu nāyaṃ bhartā nipātitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A quiet person whose activity is based on the Truth enables the world to cross mundane existence. It is by knowing such and other details that my husband was prevented from falling into hell.

## \|\| 2.28.68 \|\|

*kanyātvadhvaṃsakātpāpātpūto madupakārataḥ \|*  
*gatiṃ prayātaḥ kṛtināṃ tvaddhastavinipātitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He was sanctified by me by preventing him from committing the sin of violating virginity. That is the help rendered by me. He has now attained the goal of the virtuous and lucky men after having been struck down by you.

## \|\| 2.28.69 \|\|

*mayā tūpakṛtaṃ patye jānatyā dharmasūkṣmatām \|*  
*tvatprāṇarakṣaṇe dharmo mamābhūddvijasattama \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. My husband was helped by me who know the subtlety of Dharma. О excellent Brahmana, I have acquired merit (Dharma) in saving your life.

## \|\| 2.28.70-72 \|\|

*tena dharmeṇa kiṃ prāptamiti samyaṅnibodha me \|*  
*rākṣasīṃ yonimāpannā rākṣasasya priyā hyaham \|\| 70 \|\|*

*kāmarūpā brāhmaṇī tu sañjātā dharmakāraṇāt \|*  
*dharmaḥ kāmadughā dhenuḥ santoṣo nandanaṃ vanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vidyā mokṣakarī proktā tṛṣṇā vaitaraṇī nadī \|*  
*vaitaraṇyāṃ patanbhartā mayoddhṛta ihābhavat \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-7la. What has been achieved by that Dharma? Know it properly from me. I who am born in the species of an ogress, I who have been the wife of a Raksasa, have now become a Brahmana woman who can assume any form, the reason being Dharma.

7lb-72. Dharma is the wish-yielding cow (Kamadhenu). Satisfaction is the heavenly Nandana park. Vidya is the cause of salvation and Trsna (insatiable thirst) is the river Vaitaranl. My husband who was about to fall into Vaitaram has been redeemed by me.

## \|\| 2.28.73 \|\|

*asyāścopakṛtaṃ vipra varṇottamaniveśanāt \|*  
*iyaṃ tvatsaṅiganī bhāryā bhaviṣyati piturgṛhe \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. О Brahmana, I have helped this fair-faced girl also because she has been placed near a person who is the highest of all castes. She will be your wife in her father’s house.

## \|\| 2.28.74-75 \|\|

*ahaṃ tavāsyāśca sadā rakṣikā dharmabodhinī \|*  
*matsaṃgamātpūrvameva yā bhāryā vipra te'bhavat \|\| 74 \|\|*

*iyaṃ tvatsaṃginī bhāryā bhaviṣyati varānanā \|*  
*sāpi tiryaggatiṃ prāpya mucyate madanugrahāt \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. I will be guarding her and you for ever enlightening you with Dharma. Before my contact you had a wife, О Brahmana, who will be born as a being in lower animal species. Later on, as a result of my blessings, she will be released.

## \|\| 2.28.76 \|\|

*ahaṃ purābhave'bhūvaṃ ramaṇī lokasundarī \|*  
*kandalīti ca vikhyātā tanayaurvamunerdvija \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О Brahmana, in my previous birth I was the most beautiful woman in the world well-known as Kandali. I was the daughter of the sage Aurva.

## \|\| 2.28.77 \|\|

*tapaḥprabhāvātsañjātā yamalā mithunaṃdharā \|*  
*puruṣo me sahabhavo damito dharmakāraṇāt \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. By the power of penance I was born as one of a twin. My brother born along with me, was suppressed by Aurva himself for the cause of Dharma.

## \|\| 2.28.78-79 \|\|

*tenaivaurveṇa śiṣṭāhaṃ dattā durvāsase bhavam \|*  
*taṃ patiṃ prāpya viprendra prākkarmavaśagā hyaham \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kalahābhiratā patyā śaptā bhasmatvamāgatā \|*  
*kiñcitpāpāvaśeṣeṇa rākṣasīṃ yonimāgatā \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. I was educated and given in marriage to Durvasas. О leading Brahmana, it was a result of my previous Karman that I attained him as my husband. I quarrelled with my husband. Hence, I was cursed by him and reduced to ashes. As a little of my sins remained, I was born as ogress.

## \|\| 2.28.80 \|\|

*tatra yonau mayā labdho bhartāyaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ \|*  
*gobhilo nāma tejasvī sa tvayā vinipātitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. In that birth this brilliant leader of demons Gobhila was attained by me as my husband but he has been struck down by you.

## \|\| 2.28.81 \|\|

*śāpo'sya pūrvavayasi babhūva dvijasattama \|*  
*kasyāścidrā jakanyāyāḥ striyā'rabdhā mṛtistava \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. О excellent Brahmana, in his youth he had incurred a curse “Your death will be initiated by your wife on account of a certain princess.”

## \|\| 2.28.82 \|\|

*ahaṃ tu rākṣasī bhāvarahitā pūrvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*śubhasya balamāpannā jātā tava sahāyinī \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. As a result of my previous Karman, I have been bereft of the nature of an ogress. Being powerful on account of the auspicious actions, I become your helpmate. 4

## \|\| 2.28.83 \|\|

*duḥkhitāhaṃ kṛtā bhartrā kumāryāharaṇātpurā \|*  
*bhāryātha pāpinā brahmaṃstena vyāpādito mayā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. At the outset my husband abducted a virgin and I had been made miserable by him. Hence, О Brahmana, he has been killed by me.

## \|\| 2.28.84 \|\|

*viśvasto hi yatastvaṃ vai mama sarveṇa cetasā \|*  
*tatastvāṃ gopayiṣyāmi sarvabhāvena kāmuka \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. О lover, since you put trust in me with all your heart and soul in every respect I shall protect you in every respect.

## \|\| 2.28.85 \|\|

*eṣa te śapathaḥ satyaḥ pañcabhūtopasākṣikaḥ \|*  
*kṛtsnasya puruṣasyeha sannidhau vyāhṛto mayā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. This is my binding by oath with five elements as my witness and uttered in the presence of the all-pervading person. It is the truth.

## \|\| 2.28.86 \|\|

*na karoṣi dvijaśreṣṭha saṃvidaṃ hyanyathā kvacit \|*  
*madvākye bhavatā stheyaṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu mānada \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. О excellent Brahmana, you will not alter this agreement in any respect. О bestower of honour, you must abide by me in all activities.”

## \|\| 2.28.87 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ rākṣasyā paribhāṣitam \|*  
*pratipede vacaḥ sarvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ hi tayā tadā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. On hearing the words uttered by the ogress, the noble Brahmana carried out all instructions and she did accordingly.

## \|\| 2.28.88-89 \|\|

*tataḥ sā rākṣasī sarvaṃ sampragṛhya guhādhanam \|*  
*kareṇurūpiṇī bhūtvā pṛṣṭhe kṛtvā patiṃ mama \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tayā saha viśālākṣyā ratnāvalyā mudānvitā \|*  
*yayāvākāśamārgeṇa kāśīmabhi sulocane \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Thereafter, the demoness gathered together all wealth from the cave. She assumed the form of a she-elephant and kept my husband on her back along with Ratnavali, the large-eyed girl. Joyously she went through the path of firmament, О lady of good eyes, towards Kasl.

## Chapter 29. The description of Kasi

## \|\| 2.29.1 \|\|

*kāṣṭhīlovāca- evaṃ sā rākṣasī subhru hastinīrūpadhāriṇī \|*  
*tribhirmuhūrtaiḥ samprāptā kāśīṃ viśveśamandiram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Kashthila said:

1\. Thus, О lady of beautiful eyebrows, that ogress who had assumed the form of a she-elephant, reached the temple of Vishvesha at Ka€l within three Muhurtas.

## \|\| 2.29.2 \|\|

*uvāca tāṃ purīṃ prāpya bhartāramasitekṣaṇā \|*  
*iyaṃ pāpataroḥ kānta kuṭhārā parikīrtitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On reaching that city, the lady of black eyes spoke to her husband — “O Lord, this (city) is glorified as the axe for the cutting of the tree of sin.

## \|\| 2.29.3 \|\|

*ṣaḍūrmikāñcanasyaiṣā kānta proktā durodarī \|*  
*karmabījopaśamanī sarveṣāṃ gatidāyikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О beloved, this is said to be the dice box for the gold of six types of distresses (?) It is destructive of all seeds of Karmans, and it is the bestower of salvation on all.

## \|\| 2.29.4 \|\|

*ādyaṃ hi vaiṣṇavaṃ sthānaṃ purāṇāḥ sampracakṣate \|*  
*nāvaiṣṇave sthale muktiḥ sarvasya tu kadācana \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Puranas say that it was at first the abpde of Visnu.1 No one can ever have salvation in a holy centre not belonging to Visnu.

## \|\| 2.29.5 \|\|

*mādhavasya purī ceyaṃ pūrvamāsīddvijottama \|*  
*muktidā sarvajantūnāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О excellant Brahmana, this was formerly a city of Visnu, the bestower of salvation on all creatures and the destroyer of every one’s sin.

## \|\| 2.29.6 \|\|

*ekadā śaṅkaro devo dra ṣṭuṃ prāgātpitāmaham \|*  
*sarvalokaikakartāraṃ bhrājamānaṃ svatejasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once Lord Sankara went there to see Pitamaha (god Brahma) the sole creator of all worlds, shining with his own splendour.

## \|\| 2.29.7 \|\|

*gatvā tatra mahādevo brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ gurum \|*  
*namaskṛtya sthito hyagre vedapāṭhaṃ niśāmayan \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After going there, Mahadeva bowed down to Brahma the preceptor of the worlds. He stood in front of him listening to the recital of the Vedic lore.

## \|\| 2.29.8 \|\|

*caturbhiradbhutairvaktraiścaturo nigamānmudā \|*  
*udgirantaṃ jagannāthaṃ dṛṣṭvā prīto'bhavattadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was delighted on seeing the Lord of the Universe joyously reciting the four Vedas by means of the four wonderful faces.

## \|\| 2.29.9 \|\|

*atha tatpañcamaṃ vaktraṃ brahmaṇo bhūtanāyakaḥ \|*  
*pragalbhaṃ tamupālakṣya kṣaṇājjātaḥ samatsaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter, the leader of goblins saw the fifth face of Brahma. On observing him to be impudent and arrogant, he became malicious instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.29.10 \|\|

*sa krodhajanmā viprendra tasya prāgalbhyamakṣaman \|*  
*cakarta tannakhāgreṇa khasthaṃ vaktraṃ trilocanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О leading Brahmana, the three-eyed deity, born of anger could not brook his audacity. Hence with the tip of his nail he cut off the head stationed above in the firmament (?)

## \|\| 2.29.11 \|\|

*tacchinnaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śīrṣaṃ saṃlagnaṃ karapallave \|*  
*vāme nirdhūtamaniśaṃ na nivṛttaṃ dvijottama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О excellent Brahmana, the head of Brahma that had been severed, stuck up to the sproutlike left hand (of Siva). It did not fall off though shaken frequently.

## \|\| 2.29.12 \|\|

*brahmā tu duḥkhito bhūtvā tasthau sthāṇuṃ vyalokayan \|*  
*rudro 'pi lajjito bhūtvā nirjjagāma tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Brahma became sad. He stood there staring at Siva. Siva became ashamed and he hurriedly went out of the place.

## \|\| 2.29.13 \|\|

*bahudhā yatamāno'pi tacchiraḥ kṣeptumāturaḥ \|*  
*na śaśāka parityaktuṃ tadadbhutamabhūnmahat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Though he tried in many ways impatiently to cast off that head, he could not get rid of it. It was a great mystery.

## \|\| 2.29.14 \|\|

*cintayā vyākulo bhūtvā sasmāra garuḍadhvajam \|*  
*tena saṃsmṛtamātrastu śīghramāvirabhūcca saḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Being perturbed and worried he remembered Visnu, the Garuda-emblemed deity. The moment he was remembered, Visnu manifested himself.

## \|\| 2.29.15 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā devadeveśaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvagataṃ dvija \|*  
*nanāma śirasā namro niṣprabho vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmana, on seeing the omnipresent Visnu the Lord of the chiefs of the Devas, the bull-emblemed deity who had turned pale became humble and bent down his head.

## \|\| 2.29.16 \|\|

*taṃ tathāturamālakṣya bhītaṃ brahmadruhaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*samāśvāsyābravīdvākyaṃ tattoṣaparikārakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing (Siva) the antagonist of Brahma, sick and frightened, Hari consoled him and spoke these words that made him satisfied.

## \|\| 2.29.17 \|\|

*śambho tvayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yacchinnaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śiraḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ bhuṃkṣva sarvajña kiyatkālaṃ kṛtaṃ svayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Inasmuch as the head of Brahma had been cut off, О Sambhu, the omniscient one, you have committed a sin Experience the fruit thereof for a short while.

## \|\| 2.29.18 \|\|

*avaśyameva bhoktavyaṃ kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karma hyapi janmaśataiḥ priya \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О beloved one, a Karman performed by one, whether auspicious or inauspicious will yield its fruit which one must, of necessity, experience. Even if hundreds of births are to be taken, a Karman does not perish without being experienced.

## \|\| 2.29.19 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhitaṃ haram \|*  
*prāṇā vikalatāṃ yānti mama tvadduḥkhadarśanāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. What can I do? Where shall I go? On seeing you miserable, О Sambhu, at the sight of your misery, my Pranas are agitated and dispirited.

## \|\| 2.29.20 \|\|

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni mahānti mahatāṃ gate \|*  
*na tāni brahmahatyāyāḥ samānīti matirmama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is my opinion that even the most heinous of all great sins are not equal to Brahmana-slaughter.

## \|\| 2.29.21 \|\|

*yastvaṃ sarvasya lokasya gururdharmopadeśakaḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyābhibhūtastu kṣaṇaṃ sthātuṃ na ca kṣamaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You are the preceptor of the whole world. You are the instructor in Dharma. But, overpowered by the sin of Brahmana-slaughter you are incapable of remaining quiet even for a moment.

## \|\| 2.29.22 \|\|

*eṣā ghoratarā hatyā mīnagandhyā jarāturā \|*  
*lelihānā sureśāna grahītuṃ tvānudhāvati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This extremely terrible Hatya (the sin of Brahmana- slaughter) emits fish odour; she is senile and sick; she has put out her tongue. О Lord of Devas! She is running after you to catch you.

## \|\| 2.29.23 \|\|

*tasmānnaikatra bhavatā stheyaṃ dvādaśavatsaram \|*  
*aṭanīyaṃ hitārthāya pāpanāśābhikāmyayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence you must not stay in any single place for a while. For the sake of your benefit you have to be wandering (continuously) for twelve years, with the desire for the destruction of sins.

## \|\| 2.29.24-25 \|\|

*aṭitvā dvādaśābdāni tīrtheṣu sakaleṣu ca \|*  
*prakṣālayankaraṃ vāmaṃ bhikṣāṃ gṛhṇankapālake \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śuddhiṃ yāsyasi deveśa pāpādasmātsudāruṇāt \|*  
*ityukto viṣṇunā vipra sthāṇuḥ sarvagato'bhavat \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. You must wander for twelve years with the skull, begging for alms, washing your left hand in the holy rivers and tanks. Then, О Lord of the Devas you will become pure and be liberated from this sin.” О Brahmana, on being advised thus by Visnu, Siva went over all the places.

## \|\| 2.29.26 \|\|

*kapālamocanārthaṃ hi pāṇiṃ prakṣālayan jale \|*  
*varṣatrayaṃ bhramitvā tu prāpto badarikāśramam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In order to get rid of the skull he washed his left hand in every sacred water. Wandering thus for three years he reached the penance grove of Badarikairama.

## \|\| 2.29.27 \|\|

*bhikṣārthaṃ devadevasya dharmaputrasya mānada \|*  
*dvārastho dehi bhikṣāṃ me viṣṇo ityavadanmuhuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О bestower of honour, for the sake of alms he stood at the threshold of Dharmaputra,1 the lord of the Devas and repeatedly said — ‘‘Visnu, give me alms.”

## \|\| 2.29.28 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇo devo dṛṣṭvā dvāri sthitaṃ haram \|*  
*gṛhāṇa bhikṣāmityuktvā pradadau dakṣiṇaṃ karam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing Siva stationed at the threshold, Lord Narayana said — “Take the alms”. After saying this he offered his right hand.

## \|\| 2.29.29 \|\|

*tato haro hariṃ dṛṣṭvā bhikṣāṃ dātuṃ samudyatam \|*  
*prāharaddakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ triśūlena dvijottama \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing Hari attempting to give the alms, О excellent Brahmana, Siva struck his right hand with his trident.

## \|\| 2.29.30-33 \|\|

*tattriśūlakṣatāddhārāstisro lokabhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*prasthadvādaśahastāśca nirgatāścitravarṇikāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ekā kṣatajadhārā tu kapāle nyapatattadā \|*  
*dvitīyā tanmukhe prāptā payasyātha tṛtīyakā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jaladhārāśivaṃ prāptā harasya heturagrataḥ \|*  
*tā dhārāstrīṇi varṣāṇi saṃsevya vidhivaddharaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kiṃñcitprīto yayau kṣetraṃ kuroḥ puṇyakaraṃ dvija \|*  
*tatra gatvā haraḥsthāṇurbhūtastatra papāta ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. Through the three wounds inflicted by (the three points of) the trident, three streamlike jets came out. They were terrifying to the worlds. They had different colours; they were twelve Hastas high. One of the streams was of blood. It fell on the skull. The second, a milky stream, reached his face; the third, a stream of water came up to Siva in front of him, for the sake of saving Siva. Siva resorted to these three streams in accordance with the injunctions for the duration of three years. Becoming a little delighted, О Brahmana, he went to the holy centre of Kurukshetra. Having gone there, he became a pillar and fell down.

## \|\| 2.29.34 \|\|

*brahmahrade trivarṣāṇi magno brahmahradāmbuni \|*  
*varṣatraye gate tatra kṣatārddhāṅgo viniḥsṛtaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the holy centre of Brahma-hrada, he lay immersed in the waters of Brahmahrada. When a period of three years had elapsed he came out with half of his body wounded (?)

## \|\| 2.29.35 \|\|

*ciraṃ tuṣṭāva deveśaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvaguhāśayam \|*  
*tatastuṣṭo jagannātho varaṃ tasmai dadau tu saḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He eulogised Visnu the Lord of the Devas, abiding in the cavity of the heart of everyone, for a long time. Then the Lord of the Universe who was pleased with him granted him tile boon.

## \|\| 2.29.36-38 \|\|

*gaccha kāśīmito bhrāntvā tīrthāni bahuśo hara \|*  
*tato hariṃ namaskṛtya parītya bahudhā tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kramāttīrthāṭanaṃ kurvannavimuktapurīṃ gataḥ \|*  
*avimuktasya sīmāyāṃ prāviśadvīkṣya dhūrjaṭiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nāpaśyattāmanuprāptāṃ brahmahatyāṃ bahiḥ sthitām \|*  
*tato'sau vaiṣṇavaṃ jñātvā kṣetraṃ duritanāśanam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva prayato bhūtvā mādhavaṃ vandyamīśvaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. “О Нага, after wandering over many holy centres go to Kasi.” Thereafter, he bowed down to Hari and circumambulating him wandered over many places. Making his pilgrimage duly he reached the city of Avimukta (Kasi). After entering the limits of Avimukta, when Dhurjap (Siva) observed, he did not see Brahmahatya following him. She was standing outside. Knowing that it was a holy centre belonging to Visnu and destructive of sins he became satisfied in mind and enthusiastically eulogised Visnu, the Lord worthy of being saluted.

## \|\| 2.29.39 \|\|

*jaya jaya jagadīśa nātha viṣṇo jagadānandanidhāna vedavedya \|*  
*madhumathana nṛsiṃha pītavāso garuḍādhiṣṭhita mādhavādideva \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “Be victorious, be victorious, О Lord of the universe О Lord Visnu, the storehouse of bliss of the entire universe, knowable only through the Vedas; О suppressor of demon Madhu, О Nrsimha, О yellow-robed one, О One riding on Garuda, О Madhava, О primordial Lord.

## \|\| 2.29.40 \|\|

*vrajaramaṇa rameśa rādhikeśa tridaśeśākhilakāmapūra kṛṣṇa \|*  
*suravarakaruṇārṇavārtināśinnalinākṣādhipate vibho pareśa \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О Lord of Rama, the lover of Vrajas, (cowherd’s colony), Lord of Radha, Lord of the Devas, the fulfiller of the desires of all, О Krsna, О foremost among the Devas, О ocean of kindness, О destroyer of anguish, О lotus-eyed, О Lord of the greatest beings.

## \|\| 2.29.41 \|\|

*yadukulatilakābdhivāsa śaure kudharoddhāravidhānadakṣa dhanvin \|*  
*kalikaluṣaharāṅighrapadmayugma gṛṇadātmaprada kūrma kaśyapottha \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О Ornament of the family of Yadu, О resident of the milky ocean, О Sauri, О archer, О expert in the art of uplifting the mountain (Govardhana), О deity having a pair of the lotus-feet that destroy the sin of Kali age, О deity who bestow favour on those who eulogise thee, О Kiirma (Divine Tortoise), О son of Kasyapa (Vamana).

## \|\| 2.29.42 \|\|

*kukupativanapāvakākhilejyāsrapakālāsitavastra buddha kalkin \|*  
*bhavabhayahara bhaktavaśya gopa praṇattoddhāraka puṇyakīrtināma \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Parasurama — the fire for the forest of wicked kings, О Buddha with a saffron cloth that cleaned off blood from all sacrifices, О Kalkin, О remover of the fear of worldly existence, О deity governable by (i.e. under the influence of) the devotees, О cowherd, who lift up those who bow down to you, О Lord of sacred fame and name.

## \|\| 2.29.43 \|\|

*dharaṇibharaharāsurāripūjya prakṛtīśeśa jagannivāsa rāma \|*  
*guṇagaṇavilasaccarācareśa triguṇātīta sanātanāgrapūjya \|*  
*nijajanaparirakṣitāntakāre kamalāṅghre kamanīya padmanābha \|*  
*kamalakara kuśeśayādhivāsa priyakāmonmathana tr! yadhīśavandya \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О remover of the burden of the Earth, О Lord worthy of being worshipped by the enemies of Asuras, О Lord of Prakrti, О residential abode of the whole universe, О Rama, О Lord of the mobile and immobile beings shining with many attributes, О Lord who are beyond the three Gunas., О eternal one, О Lord worthy of being worshipped at the head of all, О Lord who protect the enemy of the annihilator Yama through your own people, О Lord with lotus-like feet, О beautiful Padmanabha, О lotus-palmed Lord, О Lord favourite of the resident of the lotus (i.e. God Brahma), О Lord, worthy of being saluted by the destroyer of Kama and the Lord of three worlds (?)

## \|\| 2.29.44 \|\|

*aghahara raghunātha yādaveśa priyabhūdeva parātparāmarejya \|*  
*haladhara duratāpaha praṇamya triguṇavyāpta jagattrikāladakṣa \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О remover of sins, О Lord of the Raghus, О Lord of the Yadavas, one who are fond of Brahmanas, О greater than the greatest one, О Lord worthy of being worshipped by the immortal beings, О wielder of the ploughshare, О remover of sins, О Lord, worthy of being bowed to; О Lord pervaded by the three Gunas, О cleverest one in the three worlds and three units of Time. 4

## \|\| 2.29.45 \|\|

*danujakulavināśanaikakarmannanaghārūḍhaphaṇīśa kaṃsakāla \|*  
*raviśaśinayana pragalbhaceṣṭa pradhutadhvānta navāmbudābha meśa \|\| 45 \|\|*

62b-63. Those men came in and requested me again and again: “O splendid lady, you have been invited by your husband. Hasten there with glee and joy. Your husband has returned endowed with plenty of wealth and jewels as well as two other wives.

79-81. О splendid lady, at his words the wealth was immediately brought by the servants. My husband offered the entire wealth to me with love and mind untarnished by deception. He honoured me with ornaments and garments, even as the two ladies, the ogress and the princess were looking on.

*ullāsakaraṇaṃ vākyaṃ kareṇa kucapīḍanam \|*

84-85. I shall have to be born in the animal kingdom thousands of times. О splendid-faced lady, the woman who does not dedicate her wealth and life to her husband will undoubtedly attain this state. By understanding this, one should save the wealth and life of one’s husband.
