6-10. “Well done, well done, О excellent Brahmana, interested in uplifting the worlds. Now I have been blessed by you of merciful soul. О Brahmana, the excellent greatness of Gaya, which is a great secret which is a pleasing narrative of Dharma, which bestows salvation on the Pitrs and which is meritorious, has been heard by me. Now О leading Brahmana, narrate the excellent greatness of Kasl.

## \|\| 2.48.8-10 \|\|

*adhunā vada viprenda kāśīmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*mayā pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ brahman kiñcitsandhyāvalīmukhāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tena me smṛtimāpannaṃ vistarādvada sāmpratam \|*  
*vasiṣṭha uvāca- tacchrutvā mohinī vākyaṃ vasustasyāḥ purohitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vedavedāṅgatattvajñaḥ prāha tāṃ śrūyatāmiti \|*  
*vasuruvāca- śubhā kāśīpurī dhanyā dhanyo devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. О Brahmana, a little of it had been formerly heard by me when orally repeated by Sandhyavall. Hence, it is being recollected by me. Now, tell it to me in detail. Vasiffha said: On hearing those words of Mohini, Vasu, her priest, who knew the reality of the Vedas and the Vedarigas spoke to her again. Vasu said: May it be heard. The city of Kasi is blessed and auspicious. Lord Mahesvara is blessed.

## \|\| 2.48.11-12 \|\|

*yaḥ sevate'niśaṃ kāśīṃ muktidāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ purīm \|*  
*yācayitvā hareḥ kṣetraṃ sthito devaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pūjayaṃstaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ pūjyamānaḥ surādibhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. To him who continuously resorts to Kasi, it is the bestower of salvation. It was a city pertaining to Visnu. The eternal lord Siva requested for it from Hari. He remained there worshipping Hrsikes'a and he was worshipped by Devas and others.

## \|\| 2.48.13 \|\|

*vārāṇasī tu bhuvanatrayasārabhūtā \|*  
*ramyā nṛṇāṃ sugatidā kila sevyamānā \|*  
*atrāgatā vividhaduṣkṛtakāriṇo'pi \|*  
*pāpakṣaye virajasaḥ sumanaḥprakāśāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Varanasi is a beautiful city. It is the essence of the three worlds. On being resorted to it, it is the bestower of good goal (salvation) on men. Persons who have resorted to this city, even though they might have committed various sins, become free from all blemishes and shine like gods.

## \|\| 2.48.14 \|\|

*idaṃ guhyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvaprāṇisukhāvaham \|*  
*mokṣadaṃ sarvajantūnāṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ śaivameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This holy centre is a mystically secret place. It is conducive to happiness to all living beings. It is the bestower of salvation on all creatures. It is pertaining to both Visnu and Siva.

## \|\| 2.48.15 \|\|

*brahmaghnagoghnagurutalpagamitradhruk ca \|*  
*nyāsāpahārakuśidādiniṣiddhavṛttiḥ \|*  
*saṃsārabhūtadṛḍhapāśavimuktadeho \|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ śivapurīṃ samupaiti martyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He may be a Brahmana-slayer, a killer of cows, a defiler of his preceptor’s bed or a betrayer of friends. He may be guilty of misappropriation of deposits on trust or he might have practised usury or adopted the basest form of maintenance — the man who approaches Varanasi, the city of Siva, shall have his self liberated from the strong bondage of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.48.16 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ tathedaṃ surasiddhajuṣṭaṃ \|*  
*samprāpya martyaḥ sukṛtaprabhāvāt \|*  
*khyāto bhavetsarvasurāsurāṇāṃ \|*  
*mṛtaśca yāyātparamaṃ padaṃ saḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Having reached this sacred place, frequented by gods and Siddhas, thanks to the power of his merit, the man shall be well-known amongst Devas and Asuras. When dead he may attain Moksa, the highest region.

## \|\| 2.48.17 \|\|

*kṣetre'sminnivasaṃti ye sukṛtino bhaktā harau vā hare \|*  
*paśyanto'nvahamādareṇa śucayaḥ santaḥ samāḥ śambhunā \|*  
*te martyā bhayaduḥkhapāparahitāḥ saṃśuddhakarmakriyāḥ \|*  
*bhitvā sambhavabandhajālagahanaṃ vindaṃti mokṣaṃ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Those meritorious persons who stay in this holy centre, are the devotees of either Нага or Hari and visit the deity every day with great respect, are as pure and saintly as Sambhu and whose activities and holy rites are very pure become free from fear, sorrow and sins. After cutting asunder the thick net of birth in Samsara they obtain great liberation.

## \|\| 2.48.18 \|\|

*dviyojanamathārddhaṃ ca pūrvapaścimataḥ sthitam \|*  
*arddhayojanavistīrṇaṃ dakṣiṇottarataḥ smṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. This Kagi ksetra extends to two and a half Yojanas (1 yojana =»3 km) from east to west and half a Yojana from North to South.

## \|\| 2.48.19 \|\|

*varaṇāsirnadī yāvadasiḥ śuṣkanadī śubhe \|*  
*eṣa kṣetrasya vistāraḥ prokto devena śaṃbhunā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. From the river Varana (Mod. Ваша) (the north) to the river Asi of dry bed (to the south), is spoken of as the area of this holy place, by god Siva.1

## \|\| 2.48.20 \|\|

*ayanaṃ tūttaraṃ jñeyaṃ timicaṇḍeśvaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ śaṅkukarṇaṃ tu oṃkāre tadanantaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Linga that is known as Timi Candesvara is the northern limit (or entrance of this ksetra). The southern end is Sankukarna based on Omkara.

## \|\| 2.48.21 \|\|

*piṅgalā nāma yattīrthaṃ āgneyī sā prakīrtitā \|*  
*śuṣkā saricca sā jñeyā lolārko yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It is described that there is a sacred pool called Pingala in the south-east corner of this sacred place. The dry river Asi is to be known as the Pingala Nadi near which stands Lolarka.

## \|\| 2.48.22 \|\|

*iḍānāmnī tu yā nāḍī sā saumyā samprakīrtitā \|*  
*varaṇā nāma sā jñeyā keśavo yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The mystic vein called Ida is described as being related to the moon and hence pleasing and auspicious. It should be known as the (river) Varana — the place where Visnu is stationed.

## \|\| 2.48.23-24 \|\|

*ābhyāṃ madhye tu yā nāḍī suṣumṇā sā prakīrtitā \|*  
*matsyodarī ca sā jñeyā visvaraṃ tatprakīrtitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vimuktaṃ na kadā yasmānmokṣyate na kadācana \|*  
*mahākṣetramidaṃ tasmādavimuktamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The mystic vein that is in between the two mystic veins is glorified as Susumna which should be known to be the Ganga (the container of fish in her belly or stream).2 This great holy centre is traditionally known as Avimuktaka3 as this has never been abandoned nor shall ever be given up (by Lord Siva or Visnu). Hence it is called quiet, soundless (visvara).

## \|\| 2.48.25 \|\|

*prayāgādapi tīrthāderadhikaṃ dustarācchubhe \|*  
*anāyāsena vai yatra mokṣaprāptiḥ prajāyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О auspicious lady, in this holy centre the attainment of liberation is possible without any strain, more easily than in such holy centres as Prayaga which is very difficult of access.

## \|\| 2.48.26-34 \|\|

*nānāvarṇā vikarṇāśca cāṇḍālā ye jugupsitāḥ \|*  
*kilbiṣaiḥ pūrṇadehāśca prakṛṣṭaiḥ pātakaistathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*bheṣajaṃ paramaṃ teṣāmavimuktaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*duṣṭāndhān dīnakṛpaṇānpāpānduṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*haro'nukampayā sarvānnayatyāśu parāṃ gatim \|*  
*kṣetramadhyādyadā gaṅgā saṅgatā saritāṃ patim \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti sā puṇyā purī jātā śubhānane \|*  
*puṇyā codaṅmukhī gaṅgā prācī caiva sarasvatī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatra muktaṃ kapālaṃ tu śivena sumahātmanā \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe tu ye gatvā piṇḍadānena vai pitṝn \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śrāddheṣu prīṇayiṣyanti teṣāṃ lokāstu bhāsvarāḥ \|*  
*brahmahā yo'bhigacchettu avimuktaṃ kadācana \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasya kṣetrasya māhātmyādbrahmahatyā nivartate \|*  
*avimuktaṃ gatā ye vai mahāpuṇyakṛto narāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*akṣayyā hyajarāścaiva videhāśca bhavaṃti te \|*  
*ājñānājjñānato vāpi striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yatkiñcidaśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ caiva kubuddhinā \|*  
*avimuktaṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ bhasmasādbhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

26-28a. There are people of various castes; there are Candelas of despicable character; there are persons whose entire person is filled with sins and great evils. Learned men know that Avimukta is a great medicine for them. Нага takes pity on wicked persons, blind ones, indigent ones, miserable ones and those who commit sins. He leads them on to great salvation.

28b-30a. О auspicious-looking lady, that city becomes holy and meritorious ever since the Gariga began to flow through the middle of the holy centre and then joined the ocean. The Ganga flows through towards the North. The Sarasvati flows towards the East.

30b-31a. The skull was left off there by Siva of great and noble soul. The worlds attained by those people who go to that holy centre and propitiate the Pitts by means of Pinda-offerings in the Sraddhas, are refulgent ones.

31b-32a. If the murderer of a Brahmana goes to Avimukta at any time, the Brahmahatya (the sin of Brahmin-slaughter) recedes due to the greatness of that holy centre.1

32b-33a. Those men of great merits who go to Avimukta become everlasting, free from old age and attain salvation and liberation from bodily bondage.

33b-34. If a man or a woman, knowingly or unknowingly commits some inauspicious act through evil intellect, all that is reduced to ashes (the moment) he enters Avimukta.1 2

## \|\| 2.48.35 \|\|

*sadā yajati yajñena sadā dānaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*sadā tapasvī bhavati hyavimukte sthito naraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A man staying in Avimukta is like a man who performs sacrifices continuously, who makes charitable gifts always and who continuously performs penance.

## \|\| 2.48.36 \|\|

*na sā gatiḥ kurukṣetre gaṅgādvāre na puṣkare \|*  
*yā gatirvihitā puṃsāmavimuktanivāsinām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The salvation attained by the residents of Avimukta cannot be attained by residing at Kurukshetra, Gangadvara or in Puskara.

## \|\| 2.48.37 \|\|

*sarvātmanā tapaḥ satyaṃ prāṇināṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*avimukte vasedyastu sa tu sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There is no doubt in this matter that all the living beings have the benefit of truthfulness and penance by all means. But he who stays in Avimukta is Mahesvara himself.

## \|\| 2.48.38 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ na sevaṃte ye mūḍhāstāmasā narāḥ \|*  
*viṇmūtrarajasāṃ madhye te vasaṃti punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those foolish men of murky mind who do not resort to Avimukta, stay again and again in the midst of faeces, urine and menstrual blood (i.e. they are born of wombs, frequently.)

## \|\| 2.48.39 \|\|

*avimukte sthitā nityaṃ pāṃśubhirvāyuneritaiḥ \|*  
*spṛṣṭā duṣkṛtakarmāṇo yāṃti vai paramāṃ gatim \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Even those persons of evil actions who come into contact with the dust particles which were lying in Avimukta, and were wafted by the wind towards them attain the greatest

## \|\| 2.48.40 \|\|

*yastatra nivasenmartyaḥ saṃyatātmā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamapi bhuñjāno vāyubhakṣasamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The man who stays there, who has controlled his mind and who has great concentration is remembered as equal to an ascetic feeding himself on wind although he may be enjoying all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.48.41 \|\|

*tatra māsaṃ vasedyastu labdhāhāro jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*samyaktena vrataṃ cīrṇaṃ mahāpāśupataṃ bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who stays there for a month, who takes food regularly, but who has controlled his sense-organs is like a person by whom the holy vow of the great Pasupata Vrata has been performed.

## \|\| 2.48.42 \|\|

*janmamṛtyubhayaṃ jitvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*niḥśreyasagatiṃ puṇyāṃ tathā yogagatiṃ labhet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He conquers the fear of birth and death; he attains the greatest goal; viz. Moksa, he obtains holy salvation and he attains the Yogic goal.

## \|\| 2.48.43 \|\|

*nahi yogagatirlabhyā janmāntaraśatairapi \|*  
*prāpyate kṣetramāhātmyātprabhāvācchaṅkarasya ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Indeed, the Yogic goal cannot be attained by ordinary persons even in hundreds of births. But it is attained here, thanks to the greatness of the holy centre and the superhuman power of Sankara.

## \|\| 2.48.44 \|\|

*ekāhārastu yastiṣṭhenmāsaṃ tatra śubhānane \|*  
*yāvajjīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ māsenaikena naśyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If a man stays there for a month taking only a single meal a day, О fair-faced lady, his sins committed throughout his life perish in a month.

## \|\| 2.48.45 \|\|

*ādehapātādyo martyo'vimuktaṃ naiva muñcati \|*  
*brahmacaryeṇa saṃyuktaḥ sa sākṣācchaṃkaro bhavet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The man who is endowed with the Vow of celibacy and who does not abandon Avimukta until the fall of the body (i.e. death) shall become Sankara himself.

## \|\| 2.48.46 \|\|

*vighnairāhanyamāno'pi yo'vimuktaṃ na ca tyajet \|*  
*sa muñcati jarāmṛtyuṃ janma caitacca naśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If anyone does not abandon Avimukta though overwhelmed by obstacles, he transcends old age and death as well as this transient life.

## \|\| 2.48.47 \|\|

*ādehapatanādye tu sevaṃte hyavimuktakam \|*  
*te mṛtā haṃsayānena divyān lokānprayāṃti hi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Those who resort to Avimukta till the fall of their bodies, go to divine worlds by means of swan-yoked vehicles after death.

## \|\| 2.48.48 \|\|

*viṣayāsaktacitto'pi tyaktabhaktimatirnaraḥ \|*  
*iha kṣetre mṛtaḥ so'pi saṃsāraṃ na punarviśet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A man’s mind may be attracted towards worldly pleasures; he may have eschewed devotion and he may be unthinking. But if he dies in this holy centre, he does not re-enter the worldly existence.1

## \|\| 2.48.49 \|\|

*svargāpavargayorheturetattīrthavaraṃ bhuvi \|*  
*yastatra pañcatāṃ yāti tasya muktirna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On this earth, this excellent holy centre is the cause for the attainment of heavenly pleasures as well as salvation.

## \|\| 2.48.50 \|\|

*janmāntarasahasreṇa yogī yatpadamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tadihaiva paraṃ mokṣaṃ maraṇādadhigacchati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The great salvation, the region that a Yogin attains in the course of a thousand births, one attains by merely dying here itself.1

## \|\| 2.48.51-52 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā vai varṇasaṅkarāḥ \|*  
*krimayaścaiva ye mlecchāḥ saṅkīrṇāḥ pāpayonayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kīṭāḥ pipīlikāścaiva ye cānye mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptāste'pi deveśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, Sudras, persons of mixed castes, worms, outcastes alien tribes, persons of sinful birth and of intercaste origin, germs, insects, ants and all kinds of animals and birds who die here in due course of time (at the hands of Kala) are remembered as lords of gods.

## \|\| 2.48.53-63 \|\|

*candrā rddhamaulayaḥ sarve lalāṭākṣā bṛṣadhvajāḥ \|*  
*prāṇāṃstyajanti ye tatra prāṇinastattvataḥ śubhe \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rudra tvaṃ te tu samprāpya modaṃte śivasannidhau \|*  
*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tiryagyonigato'pi vā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*avimukte tyajanprāṇānmuktibhāksyānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śivabhaktiparā nityaṃ nānyabhaktāśca ye narāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*taccittāstadgataprāṇā jīvanmuktā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*agnipraveśaṃ ye kuryuravimukte vicārataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kālāgnirudra sāyujyaṃ te prayānti ca mohini \|*  
*kurvantyanaśanaṃ ye tu śivabhaktāḥ suniścitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ punarāvṛttiḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|*  
*avimukte mṛtyukāle bhūtānāmīśvaraḥ svayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*karmabhiḥ preryamāṇānāṃ karṇajāpyaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*svayaṃ rāmeṇa cāpyuktaṃ śivāya śivakāriṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

*atiprasannacittena avimuktanivāsine \|*  
*mumūrṣordakṣiṇe karṇe yasya kasyāpi vā svayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*upadekṣyasi manmantraṃ sa mukto bhavitā śiva \|*  
*antakāle manuṣyāṇāṃ chidyamāneṣu karmasu \|\| 61 \|\|*

*vāyunā preryamāṇānāṃ smṛtirnaivopajāyate \|*  
*ye'vimukte sthitā rudrā bhaktaprītipradāyakāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*karṇajāpyaṃ prayacchanti ḍimicaṇḍeśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*nāvimukte mṛtaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ yāti kilbiṣī \|\| 63 \|\|*

53-54a. They will attain identity of form with Rudra viz. all of them will have crests of crescent, eyes in the forehead and emblems of bull. О auspicious lady, those who cast off their vital airs there, in fact, attain Rudrahood. They rejoice in the vicinity of Siva.

54b-55a. Whether willingly or unwillingly if one abandons one’s life at Avimukta, one shall undoubtedly attain liberation. This is true in the case of even animals.

55b-56a. Those men who had ever been devotees of Siva exclusively and not of others, those whose minds and vital airs adhere to him (lord Siva), do become living liberated souls. There is no doubt about it.

56b-57a. О MohinI, those who enter funeral pyre deliberately, in the holy centre of Avimukta attain complete identity with Rudra, the destructive fire at the end of the world.

57b-58a. There is no return to worldly existence even in hundreds and crores of Kalpas, in the case of those devotees of Siva who observe fast unto death with a steady resolve.

58b-59a. At the time of death in Avimukta, the lord of all beings himself offers the prayerful word for repetition into the ears of living beings who are urged by their Karmans.

59b-61a. It has been mentioned thus by Rama himself with great pleasure in his mind to Siva who performs auspicious things and who resides in Avimukta: — О Siva, if you yourself instruct my Mantra into the right ear of a dying person whoever he may be, he will become liberated.

6lb-63. At the time of death when the Karmans of men are being split and when they are being urged by the wind, they lose all memory. The Rudras who are stationed in Avi- mukta viz. Dimicandesvara and others are the bestowers of pleasures on devotees. They give the Taraka Mantra (by whispering it) into the ears. No sinner dying in Avimukta goes to the hell.1

## \|\| 2.48.64 \|\|

*īśvarānugṛhītā hi sarve yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*uddeśamātrātkathitā avimuktaguṇāstava \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. All persons blessed by Isvara do attain great salvation. Here the attributes of Avimukta were recounted to you only by way of illustration.

## \|\| 2.48.65-66 \|\|

*samudra syaiva ratnānāmavimuktasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*jñānavijñānaniṣṭhānāṃ paramānandamicchatām \|\| 65 \|\|*

*yā matirvihitā nūnaṃ svarnnīte tu mṛtasya sā \|*  
*prāṇāniha narastyaktvā na punarjāyate kvacit \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. The detailed explanation of the attributes of Avimukta is like that of the jewels in the ocean. The intellect of the dead, on being led to the heaven, is the same as that of those established in perfect knowledge and wisdom and those who wish for the greatest bliss. A man who abandons his vital airs here, is never born anywhere.

## \|\| 2.48.67 \|\|

*anantā sā gatistasya yogināmeva yā smṛtā \|*  
*yogapīṭhaṃ śmaśānākhyaṃ yattīrthaṃ maṇikarṇikā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. That endless salvation of that deity is like that of the Yogins. What is called Smagana1 2 (cremation ground) is the pedestal of Yoga and the Tlrtha thereof is Manikarnika.

## \|\| 2.48.68-74 \|\|

*teṣu muktiḥ samuddiṣṭā patitānāṃ svakarmaṇā \|*  
*tatrāpi sarvatīrthānāmuttamā maṇikarṇikā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*yatra nityaṃ varārohe sānnidhyaṃ dhūrjaṭeḥ smṛtam \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ yajñānāṃ yatphalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tadavāpnoti dharmātmā tatra snātvā varānane \|*  
*svasvamapyatra yo dadyād brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|\| 70 \|\|*

*śubhāṃ gatimavāpnoti hutāśa iva dīpyate \|*  
*upavāsaṃ tu yaḥ kṛtvā viprānsantarpayennaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sa sautrāmaṇiyajñasya phalamāpnoti niścitam \|*  
*tatra dīpapradānena jñānavatsphuratīndri yam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*prāpnoti dhūpadānena sthānaṃ rudra niṣevitam \|*  
*vṛṣabhaṃ taruṇaṃ saumyaṃ caturvatsatarīyutam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yo'ṅkayitvā mocayati sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*pitṛbhiḥ sahito mokṣaṃ gacchatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

68-69a. Liberation is indicated in those places by means of their Karmans in the case of fallen men. In this connection Manikarnika3 is the most excellent of all Tirthas, since О fair lady, there is perpetual presence ofDhurjati (Siva).

69b-70a. О fair-faced lady, by taking his bath there, the righteous soul attains that fruit which ten horse sacrifices are remembered to yield.

70b-71a. He who gives away all his wealth to a Brahmana who has mastered the Vedas, like the Homa-offerings into the blazing fire attains splendid goal.

71b-72a. The man who observes fast and propitiates Brahmanas decidedly attains the benefit of Sautramaniyajna (the sacrifice pertaining to Indra).

72b-73a. By offering lights, the sense-organs throb with knowledge. By offering incense, he attains that place resorted to by Rudras.

73b-74. He who marks a young gentle bull and sets it free along with four heifers, attains the greatest goal. Undoubtedly he derives liberation along with his ancestors.

## \|\| 2.48.75 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena dharmādīṃstu prakurvataḥ \|*  
*yacchivaṃ tu samuddiśya tadanantaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Of what avail is much talk? Infinite benefit accrues to one who performs Dharma etc., with Siva in view.

## \|\| 2.48.76 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ puṇyaṃ puṣpadāne prakīrtitam \|*  
*agnihotraphalaṃ dhūpe gandhe bhūdānajaṃ phalam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The merit of ten horse-sacrifices is glorified to accrue to one on giving flowers. In giving incense one gets the benefit of Agnihotra; in giving scents, the benefit is that of making charitable gifts of plots of land.

## \|\| 2.48.77 \|\|

*mārjane gopradānasya phalamatra prakīrtitam \|*  
*anulepe daśaguṇaṃ mālye daśaguṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. In Marjana (wiping off) the benefit glorified is that one gets by gifting away a cow; ten times the usual benefit accrues to one who offers unguents. While in offering garlands the benefit is ten-times that of the usual.

## \|\| 2.48.78-80 \|\|

*gīte sahasraguṇitaṃ vādye lakṣaguṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*avimukte mahādevamarcanti stuvaṃti vai \|\| 78 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavimuktāste svastiṣṭhaṃtyajarāmarāḥ \|*  
*avimuktaṃ samāsādya liṅgamarcayate naraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*kalpakoṭiśataiścāpi tasya nāsti punarbhavaḥ \|*  
*ajaro hyamaraścaiva krīḍetsa bhavasannidhau \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-79a. In (offering vocal) music the benefit is a thousand-fold; in instrumental music the benefit is hundred- thousand fold. Those who worship and eulogise Mahadeva at Avimukta are liberated from all sins, freed from old age and death. They stand in the heaven.

79b-80. If on reaching Avimukta a man worships the Linga, he has no rebirth even in hundreds and crores of Kalpas. Unaging and devoid of death he sports in the presence of Siva.

## \|\| 2.48.81-83 \|\|

*ye tu dhyānaṃ samāsādya muktātmānaḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*sanniyamyendri yagrāmaṃ japaṃti śatarudri yam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*avimukte sthitā nityaṃ kṛtārthāste dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ekāhamupavāsaṃ yaḥ kariṣyati yaśasvini \|\| 82 \|\|*

*phalaṃ varṣaśatasyeha labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ tu sāyujyaṃ gaṅgāvaruṇasaṅgamam \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-82a. The liberated souls who perform the Japa of Satarudriya with great concentration along with requisite meditation and after restraining the groups of sense-organs, the excellent Brahmanas who are stationed in Avimukta continuously are blessed and have their objects achieved.

82b-83. О famous lady, he who observes fast for a single day undoubtedly derives the benefit of observing fast for a hundred years. Henceforth the identity arising from the confluence of Ganga and Varuna.

## \|\| 2.48.84 \|\|

*śravaṇadvādaśīyogo budhavāre yadā bhavet \|*  
*tadā tasminnaraḥ snātvā sannihatyāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. When the twelfth day of the month of Sravana coincides with a Wednesday a man should take a holy bath therein. By his mere presence he derives the benefit.

## \|\| 2.48.85 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ karoti yastatra tasminkāle śubhānane \|*  
*tārayitvā pitṝnsarvānviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. He who performs Sraddha rites at that time and place, О fair faced lady, redeems the Pitrs and goes to Visnu’s world.

## \|\| 2.48.86 \|\|

*varaṇāsyostu jāhnavyāḥ saṅgame lokaviśrute \|*  
*datvāśvaṃ ca vidhānena sa bhūyo'pi na jāyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. By giving a horse as gift in accordance with the injunctions, in the world-famous confluence of the Ganga with Varana and Asi,1 the devotee is not born again (i.c. he gets Moksa).

## \|\| 2.48.87 \|\|

*yastatra saṅgameśānamarcayedbhaktimānnaraḥ \|*  
*sa sākṣāddevadeveśo nigrahānugrahe kṣamaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87 The devout man who worships the lord of the Sangama (confluence) there, is the Lord of the chiefs of Devas himself. He is competent to restrain and bless.

## \|\| 2.48.88 \|\|

*deveśvarasya pūrveṇa svayaṃ tiṣṭhati keśavaḥ \|*  
*keśavasya ca pūrveṇa viśrutaḥ saṅgameśvaraḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Kesava1 2 himself stands to the east of the lord of the Devas. To the east of Kesava is the well-known Saiiganiesvara.

## Chapter 49. Pilgrimage to КйН1

## \|\| 2.49.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- vāyavye tu diśo bhāge tasya pīṭhasya sundari \|*  
*liṅgaṃ prasthāpitaṃ tatra sagareṇa caturmukham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1\. О beautiful lady, to the north east of that seat of the deity (Sangamesvara), four-faced Linga had been installed by Sagara.

## \|\| 2.49.2 \|\|

*sāgarādvāyukoṇe tu bhadra dehaṃ saraḥ smṛtam \|*  
*gavāṃ kṣīreṇa sañjātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the north-west corner of the holy centre pertaining to Sagara is the lake Bhadradeha made out of the milk of cows. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.49.3 \|\|

*kapilānāṃ sahasrasya samyagdattasya yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate martyaḥ snānamātreṇa mohini \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Mohinl, merely by taking bath therein, a man attains the benefit of charitable gift of a thousand Tawny- coloured cows.

## \|\| 2.49.4 \|\|

*pūrvābhādra padāyuktā paurṇamāsī yadā bhavet \|*  
*tadā puṇyatamaḥ kālo hyaśvamedhaphalapradaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The period when the constellation Ptirvabhadrapada coincides with the full moon day, is highly meritorious and it yields the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.49.5 \|\|

*yatra sā dṛśyate devī vikhyātā bhīṣmacaṇḍikā \|*  
*śmaśāne tāṃ samabhyarcya na naro durgatiṃ vrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The goddess who is seen in the cremation ground is well known as Bhlsrna Gandika. By worshipping her, a man never faces a mishap.

## \|\| 2.49.6 \|\|

*antakeśvarapūrveṇa dakṣe sarveśvarasya ca \|*  
*mātalīśvarasaumye tu kṛttivāseśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Krttivasesvara1 is to the East of Antakesvara, to the South of Sarves'vara and to the north of Matallsvara.

## \|\| 2.49.7-9 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ sampūjya parāṃ gatim \|*  
*ekena janmanā devi kṛttivāse tu labhyate \|*  
*pūrvajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tapasāpi na śuddhyti \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇānnaśyate pāpaṃ tasya liṅgasya darśanāt \|*  
*kṛte tu tr! yambakaṃ pūrvaṃ tretāyāṃ kṛttivāsasam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*maheśvaraṃ tu devasya dvāpare nāma gīyate \|*  
*hastipāleśvaraṃ nāma kalau siddhaistu gīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-8a. О gentle lady, by visiting Krttivasesvara and by worshipping him, one attains the greatest goal even in a single birth. This is derived in Krttivasa. Usually the sin committed in the previous birth is not dispelled even by penance. But by visiting that Lir'iga (i.e. Krttivasa) that sin perishes instantaneously.

8b-9. In the Krtayuga, the Tryambaka Linga is to be worshipped, in the Tretayuga the linga of Kittivasas is to be worshipped. It is the Mahesvara Linga that is sung about in the Dvapara. The Linga Hastipalesvara is sung about in the Kali age by the Siddhas.

## \|\| 2.49.10 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaro devo dra ṣṭavyaśca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*yadīhettārakaṃ jñānaṃ śāśvataṃ cāmṛtapradam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If one desires to get eternal knowledge that absolves one from Samsara and grants immortality one should visit the god Krttivasesvara1 again and again.

## \|\| 2.49.11 \|\|

*darśanāddevadevasya brahmahāpi pramucyate \|*  
*sparśane pūjane caiva sarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By seeing the lord of the Dcvas even a murderer of a Brahmana is liberated from the sin. By touching and worshipping the Linga one derives the benefit of all Yajna

## \|\| 2.49.12-17 \|\|

*śraddhayā parayā devaṃ ye'canti sanātanam \|*  
*phālgunasya caturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe samāhitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*puṣpaiḥ phalaistathā patrairbhakṣyairuccāvacaistathā \|*  
*kṣīreṇa madhunā caiva toyena saha sarpiṣā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tarpanti paraṃ liṅgamarcanti śubhaṃ śivam \|*  
*ḍuṇḍukāranamaskārairnṛtyagītaistathaiva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mukhavādyairanekaiśca stotrairmatraistathaiva ca \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ bhaktyā paramayā haram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*te yāṃti paramaṃ sthānaṃ pūjayitvā ca mohini \|*  
*bhūtāyāṃ caitramāsasya yo'cayetparameśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sa ca vitteśvaraṃ prāpya krīḍate yakṣarāḍiva \|*  
*vaiśākhasya caturddaśyāṃ yo'cayetprayataḥ śivam \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-16a. On the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Phalguna, the devotees should worship the eternal lord with great faith and concentration by means of flowers, fruits, leaves and diverse kinds of foodstuffs as well as by means of milk, honey, water and ghee. They propitiate and worship the auspicious Linga by means of the sound of small hand-drums (Damarus) bowing, dancing, singing, playing on mouth organs, recitation of Stotras (hymns) and chanting Mantras. After observing fast for one night and worshipping lord Siva with deep devotion, they attain the supreme region, О Mohinl.

16b-17. He who worships Paramesvara on the fourteenth day in the month of Vaisakha,1 2 attains the world of Vaisakha (lord Karttikeya) and becomes his follower.

## \|\| 2.49.18-29 \|\|

*vaiśākhalokamāsādya tasyaivānucaro bhavet \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamāse caturdaśyāṃ yo'cayecchraddhayā haram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*svargalokamavāpnoti yāvadābhūtasamplavam \|*  
*caturddaśyāṃ śucau bhadre yo'cayetprayataḥ śivam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sūryalokaṃ samāsādya krīḍate yāvadīpsitam \|*  
*śrāvaṇasya caturddaśyāṃ kāmaliṅgaṃ samutthitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dadāti vāruṇaṃ lokaṃ krīḍate cāpsaronvitaḥ \|*  
*māsi bhādra pade yuktamarcayitvā tu śaṅkaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

*puṣpaiḥ phalaiśca vividhairindra syaiti salokatām \|*  
*pitṛpakṣe caturddaśyāṃ pūjayitvā yatheśvaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

*prāpnoti pitṛlokaṃ tu krīḍate pūjitaśca taiḥ \|*  
*prabodhamāse deveśamarcayitvā maheśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*candra loke samāsādya krīḍate yāvadīpsitam \|*  
*bahule mārgaśīrṣasya pūjayitvā pinākinam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*piṣṇulokamavāpnoti krīḍate kālamakṣayam \|*  
*arcayitvā tathā pauṣe sthāṇuṃ hṛṣṭena cetasā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*prāpnoti nairṛtaṃ sthānaṃ tenaiva saha modate \|*  
*māghe samarcayitvā vai puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*prāpnoti śivalokaṃ tu tyaktvā saṃsārasāgaram \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ devamarcayettu prayatnataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*avimukte vaseccaiva yadīcchecchāṅkaraṃ padam \|*  
*ghaṇṭākarṇo hradastatra vyāseśasya tu paścime \|\| 28 \|\|*

*snānaṃ kṛtvā hrade tasminvyāseśasya ca darśanāt \|*  
*yatra tatra mṛto devi vārāṇasyāṃ mṛto bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

18-19a. He who worships Нага faithfully in the month Jyestha on the fourteenth day, attains the heavenly world and remains there until the time of dissolution of all living beings.

19b-20a. О gentle lady, he who worships Siva with purity on the fourteenth day in the month of Asa^ha attains the world of the sun and sports himself about as much as he pleases.

20b-21a. By worshipping Yogin Sankara in the month of Bhadrapada with various flowers and fruits the devotee attains the same world as that of Indra.

21b-23a. By worshipping Isvara on the fourteenth day in the Pitrpaksa (dark half of the Bhadrapada month) the devotee attains the world of the Pitrs and being honoured by them he sports about.

23b-24a. By worshipping Mahesvara, the lord of the Devas, in the month of Prabodha (i.e. Karttika), the devotee attains the world of the moon and sports about as long as he pleases.

24b-25a. By worshipping the Pinaka-bearing lord in the dark half of the month of Margaslrsa, the devotee attains the world of Visnu and sports about there for endless Ages (time).

25b-26a. By worshipping Sthanu in the month of Pausa with a dilighted mind the devotee attains the spot pertaining to Nirrti and rejoices alongwith him.

26b-27a. By worshipping Siva with auspicious flowers, fruits and roots in the month of Magha, the devotee eschews the ocean of worldly existence and attains Sivaloka.

27b-29. If one wishes for attaining the region of Sankara, one should reside in Avimukta and assiduously worship lord Krttivases'vara. Towards the west of Vyasesa, there is the deep pool called Ghantakarna. By taking bath in that pool and by visiting Vyasesa, О gentle lady, wherever one may die one shall have the benefit of dying in Varanasi.

## \|\| 2.49.30 \|\|

*daṇḍakhāte naraḥ snātvā tarpayitvā svakānpitṝn \|*  
*narakasthāstu ye devi pitṛlokaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If the man takes a holy bath in Dandakhata and performs Tarpana rite for his deceased ancestors О gentle lady, those who are detained in the hell go to the world of Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.49.31 \|\|

*piśācatvaṃ gatā devi ye narāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ piṇḍapradānena dehasyoddharaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The uplift of those men of evil deeds who have attained Pis'aca-hood (the state of an evil spirit), О gentle lady, is through the offerings of Pimjas.

## \|\| 2.49.32-33 \|\|

*darśanāttasya khātasya kṛtakṛtyo'bhijāyate \|*  
*tatraiva lalitā devī vartate lokaśarmadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ye cā tāṃ pūjayiṣanti tasminsthāne sthitāḥ svayam \|*  
*teṣāṃ sā vividhānbhogānsampradāsyati mānade \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. By seeing that pond, one has his objects achieved: Goddess Lalita stays there and she bestows happiness on the people. Those who stay in that spot and worship her are given various pleasures by her, О bestower of honour.

## \|\| 2.49.34 \|\|

*jāgaraṃ ye tu tasyāśca puraḥ kurvaṃti dīpakaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sā hyakṣayān lokān vitariṣyati mohini \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О Mohini, she confers the imperishable worlds upon those persons who keep awake with lamps in front of her.

## \|\| 2.49.35 \|\|

*ālayaṃ ye prakurvaṃti bhūmiṃ sammārjayanti ca \|*  
*teṣāmaṣṭasahasrasya suvarṇasya phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Those who erect temples for her, those who sweep the ground thereof shall have the charitable gift of eight thousand gold pieces.

## \|\| 2.49.36 \|\|

*tāmuddiśya tu yo devi brāhmaṇānvedapāragān \|*  
*bhojayiṣyati miṣṭhānnaistasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Listen to the meritorious benefit of the person, who, О gentle lady, feeds those Brahmanas who are masters of the Vedas, with sweet cooked rice for the sake of the deity.

## \|\| 2.49.37 \|\|

*durgāloke vasetkalpamihaivāgacchate punaḥ \|*  
*naro vā yadi vā nārī sarvabhogasamanvitau \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Whether the devotee is a man or a woman, he will be blessed with all worldly pleasures. He will reside in the world of Durga for the period of a Kalpa and thereafter he will come here again.

## \|\| 2.49.38 \|\|

*dhanadhānyasamāyuktau jāyete mahatāṃ kule \|*  
*subhagau darśanīyau ca rūpayauvanagarvitau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The couples will be endowed with plenty of wealth and food grains. They will be born in the family of great persons. They will be fortunate, comely in features and proud, thanks to their beauty and youth.

## \|\| 2.49.39-42 \|\|

*bhavetāmīdṛśau devi sarvasaukhyasya bhājanau \|*  
*mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya vidyutsampātacañcalam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yena sā lalitā dṛṣṭā tasya janmabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*pṛthvīpradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ lalitāyāśca vārāṇasyāṃ pradarśanāt \|*  
*māsi māsi caturthyāṃ tu tasminkāla upoṣitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*arcayitvā tu tāṃ devīṃ jāgaraṃ tatra kārayet \|*  
*tasyārddhiḥ sakalā devi trailokyasyāpi pūjitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-40a. О gentle lady, they will be like this: — They will be the object of all pleasures. Whence is the fear of rebirth to that person who, after attaining the rare human birth as fickle as the fall of lightning, visits Lalita?

40b-41a. By seeing Lalita at Varanasi, the man attains the same benefit as one derives after circumambulating the earth.

41b-42. The devotee should observe fast on the fourth day in every month. He should then worship that goddess and keep awake during the night. О gentle lady, he gains prosperity of the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.49.43 \|\|

*nalakūbarakeśānaṃ taṃ ca sampūjya mohini \|*  
*sarvasiddhipradātāraṃ kṛtakṛtyo naro bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Mohini, after worshipping the praiseworthy Nalaktibarakesana who is the bestower of all Siddhis, the man shall have all his objects accomplished.

## \|\| 2.49.44 \|\|

*tasyaiva dakṣiṇe devi maṇikarṇīti ca śrutam \|*  
*tasya cāgre mahattīrthaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О gentle lady, to the south of it is the holy centre Manikarnl. There is a great Tirtha in front of it. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.49.45 \|\|

*maṇikarṇīśvaraṃ devaṃ kuṇḍamadhye vyavasthitam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā natvā samabhyarcya na bhūyo jaṭhare vaset \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By seeing lord Manikarnisvara1 abiding in the Kunda (the holy pool), by bowing down and then by worshipping him, one shall cease to stay in a belly once again (i.c. one is liberated from Sariisara).

## \|\| 2.49.46 \|\|

*tasya dakṣiṇapārśve tu gaṅgāyāṃ sthāpitaṃ param \|*  
*gaṅgeśvaraṃ samabhyarcya suralokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. By worshipping the great Gangesvara who is installed in the Ganga to his southern side, the devotee shall attain the world of gods (Svarga).

## \|\| 2.49.47 \|\|

*anyadāyatanaṃ vakṣye vārāṇasyāṃ sumohini \|*  
*yatra vai devadevasya ruciraṃ sthānamīpsitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Mohini, I shall describe another shrine at Varanasi. The beautiful spot dear to the lord of the Devas is there.

## \|\| 2.49.48 \|\|

*nīyamānaṃ purā liṅgaṃ subhage śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*rākṣasairantarikṣarsthvrajamānaiśca satvaram \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Once, О blessed lady, the Linga of the moon-crested lord was being taken away by Raksasas who were moving speedily through the sky.1 2

## \|\| 2.49.49 \|\|

*asmindeśe yadā prāptaṃ tadā devena ciṃtitam \|*  
*avimuktaviyogastu kathaṃ me na bhavediti \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When they reached this place, the lord thought — “How will it be possible for me to avoid being separated from the spot of Avimukta?

## \|\| 2.49.50 \|\|

*imamarthaṃ tu deveśo yāvaccintayate śubhe \|*  
*tāvatkukkuṭaśabdastu tasminsthāne babhūva ha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О auspicious lady, even as the lord of the Devas was thinking about this, a cock crew there. (There arose the crowing sound of a cock.)

## \|\| 2.49.51 \|\|

*śabdaṃ śrutvā tu taṃ devi rākṣasāstrastacetasaḥ \|*  
*liṅgamutsṛjya tatraiva prabhātasamaye gatāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О gentle lady, on hearing that sound, the Raksasas became mentally afraid. They abandoned the Liiiga there itself, at the time of the early dawn, and fled away.

## \|\| 2.49.52-53 \|\|

*gateṣu rākṣaseṣvevaṃ liṅgaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitam \|*  
*sthāne'tirucire śubhre devadevaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*avimukte tatra madhye avimuktataraṃ smṛtam \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. When the Raksasas ran away thus, the Linga remained lying there in an extremely beautiful spot. О beautiful lady, the lord of the Devas himself reappeared in the middle of Avimukta. Hence the place is known to be superior to (other places).

## \|\| 2.49.54 \|\|

*tadā vimukteti surairharasya nāma smṛtaṃ puṇyatamākṣarāḍhyam \|*  
*mokṣapradaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ ye prāṇinaḥ pañcatāṃ yāṃti tatra \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then the name Нага was remembered by the Devas as Avimukta consisting of the most sacred syllables. Avimukta is the bestower of salvation on mobile and immobile beings, particularly on those living beings who die there.

## \|\| 2.49.55 \|\|

*kukkuṭāścāpi subhage tasminsthāne sthitāḥ sadā \|*  
*adyāpi tatra dṛśyante pūjyamānāḥ śubhātmabhiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О blessed lady, cocks had always been there in that holy spot. Even today they are seen there being worshipped by auspicious souls.

## \|\| 2.49.56 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ sadā devi yaṃ śrayedīkṣayā naraḥ \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛttiḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. О gentle lady, the man who always resorts to it and observes it with his eyes is not reborn even in the course of hundreds and crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 2.49.57 \|\|

*devasya dakṣiṇe bhāge vāpī tiṣṭhati śobhanā \|*  
*tasyāstathodakaṃ pītvā nāvṛttiḥ punaratra ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. To the south of the lord, there is a splendid tank. If one drinks its water there is no return to the world here.

## \|\| 2.49.58-64 \|\|

*trīṇi liṅgāni vartante hṛdaye puruṣasya tu \|*  
*tathā yaistajjalaṃ pītaṃ te kṛtārthāstu mānavāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu tārakaṃ jñānamastyeveti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*vāpījale naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā daṇḍakanāmakam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā kaivalyaṃ labhate kṣaṇāt \|*  
*tatra sandhyāmupāsitvā brāhmaṇaḥ sakṛdeva tu \|\| 60 \|\|*

*pañcaṣaṣṭisamāḥ saṃdhyā tena copāsitā bhavet \|*  
*purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ tāṃ tu śmaśānaṃ cāvimuktakam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*avimukteśvaraṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā gaṇapatirbhavet \|*  
*avimukteśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvaiva mānavaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sadyaḥ pāpaistathā rogaiḥ paśupāśairvimucyate \|*  
*avimuktasya cāgre tu liṅgaṃ paścānmukhaṃ sthitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ ca te bhadre nāmnā vai lakṣaṇeśvaram \|*  
*tena vai dṛṣṭamātreṇa jñānavān jāyate naraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

58-59a. There are three Lingas in the hearts of man. Those men by whom the waters of that pool are drunk get their desires accomplished. There is no doubt about this that these persons possess perfect knowledge which redeems them.

59b-60a. By taking bath in the waters of the tank, by seeing the deity named Dandaka and by visiting Avimukta thereafter, one attains Kaivalya (salvation) instantaneously.

60b-61a. If a Brahmana performs the Sandhya rites there even once, it is as good as performing the Sandhya rites for sixty five years.

61b-62a. By visiting the city of Varanasi (also known as) the cremation ground (Smasana) Avimuktaka, and the lord of Avimukta one becomes the lord of the Ganas.

62b-63a. By seeing the Linga Avimuktcsvara,1 the man is immediately liberated from sins, ailments and bondages with which jlvas are fettered.

63b-64. In front of Avimukta, there is a Linga stationed there facing the West. О gentle lady, it is called Laksanesvara. If a man sees Avimukta and Laksanesvara he immediately becomes one possessing perfect spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 2.49.65 \|\|

*tasya cottarato devi liṅgaṃ caiva caturmukham \|*  
*caturtheśvaranāmedaṃ pāpabhīmocanaṃ param \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. To the north of it, О gentle lady, there is a fourfaced Linga. It is named Caturthesvara. It is excessively destructive of sins and fears.

## \|\| 2.49.66 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ vārāṇasīnāma muktidaṃ prāṇināṃ bhuvi \|*  
*avimukteśvaraṃ tatra jīvanmuktaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. To all living beings in the world the holy centre Varanasi is the bestower of salvation. But the Linga Avimuk- tesvara there is glorified as Jivanmukta (i.e. which bestows upon devotees liberation even while they are alive).

## \|\| 2.49.67 \|\|

*yatra tatra sthitasyāpi gāṇapatyaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*prāṇāṃstu tatra santyajya muktimātyantikīṃ vrajet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If a man stays anywhere there, the lordship of Ganas is ordained in respect of him. By abandoning the vital breaths there, one shall attain the ultimate salvation.

## \|\| 2.49.68 \|\|

*etadabhyantare kṣetre prathamāvaraṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tathā dvitīyāvaraṇe prācyāṃ tu maṇikarṇikā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The first Avarana (enclosure) is remembered to be the area within the above limits. In the second Avarana (enclosure) the Manikarnika is to the east.

## \|\| 2.49.69 \|\|

*saptakoṭyastu liṅgāni tatra sthāne sthitāni hi \|*  
*teṣāṃ darśanamātreṇa yajñānāṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. There are seven crores of Lingas abiding in that spot. Merely by seeing them one shall attain the benefit of (performing) Yajnas.

## \|\| 2.49.70 \|\|

*etāni siddhaliṅgāni kūpāḥ puṇyāstasthā hradāḥ \|*  
*vāpyo nadyo'tha kaṃṇḍāni tathā te'pi prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. These are Siddha (self-manifested?) Lingas. (In Kasi) all wells, tanks, ponds, rivers and pools — all of them are glorified as sacred.

## \|\| 2.49.71 \|\|

*eteṣu caiva yaḥ snānaṃ kariṣyati samāhitaḥ \|*  
*liṅgāni sparśayitvā ca saṃsāre na viśetpunaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A person who will take bath in these with concentrated mind and touch the Lingas (while bowing, worshipping etc.) will never re-enter Samsara again.

## \|\| 2.49.72 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni hyantarikṣe ca yāni tu \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye tu mukhyāni kīrtitāni mayā hi te \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. All the important holy centres that are on the Earth and in the firmament have been recounted to yon by me.

## \|\| 2.49.73 \|\|

*tīrthayātrā varārohe kathitā pāpanāśinī \|*  
*yena caiṣā kṛtā dṛṣṭā so'pi vai muktibhāgbhavet \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. О fair lady, the pilgrimage to the holy centres, that is destructive of sins, has been described by me. He who undertakes the pilgrimage and he who sees him attains salvation.

## \|\| 2.49.74 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ tu suśroṇi madhyamāvaraṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*etattu kaṇṭakaṃ nāma mṛtyukāle'mṛtapradam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. О lady of beautiful hips, Avimukta is the splendid middle Avarana (enclosure). This is named Kantaka too. At the time of death it is the bestower of final liberation from samsara.

## Chapter 50. The Glory of Кsshi

## \|\| 2.50.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yātrākālaṃ tu mohini \|*  
*devādyaistu kṛtā yā tu yathāyogyaphalāptidā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu Said: —

1\. Henceforth, О Mohini, I shall recount the proper time for the Yatra (pilgrimage) which has been undertaken by the Devas and others1 and which yields befitting benefits.

## \|\| 2.50.2 \|\|

*caitramāse tu divijairyātreyaṃ vihitā purā \|*  
*tatrasthaiḥ kāmakuṇḍe tu snānapūjanatatparaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly, in the month of Chaitra, this pilgrimage was performed by the heaven-born gods staying there at Kamakura. They were exclusively and devotedly engaged in performing ablutions and worship.

## \|\| 2.50.3 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāse tu vai siddhaiḥ kṛtā yātrā śubhānane \|*  
*rudrā vāsasya kuṇḍe tu snānapūjāparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the month of Jyestha, О splendid-faced lady, the pilgrimage was undertaken by the Siddhas devotedly engaged in the performance of religious bath and worship in the Rudra vasa Kunda(pool) which was the residence of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.50.4 \|\|

*āṣāḍhe cāpi gandharvairyātreyaṃ vihitā śubhaiḥ \|*  
*priyādevyāstu kuṇḍe vai snānapūjanakārakaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the month of Asatfha, the pilgrimage was carried out by the auspicious Gandharvas who performed their ablution and worship in the Kunda of goddess Priyadevl.

## \|\| 2.50.5 \|\|

*vidyādharaistu yātreyaṃ śrāvaṇe māsi mohini \|*  
*lakṣmīkuṇḍasthitaiścīrṇā snānārcanaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О MohinI, in the month of Sravana this pilgrimage was performed by the Vidyadharas who stayed near Laksmi- Kunda and who were devoutly engaged in the performance of ablution therein and the worship of the deity.

## \|\| 2.50.6 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyahradasthaistu snānapūjanatatparaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtā yakṣaistu yātreyamiṣamāse varānane \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О fair-faced lady, in the month of Asvina this pilgrimage was undertaken by Yaksas who, stationed at the deep pool of Markandeya were engaged in the worship and ablution therein.

## \|\| 2.50.7 \|\|

*pannagaiścaiva yātreyaṃ mārgamāse tu mohini \|*  
*koṭitīrthasthitaiścīrṇā snānapūjāvidhāyakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О MohinI, in the month of Margaslrsa, this pilgrimage was performed by the Pannagas (serpents) who stayed at the Kotitlrthas and performed ablutions and worship.

## \|\| 2.50.8 \|\|

*kapālamocanasthaistu guhyakaiḥ śubhalocane \|*  
*pauṣe māsi kṛtā yātrā snānadhyānārcanānvitaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О splendid-eyed lady, in the month of Pausa this pilgrimage was undertaken by the Guhyakas stationed at Kapala- mocana (kunda) and were engaged in the regular practice of ablution, meditation and worship.

## \|\| 2.50.9 \|\|

*kāleśvarākhyakuṇḍasthaiḥ phālgune māsi śobhane \|*  
*piśācaistu kṛtā yātrā snānapūjāditatparaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О splendid lady, in the month of Phalguna this pilgrimage was undertaken by the Pisacas stationed at the Kunda (pool) Kalegvara who were devoutly engaged in ablution, worship etc.

## \|\| 2.50.10 \|\|

*phālgune tu śubhe māse site yā tu caturdaśī \|*  
*tena sā procyate devi piśācīnāma viśrutā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence, О gentle lady it is well-known that the fourteenth day in the bright half of the auspicious month of Phalguna is called “PiSacI (CaturdasI)”.

## \|\| 2.50.11 \|\|

*atha te sampravakṣyāmi yātrākṛtyaṃ śubhānane \|*  
*kṛtena yena manujo yātrāphalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Henceforth, О splendid-faced lady, I shall tell you the duties and procedure in respect of the pilgrimage, by performing which the man shall attain the full benefit of pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.50.12 \|\|

*udakumbhāstu dātavyā miṣṭānnena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*phalapuṣpasamopetā vastraiḥ sañchāditāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Waterpots should be given as gifts accompanied with sweet-cooked rice. They should be beautiful and be covered with cloths and be presented alongwith fruits and flowers.

## \|\| 2.50.13 \|\|

*caitrasya śuklapakṣe tu tṛtīyā yā mahāphalā \|*  
*tatra gaurī tu dra ṣṭavyā bhaktibhāvena mānavaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The third day in the bright half of the month of Chaitra is highly fruitful. On that day, Gauri must be visited by men with devotional feelings.

## \|\| 2.50.14 \|\|

*snānaṃ kṛtvā tu gantavyaṃ goprekṣe tu varānane \|*  
*svardvāri kālikādevī arcitavyā prayatnataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О fair-faced lady, after taking bath the devotee should go to the holy centre Gopreksha. At Svargadvara (heavenly portals) Kalikadevi should be assiduously worshipped.

## \|\| 2.50.15 \|\|

*anyā cāpi parā proktā saṃvartā lalitā śubhā \|*  
*dra ṣṭavyā caiva sā bhaktyā sarvakāmaphalapradā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Another deity is also mentioned to be very great. She is Samvarta, the auspicious Lalita. She should be visited with devotion. She is the bestower of all desired benefit.

## \|\| 2.50.16 \|\|

*tatastu bhojayedviprāñchivabhaktāñchucivratān \|*  
*vāsobhirddakṣiṇābhiśca puṣkalābhiryathārhataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, he (the pilgrim) should feed Brahmana devotees of Siva who are observers of pure vows, and offer them clothes and sumptuous monetary gifts of befitting nature.

## \|\| 2.50.17 \|\|

*pañcagaurīḥ samuddiśya rasān gandhāndvije'payet \|*  
*uttamaṃ śreya āpnoti saubhāgyena samanvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With Райса-Gaurls in view the devotee shall dedicate tasty juices and sweet scents to a Brahmana. He will obtain excellent and great welfare and be endowed with good fortune.

## \|\| 2.50.18 \|\|

*vināyakānpravakṣyāmi kṣetrāvāse tu vighnadān \|*  
*yānsaṃpūjya naro devi nirvighnena phalaṃ labhet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I shall now mention the Vinayakas, the creators of obstacles and troubles in the residence of holy centre Kasi. О gentle lady, by worshipping them, a man attains benefit without any hindrance.

## \|\| 2.50.19-20 \|\|

*ḍhuṇḍhiṃ tu prathamaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā kilavināyakam \|*  
*devyā vināyakaṃ caiva goprekṣaṃ hastihastinaṃm \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vināyakaṃ tathaivānyaṃ sindūryaṃ nāma viśrutam \|*  
*caturthyāṃ devi dra ṣṭavyā evaṃ caiva vināyakāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Having visited Dhundhi-Vinayaka first (one should next visit) Kila-Vinayaka, Devi-Vinayaka, Go-preksya Vinayaka, Hasti-hasti-Vinayaka and lastly the famous Sindurya Vinayaka. О queen, all these Vinayakas be visited on the Caturthi (fourth Lunar) day.1

## \|\| 2.50.21 \|\|

*laḍḍukāśca pradātavyā etānuddiśya vāḍave \|*  
*etena caiva kṛtyena siddhimāñjāyate naraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With these (Vinayakas) in view, sweet-meats (sweet- balls) should be given to a Brahmana. When this duty is performed the man realises Siddhi (accomplishment of his desire)

## \|\| 2.50.22 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi caṇḍikāḥ kṣetrarakṣikāḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇe rakṣate durgā nairṛte cāntareśvarī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Henceforth, I shall enumerate the Candidas1 2 who protect the holy place (Kasi). Durga protects in the south; Antaresvarl protects in the south-west.

## \|\| 2.50.23-24 \|\|

*aṅgāreśī paścime tu vāyavye bhadra kālikā \|*  
*uttare bhīmacaṇḍā ca mahāmattā tathaiśake \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ūrddhvakeśī samāyuktā śāṅkarī pūrvataḥ smṛtā \|*  
*adhaḥkeśī tathāgneyyāṃ citraghaṇṭā ca madhyataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. AngaresI protects in the west; Bhadrakalika in the north-west; Bhimacanda in the north; Mahamatta in the north-east, Sankari accompanied by DrdhvakesI in the east, AdhahkeSi in the south-east and Citraghanta in the middle.

## \|\| 2.50.25 \|\|

*etāstu caṇḍikādevīryo vai paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭāśca tāḥ sarvāḥ kṣetraṃ rakṣaṃti tatparāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. These goddesses (Candikas) when visited by men become delighted with them. All of them eagerly protect the holy place.

## \|\| 2.50.26 \|\|

*vighnaṃ kurvaṃti satataṃ pāpināṃ devi sarvadā \|*  
*tasmāddevyaḥ sadā pūjyā rakṣārthe savināyakāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О gentle lady, they continuously create obstacles for sinners. Hence, for the sake of protection, the goddesses should always be worshipped along with the Vinayakas.

## \|\| 2.50.27 \|\|

*yadīcchetparamāṃ siddhiṃ santatiṃ vibhavaṃ sukham \|*  
*tato bhaktyā gandhapuṣpanaivedyādīnsamarppayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If one wishes for the greatest Siddhi, progeny, prosperity and happiness, one must offer scents, fragrant flowers, Naivedyas etc. with devotion.

## \|\| 2.50.28 \|\|

*anyacca te pravakṣyāmi tasminsthāne sulocane \|*  
*tisro nadyastu tatrasthā vanhati ca śubhodakāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О lady of beautiful eyes, I shall recount to you another thing in that holy spot (city). There are three rivers flowing there with splendid waters.

## \|\| 2.50.29-31 \|\|

*tāsāṃ darśanamātreṇa brahmahatyā nivartate \|*  
*ekā tu tatra trisrotā tathā mandākinī parā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*matsyodarī tṛtīyā ca etāstisrastu puṇyadāḥ \|*  
*maṃdākinī tatra puṇyā madhyameśvarasaṃsthitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saṃsthitā trisrotikā ca avimukteti puṇyadā \|*  
*matsyodarī tu oṃkāre puṇyadā sarvadaiva hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Merely by seeing them the sin of the murder of a Brahmana recedes. The first of these is Trisrota (the three- currented). The next one is MandakinI and the third is Matsyodari. These three bestow merits. Among them Manda- kini is highly meritorious. It is stationed in Madhyamesvara. Trisrota that exceedingly bestows merit, flows in Avimukta; Matsyodari is stationed at Oriikara; it is always the bestower of merit.

## \|\| 2.50.32 \|\|

*tasminsthāne yadā gaṅgā āgamiṣyati mohinī \|*  
*tadā puṇyatamaḥ kālo devānāmapi durlabhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. О MohinI, the time when the Ganga flows into that holy spot is extremely meritorious. It is difficult even to the Devas to get its advantage.

## \|\| 2.50.33 \|\|

*varaṇāsiktasalile jāhnavījalaviplute \|*  
*tatra nādeśvare puṇye snātaḥ kimanuśocati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Will anybody bewail if he takes bath in the meritorious (holy centre) Nadesvara sprinkled with the waters of Jahnavi? (No).

## \|\| 2.50.34 \|\|

*matsyodarīsamāyuktā yadā gaṅgā babhūva ha \|*  
*tasminkāle śivaḥ snānātkapālaṃ muktavāñchubhe \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О auspicious lady, Siva got rid of the skull by bathing in it at a time when the Ganga got mingled with the Matsyodari.

## \|\| 2.50.35 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ nāma tatraiva sumahatsaraḥ \|*  
*pāvanaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ puṇyadaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The great lake named Kapalamocana is there itself. It is glorified as sanctifying of all living beings. It bestows merit on them.

## \|\| 2.50.36-37 \|\|

*matsyodarījale gaṅgā oṃkāreśvarasannidhau \|*  
*tadā tasmiñjale snātvā dṛṣṭvā coṅkāramīśvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śokaṃ jarāṃ mṛtyubandhaṃ tato na spṛśate naraḥ \|*  
*tasminsnātaḥ śivaḥ sākṣādoṅkāreśvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The Ganga gets mixed with the waters of the Matsyodari near Omkaresvara. If at that time a man takes bath in its waters and visits lord Oriikara, he is not contaminated by grief, old age and the bondage of death. One who takes bath therein himself becomes that deity, called OriikareSvara.

## \|\| 2.50.38-39 \|\|

*etadra hasyamākhyātaṃ tava snehādvarānane \|*  
*akāraṃ cāpyukaraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prakīrtitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*akārastatra vijñeyo viṣṇulokagatipradaḥ \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇapārśve tu ukāraḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. О fair-faced lady, out of affection for you, this esoteric secret has been communicated to you.1 The (constituents) there are Akara (letter shA’) Ukara (letter CU’) and Makara (letter shM’). The letter ‘A’should be known as the bestower of the goal of Visnu’s world. The letter ‘U is reputed to be on its southern side.

## \|\| 2.50.40 \|\|

*tatra siddhiṃ parāṃ prāpto devācāryo bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ tatra vijñeyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ padamavyayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Brhaspati the preceptor of the Devas attained great Siddhi there. Oriikara should be known as the unchanging region of Brahman.

## \|\| 2.50.41 \|\|

*tayostathottare bhāge makāraṃ viṣṇusaṃjñitam \|*  
*tasmim̐ lliṅge tu saṃsiddhaḥ kapilarṣirmahāmuniḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. To the north side of both of them is the letter ‘M termed as Visnu’s syllable. Sage Kapila, the great ascetic achieved Siddhi at that Liriga.

## \|\| 2.50.42 \|\|

*vārāṇasīmabhyupetya pañcāyatanamuttamam \|*  
*ārādhyamāno deveśaṃ bhīṣmastatra sthito'bhavat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After coming to Varanasi, Bhisma stayed there, worshipping the lord of the Devas, the excellent Paftcayatana (five-aboded Siva).

## \|\| 2.50.43 \|\|

*tasminsthāne tu subhage svayamāvirabhūcchivaḥ \|*  
*goprekṣaka iti khyātaḥ saṃstutaḥ sarvadaivataiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In that highly hallowed spot, Siva manifested himself. He is well-known as Gopreksaka. He is eulogised by all the deities.

## \|\| 2.50.44 \|\|

*goprekṣeśvaramāgatya dṛṣṭvābhyarcya ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*na durgatimavāpnoti kalmaṣaiśca vimucyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After approaching, visiting and worshipping Gopre- ksesvara, a man never attains wretchedness. He is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.50.45 \|\|

*vanasthā dahyamānāstu surabhyo dāvavahninā \|*  
*bhramantyo'sminhrade'bhyetya śāntāstoyaṃ papustadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The cows staying in the forests and wandering about on being scorched by the forest-fire approached this deep pool of water and became calm. They drank water then.

## \|\| 2.50.46 \|\|

*kapilāhrada ityevaṃ tataḥ prabhṛti kathyate \|*  
*tatrāpi sa śivaḥ sākṣādvṛṣadhvaja iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Ever since then, this came to be called Kapilahrada (the Pool of Kapila cows.) There also Siva (who manifested himself) is as Vrsabha-dhvaja (bull-emblemed one).

## \|\| 2.50.47-50 \|\|

*sānnidhyaṃ kṛtavāndevo dṛśyamānaḥ sadā sthitaḥ \|*  
*kapilāhradatīrthe'sminsnātvā saṃyatamānasaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vṛṣadhvajaṃ śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*svarlokatāṃ mṛtastatra pūjayitvā śivo bhavet \|\| 48 \|\|*

*labhate dehabhedena gaṇatvaṃ cātidurlabham \|*  
*asminneva pradeśe tu gāvo vai brahmaṇā svayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śāntyarthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ sarvānpāvayituṃ dhruvam \|*  
*bhadra dohaṃ sarastatra puṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-49a. The lord always maintains his presence there and is always seen at that place. By taking bath in this holy Tirtha of Kapilahrada, and by visiting the bull-emblemed Siva, the devotee of well-controlled mind shall attain the benefit of all the Yajnas. On dying there, he attains the heavenly world. By worshipping Siva he becomes Siva himself. With a different physical body, he attains Gana-hood which is very difficult to attain.

49b-50. In this spot itself, cows were retained by Brahma himself for peace in all the worlds and certainly to sanctify all. (It is from their milk that) the holy splendid lake Bhadradoha is created there. It is holy and destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.50.51 \|\|

*tasminsthāne naraḥ snātaḥ sākṣādvāgīśvaro bhavet \|*  
*śivastatra samānīya sthāpitaḥ parameṣṭhinā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A man who takes bath in that spot (Tirtha^ shall himself become the lord of speech. Siva was brought there and installed by Paramesthin (god Brahma).

## \|\| 2.50.52 \|\|

*brahmaṇaścāpi saṅgṛhya viṣṇunā sthāpitaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbha ityevaṃ nāmnā tatra sthitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Collecting it from Brahma, another Linga was installed by Visnu. Siva then remained there by the name Hiranyagarbha.

## \|\| 2.50.53 \|\|

*punaścāpi tato brahmā svarlokeśvarasaṃjñakam \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa vai liṅgaṃ svarlīlaṃ kāraṇe kvacit \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thereafter, again, Brahma installed a Linga which was named Svarlokesvara (lord of heavenly world) which exhibited the divine heavenly sports at times.

## \|\| 2.50.54 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vai taṃ tu deveśaṃ śivaloke mahīyate \|*  
*prāṇāniha punastyaktvā na punarjāyate kvacit \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. By visiting that lord of the Devas, the devotee is honoured in Siva’s world. By abandoning the vital breath here, the devotee is not born again anywhere.

## \|\| 2.50.55-56 \|\|

*anantā sā gatistasya yogināmeva yā smṛtā \|*  
*asminneva mahīdeśe daityo daivatakaṇṭakaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vyāghrarūpaṃ samāsthāya nihato darpito balī \|*  
*vyāghreśvara iti khyāto nityaṃ tatra samāsthitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. His state becomes eternal which is the same as in the case of Yogins. In this very same part of the earth, a certain Daitya, the thorn to the deities, had assumed the form of a tiger. This proud and strong Daitya was killed (by the lord), who became famous as Vyaghresvara.1 He abides here continuously.

## \|\| 2.50.57-59 \|\|

*na punardurgatiṃ yāti dṛṣṭvainamamareśvaram \|*  
*himavatsthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ śaileśvaramiti sthitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvaitanmanujo bhadre na durgatimavāpnuyāt \|*  
*utpalo vidalaścaiva yau daityau brahmaṇo varāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

*strīlaulyāddarpitau dṛṣṭvā pārvatyā nihatāvubhau \|*  
*sāraṅgaṃ kantukenātra tasyedaṃ cihnamāsthitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-58a. By visiting this lord of the immortals, the devotee never faces wretchedness. The Linga that is installed by the mountain Himalaya is stationed (and known as) Saile- svara. О gentle lady, by visiting this no man will ever attain wretchedness.

58b-59. There were two Daityas Utpala and Vidala. As a result of the boon granted by Brahma, they became arrogant. Seeing that they became indulgent to women out of lustfulness, Parvati killed them with bow and with a spear. As a memento of it, this Linga has been established.

## \|\| 2.50.60 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaitanmanujo liṅgaṃ jyeṣṭhasthānaṃ samāśritam \|*  
*na śocati punarbhadre siddho janmani janmani \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. By visiting this Linga that has occupied the most important spot, no man is subjected to grief. О gentle lady, he becomes a Siddha in every one of his births.

## \|\| 2.50.61 \|\|

*samantāttasya devaistu liṅgāni sthāpitāni ca \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca tāni vai martyo dehabhede gaṇo bhavet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All round it, Lingas were installed by the Devas. By visiting there a man shall become a Gana with a different body assuming a new form after death.

## \|\| 2.50.62-63 \|\|

*nadī vārāṇasī ceyaṃ puṇyā pāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*kṣetrametadalaṅkṛtya jāhnavyā saha saṅgatā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sthāpitaṃ saṅgame cāsminbrahmaṇā liṅgamuttamam \|*  
*saṅgameśvaramityeva khyātaṃ jagati dṛśyatām \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. This river Varanasi (combined name for Varana and Asi) is sacred and destructive of sins. After embellishing this holy centre, it meets with the Jahnavl. In this confluence, an excellent Linga was installed by Brahma. It is wellknown in the whole universe as Sahgamesvara. May it be seen.

## \|\| 2.50.64 \|\|

*saṅgame devanadyośca yaḥ snātvā manujaḥ śubhe \|*  
*arcayetsaṅgameśānaṃ tasya janmabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Whence is the fear of a rebirth to that person who takes holy dip, О auspicious lady, in the confluence of the two divine rivers and worships god Sahgamesvara (lord of the confluence).

## \|\| 2.50.65 \|\|

*sthāpitaṃ liṅgametacca śukreṇa bhṛgusūnunā \|*  
*nāmnā śukreśvaraṃ bhadre sarvasiddhāmarārcitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О gentle lady, the Linga installed by Sukra, the son of Bhrigu, is known by the name Sukresvara. It is worshipped by all Siddhas and immortal ones (i.e. gods).

## \|\| 2.50.66 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaitanmānavaḥ sadyo muktaḥ syātsarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|*  
*mṛtaśca na punarjanma saṃsāre labhate naraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. By visiting this (Linga) a man shall immediately be liberated from all sins. After death, the man is never born in the world.

## \|\| 2.50.67 \|\|

*jambuko'tra hato daityo mahādevena mohini \|*  
*talliṅgaṃ tu naro dṛṣṭvā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. О Mohini, Jambuka, a great Daitya was killed here by Mahadcva. By visiting that Linga, a man shall attain all desires.

## \|\| 2.50.68-69 \|\|

*devaiḥ śakrapurogaiśca etāni sthāpitāni hi \|*  
*jānīhi puṇyaliṅgāni sarvakāmapradāni ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*evametāni sarvāṇi śivaliṅgāni mohini \|*  
*kathitāni mayā tubhyaṃ kṣetre'sminnavimuktake \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Know that all these meritorious Lingas were installed by the Devas, the leader of whom was Indra. They bestow all desires. Thus, О Mohini, all these Siva Lingas in the holy place of Avimuktaka have been recounted to you by me.

## Chapter 51. The Greatness of Kasi (concluded)

## \|\| 2.51.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- athānyatte pravakṣyāmi gaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*vārāṇāsīsthitaṃ bhadre bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said: —

1\. Now I shall narrate to you the excellent glory of the Ganga as it flows through Varanasi. It yields worldly pleasure as well as Liberation from Samsara after death.

## \|\| 2.51.2 \|\|

*avimukte kṛtaṃ yattu tadevākṣayatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*avimuktagataḥ kaścinnarakaṃ naiti kilbiṣī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Whatever meritorious deed is performed in Avi- mukta shall attain everlasting benefit. No sinner, after going to Avimukta, falls into the hell.

## \|\| 2.51.3-9 \|\|

*avimuktakṛtaṃ yattu pāpaṃ vajraṃ bhavecchubhe \|*  
*trailokye yāni tīrthāni mokṣadāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sevaṃte satataṃ gaṅgāṃ kāśyāmuttaravāhinīm \|*  
*daśāśvamedhe yaḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā viśveśvaraṃ śivam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sadyo niṣpātako bhūtvā mucyate bhavabandhanāt \|*  
*gaṅgā hi sarvataḥ puṇyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vārāṇasyāṃ viśeṣeṇa yatra cottaravāhinī \|*  
*varaṇāyāstathāsyāśca jāhnavyāḥ saṅgame naraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*snānamātreṇa sarvebhyaḥ pātakebhyaḥ pramucyate \|*  
*kāśyāmuttaravāhinyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ kārtike tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*snātvā māghe ca mucyante mahāpāpādipātakaiḥ \|*  
*sarvalokeṣu tīrthāni yāni khyātāni tāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvāṇyetāni subhage kāśyāmāyāṃti jāhnavīm \|*  
*nityaṃ parvasu sarveṣu puṇyaiścāyatanaiḥ saha \|\| 9 \|\|*

3-4a. О auspicious lady, the sin that is committed at Avimukta shall remain adamantine.1 All the salvation-yielding Tirthas in the three worlds, all of them entirely resort to the Ganga which flows towards the north at Kasi.

4b-6a. He who takes bath, at Dasasvamedha and visits Siva, Visvesvara (Lord of the universe) shall immediately become free from sins and is liberated from worldly ties. Everywhere the Ganga is holy and dispeller of the sin of murder of a Brahmana. Especially it is so at Varanasi where (the Ganga) flows towards the north.

6b-7a. Merely by taking bath at the confluence of Varana, Asl and Jahnavl, a man is liberated from all sins.

7b-8a. By taking the holy dip in the Ganga that flows towards the north at Kasi, in the months of Karttika as well as Magha, men are liberated from Mahapatakas (great sins) and other evils.

8b-9. О highly blessed lady, the well-known Tirthas in all the worlds come always to the Jahnavl at Kasi at the time of Parvans (holy occasions) alongwith the holy shrines.

## \|\| 2.51.10-14 \|\|

*uttarābhimukhīṃ gaṅgāṃ kāśyāmāyāṃti cānvaham \|*  
*mahāpātakadoṣādiduṣṭānāṃ sparśanodbhavam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vyapohituṃ svapāpaṃ ca jantupāpavimuktaye \|*  
*janmāntaraśatenāpi satkarmaniratasya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anyatra sudhiyā bhadre mokṣo labhyeta vā na vā \|*  
*ekena janmanā tvatra gaṅgāyāṃ maraṇena ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mokṣastu labhyate kāśyāṃ nareṇāvalitātmanā \|*  
*khyāto dharmanado nāma hradastatraiva sundari \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dharma eva svarūpeṇa mahāpātakanāśanaḥ \|*  
*dhūlī ca dhūtapāpā sā sarvatīrthamayī śubhā \|\| 14 \|\|*

10-11a. It is to wipe off their own sins originating from their contact with persons defiled by the defects of great sins, that they go everyday to the Ganga that flows towards the north at Kasi. The waters of Ganga are conducive to liberation from all sorts of sins.

11b-13a. О gentle lady, salvation may or may not be obtained in the course of a hundred births by an intelligent devotee who is engaged in holy rites in other holy centres. But here, by the death in the Ganga at Kasi, salvation is attained in the course of a single birth by a man whose Atman is not turned round (to the good path?).

13b-14. О beautiful lady, a deep pool named Dharma- nada is famous there itself. Dliarma (piety) stands embodied there and destroys great sins. The dust thereof purges all sins. It is auspicious and it consists of all Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.51.15-16 \|\|

*harenmahāpāpasaṅghānkūlajāniva pādapān \|*  
*kiraṇā dhūtapāpā ca puṇyatoyā sarasvatī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva pañca nadyaḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ataḥ pañcanadaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The river Dhutapapa shall dispel multitudes of great sins like the tree on its banks. The following five rivers have been glorified: — viz: Kirana, Dhutapfipa, Sarasvati of the holy waters, Ganga and Yamuna. Hence, the holy centre Paftcanada1 (spot of five rivers) has become well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.51.17 \|\|

*tatrāpluto na gṛhṇīyāddehitāṃ pāñcabhautikīm \|*  
*asminpañcanadīnāṃ tu saṅgame'ghaughabhedane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17-I8a. He who plunges into that holy river does not take up the physical body consisting of five elements (i.e. is liberated). Merely by taking bath in this confluence of five rivers, that dispels all sins, a man pierces through the bower of cosmic egg and goes to the Brahman and realises salvation.

## \|\| 2.51.18-32 \|\|

*snānamātrānnaro yāti bhitvā brahmāṇḍamaṇḍapam \|*  
*prayāge māghamāse tu samyak snānasya yatphalam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ syāddinaikena kāśyāṃ pañcanade dhruvam \|*  
*snātvā pañcanade tīrthe kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣṇuṃ mādhavamabhyarcya na bhūyo janmabhāgbhavet \|*  
*yāvatsaṅkhyāstilā dattāḥ pitṛbhyo jalatarpaṇe \|\| 20 \|\|*

*puṇye pañcanade tīrthe tṛptiḥ syāttāvadābdikī \|*  
*śraddhayā yaiḥ kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ tīrthe pañcanade śubhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ pitāmahā muktā nānāyonigatā api \|*  
*yamaloke pitṛgaṇairgātheyaṃ parigīyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mahimānaṃ pāñcanadaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrāddhavidhānataḥ \|*  
*asmākamapi vaṃśyo'tra kaścicchrāddhaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kāśyāṃ pañcanadaṃ prāpya yena mucyāmahe vayam \|*  
*tatra pañcanade tīrthe yakiñciddīyate vasu \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kalpakṣaye'pi na bhavettasya puṇyasya saṃkṣayaḥ \|*  
*vandhyāpi varṣaparyantaṃ snātvā pañcanade hrade \|\| 25 \|\|*

*samarcya maṅgalāṃ gaurīṃ putraṃ janayati dhruvam \|*  
*jalaiḥ pāñcanadaiḥ puṇyairvāsasā pariśodhitaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahāphalamavāpnoti snāpayitveha dikśrutām \|*  
*pañcāmṛtānāṃ kalaśairaṣṭottaraśatonmitaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tulito'dhikatāṃ prāpto binduḥ pāñcanadastu saḥ \|*  
*pañcakūrcena pītena yātrāśuddhirudāhṛtā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sā śuddhiḥ śraddhayā prāśya binduṃ pañcanadāmbhasām \|*  
*bhavedatha hradasnānādrā jasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yatphalaṃ tacchataguṇaṃ smṛtaṃ pañcanadāmbunā \|*  
*rājasūyāśvamedhau ca bhavetāṃ svargasādhane \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ābrahmapaṭṭikādvandvānmuktiḥ pañcanadāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*svarganadyabhiṣeko'pi na tathā sammataḥ satām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*abhiṣekaḥ pāñcanado yathānanyo varapradaḥ \|*  
*śataṃ samāstapastaptvā kṛte yatprāpyate phalam \|\| 32 \|\|*

18b-19a. Certainly, one attains in a single day by a holy dip in the Panchanada at Kasi, the same benefit as is obtained by means of an elaborate bath and ablution at Prayaga throughout the month of Magha.

19b-20a. By taking the holy dip in the Tirtha of Panchanada, by performing the rite of Tarpana for the Pitrs and by worshipping Visnu, the lord of Laksmi, one never takes rebirth.

20b-21a. The satisfaction of the Pitrs lasts for as many years as the number of gingelly seeds offered to the Pitrs in the course of the water-libation in the holy Tlrtha of Paftcanada.

21b-22a. The ancestors of those by whom the Ssaddha rite has been performed in the splendid Tlrtha of Paftcanada with great faith, shall be liberated, though they may have been born in different wombs.

22b-24a. In the world of Yama this song is being sung by the groups of Pitrs. “After seeing the greatness of Panchanada in regard to the performance of Sraddha rites, some-one belonging to our family may perform Sraddha whereby we may be able to go to the Panchanada Tlrtha at Kasi and be liberated”.

24b-26a. If any wealth is given as gift in the holy centre of Panchanada, the merit that accrues to one does not dwindle even after Kalpas pass away. Even a barren lady will certainly give birth to a son if she takes her holy dip in the deep pool of the Panchanada for a whole year and worships Mangala Gauri.

26b-27a. By performing holy ablution of the goddess well-known in all quarters (Dik-Sruta) with the holy waters of the Panchanada filtered by means of the cloth, one attains great benefit.

27b-28a. A drop of the water of the Panchanada was weighed against pots of Panchamrta hundred and eight in number and was found to be superior to it.

28b-29a. By drinking a drop of the waters of Panchanada with great faith, one attains that purity which is said to be acquired when Pancha-gavya is drunk.

29b-32. By taking the holy dip in the waters of the Paftcanada, one attains hundred times the benefit acquired by Rajasuya and Asvamedha sacrifices. The Rajasuya and Asvamedha sacrifices may be the means for attaining heaven, but through the waters of Paftcanada liberation is attained from Dvandva (mutually opposing pairs e.g. Pleasure-Pain) that covers up even the Brahman (i.e. Avidya). Even the ablution with the waters of heavenly river is not so much approved of by good men as that of the Paftcanada. It is the bestower of boons not obtained from others. By taking the holy dip for once in the Paftcanada in the month of Karttika, one derives the same benefit as is obtained by performing penance in the Krta age for a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.51.33-36 \|\|

*tatkārtike pañcanade sakṛtsnānena labhyate \|*  
*iṣṭāpūrteṣu dharmeṣu yāvajjanmakṛteṣu yat \|\| 33 \|\|*

*anyatra syātphalaṃ tasyādhikaṃ pañcanadāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*na dhūtapāpasadṛśaṃ tīrthaṃ kvāpi mahītale \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yadekasnānato naśyedaghaṃ janmatrayārjitam \|*  
*kṛte dharmanadaṃ nāma tretāyāṃ dhūtapātakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dvāpare bindutīrthaṃ ca kalau pañcanadaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*bidutīrthe naro datvā kāñcanaṃ kṛṣṇalonmitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. In the bath through the waters of the Paftcanada, one gets more benefit than is obtained through the holy rites of Istapurta performed in the course of whole life elsewhere. There is no other Tirtha on the whole of the Earth, like Dhiitapapa since, through a single bath therein, the entire sin accumulated in the course of three births perishes. In the Krta age Dharmanada is the holy Tirtha, in the Treta, it is Dhiitapapa; in the Dvapara it is Bindutlrlha and in the Kali it is Paftcanada. By making the gift of gold of the weight of a Guftja-berry in the Bindutirtha, no man shall ever become indigent. He is never devoid of happiness.

## \|\| 2.51.37-40 \|\|

*na daridro bhavetkvāpi na sukhena viyujyate \|*  
*gobhūtilahiraṇyāśvavāso'nnasthānabhūṣaṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yatkiṃñcidbindutīrthe'tra datvākṣayamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*ekāmapyāhutiṃ kṛtvā samiddhe'gnau vidhānataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*puṇye dharmanadītīrthe koṭihomaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*na pañcanadatīrthasya mahimānamanantakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ko'pi varṇayituṃ śaktaścaturvargaśubhaukasaḥ \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ bhadre kāśīmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-38a. By giving anything, whether it is a cow, a plot of land, gingclly seeds, gold, a horse, clothes, cooked rice, position or ornament, in the Bindutirtha, one shall attain an ever lasting benefit.

38b-39a. By offering a single Ahuti in accordance with the injunctions in a well-kindled fire in the holy Tirtha of Dharmanada, one shall attain the benefit of a crore of Hoinas.

39b-40. No one is competent to describe adequately the endless greatness of the Paftcanada Tirtha that is the abode of all splendour of the four-fold aims of life. Thus, О gentle lady, the excellent greatness of Kasi has been recounted to you.

## \|\| 2.51.41-42 \|\|

*sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ nṝṇāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*brahmaghno madhupaḥ svarṇasteyī ca gurutalpagaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*mahāpātakayukto'pi saṃyukto'pyupapātakaiḥ \|*  
*avimuktasya māhātmyaśravaṇācchuddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. It bestows happiness. It bestows salvation on men. It is destructive of sins. Even a Brahmana-slayer, a drink-addict, a thief of gold, a defiler of the preceptor’s bed or a person guilty of principal and subsidiary sins shall attain purity on hearing the greatness of Avimukta.

## \|\| 2.51.43 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo vedavidvānsyātkṣattriyo vijayī raṇe \|*  
*vaiśyo dhanapatiḥ śūdro viṣṇubhaktasamāgamī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A Brahmana shall become a great scholar of the Vedas; a Ksatriya shall be victorious in battle; a Vaisya shall be the lord of wealth and a iSftdra shall be an associate of the devotees of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.51.44-46 \|\|

*śravaṇādasya subhage bhūyātpaṭhanato'pi vā \|*  
*sarvayajñeṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu yatphalam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ samavāpnoti paṭhanācchravaṇādapi \|*  
*vidyārthī labhate vidyāṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bhāryārthī labhate bhāryāṃ sutārthī putramāpnuyāt \|*  
*avimuktasya māhātmyaṃ mayā te parikīrtitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. О blessed lady, by listening to this, by reading this frequently, one attains all those benefits that are mentioned in the case of all Yajnas (sacrifices) and all the merits in the case of all Tirthas. He who seeks learning shall obtain learning. He who seeks wealth shall obtain wealth. He who seeks wife shall get a wife and he who seeks son shall obtain a son. The greatness of Avimukta has been recounted #to you by me.

## \|\| 2.51.47-48 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktāya dātavyaṃ śivabhaktiratāya ca \|*  
*jagajjananibhaktāya sūryaherambasevine \|\| 47 \|\|*

*guruśuśrūṣave datvā tīrthasnānaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*śaṭhāya nindakāyāpi goviprasuravidviṣe \|*  
*gurudruhe'sūyakāya datvā mṛtyumavāpnuyāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. This must be imparted to a devotee of Visnu or to one engaged in devotion to!shiva or to a devotee of the mother of the universe or to one who serves the sun and Vighnesvara. By giving this to a person rendering service to his preceptor, one shall attain the benefit of the holy dip in a Tirtha. By giving this to a rogue, a person who censures, a person who hates Brahmanas, cows, and Devas, a person who is malicious towards the elderly persons or a person who is jealous of them, one may attain death.

## Chapter 52. The Greatness of Purusottama1 (Jagannatha of Puri)

## \|\| 2.52.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- dhanyo'si vipravarya tvaṃ kṛpāluḥ sarvadehiṣu \|*  
*yacchrutaṃ te mukhāmbhojātkāśīmāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Afohini said:

1\. О excellent Brahmin, you are blessed. You are merciful to all embodied beings. (I am blessed) because the excellent greatness of Kasi has been heard from your lotus-like mouth.

## \|\| 2.52.2 \|\|

*adhunāhaṃ kṛtārthāsmi tvayā hi pratibodhitā \|*  
*kṛpālunā nipatitābhyuddhṛtā bhavasāgarāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I feel that I have accomplished my objects in life since now I have been enlightened by you. Although I had fallen into the ocean of worldly existence, I have been redeemed by you, the merciful one.

## \|\| 2.52.3 \|\|

*adhunā śrotumicchāmi hareḥ kṣetrasya mānada \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ yatra gamanātkṛtārtho jāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Now I wish to hear, О besiower of honour, the greatness of a holy place of Hari, by going to which men become contented.

## \|\| 2.52.4 \|\|

*puruṣottamaviṣṇostu kṣetraṃ muktividhāyakam \|*  
*śrūyate hi purāṇeṣu varṇitaṃ munibhirdvijaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*
