4\. It is reported that a holy centre of Visnu, the most excellent among other centres is described in the Puranas by sage and Brahmanas as efficacious in granting Liberation from Samsara.

## \|\| 2.52.5 \|\|

*tatkathyatāṃ mahābhāga śiṣyāhaṃ yadi te priyā \|*  
*sādhavaḥ sarvalokasya satatopakṛtau sthitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. May that be recounted, О blessed one, if I am liked by you as a disciple of yours. Indeed good men are always engaged in rendering continuous service to all the people of the world. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.52.6 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi tubhyaṃ māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*puruṣottamanāmnastu kṣetrasya brahmaṇoditam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О gentle lady, listen. I shall recount to you about the excellent greatness of the holy centre named Purusottama as narrated by god Brahma.

## \|\| 2.52.7-11 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ karmabhūmirudāhṛtā \|*  
*tatrāste bhārate varṣe dakṣiṇodadhitīragaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*utkaleti samākhyātaḥ svargamokṣapradāyakaḥ \|*  
*samudrā duttaraṃ tāvadyāvadvirajamaṇḍalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*deśo'sau puṇyaśīlānāṃ guṇaiḥ sarvairalaṅkṛtaḥ \|*  
*sarvatīrthāni puṇyāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*utkale tu viśālākṣi veditavyāni tāni tu \|*  
*samudra syottare tīre tasmindeśe'khilottame \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āste guhyaṃ paraṃ kṣetraṃ muktidaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*sarvatra vālukākīrṇe pavitraṃ dharmakāmadam \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-8a. In the whole of this earth, Bharata is said to be a Karmabhumi (the land of holy rites). There, in theBharatavarsa, on the shores of the southern sea, is a land known as Utkala. It is the bestower of heaven and Moksa (salvation) on all.

8b-9a. It is to the north of the ocean and it extends upto Virajamandala (a country stretching for ten miles round Jaipur on the river Vaitarnl). This land is embellished with all the attributes of those who are habituated in performing meritorious deeds.

9b-11. О lady of large eyes, it should be known that there are many Tirthas and holy shrines. In Utkala, on the northern shores of the ocean, in that land which is the most excellent of all, there is a great holy centre which yields salvation and dispels sins. It is in a place covered with sand everywhere. It is sacred and it bestows piety and love. A large no. of verses on this fopic are common to the NP and the Brahma Purana (BM. P.), the NP, being presumably the borrower.

## \|\| 2.52.12-26 \|\|

*daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ kṣetraṃ paramadurlabham \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathā somaḥ sarasāṃ sāgaro yathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tathā samastatīrthānāṃ variṣṭhaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*vasūnāṃ pāvako yadvadrudrā ṇāṃ śaṅkaro yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tathā śreṣṭhaṃ hi tīrthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo yadvadvainateyaśca pakṣiṇām \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathā samastatīrthānāṃ variṣṭhaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*senānīnāṃ yathā skandaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo yathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*erāvato gajendrā ṇāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛguryathā \|*  
*meruḥ śikhariṇāṃ yadvannāgānāṃ ca himālayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*uccaiḥśravā yathāśvānāṃ kavīnāmuśanā yathā \|*

*indri yāṇāṃ mano yadvadbhūtānāmavanī yathā \|*

*arundhatī yathā strīṇāṃ śastrāṇāṃ kuliśaṃ yathā \|*

*sarvāṅgebhyo yathā śreṣṭhamuttamāṅgaṃ vidhātṛje \|*

*manuṣyāṇāṃ yathā rājā dhenūnāṃ kāmadhugyathā \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ sarvadhātūnāṃ sarpāṇāṃ vāsukiryathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prahlādaḥ sarvadaityānāṃ rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ yathā \|*  
*jhaṣāṇāṃ makaro yadvanmṛgāṇāṃ mṛgarāḍ yathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*varuṇo yādasāṃ yadvadyamaḥ saṃyamināṃ yathā \|*  
*kṣīrodaḥ sāgarāṇāṃ ca devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*purodhasāṃ yathā jīvaḥ kālaḥ kalayatāṃ yathā \|*

12-13a. The holy centre which is difficult of access is ten Yojanas in extent. Just as the moon is the best among constellations;1 just as the ocean is the best among lakes (water-reservoirs), so is the holy centre Purusottama the best among sacred places. #

13b-14a. Just as the fire-god is the best among Vasus, Just as Sankara is the best among Rudras, so is the holy centre Purusottama, the most excellent of all holy centres.

14b-15a. Just as the Brahmana is the best among the castes, and Vainateya (Garutja) (the excellent most) among birds, so also Purusottama is the most excellent among holy centres.

15b-16a. Just as Skanda is among commanders; Kapila among Siddhas.

16b-25a. Airavata among leading elephants; Bhrigu among great sages; Meruamong the mountains; the Himalayas among the immovables (i.e. mountains); Uccaissravas among the horses; Usanas among the wise thinkers; Vyasa among the sages; Kubera among Yaksas and Raksasas, the mind among sense-organs; the earth among the elements; the Asvattha among the trees; the wind-god among those who purify; Arun- dhati among women; the thunderbolt among weapons; like the letter ‘A’ among letters; like the Gayatrl among metres; the head (Uttamanga) among limbs; the spiritual lore of salvation among all lores; the king among men; Kamadlienu (the wish- yielding cow) among cows; gold among all metals; Vasuki among serpents; Prahlada among Daityas; Rama among the wielders of weapons; sharks among fishes; lion among beasts; Varuna among water deities; Yama among those who restrain; the milk ocean among oceans; Narada among divine sages; Brhaspati (Jupiter)among priests; Kala(Time)among reckoners; Bhaskara (thesun) among planets. Pranava (Orh) among the mantras and virtuous rites among duties — so should be known) Sripurusottama among holy centres.

25b-26. By visiting at least once, Purusottama who stands on the shore of the ocean, by knowing the Brahmavidya once, there is no further stay within the womb. Thus the holy centre is endowed with all attributes. It is highly diffiicuIt of access.

## \|\| 2.52.27 \|\|

*āste yatra varārohe vikhyātaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*jagadvyāpī sa viśvātmā deveśaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О fair lady, Purusottama, the lord of Devas, the Atman of the Universe, pervading the universe stays where the holy centre Purusottama is.

## \|\| 2.52.28-35 \|\|

*jagadyonirjagannāthastatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*ajaḥ śakraśca rudra śca devāścāgnipurogamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nivasanti mahābhāge tasmindeśe sadaiva hi \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasaḥ siddhāḥ pitaro devamānuṣāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yakṣā vidyādharāścaiva munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo vālakhilyādyāḥ kaśyapādyāḥ prajeśvarāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*suparṇāḥ kinnarā nāgāstathānye svargavāsinaḥ \|*  
*sāṅgā vedāśca catvāro śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇāni yajñāśca bahudakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*nadyaśca vividhāḥ puṇyāstīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sāgarāśca tathā śailāstasmindeśe vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ puṇyatame deśe devarṣipitṛsevite \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarvopabhogasahite vāsaḥ kasya na rocate \|*  
*śreṣṭhatvaṃ tasya devasya kiṃ cānyadadhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*āste yatra jagaddevo muktidaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*dhanyāste vibudhaprakhyā ye vasantyutkale narāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

28-29a. Where the lord of the universe, the source of origin of the universe is present, everything is established there. All the following are present therein Aja (Brahma), Indra, Rudra, Agni and other Devas; О highly blessed lady, all these stay there always in that land.

29b-35. The following too are present: — The Gandharvas, the celestial damsels, Siddhas, Pitrs, Devas, human beings, Yaksas, Vidyadharas, the sages of praise-worthy holy vows; the sages Valakhilya and others; Kasyapa and other Prajapatis; Suparnas; Kinnaras; Nagas, and other residents of heaven; the four Vedas along with their ancil- laries; the different scriptures; Itihasas, Puranas, sacrifices wherein many monetary gifits (as religious fees) are given; the different sacred rivers; the holy centres and shrines; the ocean and the mountains were established in that land. Who will not like to live in such a meritorious land inhabited by the gods, sages and Pitrs and fully equipped with all means of enjoyment? There is the surpassing excellence of that lord. What is it that surpasses that wherein the lord of the universe, Purusottama, the bestower of salvation is present? Blessed are those men who stay in Utkala and resemble the Devas.

## \|\| 2.52.36 \|\|

*tīrtharājajale snātvā paśyanti puruṣottamam \|*  
*svarge vasanti te martyā na tu te rājasālaye \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those men who take bath in the waters of the Tirtha- raja (the king of holy centres, viz. the Sea) and visit Purusottama, stay in the heaven and not in the abode of a Rajasa nature.

## \|\| 2.52.37 \|\|

*ye vasaṃtyutkale kṣetre puṇye śrīpuruṣottame \|*  
*saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ teṣāmautkalānāṃ sumedhasām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Fruitful is the life of those residents of Utkala of great intellect who habitually reside in the meritorious holy centre of Sripurusottama in Orissa.

## \|\| 2.52.38-42 \|\|

*ye paśyanti sutāmrauṣṭhaprasannāyatalocanam \|*  
*cārubhrūkeśamukuṭaṃ cārukarṇalatāñcitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*cārusmitaṃ cārudantaṃ cārukuṇḍalamaṇḍitam \|*  
*sunāsaṃ sukapolaṃ ca sulalāṭaṃ sulakṣaṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*trailokyānandajananaṃ kṛṣṇasya mukhapaṅkajam \|*  
*purā kṛtayuge devi śakratulyaparākramaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*babhūva nṛpatiḥ śrīmānindra dyumna iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*satyavādī śucirdakṣaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*rūpavānsubhagaḥ śūro dātā bhoktā priyaṃvadaḥ \|*  
*yaṣṭā samastayajñānāṃ brahmaṇyaḥ satyasaṅgaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-40a. (Blessed are they) who see the lotus-like face of Krsna, wherein the lips are very red like copper, the eyes Ъге pleasant and large, the eyebrows, the tresses and coronets are very beautiful; which is embellished with beautiful ear-rings, which is beautified with smiles, and charming earrings; wherein the teeth are beautiful and the nose, cheeks and forehead have all good characteristics and which cause delight to the three worlds.

40b-41a. О gentle lady, it is reported that formerly, in the Krta age there was a glorious king wellknown as Indradyu- mna. His exploits were like those of Indra.

41b-42. He was truthful of speech, pure, clever and competent. He was the most excellent among the warrious wielding weapons. He was charming and blessed, brave and a liberal donor. He was an enjoyer of pleasures, and pleasing in speech. He was the performer of all Yajnas, and he was friendly to Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.52.43 \|\|

*dhanurvede ca vede ca śāstre ca nipuṇaḥ kṛtī \|*  
*vallabho naranārīṇāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ yathā śaśī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He was truthful of promise. He was an adept in the Vedas, Scriptures and the science of archery. He was contented. He was popular with men and women like the moon on a Full-moon day.

## \|\| 2.52.44 \|\|

*āditya iva duṣprekṣyo madhuraścandra mā iva \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaḥ satyasampanno jitakrodho jitendri yaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He was like the sun in being too dazzling to be seen directly; he was as sweet as the moon; he was a devotee of Visnu;hewas endowed with truthfulness; he had conquered anger, he had subjugated sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.52.45 \|\|

*adhyātmavidyānirato yuyutsurdharmatatparaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sa pālayetpṛthvadyaṃ rājā sarvaguṇākaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He was engaged in spiritual learning; he was fond of virtue and piety and brave. Thus the king, the abode of all attributes, protected the earth.

## \|\| 2.52.46 \|\|

*tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā viṣṇorārādhanaṃ prati \|*  
*kathamārādhayiṣyāmi devadevaṃ janārdanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He became inclined to the propitiation of Visnu. He thought, “How shall I propitiate Janardana, the lord of the Devas.

## \|\| 2.52.47 \|\|

*kasminkṣetre'thavā tīrthe nadītīre tathāśrame \|*  
*evaṃ cintāparaḥ so'tha nirīkṣya manasā mahīm \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In which holy centre, Tirtha, or hermitage shall I do So.” Thinking thus he mentally surveyed the whole of the earth.

## \|\| 2.52.48-50 \|\|

*ālokya sarvatīrthāni yāni pāpaharāṇi ca \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi sañcintya jagāma manasā punaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vikhyātaṃ paramaṃ kṣetraṃ muktidaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*sa gatvā nṛpatistatra samṛddhabalavāhanaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ayajaccāśvamedhena vidhivadbhūridakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kārayitvā mahotsedhaṃ prāsādaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-49a. He reviewed before his mind’s eye the various holy centres of the earth that dispel sins. Finally, he decided on the well-known great holy centre Purusottama that bestows salvation.

49b-50. The king went there with the full complement of his vehicles and army. He got a lofty palace erected there. He performed a horse-sacrifice in accordance with the injunctions and distributed wealth by way of monetary gifts.

## \|\| 2.52.51-52 \|\|

*tatra saṅkarṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ subhadrā ṃ! sthāpya vīryavān \|*  
*pañcatīrthaṃ ca vidhivatkṛtvā tatra mahīpatiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japaṃ homaṃ devatāprekṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*bhaktyā cārādhya vidhivatpratyahaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*prasādāddevadevasya tato mokṣamavāptavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The powerful king installed Sankarsana, Krsna and Subhadra there. He caused five Tlrthas1 to be constructed there. With great devotion he performed ablution, charitable gift, Japa, Ноmа and the visit to the deity. He propitiated lord Purusottama every day in accordance with the injunctions and with great devotion. Thanks to the grace of the lord of the Devas, he attained salvation. Mohini enquired:

## \|\| 2.52.53-56 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- tasmin kṣetre vare puṇye vaiṣṇave puruṣottame \|\| 53 \|\|*

*kiṃ tatra pratimā pūrvaṃ susthitā vaiṣṇavī prabho \|*  
*yenāsau nṛpatistatra gatvā sabalavāhanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sthāpayāmāsa kṛṣṇaṃ ca rāmaṃ bhadrā ṃ! śubhapradām \|*  
*saṃśayo'sti mahāṃstatra vismayaśca dvijottama \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śrotumicchāmi tatsarvaṃ brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ ca yat \|*  
*vasuruvāca- śṛṇuṣva pūrvavṛttāntaṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56а. О Lord, was there an already installed image of Visnu in that excellent, meritorious sacred Vaisnavite place called Purusottama, for the sake of which the king went there along with his army and vehicles and established the images of Krsna, Balarama and Subhadra, the bestower of auspicious things. I have great doubt, О excellent Brahmana and feel a great surprise too. I wish to hear everything. Tell me the reason thereof. Vasu narrated:

## \|\| 2.52.56 \|\|

*śrotumicchāmi tatsarvaṃ brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ ca yat \|*  
*vasuruvāca- śṛṇuṣva pūrvavṛttāntaṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|\| 56 \|\|*

56b. Listen to the anecdote forming its background — a story which destroys sins.

## \|\| 2.52.57 \|\|

*pravakṣyāmi samāsena śriyā pṛṣṭaṃ ca yatpurā \|*  
*sumeroḥ kāñcane śṛṅge sarvāścaryasamanvite \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I shall succinctly narrate to you what was formerly asked by goddess Sri on the top of the golden peak of mount Sumeru which was full of all wondrous things.

## \|\| 2.52.58-61 \|\|

*tatra sthitaṃ jagannāthaṃ jagatsraṣṭāramavyayam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devī lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*papracchedaṃ mahāpraśnaṃ bhūmau sthānamanuttamam \|*  
*śrīruvāca- brūhi tvaṃ sarvalokeśa saṃśayaṃ me hṛdi sthitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*martyaloke mahāścarye bhūmau karmasudurlabhe \|*  
*lobhamohamahāgrāhe kāmakrodhamahārṇave \|\| 60 \|\|*

*yena mucyeta ātmeśa durgasaṃsārasāgarāt \|*  
*tvāmṛte nāsti loke'sminvaktā saṃśayanirṇaye \|\| 61 \|\|*

58-59a. The goddess bowed down with her head to Lord Jagannatha, the imperishable (eternal), creator of the world who was residing there. Out of her desire for the benefit of the world, she asked this following question regarding the excellent- most holy place on the earth.

Sri said:

59b-61. “O lord of all the worlds, tell me now clearing the doubts in my heart. The mortal world, the earth, is full of great miracles. It is very difficult to perform auspicious Karmans leading to Moksa here. It is a great ocean of lust and fury and contains big sharks (crocodiles) in the form of covete- ousncss and delusion. What is it, then, whereby the Atman is liberated from impassable ocean of worldly existence? Excepting you there is no one in the world who will propound everything and dispel my doubt.”

## \|\| 2.52.62 \|\|

*śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasyā devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*provāca parayā prītyā paraṃ sārāmṛtopamam \|*  
*sukhopāyaṃ susādhyaṃ ca nirāyāsaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On hearing her words thus, Janardana, the lord of the Devas, spoke with great pleasure and explained the great means of happiness that is comparable to the nectar and great essence of everything — the means that is easily achievable yield great benefit and will not cause any strain. The glorious Lord said:

## \|\| 2.52.63-64 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca- āste tīrthavaraṃ devi vikhyātaṃ puruṣottamam \|\| 63 \|\|*

## \|\| 2.52.66-72 \|\|

*dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre nyagrodho yatra tiṣṭhati \|*

*brahmahatyā pramucyeta pāpeṣvanyeṣu kā kathā \|*

*sarve vidhūtapāpāste gatā vai keśavālayam \|*

*anāyāsena vai yānti bhavanaṃ me tato narāḥ \|*

*madantikamanuprāpya praṇamya śirasābravīt \|*  
*namaste bhagavandeva lokanāthāya tejase \|\| 72 \|\|*

66-67a. On the shore of the southern sea, there is a holy (Indian) fig (Nyagrodha) tree. Even during the (close of the) kalpa, when everything is destroyed by means of great meteors (?) it is not destroyed. It remains by itself there.

67b-69a. As soon as one sees that banyan tree or if one resorts to its shade frequently, the sin of even Brahmana-slaugh ter perishes. What then about other lesser evils? Those creatures (living beings) which circumambulate it and make obeisance to it, shake off their sins. All of them go to Kesava’s abode (Vaikuntha).

69b-71a. On the southern side of the shrine of Kesava and to the north of the holy fig tree is the region of holy Dharma. By seeing the image made by the lord himself at the place, men go to my mansion without any exertion.

71b-72a. Going (along that way) once Dharmaraja (Yama) saw me, approached me and bowing down his head, spoke to me thus

72b. “Obeisance to you О lord, to the brilliant refulgence, to the lord of worlds.

73-8la. I bow down to that lord who stays in the milk- ocean; who lies down on the extensive body of Sesa; who is the most excellent one; who is the bestower of boons; who is the everlasting maker of the worlds; who is Visnu. the unborn (eternal) lord of the universe; who is omniscient; who is unconquered; who is dark in complexion like the blue lily; whose eyes resemble the lotuses; who is present everywhere, who is devoid of attributes, quiet, the unchanging creator of the universe; who is the maker of worlds; who is the lord of worlds; who is conducive to happiness; who is the ancient Purusa, worthy of being known; who is both manifest and unmanifest, who is the eternal ancient Being, who is the creator; who is a sanctifying holy being unto all the worlds; who is the preceptor of the universe; who is endowed with Srivatsa on his chest; who is bedecked in Vanamalas(garlands of sylvan flowers); who is clad in yellow garments; who has four arms who wields conch, discus and iron club; who is beautified with necklaces and armlets; who wears coronet and bracelets; who is endowed with all auspicious characteristics; who is devoid of all sense organs; who is as steady and firm as a mountain; who is subtle, eternal and of the form of fiery brilliance; who is devoid of both existence and nonexistence; pervasive and beyond Prakrti. I bow down to that lshvara, the lord of the universe, the lord bestowing happiness. Thus the lord of Dharma (Yama) eulogised me with different hymns in the vicinity of the holy fig tree. Then he made obeisance to me.

8lb-83. “О highly blessed lady, on seeing him standing with palms joined with reverence after obeisance, О gentle lady, I asked the god of Death, the reason for the eulogy, “O mighty armed Vaivasvata, you are identical with all Efevas. Why did you eulogise me thus. Tell me succinctly”. Tama said:

*yama uvāca- asminnāyatane puṇye vikhyāte puruṣottame \|*

84-85. In this holy shrine, well-known after Purusottama there is an idol made of Indranila (sapphire). It bestows all desires. О lotus-eyed deity, men devoid of desires see that idol with faith and (single-minded) emotional feelings and go to the world called Sveta (Dvlpa).

## \|\| 2.52.86 \|\|

*ataścaivaṃ na śaknomi vyāpāramarisūdana \|*

86\. Hence, О destroyer of enemies, I cannot proceed with my usual work of chastising the sinners. О great lord, be pleased. Withdraw this idol, О lord.”

## \|\| 2.52.87 \|\|

*śrutvā vaivasvatasyaitadvākyaṃ tamahamuktavān \|*

## \|\| 2.52.92-97 \|\|

*indra dyumnasya gamanaṃ kṣetrasandarśanaṃ tathā \|*

*darśanaṃ baladevasya kṛṣṇasya ca viśeṣataḥ \|*

*samudra snānamāhātmyamindra dyumnasya cāpi vai \|*

*snānaṃ kṛṣṇasya halinaḥ sarvayātrāphalaṃ tathā \|*

92-97. Indradyumna’s departure; visit to the shrine; description of the holy centre; О MohinI, its prosperity, the vision of Baladeva and of Krsna in particular and that of Subha- dra; the greatness of them all; the vision of Narasimha; the glorification of prosperity; the vision of Ananta and Vasu- deva; the glorification of his attributes; the greatness of Sveta- madhava; the description of the gateway of heaven; the sight of the ocean; the ablution therein and the performance of Tarpana rite: the greatness of ablution in the sea and of Indradyumna pool (saras); the benefit of the Paftcatirthas (five shrines and holy pools) oh the full moon day in the month of Jyestha; the bath of Krsna and holy Balarama; the benefit of all pilgrimages; the description of the world of Visnu and again of the holy place. Thus Purusottama himself described to her the truth of all these things.

## Chapter 53. The Greatness of Purusottama (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.53.1-2 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- brūhi me muniśārdūla yatpṛcchāmi purātanam \|*  
*yathā tāḥ pratimāḥ pūrvamindra dyumnena nirmitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kena caiva prakāreṇa tuṣṭastasmai sa mādhavaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vada me vipra śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

Mo him said:

1-2. О leading sage, kindly narrate to me what I ask about the ancient Being; as to how those idols were formerly made by Indradyumna and in what manner was Madhava pleased with him; O, Brahmana. elucidate everything to me, as I am eager to hear about it. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.53.3 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇuṣva cārunayane purāṇaṃ vedasammitam \|*  
*kathayāmi purāvṛttaṃ pratimānāṃ ca saṃbhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О lady of beautiful eyes, listen, I shall recount the ancient story of the origin of the idols, the mythological tradition that is on a par with the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.53.4 \|\|

*pravṛtte ca mahāyajñe prāsāde caiva nirmite \|*  
*cintā tasya babhūvātha pratimārthamaharniśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the great Sacrifice commenced and the mansion had been built, king Indradyumna began to worry about the idols, day and night.1

## \|\| 2.53.5 \|\|

*kenopāyena deveśaṃ sarvalokavibhāvanam \|*  
*sargasthityantakarttāraṃ paśyāmi puruṣottamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He pondered: “By what means can I see Purusottama the lord of the Devas, the conceiver and creator of the worlds and the cause of creation, maintenance and dissolution of the worlds?”.

## \|\| 2.53.6 \|\|

*cintāviṣṭo narendra stu naivaṃ śete divāniśam \|*  
*na bhuṅkte vividhānbhogānna ca snānaṃ prasādhanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The king who was anxious and worried could not sleep properly by day or by night. He did not enjoy the various worldly pleasures nor was he interested in taking bath or bedecking himself.

## \|\| 2.53.7 \|\|

*śailajā dārujā vāpi dhātujā vā mahītale \|*  
*viṣṇoryogyāstu pratimāḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “On the surface of the earth three types of idols befitting Visnu and marked with all characteristics are seen. Viz.: the idols made of stone, of wood or of metals.

## \|\| 2.53.8 \|\|

*etaireva trayāṇāṃ tu dayitaṃ yatsurārcitam \|*  
*sthāpite prītimabhyeti iti cintāparo'bhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The idols made of these three, when installed shall give pleasure. They shall be the beloved of the deity and worshipped by the Devas”. — Thus the king pondered over in his mind.

## \|\| 2.53.9 \|\|

*pañcarātravidhānena sampūjya puruṣottamam \|*

О Acyuta, О lord of the universe, О lord of the Devas with large eyes expressing delight, all your forms, these and others, have been mentioned by learned men — all have been worshipped and eulogised and bowed to by me.

## \|\| 2.53.23-25 \|\|

*prayacchata varaṃ mahyaṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadam \|*

23-25. Grant ye unto me that boon which bestows virtue, love, wealth and liberation. О Hari, your different forms e.g. Samkarsana and others that have been glorified are related to your worship. Hence, they have been incorporated in you, О lord of Devas. No factual difference exists between you and these forms of yours. The different forms of yours have been mentioned so, only in a secondary sense. How can man call you who are the non-dualistic one, as dualistic.

## \|\| 2.53.26 \|\|

26\. О Hari, you are but one, the pervader of all, of the nature of consciousness and unsullied: Your highest form is that which is devoid of existence as well as non-existence.

## \|\| 2.53.27-32 \|\|

*jarāvyādhiśatairyukto nānāduḥkhairnipīḍitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-28a. It is unsmeared, free from impurities, subtle, firm, steady and eternal. It is devoid of all conditioning characteristics: It is pure existence only and is well stabilised. Even a Deva does not know about it. О lord, how can I, a human being know it?

28b-30a. The other form of yours, that which is yellow- robed, four-armed, wearing the conch, discus and iron chib, having coronet and armlets, embellished with Srivatsa in the chest and bedecked in garlands of sylvan flowers, is worshipped by the Devas and others that are dependent on you.

30b-32. О lord, the most excellent one among all gods, the bestower of fearlessness (or Moksa) on the devotees, save me, О deity of beautiful lotus-like eyes, rescue me who am immersed in the ocean of worldly existence and mundane affairs. О lord of Devas, О lord of Kamala, О Madhusudana, excepting you I do not see anyone else in whom I can seek refuge. Be pleased. I am over-whelmed by hundreds of ailments and old age; I am afflicted by many miseries.

## \|\| 2.53.33 \|\|

*harṣaśokānvito mūḍhaḥ karmapāśaiḥ suyaṃtritaḥ \|*  
*patito'ha mahāraudre ghore saṃsārasāgare \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I am confounded, sometimes delighted and sometimes aggrieved; I have been bound by the nooses of Karman. I have fallen into the extremely fierce and terrible ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.53.34-35 \|\|

*viṣayodakaduṣpāre rāgadveṣasamākule \|*  
*indri yāvartagambhīre tṛṣṇāśokormisaṅkule \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nirāśraye nirālambe niḥsāre'tyantacañcale \|*  
*māyayā mohitastatra bhramāmi suciraṃ prabho \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. О lord, I am deluded by your Maya for a long time. I have been wandering (in the ocean of mundane existence) which is very difficult to cross, the ocean with worldly objects as its waters, which is highly agitated with passion and hatred; which is deep due to the whirlpools of sense-organs, and is turbulent due to the billows of greedy thirst and grief which has neither receptacle nor a support which is actually insignificant but heavily moving to and fro.

## \|\| 2.53.36-40 \|\|

*nānājātisahasreṣu jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*mayā janmānyanekāni sahasrāṇyayutāni ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vividhānyanubhūtāni saṃsāre'smiñjanārdana \|*  
*vedāḥ sāṅgā mayādhītāḥ śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇāni tathā śilpānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*asantoṣāśca santoṣāḥ sañcayā bahavo vyayāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mayā prāptā jagannātha kṣayavṛddhyduyetarāḥ \|*  
*bhāryāmitrasvabandhūnāṃ viyogāḥ saṅgamāstathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pitaro vividhā dṛṣṭā mātaraśca tathā mayā \|*  
*duḥkhāni cānubhūtāni mayā saukhyānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

36-3 7a. I am born again and again in thousands of species of creatures. О Janardana, in this world thousands and ten thousands of different births have been undergone by me.

37b-38a The Vedas have been learned by me along with their ancillaries. The different kinds of scriptures, the Itihasas the Puranas and many kinds of arts and crafts have been learned by me.

38b-39a, Dissatisfaction and satisfaction have been met with by me. Many times I have hoarded wealth. Many times I have spent (squandered) much. О lord of the universe, decline and increase, rise and fall I have faced in my life.

39b-40. I have experienced association with and separation from wives, friends and kinsmen. Different kinds of fathers and mothers have been seen by me. Many sorrows have been experienced by me and many happy occasions too.

## \|\| 2.53.41 \|\|

*prāptāśca bāndhavāḥ svasṛbhrātaro jñātayastathā \|*  
*mayoṣitaṃ tathā strīṇāṃ koṣṭhe viṇmūtrapicchile \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Relatives, sisters, brothers and kinsmen have been acquired by me. I have occupied the bellies of women, bellies that are slimy due to faeces and urine.

## \|\| 2.53.42 \|\|

*garbhavāse mahāduḥkhamanubhūtaṃ tathā prabho \|*  
*duḥkhāni yānyanekāni bālye yauvanagarvite \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О lord, while staying in the womb, great misery has been experienced by me. Miseries have been experienced during childhood as well as during haughty youth.

## \|\| 2.53.43-46 \|\|

*vārddhakye ca hṛṣīkeśa tāni prāptāni vai mayā \|*  
*maraṇe yāni duḥkhāni guptamārge yamālaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

*mayā tānyanubhūtāni narake yātanākule \|*  
*krimikīṭadrumāṇāṃ ca hastyaśvamṛgapakṣiṇām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mahiṣāṇāṃ gavāṃ caiva tathānyeṣāṃ vanaukasām \|*  
*dvijātīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śūdrā ṇāṃ caiva yoniṣu \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dhanināṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca daridrā ṇāṃ tapasvinām \|*  
*nṛpāṇāṃ nṛpabhṛtyānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ ca dehinām \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-44a. О Hrsikesa, miseries have been experienced in the course of old age by me. Those miseries that are usually experienced at death, in the secret path of Yama’s abode, and in the hell, full of tortures, have been experienced by me.

44b-46. I have been born again and again in various species, such as those of germs, insects, trees, elephants, horses, deer, birds, buffaloes, cows, and every other wild animal. I have been born in the wombs of Brahmanas, Ksatriyas Vaisyas as well as Sudras. I have been born in the abodes of rich Vaisyas, Ksatriyas, pious ascetics (Brahmanas), of kings and kings’ servants and other embodied beings.

## \|\| 2.53.47 \|\|

*gṛhe teṣāṃ samutpanno deva cāhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*gato'tmi dāsatāṃ nātha bhṛtyānāṃ bahuśo nṛṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Lord, I have been born in their houses again and again, О lord, I had worked as a slave for the servants of many men.

## \|\| 2.53.48 \|\|

*daridra tvaṃ ceśvaratvaṃ svāmitvaṃ ca tathā gataḥ \|*  
*hatā mayā hataścānyairhataṃ me ghātitā mayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I have attained poverty or affluence. Many have been killed by me. I have been killed by many others. Things belonging to me have been destroyed. Many have been caused to be killed by me.

## \|\| 2.53.49-54 \|\|

*dattaṃ me'nyairathānyebhyo mayā dattamanekaśaḥ \|*  
*pitṛmātṛsuhṛdvargakalatrāṇāṃ kṛtena ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ahaṃ hṛṣṭo'sakṛddainyaiścāśrudhautānano gataḥ \|*  
*devatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu careṣu sthāvareṣu ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*na vidyate ca tatsthānaṃ yatrāhaṃ na gataḥ prabho \|*  
*kadā me narake vāsaḥ kadā svarge jagatpate \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kadā manuṣyalokeṣu kadā tiryaggateṣu ca \|*  
*jalayantre tathā cakre kadā'vaṭanibandhane \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pātito'dhastathorddhvaṃ ca kadā madhye sthitastvaham \|*  
*tathā cāhaṃ suraśreṣṭha karmmavallīṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*evaṃ saṃsāracakre'sminbhairave lomaharṣaṇe \|*  
*bhramāmi suciraṃ kālaṃ nāntaṃ paśyāmi karhicit \|\| 54 \|\|*

49-50a. Things have been given to me by others and things have been given by me to others. I have suffered by what has been done by fathers, friends mothers and wives and have been delighted too (by what they did). On many occasions, due to misery my face has been washed by my tears.

50b-51a. О lord, there is no such spot among the Devas, animals, human beings, the mobile and immobile beings, where I have not been.

5lb-54. О lord of the universe, sometimes I stayed in hell and sometimes in heaven. Sometimes in human worlds and sometimes in animal kingdom. Just as someone, in the mechanical device for lifting water fixed to a hole fallsup and down or remains in the middle, so also О excellent one among Devas, I have had recourse to the series of my Karmans. Thus in this wheel of worldly existence, that is very terrible and that causes hairs to stand on their ends, I have been whirling for a long time. I do not see the end thereof.

## \|\| 2.53.55 \|\|

*na jāne kiṃ karomyeṣa hare vyākulitendri yaḥ \|*  
*śokatṛṣṇābhibhūtaśca kāṃdiśīko vicetanaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О Hari, I do not know what lam doing. All my sense-organs are worn out and agitated. I have been overwhelmed by grief and greed. I am a terrified fugitive. I have lost consciousness.

## \|\| 2.53.56 \|\|

*idānīṃ tvamāhaṃ deva vikalaḥ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*trāhi māṃ duḥkhitaṃ kṛṣṇa magnaṃ saṃsārasāgare \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. О lord, utterly maimed and crippled, I have now sought refuge in you. Save me, О Krsna, rescue me who am immersed in the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.53.57 \|\|

*kṛpāṃ kuru jagannātha bhakto'ha yadi manyase \|*  
*tvāmṛte nāsti me baṃdhuryo'sau cintāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О lord of the universe, be merciful if you consider me that I am your devotee. Excepting you, I have no other kinsmen who will be worrying for my sake and take my care.

## \|\| 2.53.58 \|\|

*deva tvāṃ nāthamāsādya na bhayaṃ me'sti kutracit \|*  
*jīvite maraṇe caiva yogakṣeme tathā prabho \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. О Lord, after resorting to you as the lord, I have no fear from anywhere either in life or death or about my wellbeing.

## \|\| 2.53.59 \|\|

*ye tu tvāṃ vidhivaddeva nārcayanti narādhamāḥ \|*  
*sugatistu kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhavetsaṃsārabandhanāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. How can there be good states and liberation from the bondage of worldly existence in the case of those base men who do not duly worship you, О lord?

## \|\| 2.53.60 \|\|

*kiṃ teṣāṃ kulaśīlena vidyayā jīvitena ca \|*  
*yeṣāṃ na jāyate bhaktirjagaddhātari keśave \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О what use is their nobility of birth, or good conduct or learning or even life, if they have no devotion to Kesava, the creator of the universe?

## \|\| 2.53.61 \|\|

*prakṛtiṃ tvāsurīṃ prāpya ye tvāṃ niṃndanti mohitāḥ \|*  
*patanti narake ghore jāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those who have Asuraic character and those who are deluded and those who censure you, do fall into the terrible hell and are born again and again.

## \|\| 2.53.62 \|\|

*na teṣāṃ niṣkṛtistasmādvidyate narakārṇavāt \|*  
*ye dūṣayanti durvṛttāste deva puruṣādhamāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. О lord, those who are of evil activities and those who speak ill of you are base men. They do not have any way of escape from the hellish ocean.

## \|\| 2.53.63 \|\|

*yatra yatra bhavejjanma mama karmanibandhanāt \|*  
*tatra tatra hare bhaktistvayi syādakṣatā sadā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О Hari, where I am destined to be born as a result of my Karmans, may my devotion to you be ever unimpaired.

## \|\| 2.53.64 \|\|

*ārādhya tvāṃ paraṃ daityā narāścānye'pi saṅgatāḥ \|*  
*avāpuḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ kastvāṃ deva na pūjayet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. By propitiating you, the great one, Daityas, human beings, and others too in a body have attained the greatest Siddhi. О lord, who would not like to worship you?

## \|\| 2.53.65 \|\|

*na śaknuvanti brahmādyāḥ stotuṃ tvāṃ prakṛteḥ param \|*  
*yathā cājñānabhāvena saṃstuto'si mayā prabho \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Even Brahma and others are not competent to eulogise you who are beyond Prakrti. О lord, out of my ignorance, I too have eulogised you imperfectly.

## \|\| 2.53.66 \|\|

*tatkṣamasvāparādhānme yadi te'sti dayā mayi \|*  
*kṛtāparādhe'pi hare kṣamāṃ kurvaṃti sādhavaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Hence, forgive my guilt if you have mercy towards me. О Hari, even if others commit offence, good men forgive them.

## \|\| 2.53.67-68 \|\|

*tasmātprasīda deveśa bhaktyā snehaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*stuto'si yanmayā deva bhaktibhāvena cetasā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*sāṅgaṃ bhavatu tatsarvaṃ vāsudeva namo'stu te \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Hence, О lord of the Devas, be pleased. With devotion I have resorted to your affection. О lord, you have been eulogised by me with the mind full of devotion. May that be fruitful. О Vasudeva, obeisance be to you.

## Chapter 54. The Glory of Purufottama (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.54.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- itthaṃ stutastadā tena prasanno garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*dadau tasmai tu subhage sakalaṃ manasepsitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1.2 Eulogised thus by him then, the Garuda-emblemed deity Visnu became delighted, О blessed lady, and gave him everything mentally desired by him.

## \|\| 2.54.2 \|\|

*yaḥ sampūjya jagannāthaṃ pratyahaṃ stauti mānavaḥ \|*  
*stotreṇānena matimānsa mokṣaṃ labhate dhruvam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The man who worships the lord of the universe everyday and intelligently eulogises him with this hymn, certainly attains liberation.

## \|\| 2.54.3 \|\|

*trisaṃdhyaṃ yo japedvidvānimaṃ stotravaraṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*dharmaṃ cārthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca labhate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The pure and learned man who performs the Japa of this excellent hymn during the three junctions (i.e. the dawn, dusk and midday) accomplishes (the four objectives of life, viz.) virtue, wealth, love and liberation. 1

## \|\| 2.54.4 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa lokaṃ śāśvataṃ viṣṇoryāti nirddhūtakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He who reads, listens to and narrates this with concentration and purity of mind, will shake off all sins and go to the eternal world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.54.5 \|\|

*dhanyaṃ pāpaharaṃ cedaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ śivam \|*  
*guhyaṃ sudurlabhaṃ puṇyaṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasya cit \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This is conducive to wealth. It dispels sins. It is auspicious and it yields worldly pleasures and salvation. It is an esoteric secret very difficult to be attained. It is meritorious. It should not be given to anyone and everyone (indiscriminately).

## \|\| 2.54.6 \|\|

*na nāstikāya mūrkhāya na kṛtaghnāya mānine \|*  
*na duṣṭamataye dadyānnābhaktāya kadācana \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. None shall ever impart this to an atheist, a foolish fellow, an ungrateful one, an arrogant person, a man of wicked intentions or one without devotion.

## \|\| 2.54.7 \|\|

*dātavyaṃ bhaktiyuktāya guṇaśīlānvitāya ca \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktāya śāntāya śraddhānuṣṭhānaśīline \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It should be imparted to one endowed with devotion, to one endowed with good qualities and conduct, to a devotee of Visnu, to a quiescent person and to one who is by nature faithful and who practises befitting rites and observances.

## \|\| 2.54.8 \|\|

*idaṃ samastāghavināśahetuṃ kāruṇyasaṃjñaṃ sukhamokṣadaṃ ca \|*  
*aśeṣavāñchāphaladaṃ variṣṭhaṃ stotraṃ mayoktaṃ puruṣottamasya \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This great hymn of Purusottama narrated by me is the cause of destruction of all sins; it is designated as mercy; it yields happiness and liberation. It is the most excellent one bestowing the desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.54.9 \|\|

*ye taṃ susūkṣmaṃ vimalāmbarāmaṃ dhyāyanti nityaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|*  
*te muktibhājaḥ praviśanti viṣṇuṃ mantrairyathājyaṃ hutamadhvarāgnau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Those who continuously meditate on the ancient Purusa who is very subtle and who resembles the pure firmament, attain salvation. They enter Visnu like the ghee that has been consigned to the sacrificial fire with Mantras.

## \|\| 2.54.10 \|\|

*ekaḥ sa devo bhavaduḥkhahantā paraḥ pareṣāṃ na tato'sti cānyaḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭā sa pātā sakalāntakartā viṣṇuḥ samaścākhilasārabhūtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The lord alone is the destroyer of the miseries of Samsara. He is greater than the greatest. There is none supreme to him. He is the creator, sustainer and the annihilator of all. Visnu is the same (impartial and good) to all. He is the essence of everythi ng.

## \|\| 2.54.11 \|\|

*kiṃ vidyayā kiṃ suguṇaiśca teṣāṃ yajñaiśca dānaiśca tapobhirugraiḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ na bhaktirbhavatīha kṛṣṇe jagadgurau mokṣasukhaprade ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Of what avail are these — viz. learning, good qualities, Yajnas, charitable gifts and severe penances to those persons who have no devotion to Krsna, the preceptor of the universe and the bestower of happiness and salvation.

## \|\| 2.54.12 \|\|

*loke sa dhanyaḥ sa śuciḥ sa vidvānsa eva vaktā sa ca dharmaśīlaḥ \|*  
*jñātā sa dātā sa ca satyavaktā yasyāsti bhaktiḥ puruṣottamākhye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He who cherishes devotion to the deity called Purusottama is blessed in this world. He is pure, he is a learned scholar; he is affluent speaker, he has righteous conduct. He is the knower. He is the donor. He is the speaker of truth.

## \|\| 2.54.13-14 \|\|

*stutvaivaṃ brahmatanayaḥ praṇamya ca sanātanam \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ jagannāthaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*cintāviṣṭo mahīpālaḥ kuśānāstīrya bhūtale \|*  
*vastraṃ ca tanmanā bhūtvā suṣvāpa dharaṇītale \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. О daughter of Brahma, after eulogising thus and bowing down to the eternal Vasudeva, the lord of the universe and the bestowerof all desired benefits, the worried king spread Kusha grass on the ground and spread his cloth over it. With his mind dwelling on the deity, he went to sleep on the bare ground.1

## \|\| 2.54.15 \|\|

*kathaṃ pratyakṣamabhyeti devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*mama cintāharo devaḥ kadāsāviti cintayan \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He thought to himself thus — “How will Janardana, the lord of the Devas, manifest himself to me? When shall this lord dispel my anxieties

## \|\| 2.54.16 \|\|

*suptasya tasya nūpatervāsudevo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa svapne tasmai ca cakradhṛk \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When the king went to sleep, Vasudeva, the preceptor of the universe, revealed himself to him in the dream in the form of) the wielder of the discus.

## \|\| 2.54.17-19 \|\|

*sa dadarśa ca taṃ svapne devadevaṃ jagatpatim \|*  
*śaṅkhacakradharaṃ śāntaṃ gadāpadmāgrapāṇinam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śārṅgabāṇāsiyuktaṃ ca jvalattejogramaṇḍalam \|*  
*yugāntādityavarṇābhaṃ nīlavaiḍūryasannibham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*suparṇapṛṣṭhamāsīnaṃ ṣoḍaśārddhabhujaṃ vibhum \|*  
*sa cāsau prābravīdvīkṣya sādhu rājanmahāmate \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19a. He saw in his dream the lord of the Devas, the lord of the universe, who holds the conch and the discus; who is calm; who wields the iron club and the lotus by the tip of liis hands; who is armed with the bow Sarnga, the arrows and the sword; who is encircled with the dazzling halo of brilliant refulgence: who displaced the lustre of the sun at the time of the end of the Yuga; who resembled the blue lapis lazuli in complexion, who was seated on the back of Garutfa and who had eight arms.

19b. On seeing him, the lord said “O king of great intellect, well done, О ruler of the earth, I am satisfied with this divine sacrifice, your devotion and faith. Why do you worry unnecessarily?

## \|\| 2.54.20 \|\|

*kratunānena divyena tathā bhaktyā ca śraddhayā \|*  
*tuṣṭo'smi te mahīpāla vṛthā kimanuśocasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О King, 1 shall tell you the means whereby you will get the idol that is eternal and worthy of being worshipped by the kings.

## \|\| 2.54.21-24 \|\|

*yadatra pratimā rājan rājapūjyā sanātanī \|*  
*yathā tāṃ prāpnuyā bhūpa tadupāyaṃ bravīmi te \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gatāyāmadya śarvaryāṃ nirmale bhāskarodaye \|*  
*sāgarasya jalasyānte nānādrumavibhūṣite \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jalaṃ tathaiva velāyāṃ dṛśyate yatra vai mahat \|*  
*lavaṇasyodadhe rājaṃstaraṅgaiḥ samabhiplutam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kūlālambī mahāvṛkṣaḥ sthitaḥ sthalajaleṣu ca \|*  
*velābhirhanyamānaśca na cāsau kampate dhruvaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. When this night is over and the pure sun rises up you must find out this tree. It is inside the waters of the sea. The place is beautified with various trees. On the shore also much water can be seen, О King, that has accumulated from the tides of the sea. Supported by the shore, the great tree stands there partly in water and partly on the ground. The tidal waves lash against it but it is firm and steady (and immovable). It does not quake or move.

## \|\| 2.54.25-27 \|\|

*hastena parśumādāya ūrmerantastato vraja \|*  
*ekākī viharan rājanyaṃ tvaṃ paśyasi pādapam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*idaṃ cihnaṃ samālokya cchedaya tvamaśaṅkitaḥ \|*  
*śātyamānaṃ tu taṃ vṛkṣaṃ prāṃśumadbhutadarśanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tenaiva sañcintya tadā bhūpāla darśanam \|*  
*kuru tatpratimāṃ divyāṃ jahi cintāṃ vimohinīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Take an axe in your hand and wade alone (without taking any companion) through the waves sportingly. You will notice the tree by means of snigs indicated; unhesitatingly cut it down. On seeing the huge tree of wonderful appearance felled down, you make an idol of the lord from that tree. You should cast offyour anxiety that deludes you.

## \|\| 2.54.28 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahābhāgo jagāmādarśanaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*sa cāpi svapnamālakṣya paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After saying this, Hari, the highly blessed one disappeared. The king too was extremely surprised by what he saw his dream.

## \|\| 2.54.29 \|\|

*tāṃ niśāṃ samudīkṣansa tatastadgatamānasaḥ \|*  
*vyāharanvaiṣṇavānmantrānsūktaṃ caiva tadātmakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He spent the remaining part of that night keeping awake with his mind dwelling on the lord, repeating the Mantras of Visnu and the hymn pertaining to him.

## \|\| 2.54.30 \|\|

*prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu tudgato'nanyamānasaḥ \|*  
*sa snātvā sāgare samyagyathāvadvidhinā tataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When the night dawned, with his mind not dwelling on anything else, he duly took his bath in the sea.

## \|\| 2.54.31 \|\|

*datvā dānaṃ tu viprebhyo grāmāṃśca nagarāṇi ca \|*  
*kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ karma jagāma sa nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He gave villages and cities by way of religious gifts to the Brahmanas The excellent king performed the duties of the forenoon and went ahead.

## \|\| 2.54.32 \|\|

*na ratho na padātiśca na gajo na ca sārathiḥ \|*  
*ekākī sa mahāvelāṃ praviveśa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He did not take any chariot, footsoldier, elephant or charioteer along with him. The ruler of the earth entered the great seashore, alone.

## \|\| 2.54.33 \|\|

*taṃ dadarśa mahāvṛkṣaṃ tejasvantaṃ mahādrumam \|*  
*mahāntakaṃ mahārohaṃ puṇyaṃ viphalameva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He saw the lofty tree, the brilliant great tree, the great destroyer (?) and one that has grown immensely. It was auspicious but had no fruit (viphalain).

## \|\| 2.54.34 \|\|

*mahotsavaṃ mahākāyaṃ prasuptaṃ ca jalāntike \|*  
*sāndra māñjiṣṭhavarṇābhaṃ nāmajātivivarjitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It was a means of great festival for him (Mahotsavam) (?) It had such a huge stem. It lay as though it was sleeping by the side of the wrater. It had the colour of the dense Indian madder. It had no name or genus.

## \|\| 2.54.35 \|\|

*naranāthastathā viṣṇordrumaṃ dṛṣṭvā mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*parśunā śātayāmāsa śitena ca dṛḍhena ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing the tree of Visnu, the lord of men rejoiced. With the sharp axe he cut it off steadily.

## \|\| 2.54.36 \|\|

*dvaidhībhūtā matistatra babhūvendra sakhasya ca \|*  
*nirīkṣamāṇe kāṣṭhe tu babhūvādbhutadarśanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The mind of Indra’s friend (Indradyumna) was in a dilemma. While he was looking at the wood (i.e. the tree cut by him) there appeared a miraculous sight.

## \|\| 2.54.37-39 \|\|

*viśvakarmā ca viṣṇuśca viprarūpadharāvubhau \|*  
*ājagmaturmahātmānau tathā tulyāgrajanmanau \|\| 37 \|\|*

*jvalamānau sutejobhirdivyasraggandhalepanau \|*  
*atha tau taṃ samāsādya nṛpamindra sakhaṃ tadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tāvabrūtāṃ mahārāja tvaṃ kimatra kariṣyasi \|*  
*kimayaṃ te mahābāho śātitaśca vanaspatiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. ViSvakarman and Visnu assumed the forms of Brahmanas. Those two noble souls came there. They were shining brilliantly with great lustre. They had divine scents, garlands, and unguents; they thenapproched king Indradyumna, the friend of Indra, and enquired: “O great king, what will you do here? О mighty-armed one, why was this tree felled down? This verse is he same as Brahma P. 50.21 where that Parana reads Mahdtigam i.e. great transcending (all in height), and Vipula ‘extensive, for Viphala of the NP above. Brahma P. 50.2 reads mahotsedha: ‘of great height and thickness.'

## \|\| 2.54.40 \|\|

*asahāyo mahādurge nirjane gahane vane \|*  
*mahāsindhutaṭe caiva śātito vai mahādrumaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Unaided by anyone, in this great impassable lonely and dense forest on the shores of the great sea, this huge tree has been felled down.”

## \|\| 2.54.41-42 \|\|

*tayoḥ śrutvā vacaḥ subhru sa tu rājā mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*babhāṣe vacanānyābhyāṃ mṛdūni madhurāṇi ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tau brāhmaṇau tatra candra sūryāvivāgatau \|*  
*namaskṛtya jagannāthāvavāṅmukhamavasthitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. О lady of beautiful eyebrows, on hearing their words, the king was filled with joy. On seeing those two Brah- manas who had come there like the moon and the sun, he bowed down to them, the lords of the universe, and stood there with the head bent down. Then he addressed these sweet words to them

## \|\| 2.54.43 \|\|

*deva devamanādyantamameyaṃ jagataḥ patim \|*  
*ārādhituṃ vai pratimāṃ karomīti matirmama \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “It is my intention that I should make an idol of this wood in order to propitiate the god of the Devas, the lord of the universe who has neither a beginning nor an end, the lord who cannot be measured or comprehended.

## \|\| 2.54.44 \|\|

*ahaṃ sa devadevena parameṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*svapnānte ca samuddiṣṭo bhavadbhya śrāvito mayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In the course of a dream, I have been advised by the lord of the Devas, the greatest and noblest Atman; I have recounted that to you also”.

## \|\| 2.54.45 \|\|

*yajñastadvacanaṃ śrutvā devendra pratimasya ca \|*  
*prahasya tasmai viśveśastuṣṭo vacanamabravīt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing the words of the king who was on a par with Devendra, the lord of the universe became delighted. Laughingly he spoke these words:

## \|\| 2.54.46-48 \|\|

*sādhu sādhu mahīpāla yadetanmana uttamam \|*  
*saṃsārasāgare ghore kadalīdalasannibhe \|\| 46 \|\|*

*niḥsāre duḥkhabahule kāmakrodhasamākule \|*  
*indri yāvartakalile dustare lomaharṣaṇe \|\| 47 \|\|*

*nānāvyādhiśatāvarte calabudbudasannibhe \|*  
*yataste matirutpannā viṣṇorārādhanāya vai \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. “O ruler of the earth, well done. Your mind had been excellent, since you had an inclination towards the propitiation of Visnu. This ocean of mundane existence is very terrible. It is like the leaf of a plantain tree (that can be torn easily), it is insignificant, yet it is full of miseries. It is boisterous and turbulent due to lust and furry. It is full of whirlpools of sense-organs. It is impassable and generates horripilation. Hundreds of ailments repeatedly assail the people. The ocean of worldly existence is like a transient bubble.

## \|\| 2.54.49-50 \|\|

*dhanyastvaṃ nṛpaśārdūla guṇaiḥ sarvairalaṅkṛtaḥ \|*  
*saprajā dharaṇī dhanyā saśailavanapattanā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sapuragrāmanagarā caturvarṇairalaṅkṛtā \|*  
*yatra tvaṃ nṛpaśārdūla prajāpālayitā prabhuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. О leading king, you are blessed; you are adorned with the good attributes. The whole earth inclusive of subjects is blessed. The earth where you are the overlord, inclusive of mountains, forests and cities, containing many cities, villages and towns and adorned with the people of four castes, is blessed, since you are the lord and protector of the subjects.

## \|\| 2.54.51 \|\|

*ehyehi tvaṃ mahābhāga drume'sminsukhaśītale \|*  
*āvābhyāṃ saha tiṣṭha tvaṃ kathābhirddharmasaṃśritaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О highly blessed one; Gome on, come on. Stay under this tree which is cool and pleasant. Sit here with us discussing pious and virtuous matters.

## \|\| 2.54.52 \|\|

*ayaṃ tava sahāyārthamāgataḥ śilpināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmasamaḥ sākṣānnipuṇaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This most excellent one among sculptors and artisans has come here to render help to you. He is equal to tyHva- karman himself. He is an adept in all arts and crafts.

## \|\| 2.54.53-54 \|\|

*mayoddiṣṭāṃ tu pratimāṃ karotyeṣa taṭaṃ tyaja \|*  
*śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasya tadā rājā dvijanmanaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sāgarasya taṭaṃ tyaktvā gatvā tasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*tasthau sa nṛpatiśreṣṭho vṛkṣacchāyāṃ suśītalām \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. He will make the idol thought of by you for me. Leave off the seashore”. On hearing these words of the Brah- mana, the king left the seashore and went near him. The most excellent king went and sat under the cool shade of the tree.

## \|\| 2.54.55 \|\|

*tatastasmai sa viśvātmā tadākārāṃ tadākṛtim \|*  
*śilpimukhyāya vidhije kuruṣvetyabhyabhāṣata \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereafter, О daughter of Brahma, the Atman of the universe instructed the chief of artisans — “Make these idols in their respective shapes and sizes.

## \|\| 2.54.56 \|\|

*kṛṣṇarūpaṃ paraṃ śāntaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam \|*  
*śrīvatsakaustubhadharaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The first idol shall be the form of Krsna. It shall be extremely peaceful with eyes large and resembling the petals of lotus. It must have the mark of Srivatsa and the jewel Kaus- tubha. It must wield the conch, discus and iron club.

## \|\| 2.54.57 \|\|

*gauraṃ gokṣīravarṇābhaṃ dvitīyaṃ svastikāṅkitam \|*  
*lāṅgalāstradharaṃ devamanantākhyaṃ mahābalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The second idol should be white in complexion. It must have the lustre and colour of cow's milk. It must be marked with the sign of Svastika. It is the lord wielding the ploughshare as his weapon. It is the highly mighty lord named Ananta.

## \|\| 2.54.58 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvayakṣavidyādharoragaiḥ \|*  
*na vijñāto hi tasyāntastenānanta iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. His final limit for nature has not been known by the Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas and serpents. Hence he is remembered as Ananta.

## \|\| 2.54.59 \|\|

*bhaginīṃ vāsudevasya rukmavarṇāṃ suśobhanām \|*  
*tṛtīyāṃ vai subhadrā ṃ! ca sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitām \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The third idol shall be that of the sister of Vasudeva. She has the golden complexion. She is extremely beautiful. She is Subhadra marked by all the auspicious characteristics.”

## \|\| 2.54.60 \|\|

*śrutvaitadvacanaṃ tasya viśvakarmā sukarmakṛt \|*  
*tatkṣaṇātkārayāmāsa pratimāḥ śubhalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On hearing these words of his, Visvakarman, the expert in excellent artisanship, instantaneously made those idols with beautiful and auspicious characteristics.

## \|\| 2.54.61 \|\|

*kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vicitrābhyāṃ karṇābhyāṃ suvirājitāḥ \|*  
*cakralāṅgalavinyāsahatābhyāṃ bhānusammatāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He made the idols shine resplendently with ear-rings of diverse kinds in their ears. Markings of the discus and the ploughshare were clear in the hands. They shone like the sun (?)

## \|\| 2.54.62 \|\|

*prathamaṃ śuklavarṇānāṃ śāradendusamaprabham \|*  
*suraktākṣaṃ mahākāyaṃ phaṭāvikaṭamastakam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The first idol had white colour like the lustre of the autumnal moon. The eyes were red and the body huge and there was a hood over the head. It was Bala wearing the blue cloth. He was fierce and had wonderful earrings. He held a great ploughshare and a big threshing rod. He was divine in form.

## \|\| 2.54.63 \|\|

*nīlāmbaradharaṃ cograṃ balamadbhutakuṇḍalam \|*  
*mahāhaladharaṃ divyaṃ mahāmusaladhāriṇam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The second idol resembled the blue cloud in complexion. It had eyes resembling lotuses. The lord resembled the flower of Atasi (Hemp or flax) and his eyes were as large as the petals of the lotus.

## \|\| 2.54.64 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ nīlajīmūtasannibham \|*  
*atasīpuṣpasaṅkāśaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He was Hari, Acyuta, with the Srivatsa mark on the chest, with shining yellow robes. He was divine in character, holding the discus and the conch. He dispelled all sins.

## \|\| 2.54.65-67 \|\|

*śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ bhrājatpītavāsasamacyutam \|*  
*cakrakambukaraṃ divyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ harim \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāṃ svarṇavarṇābhāṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇām \|*  
*vicitravastrasañchannāṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vicitrābharaṇopetāṃ ratnamālāvalambitām \|*  
*pīnonnatakucāṃ ramyāṃ viśvakarmā vinirmame \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. The third idol had the golden lustre. It had eyes as large as the petals of a lotus. (It was that of Subhadra) covered with various garments, bedecked in necklaces and armlets and equipped with ornaments of different kinds. There was a necklace of gems and jewels. The bosom was plump and protruding. Visvakarman thus made a beautiful idol.

## \|\| 2.54.68-69 \|\|

*sa tu rājādbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇenaikena nirmitāḥ \|*  
*divyavastrayugācchannā nānāratnairalaṅkṛtāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*sarvalakṣaṇasampannāḥ pratimāḥ sumanoharāḥ \|*  
*vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. The king saw that wonderful feat and was surprised very much. Within a moment, he saw those beautiful idols covered with pairs of divine robes, embellished with different kinds of jewels and richly endowed with all characteristics. Being very much surprised, he spoke these words.

## \|\| 2.54.70 \|\|

*kiṃ devau samanuprāptau dvijarūpadharāvubhau \|*  
*dvāvapyadbhutakarmāṇau devavṛttau tvamānuṣau \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “Is it possible that both of you are Devas who have come here assuming the forms of Brahmanas? Both of you achieve wonderful feats and divine activities. You are super-human.

## \|\| 2.54.71-72 \|\|

*devau vā mānuṣau vāpi yakṣavidyādharau varau \|*  
*kiṃ vā brahmathṛṣīkeśau vasurudrā vutāśvinau \|\| 71 \|\|*

*na vedmi satyavadbhāvau māyārūpeṇa saṃsthitau \|*  
*yuvāṃ gato'smi śaraṇamātmānaṃ vadataṃ mama \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Are you Devas or human beings, or excellent Yaksas or Vidyadharas, or Brahma and Visnu or Vasu and Rudra or the twin gods Asvins? I do not know your true nature (since) you are present here assuming a magic form. I seek refuge in you. Kindly reveal yourselves to me.” The Brahmana replied:

## \|\| 2.54.73 \|\|

*dvija uvāca- nāhaṃ devo na yakṣo vā na daityo na ca devarāṭ \|*  
*na brahmā na ca rudro 'ha viddhi māṃ puruṣottamam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73.1 “I am neither a god nor a Yaksa. I am neither a Daitya nor a king of Devas. I am neither Brahma rtor Rudra Know me as Purusottama.

## \|\| 2.54.74 \|\|

*ārtighnaṃ sarvalokānāmanantabalapauruṣam \|*  
*arcanīyo hi bhūtānāmanto yasya na vidyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. I am the destroyer of the anguish of all the worlds, I possess infinite might and manliness. I am worthy of being worshipped by all living beings. I have no end.

## \|\| 2.54.75 \|\|

*paṭhyate sarvaśāstreṣu vedānteṣu nigadyate \|*  
*yadukta dhyānagamyaṃ ca vāsudeveti yogibhiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. I am that which is learnt (i.e. described) iti all scriptures and is so recounted in the Vedantas (Upanishads). I am) that which has been spoken of by Yogins as Vasudeva who is approachable through meditation.

## \|\| 2.54.76 \|\|

*ahameva svayaṃ brahmā ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ śivo hyaham \|*  
*idro 'ha devarājaśca jagatsaṃyamano yamaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. I alone am Brahma himself. I am Visnu; I am Siva. I am Indra, the king of the Devas. I am Yama, the restrainer of the universe.

## \|\| 2.54.77-78 \|\|

*pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni tretāgnirhutabhugyathā \|*  
*varuṇo'pā patiścāhaṃ dharitrī ca mahīdharāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yatkiñcidvāṅmayaṃ loke jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*viśvarūpaṃ ca māṃ viddhi matto'nyannāsti kiñcana \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. I am all the elements such as the Earth etc.: I am the three sacrificial fires as well as the devourer of what is consigned as offerings. I am Varuna, the lord of the waters, the earth, the mountains, whatever there is in this world worthy of being spoken about (in words) — whether mobile or immobile. Know me to be the embodiment of the universe. There is nothing other than I in the whole universe.

## \|\| 2.54.79 \|\|

*prīto'ha te nṛpaśreṣṭha varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*yadiṣṭaṃ tatprayacchāmi hṛdi yatte vyavasthitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. О excellent king. I am pleased with you. О king of good holy rites, choose a boon. I shall give you whatever is desired by you, whatever is fixed into your heart.

## \|\| 2.54.80 \|\|

*maddarśanamapuṇyānāṃ svapnānte'pi na jāyate \|*  
*tvaṃ punardṛḍhabhaktitvātpratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A vision of mine is not possible even in a dream for non-meritorious persons. But, as for you, you have seen me directly, thanks to your steadfast devotion.”

## \|\| 2.54.81 \|\|

*śrutvaivaṃ vāsudevasya vacanaṃ tasya mohini \|*  
*romāñcitatanurbhūtvā idaṃ stotraṃ jagau nṛpaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. On hearing these words of Vasudeva, О Mohinl, the hairs stood on ends on the body of the king. He sang the following hymn: The King prayed:

## \|\| 2.54.82 \|\|

*rājovāca- śriyaḥkānta namaste'stu śrīpate pītavāsase \|*  
*śrīda śrīśa śrīnivāsa namaste śrīniketana \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. “O lover of Sri, obeisance be to you, О lord of Sri, Hail to the yellow-robed one; О bestower of fortune, lord of Sri, О abode of Sri, salutations to you, О abode of good fortune.

## \|\| 2.54.83 \|\|

*ādyaṃ puruṣamīśānaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvatomukham \|*  
*niṣkalaṃ paramaṃ devaṃ praṇato'smi sanātanam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. I bow down to the primordial Purusa, Isana, the lord of all, having faces all round; the greatest Deva devoid of any stigma; I bow down to the eternal one.

## \|\| 2.54.84 \|\|

*śabdātītaṃ guṇātītaṃ bhāvābhāvavivarjitam \|*  
*nirlepaṃ nirguṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sarvajñaṃ sarvabhāvanam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. I bow down to him that is beyond all words, and all attributes, and devoid of existences as well as nonexistence. I salute to one that is unsmeared i. e. extremely pure, free from attributes, subtle, omniscient and the conceiver and creator of all.

## \|\| 2.54.85 \|\|

*śaṅkhacakradharaṃ devaṃ gadāmusaladhāriṇam \|*  
*namasye varadaṃ devaṃ nīlotpaladalacchavim \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. I pay obeisance to the lord holding conch, discus, iron club and threshing rod. I shall bow down to the lord who bestows boons and has the complexion of the petals of blue lotus.

## \|\| 2.54.86 \|\|

*nāgaparyaṅkaśayanaṃ kṣīrodārṇavavāsinam \|*  
*namasye'ha hṛṣīkeśaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ harim \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. I shall salute to Hrsikcsa, Hari who lies down on his serpent couch, who stays in the milk ocean and who dispels all sins.

## \|\| 2.54.87 \|\|

*punastvāṃ devadeveśa namasye varadaṃ vibhum \|*  
*sarvalokeśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ mokṣakāraṇamavyayam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. О lord of the chiefs of the Devas, I shall again pay obeisance to you, the lord and bestower of boons, Visnu the lord of all the worlds and the immutable cause of liberation”.

## \|\| 2.54.88 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā tu taṃ devaṃ praṇipatya kṛtāñjali \|*  
*uvāca praṇato bhūtvā nipatya vasudhātale \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After eulogising the lord thus, after bowing down with palms joined in reverence, he laid himself prostrate on the ground again and said:

## \|\| 2.54.89-92 \|\|

*prīto'si yadi me nātha vṛṇomi varamuttamam \|*  
*devāḥ surāḥ sagandharvā yakṣarakṣomahoragāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*siddhavidyādharāḥ sādhyāḥ kinnarā guhyakāstathā \|*  
*ṛṣayo ye mahābhāgā nānāśāstraviśāradāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*pravrajyāyogayuktāśca vedatattvānucintakāḥ \|*  
*mokṣamārgavido ye'nye dhyāyanti param padam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*nirmalaṃ nirguṇaṃ śāntaṃ yatpaśyanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tatpadaṃ gantumicchāmi prasādātte sudurlabham \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-92. “O lord, if you are pleased with me, I shall choose this excellent boon. I wish to go to that region of yours which all these meditate upon: — viz. The Devas, Asuras, Yaksas, Raksasas and the great serpents along with the Gandharvas, Siddhas, Kinnaras, Guhyakas, Sages; those blessed persons who are experts in different scriptural texts; who are endowed with renunciation and Yogic practice; who ponder over the real meaning of the Vedic texts and who know the path of salvation as well as others; who meditate upon that highest state. Your region is devoid of impurities, free from attributes and quiescent; learned men see it. It is very difficult of access; yet I wish to attain it through your grace.” The glorious Lord (Sri Bhagavan) said: —

## \|\| 2.54.93 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca- sarvaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te yatheṣṭaṃ sarvamāpnuhi \|*  
*bhaviṣyati yathākāmaṃ matprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. “May everything concerning you be auspicious and conducive to welfare. Attain everything as desired by you. Everything will happen as you desire, thanks to my grace. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.54.94 \|\|

*daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tathā nava śatāni ca \|*  
*avicchinnaṃ mahārājyaṃ kuru tvaṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. О excellent king, rule over your great kingdom without any break for ten thousand nine hundred years.

## \|\| 2.54.95-97 \|\|

*prapadya paramaṃ divyaṃ durlabhaṃ yatsurāsuraiḥ \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ manorathaṃ śāntaṃ guhyamavyaktamavyayam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*parātparataraṃ sūkṣmaṃ nirlepaṃ nirguṇaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*cintāśokavinirmuktaṃ kriyākāraṇavarjitam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ darśayiṣyāmi vijñeyākhyaṃ paraṃ padam \|*  
*samprāpya paramānandaṃ prāpsyase paramāṃ gatim \|\| 97 \|\|*

95-97. I, therefore, shall reveal to you that supreme state called Vijfteya which is the highest, divine, very difficult to attain even by gods and demons; is perfect and bestower of all desired objects; quiescent; deserves to be kept as secret; unmanifest, unchanging, greater than the greatest, subtle, perfectly pure (unstained), devoid of attributes, eternaf, perfectly free from worries and sorrows, transcending causal relationship. After attaining it you will get the highest bliss and reach the supreme goal.

## \|\| 2.54.98-99 \|\|

*kīrtiśca tava rājendra bhavatvatra mahītale \|*  
*yāvaddharā nabho yāvadyāvaccandrā rkatārakāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*yāvatsamudrā ḥ! saptaiva yāvanmervvādiparvatāḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhanti divi devāśca yāvatsarvatra cāvyayāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. May your fame spread here on the earth as long as the earth, sky, moon, sun, stars, seven oceans, Mcru and other mountains exist here. It shall be steady as long as the eternal Devas stay in the heaven and everywhere.

## \|\| 2.54.100 \|\|

*indra dyumnasaro nāma tīrthaṃ yajñājyasambhavam \|*  
*yatra snātvā sakṛllokaḥ śakralokamavāpsyati \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Here is the Tirtha named Indradyumna saras.1 It is evolved out of the ghee used in the Yajna. By taking ablution even once in this, people will attain Sakra’s world.

## \|\| 2.54.101 \|\|

*dāpayiṣyati yaḥ piṇḍaṃ taṭe'sminnambudheḥ śubhe \|*  
*kulaikaviṃśamuddhṛtya śakralokaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. He who offers Pincjas here, on this auspicious shore of the ocean, shall redeem twentyone generations of his family and go to Sakra’s world (Heaven).

## \|\| 2.54.102 \|\|

*pūjyamāno'psarobhiśca gandharvairgītaniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*vimānena carettatra yāvadindrā ścaturdaśa \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. As long as fourteen Indras reign he will continue there, worshipped by the Apsaras and sung about by Gandh- arvas with their harmonious notes. He will move about by means of the aerial chariot.

## \|\| 2.54.103-110 \|\|

*saraso dakṣiṇe bhāge nairṛtyāṃ tu samāśrite \|*  
*nyagrodho'sti drumastatra tatsamīpe tu maṇḍapaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*ketakīvanasañchanno nānāpādapasaṅkulaḥ \|*  
*āṣāḍhasya site pakṣe pañcamyāṃ pitṛdaivate \|\| 104 \|\|*

*ṛkṣe neṣyanti nastatra nītvā sapta dināni vai \|*  
*maṇḍape sthāpayiṣyanti suveśyābhiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*krīḍāviśeṣabahulairnṛtyagītamanoharaiḥ \|*  
*cāmaraiḥ svarṇadaṇḍaiśca vyajanai ratnabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*vyañjayantyastadāsmabhyaṃ sthāsyanti paramāṅganāḥ \|*  
*brahmacārī yatiścaiva snātakāśca dvijottamāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*vānaprasthā gṛhasthāśca siddhāścānye ca vai dvijāḥ \|*  
*nānāvarṇapadaiḥ stotrairṛgyajuḥsāmaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*kariṣyanti stutiṃ rājan rāmakeśavayoḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ stutvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca sampraṇamya ca bhaktitaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*naro varṣāyutaṃ divyaṃ śrīmaddharipure vaset \|*  
*pūjyamāno'psarobhiśca gandharvairgītaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

103-104a. On the southern bank of the lake, to the south-west side of it, there is a holy fig tree. Near it a Mantjapa (pavilion) will be erected. It will be covered with a cluster of KetakI trees and surrounded by many trees.

104b-107a. On the fifth day in the bright half of the month of Asa^ha, when the constellation Magha is there, and people will take us there for seven days and instal us in the pavilion with splendid courtesans expert in diverse types of dalliance and charming in their dances and songs. They will have chowries with gold handles and fans bedecked in jewels. The great ladies must be standing there fanning us.1 2

107b-109a. Other people, the religious students, Sarui- yasins, lifelong students of Veda, excellent Brahmanas, householders, forest-hermits, Siddhas, and other twice-borns will be chanting hymns from Rk, Yajus and Saman, the hymns consisting of many words and syllables. О king, they will eulogise Rama and Kesava.

109b-110. Then after eulogising, bowing to and visiting the deity with great devotion, such a man shall stay in the glorious city of Hari for ten thousand divine years, being worshipped by Apsaras and sung about by Gandharvas with harmonious notes of music.

## \|\| 2.54.111 \|\|

*hareranucarastatra krīḍate keśavena vai \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. He sports there as an attendant of Hari with Kesava.

## \|\| 2.54.112 \|\|

*vimānenārkavarṇena ratnahāreṇa rājate \|*  
*sarve kāmā mahābhāge tiṣṭhanti bhavanottame \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. He shines with a jewelled necklace, in an aerial chariot of the refulgence of the sun. All that he desires is to abide in the excellent abode that is highly blessed.

## \|\| 2.54.113 \|\|

*tapaḥkṣayādihāgatya manuṣyo brāhmaṇo bhavet \|*  
*koṭīdhanapatiḥ śrīmāṃścaturvedo bhaveddhruvam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. After the merit of penance dwindles down, he comes here to the earth as a human being and is born as a Brahmana. He shall be the lord of crores of wealth. He shall certainly be a glorious master of the four Vedas.

## \|\| 2.54.114 \|\|

*evaṃ tasmai varaṃ dattvā kṛtvā ca samayaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ bhadre sahito viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. After granting him this boon and stipulating the conditions thus, О gentle lady, Hari vanished along with Visvakarman.

## \|\| 2.54.115 \|\|

*sa tu rājā tadā hṛṣṭo romāñcitatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ mene sandarśanāddhareḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The king became delighted. His hairs began to stand on their ends. Thanks to the visit of Hari, he considered himself blessed and of having accomplished all objectives in life.

## \|\| 2.54.116-117 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ ca rāmaṃ ca subhadrā ṃ! ca varapradām \|*  
*rathairvimānasaṅkāśairmaṇikāñcanacitritaiḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

*saṃvāhya tāṃstato rājā jayamaṅgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*ānayāmāsa matimānsāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

116-117. The king accompanied by his ministers and family priests carried the idols of Krsna, Rama and Subhadra the bestowers of boons, by means of chariots resembling aerial chariots, variously decorated with jewels and gold pieces. After carrying them along to the accompaniment of auspicious shouts of victory, he brought them to his city.

## \|\| 2.54.118-119 \|\|

*nānāvāditranirghoṣairnānāvedasvanaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya ca śubhe deśe pavitre sumanohare \|\| 118 \|\|*

*tataḥ śubhe tithau svarkṣe kāle ca śubhalakṣaṇe \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayāmāsa sumuhūrte dvijaiḥ saha \|\| 119 \|\|*

118-119. The intelligent king along with the family priests and ministers installed the idols in a splendid spot to the accompaniment of different musical instruments and the recitation of Vedic Mantras. After keeping them in a holy, charming and splendid spot for a few days, he formally got these installed through the Brahmanas on an auspicious Tithi when the constellation was favourable and on the whole the time was characterised as splendid, on an auspicious Muhurta.

## \|\| 2.54.120-121 \|\|

*yathoktena vidhānena vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*ācāryānumatenaiva sarvaṃ kṛtvā mahīpatiḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*ācāryāya tadā dattvā dakṣiṇāṃ vidhivatprabhuḥ \|*  
*ṛtvigbhyaḥ savidhānena tathānyebhyo dhanaṃ dadau \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. In accordance with the Sastric injunctions#and following the prescribed procedure to be observed and according to the precepts approved by the chief priest, the king performed every rite and gave the requisite monetary gift to the preceptor. The lord distributed wealth among the Rtviks and others in accordance with injunctions.

## \|\| 2.54.122 \|\|

*kṛtvā pratiṣṭhāṃ vidhivatprāsāde bhavanottame \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa tānsarvānviśvakarmavinirmitān \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. He installed those idols made by Visvakarman, duly, in an excellent apartment in the palace.

## \|\| 2.54.123 \|\|

*tataḥ sampūjya vidhinā nānāpuṣpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*suvarṇamaṇimuktādyairnānāvastraiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. He worshipped them duly with different fragrant flowers, gold, jewels, pearls as well as with different kinds of splendid clothes.

## \|\| 2.54.124-125 \|\|

*dadau dvijebhyo viṣayānpurāṇi nagarāṇi ca \|*  
*evaṃ bahuvidhāndattvā rājyaṃ kṛtvā yathocitam \|\| 124 \|\|*

*iṣṭvā ca vividhairyajñairdattvā dānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyastato rājā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ \|*  
*jagāma paramaṃ sthānaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 125 \|\|*

124-125. He granted large tracts of lands, cities and towns to the Brahmanas. He ruled over the kingdom in a befitting manner. He performed sacrifices in various ways. He made over charitable gifts. Contented with everything, the king eschewed all possessions. He went over to the greatest place, the great region of Visnu.

## Chapter 55. The Greatness of РигщоНата (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.55.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- kasmin kāle dvijaśreṣṭha gantavyaṃ puruṣottame \|*  
*vidhinā kena kartavyā pañcatīrthyapi mānada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said: —

1\. “O excellent Brahmana, what is that time when one should go to the shrine of Purusottama? О bestower of Honour, what are the modes whereby the Pancatlrthl1 (the pilgrimage to the five holy centres) should be performed?

## \|\| 2.55.2 \|\|

*ekaikasya ca tīrthasya snāne dāne ca yatphalam \|*  
*devatāprekṣaṇe caiva brūhi sarvaṃ pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Kindly tell me, everything, the benefit accruing from the holy ablution in each of these Tlrthas severally. Tell me the benefit of charitable gifts, visiting the deities separately”. Vasu said: —

## \|\| 2.55.3-4 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- nirāhāraḥ kurukṣetre pādenaikena yastapet \|*  
*jitendri yo jitakrodhaḥ saptasaṃvatsarāyutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā sakṛjjyeṣṭhaśukladvādaśyāṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*kṛtopavāsaḥ prāpnoti tato'dhikataraṃ phalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. “A devotee may eschew all food and perform a penance standing on a single foot for seventy thousand years controlling his sense-organs and suppressing his anger. But, if one observes fast for once on the twelfth day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha and visits Purusottama, one derives a superior benefit thereby.

## \|\| 2.55.5 \|\|

*tasmājjyeṣṭhe tu subhage prayatnena susaṃyataiḥ \|*  
*svargalokepsubhirmartyairdra ṣṭavyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hence, О blessed lady, it is in the month of Jyestha that Purusottama is to be visited ardently by self-controlled men who desire to attain heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.55.6 \|\|

*pañcatīrthīṃ ca vidhivatkṛtvā jyeṣṭhe narottamaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣasya paśyettaṃ puruṣottamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The excellent man should duly make a pilgrimage to the Pancatirthi and visit Purusottama on the twelfth day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha.

## \|\| 2.55.7 \|\|

*ye paśyantyavyayaṃ devaṃ dvādaśyāṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*te viṣṇulokamāsādya na cyavante kadācana \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Those who visit the eternal lord Purusottama on the Dvadasi (twelfth) day attain the world of Visnu. They never fall off therefrom.

## \|\| 2.55.8 \|\|

*tasmājjyeṣṭhe prayatnena gantavyaṃ vidhinandini \|*  
*kṛtvā samyakpañcatīrthīṃ dra ṣṭavyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Hence, О daughter of Brahma, one should go there ardently in the month of Jyestha. After duly visiting the five holy Tirthas (Pancatirthi) and (or after the due ablutions in the five sacred water reservoirs) Purusottama should be visited.

## \|\| 2.55.9 \|\|

*sudūrastho'pi prītātmā kīrtayetpuruṣottamam \|*  
*ahanyahani śuddhātmā so'pi viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even if the pilgrim is far off but he glorifies Purusottama with a pure soul and a delighted mind day by day, he too shall go to the city of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.55.10 \|\|

*yātrāṃ karoti kṛṣṇasya śraddhayā yaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He who, with full concentration and faith, undertakes the pilgrimage of Krsna, shall be liberated from all sins. That man shall attain Visnu’s world (Vaikuntha).

## \|\| 2.55.11 \|\|

*cakraṃ dṛṣṭvā harerdūrātprāsādopari saṃsthitam \|*  
*sahasā mucyate pāpānnaro bhaktyā praṇamya tam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By seeing from even a great distance the discus of Hari, stationed on the top of the palace (Temple) and bowing down to it, the man shall be liberated from his sins instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.55.12 \|\|

*pañcatīrthīvidhiṃ vakṣye śṛṇu mohini sāmpaṃtam \|*  
*yasyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ manujo mādhavasya priyo bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О MohinI, I shall now narrate the procedure for the holy ablution in the five Tlrthas (Pancatirthi). Listen. If this is performed duly, the man shall become a favourite of Madhava.

## \|\| 2.55.13 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyahradaṃ gatvā snātvā codaṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*nimajjettatra trīnvārānimaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The clean and pure devotee should go to the Markai^deya-Hrada1 (the Pool of Markandeya). Facing #the north he should plunge therein three times. He should repeat the following Mantra: —

## \|\| 2.55.14 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgare magnaṃ pāpagrastamacetanam \|*  
*trāhi māṃ bhaganetraghna tripurāre namo'stu te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O Bhaganetraghna (he who destroyed the eye of Bhaga). OTripurari (the destroyer of the Tripuras), save me who am immersed in the ocean of worldly existence, who have been possessed by sins and have fallen senseless. Obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 2.55.15 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāya śāntāya sarvapāpaharāya ca \|*  
*snānaṃ karomi deveśa mama naśyatu pātakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Obeisance to Siva, the quiescent god, to the destroyer of all sins. О lord of the Devas, I am taking bath. May my sins perish.”

## \|\| 2.55.16 \|\|

*nābhimātre jale sthitvā vidhivaddevatā ṛṣīn \|*  
*tilodakena matimānpitṝnanyāṃśca tarpayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The intelligent pilgrim should stand in navel-deep water. With water and gingelly seeds he should duly perform the Tarpana rite of the Devas, sages, Pitrs and others.

## \|\| 2.55.17-18 \|\|

*snātvaivaṃ ca tathācamya tato gacchecchivālayam \|*  
*praviśya devatāgāraṃ kṛtvā taṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mūlamantreṇa sampūjya mārkaṇḍeyeśamādarāt \|*  
*aghoreṇa tu mantreṇa praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. After the bath and Acamana rite, the pilgrim should go to the temple of Siva. After entering the shrine, he should circumambulate three times. With the Mula Mantra he should respectfully worship the deity Markandeyesa. Repeating the Aghora Mantra (as in Tait. Aranyaka 10.45.1 he should make obeisance and crave forgiveness.

## \|\| 2.55.19 \|\|

*trilocana namaste'stu namaste śaśibhūṣaṇa \|*  
*trāhi māṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa mahādeva namo'stu te \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O three-eyed god, obeisance be to you. О moon- bedecked one, bow be to you. Redeem me, О lotus-eyed one (?) salute to you, О Mahadeva.”

## \|\| 2.55.20 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyahrade tvevaṃ snātvā dṛṣṭvā ca śaṅkaram \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After thus taking ablution in the Markandeya Hrada and by visiting Sankara, the man derives the benefit of (the performance of) ten horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.55.21-22 \|\|
