*pāpaiḥ sarvairvinirmuktaḥ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*tatra bhuktvā varānbhogānyāvadābhūtasamplavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*iha loke samāsādya bhavedvipro bahuśrutaḥ \|*  
*śāṅkaraṃ yogamāsādya tato mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Liberated from all sins; he goes to the world of Siva. Till all the living beings are dissolved, he enjoys excellent pleasures there and comes back to this world. He is Rudra-rUpephyah born as a highly learned Brahmana. Thereafter, he adopts the Yoga of Sankara and attains salvation.

## \|\| 2.55.23 \|\|

*kalpavṛkṣaṃ tato gatvā kṛtvā taṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā mantreṇānena taṃ vaṭam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The devotee shall then go to the Kalpa tree (i.e. the Banyan tree) and circumambulate it three times. He should then worship that holy Banyan tree with great devotion, repeating the following Mantra:

## \|\| 2.55.24 \|\|

*oṃ namo'vyaktarūpāya mahate natapāline \|*  
*mahodakopaviṣṭāya nyagrodhāya namo'stu te \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Om obeisance to you of unmanifest form, to the great one, to the protector of one who bows down to you. Obeisance be to you, the holy Banyan tree growing seated in the great waters.

## \|\| 2.55.25 \|\|

*avasastvaṃ sadā kalpe hareścāyatane vaṭe \|*  
*nyagrodha hara me pāpaṃ kalpavṛkṣa namo'stu te \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You resided in the banyan tree that is the abode of Hari, always during the Kalpa. О Nyagrodha tree dispel my sin. О Kalpa tree, obeisance be to you’5.

## \|\| 2.55.26 \|\|

*bhaktyā pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā gatvā kalpavaṭaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sahasojjhati pāpaughaṃ jīrṇāṃ tvacamivoragaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By approaching the Kalpa tree the Banyan tree, and by circumambulating it with devotion, the man instantaneously dispels the multitude of sins like a serpent casting off its slough.

## \|\| 2.55.27 \|\|

*chāyāṃ tasya samākramya kalpavṛkṣasya mohini \|*  
*brahmahatyāṃ naro jahyātpāpeṣvanyeṣu kā kathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Mohinl, by coming under the shade of that Kalpa tree, a man shall dispel even the sin of the murder of a Brahmana. What then of other sins?

## \|\| 2.55.28-29 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṅgasambhūtaṃ brahmatejomayaṃ param \|*  
*nyagrodhākṛtikaṃ viṣṇuṃ praṇipatya ca vaidhasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

*rājasūyāśvayedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti cādhikam \|*  
*tathā kulaṃ samuddhṛtya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. О daughter of the creator, by visiting Visnu in the form of the holy banyan tree that is born ofKrsna’s limbs and that has the greatest brilliance of Brahman, and by bowing down to it, one attains more benefit than that of the Rajasiiya sacrifice and the horse-sacrifice. He uplifts his family and goes to the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.55.30 \|\|

*vainateyaṃ namaskṛtya kṛṣṇasya purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktastato viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By bowing down to Vainateya (Garuda) stationed in front of Krsna the devotee shall be liberated from all sins and he will go to the city of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.55.31 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vaṭaṃ vainateyaṃ yaḥ paśyetpuruṣottamam \|*  
*saṅkarṣaṇaṃ subhadrā ṃ! ca sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He who sees Purusottama, Samkarsana and Subhadra after visiting the banyan tree and Vainateya, attains the greatest goal (viz. Moksa).

## \|\| 2.55.32 \|\|

*praviśyāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ kṛtvā taṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*saṅkarṣaṇaṃ subhadrā ṃ! ca bhaktyā pūjya prasādayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After entering the shrine of Visnu and circumambulating the deity three times, the pilgrim should worship and propitiate Samkarsana and Subhadra with devotion. cf. BM. P. 57.13-14. The Banyan tree is styled as Kalpa-vrksha in BM P. 57. 12; 60, 18.

## \|\| 2.55.33 \|\|

*namaste haladhṛṅnāmne namaste musalāyudha \|*  
*namaste revatīkānta namaste bhaktavatsala \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “Obeisance to you, the deity named Haladhara (wielder of the ploughshare); Hail to you, О deity armed with the threshing pestle, salute to you, the lover of Revatl; obeisance to you О deity favourably disposed to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.55.34 \|\|

*namaste balināṃ śreṣṭha namaste dharaṇīdhara \|*  
*pralambāre namaste'stu trāhi māṃ kṛṣṇapūrvaja \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Obeisance to you, О most powerful one among the strong persons; Bow to you the supporter of the earth; obeisance be to you, О enemy of Pralamba;1 save me, О elder brother of Krsna.’

## \|\| 2.55.35-37 \|\|

*evaṃ prasādya cānantamajeyaṃ tridaśārcitam \|*  
*kailāsaśikharākāraṃ candra kāntavarānanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nīlavastradharaṃ devaṃ phaṇāvikaṭamastakam \|*  
*mahābalaṃ haladharaṃ kuṇḍalaikavibhūṣitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*rauhiṇeyaṃ naro bhaktyā labhedabhimataṃ phalam \|*  
*sarvapāpairvinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Thus propitiating Ananta, who is unconquerable, who is worshipped by the Devas; who has the shape of the peak of Kailasa; whose face is as excellent and resplendent as the moon; who is clad in blue robes; whose head is formidable due to the hood; who is highly mighty; who is wielding the ploughshare and who is bedecked only with one earring — by worshipping the son of Rohini thus with devotion, a man may attain the desired benefit. Liberated from all sins, he goes to Visnu’s world.

## \|\| 2.55.38-39 \|\|

*ābhūtasamplavaṃ yāvadbhuktvā tatra svayaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*puṇyakṣayādihāgatya pravaro yogināṃ kule \|\| 38 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇapravaro bhūtvā sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ tatra samāsādya muktiṃ prāpnoti durlabhām \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The learned devotee shall enjoy all pleasures there, till the ultimate dissolution of all living beings. When the merits are exhausted, he comes here in the world and is born in the family of Yogins. He becomes an excellent Brahmana and masters all the scriptural texts and their meanings. After attaining perfect knowledge, he attains liberation that is usually very difficult of access.

## \|\| 2.55.40 \|\|

*evamabhyarcya halinaṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśākṣaramantreṇa pūjayetsusamāhitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After worshipping Balarama (Lit. one armed with the ploughshare) thus, the clever devotee should, with great concentration, worship Krsna by means of the twelve-syllabled Mantra (viz. Oih naino Bhagavate Vasudevaya).

## \|\| 2.55.41 \|\|

*dviṣaṭvarṇakamantreṇa bhaktyā ye puruṣottamam \|*  
*pūjayanti sadā dhīrāste mokṣaṃ prāpnuvanti vai \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those self-possessed men who devoutly worship Purusottama always by means of twelve-syllabled Mantra attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.55.42 \|\|

*na tāṃ gatiṃ surā yānti yogino naiva somapāḥ \|*  
*yāṃ gatiṃ yānti vidhije dvādaśākṣaratatparāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О daughter of Brahma, neither the Devas, nor the Yogins nor the imbibers of the Soma juice attain that state which those vvho are devoted to the twelve-syllabled Mantra attain.

## \|\| 2.55.43 \|\|

*tasmāttenaiva mantreṇa bhaktyā kṛṣṇaṃ jagadgurum \|*  
*sampūjya gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ praṇipatya prasādayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hence, the devotee should worship Krsna, the preceptor of the universe, devoutly by means of scents, fragrant flowers etc., repeating that Mantra alone. After bowing to him» he should propitiate him: —

## \|\| 2.55.44 \|\|

*jaya kṛṣṇa jagannātha jaya sarvāghanāśana \|*  
*jaya cāṇūrakeśighna jaya kaṃsaniṣūdana \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “Victory to you О Krsna; О lord of the universe, be victorious; victory to you, О slayer of Canura and Kesin, О slayer of Kamsa, be victorious.

## \|\| 2.55.45 \|\|

*jaya padmapalāśākṣa jaya cakragadādhara \|*  
*jaya nīlāmbudaśyāma jaya sarvasukhaprada \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О deity with eyes resembling the petals of the lotus, be victorious; victory to you, О bearer of the discus and the iron club; О deity dark-complexioned like the blue cloud, be victorious; О bestower of all happiness, be victorious.

## \|\| 2.55.46 \|\|

*jaya deva jagatpūjya jaya saṃsāranāśana \|*  
*jaya lokapate nātha jaya vāñchāphalaprada \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О lord worthy of being worshipped by the universe» be victorious; О destroyer of worldly existence (Samsara) be victorious; О lord, О lord of the worlds, be victorious; victory to you, О deity bestowing the desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.55.47-48 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgare ghore niḥsāre duḥkhaphenile \|*  
*krodhagrāhakule raudre viṣayodakasamplave \|\| 47 \|\|*

*nānārogormikalile mohāvartasudustare \|*  
*nimagno'ha suraśreṣṭha trāhi māṃ puruṣottama \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. О Purusottama, rescue me. I am immersed in the terrible ocean of worldly existence, though factually it is insignificant. Miseries constitute its foams; it is turbulent with furious temperament constituting its sharks and crocodiles. The mundane affairs are its flood of waters; the different kinds of ailments are its waves; it is impassable due to the whirlpool of delusion.”

## \|\| 2.55.49-52 \|\|

*evaṃ prasādya deveśaṃ varadaṃ bhaktavatsalam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ devaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pīnāṃsaṃ dvibhujaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam \|*  
*mahoraskaṃ mahābāhuṃ pītavastraṃ śubhānanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ mukuṭāṅgadabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā naro'ñjali kṛtvā daṇḍavatpraṇipatya ca \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasrāṇāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mohini \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. By visiting Purusottama, with palms joined in reverence and by prostrating oneself flat, like a staff (before him) one attains, О MohinI, the benefit of thousand of horse- sacrifices. By propitiating the lord of the Devas (the devotee attains great benefits); the lord who is the bestower of boons; who is favourably disposed towards the devotees; who is the destroyer of all sins, who grants all desired benefits, that lord Krsna has two arms and plump shoulders. His eyes are as large as the petals of the lotus. His chest is large; his arms are mighty; his face is splendid. He is clad in yellow robes. He holds the conch, discus and iron club in his hands. He is bedecked with crown and armlets. He is endowed with all auspicious characteristics. He is adorned with garlands of sylvan flowers.

## \|\| 2.55.53 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu snāne dāne prakīrtitam \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. By visiting and bowing to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which has been glorified in the case of ablution in the Tirthas and the offering of charitable gifts.

## \|\| 2.55.54 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvavedeṣu sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti naraḥ kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. By bowing down to Lord Krsna, a man attains that benefit which is linked up with the Vedas and Yajnas.

## \|\| 2.55.55 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvadāneṣu vrateṣu niyameṣu ca \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. By visiting and bowing down to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which results from all charitable gifts, holy rites and observances.

## \|\| 2.55.56 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ brahmacaryeṇa samyak cīrṇena kīrtitam \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. By visiting and bowing down to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which is reputed to result from celibacy duly observed.1

## \|\| 2.55.57 \|\|

*gārhasthyena yathoktena yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. By visiting and bowing down to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which is cited as the benefit of the life of a householder duly practised.

## \|\| 2.55.58 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ vanavāsena vānaprasthasya kīrtitam \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By visiting and bowing down to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which is glorified as being yielded by dwelling in the forest to one w ho practises Vanaprastha stage of life.

## \|\| 2.55.59 \|\|

*sanyāsena yathoktena yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*narastatphalamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇamya ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. By visiting and bowing down to Krsna, a man attains that benefit which has been cited as resulting from the due observance of the life of an ascetic Sannyasin.

## \|\| 2.55.60 \|\|

*kiṃ cātra bahunoktena māhātmyaṃ tasya bhāmini \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ naro bhaktyā mokṣaṃ prāpnoti durlabham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О beautiful, woman, of what avail is much talk about its greatness? By visiting Krsna with devotion, a man attains salvation which is so difficult to attain.

## \|\| 2.55.61-62 \|\|

*pāpairvimuktaḥ śuddhātmā kalpakoṭisamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*śriyā paramayā yuktaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*sarvakāmasamṛddhena vimānena suvarcasā \|*  
*triḥsaptakulamuddhṛtya naro viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. fie will be liberated from the sins originating since crores of Kalpas. He will be endowed with the greatest glory and all attributes. After uplifting twentyone generations of his family, the man shall go to the city of Visnu by means of an aerial chariot of great brilliance richly equipped with all desirable things.

## \|\| 2.55.63 \|\|

*tataḥ kalpaśataṃ yāvadbhuktvā bhogānmanoramān \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasaiḥ sārdhaṃ yathā viṣṇuścaturbhujaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then for the duration of a hundred Kalpas, he will be enjoying pleasures sweet to the mind. He will be sporting about with Gandharvas and Apsaras like the four-armed Visnu.

## \|\| 2.55.64 \|\|

*cyutastasmādihāyāto viprāṇāṃ pravare kule \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvavedī ca jāyate gatamatsaraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Falling off from that world, he comes down here and is born in the excellent family of Brahinanas. He becomes omniscient. jHe knows everything. He eschews malice and jealous rivalry.

## \|\| 2.55.65 \|\|

*svadharmanirataḥ śānto dātā bhūtahite rataḥ \|*  
*āsādya vaiṣṇavaṃ jñānaṃ tato muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He will be engaged in his own righteous duties. He will be quiescent and charitable. He will be engaged in the welfare of all living beings. After acquiring perfect knowledge pertaining tp Visnu, he shall attain liberation.

## \|\| 2.55.66 \|\|

*tataḥ sampūjya mantreṇa subhadrā ṃ! bhaktavatsalām \|*  
*prasādayecca vidhije praṇipatya kṛtāñjali \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thereafter, bowing down to Subhadra with palms folded in reverence and with the following Mantra, the devotee should propitiate Subhadra, who is favourably disposed towards her devotees, О daughter of god Brahma.

## \|\| 2.55.67 \|\|

*namaste sarvage devi namaste śubhasaukhyade \|*  
*trāhi māṃ padmapatrākṣi kātyāyani namo'stu te \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “Obeisance to you, О omnipresent goddess; obeisance to you the bestower of auspiciousness and happiness. Protect me О KatyayanI, you who are possessed of eyes resembling the petals of a lotus.’5

## \|\| 2.55.68-70 \|\|

*evaṃ prasādyatāṃ devīṃ jagaddhātrīṃ jagaddhitām \|*  
*baledavasya bhaginīṃ subhadrā ṃ! varadāṃ śivām \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kāmagena vimānena naro viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*ābhūtasamplavaṃ yāvatkīḍitvā tatra devavat \|\| 69 \|\|*

*iha mānuṣatāṃ prāpto brāhmaṇo vedavidbhavet \|*  
*prāpya yogaṃ harestatra mokṣaṃ ca labhate dhruvam \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. Thus propitiating that goddess, the mother of the universe, Subhadra, the sister of Baladeva, the auspicious bestower of boons, the man shall go to the city of Visnu by means of an aerial chariot that can go wherever he desires to go. After sporting about there like a god till the time of final dissolution of the universe, he will take birth as a human being. He shall then be a Brahmana who knows the Vedas. After acquiring the Yoga of Hari, he certainly attains liberation.

## \|\| 2.55.71 \|\|

*niṣkramya devatāgārātkṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*praṇamyāyatane paścādvrajettatra samāhitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After coming out from the shrine, the man shall have the feeling of satisfaction (of having obtained his life’s objects). After bowing down again to the deity in the shrine, the devotee should depart from there with great concentration.

## \|\| 2.55.72 \|\|

*indra nīlamayo viṣṇuryatrāste bālukāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*antardhāne'pi taṃ natvā tato viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Even though he has disappeared, one should bow down to the place where the sapphire idol of Visnu is buried in sand. The devotee who bows down to this place shall go to the city of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.55.73 \|\|

*sarvadevamayo devo hiraṇyakaśipūddharaḥ \|*  
*yatrāste nityadā devi siṃhārddhakṛtavigrahaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. О queen, the lord with half of his body being that of a lion (viz. Narasimha) is present there always. It was he who uplifted Hiranyakasipu. He is identical with all Devas.

## \|\| 2.55.74 \|\|

*bhaktyā dṛṣṭvā tu taṃ devaṃ praṇamya nṛhariṃ śubhe \|*  
*mucyate pātakairmartyaḥ samastairnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There is no doubt in this that by visiting that lord Nrhari and by devoutly bowing to him, О splendid lady, the man is liberated from all sins. Cf. BM. P. 57.58.

## \|\| 2.55.75 \|\|

*narasiṃhasya ye bhaktā bhavanti bhuvi mānavāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kiñcitphalaṃ ca syādyadīpsitam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those men who are devotees of Narasimha on this earth have no sin attached to them at all. They derive the benefit as desired by them.

## \|\| 2.55.76 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena narasiṃhaṃ samāśrayet \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ phalaṃ yasmātprayacchati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Since he grants the benefit of all Purusarthas, viz. virtue, wealth, love and liberation, the devotee shall by all means resort to Narasimha.

## \|\| 2.55.77 \|\|

*tasmāttaṃ brahmatanaye bhaktyā sampūjayetsadā \|*  
*mṛgarājaṃ mahāvīryaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Hence, О daughter of Brahma, the devotee should always devoutly worship the highly powerful lord of animals (Nara-Simha), the bestower of all desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.55.78-80 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ striyaḥ śūdrā ntyajādayaḥ \|*  
*sampūjya tu suraśreṣṭhaṃ bhaktāḥ siṃhavapurddharam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*mucyante cāśubhādduḥkhājjanmakoṭisamudbhavāt \|*  
*sampūjya taṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ prāpnuvantyabhivāñchitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*devatvamamareśatvaṃ dhaneśatvaṃ ca bhāmini \|*  
*yakṣavidyādharatvaṃ ca tathānyacca prayacchati \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. (All the people) — the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, Sudras, women, Antyajas (outcastes) and others shall, by worshipping with devotion, the most excellent of all gods, possessing the physical form of a lion, be liberated from inauspicious misery originating from crores of births. They attain all desired things such as the state of being a god, of being the lord of the immortal beings, the state of the lord of wealth and the state of being Yaksas and Vidyadharas. О beautiful woman, he bestows these and other things.

## \|\| 2.55.81 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣva narasiṃhasya prabhāvaṃ vidhinandini \|*  
*ajitasyāprameyasya bhuktimuktipradasya ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. О daughter of the creator, listen to the powers of Narasimha, the unconquered deity, the incomprehensible god, the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.55.82 \|\|

*kaḥ śaknoti guṇānvaktuṃ samastāṃstasya suvrate \|*  
*siṃhārddhakṛtadehasya pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. О lady of good rites, who is competent to recount fully the attributes of that deity half of whose body is that of a lion? I shall tell you succinctly.

## \|\| 2.55.83 \|\|

*yāḥ kāścitsiddhayaścātra śrūyante daivamānuṣāḥ \|*  
*prasādāttasya tāḥ sarvāḥ siddhynte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There is no doubt about this that, thanks to his grace, one shall realise those Siddhis (super-human powers) both divine and human, that are heard about.

## \|\| 2.55.84 \|\|

*svarge martye ca pātāle divi toye sure nage \|*  
*prasādāttasya devasya bhavatyavyāhatā gatiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thanks to the grace of that lord, one will have unimpeded movement in the heaven, mortal world, nether worlds, firmament, water, landmass or on a mountain.

## \|\| 2.55.85 \|\|

*asādhyaṃ tasya devasya nāstyatra sacarācare \|*  
*narasiṃhasya subhage sadā bhaktānukampinaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. О blessed lady, in this world consisting of the mobile and immobile beings, there is nothing that is unachievable to lord Narasimha who is always sympathetic to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.55.86 \|\|

*vidhānaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi bhaktānāmupakārakam \|*  
*yena prasīdate cāsau siṃhārddhakṛtavigrahaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. I shall narrate the procedure that will facilitate devotees and whereby the deity half of whose body is leonine (i.e. Narasimha) is delighted.

## \|\| 2.55.87-89 \|\|

*yattattvaṃ tasya devasya tadajñātaṃ surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*śākayāvakamūlaistu phalapiṇyākasaktubhiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*payobhakṣyeṇa vā bhadre vartate sādhakeśvaraḥ \|*  
*kāsakaupīnavāsāśca dhyānayukto jitendri yaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*araṇye vijane deśe nadīsaṅgamaparvate \|*  
*siddhakṣetre coṣare ca narasiṃhāśrame tathā \|\| 89 \|\|*

87a. The real nature of that lord is unknown even to the Devas and Asuras.

87b-89. The leader of the Sadhakas (aspirant devotees) sustains himself by means of vegetables, roots, fruits, barley grains, oil cakes, powdered fried grains or milk. He wears only a lion cloth or woven Kasa grass. With the sense organs fully conquered, he meditates on the lord seated in a secluded spot, the confluence of rivers, the mountains, the Siddhaksetra (the sacred places of the Siddhas), in a barren land or in the hermitage of Narasiriiha.

## \|\| 2.55.90-93 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāpya svayaṃ cāpi pūjāṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*upapātakavāndevi mahāpātakavānapi \|\| 90 \|\|*

*mukto bhavetpātakebhyaḥ sādhako nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ tatra narasiṃhaṃ prapūjayet \|\| 91 \|\|*

*gandhapuṣpādibhirdhūpaiḥ praṇamya śirasā prabhum \|*  
*karpūracandanāktāni jātīpuṣpāṇi mastake \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pradadyānnarasiṃhasya tataḥ siddhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*bhagavānsarvakāryeṣu na kvacitpratidūyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

90-9la. He himself instals the idol and performs the worship in accordance with the injunctions. There is no doubt about this that, even if the Sadhaka is defiled by subsidiary sins or great sins, he is liberated from them.

91b-93. The devotee should circumambulate and worship Narasimha with scents, fragrant flowers, incense etc. After bowing down the head to the lord, he shall offer the Jati flowers smeared with camphor and sandal-paste on the head of Narasimha. Thereby, Siddhi is realised. In none of these acts or (bestowing of Siddhis) the lord is thwarted.

## \|\| 2.55.94-95 \|\|

*na śaktāstaṃ samākrāntuṃ brahmarudrā dayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punardānavā loke siddhagandharvamānuṣāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*vidyādharāḥ yakṣagaṇāḥ sakinnaramahoragāḥ \|*  
*te sarve pralayaṃ yānti divyā divyāgnitejasā \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Brahma, Rudraand other gods are not competent to cross him. What then is the case of Danavas in the world, and of the Siddhas, Gandharvas, human beings, Vidyadharas, Yaksas, Kinnaras and serpents? All those divine beings are annihilated by the splendour of divine fire, (of Narasimha).

## \|\| 2.55.96-97 \|\|

*sakṛjjaptvāgniśikhayā hanyātsarvānupadra vān \|*  
*trirjaptvā kavacaṃ divyaṃ saṃrakṣeddaityadānavāt \|\| 96 \|\|*

*bhūtātpiśācādra kṣobhyo ye cānye paripaṃthinaḥ \|*  
*trirjaptaṃ kavacaṃ divyamabhedyaṃ ca surāsuraiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. By performing the Japa once, the devotee shall smite all harassing persons by the flame of fire. The performance of Japa for three times of the Divine Narasimha Kavaca (mystical syllables protective like an armour) shall protect one from Daityas Danavas, goblins, ghosts, demons as well as other enemies. The Kavaca-Mantras repeated thrice cannot be split by the Devas and suras.

## \|\| 2.55.98 \|\|

*yojanadvādaśāntastu devo rakṣati sarvadā \|*  
*narasiṃho mahābhāge mahābalaparākramaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Lord Narasimha of great strength and exploits, О highly blessed lady, always protects the devotees within twelve Yojanas (I Yojana — 4 kroSas or 8 miles).

## \|\| 2.55.99-100 \|\|

*tato gatvā biladvāramupoṣya rajanītrayam \|*  
*palāśakāṣṭhaiḥ prajvālya bhagavajjātavedasam \|\| 99 \|\|*

*pālāśasamidhaṃ tatra juhuyāttrimadhuplutām \|*  
*dve'yute kañjanayane śakaṭaścaiva sādhakaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. The devotee should thereafter go to the opening of the cave and fast there for three nights. By means of the Palana twigs, he should ignite the fire and perform Homas with the Palasa twigs soaked in Trimadhu (honey, ghee, sugar) for twenty thousand times. О lady of lotus-like eyes, a cart shall come into the view of the Sadhaka.

## \|\| 2.55.101-102 \|\|

*tataḥ kavallīvivaraṃ prakaṭaṃ jāyate kṣaṇāt \|*  
*tato viśettu niḥśaṅkaḥ kavallīvivaraṃ budhaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*gacchataḥ śakaṭasyātha tamo mohaśca naśyati \|*  
*rājamārgastu vistīrṇo dṛśyate tatra mohini \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. Then, the Kavalllvivara (the opening of KavalH1 (?) shall be revealed instantaneously. The learned devotee should unhesitatingly enter the opening. As the cart proceeds, darkness and delusion perish. О MohinI, wide highway is seen there.

## \|\| 2.55.103 \|\|

*narasiṃhaṃ smaraṃstatra pātālaṃ viśate tadā \|*  
*gatvā tatra japecchuddho narasiṃhaṃ tamavyayam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Remembering Narasimha, he should enter the nether worlds. After going there, the pure devotee should perform the Japa of the immutable Narasimha.

## \|\| 2.55.104 \|\|

*tataḥ strīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi vīṇācāmarakarmaṇām \|*  
*nirgacchanti purāccaiva svāgataṃ tā vadanti ca \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Thereafter, thousands of women shall come out of the city with lutes, chowries etc. in their hands and speak words of welcome to him.

## \|\| 2.55.105 \|\|

*praveśayanti taṃ haste gṛhītvā sādhakeśvaram \|*  
*tato rasāyanaṃ divyaṃ pāyayanti sulocane \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. О lady of beautiful eyes, they will grasp the leading Sadhaka by the hand and take him into the city. They will make him drink divine Rasayana (elixir of life).

## \|\| 2.55.106 \|\|

*pītamātre divyadeho jāyate sumahābalaḥ \|*  
*krīḍate divyakanyābhiryāvadābhūtasamplavam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The moment he drinks, he will be endowed with a divine body. He will become very strong. He will be sporting about with divine virgins until the dissolution of the universe.

## \|\| 2.55.107 \|\|

*bhinnadeho vāsudevaṃ nīyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yadā na rocayantyetāstato nirgacchate punaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. (?) With a different body, he is taken to Vasudeva.1 2 When these virgins do not appeal to him, he will come out of that place.

## \|\| 2.55.108-109 \|\|

*paṭṭaṃ śūlaṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca rocanāṃ ca maṇiṃ tathā \|*  
*rasaṃ rasāyanaṃ caiva pādukāñjanameva ca \|\| 108 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāñjali ca subhage guṭikāṃ ca manaḥ śilām \|*  
*muṇḍalāṃ cākṣasūtraṃ ca ṣaṣṭhīṃ sañjīvanīṃ tathā \|\| 109 \|\|*

108-109. (Through the grace of Narasimha) the excellent Sadhaka shall obtain a magic tablet, trident, sword, yellow pigment, jewel, mercury, elixir and the collyrium and the sandals. He shall grasp the Vidyas (lores) of Gutika (magic pills)

## \|\| 2.55.110-113 \|\|

*siddhāṃ vidyāṃ ca śāstrāṇi gṛhītvā sādhakottamaḥ \|*  
*jvaladvahnisphuliṅgormiveṣṭitaṃ tridaśaṃ hṛdi \|\| 110 \|\|*

*sakṛnnyastaṃ dahetsarvaṃ vṛjinaṃ janmakoṭijam \|*  
*viṣe nyastaṃ viṣaṃ hanyātkuṣṭhaṃ hanyāttanau sthitam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*sudehabhrūṇahatyādi kṛtvā divyena śudhyati \|*  
*mahāgrahagṛhīteṣu jvalamānaṃ vicintayet \|\| 112 \|\|*

*rudanti vai tataḥ śīghraṃ naśyeyurdāruṇā grahāḥ \|*  
*bālānāṃ kaṇṭhake baddhvā rakṣā bhavati nityaśaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

110-113. It is as though the lord in the heart is enveloped by the blazing flames of the fire. Placed but once, it burns all sins originating from crores of births. Having (mastered) the mystic lore (Siddha-Vidya) and Sastras (scriptures), the lord of Sadhakas, if places in his heart the fire enveloped with flames and burning sparks only once, it burns down all of his sins and evils perpetrated in a crore of births. Placed in poison, it destroys poison; kept on the body, it dispels even leprosy. If one kills a foetus and commits similar sins and places that divine fire on his person, he is absolved of the sins (by that divine fire). One should think of the blazing deity when overwhelmed by great evil planets. The evil and terrible planets begin to cry and they perish quickly. When the amulet is tied round the necks of children it is a perpetual protection.

## \|\| 2.55.114 \|\|

*gaṇḍapiṇḍakakṛtyānāṃ nāśanaṃ kurute dhruvam \|*  
*vyādhighāte samidbhiśca ghṛtaṃ kṣīreṇa homayet \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. It certainly destroys evil spirits such as the Ganda, Pimjaka and Krtyas. In order to dispel ailments, the devotee should perform Ноmа with the sacrificial twigs, ghee and milk.

## \|\| 2.55.115 \|\|

*trisandhyaṃ māsamekaṃ tu sarvarogānvināśayet \|*  
*asādhyaṃ nāsya paśyāmi tattvasya sacarācare \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. If this is performed during the three Sandhyas (i.e. dawn, dusk and midday) for the period of a month, it will destroy all ailments. I do not find anything in the world consisting of the mobile and immobile beings, anything that is unachievable to this Tattva (principle or lore).

## \|\| 2.55.116 \|\|

*yāṃ yāṃ kāmayate siddhiṃ tāṃ tāṃ prāpnotyapi dhruvam \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ tvekaṃ pūjayitvā mṛgādhipam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. By worshipping the lord of beasts alone for hundred and eight times, the devotee certainly attains all those Siddhis whichever he may desire.

## \|\| 2.55.117-119 \|\|

*mṛttikāṃ sapta valmīke śmaśāne ca catuṣpathe \|*  
*raktacandanasammiśrāṃ gavāṃ kṣīreṇa lepayet \|\| 117 \|\|*

*siṃhasya pratimāṃ kṛtvā pramāṇena ṣaṅgulām \|*  
*bhūrjapatre viśeṣeṇa likhedro canayā tathā \|\| 118 \|\|*

*narasiṃhasya kaṇṭhe tu baddhvā caiva samantravat \|*  
*japetsaṅkhyāvihīnaṃ tu pūjayitvā jalāśaye \|\| 119 \|\|*

117-119. In the ant-hill, in the cremation ground, and in the crossroads, the devotee should smear the oil mixed with red sandal paste and cow’s milk. With this paste he should make an idol of the lion six Angulas in length; should then write (the An obvious error for Krsnaj\\na vide the same verse repeated in the Brahma P. 58-42. The Brahma P. ibid reads kama^iahm.

## \|\| 2.55.120 \|\|

*yāvanmantraṃ tu japati saptāhaṃ saṃyatendri yaḥ \|*  
*jalākīrṇā muhūrtena jāyate sarvabhedinī \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. By the time the devotee with all his sense-organs controlled, performs the Japas for seven days, the whole earth shall be showered with water. Within a Muhurta the earth will be flooded with water.

## \|\| 2.55.121-122 \|\|

*athavā śuddhavṛkṣāgre narasiṃhaṃ tu pūjayet \|*  
*japtvā cāṣṭaśataṃ tattvaṃ varṣaṃ tadvinivārayet \|\| 121 \|\|*

*tameva piñjake baddhvā bhrāmayetsādhakottamaḥ \|*  
*mahāvāto muhūrtena āgacchennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

121-122. Alternately, the devotee should sit on the top of pure tree and worship Narasimha. By performing a hundred and eight Japas of the Tattva (Narasimha Mantra), the devotee shall ward off that rain. After placing (the idol) in a cage the excellent Sadhaka shall whirl it. Within a Mahurta a great violent gust of wind shall blow.

## \|\| 2.55.123-124 \|\|

*punaścāvārayansiktāṃ saptajaptena vāriṇā \|*  
*atha tāṃ pratimāṃ dvāre nikhanedyasya sādhakaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*gotrotsādo bhavettasya uddhṛte caiva śāntidaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvai brahmatanaye pūjayedbhaktitaḥ sadā \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. He can ward it off once again by sprinkling the idol with water charged with the Mantra seven times. If the aspirant were to put that idol under the ground at the threshold of anyone the whole of his family shall be exterminated. When it is taken out, it shall accord peace. Hence О daughter of Brahma, one shall always worship it with devotion.

## \|\| 2.55.125-126 \|\|

*mṛgarājaṃ mahāvīryaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā stutvā namaskṛtya sampūjya nṛhariṃ śubhe \|\| 125 \|\|*

*prāpnuvanti narā rājyaṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ ca durlabham \|*  
*narasiṃhaṃ naro dṛṣṭvā labhedabhimataṃ phalam \|\| 126 \|\|*

125-126. By visiting, eulogising, bowing to and worshipping Nrhari, the lord of beasts who has great prowess and who bestows all desired benefits, О splendid lady, men obtain kingdom, heavenly pleasure, and liberation (from samsara) which is very difficult to get. By seeing Narasimha, a man shall achieve the desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.55.127-132 \|\|

*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*sakṛd dṛṣṭvā tu taṃ devaṃ bhaktyā siṃhavapurddharam \|\| 127 \|\|*

*mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ kāyavākcittasambhavaiḥ \|*  
*saṅgrāme saṅkaṭe durge cauravyāghrādipīḍite \|\| 128 \|\|*

*kāntāre prāṇasandehe viṣavahnijaleṣu ca \|*  
*rājādibhīṣu saṅgrāme graharogādipīḍite \|\| 129 \|\|*

*smṛtvā taṃ yo hi puruṣaḥ saṅkaṭairvipramucyate \|*  
*sūryodaye yathā nāśaṃ tamo'bhyeti mahattaram \|\| 130 \|\|*

*tathā sandarśane tasya vināśaṃ yāntyupadra vāḥ \|*  
*guṭikāṃ janapātāle pādaleparasāyanam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*narasiṃhe prasanne tu prāpnotyanyāṃśca vāñchitān \|*  
*yānyānkāmānabhidhyāyanbhajeta nṛhariṃ naraḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

127-128a. He shall be liberated form all sins. He shall go to the world of Visnu. By visiting that lord having the leonine body, with great devotion even for once, the devotee is liberated from all sins, whether physical, verbal or mental in origin.

128b-130a. A man shall necessarily remember that lord in the following circumstances: When there is a war; when there is any difficulty; when in misery, when afflicted by thieves, tigers, etc., in the forest, when there is doubt about the safety of life, when oppressed by poison, fire or water, when there is fear from the king etc., during the day of battle, when one is afflicted by evil planets ailments etc., By remembering the lord, the man is liberated from difficulties.

130b-131a. Just as dense darkness perishes at the rise of the sun, so also all torments perish when the lord is visited.

131b-132. When Narasimha is delighted the devotee achieves theGutikas (Mystic pills), Anjana (magical collyrium), the Padalepa(unguent for the foot)and the elixir of life, enabling one to go anywhere. He achieves other desired benefits too. If a man worships Nrhari meditating on other desired results, he shall undoubtedly attain those objects.”

## Chapter 56. The Greatness of РигщоНата (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.56.1-2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- anyacchṛṇu mahābhāge tasmiñchrīpuruṣottame \|*  
*tīrthavrajaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ darśanātpāpanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*anantākhyaṃ vāsudevaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktyā praṇamya ca \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto naro yāti paraṃ padam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1-2. “O blessed lady, listen to another group of TIrtha in the holy centre of Purusottama. It is highly meritorious. By the mere sight, it destroys sins. By visiting Vasudeva termed Ananta with devotion and by bowing down to him, a man shall be liberated from all sins, he shall attain the greatest region (viz. Vaikuntha)

## \|\| 2.56.3 \|\|

*śvetagaṅgāṃ naraḥ snātvā yaḥ paśyecchvetamādhavam \|*  
*matsyākhyaṃ mādhavaṃ caiva śvetadvīpaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By taking bath in the Svetaganga1 and by visiting Sveta-Madhava as well as Matsya-Madhava, the devotee goes to Sveta Dvlpa (the abode of Narayana).

## \|\| 2.56.4-10 \|\|

*tuṣārapratimaṃ śuddhaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ puṇḍarīkāyatekṣaṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śrīvatsavakṣasā yuktaṃ suprasannaṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*vanamālāvṛtoraskaṃ mukuṭāṅgadadhāriṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pītavastraṃ supīnāṃsaṃ kuṇḍalābhyāmalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*kuśāgreṇāpi rājendra śvetagāṅgeyameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*spṛṣṭvā svargaṃ gamiṣyanti viṣṇubhaktāḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*yastvimāṃ pratimāṃ paśyenmādhavākhyāṃ śaśiprabhām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śaṅkhagokṣīrasaṅkāśāmaśeṣāghavināśinīm \|*  
*tāṃ praṇamya sakṛdbhaktyā puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vihāya sarvakāmānvai viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|*  
*manvantarāṇi tatraiva devakanyābhirāvṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*gīyamānaśca gandharvaiḥ siddhavidyādharārcitaḥ \|*  
*bhunakti vipulānbhogānyatheṣṭaṃ daivataiḥ saha \|\| 10 \|\|*

4-7a. Visnu’s devotees of great concentration and purity shall attain heaven by visiting the pure deity which resembles snow in complexion; who bears conch, discus and iron club; who is endowed with all auspicious characteristics; whose chest has the mark of Srivatsa, who is delighted, who has four arms, whose chest is covered with garlands of sylvan flowers; who wears coronet and armlets; whose garments are yellow in colour; whose shoulders are plum and who is bedecked in earrings. By touching the leading king, Svetagangeya (god Sveta- Madhava), even with the tip of a KuSa grass they go to heaven.

7b-9a. He who sees this idol of lustre called Madhava, that resembles conch and cow’s milk and that destroys all sins, he who bows to that idol with eyes resembling lotuses even but once, with devotion and eschewing worldly desires is honoured in the world of Visnu.

9b-10. For many Manvantaras, he enjoys extensive pleasures as he pleases, along with the Devas, surrounded by Divine virgins, sung in praise by the Gandharvas and worshipped by Siddhas and Vidyadharas.

## \|\| 2.56.11 \|\|

*cyutastasmādihāgatya mānuṣye brāhmaṇo bhavet \|*  
*vedavedāṅgaviddhīmān bhogavāṃścirajīvitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Falling off from these, he comes to the mortal world and is born as a Brahmana knowing the Vedas and the Vedan- gas. He will be intelligent, long-lived and enjoying worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.56.12 \|\|

*gajāśvarathayānāḍhyo dhanadhānyavṛtaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*rūpavānbahubhāgyaśca putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He will be richly endowed with elephants, horses, chariots and other vehicles. He will be pure and blessed with wealth and food-grains. He shall be handsome and very fortunate. He will have sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 2.56.13 \|\|

*puruṣottamaṃ punaḥ prāpya vaṭamūle'tha sāgare \|*  
*tyaktvā dehaṃ hariṃ smṛtvā tataḥ śāntaṃ padaṃ vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He goes again unto Purusottama on the seashore at the root of the holy Banyan tree. After abandoning the body and remembering Hari he shall go to the region of calmness and peace. (Moksa)

## \|\| 2.56.14-16 \|\|

*śvetamādhavamālokya samīpe matsyamādhavam \|*  
*ekārṇave jale pūrvaṃ rūpaṃ rohitamāsthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vedānāṃ haraṇārthāya rasātalatale sthitaḥ \|*  
*cintayitvā kṣitiṃ matsyaṃ tasminsthāne vyavasthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ādhāya taruṇaṃ rūpaṃ mādhavaṃ matsyamādhavam \|*  
*praṇamya prayato bhūtvā sarvānkaṣṭānvimuñcati \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. By visiting Svetamadhava and Matsya-madhava near him and by bowing down to him with purity, the devotee should leave off all distressing features. When formerly the whole universe was vast sheet of water, the lord had at the outset assumed the form of a fish of the Rohita type. It was to redeem the Vedas (from the demon who had stolen them) that the lord thus stationed himself on the surface of Rasatala. Thinking about the earth, the fish established itself there. Then the Matsya (fish) assumed the form of a youth. That is Matsya Madhava.

## \|\| 2.56.17 \|\|

*prayāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo hariḥ svayam \|*  
*kāle punarihāyāto rājā syātpṛthivītale \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He goes to that highly excellent place where lord Hari is present himself. In due course of time, he comes down here and shall be the king on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.56.18 \|\|

*matsyamādhavamāsādya durādharṣo bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*dātā bhoktā bhavedyoddhā vaiṣṇavaḥ satyasaṅgaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By resorting to Matsya-Madhava, a man will be invincible. He will be a liberal donor, enjoyer of pleasures, a warrior, a devotee of Visnu and true to his word.

## \|\| 2.56.19-22 \|\|

*yogaṃ prāpya hareḥ paścāttato mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*matsyamādhavamāhātmyaṃ mayā te parikīrtitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmatanaye sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*mārjanaṃ tatra vakṣyāmi mārkaṇḍeyahrade śubhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

*bhaktyā tu tanmanā bhūtvā purāṇaṃ puṇyamuktidam \|*  
*mārkaṃḍeyahrade snānaṃ sarvakālaṃ praśasyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*tadvatsnānaṃ samudra sya sarvakālaṃ praśasyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-20a. Afterwards, by being enlightened in the Yoga leading to Hari, he shall attain liberation. The greatness of Matsyamadhava has been recounted by me to you. On seeing him, О daughter of Brahma, the devotee shall attain all desires.

20b-22. I shall now describe the rite of Marjana in the sacred and auspicious pool of water called Markandeyahrada. The ablution in the Markandeyahrada at all times is praised. It is an ancient rite to plunge into it with a singleminded devotion. Particularly on the CaturdasI day, the ablution is destructive of all sins. Similarly, the ablution in the ocean at all times is praised.

## \|\| 2.56.23-25 \|\|

*paurṇamāsyāṃ viśeṣeṇa hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*pūrṇimā jyeṣṭhamāsasya jyeṣṭhā ṛkṣaṃ yadā bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadā gacchedviśeṣeṇa tīrtharājaṃ paraṃ śubham \|*  
*kāyavāṅmānasaiḥ śuddhasadbhāvo'nanyamānasaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sarvadvandvavinirmukto vītarāgo vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*kṛlpavṛkṣaṃ vaṭaṃ ramyaṃ yatra sākṣājjanārdanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-24a. Particularly, on the full moon day, (the ablution in the ocean) makes one attain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice. On the full Moon day in the month of Jyestha, when the constellation is also Jyestha, the devotee shall particulary visit that king of holy centres which is exceedingly splendid.

24b-25. He should have pure and holy Sattvaic feelings physically, verbally and mentally, and his mind should not be directed towards anything else. He should be liberated from all mutually clashing opposites. He should be devoid of passions and malicious rivalry. He should circumambulate the beautiful Kalpa-tree, the banyan tree, where Janardana himself abides.

## \|\| 2.56.26-28 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvīta trīnvārānsusamāhitaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā naśyati yatpāpaṃ saptajanmasamudbhavam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*puṇyaṃ prāpnoti vipulaṃ gatimiṣṭāṃ ca mohini \|*  
*tasya nāmāni vakṣyāmi sapramāṇaṃ yuge yuge \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vaṭaṃ vaṭeśvaraṃ śāntaṃ purāṇapuruṣaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*vaṭasyaitāni nāmāni kīrtitāni kṛtādiṣu \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-27a. With great concentration, he should circumambulate it three times. On seeing it, the sin originating from seven births perishes. О Mohini, he attains an extensive merit and his desired goal.

27b-28. I shall mention to you its names in the different Yugas. The names of the banyan tree in the Krta and other Yugas have been glorified as follows: (They know them as) Vata, Vateshvara, Santa and Purana Purusa.

## \|\| 2.56.29 \|\|

*yojanaṃ pādahīnaṃ ca yojanārddhaṃ tadarddhakam \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ kalpavṛkṣasya kṛtādiṣu yathākramam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the Krta and other Yugas, the girth of the banyan tree has been respectively one Yojana, three-fourths of a Yojana, half a Yojana and one-fourth of a Yojana.

## \|\| 2.56.30 \|\|

*pūrvoktena tu mantreṇa namaskṛtvā ca taṃ vaṭam \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhimukho gaccheddhanvantaraśatatrayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After bowing down to the banyan tree, repeating the Mantra mentioned above, the devotee should go to the south at a distance of three hundred Dhanus (bows or twelve hundred hastas or cubits).

## \|\| 2.56.31 \|\|

*yatrāsau dṛśyate cihnaṃ svargadvāraṃ manoramam \|*  
*sāgarāntaḥ samākṛṣṭaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is the place where the sign, the beautiful portals of heaven, become visible within the ocean, a log of wood equipped with all auspicious attributes has been drawn.

## \|\| 2.56.32 \|\|

*praṇipatya tatastiṣṭhetparipūjya tataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpaughaistathā pāpagrahādibhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He should bow down to it, worship it and then stand by. He shall then be liberated from all the mulitudes of sins, effects of evil planets and other inauspicious things.

## \|\| 2.56.33 \|\|

*ugrasenaḥ purā dṛṣṭvā svargadvāreṇa sāgaram \|*  
*gatvā'camya śucistatra dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ param \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Formerly, Ugrasena looked at the ocean through heavenly portals. He went there. With purity of word, mind and deed, he meditated on the supreme Narayana and performed the Acamana rite.

## \|\| 2.56.34 \|\|

*nyasedaṣṭākṣaraṃ mantraṃ paścāddhastaśarīrayoḥ \|*  
*oṃ namo nārāyaṇāyeti yaṃ vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thereafter, the devotee should fix the eight-syllabled Mantra on the hand as well as on the body.1 The Mantra is what learned men utter viz. ‘Om namo Narayanaya.

## \|\| 2.56.35 \|\|

*kiṃ kāryaṃ bahubhirmantrairmanovibhavakārakaiḥ \|*  
*namo nārāyaṇāyeti mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. What purpose is served by many Mantras causing the richness of the mind? The Mantra “Namo Narayanaya5’ is that which achieves all objects.

## \|\| 2.56.36 \|\|

*āpo narasya sūnutvānnārā iti ha kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇostāstvālayaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Apah (waters) are glorified as Nara since they are the offsprings of Nara (Man). They were the former abode of Visnu. Hence Visnu is remembered as Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.37 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaparā vedā nārāyaṇaparā dvijāḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparaṃ jñānaṃ nārāyaṇaparā kriyā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Vedas are devoted to Narayana. The Brahma- nas are devoted to Narayana. Perfect knowledge is concerned with Narayana. Holy rites are related to Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.38 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaparo dharmo nārāyaṇaparaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparaṃ dānaṃ nārāyaṇaparaṃ vratam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Dharma (virtue) is concerned with Narayana. The penance is connected with Narayana, charitable gift is concerned with Narayana; holy rites are related to Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.39 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaparāḥ lokā nārāyaparāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparaṃ nityaṃ nārāyaṇaparaṃ padam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The worlds are concerned with Narayana, the Devas are devoted to Narayana; the Nitya rites (routine holy rites) are related to Narayana. The region (to be reached) is concerned with Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.40 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaparā pṛthvī nārāyaṇaparaṃ jalam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparo vahnirnārāyaṇaparaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. (All the elements are concerned with Narayana, such as the earth is devoted to Narayana; the water is related to Narayana; the fire element is concerned with Narayana; the firmament is devoted to Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.41 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaparo vāyurnārāyaṇaparaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*ahaṅkāraśca buddhiśca ubhe nārāyaṇātmake \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Vayu (wind god) is devoted to Narayana; the mind is concerned with Narayana: the Ahamkara (Ego) and the Buddhi (Intellect) both of these are of the nature of Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.42 \|\|

*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyacca yatkiñcijjīvasaṃjñitam \|*  
*sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ paraṃ caiva sarvaṃ nārāyaṇātmakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The things of the past, present and future, whatever is termed as Jlva (living individual), the gross, the subtle and the huge, everything is of the nature of Narayana.

## \|\| 2.56.43 \|\|

*nārāyaṇātparaṃ kiñcinneha paśyāmi mohini \|*  
*tena vyāptamidaṃ sarvaṃ dṛśyādṛśyaṃ carācaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О MohinI, I do not see anything here different than Narayana; this world consisting of the visible and the invisible, the mobile, and immobile beings is pervaded by him.

## \|\| 2.56.44-45 \|\|

*āpo hyāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sa cāsāvambhasāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*tasmādapsu sa ityevaṃ nārāyaṇamaghāpaham \|\| 44 \|\|*

*snānakāle viśeṣeṇa copasthāya jale śuciḥ \|*  
*smarennārāyaṇaṃ dhyāyeddhaste kāye ca vinyaset \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Waters constitute the abode of Visnu, the ocean is the lord of waters. Hence, he is in the waters. Particularly, at the time of ablution, the devotee should worship Narayana the dispeller of sins. He should remember Narayana and meditate on him. He should then perform the Nyasa rite on the hand and on the body.

## \|\| 2.56.46-47 \|\|

*oṃkāraṃ vāmakaṭyā tu nākāraṃ dakṣiṇe tathā \|*  
*rākāraṃ nābhideśe tu yakāraṃ vāmabāhuke \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ṇākāraṃ dakṣiṇe nyasya yakāraṃ mūrdhni vinyaset \|*  
*adhaścorddhvaṃ ca hṛdaye pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhato'grataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. He should fix the syllable Ora on the left hip, the syllable ‘Na on the right hip, the syllable ‘Ra’ in the umbilical region, the syllable cYa’ in the left arm and the syllable ‘ISa in the right arm. He should fix the syllable ‘Ya on the head and then fix beneath, above, sideways, in the heart behind and in front.

## \|\| 2.56.48-50 \|\|

*dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ paścādārabhetkavacaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*pūrve māṃ pātu govindo dakṣiṇe madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*paścime śrīdharo devaḥ keśavastu tathottare \|*  
*pātu viṣṇustathāgneye nairṛte mādhavo'vyayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vāyavye tu hṛṣīkeśastatheśāne ca vāmanaḥ \|*  
*bhūtale pātu vārāhastathorddhve ca trivikramaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. The learned devotee should meditate on Narayana and thereafter begin the Kavaca (protective Mantras of mystic syllables): In the east of me may Govinda protect; may Madhusiidana protect me in my south; may lord Sridhara protect me in my west; may Kesava protect me in the north; may Visnu protect me in the south-east; may the unchanging Madhava protect me in the southwest; may Hrslkesa protect me in the north-west; may Vamana protect me in the north-east; may the Boar protect me in the earth and may Trivikrama protect me in the upward direction.

## \|\| 2.56.51 \|\|

*kṛtvaivaṃ kavacaṃ paścādātmānaṃ cintayettataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After assigning the Kavaca to various parts thus, the devotee should contemplate about himself, thus — “I am lord Narayana. the wielder of the conch, discus and iron club.”

## \|\| 2.56.52-54 \|\|

*evaṃ dhyātvā tadātmānamimaṃ mantramudīrayet \|*  
*tvamagnirdvipadāṃ nātha retodhāḥ kāmadīpanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pradhānaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jīvānāṃ prabhuravyayaḥ \|*  
*amṛtasyāraṇistvaṃ hi devayonirapāṃpate \|\| 53 \|\|*

*vṛjinaṃ hara me sarvaṃ tīrtharāja namo'stu te \|*  
*evamuccārya vidhivattataḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. After meditating on the Atman thus, the devotee.should repeat this Mantra: “You are the fire-god, О lord of bipeds; you are the discharger of the semen; you are the igniter of love’s fire. You are the chief of all living beings and individual souls; you are the unchanging lord; you are the Arani of the nectar; О lord of waters, you are the source of origin of the Devas; dispel my sins, О king of Tirthas obeisance be to you”. After uttering thus duly, he should perform the rite of ablution according to injunctions.

## \|\| 2.56.55 \|\|

*anyathā brahmatanaye snānaṃ tatra na śasyate \|*  
*kṛtvā cābdaivatairmatrairabhiṣekaṃ ca mārjanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Otherwise, О daughter of Brahma, the bath there is not commended. The devotee should perform the rite of ablution and Marjana (sprinkling) within water with those Mantras the deities of which are the waters.

## \|\| 2.56.56-58 \|\|

*antarjale japanpaścāttrirāvṛtyāghamarṣaṇam \|*  
*hayamedho yathā devi sarvapāpaharaḥ kratuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ cātra sūktaṃ sarvāghamarṣaṇam \|*  
*uttīrya vāsasī dhaute nirmale paridhāya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*prāṇānāyamya cācamya sandhyāṃ copāsya bhāskaram \|*  
*upātiṣṭhettataścorddhvaṃ kṣiptvā puṣpajalāñjalim \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-57a. Then he should repeat the Mantra of Agha- marsana. О gentle lady, just as the horse-sacrifice is a Yajna that dispels sins, so also the hymn of Aghamarsana1 dispels all sins.

57b-58.He should then come out of water and wear clean washed clothes. He should then restrain his breath, perform Acamana rite and worship the sun by way of Sandhya. He should then offer in the upward direction a handful of water and flowers.

## \|\| 2.56.59 \|\|

*upasthāyorddhvabāhuśca talliṅgairbhāskaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*gāyatrīṃ pāvanīṃ devīṃ japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. With the arms raised up, he should worship the sun by means of the Mantras his symbols. Thereafter, he should repeat the holy and divine Gayatrl Mantra hundred and eight times.

## \|\| 2.56.60 \|\|

*anyāṃśca sauramantrānhi japtvā tiṣṭhansamāhitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ sūryaṃ namaskṛtyopaviśya ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Standing there with concentration, he should repeat other Mantras also pertaining to the sun. He should then circumambulate and bow to the sun and be seated.

## \|\| 2.56.61-68 \|\|

*svādhyāyaṃ prāṅmukhaḥ kṛtvā tarpayeddevamānavān \|*  
*ṛṣīnpitṝnhi svīyāṃśca vidhivannāmagotravit \|\| 61 \|\|*

*toyena tilamiśreṇa vidhivatsusamāhitaḥ \|*  
*śrāddhe havanakāle ca pāṇinaikena nirvapet \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tarpaṇe tūbhayaṃ kuryādeṣa eva vidhiḥ sadā \|*  
*anvārabdhena savyena pāṇinā dakṣiṇena tu \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tṛpyatāmiti suvyaktaṃ nāmagotreṇa vāgyataḥ \|*  
*kāyasthairyastilairmohātkaroti pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tarpitāstena pitarastvaṅmāṃsarudhirāsthibhiḥ \|*  
*jale sthitvā sthale dattaṃ sthale sthitvā jale'pitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*nopatiṣṭhati tattoyaṃ yadbhūmyāṃ na pradīyate \|*  
*pitṝṇāmakṣayaṃ sthānaṃ mahī dattā virañcinā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tasmāttatraiva dātavyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītimicchatā \|*  
*bhūmistena samutpannā bhūmyāṃ caiva tu saṃsthitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*bhūmyāṃ caiva layaṃ yānti bhūmau dadyāttato jalam \|*  
*āstīrya ca kuśānsāgrānāvāhya svasvamantrataḥ \|*  
*prācīnāgreṣu vai devānyāmyāgreṣu tathā pitṝn \|\| 68 \|\|*

61-62a. He should then face the east and recite Veda- Mantras as Svadhyaya. Then the Tarpana rite of the Devas, human beings, sages and the Pitrsofhis own family should be duly performed by the devotee who is the knower of names and Gotra. He should perform the Tarpana rite with water mixed 'with sesame seeds, according to prescribed injunction and with concentration of mind.

62b-64a. During Sraddha and the Havana (oblations to fire) rites the devotee should perform the same with a single hand. The rite of Tarpana shall be performed with both the hands. This is the standing injunction. He should perform the rite with the right hand supported by the left (?) “May they be satiated”. He shall utter these words clearly uttering the name and the Gotra but silently otherwise.

64b-65a. If anyone out of delusion performs the Tarpana rite for the Pitrs, by means of gingelly seeds clinging to the body, it is as though the Tarpana rite has been performed by means of skin, flesh, blood and bones.

65b-67a. The water libation will not reach the Pitre, if the devotee stands in water and offers on to the ground or if he stands on the ground and offers it into the water. The water should be offered standing on the ground and on to the ground. What is not offered on the ground does not reach (the Pitrs). The earth has been given by Brahma as the imperishable (eternal) place of the Pitrs. Hence (the libation) should be given only there, by the person who wishes for the pleasure of the Pitrs.

67b-68a. The earth is born out of water; the water is present therein and gets dissolved in the earth. Hence, one should offer water on the ground.

68b,c. He should spread the Kusa grass on the ground and invoke the Pitrs or the Devas by their respective Mantras. In respect of the Devas, the tips of the Kusa grass shall be towards the east, and in the case of the Pitrs (manes) they shall be towards the south.

## Chapter 57. The Glory of Purusottama: The Procedure of Worship

## \|\| 2.57.1-3 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- devān ṛṣīnpitṝṃścānyānsantarpyācamya vāgyataḥ \|*  
*hastamātraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ caturdvāraṃ suśobhanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puraṃ vilikhya vidhije tīre tasya mahodadheḥ \|*  
*madhye tatra likhetpadmamaṣṭapatraṃ sakarṇikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*evaṃ maṇḍalamālikhya pūjayettatra mohini \|*  
*aṣṭākṣaravidhānena nārāyaṇamajaṃ vibhum \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1-3. After performing the rite ofTarpana to gods, sages, Pitrs and others, the pilgrim should silently perform Acamana (religious sipping of water). О daughter of Brahma, he should draw a square of the side of a Hasta (a cubit of about eighteen inches). Is should be beautiful and should have four entrances. It represents the city of Purusottama on the shore of the great ocean. In its middle, he should draw the mystic diagram of a lotus with eight petals and the pericarp. О Mohini, he should draw the mystic diagram and worship in it, Lord Narayana, the unborn eternal deity, in accordance with the same injunctions as in the case of eight-syllabled Mantra.

## \|\| 2.57.4 \|\|

*atha te sampravakṣyāmi kāyaśodhanamuttamam \|*  
*kṣakāraṃ hṛdaye cintyaṃ raktaṃ rephasamanvitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Henceforth, I shall explain fully to you the excellent mode of purification of the physical body. The syllable Ksa in the company of the syllable Ra is red and should be thought of in the heart.

## \|\| 2.57.5 \|\|

*jvalantaṃ triśikhaṃ caiva dahantaṃ pāpasañcayam \|*  
*candra maṇḍalamadhyasthamekāraṃ mūrdhni cintayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On his head, he should think of the syllable ‘E’ as stationed in the middle of the dice of the moon and having three blazing ‘Sikhas burning down the heaps of the sins of the world.

## \|\| 2.57.6 \|\|

*śuklavarṇaṃ pravarṣantamamṛtaṃ plāvayanmahīm \|*  
*evaṃ nirddhūtapāpastu divyadehastato bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It is white in colour and it showers nectar flooding the earth. The devotee who has shaken off sins, thus shall thereafter become one with a divine body.

## \|\| 2.57.7 \|\|

*aṣṭākṣaraṃ tato mantraṃ nyaseddehātmanorbudhaḥ \|*  
*vāmapādaṃ samārabhya kramaśaścaiva vinyaset \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The learned devotee, should then fix the eight syllabled Mantra in the body as well as in the Atman. He should fix it beginning with the left foot and proceed gradually.

## \|\| 2.57.8 \|\|

*pañcāṅgaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ caiva caturvyūhaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*karaśuddhiṃ prakurvīta mūlamantreṇa sādhakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. With the Mtila mantra, the aspirant should perform the rite of purification of the hand. The Nyasa rite shall have five subsidiary limbs and four manifestations of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.57.9 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ caiva varṇaṃ tu aṅgulīṣu pṛthak pṛthak \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ pṛthivī śuklaṃ vāmapāde tu vinyaset \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He should fix each of the syllables separately on the fingers. The syllable OM is the earth. He should fix it on the left foot. It is white in colour.

## \|\| 2.57.10 \|\|

*nakārastu bhuvaḥ śyāmo dakṣiṇe tu vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*mokāraṃ kālamevāhurvāmakaṭyāṃ nidhāpayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The syllable na is dark-coloured. It is the Bhuvah (the world). It is fixed on the right foot. They call the syllable mo as Kala (Time) alone. It must be fixed in the left hip.

## \|\| 2.57.11 \|\|

*nākāraṃ pūrvabījaṃ tu dakṣiṇasyāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*rākārasteja ityāhurnābhideśe vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The syllable na (which is the previous seed) is established in the southern right side. They call ra the refulgence (the Fire element) and it is stabilised in the umbilical region.

## \|\| 2.57.12 \|\|

*vāyavyo'ya yakārastu vāmaskandhe samāśritaḥ \|*  
*ṇākāraḥ sarvadā jñeyo dakṣiṇāṃse vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The syllable ya is of gaseous nature and it has resorted to the left shoulder. The syllable na shall always be known to have been stablished in the right shoulder.

## \|\| 2.57.13-14 \|\|

*yakāro'ya śirasthaśca yatra lokā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ hṛdaye nyasya vikāraṃ vā śirasyatha \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ṣṇakāraṃ vai śikhāyāṃ tu vekāraṃ kavace nyaset \|*  
*nakāraṃ netrayostu syānmakāraṃ cāstramīritam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The syllable^ is stationed on the head, where the worlds are also stabilised. After fixing Ornkara in the heart, the syllable ‘vi’ on the head, the syllable ‘sna’ on the tuft and the syllable ‘ve’ in the Kavaca (coat of mail). He shall fix na in the eyes. The syllable mah is said to be the ‘Astra ‘miraculous weapon’.

## \|\| 2.57.15 \|\|

*lalāṭe vāsudevastu śuklavarṇaḥ samāsthitaḥ \|*  
*raktaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaścaiva mukhe vahnyarkasannibhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The (deity) Vasudeva is of white colour. It is fixed in the forehead. (He is stationed on the forehead) The deity Samkarsana is red. He is fixed in the mouth. He resembles the fire and the sun.

## \|\| 2.57.16 \|\|

*pradyumno hṛdaye pīto'niruddho mehane sthitaḥ \|*  
*sarvāṅge sarvaśaktiśca caturvyūhārcito hariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. (The manifestation called ‘Pradyumna’ is yellow in colour and is assigned in the heart and the Vyuha (manifestation) known as Aniruddha is stationed at the sex-organ. Hari thus pervades all limbs. The Almighty one is worshipped thus in his four-fold manifestations (Vyuhas) Вг. P. 57.11a reads; Sarva-bfja.

## \|\| 2.57.17 \|\|

*mamāgre'vasthito viṣṇuḥ pṛṣṭhataścāpi keśavaḥ \|*  
*govindo dakṣiṇe pārśve vāme tu madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Visnu is present in front of me; Kesava abides behind me; Govinda is present on the right side; Madhusudana is present on the left side.

## \|\| 2.57.18 \|\|

*upariṣṭāttu vaikuṇṭho vārāhaḥ pṛthivītale \|*  
*avāntaradiśo yāstu tāsu sarvāsu mādhavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Vaikuntha is present above, and Varaha /the Divine Boar) on the ground. Madhava is present in all those intermediate quarters between the main directions.

## \|\| 2.57.19 \|\|

*gacchatastiṣṭhato vāpi jāgrataḥ svapato'pi vā \|*  
*narasiṃhakṛtā guptirvāsudevamayo hyaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. My protection is effected by Narasimha whether I go or stay, whether I keep awake or am asleep. I am identical with Vasudeva.

## \|\| 2.57.20 \|\|

*evaṃ viṣṇumayo bhūtvā tataḥ karma samārabhet \|*  
*yathā dehe tathā deve sarvatattvāni yojayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After becoming identical with Visnu thus, the devotee should begin the rite. He should combine all the principles with the Deva, just as is done in the case of the physical body.

## \|\| 2.57.21 \|\|

*phakārāntaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ sarvavighnaharaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatrārkacandra vahnīnāṃ maṇḍalāni vicintayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That which ends with the syllable ‘plia’ is cited to be auspicious and destructive of all obstacles. He shall think of the spheres of the sun, moon and fire.

## \|\| 2.57.22-23 \|\|

*padmamadhye nyasedviṣṇuṃ bhuvanasyāntarasya tu \|*  
*tato vicintya thṛdaye praṇavaṃ jyotiruttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*karṇikāyāṃ samāsīnaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*aṣṭākṣaraṃ tato mantraṃ nyaseccaiva yathākramam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. In the middle of the lotus of the internal side of the cosmos, the devotee shall fix Visnu. Thereafter, he should mentally think of the excellent lustre, Pranava (om) seated in the pericarp, the eternal being of the form of brilliance. Thereafter, he should perform the Nyasa rite of the eight-syllabled Mantra in due order.

## \|\| 2.57.24 \|\|

*tena vyastasamastena pūjanaṃ paramaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*dvādaśākṣaramantreṇa yajeddevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The worship by means of that Mantra in the state of analysis and synthesis (Vyasta-Samasta) is remembered to be great: He should then worship the eternal lord by means of the twelve-syllabled Mantra.

## \|\| 2.57.25 \|\|

*tato'vadhārya hṛdaye karṇikāyāṃ bahirnyaset \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ mahāsatvaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He should then retain in the heart the immense being with four arms and lustre equal to that of crores of suns.

## \|\| 2.57.26-29 \|\|

*cintayitvā mahāyogaṃ tataścāvāhayetkramāt \|*  
*mīnarūpāvahaścaiva narasiṃhaśca vāmanaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*āyāntu devā varadā mama nārāyaṇāgrataḥ \|*  
*sumeruḥ pādapīṭhaṃ te padmakalpitamāsanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sarvatattvahitārthāya tiṣṭha tvaṃ madhusūdana \|*  
*pādyaṃ te pādayordeva padmanābha sanātana \|\| 28 \|\|*

*viṣṇo kamalapatrākṣa gṛhāṇa madhusūdana \|*  
*madhuparkaṃ mahādeva brahmādyaiḥ kalpitaṃ mayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. After thinking about the great Yoga, he should invoke the following deities in due order: (The Mantra for invocation): “O Narayana, may these Devas, the bestowers of boons come in front of me viz. he who has assumed the form of the Fish, Narasimha and Vamana.” Nydsa is the assignment of the various parts of the body to different deities (or syllables of Mantras). It is accompanied with particular Mantra, syllable or prayer to corresponding gesticulations. Literally: Vyasta — ‘inherent in or pervading all the several parts of anything/ while Samasta = ‘inherent in or pervading the whole of anything. (The Mantra for offering a seat.) “Sumeru is the pedestal for your feet. The seat has been made in the form of the lotus. О Madhusiidana, stay behind for the benefit of all living beings’. (The Mantra for Padya) ‘‘O eternal lord Padmanabha, the Padya (water for washing feet) is offered at your feet. О Visnu, О deity with the eyes like the petals of the lotus, О Madhusiidana, accept it. (The Mantra for Madhuparka and Arghya) cO great lord, accept Madhuparka prepared by me. Accept it in the company of Brahma and others. О Purusottama, accept the Arghya devoutly offered by me.

## \|\| 2.57.30-33 \|\|

*niveditaṃ ca bhaktyārghaṃ gṛhāṇa puruṣottama \|*  
*mandākinyāstato vāri sarvapāpaharaṃ śivam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gṛhāṇācamanīyaṃ tvaṃ mayā bhaktyā niveditam \|*  
*tvamāpaḥ pṛthivī caiva jyotistvaṃ vāyureva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*lokasandhṛtimātreṇa vāriṇā snāpayāmyaham \|*  
*devatantusamāyukte yajñavarṇasamanvite \|\| 32 \|\|*

*svarṇavarṇaprabhe deva vāsasī pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*śarīraṃ ca na jānāmi ceṣṭāṃ ca tava keśava \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. (The Mantra for Acamanlya): “The water of the Mandakini (the Ganga) is auspicious. It dispels all sins. Accept that as the water for the rite of Acamana. It has been offered by me with great devotion.” (The Mantra for bath): “You are the water, the earth, the fiery (element) and the wind (element). I am bathing you with the water that alone supports the worlds.” (The Mantra for offering clothes): “May these two clothes be accepted; they are woven with the divine yarn; they have the colour of the Yajria and they have the lustre and the glitter of gold.” (The Mantra for smearing the Lord with unguents): “O Kesava, neither your body nor your activities do I know perfectly.

## \|\| 2.57.34-36 \|\|

*mayā niveditaṃ gandhaṃ pratigṛhya vilipyatām \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmamantreṇa trivṛtaṃ padmayoninā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sāvitrīgranthisaṃyuktamupavītaṃ tavārpyate \|*  
*divyaratnasamāyuktā vahnibhānusamaprabhāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*gātrāṇi śobhayiṣyanti alaṅkārāstu mādhava \|*  
*sūryācandra masorjyotirvidyudagnyostathaiva ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. May the unguent offered by me be accepted and smeared.” (The Mantra for offering a sacred thread): “The sacred thread which has been made of three turns by the Lotus- born god with Mantras of Rk, Yajus and Saman and is equipped with the knot called Savitri, has been dedicated to you.” (The Mantra for decorating with ornaments): “O Madhava, the ornaments consisting of divine jewels and having the lustre of the fire and the sun will make your limbs splendid- looking”. The Mantra for waving lights): “O lord of the luminaries, you alone are the fiery refulgence of the sun and the moon of the lightning and the fire. May this light be accepted.’

## \|\| 2.57.37 \|\|

*tvameva jyotiṣāṃ deva dīpo'ya pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*vanaspatiraso divyo gandhāḍhyaḥ surabhiśca te \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. (The Mantra for offering incense): “This fragrant vegetable juice divine and presented along with sweat scents is for you. May this incense offered to you devoutly by me be accepted.’

## \|\| 2.57.38 \|\|

*mayā nivedito bhaktyā dhūpo'ya pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*annaṃ caturvidhaṃ svādu rasaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ samanvitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. (The Mantra for offering food as Naivedya): “Tasty cooked foodoffour kinds has been offered to you with devotion. It has six tastes in the varieties of dishes. О Kesava, this is the Naivedya unto you.”

## \|\| 2.57.39-41 \|\|

*mayā niveditaṃ bhaktyā naivedyaṃ tava keśava \|*  
*pūrve dale vāsudevaṃ yāmye saṅkarṣaṇaṃ nyaset \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pradyumnaṃ paścime kuryādaniruddhaṃ tathottare \|*  
*vārāhaṃ ca tathāgneye narasiṃhaṃ ca nairṛte \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ mādhavaṃ caiva tathaiśāne trivikramam \|*  
*tathāṣṭākṣaradevasya garuḍaṃ parito nyaset \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. The devotee should perform the Nyasa in the petal in the east; that of Samkarsana in the petal in the south; that of Pradyumna in the petal in the west, and that ofAnuruddha in the petal in the north. He should perform the Nyasa of the Varaha incarnation in the south-east; that of Narasimha in the south-west; that of Madhava in the north-west, that of Trivikrama in the north-east. He shall perform the Nyasa of Garuda, in front of the lord of the eight- syllabled Mantra.

## \|\| 2.57.42-43 \|\|

*vāmapārśve tathā cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset \|*  
*tathā mahāgadāṃ caiva nyaseddevasya dakṣiṇe \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tataḥ śārṅgadhanurvidvānnyaseddevasya vāmataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇe ceṣudhī divye khaḍgaṃ vāme ca vinyaset \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. He should fix the discus on the left side and the conch on the right side. The great iron club also should be fixed on the right hand side of the lord. Then the scholarly devotee should fix the bow to the left of the lord. The divine quiver shall be fixed on the right hand side and the sword on the left.

## \|\| 2.57.44-45 \|\|

*śriyaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sthāpya puṣṭimuttarato nyaset \|*  
*vanamālāṃ ca puratastataḥ śrīvatsakaustubhau \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vinyaseddhṛdayādīni pūrvādiṣu caturṣvapi \|*  
*tato'stra devadevasya koṇe caiva tu vinyaset \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. After fixing Sri to the south side, the devotee should fix Pusti to the north side and the Vana-mala (the garland of sylvan flowers) as well as the Srivatsa mark and Kaustubha gem in front of the Lord. He should fix the heart etc. in the four quarters beginning with the east. Thereafter, he shall fix the weapou of the lord of the Devas in the corner.

## \|\| 2.57.46-53 \|\|

*indra magniṃ yamaṃ caiva nirṛtiṃ varuṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*vāyuṃ dhanadamīśānamanantaṃ brahmaṇā saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pūjayettānsvakairmantrairadhaścordhvaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*evaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ maṇḍalasthaṃ janārdanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*labhedabhimatānkāmānnaro nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva vidhānena maṇḍalasthaṃ janārdanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ yastu paśyetsa praviśedviṣṇumavyayam \|*  
*sakṛdapyarcito yena vidhinānena keśavaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*janmamṛtyujarāstīrtvā viṣṇoḥ padamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaḥ smaretsatataṃ bhaktyā nārāyaṇamatandri taḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*anvahaṃ tasya vāsāya śvetadvīpaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*oṃkārādisamāyuktaṃ namaskāraṃ tadīyakam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sanāmasarvatattvānāṃ maṃtra ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*anenaina vidhānena gandhapuṣpaṃ nivedayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ekaikasya prakurvīta yathoddiṣṭaṃ krameṇa tu \|*  
*mudrā stato nibadhnīyādyathoktikramaveditam \|\| 53 \|\|*

46-48a. He should worship the following deities (the guardians of the quarters): Viz. Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirfti, Varuna, Vayu, Dhanada (Kubera), liana, Ananta and Brahma. He should worship them with their respective Mantras (in the respective quarters) and below as well as above. By worshipping thus the lord of the Devas, Janardana, stationed in the Mystic diagram, the man shall attain cherished desires

48b-50a. He who sees this Janardana stationed in the mystic diagram worshipped in accordance with this injunction, shall enter the unchanging Visnu. He, by whom Kesava is worshipped at least once in this manner shall surmount (the difficulties of bath, old age and death and attain the region of Visnu.

50b-51a. SvetadvTpa is glorified for the daily residence of that person who devoutly remembers Narayana continuously and diligently.

51b-52a. That Mantra which begins with ‘Orii Namah’ (Lit: that which contains ‘Namaskara’ accompanied with Orh at the beginning) and is embellished with word ‘Namah’ at the end (that is the Mantra: Orh namo Naray- anaya namah) is regarded as the name (or illuminator) of all principles.

52b-53. In the same order of procedure, he should offer scents and fragrant flowers unto each in the manner prescribed. He shall show the eight mystic Mudras (gestures) as indicated in the order mentioned above.

## \|\| 2.57.54 \|\|

*japaṃ caiva prakurvīta mūlamantreṇa tattvavit \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśatimaṣṭau vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He should perform Japa by means of the Mula Mantra eight, twentyeight or hundred and eight times. The knower of reality shall do thus.

## Chapter 58. The Creation of the Cosmic Egg

## \|\| 2.58.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- evaṃ sampūjya vidhivadbhaktyā taṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā paścātsāgaraṃ ca prasādayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said: —

1\. After duly and devoutly worshipping Purusottama. the devotee should bow down his head and propitiate the ocean with the following Mantra.

## \|\| 2.58.2 \|\|

*prāṇastvaṃ sarvabhūtātāṃ viśvasminsaritāṃ pate \|*  
*tīrtharāja namaste'stu trāhi māmacyutapriya \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “In the whole universe, О lord of rivers, you are the vital air (Prana) of all living beings, О Tirtharaja (King of holy centres), obeisance be to you. Save me, О favourite of Acyuta.”

## \|\| 2.58.3-4 \|\|

*snātvaivaṃ sāgare samyak tasmin kṣetravare śubhe \|*  
*tīre cābhyarcya vidhivannārāyaṇamanāmayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*rāmaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ subhadrā ṃ! ca praṇipatya ca sāgaram \|*  
*śatānāmaśvamedhānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. After duly taking the holy dip in the ocean, in that auspicious and excellent holy centre and after duly worshipping Narayana devoid of ailments and blemishes on the shore (of ocean), and after bowing down to Rama, Krsna and Subhadra, the devotee should worship the ocean. Thereby, the man attains the benefit of hundreds of horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.58.5-6 \|\|

*sarvapāpavinirmktaḥ sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*vṛndārakahariḥ śrīmān rūpayauvanagarvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena divyagandharvanādinā \|*  
*kulaikaviṃśatiṃ dhṛtvā viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. He shall be absolved of all sins. He shall be freed from all miseries. Like Hari, he shall be glorious and surrounded by the Devas. He can justifiably feel proud of beauty and youth. In an aerial chariot having the lustre of the sun and with the harmonious divine music of the Gandharvas, he shall take twentyone generations of his family and go to the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.58.7 \|\|

*bhuktvā tatra varānbhogānkrīḍitvā ca suraissaha \|*  
*cyutastasmādihāyāto brāhmaṇo brahmavittamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After enjoying various excellent pleasures there and after playing with the Devas (he will exhaust his merit and) fall off from that world. After coming here, he becomes a Brah- mana, the most excellent knower of the Brahman.

## \|\| 2.58.8 \|\|

*yaśasvī matimāñchrīmānsatyavādī jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*vedaśāstrārthavidvipro bhavetpaścāttu vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He shall then be famous, intelligent, glorious and truthful. He shall have mastery over the sense-organs. He shall become a Brahmana fully conversant with the meanings of the Vedic and scriptural texts. Then he shall be a devotee of Visnu. vide the Brahma P. Ch. 62 for comparison. Most of the verses (Viz. 1-23) in these chapters of the NP. and Brahma P. are common. The NP. however tells a different episode about the transformation of the sea-water from sweetness to saltishness (from v. 23 onwards)

## \|\| 2.58.9-11 \|\|

*yogaṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ prāpya tato mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*grahoparāge saṅkrāntyāmayane viṣuve tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yugādiṣu ca manvādau vyatīpāte dinakṣaye \|*  
*āṣāḍhyāṃ caiva kārtikyāṃ māghyāṃ vānyaśubhe tithau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ye tvatradānaṃ viprebhyaḥ prayacchanti sumedhasaḥ \|*  
*phalaṃ sahasraguṇitamanyatīrthāllabhanti te \|\| 11 \|\|*

9a. After attaining the Yoga pertaining to Visnu, he shall attain liberation.

9b-11. The men of good intellect should offer charitable gifts on the following occasions — during the eclipses, during the transit of the sun (from one house of Zodiac to another), and on both tropical and equinotical transits, on the inaugural days of the Manvantaras and Yugas, during Vyatlpatas, when the days dwindle in length, during the full-moon days in the months of Asatjha, Karttika and Magha and other auspicious Tithis. They then attain thousand times the benefit (as compared with that) derived from other holy centres.1

## \|\| 2.58.12 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ ye prayacchanti piṇḍaṃ tatra vidhānataḥ \|*  
*akṣayāṃ pitarasteṣāṃ tṛptiṃ samprāpnuvanti vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If the devotees offer balls of rice to the Pitrs there, in accordance with the injunctions, the Pitrs derive everlasting satisfaction.

## \|\| 2.58.13-15 \|\|

*evaṃ snānaphalaṃ samyak sāgarasya mayeritam \|*  
*dānasya ca phalaṃ devi piṇḍadānasya caiva hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dharmārthamokṣaphaladamāyuḥkīrtiyaśaskaram \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*nāstikāya na vaktavyaṃ śaṭhāya kṛpaṇāya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Thus, О gentle lady, the benefit of the holy bath in the ocean has been recounted by me. So also the benefit of the charitable gifts and the offerings of Pindas has been mentioned.

## \|\| 2.58.14 \|\|

*dharmārthamokṣaphaladamāyuḥkīrtiyaśaskaram \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It is the bestower of the benefit of virtue, wealth, and liberation. It grants longevity, fame and renown. It yields worldly pleasures and liberation (from Samsara) for men. It is conducive to wealth. It dispels the effects of evil dreams. It is meritorious. It annihilates all sins and bestows all desired benefits. It (this knowledge) should not be imparted to an atheist, to a knave or to a miser.

## \|\| 2.58.16 \|\|

*tāvadgarjjaṃti tīrthāni māhātmyaiḥ svaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak \|*  
*yāvanna tīrtharājasya māhātmyaṃ varṇyate dvijaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As long as the greatness of the Tirtharaja1 2 is not described by the Brahmanas, other holy centres roar with their own respective greatness separately,

## \|\| 2.58.17 \|\|

*puṣkarādīni tīrthāni prayacchanti svakaṃ phalam \|*  
*tīrtharājaḥ samudra stu sarvatīrthaphalapradaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Puskara and other Tlrthas grant only their own respective benefits. But the Tirtharaja, the ocean is the bestower of the benefit of all the Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.58.18 \|\|

*bhūtale yāni tīrthāni saritaśca sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*viśanti sāgare tāni tena vai śreṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Whichever Tirthas, holy rivers and the lakes exist on the surface of the earth, they enter the ocean. Hence it has verily attained the excellence.

## \|\| 2.58.19 \|\|

*rājā samastatīrthānāṃ sāgaraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsamastatīrthebhyaḥ śreṣṭho'sau sarvakāmadaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The ocean, the lord of the rivers, is the king of all Tirthas. Hence, it is superior to all other Tirthas. It is the bestower of all desires.

## \|\| 2.58.20 \|\|

*tamo nāśaṃ yathābhyeti bhāskare'bhyudite sati \|*  
*koṭyo navanavatyastu yatra tīrthāni santi vai \|\| 20 \|\|*

20a. When the sun rises up, the darkness perishes/(so also the sin perishes in a place).

20b. On the ocean there are ninety-nine crores of Tirthas. Hence whatever is performed there (on the seashore) such as ablution, charitable gift, Ноmа, Japa and worship of the Devas, is declared to be everlasting in the Sastras. Mohini enquired:

## \|\| 2.58.21-22 \|\|

*tasmātsnānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca homaṃ japyaṃ surārcanam \|*  
*yatkiñcitkriyate tatra tadakṣayamitīritam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mohinyuvāca- sarveṣu tu samudre ṣu kṣāro'ya saritāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ jāto guro brūhi sarvajño'si yato dvija \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Among all the oceans, how did this lord of rivers become briny? О Preceptor, tell me, since О Brahmana, you are omniscient.1 Vasu narrated:

## \|\| 2.58.23 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu vakṣyāmi subhage kṣāratvaṃ cāsya vāridheḥ \|*  
*yathā prāptaḥ purāsīcca mātrāsya jagatāmapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О lady of good fortune, listen. I shall explain the saltish state of this ocean and how this had been cursed by his mother who was the mother of the worlds.

## \|\| 2.58.24 \|\|

*purā sṛṣṭikrame jātāḥ samudrā ḥ! sapta mohini \|*  
*rādhikāgarbhasambhūtā divyadehāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Mohini, formerly in the process of creation there had been born seven oceans, born of the womb of Radha. They had divine physical bodies of various kinds.

## \|\| 2.58.25 \|\|

*ekadā rādhikānāthaḥ kāntayā saha saṅgataḥ \|*  
*āste vṛndāvane sākṣādgopagopīgavāṃpatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Once, the lord of Radha, the lord of cowherds, cowherd-lasses and cows was indulging in sexual intercourse with his lady love in the Vrndavana forest.

## \|\| 2.58.26 \|\|
