*rāsamaṇḍalamadhye tu sudīpte maṇimaṇḍape \|*  
*susnigdhayā samāyuktaḥ śṛṅgāre kāntayā tayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the middle of the group of Rasa dances, in the brilliant-jewelled Man^apa, he was in passionate union with his affectionate lady love.

## \|\| 2.58.27-28 \|\|

*te sapta sāgarā bālāḥ stanyapānakṛtakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*tataste sarvato dṛṣṭvā mātaraṃ tāṃ jagatprasūm \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṣudhārtāśca rudantastu āsedurmaṇimaṇḍapam \|*  
*tatra jagmustu te sarve stanyapānakṛtekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Those seven children, the oceans, could not see their mother, the mother of the universe, when the time for their breast-feeding had arrived. Weeping on being over-whelmed with hunger, they reached the jewelled Mantfapa. They went near it, eager to have their breast-feed.

## \|\| 2.58.29-35 \|\|

*sarve nivāritāścāpi dvārasthairvallavīgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*viviśuśca bhṛśaṃ kruddhā bālakāste stanārthinaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*upekṣitā gopikābhirmāturutsaṅgavartinaḥ \|*  
*tatastu prarudanto vai te gatvā maṇimaṇḍapam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*uccaiḥ pracukruśurdevi mātaḥ kvāsītivādinaḥ \|*  
*yadā nāhvayate mātā bālakāṃstānstanārthinaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tadā kaniṣṭhaḥ sarveṣāṃ viveśāyaṃ ratisthalam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā svasutaṃ rādhā mugdhaṃ śṛṅgārabhaṅgadam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śaśāpa kṣubhitā bhadre bhūrlokaṃ yāta mā ciram \|*  
*yataḥ śṛṅgārabhaṅgaṃ tu mama kartuṃ samudyatāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tato yūyaṃ bhuvaṃ gatvā sthāsyathaikākinaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ māturjagaddhātr! yā virañcije \|\| 34 \|\|*

*atyuccai ruruduḥ sarve viyogabhayakātarāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prasanno bhagavāñchrīkṛṣṇaḥ praṇatārtihā \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-30a. All of them were stopped by the groups of cowherdesses stationed at the entrance. The angry children impatient to have their usual breastfeed forced their entry into the МашДара. Thinking that they were only babies in the lap of their mother, the children were let in by the cowherdesses.

30b-32a. Then they went into the jewelled Mantjapa crying bitterly, “O mother, where are you?”. О queen, when the mother did not respond to the call of those children seeking breast-milk, the youngest of them all entered the actual spot of the mother’s sexual dalliance.

32b-34a. On seeing her deluded sons unwittingly causing a break in her sexual dalliance, the agitated mother, О gentle lady, cursed them — “All of you go ere long to the world of earth since you had attempted to cause break in my sexual dalliance. After going to the earth, your sons will be staying there separately alone.”

34b-35. О daughter of Brahma, on hearing the worlds of their mother, the mother of the universe, all those children cried aloud (as they were) extremely frightened of the impending separation. Thereafter, Lord Sri Kpsna, the destroyer of the anguish of those who bow down, became pleased with them.

## \|\| 2.58.36-37 \|\|

*mā bhaiṣṭa putrāstiṣṭhāmi samīpe bhavatāmaham \|*  
*dra varūpā bhavantastu pṛthagrūpacarāḥ sadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vartadhvaṃ kṣāratāṃ yātu kaniṣṭho'bhyantare sthitaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā jagannātho bālakānvisasarja ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. “O sons, do not be afraid. I shall stand near you. All of you shall be in the liquid state always with separate forms and movements. This youngest son who came well within the place shall become briny.” After saying this, the lord of the universe dismissed his sons.

## \|\| 2.58.38 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu sāntvanārthāya samīpasthaḥ sadābhavat \|*  
*yaḥ praviṣṭo ratigṛhaṃ sa kṣārodo babhūva ha \|*  
*anye tu dra varūpā vai kṣīrodādyāḥ pṛthak sthitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In order to console them, he always stood by them. He who entered the room of sexual dalliance became the briny sea. The others remained separately as the milk ocean etc. assuming liquid form. Mohini queried:

## \|\| 2.58.39 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- kā rādhā bhavatā proktā guro lokaprasūḥ satī \|*  
*tasyāstattvaṃ samākhyāhi śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О Preceptor, who is this Radha mentioned by you as the chaste lady and the mother of the worlds. Explain to me the reality about her. I am eager to listen to it.

## \|\| 2.58.40 \|\|

*purāṇeṣu rahasyaṃ tu rādhāmādhavavarṇanam \|*  
*yataḥ sarvaṃ bhavānvetti yāthātathyena suvrata \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The description of Radha and Madhava is a mysterious secret in the Puranas. Since you factually know everything, О sage of holy rites, narrate it to me. Vasirfha said:

## \|\| 2.58.41 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- tacchrutvā mohinīvākyaṃ bhūpate sa vasurmahān \|*  
*atīvabhakto govinde nimagnahṛdayo'bhavat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О King Mandhata, on hearing the words of Mohini, the magnanimous Vasu, the great devotee of Govinda, was visibly moved.

## \|\| 2.58.42 \|\|

*pulakāṅkitasarvāṅgaḥ prathṛṣṭahṛdayo mudā \|*  
*uvāca mohamāpanno mohinīṃ dvijasattamaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. (Being extremely delighted) the hair all over his body stood on their ends. His heart was overwhelmed with joy. He as it were lost his consciousness with ecstasy. The excellent Brahman a spoke to Mohini. Vasu said r1

## \|\| 2.58.43 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi rahasyātirahasyakam \|*  
*sugopyaṃ kṛṣṇacaritaṃ brahmaikatvavidhāyakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О gentle lady, listen, I shall tell you the secret of secrets. The story of Kf?na is to be guarded well. It brings about one’s union with the Brahman.

## \|\| 2.58.44 \|\|

*prakṛteḥ puruṣasyāpi niyantāraṃ vidhervidhim \|*  
*saṃhartāraṃ ca saṃharturbhagavantaṃ nato'smyaham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I bow down to the lord who controls both — the Prakrti and Purusa, who is the creator of the creators, who is the annihilator of the annihilators.

## \|\| 2.58.45 \|\|

*devi sarve'vatārāstu brahmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*avatārī svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ saguṇo nirguṇaḥ svayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О gentle lady, all the incarnations are those of the Brahman in the form of Krsna. The incarnator is Krsna himself. He is both with and without attributes.

## \|\| 2.58.46 \|\|

*sa eva rāmaḥ kṛṣṇaśca vastuto guṇataḥ pṛthak \|*  
*sarve prākṛtikā lokā goloko nirguṇaḥ svayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He alone is Rama and Krsna factually, but he is separate due to the variety of attributes. The other worlds are the creations of Prakrti. But the Goloka (i.e. Krsna’s world) itself is devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 2.58.47 \|\|

*gāvastejoṃ'śavo bhadre vedavidbhirnirūpitāḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇuśivādyāstu prākṛtā guṇanirmitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О gentle lady, the term, Gavah are the rays of brilliance, as observed (after ascertainment) by those who know the Vedas. Brahma, Visnu, Siva and others are manifestations of Prakrti evolved out of its Gunas.

## \|\| 2.58.48 \|\|

*tattejaḥ sarvadā devi nirguṇaṃ guṇakṛnmatam \|*  
*guṇāstadaṃśavo bhadre sarve vyākṛtarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О gentle lady, his refulgence is always without attributes but considered to be the cause of Gunas. The Gunas are his rays, O gentle lady all of them are the separate manifest forms.

## \|\| 2.58.49 \|\|

*vyākṛtotpādakā jñeyā rajaḥsattvatamobhidhāḥ \|*  
*avyākṛtasya puṃso hi guṇā vijñāpakāḥ śubhe \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The Gunas Rajas, Sattva and Tamas should be known as the producers of manifested forms. O splendid lady, the Gunas are mere means of knowledge of the purusa who is analysed Avyakrta.

## \|\| 2.58.50 \|\|

*dehabhūtāḥ smṛtāstasya tacchaktiḥ prakṛtirmatā \|*  
*pradhānaprakṛtiṃ prāhuḥ kāryakāraṇarūpiṇīm \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They are remembered as his bodies. His Sakti is considered to be Prakriti. They say that the Pradhana that is Prakriti is of the nature of both cause and effect.

## \|\| 2.58.51-52 \|\|

*sākṣiṇaṃ puruṣaṃ prāhurnirguṇaṃ tu sanātanam \|*  
*puruṣo vīryamādhatta prakṛtyāṃ ca tato guṇāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sattvādyā hyabhavaṃstebhyo mahattattvaṃ samudgatam \|*  
*puruṣasyecchayā tattu vyākṛtaṃ samabhūdaham \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. They say that the Purusa is the witness, eternal and devoid of attributes. Purusa deposited his energy into Prakriti. Hence, the Gunas Sattva etc. were evolved. From them the great principle (Mahattattva) took its origin. Thanks to the will of the Purusa, it became the Aharhkara (Ego) analysed into three.

## \|\| 2.58.53 \|\|

*tattridhā samabhūdbhadre dra vyajñānakriyātmakam \|*  
*vaikārikastaijasaśca tāmasaścetyahaṃ tridhā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O gentle lady, it divided itself into three, viz. the Dravya (Substance), Jiiana (Knowledge) and Kriya (Activity). Thus the Aharhkara is threefold-Vaikarika, Taijasa and Tamasa.

## \|\| 2.58.54-56 \|\|

*vaikārikānmano jajñe devā vaikārikā daśa \|\| 54 \|\|*

*digvātārkapracetośvibrahmendro pendra mitrakāḥ \|*  
*taijasānīndri yāṇyāhurjñānakarmamayāni ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śrotratvagghrāṇadṛgjihvāvijñānendri yarūpakāḥ \|*  
*karmendri yāṇi subhage vāgdormeḍhrāṅighrapāyavaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-55a. From the Vaikarika, the mind was born. The Devas evolved out of Vaikarika, and also the ten, viz.: The quarters, wind, sun, pracetas, Asv.ins, Brahma, lndra, Upendra and Mitra (inclusive of mind).

55b-56. They say that the sense-organs are evolved out of Taijasa. They are the cognitive senses and conative organs. The organs of knowledge are the ears, skin, nose, eye and tongue. O blessed lady, the organs of activity are the speech. hands, penis, feet and rectum.

## \|\| 2.58.57 \|\|

*śabdastu tāmasājjajñe tasmādākāśa eva ca \|*  
*ākāśādabhavatsparśastasmādvāyurabhūtsati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. From the Tamasa Ego sound was evolved and from it originated the sky (ether). From ether the touch was evolved. O chaste lady, from it was born the wind.

## \|\| 2.58.58 \|\|

*vāyorabhūttato rūpaṃ tasmāttejo vyajāyata \|*  
*tejasastu rasastasmādāpaḥ samabhavansati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. From the wind, Riipa (colour, form) was evolved and from it the Tejas (fiery substance) was born. From Tejas, Rasa (taste) was evolved and from it the waters ware born. O chaste lady.

## \|\| 2.58.59 \|\|

*adbhyo gandhaḥ samutpanno gandhātkṣitirajāyata \|*  
*carācarasya niṣṭhā tu bhūmāveva pradṛśyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. From the waters smell got evolved and from smell the earth was born. The stability of the mobile and immobile beings is seen dependent on the earth.

## \|\| 2.58.60 \|\|

*ākāśādiṣu tattveṣu ekadvitricaturguṇāḥ \|*  
*bhūmau pañca guṇāḥ proktā viśeṣastu tataḥ kṣiteḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the principles of Akasa etc., the number of Gur\_1as (attributes) are one, two, threeand four, but there are five attributes in the earth. Hence, the special feature of the •earth is spoken.

## \|\| 2.58.61 \|\|

*kālamāyāṃśaliṅgebhya etebhyo'ṇḍamacetanam \|*  
*samabhūccetanaṃ jātaṃ dareṇa viśatā sati \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By being urged by parts of Time and Maya, an insentient cosmic egg was evolved out of the five great elements, but it became sentient due to the entry of Purusa into it, O chaste lady.

## \|\| 2.58.62 \|\|

*tasmādaṇḍādvirāḍ jajñe so'śayiṣṭa jalāntare \|*  
*mukhādīnyasya jātāni virājo'vayavā api \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. From that egg, the Virat the immense being was born. It lay within the waters. Mouths and the other organs {)f the immense being were evolved then.

## \|\| 2.58.63 \|\|

*vacanādeśca sirddhythaṃ salilasthasya bhāmini \|*  
*tasya nābhyāmabhūtpadmaṃ sahasrārkorudīdhitiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. These limbs were evolved, O beautiful lady, in oQrder that he may be able to speak even as he lay in the water. From his umbilical region came out a lotus that had the combined brilliant light of a thousand suns.

## \|\| 2.58.64-66 \|\|

*tasminsvayambhūḥ samabhūllokānāṃ prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tena taptvā tapastīvraṃ puṃso'nujñāmavāpya ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*lokāśca lokapālāśca kalpitā brahmaṇā sati \|*  
*kaṭyādibhiradhaḥ sapta saptorddhvaṃ jaghanādibhiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*caturdaśabhirebhistu lokairbrahmāṇḍamīritam \|*  
*tasmin sasarja bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-65a. In it the selfborn lord, the great grandfather of the worlds was born. He performed a severe penance. After getting permission of the Purusa, the worlds and their guardians were created by Brahma, O chaste lady.

65b-66. From the hips downwards, the seven lower worlds and from the upper part the seven upper worlds were created. The cosmic egg consisted of these fourteen worlds. In it he created all living beings-the mobile and immobile.

## \|\| 2.58.67 \|\|

*brahmaṇo manaso jātāśvatvāraḥ sanakādayaḥ \|*  
*dehādbhāvādayo devi yairidaṃ varddhitaṃ jagat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Sanaka and the other four sons were born from the mind ofBrahma; sons like Bhrgu etc. were evolved out of his body, O gentle lady, and by these the universe is populated and flourished.

## Chapter 59 . Purushottama Mahatmyam (Contd.)

## \|\| 2.59.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- yo'sau nirañjano devaścitsvarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*jyotīrūpo mahābhāge kṛṣṇastallakṣaṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu continued:

1\. O highly blessed lady ! Now listen to the characteristics of Lord KnshJa, Janiirdana who is unsullied (blemishless), and an embodiment of consciousness and of the form of refulgence.

## \|\| 2.59.2 \|\|

*goloke sa vibhurnityaṃ jyotirabhyantare sthitaḥ \|*  
*eka eva paraṃ brahma dṛśyādṛśyasvarūpadhṛk \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. That lord is perpetually stationed in Goloka, in the midst of luminaries. He is the one without a second), supreme Brahman assuming the form that is visible and invisible.

## \|\| 2.59.3-5 \|\|

*tasmim̐ lloke tu gāvo hi gopā gopyaśca mohini \|*  
*vṛndāvanaṃ pūrvataśca śataśṛṅgastathā sarit \|\| 3 \|\|*

*virajā nāma vṛkṣāśca pakṣiṇaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ \|*  
*yāvatkālaṃ tu prakṛtirjāgarti vidhinandini \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tāvatkālaṃ tu goloke dṛśya eva vibhuḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*laye suptā gavādyāstu na jānanti vibhuṃ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-4a. In that world there are only cows, cowherds and cowherdesses. O Mohini, there is Vrindavana and as before mount Govardhana of hundred peaks, the Viraja river and trees and birds of various kinds.

4b-5. O daughter of Brahmii, as long as the Prakriti remains awake, the lord is visible as stationed in the 'Goloka.' At the time of dissolution of the universe the cows and others are asleep and hence they do not know the great all-pervading lord.

## \|\| 2.59.6-7 \|\|

*jyotiḥsamūhāntarataḥ kamanīyavapurddharaḥ \|*  
*kiśoro jaladaśyāmaḥ pītakauśāmbarāvṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvibhujo muralīhastaḥ kirīṭādivibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*āste kaivalyanāthastu rādhāvakṣasthalojjvalaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He is stationed within the multitude of luminaries. He assumes a beautiful form and physical body of a youth. He is dark-complexioned like a cloud and is clad in yellow silken robes. He has two arms and is bedecked in coronet etc. He has the flute in his hand. The lord of Kaivalya (salvation) occupies the bosom of Radha and shines brilliantly.

## \|\| 2.59.8 \|\|

*prāṇādhikapriyatamā sā rādhārādhito yayā \|*  
*suvarṇavarṇā devī sā cidrū pā prakṛteḥ parā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Radha is his beloved, more dear to him than his own vital airs. He too is propitiated by her. That divine lady has golden complexion. She is of the form of consciousness and is beyond Prakriti.

## \|\| 2.59.9 \|\|

*tayordehasthayornāsti bhedo nityasvarūpayoḥ \|*  
*dhāvalyadugdhayoryadvatpṛthivīgandhayoryathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When they are united in their bodies there is no difference between them, as in the case of the white colour and milk or as in the case of the element earth and its distinguishing quality called 'smell'. I 0. He is the cause of all causes. He cannot be specifically pointed out. What cannot be properly defined and described by even the Vedas cannot be specified by others.

## \|\| 2.59.11 \|\|

*jyotirantarataḥ proktaṃ yadrū paṃ śyāmasundaram \|*  
*śivena dṛṣṭaṃ tadrū paṃ kadāciddhynāgocaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The form that has been proclaimed as being within the luminary bodies is dark and beautiful. Once that form was visualised by Siva in the course of his meditation.

## \|\| 2.59.12 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti jānanti golokākhyānamīpsitam \|*  
*nāradādyā vidhisute sanakādyāśca yoginaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Ever since that, O daughter of Brahma, Narada and other sages as well as Sanaka and Yogins know that the description and account of the Goloka is desirable.

## \|\| 2.59.13 \|\|

*śrutaṃ dhyāyanti taṃ sarve na tairdṛṣṭaṃ kadācana \|*  
*sākṣāddra ṣṭuṃ tu tapate śivo'dyāpi sanātanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All of them meditate on him in the form that has been heard by them but never seen. Even today, the eternal lord Siva performs penance to see him directly.

## \|\| 2.59.14-15 \|\|

*naiva paśyati tadrū paṃ dhyāyati dhyānagocaram \|*  
*kadācitkrīḍatordevi rādhāmādhavayorvapuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dvidhābhūtamabhūttatra vāmāṅgaṃ tu caturbhujam \|*  
*samānarūpāvayavaṃ samānāmbarabhūṣaṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. But he does not see that form. He meditates on it and it is visible in the course of meditation. O gentle lady, on one occasion, while they were engaged in their dalliance, the body of Radha and Madhava split into two. The body to the left had four arms. The two forms had similar features and limbs, similar garments and ornaments.

## \|\| 2.59.16 \|\|

*tadvadrā dhāsvarūpaṃ ca dvidhārūpamabhūtsati \|*  
*tābhyāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ sākṣāttāvapi tatsamau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O chaste lady, similarly, the form of Radha too split into two. That form was directly seen by them. Those two were also like them.

## \|\| 2.59.17 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ tu yadrū paṃ lakṣmīkāntaṃ manoharam \|*  
*taddṛṣṭaṃ tu śivādyaiśca bhaktavṛndairanekaśaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The beautiful form that had four arms was the beloved of Laksmi. That was seen by Siva and many other groups of devotees.

## \|\| 2.59.18 \|\|

*sakṛttu brahmaṇā dṛṣṭaṃ devi rūpaṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*sṛṣṭikāryapramugdhena darśitaṃ kṛpayā svayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O gentle lady, that four-armed form was seen once by Brahma. It was revealed to him out of sympathy by the lord, on being confused in the work of creation.

## \|\| 2.59.19-20 \|\|

*lakṣmyā sanatkumārāya varṇitaṃ vidhinandini \|*  
*viṣvaksenāya tūddiṣṭaṃ svarūpaṃ tattvamūrtaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇena vidhije tato dhyāyanti sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*dharmaputreṇa deveśi nāradāya samīritam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O daughter of Brahma, it has been described by Laksmi to Sanatkumara, O daughter of Brahma, his only form has been indicated to Vishvaksena for understanding the real form, by Narayar;ta. Hence all meditate on it. O queen: the description of Goloka as being permeated by Radha and Knr:ta was described by Dharmaputra to Narada.

## \|\| 2.59.21-23 \|\|

*golokavarṇanaṃ sarvaṃ rādhākṛṣṇamayaṃ tathā \|*  
*yā tu rādhā vidhisute devī devavarārcitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sā svayaṃ śivarūpābhūtkautukena varānane \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā sahasāścaryaṃ kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mūlaprakṛtirūpaṃ tu dadhre tatsamayocitam \|*  
*viparītaṃ vapurdhṛtvā vāmadevo mudānvitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. O daughter of Brahmii, goddess Radhii, worshipped by the excellent Devas, out of curiosity assumed the form of Siva herself, O fair-faced lady. On seeing this sudden surprising feature, Krsna, lord of the chiefs of Yogis, assumed the form of the primordial Prakriti as befitting that occasion. By his assuming the form of the opposite sex, Vamadeva became joyous.

## \|\| 2.59.24-25 \|\|

*dhyāyedaharniśaṃ devaṃ durgārūpadharaṃ harim \|*  
*yā rādhā saiva lakṣmīstu sāvitrī ca sarasvatī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gaṅgā ca brahmatanaye naiva bhedo'sti vastutaḥ \|*  
*pañcadhā sā sthitā vidyā kāmadhenusvarūpiṇī \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. One should day and night meditate on lord Hari who had assumed the form of Durga. She who is Riidhii is Laksmi, Savitri, Sarasvati and Ganga. O daughter of Brahma, there is no factual difference between them. As a Vidya (lore) in the form of Kiimadhenu, she abides in these five different forms.

## \|\| 2.59.26 \|\|

*yaḥ kṛṣṇo rādhikānāthaḥ sa lakṣmīśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*sa eva brahmarūpaśca dharmo nārāyaṇastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He who is Krsna, the lord of Riidhii is glorified as the lord of Lakf?mi. He alone assumes the form of Brahma. He is Dharma and Niiriiyal}.a as well.

## \|\| 2.59.27 \|\|

*evaṃ tu pañcadhā rūpamāsthito bhagavānajaḥ \|*  
*kāryakāraṇarūpo'sau dhyāyanti jagatītale \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus the unborn eternal lord has assumed the fivefold form. He is in the form of cause and effect. People on the surface of the earth meditate on him as such.

## \|\| 2.59.28 \|\|

*tena vai premasambaddho viṣayī yaḥ śivaḥ sa tu \|*  
*rādheśaṃ rādhikārūpaṃ svayaṃ saccitsukhātmakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence, there is the love-relationship. He who is the object is Siva. The lord of Radhii is the form of Radhii, which is of the nature of existence, knowledge and happiness.

## \|\| 2.59.29 \|\|

*devatejaḥsamudbhūtā mūlaprakṛtirīśvarī \|*  
*kṛṣṇarūpā mahābhāge daityasaṃhārakāṇ! \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O blessed lady, the primordial Prakriti originated from the brilliance of the luminous lord. It is the goddess in the form of Krsna. It is the cause of destruction of the Daityas.

## \|\| 2.59.30-31 \|\|

*satī dakṣasutā bhūtvā viṣayeśaṃ śivaṃ śritā \|*  
*bharturvinindanaṃ śrutvā satī tyaktvā kalevaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*jajñe himavataḥ kṣetre menāyāṃ punareva ca \|*  
*tatastaptvā tapo bhadre śivaṃ prāpa śivapradā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. She was born as Sati, the daughter of Daksha. She resorted to Siva, the lord of the Vif?ayas (the Vif?ayin?). On hearing about the insult of her husband, Sati cast off her physical body and she was born again of Mena, the wife of Hima van. O gentle lady, after performing penance, she, the bestower of auspiciousness obtained Siva as her consort.

## \|\| 2.59.32 \|\|

*vastutaḥ kṛṣṇarādhāsau śivamohanatatparā \|*  
*jagadambāsvarūpā ca yato māyā svayaṃ vibhuḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In fact, the Krsna-cum-Radha \[ Radha who assumed the form of Krsna \] were engaged in deluding and fascinating Siva. Since Maya in the form of the mother of the universe is the lord himself.

## \|\| 2.59.33 \|\|

*ata eva brahmasute skando gaṇapatistathā \|*  
*svayaṃ kṛṣṇo gaṇapatiḥ svayaṃ skandaḥ śivo'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. That is why, O daughter of Brahma, Skanda is Ganapati; Krsna himself was Ganapati, and Skanda himself became Siva.

## \|\| 2.59.34 \|\|

*śivamevaṃ vadantyeke rādhārūpaṃ samāśritam \|*  
*kṛṣṇavakṣaḥsthalasthānaṃ tayorbhedo na lakṣyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Some say that Siva is one and has resorted to the form of Radha. The region of the chest of KnJ).a is his (their?) abode. Hence no difference is seen between them.

## \|\| 2.59.35 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo vā mūlaprakṛtiḥ śivo vā rādhikā svayam \|*  
*ekaṃ vā mithunaṃ vāpi na kenāpīti niścitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This has not been decisively arrived at by anyone whether Krsna or Siva. Radha herself is the primordial Prakriti. It has not been decided whether this principle under these names is single or a couple.

## \|\| 2.59.36 \|\|

*anirdeśyaṃ tu yadvastu tannirdeṣṭuṃ na ca kṣamam \|*  
*upalakṣaṇametaddhi yannideśanamaiśvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is not possible to describe specifically what is intrinsically indescribable. The assertion regarding Isvara (godhead) is a mere distinction. (implying something more unexpressed).

## \|\| 2.59.37 \|\|

*śāstraṃ vedāśca subhage varṇayaṃnti yadīśvaram \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ prākṛtaṃ viddhi nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyameva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O blessed lady, the scriptural texts, and the Vedas describe Isvara. That is the product of Prakriti. Surely know that it can be specifically mentioned.

## \|\| 2.59.38 \|\|

*anirdeśyaṃ tu yaddevi tannetīti niṣidhyate \|*  
*niṣedhaśeṣaḥ sa vibhuḥ kīrtitaḥ śaraṇāgataiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O gentle lady, what cannot be specifically described is being denied with the expression 'neti' (not such). What remains after negation is glorified as the overlord by those who seek refuge.

## \|\| 2.59.39 \|\|

*śāstraṃ niyāmakaṃ bhadre sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ bhavet \|*  
*karmī tu jīvaḥ kathita īśvarāṃśo vibhuḥ svayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O gentle lady, the scriptural text is that which regulates all activities. The individual soul is termed as Karmin (one who is engaged in holy rites) and Vibhu (the overlord) as a part of Isvara (Godhead) himself.

## \|\| 2.59.40-42 \|\|

*prakṛtestu paro nityo māyayā mohitaḥ śubhe \|*  
*yastu sākṣī svayaṃ pūrṇaḥ sahānuśayitā sthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*na vetti taṃ cānuśayī vedānuśayinaṃ sa tu \|*  
*śaṅkhacakragadāpadmairalaṅkṛtabhujadvayāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*prapannāste tu vijñeyāḥ dvividhā vidhinandani \|*  
*ārtadṛptavibhedana tatrārtā asahā matāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-41 a. The overlord is eternal and beyond Prakriti. O auspicious lady, the individual soul is deluded by Maya. The individual soul does not know the witness, the supreme soul who is complete in himself and is stationed along with the individual soul. But the Siikl?in knows the individual.

41 b-42. The individual souls who seek refuge in the lord have their pairs of arms adorned with the conch, discus, iron-club and lotus (?) O daughter of Brahmii, they should be known to be of two types: the Artas (the distressed ones) and the Drptas (the haughty ones). The distressed ones are those who cannot suffer.\* \*Anusayin: The consequences or result of an act (which clings to it and causes the soul after enjoying the temporary freedom from transmigration to enter other bodies).

## \|\| 2.59.43-44 \|\|

*dṛptā janmāntarasahā nirbhayāḥ sadasajjanāḥ \|*  
*ye prapannā mahālakṣmyāṃ sakhibhāvaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi prayānti vidhibodhitam \|*  
*gopījanapadasyānte vallabheti samuccaret \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44-a. The haughty ones are those who can endure rebirths. They are fearless; they are both good and bad people. I shall recount to you the Mantra of those persons who have sought refuge in Mahalaksmi and who have adopted the type of Bhakti known as friendship with the deity. They attain the status made known by god Brahma.

## \|\| 2.59.44-47 \|\|

*teṣāṃ mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi prayānti vidhibodhitam \|*  
*gopījanapadasyānte vallabheti samuccaret \|\| 44 \|\|*

*caraṇañccharaṇaṃ paścātprapadye padamīrayet \|*  
*ṣoḍaśārṇo mantrarājaḥ sākṣāllakṣmyā prakāśitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ sanatkumārāya śambhave tadanantaram \|*  
*sakhibhāvaṃ samāśritya gopikāvṛndamadhyagam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ cintayedbhadre rādhāmādhavasaṃjñakam \|*  
*guruṣvīśvarabhāvena vartteta praṇataḥ sadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

44b-45a. (The Mantra): ''At the end of the word ''Gopijana" (the group of cowherdesses) one should utter the word 'vallabha' (lover). Then carai.J.am saraiJ.am prapadye (i.e. I resort to the feet of the lover of the groups of cowherdesses)

45b-47a. ('Gopi-jana-vallabha-carai.J.am sarai.J.aril prapadye" ). This is the 'ring' of Mantras of sixteen syllables. This was revealed by Laksmi himself to Sanatkumara at the outset, and to Sambhu thereafter. O gentle lady, the devotee should adopt the status of a friend and think ofhimself as present amidst the group of cowherdesses; and name himself and Radhamadhava.

47b. He should always behave humbly regarding his preceptors as Isvara and towards Vaishnavas (devotees of Visnu) he must behave with great respect. Towards others he must have the feeling of equality. Day and night he must think about the masters with the bondage of love. During the festive occasions he shall always perform the rites of great festivals and pilgrimages. Vasu said:

## Chapter 60. Ablution of Deity

## \|\| 2.60.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- tato gacchedvidhisute tīrthaṃ yajñāṅgasambhavam \|*  
*indra dyumnasaro nāma yatrāste pāvanaṃ śubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Thereafter, the pilgrim should, Odaughter of Brahma, go to the holy centre originating from the sacrificial limb, where the splendid and holy lake called Indradyumna-Saras\* is present.

## \|\| 2.60.2 \|\|

*tatra gatvā śucirvidvānācamya manasā harim \|*  
*dhyātvopasthāya ca vibhuṃ mantramenamudīrayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After going there the pure and learned devotee shall perform the rite of Acamana and mentally meditate on Hari. After worshipping the lord, he should repeat this Mantra. \*This chapter has most of the verses common to the Brahma P. Chs. 63. 64, 65. Thus NP 1-18 are common to Ch. 63 of the Brahma P., NP. vv. 19-37 to Brahma P. Ch. 64 and NP 38-76 (to the end) to Brahma P. Ch.65. The description of Ablution of deities is ho.vever picturesque.

## \|\| 2.60.3 \|\|

*aśvamedhāṅgasambhūta tīrtha sarvāghanāśana \|*  
*snānaṃ tvayi karomyadya pāpaṃ hara namo'stu te \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. "O Tirtha, born of the limb of horse-sacrifice, O destroyer of sins, I shall take my holy bath in you. Dispel my sins. Obeisance be to you."

## \|\| 2.60.4-5 \|\|

*evamuccārya vidhivatsnātvā devān ṛṣīnpitṝn \|*  
*tilodakena vānyāṃśca santarpyācamya vāgyataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*datvā pitṝṇāṃ piṇḍāṃśca sampūjya puruṣottamam \|*  
*daśāśvamedhikaṃ samyakphalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. After uttering the above-mentioned Mantra and having performed ablution and after propitiating gods, sages and ancestors and others with water mixed with gingelly seeds and observing silence, he should perform the Acamana rite of sipping water and offer Pix;tc.fas (balls of rice) to Pitrs. After worshipping Lord Purushottama, one gets the benefit of ten horsesacrifices properly.

## \|\| 2.60.6 \|\|

*saptāvarānsapta parānvaṃśānuddhṛtya devavat \|*  
*kāmagena vimānena viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He shall uplift seven preceding generations and seven subsequent generations and shall go to the world of Vishx;tu like a god by means of the aerial chariot that moves about as he pleases.

## \|\| 2.60.7 \|\|

*bhuktvā tatra varānbhogānyāvaccandrā rkatārakam \|*  
*cyutastasmādihāyāto mokṣaṃ ca labhate dhruvam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He enjoys great and excellent pleasures there, as long as the moon, sun and stars shines Falling off from that world, he comes to this world and subsequently shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.60.8-9 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā pañcatīrthīmekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaśukle pañcadaśyāṃ yaḥ paśyetpuruṣottamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sa pūrvoktaphalaṃ prāpya krīḍitvā cācyutālaye \|*  
*prayāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yasmānnāvartate punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Mter performing the pilgrimage to the Paiicatirthi and observing fast on the eleventh day in the bright half of the month of Jyeshtha, the devotee should visit Purushottama on the fifteenth day (the full-moon day ofJyeHha). He shall thereby attain the benefit mentioned before. He shall sport about in the abode of Acyuta and go to the highest region from which he does not return to Sarhsii.ra.

## \|\| 2.60.10-11 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni saritaśca sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*puṣkariṇyastaḍāgāni vāpyaḥ kūpāstathā hradāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nānā nadyaḥ samudrā śca saptāhaṃ puruṣottame \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaśukladaśamyādi pratyakṣaṃ yānti sarvadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Whatever places of sacred waters, rivers, lakes Pushkarix;tis (lotus ponds), tanks, wells, pools, rivers and oceans are on the earth, all of them appear in the holy centre of Purushottama for seven days beginning with the tenth day in the bright half of JyeHha. They appear there always. \*This is near the GuQQ.ica mandira (or Janakapura) at a distance of.about a mile and a half from the shrine of Jagannatha.

## \|\| 2.60.12 \|\|

*snānadānādikaṃ yasmāddevatāprekṣaṇe sati \|*  
*nṛbhiryatkriyate tatra tatsarvaṃ cākṣayaṃ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O chaste lady, whatever is performed by men such as ablution, charitable gifts visiting the deity etc. at the holy place of Purushottama shall be of an everlasting benefit.

## \|\| 2.60.13 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāse tu daśamī śuklapakṣasya mohini \|*  
*harate daśa pāpāni tasmāddaśaharā smṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Mohini, the tenth day of the bright half of the month of JyeHha dispells, the ten sins. Hence, it is called Dasahara.

## \|\| 2.60.14 \|\|

*yastasyāṃ halinaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ paśyedbhadrā ṃ! ca suvrataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The man who visits the ploughshare-armed Balaratna, KnJJ.a and Subhadra on that day shall be liberated from all sins. That excellent observer of vows shall go to the world of VishQU.

## \|\| 2.60.15 \|\|

*naro dolāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā govindaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*phālgunyāṃ saṃyato bhūtvā govindasya puraṃ vrajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. By seeing Govinda Purushottama seated in the swing on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna, while observing self-control, the man shall go to the city of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.60.16-17 \|\|

*viṣuve divase prāpte pañcatīrthavidhānataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā saṅkarṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ subhadrā ṃ! ca sulocane \|\| 16 \|\|*

*naraḥ samastayajñānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti durlabham \|*  
*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. When the day of Vishuva (Equinox) arrives, O lady of beautiful eyes, the man should visit SarilkarshaQa Krsna and Subhadra in accordance with the same injunctions as in the case of Pancatirtha. By visiting these, the man attains the rare benefit of the Yajnas. Liberated from all sins he goes to the world ofVisnu.

## \|\| 2.60.18 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyanti tṛtīyāyāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ candanarūṣitam \|*  
*vaiśākhasya site pakṣe sa yātyacyutamandiram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who sees Krsna fully smeared with sandal paste the third day in the bright half of the month of Vaisakha, goes to the mansion of Acyuta.

## \|\| 2.60.19 \|\|

*yadā bhavenmahājyaiṣṭhī rāśinakṣatrayogataḥ \|*  
*prayatnena tadā martyairgantavyaṃ puruṣottamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the holy day of Mahajyaishthi arrives in view of the particular cofunction of the sign of zodiac and the constellation, men shall make special effort to go to Purushottama.

## \|\| 2.60.20 \|\|

*kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahājyeṣṭhyāṃ rāmaṃ bhadrā ṃ! ca mohini \|*  
*naro dvādaśayātrāṇāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti cādhikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By seeing Krsna, Rama and Bhadra (i.e. Subhadra) on the Mahajyaishthi day, O Mohini, the man shall attain the benefit of twelve pilgrimages or even more.

## \|\| 2.60.21-32 \|\|

*prayāge ca kurukṣetraṃ naimiṣe puṣkare gaye \|*  
*gaṅgādvāre ca kubjāmragaṅgāsāgarasaṅgame \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kokāmukhe śūkare ca mathurāyāṃ marusthale \|*  
*śālagrāme vāyutīrthe mandare sindhusāgare \|\| 22 \|\|*

*piṇḍārake citrakūṭe prabhāse kanakhale tathā \|*

*sahye ca śuktimati ca gomante cārbude tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sārasvateṣu gomatyāṃ brahmaputreṣu saptasu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vitastā candra bhāgā ca śatadrurbāhudā tathā \|*

21-32. The holy centres and sacred rivers mentioned below are not as meritorious as paying a visit to Krsna.1 They are Prayaga, Kurukshetra, Naimisha, Pushkara, Gaya, Gangadvara, Kubjamra, the confluence of the Ganga and the ocean (the mouth of the river Ganga), Kokamukha, Siikara, Mathura, Marusthala (the desert of Rajasthan), Salagrama, Vayutirtha, Mandara, Sindhusagara, Pii;t(iaraka, Citrakiita, Prabhasa, Kanakhala, Sankhoddhara, Dvaraka, Badarikasrama, Lohakiita, Asvatirtha, that dispels all sins, Kardamala, Koti-Tirtha Amarakai;ttaka, Lolarka, Jambiimarga, Somatirtha Prthiidaka (mod. Pehoa in Karnal dist), Utpalavartaka, Prthutunga, Kubjaka, Ekamraka. Kedara, Kasi, Virajii., Kalafijasha, Gokari;ta (mountains like) Srisaila, Gandhamadana, Mahendra, Malaya, Vindhya, Pariyatra, Himalaya, Sahya, Suktimat, Gomanta, Arbuda, (in rivers like) Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Gomati,. the seven Brahmaputras, Godavari, Bhimarathi, Tungabhadra, Narmada, Tapi, Payoshti, Kii.veri, Sipra, Carmai;tvati, Vitasta, Candrabhaga, Satadrii, Bahudii., Shikulya. Marudvrdha, Viplisii. Drishadvati, Sarayii, Nakaganga Gai;t(iaki, Mahanadi, Kausiki, Karatoyii., Trisrota, Madhuvii.hini, Vaitarai;ti and other rivers not mentioned here. All these are not equal to the visit to Krsna in the matter of yielding benefits.

## \|\| 2.60.33 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ snānadānena rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*tatphalaṃ kṛṣṇamālokya mahājyeṣṭhyāṃ labhennaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By visiting Krsna on the Mahajyaishthi day, a man shall obtain that benefit which one gets by taking a holy dip and offering charitable gifts when the sun is swallowed by Rii.hu (i.e. when there is solar eclipse)

## \|\| 2.60.34 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena gantavyaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ vidhisute sarvakāmaphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence, by all means, O daughter of Brahma, all those who wish to obtain desired benefits shonld put in all efforts and go to Purushottama on MahajyaiHhi day.

## \|\| 2.60.35 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ cāpi subhadra yā \|*  
*viṣṇulokaṃ naro yāti samuddhṛtya kulaṃ śatam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By visiting Rama and Kni;ta along with Subhadrii on the MahajyaiHhi day, the man goes to the world of Visnu after uplifting hundred members of his family.

## \|\| 2.60.36 \|\|

*bhuktvā tatra varānbhogānyāvadābhūtasamplavam \|*  
*puṇyakṣayādihāgatya caturvedī dvijo bhavet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He shall enjoy excellent pleasures there as long as all the living beings are not dissolved. When the merits are exhausted he comes here and is born as a Brahma:Q.a wellversed in the four Vedas.

## \|\| 2.60.37 \|\|

*svadharmanirataḥ śāntaḥ kṛṣṇabhakto jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ yogamāsthāya tato mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He will be devoted to his own duty. He will be quiescent devotee of Krsna. He will be conquering all senseorgans. By adopting the Yoga pertaining to Visnu, he shall attain salvation.

## \|\| 2.60.38 \|\|

*māsi jyeṣṭhe ca samprāpte nakṣatre cendra daivate \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ tadā snānaṃ praśastaṃ sāgarāmbhasi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the month of JyeHha when the full moon day comes in conjunction with the constellation having Indra for its deity, the ablution in the ocean is well praised.

## \|\| 2.60.39 \|\|

*sarvatīrthamayaḥ kūpastadāste sajalaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*tathā bhogavatī tatra pratyakṣā bhavati dhruvam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There is a well there which becomes identical with the Tirthas. It is full of water and pure; so also the Bhogavati (the Ganga ofthe nether-worlds) manifests itself.

## \|\| 2.60.40-42 \|\|

*tasmājjyaiṣṭhyāṃ samuddhṛtya haimādikalaśairjalam \|*  
*kṛṣṇarāmābhiṣekārthaṃ subhadrā yāśca mohini \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kṛtvā suśobhanaṃ mañcaṃ patākābhiralaṅkṛtam \|*  
*sudṛḍhaṃ sukhasañcāraṃ vastraiḥ puṣpairalaṅkṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vistīrṇaṃ dhūpitaṃ dhūpaiḥ snānārthaṃ rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*pītavastraparicchannaṃ muktāhārāvalambitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Hence, on the Jyaishthi day, O Mohini, water must be drawn out of it by means of gold or other pots for the ablution of Kn:Q.a, Rama and Subhadra. A Mafica (a raised platform) of great splendour should be erected and decorated with flags. It must be finn and of easy access. It should be decorated with clothes and flowers. It must be adequately extensive. It must be fumigated with incense for the purpose of ablution of Rama and Kn:t:J.a. It must be covered with a yellow cloth; pearl necklaces should be suspended by way of decoration.

## \|\| 2.60.43-44 \|\|

*tatra nānāvidhairvādyaiḥ kṛṣṇaṃ nīlāmbaraṃ sati \|*  
*mañce saṃsthāpya bhadrā ṃ! ca jayamaṅgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdrai ścānyaiśca mohini \|*  
*anekaśatasāhasrairvṛtaṃ strīpuruṣaistathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. O chaste lady, to the accompaniment of auspicious shouts of victory Krsna, Balarama and Subhadra should be installed on the platform. It must be surrounded by thousands of people both men and women as well as all types of castes such the Brahma:Q.as, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas Siidras and others.

## \|\| 2.60.45 \|\|

*gṛhasthāḥ snātakāścaiva yatayo brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*snāpayanti tadā kṛṣṇaṃ mañcasthaṃ sahalāyudham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Mohini, life-long students of Vedas, the householders, ascetics and religious students should bow to Kn:Q.a along with Balarama seated on the platform.

## \|\| 2.60.46 \|\|

*tathā samastatīrthāni pūrvoktāni ca sundari \|*  
*modakaiḥ puṣpamiśraiśca snāpayanti pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O beautiful woman, all the Tirthas mentioned before bathe there separately; one should bathe there offering sweets mixed with flowers.

## \|\| 2.60.47-50 \|\|

*paścātpaṭahaṃsaghoṣairbherīmurajaniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*kāhalaistālaśabdaiśca mṛdaṅgairjharjharaistathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*anyaiśca vividhairvādyairghaṇṭāsvanavimiśritaiḥ \|*

*jayaśabdaistathā stotrairvīṇāveṇunināditaiḥ \|*

*munīnāṃ vedaghoṣaiśca mantraghoṣaistathāparaiḥ \|*

47-50. Thereafter, a loud sound like roaring of the sea is heard. It is the loud sound of drums, war drums, Murajas, trumpets, cymbals, Mrda:rigas, gongs, and other types of instruments, mixed with the sound of bells, auspicious shouts of women, charming sound of eulogies, shouts of victory, drums, the sounds of flutes and lutes, of the chanting of the Vedas by the sages and the sounds of Mantras, holy hymns heightened by the singing ofSamans.

## \|\| 2.60.51 \|\|

*śyāmāvadātaveśyābhiḥ pītaraktāṃśukaistathā \|*  
*cāmarai ratnadaṇḍaiśca vījyete rāmakeśavau \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Rama and Kesava should be fanned with chowries having jewelled handles red and yellow silken cloths, by courtesans both of dark and fair complexion.

## \|\| 2.60.52-56 \|\|

*yakṣavidyādharaiḥ siddhairdevagandharvacāraṇaiḥ \|*  
*ādityā vasavo rudrā ḥ! sādhyā viśve marudgaṇāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*lokapālāstathānye ca stuvanti puruṣottamam \|*  
*namaste devadeveśa purāṇapuruṣottama \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sargasthityantakṛddeva lokanātha jagatpate \|*

*taṃ namasyāmahe bhaktyā sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*stutvaivaṃ vibudhāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ caiva mahābalam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*subhadrā ṃ! cāpi vidhije tadākāśe vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*gāyanti devagandharvā nṛtyantyapsarasastathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

52-53a. The Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sadhyas Maruts, the guardians of quarters and others along with the Yakshas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas, Devas, Gandharvas and Carai.J.aS eulogise Puru\\lottama.

53b-55a. "0 lord of the chiefs of the Devas, obeisance to you. O excellent ancient Purusa, O lord, the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation of the universe, O lord of the worlds, O lord of the universe. We shall bow down with devotion to that lord who is the refuge of the three worlds; who is favourably disposed to the Brahmai.J.as and who is the cause of salvation. The lord who is the bestower of all desired benefits."

55b-56. O daughter of Brahma, Devas shall then be stationed in the firmament after eulogising, KnQ.a, Rama of great strength and Subhadra. Devas and the Gandharvas sing while the divine damsels dance.

## \|\| 2.60.57 \|\|

*devatūryāṇi vādyante vātā vānti suśītalāḥ \|*  
*puṣpamiśraṃ tadā meghā varṣantyākāśagocarāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The divine drums and musical instruments are sounded. Cool breezes blow. The clouds in the sky shower flowers.

*dharmaśca bhagavāndevaḥ samāgacchanti sarvataḥ \|*  
*kālo yamaśca mṛtyuśca yamasyānucarāśca ye \|\| 71 \|\|*

*bahulatvācca noktā ye vividhā devatāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*te devasyābhiṣekārthaṃ samāyānti tatastataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

58-59a. The sages, Siddhas, CaraQ.as, Sakra and other Devas, sages, Pitrs, Prajapatis, Nagas and other heaven-dwellers raise shouts of victory.

59b-72. With the articles of ablution along with other auspicious requisites duly consecrated with Mantras, the following deities etc. approach Purushottama to bathe him. The deities are: Indra and Visnu of great prowess, the sun and the moon, Dhatr, Vidhatr, the firegod, the windgod, Piishan, Bhaga, Aryama, Tvashtr, Vivasvan, Arnsuman, intelligent Rudra, along with Asvins, Mitra, VaruQ.a, Rudras1, Vasus, Adityas, Valakhilyas, the sons of Marici. The Bhrgus, Ailgiras, those who abide by all learning, Pitamaha, Pulastya, Pulaha of great penance, Ailgiras, Kasyapa, Atri, Marici, Bhrgu, Hara, Pracetas, Manu, Daksha, seasons, planets, luminaries, excellent BrahmaQas, rivers in their embodied forms, the eternal Devas, the deep pools of great auspiciousness, the different kinds of Tirthas, earth, heaven, quarters, trees, excellent birds, Aditi the mother of the Devas, Hri, Sri, Svaha, Sarasvati, Uma, Saci, Sinivali, Anumati, Kuhii, Raka, DhishaJ)a and other wives of the heaven-dwellers, the Himalayas, the most excellent among the mountains, the king of serpents, Vamana, Pariyatra, the Vindhya-Meru of many peaks, Airavata with its followers, the Kalas, KaHhas, months, fortnights, seasons, day, night, years, Uccaissravas the most excellent among horses, Vamana the king of serpents, AruQa, Garul;la, creepers, herbs, lord Dharma, Kalayana, Mrtyu, and other attendants of Yama-all these come. Since they are too numerous they have not been mentioned fully. Different deities come there for the ablution of the lord.

## \|\| 2.60.73 \|\|

*divyasambhārasaṃyuktaiḥ kalaśaiḥ kāñcanaistathā \|*  
*sārasvatībhiḥ puṇyābhirdivyatoyābhireva ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. They come equipped with divine requisites, gold pots and holy waters of the Divine Sarasvati.

## \|\| 2.60.74 \|\|

*toyenākāśagaṅgāyāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmeṇa saṅgatam \|*  
*supuṣpaiḥ kumbhasalilaiḥ snāpayantyambare sthitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Staying in the sky, they bathe Kpishna along with Rama by means of the water of the celestial Ganga and waters of the pots in which flowers are mixed.

## \|\| 2.60.75 \|\|

*sañcaranti vimānāni devānāmambare tathā \|*  
*uccāvacāni divyāni kāmagāni sthirāṇi ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The divine aerial chariots of the Devas move about in the sky. Some fly high, some fly low. They can go as they please. Some are stationary.

## \|\| 2.60.76 \|\|

*divyaratnavicitrāṇi sevitānyapsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*gītairvādyaiḥ patākābhiḥ śobhitāni samantataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They are variously decorated with divine jewels. They are resorted to by the Apsaras. They are rendered splendid by means of banners and musical instruments.

## Chapter 61 . The Fruit of Pilgrimage to Purushottama Kshetra

## \|\| 2.61.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- evaṃ tadā vidhisute kṛṣṇaṃ rāmeṇa saṅgatam \|*  
*subhadrā ṃ! ca mahābhāgāḥ saṃstuvati mudānvitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1\. Thus, then O daughter of Brahma, the highly blessed

## \|\| 2.61.2 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*jaya jaya lokapāla jaya padmanābha bhūdharaṇa \|*  
*jaya jaya cādideva bahukāraṇa \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. "Hail, Hail to you, O protector of the worlds, be victorious, O Padmanabha, O supporter of the earth. Be victorious, be victorious, O primordial Lord, the cause of the universe.

## \|\| 2.61.3 \|\|

*jaya jaya vāsudeva jaya saccaraṇa satkaraṇa \|*  
*jaya jaya divyamīna jaya tridaśavara \|\| 3 \|\|*

## \|\| 2.61.4 \|\|

*jaya jaya jaladhiśayana jaya jaya yogeśa jaya vedadhara \|*  
*jaya jaya viśvamūrte jaya cakradhara \|\| 4 \|\|*

## \|\| 2.61.5 \|\|

*jaya jaya bhūtanātha jaya śrīnivāsa jaya jaya yogivara \|*  
*jaya jaya sūryanetra jaya deva varāha \|\| 5 \|\|*

## \|\| 2.61.6 \|\|

*jaya jaya kaiṭabhāre jaya jaya vedavara \|*  
*jaya jaya kūrmarūpa jaya yajñavara \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Be victorious, be victorious, O enemy of Kaitabha; be victorious, be victorious, O excellent one (mentioned in or known through) the Vedas. Victory, victory to you O Kiirmariipa (one who has assumed the form of the divine Tortoise); be victorious, O excellent Yajiia.

## \|\| 2.61.7 \|\|

*jaya jaya kamalanābha jaya śailadhara \|*  
*jaya jaya yogeśa jaya vegadhara \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Be victorious, be victorious O Kamalanabha (one with the lotus in the umbilicus); Victory to the uplifter of the mountain Govardhana. Be victorious, be victorious, O holder of Velocity. \*This chapter has many verses common to the Brahma P. Ch. 65.48ff. to Ch. 66.

## \|\| 2.61.8 \|\|

*jaya jaya viśvamūrte jaya cakradhara \|*  
*jaya jaya bhūtanātha jaya dharaṇīdhara \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Be victorious, be victorious, O Visvamurti (who are the embodiment of the universe); be victorious, O wielder of discus. Be victorious, be victorious, O lord of living beings, victory to you, O uplifter of the earth.

## \|\| 2.61.9 \|\|

*jaya jaya śeṣaśāyiñjaya pītavāsa \|*  
*jaya somakānta jaya yogavāsa jaya jaya \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Be victorious, be victorious, O Seshasayin (you who lie on the serpent Sesha) ; be victorious, O yellow-robed one. Be victorious O Somakanta (you that shine like the moon). Be victorious, O abode of Yoga; be victorious, be victorious. I 0. O Dahanacakra (you whose discus blazes like fire) be victorious. Hail, victory to you, O abode of Dharma, be victorious, be victorious, O receptacle of attributes. Be victorious, O Srinivasa, be victorious, be victorious. II. O Garu9asana (you who are seated on Garuc;l.a) be victorious. Hail to you, O abode of happiness. Be victorious, be victorious O lover of Dharma. Victory, victory to you O abode of intellect.

## \|\| 2.61.12 \|\|

*jaya jaya gahanagehanivāsa \|*  
*jaya jaya yogigamya jaya makhanivāsa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Be victorious, be victorious, O Gahanagehanivasa (one whose abode is mysterious). Be victorious, be victorious O Yogigamya (one who are knowable to the Yogins) ; Hail to you, O abode of sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.61.13 \|\|

*jaya jaya vedavedya jaya śāntikara \|*  
*jaya jaya yogicintya jaya puṣṭikara \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Be victorious, be victorious O Vedavedya (one who can be known only through the Vedas); be victorious, O Santikara (0 cause of peace and quiescence). Be victorious, be victorious, O Yogicintya (you who are to be contemplated by the Y ogins) be victorious, O PuHikara (cause of Grace or nourishment).

## \|\| 2.61.24 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇagandharvā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā stutvā namaskṛtya tadgatenāntarātmanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Be victorious, be victorious, O embodiment of knowledge; be victorious, O mine of good fortune. Be victorious, be victorious, O Bhavavedya (one who can be comprehended through devotion); be victorious, be victorious, O cause of liberation.

## \|\| 2.61.15 \|\|

*jaya vimaladeha jaya jaya sattvanilaya \|*  
*jaya jaya guṇasamūha jaya jaya yajñakara \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Be victorious, O deity whose body is free from impurities; be victorious, be victorious, O abode of Sattvic qualities. Hail, Hail to you, O GuQasamuha (you who are endowed with a multitude of attributes). Be victorious, be victorious O Yajiiakara the cause of sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.61.16 \|\|

*jaya jaya guṇavihīna jaya jaya mokṣakara \|*  
*jaya jaya bhūhiraṇya jaya jaya kāntiyuta \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Be victorious, be victorious, O deity devoid of attributes. Be victorious, be victorious, O cause of liberation. Be victorious, be victorious, O Bhiihiral).ya (you who possess lands and gold) ; be victorious, be victorious, O Kantiyuta who are endowed with shining splendour).

## \|\| 2.61.17 \|\|

*jaya lokaśaraṇa jaya jaya lakṣmīpate \|*  
*jaya paṅkajākṣa jaya jaya sṛṣṭikara \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Be victorious, O refuge of the worlds. Be victorious, be victorious, O lord of Laksmi, Be victorious O lotus-eyed one; be victorious, be victorious, O cause of creation.

## \|\| 2.61.18 \|\|

*jaya yogayuta jayātasīkusumaśyāmadeha \|*  
*jaya jaya subhadrā viṣṭadeha jaya lakṣmīpaṅkajabhogadeha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hail to you, O Yogayuta (one endowed with Yoga) ; be victorious O Atasikusuma-Syama-Deha, (one whose body is dark-complexioned like the flower of Atasi). Glory, glory to you O Samudravishtadeha (you whose body has penetrated the ocean). Be victorious, O god whose lotus-like body accords pleasure unto Laksmi.

## \|\| 2.61.19 \|\|

*jaya jaya bhaktibhāvana lokageya \|*  
*jaya lokakānta jaya paramaśānta \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Glory, glory to you O Bhaktibhavana (0 efficient cause of Devotion), O loka-geya (one worthy of being sung about by the world). Be victorious, O lover of the worlds: Be victorious O extremely quiescent one.

## \|\| 2.61.20 \|\|

*jaya jaya paramasāra jayacakradhara \|*  
*jaya bhogiyuta jaya nīlāmbara \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Be victorious, be victorious, O the highest essence; be victorious, O wielder of the discus; be victorious, O one resting on the serpent; be victorious, O bluerobed one.

## \|\| 2.61.21-22 \|\|

*jaya sāṅkhyanuta jaya kaluṣahara \|*  
*jaya kṛṣṇa jagannātha jaya saṅkarṣaṇānuja \|\| 21 \|\|*

*jaya jaya padmapalāśākṣa jaya vāñchitaphalaprada \|*  
*jaya mālāvṛtoraska jaya cakragadādhara \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Be victorious, be victorious, O deity with eyes like the petals of the lotus, Be victorious, O bestower of the desired benefit. Glory to the Deity whose chest is covered with garlands, Be victorious, O wielder of discus and iron club.

## \|\| 2.61.23-24 \|\|

*jaya padmālayākānta jaya viṣṇo namo'stu te \|*  
*evaṃ stutvā tadā devāḥ śakrādyā thṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*siddhacāraṇagandharvā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā stutvā namaskṛtya tadgatenāntarātmanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23a. Be victorious, O lord of Laksmi, be victorious O Visnu; obeisance be to you.

23b-24. After eulogising thus, Sakra and other Devas were delighted in their minds. The Siddhas, Caral).as, Gandharvas and other heaven-dwellers visited, eulogised and made obeisance to Krsna, Rama and Subhadra with their mind fully turned towards them. Then they went back to their respective residences.

## \|\| 2.61.25-31 \|\|

*kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ subhadrā ṃ! ca yānti svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam \|*  
*kapilāśatadānena yatphalaṃ puṣkare smṛtam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ kṛṣṇamālokya mañcasthaṃ sahalāyudham \|*  
*kanyāśatapradānena yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ kṛṣṇamālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ \|*  
*śataniṣkasuvarṇena bhūmidānena yatphalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ cānnadānena sarvātithyena yatphalam \|*  
*vṛṣotsargeṇa vidhivad grīṣme toyapradānataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tiladhenupradānena gajāśvarathadānataḥ \|*  
*cāndrā yaṇena cīrṇena tathā māsopavāsataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yatphalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu vratairdānaiśca yatphalam \|*  
*sasubhadrau rāmakṛṣṇau tallabhedvīkṣya mañcagau \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tasmānnaro'thavā nārī paśyettaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*snānaśeṣeṇa kṛṣṇasya toyena yadi mohini \|\| 31 \|\|*

25-26a. By visiting Krsna seated on the cushioned sofa in the company of Halayudha (Balarama), one attains that benefit which is derived by making a gift of a hundred cows, tawny-coloured variety in the holy centre of Pushkara.

26b-27a. By visiting Krsna seated on the cushioned couch a man obtains that benefit which is cited to result from the gift of a hundred virgins.

27b-31. By visiting Rama and Krsna along with Subhadra seated in the cushioned sofa, one obtains the following benefits viz. the gift of a hundred gold coins; the gift of lands; the gift of cooked rice; hospitability extended to every one; the rite of duly discharging the Vrsa (Bull); the gift of water during the summer; the gift of Tiladhenu (replica of cow in gingelly seeds); the gift of elephants, horses and chariots; the rite of Candrayana; observance of fast for a month; pilgrimage to all holy centres and holy rites and religious gifts. Hence a man or a woman must visit Purusottama. О MohinI, when duly bathed with the water that remains after Krsna has been duly bathed, the barren woman, the lady whose progeny is dead, unfortunate wretched persons, those who are affected by evil planets, those who arc possessed by Raksasas and others and those who are affected by ailments attain purity immediately. They attain desired benefits. О lady of good lustre they attain other things they desire, if they perform ablutions as per injunctions.

## \|\| 2.61.32 \|\|

*vandhyā mṛtaprajā vāpi durbhagā grahapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*rākṣasādyairgṛhītā vā tathā rogaiśca saṃhatāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All other sacred waters on the earth do not deserve even the sixteenth part of the remainder of water after the ablution of Krsna.

## \|\| 2.61.33 \|\|

*sadyastāḥ śuddhimāyānti vidhinā hyabhiṣecitāḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvantīpsitānkāmānyānyānvāñchanti suprabhe \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence the devotee should sprinkle limbs (of his body) with the sacred water that is left over after the ablution of the deity lying down in the waters. It is the sacred water that bestows all desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.61.34 \|\|

*puṇyāni yāni toyāni santyanyāni dharātale \|*  
*tāni snātāvaśeṣasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There is no doubt about this that those who visit Krsna who goes towards the south after ablution, are liberated from even the murder of a Brahmana and other sins.

## \|\| 2.61.35 \|\|

*tasmātsnānāvaśeṣeṇa jalena jalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*abhyukṣetsarvagātrāṇi sarvakāmapradena ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By visiting Krsna facing the south, a man obtains that benefit which is mentioned in the scriptures as the result of circumambulating the earth three times.

## \|\| 2.61.36 \|\|

*snātaṃ paśyanti ye kṛṣṇaṃ vrajantaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham \|*  
*brahmahatyādibhiḥ pāpairmucyante te na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By visiting Krsna proceeding to the south, one attains the benefit cited as the result of pilgrimages in the whole of the earth.

## \|\| 2.61.37-41 \|\|

*śāstreṣu yatphalaṃ proktaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇayā bhuvaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā naro labhetkṛṣṇaṃ tatphalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tīrthayātrāphalaṃ yattu pṛthivyāṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā yāntaṃ labhetkṛṣṇaṃ tatphalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham \|\| 38 \|\|*

*gaṅgādvāre ca kubjāmre kurukṣetre'kaparvaṇi \|*  
*puṣkarādiṣu cānyeṣu yatphalaṃ snānataḥ smṛtam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ dakṣiṇāsyaṃ tu kṛṣṇaṃ yāntaṃ nirīkṣya ca \|*  
*atha kiṃ bahunoktena yatphalaṃ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vedaśāstrapurāṇeṣu bhārate saṃhitādiṣu \|*  
*tatphalaṃ vīkṣya dakṣāsyau subhadrau balakeśavau \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. By visiting Krsna proceeding to the south one attains that benefit which is derivable from the holy bath at Gangadvara, Kubjamra, Kurukshetra during the solar eclipse, at Puskara and other sacred waters. Of what avail is much talk? By visiting Subhadra, Balarama and Kesava facing the south, one attains the benefit mentioned in the Vedas, scriptures, Puranas, Mahabharata, Samhitas and other works, as the fruits of meritorious rites.

## \|\| 2.61.42 \|\|

*guṇḍicāmaṇḍapaṃ yāntaṃ ye paśyanti rathe sthitam \|*  
*sabhadraṃ sabalaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ te yānti bhavanaṃ hareḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Those who see Krsna seated in the chariot along with Subhadra and Balarama and proceed to Gundica1 Mandapa go to the abode of Hari.

## \|\| 2.61.43 \|\|

*guṇḍicāyānasamaye phālgunyāṃ viṣuve tathā \|*  
*sakṛdyātrāṃ naraḥ kṛtvā viṣṇulokaṃ pragacchati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By undertaking pilgrimage even once, at the time of journey to Gundica, at the time of equinox in the month of Phalguna, a man goes to the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.61.44 \|\|

*yāvatīḥ kurute mattaryo yātrāḥ śrīpuruṣottame \|*  
*tāvatkalpaṃ viṣṇuloke vasediti viniścayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It is certain that a man will stay in the world of Visnu for as many Kalpas as the number of pilgrimages he undertakes to Sripurusottama.

## \|\| 2.61.45 \|\|

*yātrā dvādaśa sampūrṇā yadā syurvidhinandini \|*  
*tadā pratiṣṭhāṃ kurvīta vidhinā pāpanāśini \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О daughter of Brahma, when twelve pilgrimages are completed, the devotee shall perform the rite of installation in accordance with the injunctions. It will be destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.61.46 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāsi site pakṣe hyekādaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*gatvā jalāśayaṃ puṇyamācamya prayataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On the eleventh day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha, the devotee should go to the sacred waters, pure in mind and body. He should perform the rite of Acamana therein.

## \|\| 2.61.47 \|\|

*āvāhya sarvatīrthāni dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*tataḥ snānaṃ prakurvīta vidhibodhitavartmanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After invoking the holy Tirthas and meditating on Narayana, he should take holy bath in the manner indicated in the sacred precepts.

## \|\| 2.61.48 \|\|

*snātvā samyaktato devānṛṣīṃścāpi pitṝnsvakān \|*  
*santarpayettathānyāṃśca nāmagotroktipūrvakam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After the bath in a decent manner, the devotee should perform Tarpana rite for the Devas, sages, and Pitrs with the due utterance of their names and Gotras.

## \|\| 2.61.49-50 \|\|

*uttīrya vāsasī dhaute nirmale paridhāya ca \|*  
*upaspṛśya vidhānena tathopasthāya bhāskaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vedamātaramāvartya puṇyāmaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*sauramantrāṃstathā cānyāṃstriḥ parītya namedra vim \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. After coming out of the water he should wear two pure clothes and perform the Acamana rite as well as the due worship of Bhaskara the sun. He should then repeat Gayatri, the holy Mantra, the mother of the Vedas, one hundred and eight times: and also other Mantras pertaining to the sun. He should circumambulate three times and then bow to the sun.

## \|\| 2.61.51-53 \|\|

*vedoktaṃ triṣu varṇeṣu snānaṃ japyamudāthṛtam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*strīśūdra yorvarārohe vedoktavidhivarjitam \|*  
*tato vrajenmandirasthaṃ bhaktyā śrīpuruṣottamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*prakṣālya hastau pādau ca upaspṛśya yathāvidhi \|*  
*ghṛtena snāpayeddevaṃ kṣīreṇa tadanantaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. The procedure for the holy dip and the repetition of Japas is, in regard to the three castes, the same as mentioned in the Vedas. О fair lady, in regard to the Sudras and the women the repetition of the Vedic texts is to be avoided. Thereafter, he should, with devotion, go to Sri Purusottama installed in the temple. According to the injunctions, he should wash his hands and feet and perform the Acamanarite. He should bathe the lord with ghee and thereafter with milk.

## \|\| 2.61.54 \|\|

*madhugandhodakenāpi tīrthacandanavāriṇā \|*  
*tato vastrayugaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhaktyā taṃ paridhāpayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He should then bathe deity with honey, fragrant water and the water from theTirtha mixed with the sandal paste. Thereafter, the devotee should clothe the deity with excellent pair of clothes.

## \|\| 2.61.55 \|\|

*candanāgurukarpūraiḥ kuṅkumena vilepayet \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā padmaiśca puruṣottamam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55 He should smear deity with sandal paste, agallo- chum, camphor and saffron. He should worship Purusottama by means of lotuses, with great devotion.

## \|\| 2.61.56-57 \|\|

*sampūjyaivaṃ jagannāthaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ harim \|*  
*dhūpaṃ cāgurusaṃyuktaṃ dehe devasya cāgrataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*guggulaṃ ca suniṣpūtaṃ dahedghṛtasamanvitam \|*  
*dīpaṃ prajvālayedbhaktyā yathāśakti ghṛtena vai \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. After thus worshipping Hari, the lord of the universe the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation, the devotee should burn incense mixed with agallochum. He should burn Guggula (aromatic resin) of the pure variety along with ghee. With devotion he should light the lamp with ghee in accordance with his capacity.

## \|\| 2.61.58 \|\|

*anyām̐ śca dīpakāndadyāddvādaśaiva samāhitaḥ \|*  
*goghṛtena tu deveśi tilatailena vā punaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. With great concentration, he should light twelve other lamps, О goddess, with cow’s ghee or with gingelly oil.

## \|\| 2.61.59-60 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ pāyasāpūpaśaṣkulīveṣṭakāni ca \|*  
*modakaṃ phāṇikaṃ cānyatphalāni ca nivedayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*evaṃ pañcopacāreṇa sampūjya puruṣottamam \|*  
*oṃnamaḥ puruṣottamāyeti japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. The devotee then offers the following as Naived- yas viz; milk-pudding, friend pie, coiled baked pie, circular fried coils, sweet meats, molasses and fruits. After completing the worship of Purusottama by means of the fivefold services, the devotee should perform hundred and eight times the Japa of the Mantra — “Ош obeisance to Purusottama”.

## \|\| 2.61.61 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayeddevaṃ daṇḍavatpraṇipatya ca \|*  
*tato'cayedguruṃ bhaktyā puṣpavastrānulepanaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thereafter, he should propitiate the lord by bowing down and prostrating before him like a staff. Thereafter, he should honour the preceptor with devotion, with flowers, garments and unguents.

## \|\| 2.61.62-63 \|\|

*nānayorantaraṃ yasmādvidyate vidhinandini \|*  
*devasyopari kurvīta maṇḍapaṃ susamāhitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*nānāpuṣpaiḥ suviśadaṃ vicitraṃ maṇḍalaṃ puraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāvadhāraṇaṃ paścājjāgaraṃ kārayenniśi \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. О daughter of Brahma, (the preceptor should be honoured) since there is no difference between these two (i.e, the preceptor and the lord). With concentration and purity of mind, the devotee should erect the ceremonial hall (МагмДара) over the lord. The zone in front should be brilliant and variegated with flowers. After making an emphatic determination at the outset, the devotee should keep awake at night.

## \|\| 2.61.64 \|\|

*kathāṃ ca vāsudevasya gītikāṃ cāpi kārayet \|*  
*dhyāyanpaṭhanstuvandevaṃ praṇayedra janīṃ budhaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The learned devotee should cause the discourse on Vasudeva conducted and songs sung about him. He should spend the night meditating, reading and eulogising the lord.

## \|\| 2.61.65-68 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale dvādaśyāṃ dvādaśaiva tu \|*  
*nimantrayedvratasnātānbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān \|\| 65 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇajñāñchrotriyānsaṃyatendri yān \|*  
*snātvā samyagvidhānena dhautavāsā jitendri yaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*snāpayetpūrvavadbhaktyā tatrasthaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaistūpahārairnaivedyairdīpakaistathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*upacārairbahuvidhaiḥ praṇipātaiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*jāpyastutinamaskārairgītavādyairmanoharaiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-66a. Then, after the DvadasI has dawned splendidly, the devotee should invite twelve Brahmanas who are life-long students of the Vedas, who have taken a holy bath after holy rites, are well conversant with the Itihasa and the Puranas, have learned the Vedas and have restrained their sense-organs.

66b-68. After duly completing holy bath, the devotee should wear washed cloth and restrain and conquer the sense- organs. He should then bathe Purusottama who is stationed there, with devotion as before. He shall propitiate the lord of the universe with scents, fragrant flowers, presents, offerings of food, lamps, many kinds of reverential services, salutations, circum- ambulations, Japas, eulogies, prostrations, pleasant songs and instrumental music.

## \|\| 2.61.69-73 \|\|

*sampūjyaivaṃ jagannāthaṃ brāhmaṇānpūjayettataḥ \|*  
*dvādaśaiva tu gāstebhyo dattvā kanakameva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

*chatropānadyugaṃ cārpya kāṃsyapātraṃ ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tatastānbhojayedviprānbhojyaṃ pāyasapūrvakam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*pakvānnaṃ bhakṣyabhojyaṃ ca saguḍaṃ śarkarānvitam \|*  
*tato bhuktvā susantṛptānbrāhmaṇānsusthamānasān \|\| 71 \|\|*

*dvādaśaivodakumbhāṃśca grāhayettānsamodakān \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathāśakti viṣṇutulyaṃ viriṃcije \|\| 72 \|\|*

*suvarṇavastragodhānyairdra vyaiścānyairvarairbudhaḥ \|*  
*sampūjya tānnamaskṛtya imaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 73 \|\|*

69-70a. Then he should honour the Brahmanas, He should give them twelve cows, gold, an umbrella, a pair of sandals and bellmetal vessel with devotion.

70b-73. He should, thereafter, feed the Brahmanas with milkpudding at the outset. Afterwards different edibles and foodstuffs, cooked rice with jaggery and sugarcandy shall be offered to them. When the Brahmanas are satisfied after the meal and have had their rest mentally (and physically), he should offer them twelve water pots along with sweets. О daughter of Brahma, he should give them monetary gifts too according to his capacity. The learned devotee should worship them on a par with Visnu by means of gold, clothes, cows, food- grains, and other articles. After making obeisance to them, he should repeat this Mantra.

## \|\| 2.61.74 \|\|

*sarvavyāpī jagannāthaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*anādinidhano devaḥ prīyatāṃ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. (Mantra) “May the omnipresent lord who is the master of the universe, who wields conch, discus and iron club, may Purusottama, the lord devoid of beginning and death, be pleased”.

## \|\| 2.61.75 \|\|

*ityuccārya tato viprāṃstriḥ parikramya sādaram \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā bhaktyā sācāryāṃstānvisarjayet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. After uttering this and respectfully circumambulating the Brahmanas three times, the devotee should bow down his head and bid them farewell with the preceptor.

## \|\| 2.61.76-78 \|\|

*tatastānbrāhmaṇānbhaktyā cāsīmāntamanuvrajet \|*  
*anuvrajya tu tānviprānnamaskṛtya nivartya ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*bāndhavaiḥ svajanairyuktastato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā naraḥ samyaṅ nārī vā labhate phalam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*aśvamedhasahasrasya rājasūyaśatasya ca \|*  
*atītaṃ śatamuddhṛtya puruṣāṇāṃ narottamaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. He should follow the Brahmanas upto boundary line of his village with devotion. After following the Brahmanas, he should bow to them once again and return. Having returned home, he should silently take food in the company of his kins and relatives. By doing thus, the man or the woman devotee shall derive the benefit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rajasuyas. The excellent man shall uplift a hundred previous ancestors.

## \|\| 2.61.79-82 \|\|

*bhaviṣyacca śataṃ devi divyarūpadharo'vyayaḥ \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasampannaḥ sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā guṇarūpavayo'nvitaḥ \|*  
*stūyamāno'tha gandharvairapsarobhiḥ samantataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena kāmagena sthireṇa ca \|*  
*patākādhvajayuktena śatasūryaprabheṇa ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

*udyotayandiśaḥ sarvā ākāśe vigataklamaḥ \|*  
*yuvā mahābalo dhīmānviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 82 \|\|*

79-82. О gentle lady, he will uplift a hundred successors as well. He will be assuming the divine unchanging form. He will be endowed with all auspicious characteristics. He will be bedecked in all ornaments. He will be flourishing with all desires in the mind realized. He will be blessed with good attributes, comeliness and youthful age (or longevity). He will be eulogised by Gandharvas and Apsaras all round. He will be going to the world of Visnu by means of an aerial chariot that has the brilliance of the sun, which can go as he pleases, is steady, fitted with flags and banners and which has the lustre of a hundred suns. He will be brightening all the quarters thereby in the firmament. He will be devoid of exhaustion. He will become a youth of great strength and intelligence. Thus he will go to the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.61.83 \|\|

*tatra kalpaśataṃ yāvadbhuṅkte bhogānyathepsitān \|*  
*stuto munivarairdevi tiṣṭhecca vigatajvaraḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There he enjoys desired pleasures for the period of a hundred Kalpas. О gentle lady, he will stay there eulogised by excellent sages. He will be devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 2.61.84 \|\|

*yathādevo jagannāthaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*tathā'sau mudito devi dhṛtvā rūpaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. О gentle lady, just as the lord of the universe, the wielder of the conch, discus and iron club rejoices after assuming the four-armed form, so this devotee will be rejoicing in that form.

## \|\| 2.61.85 \|\|

*bhuktvā tatra varānbhogānkrīḍitvā suciraṃ sati \|*  
*tadante brahmasadanamāyātyakhilakāmadam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. О chaste lady, after enjoying excellent pleasures there and after sporting there for a long time, at the end thereof, he goes to the abode of Brahma that yields all desires.

## \|\| 2.61.86 \|\|

*siddhavidyādharaiścāpi śobhitaṃ surakinnaraiḥ \|*  
*kālaṃ navatikalpaṃ tu tatra bhuktvā sukhaṃ naraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. It is the abode that is rendered splendid by the Siddhas, Vidyadharas, Devas and Kinnaras.

## \|\| 2.61.87 \|\|

*rudra lokaṃ samāyāti sukhadaṃ sevitaṃ suraiḥ \|*  
*siddhavidyādharairyakṣairbhūṣitaṃ daityadānavaiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. After enjoying happiness there for the period of ninety Kalpas, the man goes to the world of Rudra that bestows happiness and that is resorted to by Devas, Siddhas, Vidyadharas and Yaksas. It is adorned by Daityas and Danavas.

## \|\| 2.61.88 \|\|

*aśītikalpakālaṃ tu tatra bhuktvā sukhaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*tadante yāti golokaṃ sarvabhogasamanvitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After enjoying happiness there for the period of eighty Kalpas, the man at the end of that period, goes to Goloka equipped with all means of pleasures.

## \|\| 2.61.89-91 \|\|

*surasiddhāpsarobhiśca śobhitaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*tatra saptatikalpaṃ tu bhuktvā bhogānabhīpsitān \|\| 89 \|\|*

*paścādāyāti vai lokaṃ prājāpatyamanuttamam \|*  
*ṣaṣṭikalpaṃ sukhaṃ tatra bhuktvā nānāvidhaṃ mudā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*tadante śakrabhavanaṃ nānāścaryaṃ samāvrajet \|*  
*āgatya tatra pañcāśatkalpaṃ bhuktvā sukhaṃ naraḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. It is a place rendered splendid by Devas, Siddhas and Apsaras. It is charming. He enjoys desired pleasures there for the period of seventy Kalpas. Thereafter, he goes to the excellent world of Prajapati. Joyously he experiences different kinds of happiness there for the period of sixty kalpas. At the end of that period, he shall go to Sakra’s abode containing different kinds of wonderful features. There the man enjoys happiness for the period of fifty Kalpas. He then goes to the abode of immortal ones, embellished with aerial chariots.

## \|\| 2.61.92-96 \|\|

*prapadyate'maragṛhānvimānaiḥ samalaṅkṛtān \|*  
*catvāriṃśatkalpakālaṃ bhogānbhuktvā sudurlabhān \|\| 92 \|\|*

*nākṣatraṃ lokamāyāti nānāsaukhyasamanvitam \|*  
*tatra bhuktvā varānbhogāṃstriṃśatkalpaṃ yathepsitān \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tasmādgacchati taṃ lokaṃ śaśāṅkasya viriṃñcije \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭhati somo'sau sarvadevairalaṅkṛtaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tatra viṃśatikalpaṃ tu bhuktvā bhogaṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*ādityasya tato lokamāyāti surapūjitam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tatra bhuktvā śubhānbhogandaśa kalpaṃ sunirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmādāyāti bhavanaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ sudurlabham \|\| 96 \|\|*

92-96. He enjoys rare pleasures there for the period of forty Kalpas. Then he goes to the stellar world equipped with different kinds of happiness and enjoys there excellent pleasures as desired, for the period of thirty Kalpas. О daughter of Brahma, from there he goes to the lunar world where stays the moon adorned by the Devas. After enjoying rare pleasures for the period of twenty Kalpas, he goes over to the world of the sun god worshipped by Devas. After enjoying splendid pleasures there for the period of ten Kalpas, he becomes contented and delighted; thence he goes to the abode of Gandharvas that is very inaccessible.

## \|\| 2.61.97 \|\|

*tatra bhogānsamastāṃśca kalpamekaṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*bhuktvā cāyāti medinyāṃ rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. There he enjoys all kinds of pleasures upto satiety for the period of a Kalpa. Then he comes over to the earth and is born as a righteous king.

## \|\| 2.61.98 \|\|

*cakravartī mahāvīryo guṇaiḥ sarvairalaṅkṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā rājyaṃ tu dharmeṇa yajñairiṣṭvā sadakṣiṇaiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. He becomes an emperor of great prowess. He is bedecked in all attributes. He rules over the kingdom righteously and performs Yajnas with liberal monetary gifts.

## \|\| 2.61.99 \|\|

*tadante yogināṃ lokaṃ gatvā mokṣapradaṃ śivam \|*  
*tatra bhuktvā varānbhogānyāvadābhūtasamplavam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. At the end of that period, he goes to the world of yogin that is auspicious and that bestows salvation. As long as all living beings are not dissolved, he enjoys excellent pleasures there.

## \|\| 2.61.100-101 \|\|

*tasmātpunarihāyāto jāyate yogināṃ kule \|\| 100 \|\|*

*pravare vaiṣṇave bhadre durlabhe sādhusammate \|*  
*caturvedī vipravaro brahmayajñaparaḥ sati \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. Coming therefrom he is born in the family of Yogins, in an excellent family of devotees of Visnu, difficult of access and received with approbation by the good. О chaste lady, he becomes an excellent Brahmana, a master of four Vedas, devoted to the performance of BrahmaYajna.

## \|\| 2.61.102-103 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavaṃ yogamāsādya kaivalyaṃ mokṣamāpnuyāt \|*  
*evaṃ yātrāphalaṃ tubhyaṃ proktaṃ śrīpuruṣottame \|\| 102 \|\|*

*bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṝṇāṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. By adopting Yoga pertaining to Visnu, he shall attain liberation. Thus the benefit of the pilgrimage to Purusottama has been recounted to you. It yields both worldly pleasures and salvation unto men. What else do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 62. The greatness of the most Eminent Tirtha Prayaga 'The Procedure of Pilgrimage

## \|\| 2.62.1-3 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca- etacchrutvā tu bhūpāla mohinī vidhinandinī \|*  
*puruṣottamamāhātmyaṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*punaḥ papraccha taṃ vipraṃ vasuṃ svasya purohitam \|*  
*mohinyuvāca- śrutamatyadbhutaṃ vipra puruṣottamasambhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*māhātmyaṃ cādhunā brūhi prayāgasyāpi suvrata \|*  
*tīrtharājaḥ prayāgākhyaḥ śrutaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā guro \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vasishtha Said:

1-3. О king Mandhata, on hearing this greatness of Purusottama (ksetra), that bestows worldly pleasures and salvation, MohinI the daughter of Brahma asked that Brahmana Vasu, her own family priest. Mohini requested: О Brahmana, the very wonderful glory of Purusottama ksetra has been heard. Now tell me the greatness of Prayaga too, О Brahmana, observer of holy rites. О preceptor, That the Tirtha Prayaga is the king of all Tirthas, has been heard by me before.

## \|\| 2.62.4-5 \|\|

*tanmāhātmyaṃ mamākhyāhi tīrthayātrāvidhānayuk \|*  
*sa mānyānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ tīrthānāṃ gamane dvija \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yatkarttavyaṃ ca vidhinā nṛbhirddharmaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa dvijo rājanmohinyā bhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Narrate to me its greatness along with the procedure of its pilgrimages. What specific formalities be observed by men devoted to virtuous rites in regard to special sacred places regarded as highly meritorious and respectable, Tirthas in particular.

## \|\| 2.62.6 \|\|

*sāmānyavidhipūrvaṃ tatprayāgākhyānamabravīt \|*  
*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu bhadre pravakṣyāmi tīrthābhigamane vidhim \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О king on hearing those words uttered by Mohini, that Brahmana recounted to her the traditional account of Prayaga with the enunciation of the general rules of pilgrimage at the outset. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.62.7 \|\|

*yaṃ samāśritya manujo yathoktaṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tīrthābhigamanaṃ puṇyaṃ yajñairapi viśiṣyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Listen, О gentle lady, I shall recount the rules of procedure in undertaking pilgrimages. It is only by observing those rules that a man can attain the benefit as mentioned. Goirfjg to a pilgrimage is meritorious; It surpasses even Yajnas.

## \|\| 2.62.8 \|\|

*anupoṣya trirātrāṇi tīrthānyapyabhigamya ca \|*  
*adattvā kāñcanaṃ gāśca daridro jāyate naraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A man becomes indigent by not observing fast for three days, by not giving gold in gift and by not offering cows after visiting holy places.

## \|\| 2.62.9 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairiṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*na tatphalamavāpnoti tīrthābhigamanena yat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even by performing Agnistoma and other Yajnaswith magnificent monetary gifts, one does not attain that benefit which results from undertaking pilgrimages.

## \|\| 2.62.10 \|\|

*ajñānenāpi yasyeha tīrthābhigamanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhaḥ sa svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even he who casually visits a holy centre unwittingly shall attain all desires and flourish. He is honoured in the heavently world.

## \|\| 2.62.11 \|\|

*sthānaṃ ca labhate nityaṃ dhanadhānyasamākulam \|*  
*eśvaryajñānasampūrṇaḥ sadā bhavati bhogavān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He perpetually obtains a position that is full of wealth and food-grains. He shall be full of perfect knowledge and prosperity. He shall have pleasures for ever.

## \|\| 2.62.12 \|\|

*tāritāḥ pitarastena narakātprapitāmahāḥ \|*  
*yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Pitrs (manes) and great-grand-fathers have been redeemed from hell by that person whose hands, feet and mind are well-controlled.

## \|\| 2.62.13 \|\|

*vidyā tapaśca kīrtiśca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|*  
*pratigrahādapāvṛttaḥ santuṣṭo yena kenacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who refrains from accepting monetary gifts, one who is satisfied with whatever one gets shall attain learning, penance, renown and the benefit of pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.62.14-17 \|\|

*ahaṅkāravimuktaśca sa tīrthaphalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*akalpako nirārambho laghvāhāro jitendri yaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vimuktaḥ sarvasaṅgaistu sa tīrthaphalabhāgbhavet \|*  
*tīrthānyanusarandhīraḥ śraddadhānaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kṛtapāpo viśudhyettu kiṃ punaḥ śuddhakarmakṛt \|*  
*aśraddadhānaḥ pāpārto nāstiko'cchinnasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*hetuniṣṭhaśca pañcaite na tīrthaphalabhāginaḥ \|*  
*nṛṇāṃ pāpakṛtāṃ tīrthe pāpasya śamanaṃ bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*
