*tataḥ prabhṛti lakṣmīstu viṣṇorvakṣaḥsthale sthitā \|*  
*babhūva viṣṇupatnī sā sapatnīrahitā śubhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ever since that time, Laksmi has established herself on the chest of Visnu. О auspicious lady, she became the wife of Visnu. She was devoid of any co-wife.

## \|\| 2.68.8 \|\|

*bhaviṣyakāryaṃ vijñāya devā viṣṇusamājñayā \|*  
*kāmodākhye pure devīṃ kāmodāṃ pūjayanti hi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Realising the task to be achieved in the future, Devas, at the behest of Visnu, worship goddess KamodS in the city called Kamoda.

## \|\| 2.68.9 \|\|

*sā tatra vartate nityaṃ viṣṇusaṃyogakāmyayā \|*  
*bhāryātvaṃ bhāvataḥ prāptā viṣṇudhyānaparāyaṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She stays there perpetually with the desire for the union with Visnu. She has attained the state of his wife in imagination. She is engaged in meditation on Visnu.

## \|\| 2.68.10 \|\|

*sa tatra bhāvagamyo vai viṣṇuḥ sarvagato mahān \|*  
*anayāpi tayā nityaṃ vartate tatsamīpataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Lord Visnu, the great omnipresent deity, approachable through sincerity and devotion by her, stays there perpetually near her.

## \|\| 2.68.11 \|\|

*sa devairvāsurairdevi munibhirmānavaistathā \|*  
*alakṣyadeho viśvātmā vartate dhyānagocaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О gentle lady, that deity, the Atman of the universe, is imperceptible to the Devas, Asuras, sages and human beings. He can be visualised by means of meditation.

## \|\| 2.68.12-15 \|\|

*dhyānenaiva prapaśyanti devāśca munayo vibhum \|*  
*kāmodā sā mahābhāgā yadā hasati mohini \|\| 12 \|\|*

*harṣeṇa tu samādiṣṭā tadāśrūṇi patanti ca \|*  
*ānandāśrūṇi gaṅgāyāṃ patitāni sureśvari \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kāmodākhyāni padmāni tāni tatra bhavanti ca \|*  
*pītāni ca sugandhīni mahāmodapradāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yastu bhāgyavaśāllabdhvā tāni taiḥ pūjayecchivam \|*  
*sa labhedvāñchitānkāmānityājñā pārameśvarī \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Devas and sages observe the lord only through meditation. О MohinI, when Kamoda, the highly blessed lady laughs overwhelmed with delight, tears of delight fall down into Ganga. О goddess of Devas, these tears become lotuses named Kamoda. They are yellow, fragrant and extremely pleasant. He who comes to acquire them, thanks to his good luck, and worships Siva with them, shall attain cherished desires. This is the behest of Paramegvara (The Supreme Lord Siva).

## \|\| 2.68.16 \|\|

*duḥkhajāni tathāśrūṇi kadācitprapatanti hi \|*  
*tebhyaśca tāni padmāni vigandhīnyudbhavanti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Sometimes tears of misery too fall. From those tears lotuses of bad odour crop up.

## \|\| 2.68.17 \|\|

*taistu yaḥ pūjayeddevaṃ śaṅkaraṃ lokaśaṅkaram \|*  
*sa yujyetākhilairdukhaiḥ pūrvapāpairvimohitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Deluded by the previous sins, if any one worships lord Sankara, the benefactor of the worlds, with those lotus flowers of bad odour he will be oppressed by all miseries.

## \|\| 2.68.18-21 \|\|

*gaṅgādvārādupari ca daśayojanake sthitam \|*  
*kāmodaṃ tatra varṣaikaṃ yo japeddvādaśākṣaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*varṣāṃte caitramāsasya dvādaśyāṃ vidhinandini \|*  
*vāsantīṃ ca śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā haseddharṣataḥ sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tāni padmāni sa labhennānyadā ko'pi karhicit \|*  
*tatra yaḥ snāti manuje viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dhyātvā puraṃ ca kāmodaṃ sa bhavedviṣṇuvallabhaḥ \|*  
*devātānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca vallabho nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. Kamoda is situated ten Yojanas above Ganga- dvara. The devotee should perform the Japa of twelve syllabled Mantra for the whole of a year. О daughter of Brahma, at the end of the year on the tweflh day in the month of Chaitra, she will see the splendour of the spring and thanks to her delight, will laugh continuously; then the devotee may get those lotuses and by no means at any other time. The man who is devoted to Visnu and who takes a holy bath there after contemplating on the city of Kamoda, shall bea favouriteof Visnu. There is no doubt in this that he will be a favourite with the Devas and Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.68.22 \|\|

*yo dvādaśa samāstatra tiṣṭhejjapaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*salabheddarśanaṃ sākṣātkāmodāyāḥ śubhānane \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О splendid-faced lady, he who stays there for twelve years engaged in the repetition ofjapa shall obtain the vision of Kamoda herself.

## \|\| 2.68.23 \|\|

*yaṃ yaṃ cintayate kāmaṃ tatra tīrthe naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*snānamātreṇa labhate taṃ tamaihikamaṅgane \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О lady, by means of holy bath alone, the pure man attains whatever worldly pleasure he may seek.

## \|\| 2.68.24 \|\|

*etaddhi paramaṃ tīrthaṃ labhyaṃ bhāgyavaśādbhavet \|*  
*himātyayādage bhadre durgamaṃ vikaṭasthalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О gentle lady, this is an impassable rugged place. When the snow is melted away on the mountain, this greatest Tirtha may be accessible, thanks to good luck.

## \|\| 2.68.25 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ kāmodākhyānakaṃ śubham \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā so'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus the auspicious account of Kamoda has been wholly recounted. The man who listens to this with devotion is liberated from sins.

## Chapter 69. The Greatness af Kamaksha

## \|\| 2.69.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ kāmodakākhyānaṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇyadaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*sāmprataṃ śrotumicchāmi kāmākṣāyāḥ phalaṃ dvija \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohinx said:

1\. The narrative of Kamodaka that is destructive of sins and conducive to the attainment of merit has been heard by me. О Brahmana, now I wish to hear the benefit derived from devotion of Kamakija.1

Vasu said

## \|\| 2.69.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- kāmākṣā paramā devī pūrvasyāṃ diśi saṃsthitā \|*  
*sāgarānūpataṭagā kalau siddhipradā nṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The greatest goddess Kamaksa is stationed in the eastern quarter. She is present on the shores of the marshy place near the Sea. She is the bestower of Siddhi on men in the Kali age.

## \|\| 2.69.3 \|\|

*yastatra gatvā kāmākṣāṃ sampūjya niyatāśanaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhedekāṃ niśāṃ bhadre sa paśyettāṃ dṛḍhāsanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The devotee who goes there and observing restriction in the deity, worships Kamaksa and stays a night there seating himself steadfastly, shall then visualize her, О gentle lady.

## \|\| 2.69.4 \|\|

*sā devī bhīmarūpeṇa yāti sandarśanaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā na caledyo vai sa siddhiṃ vāñchitāṃ labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. That goddess appears before men in a terrible form. He who is not moved with fear on seeing her, shall attain the desired Siddhi-

## \|\| 2.69.5 \|\|

*yastu dṛṣṭvā sureśānīṃ kāmākṣāṃ bhīmarūpiṇīm \|*  
*āsanāccalitaḥ sadyaḥ sa vikṣipto bhaveddhruvam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If on seeing the goddess of Devas, Kamaksa of terrific features, the devotee sways from his seats instantaneouly, he shall then certainly become distracted in mind and behaviour.

## \|\| 2.69.6 \|\|

*tatrāste pārvatīputraḥ siddhanātho varānane \|*  
*ugre tapasi lokaiḥ sa prekṣyate na kadācana \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О fair-faced lady, Siddhanatha1, the son of Parvatl stays there (engaged) in a severe penance. He is never seen by the people.

## \|\| 2.69.7 \|\|

*kṛtatretādvāpareṣu pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate'khilaiḥ \|*  
*kalāvantarhitastiṣṭhedyāvatpādaḥ kalervrajet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. During the three Yugas: Krta, Treta and Dvapara he was directly perceived by every one. In the Kali age, as long as the first quarter of it does not pass off, he shall stay invisible.

## \|\| 2.69.8-9 \|\|

*kaleḥ pāde gate caikasminghore ca dharātale \|*  
*sa vai pratyakṣatāṃ prāpya sādhayedakhilaṃ janam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mohanādyairupāyaistu mlecchaprāyāñjanāṃstadā \|*  
*kṛtvā vaśe mahābhāge gamayettripadaṃ kaleḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. When a quarter of the Kali age has passed off and the surface of the earth has become terrible, he becomes visible and controls the people. О blessed lady, by his powers like Mohana (fascination) Uccatana (eradication) etc., he gains control over the people most of whom are Mlecchas1 (alien out-castes). He will spend the remaininig three quarters of the Kali age by keeping them submissive.

## \|\| 2.69.10-11 \|\|

*yastatra gatvā siddheśaṃ bhaktibhāvasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*cintayedvarṣamātraṃ tu kāmākṣāṃ nityadārcayan \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sa labheddarśanaṃ svapne darśanānte samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sūcitāṃ tena siddhiṃ sa labdhvā siddho bhavedbhuvi \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The devotee should go to Siddhanatha and meditate on him with devotional feelings, for a whole year. Every day he must worship Kamaksa. He shall then gain the vision of Siddhanatha in the dream. At the end of the vision he shall have great concentration. He shall achieve Siddhi indicated by it and be a Siddha on the Earth.

## \|\| 2.69.12 \|\|

*vicaretsarvalokānāṃ kāmanāḥ pūrayañśubhe \|*  
*trilokyāṃ yāni vastūni tāni saṅkarṣayedvarāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О auspicious lady, he will be wandering, fulfilling the desires of all the worlds. By means of the boon, he will attract all the articles in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.69.13 \|\|

*sa matsyanāthaḥ kila tatra saṃstho vijñānapāraṅgama eva bhadre \|*  
*cacāra lokābhimataṃ vitanvaṃstapo'tighoraṃ na ca yāti dṛṣṭim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He is Matsyanatha (Matsyendra of the Natha cult) stationed there. О gentle lady, he has mastered the perfect knowledge. He performed a terrible penance, distributing among the people whatever they desired. But he never becomes visible.

## \|\| 2.69.14 \|\|

*yugānyanekāni purā bhramitvā lokānsamagrānahateṣṭagatyā \|*  
*tapasthito'dyāsti mahānubhāvo na kālavegena śubhe'bhibhūtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Formerly, he had roamed all over the worlds without his movement being impeded, for the period of many Yugas. Today the noble-minded personage is completely engaged in penance. О auspicious lady, he is not oppressed by the velocity of Kala (the force of the stream of time).

## \|\| 2.69.15 \|\|

*gaṇḍāntajātastu purābhave'bhūddvijasya kasyāpi sutaḥ subhadre \|*  
*sa jātamātraḥ kila puṣkarākhye dvīpe'sya pitrā hyudadhau visṛṣṭaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О highly blessed lady, in the previous birth he had been born as the son of a certain Brahmana. He was born during the astrologically evil period of a ‘Gandanta’ (the tenth astrological Yoga). Hence the moment he was born in the continent named Puskara, he was cast into the ocean by his father.

## \|\| 2.69.16 \|\|

*prakṣiptamātraṃ kila tatra bālaṃ matsyo'grasītko'pi vidherniyogāt \|*  
*tatra sthito'nekayugāni so'bhūtkālasya gatyā hyajarāmarāṅgaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As soon as he was thrown into the sea, thanks to a lucky coincidence, a certain fish swallowed the boy. For many Yugas, he remained there without ageing or dying due to the flux of time. 9

## \|\| 2.69.17 \|\|

*tataḥ kadācitpriyayā pradiṣṭo maheśvaraḥ sārddhamagaprasūtyā \|*  
*tattvopadeśāya jagāma bhadre sa lokalokācalamaprameyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter, О gentle lady, once urged by his wife, the daughter of the mountain, Mahesvara, the incomprehensible deity accompanied her to the mountain Lokaloka for the instruction in the esoteric principles.

## \|\| 2.69.18-20 \|\|

*tatsaumyaśṛṅge maṇibhiḥ pradīpte sthitvā kṣaṇārddhaṃ harimagnacetāḥ \|*  
*devīmumāṃ sampratibodhya śaktyā tālatrayeṇāpyabhibhūya sattvān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*uvāca tattvaṃ surahasyabhūtaṃ yaddvādaśārṇārthanijasvarūpam \|*  
*tatastu sā śailasutā maheśaṃ mārāntakaṃ yāvadabhipraṇamya \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ajñāya tattvaṃ samavasthitā'bhūttāvatsa matsyastu mahārṇavasthaḥ \|*  
*drutaṃ samutplutya jagāma śṛṅgaṃ yo viprabālo hyudare sthito'sya \|*  
*sa tattvasiddho'khilabandhamuktaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-19a. On its gentle and beautiful peak illuminated by jewels, the lord stood for half a moment with his mind engrossed in Hari. He enlightened spiritually goddess Uma by means of his Sakti. He drove away the Sattvas (animals, living beings) with three Talas (clapping of hands).

19b-20. He then told her the Tattva (the real principle) in the form of the meaning of the twelve-syllabled Mantra which had been an esoteric secret. The daughter of the mountain bowed down to Mahes'a, the destroyer of Mara. She understood the principle a little and sat there firmly. At that time the fish in the great ocean immediately jumped on to the peak.1 The Brahmana boy who was within its belly became a Tattva- siddha (a person who realised the principle) and freed of all bondages.

## \|\| 2.69.21 \|\|

*nirgamya matsyodarataḥ śubhāsye namaḥ pracakre bhavayoḥ purastāt \|*  
*vijñātatattvo'pi maheśvarastaṃ papraccha tadgarbhagaternidānam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О splendid-faced lady, coming out of the belly of the fish, he made obeisance in front of Siva and Uma. Though he was aware of the truth Mahesvara asked him the cause of being within the womb of the fish.

## \|\| 2.69.22-23 \|\|

*sa varṇayāmāsa yathārthameva tayoḥ puraḥ sarvamapi pravṛttam \|*  
*ākarṇya tadvṛttamanuprasannā somā maheśānumatiṃ ca kṛtvā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*taṃ kalpayāmāsa sutaṃ śubhāṅge sotsaṅga āsthāpya cucumba vaktram \|*  
*suto mamāyaṃ kila matsyanātho vijñātatattvo'khilasiddhanāthaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. In front of them, he recounted everything in the manner it had happened. On hearing what had happened to him, Uma was pleased. Getting the permission of Mahesa, she made him her son. О fair-limbed lady, placing him on her lap she kissed his face and said:- “O, is this not my Son? He is Matsyanatha, (lord of fish). He has understood the principle. Hence he is Siddhanatha for all.

## \|\| 2.69.24-25 \|\|

*nijecchayā samprati yātu lokānkīrtiṃ vitanvansukhamāvayośca \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛtyeṣa suto'mbikāyā lokānsamagrānpravihṛtya kāmam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatsiddhapīṭhaṃ samavāpya tatra tapasyupādiṣṭa ivāsthito'sti \|*  
*taṃ siddhanāthaṃ manasā vicintya naro bhavetsiddhasamastakāmaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Let him go over the worlds according to his will. May he accord happiness unto us now.” Ever since that time this son of Ambika roamed about all the worlds as he pleased. He attained the Siddhapitha.1 He has occupied that seat as one engaged in penance. By mentally meditating on Siddhanatha, a man shall be one who has realised all his desires.

## \|\| 2.69.26-27 \|\|

*saṃprāpya vidyāṃ nijavākyavāhe nimajjayetpaṇḍitavargajātam \|*  
*etāṃ kathāṃ tasya jagatpavitrāṃ śṛṇoti yaḥ karṇapathaprayātām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sa cābhikāmaṃ samavāpya bhūmau svargaṃ prayātyeva surārcitāṅighraḥ \|*  
*etanmayā te kathitaṃ sunetre śrīsiddhanāthasya caritrayuktam \|*  
*kāmākṣamāhātmyamaghaghnamādyaṃ bhūyo'pi kiṃ te pravadāmi bhadre \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27a. He will acquire learning. He will be drawing the multitudes of scholars in the current of his words (eloquent speech). He who hears this story which is the most sacred in the universe, (even though) it might have entered his ears (casually), realises whatever he desires on the Earth and goes to the heaven. His feet are worshipped by the Devas.

27b-C. Thus О lady of beautiful eyes, I have told you about the greatness of Kamaksa alongwith the story of Siddhanatha. It is destructive of sins at the outset. О gentle lady, what else shall I recount to you?

## Chapter 70. The Greatness of Prabhasa

## \|\| 2.70.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- prabhāsasya tu māhātmyaṃ vada me dvijasattama \|*  
*yacchrutvāhaṃ prasannātmā dhanyā syāṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О excellent Brahmana, recount to me the greatness of Prabhasa1 2 On hearing it I shall be delighted in my mind. May I be blessed thanks to your grace.

## \|\| 2.70.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi prabhāsākhyaṃ supuṇyadam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ pāpaharaṃ nṝṇāṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vasu said:

2\. О gentle lady, listen. I shall narrate to you the (glory of the holy ecntre named Prabhasa. It yields great merit. It is a Tirtha that dispels all sins of men. It yields worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.70.3-4 \|\|

*yasminnasaṅkhyatīrthāni vidyante vidhinandini \|*  
*someśo yatra viśveśo bhagavān girijāpatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*snātvā prabhāsake tīrthe somanāthaṃ prapūjya ca \|*  
*naro muktimavāpnoti satyametanmayoditam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. О daughter of Brahma, there are innumerable Tirthas therein. Somesa,1 the lord of the universe, the lord of the daughter of the mountain, is present there. By taking a holy bath in the Prabhasa Tirtha, and by worshipping Soma- natha, a man obtains liberation. What I have stated to you is the truth.

## \|\| 2.70.5 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ daśa dve ca prabhāsaparimaṇḍalam \|*  
*madhye'sya pīṭhikā proktā pañcayojanavistṛtā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The zone of Prabhasa extends to twelve Yojanas. In its centre is the Plthika (the pedestal). It is said to extend to five Yojanas.

## \|\| 2.70.6 \|\|

*gocarmamātraṃ tanmadhye tīrthaṃ kailāsato'dhikam \|*  
*arkasthalaṃ tatra puṇyaṃ tīrthamanyatsuśobhanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In its middle is the Tirtha extending to a Gocarma (about a hundred hands. But it excels even mount Kailasa. Another meritorious and splendid Tirtha is Arkasthala (the holy spot of the sun).

## \|\| 2.70.7-13 \|\|

*siddheśvarādiliṅgāni yatra santi sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*yatra snātvā naro bhaktyā santarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*liṅgāni pūjayitvā ca yāti rudra salokatām \|*  
*agnitīrthaṃ tathānyacca sāgarasya taṭe sthitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro devi vahnilokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*tatra devaṃ kaparddīśaṃ sopavāsaḥ prapūjya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śivalokamavāpnoti bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān \|*  
*kedāreśaṃ tato gatvā samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*svargatiṃ samavāpnoti vimānena surārcitaḥ \|*  
*bhīmeśaṃ bhairaveśaṃ ca caṇḍīśaṃ bhāskareśvaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*aṅgāreśaṃ ca gurvīśaṃ someśaṃ bhṛgujeśvaram \|*  
*śanirāhuśikhīśāṃśca kramādgaccheccaturdaśa \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhaktyā pṛthak pṛthak teṣāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā vidhānavit \|*  
*śivasālokyamāpnoti nigrahānugrahe kṣamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

7-8a. There are thousands of Lingas such as Siddhesvara etc. By performing the holy bath there, and the Tarpana rite for Pitrs and Devas with devotion, and by worshipping the Lingas, the devotee attains the same worlds as that of Rudra.

8b-9a. Another Tirtha, the Agnitlrtha,2 is situated on the shore of the sea. О gentle lady, by taking the holy dip there, the man shall attain the world of Vahni.

9b-10a. By worshipping lord KapardlSa (Siva) after observing fast, the devotee attains Siva’s world after enjoying the desired worldly pleasures.

1 Ob-1 la. The devotee shall go to Kedaresa and worship him in accordance with the injunctions. Thereby, he attains heavenly goal. He goes there by means of an aerial chariot. He is worshipped by Devas.

1 lb-13. The three deities mentioned before together with the following make fourteen, viz: BhlmeSa, Bhairvesa, Candida, Bhaskaresvara, Ahgaresa, Gurvisa, SomeSa, Bhrigujesvara, Sanlsvara, Rahvlsvara and SikhlSvara. These deities must be visited in order. By worshipping with devotion these deities severally, the devotee who knows rules of religious procedure attains the same world as Siva. He becomes competent to chastise as well as to bless others.

## \|\| 2.70.14 \|\|

*siddheśvarādipañcānyaliṅgāni vidhinandini \|*  
*samarcya labhate siddhimaihikāmuṣmikīṃ naraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О daughter of Brahma, by worshipping five other Lingas, Siddhesvara etc., the man attains Siddhi of this world as well as of the other world.

## \|\| 2.70.15 \|\|

*varārohāmajāpālāṃ maṅgalāṃ laliteśvarīm \|*  
*sampūjya kramataścaitā vipāpo jāyate naraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. By worshipping the fair lady Ajapala, Mangala and Lalitesvari, the man becomes free from sins.

## \|\| 2.70.16 \|\|

*lakṣmīśvaraṃ bāḍaveśamarghyeśaṃ kāmakeśvaram \|*  
*samabhyarcya naro bhaktyā sākṣāllokeśatāṃ vrajet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By worshipping Laksmisvara, Batfavesa, ArghyeSa and Kamakesvara with devotion, a man shall attain lordship of the worlds.

## \|\| 2.70.17 \|\|

*gaurītapovanaṃ prāpya gaurīśavaruṇeśvarau \|*  
*uṣeśvaraṃ ca sampūjya naraḥ svargatimāpnuyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By worshipping Gaurisa, Varunesvara and UseSvara after reaching the penance grove of Gaurl, the man shall attain heavenly goal.

## \|\| 2.70.18-29 \|\|

*gaṇeśaṃ ca kumāreśaṃ svākakeśakuleśvarau \|*  
*uttaṅkeśaṃ ca vahnīśaṃ gautamaṃ daityasūdanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya vidhānena na naro durgatiṃ vrajet \|*  
*cakratīrthaṃ tataḥ prāpya tatra snātvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*gaurīdevīṃ samabhyarcya naro'bhilaṣitaṃ labhet \|*  
*sannihatyāhvayaṃ tīrthaṃ prāpya tatra varānane \|\| 20 \|\|*

*snātvā santarpya devādīnsannihatyāphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*athaikādaśa liṅgāni bhūteśādīni yo'cayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sa labdhveha varānbhogānante rudra padaṃ vrajet \|*  
*ādinārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ samabhyarcya narottamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mokṣabhāgī bhaveddevi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*tataścakradharaṃ prāpya pūjayedyo vidhānataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sa tu śatruṃ vinirjitya bhogānuccāvacām̐ llabhet \|*  
*sāmbādityaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātvā niyamapūrvakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nīrogo dhanadhānyāḍhyo jāyate mānavo bhuvi \|*  
*tatastu manujaḥ prāpya devīṃ kaṇṭakaśodhinīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mahiṣaghnīṃ ca sampūjya nirbhayo jāyate naraḥ \|*  
*kapālīśaṃ ca koṭīśaṃ samabhyarcya narottamaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*susaubhāgyo bhavedevaṃ madhyayātrāṃ samāpayet \|*  
*bālabrahmābhidhaṃ paścātprāpya martyo nareśvari \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jāyate bhuktimuktīśaḥ sarvadevaprapūjitaḥ \|*  
*narakeśaṃ tataḥ prāpya saṃvarteśaṃ nidhīśvaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

*balabhadre śvaraṃ prārcya jāyate bhuktimuktimān \|*  
*gaṅgāgaṇapatiṃ prāpya samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

18-19a. By duly worshipping Ganesa, Kumaresa, Svaka- kesa, Kulesvara, CJttankesa, Vahnisa, Gautama and Daityasu- dana (the slayer of the Daityas), the man shall never go to hell (or troubles).

19b-20a. The devotee should thereafter go to Cakra Tirtha, take a holy bath in accordance with the injunctions and worship goddess Gauri; thereby the man shall obtain the desired benefits.

20b-21a. О fair-faced lady, after reaching the Tirtha called ‘Sannihatya’, the devotee shall take a holy dip and perform the rite of Tarpana to Devas and others. Thereby, he shall attain the benefit accruing from that Sannihatya Tirtha.

21b-22a. He who worships the eleven Lingas, Bhutesa and others, attains excellent pleasures and in the end shall attain the region of Rudra.

22b-23a. О gentle lady, by worshipping lord Adinara- yana, the excellent man shall attain salvation. No doubt nfeed be entertained in this respect.

23b-24a. He who goes near Cakradhara and worships him in accordance with the injunctions shall conquer his enemies and attain worldly pleasures high and low.

24b-25a. The devotee who goes to the Tlrtha Samba- dityaand takes a holy bath with due observances of restraints shall be free from ailments. The man shall be endowed with wealth and food-grains on the earth.

25b-26a. Then the man should go to the goddess Kan- takaSodhinl who slew Mahisa. By worshipping her, the man becomes fearless.

26b-27a. By worshipping Kapallsa and KotIsat the excellent man shall become extremely fortunate. Thus the middle pilgrimage shall be completed.

27b-28a. О queen of men, by going to the Tirtha Balabrahma thereafter, the man becomes a master of worldly pleasures and salvation. He will be honoured and worshipped by all Devas.

28b-29a. By worshipping Narakesa, Samvartesa, Nidlu- svara, one shall be having worldly pleasures and liberation.

29b. By resorting to Gangaganapati and worshipping him in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee derives desired benefits in this world as well as in the other world.

## \|\| 2.70.30-36 \|\|

*labhate vāñchitānkāmāniha loke paratra ca \|*  
*tato jāmbavatīṃ prāpya nadīṃ bhaktyā samāhitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*snātvā surādīnabhyarcya kṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*pāṇḍukūpe tataḥ snātvā pāṇḍaveśvaramarcayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sa naraḥ svargamāyāti krīḍate nandanādiṣu \|*  
*śatamedhaṃ lakṣamedhaṃ koṭimedhamanukramāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*liṅgatrayaṃ samabhyarcya modate divi devavat \|*  
*durvāsādityakaṃ dṛṣṭvā sampūjya ca vidhānataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam \|*  
*yādavasthalamāsādya varṣeśaṃ prārcya mānavaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*labhate vāñchitāṃ siddhiṃ devarājena satkṛtaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyāsaṅgame snātvā dadyāddhemarathaṃ dvije \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śivamuddiśya yo bhaktyā sa lokānakṣayām̐ llabhet \|*  
*nagarārkaṃ tataḥ prārcya sūryalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

30-3la. Thereafter, the man should go to the river Jambavati. By taking the holy dip with devotion and concentration and by worshipping the deity, the man shall have his objects accomplished.

31b-32a. Thereafter, he shall take a holy dip in the well Pandukupa and worship Pandavesvara. That man goes to heaven and sports about in Nandana and other parks.

32b-33a. By worshipping the three Lingas, Satamedha Laksamedha and Kotimedha in the proper order, the devotee rejoices in the heaven like a Deva.

33b-34a. By visiting Durvasadityaka and by worshipping him in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee shall undoubtedly attain the benefit of horse-sacrifice.

34b-35a. By resorting to Yadavasthali1 and by worshipping Varsesa, the man attains his coveted Siddhi. He is greeted and honoured by the king of Devas.

35b-36. After taking a holy dip in the confluence of the Hiranya, the devotee shall make a gift of a golden chariot to a Brahmana looking upon him as Siva. He who does so with devotion shall obtain everlasting worlds. By worshipping Nagararka thereafter, this devotee shall attain the world of the sun.

## \|\| 2.70.37 \|\|

*nagarādityapārśve tu balakṛṣṇau subhadri kām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sampūjya vidhinā kṛṣṇasāyujyamāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By visiting and duly worshipping Bala, Krsna and Subhaclra near Nagaraditya, one shall attain the sayujya (identity) with Krsna.

## \|\| 2.70.38 \|\|

*kumārikāṃ tataḥ prāpya samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*labhate vāṃchitānkāmāñjayecchakraṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereafter, the devotee shall go to Kumarika Tirtha and worship the deity in accordance with the injunctions. There is no doubt about this that he attains cherished desires and conquers even Indra.

## \|\| 2.70.39-42 \|\|

*kṣetrapālaṃ tato'bhyarcya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*brahmeśvaraṃ ca saṃpūjya sarasvatyāstaṭe sthitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*piṅgalākhyāṃ nadīṃ prāpya snātvā tatra surādikān \|\| 40 \|\|*

*santarpya śrāddhakṛnmartyo neha bhūyo'bhijāyate \|*  
*saṅgameśaṃ samabhyarcya na naro durgatiṃ vrajet \|\| 41 \|\|*

*samprārcya śaṅkarādityaṃ ghaṭeśaṃ ca maheśvaram \|*  
*mānavaḥ sakalānkāmānprāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

39a. By worshipping Ksetrapala thereafter, he shall attain all desired benefits.

39b-40a. By worshipping Brahinesvara installed on the banks of Sarasvati1 2 the devotee shall be freed from all sins. He is honoured in the world of Brahma.

40b-41a. lie should then go to the river Pingala and take a holy dip there. By performing Sraddha, the man is not born here again. By worshipping Sahgamesa, the man wards off misfortune or hell.

41b-42. By worshipping Sankaraditya, and Ghantesa, the great lord, a man shall attain all cherished desires. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.70.43 \|\|

*ṛṣitīrthaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātvā niyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣīṃstatra samabhyarcya sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The devotee should then go to the Rsi Tirtha and take a holy bath with full control of the mind. By worshipping the sages there, he shall attain the benefits of all the Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.70.44 \|\|

*nandādityaṃ tataḥ prārcya mucyate sarvarogataḥ \|*  
*tritakūpaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātvā yāti divaṃ naraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. By worshipping Nandaditya thereafter, he is liberated from all ailments. By resorting to Tritakupa and by taking the holy dip therein, he goes to the heaven.

## \|\| 2.70.45 \|\|

*śaśopāne naraḥ snātvā devānpaśyati mohini \|*  
*vāñchitāṃśca labhetkāmānsatyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О Mohinl, by taking a holy dip in ‘Sasopana5 the man sees Devas and attains all desired benefits. Truth: It is the truth that has been stated by me.

## \|\| 2.70.46-47 \|\|

*parṇādityaṃ naro dṛṣṭvā nīrogo bhogavānbhavet \|*  
*tato nyaṅkumatīṃ prāpya snātvā tatra vidhānataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*siddheśvaraṃ samarcyātra aṇimādikasiddhibhāk \|*  
*vārāhasvāminaṃ dṛṣṭvā mucyate bhavasāgarāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. By visiting Parnaditya, the man becomes free from ailments and enjoys worldly pleasures. By resorting to Nyanku- mati, by taking the holy dip there in accordance with the injunctions and by worshipping Siddhesvara, the devotee shall attain Anima (minuteness) and other Siddhis. By visiting Varahasvamin, one is liberated from the ocean of mundane existence.

## \|\| 2.70.48 \|\|

*chāyāliṅgaṃ samabhyarcya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*gulphaṃ dṛṣṭvā naro'bhyarcya cāndrā yaṇaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. By worshipping Chayalinga one is liberated from all sins. By visiting Gulpha and worshipping him one shall attain the benefit of observance of the Candrayana vow.

## \|\| 2.70.49 \|\|

*devīṃ kanakanandāṃ ca samabhyarcya naraḥ sati \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti dehānte svargatiṃ labhet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О chaste lady, by worshipping goddess Kana- kananda, the devotee attains all cherished desires. On death he attains heavenly goal.

## \|\| 2.70.50-53 \|\|

*kuntīśvaraṃ samabhyarcya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*gaṅgeśvaraṃ samabhyarcya gaṅgāyāṃ manujaḥ plutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*trividhebhyo'pi pāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*camasodbhedake snātvā piṇḍadānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gayākoṭiguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ sa labhennātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tatastu vidhije gatvā vidurāśramamuttamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*trigaṃ tribhuvaneśaṃ ca sampūjyātra sukhī bhavet \|*  
*maṅkaṇeśvaramabhyarcya labhate sadgatiṃ naraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-5la. By worshipping Kuntlsvara, one is liberated from all sins. The man who takes a plunge in the Ganga and worships Gangesvara is liberated from the three types of sins.

51b-52a. He who takes a holy dip in Camasodbhedaka and offers balls of rice, obtains a merit a crore of times more than at Gaya. There is no doubt about this.

52b-53. Thereafter, О daughter of Brahma, the devotee should go to the excellent Vidurasrama and worship Triga, the lord of the three worlds. Thereby, he shall be happy. By worshipping Mankanesvara, the man attains good goal(i.e. heaven).

## \|\| 2.70.54-55 \|\|

*traipuraṃ ca triliṅgaṃ tu prārcya pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*ṣaṇḍatīrthaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātvā svarṇaprado naraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā śaivaṃ padamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*sūryaprācyāṃ naraḥ snātvā vipāpmā bhogāvānbhavet \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. By worshipping Traipura and Trilinga, one is liberated from sins. Thereafter, the man shall resort to Santfa-tirtha, take a holy dip there and make a gift of gold. Thereafter, he shall be purified of all sins. He shall attain the region of Siva. By taking a holy dip in SuryapracI, the man shall be devoid of sins and enjoy worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.70.56-57 \|\|

*trilocane naraḥ snātvā rudra lokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*devikāyāmumānāthaṃ samarcya manujottamaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*labhate vāñchitānkāmāndehānte svargamāpnuyāt \|*  
*bhūdvāraṃ tu samabhyarcya labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. By taking a holy dip in the Tirtha, Trilocana, the man attains Rudraloka. By worshipping Umanatha in the Devika river the excellent man attains desired benefits. On death he shall attain heavenly benefit. By worshipping Bhu- dvara the devotee shall attain the cherished desire.

## \|\| 2.70.58-59 \|\|

*śūlasthāne tu vālmīkiṃ namaskṛtya kavirbhavet \|*  
*cyavanārkaṃ tataḥ prārcya sarvakāmasamṛddhimān \|\| 58 \|\|*

*cyavaneśārcanānmartyaḥ śivasyānucaro bhavet \|*  
*pajāpāleśamabhyarcya dhanadhānyānvito bhavet \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. By making obeisance to Valmiki in Siilasthana, the devotee shall become a poet. By worshipping Cyavanarka one shall be richly endowed with all desired benefits. Through the worship of CyavaneSa, the man shall become the attendant of Siva. By worshipping Prajapalesa, the devotee shall be endowed with wealth and foodgrains.

## \|\| 2.70.60 \|\|

*bālārkapūjako martyo vidyāvāndhanavān bhavet \|*  
*kuberasthānake snātvā nidhiṃ prāpnoti niścitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A man who worships Balarka shall be endowed with learning and wealth. By taking a holy dip in Kuberasthana the devotee shall certainly obtain a treasure-trove.

## \|\| 2.70.61 \|\|

*ṛṣitoyanadīṃ prāpya snātvā tatra naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*datvā suvarṇaṃ viprāya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By resorting to the river Rsitoya, by taking holy bath there, and by giving gold to a Brahmana as gift, the man becomes pure and is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.70.62 \|\|

*saṅgāleśvaramabhyarcya rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*nāradādityamabhyarcya trikālajñānavānbhavet \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. By worshipping Srgalesvara, the devotee is honoured in the Rudraloka. By worshipping Naradaditya the devotee shall become endowed with the perfect knowledge of the three units of time.

## \|\| 2.70.63-64 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇaṃ prārcya muktibhāgī naro bhaveta \|*  
*taptakuṇḍodake snātvā mūlacaṇḍīśamarcayet \|\| 63 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto vāñchitārthaṃ labhennaraḥ \|*  
*vināyakaṃ caturvaktramabhyarcyāpnoti kāmitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. By worshipping Narayana the man shall attain liberation. After taking a holy dip in the waters of Tapta- kunda, the devotee should worship MulacandlSa. The man shall be absolved of all sins. He shall attain the desired object. By worshipping the fourfaced deity Vinayaka, the devotee attains the desired benefit.

## \|\| 2.70.65 \|\|

*kalambeśvaramabhyarcya dhanadhānyasamṛddhimān \|*  
*gopālasvāmipūjāto gomānvai dhanavānkaviḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. By worshipping Kambala, the devotee is endowed with flourishing wealth and food-grains. Through the worship of Gopalasvamin, the devotee will possess cows and wealth. He will become a poet or a wise man.

## \|\| 2.70.66 \|\|

*bakulasvāmino'bhyarcā nṛṇāṃ svargatidāyinī \|*  
*sampūjya mārutāṃ devīṃ sarvakāmaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The worship of Bakulasvamin is the bestower of heavenly goal unto the man. By worshipping the goddess of Maruts, one shall attain the desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.70.67 \|\|

*kṣemādityārcanānmartyaḥ kṣemī siddhārthasatyabhāk \|*  
*unnatākhyaṃ vighnarājaṃ prārcya vighnairna hanyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Through the worship of Ksemaditya, the man shall attain welfare and truthfully partake of all relished objects. By worshipping Vighnaraja Unnata, the devotee is not impeded by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.70.68 \|\|

*jalasvāmī kālameghaḥ pūjitau sarvasiddhidau \|*  
*rukmiṇī pūjitā devī vāñchitārthapradā nṛṇām \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The two deities Jalasvamin and Kalamegha, wlien worshipped, bestow all Siddhis. When the goddess Rukmini is worshipped, she bestows the desired objects on men.

## \|\| 2.70.69 \|\|

*durvāseśaṃ ca piṅgeśaṃ prārcya pāpairvimucyate \|*  
*bhadrā yāḥ saṅgame snātvā naro bhadrā ṇi paśyati \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. By worshipping Durvasesa and Piiigesa, the devotee is liberated from sins. By taking the holy dip in the confluence of Bhadra, the man sees auspicious things.

## \|\| 2.70.70 \|\|

*śaṅkhāvarte naraḥ snātvā sarvasiddhīśvaro bhavet \|*  
*mokṣatīrthe naraḥ snātvā bhavenmukto bhavārṇavāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. By taking tiie holy dip in Sankhavarta, the man shall become the master of all Siddhis. By taking the holy bath in the Moksa Tirtha, the man shall be liberated from the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.70.71 \|\|

*goṣpadasnānamātreṇa sarvasaukhyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*nārāyaṇagṛhe gatvā naro bhūyo na śocati \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Merely by means of ablution in the Gospada (the pit made by the hoofs of cows), one shall attain all happiness. After going to the abode of Narayana, a man does not grieve again.

## \|\| 2.70.72 \|\|

*jāleśvarārcanātpuṃsāṃ siddhayaḥ syurabhīpsitāḥ \|*  
*snāto huṅkārakūpe tu garbhavāsaṃ na cāpnuyāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Through the worship ofjalcsvara, a man shall realise all desired Siddhis. One who takes a holy dip in the well Humkarakiipa shall never attain a residence in the womb thereafter.

## \|\| 2.70.73 \|\|

*tathā caṇḍīśamabhyarcya sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*vighneśamāśāpuragaṃ prārcya vighnaṃ na cāpnuyāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. By worshipping Gandlsa one shall attain the benefit of all Tlrthas. By worshipping Vighnesa stationed in Asiipura, one shall never be harassed by obstacles.

## \|\| 2.70.74 \|\|

*kalākuṇḍāpluto martyo muktibhāgī na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kapileśaṃ samabhyarcya kapilāyūthamāpnuyāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. A man taking the holy plunge in the Kalakunda shall undoubtedly attain salvation. By worshipping Kapilesa one shall attain a herd of Kapilas (tawny-coloured cows).

## \|\| 2.70.75 \|\|

*jaradgaveśvaraṃ prārcya jarasā nābhibhūyate \|*  
*naleśvarārcako bhogī karkkoṭeśārcako dhanī \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. By worshipping Jaradgavesvara the devotee is never overwhelmed by old age. The worshipper of Nalesvara is an enjoyer of pleasures. The worshipper of Karkotcsa is a wealthy man.

## \|\| 2.70.76 \|\|

*hāṭakeśvarapūjātaḥ pūryante sarvakāmanāḥ \|*  
*nāradeśārcako bhaktiṃ labhedviṣṇau ca śaṅkare \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Through the worship of Hatakesvara all the desires are fulfilled. The worshipper of Naradesa shall obtain devotion to Visnu and Sankara.

## \|\| 2.70.77 \|\|

*svargārho jāyate'bhyarcya devīṃ mantravibhūṣaṇām \|*  
*durgakūṭaṃ gaṇapatiṃ pūjayitvā sukhī bhavet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. By worshipping goddess Man travibhu Sana, the devotee becomes one who deserves heaven. By worshipping Ganapati and Durgakuta, one shall be ever happy.

## \|\| 2.70.78 \|\|

*dhanadhānyayuto bhūyātpūjayankauraveśvarīm \|*  
*suparṇelāṃ bhairavīṃ ca pūjayitvā sukhī bhavet \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A person who worships KauraveSvaii shall become one endowed with wealth and food-grains. By worshipping Suparnesa and Bhairavi, one shall be blessed with happiness.

## \|\| 2.70.79 \|\|

*mallatīrthe naraḥ snātvā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|*  
*kardamāle naraḥ snātvā pātakairviprayujyate \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. By taking a holy dip in Bhala Tirtha.1 the man is absolved of all sins. By taking a holy bath in Kardamala, one is relieved of sins.

## \|\| 2.70.80 \|\|

*guptasomeśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā na bhūyo'hati śocitum \|*  
*bahusvarṇeśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā svargatiṃ samavāpnuyāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. By visiting Guptasomcsvara (the hidden Somesvara) one ceases to grieve further. By visiting Bahusvarnesvara one shall attain heavenly goal.

## \|\| 2.70.81 \|\|

*śṛṅgeśvarārcako martyo na duḥkhairabhibhūyate \|*  
*tīrthe nārāyaṇe snātvā muktimāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The man who worships Srngesvara is not attacked by miseries. By taking a holy dip in the Tirtha Narayana, the man obtains liberation.

## \|\| 2.70.82 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeśvaramabhyarcya dīrghāyurjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*tathā koṭīhrade snātvābhyarcya koṭīśvaraṃ sukhī \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. By worshipping Markandesvara, the man becomes longlived. By taking the holy dip in the Kotihrada and by worshipping Kotisvara one becomes happy.

## \|\| 2.70.83 \|\|

*siddhasthāne punaḥ snātvā tatra liṅgāni pūjayet \|*  
*asaṅkhyātāni yo martyaḥ sa siddho jāyate bhuvi \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. By performing ablution in Siddhasthana and by worshipping numerous Lingas thereof, the man shall become a Siddha on the earth.

## \|\| 2.70.84-86 \|\|

*dāmodaragṛhaṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhamāpnotyanuttamam \|*  
*vastrāpathaṃ prabhāsasya nābhisthāne sthitaṃ śubhe \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tatrābhyarcya bhavaṃ sākṣādbhavedbhavasamaḥ svayam \|*  
*dāmodare svarṇarekhā brahmakuṇḍaṃ ca raivate \|\| 85 \|\|*

*kuntīśa ujjayante tu bhīmeśaśca mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ ca sarvasvaṃ kṣetre vastrāpathe smṛtam \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-85a. By visiting Damodaragrha one attains excellent happiness. О auspicious lad), the holy centre Vastrapatha is situated in the navel region of Prabhasa. By worshipping god Bhava (Siva) there, one shall directly become equal to Siva.

85b-86. The Svavnarckha (the line of gold) is in Damo- dara. Brahmakunda (holy pool of Brahma) is in Raivata. Kuntls'a and the highly refulgent Bhlmesa are in Ujjayanta (mount Girnar). And Mrglkunda and Sarvasva — all these are remembered to be at the holy spot called Vastrapatha.

## \|\| 2.70.87 \|\|

*eteṣu kramaśaḥ snātvā devānabhyarcya yatnataḥ \|*  
*pitṝnsantarpya toyena sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. By taking the holy bath in these, in the order, by worshipping Devas assiduously and by performing Tarpana rite with water, one shall attain the benefit of all Tlrthas.

## \|\| 2.70.88 \|\|

*dunnābile naraḥ snātvā bhuktabhogo divaṃ vrajet \|*  
*gaṅgeśvaraṃ tato'bhyarcya gaṅgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. By taking the holy dip in Dunnabila and enjoying the pleasures one shall go to the heaven. By worshipping Gangesvara thereafter, one shall attain the benefit of the holy bath in Ganga.

## \|\| 2.70.89-90 \|\|

*girau raivatake devi santi tīrthānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*teṣu snātvā naro bhaktyā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān \|\| 89 \|\|*

*indrā dilokapānprārcya bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati \|*  
*etānyuddeśatastīrthānyuktāni tava sundari \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. О gentle lady, there are many Tirthas on the mountain Raivataka (or Girnar). By taking a holy dip in them and by worshipping with devotion, Brahma, Visnu, MaheSvara, Indra and other guardians of the worlds, the man obtains worldly pleasures and liberation. О beautiful lady, these Tirthas have been narrated to you in brief.

## \|\| 2.70.91 \|\|

*avāntarāṇyanantāni tāni vaktuṃ na śakyate \|*  
*ekaikasyāpi tīrthasya santi vistarataḥ kathāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In their midst there are infinite numbers of them. It is not possible to recount them all. There are detailed stories for each and everyone of these Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.70.92-95 \|\|

*ataḥ saṃkṣipya gaditaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ prabhāsajam \|*  
*na prabhāsasamaṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu mohini \|\| 92 \|\|*

*yatra snāto'pi manujaḥ svargiṇā sparddhate śubhe \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ ca prabhāsasya likhitaṃ vartate gṛhe \|\| 93 \|\|*

*yatra tatra na bhītiḥ syādbhūtacaurāhiśatrujā \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*prabhāsatīrthamāhātmyaṃ so'pi sadgatimāpnuyāt \|\| 95 \|\|*

92-93a. Hence, the merit accruing from Prabhasa has been succinctly mentioned by me. О Mohini, there is no other Tlrtha in all the three worlds, equal to Prabhasa. О auspicious lady, a man who takes a holy bath there competes with heaven- dwellers.

93b-95. If the greatness of Prabhasa is written and kept in the house, there can be no danger or fear from goblins, thieves, serpents and enemies. He who devoutly listens to this and he who narrates this with concentration shall attain the goal of the good.

## Chapter 71. The Greatness of Pufkara

## \|\| 2.71.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ prabhāsamāhātmyaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhātipuṇyadam \|*  
*adhunā śrotumicchāmi māhātmyaṃ puṣkarodbhavam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О excellent Brahmana, the greatness of Prabhasa that is extremely conducive to the attainment of merit has been heard. Now I wish to hear the glory of Puskara.1

## \|\| 2.71.2 \|\|

*yadādyaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*matpituryajñasadanaṃ tanmamākhyāhi vistarāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It is the first one among the Tirthas. It is sacred and destructive of sins. It is the abode of the Yajna of my father. Kindly narrate it to me in detail. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.71.3 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu bhadre pravakṣyāmi narāṇāṃ kāmadaṃ sadā \|*  
*puṇyaṃ puṣkaramāhātmyaṃ bahutīrthasamanvitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О gentle lady, I shall recount to you the meritorious greatness of Puskara. Listen. It yields the desired benefits to all men always. It has within it many Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.71.4-6 \|\|

*viṣṇunā sahitā devā yatrendrā dyā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*gajavaktraḥ kumāraśca raivataśca divākaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śivadūtī tathā devī kṣetrakṣemakarī sadā \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe tu puṣkarāraṇye yastiṣṭhati nirudyamī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aṣṭāṅgayogajaṃ puṇyaṃ sa labhennātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nātaḥ parataraṃ kiñcitkṣetramastīha bhūtale \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Indra and other Devas have settled here along with Visnu. The elephant-faced lord, the sun-god, Kumara and Raivata are present here. So also goddess Sivadutl always stays here. She brings about the happiness of the holy centre. He who stays in the forest of Puskara1 in the holy month of Jyestha, without exerting himself in worldly activities shall undoubtedly attain the merit of Yoga consisting of eight subdivisions. In this world there is no other centre holier than this.

## \|\| 2.71.7-8 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena sevyametannarottamaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā vā kṣetravāsinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sarvātmanā brahmabhaktā bhūtānugrahakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*te yānti brahmaṇo lokaṃ yatra gacchanti yoginaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Hence, this must be resorted to by excellent men with all possible efforts. The Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras whoever stay in the holy centre, are devotees of Brahma in all respects. They bless all living beings. They go to the world of Brahma where Yogins go.

## \|\| 2.71.9 \|\|

*yo naraḥ sarvatīrtheṣu yatphalaṃ labhate plutaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ sa labhenmartyo jyeṣṭhakuṇḍe sakṛtplutaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The merit that a man obtains by plunging into all Tirthas is derived by the man who takes the holy dip but once in the Jyes tha Kunda (a holy pool of that name).

## \|\| 2.71.10 \|\|

*puṣkarāraṇyamāsādya yatra prācī sarasvatī \|*  
*matiḥ smṛtirdayā prajñā medhā buddhisamāhvayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After reaching the forest of Puskara where the river Eastern Sarasvati flows, a man is endowed with intelligence, memory, mercy, judgement, retentive power and comprehension.

## \|\| 2.71.11 \|\|

*tatrasthaṃ tajjalaṃ ye'pi prapaśyanti taṭe sthitāḥ \|*  
*te'pyaśvamedhayajñasya phalaṃ prāpya vrajanti kam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Those who stand on the banks of these rivers and merely look at the waters, attain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice and derive happiness.

## \|\| 2.71.12 \|\|

*trīṇi śṛṅgāṇi śubhrāṇi trīṇi prasravaṇāni ca \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamadhyakaniṣṭhāni trīṇi tatra sarāṃsi ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There are three famous and pure peaks. Tfcere are three springs. There are three lakes also which are called Jyestha, Madhya and Kanistha.1

## \|\| 2.71.13-14 \|\|

*tatrānyatsumahattīrthaṃ nandā nāma sarasvatī \|*  
*yatra paścimadiśyāste saraso yojane sati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā vidhānena gāṃ ca dattvā payasvinīm \|*  
*viprāya vedaviduṣe vrajedbrahmakṣayaṃ naraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. There is another very great Tirtha called Nanda Sarasvati, О chaste lady, to the west of that lake, about a Yojana from it. By taking the holy dip therein in accordance with the injunctions, and by making a gift of a milch cow to a Brahmana who is a Vedic Scholar, the man shall attain the abode of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.71.15 \|\|

*koṭitīrthaṃ tathātrāsti yatrarṣikoṭirāgatā \|*  
*tatra snātvā dvijānprārcya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There is a Kotitlrtha here where a crore of sages had come. By taking a holy dip there and by worshipping Brahmanas, the devotee is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.71.16 \|\|

*agastyāśramamāsādya snātvā sampūjya kumbhajam \|*  
*dīrghāyurjāyate bhogī dehānte svargatiṃ labhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By resorting to the hermitage of Agastya,1 2 by taking the holy dip there and by worshipping the pitcher-born sage Agastya, the devotee becomes long-lived and enjoys pleasures. On death he attains heavenly goal.

## \|\| 2.71.17 \|\|

*saptarṣīṇāṃ tathā prāpya tatrāśramamananyadhīḥ \|*  
*snātvā sampūjya bhaktyā tām̐ llabhate tatsalokatām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The devotee should then go to the hermitage of seven sages. With the intellect not turned to anything else he should take a holy bath there and worship them with devotion. Thereby, he attains the same world as they.

## \|\| 2.71.18 \|\|

*manūnāmāśrame snātvā pūjāmāpnoti sarvataḥ \|*  
*gaṅgāvinirgame snātvā gaṅgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By taking a holy dip in the hermitage of the Manus, the devotee is worshipped from all quarters. By taking a holy bath at the source of Ganga, he attains the benefit of a holy dip in Ganga itself.

## \|\| 2.71.19 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe tu puṣkare snātvā gāṃ ca dattvā dvijātaye \|*  
*bhuktveha bhogānakhilānbrahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By performing ablution in the Jyestha Puskara lake and by making a gift of a cow to a Brahmana, the devotee enjoys all pleasures here and is honoured in the world of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.71.20 \|\|

*madhyame puṣkare snātvā brāhmaṇāya mahīṃ dadat \|*  
*viṣṇulokamavāpnoti vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By taking a holy dip in the Madhyama (middle) Puskara lake and by giving a plot of land to a Brahmana, the devotee attains the world of Visnu riding in an excellent aerial chariot.

## \|\| 2.71.21 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhe tu naraḥ snātvā dattvā viprāya kāñcanam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpyānte rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A man who takes a holy dip in the Kanistha Puskara lake and gives gold as a gift to a BrAhmana attains all desired benefits and in the end is honoured in (lie world of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.71.22 \|\|

*tato viṣṇupade snātvā dattvā kiñciddvijātaye \|*  
*labhate sakalānkāmān viṣṇoścaiva prasādataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By taking a holy dip in Visnupada and by giving something as gift to a Brahmana, the devotee attains all desired benefits, thanks to the grace of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.71.23 \|\|

*nāgatīrthe tataḥ snātvā nāgānabhyarcya mānavāḥ \|*  
*dattvā dānaṃ dvijātibhyo modate tridive yugam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By taking a holy bath in the Nagatlrlha, by worshipping the Nagas (Serpents) and by giving gifts to Brahmanas, he rejoices in heaven for the period of a Yuga.

## \|\| 2.71.24 \|\|

*piśācatīrthake snātvā dattvā viprāya bhojanam \|*  
*na kadācitpiśācatvaṃ prāpnoti tridivaṃ vrajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By performing ablution in the Pisacatirtha and by giving food to a Brahmana, the devotee avoids the state of becoming a Pisaca (ghost). He shall go to heaven.

## \|\| 2.71.25 \|\|

*śivadūtīhrade snātvā tatra śambhuṃ samarcya ca \|*  
*viprānsambhojya miṣṭānnaṃ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By taking a holy dip in the Sivadutihrada (the deep pool of that name), by worshipping Sambhu and by feeding the Brahmanas on sweet cooked rice, the devotee is honoured in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.71.26 \|\|

*ākāśapuṣkare snātvā mantrayogaphalaprade \|*  
*naro muktimavāpnoti satyaṃ satyaṃ tavoditam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By taking a holy bath in the Akasa Puskara1 that yields the benefit of the Mantras and Yogas, the man attains liberation, Truth; the truth has been stated to you.

## \|\| 2.71.27 \|\|

*āpohiṣṭhādibhirmantrairākāśasthaṃ vicintya tat \|*  
*snāyādyaḥ puṣkarāraṇye sa labhecchāśvataṃ padam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He who meditates on the deity abiding in Akasa (a holy lake of that name) after taking a holy bath in Pus- kararanya uttering the Mantras Apo hi stha etc. attains the eternal region.

## \|\| 2.71.28 \|\|

*āgneyaṃ tu yadā ṛkṣaṃ kārtikyāṃ bhavati kvacit \|*  
*mahatī sā tithistatra snānamākāśapuṣkare \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If the constellation pertaining to fire-god coincides with the full moon day in the month of Karttika, that Tithi is very great. The holy dip on that day in Akasa Puskara is meritorious.

## \|\| 2.71.29 \|\|

*yāmyarkṣayoge kārtikyāṃ madhyame snānakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti yannabhaḥpuṣkarodbhavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The man who takes a holy dip in the Madhyama Puskara lake when the constellation pertaining to Yama coincides with the full moon day in the month of Karttika derives the same benefit as originates from the holy lake Akasa puskara.

## \|\| 2.71.30 \|\|

*prājāpatyarkṣayuktāyāṃ kārtikyāṃ tu kaniṣṭhake \|*  
*snātastatphalamāpnoti yadviyatpuṣkarodbhavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The man who takes a holy dip in the Kanistha Puskara lake when the constellation pertaining to the deity Prajapati (Rohini?) coincides with the full moon day in the month of Karttika derives the same benefit as originating from bathing in the holy lake Akasa Puskara.

## \|\| 2.71.31 \|\|

*nandā cārke gurau some yāmye vahnau vidhau kramāt \|*  
*yadā nabhaḥ puṣkarotthaṃ tadā syātsakalaṃ phalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the sun is with the constellation Bharani, the Jupiter is associated with Krttika and the moon is with the constellation Rohini and it is the Nanda tithi, a bath taken at Puskara gives the full benefit of ablution in the Akasa Puskara.

## \|\| 2.71.32 \|\|

*viśākhāyāṃ yadā bhānuḥ kṛttikāyāṃ ca candra māḥ \|*  
*tadā nabhaḥpuṣkarākhye yoge snāto divaṃ vrajet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When the sun is in the constellation Visakha and the moon is in Krttika (the constellation Pleiads), that conjunction (yoga) is called Akasa Puskara — A person taking bath (in the Puskara lake at this juncture) goes to heaven.

## \|\| 2.71.33 \|\|

*antarikṣāvatīrṇe'smistīrthe paitāmahe śubhe \|*  
*kurvanti ye narāḥ snānaṃ teṣāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. This is an auspicious Tirtha belonging to Brahma. It has descended from the firmament. Those men who take a holy dip therein shall have the worlds of great rise and prosperity.

## \|\| 2.71.34 \|\|

*pañcasrotaḥsarasvatyāṃ puṣkarāraṇyake sati \|*  
*kṛtāni munibhiḥ siddhaistīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О chaste lady, many Tlrthas and shrines have been created by the sages and Siddhas in the forest of Puskara- ranyaka in the Sarasvati of Pancasrotas (five currents).

## \|\| 2.71.35 \|\|

*teṣu sarveṣu vijñeyā dharmahetuḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*hāṭakakṣitigaurīṇāṃ dānaṃ teṣu mahāphalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It should be known that the Sarasvati river is the cause of virtue and piety in all these. The charitable gifts of gold, plots of land and girls eight years of age in those Tlrthas yield great benefit.

## \|\| 2.71.36 \|\|

*dhānyānyapi tilāṃścāpi yo'tra dadyāddvijottame \|*  
*sa naro labhate bhogānihāmutra parāṃ gatim \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He too who gives gifts of grains, gingelly seeds etc. to an excellent Brahinana in this holy centre derives worldly pleasures in this world. That man attains excellent state in the other world.

## \|\| 2.71.37 \|\|

*saṅge gaṅgāsarasvatyoryaḥ snātvā pūjayeddvijān \|*  
*sa prāpnoti gatiṃ cāgryāṃ bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He who takes a holy dip in the confluence of Ganga and the Sarasvati and worships Brahmanas attains the highest goal after enjoying the desired pleasures in this world.

## \|\| 2.71.38 \|\|

*aviyogābhidhāyāṃ tu vāpyāṃ snātvā naraḥ sati \|*  
*piṇḍaṃ dattvā vidhānena pitṝnnayati vai divam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The man who takes a holy bath in the tank called Aviyoga (non-separation) and offers Pimjas in accordance with the injunctions, leads the Pitrs to the heaven.

## \|\| 2.71.39 \|\|

*tathā saubhāgyakūpe tu snātvā santarpya pūrvajān \|*  
*sadgatiṃ labhate martyo saubhāgyaṃ cātulaṃ bhuvi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. By taking a holy bath in the well called Saubha- gyakupa and by performing the Tarpana rite to the ancestors, the man attains good goal as well as unequalled good fortune on the earth.

## \|\| 2.71.40 \|\|

*maryādā parvatau dvau tu snātvā spṛṣṭvā samarcya ca \|*  
*vāñchitām̐ llabhate lokānsāṅgayātrāphalaṃ tathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By taking a holy dip near, by touching and by worshipping the two mountains of delimitation of the boundary, the devotee attains the desired worlds as well as the benefit of pilgrimage with all its ancillaries.

## \|\| 2.71.41 \|\|

*ajagandhaṃ śivaṃ prāpya samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*labhate vāñchitānkāmāniha loke paratra ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By resorting to the deity Siva called Ajagandha and by worshipping the lord in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee derives the desired benefits in this as well as in the other world.

## \|\| 2.71.42 \|\|

*saraso dakṣiṇe bhāge sāvitrīṃ parvatopari \|*  
*saṃsthitāṃ yaḥ samabhyarcetso'pi vedasya tattvavit \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He who worships Savitri1 installed on the mountain to the south of the lake shall be the knower of reality (of the principles) of the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.71.43-47 \|\|

*vārāhasya nṛsiṃhasya brahmaṇaśca harestathā \|*  
*śivasya cāpi sūryasya somasya ca guhasya ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pārvatyā jvalanasyāpi tatra tīrthāni mohini \|*  
*pṛthak teṣu mahābhāge naraḥ snātvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dānaṃ ca dattvā viprebhyo labhate gatimuttamām \|*  
*puṣkare durlabhaṃ snānaṃ puṣkare durlabhaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*puṣkare durlabhaṃ dānaṃ puṣkare durlabhā sthitiḥ \|*  
*śatayojanasaṃstho'pi snānakāle tu yo naraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*puṣkaraṃ cintayedbhaktyā sa tatsnānaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*maṅkaṇādyāstapaḥsiddhāḥ sevante puṣkaraṃ mudā \|\| 47 \|\|*

43-45a. О Mohini, there arc separate Tirthas pertaining to Varaha, Nrsimha, Brahma, Hari, Siva, Surya (the Sun-god), Soma (Moon god), Guha, Parvatl and Jvalana (fire-god). О blessed lady, by taking a holy bath with great concentration and by making charitable gifts to Brahmanas, the devotee attains good goal.

45b-46a. It is rare that people get opportunity of taking the holy dip, or performing penance, or making charitable gifts or staying in Puskara.

46b-47a. Even if one is stationed a hundred Yojanas away from Puskara but if one remembers Puskara devoutly at the time of bathing, the devotee shall attain the benefit of a holy dip in Puskara itself.

47b. Mankana and others who attained Siddhi by their penance resorted to Puskara with delight.

## \|\| 2.71.48-50 \|\|

*yatra tatra gato bhāgyātkāmitāṃ siddhimāpnuyāt \|*  
*puṣkareti ca nāmāpi yenoktaṃ vidhinandini \|\| 48 \|\|*

*puṣkarasnānajaṃ puṇyaṃ labhetso'pi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā māhātmyaṃ puṣkarasya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*so'pi snānaphalaṃ prāpya modate divi devavat \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. In whatever place he may go, at Puskara, the pilgrim attains Siddhi desired by him. He too who merftions the name of Puskara, О daughter of Brahma, derives the merits of taking a holy bath in Puskara. There is no doubt about this. He who listens to the greatness of Puskara with devotion shall attain the merit of holy ablution therein. He rejoices in heaven like a Deva.

## Chapter 72. The Power of Austerities of Gautama

## \|\| 2.72.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ puṣkaramāhātmyaṃ vaso pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*gautamāśramamāhātmyamadhunā kīrtaya prabho \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О holy lord, О Vasu, the greatness of Puskara is heard. It is destructive of sins. Now kindly recount the greatness of the hermitage of Gautama.1 Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.72.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi gautamāśramamuttamam \|*  
*yatra gatvā naro bhaktyā na bhūyo'hati yātanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О gentle lady, listen. I shall recount the excellent hermitage of Gautama. By visiting this place, the man does not encounter tortures any further.

## \|\| 2.72.3 \|\|

*gautamasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ devarṣigaṇasevitam \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvopadra vaśāntidam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The hermitage of Gautama is meritorious. It is resorted to by multitudes of Devas and sages. It dispels all sins. It bestows peace and calmness from all kinds of harassments.

## \|\| 2.72.4 \|\|

*sevate dvādaśābdaṃ yo bhaktibhāvasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa śaivaṃ labhate dhāma yatra gatvā na śocati \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He who is endowed with devotional feelings and resorts to the hermitage of Gautama for a period of twelve years, attains the abode of Siva. After going there, one ceases to suffer from any misery.

## \|\| 2.72.5 \|\|

*māyādevīsuto yatra tapasyugre samāsthitaḥ \|*  
*tatra godāvarī gaṅgā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The place where the son of Mayadevi is engrossed in a severe penance, the Godavari and Ganga are destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.72.6 \|\|

*tapasyato munestasya dvādaśābdamavarṣaṇam \|*  
*babhūva ghoraṃ vidhije sarvasattvakṣayaṅkaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О daughter of Brahma, while that sage was performing penance, there was a terrible drought lasting for twelve years. It was destructive of all animals.

## \|\| 2.72.7 \|\|

*tasminnugre tu durbhikṣe kṣutkṣāmā munayo'khilāḥ \|*  
*nānādeśebhya āyātā gautamasyāśramaṃ śubhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In that terrible period of famine, the sages became emaciated due to hunger. О splendid lady, they came from different lands to the hermitage of Gautama.

## \|\| 2.72.8 \|\|

*cakrurvijñāpanaṃ tasya gautamasya tapasyataḥ \|*  
*dehi no bhojanaṃ yena prāṇāstiṣṭhanti varṣmasu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They submitted to Gautama who was performing penance, “Give us food whereby our life may cling to our bodies.”

## \|\| 2.72.9 \|\|

*evaṃ vijñāpitastaistu munibhirgautamo muniḥ \|*  
*jātānukampastānāha viśvastāṃstapaso balāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus requested by the sages, sage Gautama became sympathetic and merciful. He told them who were confident of success due to the strength of penance. Gautama said:

## \|\| 2.72.10 \|\|

*gautama uvāca- tiṣṭhadhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve mamāśramasamīpataḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ vaḥ pradāsyāmi yāvaddurbhikṣamādṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O sages, all of you stay in my hermitage. As long as the famine lasts, I shall respectfully give you food regularly.”

## \|\| 2.72.11 \|\|

*viśvāsyaivamṛṣīnsarvāngautamastapaso balāt \|*  
*dadhyau prasannamanasā gaṅgāṃ sarvārthasādhinīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After assuring the sages thus, thanks to his reliance on the strength of his penance, Gautama meditated on Ganga that realizes all objects. With great delight in his mind, he meditated on Ganga.

## \|\| 2.72.12-13 \|\|

*smṛtamātrā tu sā devī tatrodbhūtā dharātalāt \|*  
*tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā munirgaṃgāṃ samplāvitadharātalām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prātaruptvā kṣitau śālīnpakvānmadhyāhnake'lunāt \|*  
*śālyannena tatastena tānṛṣīnsamabhojayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Immediately after being remembered, the goddess Ganga came out from the bowels of the earth. On seeing Ganga that flooded the whole surface of the earth, the sage sowed paddy seeds, in the morning and reaped the ripe harvest at midday. With the grains of that Sali rice, he fed those sages.

## \|\| 2.72.14 \|\|

*tataste munayaḥ prītā bhuktvānnaṃ tṛptimāgatāḥ \|*  
*nivāsaṃ cakrire tatra gautamāśramake mudā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the sages became delighted, partaking of the cooked rice they became contented. Joyously they took up their residence in the hermitage of Gautama.

## \|\| 2.72.15 \|\|

*evaṃ pratidinaṃ bhadre śālibhiḥ pakvatāṃ gataiḥ \|*  
*ātithyaṃ vidadhe teṣāṃ bhaktibhāvasamanvitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О gentle lady, with great devotional feelings, tlfe sage thus extended his hospitality to those sages by means of the Sali rice-grains that ripened everyday.

## \|\| 2.72.16 \|\|

*tatastasya munīndra sya dvijānbhojayato'nvaham \|*  
*vyatīyāya ca durbhikṣaṃ dvādaśābdāntakālataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even as the leading sage fed those Brahmanas everyday, the famine ceased at the end of twelve years.

## \|\| 2.72.17 \|\|

*tataste munayaḥ sarve subhikṣe kāla āgate \|*  
*vijñāpya taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ jagmurdeśānsvakānpunaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When the time of plenty arrived, all those sages informed the excellent sage and went back to their respective lands once again.

## \|\| 2.72.18 \|\|

*evaṃprabhāvaḥ sa munirgautamastatra mohini \|*  
*tapastepe bahutithaṃ kālaṃ niyamitendri yaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О MohinI, sage Gautama whose prowess was of such a nature performed penance for many years with perfect control over his sense-organs.

## \|\| 2.72.19 \|\|

*tatastattapasā tuṣṭo bhagavānambikāpatiḥ \|*  
*sagaṇo darśanaṃ yāto varaṃ brūhītyuvāca ha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thereafter, lord Ambikapati (Siva) became delighted with his penance. He appeared before the sage accompanied by Ganas and said — “Tell me, what is the boon you would choose to have?”

## \|\| 2.72.20 \|\|

*tato munivaro dṛṣṭvā devadevamupāpatim \|*  
*tr! yambakaṃ sa namaścakre nipatya bhuvi tatpuraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing Siva, the lord of Devas, the three-eyed deity, the excellent sage fell on the ground in front of him and made obeisance.

## \|\| 2.72.21 \|\|

*tata utthāya sahasā kṛtāñjalirupasthitaḥ \|*  
*provāca dehi me bhaktiṃ pādayostava nityadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Rising up immediately, he joined his palms in reverence and prayed to Him, “Grant me devotion unto your feet for ever.

## \|\| 2.72.22 \|\|

*mamāśramasamīpe'tra parvatopari śaṅkara \|*  
*tvāmevaṃ saṃsthitaṃ paśyāmyeṣa eva varo mama \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Sankara, may I see you stationed on the mountain here near my hermitage. This is the boon I wish to have.”

## \|\| 2.72.23 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ pārvatīnātho bhaktānāṃ vāñchitapradaḥ \|*  
*tatra dattvā svasānnidhyaṃ sadyaḥ prītaṃ cakāra tam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus requested, Siva, the consort of Parvati, the bestower of desires on the devotees, granted him his presence there and made him delighted.

## \|\| 2.72.24 \|\|

*tena rūpeṇa tatraiva nyavasat tr! yambakaḥ sati \|*  
*sa giristr! yambakākhyastu tataḥ prabhṛti kīrtyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О chaste lady, the three-eyed lord stayed there in that very same form. Ever since that day, that mountain is glorified by the name Tryambaka.

## \|\| 2.72.25 \|\|

*ye tu godāvarīṃ gaṅgāṃ prāpya bhaktiyutā narāḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ kurvanti subhage te syurmuktā bhavārṇavāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who resort to Godavari, Ganga and take their holy dip with devotion, are liberated from the ocean of worldly existence, О blessed lady.

## \|\| 2.72.26 \|\|

*snātvā godāvarītoye tr! yambakaṃ ye giristhitam \|*  
*upacāraiḥ pūjayanti te syuḥ sākṣānmaheśvarāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By taking a holy bath in the waters of Godavari and by worshipping Tryambaka stationed on the mountain by means of services, the devotees shall become MaheSvara themselves.

## \|\| 2.72.27 \|\|

*tr! yambakasya tu māhātmyaṃ saṃkṣepādvarṇitaṃ mayā \|*  
*brahmāpi vistarādvaktuṃ tava tātaḥ kṣamo nahi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The greatness of Tryambaka has been succinctly described by me. Even your father Brahma is not competent to describe it in detail.

## \|\| 2.72.28 \|\|

*tato godāvarī yāvatsākṣāddarśanatāṃ gatā \|*  
*tāvadapyāśramāḥ puṇyāstatra santi hyanekaśaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As far as Godavari is directly visible, there are many holy hermitages on its bank.

## \|\| 2.72.29 \|\|

*teṣu snātvā vidhānena santarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|*  
*naro'bhilaṣitānkāmānprāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. There is no doubt about this that by having a holy dip in them in accordance with injunctions and by performing a Tarpana rite to the Pitrs and deities, a man attains his cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.72.30 \|\|

*prakāśā tu kvacidbhadre kvacidguptā tataḥ param \|*  
*plāvayāmāsa dharaṇīṃ puṇyā godāvarī nadī \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О gentle lady, visible in some places and hidden thereafter, the meritorious river Godavari flooded the earth.

## \|\| 2.72.31 \|\|

*yatra prakaṭatāṃ yātā nṛṇāṃ bhaktyā maheśvarī \|*  
*tatra tīrthaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ snānamātrādaghāpaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Where the great goddess Godavari had manifested herself, thanks to the devotion of men, the Tlrtha is highly meritorious. A mere holy dip therein is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.72.32 \|\|

*tataḥ pañcavaṭīṃ prāpya sā devī niyatavratā \|*  
*suprakāśamanuprāptā lokānāṃ gatidāyinī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereafter, the goddess of invariable holy rites reached Paftcavati and manifested herself clearly. She is the bestower of good goal Moksa to the people.

## \|\| 2.72.33 \|\|

*godāvaryāṃ pañcavaṭyāṃ yaḥ snāyānniyatavrataḥ \|*  
*sa naraḥ prāpnuyātkāmānabhīṣṭānvidhinandini \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О daughter of Brahma, he who takes a holy dip in the Godavari at Paftcavati and observes holy rites, invariably shall attain cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.72.34 \|\|

*yadā tretāyuge rāmaḥ pañcavaṭyāmupāgataḥ \|*  
*sabhāryaḥ sānujastatra vasanpuṇyatarāṃ vyadhāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the Tretayuga, Rama came to Paftcavati and stayed there along with his wife and his younger brother. By staying here he made the river holier.

## \|\| 2.72.35 \|\|

*ityetsarvamākhyātaṃ gautamāśramajaṃ śubhe \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ paṭhatāṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaghnaṃ vāñchitapradam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О splendid lady, everything has thus been recounted regarding the hermitage of Gautama. It is destructive of sins of those who hear and those who read. It bestows the desired benefit.

## Chapter 73. The Greatness of TryambakeSvara

## \|\| 2.73.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ guro tvayā proktaṃ puṇyākhyānaṃ ca gautamam \|*  
*tr! yambakasya ca māhātmyaṃ godāpañcavaṭībhavam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О preceptor, the sacred anecdote of Gautama recounted by you has been heard. So also the greatness of Tryambaka at Panchavati on the Godavari.

## \|\| 2.73.2-5 \|\|

*adhunā śrotumicchāmi puṇḍarīkapurodbhavam \|*  
*yathā tatra mahādevastāṇḍavaṃ nṛtyamācarat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tathā vada mahīdeva puṇyātpuṇyataraṃ mama \|*  
*vasuruvāca- bhaktavaśyo mahādevaḥ sadyo varada eva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prākaṭyaṃ yāti bhaktānāṃ karoti ca tadicchayā \|*  
*ekadā jaiminirnāmnā vyāsaśiṣyo munīśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*agniveśādibhiḥ śiṣyaiḥ sārddhaṃ tīrthānyaṭannagāt \|*  
*puṇḍarīkapuraṃ sākṣāddevarājapuropamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-4a. Now I wish to hear the greatness of Pundarlka- pura1 and also how Mahadeva performed Tandava dance. О god on the earth (Brahmana), it is more meritorious than the most meritorious holy centres. Vasusaid: Mahadeva is under the control of the devotees. He is the bestower of boons immediately. He manifests himself before the devotees and carries out what they wish.

4b-5. On one occasion, the great sage Jaimini, the disciple of Vyasa was going on a pilgrimage to a holy place along with Agnivesa and other disciples. He went to the city of Pun- darlka, comparable to the city of the king of Devas.

## \|\| 2.73.6-9 \|\|

*sarvato'laṅkṛtaṃ śrīmatsarvartukusumadrumaiḥ \|*  
*śobhitaṃ śītalacchāyaiḥ śubhravārijalāśayaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nānāvayaḥkulākīrṇaiḥ suramyaiḥ kamalākaraiḥ \|*  
*nārībhirapsarobhiśca nṛbhirvidyādharadyubhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vilasadbhavanaiḥ śubhrairvimānamiva rājate \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śobhāṃ munistasya purasya prītimānbhṛśam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*babhūva ca manaścakre snātuṃ tatra sarovare \|*  
*snigdhacchāyairdrumairyukte nānāpuṣpasugandhite \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. It is prosperous and glorious. It is adorned on all sides by the trees blossoming in all seasons. It is rendered splendid by means of trees with cool shade, by large reservoirs of clear water; with very beautiful lotus-ponds which were occupied by different kinds of birds. It is frequented by women, celestial damsels and men having the lustre of Vidyadharas. It shines like an aerial chariot with pure shining houses. On seeing the splendour of that city, the sage became highly delighted. He was inclined to take a holy bath there in that excellent lake which is rendered fragrant by means of different kinds of flowers and trees with pleasant shades.

## \|\| 2.73.10 \|\|

*viśramya taruchāyāḍhye taṭe tasya kṣaṇaṃ muniḥ \|*  
*snātvā nityāḥ kriyāścakre devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After taking rest for a short while on the banks having thick shade, the sage took a holy dip and performed the daily routine rites including the rites of Tarpana to the Devas, sages and Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.73.11 \|\|

*nirmāya pārthivaṃ liṅgaṃ vividhairupacārakaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa vidhivatpādyārghyādyairanākulaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He made a Linga out of earth (clay) and worshipped it with various services such as Padya, Arghya and others duly. He was not agitated.

## \|\| 2.73.12-13 \|\|

*gandhairdhūpaistathā dīpairnaivedyairvividhairapi \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ prārcya sthito yāvadabhūnmuniḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tāvatprasanno bhagavānsākṣātkāramupāgataḥ \|*  
*tasminneva ca mṛlliṅge nānāratnaprabhodgame \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. He adored Siva by means of scents, fragrant incense, lamps, Naivedyas and different fragrant flowers. When the sage stood by after worship, the lord who was pleased with him, manifested himself to him in that very same clay, Linga emitting the lustre of different kinds of jewels.

## \|\| 2.73.14-18 \|\|

*tataḥ sa jaiminirdṛṣṭvā sākṣāddevamumāpatim \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau punarutthāya sāñjali \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prāha prapannārtiharaṃ harārddhāṅgaṃ hariṃ vibhum \|*  
*jaiminiruvāca- dhanyo'smi kṛtakṛtyo'smi devadeva jagatpate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yastvaṃ brahmādibhirdhyeyaḥ sākṣānmaddṛṣṭigocaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prasannaḥ sa vibhurgirīśo'sya nijaṃ karam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śirasyādhāyāgadattaṃ brūhi putra kimicchasi \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ śambhorjaiminiḥ pratyuvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*devaṃ sāmbaṃ savighneśaṃ sakumāraṃ vilokaye \|*  
*tataḥ sāmbaḥ saputro'sya śaṅkaro darśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-15a. On seeing lord Siva directly, Jaimini fell on the ground like a staff. After getting up again he stood with palms joined in reverence. He then addressed Hari, half of whose body was that of Siva, who dispels the anguish of those who seek shelter in him. Jaimini said:

15b-16a “O God of gods, the Lord of the universe, I am blessed. I feel that I have accomplished all objectives of life inasmuch as you who are worthy of being meditated upon by great gods like Brahma and others have personally revealed yourself before my eyes.”

16b-17a. Then the delighted lord Girisa placed his hand on Jaimini’s head and told him — “O dear son, tell me what you wish?

17b-18. On hearing those words of Sambhu, Jaimini replied, “May I see the lord accompanied by Amba (Parvatl) Vighnesa (Ganapati) and Kumara (Karttikeya). Then Sankara appeared before him accompanied by his son as well as by Amba.

## \|\| 2.73.19-22 \|\|

*punaḥ prāha prasannātmā brūhi putra kimicchasi \|*  
*athāsya jaiminirvīkṣya kṛpālutvaṃ jagadguroḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*smayannāha samīkṣe tvāṃ tāṇḍavaṃ naṭanaṃ gatam \|*  
*atha tadvāñchitaṃ kartuṃ bhagavānambikāpatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sasmāra pramathānsarvānnānākrīḍāviśāradān \|*  
*smṛtamātrāstu te sarve nandibhṛṅgipurogamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*samājagmuḥ prajalpantaḥ kautūhalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*savighneśakumārāmbaṃ te namaskṛtya vāgyatāḥ \|*  
*tasthuḥ prāñjalayo devadevasyājñāsamīkṣakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19a. Then the delighted lord asked again — “Tell me, dear son, what do you wish?”

19b-20a. On seeing the merciful nature of the lord, of the preceptor of the universe, Jaimini smilingly said — May I see you performing the Tandava dance”1

20b-21a. Then, in order to fulfil that desire of his, lord Ambikapati remembered Siva, Pramathas who are experts in different sports.

2lb-22. The moment they were remembered, all of фет led by Nandin, Bhrngin and others came there chattering enthusiastically. After bowing down to the lord accompanied by VighneSa (Ganesa) Кйтага (Karttikeya) and Amba they remained silent and stood there with palms joined in reverence. They eagerly waited for the behests of the lord of the Devas.

## \|\| 2.73.23 \|\|

*tato haro harājñayā vidhāya rūpamadbhutaṃ \|*  
*pranartumudyato babhau vicitraveṣabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*vilolanāgavallarīddhakakṣaīṣadutsitā- nano lalāṭaśobhitendulekha ūrdhvadordhvajaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then at the behest of Jaimini, Siva assumed a wonderful form with ornaments and dress of variegated nature, and began to dance. He shone with the tremulous creeper-like serpents appearing as kindled fire. A slight smile flickered over his face. The crescent moon rendered the forehead splendid. His arms were lifted up like a banner.

## \|\| 2.73.24 \|\|

*sudṛgviliptabhasmadeharugjitenducandri ko jaṭākalāpanissaratsurāpagārdra vigrahaḥ \|*  
*lalāṭalocanojjvalatkṛśānutaptaśītaguḥ sravatsudhānujīvitaiṇabhūpakṛttihuṅkṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He excelled the moon (in beauty and splendour) and its light by the brilliances of Bhasman (ashes) applied all over his body by him of beautiful eyes (or by his beautiful-eyed consort Parvatl). His body had been rendered wet by the sprinkling of water of the celestial river (Ganga) that flowed out of his matted hair. The crescent of the moon (on his crest was scorched by his blazing eye in the forehead but the nectar that oozed out of the moon brought back to life the hide of the king of beasts who created a roaring hissing sound.

## \|\| 2.73.25 \|\|

*kumāravāhakekicañcukṛṣṭanāgaphuṅkṛto galatsudhānujīvadabjayonituṇḍatuṅkṛtaḥ \|*  
*phaṇiprabhītavighnarājavāhanākhucuṅkṛto mṛgendra nādabhīṣitākṣatanmahokṣabhāṅkṛtaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the peacock, the vehicle of Kumara, caught hold of a serpent with its beak, it began to hiss (Phunkrta). The head of the lotus-born deity (god Brahma) was enlivened by the nectar that was oozing out, and he was reviled by it (Tumkrta). The mouse that is the vehicle of Vighnaraja(Ganesa) was afraid of the serpent and so it squealed (Cunkrta). His own great bull became afraid at the roaring sound of the lion (that was resucitated), the fear was visible in its eyes and it began to bellow.

## \|\| 2.73.26 \|\|

*muhuḥ padāmbujaprapātakampitāvanītalaḥ prakṛṣṭavādyahṛṣṭagātraromarājikaṇṭakaḥ \|*  
*surāsurendra mauliratnabhāsitāṅighrapaṅkajo gaṇeśakārtikeyaśailaputrivīkṣitānanaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. His lotus-like feet fell frequently on the surface of the earth that shook thereby. When he heard the excellent sound of musical instruments, he was delighted and hairs stood on their ends. His lotus-like feet were further brightened up by the the jewels on the crowns of the Devas and Asuras. GaneSa, Karttikeya and Sailaputrl (daughter of the mountain-Parvatl) were eagerly looking at his face.

## \|\| 2.73.27 \|\|

*pravṛddhaharṣabhaktavṛndasamyaguktasañjayaḥ pravṛttatāṇḍavairvibhurbabhau diśo'vabhāsayan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The devotees who were highly delighted shouted cries of victory for him. The lord shone brilliantly with the Tandava dance that followed. He brightened the quarters.

## \|\| 2.73.28 \|\|

*athānandārṇave magno dṛṣṭvā nṛtyaṃ maheśituḥ \|*  
*jaiminirvedapādena stavenāstautsamāhitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then, on seeing the dance of MaheSa Jaimini was immersed in the ocean of bliss. With great concentration, he eulogised the lord with hymn consisting of verses having one quatrain from the Vedic texts in each. The Veda-Pdda Hymn i1 V.

## \|\| 2.73.29 \|\|

*viriñciviṣṇugiriśapraṇatāṅighrasaroruhe \|*  
*jagatsūte namastubhyaṃ devi kāmpilyavāsini \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О goddess residing Kampilya, О mother of the universe, О deity whose lotus-like feet arc bowed to by Brahma, Visnu and Siva, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 2.73.30 \|\|

*vighneśavidhimārtaṇḍacandre ndro pendra vandita \|*  
*namo gaṇapate tubhyaṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmaṇaspate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О Ganapati, obeisance to you, О deity saluted by Ganesa, Brahma, Sun, Moon, Indra and Visnu, О lord of Brahman or Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.73.31 \|\|

*umākomalahastābjasambhāvitalalāṭakam \|*  
*hiraṇyakuṇḍalaṃ vaṃde kumāraṃ puṣkarasrajam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I salute Kumara who has gold earrings, whose forehead is stroked by the lotus-like tender hands ofUma and who wears lotus garlands.

## \|\| 2.73.32 \|\|

*śivaṃ brahmādidurdarśaṃ naraḥ kaḥ stotumarhati \|*  
*darśanātte stutirme sā cābhrādvṛṣṭirivājani \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Which man can adequately eulogise Siva, imperceptible to Brahma and others. By your vision my eulogy is born like the shower from the cloud.

## \|\| 2.73.33 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāya sāmbāya namaḥ śarvāya śambhave \|*  
*namo naṭāya rudrā ya sadasaspataye namaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Obeisance to Siva accompanied by Amba, obeisance to Sarva, to Sambhu, Obeisance to Rudra who dances; obeisance to Sadasaspati (the lord of the assembly).

## \|\| 2.73.34 \|\|

*pādabhinnāya lokāya maulibhinnāṇḍabhittaye \|*  
*bhujabhrāntadigantāya bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Obeisance to the deity who has split the world with his feet; who has split the walls of the egg (i.e. cosmic egg) with his head, who has wandered over the ends of quarters with his arms (the arms are stretched on to the quarters), obeisance to the lord of living beings.

## \|\| 2.73.35 \|\|

*kvaṇannūpurayugmāya vilasatkṛttivāsase \|*  
*phaṇīndra mekhalāyāstu paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hail be to the deity having a pair of jingling anklets, to the deity wearing shining hides as clothes; obeisance to the deity having the lord of serpents as a girdle, obeisance to the lord of Pagus (Individual souls).

## \|\| 2.73.36 \|\|
