*kālakālāya somāya yogine śūlapāṇaye \|*  
*asthibhūṣāya śuddhāya jagatāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Salute to Soma; Kalakiila (Death unto the god of death); obeisance to the trident-armed Yogin. Bow to the pure one bedecked in bones; obeisance to the lord of the worlds.

## \|\| 2.73.37 \|\|

*pātre sarvasya jagato netre sarvadivaukasām \|*  
*gotrāṇāṃ pataye tubhyaṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Obeisance to the protector of the entire universe; Obeisance to the leader of all heaven-dwellers, obeisance to you the lord of mountains; obeisance to the lord of holy centres.

## \|\| 2.73.38 \|\|

*śaṅkarāya namastubhyaṃ maṅgalāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*dhanānāṃ pataye tubhyamannānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*ātmādhipataye tubhyaṃ namo mīḍhuṣṭamāya ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Obeisance to Sankara (the bestower of bliss), salute to Mangala (the auspicious Deity), obeisance to the lord of riches, Hail to you the lord of food, obeisance to you the lord of Atman; obeisance to the most bountiful god.

## \|\| 2.73.39 \|\|

*aṣṭāṅgāyātihṛdyāya kliṣṭabhakteṣṭadāyine \|*  
*iṣṭighnāya sutuṣṭāya puṣṭānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Obeisance to the eight-limbed one (one having the eight cosmic bodies). Salute to the excessively hearty one. Obeisance to the bestower of the desired things on devotees in distress. Hail to the destroyer of sacrifice; obeisance to the most delighted deity; obeisance to the lord of well nourished beings.

## \|\| 2.73.40 \|\|

*pañcabhūtādhipataye kālādhipataye namaḥ \|*  
*nama ātmādhipataye diśāṃ ca pataye namaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Hail to the lord of five elements; obeisance to the overlord of Kala (God of Death, Time); obeisance to the lord of Atman; obeisance to the lord of the quarters.

## \|\| 2.73.41 \|\|

*viśvakatre maheśāya viśvabhartre pinākine \|*  
*viśvahantre'gninetrāya viśvarūpāya vai namaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Obeisance to Mahesa, the creator of the universe; Hail to thePinaka-bearing god, the sustainer of the universe; obeisance to the fiery-eyed destroyer of the universe; obeisance to the one having manifold forms.

## \|\| 2.73.42 \|\|

*īśāna te tatpuruṣa namo ghoraya te sadā \|*  
*vāmadeva namaste'stu sadyojātāya vai namaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Isana, obeisance to you; О Tatpurusa, obeisance to you; obeisance always unto you, to Aghora; О Vamadeva,. obeisance be to you. Obeisance to Sadyojata (a form of Siva).

## \|\| 2.73.43 \|\|

*bhūtibhūṣāya bhaktānāṃ bhītibhaṅgapradāyine \|*  
*namo bhavāya bhargāya namo rudrā ya mīḍhuṣe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Obeisance to one embellished with Bhasman. Hail to the destroyer of the fear of devotees. A bow to Bhava; to Bharga; to Rudra, to Mltfhus (the liberal god).

## \|\| 2.73.44 \|\|

*sahasrāmbāya sāmbāya sahasrābhīṣave namaḥ \|*  
*sahasrabāhave tubhyaṃ sahasrākṣāya mīḍhuṣe \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Obeisance to the thousand-eyed deity; to the deity accompanied by Amba; obeisance to the thousand-rayed one; obeisance to the thousand-armed one; obeisance to the thousandeyed Midhus (sun-god).

## \|\| 2.73.45 \|\|

*sukapolāya somāya sulalāṭāya subhruve \|*  
*sudehāya namastubhyaṃ sumṛḍīkāya mīḍhuṣe \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hail to the god with good cheeks. Obeisance to Soma with good forehead; obeisance to one with good eyebrows; to one with good physical body; salute to you to extremely compassionate bountiful Lord.

## \|\| 2.73.46 \|\|

*bhavakleśanimittorubhayacchedakṛte sadā \|*  
*namastubhyamaṣāḍhāya sahamānāya mīḍhuṣe \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Obeisance to one who always dispels the tremendous fear caused by the distress of worldly existence; Hail to you the invincible god; obeisance to MIdhus (the bountiful god) the victorious deity.

## \|\| 2.73.47 \|\|

*vaṃde'ha devamānandasandohaṃ lāsyasundaram \|*  
*samastajagatāṃ nāthaṃ sadasaspatimadbhutam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I salute the lord who is mass of bliss; I salute the lord who is beautiful in the course of his dance, who is the lord of all the worlds and who is the wonderful Sadasaspati (lord of the assembly).

## \|\| 2.73.48 \|\|

*sujaṅghaṃ sundaraṃ kṣaumaṃ rakṣobhūtakṣatikṣamam \|*  
*yakṣeśeṣṭaṃ namāmīśamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ prabhum \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I bow down to the imperishable supreme lord; to Isa of fine-calf; to Isa wearing beautiful silken cloth (?) I bow down to the lord who is capable of destroying demons and goblins. I bow to the lord whose friend is the lord of the Yaksas.

## \|\| 2.73.49 \|\|

*arddhālakamavastrārddhamasthyutpaladalasrajam \|*  
*arddhapuṃlakṣaṇaṃ vaṃde puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I bow down to the half-man and half woman deity who is both dark and tawny-complexioned; who has half the characteristics of man; who has forelocks in one half of his body, who is naked in one half of his body and who wears the garlands of bones and lotus petals. (This is the Ardha-narl form of Siva.)

## \|\| 2.73.50 \|\|

*sakṛtpraṇatasaṃsāramahāsāgaratārakam \|*  
*praṇamāmi tamīśānaṃ jagatastasthuṣaspatim \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I bow down to Isana who is the lord of the mobile and immobile beings and who enables those who bow down but once, to him to cross the great ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.73.51 \|\|

*dhātāraṃ jagatāmīśaṃ dātāraṃ sarvasampadām \|*  
*netāraṃ marutāṃ vaṃde jetāramaparājitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. I salute Isa who is the creator of the worlds; who is bestower of riches; who is the leader of Maruts (Devas) and who is the unvanquished conqueror.

## \|\| 2.73.52 \|\|

*taṃ tvāmantakanetāraṃ vaṃde mandākinīdharam \|*  
*dadhāti vidadhadyo māmimāni trīṇi viṣṭapā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I bow down to you the leader of the god of death, I salute to the upholder of the Mandakini — Ganga-river on the head, I salute the lord who created these three worlds and who supports us all.

## \|\| 2.73.53 \|\|

*sarvajñaṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaṃ kaviṃ vaṃde tamīśvaram \|*  
*yataśca yajuṣā sārddhamṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I salute that lshvara who is omniscient; omnipresent, who is identical with all, who is a seer from whom Vedas viz. the Rks and Samans originated along witl/ the Yajus.

## \|\| 2.73.54 \|\|

*bhavantaṃ sudṛśaṃ vaṃde bhūtabhavyabhavanti ca \|*  
*tyajantītarakarmāṇi yo viśvābhirvipaśyati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I salute Lord Siva, the excellent seer, out of fear from whom the past, present and future beings abstain from other (i.e. sinful) deeds and who overviews the universe on all sides.

## \|\| 2.73.55 \|\|

*haraṃ suraniyantāraṃ harantamahamānataḥ \|*  
*yadājñayā jagatsarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I bow down to that Нага who annihilates, who restrains and checks the Devas and at whose behest Narayana pervades the universe and stands by.

## \|\| 2.73.56 \|\|

*taṃ namāmi mahādevaṃ yanniyogādidaṃ jagat \|*  
*kalpādau bhagavāndhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I bow down to that Mahadeva at whose behest, god Brahma, the creator created this universe at the beginning of the Kalpa in the same manner as it was before.

## \|\| 2.73.57 \|\|

*īśvaraṃ tamahaṃ devaṃ yasya liṅgamaharniśam \|*  
*yajante saha bhāryābhirindra jyeṣṭhā marudgaṇāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I salute that ISvara whose Linga is worshipped day and night by the hosts of Maruts (Devas) whose eldest member is Indra, along with their wives.

## \|\| 2.73.58 \|\|

*namāmi tamimaṃ rudraṃ yamabhyarcya sakṛtpurā \|*  
*avāpuḥ svaṃ svamaiśvaryaṃ devāsaḥ pūṣarātayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I bow down to that Rudra by worshipping whom only for once formerly the Devas, Pusa and others attained their respective prowess and position.

## \|\| 2.73.59 \|\|

*taṃ vaṃde devamīśānaṃ yaṃ śivaṃ hṛdayāṃbuje \|*  
*satataṃ yatayaḥ śāntāḥ sañjānānā upāsate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I salute that god Isana who is Siva. The quiescent ascetics know him well and worship him perpetually.

## \|\| 2.73.60 \|\|

*tadasmai satataṃ kurmo namaḥ kamalakāntaye \|*  
*umākucapaṭoraska yā te rudra śivā tanūḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Perpetually do we offer obeisance to that auspicious body of yours, О Rudra, that has the splendour and refulgence of the lotus. О deity who have the cloth over the breasts of Uma spreading over his chest we bow down to it.

## \|\| 2.73.61 \|\|

*namaste rudra bhāvāya namaste rudra kelaye \|*  
*namaste rudra śāntyai ca namaste rudra manyave \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Obeisance to you of terrible emotional feelings. Obeisance to you of terrible sports; obeisanee to you of fierce (very deep) quiescence; obeisance to you of terrible anger.

## \|\| 2.73.62 \|\|

*vedāśvarathaniṣṭhābhyāṃ pādābhyāṃ tripurāntaka \|*  
*bāṇakārmukayuktābhyāṃ bāhubhyāmuta te namaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. О destroyer of Tripuras, obeisance to you whose feet rest on the chariots and horses of the Vedas and whose arms are equipped with the bow and arrows at the time of the conquest of Tripura).

## \|\| 2.73.63 \|\|

*namaste vāsukijyāya viṣkirāya ca śaṅkara \|*  
*mahate merurūpāya namaste astu dhanvane \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O, Sankara, I bow down to you whose bow-string is the serpent Vasuki and who scatters arrows? May my salutes be to the great archer with Meru as the bow. devam is probably a misprint for Vande.

## \|\| 2.73.64 \|\|

*namaḥ paraśave te'stu śūlāyātularociṣe \|*  
*hayagrīvātmane tubhyamutota iṣave namaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Obeisance to you to your, Parasu (axe), to your trident of incomparable glitter. Salute to one identical with Hayagriva (the horse-necked) or obeisance to your arrow.

## \|\| 2.73.65 \|\|

*suretaravadhūhārahārīṇi hara yāni te \|*  
*anyānyastrāṇyahaṃ tūṇa idaṃ tebhyo'karaṃ namaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О Нага, whatever other weapons are in your quiver they remove the necklaces of the wives of Asuras (i.e. they kill the Asura husbands, thus making them widows) I make obeisance to them.

## \|\| 2.73.66 \|\|

*dharādharasutālīlāsarojāhatabāhave \|*  
*tasmai tubhyamaghorāya namo asmā śravasya ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Obeisance to you, to Aghora whose arms have been gently stroked with a toy-lotus by the daughter of the mountain. Obeisance to him who is praiseworthy to us.

## \|\| 2.73.67 \|\|

*rakṣa māmajñamakṣīṇamaśikṣitamananyagam \|*  
*anāthaṃ dīnamāpannaṃ daridraṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. О Nllalohita, (Siva) save me who am ignorant, uneducated, devoid of any other person for shelter and I am leaderless, indigent and wretched and in adversity.

## \|\| 2.73.68 \|\|

*durmukhaṃ duṣkriyaṃ duṣṭaṃ rakṣa māmīśa durdaśam \|*  
*ādṛśā tamahaṃ na tvadanyaṃ vindāmi rādhase \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О Isa, protect me who am wicked and in a wretched condition. My face is deformed and I am of evil activities. With this vision of mine I do not see anyone other than you for my propitiation.

## \|\| 2.73.69 \|\|

*bhavākhyenāgninā śambho rāgadveṣamadārciṣā \|*  
*dayālo dahyamānānāmasmākamavitā bhava \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О merciful Sambhu, be our protector. We are being burned by the fire of worldly existence which has love, hatred and pride for its flames.

## \|\| 2.73.70 \|\|

*paradāraṃ parāvāsaṃ paravastraṃ parāśrayam \|*  
*hara pāhi parānnaṃ māṃ puruṇāmanpuruṣṭuta \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О Нага, of many great names, О oft-eulogised deity, protect me. I am after other men’s wives. I live in other’s houses. I am clad in others’ clothes. I depend upon others’ shelter. I eat other mens’ food.

## \|\| 2.73.71 \|\|

*laukikairyatkṛtaṃ duṣṭairnāvamānaṃ sahāmahe \|*  
*deveśa tava dāsebhyo bhūridā bhūri dehi naḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. We do not endure insult heaped on your servants (i.e. devotees) by wicked people of the world. О lord of Devas, give us in plenty for many occasions.

## \|\| 2.73.72 \|\|

*kulokānāmayatnānāṃ garviṇāmīśa paśyatām \|*  
*asmabhyaṃ kṣetramāyuśca vasu spārhaṃ tadābhara \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. О lord, even as the haughty wicked persons who never exert themselves, look on, fill us with all desired wealth. Grant us field and longevity.

## \|\| 2.73.73 \|\|

*yāñcāto mahatīṃ lajjāmasmadīyāṃ ghṛṇānidhe \|*  
*tvameva vetsi nastūrṇamidaṃ stotṛbhya ābhara \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. О storehouse of kindness, you are indeed aware of our great feelings of shame for begging. Grant us to the full the eulogisers with all these riches.

## \|\| 2.73.74 \|\|

*jāyā mātā pitā cānye māṃ dviṣantyamitaṃ kṛśam \|*  
*dehi me mahatīṃ vidyāṃ rāyā viśvapuṣā saha \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. My wife, mother, father and others excessively hate me. I am so very lean (indigent); Grant me great learning along with the wealth that nourishes the universe.

## \|\| 2.73.75 \|\|

*adṛṣṭārtheṣu sarveṣu dṛṣṭārtheṣvapi karmasu \|*  
*merudhanvannaśaktebhyo balaṃ dhehi tanūṣu naḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. We are incompetent to perform rites whether the results are visible or invisible. О deity with Mem as your bow, grant the requisite strength to our bodies.

## \|\| 2.73.76 \|\|

*labdhāniṣṭasahasrasya nityamiṣṭaviyoginaḥ \|*  
*hṛdro gaṃ mama deveśa harimāṇaṃ ca nāśaya \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. О lord of Devas, I have incurred a thousand evils. Everyday, I am being separated from what is desired and desirable. Do destroy the ailment in my heart and also this death.

## \|\| 2.73.77 \|\|

*ye ye rogāḥ piśācā vā narā devāśca māmiha \|*  
*bādhante devatāḥ sarvā nibādhasva mahānasi \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Whatever ailments, ghosts, men and Devas oppress me, free me from oppression of all these. You are indeed very great.

## \|\| 2.73.78 \|\|

*tvameva rakṣitāsmākamanyaḥ kaścinna vidyate \|*  
*tasmātsvīkṛtya deveśa rakṣā ṇo brahmaṇaspate \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. You alone are our protector. There is no one else to rescue us. Hence, О lord of Devas, О lord of Brahma, accept us and protect us.

## \|\| 2.73.79 \|\|

*tvamevomāpate mātā tvaṃ pitā tvaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tvamāyustvaṃ matistvaṃ śrīruta bhrātota naḥ sakhā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. О lord of Uma, you alone are my mother; you alone are my father, you are my grandfather. You are my longevity. You are intellect. You are glory. You are my brother. You are my friend.

## \|\| 2.73.80 \|\|

*yatastvameva deveśa kartā sarvasya karmaṇaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kṣamasva tatsarvaṃ yanmayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Since, you alone are the doer of all rites, О lord of gods, forgive every evil deed committed by me.

## \|\| 2.73.81 \|\|

*tvatsamo na prabhutvena phalgutvena ca matsamaḥ \|*  
*tato deva mahādeva tvamasmākaṃ tavasmasi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. There is no one else equal to you in lordly glory. There is no one equal to me in worthlessness. Hence, О Lord Mahadeva you are mine and I am yours.

## \|\| 2.73.82 \|\|

*susmitaṃ bhasmagaurāṅgaṃ taruṇādityavigraham \|*  
*prasannavadanaṃ saumyaṃ gāye tvā namasā girā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In reverential terms do I sing of you who are so gentle, whose smile is so sweet; whose person appears white with ashes; whose body is refulgent as the midday sun and whose face is beaming with delight.

## \|\| 2.73.83 \|\|

*eṣa eva varo'smākaṃ nṛtyantaṃ tvāṃ sabhāpatim \|*  
*lokayantamumākāntaṃ paśyema śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. It is our desired boon that we may continue to look at you, the president of the assembly while you should go on dancing for a hundred years looking favourably at us.

## \|\| 2.73.84 \|\|

*arogiṇo mahābhāgā vidvāṃsaśca bahuśrutāḥ \|*  
*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena jīvema śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. О lord, due to your favour we may live for a hundred years; may we be blessed ones, learned, scholars conversant with Vedic texts and free from ailments.

## \|\| 2.73.85 \|\|

*sadārā bandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ tvadīyaṃ tāṇḍavāmṛtam \|*  
*pibantaḥ kāmamīśānaṃ nandāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. О Isana may we rejoice for a hundred years, drinking to our heart’s content the nectar of your Tantfava dance, sharing it with our wives and kinsmen. The reading namasd gird may mean, ‘paying our obeisance to you, we praise you in words, but if the reading be manasd gird: ‘I sing with my heart and soul and in words.’

## \|\| 2.73.86 \|\|

*devadeva mahādeva tvadīyāṅighrasaroruham \|*  
*kāmaṃ madhumayaṃ pītvā modāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. О lord of Devas О Mahadeva, may we be happy for a hundred years, drinking honey, from your lotus-like feet to our heart’s content.

## \|\| 2.73.87 \|\|

*kīṭā nāgāḥ piśācā vā ye vā ke vā bhave bhave \|*  
*tava dāsā mahādeva bhavāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. May we be your servants, О Mahadeva for hundreds of years in every birth whether we are born as worms or serpents, ghosts or any other being.

## \|\| 2.73.88 \|\|

*sabhāyāmīśa te deva nṛtyavādyagalasvanam \|*  
*śravaṇābhyāṃ mahādeva śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. О lord Isha, О Mahadeva, may we hear fora hundred years, with our ears the sound of your vocal music, instrumental music, and behold your dance in the assembly chamber.

## \|\| 2.73.89 \|\|

*smṛtimātreṇa saṃsāravināśanakarāṇi te \|*  
*nāmāni khalu divyāni prabravāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. May we repeat for a hundred years your divine names that destroy mundane existence, thanks to their mere remembrance.

## \|\| 2.73.90 \|\|

*iṣusandhānamātreṇa dagdhatripura dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*ādhibhirvyādhibhirnityamajitāḥ syāma śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. О Dhurjati (god with a massive matted locks of hair), О deity who burned the three cities merely by fixing the arrow to the bow, may we be unconquered by mental anguishes and bodily ailments perpetually for a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.73.91 \|\|

*cārucāmīkarābhāsaṃ gaurīkucapaṭorasam \|*  
*kadā nu lokayiṣyāmi yuvānaṃ viśpatiṃ kavim \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. When will I see the youthful poet, the lord of the subjects, the deity who has the charming lustre of gold and whose chest is in contact with the cloth over the breasts of Gauri?

## \|\| 2.73.92 \|\|

*pramathendrā vṛtaṃ prītavadanaṃ priyavāsasam \|*  
*seviṣye'ha kadā sāmbaṃ subhāsaṃ śukraśociṣam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. When will I serve that greatly lustrous Samba who is surrounded by the Pramathas (all goblin-attendants), whose face is beaming with delight, who is fond of clothes (?), whose semen is of brilliant radiance.

## \|\| 2.73.93 \|\|

*bahvenasaṃ māmakṛtapuṇyaleśaṃ ca durmatim \|*  
*svīkariṣyati kiṃ nvīśo nīlagrīvo vilohitaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Will Isa, the blue-necked deity of special reddish complexion accept me who have committed many sins, have not performed even the smallest of meritorious deeds and am of wicked mind.

## \|\| 2.73.94 \|\|

*kālaśūlānalāsaktaṃ bhītaṃ vyākulamānasam \|*  
*kadā nu dra kṣyatīśo māṃ tuvigrīvo anānataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. When Isha of powerful neck who does not bow down (to anyone else) see me who am frightened, whose mind is agitated and who am (pierced and) fixed to the fiery trident of Kala (god of death)?

## \|\| 2.73.95 \|\|

*gāyakā yūyamāyāta yadi rāgādilipsavaḥ \|*  
*dhanadasya sakhāyaṃ tamupāsmai gāyatā naraḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. О men, О songsters, if you are desirous of attaining the fulfilment of love etc., come on. Sing the glory of the friend of Dhanada (Kubera).

## \|\| 2.73.96 \|\|

*svastyastu sakhi te jihve vidyādāturumāpateḥ \|*  
*stavamuccataraṃ brūhi jayatāmiva dundubhiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. О my tongue, hail to thee. Loudly proclaim the eulogy of the hymn of the lord of Uma, the bestower of learning. Be as loud as the trumpet of a victorious king.

## \|\| 2.73.97 \|\|

*cetayājana dha śāntastvaṃ nedaṃ vedākhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*asya tṛptyākhilaṃ śambhorgauro na tṛṣitaḥ piba \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. (Defective) О you unborn one! You are quiescent. Do you not know that by Siva’s satisfaction the whole world gets satiated? Drink of his name if you are thirsty.

## \|\| 2.73.98 \|\|

*sugandhiṃ ca sukhasparśaṃ kāmadaṃ somabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*gāḍhamāliṅga maccittaṃ yoṣā jāramiva priyam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. О my mind, like a woman who embraces her beloved paramour embrace closely the deity who bestows the cherished desires, who is adorned by the moon, whose touch is pleasant and whose fragrance is enchanting.

## \|\| 2.73.99 \|\|

*mahāmayūkhāya mahābhujāya mahāśarīrāya mahāmbarāya \|*  
*mahākirīṭāya maheśvarāya maho mahīṃ suṣṭutimīrayāmi \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. I recite the best of hymns that is greater than the greatest, unto Mahesvara whose resplendent ray is great; whose arms are greatly mighty; whose body is immensely big; whose clothes are large and whose crown is big.

## \|\| 2.73.100 \|\|

*yathākathañcidra citābhirīṣatprasannataścārubhirādareṇa \|*  
*prapūjayāmi stutibhirmaheśamaṣāḍhamugraṃ sahamānamābhiḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. With these beautiful hymns I worship Ugramahesa who is invincible, and proud. The hymns have been composed with great difficulty, yet with great respect, for the slightest of the pleasure of the lord.

## \|\| 2.73.101 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāya tripurāntakāya jagattrayeśāya digambarāya \|*  
*namo'stu mukhyāya harāya bhūyo namo jaghanyāya ca budhniyāya \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Obeisance to Siva, the destroyer of the three cities, Hail to the lord of the three worlds. Obeisance to the naked deity. Salute be to Нага the chief of deities. Obeisence to the lowest of all deities. Obeisance to one who is at the base of all.

## \|\| 2.73.102 \|\|

*namo vikārāya vikāriṇe te namo bhavāyāstu bhavodbhavāya \|*  
*bahuprajātyantavicitrarūpa yataḥ prasūtā jagataḥ prasūtiḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Obeisance to the Vikara (effect); obeisance to the Vikarin (cause), obeisance to you, to Bhava; obeisance to the source of origin of the world. Obeisance to you, О deity of many progenies, О deity of very wonderful features from whom the entire universe is born.

## \|\| 2.73.103 \|\|

*tasmai sureśorukirīṭanānāratnāvṛtāṣṭāpadaviṣṭarāya \|*  
*bhasmāṅgarāgāya namaḥ parasmai yasmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiñcit \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Obeisance to the deity whose foot-stool is encircled by the lustre of different jewels on the crowns of leading Devas, to the deity whose unguent is Bhasman (ashes); obeisance to the greatest deity than whom there is nothing greater.

## \|\| 2.73.104 \|\|

*sarpādhirājauṣadhināthayuddhakṣubhyajjaṭāmaṇḍalagahvarāya \|*  
*tubhyaṃ namaḥ sundaratāṇḍavāya yasminnidaṃ sañcavicaiti sarvam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Obeisance to you who perform beautiful Tantjava dance. Within the mass of your matted hair, the king of serpents and the lord of herbs (moon) come into clash and so it is agitated. Obeisance to you in whom all this meets together and from whom all this departs.

## \|\| 2.73.105 \|\|

*murārinetrārcitapādapadmamumāṅighralākṣāpariraktapāṇim \|*  
*namāmi devaṃ vṛṣanīlakaṇṭhaṃ hiraṇyadantaṃ śucivarṇamārāt \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. I bow down to the lord whose neck is as blue as the peacock’s plumage; whose lotus-like feet are worshipped by Visnu; whose hands are reddish, thanks to the lac-juice from the feet of Uma; whose teeth have the golden lustre and who is fair-complexioned I go near him and bow down to him.

## \|\| 2.73.106 \|\|

*anantamavyaktamacintyamekaṃ harantamāśāmbaramambarāṅgam \|*  
*ajaṃ purāṇaṃ praṇamāmi yūpamaṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyān \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. I bow down to that Нага who is infinite, unmanifest, beyond contemplation or thinking; who is single, and has the quarters for his garments (i.e. is naked); who is unborn, who is an ancient sacrificial post and one whose body is the sky. He is more minute than the atom. He is greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 2.73.107 \|\|

*antaḥsthamātmānamajaṃ na dṛṣṭvā bhramanti mūḍhā girigahvareṣu \|*  
*paścādudagdakṣiṇataḥ purastādadhaḥ svidāsī3dupari svidāsī3t \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Without seeing the eternal Atman stationed within, foolish persons wander among the mountain caves; to the west, to the north, to the south and to the east. They do not know whether he is below or whether he is above.

## \|\| 2.73.108 \|\|

*imaṃ namāmīśvaramindumaule śivaṃ mahānandamaśokaduḥkham \|*  
*hṛdaṃbuje tiṣṭhati yaḥ parātmā yataśca sarvāḥ pradiśo diśaśca \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. О Moon-crested lord, I bow down to this lord Siva of great bliss; devoid of sorrow and pain; who is the great Atman, who stays in the lotus-like cavity of the heart and from whom the quarters and the interstices of the quarters originate.

## \|\| 2.73.109 \|\|

*rāgādikāpaṭyasamudbhavena bhāntaṃ bhavākhyena mahāmayena \|*  
*vilokya māṃ pālaya candra maule bhiṣaktamaṃ tvā bhiṣajāṃ śṛṇomi \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. О Moon-crested lord, I hear that you are the greatest of all physicians. See me who appear with the great ailment named Bhava (mundane existence) originating from lust, deception etc. and protect me.

## \|\| 2.73.110 \|\|

*duḥkhāmburāśiṃ sukhaleśahīnamaspṛṣṭapuṇyaṃ bahupātakaṃ mām \|*  
*mṛtyoḥ karasthaṃ bhava rakṣa bhītaṃ paścātpurastādadharādudaktāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. I am drowning in the ocean of distress. I do not have even an iota of happiness. I have not even touched anything meritorious. I have committed many sins and I am within the grip of the god of death. I am, therefore, frightened. Protect me from behind, from front, from below and from above.

## \|\| 2.73.111 \|\|

*girīndra jācārumukhāvalokasuśītayā deva tavaiva dṛṣṭyā \|*  
*vayaṃ dayāpūritayaiva pūrṇamapo na nāvā duritā tarema \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. О Lord, we are blessed with thy vision alone that is full of mercy and that is very cool, thanks to glancing at the charming face of Parvatl. With that we shall cross the miseries and evils even as one crosses the waters by means of a boat.

## \|\| 2.73.112 \|\|

*apārasaṃsārasamudra madhye nimagnamutkrośamanalparāgam \|*  
*māmakṣamaṃ pāhi maheśajuṣṭamojiṣṭhayā dakṣiṇayeva rātim \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. I am immersed in the middle of boundless ocean of worldly existence. I clamour. My passion is by nomeans little. I am helpless. О MaheSa, save me who have served you as one serves a donor by means of sumptuous Daksina.

## \|\| 2.73.113 \|\|

*smaranpurā sañcitapātakāni kharaṃ yamasyāpi mukhaṃ yamāre \|*  
*bibhemi me dehi yatheṣṭamāyuryadi kṣitāyuryadi vā paretaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. О enemy of Yama, remembering my sins accumulated formerly and the harsh and rough face of Yama, I fear enormously. Grant me sufficient life, should I be dead or should my life be broken.

## \|\| 2.73.114 \|\|

*sugandhibhiḥ sundarabhasmagaurairanantabhogairmṛdulairaghoraiḥ \|*  
*imaṃ kadāliṅgati māṃ pinākī sthirebhiraṅgaiḥ pururūpa ugraḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When will the Pinaka-bearing Ugra of many forms and features embrace me with his steady limbs, that emit fragrance, that are white, due to the fine Bhasman, that contain infinite means of pleasure and that are soft and mild?

## \|\| 2.73.115 \|\|

*krośantamīśaṃ patitaṃ bhavābdhau nākusthamaṇḍūkamivātibhītam \|*  
*kadā nu māṃ rakṣati devadevo hiraṇyarūpaḥ sa hiraṇyasandṛk \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. When will that lord of Devas who has golden features and golden vision protect me? I am shouting loud to the lord. I am fallen into the ocean of worldly existence. I am extremely frightened like a frog stationed in an anthill wherein a serpent dwells.

## \|\| 2.73.116 \|\|

*cārusmitaṃ candra kalāvataṃsaṃ gaurīkaṭākṣāruhayugmanetram \|*  
*ālokayiṣyāmi kadā nu sāmbamādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. When will I see Samba (Siva) who has the colour and lustre of the sun, who is beyond darkness, whose smiles are charming, who is adorned with the digit of the moon and whose pair of eyes mingle with the side-glances of Gaurl?

## \|\| 2.73.117 \|\|

*āgacchatānādimumukṣavo ye yūyaṃ śivaṃ cintayatāntare'bje \|*  
*dhyāyanti muktyarthamamuṃ hi nityaṃ vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. О ye primordial souls desirous of liberation, come and think of Siva within your lotus-like heart. Indeed those persons who have decisively learnt the perfect Vedantic knowledge, perpetually meditate on him for the sake of salvation.

## \|\| 2.73.118 \|\|

*āyāta yūyaṃ bhavatādhipatye kāmaṃ gaheśaṃ giriśaṃ yajadhvam \|*  
*evaṃ purābhyarcya hiraṇyagarbho bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Gome, ye and take up the worship of Mahesa, Girisa (Siva) to your heart’s content for the overlordship of the world. By worshipping him formerly, Hiranyagarbha (Brahma) became the sole lord of living beings.

## \|\| 2.73.119 \|\|

*ekāyanaṃ te vipulāṃ śriyaṃ te śrīkaṇṭhamenaṃ sukṛtā namantām \|*  
*śrīmānayaṃ śrīpativandyapādaḥ śrīṇāmudāro dharuṇo rayīṇām \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. May they bow down to the single goal, the extensive glory; may those meritorious persons bow down to this Srikantha. He is glorious and prosperous. His feet are worthy of being saluted by the lord of Sri (Visnu). He is liberal. He is the supporter and bestower of prosperity and riches.

## \|\| 2.73.120 \|\|

*suputrakāmā api ye manuṣyā yuvānamenaṃ giriśaṃ yajantām \|*  
*yataḥ svayambhūrjagato vidhātā hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. May those men who are desirous of good sons, worship this youthful Girisa from whom Hiranyagarbha originated formerly — Hiranyagarbha who is self-born and who is the creator of the universe.

## \|\| 2.73.121 \|\|

*alaṃ kimuktairbahubhiḥ samīhitaṃ samastamasyāśrayaṇena sidhyati \|*  
*purainamāśritya hi kumbhasambhavo divā na naktaṃ palito yuvājani \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Of what avail is much talk? Enough has been said. By resorting to him everything desired can be realised. By resorting to him day and night, formerly, sage Kumbhasambhava (the pot-bom Agastya) whose hairs had turned grey became a youth once again.

## \|\| 2.73.122 \|\|

*anyatparityajya mamākṣibhṛṅgāḥ sarvaṃ sadainaṃ śivamāśrayadhvam \|*  
*āmodavāneṣa mṛduḥ śivāya svāduḥṣkilāyaṃ madhumām̐ utāyam \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. О bees of my eyes (i.e. my eyes that resemble the bees) eschew everything else. Always resort to Siva. He is full of fragrance. He is soft. He is conducive to happiness. He is full of sweetness. Or is he a honeyed one?

## \|\| 2.73.123 \|\|

*bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ pratimānahīno vinirjjitāśeṣanarāmaraśca \|*  
*namaśca te vāṇi maheśamenaṃ stuhi śrutaṃ gartasadaṃ yuvānam \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. (If you worship Siva) you will be one devoid of a rival. You will be one who has conquered all men and gods. Obeisance to you О Speech? Eulogise this well-known youth seated in the pit (i.e. the cavity of the heart).

## \|\| 2.73.124 \|\|

*yadyanmanaścintayasi tvamiṣṭaṃ tattadbhaviṣyatyakhilaṃ dhruvaṃ te \|*  
*duḥkhena vṛttiṃ viṣaye kadācidyakṣvāmahe saumanasāya rudra m \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. О mind, whatever you think and desire for shall certainly and permanently accrue to you. The mind dwelling on worldly objects shall bring in misery (?) For the sake of good mentality we shall worship Rudra.

## \|\| 2.73.125 \|\|

*ajñānayogādapacārakarma yatpūrvamasmābhiranuṣṭhitaṃ te \|*  
*tadeva soḍhvā sakalaṃ dayālo piteva putrānpati no juṣasva \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. О merciful one, if out of ignorance we have improperly offended you before, forgive us entirely. Be to us like a father unto his sons.

## \|\| 2.73.126 \|\|

*saṃsārākhyakruddhasarpeṇa tīvrai rāgadveṣonmādalobhādidantaiḥ \|*  
*daṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā māṃ dayāluḥ pinākī devastrātā trāyatāmaprayucchan \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. On seeing me bitten by the infuriated serpent called worldly existence with the fangs such as lust, hatred, madness, covctiousness may the merciful Pinaka-bearing- lord, the protector, protect me carefully without absentmindedness).

## \|\| 2.73.127 \|\|

*ityuktvānte ye samādhernamante rudra tvāṃ te yānti janmāhidaṣṭāḥ \|*  
*santo nīlagrīvasūtrātmanāhaṃ tattvā yāmi brahmaṇā vandamānaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. (?) After saying this, those who, О Rudra, bow down to you at the end of Samadhi (ecstatic trance) go (to heaven) (though) they be bitten by the serpent of rebirth (Saiiisara). But I shall go unto you as a sutratman of the bluenecked deity while I shall be saluted even by Brahma.

## \|\| 2.73.128 \|\|

*bhavādhibhīṣaṇajvareṇa pīḍitānmahāmayānaśeṣapātakālayānadūrakālalocanān \|*  
*anāthanātha te kareṇa bheṣajena kālahā \|*  
*udūṣuṇo vaso mahe mṛśasva śūra rādhase \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. О heroic deity, stroke with your hand that is a penacea like ginger or pepper. О lord of the helpless ones, stroke us who are afflicted by the terrible fever of worldly existence, who have great ailments, who are the abodes of all sins and from whom the eyes of Kala are not far off. You are the slayer of Kala and you are being propitiated.

## \|\| 2.73.129 \|\|

*jayema yena sarvametadiṣṭamaṣṭadiggaṇaṃ \|*  
*bhuvaḥ sthalaṃ divaḥ sthalaṃ nabhaḥsthalaṃ ca tadgatam \|*  
*ya eṣa sarvadevadānavaprabhuḥ sabhāpatiḥ \|*  
*sa no dadātu taṃ rayiṃ puruṃ piśaṅgasaṅdṛśam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. May he who is the lord of all Devas and Danavas, who is the lord of the assembly-chamber, give us that great wealth, that tawny-coloured vision (?) whereby we shall conquer all these desired eight quarters, the places of the earth, of heaven, and of firmament and can have movement therein.

## \|\| 2.73.130 \|\|

*namo bhavāya te harāya bhūtibhāsitorase \|*  
*namo bhavābhibhūtibhītisaṅgine pinākine \|*  
*namaḥ śivāya viśvapāya śāśvatāya helaye \|*  
*na yasya hanyate sakhā na jīyate kadācana \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Obeisance to you, to Bhava, to Нага, Obeisance to the deity whose chest shines with the Bhasman, who is the comrade when one is afflicted by the fear of the attack of worldly existence (Samsara). Obeisance to the Pinaka-bearing deity. Hail to Siva, the protector of the universe; obeisance to the deity of perpetual dalliance; Bow to that lord whose,com- rade is never conquered nor killed.

## \|\| 2.73.131 \|\|

*surapatipataye namo namaḥ prajāpatipataye namo namaḥ \|*  
*kṣitipatipataye namo namo'mbikāpataya umāpataye namo namaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Obeisance, obeisance to the lord of the chiefs of gods, Hail, Hail to the lord of Prajapati; obeisance, obeisance, to the lord of the rulers of the earth; Bow again and again to the lord of Ambika, obeisance, obeisance to the lord of Uma.

## \|\| 2.73.132 \|\|

*vināyakaṃ vandanamastakāhatasvanādyasaṅghṛṣṭakirīṭamastakam \|*  
*namāmi nityaṃ praṇatārtināśanaṃ kaviṃ kavīnāmupamaśravastamam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. I bow down to Vinayaka, the permanent destroyer of the anguish of those who bow down; who is the poet of poets (or the wisest among the wise) and who is the most renowned. His crown or head has never been scraped due to the bowing down or its sound (?) (i.e. He has not bowed to anyone).

## \|\| 2.73.133 \|\|

*devā yuddhe yāge viprāstrapyāhvayaṃ dha dvayaṃ vindanti skandam \|*  
*vaṃde subrahmaṇyoṃ subrahmaṇyoṃ subrahmaṇyom \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The Devas obtain Skanda in the battle (as their leader). The Brahmanas obtain him in the sacrifice. His name is mentioned in the Vedas. I salute Subrahmanya, Оm, О Subrahmanya, Оm, О Subrahmanya, Om.

## \|\| 2.73.134 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāyai jagadambikāyai śivapriyāyai śivavigrahāyai \|*  
*samudbabhūvādri pateḥ sutā yā catuṣkapardā yuvatiḥ supeśāḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Obeisance to Siva (Parvatl), the mother of the universe, the beloved of Siva; salute to the goddess whose person is one with that of Siva. It was she who was born as the daughter of the mountain. She had braids of four matted hair. She was a lovely and elegant youthful maiden.

## \|\| 2.73.135 \|\|

*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ maṇinūpurāṃghriṃ prasannavaktrāṃ śukapadmahastām \|*  
*viśālanetrāṃ praṇamāmi gaurīṃ vacovidaṃ vācamudīrayantīm \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. I bow down to Gauri whose colour and lustre is that of gold, the anklets of whose feet are set with jewels, whose face is delighted, who has a parrot and a lotus in her hands and whose eyes are large. She is the person well conversant with words she speaks.

## \|\| 2.73.136 \|\|

*namāmi menātanayāmameyāmimāmumāṃ kāntimatīmameyām \|*  
*karoti yā bhūtisitau stanau dvau priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ pariṣasvajānā \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. I bow down to this Uma who is the daughter of Mena, who cannot be comprehended, who is full of splendour, who cannot be measured and who makes her breasts whitened by means of the Bhasman at the time of embracing her beloved lord.

## \|\| 2.73.137 \|\|

*kāntāmumāṃ kāntanibhāṅgakāntiṃ bhāntāmupāttānataharyajendrā m \|*  
*nato'smi yāste giriśasya pārśve viśvāni devī bhuvanāni caṣṭe \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. I bow down to Uma, who is resplendent, whose refulgence of limbs is magnet-like inaction and whom Hari, Brahma and Indra bow down to. She is the goddess who stays near Girina (Siva) and surveys the worlds.

## \|\| 2.73.138 \|\|

*vaṃde gaurīṃ tuṅgapīnastanīṃ tāṃ candrā cūḍāṃ kliṣṭasarvāṅgarāgām \|*  
*yaiṣā duḥkhiprāṇināmātmakāntiṃ devīṃ devīṃ rādhase codayantīm \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. I salute Gauri whose breasts are prominent and plump; whose crest jewel is the moon; whose unguent all over the body is disturbed and who, for the sake of miserable living beings, urges her own splendour to be propitiated for the accomplishment of their desires.

## \|\| 2.73.139 \|\|

*enāṃ vaṃde dīnarakṣāvinodāṃ menākanyāṃ mānadānandadātrīm \|*  
*yā vidyānāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca vācāmeṣā netrī rādhasaḥ sūnṛtānām \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. I salute this daughter of Mena whose pastime is the protection of the wretched ones; who bestows honour and bliss; who is master of the lores and the auspicious words and who makes use of affable and courteous words for propitiation.

## \|\| 2.73.140 \|\|

*saṃsāratāporubhayāpahantrī bhavāni bhojyābharaṇaikabhoge \|*  
*dhiyaṃ varāṃ dehi śive nirargalāṃ yayāti viśvā duritā tarema \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. О BhavanI, О goddess Siva who dispel the great fear of distress of worldly existence, whose sole pleasure is your ornaments (?), grant us an excellent intellect free from hindrances whereby we shall cross all evils.

## \|\| 2.73.141 \|\|

*śive kathaṃ tvatsamatā kva dīyate jagatkṛtiḥ kelirayaṃ śivaḥ patiḥ \|*  
*haristu dāso'nucarīndirā śacī sarasvatī vā subhagādadirvasu \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. О Siva, where and how can your equality be extended to? The creation of the universe is your sport; Siva is your husband. Hari is your servant; Indira (Laksmi) is your maid-servant. So also are Saci and Sarasvati. You are the fortunate (blessed) bestower of wealth.” Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.73.142 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- ityanena staveneśaṃ stutyetthaṃ sa mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*snehāśrupūrṇanayanaḥ praṇanāma sabhāpatim \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. After eulogising Siva thus with this hymn, that great sage, bowed down to Sabhapati (the lord of the assembly chamber). His eyes were filled with tears of affection.

## \|\| 2.73.143 \|\|

*muhurmuhuḥ pibannīśaṃ tāṇḍavāmṛtamaṅgalam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpyānte gāṇapatyamavāpa ha \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. He frequently imbibed the auspicious nectar of the Tan^ava of Isa. After attaining all cherished desires, he obtained the state of being the chieftain of the Siva Ganas at the end.

## \|\| 2.73.144 \|\|

*imaṃ stavaṃ jaimininā vacoditaṃ dvijottamo yaḥ paṭhatīha bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tamiṣṭavāksiddhimatidyutiśriyaḥ pariṣvajante janayo yathā patim \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Like the women who embrace their husbands, pleasing words, realisation of powers, intellect, splendour and prosperity embrace that excellent twice-born who devoutly reads this hymn orally expressed by Jaimini.

## \|\| 2.73.145 \|\|

*mahīpatiryastu yuyutsurādarādamuṃ paṭhatyasya tathaiva sādarāt \|*  
*prayānti śīghraṃ pramadāntakāntikaṃ bhiyaṃ dadhānā hṛdayeṣu śatravaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. If a king who is desirous of fighting, reads this hymn with respect, his enemies will quickly repair to the presence of the haughty god of death, entertaining fear in their hearts.

## \|\| 2.73.146 \|\|

*traivarṇikeṣvanyatamo ya enaṃ nityaṃ kadācitpaṭhatīśabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*kalevarānte śivapārśvavartī nirañjanaḥ sāmyamupaiti divyam \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. If a person belonging to one of the first three castes reads this eulogy ever and anon with devotional feelings towards Ha, at the end of the fall of his body (i.e. death), he remains at the sides of Siva. He becomes pure and attains divine equality.

## \|\| 2.73.147 \|\|

*labhante paṭhanto matiṃ buddhikāmā labhante tathaiva śriyaṃ puṣṭikāmāḥ \|*  
*labhante hi dhānyaṃ narā dhānyakāmā labhante ha putrānnarāḥ putrakāmāḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Those who are desirous of intellect and then read the hymn derive good intelligence. Similarly, those who are desirous of nourishment derive splendour and glory; mey who are desirous of food-grains obtain food-grains. Men who are desirous of sons get sons.

## \|\| 2.73.148 \|\|

*pādaṃ vāpyarddhapādaṃ vā ślokaṃ ślokārddhameva vā \|*  
*yastu dhārayate nityaṃ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. He who retains in memory a quatrain or half of it, from this hymn, goes to the world of Siva.

## \|\| 2.73.149 \|\|

*yatra nṛttaṃ śivaścakre tāṇḍavaṃ tatsthalaṃ śubhe \|*  
*puṇyātpuṇyataraṃ tīrthaṃ tatra snātvā vimucyate \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. О splendid lady, that spot is a great Tirtha where Siva performed his Tandava dance. It is more meritorious than the most meritorious of the Tlrthas. By taking a holy bath there, one is liberated.

## \|\| 2.73.150 \|\|

*yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ manujottama \|*  
*pūrvajānsa nayetsvargaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. The excellent man who performs Sraddha to the Pitrs there, leads his ancestors to the heaven. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 2.73.151 \|\|

*gāṃ suvarṇaṃ dharāṃ śayyāṃ vastramātapavāraṇam \|*  
*pānamannaṃ dvije dadyāttatra tatsarvamakṣayam \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. If he gives a Brahmana, a cow, gold, plot of land, bed, cloth, umbrella, beverages, or cooked rice at that place, it becomes everlasting.

## \|\| 2.73.152 \|\|

*etadākhyānakaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇḍarīka purodbhavam \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi so'pi rudra priyo bhavet \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. He who listens to, or narrates this story of Punda- rlkapura shall be the favourite of Rudra.

## Chapter 74. Thi Glory of Gokarna

## \|\| 2.74.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- puṇḍarīkapurākhyānaṃ tvayā proktaṃ śrutaṃ guro \|*  
*gokarṇasyādya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ me samādiśa \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О preceptor, the narrative of Pundarikapura recounted by you, has been heard. Kindly instruct me in the greatness of the holy centre Gokarna.1

## \|\| 2.74.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu mohini vakṣyāmi tīrthaṃ puṇyapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*gokarṇākhyaṃ harakṣetraṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vasu said:

2\. Listen, О MohinI, I shall recount to you the Tlrtha Gokarna, which is a holy centre of Нага; which yields merit unto men and which is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.74.3 \|\|

*paścimasthasamudra sya tīre'sti varavarṇini \|*  
*sārddhayojanavistāraṃ darśanādapi muktidam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О fair-complexioned lady, it is situated on the shores of the western sea. It extends to one and a half Yojanas. By its mere sight it yields salvation.

## \|\| 2.74.4 \|\|

*sagarasyātmajairdevi khanite bhūtale kramāt \|*  
*sāgaro varddhitastvārātplāvayāmāsa medinīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the surface of the earth was gradually dug up by the sons of Sagara, О gentle lady, the ocean increased in size and flooded the land nearby.

## \|\| 2.74.5-8 \|\|

*triṃśadyojanavistārāṃ satīrthakṣetrakānanām \|*  
*tatastannilayāḥ sarve sadevāsuramānavāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatsthānaṃ samparityajya sahyādigiriṣu sthitāḥ \|*  
*tato guhyaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ gokarṇākhyaṃ samudra gam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cintayanto munivarāstaduddhāre matiṃ dadhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sammantr! ya te sarve parvatopatyakāsthitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mahendrā calasaṃsthānaṃ parśurāmaṃ didṛkṣavaḥ \|*  
*jagmurmunivarā devi gokarṇoddhārakāṃkṣayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-6a. It flooded an area extending to thirty Yojanas (360 kms) inclusive of the holy centre, sacred water-reservoirs and forests. Then Devas, Asuras and human beings who had been staying there left that spot and occupied Sahya and other mountains.

6b-7a. As they pondered over the fact that the holy centre named Gokarna became hidden under the sea, the excellent sages made up their mind to reclaim it from the sea.

7b-8. All of them who had occupied the upper ridges of the mountain consulted together. Desirous of seeing Para- surama who had settled on the mountain Mahendra, О gentle lady, the excellent sages went there with the desire of reclaiming Gokarna.

## \|\| 2.74.9-10 \|\|

*samāruhya tu taṃ śailaṃ dadṛśustasya cāśramam \|*  
*praśāntakrūrasatvāḍhyaṃ sarvartuṣu sukhāvaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

*phalitaiḥ puṣpitairvṛkṣairgahanaṃ tattapovanam \|*  
*snigdhacchāyamanaupapyaṃ svāmodisukhamārutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. After climbing the mountain, they saw his hermitage that was pleasing in all the seasons; that was teeming with both wild ruthless animals as well as tame and domesticated ones. The whole penance-grove contained a dense growth of fruit-bearing trees in full bloom. It spread its cool shade; it was incomparable. The wind was very fragrant and pleasant.

## \|\| 2.74.11 \|\|

*taṃ tadāśramamāsādya brahmaghoṣanināditam \|*  
*viviśurthṛṣṭamanaso yathāvṛddhapuraḥsaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After reaching the penance-grove, they entered the hermitage that was resonant with Vedic chants. They were delighted in their minds, and they went in (in the order of their seniority in age) with the aged ones going ahead. submerged in the sea-water and how sages went in deputation to Parasurama who ordered the sea-god to vacate this part of the land around Gokarna lest he should be constrained to evaporate the sea by his missiles. The seagod yielded. The story is similar to that of Dasarathi Rama at the time of building Sttu to Lanka.

## \|\| 2.74.12 \|\|

*brahmāsane sukhāsīnaṃ mṛdukṛṣṇājinottare \|*  
*śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ śāntaṃ dadṛśustaṃ tapodhanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They saw that ascetic comfortably seated in the pasture on Brahmasana over a soft deer-skin and surrounded by disciples.

## \|\| 2.74.13 \|\|

*kālāgnimiva lokāṃstrīndagdhvā śāntaṃ tapaḥ sthitam \|*  
*te sametya bhṛguśreṣṭhaṃ vinayena vavandire \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They approached the sage how was the most excellent one among the descendants of Bhrigu; who was like.the resplendent fire of world destruction that had become tranquil after burning the three worlds, and they saluted him humbly.

## \|\| 2.74.14 \|\|

*tatastānāgatāndṛṣṭvā munīnbhṛgukulodvahaḥ \|*  
*arghyapādyādibhiḥ samyakpūjayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing those sages come, the leading scion of the family of Bhrigu, properly (with due formalities) and respectfully greeted them with Arghya, Padya etc.

## \|\| 2.74.15-16 \|\|

*tānāsīnānkṛtātithyānuvāca bhṛgunandanaḥ \|*  
*svāgataṃ vo mahābhāgā yadarthamiha cāgatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadvadadhvaṃ suviśvastāḥ karaṇīyaṃ mayāsti yat \|*  
*tato'bruvanmuniśreṣṭhā yadarthaṃ rāmamāgatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. When they were seated after the hospitality had been duly extended, the descendant of Bhrigu (Parasurama) said: — “O blessed ones, welcome to you. Tell me wherefore you have come here? Confide in me. What is it that I can do for you?” Then the excellent sages told Rama why they had come.

## \|\| 2.74.17 \|\|

*avehyasmān bhṛguśreṣṭha gokarṇanilayānmunīn \|*  
*khanadbhiḥ sāgarairbhūmiṃ tasmāttīrthādvivāsitān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “O excellent descendant of Bhrigu, know us to be the sages residing in Gokarna. We have been dislodged from that holy centre by the sons of Sagara who were digging the earth.

## \|\| 2.74.18 \|\|

*sa tvamātmaprabhāveṇa kṣetrapravaramadya naḥ \|*  
*dātumarhasi viprendra samutsāryārṇavodakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О leading Brahmana, it behoves you to grant us back the excellent holy place (called Gokarna) by means of your own power, after causing the waters of the ocean to recede”.

## \|\| 2.74.19-21 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ nyastaśastro vyacintayat \|*  
*tato vicintya bhagavāndharmyaṃ sādhvabhirakṣaṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pragṛhya svadhanurbāṇānsampratasthe sa taiḥ samam \|*  
*so'varuhya mahendrā dre rdiśaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*samuddiśya yayau śīghraṃ sa svamullaṅghya parvatam \|*  
*samprāptaḥ sāgarataṭaṃ sārddhaṃ gokarṇāvāsibhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-20a. On hearing their words, the sage who had already set aside his weapons, thought over the problem. He considered that the protection of good men was righteous on his part and so took up his bow and arrows. He set off along with them.

20b-21. Descending from the mountain Mahendra, he hastened in the direction of the South-West. Quickly crossing the mountain, he reached the sea-shore along with the residents of Gokarna.

## \|\| 2.74.22 \|\|

*muhūrttaṃ tatra viśramya varuṇaṃ yādasāṃ patim \|*  
*meghagabhīrayā vācā provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After resting there for a short while, the most eloquent sage spoke to Varuna, the lord of aquatic animals, in a voice as resonant as thunder.

## \|\| 2.74.23 \|\|

*rāmo'ha bhārgavaḥ prāpto munibhiḥ saha kāryavān \|*  
*praceto darśanaṃ dehi kāryamātyāyikaṃ tvayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O Pracetas (Varuna) reveal yourself to me. I am Rama, the descendant of Bhrigu. I have come here along with the sages on a certain mission. There is an urgent task to be performed by you”.

## \|\| 2.74.24 \|\|

*evaṃ rāmasamāhūto yādaḥpatirahantayā \|*  
*śrutvāpi tasya tadvākyaṃ nāyāto rāmasannidhau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Although the lord of the aquatic animals was thus called by Rama, and although he heard his words clearly, Varuna, the lord of aquatic animals, out of haughtiness, did not come to Rama.

## \|\| 2.74.25 \|\|

*evaṃ punaḥ punastena samāhūto'pi nāgataḥ \|*  
*yadā tadābhisaṃkruddho dhanurjagrāha bhārgavaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When he did not come out even after being repeatedly invoked, Bhargava (Parasurama) became infuriated and seized his bow.

## \|\| 2.74.26 \|\|

*tasminsandhāya viśikhaṃ vahnidevaṃ tu bhārgavam \|*  
*astraṃ saṃyojayāmāsa śoṣaṇāya saritpateḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Bhargava fixed to that bow, an arrow, the deity of which was the firegod, for drying up the lord of the rivers, the ocean.

## \|\| 2.74.27 \|\|

*tasminsaṃyojite'stre tu bhārgaveṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*saṃkṣubdhaḥ sāgaro bhadre yādogaṇasamākulaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When the miraculous missile was fitted on to the bow by Bhargava of great soul, О gentle lady, the ocean became agitated. The aquatic animals were in a confused state.

## \|\| 2.74.28 \|\|

*varuṇo'strābhisantapto rāmasya bhayasamplutaḥ \|*  
*svarūpeṇa samāgatya rāmapādau samagrahīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Scorched by the missile of Rama, Varuna became exceedingly frightened. Approaching him in his own personal form Varuna grasped Rama’s feet in reverence.

## \|\| 2.74.29 \|\|

*tato'stra sa vinirvartya varuṇaṃ prāha satvaram \|*  
*gokarṇo dṛśyatāṃ deva utsarpaya jalaṃ kila \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then Rama withdrew his missile and immediately spoke to Varuna, “O lord, let Gokarna be visible, cause your water to recede”.

## \|\| 2.74.30-35 \|\|

*tato rāmājñayā so'pi gokarṇodakamāharat \|*  
*rāmo'pi taṃ samabhyarcya gokarṇaṃ nāma śaṅkaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*prāptaḥ punarmahendrā drau tasthustatraiva te dvijāḥ \|*  
*yatra sarve tapastaptvā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ prāptāḥ punarāvṛttivarjitam \|*  
*tatkṣetrasya prabhāveṇa prītyā bhūtagaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*devyā ca sakalairdevairnityaṃ vasati śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*enāṃsi darśanāttasya gokarṇasya maheśituḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sadyo viyujya gacchanti pravāte śuṣkaparṇavat \|*  
*tatkṣetrasevanaratirnṛṇāṃ jātu na jāyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nirbandhena tu ye tatra prāṇinaḥ sthirajaṅgamāḥ \|*  
*mriyante devi sadyaste svargaṃ yānti sanātanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

30-3la. Then at the behest of Rama, the ocean withdrew the water flooding Gokarna. After worshipping lord Sankara at the holy place called Gokarna, Rama went back to the mountain Mahendra. Those Brahmanas however stayed there itself.

31b-32a. All of those sages observed holy rites, performed penance and attained great bliss. They attained a state from which there was no return, thanks to his love for that holy centre.

32b-33a. Being conscious of its greatness Sankara perpetually stays there with Bhutas(goblins), Devas and goddess Parvati. By visiting Mahesa (Siva) at Gokarna, sins are dispelled immediately like a dry leaf in a storm.

33b-35. It is not out of compulsion that men become interested in resorting to that holy centre. All living beings mobile and immobile, that die there, immediately go to the eternal heaven.

## \|\| 2.74.36 \|\|

*smṛtyāpi sakalaiḥ pāpairyasya mucyeta mānavaḥ \|*  
*tadgokarṇābhidhaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvatīrthaniketanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The holy place named Gokarna by mere remembrance of which a man will become absolved of all sins, is the abode of all Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.74.37 \|\|

*snātvā kṣetreṣu sarveṣu yajantaśca sadāśivam \|*  
*labhante yatphalaṃ martyāstatsarvaṃ tatra darśanāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Through the vision of the deity, these men derive those benefits which they derive by taking holy bath щ all other sacred places and by worshipping SadaSiva.

## \|\| 2.74.38 \|\|

*kāmakrodhādibhirhīnā ye tatra nivasanti vai \|*  
*acireṇaiva kālena te siddhiṃ prāpnuvanti hi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who stay there free from lust, fury etc. attain Siddhi in a short time.

## \|\| 2.74.39 \|\|

*japahomaratāḥ śāntā niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*vasanti tasminye te hi siddhiṃ prāpsyantyabhīpsitām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Those who stay there wedded to the vow of celibacy, quiescent and invariably engaged in Japas and Homas accomplish their desired Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.74.40 \|\|

*dānahomajapādyaṃ ca pitṛdevadvijārcanam \|*  
*anyasmātkoṭiguṇitaṃ bhavettasminphalaṃ sati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О chaste lady, the benefit accruing from charitable gifts, Homas, Japas etc and the worship of Pitrs, Devas and Brahmanas at that place is a crorc times more than that in other centres.

## \|\| 2.74.41 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ bhadre gokarṇakṣetrasambhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāmapi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus, О gentle lady, the greatness of the sacred place called Gokarna has been recounted to you. It dispels all sins of those who listen to and read it.

## Chapter 75. The Greatness of Laksmandcala

## \|\| 2.75.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ gokarṇamāhātmyaṃ vaso pāpavināśanam \|*  
*lakṣmaṇasyāpi māhātmyaṃ vaktumarhasi sāmpratam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О Vasu, the greatness of Gokarna that is destructive of sins has been heard. Now it behoves you to recount the greatness of Laksmana also.

## \|\| 2.75.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi māhātmyaṃ lakṣmaṇasya ca \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā manujo devaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vasu said:

2\. О gentle lady, listen. I shall describe the greatness of Laksmana. On seeing the deity there, a man is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.75.3-5 \|\|

*caturvyūhāvatāre yo devaḥ sakarṣaṇaḥ svayay \|*  
*sarvabhūmaṇḍalaṃ hyetatsahasravadanaḥ svarāṭ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ekasmiñchirasi nyastaṃ nāvaitsiddhārthakopamam \|*  
*devo nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣādrā mo brahmādivanditaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pradyumno bharato bhadre śatrughno hyaniruddhakaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmaṇastu mahābhāge svayaṃ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. (The Caturvyuha concept is applied to Rama here). The god (Laksmana) is Sankarsana himself out of the incarnation of the four Vyuhas (manifestations of Lord Visnu or Vasudeva.) He is the thousand-hooded serpent Sesa.

## \|\| 2.75.6 \|\|

*brahmādyaiḥ prārthitaḥ pūrvaṃ sākṣāddevo ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*rāmādināmabhirjajñe caturddhā diggrathānnṛpāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On being requested by Brahma and others formerly, lord Ramapati (Lord of Laksmi, Visnu) was born of king Dasaratha in four forms with the names of Rama etc.

## \|\| 2.75.7 \|\|

*tataḥ kālāntare devi viśvāmitro munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*yajñarakṣārthamāgatya prārthayadrā malakṣmaṇau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After some time, О gentle lady, the leading sage Visvamitra approached the king and requested him for Rama and Laksmana for guarding his Yajna.

## \|\| 2.75.8 \|\|

*tato rājā daśarathaḥ prāṇebhyo'pi priyau sutau \|*  
*muneḥ śāpabhayādbhīto dadau tau rāmalakṣmaṇau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Afraid of the curse of the sage, king Dasaratha entrusted to him his sons Rama and Laksmana who were loved by him more than his own life.

## \|\| 2.75.9-11 \|\|

*gatvā yajñaṃ munīndra sya gādhipasya rarakṣatuḥ \|*  
*satāḍakaṃ subāhuṃ tu hatvā prakṣipya dūrataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mārīcaṃ mānavāstreṇa viśvāmitramatoṣayat \|*  
*tataḥ prītānmuniśreṣṭhādastragrāmamavāpya ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*uvāca sa kiyatkālaṃ sānujastena satkṛtaḥ \|*  
*vaidehanagaraṃ nīto viśvāmitreṇa tatparam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-10a. They went to the forest and guarded the Yajna of Visvamitra, the leading sage. Rama killed Subahu and Tadaka. With the arrow charged with the missile called Manavastra, he cast off Marlca far into the ocean. Thus he pleased Visvamitra.

10b-ll. From the excellent sage who was delighted, he acquired a group of miraculous missiles. For sometime, he stayed there with his younger brother duly honoured by the sage. Thereafter, he was taken to the city of Janaka by Visvamitra.

## \|\| 2.75.12 \|\|

*tatastu rājā janako viśvāmitraṃ susatkṛtam \|*  
*papraccha bālakāvetau kasya kṣatrakuleśituḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then king Janaka asked Visvamitra who had been duly received and honoured. “Of what great Ksatriya king’s sons are these boys?

## \|\| 2.75.13 \|\|

*tatastasmai munivaro rājño daśarathasya tau \|*  
*putrau nivedayāmāsa bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then the excellent sage told him that they were two brothers Rama and Laksmana and that they were the sons of king Dasaratha. gave up his mortal coil. The NP. states that after Rama’s order, Lakshmana went to the south and performed penance on a certain hill and gave up his body by a Yogic process after Rama’s departure to heaven. The information about Lakshmanacala is too scanty to locate it geographically.

## \|\| 2.75.14 \|\|

*tato videhaḥ saprīto dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇam \|*  
*sītormilākhyayoḥ putr! yoścetasākalpayatpatī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing Rama and Laksmana the king of Videha Janaka, became much delighted. In his mind he decided that they should become the husbands of his daughters Sita and Urmila.

## \|\| 2.75.15-26 \|\|

*trikālajñastu sa munirjñātvā tasya manogatam \|*  
*modamāno'tha janakaṃ prāha darśaya taddhanuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sītāsvayaṃvare nyastaṃ nyāsabhūtaṃ maheśituḥ \|*  
*rājā śrutvā tu tadvākyaṃ viśvāmitrasya satvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhṛtyatriśatyānāyyāsmai darśayāmāsa sādaram \|*  
*rāmaścaṇḍīśacāpaṃ tadvāmadoṣṇoddharan kṣaṇāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sajyaṃ vikṛṣya sahasā babhañjekṣumivebharāṭ \|*  
*tato'ti mithilaḥ prītaḥ sve kanye rāmalakṣmaṇau \|\| 18 \|\|*

*samabhyarcyārpayāmāsa tābhyāṃ te vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*jñātvā munivarādanyau rājño daśarathasya tu \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ saha tamāhūya bhrātṛkanye adāpayat \|*  
*tataḥ sa kṛtadāraistu caturbhistanayaiḥ saha \|\| 20 \|\|*

*samarcito videhenāyodhyāṃ munyājñayā yayau \|*  
*mārge bhṛgupaterdarpaṃ śamayitvā sa rāghavaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pitṛbhrātṛyutaḥ śrīmānmumude bahuvatsarān \|*  
*paṇḍitaistu vasiṣṭhādyairbodhito'sau nijaṃ mahaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*brahmākhyaṃ bubudhe rāmo mānuṣatvaṃ viḍambayan \|*  
*tato daśaratho rājā jñātajñeyaṃ nijaṃ sutam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rāmaṃ samudyato hṛṣṭo yauvarājye'bhiṣecitum \|*  
*yajjñātvā kaikayī devī rājñaḥ preṣṭhā kanīyasī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sannivārya haṭhāttasya putrasya tadarocata \|*  
*tato rāmo mude tasyāḥ pitrānanumato yayau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sabhāryaḥ saḥ sasaumitriścitrakūṭaṃ giriṃ śubhe \|*  
*kiyatkālamuvāsāsau tatraiva muniveṣadhṛk \|\| 26 \|\|*

15-16a. The sage who was aware of the three unitsof time understood his desire. He joyfully told Janaka, “show him that bow which had been a deposit of Maheshvara and has been placed in the Svayamvara (self-choice of a husband by the girl) of Sita.

16b-17a. On hearing the words of Vi svamitra, the king got that bow brought immediately through three hundred of his servants. He showed it to Rama with great enthusiasm.

17b-18a. With his left hand, Rama lifted that bow of Siva instantaneously. He tied the string, stretched it and broke it suddenly like a lordly elephant breaking a sugarcane stem.

18b-19a. Then the king of Mithila (Janaka) was highly pleased. He duly honoured Rama and Laksmana and offered his two daughters to them in accordance with the Sastric injunction.

19b-20a. From the leading sage Vi svamitra he understood that king Dasaratha had two more sons. He invited Dasaratha along with those two sons and gave in marriage his brother’s daughters to them.

20b-22a. He was duly honoured by Videha. At the behest of the sage, king Dasaratha went back to Ayodhya along with all the four sons who had been duly married. On the way, Rama suppressed the haughtiness of Parasurama. Along with his brothers and father, he spent many years at Ayodhya joyously.

22b-23a. He had his own splendour explained to him by Vasisthaand other scholars. Rama understood his own splendour called Brahman, but he pretended to be a human being.

23b-25a. Then king Dasaratha became delighted on observing that his son had learnt everything that should be learnt. He, therefore, made preparations for crowning him as the Heir-Apparent. Kaikeyi, the youngest but the most beloved of all his queens, came to know of this. With stubbornness, she prevented it and wanted her own son to be crowned thus.

25b-26. To please her, Rama went to the forest though not permitted by his father. Accompanied by his wife Sita and Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, he went to Citrakiita hill, О splendid lady. For some time he remained there alone, assuming the dress and features of sages.

## \|\| 2.75.27-31 \|\|

*mātāmahagṛhāttacca śrutvā'yātaḥ piturvadham \|*  
*sa vijñāya mṛtaṃ tātaṃ hā rāmeti virāviṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dhikkṛtya kaikayīṃ yāto rāmaṃ sa vinivartitum \|*  
*tataḥ svapāduke datvā bharataṃ vinivartya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*rāmo'treścāpyagastyasya sutīkṣṇasyāśrameṣvagāt \|*  
*teṣu dvādaśa varṣāṇi gamayitvā raghūdvahaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhāryānujānvitaḥ śrīmāṃstataḥ pañcavaṭīmagāt \|*  
*tatrāvasajjanasthāne triśiraḥkharadūṣaṇān \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śūrpaṇakhyā vikṛtayā preritānsa vyanāśayat \|*  
*tato rakṣaḥsahasraiśca caturddaśabhirāgatān \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-28a. On hearing of the death of his father, Bharata returned from his maternal uncle’s house. On knowing that his father had died crying ‘‘Ha Rama”, Bharata rebuked Kaikeyi and went to Rama to persuade him to return.

28b-31. Rama gave his sandals and made Bharata return. He then went to the hermitages of Atri, Agastya and Sutlksna, Thus he spent twelve years in those places. The prosperous scion of the family of Raghu (i.e. Rama) went to Paftcavati accompanied by his wife and younger brother. He stayed in the place called Janasthana. He slew Trisiras, Khara and Diisana who had been incited by Surpanakha who was rendered ugly by Laksmana. Then fourteen thousand Raksasas came there. With the iron arrows, having feathers of variegated colours, he (Rama) led them to Yama’s abode.

## \|\| 2.75.32-33 \|\|

*vicitravājairnārācairyamakṣayamanīnayat \|*  
*yacchrutvā rakṣasāṃ rājā mārīcaṃ kāñcanaṃ mṛgam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*darśayitvāpavāhyaitau sītāṃ hṛtvā jaṭāyuṣam \|*  
*rundhānaṃ mārgamāhatya laṅkāyāṃ samupānayat \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. On hearing about this, the king of Raksasas (i.e. Ravana) caused them to go away (from the hut) by showing Marica who had assumed the form of a golden deer, and abducted Sita. He killed Jatayus who had obstructed him on the way. He then took Sita to Lanka.

## \|\| 2.75.34-37 \|\|

*āgatya tau hṛtāṃ sītāṃ mārgamāṇau samantataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā jaṭāyuṣaṃ śāntaṃ dagdhvā hatvā kabandhakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śabarīmanukampyātha ṛṣyamūkamupāgatau \|*  
*tatastu hanumadvākyātsvasakhyuḥ plavageśituḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vidviṣaṃ vālinaṃ hatvā sugrīvamakaronnṛpam \|*  
*tadājñaptāstu te kīśāḥ sarvataḥ samupāgatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*hanumatpramukhāḥ sītāṃ mārganto dakṣiṇodadhim \|*  
*prāpya sampātivacanāllaṅkāyāṃ niścayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-35a. The brothers returned and began to search for Sita who had been abducted. They saw Jatayu and cremated him when he died. Rama then killed Kabandha, blessed Sabari and came to Rsyamuka.

35b-36a. At the instance of Hanuman, he became the friend of Sugriva, the king of Monkeys. He then killed Valin his enemy and made Sugriva the king.

36b-37. On being ordered by Sugriva, the monkeys who had come from all places and whose leader was Hunuman, searched for Sita. They then reached the southern ocean. From the words of Sampati they came to the conclusion that she (Sita) was in Lanka.

## \|\| 2.75.38 \|\|

*tatastu hanumānekaḥ prāpya laṅkāṃ purīṃ kapiḥ \|*  
*samudra sya pare pāre'paśyadrā mapriyāṃ satīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then the monkey Hanuman alone reached Lanka, on the other shore of the ocean. There he saw the chaste lady, Xhe wife of Rama.

## \|\| 2.75.39-40 \|\|

*dattvā rāmāṅgulīratnaṃ viśvāsamupapādya tām \|*  
*tayoḥ kuśalamāśrāvya labdhvā cūḍāmaṇiṃ tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*bhaṅktvā cāśokavanikāṃ hatvā cākṣaṃ sasainyakam \|*  
*indra jidbandhanātprāpya sambhāṣyāpi ca rāvaṇam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. He created confidence in her by giving her the jewelled ring of Rama. He told her that both of them were hale and hearty. From her he took the crest-jewel. He then destroyed the trees in the Asoka grove, and killed Aksa (the prinqp) along with his army. He voluntarily submitted to captivity at the hands of Indrajit and so could talk to Ravana.

## \|\| 2.75.41 \|\|

*dagdhvā laṅkāṃ purīṃ kṛtsnāṃ punardṛṣṭvā tu maithilīm \|*  
*labdhājño'ṇavamullaṅghya rāmāyaināṃ nyavedayat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He then burned the entire city of Lafika and met Sita once again. After taking her permission, he crossed the ocean and told Rama about her.

## \|\| 2.75.42 \|\|

*śrutvā rāmo'pi tāṃ sītāṃ rākṣasasya nivāsagām \|*  
*sārddhaṃ sa kapisainyena samprāpto makarālayam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing that Sita was in the abode of the demon, he came to the ocean along with an army of monkeys.

## \|\| 2.75.43 \|\|

*sāgarānumatenāsau setuṃ baddhvā mahodadhau \|*  
*adri kūṭeḥ paraṃ tīraṃ prāpya senāṃ nyaveśayat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. With the permission of the ocean, he caused the bridge to be made over the great sea by means of huge boulders from the peaks of mountains and reached the other shore. He encamped his army there.

## \|\| 2.75.44 \|\|

*tato'sau rāvaṇo bhrātrā bodhito'pi kanīyasā \|*  
*pradānaṃ tatra maithilyāstadbhartre na tvarocayat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Although his younger brother Vibhisana advised Ravana to return Sita to her husband, he did not like it.

## \|\| 2.75.45 \|\|

*padā hatastatastena rāvaṇena vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*samprāptaḥ śaraṇaṃ rāmaṃ rāmo laṅkāmupāruṇat \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Kicked by Ravana, Viblnsana sought refuge in Rama and Rama laid siege to Lanka.

## \|\| 2.75.46 \|\|

*tatastu mantriṇo'mātyāḥ putrā bhṛtyāḥ pracoditāḥ \|*  
*yuddhāya te kṣayaṃ nītāstābhyāṃ saṃkhye kapīśvaraiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereafter, his counsellors, ministers, sons and servants were ordered by him to fight. In the battle with those two, they were all destroyed by the leading monkeys.

## \|\| 2.75.47 \|\|

*lakṣmaṇaḥ śakrajetāraṃ jaghnivānniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*rāmo'pi kumbhaśravaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ cāpyajīghanat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Laksmana killed Indrajit by means of sharp arrows. Rama killed Kumbhakarna and Ravana.

## \|\| 2.75.48-49 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇena tatkṛtyaṃ kārayitvā nijāṃ priyām \|*  
*vahnau saṃśodhya datvāsmai rāmo rakṣogaṇeśatām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*laṅkāmāyuśca kalpāntaṃ yayau cīrṇavrataḥ purīm \|*  
*puṣpakeṇa vimānena sasugrīvavibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. He made Vibhisana perform the obsequies of Ravana. He asked his beloved to enter fire and purify herself. Rama then gave Vibhisana the lordship of the Raksasas, the city of Lanka and life till the end of the Kalpa. Having thus completed his holy vow of spending fourteen years in the forest, Rama returned to Ayodhya by the aerial chariot Puspaka along with Sugriva and Vibhisana.

## \|\| 2.75.50-51 \|\|

*nandigrāmasthabharataṃ nītvāyodhyāṃ samāviśat \|*  
*mātṝḥ praṇamya tāḥ sarvā bhrātaraste purodhasā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhenānuvijñāpya rāmaṃ rājye'bhyaṣecayan \|*  
*tato rāmo'pi bhagavānprajāḥ śāsannivaurasān \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Taking Bharata who was staying in Nandi-Grama, he entered the city of Ayodhya. He then bowed to all mothers. The other brothers made the priest Vasistha crown Rama in the kingdom Lord Rama ruled over the subjects as though they were his own bosom-born sons.

## \|\| 2.75.52 \|\|

*lokāpavādātsantrastaḥ sītāṃ tatyāja dharmavit \|*  
*sā tu samprāpya vālmīkerāśramaṃ nyavasatsukham \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The knower of virtue (Dharma) as he was, he was frightened due to the rumour current among the people and so he abandoned Sita. Sita reached the hermitage of Valmlki and lived there comfortably.

## \|\| 2.75.53-54 \|\|

*putrau ca suṣuve tatra nāmnā khyātau kuśīlavau \|*  
*vālmīkistu tayoḥ kṛtvā yathā samuditāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rāmāyaṇaṃ viracyaitāvadhyāpayadudāradhīḥ \|*  
*tau gāyamānau satreṣu munīnāṃ khyātimāgatau \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. She gave birth to two sons well-known by the name of Kusa and Lava. They were good singers. After performing the requisite holy rites for them, Valmlki the liberal- minded sage, composed Ramayana and taught it to them. The two brothers used to sing this in the Yajnas and assemblies of the sages and so they became famous.

## \|\| 2.75.55-58 \|\|

*yajñe rāmasya samprāptau vājimedhe pravartite \|*  
*tatra tābhyāṃ tu tadgītaṃ svacaritraṃ prasannadhīḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*munimākārayāmāsa sasītaṃ tatra saṃsadi \|*  
*sā tu rāmāya tau putrau nivedya jagatījaniḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jagatyā vivaraṃ bhūyo viveśāsīttadadbhutam \|*  
*tataḥ paraṃ brahmacaryaṃ yajñameva trayodaśa \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sahasrābdānprakuvārṇastasthau bhuvi raghūttamaḥ \|*  
*tatastu kāle durvāsāḥ samprāpto rāghavaṃ prati \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-57a. When Rama performed a horse-sacrifice, they came to that assembly and sang the poem. Delighted to hear his own story sung, Rama invited the sage along with Sita. Sita, the mother of the universe, informed Rama that they were his sons. She entered a crevice in the ground. It was a great miracle.

57b-58a. Thereafter, Rama observed the vow of celibacy and performed Yajnas and other rites. For thirteen thousand years, the most excellent among theRaghus stayed on the earth.

58b. Then after some time Durvasa came there, on being sent by Brahma for going back to Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 2.75.59-60 \|\|

*brahmaṇā preṣito bhadre vaikuṇṭhagamanāya ca \|*  
*sa ekāntagato rāmaṃ prāha ko'pīha nā'vrajet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*āgato vadhyatāṃ yātu rāmastatpratijajñivān \|*  
*sa lakṣmaṇaṃ samāhūya provāca raghunandanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. О gentle lady, in an isolated place he told Rama ‘‘Let no one come here. If anyone comes, let him be worthy of being killed”. Rama promised it.

## \|\| 2.75.61 \|\|

*dvāri tiṣṭhātra nirviṣṭo vadhyatāṃ me prayāsyati \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya rāmasyājñāṃ samācaran \|\| 61 \|\|*

61 Rama called Laksmana and said: — “Stand here at the threshold. He who comes in will be worthy of being killed”. He said, “So be it” and began to carry out Rama’s behest. He did not allow anyone to go near Rama.

## \|\| 2.75.62-65 \|\|

*praveśanaṃ na kasyāpi pradadau rāmasannidhau \|*  
*evamekāntagaṃ rāmaṃ kālasaṃvidamāsthitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*jñātvātha dvāri durvāsā lakṣmaṇaṃ samupāgamat \|*  
*tamāgataṃ tu saṃprekṣya saumitriḥ praṇipatya ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

*muhūrtaṃ pālayetyāha mantravyagro'sti rāghavaḥ \|*  
*durvāsāstadvacaḥ śrutvā kālasyārthavidhāyakaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kruddhaḥ provāca saumitriṃ dehi me'ntapraveśanam \|*  
*no cettvāṃ bhasmasātsadyaḥ kariṣyāmi vicāraya \|\| 65 \|\|*

62-64a. While Rama was sitting alone with Kala and discussing, Durvasa who came to know it approached Laksmana. On seeing him come Laksmana told him after due prostrations — “Kindly wait for a while. Rama is busy in the council chamber.”

64b-65. On hearing these words, Durvasas who wanted to carry out the purpose ofYama(godof death) said to Laksmana angrily — “Allow me to enter; otherwise I will reduce you to ashes. Remember it”.

## \|\| 2.75.66 \|\|

*vaco durvāsasaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇo jātasambhramaḥ \|*  
*munerbhīto viveśāntarvijñāpayitumagrajam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On hearing the words of Durvasas, Laksmana became perplexed. Afraid of the sage, he entered within to inform his elder brother.

## \|\| 2.75.67 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tu lakṣmaṇaṃ kāla utthāya kṛtamantrakaḥ \|*  
*pratijñāṃ pālayetyuktvā yayau rāmavisarjjitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On seeing Laksmana, Kala who had already completed his discussion stood up and said: — “Keep your promise” He was bidden farewell to by Rama and went away.

## \|\| 2.75.68 \|\|

*tato niṣkramya bhagavān rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*pratoṣya taṃ muniṃ prīto durvāsasamabhojayat \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then Lord Rama, the most excellent among the righteous ones, came out and propitiated the sage Durvasa and fed him.

## \|\| 2.75.69-70 \|\|

*bhojayitvā praṇamyainaṃ visṛjya prāha lakṣmaṇam \|*  
*bhrātarlakṣmaṇa samprāptaṃ saṅkaṭaṃ dharmakāraṇāt \|\| 69 \|\|*

*yattvaṃ me vadhyatāṃ prāpto daivaṃ hi balavattaram \|*  
*mayā tyaktastato vīra yathecchaṃ gaccha sāmpratam \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. After feeding him and bidding him farewell after due obeisance, Rama said to Laksmana — ” Brother, Laksmana, a delicate situation has arisen due to Dharma. As a result of it, you have become worthy of being killed by me. Fate indeed is more powerful. Abandoned by me, now you can go wherever you please.”

## \|\| 2.75.71 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ rāmaṃ satyadharme vyavasthitam \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritya tapaścakre nagopari \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Laksmana bowed down to Rama who adhered to Truth and Virtue. He went towards the south and performed a penance on the mountain.

## \|\| 2.75.72 \|\|

*tato rāmo'pi bhagavānbrahmaprārthanayā punaḥ \|*  
*svadhāmāviśadavyagraḥ sasāketaḥ sakośalaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Lord Rama too, at the request to Brahma, re-entered his abode without excitement. The people of Ayodhya and Kosala accompanied him.

## \|\| 2.75.73 \|\|

*gopratāre sarayvāṃ ye rāmaṃ sañcintya samplutāḥ \|*  
*te rāmadhāma viviśurdivyāṅgā yogidurlabham \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who thought of Rama and plunged themselves in Gopratara in the Sarayu entered Rama’s splendid abode that is rare even to the Yogins. They attained divine bodies.

## \|\| 2.75.74 \|\|

*lakṣmaṇastu kiyatkālaṃ tapoyogabalānvitaḥ \|*  
*rāmānugamanenaiva svadhāmāviśadavyayam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. After performing penance and observing Yogic practices, Laksmana followed Rama by his Yogic power. He then re-entered his unchanging abode.

## \|\| 2.75.75 \|\|

*sānnidhyaṃ parvate tasmindattvā saumitriranvaham \|*  
*cakraṃ nijādhikāraṃ sa tatastatkṣetramuttamam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Laksmana granted that mountain his perpetual prese- ence and then continued his regular duty. Hence, this holy centre is excellent.

## \|\| 2.75.76 \|\|

*ye paśyanti narā bhaktyā lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇācale \|*  
*te kṛtārthā na sandeho gacchanti harimandiram \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Those who see Laksmana on the Laksmana mountain with great devotion, are blessed and contented. There is no doubt about this that they go to the abode of Hari.

## \|\| 2.75.77 \|\|

*tatra dānaṃ praśaṃsanti svarṇagobhūmivājinām \|*  
*dattaṃ tatrākṣayaṃ sarvaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. They praise charitable gifts in the place, of gold, plots of land, cows and horses. Whatever is given becomes everlasting in its benefit. The homa and the Japa too derive great benefits.

## \|\| 2.75.78 \|\|

*bahunā kimihoktena darśanaṃ tasya durlabham \|*  
*agastyājñāntarā devi dṛṣṭe muktirna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Of what avail is much talk? Its mere sight is of rare occurrence. О gentle lady, if it is seen, there is salvation undoubtedly.

## \|\| 2.75.79 \|\|

*etadrā macaritraṃ tu lakṣmaṇākhyānaṃsayutam \|*  
*śrāvayedyo'pi śṛṇuyātsyātāṃ tau rāmavallabhau \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Both he who listens to this story of Rama along with the anecdote of Laksmana and he who tells this story become great favourites of Rama.

## Chapter 76. The Greatness of Setu

## \|\| 2.76.2-5 \|\|

*adhunā śrotumicchāmi setumāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi setumāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā manujo devi mucyate bhavasāgarāt \|*  
*setoḥ sandarśanaṃ puṇyaṃ yatra rāmeśvaro vibhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*darśanādeva martyānāmamaratvaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*rāmeśvaraṃ tu sampūjya naro niyatamānasaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarvāḥ samaśnute bhūtīrnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*cakratīrthamihānyacca vartate pāpanāśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Mohini said:

l-2a. О excellent Brahmana, well done. It is very nice, that the Ramayana has been narrated by you. It is destructive of all sins of men and conducive to the increase of merits. Now I wish to hear the excellent greatness of Setu.1 Vasu said:

2b-3a. О gentle lady, listen, I shall recount to you the excellent greatness of Setu on seeing which, О queen, one is liberated from the ocean of worldly existence.

3b-5. The very sight of the Setu is meritorious. Lord Ramesvara there grants immortality to men by its vision only. By worshipping Ramesvara with fully controlled mind, a man enjoys all prosperities and glories. No doubt need be entertained in this respect. There is another holy centre here Viz.: Cakratirtha. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.76.6-9 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homastatrānantyaṃ vigāhate \|*  
*tālatīrthaṃ tu samprāpya yaḥ snāyāttatra mānavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sa uttamāṃ janiṃ labdhvā modate devavadbhuvi \|*  
*tataḥ samprāpya subhage tīrthaṃ pāpavināśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*snātvā nirdhūtapāpo'sau naraḥ svarge mahīyate \|*  
*sītākuṇḍe tataḥ prāpya snānaṃ samyagvidhāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tarpayitvā pitṝndevānsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*maṅgalaṃ tīrthamāsādya snātvā mucyeta pātakān \|\| 9 \|\|*

6a. The holy bath, charitable gifts, Japa and Ноmа there, facilitate everlasting benefits. The line of rocks jutting out of the sea between Ramesvara ashri Lanka is supposed to be the relic of the bridge that was built by Rama with the help of monkeys. It is regarded holy even in the Bh. P. (VIII. 14.31,X.79.15) Parasara (XII.65-67) recommends a visit to Setu as atonement for Brahmahatya.

6b-7a. He who goes to Talatirtha and takes his holy dip there, attains excellent birth and rejoices on the earth like a Deva.

7b-8a. Then, О blessed lady, after reaching the holy centre Papavinasana (a Tirtha Destructive of sins) and by taking a holy bath, the man is rid of all sins. He is honoured in the heaven.

8b-9a. He should then go to Sltakuncja and perform the rite of ablution perfectly. By performing the Tarpana rite of the Pitrs and Devas, he shall attain all desires.

9b. By approaching the Mangala (auspicious) Tirtha and by taking a holy dip, he is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 2.76.10 \|\|

*snātvaivāmṛtavāpyāṃ tu mānavo'maratāṃ labhet \|*  
*brahmakuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By taking a holy bath in the tank called Amrtavapi the man attains immortality. By taking a holy bath in Brahmakunda a man shall attain the world of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.76.11 \|\|

*snātvā lakṣmaṇatīrthe vai naro yogagatiṃ vrajet \|*  
*jaṭātīrthe naraḥ snātvā nīrogī jāyate bhuvi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By performing ablution in the Tirtha of Laksmana, a man attains the goal of Yogins. By taking the holy dip in Jatatirtha a man becomes free from illness.

## \|\| 2.76.12 \|\|

*hanumatkuṇḍake snātvā durjayo jāyate'ribhiḥ \|*  
*agastyatīrtha āplutya putravāndhanavānbhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By taking a holy bath in the Hanumatkunda a the man becomes unconquerable to the enemies. By plunging into the Agastya Tirtha, the man becomes blessed with sons and wealth.

## \|\| 2.76.13 \|\|

*rāmakuṇḍe pluto martyo rāmasālokyamāpnuyāt \|*  
*lakṣmītīrthābhiṣekeṇa lakṣmīvān rūpavānbhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The man who plunges into the Ramakunda attains the world of Rama. By means of ablution in the Laksmitirtha, the man shall become fortunate and handsome.

## \|\| 2.76.14 \|\|

*agnitīrthe naraḥ snātvā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|*  
*snānena śivatīrthe tu śivalokagatirbhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*
