14\. By taking a holy dip in the Agnitirtha, the man is liberated from all sins. By means of ablution in the Sivatirtha, the attainment of Siva’s world becomes possible.

## \|\| 2.76.15 \|\|

*śaṅkhatīrthe tu saṃsnāto na naro durgatiṃ vrajet \|*  
*yamunādiṣu tīrtheṣu naraḥ snātvā divaṃ vrajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who has taken a holy dip in the Sankha- tirtha does not attain a wretched state (hell). By taking a holy dip in the Tirthas, Yamuna etc. he goes to the heaven.

## \|\| 2.76.16 \|\|

*koṭitīrthe tu samplutya sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*sādhyāmṛte plute yāti naraḥ sādhyasalokatām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By plunging into the Koptirtha one attains the benefit of all Tirthas. A man who takes a plunge into the Sadhyamrta attains the same world as that of the Sadhyas.

## \|\| 2.76.17 \|\|

*sarvatīrthe naraḥ snātvā labhetkāmānabhīpsitān \|*  
*dhanuṣkoṭyāṃ tu vidhivatsnāto mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By taking a holy dip in the Sarvatirtha, a man attains cherished desires. One who takes a holy dip in the Dhanuskop duly, is liberated from bondage.

## \|\| 2.76.18 \|\|

*kṣīrakuṃḍāpluto martyo bhogānuccāvacām̐ llabhet \|*  
*kapitīrthe naraḥ snātvā na viyoniṃ samālabhet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A man taking a plunge in the K?Ira-kun

## \|\| 2.76.19 \|\|

*gāyatr! yāṃ ca sarasvatyāṃ snāto mucyeta kilbiṣāt \|*  
*ṛṇamocanatīrthādau snātvā mukto bhavedṛṇāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One who takes a holy dip in the Gayatrl and the Sarasvati is liberated from sins. By taking a holy dip in the Tirtha Rnamocana etc. the devotee is rid of indebtedness.

## \|\| 2.76.20 \|\|

*ityetatsetutīrthānāṃ māhātmyaṃ gaditaṃ śubhe \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О splendid lady, thus the greatness of the Tirthas at the Setu has been recounted. It is destructive of all sins of those who read and those who listen to it.

## Chapter 77. Sanctity of the Tirthas in Narmada

## \|\| 2.77.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ mayā dvijaśreṣṭha setumāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*adhunā śrotumicchāmi narmadātīrthasaṅgraham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О excellent Brahmana, the excellent greatness of Setu has been heard by me. Now I wish to hear the collected list of the Tirthas on the river Narmada.1 Vasil said:

## \|\| 2.77.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu mohini vakṣyāmi narmadobhayatīragam \|*  
*catuḥśataṃ mukhyatamaṃ proktaṃ tīrthakadambakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Listen, О Mohini, I shall recount every thing. There are four hundred most important Tirthas on both the banks of the Narmada together.

## \|\| 2.77.3 \|\|

*ekādaśottare tīre dakṣiṇe ca triviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*pañcatriṃśattamaḥ prokto revāsāgarasaṅgamaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There are eleven Tirthas on the northern bank and twentythree on the southern bank. The thirtyfifth TIrtha is said to be at the meeting place of the Reva with the sea.

## \|\| 2.77.4 \|\|

*oṃkāratīrthaṃ parito nagādamarakaṇṭakāt \|*  
*krośadvaye sarvadikṣu sārddhakoṭitrayī sthitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. From the mountain Amarakantaka (where the Narmada rises) round the Omkara Tirtha within two Kfoshas kms) in all the quarters, there are three and a half crores of Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.77.5 \|\|

*koṭirekā tu tīrthānāṃ kapilāsaṅgame sthitā \|*  
*aśokavanikāyāṃ ca tīrthalakṣaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There are a crore of Tirthas situated in the confluence of the Kapila (with the Narmada). A hundred thousand Tirthas are founded in the Asoka grove.

## \|\| 2.77.6 \|\|

*śatamaṅgāragartāyāḥ kubjāyā ayutaṃ tathā \|*  
*sahasraṃ vāyusaṅge tu sarasvatyāḥ śataṃ sthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A hundred Tirthas are at the Angaragarta, ten thousand at Kubja, a thousand in the confluence with Vayu and a hundred Tirthas of Sarasvati are situated here.

## \|\| 2.77.7 \|\|

*śatadvayaṃ śuklatīrthe sahasraṃ viṣṇutīrthake \|*  
*māhiṣmatyāṃ ca sāhasraṃ śūlabhede'yutaṃ viduḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They know that there are two hundred holy spots in the Suklatirtha, a thousand in Visnutirtha, a thousand in Mahismati and ten thousand holy spots in the Sulabheda.

## \|\| 2.77.8 \|\|

*devagrāme sahasraṃ colūke saptaśatī sthitā \|*  
*tīrthānyaṣṭottaraśataṃ maṇinadyāśca saṅgame \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There are a thousand holy spots in the Devagrama village, there are seven hundred in Uliika. There are a hundred and eight Tirthas at the confluence of the Maninadi

## \|\| 2.77.9 \|\|

*vaidyanāthe ca tāvanti tāvantyeva ghaṭeśvare \|*  
*sārddhalakṣaṃ ca tīrthānāṃ sthitaṃ revābdhisaṅgame \|\| 9 \|\|*

9 As many Tirthas are in Vaidyanatha, and as many in Ghatesvara. There are a hundred and fifty thousand sacred places in the meeting place of Reva (Narmada) and the sea.

## \|\| 2.77.10 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi vyāse dvīpaśatāni ca \|*  
*saṅgame tu karañjāyāḥ sthitamaṣṭottarāyutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There are eightyeight thousand Tirthas in Vyasa and also hundreds of islands. In the confluence of the Karafija, ten thousand and eight Tirthas are situated.

## \|\| 2.77.11 \|\|

*eraṇḍīsaṅgame tadvattīrthānyaṣṭādhikaṃ śatam \|*  
*dhūtapāpe'ṣṭaṣaṣṭiśca sārddhakoṭiśca kokile \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In the confluence of the Erandi (modern Uri) there are a hundred and eight Tirthas, there are sixtyeight tirthas, in the Dhutapapa and one and a half crores in the Kokila.

## \|\| 2.77.12 \|\|

*sahasraṃ romakeśe ca dvādaśārke sahasrakam \|*  
*lakṣāṣṭake sahasre dve śuklatīrthe nareśvari \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О queen of men, there are a thousand Tirthas in Romakeia and a thousand in DvadaSarka. In the Suklatirtha there are eight hundred lakhs and two thousand Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.77.13 \|\|

*saṅgameṣu tu sarveṣu śatamaṣṭādhikaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*kāveryāḥ saṅgame nande tīrthapañcaśatī sthitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They know that in all confluences of rivers with Narmada there are hundred and eight Tirthas. There are five hundred Tirthas in Nanda, the confluence of the river Kaveri. v.l. At the confluence of Kubja with Narmada.

## \|\| 2.77.14 \|\|

*bhṛgoḥ kṣetre ca tīrthānāṃ koṭirekā vyavasthitā \|*  
*bhārabhūtyāṃ ca tīrthānāṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ sthitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the Ksetra (holy centre)of Bhrigu, there are a crore of Tirthas. In Bharabhrti there are a hundred and eight Tirthas.

## \|\| 2.77.15 \|\|

*akrūreśe sārddhaśataṃ vimaleśe daśāyutam \|*  
*sā sārddhakoṭirityeṣā tīrthasaṃjñā ca nārmade \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There are a hundred and fifty Tirthas in AkriireSa and hundred thousand in Vimalesa. In the sphere of Narmada, the number of Tirthas is one and a half crores.

## \|\| 2.77.16 \|\|

*daśādityasya nava ca kapilasyāṣṭa vai vidhoḥ \|*  
*nandinaḥ koṭisaṃjñāni tathaivāṣṭa śubhānane \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О splendid-faced lady, there are ten Tirthas of the sun, nine of Kapila and eight of Vidhu (the Moon god). There are a crore and eight Tirthas of Nandin.

## \|\| 2.77.17 \|\|

*nāgāgnisiddhāvartāni saptasaṃkhyāni mohini \|*  
*kedārendri yavārīśanaṃdidaivāni pañca vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Mohini, there are seven Tirthas in each of these holy spots namely Nagavarta, Agnyavarta and Siddha- varta and there are five Tirthas named Kedaradaiva, Indriya- daiva, Varidaiva, Isadaiva and Nandi daiva.

## \|\| 2.77.18-19 \|\|

*yameśā vaidyanāthāśca vāmanāṅgārakeśvarāḥ \|*  
*sārasvatā munīśāśca dārukeśāśca gautamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*catvāra eva gaditāstrayo vai vimaleśvarāḥ \|*  
*sahasrayajñabhīṣmeśāssvarṇatīrthāni cāpi hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The following are mentioned to be of four Tirthas in each Viz: Yamela, Vaidyanatha, Vamana, Angarakesvara, Sarasvata, Munis'a, Darukes'a and Gautama. There are three Tirthas at Vimalesvara. There are then the Tirthas of SahasraYajna, Bhismesa and Svarna Tirtha.

## \|\| 2.77.20 \|\|

*dhautapāpakarañjeśaṛṇamuktiguhāhvayam \|*  
*daśāśvamedhanandākhyaṃ manmatheśākhyabhārgavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The following are great Tirthas viz. Dhautapapa, KaranjeSa Rnamuktiguha, Dasasvamedha, Nanda, Manmathesa and Bhargava.

## \|\| 2.77.21-23 \|\|

*parāśarāyonisaṃjñaṃ vyāsākhyapitṛnandikam \|*  
*gopeśamāruteśākhyaṃ jaṅgaleśākhyaśuklakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*akṣareśaṃ pippaleśaṃ māṇḍavyadīpakeśvaram \|*  
*uttareśamaśokeśaṃ yodhaneśaṃ ca rauhiṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*lukeśaṃ ca dvisaṅkhyākaṃ pratyekaṃ gaditaṃ śubhe \|*  
*saikonaviṃśatiśataṃ tīrthānyekaikaśaḥ śubhe \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. О auspicious lady, each of these is a great Tirtha Parasara, Ayoni, Vyasa, Pitrnandi, Gopesa, Marutesa, Jangalesa, Suklaka, Aksarcsa, Pippalesa, Marinavyesvara, Dipakesvara, Uttare^a, Asokesa, Yodhanesa and Rauhina, Lokesa is said to be two in nnmber. There are one thousand nine hundred individual Tirthas, О fair one.

## \|\| 2.77.24 \|\|

*stabakeṣu ca tīrthāni dviśataṃ ca caturddaśam \|*  
*śaivānyetāni tīrthāni vaiṣṇavāni dviviṃśatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In groups there are two hundred and four hundred Tirthas. There are Tirthas pertaining to Siva. The Tirthas pertaining to Visnu are twentytwo.

## \|\| 2.77.25 \|\|

*brāhmāṇi sarvatīrthāni śāktānyaṣṭau ca viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*teṣu sapta ca mātṝṇāṃ trīṇi brāhmyāḥ śubhānane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. All these Tirthas pertain to Brahma; twentyeight Tirthas pertain to Sakti. Among them, О splendid-faced lady, seven pertain to Mothers and three to Brahmi.

## \|\| 2.77.26 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavyā dve tathā bhadre raudrī śeṣeṣu saṃsthitā \|*  
*tathaikaṃ kṣetrapālasya tīrthamuktaṃ śubhānane \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There are two Tirthas of Vaisnavi. О gentle lady, Raudri (among the Mothers) is stationed in the remaining Tirthas. О splendid-faced lady, one Tirtha is mentioned as that of Ksetrapala.

## \|\| 2.77.27 \|\|

*avāntarāṇi guhyāni prakaṭāni ca mohini \|*  
*sārddhatrikoṭitīrthāni gaditānīha vāyunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Mohini, three and a half crores of Tirthas have been mentioned by Vayu. They arc intermediary Tirthas. Some are hidden and some manifest.

## \|\| 2.77.28-29 \|\|

*divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca revāyāṃ tāni santi ca \|*  
*yastveteṣu mahābhāge yatra kutrāpi mānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*snānaṃ karoti śuddhātmā sa labheduttamāṃ gatim \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homo vedādhyayanamarcanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29а. These Tirthas are in the Reva (Narmada) region on the ground} in the atmosphere or in the heaven. The man who takes a holy dip anywhere in these Tirthas, О blessed lady, becomes pure in soul and attains excellent goal.

## \|\| 2.77.29-35 \|\|

*snānaṃ karoti śuddhātmā sa labheduttamāṃ gatim \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homo vedādhyayanamarcanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti narmadāyāstaṭe kṛtam \|*  
*tr! yahātsārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptāhādyāmunaṃ sati \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gāṅgaṃ sakṛtplavātpuṇyaṃ darśanādeva nārmadam \|*  
*ityeṣa kathito devi narmadātīrthasaṅgrahaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*smaratāmapi martyānāṃ mahāpātakaśāntidaḥ \|*  
*ya imaṃ śṛṇuyānmartyo narmadātīrthasaṅgraham \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śrāvayedvā paṭhedbhadre so'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*yadgṛhe likhitaṃ caitanmāhātmyaṃ narmadābhavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vidyate'bhyarcitaṃ tatra na mārī nāgnijaṃ bhayam \|*  
*na rājacauraśatrubhyo bhayaṃ rogabhayaṃ na ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tadgṛhaṃ pūryyate lakṣmyā dhanairddhānyairnirantaram \|*  
*putrapautrādikānāṃ ca vivāhādyaiḥ sumaṅgalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

29b-30a. Holy dip, charitable gift, Japa, Ноmа, the study of the Vedas and the worship of the deity, everything performed on the banks of Narmada has everlasting benefits.

30b-31a. The waters of Sarasvati sanctify in three days. О chaste lady, the waters of Yamuna sanctify in seven days. The waters of Ganga are meritorious even in a single dip; but the waters of Narmada are holy even by their sight.

31b-32a. Thus, О gentle lady, the multitudes of Tirthas on Narmada have been listed. These Tirthas suppress great sins of those who remember them.

32b-35. The man who hears about these Tirthas, he who narrates and he who reads this list, О gentle lady, is liberated from sins. There is no fear of pestilence, or from arson in the house where these names of Tirthas have been written down and are revered too. There is no fear from kings, thieves and enemies, nor from sickness. That house is filled with fortune, riches and food-grains perpetually. It is always joyous and auspicious through the marriage and other celebrations of sons, grandsons etc.

## Chapter 78. The Glory of Avanti

## \|\| 2.78.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- atyadbhutamidaṃ vipra māhāmtyaṃ narmadābhavam \|*  
*śrutaṃ tvayā nigaditaṃ nṛṇāṃ pāpavināśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohini said:

1\. О Brahmana, very wonderful is this greatness of Narmada. It has been heard by me as it was described by you. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 2.78.2 \|\|

*adhunā tu mahābhāga brūhi me'vantisambhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ devavandyasya mahākālasya ca prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О blessed holy lord, now tell me the greatness of Avanti1 and that of Mahakala worthy of being adored by the Devas. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.78.3 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu bhadre pravakṣyāmi hyavantyāḥ puṇyadaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ yathāvatparikīrtitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О gentle lady, listen. I shall recount the greatness of Avanti. If duly glorified, it yields merit unto men and destroys their sins.

## \|\| 2.78.4 \|\|

*mahākālavanaṃ puṇyaṃ tapaḥsthānamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra devo mahākālaḥ sthitastapasi nityadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The grove Mahakalavana is meritorious. It is an excellent place for penance. Lord Mahakala is perpetually engaged in penance there.

## \|\| 2.78.5 \|\|

*mahākālavanātkṣetraṃ nāparaṃ vidyate bhuvi \|*  
*yatra gatvā naro devi sparddhate daivataiḥ saha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is no other holy centre on the earth greater than Mahakalavana. О gentle lady, by visiting it, a man competes with the deities.

## \|\| 2.78.6 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ nāma yatra tīrthaṃ sulocane \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā brahmahāpi viśudhyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О lady of beautiful eyes, by taking a holy dip in the Tirtha named Kapalamocana, with devotion, even a Brahmana- slaycr becomes sanctified.

## \|\| 2.78.7 \|\|

*tathā kalakaleśākhyaṃ devamabhyarcya mānavaḥ \|*  
*vivāde jayamāpnoti kāryasiddhiṃ ca santatam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly, by worshipping the deity called Kalakalesa, the man gains victory in disputes and always succeeds in his undertakings.

## \|\| 2.78.8 \|\|

*atrānyadapsaraḥkuṇḍaṃ tīrthaṃ tatrāpluto naraḥ \|*  
*subhago bhogavānbhūyātsākṣātkandarppasannibhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There is another Tirtha here viz: the Apsarahkunda. The man who plunges therein shall become blessed and enjoy all worldly pleasures. He shall be like Kandarpa (cupid) himself.

## \|\| 2.78.9 \|\|

*mahiṣākhye tathā kuṇḍe snātaḥ śatrūñjayedra ṇe \|*  
*snātastu rudra sarasi rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who takes a holy dip in the Kun^a called Mahisa shall conquer the enemies in battle. One who takes a holy dip in the lake Rudrasaras is honoured in the world of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.78.10 \|\|

*kuṇḍaveśvaramāsādya samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*vyāpāre lābhamāpnoti jāyate ca śivapriyaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By visiting Kunclalesvara and by worshipping the deity in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee gains in business and activities and becomes a favourite of Siva.

## \|\| 2.78.11 \|\|

*vidyādharāhvaye tīrthe nara snātvā viśudhyati \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeśvaramabhyarcya dīrghāyuśca dhanī bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By taking a holy dip in the Tirtha called Vidya- dhara, the man becomes purified. By worshipping Markande- ivara the devotee becomes rich and long-lived.

## \|\| 2.78.12 \|\|

*sampūjya śītalāṃ devīṃ naraḥ kālavane sthitām \|*  
*visphoṭakabhayaṃ naiva kadācittasya jāyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If a man worships goddess Sltala stationed in Kalavana, he need never fear swelling boils (smallpox).

## \|\| 2.78.13 \|\|

*svargadvāraṃ samāsādya snātvābhyarcya sadāśivam \|*  
*naro na durgatiṃ yāti svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By visiting the holy centre Svargadvara, by taking a holy bath and by worshipping SadaSiva, a man never attains wretchedness. He is honoured in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.78.14 \|\|

*rājasthalaṃ naraḥ prāpya tataḥ sāmudri ke plutaḥ \|*  
*snānasya sarvatīrthānāṃ labhate phalamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By visiting the holy centre Rajasthala and taking a holy dip in the oceanic Tirtha, the devotee attains the excellent benefit of holy ablution in all the Tlrthas.

## \|\| 2.78.15 \|\|

*śaṅkarasya tathā vāpyāṃ snātvā niyamavānnaraḥ \|*  
*prāpyeha vāñchitān bhogānante rudra puraṃ vrajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. By taking a holy bath in the tank of Sankara, the man of regular holy observances attains desired pleasures and in the end goes to the city of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.78.16-17 \|\|

*śaṅkarādityamabhyarcya naraḥ syādduṣpradharṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*snātastu nīlagaṅgāyāṃ devīṃ gandhavatīṃ naraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sampūjya bhaktibhāvena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*daśāśvamedhike snātvā vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. By worshipping Sankaraditya, a man shall be invincible. By taking a holy dip in the Nilaganga and by devoutly worshipping goddess Gandhavati, the man is liberated from all sins. By taking a holy dip in Dasasvamedha, one attains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.78.18 \|\|

*atha martyaḥ samāsādya ekānaṃśāṃ sureśvarīm \|*  
*sampūjya gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By visiting the shrine of the goddess Ekanamsa (?), and by worshipping the goddess of Devas with scents, fragrant flowers etc. one attains the desired benefits.

## \|\| 2.78.19-21 \|\|

*harasiddhiṃ naro'bhyarcya sarvasiddhīśvaro bhavet \|*  
*piśācakādikānmartyaḥ samabhyarcya caturddaśa \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*hanumatkeśvaraṃ prārcetsnātvā rudra sarovare \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yo naraḥ śraddhayā yuktaḥ sa labhetsampado'khilāḥ \|*  
*vālmīkeśvaramabhyarcya sarvavidyānidhirbhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-20a. By worshipping Harasiddhi a man shall be a lord of all Siddhis. By worshipping the fourteen deities beginning with Pigacaka, a man obtains the desired benefits. No doubt need be entertained in this regard.

20b-21. The man who takes a holy dip in the lake of Rudras and worships Hanumatkesvara with faith, shall attain riches. By worshipping Valmlkesvara, one shall become a storehouse of all lores.

## \|\| 2.78.22 \|\|

*śukreśvarādiliṅgāni yo'cayecchraddhayā naraḥ \|*  
*sa syādakhilabhogāḍhyaḥ sarvarogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The man who worships Sukresvara and other Lingas faithfully shall be richly endowed with worldly pleasures and shall be free from ailments.

## \|\| 2.78.23 \|\|

*pañceśānaṃ samabhyarcya syānnaraḥ sarvasaddhibhāk \|*  
*kuśasthaladyaṃ parikramya vāñchitaṃ labhate phalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By worshipping Райсе^апа, a man shall attain all Siddhis. By roaming over Kusasthali, the devotee attains the desired benefit.

## \|\| 2.78.24 \|\|

*akrūreśaṃ tu sampūjya krūrebhyo'pyabhayaṃ labhet \|*  
*mandākinyāṃ samāplutya gaṅgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By worshipping Акгйгеshа, one attains fearlessness from cruel persons and beings. By taking a holy plunge in Mandakini, one shall attain the benefit of a holy dip in the Ganga.

## \|\| 2.78.25 \|\|

*aṅkapādaṃ naro'bhyarcya śivasyānucaro bhavet \|*  
*candrā dityaṃ prapūjyātha bhogānnānāvidhām̐ llabhet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By worshipping Ankapada, a man shall become an attendant of Siva. By worshipping Gandraditya, one shall attain different worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.78.26 \|\|

*karabheśvaramabhyarcya yānasaukhyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*laḍḍukapriyavighneśaṃ samabhyarcya sukhī bhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By worshipping Karabhesvara, one shall attain happiness of vehicles. By worshipping Lad\<;lukapriya Vighnesa (Vighnesa fond of sweets) one shall be happy.

## \|\| 2.78.27-29 \|\|

*kusumeśādikānprārcya sarvānbhogānsamaśnute \|*  
*yajñavāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā mārkaṇḍeśaṃ samarcya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sarvayajñaphalaṃ labdhvā yugamekaṃ vaseddivi \|*  
*somavatyāṃ naraḥ snātvābhyarcya someśvaraṃ sati \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vāñchitām̐ llabhate kāmānihāmutra ca mohini \|*  
*yātanākalane snātvā yātanāṃ naiva paśyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-28a. By worshipping Kusumesa and others, one enjoys all pleasures. By taking a holy dip in the Yajnavapi and by worshipping Markandesa, the man obtains the benefit of all Yajiias. He stays in heaven for the period of a Yuga.

28b-29. О chaste lady, by taking the holy dip in the Somavatl and by worshipping Somes vara, the man obtains the desired benefits both here and hereafter. О Mohini, by worshipping in Yatanakalana, the man never faces tortures in hell.

## \|\| 2.78.30-31 \|\|

*narakeśaṃ samabhyarcya svargalokagatiṃ labhet \|*  
*kedāreśaṃ tataḥ prārcya rāmeśvaramathāpi vā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saubhāgyeśaṃ narādityaṃ labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam \|*  
*keśavārkaṃ tu sampūjya naraḥ syātkeśavapriyaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. By worshipping Narakesa, one attains the goal of heavenly world. By worshipping Kedaresa, Ratnesvara, Saubhagyesa and Naraditya, the devotee obtains the desired benefit. By worshipping Kesavarka, the man shall be a favourite of Kesava.

## \|\| 2.78.32-36 \|\|

*śaktibhede tataḥ snātvā mucyate'tyugrasaṅkaṭāt \|*  
*svarṇakṣurabrahmavāpyāṃ snātvābhyarcyābhayeśvaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*agastyeśaṃ ca vidhije sampadāmayanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*oṃkāreśādiliṅgāni yo naraḥ samyagarcayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sa labhedakhilānkāmānmaheśasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*mahākālavane devi liṅgasaṅkhyā na vidyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yatra tatra sthitaṃ liṅgaṃ sampūjya syācchivapriyaḥ \|*  
*tathā kanakaśṛṅgāhvā kuśasthalyapyavantikā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tathā padmāvatī devī kumudvatyujjayinyapi \|*  
*pratikalpābhidhā bhinnā viśālākhyāmarāvatī \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-34a. By taking a holy dip in Saktibheda, one is liberated from terrible and difficult calamities. By taking a holy dip in Svarnaksura Brahmavapl and by worshipping Abhayesvara and Agastyesa, О daughter of Brahma, one shall become the abode of all riches. The man who perfectly worships Orhkaresa and other Lingas, shall obtain all desires. Thanks to the grace of Mahesa.

34b-35a. О gentle lady, there is no limit to the number of Lingas in Mahakalavana. By worshipping any Li nga situated anywhere, one shall be a favourite of Siva.

35b-36. The names of Avanti are Kanakasrnga, Kusa- sthali, Avantika, Padmavatl, Kumudvati and Ujjayinl. In every Kalpa it has a different name. It is called Vishala and Amaravati as well.

## \|\| 2.78.37 \|\|

*śiprāyāṃ vai naraḥ snātvā yo maheśaṃ samarcayet \|*  
*sa labhetsakalānkāmandevayostu prasādataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The man who takes bath in Sipra river and worships Mahesa, shall attain his cherished desires, thanks to the grace of the deity.

## \|\| 2.78.38-44 \|\|

*snātvā tu gomatīkuṇḍe svargatiṃ labhate naraḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍe tu vāmane snātvā stauti nāmasahasrataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śrīdharaṃ sarvadeveśaṃ yaḥ sa sākṣāddharirbhuvi \|*  
*snātvā vīreśasarasi yo'cayetkālabhairavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sa sarvāḥ sampado bhuktvā śivalokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaḥ kuṭumbeśvaraṃ prāpya pūjayedupacārakaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*samprāpya vividhānkāmānante svargagatiṃ labhet \|*  
*devaprayāgasarasi yo'cayeddevamādhavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sa bhaktiṃ mādhave prāpya padaṃ viṣṇoḥ samāpnuyāt \|*  
*kakarājasya tīrthe tu snātvā prayatamānasaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sarvarogavinirmukto dhanī bhogī bhavetsati \|*  
*antargṛhasya yātrāyāṃ vighneśaṃ bhairavaṃ hyumām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rudrā dityānsurānanyānyo'cayecchraddhayā naraḥ \|*  
*yathālabdhopacārādyaiḥ sa bhavetsvargalokabhāk \|\| 44 \|\|*

38-39a. By taking a holy dip in the Gomati Kuncta the man obtains heavenly goal. By taking a holy dip in Vamana Kumja, by eulogising Sridhara, the lord of all Devas, by uttering his thousand names, a man shall become Hari himself on the earth.

39b-40a. He who takes a holy dip in the lake VlreSa- saras and worships Kalabhairava, enjoys riches and attains Siva’s world.

40b-41a. He who visits Kutumbesvara and worships him with various means of service, achieves his different cherished desires, and in the end achieves heavenly goal.

41b-42a. He who worships Devamadhava in the Devaprayagasaras derives devotion for Madhava and attains the region ofVisnu.

42b-43a. О chaste lady, he who takes a holy bath in the Tirtha of Karkaraja with controlled mind, shall be rid of all ailments. He shall become rich and enjoyer of pleasures.

43b-44. The man who faithfully worships Vighnesa Bhairava, Uma, Rudras, Adityas and other Devas in the course of his pilgrimage in the Antargrha (?) with whatever means that are available, shall gain heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.78.45-46 \|\|

*rudra saraḥprabhṛtiṣu tīrthānyanyāni bhāmini \|*  
*bahūni teṣu cābhyarcya śaṅkaraṃ syātsukhī naraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*aṣṭatīrthyāṃ naraḥ snātvā sāṅgaṃ yātrāphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*kālāraṇyasya vidhije satyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. О lady, there are many other Tlrthas in Rudrasaras. By worshipping Sankara in them, the man shall be happy. By taking a holy dip in the AstatirthI (collection of eight Tirthas), the man obtains the benefit of pilgrimage to Kalaranya. О daughter of Brahma, truth, it is the truth that has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 2.78.47 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*avantyā yannaraḥ śrutvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus everything in regard to the greatness of Avanti has been narrated. By listing to the greatness of Avanti, the man is liberated from all sins.

## Chapter 79. The Greatness of Mathura

## \|\| 2.79.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- śrutaṃ hyavantyā māhātmyaṃ vaso pāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*adhunā śrotumicchāmi māhātmyaṃ mathurābhavam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohinl requested:

1\. О Vasu, the greatness of Avanti that is destructive of sins of men, has been heard. Now I wish to hear the greatness of Mathura.1 Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.79.2 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu mohini vakṣyāmi mathurāyāḥ śubhāvaham \|*  
*vaibhavaṃ yatra bhagavāñjātaḥ padmabhuvārthitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Mohini, listen. I shall recount the greatness of Mathura that is conducive to auspiciousness. It was here that the lord was born on being requested by the lotus-born deity Brahma.

## \|\| 2.79.3 \|\|

*āvirbhūya vibhustatra samprāpto nandagokulam \|*  
*tatra sthitvākhilāḥ krīḍāścakāra saha gopakaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After manifesting himself there, the lord went over to the cowherds’ colony of Nanda. Staying there, he played all games in the company of young cowherds.

## \|\| 2.79.4 \|\|

*hatvā ca kaṃsaprahitānpūtanādīnniśācarān \|*  
*vijahāra sa gopībhirvaneṣu dvādaśasvapi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After killing demons beginning with Putana, sent by Karhsa, he sported in the twelve forests along with the cowherd esses.

## \|\| 2.79.5 \|\|

*vaneṣu yāni tīrthāni santi yāni ca māthure \|*  
*tāni te'ha pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu mohini sāmpratam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Mohinl, listen. Now I shall recount to you those Tlrthas that are in the forests and in the area of Mathura.

## \|\| 2.79.6 \|\|

*ādyaṃ madhuvanaṃ nāma snāto yatra narottamaḥ \|*  
*santarpya devarṣipitṝnviṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The first forest1 2 is what is called Madhuvana. By taking a holy bath there and performing the Tarpana rites unto the Devas, sages and Pitrs, the excellent man is honoured in the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.7 \|\|

*atha tālāhvayaṃ devi dvitīyaṃ vanamuttamam \|*  
*yatra snāto naro bhaktyā kṛtakṛtyaḥ prajāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О gentle lady, the second excellent forest is what is called Tala. The man who takes a holy bath there with devotion, has all his objectives in life accomplished.

## \|\| 2.79.8 \|\|

*kumudākhyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu yatra snātvā sulocane \|*  
*labhate vāñchitānkāmānihāmutra ca modate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О lady of beautiful eyes, the third one is what is called Kumuda. By taking a holy bath there, the devotee attains cherished desires and rejoices here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.79.9 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmyavanaṃ nāma caturthaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*bahutīrthānvitaṃ yatra gatvā syādviṣṇulokabhāk \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The fourth one is glorified by the name of Kamya- vana. It contains many Tlrthas. By visiting it one attains the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.10 \|\|

*yattatra vimalaṃ kuṇḍaṃ sarvatīrthottamottamam \|*  
*tatra snāto naro bhadre labhate vaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There is an excellent Tlrtha called Vimala Kun

## \|\| 2.79.11 \|\|

*pañcamaṃ bahulākhyaṃ tu vanaṃ pāpavināśanam \|*  
*yatra snātastu manujaḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The fifth forest that is destructive of sins, is called Bahula. By taking a holy ablution, the man attains all desires.

## \|\| 2.79.12 \|\|

*asti bhadra vanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ snāto'tra mānavaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇadevaprasādena sarvabhadrā ṇi paśyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There is the sixth forest named Bhadravana. The man who takes a bath here, sees everything auspicious, thanks to the grace of lord Krsna.

## \|\| 2.79.13 \|\|

*khādiraṃ tu vanaṃ devi saptamaṃ yatra mānavaḥ \|*  
*snānamātreṇa labhate tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О gentle lady, the seventh forest is Khadira Vana. Merely by taking a holy dip here, the man attains that greatest region of Visnu..

## \|\| 2.79.14 \|\|

*mahāvanaṃ cāṣṭamaṃ te sadaiva harivallabham \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā manujo bhaktyā śakraloke mahīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The eighth forest is Mahavana most liked by Hari. By visiting it with devotion, the man is honoured in the world of Indra (i.e. heaven).

## \|\| 2.79.15 \|\|

*lohajaṅghaṃ tu navamaṃ vanaṃ yatrāpluto naraḥ \|*  
*mahāviṣṇuprasādena bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The ninth forest is Lohajangha. The man who takes a holy bath there, attains worldly pleasures and salvation, thanks to the grace of MahaVisnu.

## \|\| 2.79.16 \|\|

*bilvāraṇyaṃ tu daśamaṃ yatra snātaḥ sumadhyame \|*  
*śaivaṃ vā vaiṣṇavaṃ vāpi yāti lokaṃ nijecchayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О lady of beautiful waist, Bilva is the tenth forest. He who takes a holy dip there, goes to the world of Siva or Visnu as he pleases.

## \|\| 2.79.17 \|\|

*ekādaśaṃ tu bhāṇḍīraṃ yogināmativallabham \|*  
*yatra snāto naro bhaktyā sarvapāpairvimucyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The eleventh forest is Bhandlra, most liked by the Yogins. The man who devoutly takes a bath there, is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.79.18 \|\|

*vṛndāvanaṃ dvādaśaṃ tu sarvapāpanikṛntanam \|*  
*yatsamaṃ na dharāpṛṣṭhe vanamastyaparaṃ sati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Vrndavana is the twelfth one. It destroys all sins. О chaste lady, there is no other forest equal to this on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.79.19 \|\|

*yatra snātastu manujo devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*kṛtvā ṛṇatrayānmukto viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The man who takes a holy bath there and performs Tarpana to the Devas, sages and Pitfs, becomes liberated from the three-fold indebtedness. He is honoured in the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.20 \|\|

*viṃśatiryojanānāṃ tu māthuraṃ parimaṇḍalam \|*  
*yatra kutrāplutastatra viṣṇubhaktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The precincts of the holy centre Mathura extend to twenty Yojanas (240 kms). If any person takes a holy bath anywhere within this area, he shall attain devotion to Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.21 \|\|

*tanmadhye mathurā nāma purī sarvottamottamā \|*  
*yasyā darśanamātreṇa bhaktiṃ vindati mādhave \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Within it, is the city named Mathura. It is the most excellent of all cities. Merely by seeing it, one obtains devotion to Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.22 \|\|

*viśrāntisaṃjñakaṃ yatra tīrtharatnaṃ nareśvari \|*  
*tatra snāto naro bhaktyā vaiṣṇavaṃ labhate padam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О queen of men, there is a jewel among Tirthas named Visranti.1 The man who devoutly takes a holy dip there, attains the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.23 \|\|

*viśrānternikaṭe dakṣe vimuktaṃ tīrthamuttam \|*  
*tatra snāto naro bhaktyā muktimāpnoti niścitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Near Visranti and to the south of it, is the excellent Tirtha viz. Vimukta. It is certain that the man who devoutly takes bath there attains liberation.

## \|\| 2.79.24 \|\|

*tato'pi dakṣiṇe bhāge rāmatīrthaṃ janeśvari \|*  
*yatra snāto naro'jñānabandhānmukto bhaveddhruvam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О queen of the people, still south of it, is the Rama Tirtha. The man who takes a holy bath there shall certainly be liberated from the bondage of ignorance.

## \|\| 2.79.25 \|\|

*saṃsāramokṣaṇaṃ tasmāddakṣiṇe tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu manujo viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To the south of this, is the excellent Tirtha called Samsara Moksana. A man who takes a holy dip there, is honoured in the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.26 \|\|

*prayāgākhyaṃ tato dakṣe tīrthaṃ tridaśadurlabham \|*  
*snātastatra naro devi agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. To the south of this is the Tirtha called Prayaga. It is difficult of access even to the Devas. О gentle lady, the man who takes a holy dip there shall obtain the benefit of Agnistoma.

## \|\| 2.79.27 \|\|

*tataḥ kanakhalaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra snāto naraḥ sati \|*  
*svargamāsādya dehānte modate nandanādiṣu \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter, is the Tirtha Kanakhala. О chaste lady, the man who takes a holy bath there, attains heaven. After death he rejoices in the Nandana Park and other places.

## \|\| 2.79.28 \|\|

*taddakṣe tindukaṃ tīrthaṃ yasminsnāto narottamaḥ \|*  
*rājasūyaphalaṃ prāpya modate divi devavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. To the south of it is the holy centre Tinduka. The excellent man who takes a holy bath there attains the benefit of Rajasuya sacrifice. He rejoices in heaven like a Deva.

## \|\| 2.79.29 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ paṭusvāmitīrthaṃ bhāskaravallabham \|*  
*snātvā yatra raviṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuktabhogo divaṃ vrajet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Beyond that is the holy centre Patusvami Tlrtha. It is a favourite of the Sun-god. By taking a holy bath dnd seeing the Sun, the devotee enjoys all worldly pleasures and goes to heaven.

## \|\| 2.79.30 \|\|

*tasmāddakṣiṇato bhadre dhruvatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra snāto dhruvaṃ dṛṣṭvā labhate vaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О gentle lady, to the south of it is the excellent Dhruva Tirtha. By taking a holy bath and by having a sight of Dhruva (pole star), the devotee obtains the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.31 \|\|

*dhruvatīrthāttato dakṣe tīrthaṃ saptarṣisevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā munīndṛṣṭvā ṛṣiloke pramodate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Beyond Dhruva Tirtha, to the south of it is the Tlrtha frequented by seven sages. By taking the holy plunge and by visiting the sages, the devotee rejoices in the world of sages.

## \|\| 2.79.32 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe ṛṣitīrthasya mokṣatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yatra vai snānamātreṇa mucyate sarvapāpataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. To the south of Rsitirtha is the excellent Moksa Tirtha. Merely by taking a holy bath therein, one is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.79.33 \|\|

*taddakṣe bodhinītīrthaṃ snātvā yatra tu mānavaḥ \|*  
*datvā piṇḍaṃ pitṛbhyaśca nayettāṃstridaśālayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. To the south of it is Bodhini Tirtha. The man who takes a holy dip there and offers Pinda to the Pitrs leads them to the heaven.

## \|\| 2.79.34 \|\|

*taddakṣe koṭitīrthaṃ vai yatra snānena mānavaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. To the south of it is Koti Tirtha. By taking the bath therein, a man is liberated from all sins. He shall attain the world of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.35 \|\|

*viśrānteruttare bhāge tīrthamastyasikuṇḍakam \|*  
*yatra snāto naro devi vaiṣṇavaṃ labhate padam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. To the northern side of Visranti is the holy centre Asikundaka. О gentle lady, the man who takes a holy bath there attains the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.79.36 \|\|

*asikuṇḍasya saumye tu navatīrthaṃ sulocane \|*  
*yatra vai snānato martyaḥ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О lady of beautiful eyes, Nava Tirtha is to the north of Asikunda. By taking a holy dip there, the man is honoured in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.79.37 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ saṃyamanaṃ nāma tata uttarataḥ sthitam \|*  
*tatra snānena dānena yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Tirtha called Samyamana is situated to the north of it. By taking a holy dip therein and offering charitable gifts, the devotee does not see the world of Yama.

## \|\| 2.79.38 \|\|

*taduttare paraṃ tīrthaṃ dhārāyatanasaṃjñakam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu manujaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha modate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. To the north of it there is a great Tirtha Dharayatana. By taking the holy bath therein, the man rejoices in the company of ancestors.

## \|\| 2.79.39 \|\|

*taduttare nāgatīrthaṃ yatra snānena mohini \|*  
*sarpebhyo hyabhayaṃ labdhvā svarge loke mahīyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. To the north of it is the Naga Tirtha. О Mohinl, by taking a holy dip therein the devotee derives fearlessness, protection from the serpents. He is honoured in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.79.40 \|\|

*taduttare brahmalokaṃ ghaṇṭābharaṇakāhvayam \|*  
*snānātpāpāpahaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmalokagatipradam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. To the north of it is theTlrtha named Brahmaloka- Ghantabharanaka. By means of a holy dip this Tirtha dispels all sins. It bestows the goal of the world of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.79.41 \|\|

*asmātsaumye paraṃ tīrthe somākhyaṃ yatra samplutaḥ \|*  
*somalokamavāpnoti vipāpo manujottamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. To the north of this is the great Tirtha named Soma. He who takes a holy plunge in it, attains the world of Soma (Moon). Rid of sins he becomes the most excellent of men.

## \|\| 2.79.42 \|\|

*snātvā prācīsarasvatyāṃ tasmāduttarataḥ śubhe \|*  
*yatra vai snānamātreṇa naro vāgīśvaro bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О auspicious lady, one should take a holy bath in Praci Sarasvati which is to the north of it. Merely by taking a holy dip there, the man shall become the lord of speech.

## \|\| 2.79.43 \|\|

*taduttare cakratīrthaṃ yatra snātastu mānavaḥ \|*  
*jitvā śatrugaṇaṃ svarge modate yugasaptakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. To the north of it is the Gakra Tirtha. The man who takes a holy dip there, conquers hosts of his enemies and rejoices in heaven for the period of seven Yugas.

## \|\| 2.79.44 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ tasmāduttarataḥ sthitam \|*  
*yatra snānena subhage vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О blessed lady, the Tirtha Dasasvamedha is situated to the north of it. By taking a holy dip therein, one shall attain the benefit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.79.45 \|\|

*gokarṇākhyaṃ śivaṃ tatra sampūjya vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpyānte śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By worshipping Siva designated Gokarna, in accordance with the injunctions, the man attains his cherished desires. In the end he is honoured in the world of Siva.

## \|\| 2.79.46 \|\|

*vighnarājāhvayaṃ tīrthaṃ tasmāduttarataḥ sthitam \|*  
*yatra snātvā hyavighnena sarvakarmaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. To the north of it is situated the Tirtha named Vighna-Raja. By taking a holy bath there one shall attain the benefit of his holy rites without an obstacle.

## \|\| 2.79.47 \|\|

*taduttare hyanantākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ tatrāpluto naraḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatitīrthānāṃ māthurāṇāṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. To the north of it is the Tirtha named Ananta. The man who takes a holy bath there shall attain the benefit of twentyfour Tirthas of Mathura.

## \|\| 2.79.48 \|\|

*mathurāyāṃ mahābhāge sākṣāddevo hariḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*caturvyūhasvarūpeṇa māthurāṇāṃ vimuktidaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О blessed lady, Lord Hari himself is stationed in Mathura, in the form of Caturvyuha (four manifestations of Visnu). He is the bestower of liberation on the citizens of Mathura.

## \|\| 2.79.49 \|\|

*ekā vārāhamūrtiśca parā nārāyaṇāhvayā \|*  
*vāmanākhyā tṛtīyā ca caturthī haladhāriṇī \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The four manifestations are: one is the form of Varaha (the Divine Boar), another one is called Narayana; the third form is called Vamana and the fourth is Haladhara (i.e. Sankarsana) 1

## \|\| 2.79.50 \|\|

*caturvyūhadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*naro muktimavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. By visiting the lord of the four Vyuhas and by worshipping him in accordance with the injunctions, man attains liberation.

## \|\| 2.79.51 \|\|

*raṅgeśaṃ cāpi bhūteśaṃ mahāvidyāṃ ca bhairavam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sampūjya vidhivattīrthayātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. By visiting and duly worshipping RangeSa, Bhutesa, Mahavidya and Bhairava, the devotee shall attain the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.79.52 \|\|

*catuḥsāmudri ke kūpe kubjāyāśca gaṇeśituḥ \|*  
*tathā kṛṣṇākhyagaṅgāyāṃ snātvā mucyeta pātakāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. By taking a holy dip in the Catuhsamudrika (where four oceans meet), the well of Kubja and Ganga called Krsna and of the lord of Ganas (attendants), the devotee is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 2.79.53 \|\|

*sarvasya māthurākhyasya maṇḍalasya śubhānane \|*  
*ādhipatye sthito devaḥ keśavaḥ kleśanāśanaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О auspicious-faced lady, lord Kesava, the destroyer of all miseries presides as the overlord of the entire zone called Mathura.

## \|\| 2.79.54 \|\|

*adṛṣṭvā keśavaṃ bhadre māthure puṇyamaṇḍale \|*  
*janurnirarthakaṃ tasya saṃsaredbhavasāgare \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О gentle lady, if one does not see Kesava in the sacred zone of Mathura, one’s life becomes purposeless. He will drift about in the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.79.55-56 \|\|

*anyānyasaṅkhyatīrthāni tatra santi śubhānane \|*  
*snātvā teṣvapi dattvā ca kiñcittatra sthitāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*naro na durgatiṃ yāti satyaṃ tubhyaṃ mayoditam \|*  
*mathurāyāśca māhātmyaṃ śrāvayedyaḥ śṛṇoti ca \|*  
*so'pi bhaktiṃ harau labdhvā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. О splendid-faced lady, there are many other numerous Tlrthas there. By taking a holy dip therein and by giving something to the people staying there, a man wards off a wretched state. He does not go to hell. The truth has been stated to you. He who narrates or listens to the greatness of Mathura attains devotion to Hari and (thereafter) attains all cherished desires.

## Chapter 80. The Glory of Vrndavana

## \|\| 2.80.1 \|\|

*mohinyuvāca- mathurāyāstu māhātmyaṃ vanānāṃ cāpi mānada \|*  
*śrutaṃ vṛndāvanasyāpi rahasyaṃ kiñcidīraya \|\| 1 \|\|*

Mohinl requested:

1\. О bestower of honour, the greatness of Mathura and the forests has been heard. Tell me a little about the secret of Vrndavana too.

## \|\| 2.80.2 \|\|

*vṛndāraṇyaṃ bhuvo brahmankīrtirūpaṃ rahogatam \|*  
*tacchrotuṃ mama vāñchāsti tannirūpaya vistarāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Brahmana, Vrndavana is, as it were, the glory of the earth preserved in secret. I desire to hear about it. Narrate it to me in detail. Vasu said:

## \|\| 2.80.3 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- śṛṇu devi rahasyaṃ me vṛndāraṇyasamudbhavam \|*  
*yanna kasmaicidākhyātaṃ mayā prāpya gurūttamāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О gentle lady, listen to the esoteric secret from me about Vrndavana. After acquiring it from the excellent preceptor, it has never been recounted by me to anyone.

## \|\| 2.80.4 \|\|

*gurave kathitaṃ bhadre nāradena mahātmanā \|*  
*vṛndayā nāradāyoktaṃ rahasyaṃ gopikāpateḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О gentle lady, the secret of the lord of the cowherd- esses had been communicated to my preceptor by Narada of great soul. But it had been at first confided to Narada by Vrnda.

## \|\| 2.80.5-6 \|\|

*tatte'ha sampravakṣyāmi jagaduddhārakāraṇam \|*  
*ekadā nārado lokānparyaṭanbhagavatpriyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vṛndāraṇyaṃ samāsādya tasthau puṣpasarastaṭe \|*  
*paścimottarato devi māthure maṇḍale sthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. That I shall recount to you as it is conducive to the uplift of the universe. On one occasion, Narada, the dear friend of the lord, was wandering over the worlds. He reached Vrndavana and stopped on the banks of the lake Puspasaras. О gentle lady, it is situated in the north-west sector of the sacred place Mathura.

## \|\| 2.80.7 \|\|

*vṛndāraṇyaṃ turīyāṃśaṃ gopikeśarahaḥsthalam \|*  
*govarddhano yatra giriḥ sakhisthalasamīpataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A fourth part of Vrndavana is the secret rendezvous of the lord of cowherdesses. The mountain Govardhana is also there near the Sakhlsthala. (the rendezvous of his friend).

## \|\| 2.80.8 \|\|

*vṛndāyāstattapo'raṇyaṃ nandigrāmānuyāmunam \|*  
*taṭe tu yāmune ramye ramyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ sati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That is the penance grove of Vrnda. It is in Nandi- grama near the Yamuna. О chaste lady, the beautiful Vrndavana is on the charming banks of the Yamuna.

## \|\| 2.80.9 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ tatrāpi subhage supuṇyaṃ kausumaṃ saraḥ \|*  
*vṛndāyāstu taṭe ramye āśramo'tisukhāvahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О blessed lady, the highly meritorious Puspasaras lake is also there. On the same beautiful bank is the hermitage of Vrnda which is extremely conducive to pleasure.

## \|\| 2.80.10-11 \|\|

*nityaṃ viśramate yatra madhyāhne sakhibhirhariḥ \|*  
*muhūrtaṃ sa tu viśramya snigdhacchāyatarostale \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śītalaṃ puṣpasaraso vāryupaspṛśya nāradaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā mādhyāhnikaṃ karma tasthau tatra sarastaṭe \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. It is here that Hari takes rest every day at midday along with his woman friends. Narada resorted for a short while in the cool shade of a tree. He drank the cool water of the lake Puspasaras after performing the midday holy rites. He sat on the bank of the lake.

## \|\| 2.80.12 \|\|

*tatra vṛndāśrame ramye gopyo gopāśca mohini \|*  
*āyānti vargaśo yānti nāradasya vipaśyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Even as Narada sat watching, О Mohim, cowherds and cowherdesses came into that beautiful hermitage of Vrnda in groups and in groups they went away.1

## \|\| 2.80.13 \|\|

*athaivaṃ yāmamekaṃ tu tatra sthitvā tu nāradaḥ \|*  
*praharārddhāvaśiṣṭe'hni viveśāśramamadbhutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the period of a Yama (three hours) he stayed there thus, when the day was short of half a Prahara he entered the wonderful hermitage. Г VV. 12-33 describe how Narada who wanted to know the Secret of Love-Devotion to Kf?na, was changed into a woman and enjoyed by Lord Кг9ДО\<

## \|\| 2.80.14 \|\|

*yatra vṛndā sthitā devī kṛṣṇabhaktiparāyaṇā \|*  
*samāgatānāṃ satkāraṃ vidadhānā phalādibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Vrnda, the gentle lady devoted to the love of Krsna was staying there receiving the visitors and extending hospitality to them with fruits etc.

## \|\| 2.80.15 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāpasīṃ bhadre nāradaḥ sādhusammataḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya vinamrāṅgo niṣasāda dharātale \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О gentle lady, on seeing that ascetic woman, Narada who was highly esteemed by saintly persons, bowed down to her, with great humility. He sat on the bare ground.

## \|\| 2.80.16 \|\|

*tataḥ sā dhyānayogānte samunmīlya vilocane \|*  
*āsanaṃ sandideśātho'tithaye nāradāya vai \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At the end of her meditation and Yogic practice, Vrnda opened her eyes. She offered a seat to Narada who was the guest.

## \|\| 2.80.17 \|\|

*tataḥ sa nāradastatra satkṛto vṛndayāvasat \|*  
*rahasyaṃ gopikeśasya tasyā jijñāsurādarāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Desirous of knowing the secret of the lord of cowherd- esses (i.e. Krsna) from her, Narada stayed there on being respectfully honoured by Vrnda.

## \|\| 2.80.18 \|\|

*tayā kṛtāṃ satkṛtiṃ tu svīkṛtya vidhinandanaḥ \|*  
*suprasannāntarāṃ vṛndāṃ jñātvā hārdaṃ vyajijñapat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The son of Brahma (i.e. Narada) accepted the hospitality extended by her. Knowing that she was delighted in her mind, he informed her of his heart-felt desire.

## \|\| 2.80.19 \|\|

*sā tu tadvāñchitaṃ jñātvā dhyānayogena bhāmini \|*  
*svasakhīṃ mādhavīṃ tatra samāhūyābravīdidam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Having gauged his desire of knowledge with her Yogic power and meditation, О beautiful lady, she sent for her friend named Madhavi and told her:

## \|\| 2.80.20 \|\|

*mādhavi priyametasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sampādaya yathā mahyamāśramasya supuṇyatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “O Madhavi, see that Narada, the great soul, realizes his desire so that the meritoriousness of myself and this hermitage is enhanced.

## \|\| 2.80.21 \|\|

*svāśramaṃ hyāgatasyaiva yo na sampādayetpriyam \|*  
*niṣphalo hyāśramastasya pherurājagṛhopamaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If one does not carry out the loving request of a visitor to the hermitage, it is in vain. It is comparable to a jackal’s den.

## \|\| 2.80.22 \|\|

*atha sā mādhavī devī nītvā nāradamājñayā \|*  
*svādhiṣṭhātr! yāstu vṛndāyāḥ sarasastaṭamuttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At the behest of her mistress Vrnda, Madhavi, the good lady, took Narada to the excellent bank of a lake.

## \|\| 2.80.23-27 \|\|

*paścimottaratastasmin snātuṃ taṃ sandideśa ha \|*  
*tatastadājñayā bhadre nārado devadarśanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nimamajja jale tasmindhyāyañchrīkṛṣṇasaṅgamam \|*  
*nimajjamāne sarasi nārade munisattame \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yayau vṛndāntike bhadre saṃvidhāya tadīpsitam \|*  
*athāsau nāradastatra sannimajyodgatastadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dadarśa nijamātmānaṃ vanitārūpamadbhutam \|*  
*tatastu parito vīkṣya nāradī sā śucismitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūrvottarāyāṃ tiṣṭhantī āhvayantī kareṅgitaiḥ \|*  
*dadarśa vanitāṃ ramyāṃ bhūṣitāṃ bhūṣaṇottamaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

23-25a. She directed him to take his holy bath facing the north-west. Then, О gentle lady, at the behest of that lady, Narada of divine vision dipped himself into the water meditating on SriKrsna’s contact. When the excellent sage Narada plunged into the lake, the lady Madhavi went back to Vrnda, О gentle lady, after completing her task of carrying out his wish.

25b-26a. Narada came out of the water after the plunge and found himself in the form of a woman. It was very surprising.

26b-27. Naradi (the lady Narada) smilingly glanced all round and saw a woman stationed in the north-east. She was beautiful and was bedecked in excellent ornaments. She was beckoning with the gesticulations of her hand to Narad! to come towards her.

## \|\| 2.80.28 \|\|

*tatastayā samāhūtā nāradī sā tadantikam \|*  
*prāptā viśvāsitā svasthā nītā cāpi sthalāntaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Narad! was called by her and so she went near that lady. After instilling confidence into her, she was taken to another place.

## \|\| 2.80.29 \|\|

*ratnaprākārakhacite bhavane vanitākule \|*  
*prāpayya tāṃ nivṛttāsau sāpi tābhiḥ susatkṛtā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Narad! was taken by the lady to a certain chamber full of woman and ornamentally decorated with gems and jewels. The lady withdrew thereafter and Narad! was received duly by those women.

## \|\| 2.80.30 \|\|

*viśākhādisakhīvṛndairāśvāsyā'lyaikayā tataḥ \|*  
*prāpitābhyantare devi sāpaśyadgopikeśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. She was received by the groups of companions, Visakha etc. After consoling her, О gentle lady, she was taken within the inner chamber by a maid. There Narad! saw the lord of the cowherdesses.

## \|\| 2.80.31 \|\|

*dūtyāṃ tasyāṃ nivṛttāyāṃ samāhūtā priyeṇa sā \|*  
*nāradī praṇipatyeśaṃ lajjā namrāntikaṃ yayau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the messengers returned, Narad! was called by the lover of cowherdesses. After bowing down to the lord, she went near him bashfully.

## \|\| 2.80.32 \|\|

*rasikena samāśliṣya ramayitvā visarjjitā \|*  
*krameṇaiva tu samprāptā sā punaḥ kausumaṃ saraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The man of taste (LordKrsna) embraced her, had the sportful dalliance with her and then dismissed her. Gradually she came once again to the lake Puspasaras.

## \|\| 2.80.33 \|\|

*sā punastatra mādhavyā majjitā dakṣapaścime \|*  
*puṃbhāvamabhisamprāpto nārado vismito'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She was then made to plunge into the lake on the south-west side. Narada then regained his manhood. He was surprised at it.

## \|\| 2.80.34 \|\|

*tato vṛndājñayā tatra sarasaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇe \|*  
*ekāntaṃ tapa āsthāya tasthau tatprekṣaṇotsukaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At the behest of Vrnda, Narada performed a penance in the south-eastern side of the lake in an isolated spot and stayed there eagerly to see that (?).

## \|\| 2.80.35 \|\|

*evaṃ tapasyatastasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vṛndayā preṣitairvṛttiṃ nijāṃ kalpayataḥ phalaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Narada thus continued his penance sustaining himself with the fruits sent by Vrnda.

## \|\| 2.80.36 \|\|

*ekadā nāradastatra vicarannāśramāntare \|*  
*śuśrāva saubhagaṃ śabdaṃ kayācitsamudīritam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Once Narada was moving about here and there within his hermitage. He heard some charming sound uttered by some lady.

## \|\| 2.80.37 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kautukāviṣṭo nārado'dhyātmadarśanaḥ \|*  
*vicinvanvanamāsthāya na dadarśa ca tatpadam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing it, Narada of a spiritual vision became curious. He searched the forest but could not see any trace of the person.

## \|\| 2.80.38 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo vṛndāṃ papraccha sādaram \|*  
*sāpi tasmai samācakhyau kubjāvṛttāntamāditaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Surprised much at this, he respectfully asked Vrnda about it. She narrated to him the story of the Kubja (humpbacked lady) from the beginning.

## \|\| 2.80.39 \|\|

*bhūmyantaragṛhasthānā kubjā nārī varā vibhoḥ \|*  
*kāmamekāntake sveśaṃ samupācarati svayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This hump-backed lady is stationed in a house underground. She is the excellent beloved of the lord. In an isolated place, she receives her Lord and renders service to him to his heart’s content.

## \|\| 2.80.40 \|\|

*na tāṃ ko'pi muniśreṣṭha vijānāti mayā vinā \|*  
*tataḥ saṃkṣepato vakṣye yāṃ didṛkṣustapo'caraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О excellent sage, excepting me no one knows her. Hence I shall succinctly narrate. It is because you were desirous of seeing her that you performed the penance.

## \|\| 2.80.41 \|\|

*prātaḥ prabodhito mātrā snātvā bhuktvānugānvitaḥ \|*  
*gocāraṇāya vipine vṛndāvana upāviśat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Early in the morning, Krsna was wakened up by his mother. He took his bath and breakfast. Followed by his friends he went to the forest for grazing the cows. In that connection he entered Vrndavana.

## \|\| 2.80.42 \|\|

*sakhibhirgopakaiḥ krīḍāṃ kurvansaṃvārayaṃśca gāḥ \|*  
*dvitraiḥ priyasakhairatra mamāśrama upāvrajat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He spent his time sporting about along with his friends (the cowherds) and preventing the cows (from straying). He entered my hermitage along with his two or three dear friends.

## \|\| 2.80.43 \|\|

*mayā prakalpitairvatsabhavane sārvakāmike \|*  
*phalamūlādibhirbhakṣyaistarpitaḥ priyayā'svapat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43 Propitiated by means of fruits, roots and other edibles offered by me, he used to sleep along with his beloved lady in the calf-shed covetable by everyone.

## \|\| 2.80.44 \|\|

*susakhyā rādhayā tatra sevyamāno vrajapriyaḥ \|*  
*sārddhayāmaṃ viharati nikuñjeṣu pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 44 \|\|*

44- The cowherd fond of cowherds’ colony was served by his intimate lady friend Radha. Thus, he used to sport about in different bowers severally for a period of about four hours and a half.

## \|\| 2.80.45 \|\|

*rādhādibhistatra supto vījitaḥ śayanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sārddhayāme svayaṃ buddho nijāḥ saṃmānya tāḥ priyāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. While he was asleep there, he was fanned by Radha and others. Within a Yama and a half, he himself used to wake up and honour his beloved ones.

## \|\| 2.80.46-47 \|\|

*gopairgobhirvṛtaḥ sāyaṃ vrajaṃ yāti praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*sakhyaṃ sakhisthalaṃ prāpya priyāṃ sañcaya rādhikām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tayā saha viśālākṣyaḥ svagehānyānti cānvaham \|*  
*evaṃ gatāgataṃ kurvallīm̐ lāṃ nityamupāgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Surrounded by cowherds and cows, he delightedly used to go back to the cowherds’ colony in the evening. His female friends used to take Radha1, his beloved to the spot called Sakhi-Sthala. Every day the beautiful ladies of large eyes, used to go to their own houses along with her. Coming to and fro like this sportingly, he frequented that place everyday.

## \|\| 2.80.48 \|\|

*mayaiva dṛśyate vatsa nāpi brahmabhavādibhiḥ \|*  
*mayāpyalakṣitaṃ vatsa kubjāsaṅketavaibhavam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He is seen, О dear one, only by me and not by god Brahma, Siva and others. О dear one, the grandeur of the rendezvous of the hump-backed lady was not observed even by me.

## \|\| 2.80.49 \|\|

*prītapriyoktyā jānāmi sugopyaṃ pravadāmi te \|*  
*aṅgarāgārpaṇātpuṇyātprāptā saṅketamuttamam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I know it through the utterance of the delighted lover. I am telling you a secret that should be well guarded as well. She got this excellent rendezvous through the merit accruing from the offer of unguents to Lord Krsna.

## \|\| 2.80.50-52 \|\|

*sadā sā sevanavyagrā saikaikenāpyanekadhā \|*  
*śatakoṭimitānyevaṃ mithunāni vasanti hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kubjākṛṣṇānurūpāṇi nānākrīḍāparāṇi ca \|*  
*sambhūtānyādyamithunātsthāvaraṃ bhāṣayantyapi \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gatāgatavihīnāni nityaṃ navanavāni ca \|*  
*tadagamyaṃ tṛtīyasya dvitīyasyaikatāṃ gatam \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. She was always eagerly occupied in Krsna’s service. She was alone and he too was alone. But there are hundred crores of similar couples imitating Kubja and Krsna and engaged in different kinds of dalliance. Born of the first pair they enliven the immobile ones as well. Though they are devoid of going (out of existence?) and coming (into existence), they are still ever fresh and new (?) (Defective) that is unapproachable to the third person where the second person becomes united with one.1

## \|\| 2.80.53 \|\|

*rūpaṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ vipra sṛṣṭisthitilayaikalam \|*  
*ekaivāhaṃ vijānāmi śrutaṃ śrutvā tvamapyatha \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О Brahmana, their form comprising in itself the origination, sustenance and dissolution of the universe is extraordinary. I alone know this. Having heard what has been heard you too know this.

## \|\| 2.80.54-55 \|\|

*dagdhaḥ ṣaṭkarṇago mantra ityuktaṃ samupācara \|*  
*śrutvaitaddurlabhaṃ so'pi vṛndoktyā nārado muniḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ubhayaṃ cintayanprāpto munistatraiva tatparam \|*  
*etadra hasyaṃ vidhije viṣayaṃ guruśiṣyayoḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. A Mantra (what is secretly discussed) is burnt (doomed) if it reaches six ears. Follow (in practice) this saying. On hearing this highly inaccessible secret through the utterance of Vrnda, sage Narada thought of both. The sage acquired that great principle. О daughter of Brahma, this is the subject-matter between a preceptor and a disciple.

## \|\| 2.80.56 \|\|

*nva ko'pyaparo vetti dharmaḥ saivāvayorapi \|*  
*eka eva vijānāti vaktuḥ śrotaikataḥ śubhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. They alone understand not anyone else. The same principle holds good in regard to us both. О auspicious lady, only one knows; there is only one hearer and he knows from one the speaker.

## \|\| 2.80.57 \|\|

*tadekaṃ tattvamevāsti neha nānāsti kiñcana \|*  
*gaditaṃ te mahābhāge rahasyaṃ gopikeśituḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence, there is only one reality. There are not many things here. О highly-blessed lady, the secret of the lord of cowherd esses has been related to you.

## \|\| 2.80.58-77 \|\|

*prakāśācaritaṃ cāpi vakṣye samyaṅniśāmaya \|*  
*yatra sandarśitaṃ tattvaṃ tvatpitre vidhinandini \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tadbrahmakuṇḍametaddhi puṇyaṃ vṛndāvane vane \|*  
*tatra yaḥ snāti manujo mūlaveṣaṃ vibhāvayan \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vaibhavaṃ paśyate kiñcidevaṃ nityavihāriṇaḥ \|*  
*śakreṇa jñātatattvena govindo yatra cintitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*govindakuṇḍaṃ tadbhadre snātvā tatrāpi tallabhet \|*  
*ekānekasvarūpeṇa yatra kuñjavihāriṇā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*vallavībhiḥ samārabdho rāsastadapi tadvidham \|*  
*yatra nandādayo gopā dadṛśurvaibhavaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tacca tattvaprakāśākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ śrīyamunājale \|*  
*darśitaṃ yatra gopānāṃ kāliyasya vimardanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tacca puṇyaṃ samākhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ pāpāpahaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*dāvāgnermocitā yatra sastrībāladhanārbhakāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*gopāḥ kṛṣṇena tatpuṇyaṃ tīrthaṃ snānādaghāpaham \|*  
*yatra keśī hatastena līlayaiva hayākṛtiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tatra snātastu manujo labhate dhāma vaiṣṇavabh \|*  
*yatra duṣṭo vṛṣastena hatastatrābhavacchuciḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ariṣṭakuṇḍaṃ vikhyātaṃ snānamātreṇa muktidam \|*  
*dhenuko'gho bako vatso vyomo lambāsuro'pi ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

*hatāḥ kṛṣṇena līlāsu tatra tīrthāni yānyapi \|*  
*teṣu snātvā naro bhaktaḥ santarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*labhate vāñchitānkāmān gopālasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*suptaṃ bhuktaṃ vicaritaṃ śrutaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vilakṣaṇam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ yatra ca tatkṣetraṃ snānātsvargagatipradam \|*  
*śrutaḥ sañcintito dṛṣṭo nataḥ śliṣṭaḥ stuto'thitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yatra puṇyanarairbhadre tacca tīrthaṃ gatipradam \|*  
*yatra śrīrādhayā bhadre tapastaptaṃ sudāruṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tacchrīkuṇḍaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ snāne dāne japādike \|*  
*vatsatīrthe candra sarastathaivāpsarasāṃ saraḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*rudra kuṇḍaṃ kāmakuṇḍaṃ paramaṃ mandiraṃ hareḥ \|*  
*viśālālakanandāḍhyā nīpakhaṇḍaṃ manoharam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vimalaṃ dharmakuṇḍaṃ ca bhojanasthalameva ca \|*  
*balasthānaṃ bṛhatsānuḥ saṅketasthānakaṃ hareḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*naṃdigrāmaḥ kiśoryāśca kuṇḍaṃ kokilakānanam \|*  
*śeṣaśāyipayo'bdhiśca krīḍādeśo'kṣayo vaṭaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*rāmakuṇḍaṃ cīracauryaṃ bhadra bhāṇḍīrabilvakam \|*  
*mānāhvaṃ ca saraḥ puṇyaṃ pulinaṃ bhaktabhojanam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*akrūraṃ tārkṣyagovindaṃ bahulāraṇyakaṃ śubhe \|*  
*etadvṛndāvanaṃ nāma samantātpañcayojanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

58-60a. I shall narrate to you the open public behaviour of the lord. Listen with proper attention. О daughter of Brahma, in the forest of Vrndavana, this Brahmakuncja is highly meritorious. It is the place where Reality was clearly manifested to your father. The man who takes a holy dip there, pondering over the original dress and feature, visualizes a part of the grandeur of the Eternal Player.

60b-61a. О gentle lady, it is Govindakuntja where Govinda was pondered over by Indra who understood the Tattva (the real principle). By taking the holy dip there one shall attain ‘That’.

61b-62a. Where the Rasa dance was begun by Kuftjaviharin (one who sports about in bowers i.e. Lord Krsna) who assumed single as well as multifarious forms and danced with the cowherdesses, a Tirtha has been formed of the same nature and efficacy. By taking a holy dip therein, one can realise the lord.

62b-63a. At the spot where Nanda and other cowherds saw the magnificence of the omnipresent Lord, is a Tirtha called by the name Tattva-Prakasa (Revealer of Reality). It is waters of Sri Yamuna.

63b-64a. The place where the encounter with and pounding of Kaliya was shown to the cowherds is mentioned as a meritorious Tirtha. It is destructive of sins of men.

64b-65a. The place where the cowherds were rescued from the forest fire along with their womenfolk, children, infants and wealth by Krsna is a holy Tirtha. which is destructive of sins by means of a holy dip therein

65b-66a. A man who takes a holy dip in the place where demon Kesinwho had assumed the form of a horse had been killed by Krsna playfully, attains the abode of Visnu.

66b-67a. The place where the wicked demon Vrsa was killed by him who thereby became pure, is well known as Aristakunda. It yields salvation merely through holy dip therein.

67b-69a. There are Tlrthas in the places where the demons Dhenuka, Agha, Baka, Vatsa, Vyoma and Lamba were killed by Krsna sportively. By taking bath and by performing Tarpana rites devoutly to the Pitrs and the Devas, the devotee attains the desired benefits, thanks to the favour of Gopala.

69b-70a. The places where he slept, took food, walked about, something was heard by him, or seen by him, or committed by him in an extraordinary manner are all K?etras (holy centres). They yield heavenly goal by means of a holy dip therein, О gentle lady.

70b-71a. Wherever he was heard, thought about, seen, bowed, embraced, eulogised or requested for by meritorious persons, there exists a Tirtha that bestows salvation.

71b-72a. О gentle lady, the place where a terrible penance was performed by Sriradha is Sri Kunda which is highly meritorious for a holy dip, charitable gifts, Japa and other things.

72b-77. The holy place of Vrndavana extends to five Yojanas (60 kms.) all round and the following arc the main Tirthas: Vatsitirtha, Gandrasaras, Apsaras lake, Rudrakunda, Kamakunda, the great temple of Hari, Visala (rich in merit by) having the Alakananda, the beautiful Nipakhanda, Dharmakunda, devoid of impurities, the spot of Krsna’s taking meals, the region of Bala, Brhatsanu, the place of rendezvous of Hari, Nandigrama, Kunda (holy pool) of Kisorl (girl), Kokilakanana (the forest of cuckoos), the milk ocean of Sesasayin, Krldadesa (the place of sports), Aksayavata, Ramakunda, Ciracaurya (the place where garments of cowherdesses were stolen by Krsna), Bhadrabhandirabilvaka, the sacred lake called Mana, the bank called Bhaktabhojana, the Akrfira Tirtha, Tarksyagovinda and Bahularanyaka. О auspicious lady, such is the holy centre Vi ndavana.

## \|\| 2.80.78 \|\|

*supuṇyaṃ puṇyakṛjjuṣṭaṃ darśanādeva muktidam \|*  
*yasya sandarśanaṃ devā vāñchanti ca sudurlabham \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. It is very holy. It is resorted to by the meritorious persons. By its mere sight, it bestows salvation. Even the Devas desire for its view which is difficult of access (even to them).

## \|\| 2.80.79-82 \|\|

*līlāmābhyantarīṃ dra ṣṭuṃ tapasāpi na ca kṣamāḥ \|*  
*sarvatra saṅgamutsṛjya yastu vṛndāvanaṃ śrayet \|\| 79 \|\|*

*na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcittriṣu lokeṣu bhāmini \|*  
*vṛndāvaneti nāmāpi yaḥ samuccarati priye \|\| 80 \|\|*

*tasyāpi bhaktirbhavati satataṃ nandanandane \|*  
*yatra vṛndāvane puṇye naranārīplavaṅgamāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kṛmikīṭapataṅgādyāḥ khagā vṛkṣā nagā mṛgāḥ \|*  
*samuccaranti satataṃ rādhākṛṣṇeti mohini \|\| 82 \|\|*

79-80a. People are not competent to witness the interior sport even by means of penance. О beautiful woman, in all the three worlds, there is nothing difficult of access to that person who eschews attachment everywhere and resorts to Vrndavana.

80b-81a. О lady (dear to all), perpetual devotion to Nandanandana rises up even in a person who utters the name ‘Vrndavana’.

81b-82. О Mohini, in the holy Vrndavana, men, women, monkeys, worms, insects, locusts, birds, trees, deer, mountains always utter the names Rad ha and Krsna.

## \|\| 2.80.83 \|\|

*kṛṣṇamāyābhibhūtānāṃ kāmakaśmalacetasām \|*  
*svapne'pi durlabhaṃ puṃsāṃ manye vṛndāvanekṣaṇam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. I think that a visit to Vrndavana is difficult to those men who are overwhelmed by Krsna’s Maya and whose minds arc defiled by lust.

## \|\| 2.80.84 \|\|

*vṛndāraṇyaṃ tu yairdṛṣṭaṃ naraiḥ sukṛtibhiḥ śubhe \|*  
*taiḥ kṛtaṃ saphalaṃ janma kṛpāpātrāṇi te hareḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. О auspicious lady, their lives have been rendered fruitful by those meritorious persons by whom Vrndavana has been visited. They deserve the compassion of Hari.

## \|\| 2.80.85 \|\|

*kiṃ punarbahunoktena śrutena vidhinandini \|*  
*sevyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ bhavyaṃ muktimabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. О daughter of Brahma, of what use is much talk said and heard? The splendid and meritorious Vrndavana must be resorted to by those who desire to attain liberation.

## \|\| 2.80.86 \|\|

*dṛśyaṃ gamyaṃ ca saṃsekhyaṃ dhyeyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ sadā \|*  
*nāsti loke samaṃ tasya bhuvi kīrtivivarddhanam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Vrndavana must be seen, approached, resorted to and meditated upon always. There is nothing else on the earth that is as conducive to the enhancement of glory.

## \|\| 2.80.87 \|\|

*yatra govarddhano nāma dvijaḥ kalpe purātane \|*  
*viraktaḥ sarvasaṃsārāttaptavānparamaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. It was here that in an ancient Kalpa, a Brahmana named Govardhana performed a great penance after becoming detached from the entire world.

## \|\| 2.80.88 \|\|

*tadgatvā devi deveśo bhagavānviṣṇuravyayaḥ \|*  
*krīḍāsthānaṃ nijaṃ prāpto varaṃ dātuṃ dvijanmane \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. О gentle lady, the unchanging lord Visnu, the lord of Devas, went to that place of his in order to grant the boon to that Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.80.89-92 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā devadeveśaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*vilasatkaustubhoraskaṃ makarākṛtikuṇḍalam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sukirīṭaṃ sukaṭakaṃ kalanūpurabhūṣitam \|*  
*vanamālānivītāṅgaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*pītakauśeyavasanaṃ navāmbudasamaprabham \|*  
*sunābhiṃ sundaragrīvaṃ sukapolaṃ sunāsikam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*sudvijaṃ susmitaṃ suṣṭhujānūrubhujamadhyakam \|*  
*kṛpārṇavaṃ pramuditaṃ suprasannamukhāmbujam \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-92. The Brahmana saw the lord of gods thus; He was holding the conch, discus and iron club. The jewel Kaustubha was shining on his chest. His earrings had the shape of the shark. He had a good crown and beautiful bangles. He was bedecked in anklets that produced a sweet jingling sound. A garland of sylvan flowers was worn round his neck. There was a mark of Srivatsa on his chest. He was clad in a yellow silken garment. He had the lustre of a fresh cloud. His umbilicus, neck, cheeks, nose, teeth, knees, thigh, and the waist were all fine and beautiful. He was an ocean of mercy. He was joyous: His lotus-like face indicated his pleasure.

## \|\| 2.80.93 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā sa sahasotthāya nanāma bhuvi daṇḍavat \|*  
*varaṃ brūhīti nirddiṣṭo prāha govarddhano harim \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. On seeing the lord, the Brahmana got up immediately and prostrated on the ground straight as a staff. On being asked, ‘‘Tell me the boon you wish to choose”, Govardhana said to Hari:

## \|\| 2.80.94-96 \|\|

*padbhyāmākramya matpṛṣṭhe tiṣṭha caiva varo mama \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhaktavaśyo vai vicintya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tasthau tatpṛṣṭhamākramya tadā bhūyo dvijo'bravīt \|*  
*nāhaṃ tvāmutsahe deva nijapṛṣṭhe jagatpate \|\| 95 \|\|*

*avatārayituṃ tasmādevameva sthiro bhava \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti viśvātmā tyaktvā govarddhanaṃ dvijam \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96a. “Place your feet on my back and stand there. This is the boon I crave for”. On hearing it, the lord thought over it again and again and finally stood on his back. Then the Brahmana said again: “O lord, О lord of the universe, I cannot approve of letting you come down from my back. Hence, be steady like this. 1

96b. Ever since that time, the lord, the Atman of the universe did not abandon the Brahmana Govardhana who assumed the form of a mountain. In some cases he goes to Yogivana.

## \|\| 2.80.97-99 \|\|

*girirūpadharaṃ yāti nityaṃ yogivanaṃ kvacit \|*  
*kṛṣṇāvatāre bhagavān jñātvā govarddhanaṃ dvijam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*samprāptaṃ nijasārūpyaṃ nandādyaiḥ samabhojayat \|*  
*annakūṭena dohena tarpayitvācalaṃ dvijam \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tṛṭparītaṃ samājñāya navameghānapāyayat \|*  
*mitraṃ sa vāsudevasya sañjātaṃ tena karmaṇā \|\| 99 \|\|*

97-99. During the time of his incarnation as Krsna, the lord knew that the Brahmana Govardhana had attained Sarupya (the identity of form) with himself. Hence, he fed him through Nanda and others by means of a heap of cooked rice and milk. After propitiating the Brahmana turned into a mountain he realized that he was thirsty. So he made him drink from the fresh clouds. By this action he became a friend of Vasudeva.

## \|\| 2.80.100 \|\|

*taṃ yo bhaktyā naro devi pūjayedupacārakaiḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ parikrāmenna tasya punarudbhavaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. О gentle lady, the man who devoutly worships the mountain by means of services and circumambulates it, gets no rebirth.

## \|\| 2.80.101 \|\|

*govarddhano giriḥ puṇyo jāto harinivāsataḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā darśanenālamanyapuṇyācalasya ca \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The mountain Govardhana has become meritorious, thanks to the residence ofHari. If one visits this, he need not visit other holy mountains.

## \|\| 2.80.102 \|\|

*yāmunaṃ pulinaṃ ramyaṃ kṛṣṇavikrīḍanāñcitam \|*  
*tvameva brūhi subhage kvānyatra jagatītale \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The sand-banks of the Yamuna are beautiful and rendered more so by the sports of Krsna, О blessed lady, say yourself: Where else on the surface of the earth, can you sec a holier place?

## \|\| 2.80.103 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tyaktvā vananadīgirīn \|*  
*supuṇyānpuṇyadān nṝṇāṃ sevyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ sadā \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Hence, after abandoning other holy forests, rivers and mountains that yield merit unto men, Vrndavana should always be resorted to.

## \|\| 2.80.104 \|\|

*yamī puṇyā nadī yatra puṇyo govarddhano giriḥ \|*  
*tatkiṃ vṛndāvanātpuṇyamaraṇyaṃ bhuvi vidyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The river Yami (Yamuna) is holy. The mountain Govardhana is holy. Hence, is there any forest on the earth holier than Vrndavana?

## \|\| 2.80.105 \|\|

*kalikalmaṣabhītānāṃ viṣayāsaktacetasām \|*  
*nānyaṃ vṛndāvanātsevyamasti lokeṣvaṣi triṣu \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. There is nothing else worthy of being resorted to by persons whose minds are deeply attached to worldly objects and who are afraid of the sins of Kali age. There is no other place in the three worlds but Vrndavana that is worthy of being resorted to.

## \|\| 2.80.106 \|\|

*yasminnityaṃ vicarati harirgopagogopikābhi- rbarhāpīḍī naṭavaravapuḥ karṇikārāvataṃsī \|*  
*vaṃśīhaṃsīsvanajitaravo vaijayantīvṛtāṅgo \|*  
*nandasyāṅgāddhṛtamaṇigaṇo yaśca haṃso'hamākhyaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. In it Hari roams about all the while along with the cows, cowherds and cowherdesses. Peacock feathers adorn his crest. He has the form of an excellent dancer. Karnikara flowers adorn his ears. By the sound of his flute, the sound of the female swan is conquered (i.e. it excels it). VaijayantI garland covers his body. He has acquired a number of jewels from Nanda’s person. He is the supreme soul called Hamsa (swan) and Aham (?)

## \|\| 2.80.107 \|\|

*yasya dhyānaṃ nagajaniyuto'harniśaṃ vai girīśo \|*  
*bhaktiklinno rahasi kurute hyarddhanārīśvarākhyaḥ \|*  
*gāyatrīṃ strīṃ hṛdayakuhare padmayonirvidhatte \|*  
*netrairindro daśaśatamitairvīkṣate vai śacīṃ tām \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Girisa (Siva) who melts (i.e. is overwhelmed) with devotion, meditates on him day and night in the company of the daughter of the mountain (Parvati) in secret. He is indeed called Ardhanarlsvara. The lotus-born deity Brahma keeps his wife Gayatri within the cavity of his heart. Indra looks at Saci with his thousand eyes (?)

## \|\| 2.80.108 \|\|

*aśrotreśo rahasi vanitāṃ rakṣati svāṃ rasajño \|*  
*vaṃśīnādaśravaṇajabhiyā kānyavārtā janānām \|*  
*chedaṃ śoṣaṃ tadanu dahanaṃ bhedanaṃ prāpya yāsī- cchrīgopīśāgharajanisudhāṃ sādaraṃ śīlayantī \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. (Defective) A person who appreciates the taste but not a master of the ear confines his wife in a secret (isolated) place due to the fear of hearing the sound of the flute. What else is the popular talk? The flute (which was originally a piece of bamboo) underwent the process of cutting, drying, burning and perforation (?). Still it yearned to imbibe the nectar from the lips of the lord of cowherdesses.

## \|\| 2.80.109 \|\|

*yābhirvṛndāvanamanugato nandasūnuḥ kṣapāsu \|*  
*reme candrā śuṃ!kalitasamudyotabhadre nikuñje \|*  
*tāsāṃ diṣṭaṃ kimahamadhunā varṇaye ballavīnāṃ \|*  
*yāsāṃ sākṣāccaraṇajarajaḥ śrīśavidhyādyalabhyam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. How can I describe the good fortune of those Ballavls (cowherdesses) accompanied by whom, the son of Nanda came to Vrndavana during the nights and sported in dalliance in the bowers brightly illuminated by the rays of the moon. Even the dust from their feet is not attainable to Sri (Laksmi), Siva, Brahma and oth ers.

## \|\| 2.80.110 \|\|

*yatra prāptāstṛṇamṛgakhagā ye kṛmiprāṇivṛndā- vṛndāraṇye vidhihararamābhyarhaṇīyā bhavanti \|*  
*tatsamprāpyādvayapadarato brahmabhūyaṃ gataḥkau \|*  
*premasnigdho viharati sukhāmbhodhikallolamagnaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Even the grasses, deer, birds, worms and other living beings that have attained Vrndavana are worthy of being worshipped by Brahma, Нага and Rama (Laksmi). A person who comes there and is engaged in the nondualistic states (of the Lord) and who has attained Brahman-hood becomes happy in love and plays about immersed in the billows of the ocean of happiness.

## \|\| 2.80.111 \|\|

*yatra krūrāḥ sahajamasubhṛdvrātajātā visṛjya \|*  
*vairaṃ svairaṃ suhṛda iva tatsaukhyamevāśrayaṃte \|*  
*tatkiṃ prāpya prabhumiva janaḥ samparityajya gacchan \|*  
*kvāpyanyatra prabhavati sukhī kṛṣṇamāyākaraṇḍe \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. There (in Vrndavana) wild beasts of prey forget their natural enmity and behave like friends and enjoy the bliss of Vrndavana. If one eschews this and goes elsewhere, can he be happy (in the world) that is a boxofKrsna’s Maya? Gan a person who eschews lord of wealth and goes elsewhere get wealth?

## \|\| 2.80.112 \|\|

*vṛndāraṇyaṃ tadakhiladharāpuṇyarūpaṃ śrayanme \|*  
*svāntaṃ dhvāntaṃ jagadidamadhaḥ kṛtya varvarti śaśvat \|*  
*gopīnāthaḥ pratipadamapi premasaṅiklannacetā \|*  
*nīcaṃ voccaṃ na ca gaṇayati proddharatyeva bhaktān \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. That Vrndavana forest is the form of the merit of the whole world. Resorting to it, the darkness in my mind (is dispelled). I am able to excel the whole world and keep it permanently suppressed. At every step, the lord of the cowherdesses is soaked in love. He does not differentiate between a high born and a low born person, but uplifts all devotees irrespective of their states.

## \|\| 2.80.113 \|\|

*gopān gopīḥ khagamṛganagāgopagobhūrajāṃsi \|*  
*smṛtvā dṛṣṭvā praṇamati jane premarajjvā nibaddhaḥ \|*  
*dāsyaṃ bhakte kalayatitarāṃ tatkimanyaṃ vrajeśāt \|*  
*sevyaṃ devaṃ gaṇaya vidhije'ha tu jānāmi naiva \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Lord Krsna is prepared even to serve a devotee who remembers and sees the cowherds, cowherdesses, birds, deer, mountains and the dust of the land trodden by the cows and the cowherds and bows down. He is tied to them by means of the rope of love. Hence do not think of any other lord worthy of being resorted to, other than the lord of the cowherd’s colony. О daughter of Brahma I do not know any other such deity.

## \|\| 2.80.114 \|\|

*etatsaṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ vṛndāraṇyasamudbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vidhije tubhyaṃ vaktavyaṃ nāvaśeṣitam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thus the greatness of the forest of Vrndavana has been succinctly narrated to you, О daughter of Brahma. There remains nothing to be recounted.

## \|\| 2.80.115 \|\|

*saṃsārabhītairmanujairetadeva sadānaghaiḥ \|*  
*śrotavyaṃ kīrtanīyaṃ ca smartavyaṃ dhyeyameva ca \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. This alone should always be heard, glorified, remembered and meditated upon by sinless men afraid of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.80.116 \|\|

*vṛndāraṇyasya māhātmyaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*kīrtayedvāpi vidhije so'pi viṣṇurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. О daughter of Brahma, the pure man who listens, to the greatness of Vrndavana and glorifies it, is undoubtedly Visnu himself.

## Chapter 81. The Review of the Story of Vasu

## \|\| 2.81.1 \|\|

*vasuruvāca- yadetatkīrtitaṃ devi tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*tallabhasva mahābhāge caritvā tīrthamaṇḍalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasu said:

1\. О blessed lady, attain everything that has been glorified in the section on the excellent greatness of the Tlrthas, by undertaking pilgrimage to the zones of Tlrthas (holy centres), О queen.'

## \|\| 2.81.2 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmāṇamāmantr! ya pitaraṃ te nareśvari \|*  
*vṛndāvanamupāgamya cariṣyāmi mṛgaiḥ saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О queen of men, I shall invite Brahma, your father, and going back to Vrndavana roam about along with the deer.

## \|\| 2.81.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca- ityuktvā mohinīṃ viprā vasustasyāḥ purohitaḥ \|*  
*satkṛtya pūjito'bhīkṣṇaṃ brahmalokaṃ yayau tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sdta said:

3\. After saying thus to MohinI, О Brahmanas, Vasu, her priest was honoured and repeatedly worshipped. Thereafter, he went to the world of Brahma. 9

## \|\| 2.81.4 \|\|

*sa gatvā tatra dhātāraṃ brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ vidhim \|*  
*praṇamya mohinīvṛttaṃ taṃ kārtsnyena nyavedayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After going there he bowed down to god Brahma, the creator, the maker of the worlds and reported to him the complete details ofMohinl’s activities.

## \|\| 2.81.5 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ brahmā brāhmaṇasya vasordvijāḥ \|*  
*prasannaḥ prāha taṃ vatsa sukṛtaṃ hi tvayā kṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing the words of the Brahmana Vasu, О Brahmanas, Brahma was delighted. He said to him — ” О dear one, indeed you have accomplished a meritorious work.

## \|\| 2.81.6 \|\|

*yā mayā mohinī vipra devakāryārthamātmajā \|*  
*niyuktā'kṛtakāryā sā tvayā śaptā kṣayaṃ gatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О Brahmana, the daughter of mine, MohinI, who had been engaged by me for the purpose of Devas was unsuccessful in her mission. She was cursed by you and her destruction was effected.
